name: Stay, Build, Flourish: Nova Scotia
future_picture_statement: Young people in Nova Scotia build fulfilling lives — whether in emerging industries or established trades, in entrepreneurial ventures or community services, in technology or the arts — drawn to stay or return by a welcoming province where diverse communities thrive and quality of life rivals any region in Canada or beyond.

obstacles.title: Structural Economic Scale and Capital Constraints
obstacles.description: A small, fragmented market, thin supply chains, limited patient and risk capital, and procurement/regulatory barriers constrain firm formation, scaling, and commercialization across sectors. Without stronger capital flows, anchor customers, and market access, high-quality opportunities for young people remain scarce and brittle.

obstacles.title: Livability and Enabling Infrastructure Gaps
obstacles.description: Systems that produce and maintain housing, transit and regional connectivity, healthcare and mental health access, childcare, broadband, and climate-resilient community assets are under-capacity and slow to deliver. Financing, permitting, and coordination bottlenecks raise costs and limit access, making staying or returning untenable even when jobs exist.

obstacles.title: Fragmented Policy and Governance Architecture
obstacles.description: Siloed ministries, municipal–provincial–federal misalignment, short funding cycles, program churn, and unclear accountability impede coherent strategy and execution. The absence of cross-sector coordination and shared metrics diffuses resources and slows delivery on youth, workforce, innovation, and community priorities.

obstacles.title: Talent and Mobility System Misalignment
obstacles.description: Education, training, apprenticeship, immigration, credential recognition, and employer practices are weakly integrated with current and emerging sector needs. Thin co-op/apprenticeship capacity, friction in interprovincial and immigration pathways, and underused remote/circular work options prevent opportunities and people from matching at the right time and place.

obstacles.title: Systemic Exclusion and Weak Sense of Belonging
obstacles.description: Enduring racism, colonial structures, and bias limit access to capital, land, networks, and decision-making for Indigenous, African Nova Scotian, Acadian, rural, newcomer, and 2SLGBTQIA+ youth. Under-resourced cultural and community supports and low representation in institutions depress participation and retention regardless of economic conditions.

obstacles.title: Negative Narrative and Perception Trap
obstacles.description: A dominant story frames success as leaving Nova Scotia, reinforced by peer pressure, guidance signals, national employer pull, and limited visibility of local wins. Weak youth-facing place and employer branding and sparse celebration of homegrown success create a self-reinforcing cycle that lowers intent to stay or return and blunts policy impact.

obstacles.title: Insufficient Quality Jobs and Career Ladders
obstacles.description: Too few stable, well-paying roles with clear advancement—especially outside Halifax—push young people to larger centres.

solutions.text: Community-led Mini Incubators and Makerspaces: Convert underused municipal or non-profit spaces into low-cost incubators and makerspaces that provide equipment, mentorship, and business supports for startups, social enterprises, and skilled tradespeople to prototype, scale and hire locally.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.organization: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: Start-Up Yard is an ocean-technology incubator located in a repurposed federal Coast Guard facility, providing access to shared workshops, prototyping labs, machine shop, wet labs, and a deepwater testing wharf. It delivers structured mentorship, business advisory, and market development supports that help startups and trades-focused suppliers prototype, scale, and hire locally within Nova Scotia’s blue economy.

resources.name: Navigate Startup House
resources.organization: Navigate (Cape Breton University + Cape Breton Partnership)
resources.description: Navigate provides low-cost co-working, a makerspace-style prototyping area, and entrepreneurial programming from a renovated community innovation hub in Sydney’s downtown. Through mentorship, workshops, and one-on-one business coaching (delivered by a partnership of Cape Breton University and the Cape Breton Partnership), it enables startups, social enterprises, and tradespeople in Cape Breton to build, test, and grow companies without leaving the region.

resources.name: Rural Innovation Centre (RIC) at the Perennia Innovation Centre
resources.description: The Rural Innovation Centre offers incubator space, shared labs, pilot-scale processing facilities, and technical advisory services for agri-food and bioresource startups in a provincially owned facility in Bible Hill. It pairs equipment access with mentorship, product development support, and business advisory to help rural entrepreneurs prototype, scale production, and create quality local jobs.
resources.address: 90 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: North Queens Business Hub
resources.description: Located in a repurposed municipal building in Caledonia, the North Queens Business Hub provides affordable co-working space, meeting rooms, and shared equipment alongside regular workshops and one-on-one small business support. By lowering the barriers to space and business services in a rural community, it serves as a mini-incubator that helps freelancers, tradespeople, and early-stage ventures start, operate, and hire locally.

solutions.text: Local Apprenticeship and Mentorship Network: Create a community-managed registry that matches apprentices with local employers, retired tradespeople mentors, and peer cohorts, coordinates block-release training, and promotes clear local career ladders in trades and technical fields.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY connects high school students across Nova Scotia with paid summer placements in the construction sector, pairing them with local employers and on-the-job journeyperson mentors. The program maps clear pathways into apprenticeship, facilitates safety and introductory training, and links participants with NSAA/NSCC for block-release training after they register as apprentices—creating a local pipeline and visible career ladder in the skilled trades.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: NSCC Apprenticeship Training
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College delivers the in-school technical (block-release and day-release) training for dozens of designated trades, organizing cohorts and schedules in coordination with employers and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency. Through labs, industry partnerships, and campus-based supports, NSCC helps apprentices connect with local employers and mentors while progressing along clear pathways from entry-level apprentice to certified journeyperson and beyond.

resources.name: Irving Shipbuilding Centre of Excellence (ISCE) and Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) and Irving Shipbuilding Inc.
resources.description: This partnership recruits and supports cohorts—often from underrepresented communities—into shipbuilding trades, matching learners with Irving Shipbuilding and supply-chain employers and pairing them with experienced journeyperson mentors on the job. NSCC coordinates the block-release technical training for these cohorts, and the program lays out clear progression from pre-apprenticeship through registered apprenticeship to Red Seal certification, strengthening local career ladders in advanced manufacturing and marine trades.

resources.name: Carpenters Local 83 Apprenticeship & Training
resources.organization: Atlantic Canada Regional Council of Carpenters, Millwrights and Allied Workers (Local 83)
resources.description: Through its hiring hall and training centre, Local 83 connects apprentice carpenters with signatory contractors across Nova Scotia and ensures mentorship by certified journeypersons on worksites and in training. The union coordinates with NSCC and the provincial apprenticeship system for block-release schooling and provides a clear, supported career ladder—from entry-level apprentice to Red Seal carpenter—with ongoing upskilling delivered by experienced (often retired) trades professionals.
resources.address: 1000 Sackville Drive, Lower Sackville, NS B4E 1S4

solutions.text: Regional Employer Consortium for Career Pathways: Form a consortium of local employers, schools and colleges to map in-demand jobs, agree on transferable competencies, create stacked credentials, and coordinate rotating placements so workers can progress across firms and sectors.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Irving Shipbuilding Inc. in partnership with Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency
resources.description: A multi-employer, education, and community consortium led by Irving Shipbuilding and NSCC that co-designs training aligned to in-demand marine trades (e.g., welding, metal fabrication) and maps competencies needed for shipbuilding careers. The program uses stackable credentials (trade readiness, CWB welding tickets, apprenticeship levels) and coordinates paid work-integrated learning and on-the-job training at the Halifax Shipyard and partner firms, enabling participants to progress from pre-apprenticeship into Red Seal pathways across employers in the marine sector.

resources.name: COVE Workforce Initiative
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE convenes ocean-technology employers, colleges/universities, and government to identify in-demand roles and shared, transferable competencies across subsectors like marine robotics, sensors, and maritime operations. Through co-designed micro-credentials, industry-informed training, and internships/co-op placements that span multiple tenant companies at the COVE campus and beyond, the initiative builds stackable, portable credentials and facilitates rotational experiences so talent can progress across firms within the ocean sector.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.organization: Construction Association of Nova Scotia (CANS), in partnership with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and Nova Scotia’s Regional Centres for Education
resources.description: BFY is a province-wide consortium led by the Construction Association of Nova Scotia with employers, school boards, and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency to create clear pathways into construction trades. Students complete industry-recognized, stackable safety and trade-readiness credentials and undertake paid summer co-op placements with multiple construction firms, earning apprenticeship credit and exposure to different trades—laying a competency-based foundation to move between employers and advance into full apprenticeships.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program
resources.description: The provincial apprenticeship system partners with sector councils, unions, employers, and NSCC to map in-demand trades to detailed competency profiles and training standards. It supports stacked credentials (youth apprenticeship, pre-apprenticeship, level training to Red Seal) and enables apprentices to move among sponsoring employers or through joint employer arrangements to complete the full scope of required competencies—coordinating rotations and placements that build portable skills and career mobility across firms and sectors.

solutions.text: Community-run Remote Work Hubs and Coworking Spaces: Establish affordable coworking hubs with reliable broadband, meeting rooms and business supports to attract remote workers, help local entrepreneurs scale, and host employer-led training and hiring events.

resources.name: IGNITE Yarmouth Coworking Space
resources.description: IGNITE’s Yarmouth hub provides affordable coworking desks, private offices, and meeting rooms with high-speed internet for remote workers, startups, and small businesses. The space delivers business supports—mentorship, programming, and workshops—and regularly hosts employer-led training, networking, and hiring events that connect local talent with companies and scale-ups across Atlantic Canada.

resources.name: IGNITE Pictou County Coworking Space
resources.description: IGNITE’s New Glasgow location offers open desks, private offices, boardrooms, and maker/innovation spaces with reliable broadband, enabling remote workers and entrepreneurs to operate from northeastern Nova Scotia. It delivers programming, mentorship, and partnerships with employers to run training sessions, pitch nights, and recruitment/networking events that help residents access quality jobs and build career pathways locally.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

resources.name: CO3 Community Coworking Space
resources.description: CO3 is a community-run coworking hub on the South Shore that offers day passes and memberships for affordable desks, meeting rooms, and event space with dependable broadband. The space supports local entrepreneurs and remote professionals by hosting business workshops, peer meetups, and employer information sessions in partnership with regional organizations, helping people work, learn, and connect without leaving the region.

resources.name: Navigate Startup House
resources.organization: Navigate (partnership of Cape Breton University and NSCC Marconi Campus)
resources.description: Navigate Startup House provides shared workspaces, private offices, and meeting rooms with high-speed internet for founders, freelancers, and remote workers in downtown Sydney. As a partnership-driven hub, it delivers mentorship and business supports and hosts employer-led workshops, networking, and hiring events that strengthen career pathways and retain talent in Cape Breton.

solutions.text: Local Micro-credential and Training Partnerships: Partner with community colleges, adult learning centres and employers to deliver short, stackable certifications tailored to local industry needs (e.g., healthcare supports, advanced manufacturing, digital skills) with clear links to local job openings.

resources.name: NSCC MicroCredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College delivers short, stackable micro-credentials co-designed with local employers in sectors such as healthcare supports, advanced manufacturing, oceans, and digital skills. Courses are offered across NSCC campuses and online, issue digital badges, and are aligned to regional labour market needs; learners are connected to local job openings through NSCC Career Services, employer partnerships, and work-integrated projects.

resources.name: Skills for Hire Atlantic
resources.description: Skills for Hire Atlantic is a short, cohort-based training initiative that provides stackable, industry-aligned credentials in in-demand digital skills (e.g., data, cloud, web, cybersecurity) developed with input from Nova Scotia and Atlantic Canadian tech employers. The program includes employer-led projects, career coaching, networking and job fairs, and direct connections to hiring partners, helping graduates transition into local entry-level roles quickly.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 309, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: CANS WORKS – Construction Job Readiness Program
resources.description: CANS WORKS delivers short, stackable site-readiness and safety certifications (e.g., WHMIS, Fall Protection, First Aid, Traffic Control) tailored to employer requirements in Nova Scotia’s construction sector. The program partners with Nova Scotia Works and construction employers to provide hands-on training, job search support, and employer interviews/placements that link participants directly to current job openings across the province.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Open Learning Microcredentials
resources.organization: Dalhousie University — Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development offers short, stackable micro-credentials and digital badges in areas like data analytics, leadership, and project management that are developed with employer input. Programs emphasize applied projects and pathways that build toward larger certificates, and the faculty partners with organizations on cohort upskilling while connecting learners to hiring networks and local opportunities.

solutions.text: Community Investment in Worker Cooperatives: Support the creation and scaling of worker-owned cooperatives (in food, construction, tourism, digital services) through seed funding, shared back-office services, and procurement commitments to create stable, locally rooted jobs.

resources.name: Social Procurement Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Social Procurement Program embeds social value criteria into public purchasing, awarding evaluation points for bids that deliver community benefits and inclusive employment. This creates concrete procurement opportunities that worker-owned cooperatives can compete for, providing the predictable revenue streams needed to launch and scale locally rooted, stable jobs across sectors like construction, food, tourism, and digital services.

resources.name: International Centre for Co-operative Management (ICCM)
resources.organization: Sobey School of Business, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: ICCM delivers specialized education and advisory services that help start and scale cooperatives, including worker co-ops, by strengthening governance, finance, operations, and leadership capacity. By providing shared back-office know-how (e.g., financial management systems, HR practices, and governance frameworks) and tailored training, ICCM equips Nova Scotia co-ops to create quality, locally rooted jobs and build clear career ladders for young workers.

resources.name: Just Us! Coffee Roasters Co-op
resources.description: Just Us! is a worker-owned cooperative that has created stable, living-wage employment in the Annapolis Valley while demonstrating a successful pathway for worker ownership in food processing and retail. Through community-rooted ownership and long-term supply and purchasing relationships with local institutions and retailers, the co-op models how worker ownership can anchor jobs outside Halifax and provide advancement opportunities for young workers.

solutions.text: Youth Entrepreneurship Grants and Mentoring: Create small grants, in-kind supports and mentorship programs for youth-led startups and social enterprises to help young people launch businesses locally and learn practical business growth and hiring skills.

resources.name: CEED Youth Entrepreneurship Programs
resources.description: CEED delivers youth-focused entrepreneurship training, coaching, and mentorship to help young people start and grow businesses in Nova Scotia. The programs pair practical workshops and one-on-one advising with access to startup financing (including microloans) and pitch opportunities, providing both in-kind supports and early-stage capital so youth-led ventures can hire and scale locally.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: IGNITE Youth
resources.description: IGNITE Youth runs entrepreneurship camps, challenges, and accelerator-style programming across rural Nova Scotia that connect students and young founders with mentors, workspace, and prototyping tools. Many activities culminate in pitch events with cash awards and ongoing coaching, giving youth-led startups and social enterprises both grant-style funding and in-kind supports to launch and grow in their home communities.
resources.address: 208 Main Street, Unit 102, Yarmouth, NS B5A 1C8

resources.name: SMU Startup Accelerator
resources.organization: Arthur L. Irving Entrepreneurship Centre, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: The SMU Startup Accelerator supports Saint Mary’s University students and recent graduates with intensive mentorship, workshops, co-working space, and seed funding stipends/microgrants to launch ventures. By combining capital with in-kind supports and expert guidance, the program helps youth founders build practical business, growth, and hiring skills while creating jobs in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Navigate Student Incubator
resources.organization: Navigate Startup House (Cape Breton University & NSCC Marconi)
resources.description: Navigate provides student and youth entrepreneurs in Cape Breton with free co-working space, mentorship, and programming to validate ideas and build ventures locally. It offers in-kind supports (workspace, advisory, network access) and connects participants to regional pitch competitions and small grants, helping youth-led startups gain early funding and develop the skills to grow and hire.

solutions.text: Local Procurement and Hire-Local Pledges: Encourage municipal governments, hospitals and school boards to adopt buy-local and hire-local policies and targets, including subcontracting to local firms and prioritizing hires that create career ladder opportunities.

resources.name: Sustainable Procurement Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Sustainable Procurement Program embeds social and local economic value into public purchasing by adding evaluation criteria that encourage bidders to use local subcontractors, support supplier diversity, and deliver workforce development outcomes. By rewarding proposals that include apprenticeships, on‑the‑job training, and living‑wage commitments, HRM’s tenders help create quality, career‑ladder jobs for local residents. This municipal approach operationalizes buy‑local and hire‑local goals across construction, services, and goods contracts.

resources.name: Supplier Development Program
resources.description: The Province of Nova Scotia’s Supplier Development Program helps small and medium-sized Nova Scotia firms sell to the public sector—municipalities, health authorities, universities, and school boards—through training, meet‑the‑buyer events, and guidance on bidding. By building institutional buyer–supplier connections and encouraging buyers to structure procurements that enable local participation and subcontracting, the program advances buy‑local priorities. The resulting contracts support stable employment and can include requirements that foster apprenticeships and career progression in local firms.

resources.name: Farm to School Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Farm to Cafeteria Canada (Nova Scotia partners include Ecology Action Centre)
resources.description: Farm to School Nova Scotia works with schools and school boards to increase the amount of Nova Scotia–grown food served in cafeterias and meal programs, building procurement relationships with local farmers, fishers, and food producers. By shifting institutional spend to local suppliers and offering implementation support (menus, sourcing, and vendor onboarding), the program grows stable markets that enable local food businesses to hire and advance staff. This buy‑local model directly applies the hire/buy‑local solution within the education sector while strengthening community food economies.

solutions.text: Community Returner and Alumni Engagement Program: Build a local outreach program connecting former residents, students and remote diasporas with job openings, mentoring roles and return incentives (housing, startup support) to entice talent back and facilitate re-entry into local careers.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program links recent graduates, newcomers, and returning Nova Scotians with established local professionals (Connectors) for one-on-one networking that leads to informational interviews, job referrals, and mentorship. By actively engaging alumni and diaspora talent with employers and sector leaders, the program helps people re-enter the local job market, build networks quickly, and access quality career opportunities in communities across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Hire Me Cape Breton
resources.description: Hire Me Cape Breton connects Cape Breton–Unama’ki employers with talent, including former residents, students, and diaspora professionals looking to return. The platform showcases local job openings, promotes success stories of returnees, and offers pathways to employer introductions and relocation guidance, helping returners plug into real opportunities and community networks outside larger urban centres.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program matches internationally trained professionals and other newcomers with mentors working in their field in Nova Scotia to provide sector-specific advice, networking, and job search connections. This guided re-entry support mirrors a returner engagement approach by helping participants build local networks and access quality roles, especially valuable for those re-establishing careers in the province.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Plan To SucCEED
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED’s Plan To SucCEED program provides hands-on startup training, mentorship, and access to financing supports that help aspiring and returning entrepreneurs launch businesses in Nova Scotia. By offering structured coaching and connections to the local startup ecosystem, it functions as a return incentive that enables alumni and former residents to come back, create their own jobs, and contribute to sustainable career paths in their home communities.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 121, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Shared Employee Pool and Job-Share Platform: Create a community-managed platform where small employers can share staff time, post part-time-to-full-time ladders, and coordinate training so workers can combine roles that lead to stable, full-time careers.

resources.name: AgJobsNS (Farm and Workforce Development Program)
resources.description: AgJobsNS is a province-wide job platform run by the Nova Scotia Federation of Agriculture that connects multiple small farm and agri-food employers to a shared pool of candidates. Workforce advisors help employers coordinate hiring, onboarding, and sector-specific training so workers can stack seasonal and part-time roles and progress toward steadier, full-time employment within the agricultural sector.
resources.address: 7 Mellor Avenue, Unit 2, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0E8

resources.name: Digital Nova Scotia Job Portal (with Skills for Hire Atlantic)
resources.description: Digital Nova Scotia’s Job Portal provides a shared talent pool for small and mid-sized tech-enabled employers across the province to post roles, internships, and project-based work. Through its Skills for Hire Atlantic training and other industry-led upskilling, DNS helps employers coordinate training pipelines while enabling candidates to combine part-time/contract roles into career ladders that lead to stable, full-time opportunities in the tech sector and beyond.
resources.address: 45 Alderney Drive, Suite 204, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 2N6

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency registers apprentices and employers, coordinates in-class technical training, and facilitates placements across many small and medium employers—effectively creating a shared labour pool. Apprentices often accumulate hours with multiple employers while advancing along a clear, paid career ladder to journeyperson certification, resulting in stable, full-time careers across trades in both urban and rural Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 2021 Brunswick Street, 10th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 2S9

resources.name: Cape Breton Job Board and Talent Pool
resources.description: The Cape Breton Partnership maintains an island-wide job board and talent pool that lets small employers in sectors like tourism, retail, and light industry tap a shared candidate base. By partnering with Nova Scotia Works and post-secondary programs, the initiative helps coordinate training and enables workers to combine seasonal or part-time roles across employers, supporting pathways toward year-round, full-time employment on the Island.

resources.name: Customized Employment & Job Development (Nova Scotia Works)
resources.description: TEAM Work Cooperative’s Nova Scotia Works services broker customized employment, job carving, and job-share arrangements with multiple small employers. Staff coordinate on-the-job training and combine part-time placements so clients can build hours and skills that lead to stable, full-time roles—particularly valuable for youth, newcomers, and people facing barriers to employment.

solutions.text: Local Career Ladders Mapping and Communication Campaign: Work with employers and educators to map typical career progressions in key local sectors, publish clear steps and required credentials, and run outreach so young people see realistic local advancement paths.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is an employer-educator partnership that lays out a clear progression for careers in shipbuilding, from pre-apprenticeship training through apprenticeship to Red Seal certification and advanced roles. Led by NSCC with industry partners, it publishes the steps, credentials, and supports required at each stage and runs targeted outreach to underrepresented youth so they can see realistic, local advancement paths in the marine sector.

resources.name: THRSC Atlantic Career Pathways
resources.organization: Trucking Human Resource Sector Council Atlantic
resources.description: THRSC Atlantic maps career ladders across the trucking and logistics sector in Nova Scotia—from entry-level roles (e.g., dock worker) to professional driver, dispatcher, fleet supervisor, and logistics manager—detailing required certifications such as Class 1 licensing and air brake endorsements. The council works directly with employers and training providers to publish these pathways and delivers outreach in schools and communities so young people understand local opportunities and how to advance.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Tourism Human Resource Council (NSTHRC)
resources.organization: Tourism Industry Association of Nova Scotia (TIANS)
resources.description: NSTHRC develops and communicates career pathways in tourism and hospitality—showing how roles like front-desk agent or line cook can progress to department head, executive chef, or general manager—and outlines the credentials and training required (e.g., food safety, responsible beverage service). Working with employers and educators, the council publishes occupational profiles and runs outreach and career campaigns to help youth see viable advancement routes across Nova Scotia’s tourism sector.

resources.name: Farm and Workforce Development
resources.description: This program maps clear agricultural career pathways in Nova Scotia—from farm worker to equipment operator, herdsperson, supervisor, and farm manager/owner—and shares the training and credentials required at each step (e.g., pesticide applicator certification, livestock handling, equipment tickets). In collaboration with employers, schools, and training partners, it publishes guidance and runs outreach to help youth and career-seekers understand realistic, local advancement paths in the agri-food sector.
resources.address: 7 Atlantic Central Drive, East Mountain, NS B6L 2Z2

solutions.text: Childcare and Housing Partnerships to Support Workforce Retention: Coordinate community-level childcare cooperatives, employer-subsidized childcare slots and partnerships with housing providers to reduce barriers that prevent workers (especially young families) from staying in the region.

resources.name: Supportive Housing for Young Mothers (SHYM)
resources.description: SHYM provides safe, affordable, supported housing for young mothers and their children while connecting residents to licensed childcare through partner centres and on-site early learning/parenting supports. By combining stable housing with coordinated access to childcare and employment navigation, the program removes key barriers that prevent young families from working, studying, and staying in the Halifax region—advancing workforce retention.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC) and Housing/Settlement Supports
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS offers on-site Care for Newcomer Children while parents attend language, employment, and bridging programs, directly reducing childcare barriers to job entry and advancement. In tandem, ISANS’ settlement and housing teams work with landlords and housing providers to help families secure stable housing near work and services—an integrated approach that supports newcomer families to join and remain in Nova Scotia’s workforce.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Kepmite'tmnej Aboriginal Head Start & Housing Supports
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre delivers Aboriginal Head Start early learning programming and wraparound family supports that help parents access employment, training, and community services. Alongside this, MNFC’s housing support workers assist families in finding and maintaining safe, affordable housing—pairing childcare and housing stability to reduce barriers that can push urban Indigenous families out of the workforce or out of the province.

resources.name: Aberdeen Hospital Day Care Centre (Employee Child Care)
resources.description: Located on the Aberdeen Hospital campus, this employer-supported child care helps Nova Scotia Health staff—many of whom work shifts—secure reliable, nearby care for their children. By reducing child care access and scheduling barriers for health-care workers in Pictou County (outside Halifax), the program supports recruitment and retention in stable, in-demand jobs.
resources.address: 835 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3S6

solutions.text: Sector Cluster Projects (e.g., Creative, Agri-food, Clean Tech): Mobilize local stakeholders to launch targeted cluster initiatives that bundle marketing, shared equipment, training and joint hiring to grow higher-quality jobs and visible career ladders in regionally relevant sectors.

resources.name: Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE is an ocean-technology cluster on Dartmouth’s waterfront that co-locates startups, SMEs, anchor firms, and researchers to accelerate commercialization. It provides shared facilities—labs, prototyping space, marine testing infrastructure, and wharf access—along with industry training, internships, and networking that connect employers to talent. By bundling sector marketing, common infrastructure, and coordinated hiring and skills development, COVE grows higher-quality ocean-tech jobs and clear career pathways across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Perennia Innovation Centre
resources.description: The Perennia Innovation Centre anchors an agri-food cluster by offering shared pilot-scale food processing suites, analytical labs, and technical expertise to help producers and processors commercialize safely and meet market standards. Perennia bundles sector-wide support including food-safety training, technical workshops, and advisory services with market-development and branding assistance for Nova Scotia products. This integrated approach connects firms to common equipment and skills pipelines, improving job quality and advancement opportunities in the province’s agri-food sector.
resources.address: 45 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: Verschuren Centre for Sustainability in Energy and the Environment
resources.description: The Verschuren Centre is a clean-tech and biomanufacturing scale-up hub that brings together companies, researchers, and investors to commercialize low-carbon technologies in Cape Breton. It offers shared pilot facilities, wet labs, and bioprocessing equipment alongside applied R&D teams, workforce training, co-ops, and industry internships. By coupling common infrastructure with coordinated talent development and market support, the Centre enables firms to scale locally, creating higher-quality jobs and visible career ladders in Nova Scotia’s clean-tech economy.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

resources.name: BioNova – Nova Scotia Life Sciences Industry Association
resources.description: BioNova leads the province’s life sciences cluster by coordinating sector marketing (e.g., BioPort), business acceleration, and talent initiatives that connect companies to skilled workers. Working with partners at the Life Sciences Research Institute, it facilitates access to shared labs and specialized equipment, and provides peer training and mentorship for scaling firms. This cluster approach bundles common infrastructure, skills development, and hiring pipelines to expand high-quality jobs and advancement pathways in Nova Scotia’s bioscience sector.

solutions.text: Local Job-Shadowing and School-Employer Linkages: Organize regular job-shadow days, co-op placements and employer talks in high schools and community centres so young people encounter real career options outside major centres and begin building local networks.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth
resources.organization: Construction Association of Nova Scotia (in partnership with Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and EECD)
resources.description: Building Futures for Youth places Grade 10–12 students in paid, construction-industry summer work terms across Nova Scotia, with industry-standard safety training and high school credit options. The program partners with local employers for jobsite tours, job-shadowing, and employer talks, giving youth real exposure to skilled trades and direct connections to workplaces outside major centres.
resources.address: 3845 Joseph Howe Drive, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3L 4H9

resources.name: Co-operative Education (Co-op) Program
resources.description: HRCE’s Co-op program partners high schools with local employers to provide semester-long placements, job-shadow days, and in-school employer presentations that align with students’ career interests. Through supervised workplace learning and reflective coursework, students earn credits while building networks with businesses and organizations throughout the Halifax region and nearby communities.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Career Rising
resources.description: Career Rising connects rural and small-town youth with local co-operatives and community employers for paid summer jobs, workplace tours, and mentorship. The program includes employer talks and job-shadowing opportunities coordinated through community hubs, helping young people explore careers close to home and build lasting networks with local businesses.
resources.address: 60 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: NSCC Co-op and Work-Integrated Learning
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Institute of Technology Campus
resources.description: NSCC integrates co-op terms, practicums, and industry projects across campuses province-wide, matching students with employers in sectors like trades, IT, health, and community services. Many programs host employer talks, networking events, and short job-shadow experiences, enabling learners to explore real roles and build local connections in communities outside Halifax.

obstacles.title: Wages Lagging Cost of Living
obstacles.description: Entry-level pay and salary growth often trail housing, food, and transportation costs, undermining quality of life.

solutions.text: Community Living Wage Campaign: Mobilize municipalities, businesses and non-profits to adopt and publicize a locally calculated living wage for entry-level roles; provide guidance and recognition (e.g., ‘Living Wage Employer’ designation) to encourage pay increases across sectors.

resources.name: Certified Living Wage Employer Program (Nova Scotia)
resources.organization: Human Development Council – Living Wage Atlantic Canada
resources.description: Living Wage Atlantic Canada operates a certification program across Nova Scotia that recognizes employers who commit to paying at least the locally calculated living wage. The program provides guidance on wage/benefit structures, helps employers implement living-wage policies, and publicly recognizes them with a 'Certified Living Wage Employer' designation and directory—mobilizing municipalities, businesses, and non-profits to adopt and promote living wages.
resources.address: 139 Prince Edward Street, Saint John, NB E2L 3S3

resources.name: Certified Living Wage Employer – Ecology Action Centre
resources.description: Ecology Action Centre is a Certified Living Wage Employer in Halifax, committing to pay at least the locally calculated living wage to all staff and contracted workers. By publicly promoting its designation and sharing implementation practices with peers and suppliers, EAC advances sector-wide adoption of living-wage standards in Nova Scotia, aligning with campaigns that encourage recognition and pay increases across organizations.

resources.name: Town of Wolfville Living Wage Policy
resources.description: The Town of Wolfville has adopted a living-wage policy that sets minimum pay for municipal employees and contracted services at or above the locally calculated living wage. The municipality publicizes the policy and integrates living-wage expectations into procurement, modeling the approach for local employers and encouraging broader uptake and recognition of living-wage standards in the community.

solutions.text: Local Hiring & Apprenticeship Partnerships: Create coordinated programs between local employers, community colleges and unions that guarantee paid internships, apprenticeships and clear wage progression pathways for young people entering trades and emerging industries.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth
resources.description: Building Futures for Youth places Grade 10–12 students in paid summer jobs with construction employers across Nova Scotia, pairing safety training and industry mentorship with real work experience. The program is delivered in partnership with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and NSCC, so hours can count toward apprenticeship and graduates have a clear path to register as apprentices. As they transition into apprenticeship, participants move onto union/employer wage scales with defined step increases toward journeyperson rates, directly addressing wage progression.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Irving Shipbuilding Inc. (in partnership with Nova Scotia Community College and Unifor Marine Workers Federation Local 1)
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based program delivered by NSCC in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding and the Unifor Marine Workers Federation, recruiting Nova Scotians—often from underrepresented groups—into welding, metal fabrication and other shipbuilding trades. Students receive college training plus paid work terms at the Halifax Shipyard that transition into registered apprenticeships with employer sponsorship. Apprentices work under a collective agreement with guaranteed wage steps that rise with each apprenticeship level and certification, ensuring clear wage progression toward Red Seal status.

resources.name: NSCC Apprenticeship Training
resources.description: NSCC delivers the in-school technical training for registered apprentices across dozens of Red Seal and provincial trades in Nova Scotia, coordinating intakes with local employers and unions. Apprentices are paid employees sponsored by employers while they complete blocks of technical training, with wages increasing at defined steps tied to hours and apprenticeship levels set by the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and collective agreements. This coordinated model links education and industry to provide paid, progressive pathways into high-demand trades.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Power Apprenticeship Programs
resources.description: Nova Scotia Power recruits and trains apprentices for skilled trades such as powerline technicians and industrial electricians, combining paid on‑the‑job learning with technical training delivered through partners like NSCC. Apprentices are hired as employees from day one and progress through clearly defined wage steps under collective agreements (e.g., with IBEW), culminating in journeyperson rates upon certification. The utility’s employer-college-union partnership ensures paid training, industry-recognized credentials, and transparent wage progression in an essential sector.
resources.address: 1223 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

solutions.text: Community-Based Wage Top-Up Fund: Establish a locally administered private-public fund (supported by foundations, businesses and municipal seed money) that provides temporary wage top-ups or retention bonuses for young workers in high-cost roles while they upskill.

resources.name: Wage Subsidy Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Wage Subsidy Program provides time-limited wage subsidies to employers who hire immigrant job seekers, offsetting payroll costs while the new employee receives on‑the‑job training and skills development. By temporarily topping up wages through a locally administered, multi‑funded program, it helps early‑career workers bridge experience gaps and remain in roles as they upskill. This directly addresses cost‑of‑living pressures and supports retention in sectors facing hiring and training challenges.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship Program
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s Clean Leadership program provides wage subsidies to host employers across Nova Scotia to hire youth for paid, skill‑building internships in the clean economy. The subsidy acts as a temporary wage top‑up that enables employers to pay competitive wages while interns gain training, mentorship, and industry‑recognized experience. This public‑ and privately supported initiative helps young workers remain in their communities, build careers, and transition into longer‑term employment.

solutions.text: Affordable Cooperative Housing Initiatives: Support community land trusts and housing co-ops that develop stable, below-market rental or ownership options targeted at young workers and families to reduce housing cost pressures.

resources.name: Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia builds and sells homes to eligible working families using affordable, geared-to-income mortgages with no down payment, creating stable, below-market homeownership options. By keeping monthly housing costs predictable and tied to income, the program eases cost-of-living pressures for young workers and families. Habitat retains affordability through its model and homeowner supports, helping households build equity while maintaining long-term community stability.

resources.name: New Dawn Affordable Housing
resources.description: New Dawn Enterprises develops and manages below-market rental housing in Sydney and surrounding areas, offering stable, long-term homes that working families can afford. As a community-based, non-profit developer and owner, New Dawn keeps units in community hands and prioritizes affordability over profit, reducing exposure to rent spikes. Its projects add mixed-income, quality apartments that align with local wages, helping young workers establish roots and thrive.

solutions.text: Neighborhood Childcare Co-ops and Subsidy Pools: Help community groups form cooperative childcare programs and local subsidy pools (through employers and charities) to lower childcare costs that hinder young workers’ ability to accept better-paying roles.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides on-site, no-cost Care for Newcomer Children while parents and guardians attend employment, language, and settlement programs. By removing childcare expenses through charitable and government-funded support, CNC functions as a local subsidy pool that helps young workers and jobseekers accept training and job opportunities they might otherwise have to decline.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Aboriginal Head Start (AHS) Early Childhood Program
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre delivers a free, culturally grounded early childhood program for Indigenous families, offering part-day childcare, nutrition, and family supports. As a community-run, federally funded initiative, AHS effectively subsidizes childcare costs for families so parents can pursue employment, education, or training without prohibitive fees.

resources.name: Chebucto Family Centre Childminding & Family Support
resources.organization: Home of the Guardian Angel (Chebucto Family Centre)
resources.description: Chebucto Family Centre offers free on-site childminding during employment-support workshops, prenatal/postnatal sessions, and other programs, reducing immediate childcare costs that can block access to jobs or training. Funded by donors and partners, the Centre also helps families navigate provincial subsidies and connect with nearby regulated care, aligning with community-based subsidy pooling and co-operative support models.

solutions.text: Local Procurement & Living Wage Clauses: Encourage towns and regional authorities to include living-wage and local-hire clauses in procurement and development agreements to raise wages indirectly by creating demand for decent-paid local jobs.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Social Procurement Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality integrates social value into its purchasing by using evaluation criteria and contract clauses that promote local hiring, apprenticeships, supplier diversity, and decent work. The municipality has included living-wage provisions in specific service contracts (such as solid waste collection) and encourages local workforce participation in development agreements, raising wage standards indirectly by creating demand for better-paid local jobs.

resources.name: Community Benefits and Social Procurement for Major Projects
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia embeds community benefits into procurement and development agreements for provincial infrastructure projects, requiring contractors to prioritize local hiring, apprenticeship and workforce development, and opportunities for Nova Scotian suppliers. These procurements also set expectations for fair compensation aligned with living-wage benchmarks where appropriate, leveraging public contracts to grow decent-paid local jobs.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 301, Halifax, NS B3J 1S7

resources.name: Buy Social Procurement Advisory and Certification (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Common Good Solutions provides social procurement training and hands-on support to municipalities, universities, health authorities, and developers in Nova Scotia to include local-hire, community benefit, and living-wage language in RFPs and contracts. It also helps suppliers meet decent work and living-wage expectations and access Buy Social certification, channeling public and institutional spending toward better-paid local employment.
resources.address: 5557 Cunard Street, Suite C, Halifax, NS B3K 1C5

solutions.text: Microgrants & Start-up Supports for Young Entrepreneurs: Provide small grants, rent-free pop-up retail space, mentorship and reduced-fee licensing to help young entrepreneurs launch businesses that generate higher personal incomes locally.

resources.name: CEED Entrepreneurship Programs
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED delivers training, coaching, and financing to help young and early-stage entrepreneurs launch and grow businesses in Nova Scotia. Programs pair hands-on mentorship and workshops with access to small-scale financing (e.g., CEED Micro and Startup/Expansion loans) and a collaborative workspace, helping founders cover early costs like equipment, initial inventory, or permits. By reducing barriers to start-up and providing ongoing guidance, CEED supports young entrepreneurs in building sustainable income locally.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Volta Residency and Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta is Atlantic Canada’s innovation hub offering subsidized workspace, mentorship, and programming for tech-enabled startups. Its Residency provides entrepreneurs with community, advisor access, and reduced overhead, while the Volta Cohort program awards funding to early-stage companies alongside intensive mentorship and investor connections. These supports lower start-up costs and accelerate revenue generation for young founders building companies in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Downtown Truro Pop-Up Shop Program
resources.description: This initiative activates vacant storefronts by offering short-term, subsidized or rent-free retail pop-up spaces to new and emerging entrepreneurs. Participants receive coaching on merchandising, marketing, and permits, along with promotional support from the business association, allowing youth and first-time founders to test concepts with minimal overhead. The program helps entrepreneurs build local customer bases and income while de-risking the path to a permanent location.

resources.name: CBDC Blue Water Youth Loan Program
resources.organization: CBDC Blue Water (Community Business Development Corporation)
resources.description: CBDC Blue Water offers flexible Youth Loans (typically up to $20,000) along with one-on-one business counselling to help entrepreneurs aged 18–34 start or expand ventures in rural Nova Scotia. The program pairs accessible financing with mentorship on business planning, cash flow, and licensing requirements, reducing start-up barriers for young founders. By combining capital with advisory support, it enables youth-led businesses to launch and increase local earning potential.
resources.address: 61 Stella Drive, Unit 204, Musquodoboit Harbour, NS B0J 2L0

resources.name: Business Is Jammin’ Youth Entrepreneurship Programs
resources.organization: Business Is Jammin’ (a program of the Black Business Initiative)
resources.description: Business Is Jammin’ delivers entrepreneurship education, mentorship, and pitch events that provide startup cash awards to Black youth across Nova Scotia. Through workshops, camps, and coaching, participants gain the skills and support to launch micro-enterprises and creative ventures, often accessing small grants or prize funding to cover initial costs. The program helps young entrepreneurs build confidence, revenue, and community connections while growing businesses locally.
resources.address: 1660 Hollis Street, Suite 910, Halifax, NS B3J 1V7

solutions.text: Community Transit & Commute Subsidies: Implement municipal transit improvements, subsidized transit passes for low-wage workers, and coordinated ride-share programs to lower transportation costs and expand access to better-paying jobs.

resources.name: Affordable Access Program – Low Income Transit Pass
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Affordable Access Program provides a 50% discount on Halifax Transit monthly passes for eligible low-income residents. The subsidy directly lowers commuting costs for low-wage workers and job seekers, enabling reliable access to employment, training, and services across the city’s bus and ferry network. By reducing the financial barrier to transit, the program supports workforce participation and mobility for young people and families.

resources.name: Employer Transit Pass (EPass) Program
resources.description: Halifax Transit’s EPass program partners with employers to offer their staff discounted, year-round transit passes via payroll deduction. This employer-based subsidy lowers commuting costs, supports shift and entry-level workers, and encourages sustainable travel to major job hubs served by HRM’s bus and ferry routes. The program helps retain talent by making daily travel more affordable and predictable.

resources.name: Kings Transit Authority (Regional Bus Service)
resources.description: Kings Transit Authority operates fixed-route public transit linking communities from Weymouth to Wolfville across the Annapolis Valley. With affordable fares and monthly passes, the service connects residents to employment centers, colleges, industrial parks, and retail corridors, reducing the need for private vehicles. By improving regional mobility, it expands access to better-paying jobs for workers and youth in rural and small-town Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

resources.name: BayRides Community Transportation
resources.organization: BayRides (St. Margarets Bay Community Transportation Society)
resources.description: BayRides is a non-profit community transit service providing accessible, door-to-door and pre-booked rides throughout St. Margarets Bay and surrounding rural HRM. Supported by municipal and community funding, BayRides offers low, predictable fares and coordinated trips to work, training, and essential services, including links to Halifax Transit hubs. This demand-responsive model reduces transportation costs and fills gaps where fixed-route buses are limited, improving job access for low-wage and carless workers.

solutions.text: Shared Workplaces and Remote Work Hubs: Develop affordable co-working and remote work hubs in smaller towns to let young residents access higher-paying remote jobs while staying local, reducing relocation pressure and commuting costs.

resources.name: WorkEvolved Coworking Community
resources.description: WorkEvolved provides affordable coworking memberships, hot desks, private offices, and meeting rooms with high-speed internet in downtown Truro. By giving freelancers, remote employees, and entrepreneurs professional space and amenities close to home, it helps young residents access remote and higher-paying jobs without relocating or commuting to larger centres.

resources.name: Navigate Startup House
resources.organization: Navigate Startup Ecosystem (Cape Breton University and NSCC)
resources.description: Navigate Startup House offers low-cost coworking desks, meeting rooms, and community programming that supports entrepreneurs, freelancers, and remote workers in Sydney, Cape Breton. The space enables young people to work for clients and employers anywhere while remaining in their community, reducing relocation pressure and daily commuting costs.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Yarmouth Innovation Hub
resources.description: IGNITE’s Yarmouth hub provides shared workspaces, meeting rooms, high-speed internet, and entrepreneurial supports designed for rural innovators, remote workers, and startups. By offering affordable, professional facilities in a smaller town, it helps young residents stay local while connecting to remote jobs and clients across Canada and beyond.

solutions.text: Skills-upskilling & Career Ladder Workshops: Run community-led short-course bootcamps, credential bridging and mentorship programs (in partnership with colleges/employers) that help entry-level workers move into higher-wage roles faster.

resources.name: Profession-Specific Bridging & Mentorship Programs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers sector- and occupation-specific bridging programs that help internationally trained and entry-level workers upgrade credentials, gain Canadian workplace skills, and connect with regulated bodies and employers. Short courses cover essential and technical skills, sector language, and licensing pathways, paired with mentorship and employer networking. This approach accelerates movement into higher-wage roles by closing skills and credential gaps and providing direct employer connections.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based program that blends essential skills bootcamps, NSCC trades training, and on-the-job learning with Irving Shipbuilding and union partners. Participants receive academic upgrading, safety certifications, and mentorship while completing an NSCC credential that bridges directly to well-paid shipbuilding trades. The employer-connected model moves entry-level workers into higher-wage, in-demand roles faster.

resources.name: Women in Trades and Technology (WITT)
resources.description: WITT offers short, intensive pre-apprenticeship training and career readiness workshops for women and gender-diverse people exploring skilled trades and technology careers. Participants earn industry-recognized safety tickets, receive mentorship and job coaching, and are connected with NSCC programs and local employers for placements and apprenticeships. The program provides a clear, supported ladder into higher-wage trades and tech roles.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program matches entry-level job seekers, recent graduates, and newcomers with established industry professionals for structured networking, career guidance, and warm introductions to employers. Through mentorship meetings and tailored workshops, participants learn sector expectations and rapidly expand employer contacts, enabling faster transitions into higher-wage, in-demand roles. The program operates across multiple industries in partnership with local businesses.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Energy Efficiency & Utility Support Programs: Coordinate local bulk-buy and retrofit programs (insulation, heat pumps, efficient appliances) and targeted utility relief for low-wage households to reduce monthly living costs.

resources.name: Home Energy Assessment
resources.description: Efficiency Nova Scotia’s Home Energy Assessment connects households with an energy advisor to identify cost-saving retrofits and provides rebates for insulation, heat pumps, and efficient equipment. By coordinating a network of certified contractors and incentives, the program lowers upfront costs and enables bulk uptake of common upgrades, directly reducing monthly energy bills for Nova Scotians.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: HomeWarming
resources.organization: Clean Foundation and EfficiencyOne (Efficiency Nova Scotia)
resources.description: HomeWarming provides no-cost home energy retrofits—such as insulation, air sealing, and heating system improvements—for income-qualified Nova Scotians. Delivered by Clean Foundation and EfficiencyOne, the program targets low-wage households to cut energy waste and utility bills, implementing coordinated retrofit services that reduce monthly living costs.

resources.name: Solar City Program
resources.description: Halifax’s Solar City Program offers property-assessed (PACE) financing and a coordinated, pre-qualified vendor list to help residents install solar PV and solar hot water systems. By aggregating demand and streamlining procurement and financing, it functions as a local bulk-buy initiative that lowers upfront costs and helps households reduce ongoing electricity bills.

resources.name: Heating Assistance Rebate Program (HARP)
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia — Service Nova Scotia
resources.description: HARP provides an annual rebate to help low- and modest-income Nova Scotian households with home heating costs, including electricity, oil, propane, wood, and other fuels. This targeted utility relief reduces energy burden for wage-constrained families, complementing retrofit programs by lowering near-term monthly living costs.
resources.address: Maritime Centre, 1505 Barrington Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

solutions.text: Food Security & Affordable Grocery Initiatives: Support food co-ops, community gardens, farmers’ market discount programs and bulk-buy purchasing groups that lower household food costs for young families and individuals.

resources.name: Dartmouth North Community Food Centre
resources.organization: Dartmouth Family Centre / Dartmouth North Community Food Centre
resources.description: The Dartmouth North Community Food Centre runs affordable produce markets, community meals, and gardening programs that increase access to fresh, healthy food for local families. By offering low-cost fruits and vegetables, teaching food skills, and supporting community gardens, the Centre directly lowers grocery costs and strengthens local food security.

resources.name: Good Food Access Program
resources.description: The Good Food Access Program at the New Glasgow Farmers Market provides subsidized Fresh Food Boxes and Market Bucks that help households purchase local produce at reduced cost. By combining bulk-buy produce boxes with discount vouchers for market vendors, the program lowers weekly grocery bills while supporting local growers.
resources.address: 620 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3S2

resources.name: Nourishing Communities Food Coupon Program
resources.description: The Wolfville Farmers’ Market’s Nourishing Communities program distributes weekly food coupons that can be spent with market vendors on fresh produce and staples. This targeted discount initiative improves affordability for low-income residents and families while keeping dollars within the local food economy.

resources.name: Square Roots Pay-What-You-Can Produce Bundles
resources.organization: Square Roots Food Program (Enactus Saint Mary’s University)
resources.description: Square Roots offers pay-what-you-can 10–20 lb produce bundles made from rescued or surplus fruits and vegetables, with community pickup hubs across Nova Scotia. By aggregating bulk purchases and reducing food waste, the program provides affordable groceries for individuals and families while strengthening local food access.

solutions.text: Financial Coaching and Benefits Navigation: Provide free or low-cost financial literacy, debt counseling and benefits navigation through libraries and community centres so young workers maximize income and access supports that improve disposable income.

resources.name: Community Volunteer Income Tax Program (CVITP) and Money Matters at Halifax Public Libraries
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts free CVITP tax clinics and Money Matters financial literacy workshops across its branches. These services help individuals file taxes to access federal and provincial benefits and credits, and build budgeting, credit, and debt management skills—directly improving disposable income for young workers. Librarians and partner organizations provide one-on-one guidance and referrals to community supports, functioning as an accessible benefits navigation hub.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Free Income Tax Clinic & Community Navigator
resources.description: Chebucto Connections operates a free CVITP income tax clinic and offers a Community Navigator who assists residents with applications for benefits and income supports (e.g., GST/HST credit, Canada Workers Benefit, and provincial programs). They also host practical financial literacy sessions with partner agencies, providing low-barrier coaching through a neighborhood community centre to help young workers manage debt, budget, and maximize available supports.
resources.address: 531 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1X3

resources.name: Financial Literacy for Newcomers
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers free and low-cost workshops and one-on-one coaching on banking, credit, budgeting, and taxes for newcomers, alongside settlement and employment counselors who help clients navigate benefits and income supports. By pairing financial education with individualized benefits navigation (e.g., tax credits, income-tested programs), the program helps young workers new to Nova Scotia increase disposable income and build financial stability.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: CVITP Tax Clinics and Money Matters Workshops at Cape Breton Regional Library
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library branches host free Community Volunteer Income Tax Program clinics and Money Matters financial literacy workshops. These services help residents file taxes to unlock benefits and credits and provide practical coaching on budgeting, credit, and managing debt—delivered in trusted library settings that make financial help accessible to young workers across the region.

solutions.text: Advocacy & Collective Voice Network: Form local youth-employment coalitions to collect data on wage gaps, lobby provincial and municipal governments for policy changes (minimum-wage adjustments, targeted tax relief) and amplify employer accountability locally.

resources.name: Young Workers Committee
resources.description: The Young Workers Committee organizes young workers and student labour activists across Nova Scotia to build a collective voice for decent work and fair wages. It gathers data and stories on wage gaps and precarious work, then lobbies provincial and municipal governments for policies like minimum-wage increases, paid sick days, and fair scheduling, while pressing local employers to adopt living-wage practices and better entry-level pay.
resources.address: 3700 Kempt Road, Suite 5, Halifax, NS B3K 4X8

resources.name: Nova Scotia Living Wage Reports & Campaign
resources.organization: Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives – Nova Scotia Office
resources.description: CCPA–NS produces rigorous, community-specific living wage calculations (e.g., Halifax, Cape Breton) and analyzes wage gaps relative to the cost of housing, food, and transportation. Using this local data, the office briefs municipal and provincial decision-makers and works with community coalitions to advance policies such as living-wage procurement, minimum-wage adjustments, and targeted tax relief for low-wage workers, while publicly benchmarking employer accountability to living-wage standards.
resources.address: Saint Mary’s University, 923 Robie Street, Halifax, NS B3H 3C3

resources.name: Living Wage for Halifax
resources.description: United Way Halifax convenes employers, community groups, and advocates to champion adoption of a local living wage and to close wage gaps affecting youth and other low-wage workers. The initiative leverages local affordability and wage data to encourage employers to publicly commit to paying at least the Halifax living wage and collaborates with municipal and provincial partners to embed living-wage and related policy changes that raise entry-level pay.

resources.name: Policy, Research & Evaluation
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Policy, Research & Evaluation unit analyzes labour market outcomes and wage gaps for newcomers—including youth—and convenes employers and government partners to advance fair employment practices. Through policy submissions, employer roundtables, and community coalitions, it advocates for equitable wages, fair credential recognition, and targeted tax measures that improve entry-level pay, while promoting employer accountability for inclusive, decent work.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

obstacles.title: Housing Affordability and Availability
obstacles.description: Limited rental supply, rising prices, and slow construction approvals make it hard for young people to settle or return.

solutions.text: Community Land Trust (CLT): Form a local nonprofit CLT to buy and hold land for permanently affordable housing; community members govern the trust to ensure homes remain affordable for young people and returning residents.

resources.name: New Dawn Affordable Housing (Community-Owned Rental Homes)
resources.description: New Dawn Enterprises acquires, develops, and stewards land and buildings to provide long-term affordable rental housing in Cape Breton. Governed by a community-based nonprofit board, New Dawn keeps properties in community ownership and applies long-term affordability terms, aligning with the core CLT model of separating land ownership from market pressures to ensure homes remain affordable for local residents over time.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia acquires land and builds homes that are sold to partner families with affordable, non-profit mortgages and resale restrictions, ensuring affordability is protected over the long term. As a community-governed nonprofit that holds and assembles land for housing and uses legal mechanisms to keep homes affordable across ownership transfers, the program operationalizes key CLT principles of community stewardship and permanent affordability.

solutions.text: Housing Cooperatives: Support creation of resident-run housing co-ops by providing organizing help, seed funding, and governance training so groups of young people can collectively secure stable, lower-cost housing.

resources.name: Community Housing Growth Fund (Nova Scotia)
resources.organization: Housing Nova Scotia (Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
resources.description: The Community Housing Growth Fund provides seed funding, planning/pre-development grants, and capacity-building supports to community housing organizations, including emerging housing co-operatives, across Nova Scotia. Delivered in partnership with sector experts, the fund backs organizing efforts, governance training, and technical assistance so groups—including youth-led initiatives—can launch resident-run co-ops that deliver stable, lower-cost housing.

resources.name: Co‑operative Development Services
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Co‑operative Council offers hands-on support to groups starting co-operatives, including housing co-ops. Staff assist with community organizing, incorporation, business planning, and board/governance training, and connect groups to credit unions and social finance for seed capital—helping young people collectively create and run resident-governed, affordable housing.
resources.address: 269 Main Street, Suite 303, Truro, NS B2N 1C6

resources.name: Atlantic Support for Housing Co‑ops
resources.organization: Co‑operative Housing Federation of Canada (CHF Canada)
resources.description: CHF Canada provides training, development advice, and governance resources to new and existing housing co-operatives in Nova Scotia. Through workshops, board training, member education, and development support, they help resident groups organize effective co-op governance and access tools and programs (including refinancing and growth supports) that keep housing stable and affordable.
resources.address: 225 Metcalfe Street, Suite 311, Ottawa, ON K2P 1P9

solutions.text: Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Program: Run community workshops, design clinics and small grants/interest-free loans to help homeowners add basement suites/laneways/garage apartments to increase rental supply while preserving neighborhood form.

resources.name: Secondary Suite Incentive Program (SSIP)
resources.description: CMHC’s SSIP provides interest-free, forgivable loans to homeowners to create new accessory dwelling units such as basement apartments, garden suites, or laneway suites and rent them at affordable rates for a set period. In Nova Scotia, eligible homeowners can use SSIP financing to design and build legal ADUs, with CMHC offering application guidance and resources that function like a financing/design support to help increase rental supply while maintaining neighbourhood form.

resources.name: Secondary and Backyard Suites (ADUs) — Resources, Permitting and Homeowner Sessions
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality has legalized secondary and backyard suites and provides step-by-step homeowner guides, design and permitting checklists, and pre-application meetings to help residents add legal basement, backyard, or garage apartments. HRM also hosts information sessions and offers one-on-one support with Planning & Development staff—effectively a community design/permit clinic—to streamline approvals and expand gentle-density rental options.

resources.name: Backyard and Secondary Suites — Homeowner Guidance & Permitting Support
resources.description: The Town of Wolfville allows secondary and backyard (garden/carriage) suites and provides homeowner-facing guidance through its Planning Department, including pre-application consultations and checklists to ensure designs meet zoning, servicing, and building-code requirements. These supports function as a practical design/permit clinic that helps residents create compliant ADUs, adding rental supply while fitting established neighbourhood character.

solutions.text: Local Affordable Housing Fund: Pool donations, local business contributions and municipal seed money into a community-managed revolving fund that finances down payments, conversions, or quick repairs for affordable units.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia pools donations from individuals, local businesses, and public partners to build and repair homes, then provides families with affordable, no-interest mortgages. Mortgage repayments flow back into Habitat’s fund, creating a revolving pool of capital that finances additional builds and critical repairs. This directly implements the solution by aggregating local contributions into a community-managed fund that finances down-payment-like entry into homeownership and quick repairs that preserve affordable units.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: New Dawn’s Community Investment Fund pools capital from local residents and businesses under Nova Scotia’s CEDIF model to provide patient, revolving financing for community projects, including the acquisition, conversion, and rehabilitation of housing.
