As loans are repaid, capital is recycled into new projects, enabling ongoing investment in affordable and supportive housing in Cape Breton. This implements the solution by channeling locally sourced, community-managed funds into conversions and repairs that expand and preserve affordable units.

resources.name: Affordable Housing Reserve Fund
resources.description: The Town of Wolfville’s Affordable Housing Reserve Fund aggregates municipal allocations, developer density-bonus contributions, and community donations to support affordable housing initiatives. Funds are granted or loaned to non-profit and private partners for projects such as conversions, rehabilitation, and preservation of affordable rental units. This implements the solution by pooling local and municipal resources into a dedicated, locally managed fund that can be deployed quickly for repairs and to bring new affordable units online.

resources.name: Affordable Housing Reserve Fund
resources.description: The Town of Lunenburg’s Affordable Housing Reserve Fund combines municipal seed money, developer contributions, and community donations to finance affordable housing creation and preservation. The fund supports projects that include rehabilitation and adaptive reuse/conversions to expand the local stock of affordable units. This implements the solution by pooling local capital into a community-focused vehicle that can finance quick repairs and project readiness for affordable housing.

solutions.text: Modular/Prefab Pilot Projects: Partner with local builders and trades training programs to pilot modular or prefabricated homes on community land or church lots — faster, cheaper rental units that also create local jobs.

resources.name: Modular Supportive Housing Initiative (HRM)
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia coordinates the rapid deployment of modular, prefabricated supportive housing on provincially or municipally owned community lands in the Halifax Region. By procuring modular units and contracting local builders and trades for site servicing and assembly, the initiative delivers rental units much faster and at lower cost while creating local construction jobs and adding urgently needed supply.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Cape Breton University Modular Student Housing
resources.description: To relieve pressure on the local rental market, CBU has added residence capacity using modular/prefabricated buildings installed on campus land. The university worked with regional contractors for site preparation, transport, and rapid assembly, creating managed, affordable rental options for students while generating local jobs and delivering units in months rather than years.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

resources.name: NSCC Community-Built Prefab/Tiny Home Projects
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College engages carpentry, electrical, and related trades students in building modular or panelized small homes and tiny homes as applied learning projects with municipalities and non-profits across the province. These collaborations pilot fast, lower-cost prefabricated units that can be placed on community or institutional land as affordable or supportive rentals, adding supply while training local talent and supporting the regional construction workforce.

solutions.text: Vacant Property Activation and Matchmaking: Create a volunteer-run inventory of vacant homes/units and broker short- or long-term matches between owners and young renters or recent returnees, combined with small rehab teams to make units move-in ready.

resources.name: Off-Campus Housing and Community Host Program
resources.description: Cape Breton University maintains an active inventory of spare rooms, suites, and vacant rental units offered by local homeowners and property owners, and matches them with students and other young renters arriving to the island. The housing team brokers introductions, shares standards and checklists to bring spaces to move-in readiness, and connects hosts with community supports (e.g., furnishing and setup) so underused housing can be quickly activated.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

resources.name: Housing Support Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Housing Support team recruits landlords and homeowners with vacant units and compiles a rolling inventory of available rentals, then screens and matches newcomers (many of whom are young adults and recent arrivals to the workforce) to suitable, affordable options. Staff coordinate with owners to resolve readiness issues, share move-in standards, and link volunteers and partner agencies (e.g., furniture banks, minor setup help) to activate units quickly.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: SMU Homestay Program
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University recruits local homeowners with vacant bedrooms and assembles a vetted inventory of host homes, then matches them with students and young newcomers seeking affordable accommodation. The program brokers agreements, provides standards and orientation to ensure spaces are safe and move-in ready, and offers ongoing support to both hosts and renters to keep placements stable.

resources.name: Acadia Homestay (English Language Centre)
resources.description: Acadia University’s Homestay program maintains a roster of local households with spare rooms and matches them with students and young adults in language and academic programs who need affordable housing. Staff screen hosts, outline readiness requirements (furnishings, safety, and basic amenities), and support both parties through placement to efficiently activate underused housing stock.

solutions.text: Shared-Equity and Co-ownership Programs: Develop community-managed shared-equity schemes where an organization helps cover part of a purchase in return for a resale restriction, making homeownership affordable while preserving long-term affordability.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia sells homes to eligible first-time buyers at an affordable price and carries a portion of the value as a no-interest, deferred second mortgage. This shared-equity structure lowers the upfront purchase cost and includes resale conditions (such as a right of first refusal and shared appreciation), which helps preserve long-term affordability for future buyers.

resources.name: Treehouse Village Ecohousing
resources.description: Treehouse Village is a resident-developed cohousing community where households own their individual homes and co-own extensive common facilities through a condominium corporation. This co-ownership model reduces per-unit costs by sharing land and amenities, and governance is community-managed to maintain affordability and long-term sustainability, aligning with the co-ownership dimension of the solution.

solutions.text: Tenant-Landlord Support & Mediation Hub: Operate a local mediation and education service that helps prevent evictions, supports stable tenancies, and offers incentives or recognition for landlords who provide long-term, fair-market rentals to young people.

resources.name: Residential Tenancies Program
resources.organization: Service Nova Scotia and Internal Services, Government of Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Residential Tenancies Program provides landlord–tenant dispute resolution through mediation (conciliation) and hearings led by Residential Tenancy Officers, helping prevent evictions and stabilize tenancies before conflicts escalate. It also offers plain-language guides, forms, and education for both tenants and landlords, promoting fair rental practices and long-term, stable housing arrangements for young renters.
resources.address: 300 Horseshoe Lake Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 0B7

resources.name: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service (Tenancy Law Services)
resources.organization: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service, Schulich School of Law, Dalhousie University
resources.description: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service offers legal advice and representation to low-income tenants, negotiating with landlords and seeking mediated resolutions to avoid evictions. The clinic also delivers public legal education on tenant rights and responsibilities, directly supporting stable tenancies and helping young people maintain fair-market rentals.

resources.name: Housing and Settlement Services (Landlord–Tenant Support)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS helps newcomers, including many young adults, secure and keep rental housing by providing tenant education, lease navigation, and liaison services with landlords to resolve issues early. Through information sessions for tenants and outreach to landlords, ISANS reduces misunderstandings and encourages longer-term, fair-market rentals, offering landlords a consistent point of contact and culturally informed support that acts as a practical incentive to rent to younger tenants.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Youth Housing Support Program
resources.description: The Portal supports youth aged 16–24 to find and keep market rentals by offering tenant education (including life-skills and readiness training), help understanding leases, and mediation with landlords when issues arise. The program builds partnerships with local landlords and provides ongoing case management and problem-solving, which reassures landlords and promotes longer-term, fair-market tenancies for young people.

solutions.text: Microloans for Home Repairs and Rental Conversions: Offer low-interest microloans or matched grants to homeowners who convert underused spaces into rental suites or repair existing rental units to keep supply habitable and affordable.

resources.name: Secondary and Backyard Suite Incentive Program
resources.organization: Housing Nova Scotia (Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
resources.description: A provincial incentive that provides forgivable loans/matched grants to homeowners to create secondary suites within existing homes or build detached backyard suites. In return for assistance, owners agree to rent the new units at or below market benchmarks for a set period, directly increasing gentle-density rental supply and keeping it affordable.

resources.name: Rental Property Repair Program
resources.organization: Housing Nova Scotia (Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
resources.description: Financial assistance for landlords to complete health, safety, and structural repairs to existing rental units, typically through low-interest or forgivable loans tied to affordability conditions. Landlords commit to maintaining rents at affordable levels for a defined period, preserving existing rental stock and preventing the loss of units due to disrepair.

resources.name: Homeowner Repair Program
resources.organization: Housing Nova Scotia (Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
resources.description: Provides forgivable loans to low-income homeowners to carry out essential repairs (e.g., roofing, heating, electrical, plumbing) so homes remain safe and habitable. By financing critical repairs, the program helps preserve lower-cost housing and can enable future creation of secondary suites, supporting the overall supply of affordable housing.

solutions.text: Employer-Community Housing Partnerships: Coordinate between local employers, chambers of commerce and community groups to develop employer-assisted housing (rent guarantees, down-payment support, dedicated rental blocks) targeted at recruiting and retaining young workers.

resources.name: Team Member Housing
resources.description: Cabot Cape Breton operates dedicated, employer-provided staff housing near its resort properties in Inverness, including purpose-built accommodations and blocks of local rentals secured for seasonal staff. By lowering housing barriers for new hires—many of whom are young workers relocating for hospitality roles—and coordinating with community landlords, this employer-assisted housing supports recruitment and retention in a tight local rental market.

resources.name: Team Member Housing Program
resources.description: Fox Harb’r Resort provides subsidized on-site and nearby staff accommodations for seasonal and full-time employees and works with local property owners to expand capacity during peak periods. By securing dedicated housing close to the workplace, the resort reduces relocation friction and living costs, helping attract and retain young workers in a region with limited rental availability.
resources.address: 1337 Fox Harbour Road, Fox Harbour, NS B0K 1Y0

resources.name: Team Member Housing and Local Rentals
resources.description: White Point Beach Resort maintains employer-assisted staff housing and coordinates with nearby landlords to secure additional rooms and apartments during busy seasons. These dedicated rental blocks and partnerships help overcome local housing scarcity, enabling the resort to recruit and retain young hospitality workers in Queens County.
resources.address: 75 White Point Beach Resort Road, White Point, NS B0T 1G0

resources.name: Physician and Medical Learner Accommodations
resources.organization: Health Services Foundation of the South Shore
resources.description: The Health Services Foundation of the South Shore manages apartments and temporary accommodations for medical residents, locums, and newly recruited physicians working with Nova Scotia Health in Lunenburg and Queens counties. Funded by community donors and business partners and coordinated with employer recruitment teams, these dedicated units reduce housing barriers and costs, directly supporting the recruitment and retention of early‑career healthcare professionals.
resources.address: 90 Glen Allan Drive, Bridgewater, NS B4V 3S6

solutions.text: Pop-up and Tiny Home Transitional Housing: Organize temporary tiny-home villages or repurpose modular units on community-owned sites to provide transitional housing for young people moving back or starting careers while permanent supply is developed.

resources.name: Halifax Modular Supportive Housing – Chain Lake Site
resources.organization: Out of the Cold Community Association (operating for Halifax Regional Municipality)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality partnered with Out of the Cold Community Association to deploy modular, tiny-home–style units as transitional housing at the Chain Lake Drive site. The village of prefabricated units provides private sleeping spaces with shared supports, creating a rapid, pop-up community that gives people (including younger residents starting work or returning to the city) stable housing while longer-term supply is built.
resources.address: 61 Chain Lake Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 1A9

resources.name: Sunflower Court (Rapid Modular Housing)
resources.description: Adsum for Women & Children developed Sunflower Court as a rapid, modular housing community in the Halifax area, using factory-built units assembled on site to quickly create supportive, transitional homes. The project functions much like a tiny-home village, offering immediate, stable housing and wraparound supports while residents work toward permanent housing, training, or employment.

solutions.text: Local Rental Match Platform and Roommate Network: Build a community-run online/offline platform to match young people with available rooms, roommates, and hosts (including intergenerational housing opportunities), reducing search time and informal barriers.

resources.name: Off-Campus Living (Room and Roommate Listings)
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Off-Campus Living service partners with rental listing platforms and local landlords/hosts to post rooms in shared houses, basement suites, and apartments, along with a roommate-finder tool for students. The service reduces search time and barriers by centralizing vetted listings, sharing tenant education resources, and offering guidance on leases and safer housing searches, which can include intergenerational arrangements where seniors or families rent spare rooms to students.
resources.address: LeMarchant Place, 1246 LeMarchant Street, Halifax, NS B3H 3P7

resources.name: Off-Campus Housing and Roommate Finder
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University connects students with an online housing marketplace and roommate-matching tools where local landlords and hosts list rooms and shared accommodations. The service streamlines the search for affordable rentals, provides tips on tenant rights and avoiding scams, and supports connections that can include homestay-style and intergenerational options for students seeking rooms in family or senior households.

resources.name: Off-Campus Housing Support (Listings and Shared Housing Guidance)
resources.description: The University of King’s College directs students to local room and roommate listings and provides guidance on navigating Halifax’s rental market, including shared housing. By pointing students to vetted platforms and community listings, staff help reduce informal barriers and connect students with hosts and multigenerational households renting spare rooms, improving affordability and fit.

resources.name: Off-Campus Housing Listings and Roommate Matching
resources.description: Acadia University’s off-campus support links students with an online marketplace of local listings for rooms in shared houses and apartments and roommate-finder features. This central hub reduces search time, connects students with landlords and hosts across the Annapolis Valley (including households offering rooms), and provides practical resources to navigate leases and community norms.

solutions.text: Community Advocacy for Faster Approvals and Inclusionary Policies: Mobilize neighborhood associations, businesses and youth groups to advocate at council for faster permitting for modest infill, inclusionary zoning on new developments, and incentives for small-scale rental projects.

resources.name: Our HRM Alliance
resources.description: A coalition hosted by the Ecology Action Centre that mobilizes community groups, residents, and businesses to engage in Halifax Regional Council processes on planning and housing. The Alliance advocates for faster, as-of-right approvals for modest infill in serviced areas, pushes for affordability tools such as inclusionary zoning, and supports incentives for small-scale rentals like secondary suites and backyard units through submissions, deputations, and public campaigns.

resources.name: Policy & Advocacy (Housing and Development Files)
resources.description: The Halifax Chamber of Commerce mobilizes its business membership to advocate at Halifax Regional Council and the Province for streamlined permitting, reduced red tape for infill and gentle density, and incentives that unlock private investment in small-scale rental projects. Through policy submissions, committee work, and public forums, the Chamber builds cross-sector support to expand rental supply and improve housing affordability.
resources.address: 32 Akerley Boulevard, Unit 1, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1N1

resources.name: Youth Advisory Committee (YAC)
resources.description: HRM’s Youth Advisory Committee engages young residents to provide recommendations to Regional Council on policies that affect them, including housing and planning matters. YAC members participate in consultations and hearings to champion faster approvals for gentle infill, affordability measures such as inclusionary policies, and incentives for small rental units—ensuring youth voices inform council decisions.

solutions.text: Neighborhood Densification Charrettes and Design Guides: Host local design charrettes to identify low-impact densification opportunities (laneway homes, triplexes) and produce community-backed design guides to speed approvals and reduce NIMBY resistance.

resources.name: Centre Plan – Land Use By-law and Design Manual
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Centre Plan was built through extensive public engagement, including design workshops with neighbourhood groups, to identify appropriate places and forms for small-scale residential infill and missing‑middle housing. The adopted Design Manual sets clear, community-backed built-form standards (heights, massing, setbacks and frontage conditions) that allow as‑of‑right approvals for triplexes, townhouses and low-rise infill in designated areas, streamlining permits and reducing discretionary conflicts that often drive NIMBY resistance.

resources.name: Secondary and Backyard Suites
resources.description: HRM’s Secondary and Backyard Suites initiative legalized accessory dwelling units (including backyard/laneway-style suites) after a series of public workshops and consultations to surface neighbourhood concerns and opportunities. The municipality publishes clear design and permitting guidelines (setbacks, height, servicing and access), enabling small-scale, low-impact densification with predictable, staff-level approvals—adding rental supply while reducing NIMBY pushback through transparent, community-informed rules.

resources.name: Community Design Workshop (CDW)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Community Design Workshop partners annually with Nova Scotia towns and municipalities to run intensive public design charrettes focused on gentle neighbourhood infill, main-street intensification and housing choice. These charrettes produce illustrated concepts and community-backed design guidelines that municipalities use to update policies and fast-track approvals for missing‑middle housing (e.g., accessory suites, duplexes/triplexes and small multiplexes) with less public opposition.
resources.address: 5410 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E1

resources.name: Plan Wolfville (Municipal Planning Strategy & Core Area Design Guidelines)
resources.description: Through the Plan Wolfville process, the Town held public design workshops/charrettes to identify where and how gentle density—such as accessory/secondary suites, small multiplexes and townhouses—could fit within existing neighbourhoods. The resulting policies and Core Area architectural/design guidelines provide clear, pre-approved forms and infill standards that streamline approvals and address neighbourhood concerns with community-vetted solutions.

resources.name: Kings 2050 – Community Charrettes and Growth Centre Design Guidelines
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings – Planning & Development
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings conducted multi-day community design charrettes across its Growth Centres (e.g., New Minas, Canning) to co-create small-scale densification scenarios and main-street infill options. The adopted secondary plans and design guidelines translate this input into clear, form-based standards for accessory/secondary suites, duplexes/triplexes and townhouses, enabling as‑of‑right approvals that add housing while reducing NIMBY friction through shared, illustrated expectations.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

solutions.text: Volunteer Rehab and Skills-Training Crews: Create volunteer teams combining trades students and community volunteers to renovate vacant or substandard units, pairing skill-building opportunities with increases in safe, affordable housing stock.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia — Volunteer Build Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia organizes volunteer build crews—often including trades students from NSCC and local universities—who work alongside experienced staff and trades professionals to construct and, when suitable, rehabilitate homes. By leveraging community volunteers and student placements, the program increases the supply of safe, energy‑efficient, entry-level affordable homes for families across the province. These supervised builds and rehabs both expand affordable housing stock and provide hands-on skill development for emerging tradespeople.

resources.name: NSCC Service Learning and Community Projects (Trades)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College engages carpentry, electrical, plumbing, and related trades students in supervised service-learning projects that partner with non-profit housing providers to build and refurbish units. Students gain practical, industry-standard experience while working shoulder-to-shoulder with community volunteers and journeyperson instructors on real construction and renovation sites. This model directly supports the creation of safe, affordable housing while simultaneously developing a job-ready local trades workforce.

obstacles.title: Childcare Access and Affordability
obstacles.description: Insufficient spaces, staffing shortages, and uneven hours hinder workforce participation for young families.

solutions.text: Community Childcare Co-op: A parent-run cooperative that pools resources and staffing to operate an affordable, locally governed childcare centre with sliding-scale fees and volunteer support to reduce operating costs.

resources.name: King's Co-op Daycare
resources.description: A parent-run, non-profit co-operative childcare centre located on the University of King's College campus in Halifax. Families are co-op members who participate in governance and contribute volunteer time for maintenance, fundraising, and program support, which helps reduce operating costs and tailor hours to local needs. By pooling member resources and recognizing provincial fee subsidies, the centre delivers affordable, locally governed care aligned with the Community Childcare Co-op model.

resources.name: CBU Day Care Co-operative
resources.description: A licensed, parent-governed daycare co-operative serving students, staff, and the wider community at Cape Breton University in Sydney. Member families elect the board and contribute volunteer hours to operations and fundraising, which helps keep fees lower and extend care hours around class and shift schedules. The centre pools campus and community resources and accepts provincial fee subsidies, implementing a cooperative, locally governed approach to affordable childcare.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

solutions.text: Employer-Community Partnership Hubs: Local employers partner with community groups to create on-site or nearby childcare hubs offering flexible hours aligned with shift schedules and employer-subsidized spots for employees.

resources.name: Kids & Company Corporate Child Care Partnership – Halifax (Bayers Road)
resources.description: Kids & Company operates a licensed child care hub that partners with local employers in Halifax to offer priority enrollment, employer-subsidized/discounted spots, and backup care for employees. Located in a major employment corridor, the centre provides extended hours and flexible scheduling options that align with shift-based work, allowing participating employers to support staff retention and reduce absenteeism.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 118, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Kids & Company Corporate Child Care Partnership – Dartmouth (Burnside)
resources.description: Situated near Burnside Industrial Park, this Kids & Company location collaborates with employers to reserve and subsidize child care spaces for their workforce while providing priority access and national backup care benefits. The centre’s extended hours and flexible routines help align care with shift schedules common in logistics, manufacturing, and service roles, functioning as a nearby hub that eases access and affordability for employees.
resources.address: 202 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 120, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1T5

solutions.text: Shared Micro-Centres in Repurposed Spaces: Convert underused municipal buildings, libraries, faith spaces, or storefronts into small, licensed childcare rooms that share administration and rotate usage across neighborhoods.

resources.name: YMCA East Dartmouth Early Learning Centre
resources.description: The YMCA operates a licensed early learning program inside the municipal East Dartmouth Community Centre, converting multipurpose rooms into small childcare classrooms. As part of the YMCA’s multi-site network across HRM, the centre shares administration, staffing pools, and enrolment systems with other neighbourhood sites, extending hours and improving coverage while leveraging underused public space.

resources.name: YWCA Halifax – Early Learning and Child Care Centre (Spryfield)
resources.description: YWCA Halifax runs a licensed early learning centre within its Spryfield community hub, a repurposed storefront/office space adapted into multiple small childcare rooms. The micro-classrooms operate under centralized administration with coordinated staffing and program supports across YWCA services, improving access, flexibility, and hours for local families while making productive use of existing community infrastructure.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

solutions.text: Community Training and Apprenticeship Program: Partner with local colleges and community organizations to offer subsidized ECE training, practicum placements, and hiring pipelines that recruit and retain early childhood educators locally.

resources.name: Early Childhood Education Diploma
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE) delivers a provincially approved ECE diploma that includes multiple supervised practicum placements in NSCECE lab schools and licensed community child care centres across Nova Scotia. NSCECE partners with local employers to create direct hiring pipelines for graduates and connects students with provincial bursaries and tuition supports that subsidize training costs, helping recruit and retain ECEs locally.

resources.name: Early Childhood Education Work and Learn Pathway
resources.description: NSCC’s Work and Learn pathway enables participants to earn their Early Childhood Education credential while employed in licensed child care, blending paid on-the-job learning with subsidized coursework delivered in partnership with the Province of Nova Scotia. Learners complete structured practicums and workplace mentorship with local centres that frequently convert into job offers, establishing a sustained hiring pipeline and improving ECE recruitment and retention across the province.

solutions.text: Time-Bank Babysitting Network: A community time-bank where parents and caregivers exchange hours of childcare rather than money, improving access for families with irregular budgets and schedules.

resources.name: Halifax Plays Babysitting Co-op
resources.description: A volunteer-run babysitting cooperative where member families exchange child care using time credits instead of money. Parents earn one hour of credit for each hour they provide care to another member’s children and can spend those credits when they need care, making child care more flexible and affordable for families with irregular schedules.
resources.address: St. Andrew's Community Centre, 3380 Barnstead Lane, Halifax, NS B3K 5M6

solutions.text: Neighborhood Babysitting Co-op & Emergency Pool: Volunteer-run registry of trained back-up caregivers who can provide emergency or short-notice care, reducing gaps when regular programs are closed or staffed short.

resources.name: Emergency Child Care
resources.organization: Halifax & Region Military Family Resource Centre
resources.description: The Halifax & Region MFRC’s Emergency Child Care program provides short-notice and emergency back-up care for Canadian Armed Forces families when duty changes, deployments, illness, or unexpected events make regular child care unavailable. The centre maintains a pool of screened, trained caregivers and coordinates placements (including evenings and weekends), bridging gaps when centres close or staffing is short so parents can sustain work and essential appointments.

resources.name: Emergency Child Care
resources.description: GMFRC coordinates emergency and short-notice child care for military families in the Annapolis Valley when regular arrangements fall through due to shift changes, training, deployments, illness, or centre closures. The program draws on a roster of vetted caregivers and arranges placements quickly, providing a reliable back-up option that helps parents maintain employment and attend critical appointments.

resources.name: Volunteer Child-Minding and Family Support
resources.organization: Chebucto Family Centre (Home of the Guardian Angel)
resources.description: Chebucto Family Centre coordinates a volunteer-based child-minding network that offers short-term, on-call care so parents can attend work shifts, medical or legal appointments, or manage crises when regular child care is unavailable. The centre recruits, screens, and supports trained volunteers and staff to provide temporary care on-site or in the community, effectively serving as a neighbourhood back-up caregiver pool that helps families bridge gaps caused by closures and staffing shortages.

solutions.text: Mobile and Pop-up Childcare Services: A portable childcare team that sets up pop-up rooms for festivals, community events, or temporary worksite needs, increasing flexibility for families and employers.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC) Childminding
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS operates Care for Newcomer Children (CNC) childminding that sets up temporary, fully equipped child-safe rooms wherever newcomer programs are delivered. Their trained staff bring portable materials and safety equipment to ISANS sites and partner venues so parents can attend language classes, job fairs, employer info sessions, and community events. This mobile, pop-up model expands access to short-term childcare exactly when and where families need it.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC) – Pop-up Childminding for Newcomer Programs
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth – Centre for Immigrant Programs (CIP) and YREACH
resources.description: The YMCA’s immigrant services team provides CNC childminding that travels with their programs across HRM and other Nova Scotia communities via YREACH. Staff create pop-up childcare spaces at community centres, libraries, employer sessions, and special events so parents can participate in settlement, employment, and training activities. This portable approach increases flexibility for families and partner employers hosting short-term or after-hours programs.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 201, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Child Minding for Programs & Community Events
resources.description: YWCA Halifax provides on-site child minding to remove childcare barriers for women, gender-diverse people, and families attending employment, training, and community programs. Their team can bring portable equipment and set up short-term childcare rooms at partner sites, employer-hosted sessions, or community events, enabling flexible participation outside typical childcare hours. This pop-up model supports both families and organizations running time-limited activities.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

solutions.text: Sliding-Scale & Community Subsidy Fund: A local subsidy fund, managed by a community board, that top-ups fees for families in need and enables providers to offer sliding-scale pricing while maintaining staff wages.

resources.name: YMCA Financial Assistance for Child Care
resources.description: The YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth offers a donor-funded financial assistance program that reduces child care fees for families based on need. As a community-governed, non-profit organization, the YMCA uses this subsidy fund to enable sliding-scale pricing while ensuring providers receive full program revenues to maintain staffing and quality. This top-up support complements any provincial subsidy, bridging remaining gaps so families can access licensed care.

resources.name: EXCEL Before & After School Program – Fee Assistance
resources.description: HRCE’s EXCEL program provides supervised, school-based child care before and after school, and offers need-based fee assistance for families facing financial barriers. This assistance functions as a community-managed subsidy within the public education system, allowing sliding-scale access while preserving staffing levels and program quality. By topping up fees, EXCEL helps parents maintain employment and training schedules without providers absorbing revenue shortfalls.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Tuition Adjustment Program (Early Years & Aftercare)
resources.description: South Shore Waldorf School & Kindergarten operates a community-supported Tuition Adjustment Program that provides sliding-scale fee reductions for its early childhood programs and aftercare. Governed by a non-profit board, the school leverages donations and community funds to top up operating revenue so educators’ wages and program quality are sustained while reducing family costs. This model directly implements a local subsidy fund that expands access to child care-like hours for young families.

solutions.text: After-School and Extended-Hours Program Network: Coordinate school, recreation and community centre programs to provide seamless after-school and evening care options that support parents with nonstandard hours.

resources.name: Canada Games Centre After School Program
resources.description: The Canada Games Centre runs a licensed after-school program for elementary students that includes school pick-up, healthy snacks, and daily sport, swim, and recreation activities until 6:00 pm. Situated in a major community recreation facility, families can pair after-school care with evening aquatics and sport programs in the same building, creating seamless coverage beyond the school day. The program coordinates with nearby schools and leverages municipal recreation resources to support parents working nonstandard hours.
resources.address: 26 Thomas Raddall Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 0E2

resources.name: Halifax Public Libraries After-School Programs
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries offers free, supervised after-school drop-ins, homework help, and STEAM clubs at branches across HRM, many extending into the early evening. Staff coordinate with nearby schools and community partners to provide a safe, consistent place for children and teens after classes, bridging the gap between school dismissal and parents’ shift end times. These programs complement school-based and municipal recreation offerings, forming a coordinated network of after-school and evening options.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: YMCA Before & After School Child Care (Cape Breton)
resources.description: The YMCA of Cape Breton delivers before- and after-school child care across multiple school sites and at the downtown YMCA centre, with extended hours and financial assistance available. By operating in schools and at the YMCA facility, families can transition to evening swim lessons, youth clubs, and sport programs without additional travel, effectively linking school, community, and recreation spaces. This coordinated model expands access to reliable care beyond the regular school day for shift-working parents in Sydney and surrounding communities.

resources.name: Pathways to Education Spryfield
resources.description: Chebucto Connections’ Pathways to Education Spryfield provides structured after-school tutoring, mentoring, meals, and bus tickets for high school students four evenings per week at the Captain William Spry Community Centre and partner schools. The program works closely with school staff, families, and community organizations to keep youth engaged and supervised into the early evening, complementing daytime schooling and municipal recreation. By extending supports after school and into evening hours in a community hub, it fills coverage gaps that challenge parents with nonstandard work schedules.
resources.address: 531 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1X3

solutions.text: Childcare Shared Services Cooperative: A municipal or community-led shared-services model that centralizes licensing, payroll, procurement, and compliance for small providers to lower admin costs and increase capacity.

resources.name: NSCECE Family Home Child Care Agency
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE)
resources.description: The NSCECE Family Home Child Care Agency serves as a shared-services hub for multiple independent home-based child care providers across the Halifax region. It centralizes licensing support, compliance monitoring, parent intake and placement, training, policies, and administrative tasks such as invoicing/receipts and subsidy processing—reducing administrative burden and costs so small providers can focus on care and expand capacity and hours.

resources.name: East Hants & Area Family Home Child Care Agency
resources.description: This licensed agency provides a centralized shared-services model for home-based child care providers in East Hants and surrounding communities. It handles compliance oversight with provincial standards, parent referrals and enrollment, training, forms and record-keeping systems, and support with billing and subsidy administration—lowering administrative costs and enabling small providers to add spaces and offer more flexible hours.

resources.name: Cape Breton Family Home Child Care Agency
resources.organization: Cape Breton Family Place Resource Centre
resources.description: Operating as a shared-services framework, this agency centralizes licensing support, ongoing compliance monitoring, family intake and placement, educator recruitment, training, and back-office supports (templates, policies, billing support, and subsidy processing) for multiple small home-based providers. By pooling these administrative functions, it reduces overhead, stabilizes operations, and helps providers increase capacity to meet local demand.

resources.name: Pictou County Family Home Child Care Agency
resources.organization: Kids First Association (Pictou County Kids First Family Resource Program)
resources.description: This agency delivers a shared-services model for independent home child care providers in Pictou County by centralizing regulatory compliance, provider onboarding and training, parent intake and matching, and administrative processes such as invoicing and subsidy coordination. The approach lowers administrative workload and costs for small providers and supports the creation of more regulated spaces with consistent quality.
resources.address: 110 Provost Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 2P4

solutions.text: Community Transportation to Childcare Hubs: Volunteer-driven or subsidized shuttle services connecting residential areas to centralized childcare hubs, improving access for families without convenient transit.

resources.name: Pre-Primary Transportation (HRCE)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Centre for Education provides subsidized busing for eligible children enrolled in the province’s school-based Pre-Primary (early learning) program. By connecting neighborhoods to centralized school hubs that host Pre-Primary classrooms, this service functions as a shuttle to childcare/early learning sites for families who lack convenient transit, reducing access barriers tied to distance and scheduling.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: BGC Greater Halifax After-School Transportation
resources.organization: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Halifax
resources.description: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Halifax operates licensed school-age childcare programs and runs daily bus/van pickups from multiple schools and neighborhood points to its club sites. These runs act as community shuttles to centralized childcare hubs, enabling families—especially those without cars or convenient transit—to reliably access after-school care aligned with parents’ work hours.

resources.name: YMCA Child Care Transportation (Before & After School)
resources.description: The YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth operates licensed child care and school-age programs and offers site-specific transportation where available, using YMCA buses/vans to shuttle children from designated schools or pickup points to centralized YMCA childcare hubs. This subsidized, coordinated transport improves access for families with limited transit options and aligns with workday schedules.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Community Transit (Eastern Shore & Musquodoboit Valley)
resources.description: MusGo Rider is a community, door-to-door transit co-operative offering accessible, pre-booked rides across the Eastern Shore and Musquodoboit Valley. Families use MusGo to reach licensed daycares and early-years centres, effectively creating a community shuttle link between residential areas and childcare hubs; the service is provincially and municipally supported to keep fares affordable.
resources.address: 71 Park Road, Musquodoboit Harbour, NS B0J 2L0

resources.name: Kings Point-to-Point Transit (Childcare Access Rides)
resources.description: Kings Point-to-Point Transit provides accessible, demand-responsive transportation throughout Kings County, including trips to daycares, family resource centres, and pre-primary sites. By offering affordable, scheduled pickups from home or community points to centralized childcare hubs, it reduces transportation barriers for working families in rural and small-town communities.
resources.address: 14 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

solutions.text: Intergenerational Care Programs: Link seniors' centres and retirement homes with childcare providers for shared programming where elders support children and receive social engagement and modest compensation.

resources.name: Intergenerational Programming (Northwood Halifax Campus)
resources.description: Northwood’s Halifax campus runs ongoing intergenerational programming that brings licensed child care centres and early years classes into the residence for weekly shared activities such as story time, music, art and free play. Seniors participate as “grand-friends” alongside early childhood educators, adding caring adults during programming blocks while gaining meaningful social engagement; childcare partners benefit from enriched curriculum and reliable, welcoming community space.

resources.name: Intergenerational Connections – Parkland at the Lakes
resources.description: Life enrichment staff at Parkland at the Lakes coordinate regular visits and co-programmed sessions with nearby licensed child care centres and preschools. Residents volunteer as program helpers—reading with children, assisting with crafts and music, and sharing skills—while child care partners use Parkland’s common rooms for group time, creating shared programming that supports early learning and increases social engagement for older adults.

resources.name: Intergenerational Play and Grandfriends (Ocean View)
resources.description: Ocean View partners with local daycares and Early Years programs to host on-site intergenerational playgroups and recurring grandfriends visits. Residents support ECE-led activities—reading circles, sensory play, and music—providing additional caring adults and a community venue for child care partners, while older adults benefit from purposeful social connection and reduced isolation.
resources.address: 1907 Caldwell Road, Eastern Passage, NS B3G 1M3

resources.name: Intergenerational Program – Glen Haven Manor
resources.description: Glen Haven Manor’s intergenerational program brings young children from community child care centres into the long-term care home for planned activities including reading, crafts and music. Elders engage as storytellers and play companions alongside early childhood educators, strengthening early learning with additional adult attention while fostering meaningful relationships and social wellness for residents.
resources.address: 739 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3S1

solutions.text: Local Seed Grants and Social Enterprise Models: Community foundations and municipalities offer seed grants and small-business supports to encourage social-enterprise childcare start-ups that prioritize affordability and local hiring.

resources.name: HRM Community Grants Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Community Grants Program provides seed and project funding to non-profit organizations delivering community services, which can include establishing or expanding affordable, community-run childcare. These small grants help groups cover start-up and capital costs, pilot new models, and scale services, supporting social-enterprise approaches that prioritize affordability and local hiring in neighbourhoods with limited childcare options.

resources.name: CBDC Hants-Kings – Small Business Financing & Advisory
resources.description: CBDC Hants-Kings offers microloans, social enterprise financing, and hands-on business advisory services that help launch and grow childcare ventures across rural and small-town communities. By providing accessible capital, coaching, and training, the program enables community-led and cooperative childcare start-ups to build sustainable operations that emphasize affordability and hire locally.

resources.name: Common Good Solutions – Social Enterprise Incubation & Investment
resources.description: Common Good Solutions supports social enterprise start-ups with training, coaching, and access to impact investment, helping community groups design and launch childcare models that balance financial sustainability with affordability and local employment. Their incubation and advisory services guide founders through business planning, revenue strategies, and measurement of social outcomes, enabling viable, community-anchored childcare solutions.

resources.name: Town of Truro – Grants to Organizations Program
resources.description: Truro’s Grants to Organizations Program provides small grants to local non-profits for community development projects, which can include starting or expanding affordable, community-run childcare. These seed funds help with early-stage costs, equipment, and pilot initiatives, enabling social-enterprise childcare models that respond to local staffing and access needs while creating jobs for residents.

solutions.text: Parent Cooperative Scheduling Platform: A community-built scheduling app where parents coordinate shift swaps, shared nanny schedules, and cooperative care blocks to maximize utilization and reduce costs.

resources.name: Parent Co-operative Childcare Exchange (Chebucto Family Centre)
resources.organization: Home of the Guardian Angel (Chebucto Family Centre)
resources.description: Chebucto Family Centre facilitates a parent-led childcare exchange where families coordinate child-minding swaps, shared nanny schedules, and cooperative care blocks. Parents use shared online calendars and simple scheduling tools to post availability, request coverage, and swap shifts, maximizing existing community capacity and lowering out-of-pocket costs for care.

resources.name: Newcomer Parents Care Co-op (ISANS)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS supports newcomer families to form cooperative childcare groups that coordinate coverage for language classes, job interviews, and shift work. Staff help cohorts set up a scheduling platform using group messaging and shared calendars so parents can arrange care swaps, create rotating care blocks, and organize shared nanny arrangements to reduce costs and increase flexibility.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Dartmouth Parents Childcare Swap & Nanny Share Network
resources.organization: Dartmouth Family Centre & Dartmouth North Community Food Centre
resources.description: Dartmouth Family Centre convenes local parents to build a cooperative scheduling network for babysitting swaps, part-time care coordination, and nanny shares. Using a simple app and online sign-up calendars, families can post needs, trade hours, and align part-time schedules into shared care blocks, improving access during non-standard hours and reducing overall childcare expenses.
resources.address: 107 Albro Lake Road, Dartmouth, NS B3A 3Y2

solutions.text: Community Advocacy & Planning Forum: A citizen-led forum to gather family voices, map local childcare deserts, and work with municipal planners to secure zoning changes, capital funding, and long-term childcare strategy.

resources.name: Planning & Development – Community Planning and Engagement for Child Care Facilities
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Planning & Development department runs ongoing public engagement on municipal strategies and land-use by-laws, gathering families’ input on where child care is needed, operating hours, and barriers to access. Staff analyze licensing data, demographics, and feedback to identify service gaps and propose zoning amendments that enable centres and family home child care in more neighbourhoods, while coordinating with provincial/federal partners on capital funding and embedding child care access in long-term growth plans.

resources.name: Planning & Development – Child Care Facility Zoning & Public Engagement
resources.organization: Cape Breton Regional Municipality – Planning & Development
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Municipality’s Planning & Development team consults residents, parents, and child care providers to pinpoint neighbourhoods with limited access and to inform updates to the Municipal Planning Strategy and Land-Use By-law related to child care uses. Through workshops and hearings, they gather family voices, map local gaps alongside community input, and advance zoning changes and site approvals for new or expanded child care spaces, aligning these with infrastructure and funding opportunities as part of longer-term community planning.

obstacles.title: Primary Care and Mental Health Gaps
obstacles.description: Long wait times and lack of family doctors and mental health supports reduce confidence in staying long term.

solutions.text: Community Nurse Practitioner Clinic: Establish a community-run clinic staffed by nurse practitioners and physician assistants on a rotating schedule to provide primary care, triage, routine chronic care, and referrals for mental health supports with extended evening/weekend hours.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Primary Care Clinics (Cobequid Community Health Centre site)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health runs rotating primary care clinics for unattached patients at community sites like the Cobequid Community Health Centre, often on evenings and weekends. Clinics are staffed by nurse practitioners and other primary care providers who triage issues, manage routine and chronic care (e.g., prescription refills, blood pressure/diabetes checks), and provide referrals to mental health and addictions services and community resources—directly aligning with the community nurse practitioner clinic model.
resources.address: 40 Freer Lane, Lower Sackville, NS B4C 0A2

resources.name: North End Community Health Centre (Primary Health Care)
resources.description: A community-governed health centre providing primary care through an interdisciplinary team that includes nurse practitioners, offering assessment/triage, chronic disease management, and same-day access options for local residents. The centre integrates on-site counselling and connects clients with mental health and addictions supports, reflecting the solution’s focus on NP-led community clinics that coordinate referrals and accessible care.

resources.name: Eskasoni Health Centre (Primary Care and Mental Health Services)
resources.organization: Eskasoni First Nation – Health and Wellness
resources.description: The Eskasoni Health Centre delivers community-run primary care with nurse practitioners and family health teams that provide triage, routine and chronic care, and health promotion for Eskasoni First Nation. It offers integrated mental health and addiction services and coordinates referrals to specialized supports, aligning with an NP-led community clinic model that improves access and continuity of care.

solutions.text: Peer Mental Health Support Networks: Create volunteer-led peer support groups and peer navigator programs run from community centres and libraries that offer regular drop-in sessions, crisis navigation, and connection to professional services.

resources.name: Laing House Peer Support Program
resources.description: Laing House is a youth-driven organization for people aged 16–29 living with mental illness, offering daily peer-led drop-in programming, support groups, and community activities. Trained youth peer leaders and staff facilitate connections to primary care, counseling, and psychiatric services, and help members navigate crisis supports. Programs are run from a welcoming, youth-centered space and often partner with libraries and community venues to reduce wait-time barriers and build supportive networks.

resources.name: Community Navigators (Library-Based Social Work & Navigation)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts Community Navigators who provide free drop-in navigation and referrals to mental health, primary care, housing, and crisis resources across multiple branches. Libraries also routinely host partner-led, volunteer and peer-run mental health support groups and drop-in circles in their community rooms, creating low-barrier, neighborhood-based hubs for help. This directly aligns with peer support and navigator access in community spaces, reducing wait-time stress and connecting people quickly to professional services.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Peer Support Nova Scotia (Adult Peer Support)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health, Mental Health and Addictions Program
resources.description: Peer Support Nova Scotia embeds trained peer support workers with lived experience within Nova Scotia Health’s Mental Health & Addictions Program to offer one-on-one and group peer support, both in clinical and community settings. Many sessions are delivered in accessible community locations and help people navigate crisis options and connect to clinicians, family doctors, and counseling. The program complements primary care by providing regular, recovery-oriented peer support and guided pathways to professional services.

resources.name: Community Mental Health & Navigation (Drop-in and Peer-Informed Supports)
resources.description: The North End Community Health Centre operates community-based drop-ins and outreach that include peer-informed support and navigation for mental health and substance use. Peer and outreach workers meet people where they are—at the health centre and in neighborhood settings—to guide them to primary care providers, counseling, and crisis resources, reducing barriers and wait-time uncertainty. As a trusted community hub, it anchors ongoing, low-barrier support in a familiar space and connects residents directly to professional services.

resources.name: Phoenix Centre for Youth (Drop-in & Navigation)
resources.description: Phoenix Centre for Youth provides a daily drop-in for youth ages 16–24 that includes peer-style support, basic needs, and on-site navigation to primary care and mental health services. Staff and peer mentors help young people access counseling, crisis lines, and community clinics, while building supportive peer networks in a safe, youth-friendly space. This model offers consistent, low-barrier, community-based support that shortens the path to professional help.

solutions.text: Telehealth Hubs in Public Spaces: Set up private telehealth booths in municipal buildings, community centres and libraries with reliable internet, devices, and trained volunteers to help residents access virtual primary care and counselling appointments.

resources.name: Bookable Study Rooms and Phone Booths (Telehealth-Friendly Spaces)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries offers private study rooms and phone booths at branches like Halifax Central Library that residents routinely use for virtual medical and counselling appointments. Libraries provide free high-speed Wi‑Fi, public computers and loanable devices, and staff tech help to connect to Nova Scotia Health–supported virtual care platforms (e.g., Zoom/Maple), effectively creating a telehealth hub in a trusted public space.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Community Meeting Rooms (Telehealth Use by Appointment)
resources.description: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library provides bookable, private community rooms with reliable internet at branches such as New Glasgow Public Library, enabling residents to attend virtual primary care and mental health counselling sessions. Staff can assist with device setup and video platforms, and patrons can use library computers or borrow devices—functioning as a practical telehealth hub in a public library setting.
resources.address: 182 Dalhousie Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 4M7

resources.name: Book a Room (Private Telehealth-Friendly Spaces)
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library’s McConnell Library offers bookable private rooms and strong Wi‑Fi that community members use for virtual doctor and counselling appointments. Staff provide basic tech help, and patrons can access library devices as needed—creating a library-based telehealth access point that reduces travel and connectivity barriers.

resources.name: Study Rooms (Telehealth Support in Community Library)
resources.description: South Shore Public Libraries’ Margaret Hennigar Public Library in Bridgewater provides private study rooms with dependable internet that residents can reserve for virtual health and mental health appointments. Library staff offer help with devices and video platforms, turning a community library into a convenient telehealth hub.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

solutions.text: Local Mental Health First Aid Training: Offer regular subsidized Mental Health First Aid and youth-focused training for teachers, employers, faith groups, coaches and volunteers so more community members can recognize issues early and make appropriate referrals.

resources.name: Mental Health First Aid (MHFA) Training – Nova Scotia & PEI
resources.organization: St. John Ambulance Nova Scotia/PEI Council
resources.description: St. John Ambulance delivers the nationally recognized Mental Health First Aid program in communities and workplaces across Nova Scotia, with offerings that include youth-focused content. Courses equip teachers, employers, coaches, faith leaders, and volunteers to recognize emerging mental health and substance use problems, provide initial support, and refer individuals to appropriate professional help. As a charity, SJA frequently offers discounted group rates and community/classroom-based sessions that reduce cost barriers for nonprofits and local organizations.
resources.address: 72 Highfield Park Drive, Unit 5, Dartmouth, NS B3A 4X2

resources.name: Mental Health First Aid (Supporting Youth) – Professional Learning for Educators
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Teachers Union sponsors and hosts Mental Health First Aid (including youth-focused modules) as part of its professional learning for teachers, school leaders, specialists, and support staff province-wide. Training helps educators and coaches identify early signs of mental health concerns in students, engage in supportive conversations, and connect young people with school-based or community mental health services. Sessions are offered at low or no cost to members, effectively subsidizing access to MHFA across schools in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 3106 Joseph Howe Drive, Halifax, NS B3L 4L7

resources.name: Mental Health First Aid (Supporting Youth) – Campus and Community Training
resources.description: Dalhousie Student Health & Wellness offers Mental Health First Aid (including youth-focused content) for faculty, staff, student leaders, and community-facing roles such as residence assistants and coaches. The program builds confidence to notice warning signs, provide initial help, and make timely referrals to on-campus and community mental health resources. Trainings are frequently provided at low or no cost to participants, expanding MHFA capacity in the broader Halifax community.

resources.name: Mental Health in Sport – Coach and Volunteer Training
resources.description: Sport Nova Scotia promotes and hosts youth-focused mental health literacy for coaches and sport leaders (e.g., the Coaching Association of Canada’s Mental Health in Sport training). These workshops help community coaches and volunteers recognize when young athletes may be struggling, have supportive conversations, and connect them to appropriate mental health services. Sport Nova Scotia and its member organizations often subsidize or bundle these trainings within coach development pathways to improve accessibility across local clubs and associations.
resources.address: 5516 Spring Garden Road, 4th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 1G6

solutions.text: Community Health Navigation Service: Create a staffed navigation program (phone and in-person) to help people find family doctors, schedule appointments, apply for sliding-scale counseling, and coordinate follow-up care across services.

resources.name: Health and Wellness – Health System Navigation
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides phone and in‑person health system navigation to help newcomers understand and access primary and mental health care in Nova Scotia. Staff assist clients to get attached to a family doctor or nurse practitioner, book primary and specialist appointments, and arrange interpretation. They also connect clients to mental health supports, including free and sliding‑scale counseling programs, and coordinate follow‑up between providers and settlement services.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Social Work and Care Navigation
resources.description: NECHC integrates primary care with social work and patient navigation to remove barriers to access. Navigators help clients register for and secure a family doctor or nurse practitioner, schedule clinic and specialist appointments, and address practical issues like transportation or coverage. They connect people with counseling resources (including low‑/sliding‑fee options) and coordinate follow‑up across services such as MOSH, addictions supports, and community partners.

resources.name: Wellness Navigation and Peer Support
resources.organization: Canadian Mental Health Association, Halifax‑Dartmouth Branch
resources.description: CMHA Halifax‑Dartmouth offers staffed wellness navigation that helps individuals identify needs and access the right mix of primary and mental health services. Navigators provide phone and in‑person support to book counseling (including low‑cost and sliding‑scale options), connect to family practices and community clinics, and make referrals. They also coordinate follow‑up to ensure people transition smoothly between services and stay engaged in care.

resources.name: Health & Wellness Program (Navigation)
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre provides culturally safe health navigation for urban Indigenous community members. Staff help people get connected to family doctors or nurse practitioners, arrange and attend appointments, and access mental wellness supports; they also assist clients in applying for covered and low‑/no‑cost counseling (e.g., through NIHB and community programs). Navigators coordinate follow‑up with hospitals, community services, and social supports to ensure continuous care.

solutions.text: Student Placement Partnerships: Partner with nursing, social work, counselling and medical schools to host student placements and supervised clinics locally, increasing services while providing training and recruitment pathways.

resources.name: North End Community Health Centre – Learner Placement Program
resources.description: The North End Community Health Centre (NECHC) is a community-based primary health and mental health provider that partners with Dalhousie and other Atlantic universities to host placements for medical, nursing, social work, counselling, and pharmacy students. Learners work in supervised clinics (including primary care, mental health, and outreach like MOSH) that expand appointment capacity while providing hands-on training and a direct recruitment pathway into Nova Scotia’s community health system.

resources.name: Halifax Sexual Health Centre – Teaching Clinic
resources.description: Halifax Sexual Health Centre is a nonprofit clinic that serves the public while acting as a formal teaching site for Dalhousie University medical residents and medical and nursing students. Under supervision by licensed clinicians, students provide sexual and reproductive health services, which increases local access to care and creates a practical training and recruitment pipeline for primary and community health in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 302, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Dalhousie Family Medicine Teaching Unit – Halifax (Mumford)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Department of Family Medicine
resources.description: This academic family practice provides comprehensive primary care to the public while training Dalhousie University family medicine residents and medical learners in a supervised clinical setting. The teaching unit increases the number of available appointments for community members and builds a direct pipeline for recruiting new family physicians to practice in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Acadia University Psychology Training Clinic
resources.description: The Acadia Psychology Clinic offers low-cost psychological assessment and therapy to the public delivered by graduate students in Clinical Psychology under the supervision of licensed psychologists. By hosting practicum and internship placements locally, the clinic expands access to mental health services in the Annapolis Valley while training and retaining future psychologists for Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Sliding-Scale Counselling Fund: Establish a community-managed fund (supported by municipal seed money, local business contributions and fundraising) to subsidize short-term counselling for residents on low or moderate incomes.

resources.name: Affordable Counselling Program
resources.organization: Canadian Mental Health Association, Halifax-Dartmouth Branch
resources.description: CMHA Halifax-Dartmouth offers short-term counselling on a sliding fee scale based on income, making services accessible to residents with low or moderate incomes. The program is sustained by grants, donations, and fee contributions, effectively subsidizing counselling costs and helping reduce barriers and wait times in the public system.

resources.name: Dalhousie Psychology Clinic
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Department of Psychology & Neuroscience
resources.description: The clinic provides evidence-based, time-limited therapy delivered by graduate trainees under the supervision of registered psychologists, with fees set on a sliding scale. University support together with client fees subsidize care for community members, increasing affordable access to counselling for those without private insurance or the means to pay full fees.

resources.name: Applied Psychology Services (APS) Clinic
resources.organization: Mount Saint Vincent University, Department of Psychology
resources.description: APS offers community counselling provided by graduate students in psychology under supervision, using a sliding-scale fee structure to keep costs low. Supported by the university and program revenues, APS subsidizes short-term counselling for individuals and families, aligning with efforts to reduce financial barriers to mental health support.

resources.name: ISANS Wellness Counselling
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides free, short-term mental health counselling and wellness support to immigrants and refugees, removing cost as a barrier to timely care. Services are funded by government and community partners, effectively subsidizing counselling for low- and moderate-income newcomers facing long wait times in the broader system.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Employer Mental Health Consortium: Form a local consortium of employers to share the cost of on-site or virtual counselling, provide flexible leave for appointments, and coordinate retention incentives tied to health benefits for new hires.

resources.name: Chambers of Commerce Group Insurance Plan
resources.description: The Chambers Plan pools thousands of small and medium-sized employers, including many in Nova Scotia, to make group benefits with mental health supports affordable through shared risk and cost. Through the Halifax Chamber, local employers can join to offer employees EFAP and virtual counselling, and use immediate coverage for new hires as a retention incentive; members also receive HR advisory resources that support policies like flexible paid time for counselling appointments.
resources.address: 32 Akerley Boulevard, Unit 100, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1N1

resources.name: CANS Group Benefits Program
resources.description: The Construction Association of Nova Scotia offers a pooled group benefits program that lets member employers share the cost of health and mental health coverage, including EFAP and virtual counselling options. By leveraging sector-wide purchasing power, firms can extend counselling supports from day one as a retention tool for apprentices and new hires, while CANS’ employer resources and training help members adopt flexible leave practices for medical and counselling appointments.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 101, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Health Association Nova Scotia Employee Benefits Plan
resources.description: Health Association Nova Scotia administers a multi-employer benefits plan for continuing care, disability support, and community health organizations across the province, pooling employers to reduce costs. The plan includes comprehensive mental health coverage and EFAP with virtual counselling, and HANS provides HR and policy guidance so member organizations can use benefits and flexible leave for appointments as part of recruitment and retention strategies for new hires.
resources.address: 2 Bluewater Road, Suite 150, Bedford, NS B4B 1G7

resources.name: Medavie Blue Cross Group Benefits & Connected Care
resources.description: Medavie Blue Cross serves many Nova Scotia employers with group benefits that include virtual mental health services through its Connected Care platform and EFAP options, enabling shared-cost access to counselling. Employers can select pooled or fully insured plans and set eligibility (e.g., coverage beginning at hire) to support retention of new employees, while facilitating flexible access to counselling appointments during work hours through virtual care.

solutions.text: Mobile Primary Care and Wellness Clinics: Operate a regular mobile clinic that visits rural neighbourhoods and high-need areas offering basic primary care, vaccinations, screening, and referrals to mental health resources.

resources.name: Mobile Primary Care Clinics
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health operates rotating mobile primary care clinics that travel to rural and high-need communities to provide same-day basic care such as assessments, prescriptions, simple diagnostics, routine vaccinations, and health screening. These clinics help people without a family doctor access timely care and include on-site navigation and referrals to mental health and addictions services and appropriate follow-up in the health system.

resources.name: Mobile Outreach Street Health (MOSH)
resources.description: MOSH runs a mobile primary care and harm-reduction service that brings nurses, physicians, and outreach workers directly to shelters, encampments, and underserved neighbourhoods across the Halifax region. The team provides on-the-spot primary care, immunizations, wound care, STI testing, and health screening, and connects clients to mental health, addictions, and social supports through warm referrals and coordinated follow-up.

resources.name: Community Paramedicine and Mobile Integrated Health
resources.organization: Emergency Health Services (Medavie Health Services Nova Scotia)
resources.description: EHS community paramedics deliver mobile clinics and in-home care in rural and high-need communities, offering assessments for minor/urgent concerns, chronic disease monitoring, vaccinations (e.g., flu/COVID), and health screenings to reduce emergency department use and bridge primary care gaps. Paramedic teams coordinate with primary care and Nova Scotia Health to arrange follow-up and make referrals to mental health and addictions resources so patients can access comprehensive support close to home.
resources.address: 239 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2B2

solutions.text: Community Transportation for Appointments: Organize volunteer driver programs or low-cost shuttles specifically to get residents to primary care and mental health appointments, reducing missed visits and improving continuity of care.

resources.name: Access-A-Bus
resources.description: Access-A-Bus is Halifax Transit’s door-to-door, shared-ride service for people with disabilities who cannot use conventional transit. It provides low-cost, pre-booked transportation to medical and mental health appointments, improving continuity of care by reducing missed visits across the Halifax Regional Municipality.

resources.name: BayRides Community Transportation Service
resources.organization: BayRides (St. Margaret’s Bay Community Transportation Society)
resources.description: BayRides is a community-run, door-to-door transportation service in the St. Margaret’s Bay area that offers affordable rides to primary care, specialist, and mental health appointments. By operating scheduled and on-demand trips with accessible vehicles, it reduces transportation barriers and helps residents keep critical health appointments.
resources.address: 5289 St. Margarets Bay Road, Upper Tantallon, NS B3Z 2J2

resources.name: Canadian Red Cross Transportation Services – Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Canadian Red Cross, Nova Scotia Region
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross operates volunteer-based transportation for people who need help getting to medical and mental health appointments across parts of Nova Scotia.
