Using screened volunteer drivers and low-cost rides, the program ensures clients can access primary care, diagnostics, counseling, and other health services reliably.

solutions.text: Integrated School-Based Mental Health Teams: Work with school boards to place counsellors, social workers and family clinicians in schools to provide quick access for youth, early intervention, and seamless links to community services.

resources.name: SchoolsPlus (Province-wide)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: SchoolsPlus is a province-wide initiative that embeds SchoolsPlus Facilitators, Community Outreach Workers, and partnered mental health clinicians directly in public schools. By coordinating on-site counselling, social work support, and family services, SchoolsPlus provides early intervention and quick access for youth while creating warm handoffs to community mental health and addictions care. The integrated, school-based team model reduces wait times and improves continuity of care by linking students and families seamlessly with Nova Scotia Health/IWK and local community agencies.

resources.name: HRCE SchoolsPlus
resources.description: HRCE SchoolsPlus places facilitators, social workers, and community outreach workers in schools across the Halifax region, with IWK/Nova Scotia Health clinicians regularly providing on-site mental health care. The teams offer walk-in counselling, brief therapy, group programming, and coordinated referrals, ensuring youth receive early intervention and rapid access without navigating complex systems. Through close collaboration with school staff and community partners, they create seamless links to specialized services for students and families.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: IWK School-Based Mental Health and Addictions Services
resources.description: IWK clinicians work within Halifax-area schools in partnership with SchoolsPlus and school staff to provide assessment, brief therapy, and care coordination directly where youth learn. By co-locating mental health practitioners in schools, the program accelerates access, offers early intervention, and reduces barriers to care for students and families. Clinicians ensure seamless transitions to specialized hospital and community services when needed, strengthening continuity of care.

resources.name: AVRCE SchoolsPlus
resources.organization: Annapolis Valley Regional Centre for Education
resources.description: AVRCE SchoolsPlus coordinates school-based teams—facilitators, outreach workers, and partnered mental health clinicians—embedded across Annapolis Valley schools to provide on-site counselling and social supports. The program focuses on early identification and intervention, reducing wait times by meeting students where they are and linking families to Nova Scotia Health and local community services. Integrated case planning and warm handoffs ensure youth receive the right support at the right time.

solutions.text: Cultural and Indigenous Healing Partnerships: Develop formal partnerships with Indigenous healers and cultural service providers to offer culturally safe mental health programming and broaden the types of supports available locally.

resources.name: Health & Wellness Program
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Health & Wellness Program provides Indigenous-led mental wellness supports including Elders-in-Residence, traditional counselling, sharing circles, and land-based healing. By formally partnering with Mi’kmaw Knowledge Keepers and cultural service providers, the Centre offers culturally safe programming and connects community members to primary and mental health services, broadening the types of supports available locally.

resources.name: Indigenous Health Program
resources.description: IWK Health’s Indigenous Health Program supports Indigenous children, youth, and families through Indigenous Patient Navigators and access to traditional healing practices (e.g., smudging, ceremony) within the hospital and community. The program maintains formal partnerships with Mi’kmaw Elders and cultural service providers to integrate cultural safety and traditional wellness alongside clinical mental health care, improving timely, culturally grounded support.

resources.name: Elders in Residence Program
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Elders in Residence Program connects Indigenous students with Mi’kmaw and other Indigenous Elders for one-on-one support, sharing circles, cultural teachings, and care navigation. Through formal partnerships with Knowledge Keepers and cultural practitioners, the university offers culturally safe mental wellness supports that complement conventional counselling and reduce barriers to accessing help.

resources.name: Unama’ki College Elders in Residence and Indigenous Student Support
resources.description: Unama’ki College at Cape Breton University provides Elders-in-Residence, sharing circles, language and culture-based wellness activities, and ceremonial supports for Indigenous students. These services are delivered through formal relationships with local Mi’kmaw Elders and cultural service providers, embedding traditional healing alongside counselling to expand culturally safe mental health supports on campus and in the local community.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

solutions.text: Rapid Volunteer Roster for Crisis Coverage: Create a trained volunteer roster (retired nurses, counsellors, social workers) who can provide short-term coverage and crisis response while clients wait for permanent providers.

resources.name: Friendly Calls (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross Friendly Calls program uses a roster of trained volunteers to provide regular phone-based wellness checks, psychosocial first aid, and referrals to community and health resources. By offering immediate, short-term supportive contact—often from experienced volunteers—it helps buffer isolation and mental health strain while clients wait for permanent primary care or counselling providers.

resources.name: Victim Services Unit
resources.description: Halifax Regional Police’s Victim Services Unit deploys trained volunteer responders who provide immediate crisis intervention, safety planning, and short-term emotional support to victims of crime and trauma. This rapid volunteer roster offers stabilization and navigation to health and mental health resources, bridging the gap until clients can access ongoing services such as family physicians, counsellors, or social workers.

resources.name: Medical First Responder (MFR) Units – Nova Scotia
resources.description: St. John Ambulance organizes trained volunteer Medical First Responders who provide rapid on-scene first aid, wellness checks, and psychosocial support in emergencies and community incidents. Their mobilized volunteer roster stabilizes individuals and connects them to appropriate care, acting as short-term coverage in crises while people await access to primary care or mental health providers.
resources.address: 72 Highfield Park Drive, Unit 121, Dartmouth, NS B3A 4X2

resources.name: Peer Support Groups and Navigation
resources.organization: Canadian Mental Health Association, Halifax-Dartmouth Branch
resources.description: CMHA Halifax-Dartmouth runs peer-led support groups and one-to-one peer support facilitated by trained volunteers with lived experience, offering immediate emotional support and system navigation. These services provide short-term, low-barrier coverage that helps people cope and stay connected while waiting for appointments with family doctors, therapists, or specialized mental health providers.

solutions.text: Community Provider Recruitment Campaign: Coordinate a local recruitment package promoting quality of life, housing support, spousal employment help, and relocation bonuses to attract family doctors, nurse practitioners and therapists to the area.

resources.name: Office of Healthcare Professionals Recruitment (PracticeNS)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Health and Wellness — Office of Healthcare Professionals Recruitment
resources.description: The province’s Office of Healthcare Professionals Recruitment runs PracticeNS, a coordinated recruitment portal and concierge-style service that markets Nova Scotia’s quality of life and matches family doctors, nurse practitioners, and therapists to communities. The team organizes site visits, provides relocation incentives, and connects candidates and their partners to housing options, schools, and spousal employment supports in collaboration with municipal and community partners.
resources.address: 1894 Barrington Street, 4th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 2A8

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Physician Recruitment
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s provincial recruitment program actively attracts family physicians and nurse practitioners with relocation assistance, signing incentives, and a dedicated recruitment team. They coordinate community tours, promote local lifestyle advantages, and connect candidates with housing resources and spousal employment networks, aligning directly with a comprehensive community recruitment package.

resources.name: Physician Recruitment & Retention
resources.description: Doctors Nova Scotia partners with communities and the province to recruit and retain family physicians, providing tools and guidance for community-led campaigns that highlight quality of life and practice supports. Their resources and advisory support help assemble local packages that include relocation guidance, introductions to housing and schools, and connections for spousal employment.
resources.address: 1559 Brunswick Street, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3J 2G1

resources.name: IWK Health Talent Acquisition
resources.description: IWK Health recruits nurses, nurse practitioners, therapists, and physicians with a dedicated talent acquisition team that provides relocation assistance and onboarding support. They promote Halifax’s quality of life, coordinate with local partners for housing information and spousal employment referrals, and guide candidates through settlement to improve long-term retention.

solutions.text: Wellness Hubs and Drop-in Centres: Open community wellness hubs offering daytime drop-in mental health check-ins, group programs (art, job skills, mindfulness), and connections to primary care referrals in a non-clinical setting.

resources.name: Laing House (Youth Peer Support Centre)
resources.description: Laing House is a youth-driven, non-clinical drop-in centre for people aged 16–29 living with mental illness. It offers daily peer support check-ins and group programs such as art, music, life skills, and mindfulness that build coping and social connection. Staff and peer leaders also help members navigate and connect to primary care and community mental health services, reducing wait-time barriers in a welcoming, stigma-free setting.

resources.name: Phoenix Centre for Youth (PCFY)
resources.description: PCFY is a low-barrier, daytime drop-in hub for youth ages 16–24 that provides supportive mental health check-ins, case management, and a safe, welcoming space. The Centre runs group programs (e.g., arts, employment readiness, life skills, and wellness activities) and connects youth to primary care through in-house health services and referrals to community providers. This non-clinical setting helps young people access timely support and navigate long wait lists for formal care.

resources.name: The North Grove Community Hub
resources.description: The North Grove operates a welcoming, non-clinical community hub with drop-in resource navigation and supportive check-ins through on-site staff and social workers. It offers group programs that foster wellness and life skills—such as community kitchens, gardening, parenting support, and peer groups—and regularly partners with local services to link residents to primary care and mental health supports. This approach reduces barriers to care while building community connection and resilience.

resources.name: Ally Centre of Cape Breton – Drop-in & Wellness Programs
resources.description: The Ally Centre runs a harm reduction–focused, non-judgmental drop-in space offering daily wellness check-ins, outreach nursing, and peer support. It provides group programming (health education, life skills, and peer groups) and actively connects people to primary care and mental health services through referrals and accompaniment. The centre functions as a community wellness hub that lowers access barriers for those facing long wait times or limited provider availability.

obstacles.title: Transportation and Regional Mobility
obstacles.description: Sparse rural transit, limited intercity options, and car dependence isolate communities and constrain job access.

solutions.text: Community Shuttle Cooperative: A locally governed cooperative that runs scheduled shuttles between villages, town centers and employment hubs using community-owned or leased minibuses. Members help plan routes, manage operations, set fares and rotate driving/administrative duties to keep costs low and responsive to local needs.

resources.name: Kings Transit Authority
resources.description: Kings Transit Authority operates scheduled fixed-route buses connecting rural villages and towns across the Annapolis Valley to employment hubs, colleges, health services, and shopping areas. Governed by participating municipalities with community input, it keeps fares low and adjusts routes/timetables based on local needs, functioning much like a community shuttle network that links dispersed communities.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

resources.name: MusGo Rider Co-operative Ltd.
resources.description: MusGo Rider is a member-governed transportation co-operative serving the Eastern Shore of Halifax Regional Municipality, running scheduled shuttle runs and pre-booked services that connect coastal communities with town centers, services, and jobs. As a co-op, local members help set fares, plan routes, and support operations, using community-owned/leased vans and rotating staff/volunteers to keep costs affordable and services responsive.

resources.name: Colchester Transportation Cooperative Limited (CTCL)
resources.description: CTCL is a community transportation co-operative that links rural Colchester County residents with Truro and nearby service and employment centres through scheduled shuttles and coordinated trips. Member representation on its board guides fare policy and service design, and the co-op model enables community-driven route planning and shared operations using minibuses and vans.

solutions.text: Volunteer Driver Network: A coordinated volunteer program where screened community volunteers provide rides for seniors, jobseekers, students and shift workers for trips that public transit doesn't serve (early/late shifts, medical appointments, interviews). Use simple scheduling, mileage reimbursement, and local nonprofit coordination.

resources.name: Wheels of Hope (Transportation Services) – Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Canadian Cancer Society – The Lodge That Gives
resources.description: Wheels of Hope coordinates screened volunteer drivers to provide door-to-door rides for people undergoing cancer treatment across Nova Scotia, covering trips that public transit often cannot, such as early-morning or out-of-town medical appointments. Volunteers use their own vehicles, scheduling is arranged through the program, and mileage/expense supports are provided so service remains affordable and reliable for clients.

resources.name: Volunteer Transportation Program – Annapolis Valley
resources.description: VON’s Volunteer Transportation Program recruits and screens community volunteers to drive clients to essential appointments and errands when other transportation options are limited, especially in rural communities. Rides are scheduled through the local VON office, with volunteers using their own vehicles and receiving mileage reimbursement, directly addressing gaps in public transit for seniors, patients, and others who need to reach work-related or health appointments.

solutions.text: Local Ride‑Share Platform: A community-run digital bulletin or app (low‑bandwidth web version plus phone-in option) that matches drivers and passengers for regular commutes, one‑time long-distance trips or event travel. Operated by a local nonprofit or municipal partnership to prioritize safety and affordability rather than profit.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Cooperative (Eastern Shore and Musquodoboit Valley)
resources.description: MusGo Rider is a nonprofit community transportation co‑operative that matches screened volunteer and community drivers with passengers for regular commutes, medical appointments, shopping, and inter‑community trips along Nova Scotia’s Eastern Shore. Riders can book through a low‑bandwidth website form or by phone, and dispatchers coordinate safe, affordable rides by pairing available drivers with rider requests—effectively operating a community ride‑share system focused on access and safety rather than profit.

resources.name: Kings Point‑to‑Point Transit Ride‑Match Service
resources.description: Kings Point‑to‑Point Transit is a nonprofit service that coordinates ride‑sharing by matching riders with community and volunteer drivers for work commutes, training, medical, and other trips across Kings County and to out‑of‑area destinations when needed. Requests can be placed via a simple online form or by phone, and dispatchers schedule the most suitable driver—providing a safe, affordable, community‑run alternative to commercial ride‑hailing that aligns with a low‑bandwidth ride‑share platform model.
resources.address: 14 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

solutions.text: E‑Bike and Cargo Bike Library: A shared fleet of e‑bikes, cargo e‑bikes and accessories maintained by a community group or library that allows residents to make short trips, last‑mile commutes and errands without a car. Includes training, maintenance workshops and subsidized memberships for low‑income residents.

resources.name: E-Bike Lending Library
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings — Recreation Services
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings operates a no-cost e-bike lending library that allows residents to borrow electric-assist bicycles and accessories for several days at a time. The program provides basic safety orientation and route-planning support so people can try short trips, commutes, and errands without a car, particularly in rural areas with limited transit. By removing upfront cost barriers and including gear like helmets and bike bags, it functions as a community bike library aligned with last-mile mobility goals.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: MODL E-Bike Loan Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg — Recreation & Community Services
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg offers a community e-bike loan program that lets residents borrow pedal-assist bikes and accessories for short-term use. Staff provide an introduction to e-bike operation, charging, and basic maintenance, enabling people to replace short car trips and connect to work or services where transit is sparse. The program supports low-barrier access by offering free loans and outreach to communities across the district.

solutions.text: Demand‑Responsive Microtransit Pilots: Short-term community pilots using small vehicles on-demand (book by app or phone) to connect people to main transit corridors, health centres and job sites. Data from pilots helps adjust routes and schedules to actual local travel patterns before scaling up.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Co-operative Ltd. — On-Demand Community Transit
resources.description: MusGo Rider operates demand-responsive, door-to-door microtransit across the Eastern Shore, letting riders book trips by phone to reach Halifax Transit hubs, health centres, jobs, and education. Using small vehicles and dispatch software, they group trips dynamically and monitor ridership data to refine service zones and hours; pilots in new catchment areas inform route adjustments before scaling.

resources.name: BayRides — On-Demand Community Transit
resources.description: BayRides provides demand-responsive microtransit in the St. Margaret’s Bay area with bookings by phone and online, using small buses/vans to connect residents to Halifax Transit park-and-ride locations, medical appointments, and local employment. The service began as a community pilot and continues to use trip and booking data to adjust operating hours, service boundaries, and vehicle deployment before expanding further.
resources.address: 5229 St Margarets Bay Road, Upper Tantallon, NS B3Z 1E3

solutions.text: Employer‑Community Commuter Partnerships: Local employers, town councils and community groups collaborate to create shared commuter solutions: pooled shuttles to industrial parks, staggered shift coordination, employer-provided transit subsidies, and ride-pooling incentives to reduce single-occupant car trips.

resources.name: Employer Transit Pass Program (EPass)
resources.description: Halifax Transit’s EPass is a corporate transit-pass program where employers partner with the municipality to provide their employees discounted monthly bus and ferry passes via payroll deduction. By lowering the cost barrier and coordinating with large worksites and institutions, EPass directly supports employer-provided transit subsidies and reduces single-occupant vehicle commuting. Many participating employers pair EPass with workplace policies (e.g., reduced parking, flexible or staggered shifts) to reinforce shared commuter solutions.

resources.name: SmartTrip Halifax (Employer Commuter Options Program)
resources.description: SmartTrip is Halifax Regional Municipality’s employer-focused travel demand management program that helps workplaces develop commuter plans, coordinate staggered shifts, and run carpool/vanpool matching and incentive campaigns. The program partners with employers, post-secondary institutions, and community groups to implement ride-pooling, promote transit, and connect staff to benefits like EPass and Emergency Ride Home—reducing single-occupant trips to major job centres. SmartTrip provides resources, data, and engagement support so employers and local councils can collaboratively deliver shared commuter solutions.

resources.name: CarShare Atlantic for Business (Corporate Membership)
resources.description: CarShare Atlantic partners with employers and institutions across Halifax to offer corporate carshare memberships and on-site vehicles so staff can commute by transit, shuttle, or carpool and still access a car for work trips. This arrangement helps employers reduce parking demand and single-occupant commuting by enabling shared commuting to the workplace and shifting necessary daytime travel to a pooled fleet. Employers often combine the corporate plan with transit subsidies and ride-pooling incentives to support a comprehensive shared-commuter strategy.
resources.address: 5553 Bloomfield Street, Suite 209, Halifax, NS B3K 1S7

solutions.text: Mobility Hubs and Improved Park‑and‑Ride: Develop small local mobility hubs (safe waiting areas, bike parking, EV charging, real‑time info boards) at strategic locations where community shuttles, intercity buses and ride‑shares connect. Community builds and maintains shelters and signage to make transfers easier and safer.

resources.name: Bridge Terminal (Mobility Hub)
resources.description: Halifax Transit’s Bridge Terminal is a major mobility hub where numerous urban and suburban routes converge, providing heated indoor waiting areas, accessible shelters, bike racks, and real-time digital departure displays with clear wayfinding signage. The terminal is adjacent to ride-hail/taxi pick-up zones and local active transportation connections, making transfers safer and quicker for regional commuters. By concentrating services and amenities in one place, it functions as a practical mobility hub that eases first/last-mile connections.

resources.name: Sackville Transit Terminal Park & Ride
resources.description: The Sackville Terminal serves as a park-and-ride mobility hub for commuters from Lower Sackville, Beaver Bank, and nearby rural communities, with a large Park & Ride lot, sheltered platforms, bicycle parking, and real-time departure information. Multiple local and express routes connect here, and the site includes designated pick-up/drop-off zones that support carpools and ride-hail services. This layout reduces car dependence by making transfers to Halifax more convenient and safe.
resources.address: 7 Walker Avenue, Lower Sackville, NS B4C 4A1

resources.name: Maritime Bus – Halifax Bus Terminal
resources.description: Maritime Bus’s Halifax Terminal is the province’s primary intercity coach hub, offering indoor waiting, ticketing, posted schedules and online real-time updates, and safe boarding areas. Located steps from Halifax Transit routes and common ride-hail/taxi pickup points, it enables seamless transfers between intercity buses, local transit, and shared rides. This co-location advances the mobility hub concept by linking long-distance travel with first/last-mile options.

resources.name: Lunenburg County Lifestyle Centre (LCLC) Transit Hub
resources.description: The LCLC functions as a community mobility hub in Bridgewater where Bridgewater Transit routes stop at a well-marked, accessible facility that includes sheltered waiting areas, bike racks, and on-site EV charging. Clear signage and a safe campus layout make it an easy transfer point for local buses, Lunenburg County Wheels/community transit, and ride-hail/taxi services. By hosting multiple modes and amenities at one site, it improves regional connectivity and first/last‑mile access for residents.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

solutions.text: Intercommunity Weekend/Seasonal Shuttle: Community-organized weekend or seasonal intercity shuttle service (farm markets, festivals, student travel, regional job fairs) that fills gaps left by infrequent intercity routes and demonstrates demand for more regular service.

resources.name: PC Connect Special Event and Weekend Service
resources.organization: Municipality of Pictou County (PC Connect Rural Transit)
resources.description: PC Connect is the rural transit system for Pictou County that operates intercommunity routes on weekdays and Saturdays, with added or extended runs aligned to seasonal events like farmers’ markets and regional festivals. On weekends and event days, these buses act as community shuttles linking Pictou, New Glasgow, Stellarton, Westville, and Trenton so residents, students, and visitors can get to activities without a car. By filling mobility gaps when intercity options are limited, the service demonstrates demand for more frequent regional transit.

resources.name: Maritime Bus Acadia University Connector
resources.description: Maritime Bus runs semester-timed Friday/Sunday and holiday shuttles during the academic year between Wolfville (Acadia University) and Halifax/Halifax Stanfield International Airport to match peak student travel. This targeted, seasonal schedule supplements the regular intercity network and provides reliable weekend mobility for youth and students without cars. By aggregating demand around weekends and breaks, the connector illustrates the viability of sustained intercommunity service between the Annapolis Valley and Halifax.

solutions.text: Community Transit Fare Support Fund: A locally administered subsidy program funded by municipal contributions, local charities and fundraising to provide reduced-cost transit passes for youth, trainees and low‑income jobseekers to improve access to education and employment.

resources.name: Affordable Access Transit Pass
resources.description: Halifax’s Affordable Access Transit Pass provides a 50% discount on monthly Halifax Transit passes for residents who meet low-income criteria. By lowering the cost of transit for youth, trainees, and jobseekers, the program reduces transportation barriers to education, training, and employment opportunities across the municipality.

resources.name: Student Transit Pass Program
resources.organization: Halifax Regional Municipality (Halifax Transit) in partnership with Halifax Regional Centre for Education (HRCE) and Conseil scolaire acadien provincial (CSAP)
resources.description: This program provides eligible junior and senior high students at participating HRCE and CSAP schools with a Halifax Transit pass valid seven days a week, year-round. By eliminating fares for youth, it supports reliable access to school, co-op placements, part-time work, training, and extracurriculars, directly advancing education and early employment pathways.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Affordable Access Program (Transit Subsidy)
resources.description: Bridgewater’s Affordable Access Program offers reduced-cost Bridgewater Transit passes to residents with low incomes. The municipally administered subsidy lowers transportation costs so youth, trainees, and jobseekers can reliably reach school, training sites, interviews, and workplaces throughout the town and surrounding area.

resources.name: Transportation Support (Bus Tickets) for Program Participants
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides bus tickets and, when appropriate, monthly transit passes to eligible newcomers so they can attend language and employment training, job search workshops, interviews, and work placements. This locally administered fare support, funded through program contracts and community donations, directly reduces transportation costs that can prevent clients from accessing education and employment.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1W1

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works – Transportation Assistance
resources.description: TEAM Work Cooperative, a Nova Scotia Works centre, offers transportation assistance such as Halifax Transit tickets or passes to eligible jobseekers engaged in employment services, training, and work search. By subsidizing transit fares through provincially funded employment programs and community supports, it removes a key barrier to interviews, courses, and starting new jobs.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

solutions.text: Active Transportation Improvements: Community-led projects to build and maintain walking paths, sidewalks, safe crossings and short on‑road bike lanes that connect neighbourhoods to bus stops, schools and job sites. Volunteer build days, adopt‑a‑path programs and local fundraising make small infrastructure upgrades possible.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Active Transportation Program
resources.description: HRM’s Active Transportation Program delivers small-scale walking and cycling connections—sidewalk infill, safe crossings, local bikeways, and multi-use paths—that link neighbourhoods to Halifax Transit stops, schools, and employment areas. The program also partners with community trail associations to plan and build greenway segments, supports volunteer trail work days through grants and materials, and coordinates quick-build safety improvements that can be community-led and locally fundraised.

resources.name: Blue Route
resources.description: The Blue Route is a province-wide on-road cycling network led by Cycling Nova Scotia that develops signed routes, paved-shoulder segments, and short in-town bike lanes to safely connect communities with schools, workplaces, and transit hubs. Working with municipalities and local volunteers, the initiative uses low-cost treatments, wayfinding, and community partnerships to close gaps and create practical everyday cycling connections.
resources.address: 5516 Spring Garden Road, 4th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 1G6

resources.name: Cole Harbour Parks & Trails Association – Community Trails
resources.description: CHPTA is a volunteer-led group that builds, maintains, and upgrades multi-use paths like the Bissett Lake and Salt Marsh trails, creating safe walking and cycling links between neighbourhoods, schools, transit stops, and local businesses in Cole Harbour/Dartmouth. The association hosts volunteer trail work days, runs adopt-a-trail style stewardship, and raises local funds to deliver small infrastructure improvements such as surface upgrades, bridges, signage, and safer road crossings.

resources.name: Ecology Action Centre – Transportation Program
resources.description: EAC’s Transportation Program supports community-led active transportation by organizing pop-up bike lanes, safe crossing demos, school travel planning, and quick-build street improvements that make it easier to walk and bike to bus stops, schools, and job sites. Working with local volunteers and municipalities across Nova Scotia, the program provides technical guidance, materials, and engagement to help communities pilot and fundraise for small infrastructure upgrades.

solutions.text: Community EV Charging and Car‑Share Nodes: Local organizations partner with businesses and municipalities to install shared EV chargers and host a small community car‑share of electric vehicles for short trips, reducing long‑term car ownership needs and making electrified transport more accessible.

resources.name: Communauto Atlantic – Halifax EV Car-Share Network
resources.description: Communauto Atlantic operates a station-based car-share across Halifax Regional Municipality with a growing fleet of electric vehicles and hybrids. Working with the municipality, campuses, and property owners to place vehicles next to Level 2 public chargers, they create neighborhood nodes where residents can book an EV for short trips, lowering the need for personal car ownership and expanding access to electrified transport.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality CarShare Parking Program and Municipal EV Charging
resources.description: HRM designates on‑street and off‑street parking stalls for car‑share vehicles and is installing public EV charging at municipal sites, enabling co‑located charging and shared cars. By formalizing car‑share spaces and supplying power for EVs, the municipality helps create community charging and car‑share nodes that residents can access for quick errands and inter‑neighborhood trips without owning a car.

resources.name: Dalhousie University – Campus EV Charging and Communauto Car‑Share Pods
resources.description: Dalhousie operates Level 2 EV charging on campus and hosts Communauto Atlantic car‑share vehicles in designated parking areas, integrating shared mobility with charging infrastructure. These campus nodes let students, staff, and nearby residents book an electric car for short trips while using shared chargers, reducing the need for long‑term car ownership in central Halifax.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University – EV Charging and Communauto Car‑Share Access
resources.description: Saint Mary’s provides on‑campus EV charging and collaborates with Communauto Atlantic to make car‑share vehicles available on and around campus, linking shared EVs with reliable charging. This hub model offers students and South End residents convenient access to electric cars for errands and appointments, supporting reduced private car dependence.

solutions.text: Local Transit Advocacy and Planning Group: A resident-led working group that collects travel data, runs community consultations, advocates to regional and provincial governments, and pilots low-cost solutions. They act as a bridge between local needs and funding opportunities for larger projects.

resources.name: Transportation & Active Mobility Program
resources.description: Ecology Action Centre’s Transportation & Active Mobility team organizes resident-led engagement on transportation across Nova Scotia, including travel surveys, street audits, and pop-up demonstrations to test low-cost improvements. They convene community consultations, produce evidence-based recommendations, and advocate to municipal and provincial decision-makers, helping local groups translate needs into fundable projects and pilots (e.g., School Streets, Open Streets, and tactical urbanism trials).

resources.name: Blue Route Initiative
resources.description: Cycling Nova Scotia’s Blue Route Initiative partners with residents, municipalities, and the province to plan and phase in a connected, low-cost active transportation network that improves everyday mobility between communities. The team conducts community consultations and route audits, gathers user feedback and count data, and advocates for policy and funding, helping local groups secure grants and pilot signage, wayfinding, and safety enhancements that bridge local needs to larger infrastructure investments.
resources.address: 5516 Spring Garden Road, 4th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 1G6

resources.name: Dalhousie Transportation Collaboratory (DalTRAC)
resources.description: DalTRAC partners with communities and municipalities across Nova Scotia to collect travel behavior data (e.g., the NovaTRAC household travel survey), run public workshops, and evaluate rural and small‑town mobility options. Their analyses and pilot evaluations support resident-led advocacy and help local groups prepare strong evidence-based applications for provincial and federal funding, effectively linking community-identified needs to scalable transportation solutions.

obstacles.title: Digital Connectivity Gaps
obstacles.description: Uneven high-speed internet in rural and coastal areas restricts remote work, learning, and entrepreneurship.

solutions.text: Community Broadband Co-op: Residents, businesses and municipalities form a cooperative to finance, build and operate local high-speed networks (fiber or fixed wireless), access provincial/federal grants as a single applicant, negotiate bulk rates, and keep pricing affordable for students, entrepreneurs and tradespeople.

resources.name: Pictou County Internet (Rural Broadband Project)
resources.organization: Pictou County Municipal Services Corporation (Municipality of Pictou County)
resources.description: Pictou County created a public, community-owned internet service to finance, build, and operate local high-speed connectivity using a mix of fixed wireless and fiber in underserved rural areas. Acting as a single municipal entity, it aggregates demand from residents and businesses to secure provincial/federal funding and negotiate bulk backhaul, then offers cost-recovery retail plans to keep service affordable for students, entrepreneurs, and tradespeople.

resources.name: Valley Community Fibre Network (VCFN)
resources.description: VCFN is an open-access, community-owned fiber backbone created by municipalities and public institutions in the Annapolis Valley to pool resources and lower transport costs for last‑mile providers. By leasing dark fiber to ISPs, schools, and businesses, it enables community and municipal broadband initiatives to extend high-speed service into rural communities, leveraging collective investment and public funding to keep prices competitive.

resources.name: Chebucto Community Net
resources.description: Chebucto Community Net is a member-driven, non-profit ISP that operates community internet services and supports shared-access projects, keeping connectivity affordable for households, students, and small enterprises. It embodies a cooperative model by aggregating community demand, negotiating wholesale access, and reinvesting revenues into local network services and digital inclusion initiatives.
resources.address: Room 125, Chase Building, 6136 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

solutions.text: Public Wi‑Fi and Remote Work Hubs: Convert town halls, libraries, community centres and unused storefronts into 24/7 or extended-hour secure Wi‑Fi zones and low-cost coworking spaces with desks, printers and meeting rooms to support remote work and learning.

resources.name: Halifax Central Library
resources.description: Halifax Central Library offers free, secure Wi‑Fi, open work tables, quiet study pods, public computers, printers, and multiple bookable meeting rooms—creating a de facto coworking environment for students, entrepreneurs, and remote workers. Many Halifax Public Libraries branches broadcast Wi‑Fi that can be accessed from outside the building after hours, expanding connectivity beyond open times and supporting remote work and learning in the community.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: James McConnell Memorial Library
resources.description: As the flagship branch of the Cape Breton Regional Library, the McConnell Library provides free public Wi‑Fi, study tables, public computers, printers, and a bookable community room—functioning as a low-cost workspace for remote workers, learners, and small teams. Wi‑Fi access is available during open hours and can often be reached from outside the building after hours, increasing connectivity for residents in Sydney and surrounding communities.

resources.name: Colchester-East Hants Public Library – Truro Branch
resources.description: The Truro Library provides secure, free Wi‑Fi, study areas, public computers, printers, and bookable meeting rooms—offering an accessible, low-cost coworking environment for remote workers, students, and entrepreneurs. Its location serves as a community connectivity hub, with Wi‑Fi available inside during open hours and typically reachable outside after hours, helping bridge digital gaps in central Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Navigate Startup House
resources.organization: Navigate (a partnership of Cape Breton University and NSCC)
resources.description: Navigate Startup House operates a downtown coworking hub with secure high‑speed Wi‑Fi, hot desks, dedicated desks, meeting rooms, and printing—supporting remote work, startups, and freelancers in Cape Breton. The space offers low-cost memberships and extended-hour access for members, transforming a central urban site into an always‑ready workspace for learning and entrepreneurship.

solutions.text: School and Library Access Programs: Coordinate with school boards and public libraries to extend building access, loan portable hotspots and devices, and run evening/weekend study and maker-space sessions so rural youth can access high-speed connectivity and equipment close to home.

resources.name: Borrow the Internet
resources.description: South Shore Public Libraries’ Borrow the Internet program lends portable Wi‑Fi hotspots so residents, including rural youth, can take high‑speed connectivity home or access it from nearby branches. Libraries in the system also offer evening and weekend hours, public computers, and hands‑on maker and STEAM programs (like 3D printing and coding clubs), giving students study spaces and equipment access outside of school time.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

resources.name: WiFi To Go
resources.description: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library’s WiFi To Go service provides loanable mobile hotspots that patrons can borrow to get online from home or on the go, addressing connectivity gaps across rural communities. The library system also maintains public computers, study spaces, and regular evening/weekend maker and tech programming at branches like New Glasgow and Antigonish, enabling youth to work on homework and creative projects with reliable internet and equipment.
resources.address: 182 Dalhousie Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 4C7

resources.name: WiFi To Go
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library’s WiFi To Go program lends portable Wi‑Fi hotspots to cardholders, helping families and youth in communities across Cape Breton access broadband where home service is limited. Branches like McConnell Library also offer extended hours, computers, and maker‑style workshops (e.g., coding, 3D printing demos), creating evening and weekend opportunities for students to study and explore technology.

resources.name: Borrow the Internet
resources.description: Annapolis Valley Regional Library’s Borrow the Internet initiative allows patrons to check out mobile Wi‑Fi hotspots, ensuring rural households can access high‑speed internet for schoolwork and entrepreneurship. AVRL branches provide evening/weekend access to study areas, public computers, and maker/tech programming, so youth can use connectivity and equipment close to home when schools are closed.

solutions.text: Local ISP Partnership and Demand Aggregation: Aggregate household and business demand across neighbouring communities to create bulk-buy incentives, then partner with regional ISPs or co-ops to secure competitive last-mile builds or service upgrades.

resources.name: Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative (IFNSI)
resources.description: IFNSI aggregates demand from rural and coastal communities by mapping underserved premises and bundling neighboring areas into larger project clusters. It then runs competitive procurements and partners with regional ISPs (e.g., Bell, Seaside, Xplore) to deliver last‑mile fibre, cable, or fixed‑wireless builds and upgrades, leveraging pooled public funding to secure better pricing and faster timelines.
resources.address: 1741 Lower Water Street, Suite 600, Halifax, NS B3J 0J2

resources.name: East Hants Rural High-Speed Internet Project
resources.description: The Municipality of East Hants aggregates resident and business demand through sign‑up lists, speed tests, and surveys across neighboring rural communities to create a strong bulk‑buy case. Using this consolidated demand, the municipality co-invests and partners with ISPs (e.g., Bell Aliant, Xplore) and provincial programs to secure competitive last‑mile fibre and fixed‑wireless builds and service upgrades.

resources.name: Antigonish County Rural Broadband Initiative
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Antigonish
resources.description: Antigonish County conducts pre‑registration campaigns and collects address‑level demand across multiple neighboring communities to bundle them into viable build zones. The County then partners with regional ISPs under provincial initiatives to negotiate last‑mile fibre and fixed‑wireless expansions, using pooled demand and co‑funding to reduce per‑premise costs and accelerate deployment.
resources.address: 285 Beech Hill Road, Antigonish, NS B2G 0B4

resources.name: MODG High-Speed Internet Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Guysborough
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Guysborough aggregates demand across dispersed coastal communities and creates bulk commitments to attract competitive bids. MODG partners with regional ISPs—such as Seaside Communications—through structured agreements and co‑funding to deliver last‑mile fibre builds and service upgrades based on the aggregated, cross‑community demand.

resources.name: Seaside Communications Rural Fibre Builds
resources.description: Seaside Communications partners with Build Nova Scotia and municipalities that aggregate demand across neighboring rural communities to form viable build clusters. The ISP uses these bulk commitments and community sign‑ups to design and deliver last‑mile FTTH and fixed‑wireless upgrades, offering competitive pricing and timelines tied to the aggregated demand.

solutions.text: Community Mesh Network Pilots: Deploy low-cost mesh wireless nodes on public buildings and volunteer rooftops to create resilient neighbourhood networks that provide basic broadband and can be scaled or linked to fiber backhaul.

resources.name: Halifax Waterfront Free Public WiFi
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia operates a free public WiFi network along the Halifax waterfront using multiple outdoor access points mounted on light standards and public buildings. The nodes use wireless mesh backhaul to create continuous coverage and resiliency across the boardwalk and adjacent public spaces, and are linked to fiber where available—functioning as a community mesh pilot that can be extended into nearby neighbourhoods.
resources.address: 1751 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S5

resources.name: Halifax Public Wi‑Fi
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality provides free WiFi in key public spaces (e.g., squares, parks, and civic sites) using clustered outdoor wireless nodes on municipal infrastructure. The system employs meshed access points to span large outdoor areas and ties into municipal fiber where possible, offering a resilient neighbourhood‑scale network that fills connectivity gaps for residents, students, and remote workers.

resources.name: Lunenburg Downtown Free Public WiFi
resources.description: The Town of Lunenburg maintains a free WiFi network covering parts of Old Town and the waterfront by placing outdoor access points on municipal buildings and street fixtures. These low‑cost nodes operate in a wireless mesh to extend coverage block‑to‑block and can be linked to fiber backhaul, providing basic broadband access for residents, visitors, and local entrepreneurs.

resources.name: Downtown Truro Free Public WiFi
resources.description: The Town of Truro provides free WiFi across key downtown corridors with outdoor access points installed on streetlights and civic buildings. The deployment uses a mesh topology to interconnect nodes and bridge around obstacles, creating a resilient neighbourhood network that can be scaled and tied to existing fiber backhaul to support students, remote workers, and small businesses.

solutions.text: Mobile Connectivity Units: Equip a van or bus with satellite or cellular backhaul and Wi‑Fi to serve remote pockets on a scheduled route for classes, telehealth, entrepreneurship clinics and pop-up coworking days.

resources.name: Mobile Library (Bookmobile)
resources.description: South Shore Public Libraries operates a Mobile Library that travels a scheduled route to rural communities, providing free onboard Wi‑Fi, public computers, printing, and digital literacy programming. By bringing a Wi‑Fi‑equipped vehicle with cellular backhaul directly to underserved areas, it enables residents to access online classes, telehealth appointments, job searches, and pop‑up coworking opportunities where fixed broadband is limited.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Mobile Innovation Lab
resources.description: IGNITE’s Mobile Innovation Lab is a technology‑equipped van that brings workshops, entrepreneurship clinics, and hands‑on digital training to rural and small communities across Nova Scotia. Outfitted with portable Wi‑Fi via cellular backhaul, the lab supports pop‑up coworking, maker sessions, and startup office hours at community halls, schools, and libraries, helping residents learn, build ventures, and connect online where reliable broadband is scarce.

resources.name: Mobile Primary Care Clinics
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health deploys Mobile Primary Care Clinics that set up in communities on scheduled dates, using cellular connectivity and onboard Wi‑Fi to run clinical systems, virtual consultations, and patient registration. These units extend access to care and enable telehealth in areas with limited fixed internet, reducing travel barriers and helping residents connect with VirtualCareNS and other digital health services.
resources.address: 90 Lovett Lake Court, Halifax, NS B3S 0H6

solutions.text: Digital Access Microgrants: Community foundations and local businesses provide small grants or subsidies for modem/router purchase, installation, or subsidized monthly service for students, apprentices, startups and low-income households.

resources.name: Connecting Families (Eastlink)
resources.description: Through the Government of Canada’s Connecting Families program, Eastlink provides eligible low‑income families and seniors in Nova Scotia with high‑speed home internet at a significantly reduced monthly rate. The offer subsidizes monthly service and typically includes provider‑supplied modem/router equipment and installation at low or no additional cost, directly addressing affordability barriers to connectivity for households with students and apprentices.

resources.name: Connecting Families (Bell Aliant)
resources.description: Bell Aliant participates in the federal Connecting Families program to offer eligible low‑income families and seniors across Nova Scotia high‑speed internet at a discounted monthly price. This directly subsidizes ongoing service costs and includes provider equipment (e.g., modem/router) and standard installation, helping students, apprentices, and low‑income households stay connected for remote learning and work.

resources.name: Student Emergency Fund – Technology & Connectivity Support
resources.description: NSCC’s Student Emergency Fund provides rapid, small bursaries that students can use for urgent technology and connectivity needs, including paying for home internet service, purchasing or replacing a modem/router, or covering installation fees. By offsetting these costs, the fund helps learners in urban, rural, and coastal communities maintain reliable access for online classes, apprenticeships, and work-integrated learning.

resources.name: Dalhousie Student Bursary and Emergency Funding (Technology & Internet Costs)
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s bursary and emergency funding streams can be used by students with financial need to cover essential connectivity expenses, such as monthly internet bills, data top‑ups, and the purchase of home networking equipment (modems/routers). These microgrants remove cost barriers to reliable internet access required for remote coursework, co‑ops, and research.

solutions.text: Infrastructure Mapping and Community Reporting Platform: Maintain an open, crowd-sourced map of speeds, outages and dead zones to inform investment priorities, support grant applications, and give ISPs and government clear evidence of need.

resources.name: Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative – Coverage Map and Community Feedback
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia maintains a provincial internet coverage map and invites residents to check their civic address and submit feedback about service levels and gaps. This crowdsourced input, combined with provider data and speed-test evidence, helps prioritize underserved areas for investment and supports grant applications by giving ISPs and government clear, mapped evidence of need.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Kings County Internet Speed Test and Mapping (CIRA Partnership)
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings encourages residents and businesses to run the CIRA Internet Performance Test, creating an open map of actual speeds across the county. The aggregated, public results highlight outages, dead zones, and underperforming areas to guide advocacy to ISPs, inform investment priorities, and strengthen applications to provincial and federal broadband funding programs.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: MODL Internet Speed Test and Coverage Mapping
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg runs an ongoing internet speed testing campaign using CIRA’s crowd-sourced platform to map actual service performance across communities. The open data and maps identify connectivity gaps and outages, helping the municipality and partners prioritize projects, engage ISPs, and prepare evidence-based submissions for connectivity grants.

resources.name: Colchester County Internet Speed Test Mapping
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: Colchester County invites residents to complete community internet speed tests that feed into a public map of service quality and dead zones. The resulting crowd-sourced dataset supports the County’s broadband planning, strengthens funding proposals, and provides ISPs and governments with clear, location-based evidence of need.

solutions.text: Tower and Pole Sharing Consortium: Municipalities and landowners form a consortium to coordinate site leases, share costs of towers, poles and backhaul, and streamline approvals so multiple providers can deliver service to underserved areas.

resources.name: Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative (IFI)
resources.description: IFI is the province’s coordinated rural broadband build program that assembles municipalities, landowners, and internet service providers to expand coverage. Build Nova Scotia secures sites and rights-of-way for towers, poles, and fiber backhaul, sets open-access and co-location requirements on publicly funded infrastructure, and streamlines approvals with municipal units and utilities so multiple providers can serve underserved communities.
resources.address: 1741 Lower Water Street, Suite 600, Halifax, NS B3J 0J2

resources.name: Joint Use (Pole Attachment) Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Power’s Joint Use program manages shared access to utility poles and related structures for telecommunications providers and municipalities. It standardizes site leasing, cost-sharing, make-ready work, and permitting so multiple providers can co-locate on the same poles and routes, accelerating deployments and backhaul extensions in rural and coastal areas.
resources.address: 1223 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

solutions.text: Digital Skills and Remote Work Training: Run community-led programs teaching remote-work tools, cybersecurity, online entrepreneurship and digital job-readiness so residents can fully leverage improved connectivity.

resources.name: Tech Help and Digital Literacy Programs
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries runs ongoing Tech Help sessions and digital literacy classes that teach residents how to use devices, email, cloud storage, video conferencing tools (Zoom/Teams), and online safety/cybersecurity basics. Staff provide one-on-one coaching and job-readiness workshops covering online resumes, LinkedIn, and virtual interviews, enabling people to work and learn remotely and participate in the digital economy.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Digital Job Search & Remote Work Workshops
resources.description: As a Nova Scotia Works centre, Job Junction offers free workshops and coaching on digital job search, LinkedIn, virtual interviewing, and using remote-work tools like Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Workspace. They provide computer lab access and staff guidance on cybersecurity and online professionalism, preparing clients for remote employment, freelancing, and digitally enabled careers.
resources.address: 6950 Mumford Road, Suite 0140, Halifax, NS B3L 4W1

resources.name: Startup & Grow Programs (Digital Entrepreneurship Training)
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED’s Startup and Grow programs mentor aspiring and existing entrepreneurs in building and scaling online businesses, with modules on e-commerce platforms, digital marketing, cyber safety for small business, and remote collaboration tools. Through coaching, peer cohorts, and hands-on training delivered in-person and online, CEED equips Nova Scotians to launch and operate ventures from anywhere with improved connectivity.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Tech Help and Cyber Safety Workshops (McConnell Library)
resources.description: The Cape Breton Regional Library delivers Tech Help drop-ins and workshops at branches like McConnell Library that cover computer basics, internet safety/cybersecurity, cloud tools, and video conferencing for remote work and learning. Staff assist patrons with device setup, resumes and online profiles, and navigating digital job applications so rural residents can access remote jobs and training opportunities.

resources.name: Tech Learning & E-Literacy (Margaret Hennigar Public Library)
resources.description: South Shore Public Libraries runs regular technology classes and one-on-one support that teach email, file sharing, cloud apps, and video meeting platforms, alongside online privacy and cybersecurity. They also host employment-focused sessions on digital job search and remote work readiness, enabling residents in rural communities to use improved connectivity for work, learning, and entrepreneurship.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

solutions.text: Device Loan and Repair Network: Establish a community library of laptops, tablets and portable hotspots with an associated volunteer repair cafe so students and entrepreneurs have reliable devices while building local technical capacity.

resources.name: Technology Lending (WiFi Hotspots & Chromebooks)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries lends portable WiFi hotspots and Chromebooks so residents can get online and access a reliable device for work, learning, job searches, and entrepreneurship. The library system also hosts hands-on tech help and periodic community repair events in partnership with local volunteer fixers, aligning with the solution’s combined device-loan and repair support to build local technical capacity.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Repair Café Halifax
resources.description: Repair Café Halifax is a volunteer-run program where community members bring broken laptops, tablets, phones, and small electronics to be diagnosed and repaired for free alongside experienced fixers. By extending device life, sharing skills, and often hosting events at public libraries and community centres, the initiative delivers the repair-café component of the solution and grows local technical capacity to keep students and entrepreneurs reliably connected.

resources.name: Mobile Hotspots and Chromebook Lending
resources.description: Colchester-East Hants Public Library lends mobile WiFi hotspots and Chromebooks, giving residents in rural communities access to high-speed internet and a working device for school, job hunting, telehealth, and small business tasks. Staff also provide digital help sessions, which complements the device lending by building user confidence and ensuring borrowers can effectively use the technology.

resources.name: WiFi-to-Go and Chromebook Lending
resources.description: Western Counties Regional Library offers WiFi-to-Go hotspots and Chromebook lending so people across Digby, Shelburne, and Yarmouth counties can stay connected and productive even where home internet is limited. The program directly addresses digital connectivity gaps for students, job seekers, and entrepreneurs by pairing loanable devices with portable internet access.

solutions.text: Public-Private Last‑Mile Innovation Fund: Create a locally managed fund seeded by municipalities, businesses and community donors to match provincial/federal grants for last-mile builds, small-cell installations and community backhaul projects prioritized by local need.

resources.name: Lunenburg County High-Speed Internet Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg (with neighbouring towns and ISPs) created a locally managed capital program to co-fund last‑mile fibre and fixed‑wireless builds, closing financing gaps that prevented service in rural roads and coastal communities. Municipal dollars are combined with private ISP investment and matched to provincial/federal programs (e.g., Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative and Universal Broadband Fund), enabling small-cell sites, new towers, and backhaul upgrades. Projects are prioritized using local coverage maps and community input to target unserved areas first.

resources.name: Kings County Rural Internet Initiative
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: Kings County operates a municipal broadband capital program that leverages local funds to match provincial and federal grants for last‑mile fibre extensions, fixed‑wireless infill, and community backhaul improvements. The County cost‑shares with private providers and aligns with programs like the Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative and the Universal Broadband Fund to accelerate builds in underserved villages and agricultural areas. Project selection is guided by local need, speed gaps, and readiness of community partners.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Pictou County Rural Broadband Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Pictou
resources.description: Pictou County established a local broadband funding stream that co-invests with internet service providers and matches provincial/federal connectivity programs to reach last‑mile homes and businesses. The initiative supports fibre spurs, small‑cell and tower deployments, and targeted backhaul where gaps persist, with priorities set using county mapping and resident reports. By blending municipal, private, and higher‑order government dollars, the project advances service to rural communities that otherwise would be uneconomic to serve.

resources.name: Guysborough County High-Speed Internet Initiative
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Guysborough
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Guysborough runs an ongoing connectivity program that invests municipal funds alongside private ISP capital to extend last‑mile coverage and improve regional backhaul. The municipality regularly stacks its contributions with provincial and federal grants (e.g., Universal Broadband Fund) to finance new towers, small‑cell sites, and fibre builds prioritized by local service gaps. This public‑private funding model has steadily expanded reliable service to remote coastal communities across Guysborough County.

obstacles.title: Skills Mismatch and Training Pathways
obstacles.description: Programs and credentials don’t always align with employer needs; limited co-ops/apprenticeships slow school-to-work transitions.

solutions.text: Community Employer-Education Roundtables: Regular local roundtables where employers, high schools, community colleges, universities, and training providers map current and emerging skill needs, co-design curricula, and commit to concrete co-op/apprenticeship slots. The community organizes and documents outcomes so training aligns to local demand.

resources.name: Program Advisory Committees (PACs)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College convenes Program Advisory Committees for nearly every program, bringing together local employers, faculty, high schools, and training partners to map current and emerging skill needs. These roundtables co-design and update curricula, identify equipment/technology requirements, and secure co-op and work-integrated learning placements; outcomes are documented and feed directly into program revisions so training aligns to regional labour market demand.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.organization: Construction Association of Nova Scotia (with Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, NSCC, and education partners)
resources.description: BFY is a province-wide partnership that convenes employers, high schools, the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, NSCC, and government to identify construction-sector skill needs and create clear pathways from school to apprenticeship. Through regional planning roundtables, partners align safety and job-readiness training, co-design work experiences, and employers commit to paid summer placements that often transition into apprenticeship; results and student outcomes are tracked to refine training and placement targets annually.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

resources.name: Workforce Development Employer Roundtables
resources.description: Halifax Partnership regularly hosts employer-education roundtables that gather local companies, universities, NSCC, and training providers to surface real-time skill gaps and coordinate responses. These sessions inform curriculum tweaks, help partners stand up targeted micro-credentials, and secure employer commitments for internships, co-ops, and entry-level roles; the Partnership publishes labour market insights and meeting takeaways that education partners use to adjust programming.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Faculty of Computer Science External Advisory Council and Co-op Employer Roundtables
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Faculty of Computer Science convenes an External Advisory Council and recurring employer roundtables that include tech companies, startup leaders, and public-sector employers to map evolving competencies in fields like AI, cybersecurity, and data science. Feedback directly shapes course content and new credentials while employers commit to specific co-op and internship placements through the faculty’s co-op office; meeting outcomes and curriculum changes are documented and reviewed each cycle.

solutions.text: Local Industry Micro‑credential Program: A community-managed stackable micro‑credential initiative developed with local businesses to certify specific, job‑ready skills (short courses, badges) that employers recognize and prioritize for hiring and promotions.

resources.name: NSCC Micro-credentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College offers short, stackable micro-credentials that are co-designed with Nova Scotia employers across sectors such as ICT, oceans, health care, and the skilled trades. Each competency-based course issues a digital badge that employers recognize for hiring and advancement, and many badges stack toward NSCC certificates or diplomas, accelerating school-to-work transitions.

resources.name: Dalhousie Open Learning & Career Development Micro-credentials
resources.organization: Dalhousie University — Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Open Learning & Career Development delivers employer-aligned micro-credentials in areas like data analytics, cybersecurity, project management, and health leadership. Built with input from Nova Scotia industry advisory groups, these short, job-focused courses award portable digital badges and can be stacked into larger professional certificates, giving employers validated, skill-specific signals for recruiting and promotions.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Micro-credentials
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University (Continuing Education / Executive & Professional Development)
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University offers micro-credentials through Continuing Education and Executive & Professional Development that target in-demand skills in business analysis, digital marketing, data, and leadership. Programs are created with employer advisory input from the Halifax region, produce verifiable digital badges, and are designed to be stackable toward advanced certificates, helping local businesses hire for proven, job-ready competencies.

resources.name: Cape Breton University Micro-credentials
resources.description: Cape Breton University provides stackable micro-credentials developed with regional employers to address labour needs in sectors like tourism, energy, and community services. Learners earn digital badges for discrete, job-ready skills that local employers recognize, and many micro-credentials ladder into further study or formal certificate pathways to speed up entry and progression in the workforce.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

solutions.text: Shared Work‑Integrated Learning (WIL) Hub: A municipal or non-profit run hub that brokers co-op, internship and apprenticeship placements among small employers, provides placement coordination, onboarding support, and small-stipend funding to make placements viable for local businesses.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship Program
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s Clean Leadership Summer Internship Program brokers paid summer placements for high school and post-secondary students with municipalities, nonprofits, and small businesses across Nova Scotia. The program centrally recruits and matches students to employer projects, provides onboarding and workplace-readiness training, and administers wage subsidies that reduce costs for small employers—functioning as a shared WIL hub that coordinates logistics and funding.

resources.name: COVE Internship Program
resources.description: COVE’s Internship Program connects Nova Scotia post-secondary students with ocean-technology startups and SMEs, acting as a broker between employers and talent in the province’s blue economy. COVE coordinates recruitment and matching, offers onboarding supports and industry exposure, and leverages partner funding to provide stipends or wage subsidies—making placements viable for smaller firms while accelerating students’ work-integrated learning.

resources.name: NSCC Co-operative Education & Work-Integrated Learning
resources.description: NSCC’s WIL office partners with employers—particularly small and medium-sized enterprises across Nova Scotia—to broker co-op, internship, and applied project placements for college learners. The team supports job scoping, student matching, onboarding and supervision guidance, and helps employers access wage-subsidy programs (e.g., CEI/SWPP), effectively serving as a shared coordination hub that lowers barriers for small businesses to host students.

resources.name: SMU Entrepreneurship Centre – Student Employment Program (RBC Talent Fund)
resources.description: The SMU Entrepreneurship Centre brokers short-term internships and co-op-style placements for students with startups and SMEs across Nova Scotia, providing hands-on coordination from employer matching to onboarding. Through the RBC Talent Fund and related supports, the Centre offsets wages/stipends for small employers and delivers training and mentorship to students—operating as a shared WIL hub that makes placements financially and operationally feasible for local businesses.

resources.name: Acadia Co-operative Education Program
resources.description: Acadia’s Co-op Program brokers paid work terms with employers across Nova Scotia—including many small businesses—by recruiting candidates, facilitating interviews, and coordinating learning objectives and onboarding. The program advises employers on wage-subsidy options (e.g., CEI/SWPP) and provides ongoing support to ensure high-quality placements, operating as a centralized WIL conduit that aligns student skills with real workplace needs.

solutions.text: Sector Partnership Apprenticeship Pools: Community-led consortia in key sectors (e.g., fisheries tech, green construction, digital services) that pool resources to sponsor apprenticeships across multiple employers, ensuring small firms can participate and apprentices gain varied workplace experience.

resources.name: Irving Shipbuilding Centre of Excellence – Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Irving Shipbuilding Centre of Excellence
resources.description: A multi-partner sector consortium led by NSCC and Irving Shipbuilding that recruits cohorts (including underrepresented groups) and delivers pre-apprenticeship training followed by sponsored apprenticeships in welding, metal fabrication, and related trades. The Centre coordinates placements across Irving Shipbuilding and its Nova Scotia supply-chain companies, pooling employers so small and mid-sized firms can host apprentices without heavy administrative burden. Apprentices gain varied on-the-job experience across multiple worksites while training remains aligned to industry needs.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship Program
resources.description: Clean Foundation convenes a province-wide network of municipalities, non-profits, and green-sector businesses to host paid, mentored placements in clean energy, green construction, and environmental services. Acting as a central coordinator (and in some cases employer-of-record), it pools opportunities across many small employers and provides common training and supports, enabling SMEs to participate while interns build stackable, job-aligned skills. This sector partnership model functions as an apprenticeship-style pool in the green economy, accelerating school-to-work transitions and aligning skills with employer demand.

resources.name: COVE Ocean Technology Internship Program
resources.description: COVE convenes a consortium of Nova Scotia ocean- and fisheries-technology firms and coordinates paid work-integrated learning placements across multiple small and mid-sized employers on the Dartmouth waterfront and beyond. As a single gateway, COVE pools employer demand, provides common onboarding and industry mentorship, and organizes multi-employer placement pathways so participants gain varied workplace experience aligned to ocean tech skills needs. This sector partnership approach reduces hiring and supervision barriers for SMEs while building a sustainable talent pipeline for the ocean economy.

solutions.text: Youth Career Mentorship Network: A volunteer-based network linking local professionals and tradespeople with young people for short-term job shadowing, project mentorship, and mock workplace projects — improving career awareness and soft skills while building employer connections.

resources.name: Techsploration Program
resources.description: Techsploration connects female and gender-diverse students in grades 9–12 with women role models working in skilled trades, engineering, and technology across Nova Scotia. Through workplace tours, dedicated job shadowing days, and hands-on team projects guided by volunteer mentors, participants gain career awareness, develop communication and teamwork skills, and build direct connections with potential employers—closely aligning youth learning with real industry needs.
resources.address: 100 Ilsley Avenue, Unit 110, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1L3

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program matches recent graduates and young professionals with established business and community leaders for one-on-one informational interviews and targeted networking introductions. By facilitating warm referrals to employers across sectors—and encouraging job shadowing or project conversations where appropriate—the program builds soft skills, industry awareness, and direct employer connections that speed the transition from school to meaningful work.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
