resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program pairs newcomer youth and early‑career professionals with experienced local mentors in their field for structured, time‑limited mentoring. Mentors provide sector insight, workplace culture coaching, and targeted networking; many pairs arrange workplace visits or short job shadowing, helping mentees build work readiness, soft skills, and employer connections that align with Nova Scotia’s labour market.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Pathways to Education Spryfield
resources.description: Pathways to Education Spryfield supports high school students with academic supports alongside career mentoring and exposure to local workplaces. Staff and volunteer mentors coordinate employer talks, workplace tours, and project‑based activities that mirror real job tasks, helping youth build communication, teamwork, and decision‑making skills while forming relationships with professionals who can open doors to jobs, co‑ops, and apprenticeships.
resources.address: 531 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1X3

solutions.text: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Clinics: Community centers offering regular RPL workshops and assessment days to help young people and newcomers convert informal, volunteer, or on-the-job experience into recognized credentials that local employers accept.

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS offers RPL workshops, portfolio-development sessions, and one-on-one coaching that help immigrants document volunteer, informal, and on-the-job learning against Canadian occupational standards. They coordinate with regulators and employers, host sector-specific clinics, and support clients to prepare for challenge exams or competency assessments so experience is converted into credentials and classifications Nova Scotia employers accept.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
resources.description: NSCC runs ongoing RPL information sessions, portfolio workshops, challenge exams, and skills demonstrations that grant credit for informal and work-based learning. By converting prior experience into course credit and advanced standing recognized by local employers, NSCC shortens training time and speeds transitions into co-ops, apprenticeships, and jobs across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Trade Qualifier and Prior Learning Assessment
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency assesses prior work experience and competencies through the Trade Qualifier route, scheduling assessment days and practical exams so experienced workers and newcomers can challenge certification. Recognized hours and successful assessments lead to provincial trade certification or direct entry into apprenticeship, credentials that employers across Nova Scotia accept.

resources.name: Prior Learning Assessment and Recognition (PLAR)
resources.description: CBU provides PLAR portfolio assessments, challenge exams, and interviews that translate informal, volunteer, and on-the-job learning into academic credit. These structured assessments reduce time-to-credential for young people and working learners, with credits recognized by regional employers through diplomas and degrees tied to local labour-market needs.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

solutions.text: Mobile Training and Maker Labs: A traveling training unit or pop-up maker lab that brings hands-on, short-term training (e.g., welding, coding bootcamps, digital media) to rural communities, lowering barriers to accessing in-demand skills nearby.

resources.name: NSCC Mobile Welding Lab
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College operates a mobile welding lab housed in a trailer outfitted with multiple welding stations, ventilation, safety equipment, and instructional technology. NSCC instructors deliver short, hands-on courses and upskilling modules directly in rural communities and at partner sites, helping learners earn entry-level competencies and safety tickets aligned to employer and apprenticeship needs without having to travel to a campus.

resources.name: Construction Trades Exhibition (CTE) Mobile Trailer
resources.description: The CTE is a traveling, interactive trades trailer that visits schools and communities across Nova Scotia with hands-on stations and simulators (e.g., carpentry, electrical, welding/VR) led by industry-connected facilitators. It provides short, practical experiences that introduce in-demand construction skills and connects youth to apprenticeship pathways and employers, reducing access barriers for rural learners.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: SuperNOVA Mobile Camps and Workshops
resources.description: SuperNOVA at Dalhousie University delivers mobile STEM programs—such as coding, robotics, and digital design—by bringing equipment, instructors, and pop-up labs to rural schools and community venues across Nova Scotia. These short, hands-on workshops build foundational tech skills aligned with emerging workforce needs and help bridge school-to-work pathways by exposing youth to practical, in-demand competencies.

resources.name: Discovery on the Go (Outreach)
resources.description: Discovery Centre’s mobile outreach team brings portable maker and digital media kits—such as robotics, circuits, 3D design, and coding activities—to libraries, schools, and community hubs throughout rural Nova Scotia. These short, facilitated sessions provide hands-on, near-to-home training that strengthens digital literacy and creative tech skills, helping youth explore pathways into technology and creative industries.
resources.address: 1215 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

solutions.text: Employer-Funded Stipend Matching Pool: A community-managed fund that matches small employer contributions to provide stipends for co-op students and apprentices, making placements financially sustainable for businesses and accessible to youth.

resources.name: Co-operative Education Incentive (CEI)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: The Co-operative Education Incentive provides wage subsidies to employers that hire co-op students from Nova Scotia post-secondary institutions. By cost-sharing student wages, the program effectively matches employer contributions to create paid placements, reducing the financial barrier for SMEs and nonprofits. This matching approach expands the number of quality co-op opportunities and aligns student skills with employer needs.

resources.name: Apprenticeship START
resources.description: Apprenticeship START offers financial incentives to employers that hire, retain, and mentor Nova Scotia apprentices, reimbursing a portion of wages at key milestones. This functions as a matching pool that offsets employer payroll costs, enabling more businesses—especially small employers—to offer paid apprenticeship placements. The program strengthens school-to-work transitions by ensuring apprentices can earn while they learn in high-demand trades.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship Program
resources.description: Clean Leadership pools provincial/federal funding and employer contributions to provide paid summer internships with municipalities, nonprofits, and SMEs across Nova Scotia’s clean economy. The program matches a portion of employer-paid wages, creating a centralized fund that makes stipends feasible for host organizations. This model expands accessible, work-integrated learning opportunities for youth while aligning hands-on experience with in-demand sustainability skills.

resources.name: Digital Skills for Youth (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Administered by Digital Nova Scotia, the Digital Skills for Youth program cost-shares intern wages for youth placed with SMEs and nonprofits in technology-enabled roles. Employers contribute to salaries and receive a matching subsidy from the program, effectively creating a pooled fund that supports paid, work-integrated learning. This lowers hiring risk for smaller firms and gives recent graduates practical experience aligned with industry needs.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

solutions.text: Local Career Navigation Centers: One-stop community centers (physical + virtual) that help youth explore local career pathways, apply for co-ops/apprenticeships, access training funds, and connect to employers with real-time openings and micro-credential options.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Centre – TEAM Work Cooperative
resources.description: A Nova Scotia Works employment services centre that provides one-stop, in-person and virtual career navigation for youth and jobseekers in Halifax. Services include career coaching, labour-market information, resume and interview support, employer outreach and a live job board; staff also help clients apply for apprenticeships/co-ops and access training and wage-subsidy funds (e.g., Skills Development, START), and connect them to short, industry-aligned micro-credentials through partners such as NSCC and sector councils.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works – Opportunity Place Resource Association
resources.organization: Opportunity Place Resource Association (Nova Scotia Works)
resources.description: This Nova Scotia Works centre offers a one-stop hub in Dartmouth (with virtual access) where youth and jobseekers explore local career pathways, get personalized career counselling, and connect to employers posting real-time openings. Staff support applications to apprenticeships/co-ops, help clients access training and wage subsidies, and guide them to short courses and micro-credentials aligned with regional employer needs.
resources.address: 33 Ochterloney Street, Suite 210, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 4P5

resources.name: NSCC Career Services
resources.description: NSCC’s campus-based and virtual career centres help students and recent graduates navigate local career pathways, secure co-ops and work-integrated learning placements, and connect with employers through job boards, career fairs, and recruitment events. NSCC also offers industry-aligned micro-credentials and short upskilling programs; Career Services advisors help learners plan training, access funding supports, and transition into in-demand roles across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Halifax Partnership – Connector Program
resources.description: A structured navigation and networking program that introduces students, recent graduates, and newcomers to established ‘Connectors’ in their field to surface real-time opportunities and employer needs. Through curated one-on-one meetings (virtual and in-person), sector insights, and referrals to hiring managers, it accelerates school-to-work transitions and complements co-op/apprenticeship pathways by building direct employer connections in the local labour market.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Community Skills Forecast and Vacancy Board: A publicly accessible local dashboard maintained by community partners showing short-term and long-term employer needs, projected vacancies, and priority skills — used to guide training providers and student choices.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Labour Market Information and Job Board
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration (Nova Scotia Works)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Works maintains a province-wide, publicly accessible job board and labour market information hub that aggregates real-time vacancies, highlights in-demand occupations, and surfaces the top skills employers are seeking across regions. The dashboard and reports are used by community partners and training providers to align programs with short- and long-term employer needs, helping students and job seekers choose pathways that match projected vacancies and priority skills.

resources.name: Halifax Partnership Labour Market Dashboard and Halifax Index
resources.description: Halifax Partnership publishes real-time labour market dashboards and the annual Halifax Index, tracking job postings by occupation and skills, labour force trends, and longer-term demographic and industry forecasts for the Halifax region. These insights are used by employers, post-secondary institutions, and training providers to target priority skills and adjust programs, guiding students and job seekers toward areas of current and projected demand.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: COVE Ocean Jobs Board and Talent Pipeline
resources.description: COVE curates an ocean-sector jobs board and convenes industry, post-secondary, and workforce partners to identify priority technical and transferable skills needed in blue economy roles. By showcasing current vacancies and translating employer needs into training collaborations and work-integrated learning opportunities, COVE helps align education pathways with short-term hiring and longer-term talent forecasts in Nova Scotia’s ocean industries.

solutions.text: School-Enterprise Project Partnerships: Programs where schools partner with local businesses and non-profits on real projects (product design, service delivery, community events) that count for credit and provide tangible experience employers value.

resources.name: NSCC Industry-Partnered Capstone and Applied Research Projects
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College integrates employer-sponsored capstone and applied research projects into diploma and degree programs, where student teams deliver real solutions for local businesses and non-profits. These projects are assessed for academic credit and are scoped with industry partners, aligning curriculum with current labour market needs while giving learners tangible, portfolio-ready experience.

resources.name: Management Without Borders (MWB)
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Management Without Borders is a for-credit, interdisciplinary project course where graduate students collaborate with external organizations to solve real management, policy, and community challenges. Client partners from business, government, and non-profits co-define deliverables, ensuring students apply classroom learning to practical needs that employers value.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Service Learning Program
resources.description: SMU’s Service Learning Program embeds community-partnered projects directly into academic courses, enabling students to complete for-credit work with local non-profits and businesses. Projects range from research and consulting to event delivery and program design, giving students employer-relevant experience while addressing real organizational needs.

resources.name: NSCAD Design Studio Client Projects
resources.description: NSCAD University’s design studio courses regularly engage students in client-based projects for local companies, social enterprises, and arts organizations, with outcomes such as visual identities, product concepts, and campaign assets. These engagements are structured for academic credit, aligning design curriculum with real market briefs and professional workflows.

resources.name: Options and Opportunities (O2) Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: The O2 high school program connects students with local employers and community partners through for-credit community-based learning, co-operative education, and applied projects. By integrating hands-on projects and workplace experiences with curriculum, O2 strengthens school-to-work pathways and ensures skills development aligns with employer needs across trades, services, and emerging sectors.

solutions.text: Youth Entrepreneurship Incubator with Work-Study: A community incubator that supports young entrepreneurs with mentoring, space, and short-term paid work-study placements within startups, combining entrepreneurial skill-building with workplace experience recognized by local industry.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE is an oceantech incubator that provides resident startups with workspace, prototyping facilities, and intensive mentorship from industry experts. COVE also coordinates student co-ops and short-term paid internships with resident companies and partners, giving young people hands-on work-study experience in startups that is recognized by employers while they build entrepreneurial skills inside the incubator.

resources.name: Ready2Launch
resources.description: Ready2Launch is Dal Innovates’ summer accelerator that pays student teams to work full-time on building their ventures while receiving mentorship, structured workshops, and access to university co-working and prototyping resources. The paid work-study model provides practical startup experience and industry-recognized work-integrated learning, directly addressing skills mismatches and easing school-to-work transitions.

resources.name: SMU Entrepreneurship Centre – Work Integrated Learning (WIL) Programs
resources.description: The SMU Entrepreneurship Centre runs Work Integrated Learning programs that place students in paid, short-term roles with startups and small businesses while providing coaching, venture-building supports, and access to the Spark Zone sandbox community and space. By combining mentorship, entrepreneurial training, and real workplace experience inside local startups, the Centre helps students align skills with employer needs and explore launching ventures of their own.

resources.name: Youth Employability Project (YEP)
resources.organization: CEED – Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development
resources.description: CEED’s Youth Employability Project supports youth aged 15–30 with entrepreneurship training, coaching, and wraparound supports, and connects them to paid work placements with local SMEs and startups. Operating out of CEED’s Halifax hub, participants benefit from mentorship and a collaborative startup environment while gaining recognized workplace experience that strengthens entrepreneurial career pathways.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

obstacles.title: Credential Recognition and Experience Barriers
obstacles.description: Newcomers and interprovincial movers face slow recognition of qualifications and ‘no experience, no job’ cycles.

solutions.text: Community Mentorship Network: Create a local mentorship program pairing newcomers and interprovincial movers with experienced Nova Scotia professionals for career coaching, networking, references and guided workplace orientation.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS pairs internationally trained newcomers with experienced Nova Scotia professionals in their field for one-on-one mentoring, industry insights, and targeted networking introductions. Through goal-setting, workplace culture orientation, and facilitated connections that can lead to references and informational interviews, the program helps newcomers overcome credential recognition delays and the ‘no local experience, no job’ barrier.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program links job-ready newcomers, recent graduates, and professionals relocating to Halifax with established local ‘Connectors’ for brief, targeted meetings. These introductions expand participants’ professional networks, generate referrals and informational interviews, and provide practical orientation to the local labour market—addressing credential and experience barriers by opening doors to mentors, references, and employer contacts.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Micro‑Internships and Work‑Shadow Placements: Coordinate short, paid micro‑internships and job‑shadow opportunities with local small businesses and non‑profits to give candidates Canadian work experience and employer references.

resources.name: Workplace Experience Program (WEP)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS coordinates short-term, employer-hosted work placements and job-shadowing for internationally trained newcomers with local small businesses and non-profits across Nova Scotia. These structured placements (often 4–12 weeks) build Canadian work experience, references, and networks, and may include wage subsidies or mentorship to help participants overcome the “no experience, no job” barrier.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s program places youth and recent graduates in 9–15 week paid micro-internships with environmental non-profits, municipalities, and small businesses across Nova Scotia. Interns gain supervised, hands-on Canadian work experience and local employer references while host organizations receive subsidized talent for short projects that often lead to longer-term opportunities.

resources.name: Work Experience and Job Shadow Placements
resources.description: TEAM Work Cooperative (a Nova Scotia Works employment centre) brokers short, time-limited work experiences, paid wage-subsidy trials, and job-shadow opportunities with local SMEs and non-profits. These customized placements provide clients— including newcomers and young jobseekers— with Canadian workplace exposure, references, and a pathway to sustained employment.

solutions.text: Skills Recognition Clinics: Host regular community clinics where volunteers and credential navigators help people translate, document and present foreign or out‑of‑province qualifications and create skills portfolios employers understand.

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ RPL service offers one-on-one advising and small-group clinics where credential navigators help newcomers map foreign education and work experience to Canadian standards. They guide clients to translate and verify documents, document competencies, and build employer-ready skills portfolios, and connect them to licensing and bridging options where required.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Services
resources.description: NSCC’s RPL advisors run portfolio-development workshops and one-on-one clinics to assess and document prior learning gained outside Nova Scotia or Canada. They help individuals translate training and experience into recognized competencies or credits and produce clear skills portfolios that employers and program admissions teams understand.

resources.name: Internationally Educated Nurses (IEN) Pathway
resources.description: NSCN provides registration advisors who act as credential navigators for internationally educated nurses, guiding them through document translation, verification and competency assessment. Through information sessions and individualized support, they help candidates assemble evidence and portfolios that demonstrate skills and meet Nova Scotia’s licensing requirements, easing entry to employment.

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
resources.description: CBU’s RPL office offers portfolio-development clinics and assessments that translate foreign or out-of-province learning and work experience into recognized credit or documented competencies. Advisors help applicants collect, organize and present evidence of skills in Canadian terms so employers and academic programs can readily evaluate their qualifications.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

solutions.text: Employer 'Hire for Skills' Pledge: Ask local employers to commit publicly to skills‑based hiring practices (competency tests, trial tasks, anchored references) and promote participating employers to jobseekers.

resources.name: Employer Support Services (including SkillsMatch, On-the-Job Training, and Practice Interviews)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS works directly with Nova Scotia employers to adopt skills-based recruitment, providing tools to screen for competencies, arrange short work trials/placements, and use anchored references from mentors and supervisors rather than relying solely on foreign credentials or ‘Canadian experience.’ Employers who commit to these practices are promoted to jobseekers through ISANS’ SkillsMatch job board, hiring fairs, and sector-specific events, helping newcomers and interprovincial movers demonstrate ability and secure roles.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1H6

resources.name: Game Changers Youth Retention Employer Pledge
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s Game Changers initiative invites employers to publicly pledge to hire for skills by offering co-ops, internships, and entry-level roles where performance and task-based trials matter more than years of experience. Participating employers are showcased in talent campaigns and networking events, signaling to youth and newcomers that these workplaces practice skills-first hiring and help break the ‘no experience, no job’ cycle.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY partners with construction employers across Nova Scotia who pledge to provide paid summer placements for high school students and assess them on demonstrated competencies and safety practices on the job. Employers are publicly listed and celebrated through CANS channels, creating visible pathways where trial tasks, supervisor evaluations, and anchored references open doors to apprenticeships and full-time roles without over-weighting formal credentials.
resources.address: 260 Brownlow Avenue, Unit 3, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1V9

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.description: NSCC’s Pathways to Shipbuilding, delivered with industry partners like Irving Shipbuilding, prepares diverse cohorts for marine trades and production roles and includes employer commitments to hire graduates based on proven, assessed competencies. The program combines intensive technical training with work-integrated learning and employer-designed task evaluations, and it publicly highlights hiring partners, making skills-first pathways transparent to jobseekers.

solutions.text: Community Bridging Courses and Micro‑Credentials: Partner with regional colleges and training providers to run locally adapted bridging programs and short micro‑credentials that close specific skill gaps for in‑demand jobs.

resources.name: ISANS Bridging Programs for Internationally Trained Professionals
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers sector-specific bridging programs that help internationally trained professionals close targeted skill and experience gaps to meet Nova Scotian employer and licensing expectations. Through short, locally adapted courses, occupation-specific language training, mentoring, and employer connections—often in partnership with colleges and regulatory bodies—participants gain the competencies and Canadian context needed to transition into in-demand jobs.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Internationally Educated Nurses (IEN) Competency Bridging Program
resources.organization: Registered Nurses Professional Development Centre (RNPDC), Nova Scotia Health
resources.description: RNPDC’s IEN Bridging Program provides targeted coursework, simulation labs, and supervised clinical placements to help internationally educated nurses meet the Nova Scotia College of Nursing’s competency and practice requirements. This structured, locally adapted bridge closes specific skill gaps and accelerates credential recognition so participants can enter in-demand nursing roles in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Bethune Building, 11th Floor, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: Skills for Hire Atlantic
resources.description: Skills for Hire Atlantic offers free, cohort-based micro-credential training aligned to in-demand tech roles (e.g., cloud, data, cybersecurity) and developed with employer input. The program provides short, stackable courses, industry-recognized badges, career coaching, and employer connections to help jobseekers—including newcomers and career changers—bridge directly into entry-level roles and overcome the ‘no experience, no job’ barrier.
resources.address: 1657 Barrington Street, Suite 410, Halifax, NS B3J 2A1

resources.name: NSCC Microcredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College delivers short, industry-aligned micro-credentials co-designed with employers across sectors like oceans, ICT, health care support, and skilled trades. These flexible, locally adapted credentials recognize prior learning and target specific skill gaps, enabling learners—including newcomers and interprovincial movers—to quickly validate competencies and bridge into high-demand jobs across the province.

solutions.text: Volunteer Experience Conversion Program: Establish standards and templates for documenting volunteer and community work so it can be presented as verifiable, relevant experience to employers and regulators.

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ RPL service helps newcomers document skills and competencies gained through volunteer and community roles using structured portfolio templates, competency mapping, and assessor validation. The program converts informal and non-formal learning into verifiable evidence that can be shared with employers and licensing bodies, directly addressing credential and experience barriers.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
resources.description: NSCC’s RPL program provides formal processes and templates for learners to compile evidence of learning from volunteer and community service, including validated references, task logs, and competency statements. Assessed outcomes are recorded on official transcripts or credit equivalencies, giving participants a standardized, employer- and regulator-recognized way to present volunteer experience as relevant qualifications.

resources.name: Co-Curricular Record (CCR)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s CCR is an official, institutionally verified document that records students’ volunteer and leadership experiences, time commitments, and mapped competencies using standardized activity descriptions. Staff guide students to translate community involvement into employer-ready language, producing a recognized, verifiable record that employers and professional programs use to assess relevant experience.

resources.name: Volunteer Program
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries manages volunteer roles with clear position descriptions, tracked hours, and reference/confirmation letters that verify duties and skills. These standardized records help volunteers present community service as credible, job-relevant experience to employers and, where applicable, support applications to regulated programs.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Local Credential Translation & Navigation Hub: Set up a one‑stop community hub (online and in‑person) that helps newcomers identify which credentials need formal assessment, which employers accept alternatives, and how to start evaluations.

resources.name: Employment Services (Qualifications Recognition Advising)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides a one-stop hub where employment specialists help newcomers understand which occupations in Nova Scotia are regulated, what credential assessments (e.g., WES) or licensing steps are required, and how to start those evaluations. They also advise on unregulated roles and employers open to alternative proofs of skills, run workshops on foreign qualification recognition, and offer online and in-person appointments to map a step-by-step plan into work.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Atlantic Immigrant Career Loan Fund (AICLF)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: AICLF combines tailored career navigation with micro-loans to help internationally trained newcomers finance and complete required assessments, courses, and exams for credential recognition in Nova Scotia. Advisors work with clients to identify which credentials need formal evaluation, outline licensing pathways, and connect them with employers willing to consider alternative qualifications while full recognition is in progress, offering both online and in-person support.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Services
resources.description: NSCC’s RPL advisors help newcomers translate international education and work experience into Canadian-recognized credit through Prior Learning Assessment and Recognition, and guide when external credential assessments are necessary and how to initiate them. By mapping competencies to program requirements and liaising with employers and industry, the service provides an in-person and online navigation point for pathways that can substitute for formal local experience while building toward full recognition.

solutions.text: Peer‑to‑Peer Job Matching Platform: Develop a community‑run digital platform that matches employers with newcomers based on demonstrated skills and project portfolios rather than only formal credentials.

resources.name: ISANS SkillsMatch Online Recruitment Tool
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: SkillsMatch is a digital talent-matching platform run by ISANS that enables employers to search and connect with immigrant and refugee job seekers in Nova Scotia based on demonstrated skills, experience, and portfolios rather than relying solely on formal credentials. Candidates maintain detailed profiles showcasing competencies, projects, and language abilities, allowing employers to short‑list talent for project work, trials, or roles that emphasize practical capability and fit. This peer‑to‑peer matching reduces the ‘no experience, no job’ barrier by facilitating direct connections and evidence‑based hiring.

resources.name: Connector+ (Halifax Connector Program Digital Platform)
resources.description: Connector+ is a community‑run digital platform from the Halifax Connector Program that matches newcomers and recent graduates with local employers and industry ‘Connectors’ based on skills, career interests, and portfolios. Through in‑app profiles, portfolio links, and targeted introductions, job seekers build networks and secure informational interviews and project opportunities that showcase capability over formal credential checks. This peer‑to‑peer approach helps break experience barriers by creating direct, skill‑focused pathways into the workforce.

resources.name: NSCC Work-Integrated Learning Projects via Riipen
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College uses the Riipen digital platform to match learners—including many newcomers and internationally trained professionals upgrading skills—with Nova Scotia employers for real projects based on portfolios, competencies, and interests. Employers post scoped projects and select students by reviewing showcased work and skills, enabling evidence‑based hiring pipelines that often lead to paid roles. This project‑first, skills‑verified model directly addresses credential recognition barriers by letting candidates prove capability through deliverables.

solutions.text: Small‑Business Apprenticeship Sponsorships: Mobilize local businesses to sponsor apprenticeship and co‑op positions with support from community groups (recruitment help, onboarding mentors, small wage supplements).

resources.name: Co-operative Education Incentive (CEI)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: The Co-operative Education Incentive provides wage subsidies to Nova Scotia employers to hire co-op students from post-secondary institutions for paid, career-related work terms. By lowering hiring costs and requiring meaningful supervision, CEI mobilizes small businesses to sponsor co-op positions while students receive mentorship and real work experience that helps overcome the 'no experience, no job' barrier.

resources.name: NSCC Co-operative Education & Work-Integrated Learning
resources.description: NSCC partners with local employers across Nova Scotia to create co-op and work-integrated learning placements, handling recruitment, candidate matching, and faculty advisor support for onboarding and mentorship. The college also guides small businesses to access wage supports like CEI, helping them sponsor student roles that build job-ready experience and smooth pathways into apprenticeships and full-time work.

resources.name: ISANS Employer Support Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS helps Nova Scotia employers recruit and onboard immigrant talent through pre-screening, job matching, and workplace culture/onboarding support, including mentorship and coaching for supervisors. The organization connects small businesses with wage-subsidy programs and collaborates with sector partners (including the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency) to arrange work placements and apprenticeship entries that address credential recognition and experience gaps.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship Program
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s program places youth and post-secondary students in paid summer internships with host employers across Nova Scotia, many of which are small businesses and community organizations. Clean Foundation recruits candidates, provides job-readiness training and ongoing mentor check-ins, and offers wage subsidies to employers—enabling sponsors to create high-quality work terms that build experience and reduce hiring risk.

solutions.text: Employer‑Newcomer Roundtables: Host regular local roundtables where employers, regulators, training providers and newcomers identify specific recognition barriers and co‑design practical fixes and pilots.

resources.name: ISANS Employer Support Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS convenes regular sector-specific roundtables and information sessions that bring together employers, licensing/regulatory bodies, training providers, and immigrant jobseekers to surface credential-recognition and “Canadian experience” barriers. Through these co-design sessions, partners pilot practical fixes such as bridging courses, occupation-specific language training, mentorship/supervised practice placements, and streamlined hiring practices, which ISANS then supports employers to implement.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1H8

resources.name: Halifax Local Immigration Partnership (HLIP)
resources.description: HLIP is a multi-sector council that regularly hosts employer–newcomer roundtables and working groups focused on improving immigrant employment and credential recognition in Halifax. These sessions convene employers, post-secondary and training providers, regulatory bodies, and immigrants to map barriers and co-develop pilot solutions such as mentorship networks, micro-credential pathways, and employer toolkits, which are then tested and scaled with local partners.

resources.name: Cape Breton Local Immigration Partnership (CBLIP)
resources.description: CBLIP organizes recurring employer roundtables and community forums that bring employers, sector councils, training providers, regulators, and immigrant residents together to address hiring and recognition of international qualifications in Cape Breton. The partnership co-designs and supports pilots—such as trial work placements, recognition-of-prior-learning pathways, and employer training—to reduce ‘no experience, no job’ cycles and improve local credential recognition practices.

solutions.text: Industry‑Specific Language and Workplace Labs: Offer community centre programs focused on sector language, communications, interview simulations and workplace culture for technology, trades, health care and service industries.

resources.name: English for Work
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ English for Work provides occupation-focused language training that helps newcomers build the specific vocabulary, communication skills, and workplace culture knowledge needed in sectors such as technology, skilled trades, health care, and customer service. Classes integrate resume and interview preparation, role‑plays, and simulations to help participants practice real-world scenarios and overcome the ‘no experience, no job’ barrier.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Practice Interview Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: This ISANS program matches job seekers with volunteer interviewers—often hiring managers and HR professionals from technology, trades, health care, and service industries—to conduct sector-specific mock interviews. Participants receive detailed feedback on communication, technical language usage, and Canadian workplace expectations, strengthening their readiness for real interviews and helping bridge credential and experience gaps.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: English in the Workplace (EiWP)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: EiWP delivers customized, on‑site language and communication training tailored to an employer’s sector—such as continuing care and nursing, construction trades, hospitality/service, and IT—so staff can learn the terminology, safety language, customer interactions, and team communications required on the job. The training uses workplace scenarios and lab‑style practice to improve productivity and integration while addressing sector‑specific communication barriers.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Newcomer Entrepreneurship Incubator: Provide locally accessible incubator supports — mentoring, micro‑grants, legal and accounting clinics — enabling credential‑constrained individuals to start businesses and hire locally.

resources.name: ISANS Business Services (Immigrant Entrepreneurship)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides immigrant entrepreneurs with one‑on‑one business counselling, mentorship matching, and training workshops on planning, marketing, and bookkeeping. They also help clients access financing and small loans through partners and host information sessions and clinics with accountants and lawyers to navigate regulations and business setup. These incubator‑style supports directly reduce credential and experience barriers so newcomers can start businesses and create local jobs.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: CEED Microloan Program and Entrepreneurship Incubator
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED offers accessible entrepreneurship training, one‑on‑one coaching, mentorship, and co‑working to early‑stage founders, including newcomers and youth. Its Microloan Program and financing readiness supports help credential‑constrained individuals secure startup capital, while practical workshops and clinics cover bookkeeping, taxes, and registration with local professionals. This combination of mentoring, micro‑financing, and technical clinics functions as a locally accessible incubator that enables new entrepreneurs to launch and hire in their communities.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Dalhousie Business Law Clinic
resources.organization: Schulich School of Law, Dalhousie University
resources.description: The clinic provides free or low‑cost legal information and services to startups, social enterprises, and small businesses on incorporation, contracts, regulatory compliance, and intellectual property, delivered by law students under lawyer supervision. By offering accessible legal clinics, it removes a major barrier for newcomer and first‑time entrepreneurs who may lack recognized credentials or local networks, complementing mentorship and financing supports so they can formalize operations and hire locally.
resources.address: Weldon Law Building, 6061 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4H9

solutions.text: Community Reference Bank: Create a verified repository where civic groups, volunteer supervisors and educators can submit standardized references and competency attestations for local jobseekers.

resources.name: Apprenticeship Training Records and e-Logbook
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency maintains standardized training records and an electronic logbook where journeypersons and supervisors verify an apprentice’s hours and competencies as they are achieved. This creates a province-recognized, centralized repository of verified competency attestations that jobseekers can present to employers, directly addressing experience and credential recognition barriers in the skilled trades.

resources.name: Co-Curricular Record (CCR)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s CCR is an official, verified record of students’ leadership, volunteer, and experiential learning activities, with each entry confirmed by a designated supervisor and mapped to defined competencies. It functions as a standardized, shareable repository of references and competency attestations that employers can trust, helping young jobseekers demonstrate community-validated experience beyond formal credentials.

resources.name: Co-Curricular Record (CCR)
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University offers an official CCR where students document volunteer, leadership, and experiential roles that are verified by campus and community supervisors and tied to core competencies. This provides a centralized, standardized reference bank that students can share with employers to prove community-engaged skills and experience, mitigating the ‘no experience, no job’ barrier.

resources.name: MyCreds Digital Credential Wallet (NSCC)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College issues secure, verifiable digital credentials through the MyCreds platform, enabling learners to store and share official transcripts, diplomas, and micro‑credentials with employers. As an educator-verified repository, it standardizes competency attestations and expedites recognition of qualifications for jobseekers across sectors.

solutions.text: Recognition Awareness and Employer Education Campaign: Run local campaigns and workshops to educate employers about transferrable skills, alternative evidence of competence, and best practices for assessing non‑Canadian experience.

resources.name: Workplace Culture Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Workplace Culture Program delivers employer-focused training, webinars, and customized workshops that help HR teams and managers recognize transferable skills and evaluate international qualifications. The program provides practical tools on alternative evidence of competence (e.g., portfolios, skills assessments, micro-credentials) and best practices for fairly assessing non-Canadian experience, complemented by one-on-one advising and employer resources.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1H7

resources.name: YREACH
resources.description: YREACH provides employer outreach across urban and rural Nova Scotia, offering presentations, lunch-and-learns, and HR coaching on inclusive hiring and retention of newcomers. Sessions guide employers on recognizing transferable skills, using alternative proofs of competence, and navigating credential recognition resources so that international experience is assessed fairly in recruitment.

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Services
resources.description: NSCC’s RPL Services work with industry and community partners to deliver workshops and guidance on assessing competencies through challenge exams, demonstrations, and portfolio assessments. These employer-facing sessions build awareness of transferable skills and provide practical frameworks to recognize international education and work experience as valid evidence of competence.

solutions.text: Municipal Hiring Pilots and Preferential Procurement: Encourage municipal governments and public agencies to pilot hiring people with alternative credentials and to give preference to local contractors who demonstrate inclusive hiring and training.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Newcomer Internship Program
resources.description: The Halifax Regional Municipality offers a paid internship program for internationally trained professionals and recent newcomers to gain Canadian municipal work experience. The program uses skills-based screening and recognizes alternative credentials and micro-credentials to place candidates across municipal departments, directly addressing the 'no Canadian experience' barrier. By piloting inclusive municipal hiring pathways, HRM models how public agencies can validate alternative credentials and open doors to sustained employment.

resources.name: Cogswell District Redevelopment – Community Benefits and Social Procurement Requirements
resources.description: For the Cogswell District Redevelopment, HRM embedded community benefits and social procurement requirements into construction tenders to drive inclusive hiring and training. Bidders receive evaluation points for workforce development plans—such as hiring apprentices and workers from underrepresented groups (including Mi'kmaw, African Nova Scotian, and newcomers), recognizing alternative training pathways, and delivering on-the-job training. This preferential procurement approach channels municipal spending to contractors that demonstrate inclusive hiring and training practices, operationalizing the solution.

resources.name: Procurement Assistance Nova Scotia (PANS) and Supplier Diversity
resources.description: PANS helps local and diverse suppliers—including newcomer- and youth-led firms—participate in provincial procurement and supports departments to include supplier diversity and community benefits in solicitations. Provincial procurement tools allow weighting for social value and workforce development commitments, giving preference to vendors with inclusive hiring, apprenticeships, and training practices. This advances preferential public procurement and creates pathways for candidates with alternative credentials to gain experience through contractors on government projects.

resources.name: Immigrant Internship Program (Public Sector Placements)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Immigrant Internship Program partners with the Province of Nova Scotia and municipal/public sector employers to place internationally educated professionals in paid internships. Candidates are assessed on skills and foreign credentials, gaining Canadian work experience within government settings to overcome 'no experience, no job' barriers. As a public-sector hiring pilot, it validates alternative credentials and builds pathways to longer-term employment in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

obstacles.title: Barriers to Entrepreneurship and Small Business Growth
obstacles.description: Access to capital, mentorship, affordable space, and streamlined permitting remains inconsistent, especially outside HRM.

solutions.text: Community Microloan Fund: A locally governed revolving microloan fund seeded by residents, businesses, and philanthropic groups to provide small, low-interest loans and loan guarantees to entrepreneurs outside HRM who lack access to traditional capital.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Small Business Loan Guarantee Program (delivered by East Coast Credit Union)
resources.description: East Coast Credit Union, a member-owned financial cooperative, delivers the Nova Scotia Small Business Loan Guarantee Program across rural communities. It provides small, low-interest business loans with a provincial guarantee to entrepreneurs who may be declined by traditional lenders; funds are sourced from local member deposits and revolve back into the community as loans are repaid. Local governance and branch presence outside HRM make it accessible to entrepreneurs in Antigonish and surrounding counties.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Small Business Loan Guarantee Program (delivered by Valley Credit Union)
resources.description: Valley Credit Union is a community-governed financial cooperative serving the Annapolis Valley and Western Nova Scotia. Through the Nova Scotia Small Business Loan Guarantee Program and its own small business lending, it offers small, affordable loans and guarantees to startups and growing firms that may lack collateral, with capital mobilized from local members and businesses and recycled as loans are repaid. This directly addresses rural access-to-capital gaps outside HRM.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Small Business Loan Guarantee Program (delivered by Community Credit Union of Cumberland Colchester)
resources.organization: Community Credit Union of Cumberland Colchester
resources.description: Community Credit Union of Cumberland Colchester participates in the Nova Scotia Small Business Loan Guarantee Program to expand financing access for entrepreneurs in northern Nova Scotia. As a locally owned credit union, it pools deposits from residents and businesses to provide small, low-interest loans that are provincially guaranteed, creating a revolving source of community capital. Its Amherst branch serves entrepreneurs outside HRM with relationship-based lending and mentorship referrals.

solutions.text: Volunteer Mentor Circles: Neighborhood- and sector-based mentor groups of retired business owners, tradespeople, and professionals who meet regularly (in-person or online) to advise new entrepreneurs on planning, financing, and operations.

resources.name: ISANS Business Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS) matches newcomer entrepreneurs with volunteer mentors—often retired or semi-retired business owners, tradespeople, and professionals—in the same sector. Pairs and small mentor circles meet regularly (in person and online) to work through business planning, financing options, permitting, and day-to-day operations, giving practical, context-specific advice and networks across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1H4

resources.name: PeerSpark
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: PeerSpark is a cohort-based program that forms facilitated peer mentoring circles for women-identifying entrepreneurs, drawing on a province-wide network of volunteer advisors and alumni—including retired executives and seasoned professionals. Groups meet regularly online and at the Centre’s hub to work through business planning, access to capital, sales operations, and growth management, providing ongoing, sector-aware guidance and accountability.
resources.address: 166 Bedford Highway, 3rd Floor McCain Centre, Halifax, NS B3M 2J6

resources.name: Volta Office Hours and Mentorship
resources.description: Volta convenes volunteer mentors—experienced founders, retired industry leaders, and functional experts—for recurring Office Hours and group clinics that advise early-stage entrepreneurs. These sessions, delivered in person at Volta and virtually across Nova Scotia, focus on business planning, fundraising and financing, sales pipelines, and operational best practices, often organizing conversations by sector and stage to create effective mentor circles.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Mentorship Program
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic coordinates sector-based mentor circles across rural Western and Northern Nova Scotia, engaging volunteer mentors—including retired fishery operators, trades professionals, and former founders—to guide local startups and small businesses. Through recurring roundtables and one-on-one sessions hosted at its hubs and online, participants receive hands-on support with business plans, financing pathways, permitting, and operational problem-solving.

resources.name: CEED Mentoring Program
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED’s mentoring program connects new and growing entrepreneurs with a volunteer network of advisors—including retired business owners and professionals—through facilitated small-group sessions and one-on-one mentoring. Meetings occur regularly at CEED’s Halifax hub and online, with mentors providing practical guidance on business planning, financing options, cash flow, marketing, and operations, often organizing circles by industry or business stage.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Shared Workspaces and Maker Hubs: Transform underused community buildings into affordable coworking and maker spaces run as cooperatives or nonprofits, offering desks, workshops, meeting rooms and subsidized rates for startups.

resources.name: Volta Coworking and Startup Hub
resources.description: Volta is a nonprofit innovation hub that provides affordable coworking desks, offices, meeting rooms, and event space for startups and founders. It implements the solution by converting large floors within the Maritime Centre into shared workspaces run by a nonprofit, offering subsidized resident memberships, mentorship, and programming to reduce early-stage costs and barriers.

resources.name: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship) Shared Offices, Labs, and Workshops
resources.description: COVE is a nonprofit ocean-tech hub that transforms a former coast guard site into shared coworking offices, prototyping labs, and marine workshops for startups and SMEs. It advances the solution by providing subsidized or program-supported access to specialized facilities, meeting rooms, and a collaborative community, lowering costs for entrepreneurs and enabling hands-on making and testing.

resources.name: CEED Co-Working (Centre for Entrepreneurship Education & Development)
resources.description: CEED, a nonprofit organization, operates an affordable coworking space with hot desks, dedicated desks, meeting rooms, and training facilities for aspiring and early-stage entrepreneurs. It implements the solution by offering subsidized memberships alongside mentorship and business development programs, reducing space costs and providing community support for startups across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Navigate Startup House
resources.organization: Navigate Startup (a partnership supported by Cape Breton University and Nova Scotia Community College)
resources.description: Navigate Startup House is a nonprofit coworking hub that provides low-cost desks, meeting rooms, and community programming for entrepreneurs in Cape Breton. By repurposing a community building into a shared workspace and connecting founders to mentorship and resources, it delivers the cooperative-style support and affordable space central to the solution, especially outside HRM.

resources.name: Halifax Central Library Creative Labs and Bookable Workspaces
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries operates free and low-cost maker and creative labs (including 3D printing, audio/video studios) and provides bookable meeting rooms and open work areas for the public. As a publicly funded nonprofit, it implements the solution by offering accessible shared work and maker spaces, enabling startups and creators to prototype, meet, and work without prohibitive costs.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Pop-up Retail & Kitchen Program: A community-run calendar and space-rotation program that lets entrepreneurs test products and food concepts in vacant storefronts, festivals, or community kitchens with minimal upfront costs.

resources.name: Salt Yard Pop-Up Vendor Program
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia curates seasonal pop-up retail kiosks along the Halifax waterfront, providing short-term, low-cost vending spaces with shared amenities like power and foot-traffic marketing. The rotating vendor model and centrally managed calendar allow new and small businesses to test products, refine offerings, and reach large festival and tourism audiences without long leases.
resources.address: 1751 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S5

resources.name: Halifax Seaport Farmers’ Market Vendor Program
resources.description: The Seaport Market offers flexible, short-term vendor tables and day-stalls that let food and craft entrepreneurs trial products and build customers with minimal upfront costs. Market management rotates vendors through a weekly calendar and special events, functioning as a real-world testbed for new brands while providing guidance on market readiness and food safety requirements.

resources.name: Alderney Landing Commercial Kitchen and Farmers’ Market
resources.description: Alderney Landing operates an inspected, bookable commercial kitchen and a waterfront farmers’ market that offers low-cost, short-term vendor spaces. Entrepreneurs can produce small batches in the community kitchen and immediately test products at market pop-ups and festivals on-site, with staff support for scheduling and basic permitting guidance.

resources.name: Wolfville Farmers’ Market Kitchen and Pop-Up Vendor Program
resources.description: The Wolfville Farmers’ Market provides rotating, low-commitment vendor stalls and a rentable commercial kitchen that allows startups to develop recipes and test demand without a long-term lease. The market’s community-run calendar, regular crowds, and vendor support help entrepreneurs pilot food concepts, refine packaging and pricing, and scale into permanent operations.

resources.name: Truro Farmers’ Market Pop-Up Vendor Program
resources.description: The Truro Farmers’ Market offers short-term, affordable tables and seasonal pop-up opportunities for new food and retail entrepreneurs to trial products and gather customer feedback. Its rotating vendor schedule and community events provide an accessible first step into commerce, reducing risk and space costs for small businesses outside HRM.

solutions.text: Permit Navigation Volunteer Corps: A trained volunteer network (including retired municipal staff and planners) offering free one-on-one help, checklists and application review to speed up permitting for small businesses in rural towns.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Business Navigators
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia – Office of Regulatory Affairs and Service Effectiveness
resources.description: A free, province-wide service that provides one-on-one guidance to entrepreneurs on permits, licenses, and regulatory requirements at the municipal, provincial, and federal levels. Navigators offer tailored checklists, connect applicants with the correct officials, and review applications for completeness to reduce back-and-forth—speeding up permitting for small businesses, including those in rural communities.

resources.name: Cape Breton Partnership – Business Services
resources.description: Business advisors provide hands-on, no-cost support to startups and small firms across Cape Breton and Victoria Counties, including help understanding zoning, development, and licensing requirements in local municipalities. The team coordinates pre-application discussions, shares step-by-step checklists, and reviews submission packages to reduce delays and streamline permitting for rural businesses.

resources.name: Acadia Entrepreneurship Centre – Business Advisory Services
resources.description: AEC advisors work one-on-one with entrepreneurs and small businesses across the Annapolis Valley and rural Nova Scotia to map regulatory steps and prepare permitting and licensing applications. They provide practical checklists, connect clients with municipal planning staff, and review documents to ensure completeness—helping reduce processing time for permits in smaller towns.

resources.name: Planning & Development – Pre-Application and Permitting Support
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: Planning staff offer free pre-application consultations, permit checklists, and step-by-step guidance for development, building, and sign permits. They review submissions for completeness and coordinate with inspection services, helping small businesses in rural communities navigate municipal permitting more efficiently and avoid delays.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

solutions.text: Local Investment Clubs and Angel Networks: Organize community investors into formal clubs that pool capital to make small equity investments in local startups, with mentorship and due-diligence support from experienced volunteers.

resources.name: Community Economic Development Investment Funds (CEDIF) Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Finance and Treasury Board
resources.description: The Province of Nova Scotia’s CEDIF Program enables communities to organize local investors into formal investment co-operatives or funds that pool small contributions and make equity or patient-capital investments in Nova Scotia businesses. The model functions like a structured local investment club, with volunteer boards providing governance and due diligence and many funds pairing capital with mentorship from experienced businesspeople, expanding access to early-stage financing and guidance across rural and urban communities.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: New Dawn raises capital from local residents through its provincially sanctioned CEDIF offerings and reinvests those pooled funds into startups and growing small businesses across Cape Breton. Guided by a volunteer investment committee and supported by the broader New Dawn enterprise network, the fund undertakes due diligence and pairs entrepreneurs with mentorship and community connections, directly addressing access-to-capital and advisory gaps outside HRM.

solutions.text: Community Land Trust for Commercial Space: Create a community land trust that buys or leases commercial properties and sublets them at below-market rates to local small businesses, ensuring long-term affordable space outside HRM.

resources.name: New Dawn Centre for Social Innovation
resources.description: New Dawn Enterprises owns and manages this multi-tenant commercial campus, redeveloping community buildings to provide long-term, affordable office and studio space for local small businesses, nonprofits, and social enterprises in downtown Sydney. By holding the property in community hands and subletting at mission-driven, below-market rates with flexible terms, it stabilizes costs for entrepreneurs and preserves accessible commercial space outside HRM.

resources.name: Eltuek Arts Centre
resources.description: Operated by New Dawn, Eltuek Arts Centre redeveloped a landmark property into a community-owned facility that leases studios, offices, and shared production spaces to artists, creative micro-enterprises, and cultural nonprofits. The centre sublets these commercial workspaces at accessible, community-based rates and with stable tenancy, ensuring long-term affordable space for creative businesses in Cape Breton, outside HRM.

resources.name: Mahone Bay Centre – Community & Business Spaces
resources.description: The Mahone Bay Centre Society owns a former school that has been converted into a community hub offering affordable offices, studios, and classrooms to local artisans, wellness practitioners, nonprofits, and small businesses. By keeping the property in community ownership and leasing commercial spaces at community-rate, often below-market rents, it provides stable, long-term space for local enterprises in Lunenburg County.
resources.address: 45 School Street, Mahone Bay, NS B0J 2E0

resources.name: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design – Studios and Maker Spaces
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: This nonprofit owns and operates a downtown facility that provides studio rentals, shared maker spaces, and retail opportunities to local artisans and craft-based small businesses. Through subsidized, below-market studio leases and shared equipment, it lowers overhead and secures long-term, affordable commercial space for entrepreneurs in Sydney, outside HRM.

solutions.text: One-Stop Mobile Business Support Unit: A traveling team (staffed by volunteers and small-business advisors) that visits rural communities on a schedule to provide startup clinics, permit help, funding advice and mentorship sign-ups.

resources.name: ISANS Business Services – Rural Pop-up Advising Clinics
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Business Services team regularly travels to rural communities across Nova Scotia to host pop-up startup clinics and one-on-one advising sessions for immigrant and newcomer entrepreneurs. These clinics provide practical help with registering a business and navigating local permits and licensing, guidance on funding options (e.g., CBDCs, Futurpreneur, BDC), and on-the-spot enrollment into ISANS training and mentorship programs—delivering a one-stop, mobile support model outside HRM.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Volta on the Road
resources.description: Volta’s team and mentor network run traveling “on the road” pop-up clinics and office hours in communities across Nova Scotia, bringing startup advising directly to rural founders. These visits bundle startup diagnostics, mentorship sign-ups, and practical guidance on permits, incorporation, and funding pathways in collaboration with local partners—functioning as a one-stop mobile support unit for entrepreneurs outside Halifax.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, 7th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

solutions.text: Procurement & Buy-Local Campaigns: Community-driven campaigns and local procurement pledges encouraging residents, institutions and businesses to buy from local startups and social enterprises, increasing early revenues and investment appeal.

resources.name: Downtown Dartmouth Dollars
resources.description: Downtown Dartmouth Dollars is a local gift-card/currency program and ongoing shop-local campaign that channels spending to independent businesses in Downtown Dartmouth. The program is promoted to residents and employers as a way to purchase goods and services from local startups and social enterprises, often used by companies for staff rewards and event procurement, thereby increasing early revenues and visibility for new ventures.

resources.name: Downtown Truro Dollars
resources.description: Downtown Truro Dollars is a buy-local gift certificate and marketing campaign that encourages residents, visitors, and local institutions to purchase from participating small businesses in Truro’s core. By steering consumer and corporate purchases to local retailers, makers, and startups, the program accelerates early revenues and strengthens demand for emerging enterprises.

resources.name: Lunenburg Dollars
resources.description: Lunenburg Dollars is a community currency and shop-local initiative accepted by a network of independent businesses in and around Lunenburg. The program promotes resident and visitor spending with local producers, artisans, and service startups, and is also used by employers for gifting and procurement, keeping purchasing power within the local economy and bolstering early-stage revenues.
resources.address: 11 Blockhouse Hill Road, Lunenburg, NS B0J 2C0

resources.name: Social Procurement Program
resources.description: HRM’s Social Procurement Program embeds community benefits and inclusive purchasing practices in municipal contracts, creating opportunities for local small businesses, diverse suppliers, and social enterprises to sell to the municipality. Through supplier outreach and evaluation criteria that value local impact, the program directs institutional procurement toward Nova Scotia-based vendors, generating revenue streams that help startups grow and invest.

resources.name: Love Local Cape Breton
resources.organization: Cape Breton Regional Chamber of Commerce
resources.description: Love Local Cape Breton is an ongoing awareness and purchasing campaign that spotlights Cape Breton–based businesses and encourages residents and organizations to choose local for everyday purchases, gifting, and corporate procurement. Through promotional drives, directories, and partnerships with employers, the campaign channels spending to startups and social enterprises across the island, boosting early revenues and market confidence.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

solutions.text: Peer Equipment & Tool Libraries: Community-run libraries where entrepreneurs can borrow specialized equipment (kitchen tools, fabrication machines, audiovisual gear) reducing capital costs for startups and makers.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: A volunteer-run lending library that provides access to hundreds of hand and power tools for woodworking, home renovation, gardening, and light fabrication. By letting entrepreneurs, tradespeople, and makers borrow specialized tools instead of purchasing them, it reduces startup and operating costs and supports small business and community projects.

resources.name: AFCOOP Equipment Rentals
resources.description: AFCOOP maintains a community equipment library of professional film and media gear—cameras, lenses, lighting, sound, and grip—available to members at subsidized rates. This shared inventory allows filmmakers and creative entrepreneurs to produce commercial and artistic projects without the high upfront cost of owning audiovisual equipment.

resources.name: CFAT Equipment & Facilities Access
resources.description: CFAT offers a lending library of media arts equipment—including video and audio gear—and access to edit suites and production facilities for members. Sliding-scale rentals and training lower capital barriers for artists and media-based entrepreneurs to prototype, produce, and distribute work.

resources.name: Library of Things
resources.description: A system-wide collection of non-traditional items—such as creative equipment, small tools, and tech kits—available for cardholders to borrow across the region. By providing access to gear like sewing and crafting tools and select audiovisual/tech items, it enables makers and small ventures to test ideas and deliver services without purchasing equipment.

solutions.text: Business Plan & Pitch Nights with Seed Grants: Regular community pitch events where finalists receive small seed grants or in-kind support (space, legal help, mentorship) funded by local sponsors and voters, building local ownership of startups.

resources.name: Volta Cohort Pitch Competition
resources.description: Volta Cohort is a recurring pitch event where early-stage founders compete for seed funding and in-kind resources. Winners receive seed investments along with mentorship, workspace access, and professional services from Volta’s partner network, directly addressing gaps in early capital, coaching, and affordable space for Nova Scotia startups.

resources.name: Starting Point Pitch Competition
resources.description: Starting Point is SMUEC’s annual entrepreneurship conference featuring a live pitch competition where student and early-stage entrepreneurs present their business plans to judges and audiences. Cash awards and in-kind supports (legal, accounting, and ongoing mentorship from local sponsors) help winners validate ideas and launch, lowering barriers to capital and guidance for young founders across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: BioInnovation Challenge
resources.organization: BioNova (Nova Scotia Life Sciences Industry Association)
resources.description: The BioInnovation Challenge is an annual life sciences pitch competition that provides early-stage biotech and medtech ventures with seed funding opportunities and in-kind support. Finalists receive coaching and then pitch for cash prizes plus services such as legal/IP advisory and mentorship from industry sponsors, accelerating commercialization for Nova Scotia startups in this sector.

resources.name: Ocean Startup Challenge
resources.description: The Ocean Startup Challenge is a pitch-based grant program run from Nova Scotia that provides non-dilutive seed funding to early-stage ocean technology companies. Teams participate in public pitch events and receive mentorship, training, and in-kind services from industry partners and sponsors, building local support networks and reducing barriers to capital and expert guidance for coastal entrepreneurs.

solutions.text: Municipal Partnership Advocacy Groups: Local business associations and community groups collaborate to lobby municipal councils for streamlined permitting templates, faster approvals, and common-sense zoning updates in outlying areas.

resources.name: Policy & Advocacy
resources.description: The Halifax Chamber of Commerce’s Policy & Advocacy work convenes local businesses and community groups to deliver unified recommendations to Halifax Regional Council to reduce red tape.
