Through policy submissions, roundtables with municipal planning/permitting staff, and public campaigns, they press for standardized permit templates, digitized and faster approvals, and modernized land-use bylaws that make it easier to start and expand businesses.

resources.name: Business Advocacy and Municipal Engagement
resources.description: The Cape Breton Partnership brings together employers, sector groups, and community organizations to work directly with Cape Breton Regional Municipality and rural municipal units on improving the development environment. By coordinating business roundtables with planning offices, submitting joint letters and research to councils, and helping municipalities adopt clearer permit checklists and consistent zoning interpretations, it advocates for faster, simpler approvals and common-sense zoning updates across outlying Cape Breton communities.

resources.name: Advocacy & Municipal Liaison
resources.description: Downtown Truro Partnership represents member businesses in regular meetings with the Town of Truro and the Municipality of Colchester to remove barriers to opening and growing downtown enterprises. It advocates for streamlined sign and patio permits, standardized application templates, quicker approvals, and practical zoning and parking updates, channeling coordinated feedback from merchants to council to make local regulations more small-business friendly outside HRM.

solutions.text: University–Community Incubator Partnerships: Partner post-secondary institutions with rural communities to offer satellite incubators, student consulting teams, and shared research resources that support local entrepreneurs with expertise and facilities.

resources.name: Acadia Entrepreneurship Centre – Rural Innovation Centre
resources.description: The Rural Innovation Centre provides incubator-style workspace, coaching, and advisory services to entrepreneurs across the Annapolis Valley. It mobilizes Acadia University students and faculty through student consulting teams, market research, and business planning support for local ventures. Working with municipalities and the Valley REN, it functions as a satellite university–community hub that connects rural founders to campus expertise, mentorship, and shared resources.
resources.address: Patterson Hall, 24 University Avenue, Wolfville, NS B4P 2R6

resources.name: Cultiv8 Sandbox (Dalhousie Faculty of Agriculture)
resources.description: Cultiv8 is a Nova Scotia Sandbox at Dalhousie’s Agricultural Campus that helps agri-food and rural innovators develop, test, and commercialize ideas. It offers entrepreneurship coaching, workshops, and access to makerspace/prototyping and campus research assets such as labs and greenhouses. Student teams from the Faculty of Agriculture work with local producers and startups on applied projects and consulting, bringing university expertise and facilities to rural businesses.
resources.address: Dalhousie Agricultural Campus, 62 Cumming Drive, Truro, NS B2N 4H5

resources.name: Navigate Startup House
resources.organization: Cape Breton University and Nova Scotia Community College (Navigate)
resources.description: Navigate is a partnership of Cape Breton University and Nova Scotia Community College that operates co-working and incubation spaces supporting startups across Cape Breton. It connects entrepreneurs with student talent and faculty mentors, hosts consulting projects and accelerator programming, and provides access to shared resources and expert advisors. By colocating with community partners and leveraging campus assets, it acts as a university–community incubator bringing space, mentorship, and research linkages to rural founders.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – New Glasgow
resources.description: IGNITE is a rural innovation hub that partners with NSCC campuses and Nova Scotia universities to deliver incubation, mentorship, and applied research connections for local entrepreneurs. The New Glasgow site provides affordable space, programming, and access to student consulting teams and faculty expertise, serving founders from Pictou County and surrounding communities. Through these post-secondary partnerships, it functions as a satellite incubator linking rural ventures to talent, facilities, and commercialization supports.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

solutions.text: Community Mentorship App/Portal: A simple local digital platform that matches entrepreneurs with volunteer mentors, lists funding opportunities, permits checklists and available community spaces, with localized search for areas outside HRM.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Business Navigators
resources.description: A free provincial service that provides entrepreneurs with one-on-one guidance and an online portal to understand permits, licenses, and regulatory requirements across Nova Scotia. They publish step-by-step checklists and link to municipal permitting systems, helping founders streamline approvals outside HRM as well. The team also connects entrepreneurs to local supports and funding programs, complementing mentorship platforms with regulatory navigation.

resources.name: Volta
resources.description: Volta operates an online mentor and advisor network that matches startups with volunteer experts, along with a resource hub listing funding opportunities (e.g., Volta Cohort, partner grants) and programs. The platform integrates with bookable community workspaces and meeting rooms at Volta’s hub, offering both digital matching and affordable physical space. This mirrors a community mentorship portal by centralizing mentorship, funding, and space access for entrepreneurs across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic
resources.description: IGNITE runs rural innovation hubs and a digital community platform that connects entrepreneurs outside HRM with volunteer mentors, workshops, and partner supports. Their site aggregates funding opportunities, business resources, and events for southwestern and northern Nova Scotia, and they provide affordable coworking desks, labs, and meeting rooms that can be booked online. This localized, rural-first model implements the mentorship portal concept with space access and resource navigation beyond Halifax.

resources.name: The Spark Zone (Entrepreneurship Sandbox)
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University – The Spark Zone
resources.description: The Spark Zone provides an online intake and matching process to pair founders with volunteer mentors, coaches, and advisors drawn from multiple partner institutions. It curates guides to grants and early-stage funding, offers venture-readiness and basic permitting pathway checklists, and provides access to campus-based makerspaces and meeting rooms across partner sites. As a multi-campus digital gateway plus shared spaces, it functions like a community mentorship portal serving HRM and nearby communities.

solutions.text: Cooperative Ownership Models: Support cooperative business models where workers or community members buy equity collectively, reducing individual capital needs and keeping businesses anchored locally with shared governance.

resources.name: Antigonish Farmers’ Market Co-operative
resources.description: A vendor-owned co-operative that operates a year-round public market, pooling member resources to provide shared retail space, marketing, and governance for small producers and entrepreneurs. By collectively owning the market and its infrastructure, vendors reduce individual startup and overhead costs while keeping decision-making local through democratic member control.

resources.name: Halifax Brewery Market (Historic Farmers’ Market Co-operative)
resources.description: A long-standing, vendor-run co-operative that provides shared, low-barrier retail space and coordinated marketing for small food, craft, and farm businesses in downtown Halifax. Member-owners collectively govern the market and share costs, enabling entrepreneurs to enter and grow without the capital required for standalone storefronts while anchoring activity in the community.
resources.address: 1496 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1R9

resources.name: Just Us! Coffee Roasters Co-op
resources.organization: Just Us! Coffee Roasters Co-op Ltd.
resources.description: A worker-owned co-operative roastery and cafe network where employees hold equity and make decisions democratically. Collective ownership spreads capital requirements among worker-members and keeps profits and governance rooted in Nova Scotia’s communities while supporting ethical supply chains and local jobs.
resources.address: 11865 Nova Scotia Trunk 1, Grand Pré, NS B0P 1M0

resources.name: Victoria Co-operative Fisheries
resources.description: A fisher-owned processing and marketing co-operative in Cape Breton that enables independent harvesters to pool capital for facilities, equipment, and distribution. Through shared ownership and governance, members reduce individual financial burden, secure fair market access, and keep the seafood value chain rooted in local communities.
resources.address: 7353 Cabot Trail, New Haven, NS B0C 1N0

resources.name: Scotian Gold Cooperative
resources.description: A grower-owned tree fruit co-operative that operates shared packing, storage, and marketing infrastructure for apple producers across Nova Scotia. By owning equity collectively, farmer-members reduce the capital required for processing and market access, strengthen bargaining power, and keep governance and economic benefits within rural communities.

obstacles.title: Industry Concentration and Seasonality
obstacles.description: Reliance on a few sectors and seasonal work reduces stability and pushes talent to diversified economies elsewhere.

solutions.text: Community Business Incubator and Co-working Hub: Create a locally run incubator that offers affordable desk space, mentorship, legal and accounting clinics, and shared equipment to help startups and seasonal entrepreneurs scale into year-round operations.

resources.name: Volta Residency and Co-working
resources.description: Volta operates a large startup hub that offers affordable co-working desks, private offices, meeting rooms, and shared amenities for founders building companies in Nova Scotia. Resident companies receive structured mentorship, founder-in-residence guidance, investor connections, and regular office hours with legal and accounting partners—practical supports that help entrepreneurs professionalize and grow beyond seasonal revenue cycles. By lowering overhead and providing wraparound advisory services, Volta functions as a community-run incubator that helps startups scale into sustainable, year-round operations.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE is an oceantech incubator that provides co-working space, shared prototyping labs, machine shop access, and testing facilities to help founders build and validate products in Nova Scotia. Companies benefit from specialized mentorship, industry advisors, and connections to legal, IP, and accounting supports through COVE’s partner network—resources that reduce barriers and risk for early-stage and seasonal ventures. The combination of space, shared equipment, and expert clinics helps firms stabilize operations and grow into year-round businesses in a globally competitive sector.

resources.name: CEED | The Exchange (Co-working & Business Advisory)
resources.organization: CEED – Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development
resources.description: CEED’s Exchange provides affordable co-working desks, meeting rooms, and a collaborative hub alongside CEED’s entrepreneurship training, advisory, and small-business financing programs. Entrepreneurs receive mentorship, workshops on finance and bookkeeping, and facilitated connections to legal and accounting supports through partner clinics—practical services that help seasonal and early-stage ventures formalize operations and manage cash flow year-round. By combining workspace with hands-on advisory and access to shared resources, CEED functions as a community business incubator that helps founders scale sustainably in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Year-round Cultural and Events Calendar: Organize community-led festivals, markets, workshops and performances in shoulder and off-seasons to smooth demand for hospitality and creative work and to keep visitor flows and local spending more consistent.

resources.name: Evergreen Festival
resources.description: Evergreen Festival is a multi-week winter celebration in late November and December featuring outdoor light installations, artisan markets, live music, and cultural programming throughout downtown Halifax and the waterfront. By activating public spaces and venues in the off-season, it drives foot traffic to local businesses and creates paid opportunities for artists, vendors, and hospitality workers, smoothing seasonal demand.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 2A2

resources.name: Downtown Dartmouth Ice Festival
resources.description: This annual winter festival showcases large-scale ice sculptures, live carving demonstrations, music, and family-friendly activities across downtown Dartmouth in late January/February. It intentionally brings residents and visitors out during a slower period, boosting sales for local restaurants and shops and providing paid gigs for carvers, performers, and event crews.

resources.name: Wolfville Farmers' Market (Year-Round Market & Events)
resources.description: The Wolfville Farmers' Market operates year-round with Saturday markets and mid-week events, including winter indoor markets, community suppers, workshops, and artisan pop-ups. This consistent calendar supports farmers, makers, and musicians through shoulder seasons and sustains local spending and hospitality activity even in colder months.

resources.name: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design — Year-Round Programs
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: The Centre delivers exhibitions, artisan markets, and hands-on workshops throughout the year, with robust fall and winter programming that draws participants and visitors to downtown Sydney. By providing off-season classes and shows, it maintains paid opportunities for craftspeople and artists while supporting nearby hospitality and retail businesses in slower months.

resources.name: Truro Winter Long John Festival
resources.description: A week-long celebration each February featuring outdoor activities, live entertainment, workshops, and downtown promotions designed to get residents and visitors out in winter. The festival’s off-season schedule lifts local retail and dining while creating paid performance and event work, helping to stabilize demand beyond the summer.

solutions.text: Skills and Micro-credential Programs: Partner with colleges, employers and community groups to run short, affordable training and micro-credential courses tied to local growth sectors and transferable skills, with flexible scheduling for seasonal workers.

resources.name: NSCC MicroCredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College offers short, stackable micro-credentials that focus on in-demand skills across sectors such as oceans and marine, IT and cybersecurity, healthcare, construction, and clean/green technologies. Courses are designed with employer input, priced affordably, and delivered in flexible formats (online, part-time, evenings) so seasonal workers can upskill or reskill quickly and stack digital badges toward larger credentials tied to local growth industries.

resources.name: Dalhousie Micro-credentials (Open Learning & Career Development)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development delivers micro-credentials and short courses in areas like data analytics, project management, digital skills, and sustainability—developed in collaboration with industry and professional associations. Programs are modular, affordable, and often offered online or in blended/part-time formats, enabling seasonal and underemployed workers to earn employer-recognized badges aligned with Nova Scotia’s emerging and established sectors.

resources.name: Professional and Continuing Studies Micro-credentials
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University – Professional and Continuing Studies
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University’s Professional and Continuing Studies offers micro-credentials and digital badges in transferable, career-ready skills such as business analysis, leadership, project management, and data-driven decision-making. Programs are short, cost-effective, and scheduled flexibly (evenings/online), helping seasonal workers and early-career talent quickly build competencies that align with employer needs in Nova Scotia’s growing sectors.

resources.name: Sector-Specific Employment and Skills Programs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers short, employer-connected training and upskilling programs for newcomers in growth fields like IT, healthcare, and skilled trades, often in partnership with colleges and Nova Scotia employers. These programs are modular, frequently offered online or during flexible hours, and include job readiness supports—enabling seasonal and underemployed workers to gain recognized skills and micro-credentials that translate directly to local job opportunities.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Local Apprenticeship and Mentorship Network: Build a community brokerage that matches youth and career-changers with apprenticeships, mentorships and paid short-term placements in local businesses across diverse sectors.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s Clean Leadership Summer Internship places youth and early-career talent in paid, short-term positions with municipalities, non-profits, utilities, and private companies across Nova Scotia’s environmental sector. The program functions as a broker by matching candidates to host employers, providing training and mentorship, and helping participants build local professional networks that can lead to longer-term employment.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS matches immigrant and newcomer professionals—including youth and career-changers—with volunteer mentors working in Nova Scotia businesses and public sector organizations. Through structured mentorship, networking, and employer engagement that often leads to informational interviews and placements, the program acts as a local brokerage that connects talent to opportunities across diverse sectors.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: COVE Internship Program
resources.description: COVE brokers paid internships and talent-development opportunities with ocean-technology companies across Nova Scotia, connecting students and early-career candidates to short-term roles and industry mentors. By coordinating employer matches, career coaching, and on-the-job mentorship, the program builds local pathways into a fast-growing sector and encourages participants to stay and advance in the province.

resources.name: Co-operative Education and Work-Integrated Learning (WIL)
resources.description: NSCC’s WIL programs coordinate paid co-op terms, practicums, and apprenticeship pathways by matching students and adult learners with local employers in trades, technology, health, business, and creative industries. Acting as a province-wide broker, NSCC links learners to mentored, short-term placements that develop in-demand skills and frequently convert into longer-term employment in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Co-operative Education Program
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University Co-op brokers paid work terms with Nova Scotia employers in sectors such as finance, analytics, marketing, science, and the arts, pairing students with supervisors who provide mentorship and industry exposure. By facilitating short-term, career-relevant placements and employer-student matching, the program strengthens local talent pipelines and encourages graduates to launch careers in the province.

solutions.text: Community Investment and Microloan Fund: Establish a community-controlled seed fund and microloan program to finance small businesses, value-added processing, off-season tourism products and innovations that diversify the local economy.

resources.name: CEED Microloan Program
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides microloans to startups and small businesses across Nova Scotia, typically up to $20,000, along with coaching and training. The financing helps entrepreneurs purchase equipment, develop value-added products, and bridge seasonal cash flow, enabling off-season tourism offerings and innovations that diversify local economies.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: ISANS Immigrant Business Loan
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS offers a microloan program for newcomer entrepreneurs in Nova Scotia, delivered in partnership with local credit unions, to finance startup and expansion needs such as working capital, equipment, and product development. These loans, coupled with business advisory services, enable immigrants to launch or grow small businesses, add value to local supply chains, and create year-round offerings that reduce seasonality.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: BBI Business Loan Program
resources.description: BBI provides accessible financing and advisory support to Black entrepreneurs in Nova Scotia, including microloans and growth capital for startups and existing businesses. Funds can be used for equipment, inventory, marketing, and seasonal diversification (e.g., value-added processing or off-season tourism products), helping broaden the province’s economic base and create stable employment.
resources.address: 1660 Hollis Street, Suite 810, Halifax, NS B3J 1V7

solutions.text: Buy Local and Sector Diversification Campaign: Run campaigns and business-to-business initiatives that encourage residents and institutions to purchase locally made and season-extending products and services, supporting emerging local industries.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Loyal
resources.description: Nova Scotia Loyal is a province-wide buy-local campaign that provides shared branding, marketing assets, and promotional tools encouraging residents and organizations to choose Nova Scotian products and services year-round. By amplifying demand across food, craft, retail, tourism, and professional services, it helps diversify the economy beyond seasonal peaks and supports emerging local industries. The campaign also engages businesses and communities to run localized initiatives, strengthening B2B connections and institutional procurement of local goods.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 301, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Wolfville Farmers’ Market & WFM2Go
resources.description: The Wolfville Farmers’ Market operates a year-round market and WFM2Go, an online marketplace with scheduled pickups and deliveries that extend local purchasing beyond traditional seasons. It aggregates offerings from farms, fisheries, and makers to increase steady demand and convenience for households and workplaces, supporting sector diversification in agri-food and value-added products. The market also facilitates connections between producers and restaurants or community organizations, strengthening local supply chains.

resources.name: Halifax Brewery Market
resources.description: The Halifax Brewery Market is a weekly, year-round indoor market that encourages residents to buy directly from local farmers, food producers, and artisans, providing steady off-season revenue for vendors. By showcasing a diverse mix of food, craft, and wellness entrepreneurs, it supports sector diversification and growth of emerging local businesses. Its consistent schedule and indoor venue help extend sales opportunities beyond peak tourist seasons.
resources.address: 1496 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1R9

resources.name: Centre for Craft Nova Scotia – Designer Craft Shop and Markets
resources.organization: Craft Nova Scotia (Centre for Craft Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Centre for Craft Nova Scotia operates a year-round Designer Craft Shop and seasonal markets that promote purchasing locally made craft, art, and design. These programs channel consumer and corporate spending toward Nova Scotian makers—supporting the creative sector as an emerging industry and diversifying income beyond tourism-heavy months. The Centre also facilitates B2B opportunities such as corporate and institutional sourcing of locally made products.

resources.name: Alderney Landing Farmers’ Market
resources.description: Alderney Landing hosts a year-round indoor farmers’ market that connects consumers with local farmers, fishers, food producers, and artisans, promoting steady buy-local activity across all seasons. By providing a consistent venue for small and emerging businesses to reach customers and partner with nearby restaurants and retailers, the market helps diversify the local economy. Regular themed events and holiday markets further extend sales windows for vendors beyond the traditional high season.

solutions.text: Shared-use Facilities and Pop-up Spaces: Convert underused community buildings into shared kitchens, fabrication labs, studios or retail pop-up spaces that lower start-up costs and help seasonal businesses test year-round offerings.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Innovation Hub (Yarmouth)
resources.description: IGNITE operates shared, publicly accessible prototyping labs and coworking spaces that include 3D printers, electronics benches, and light fabrication tools. By giving startups and seasonal entrepreneurs low-cost access to fabrication equipment and meeting/event space, the hub lets them prototype products, pilot services, and build year-round revenue streams without the overhead of owning facilities.

resources.name: New Glasgow Farmers Market — Market Kitchen
resources.description: The Market Kitchen is a certified shared-use commercial kitchen inside the New Glasgow Farmers Market that food entrepreneurs can rent for production, workshops, and pop-up meals. It reduces start-up costs for small and seasonal producers by providing compliant space and built-in market access, helping them test and sell products year-round beyond peak tourism months.
resources.address: 620 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3S2

resources.name: Alderney Landing Community Market & Pop-Up Events
resources.description: Alderney Landing converts its cultural centre into a weekly indoor market and frequent pop-up retail and festival spaces where small vendors can sell with minimal overhead. By offering flexible, short-term booths and event space, it enables seasonal businesses to test new products and maintain a presence through the winter, smoothing revenue across the year.

resources.name: Halifax Brewery Market
resources.description: Housed in the historic Brewery building, this year-round indoor market provides shared vendor stalls and pop-up retail opportunities for local makers and producers. The low-commitment, flexible format helps seasonal and emerging businesses test offerings, build brands, and generate off-season sales without the cost of permanent storefronts.
resources.address: 1496 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1R9

resources.name: Eltuek Arts Centre (Studios and Shared Creative Spaces)
resources.description: Eltuek repurposes a former convent into affordable studios, workshops, and gallery/event spaces for artists, cultural workers, and creative entrepreneurs. By offering shared-use facilities for production and pop-up exhibitions/markets, it lowers barriers to entry and supports creative enterprises to operate and earn income year-round, diversifying the local economy beyond seasonal peaks.

solutions.text: Remote Worker and Returner Attraction Program: Offer a locally promoted package of incentives and services for remote workers and former residents—co-working access, childcare options, housing navigation and welcome events—to attract talent year-round.

resources.name: Halifax Connector Program
resources.description: The Halifax Connector Program pairs job seekers—including new graduates, newcomers, and returning residents—with established ‘Connectors’ in their field for one-on-one meetings and warm introductions. By rapidly building professional and community networks, hosting networking events, and signposting local services (such as housing and settlement resources), it helps remote workers and returnees integrate and find year-round opportunities, supporting retention beyond seasonal work.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Volta Innovation Hub
resources.description: Volta is Atlantic Canada’s largest innovation hub, offering flexible co-working memberships, meeting rooms, and a community for tech startups, freelancers, and remote employees. Through regular workshops, meetups, mentorship, and a welcoming ‘landing pad’ for relocators, Volta gives remote workers and returning Nova Scotians access to workspace, networks, and programming year-round—strengthening the local tech ecosystem beyond seasonal cycles.

resources.name: Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE provides shared offices, co-working, labs, and prototyping spaces for ocean-technology companies and professionals. With ongoing industry programming, networking events, and support for companies and individuals relocating to Nova Scotia, COVE offers remote workers and returners a sector-focused place to work and connect all year, helping diversify the economy and reduce reliance on seasonal employment.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Yarmouth Innovation Hub & Coworking
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic operates innovation hubs and co-working spaces that support entrepreneurs, students, and remote workers in rural Nova Scotia. Its Yarmouth hub provides desks, meeting rooms, programs, and community events, and connects members to local partners for housing and settlement questions—making it easier for returnees and remote professionals to establish themselves and contribute to the local economy year-round.

resources.name: CO3 Coworking & Community Space
resources.description: CO3 is a community-focused co-working space in Bridgewater that offers flexible desks, private offices, and meeting rooms for freelancers, remote employees, and small teams. By hosting regular meetups and newcomer-friendly events and serving as a central, year-round workspace, CO3 supports remote worker attraction and retention in Lunenburg County, complementing broader efforts to diversify employment beyond seasonal sectors.

solutions.text: Cross-sector Economic Diversification Council: Form a community council of business owners, non-profits, education and municipal reps to identify gaps, coordinate training, pool marketing, and develop strategies to reduce sector reliance and seasonality.

resources.name: Halifax Partnership – Inclusive Economic Strategy (People. Planet. Prosperity.)
resources.description: Halifax Partnership leads the city’s cross-sector economic strategy by convening business leaders, post-secondary institutions, non-profits, and municipal representatives to identify gaps, align workforce training, and coordinate investment attraction. Through initiatives like the Connector Program and sector collaborations, it pools marketing efforts and drives diversification beyond seasonal industries, helping retain and attract young talent with year-round opportunities.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 810, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

resources.name: Cape Breton Regional Enterprise Network (via Cape Breton Partnership)
resources.description: The Cape Breton Partnership operates the island’s Regional Enterprise Network, uniting municipalities, businesses, education (CBU/NSCC), and community organizations to set shared priorities for industry diversification and workforce development. It coordinates employer needs with training providers, leads joint investment and talent marketing, and establishes sector tables (e.g., ocean industries, clean energy, tourism shoulder-season growth) to reduce reliance on a few seasonal sectors.

resources.name: Western Regional Enterprise Network (Western REN)
resources.description: Western REN brings together municipalities, local businesses, non-profits, and education partners across Digby, Yarmouth, and Shelburne counties to coordinate regional economic development. Through business outreach (e.g., BusinessNOW), sector and workforce tables, and joint marketing, it identifies skills gaps, aligns training with NSCC and employers, and advances diversification strategies that build year-round employment beyond seasonal industries.

resources.name: Eastern Strait Regional Enterprise Network (ESREN)
resources.description: ESREN convenes a cross-sector council of municipalities, businesses, post-secondary partners, and community groups in the Eastern Strait region (Antigonish, Guysborough, St. Mary’s, and Port Hawkesbury) to plan and deliver diversification initiatives. It coordinates training with education providers, facilitates sector development (e.g., ocean industries, value-added resource sectors, tourism shoulder seasons), and undertakes joint investment/talent marketing to reduce seasonality and broaden the local economy.
resources.address: 32 Paint Street, Unit 4, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 3J8

solutions.text: Value-added Agriculture and Food Processing Co-op: Support farmers and fishers to form co-ops that produce processed, preserved and specialty goods for year-round sales, extending employment and stabilizing incomes beyond harvest seasons.

resources.name: Scotian Gold Cooperative Limited
resources.description: A grower-owned apple cooperative in the Annapolis Valley that operates large-scale packing, controlled-atmosphere storage, and juice/cider processing to turn raw fruit into branded, shelf-stable products. This value-added processing and year-round marketing extend employment in rural communities and stabilize member growers’ incomes beyond the fall harvest.

resources.name: Victoria Co-operative Fisheries Ltd.
resources.description: A fisher-owned cooperative in northern Cape Breton that operates seafood processing facilities for lobster, crab, shrimp, and other species, including cooking, freezing, packing, and specialty product lines. By converting seasonal catches into frozen and specialty products for year-round export sales, the co-op extends work beyond peak fishing seasons and returns more value to member harvesters.
resources.address: 150 New Haven Road, New Haven, NS B0C 1N0

resources.name: Perennia Food and Beverage Innovation
resources.description: Perennia’s program helps farm and fish co-ops and small processors develop value-added foods through recipe and process development, shelf-life testing, food-safety (HACCP) support, and access to pilot-scale processing equipment. By enabling producers to create preserved and specialty products that can be sold year-round, Perennia directly supports the value-added co-op model and more stable rural employment.
resources.address: 32 Main Street, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2Z2

resources.name: Wolfville Farmers’ Market Co-operative
resources.description: A producer-run cooperative operating a year-round market and the WFM2Go online store, giving farmers and food businesses consistent weekly sales channels for preserved, processed, and specialty items. The co-op model aggregates and markets members’ value-added goods across seasons, strengthening local incomes and reducing the effects of harvest seasonality.

resources.name: Truro Farmers’ Market Cooperative
resources.description: A cooperative market operating year-round in downtown Truro that provides stall space and programming for farmers, fishers, and food entrepreneurs to sell preserves, smoked/processed meats and fish, cheeses, baked goods, and other specialty foods. By maintaining steady weekly retail access for value-added products, the co-op helps extend employment and stabilize revenues for primary producers beyond peak seasons.

solutions.text: Affordable Housing and Childcare Initiatives: Mobilize community land trusts, cooperative housing projects and shared childcare programs to remove barriers that push workers to leave and to make local jobs viable year-round.

resources.name: Dartmouth Family Home Child Care Agency
resources.description: A provincially licensed agency that recruits, trains, and supports regulated home-based child care providers across Dartmouth and HRM, offering flexible full-time and part-time spaces year-round. By coordinating shared standards, subsidies, and wraparound family supports, it removes child care barriers that keep parents—especially those in seasonal sectors—out of the workforce, helping families remain and thrive locally.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia builds and rehabilitates modest, energy-efficient homes and sells them to working families through affordable, geared-to-income mortgages. By expanding attainable, community-driven housing options, the program stabilizes housing costs for low- and moderate-income workers, reducing the pressure to relocate and supporting year-round participation in the local economy.

solutions.text: School-to-Community Career Pathways: Create local career pathway programs connecting K-12 and post-secondary students with community employers for internships, project work and entrepreneurship projects that expose youth to diverse local opportunities.

resources.name: Co-op Education & Work-Integrated Learning (WIL)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College’s Co-op and WIL programs place students with local employers for paid co-op terms, practicums, and applied projects across sectors such as oceans, IT, trades, health, and creative industries. By embedding work experience in diploma and certificate programs province-wide, NSCC connects post-secondary learners directly with community businesses and organizations, helping diversify career exposure beyond seasonal work and building long-term local talent pipelines.

resources.name: Dal Innovates (Launch Programs & Ready2Launch)
resources.description: Dal Innovates provides experiential entrepreneurship and innovation programs that pair students with mentors, founders, and industry partners to build startups and solve real community and industry challenges. Through summer accelerators, applied research sprints, and venture-building internships, students gain hands-on experience and connections to employers across emerging and established sectors in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Navigate Startup House – Student Entrepreneurship and Community Projects
resources.description: Navigate supports student and recent graduate entrepreneurs from Cape Breton University and NSCC by connecting them with local mentors, industry partners, and community clients for real-world projects and venture development. Through workspace, programming, and employer-engaged challenges, students explore local opportunities, develop startups, and engage with businesses across the island’s diversified economy.

resources.name: NSCAD University Co-op Education
resources.description: NSCAD’s Co-op Education program places undergraduate students from design, craft, and fine arts with museums, galleries, studios, startups, and creative businesses for structured work terms. These placements give students industry experience, mentorship, and networks in Nova Scotia’s cultural and creative sectors, showcasing diverse, year-round career paths in the province.

resources.name: Skills Canada Nova Scotia – School Engagement & Industry Partnerships
resources.description: Skills Canada Nova Scotia delivers in-school presentations, industry-led workshops, and skills camps that connect junior and senior high students with trades and technology mentors and employers. Through hands-on projects and competitions supported by local industry, students gain early exposure to diverse, in-demand careers and direct pathways to apprenticeships and further training in the province.
resources.address: 201 Brownlow Avenue, Unit 9, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1W2

obstacles.title: Underinvestment in Arts, Culture, and Recreation
obstacles.description: Limited venues, affordable creative spaces, and year-round programming weaken the vibrancy that attracts and retains youth.

solutions.text: Community Arts Hub (repurpose vacant buildings): Transform underused municipal or commercial spaces into multi-use arts hubs managed by a community board, offering studios, rehearsal rooms, exhibition space and shared event areas at reduced rent.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op is a community-owned performance and arts hub in a repurposed commercial space on Gottingen Street. It offers a black-box theatre, rehearsal time, meeting rooms and exhibition walls to artists and community groups at accessible, subsidized rental rates, with equipment available in-house. As a co-operative governed by a member-elected board, it keeps space affordable and community-managed in line with the arts hub model.

resources.name: Eltuek Arts Centre
resources.description: Eltuek Arts Centre transformed a former convent and arts school into a multi-tenant arts hub for Cape Breton. The facility provides long-term artist studios, shared workrooms, galleries, and meeting/event rooms rented at accessible rates to local creatives and nonprofits. Operated by a community-based charitable organization, it ensures year-round programming and affordable, shared arts infrastructure.

resources.name: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design revitalized a downtown commercial building into a community craft hub with shared studios and public-facing spaces. It houses fully equipped studios (clay, metal/jewellery, textiles, and more), a gallery, classrooms, and incubator workspaces available to members and emerging artists at low-cost rates. As a nonprofit governed by a volunteer board, it prioritizes affordable access and shared resources for creatives year-round.

resources.name: The Old School Community Gathering Place
resources.organization: The Old School Community Gathering Place Society
resources.description: The Old School Community Gathering Place converted a decommissioned rural school into a multi-use arts and community centre. It offers artist studios, a performance/rehearsal hall, gallery, and meeting rooms that local groups and young creatives can rent at reduced community rates. Run by a local nonprofit society with a volunteer board, it keeps governance and programming rooted in community needs.

resources.name: ArtsPlace Gallery (ARCAC)
resources.description: ARCAC’s ArtsPlace Gallery operates out of a repurposed main-street building as an arts hub for the Annapolis Valley. In addition to exhibitions, it provides a classroom studio, artist-in-residence workspace, and multipurpose rooms that are rented to artists and community groups at affordable rates. The member-based nonprofit, led by a community board, sustains year-round creative activity and shared event programming.
resources.address: 396 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

solutions.text: Shared Equipment Library and Makerspace: Create a lending library of tools, AV gear, instruments and fabrication equipment so artists and small groups can produce work without large upfront costs.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: A member-run lending library offering hundreds of hand and power tools, from drills and saws to specialty fabrication tools. By allowing members to borrow equipment instead of buying it, the library directly reduces upfront costs for artists, makers, and community groups producing sets, installations, props, and creative projects.

resources.name: Equipment Rentals and Production Facilities
resources.description: CFAT provides affordable access to professional media arts equipment—including cameras, audio recorders, lighting, projectors—and on-site edit suites and production spaces for members. This shared equipment model lets independent artists and small collectives produce film, video, and sound works without major capital purchases.

resources.name: AFCOOP Equipment Rental and Post-Production Suites
resources.description: AFCOOP operates a comprehensive shared equipment library with cinema cameras, lenses, lighting, grip, and sound gear, plus edit suites and post-production facilities at subsidized member rates. Filmmakers and small crews can access professional tools and spaces to develop and complete projects without prohibitive upfront costs.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio & Media Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: Halifax Central Library hosts public makerspaces that provide free or low-cost access to 3D printers, sewing machines, Cricut cutters, digitization tools, and bookable audio/video studios. The Library also supports borrowing of creative equipment (including musical instruments through the Sun Life Musical Instrument Lending Library), enabling youth, artists, and community groups to produce media and art without purchasing gear.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Pop-up and Mobile Venues: Organize rotating pop-up shows, performances and markets in vacant storefronts, parks and community centres to activate spaces and test demand for long-term venues.

resources.name: Halifax Fringe Festival
resources.description: An annual multi-venue performing arts festival that programs pop-up theatre, comedy, dance, and music in unconventional spaces across Halifax and Dartmouth, including bars, galleries, storefronts, and outdoor sites. By activating temporary stages and short-term venues, the festival tests audience demand in different neighbourhoods and helps artists and organizers pilot concepts that can grow into longer-term offerings.

resources.name: STAGES Theatre Festival
resources.description: Eastern Front Theatre’s annual festival showcases new and experimental work using site-specific and pop-up venues throughout downtown Dartmouth and Halifax—such as storefronts, waterfront spaces, and community hubs. These rotating temporary stages bring live performance to public places, animating underused areas and gauging interest that can inform future, longer-term venue development.

resources.name: Downtown Sydney Night Market
resources.description: A recurring summer series that transforms Charlotte Street and adjacent public spaces into a pop-up marketplace with local vendors, artisans, food, and live entertainment. By temporarily pedestrianizing streets and activating storefronts and plazas, the Night Market tests demand for year-round retail and cultural programming while drawing people back to the urban core.

resources.name: Wolfville Night Market
resources.description: A summer street-market series that closes sections of Main Street for rotating pop-up vendors, local food, and live performances in the heart of Wolfville. The temporary activation of public right-of-way and nearby parks creates a lively cultural hub, offering emerging businesses and artists a low-barrier way to test offerings and audience interest.

resources.name: Pop-Up Libraries & Mobile Outreach
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries regularly deploys pop-up libraries and mobile cultural programming to parks, community centres, markets, and festivals across HRM. These temporary setups offer performances, workshops, and creative activities that animate public spaces and help identify neighbourhoods with demand for expanded, longer-term arts and literacy programming.

solutions.text: Community Microgrant Program: Establish a locally funded microgrant program (crowdfunded or supported by businesses) that provides small, rapid grants to artists and grassroots organizers for projects and programming.

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty Placemaking Grant Program
resources.description: Downtown Halifax Business Commission provides small, fast-turnaround grants to artists and community groups to create public art and placemaking projects such as murals, storefront installations, and pop-up activations. Funded by local businesses through the business improvement district, the program functions as a community microgrant, seeding grassroots cultural projects that animate public space and expand year-round arts programming.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 2A2

resources.name: Community Grants Program (Cultural & Community Activities)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Community Grants Program offers small project grants to non-profit groups for cultural activities, festivals, and community arts programming. These microgrants help grassroots organizers and artists quickly access modest funding to pilot events, activate venues, and deliver year-round cultural programming that strengthens local vibrancy.

resources.name: Music Nova Scotia Investment Program (Artist Development & Project Grants)
resources.description: Music Nova Scotia administers small project grants to Nova Scotia musicians and music entrepreneurs for activities like recording, marketing, touring, and showcases. These microgrants provide rapid, targeted support to individual artists and grassroots organizers to create and present work, expand programming, and build sustainable careers in the cultural sector.

resources.name: Event Partnership Program
resources.description: Downtown Truro Partnership offers small cash and in-kind microgrants to community groups and artists to deliver downtown events, pop-ups, live performances, and cultural activations. Funded by local businesses through the business improvement district, the program acts as a quick, accessible support to seed grassroots arts programming that increases year-round vibrancy.

solutions.text: Business–Arts Partnership Network: Build formal partnerships between local businesses and artists (sponsorships, storefront exhibitions, commissioning, cross-promotion) to generate revenue and exposure for creators.

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty Placemaking Program
resources.description: Downtown Halifax Business Commission’s Gritty to Pretty funds and brokers partnerships between property owners/businesses and local artists to produce murals, storefront/window art, and placemaking installations. Businesses sponsor and host the works on their façades and in windows, while DHBC coordinates commissions and co-marketing, generating paid opportunities and high-visibility exposure for artists year-round.

resources.name: Downtown Dartmouth Public Art & Mural Program
resources.description: The Downtown Dartmouth Business Commission works with merchants and property owners to commission murals, window art, and other installations on commercial buildings and in storefronts. The program connects businesses with local artists, secures sponsorships, and provides cross-promotion through maps, social media, and events—delivering paid commissions and sustained visibility for creators while animating the business district.

resources.name: Corporate Art Rental Program
resources.organization: Art Sales & Rental Society (in association with the Art Gallery of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Art Sales & Rental Society connects Nova Scotian artists with corporate clients by curating, renting, and selling artwork for offices, storefronts, hotels, and public-facing spaces. Through ongoing rotations, commissions, and tailored placements, businesses sponsor and showcase local art while artists gain steady revenue, professional exposure, and promotional support.

resources.name: Downtown Truro Murals & Public Art Program
resources.description: Downtown Truro Partnership collaborates with businesses and property owners to commission murals, sculptures, and window displays that enliven commercial corridors. The initiative issues calls for artists, coordinates installations, and drives cross-promotion through walking tours and digital marketing, creating paid work for artists while drawing customers to participating storefronts.

resources.name: Halifax Waterfront Public Art and Activation
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia commissions and curates public art and cultural activations along the Halifax waterfront in partnership with nearby businesses, property tenants, and sponsors. Rotating exhibitions, performances, and site-specific works attract foot traffic to local storefronts while paying artists for commissions and leveraging coordinated cross-promotion across the district.
resources.address: 1751 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S5

solutions.text: Artist Residency and School Mentorships: Match local artists with schools and community groups for in-residence projects, skill-sharing and paid mentorship that strengthens intergenerational connections and keeps youth engaged.

resources.name: PAINTS (Professional Artists in the Schools)
resources.description: PAINTS connects professional visual artists with P–12 classrooms across Nova Scotia for paid, curriculum-connected residencies ranging from single sessions to multi-week projects. Artists mentor students and teachers through hands-on art-making, building skills and intergenerational connections while keeping youth engaged in creative practice.

resources.name: Writers in the Schools (WITS)
resources.description: WITS pairs published authors, poets, and storytellers with schools across Nova Scotia for paid classroom visits and multi-visit residencies that develop students’ writing and storytelling skills. Through mentorship, readings, and workshops, local writers share craft knowledge and foster youth engagement with language arts in partnership with teachers and community groups.

resources.name: ArtsReach School & Community Outreach
resources.organization: The Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: ArtsReach brings professional artists from multiple disciplines into rural schools and community organizations for paid residencies, collaborative projects, and mentorship. The program supports hands-on learning and intergenerational skill-sharing, and Ross Creek’s on-site artist residencies include outreach that keeps local youth engaged year-round.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

resources.name: PERFORM! Artist in the Schools Program
resources.description: PERFORM! connects professional theatre artists and companies with Nova Scotia schools for subsidized, paid workshops and in-class residencies in acting, playwriting, movement, and production. Artists mentor students and collaborate with educators on project-based learning that strengthens community ties and deepens youth engagement in the performing arts.

solutions.text: Cooperative Theatre/Gallery Models: Form artist-run cooperatives to operate theatres, galleries and rehearsal spaces democratically, sharing costs, booking and revenue to lower barriers for participants.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op
resources.description: A member-owned, artist-run cooperative that operates a black box theatre and rehearsal space on Halifax’s Gottingen Street. Members collectively govern the venue, share operating costs through memberships and rentals, and coordinate bookings via a transparent calendar. By offering affordable rental rates and reinvesting revenue into the space, the co-op lowers barriers for emerging artists and community groups to produce and present work.

resources.name: ViewPoint Gallery
resources.description: An artist-run photography cooperative where member photographers co-manage the gallery, share staffing and curation duties, and split operating costs through dues and commissions. The cooperative model provides equitable access to exhibition slots, professional development, and shared marketing that would be cost-prohibitive individually. Sales revenue returns primarily to artists with a modest commission sustaining the gallery, keeping participation affordable.

resources.name: ART 1274 Hollis Gallery
resources.description: A downtown Halifax artists’ cooperative gallery where member artists jointly operate the space, schedule exhibitions, and staff the gallery. Members pool resources to cover rent, marketing, and administration, while gallery sales use a commission model that sustains operations and returns revenue to artists. This shared, democratic structure reduces individual costs and provides ongoing exhibition opportunities.

resources.name: Lunenburg Art Gallery
resources.description: A member-run, cooperative gallery in historic Lunenburg where local artists collaboratively manage exhibitions, staffing, and programming. Operating costs are shared through membership and commissions, and decisions are made democratically by the artist members. The co-op model provides an accessible, year-round venue for artists to show and sell work, strengthening the cultural vitality of the community.

solutions.text: Year-Round Programming Consortium: Coordinate a coalition of festivals, venues and community groups to produce staggered, seasonal programming so cultural activity continues throughout the year rather than peaking only in summer.

resources.name: Evergreen Festival
resources.organization: Downtown Halifax Business Commission (in partnership with Build Nova Scotia and community partners)
resources.description: A winter city-wide festival that unites arts groups, venues, waterfront sites, markets, and small businesses to keep cultural activity vibrant through late fall and early winter. By coordinating concerts, light installations, artisan markets, and community events across partner sites, it staggers programming outside the summer peak and builds a coalition of presenters that sustains year-round cultural momentum.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

resources.name: Halifax Fringe Festival & Fringe Presents
resources.description: Halifax Fringe coordinates dozens of independent producers and multiple venues for its annual festival, and extends that network with Fringe Presents shows throughout the year. By brokering partnerships between theatres, bars, galleries, and community spaces across seasons, it staggers performances beyond the summer peak and maintains consistent opportunities for artists and audiences.

resources.name: Folk Harbour Concert Series (plus Lunenburg Folk Harbour Festival)
resources.description: Beyond its flagship summer festival, Folk Harbour runs a curated concert series through fall, winter, and spring in partnership with local venues and community groups. This coordinated, seasonal programming keeps live music active year-round in Lunenburg, staggering events across months and leveraging a coalition of hosts (churches, halls, and cultural spaces) to sustain cultural vibrancy.

resources.name: Symphony Nova Scotia Season & Community Concerts
resources.description: Symphony Nova Scotia presents a full September–May season of classical, pops, and family programs across multiple partner venues (e.g., Rebecca Cohn Auditorium, Alderney Landing) and collaborates with schools and community groups for outreach concerts. This multi-venue, multi-partner approach staggers programming across the calendar, distributing cultural activity beyond summer and into regular, year-round offerings.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 504, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

resources.name: Alderney Landing Year-Round Cultural Programming
resources.description: Alderney Landing functions as a community hub coordinating festivals (e.g., Canada Day, Natal Day, Christkindlmarket), concerts, markets, theatre, and cultural gatherings with local partners across all seasons. By aligning municipal, community, and arts stakeholders and hosting events throughout the year, it creates staggered, seasonal programming that keeps Dartmouth’s waterfront culturally active beyond the summer peak.

solutions.text: Affordable Studio Conversion Initiative: Organize community investment and partnerships with non-profits to convert low-cost housing or light industrial spaces into long-term, affordable artist studios with secure leases.

resources.name: Eltuek Arts Centre – Artist Studios
resources.description: Eltuek Arts Centre transformed the former Holy Angels Convent into a multi-tenant arts hub with individual artist studios, workrooms, and shared production spaces. Operated by community development non-profit New Dawn Enterprises, the centre offers affordable, secure studio rentals and maintains below-market rates through public/private partnerships and ongoing community investment. This conversion creates long-term, year-round creative space that anchors artists in Cape Breton.

resources.name: Wonder’neath Studios and Community Studio
resources.description: Wonder’neath Art Society rehabilitated a former commercial/light-industrial building in Halifax’s North End into a network of private artist studios and a public community studio. As a non-profit, it provides subsidized, secure studio rentals to local artists and sustains affordability through grants, donations, and partnerships with community organizations. This conversion expands year-round, affordable creative workspace while supporting public arts programming.

resources.name: The Old School Community Gathering Place – Artist Studios
resources.organization: The Old School Community Gathering Place Society
resources.description: The Old School Community Gathering Place converted a decommissioned rural school into a community arts hub with rentable studios and maker spaces for artists and creative entrepreneurs. Run by a local non-profit society, the facility offers secure, long-term studio rentals at below-market rates sustained by community fundraising, partnerships, and public grants. This approach reuses underutilized infrastructure to provide stable, affordable creative space on the Eastern Shore.

resources.name: Parrsboro Creative – Artist Relocation Program and Cultural Campus
resources.description: Parrsboro Creative partners with property owners and the municipality to repurpose vacant and underused Main Street buildings into affordable artist studios and live/work spaces. The non-profit helps artists secure stable leases and supports build-outs and conversions, using grants and community investment to keep costs low. This initiative builds a year-round creative district that attracts and retains artists in rural Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Timebanking and Barter Networks for Space/Skills: Set up a local timebank where creatives can trade rehearsal time, tutoring, venue management and technical skills instead of paying cash, reducing operating costs and building reciprocity.

resources.name: Radstorm
resources.description: Radstorm is a member-run arts and music collective that lets artists exchange volunteer time and technical help for access to rehearsal space, show bookings, and shared studios (screenprinting, zine library, etc.). By staffing shows, running sound, helping with maintenance, or mentoring others, members effectively ‘pay’ with time instead of cash, lowering costs for creatives and keeping space accessible.

resources.name: Anchor Archive Zine Library
resources.description: Anchor Archive is a volunteer-run zine and print resource that enables people to trade volunteer shifts and skill-sharing (cataloguing, event hosting, RISO/screenprinting support) for access to tools, production time, and space. This barter-style model reduces cash barriers for artists and writers while building a reciprocal network for tutoring, workshop facilitation, and production support.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op
resources.description: A member-owned performance venue that uses a cooperative model to keep space affordable by facilitating in-kind exchanges: artists contribute volunteer shifts (front-of-house, tech, venue management) and co-production support to receive reduced or waived rental fees. Through sliding-scale and community access policies, the co-op operationalizes a barter network where time and skills can substitute for cash in securing rehearsal and performance time.

resources.name: The Deanery Project
resources.description: The Deanery Project is a rural arts, environment, and community hub that offers work-trade arrangements—volunteer hours in facilities, events, teaching, or technical support can be exchanged for studio/workshop access, rehearsal/event space, and training. This practice functions as a timebank for creatives, reducing cash costs while building local capacity in venue operations and hands-on technical skills.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

resources.name: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: Ross Creek runs volunteer and work-exchange opportunities where artists and youth trade time—supporting events, facilities, and technical production—for bursaries, discounted program fees, and access to studios and rehearsal/performance spaces. By recognizing time and skills as currency, the centre sustains a reciprocal network that offsets operating costs for creatives and expands year-round programming.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

solutions.text: Public Art and Placemaking Projects: Commission community-led murals, performances and installations that beautify public spaces, attract visitors and create year-round cultural landmarks.

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty Placemaking Program
resources.description: Downtown Halifax Business Commission’s Gritty to Pretty program funds and commissions community-led murals, sculptures, light installations, and creative wayfinding in underused and high-traffic urban spaces. By pairing local artists with property owners and community groups, it beautifies streetscapes, draws visitors to small businesses, and creates lasting cultural landmarks that animate Downtown Halifax year-round.

resources.name: Halifax Waterfront Public Art and Placemaking
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia curates permanent and temporary public artworks, light installations, and performance spaces along the Halifax and Dartmouth waterfronts in partnership with local artists and community groups. These place-based projects enliven promenades and public squares, attract residents and visitors in all seasons, and establish cultural landmarks that support the regional creative economy.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 301, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Downtown Dartmouth Public Art and Placemaking
resources.description: The Downtown Dartmouth Business Commission works with local artists, businesses, and residents to commission murals, utility-box art, and seasonal installations throughout the downtown core. These projects revitalize laneways and storefronts, create walkable arts experiences, and host performances that attract visitors and build a year-round cultural identity for the district.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Public Art Program
resources.description: HRM’s Public Art Program commissions community-engaged murals, sculptures, and artist-led activations in parks, libraries, streetscapes, and civic buildings across the municipality. Through open calls and partnerships with neighbourhood groups, the program funds and maintains installations that beautify public spaces, reflect local stories, and serve as year-round cultural landmarks.

resources.name: Lumière Cape Breton: Art at Night
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: Lumière commissions site-specific installations, performances, and community projects that transform downtown Sydney and nearby public spaces into open-air galleries. By activating streetscapes, storefronts, and civic squares with contemporary art, the festival draws significant audiences, supports local creators, and leaves behind cultural touchpoints that encourage ongoing public engagement with the arts.

solutions.text: Local Crowdfunding and Community Investment Platform: Host a community crowdfunding portal with matched-fund rounds from local donors or municipalities to finance venue upgrades, equipment purchases and program development.

resources.name: Bus Stop Theatre Community Bond Campaign
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-operative invited local residents to invest directly through a community bond offering hosted on its own online portal to purchase and upgrade its venue on Gottingen Street. Community investment was paired with matched public capital contributions from Halifax Regional Municipality and the Province of Nova Scotia, financing building acquisition, technical equipment, and expanded year-round programming.

resources.name: Keep the HAT – Community Crowdfunding and Godparent Program
resources.description: Highland Arts Theatre runs an ongoing local crowdfunding effort via its website and CanadaHelps, including the ‘Godparent’ monthly donor program and time-limited matching challenges from local businesses and philanthropists. These matched-fund rounds finance venue maintenance and upgrades, production equipment, and sustained year-round programming that engages youth and emerging artists in Cape Breton.

resources.name: Chester Playhouse Rebuild Community Fundraising
resources.description: Following a 2021 fire, Chester Playhouse launched a community crowdfunding campaign through its website/CanadaHelps with periodic local matching-gift rounds, combined with municipal and provincial contributions. The matched funds supported reconstruction of the theatre, purchase of stage and sound equipment, and the restoration of diverse, year-round programming for the community.

resources.name: Neptune Theatre Donor‑Matched Crowdfunding Campaigns
resources.description: Neptune Theatre regularly runs donor-matched crowdfunding drives on its website and social channels, where local sponsors match community gifts during specific campaign windows. These matched-fund rounds are directed to facility improvements (lighting, accessibility, seating), essential production equipment, and program development that provides opportunities for young artists and audiences in Halifax.

solutions.text: Paid Youth Apprenticeships and Gig Platforms: Develop municipal or business-subsidized paid apprenticeship programs and a local gig board that connects young creatives with short-term paid opportunities in events, production and arts administration.

resources.name: FILM 5 Trainee Program
resources.description: AFCOOP’s FILM 5 Trainee Program places emerging filmmakers and crew in paid, mentored apprentice roles on short film productions in Nova Scotia. Participants receive department-specific training (camera, sound, art, production, etc.) and on‑set experience with honoraria supported by public funders and industry partners. This directly connects young creatives to short‑term paid production gigs and builds a pathway into the screen sector.

resources.name: NSCAD Co-operative Education (Co-op) Program
resources.description: NSCAD’s Co-op program matches students with paid work terms in galleries, museums, design studios, film/animation companies, festivals, and arts nonprofits across Nova Scotia. Staff broker placements and support both employers and students, turning arts administration and production roles into structured, remunerated apprenticeships. The program leverages employer wages and available subsidies/tax credits to create short-term paid opportunities that build portfolios and networks for young creatives.

resources.name: Arts Nova Scotia Opportunities Board
resources.organization: Arts Nova Scotia (Province of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Arts Nova Scotia curates a province-wide opportunities board listing paid contracts, jobs, calls for artists, and project-based gigs across festivals, theatres, galleries, and arts organizations. As a publicly funded, centralized platform, it connects young creatives to short-term paid roles in events, production, and arts administration. This functions as a local gig board that strengthens access to compensated creative work throughout Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Craft Apprenticeship Program (CAP)
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: CAP pairs emerging craftspeople with established artisans and studios for paid, time-limited apprenticeships on Cape Breton Island. Apprentices receive stipends while learning production techniques, business operations, and participation in creative markets/events. The program directly implements the solution by creating compensated, mentored placements that launch youth into sustainable creative production careers.

resources.name: Professional Artists in the Schools (PAINTS)
resources.description: PAINTS connects visual artists with schools across Nova Scotia for paid workshops and short projects, handling bookings and artist fees centrally. Many emerging and young artists use PAINTS as a steady stream of short-term, compensated gigs that build experience in project delivery and arts administration. By brokering and funding artist engagements, PAINTS functions as a practical gig platform for youth in the creative sector.
resources.address: 1113 Marginal Road, Suite 280, Halifax, NS B3H 4P7

solutions.text: Advocacy for Flexible Zoning and Short-Term Leases: Mobilize residents to work with municipal councils to allow adaptive reuse, pop-up permits and affordable short-term leases that make it easier for arts ventures to access space.

resources.name: Busking and Street Performers Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality issues low-cost permits that allow musicians, theatre artists, and other performers to use sidewalks, plazas, and parks for pop-up shows. By streamlining right-of-way permissions and seasonal permits, the program lowers barriers and creates flexible, short-term access to public space for arts ventures, directly aligning with advocacy for pop-up permitting and adaptive use of civic areas.

resources.name: Halifax Seaport Farmers’ Market Vendor Program
resources.description: The market offers affordable, short-term stalls and seasonal pop-up opportunities for local artisans, makers, and cultural vendors on the Halifax waterfront. This flexible, low-commitment leasing model helps creative entrepreneurs access high-traffic space and adaptively reuses port facilities for cultural programming.

resources.name: Alderney Landing Community Market & Pop-Up Rentals
resources.description: Alderney Landing runs weekly markets and short-term gallery and event rentals that give artists, craftspeople, and cultural groups flexible access to indoor and outdoor spaces on the Dartmouth waterfront. Working within municipal permitting frameworks, it enables affordable pop-up exhibitions, vendor booths, and festivals that activate public space and expand year-round arts activity.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op Rentals
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op provides subsidized, short-term rentals of a fully equipped performance venue for independent artists, enabling pop-up shows, rehearsals, and festivals without long-term leases. The co-operative model keeps costs low and demonstrates adaptive reuse and flexible access to cultural infrastructure in collaboration with community and municipal partners.

resources.name: CRAFT LAIR (Local Artist in Residence)
resources.organization: Craft Nova Scotia / Mary E. Black Gallery
resources.description: Hosted by the Mary E. Black Gallery, CRAFT LAIR provides rotating, short-term studio and exhibition space where craft artists engage the public in a pop-up, storefront-style setting. This model offers flexible, temporary access to a prominent cultural venue on the waterfront, lowering barriers for artists to test ideas and reach audiences without long-term commitments.

solutions.text: Social Enterprise Models for Sustainability: Encourage arts groups to adopt social enterprise practices (ticketed workshops, cafés, merch, venue rentals) to generate reliable income that subsidizes free or low-cost programming.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op
resources.description: A member-owned performing arts venue that sustains operations through affordable space rentals to artists and community groups, ticketed presentations and festivals, and licensed bar sales during events. These earned-revenue streams are reinvested to keep rental rates low, support pay-what-you-can and community programming, and provide year-round access to an inclusive creative space—directly aligning with a social enterprise model that subsidizes low-cost arts activities.

resources.name: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: A rural arts hub that operates tuition-based camps and workshops, ticketed performances (with resident company Two Planks and a Passion Theatre), and facility rentals for retreats and events. Revenue from classes, shows, and rentals is strategically used to fund bursaries, subsidize youth and community arts programs, and deliver free or low-cost cultural activities throughout the year—demonstrating a social enterprise approach that sustains accessible arts in the region.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

resources.name: King's Theatre
resources.description: A non-profit performing arts venue presenting ticketed films, concerts, and live theatre, while also offering venue rentals, memberships, and concessions. This earned income helps keep ticket prices accessible, supports free or low-cost youth outreach and school programs, and underwrites community presentations—using a social enterprise model to maintain vibrant year-round arts in a rural community.
resources.address: 209 St George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

resources.name: Lunenburg School of the Arts
resources.description: A community arts school that runs fee-based workshops and courses, operates a small gallery/shop featuring artist-made work, and rents its facility for events. Income from classes, merchandise sales, and rentals is reinvested to provide scholarships, bursaries, and free or low-cost community programming—showcasing a sustainable social enterprise model that broadens access to arts education for youth and adults.

resources.name: Centre for Craft Nova Scotia
resources.description: A sector organization that operates the Mary E. Black Gallery and The Craft Shop, while offering paid craft courses and studio rentals.
