resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Centre of Geographic Sciences (COGS)
resources.description: AGRG at NSCC’s Centre of Geographic Sciences partners with Nova Scotia municipalities, the provincial Emergency Management Office, and local fire departments to collect LiDAR/UAV/bathymetric data and produce high-resolution coastal flood and storm-surge models. The group shares maps, datasets, and training with planners and first responders so communities can integrate the modelling and historical flood records into land-use decisions, emergency routing, and infrastructure resilience planning.

resources.name: Bras d’Or Lakes Collaborative Environmental Planning Initiative (CEPI)
resources.organization: Unama’ki Institute of Natural Resources (UINR) – Secretariat Host
resources.description: CEPI brings together Mi’kmaq knowledge holders, Cape Breton University researchers, municipal planners, and provincial/federal agencies to share science, monitoring data, and traditional knowledge on storm impacts, water levels, and shoreline change across the Bras d’Or watershed. Through a Two-Eyed Seeing approach, CEPI maintains shared information and convenes partners so communities and emergency officials can apply both modelling and Mi’kmaw knowledge in flood preparedness, coastal planning, and habitat protection.

solutions.text: Advocacy and Coalition-Building for Policy Change: Form community coalitions to lobby municipal and provincial governments for stronger zoning, affordable insurance programs, infrastructure investments and incentives for resilient building practices.

resources.name: Coastal Protection and Climate Action
resources.description: Ecology Action Centre convenes coalitions of community groups, youth, small businesses, and municipal leaders across Nova Scotia to advocate for strong coastal setbacks, floodplain protections, and resilient land-use zoning. They lobby municipal councils and the Province to fully implement and strengthen the Coastal Protection Act, secure funding for stormwater and shoreline-resilience infrastructure, and create incentives and insurance reforms that reward resilient building practices.

resources.name: Law Reform and Policy Program
resources.description: East Coast Environmental Law supports coalitions of residents, Mi’kmaw communities, and municipalities with legal research, model bylaws, and submissions that press for stronger coastal protection, flood risk management, and climate-informed zoning. They coordinate public-interest interventions and workshops that influence provincial regulations and municipal planning, aiming to advance affordable, climate-resilient insurance frameworks and infrastructure investments.

resources.name: Climate Adaptation Program
resources.description: Clean Foundation brings together municipalities, provincial departments, and community organizations to assess climate risks and co-develop adaptation strategies, then advances policy recommendations to councils and the Province. Through these cross-sector coalitions, they advocate for resilient infrastructure funding, updated zoning and building standards, and incentive programs that help homeowners and businesses implement resilient practices that can also reduce insurance risk.
resources.address: 126 Chain Lake Drive, Suite 3B, Halifax, NS B3S 1A2

resources.name: Climate Change Program
resources.description: Coastal Action convenes municipalities, researchers, and residents on Nova Scotia’s South Shore to plan for sea-level rise, storm surge, and flooding, and to advocate for nature-based and engineered resilience investments. Their coalition-building informs stronger coastal zoning and stormwater bylaws, and they promote incentives and funding proposals that support resilient retrofits and shoreline protection best practices.
resources.address: 37 Tannery Road, Unit 2, Lunenburg, NS B0J 2C0

obstacles.title: International Student and Newcomer Retention
obstacles.description: Housing scarcity, work-permit uncertainty, and limited settlement supports reduce the likelihood of staying after graduation.

solutions.text: Community-led Graduate Housing Co-ops: Form non-profit, community-run housing co-operatives that reserve units for recent graduates and international students transitioning off-campus. Co-ops can offer below-market rents, flexible lease terms, and peer support to bridge the gap between student housing and private rentals.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Housing
resources.description: New Dawn Community Housing, operated by the community-development co‑operative New Dawn Enterprises, provides below‑market, non‑profit rental housing in Sydney and partners with its immigration and settlement services to support newcomers and recent graduates who are transitioning to independent living. While not exclusively for students, the community‑run governance model, flexible leasing, and on‑site wraparound supports (including employment and settlement navigation) implement the co‑op style solution by bridging the gap between campus housing and the private rental market for young people and international graduates.

resources.name: Affordable Housing Association of Nova Scotia (Development and Community Housing Support)
resources.organization: Affordable Housing Association of Nova Scotia
resources.description: AHANS is a province‑wide non‑profit that helps community groups plan, finance, and operate affordable housing, including co‑operative and non‑profit models that can reserve units for recent graduates and international students. By offering development services, property management support, and partnerships for tenant services, AHANS enables community‑led housing with below‑market rents, flexible tenancy approaches, and peer/community support—key features of the graduate housing co‑op solution.
resources.address: 2717 Gladstone Street, Suite 313, Halifax, NS B3K 0A4

resources.name: ISANS Housing & Settlement Supports
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides housing navigation, tenant education, and landlord partnerships for newcomers across Nova Scotia, helping international students and graduates secure stable, affordable rentals and connect with community‑run housing options. By linking clients to non‑profit and co‑operative housing providers and advocating for flexible leases and supportive tenancies, ISANS operationalizes the community‑led co‑op approach that eases the transition from campus housing to independent living.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Landlord Partnership & Trusted-Renter Program: Create a local certification program that trains landlords on fair practices for newcomers, connects them with screened international students and graduates, and offers landlords small incentives (e.g., vacancy advertising support or municipal tax rebates) to rent to recent graduates.

resources.name: Landlord Engagement Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Landlord Engagement Program partners with private landlords and property managers to reduce barriers for immigrants and international graduates seeking rental housing. The team delivers information sessions on Nova Scotia’s Residential Tenancies rules and culturally responsive renting, supports landlords one-on-one, and promotes vacancies to ISANS clients who have completed settlement and rental readiness supports. By connecting trained landlords with ready-to-rent newcomers and circulating listings through ISANS channels, the program functions as a local landlord partnership and trusted-renter model.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1H4

resources.name: YREACH Landlord Outreach and Newcomer Housing Support
resources.description: YREACH, the YMCA’s province-wide newcomer program, helps landlords across Nova Scotia rent successfully to immigrants and international students/graduates. Staff host landlord info sessions on tenant rights/responsibilities and inclusive practices, mediate expectations with culturally informed guidance, and match landlords with clients who have completed settlement and rental-readiness supports. YREACH also shares available units through its settlement networks—an advertising incentive for participating landlords—while providing ongoing support after move-in.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Off-Campus Housing and Landlord Listings (Places4Students)
resources.description: Cape Breton University’s Off-Campus Housing service partners with Places4Students to connect property owners with CBU’s student population, which includes many international students and recent graduates. The service provides rental guides and information on Nova Scotia tenancy standards, promotes landlord listings directly to students (an advertising incentive), and helps students prepare as responsible tenants. This combination of landlord outreach, education, and a curated listings channel advances a landlord-partnership and trusted-renter approach.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

resources.name: Off-Campus Housing: Landlord and Tenant Education & Listings
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Off-Campus Housing service connects landlords with Dal students and recent graduates, including many international students, through a curated listings platform and targeted outreach. It offers guides on fair rental practices and local tenancy law, hosts renting webinars, and provides landlords a direct advertising channel to the Dal community—an incentive to participate. By pairing education with matchmaking, the service supports a trusted-renter model that helps newcomers transition into stable housing.

solutions.text: Municipal Zoning for Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs): Advocate for and support municipal changes to permit and fast-track ADUs and secondary suites in neighbourhoods near campuses and employment hubs, increasing affordable rental stock suitable for young newcomers and graduates.

resources.name: Secondary and Backyard Suites (HRM)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality amended its planning rules to permit secondary suites and backyard suites as-of-right on most residential lots and provides a clear permitting pathway through Planning & Development. By reducing zoning barriers and clarifying approvals, HRM enables homeowners near universities (Dalhousie, Saint Mary’s, NSCC) and major employment nodes in Halifax and Dartmouth to add ADUs, increasing affordable rental options for students, newcomers, and recent graduates.

resources.name: Secondary and Garden Suites Policy
resources.description: The Town of Wolfville’s Municipal Planning Strategy and Land Use By-law allow secondary suites and garden suites on residential properties with a simplified development-permit process and parking flexibility in central areas. Adjacent to Acadia University and downtown employment, these permissions support homeowner-built ADUs that add gentle-density rentals suited to students, recent graduates, and newcomers within walking distance of campus and jobs.

resources.name: Secondary and Backyard Suites (Envision Kings)
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: Under the Envision Kings planning framework, the Municipality of the County of Kings permits secondary and backyard suites as-of-right in serviced growth centres and many residential zones, supported by standardized applications and staff guidance. This approach accelerates homeowner-led ADUs around employment hubs in Kentville, New Minas, and Coldbrook and in communities near Acadia University, adding diverse, attainable rentals for young workers and newcomers.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Secondary and Garden Suites — Land Use By-law
resources.description: The Town of Antigonish has adopted Land Use By-law provisions enabling secondary suites and garden suites across town, with clear checklists and a straightforward development permit process. Located near St. Francis Xavier University and downtown jobs, these ADU permissions make it easier for property owners to add modest rental units that support students, international graduates, and new residents seeking affordable housing.

solutions.text: Work-Permit & Immigration Navigation Clinics: Host regular community-run legal-navigation clinics (in partnership with local immigration lawyers, university legal clinics, and settlement agencies) to help graduates and newcomers understand PGWP timelines, employer-sponsored pathways, provincial nominee programs, and document preparation.

resources.name: Immigration Advising & PGWP Workshops
resources.description: Dalhousie’s International Centre runs recurring immigration clinics and workshops that explain Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) timelines, implied status, and next steps, along with pathways to permanent residence such as the Nova Scotia Nominee Program (NSNP) and the Atlantic Immigration Program. Regulated advisors provide one-on-one and group guidance on document preparation, maintaining status, and employer-supported options, helping students navigate forms and requirements and referring to settlement/legal partners when needed.

resources.name: International Student Immigration Advising
resources.description: Saint Mary’s International Centre provides regular immigration advising sessions and clinics focused on PGWP eligibility and timelines, work authorization during and after studies, and next steps toward PR through NSNP and other pathways. Advisors host workshops and drop-in hours to review documents, clarify application steps, and connect students with settlement agencies or immigration lawyers for complex cases, directly addressing work-permit uncertainty and retention.

resources.name: Immigration Information Sessions and One‑to‑One Support
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS offers ongoing immigration navigation sessions that cover employer-supported pathways, the Nova Scotia Nominee Program, and the Atlantic Immigration Program, along with orientation on PGWP-related steps for graduates. Settlement staff provide individualized document guidance, application checklists, and referrals, and host community clinics and info events with government and legal partners to help newcomers understand options and prepare strong submissions.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Newcomer Settlement and Immigration Support Clinics
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth – Centre for Immigrant Programs
resources.description: The YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs runs regular group workshops and drop-in navigation clinics that explain work permits, PGWP steps, and provincial nominee options, while settlement counselors offer one-on-one help with forms and supporting documents. The program connects clients to licensed immigration professionals for complex matters and collaborates with community partners to reduce barriers and improve newcomer retention in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Employer-to-Graduate Hiring Pledge: Encourage local employers to sign a pledge to create pathways for international students and recent grads (internships, co-ops, apprenticeship conversions) and to work with community groups on sponsorship or employer-specific work-permit documentation.

resources.name: Atlantic Immigration Program – Employer Designation (Nova Scotia)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: Nova Scotia Labour, Skills and Immigration designates local employers under the Atlantic Immigration Program (AIP), requiring them to commit to onboarding and settlement supports for international students and recent graduates. Designated employers can endorse candidates for employer-specific work permits and permanent residence, streamlining documentation and creating clear pathways from co-ops or internships into full-time roles.

resources.name: Employer Support Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Employer Support Services help Nova Scotia employers build hiring pathways for international students and newcomers through mentorships, work placements, and on-the-job training that often lead to permanent roles. The team advises employers on immigration options (e.g., AIP and employer-specific work permits), assists with required documentation, and connects companies with settlement partners—operationalizing an employer commitment to create and sustain pathways from graduation to long-term employment.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Graduate to Opportunity (GTO)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: GTO provides wage subsidies to Nova Scotia employers that hire recent post-secondary graduates, including eligible international graduates, encouraging the conversion of co-ops and internships into entry-level jobs. By lowering hiring risk and aligning with immigration pathways like AIP or provincial nominee streams, the program supports employer commitments that can lead to sustained employment and, where appropriate, employer-supported work-permit documentation.

resources.name: Co-op and Work-Integrated Learning (WIL)
resources.description: NSCC’s Co-op and WIL programs connect local employers with students—including many international learners—for structured co-ops, internships, and applied projects that frequently lead to full-time offers after graduation. Career Services helps employers design pathways from placement to employment and refers companies to immigrant-serving partners and provincial programs (e.g., AIP) when they wish to support employer-specific work-permit documentation to retain graduates in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Credential-Recognition & Skills Bridging Workshops: Organize community-led workshops and micro-credential programs with industry associations to help internationally trained graduates translate foreign credentials, gain local licenses, or complete short bridging courses required by employers.

resources.name: Career Pathways: Licensing & Credential Recognition
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers credential-recognition services and licensing pathway workshops that help internationally educated professionals understand regulatory requirements, map their foreign education to Nova Scotia standards, and prepare applications to licensing bodies. Through sector-specific bridging courses and short, employer-informed training developed with industry and regulators (e.g., engineering, health, IT), participants gain the local competencies and micro-credentials needed to meet hiring expectations.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Qualifying Program for Internationally Trained Dentists
resources.description: Dalhousie’s two-year Qualifying Program is a structured bridging pathway that enables internationally trained dentists to complete targeted coursework and intensive clinical training aligned with Canadian standards. Graduates earn the credentials required to sit for Canadian examinations and meet provincial licensing requirements, directly addressing credential translation and employer-recognized competencies.

resources.name: Practice Ready Assessment Nova Scotia (PRA-NS)
resources.organization: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Nova Scotia
resources.description: PRA-NS provides internationally educated physicians with a structured orientation and supervised clinical field assessment to demonstrate practice readiness in Nova Scotia. The program bridges foreign medical training to local licensure by evaluating competencies against provincial standards and guiding candidates through the credentialing and registration process.
resources.address: 1559 Brunswick Street, Suite 400, Halifax, NS B3J 2G1

resources.name: Competency Assessment Program (CAP) and Bridging for Internationally Educated Nurses
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health – Registered Nurses Professional Development Centre (RNPDC)
resources.description: RNPDC assesses the competencies of internationally educated nurses and provides individualized bridging, including simulation labs, targeted coursework, and supervised practice to meet Nova Scotia College of Nursing requirements. These tailored modules function as short bridging courses that translate prior learning into locally recognized competencies, supporting timely licensure and employability.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, 3rd Floor Bethune Building, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

solutions.text: Mentor Circles & Career Navigation Networks: Build peer and professional mentor networks pairing newcomers with local alumni, tradespeople, entrepreneurs and HR professionals to provide job search support, cultural onboarding, and introductions to local industry networks.

resources.name: Career Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS matches internationally trained newcomers with volunteer mentors who are established professionals in the same field. Mentors provide job search guidance, workplace culture insights, and facilitate warm introductions to their industry contacts and HR professionals, helping newcomers build local networks and navigate Nova Scotia’s labour market.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Connector Program – Halifax
resources.description: The Connector Program pairs newcomers and recent graduates with local business leaders, HR professionals, and entrepreneurs for one-on-one informational meetings. Each meeting leads to at least three warm referrals, rapidly expanding participants’ professional networks, providing cultural onboarding to local workplace norms, and opening access to hidden job opportunities in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Study and Stay – Nova Scotia
resources.description: This retention program supports final-year international students with career coaching, mentorship, and networking to transition into Nova Scotia’s workforce. Participants are matched with local mentors and HR professionals, join mentor circles, and receive targeted job search support and cultural onboarding, building strong ties to employers and alumni networks across the province.
resources.address: 1888 Brunswick Street, Suite 708, Halifax, NS B3J 3J8

solutions.text: Community Internship & Apprenticeship Hubs: Create a local hub that aggregates short-term paid placements across nonprofits, small businesses and trades, explicitly reserved for international students and recent grads to gain Canadian experience and references.

resources.name: Study and Stay Nova Scotia
resources.description: Study and Stay Nova Scotia is a province-wide retention program dedicated to international students in their final years of study and as recent graduates, helping them build careers and remain in the province. The program aggregates employer partners across nonprofits, small businesses, and growth sectors to provide paid work-integrated learning, internships, and mentorship, giving participants Canadian experience and local references while streamlining hiring for employers.
resources.address: 1888 Brunswick Street, Suite 806, Halifax, NS B3J 3J8

resources.name: Employment and Work Placement Services for Newcomers
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS serves immigrants and international student graduates by coordinating employer connections, mentorship, and wage-subsidized work placements across sectors, including nonprofits, small businesses, and trades. Acting as a central hub, ISANS matches candidates to short-term paid roles, provides pre-employment training and on-the-job support, and helps participants secure Canadian work experience and references to transition into longer-term employment.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program (including START incentives)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency operates the province’s central hub for paid, on-the-job apprenticeships across dozens of skilled trades, connecting apprentices with small businesses and trades employers. The agency registers apprentices (including newcomers and international graduates with valid work authorization) and provides employer incentives like the START program to expand short-term paid placements, enabling participants to gain Canadian experience, accumulate hours toward certification, and secure local references.

solutions.text: Microloan & Startup Incubator Programs for Newcomer Entrepreneurs: Establish community microloan funds and incubator spaces that offer mentorship, low-cost workspace, and seed funding to international alumni who want to start businesses, reducing the barrier of capital and local market knowledge.

resources.name: ISANS Business Development Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Business Development Services support immigrants and international graduates to start and grow businesses through one-on-one advising, market research, business planning, and mentorship. The team connects clients to financing, including microloans and small business loans through partner credit unions and Futurpreneur, while delivering workshops on regulations and the Nova Scotia market. By combining access to capital with tailored coaching and networks, ISANS reduces barriers to funding and local market knowledge for newcomer entrepreneurs.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: CEED Impact Loan
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: The CEED Impact Loan provides microloans to early-stage entrepreneurs in Nova Scotia, paired with mandatory training and ongoing advisory support to strengthen business fundamentals. Newcomer and international alumni founders are eligible and receive mentorship, workshops, and connections to local partners that demystify the Nova Scotia market. This blend of capital plus coaching functions as an incubator-like pathway that lowers financial and knowledge barriers for newcomer-led startups.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Volta Residency
resources.description: Volta Residency is an incubator that offers subsidized office space, mentorship from experienced founders and advisors, and structured programming for early-stage startups in Halifax. Newcomer-founded companies can access community events, advisor networks, and investor introductions; Volta also runs the Volta Cohort program that provides seed funding to selected startups. The residency’s low-cost workspace and wraparound supports help international alumni reduce barriers to launching and scaling businesses in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 1300, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

solutions.text: Settlement Peer-Host & Welcome Circles: Organize volunteer 'host family' or 'welcome circle' programs where local households and community groups support newcomers with short-term housing referrals, orientation to local services, and social connection during early settlement.

resources.name: Community Connections Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections Program matches newcomers and refugee families with local volunteer hosts, mentors, and conversation circles to build social networks and navigate life in Nova Scotia. Volunteers provide practical orientation to local services (health, transportation, schools, community resources) and share neighbourhood knowledge, including referrals and tips to find short‑term and longer‑term housing, helping newcomers settle confidently in their first months.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: YREACH Community Connections & Host
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth – YREACH (YMCA Settlement Services)
resources.description: YREACH engages volunteers across Nova Scotia to form welcoming circles and host-style matches that befriend newcomers, accompany them to appointments, and orient them to services in their communities. Volunteers help with practical settlement needs—including introductions to landlords, housing search referrals, and neighbourhood know‑how—while creating social connections that improve early settlement and retention.

resources.name: Community Support & Settlement Volunteers
resources.description: The Halifax Refugee Clinic mobilizes trained volunteers to act as settlement supports and welcome teams for refugee claimants, assisting with housing searches, furnishing setups, and orientation to local services. These volunteer circles provide social connection and practical guidance—from navigating transit and health care to connecting with community resources—reducing isolation during the critical early settlement period.
resources.address: 5590 North Street, Suite 203, Halifax, NS B3K 1N2

resources.name: International Student Peer Mentorship Program
resources.description: Dalhousie’s peer mentorship program pairs new international students with trained upper‑year student mentors who act as local guides and informal hosts. Mentors help newcomers understand campus and community services, share practical tips on neighbourhoods and housing searches, and build social connections that support students’ successful transition and longer‑term retention in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Childcare & Family Support Partnerships: Coordinate community-run affordable childcare cooperatives and referral networks aimed at making Nova Scotia more viable for international graduates with families, including shared-care models and employer-subsidized slots.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC) and Childcare Navigation
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides on-site Care for Newcomer Children (CNC) so parents can attend language, employment, and settlement programs, and its staff actively help families locate licensed child care, apply for provincial fee subsidies, and navigate waitlists. This coordinated referral support connects newcomer and international graduate families with affordable, community-based child care options across Nova Scotia. By reducing care barriers during the critical transition to work or further study, ISANS strengthens family stability and improves the likelihood that international graduates remain in the province.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Family Home Child Care Agency
resources.description: EHFRC operates a licensed Family Home Child Care Agency that recruits, supports, and monitors multiple home-based providers, creating a shared-care network with flexible hours and community-rooted affordability. Families are matched to regulated caregivers close to home or work and receive help accessing provincial child care subsidies, making licensed care more attainable for students, recent graduates, and newcomers in suburban and rural communities. This coordinated model expands affordable options beyond centre-based care and stabilizes child care access for families building their lives in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: MSVU Child Study Centre Early Learning Program
resources.description: The on-campus Child Study Centre offers licensed early learning and child care for children of MSVU students, staff, faculty, and the surrounding community, with priority access that supports student-parents, including international graduate students. Staff guide families to provincial affordability measures (e.g., fee reductions and subsidies) and coordinate schedules that align with academic and work commitments, reducing care-related barriers to study and employment. This employer-affiliated model helps retain international graduates by making family life more feasible while completing studies or starting careers in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: NSCECE Lab School Early Learning Centres
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE)
resources.description: NSCECE operates multiple non-profit, licensed lab school centres in Halifax that provide affordable, high-quality child care while training early childhood educators, strengthening the community-run child care ecosystem. Families receive support with placements and information on fee reductions and subsidies under Nova Scotia’s early learning and child care system, improving access for newcomers and recent graduates with children. By expanding regulated capacity and coordinating with community partners, the lab schools function as a practical hub that connects families to reliable care options needed to live, work, and study in the province.

solutions.text: Local Awareness Campaign & 'Stay in Nova Scotia' Ambassador Program: Run community campaigns featuring success stories of international graduates who stayed, plus an ambassador program where recent alumni travel to campus events and community fairs to showcase pathways, supports, and quality-of-life reasons to remain or return.

resources.name: Study and Stay Nova Scotia
resources.description: Study and Stay Nova Scotia supports international students to build careers and lives in the province by pairing them with mentors, hosting employer networking events, and delivering immigration pathway workshops. The program also spotlights alumni success stories and deploys recent graduates as peer ambassadors at campus events and community fairs to share first-hand experiences, available supports, and quality-of-life reasons to remain in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1888 Brunswick Street, Suite 405, Halifax, NS B3J 3J8

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: The Connector Program mobilizes volunteer business and community leaders as local ambassadors who meet one-on-one with international students and recent graduates, including at campus career events and community fairs, to introduce them to professional networks and job leads in Nova Scotia. It regularly shares participant success stories and provides practical guidance on pathways to work and settlement, reinforcing reasons to stay and anchoring newcomers in the local community.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 701, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Community Connections
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: Community Connections recruits local volunteers as ‘community ambassadors’ who mentor newcomers and international graduates, and often participate in outreach at schools, campuses, and community events to share real-life settlement stories and local supports. ISANS also runs public engagement and storytelling initiatives that highlight immigrant and international graduate successes, building awareness of Nova Scotia’s pathways, services, and quality of life to encourage graduates to stay.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Halifax Immigration Partnership (HIP)
resources.description: HIP coordinates a city-wide network of employers, post-secondary institutions, and community groups to improve newcomer retention, hosting ambassador-style panels and info sessions at campuses and community venues where recent alumni and immigrants share pathways to stay and thrive in Halifax. The partnership also develops and amplifies newcomer success stories and practical resources on housing, work permits, and settlement supports—functioning as an ongoing local awareness campaign to encourage international graduates to remain.

resources.name: YREACH – YMCA Newcomer Community Integration
resources.description: YREACH provides provincewide outreach that brings settlement staff and trained volunteer ambassadors to NSCC campuses, universities, and community fairs to present on work-permit options, immigration pathways, housing, and employment supports. The team highlights newcomer and international graduate success stories and connects participants to local services, creating a sustained awareness effort that showcases why building a life in Nova Scotia is attainable and rewarding.

obstacles.title: Regional Disparities
obstacles.description: Opportunities, services, and amenities are concentrated in HRM, leaving many rural and small communities behind.

solutions.text: Community Broadband Cooperatives: Form locally governed cooperatives to fund, build and manage high-speed internet infrastructure so rural homes, businesses and remote workers get reliable access comparable to HRM.

resources.name: Pictou County Internet Inc. (PCII)
resources.organization: Pictou County Internet Inc. (Municipality of Pictou County)
resources.description: PCII is a community-governed, municipally controlled broadband utility created by the Municipality of Pictou County to plan, finance, build, and operate high-speed internet in rural communities across the county. By owning local last‑mile and middle‑mile infrastructure and reinvesting locally, it functions much like a broadband cooperative—aligning governance with community needs and delivering fiber-based service to homes, farms, and small businesses that historically lacked reliable connectivity.

resources.name: Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative (IFNSI)
resources.description: IFNSI is the province’s program to extend high‑speed internet to underserved rural and small communities through locally led builds, including municipal and community-owned networks and First Nations partnerships. By structuring funding and delivery so communities can plan and govern solutions—and by supporting open-access and co‑operative-style ownership where feasible—the initiative enables locally controlled infrastructure that brings rural service up to HRM‑comparable speeds.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 300, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Rural Internet Financing Program
resources.description: This financing program provides long-term, low‑cost capital to Nova Scotia municipalities to fund community‑owned broadband infrastructure, including cooperative and municipal-utility models. By enabling local entities to finance fiber and fixed‑wireless builds under community governance, it directly supports the creation of sustainable, locally managed networks that improve rural connectivity and economic opportunity.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 1501, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

solutions.text: Multi-Service Community Hubs: Convert or build centrally located hubs that combine coworking, training, health outreach, daycare drop-in, library services and meeting space to create one-stop access to amenities.

resources.name: The North Grove (Community Food Centre & Family Centre)
resources.description: The North Grove is a multi-service community hub that combines a family resource centre with a community food centre to provide one-stop access to programs in a high-need neighbourhood. It offers early-years drop-in and parenting support, community meals and food access, employment and life-skills training, partner-led health and social service outreach, and indoor/outdoor meeting spaces. By co-locating services and programming, it reduces barriers for youth and families outside central Halifax and supports community wellbeing and skills development.

resources.name: Digby Community Hub
resources.description: Operated by the Digby Area Learning Association, the Digby Community Hub co-locates Nova Scotia Works employment services, adult learning, digital access, and youth programming under one roof. It provides classrooms, public computers and drop-in workspaces, workshops and training, and bookable meeting rooms, with partner agencies offering outreach clinics and information sessions. This centralized access point helps rural residents find training, jobs, and supports without traveling to larger centres.

resources.name: New Dawn Centre for Social Innovation
resources.description: The New Dawn Centre for Social Innovation is a community hub that houses coworking spaces, offices for nonprofits and social enterprises, training rooms, and event/meeting spaces. By co-locating entrepreneurship supports, arts and culture organizations, and social/health service providers in downtown Sydney, it creates a one-stop venue for youth, newcomers, and community members to access programs, mentorship, and services. Regular workshops, skills training, and partner-led clinics make it a practical rural alternative to centralized urban services.

resources.name: The Deanery Project
resources.description: The Deanery Project is a rural community hub offering training in sustainability, green building, arts and culture, and outdoor education, alongside coworking/remote work spaces and bookable meeting venues. It hosts community events, maker and skills workshops, youth programs, and partner-led wellness and active transportation initiatives, creating a single access point for learning, work, and community life on the Eastern Shore. By aggregating services and spaces in a remote area, it reduces travel barriers and supports local livelihoods.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

solutions.text: Local Transportation Networks: Organize community-run shuttle services, ride-shares, and demand-responsive transit linking small communities to regional job centres, schools and health facilities.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Eastern Shore
resources.description: MusGo Rider is a community-run, demand-responsive transportation co‑operative serving rural communities along the Eastern Shore. Riders pre-book door-to-door trips for work, school, medical appointments, and shopping, with connections to Halifax/Dartmouth and regional services. This directly implements community shuttle and ride-share style service that links small communities to job centres, health facilities, and education.

resources.name: BayRides Community Transit
resources.description: BayRides provides pre-booked, door-to-door community transit across the St. Margaret’s Bay area, connecting residents in small coastal and rural communities to Halifax Transit hubs, workplaces, schools, and medical services. The service operates flexible, demand-responsive shuttles that reduce transportation barriers and improve access to regional amenities.
resources.address: 5288 St. Margarets Bay Road, Upper Tantallon, NS B3Z 2H9

resources.name: Kings Transit Authority – Annapolis Valley Regional Bus Service
resources.description: Kings Transit operates regional bus routes that connect small towns and rural communities throughout the Annapolis Valley with major job centres, Acadia University in Wolfville, Valley Regional Hospital in Kentville, and commercial hubs in New Minas. While primarily fixed‑route, the system functions as a local transportation network that links dispersed communities to essential services and opportunities.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

solutions.text: Youth Apprenticeship and Placement Programs: Partner with local employers and tradespeople to create paid internships, apprenticeships and summer placements for youth across local industries to build careers at home.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship Program
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s program places high school and post-secondary youth in paid summer internships with municipalities, Mi’kmaw communities, non-profits, and private-sector employers across Nova Scotia. Interns gain hands-on experience in environmental projects while working at host organizations in both rural and urban communities, directly creating local paid placements that build skills and careers at home.

resources.name: Co-operative Education Incentive (CEI)
resources.organization: Province of Nova Scotia — Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: CEI provides wage subsidies to Nova Scotia employers to hire post-secondary co-op students for paid work terms in a wide range of industries. By lowering the cost to take on students, the program expands quality paid placements across the province—supporting employers in rural and small communities as well as HRM and helping youth build local career pathways.

resources.name: START Program (Employment and Apprenticeship Incentive)
resources.organization: Province of Nova Scotia — Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: The START Program offers financial incentives to Nova Scotia employers to hire unemployed or underemployed job seekers, including creating apprenticeship positions in the skilled trades. This supports paid, on-the-job training and long-term employment across urban and rural communities, helping youth start and continue careers with local businesses close to home.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding Inc.)
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a collaborative NSCC program with Irving Shipbuilding that recruits cohorts (including youth from underrepresented communities) into paid, work-integrated training that leads to registered apprenticeships in trades like welding and metal fabrication. Students receive technical training at NSCC and transition into on-the-job placements with Halifax Shipyard and supply-chain employers, creating clear, local career pathways in Nova Scotia’s marine industry.

solutions.text: Micro-Grant and Seed Funding Pools: Establish small, locally-managed grants to support startups, social enterprises, arts projects and community initiatives that keep investment and jobs local.

resources.name: Spark Nova Scotia
resources.description: Spark Nova Scotia is a province-wide startup competition that provides non-dilutive seed funding and mentorship to early-stage entrepreneurs across regional streams (e.g., Cape Breton, Northern, South Shore, Valley, Western). These small grants help founders validate ideas and build companies where they live, keeping investment and jobs in rural and small communities. By running regional cohorts with local partners, Spark decentralizes support beyond HRM and strengthens community-based innovation ecosystems.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 1101, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

resources.name: CBRM Community Grants Program
resources.description: The CBRM Community Grants Program offers small, locally managed grants to non-profit groups for community development, arts and culture, recreation, and social inclusion projects across Cape Breton communities. These micro-grants enable grassroots organizations to hire locally, run programs, and improve amenities without leaving the island. By targeting community-led initiatives, the program keeps funds circulating in neighbourhoods outside HRM and builds local capacity.

resources.name: Municipality of the County of Inverness Community Grants Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Inverness
resources.description: This annual program provides small grants to volunteer groups, social enterprises, and cultural organizations across the County of Inverness. Funding supports local projects—from festivals to community services—that stimulate rural economies, sustain jobs, and enhance quality of life in smaller communities. Administered locally, the program ensures decision-making and investment remain in the county.
resources.address: 375 Main Street, Port Hood, NS B0E 2W0

resources.name: Downtown Truro Partnership Façade Improvement Program
resources.description: The Façade Improvement Program provides small matching grants to downtown businesses and property owners to upgrade storefronts, signage, and accessibility. These micro-investments stimulate local spending on trades and design services, support small business resilience, and enhance the appeal of a rural commercial core. By keeping capital improvements and contracts local, the program sustains jobs and attracts foot traffic and new ventures in Truro.

resources.name: Ulnooweg Indigenous Communities Foundation Community Grants
resources.description: Ulnooweg Indigenous Communities Foundation provides community grants to Mi'kmaq communities and Indigenous-led organizations across Nova Scotia and Atlantic Canada for culture, youth, entrepreneurship, and community well-being projects. These micro-grants are managed in close partnership with communities, enabling locally driven initiatives that create employment, support Indigenous entrepreneurs and artists, and build capacity where people live. The approach keeps resources in Mi'kma'ki’s rural communities and addresses regional inequities by investing directly at the community level.

solutions.text: Pop-Up Business Incubators: Host temporary incubator spaces in vacant storefronts for entrepreneurs to test products/services, receive mentoring, and attract customers without long-term rent commitments.

resources.name: Downtown Truro Pop-Up Shop Program
resources.description: Downtown Truro Partnership collaborates with local landlords to activate vacant storefronts as short-term pop-up retail incubators, typically for 1–3 months. Entrepreneurs get a low-risk way to test products and services, receive promotional support and mentorship through local partners (e.g., CBDC and regional economic development groups), and build a customer base with the goal of transitioning to permanent tenancy if viable.

resources.name: Kentville Pop-Up Retail Incubator
resources.description: The Kentville Business Community works with property owners to provide short-term use of empty Main Street storefronts for emerging businesses. Participants gain a turn-key space to pilot offerings without long leases, plus connections to local mentors and business supports (including the Acadia Entrepreneurship Centre and CBDC), helping rural founders validate demand and convert to longer-term leases in the downtown.

solutions.text: Shared Equipment and Maker Spaces: Create communal workshops with tools, machinery and digital fabrication equipment that small businesses, artisans and students can access affordably.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: A public makerspace featuring 3D printers, sewing machines, vinyl cutters, and other fabrication tools that residents can book for free or low cost. It enables entrepreneurs, students, and artists to prototype products, create custom items, and learn digital fabrication skills with staff support—making advanced equipment accessible to people who can’t afford their own setups.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: A community tool-lending library offering affordable memberships to borrow hundreds of hand and power tools, plus access to workshops and skill-building sessions. By sharing equipment and providing a communal workshop environment, it reduces startup costs for small businesses, tradespeople, and makers who need occasional access to specialized tools.

resources.name: Creative Lab (Truro Library)
resources.description: A library-based makerspace with 3D printing, vinyl cutting, and creative tech kits that community members can book and use with guidance from staff. It provides affordable access to digital fabrication and creative tools for youth, students, and small business owners in Colchester-East Hants, supporting prototyping, custom production, and skills development.

resources.name: Innovation Lab (Margaret Hennigar Public Library)
resources.description: A community makerspace offering equipment such as 3D printers and creative design tools at the Bridgewater library, with orientations and bookable sessions. It enables local entrepreneurs, artisans, and students on the South Shore to experiment, prototype, and fabricate without high upfront costs for equipment.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

resources.name: Creative Studio (James McConnell Memorial Library)
resources.description: A public creative studio featuring 3D printers, sewing machines, and digital cutting tools that community members in Cape Breton can access through appointments and programs. It expands affordable access to maker equipment for students, artists, and small businesses in Sydney and surrounding communities, helping them learn skills and produce prototypes or small runs.

solutions.text: Local Skills and Digital Literacy Training: Run regular community-led workshops on digital skills, trades, business management and remote work practices in partnership with colleges and employers.

resources.name: ISANS Employment Services and Business Development
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers ongoing digital literacy, job search, and career-readiness workshops along with entrepreneurship training for newcomers, offered in-person and online to reach communities across Nova Scotia. Programs include employer-led info sessions, mentoring and the Connector Program, directly linking participants to local employers and remote work opportunities while building practical digital and business skills. This implements the solution by providing community-accessible training and employer partnerships that help young people and newcomers build careers in both established trades and emerging industries.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: NSCC Continuing Education & Customized Training
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) — Burridge Campus
resources.description: NSCC offers short courses, micro-credentials, and customized community training in digital skills, trades fundamentals/safety, and small business management, delivered at campuses and via outreach in rural communities. Developed with local employers and industry partners, these workshops help residents upskill for in-demand roles and succeed in remote or hybrid work. This implements the solution by aligning community-led learning with employer needs and providing practical, accessible training across the province.

resources.name: PARL Tech Help and Digital Literacy Workshops
resources.description: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library branches host free, recurring Tech Help sessions and digital literacy workshops (devices, internet safety, e-services, basic productivity tools), often co-hosted with community groups and employment services. Sessions support job seekers, entrepreneurs, and learners with practical digital skills needed for online job search, remote work, and business operations. This implements the solution by providing community-led, locally accessible training that reduces rural digital gaps and connects participants with partner colleges and employers through info sessions and events.

resources.name: Centre for Women in Business Training & Advisory Programs
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business delivers regular workshops and cohort-based programs on digital marketing, e-commerce, financial management, and leading remote teams, offered province-wide in partnership with CBDCs, universities, and local employers. Programming is hybrid and often hosted with regional partners to ensure access for rural and small communities. This implements the solution by providing community-driven business and digital skills training that helps entrepreneurs and professionals build sustainable careers across Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Affordable Housing Initiatives: Assemble community land trusts, re-purpose vacant buildings and support co-housing models to increase affordable options for young families and workers.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia – Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia partners with working low- to moderate-income families to build or rehabilitate homes and provide affordable, geared-to-income mortgages. By lowering entry barriers to homeownership and occasionally renovating existing properties, Habitat directly expands affordable housing options for young families and workers across communities beyond HRM.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Housing and Adaptive Reuse Projects
resources.description: New Dawn Enterprises develops and stewards affordable rental housing in Cape Breton while adaptively reusing underutilized and heritage buildings for community benefit. By maintaining community-owned housing and converting vacant properties into livable spaces, New Dawn increases affordable options for local workers and families in a rural region often overlooked by major developments.

resources.name: Cornwallis Park Housing (Former CFB Cornwallis Redevelopment)
resources.description: Annapolis Basin Development Inc. repurposes former military base buildings at Cornwallis Park into rental apartments and community facilities, turning vacant structures into attainable housing in rural Nova Scotia. This adaptive reuse increases the local supply of affordable units for families, newcomers, and workers, helping counter regional disparities outside HRM.
resources.address: 268 Marine Drive, Cornwallis Park, NS B0S 1H0

resources.name: Treehouse Village Ecohousing
resources.description: Treehouse Village Ecohousing is a resident-led cohousing community in Bridgewater that offers private, efficient homes clustered around shared amenities (a common house, guest rooms, and communal spaces) to reduce housing costs and foster mutual support. By advancing a co-housing model outside HRM, it creates new, community-oriented and more affordable living options for families and remote or local workers in the South Shore region.

solutions.text: Regional Mentorship Networks: Pair experienced local entrepreneurs, artists and tradespeople with youth and new residents for career guidance, business support and retention.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS matches internationally trained professionals and immigrant entrepreneurs with established Nova Scotia mentors in the same field for career guidance, networking, and business advice. The program supports newcomers across the province (including rural communities through virtual matching), helping them connect with local employers, entrepreneurs, and tradespeople to secure meaningful work and stay in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YREACH Host Program
resources.description: The YMCA’s YREACH Host Program pairs newcomers with local volunteer hosts and professional contacts across many rural and small communities in Nova Scotia to build social and career networks. Through informational interviews, introductions to local entrepreneurs and employers, and community orientation, it provides practical mentorship that supports employment, business start-up, and long-term retention outside HRM.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: COVE Mentoring Program
resources.description: COVE connects ocean-sector startups, students, and early-career professionals with seasoned industry leaders, engineers, and tradespeople for one-on-one and cohort-based mentorship. By linking emerging companies and talent from across Nova Scotia with local experts, it accelerates business growth, provides career guidance, and strengthens regional retention in blue-economy communities beyond HRM.

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic
resources.organization: Rowe School of Business, Dalhousie University
resources.description: CDL–Atlantic runs a mentorship-driven venture program that pairs early-stage founders (including youth-led and newcomer-led startups) with experienced entrepreneurs, investors, and domain experts for intensive guidance and business scaling. Hosted at Dalhousie University, it draws mentors and companies from across Nova Scotia, providing structured goal-setting, networking, and support that helps founders build viable ventures and remain in the region.

solutions.text: Local Procurement and Buy-Local Campaigns: Encourage municipalities, schools and institutions to prioritize local suppliers and contractors to grow a stable market for rural businesses.

resources.name: Social Procurement Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Social Procurement Program embeds local economic benefits and community outcomes into how the municipality buys goods and services. Through evaluation criteria, supplier outreach, and targeted opportunities for SMEs and diverse local vendors, HRM encourages departments and prime contractors to work with Nova Scotia-based suppliers. This helps create steady demand for rural businesses that can supply municipal projects, aligning with buy-local goals while complying with trade agreements.

resources.name: Farm to School Nova Scotia
resources.description: Farm to School Nova Scotia supports schools to procure and serve more locally grown and produced foods through grants, toolkits, and connections to nearby farmers and food hubs. By helping cafeterias and meal programs source from local suppliers, the initiative creates reliable institutional markets for rural producers and food processors. It builds capacity in school communities to prioritize local procurement, strengthening regional food economies and keeping dollars in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Purchasing and Tendering Policy (Local Vendor Support)
resources.description: The Town of Bridgewater’s purchasing policy encourages fair, open competition while recognizing the value of local suppliers where permitted by trade agreements. Through procurement practices and vendor engagement, the Town helps ensure municipal departments consider Nova Scotia-based businesses for goods, services, and construction. This approach channels stable public-sector demand to local and regional suppliers, supporting rural enterprises on the South Shore.

solutions.text: Cultural and Place-Making Events: Organize festivals, markets, public art, and storytelling nights that celebrate local identity, attract visitors, and make communities more appealing places to live.

resources.name: KitchenFest!
resources.organization: Colaisde na Gàidhlig / The Gaelic College
resources.description: KitchenFest! is a week-long, island-wide festival showcasing Cape Breton’s Gaelic music, dance, and storytelling through community ceilidhs, concerts, and workshops in rural halls and venues. By activating local spaces across smaller communities, it celebrates place-based identity, draws visitors beyond urban centres, and creates vibrant gathering spots that make these communities more attractive for residents and youth.
resources.address: 51779 Cabot Trail, St. Anns, NS B0C 1H0

resources.name: Lunenburg Folk Harbour Festival
resources.description: This multi-day waterfront festival presents folk, traditional, and roots music on outdoor and indoor stages throughout historic Lunenburg, complemented by workshops, sessions, and community events. It animates public spaces, elevates local culture, and brings visitors to a small town on the South Shore, strengthening year-round vibrancy and economic opportunity beyond HRM.

resources.name: Paint the Town (Annapolis Royal Plein Air Art Festival)
resources.description: Paint the Town is a two-day plein air festival where artists create works throughout Annapolis Royal’s streets, gardens, and waterfront, culminating in public art displays and live auctions. The event transforms the town into an open-air gallery, drawing visitors to local businesses and public spaces while celebrating regional identity and making the community a more compelling place to live and return to.
resources.address: 396 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

resources.name: Festival de la Mi-Carême (Mi-Carême Cultural Program)
resources.organization: La Société Mi-Carême (Centre de la Mi-Carême)
resources.description: Rooted in Acadian tradition, Festival de la Mi-Carême features mask-making, storytelling nights, parades, and exhibitions that animate Grand-Étang and neighbouring communities each spring. By bringing residents and visitors together in shared cultural spaces and public celebrations, it strengthens local identity, supports artists and artisans, and boosts rural cultural tourism.
resources.address: 51 Old Cabot Trail, Grand-Étang, NS B0E 1L0

resources.name: Daily Ceilidhs & Community Events
resources.description: The Celtic Music Interpretive Centre hosts daily live ceilidhs, dance events, and cultural workshops that celebrate Cape Breton’s musical heritage in the rural community of Judique. These ongoing gatherings activate a community hub, attract visitors year-round, and provide opportunities for local musicians and youth to participate in and sustain place-based culture.

solutions.text: Mobile Service Delivery: Deploy mobile clinics, library vans, legal aid and skills trainers that visit remote communities on scheduled routes to deliver essential services.

resources.name: Mobile Primary Care Clinics
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health operates Mobile Primary Care Clinics that travel to communities across the province on scheduled dates to provide walk-in and appointment-based care, such as assessments, prescription renewals, testing, and referrals. By bringing primary health services directly to rural and underserviced areas, the clinics reduce travel barriers and wait times for residents outside Halifax Regional Municipality. This mobile model helps close regional gaps in access to essential healthcare.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Breast Screening Program – Mobile Mammography Unit
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Breast Screening Program operates a mobile digital mammography unit that visits rural and remote communities on a rotating schedule to provide breast cancer screening. Partnering with local community sites, the unit delivers preventive care without requiring patients to travel long distances to urban centres. This mobile service increases early detection and supports equitable access to essential diagnostics.

resources.name: Mobile Outreach Clinic (Dentistry)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Faculty of Dentistry operates a fully equipped mobile dental clinic that travels to underserved communities and long-term care facilities across Nova Scotia to provide exams, cleanings, fillings, and urgent care. Staffed by dental professionals and supervised students, the clinic removes transportation and cost barriers for rural residents. This mobile delivery expands access to essential oral health services beyond urban centres.

resources.name: Cape Breton Regional Library Bookmobile
resources.description: The Cape Breton Regional Library Bookmobile functions as a traveling library branch with scheduled stops in rural communities, lending books and other materials and providing access to programs and digital resources. The service offers Wi‑Fi and basic tech help, connecting residents to information and learning opportunities where fixed branches are distant. By delivering library services on wheels, it reduces regional disparities in access to education and cultural amenities.

solutions.text: Regional Education Partnerships: Partner with regional colleges and schools to offer satellite courses, apprenticeships and credit programs locally, reducing the need for relocation to HRM.

resources.name: NSCC Strait Area Campus — Apprenticeship Technical Training and Trades Programs
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College’s Strait Area Campus delivers trades certificates, diplomas, and in-school apprenticeship technical training in partnership with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and local employers. The campus also works with nearby high schools and regional education centres to offer dual-credit and pathway options so students can earn post-secondary credits without relocating to Halifax. This place-based delivery model brings satellite courses and hands-on labs to Port Hawkesbury, aligning training with local industry needs in marine, energy, and skilled trades.
resources.address: 226 Reeves Street, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 2A2

resources.name: Université Sainte-Anne — Satellite Campuses and Community-Based Programs
resources.description: Université Sainte-Anne operates multiple satellite campuses (e.g., Church Point main campus, Halifax, Tusket, and Petit-de-Grat) and partners with francophone schools and community organizations to deliver credit programs, upgrading, and continuing education close to home. By bringing post-secondary courses, professional training, and language programs to rural Acadian communities, students can start or complete credentials locally rather than moving to HRM. These regional offerings are coordinated with local employers and school boards to match community demand and support local employment.

resources.name: Dalhousie Family Medicine — South West Nova (Yarmouth) Distributed Residency Program
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Department of Family Medicine
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Department of Family Medicine partners with Nova Scotia Health and regional hospitals to deliver residency training sites outside HRM, including the South West Nova program based at Yarmouth Regional Hospital. Residents complete accredited, hands-on clinical education and academic seminars locally, supported by community preceptors and interprofessional teams. This distributed model functions like an apprenticeship in clinical practice, keeping learners in rural communities while building local healthcare capacity.

solutions.text: Community-Owned Renewable Energy Projects: Develop small-scale community wind, solar or biomass projects that reduce utility costs, create local revenue and provide jobs.

resources.name: Mahone Bay Community Solar Garden
resources.organization: Town of Mahone Bay Electric Utility
resources.description: The Town of Mahone Bay Electric Utility developed a subscriber-based community solar garden that lets residents and businesses purchase shares and receive credits on their municipal electric bills, directly reducing local utility costs. Because it is owned and operated by the community utility, revenues stay in Mahone Bay and support local employment through construction, operations, and maintenance. As a small-town project outside HRM, it demonstrates how community-owned renewables can strengthen rural economies and keep energy dollars local.
resources.address: 493 Main Street, Mahone Bay, NS B0J 2E0

resources.name: Berwick Community Solar Garden
resources.description: The Berwick Electric Commission operates a community solar garden where customers subscribe to panels and receive bill credits for the energy produced, lowering electricity costs for local households and businesses. Owned by the municipal utility, the project keeps generation revenues within the town and creates local jobs for installation and ongoing maintenance. This community-scale renewable initiative helps a rural Nova Scotia community build resilient, affordable energy outside HRM.

resources.name: Antigonish Community Solar Garden
resources.description: The Town of Antigonish Electric Utility is implementing a community solar garden that allows utility customers to purchase subscriptions and receive credits on their bills, reducing monthly energy expenses. As a municipally owned project, it keeps profits and decision-making in the community, supporting local jobs and training while expanding clean energy in a small university town outside HRM. The initiative diversifies the local economy and demonstrates how community-owned renewables can attract and retain young people through lower living costs and green jobs.

resources.name: Ellershouse Wind Farm
resources.organization: Alternative Resource Energy Authority (Towns of Antigonish, Berwick, and Mahone Bay)
resources.description: Ellershouse Wind Farm is owned by the Alternative Resource Energy Authority (AREA), a partnership of the Towns of Antigonish, Berwick, and Mahone Bay, supplying locally generated wind power to their municipal electric utilities. Community ownership keeps energy revenues within these rural towns, supports operations and maintenance jobs, and helps stabilize electricity rates for local customers. The project exemplifies small-scale, community-owned wind generation that reduces costs and strengthens economic opportunities outside HRM.
resources.address: 493 Main Street, Mahone Bay, NS B0J 2E0

solutions.text: Childcare Co-operatives and Shared Care: Support parent-led childcare co-ops and shared caregiver networks to expand affordable childcare options enabling parents to work locally.

resources.name: East Hants Family Home Child Care Agency
resources.description: A licensed family home child care agency that recruits, approves, and supports home-based caregivers across East Hants, creating a coordinated network of local child care options. By connecting families with vetted providers in their own communities and offering training, monitoring, and subsidies where eligible, the agency expands affordable, flexible child care so parents can work locally. This shared caregiver network model directly addresses rural access gaps outside HRM.

resources.name: Co-operative Development Services (Childcare Co-op Support)
resources.description: This province-wide program helps community and parent groups form co-operatives, providing feasibility support, incorporation guidance, governance training, and access to financing tools. Parents looking to launch childcare co-operatives receive technical assistance to design member-led, affordable models that reflect local needs—especially valuable in rural communities with limited centre-based care. By enabling co-op start-up and sustainability, the program grows parent-led childcare capacity across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 90 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: YMCA Family Home Child Care (FHCC)
resources.description: The YMCA operates a licensed Family Home Child Care agency that recruits and supports home-based educators, creating a network of small, neighbourhood programs across HRM and nearby communities. Families are matched to approved caregivers, with ongoing quality assurance and educator training, making child care more accessible and affordable outside traditional centres. This shared caregiver network model increases options for parents to work and study locally.

solutions.text: Flexible Zoning and Pop-Up Permits: Advocate for municipal changes that allow flexible use of properties (pop-up shops, home-based businesses, live-work spaces) to stimulate local entrepreneurship.

resources.name: Town of Wolfville Vending By-law (Temporary Vending Permits)
resources.description: Wolfville’s Vending By-law issues temporary permits for mobile vendors, markets, and special-event pop-ups, allowing short-term commercial use of sidewalks, parks, and other public spaces. Paired with the Town’s land use by-law that supports home occupations and mixed-use in the downtown, it enables live-work and home-based entrepreneurship, creating low-barrier ways for young founders to test and grow businesses outside HRM.

resources.name: Municipality of the County of Kings Land Use By-law (Home-Based Business & Live/Work Provisions)
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: Kings County’s Land Use By-law permits tiered home-based businesses across rural and village areas and allows mixed-use/live-work arrangements in designated growth centres. Streamlined development permits let residents operate studios, services, and small retail from homes or flexible commercial spaces, supporting pop-up and seasonal entrepreneurship in smaller communities.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Town of Lunenburg Vending By-law and Sidewalk Café Permits
resources.description: Lunenburg issues seasonal vending and sidewalk café permits that temporarily convert portions of streets and public spaces into commercial use, enabling pop-up retail, artisans, and food vendors. Its planning framework also permits home occupations in residential zones, supporting live-work setups that let residents start and operate small businesses locally.

resources.name: Cape Breton Regional Municipality Mobile Vending and Temporary Event Permits
resources.description: CBRM licenses mobile vendors and issues temporary event permits that enable pop-up retail and food operations on public property across urban and rural communities in Cape Breton. The municipality’s land use policies also allow home occupations, supporting flexible live-work entrepreneurship and lowering barriers for small business starts outside Halifax.

solutions.text: Tourism and Creative Economy Networks: Form regional networks linking artists, cultural producers and tourism operators to package experiences that draw visitors and support year-round employment.

resources.name: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design convenes artisans across Cape Breton and works with Destination Cape Breton and tourism operators to develop studio tours, hands-on workshops, and retail/gallery routes that attract visitors to rural communities year-round. By coordinating marketing (maps, itineraries), training, and experience packaging among artists, cultural producers, accommodations, and tour providers, the Centre functions as a regional creative economy network that drives visitation beyond peak season and creates sustained income opportunities for makers.

resources.name: Canada’s Musical Coast
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Inverness
resources.description: Canada’s Musical Coast is a county-wide initiative that connects musicians, cultural venues, festivals, artisans, and tourism operators along Cape Breton’s west coast to promote live music and cultural experiences as travel draws. The program coordinates joint marketing, event calendars, and experience packages (e.g., ceilidhs paired with local food, outdoor activities, and accommodations), building a regional network that channels visitors to multiple rural communities and supports year-round creative employment.
resources.address: 375 Main Street, Port Hood, NS B0E 2W0
