resources.name: Ship’s Company Theatre
resources.description: Ship’s Company Theatre partners with local museums, guides, restaurants, and inns in Parrsboro and the Fundy Shore to bundle theatre performances with cultural and nature-based experiences (e.g., fossil tours, tidal viewing, and dining packages). By collaborating with regional tourism operators and artists to co-create marketable itineraries and shoulder-season programming, the theatre anchors a local creative tourism network that boosts rural visitation and sustains employment beyond the summer.
resources.address: 18 Lower Main Street, Parrsboro, NS B0M 1S0

resources.name: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts collaborates with wineries, farms, accommodations, and tourism operators in the Annapolis Valley to create arts-based experiences and packages (e.g., outdoor theatre with Two Planks and a Passion, workshops, and culinary pairings) that draw visitors to a rural area. Acting as a hub that links artists and cultural producers with the tourism sector, the Centre develops year-round programming and itineraries that broaden regional appeal and provide sustained work for artists and local businesses.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

solutions.text: Community Transportation Volunteer Programs: Coordinate volunteer driver programs and ride-matching platforms to help residents access services and employment when public transit isn't available.

resources.name: East Hants Community Rider
resources.description: East Hants Community Rider coordinates a volunteer driver program that provides door-to-door rides for rural residents to get to work, training, healthcare, and essential services when public transit is limited or unavailable. Riders are matched to vetted volunteer drivers through a centralized dispatch and scheduling system, making it possible to connect isolated communities with employment and services across East Hants and beyond. The program reduces transportation barriers for youth and families, supporting equitable access to opportunities outside of Halifax.

resources.name: Wheels of Hope (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Wheels of Hope is a province-wide volunteer driver program that helps Nova Scotians travel to cancer-related medical appointments when they cannot access public transit. The service uses a centralized intake and ride-matching system to connect clients with volunteer drivers, enabling residents from rural and small communities to reach healthcare services that are often concentrated in Halifax and regional centres. By reducing travel barriers, the program supports quality of life and continuity of care for people living outside major transit corridors.

solutions.text: Local Data & Opportunity Mapping: Collect and publish community-level data on jobs, housing, broadband and services so leaders can identify gaps, target investments and measure progress.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Open Data Portal
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Open Data Portal provides free public access to province-wide datasets, including geospatial layers and APIs on employment, demographics, housing and property, infrastructure, and public services. By publishing community-level and mapping-ready data, it enables municipal leaders, nonprofits, and economic developers to identify gaps, target investments in underserved areas, and measure progress over time.
resources.address: One Government Place, 1700 Granville Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1X5

resources.name: Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative (IFNSI)
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia’s Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative publishes public broadband coverage maps, community-by-community project updates, and service availability information. This mapping identifies unserved and underserved rural areas, guides investment decisions with ISPs and governments, and tracks progress toward universal high‑speed access—directly addressing regional disparities in digital connectivity.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Halifax Open Data
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Open Data program releases geospatial data and interactive maps covering land use, development permits, transit routes, recreation and community service locations, Wi‑Fi hotspots, and more. Community‑level data enables planners, service providers, and community groups to visualize neighborhood conditions, identify service gaps, and prioritize investments that improve quality of life across HRM.

resources.name: CBRM Open Data Portal
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Municipality’s Open Data portal provides GIS layers and map applications for land use, infrastructure, transportation, civic addresses, and municipal service locations. These community‑level datasets support local governments, businesses, and nonprofits to pinpoint underserved communities in Cape Breton, target economic development and service investments, and monitor progress over time.

solutions.text: Inter-Community Collaboration Forums: Host regular forums between neighboring towns and rural areas to coordinate economic development, share resources and pursue joint grant opportunities.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Western Hub (Yarmouth)
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic’s Western Hub convenes regular cross-municipal forums, roundtables, and cohort sessions that bring together leaders from Yarmouth, Digby, and Shelburne counties, along with rural communities and First Nations partners. These gatherings coordinate regional economic development priorities, share resources like innovation spaces and mentorship networks, and help communities collaborate on joint funding proposals to provincial and federal programs.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Northern Hub (New Glasgow)
resources.description: IGNITE’s Northern Hub hosts ongoing inter-community collaboration forums and project working groups across Pictou, Antigonish, and Guysborough, connecting municipal staff, local businesses, nonprofits, and post-secondary partners. These sessions align regional economic initiatives, enable shared use of resources and facilities, and support the development of joint grant applications for innovation, workforce, and entrepreneurship projects.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3R2

resources.name: Cape Breton Partnership – Regional Collaboration & Sector Roundtables
resources.description: The Cape Breton Partnership facilitates island-wide collaboration by hosting recurring regional forums and sector roundtables that include municipal units from across Cape Breton–Unama’ki, rural communities, and Mi’kmaw communities. These convenings coordinate economic development strategies, foster cross-community resource sharing, and help partners pursue joint funding for infrastructure, workforce, and industry diversification projects.

resources.name: Annapolis Valley Chamber – Regional Economic Forums
resources.description: The Annapolis Valley Chamber organizes regular regional forums and policy dialogues that bring together municipalities, towns, and rural communities across the Valley to coordinate on economic development priorities. These events facilitate shared planning, connect partners to pooled services and business supports, and help stakeholders collaborate on joint funding proposals for regional initiatives.

solutions.text: Volunteer-Led Welcome and Retention Programs: Create local welcome teams that help new residents and returning youth connect to housing, jobs, social groups and mentoring to encourage settling locally.

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: The Cape Breton Welcome Network mobilizes local volunteer Welcome Groups and Ambassadors across communities on Cape Breton Island to greet and support newcomers and returnees. Volunteers host meet-ups, share practical information on housing, schools, transportation, and recreation, and make introductions to employers, mentors, and community groups to help people settle and stay. This volunteer-led model directly addresses rural retention by building social ties and pathways to jobs and services outside HRM.

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: The Connector Program links recent graduates, newcomers, international students, and returning youth with volunteer ‘Connectors’—local business and community leaders—who provide warm introductions to three contacts in their networks. These one-on-one meetings open doors to job leads, mentorship, and professional associations while also pointing participants to community groups and services. By expanding networks and a sense of belonging, the program helps participants build careers and put down roots in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Community Connections (Volunteers & Mentorship)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections program recruits and trains community volunteers to act as host matches, conversation partners, and settlement mentors for newcomers, helping them navigate housing searches, transit, schools, and local services. It also offers professional mentorship and networking activities that connect participants with employers and industry groups across Nova Scotia. These volunteer-led supports foster social belonging and job pathways that encourage newcomers and returning youth to settle locally.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Adaptive Reuse of Vacant Spaces: Convert underused municipal or commercial buildings into affordable studios, small business units, training centres or youth housing to revitalize main streets.

resources.name: Eltuek Arts Centre
resources.description: Eltuek Arts Centre converted the former Holy Angels High School—an underused institutional site in downtown Sydney—into a multi-tenant arts and culture hub with affordable studios, shared production spaces, and community programming. By providing low-cost workspaces and venues for artists, creative entrepreneurs, and youth-focused initiatives, it brings daily activity and foot traffic back to George Street. This adaptive reuse strengthens the local creative economy and revitalizes the main street core outside HRM.

resources.name: Community Credit Union Business Innovation Centre
resources.organization: Community Credit Union of Cumberland Colchester
resources.description: The Centre revitalized a previously underutilized downtown Amherst building into a co-working, training, and startup incubation hub with small business offices and meeting rooms. It delivers workshops, mentorship, and shared services that lower barriers for entrepreneurs and youth-led ventures in rural Northern Nova Scotia. This adaptive reuse activates the main street by clustering small businesses and programs in a central, walkable location.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic (Yarmouth Hub)
resources.description: IGNITE’s Yarmouth Hub repurposes upper-floor space in a historic Main Street commercial building into a co-working studio, prototyping lab, and event/training centre for startups and students. By offering affordable desks, maker resources, and entrepreneurship programming, it supports youth and early-stage companies in Southwestern Nova Scotia. The adaptive reuse brings innovators to the town core, boosting activity and local businesses on Main Street.

resources.name: Lunenburg Academy of Music Performance (LAMP)
resources.description: LAMP operates within the restored Lunenburg Academy—an historic public school—adaptively reusing the landmark into rehearsal rooms, studios, and a training campus for emerging and professional musicians. It provides instruction, residencies, and community performances that attract young talent to a small-town setting and sustain year-round cultural activity. This reuse preserves a civic asset while strengthening Lunenburg’s downtown economy through arts-based programming.

resources.name: Chester Art Centre
resources.description: Chester Art Centre transformed an existing village property into galleries, studios, and classrooms that offer affordable workspace and continuous arts training. By hosting workshops, exhibitions, and maker programs for all ages, it supports creative micro-enterprises and draws residents and visitors into the heart of Chester. This adaptive reuse directly contributes to main street vitality and opportunities for youth and early-career artists on the South Shore.

solutions.text: Local Health and Wellness Partnerships: Partner with regional health authorities and volunteers to expand mental health supports, addiction services and wellness programming locally.

resources.name: Community Health Boards – Wellness Funds (Western Zone)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health – Community Health Boards (Western Zone)
resources.description: Volunteer-led Community Health Boards, supported by Nova Scotia Health Public Health, provide Wellness Funds grants to local groups to expand mental health supports, addiction services, and community wellness programming. This initiative partners the regional health authority with community volunteers to identify local priorities and resource grassroots projects in rural and small communities across the Western Zone, reducing regional disparities.
resources.address: 90 Glen Allan Drive, Bridgewater, NS B4V 3S6

resources.name: Mobile Outreach Street Health (MOSH)
resources.description: MOSH is a collaborative outreach program that brings primary care, mental health, addictions support, and harm-reduction services directly to people where they live, including shelters and community sites. Operated by the North End Community Health Centre in partnership with Nova Scotia Health and supported by volunteer clinicians and community partners, it expands local access to mental wellness and addiction services and connects clients to ongoing supports.

resources.name: Recovery Support Centre – Aberdeen Hospital (Northern Zone)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health – Mental Health and Addictions Program
resources.description: The Recovery Support Centre provides same-day, no-appointment access to addictions care, including assessment, withdrawal management planning, and referrals to community programs. As part of Nova Scotia Health’s Mental Health and Addictions Program, the centre collaborates with local partners and peer-support groups to connect people to ongoing community-based services, strengthening local addiction and wellness supports outside major urban centres.
resources.address: 835 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3S6

resources.name: Antigonish Women’s Resource Centre & Sexual Assault Services – Counseling and Outreach
resources.organization: Antigonish Women’s Resource Centre & Sexual Assault Services
resources.description: AWRC&SAS provides free counseling, crisis support, and outreach programming that address trauma, mental health, and wellness needs in Antigonish and surrounding rural communities. Working in partnership with Nova Scotia Health services and trained community volunteers (including support group facilitators and hospital accompaniment volunteers), the centre expands access to localized mental health and wellness supports and navigation for those facing barriers.
resources.address: 219 Main Street, Suite 302, Antigonish, NS B2G 2C1

obstacles.title: Housing affordability and supply constraints
obstacles.description: Limited rental and entry-level ownership options, slow approvals, and construction bottlenecks push costs up and deter young people from settling or returning.

solutions.text: Community Land Trusts (CLTs): Local groups pool resources to buy and hold land permanently for affordable housing, ensuring long-term rental or ownership affordability and preventing speculative price increases.

resources.name: New Dawn Enterprises Affordable Housing
resources.description: New Dawn acquires, owns, and stewards residential properties as a community-controlled nonprofit to provide below-market rental housing in Cape Breton. By keeping land and buildings in nonprofit ownership over the long term, they remove homes from speculative markets and ensure affordability is preserved for future tenants—functionally implementing the community land trust approach in practice.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat NS partners with communities to acquire land and build homes that are sold to eligible families with affordability protections such as resale restrictions and rights of first refusal, preventing speculative price increases. By combining donated land, volunteer labor, and community financing, Habitat keeps housing costs low and maintains long-term affordability—aligning with the core principles of community land stewardship.

resources.name: AKOMA Community Land Development (Affordable Housing)
resources.description: AKOMA, an African Nova Scotian community nonprofit, holds and develops the former Nova Scotia Home for Colored Children lands to deliver community-benefit projects including affordable housing. By retaining community ownership of the land and partnering on mixed-income, affordable developments, AKOMA keeps housing out of speculative markets and ensures long-term affordability and control remain with the community.

solutions.text: Housing Cooperatives: Form resident-owned co-ops where members share ownership and governance, lowering costs through collective management and stabilizing supply for young people and families.

resources.name: Co-operative and Non-Profit Housing Program
resources.organization: Housing Nova Scotia (Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
resources.description: Housing Nova Scotia’s Co-operative and Non-Profit Housing Program supports resident-owned housing co-operatives by providing financing for capital repairs, asset management oversight, and guidance on governance and compliance. By strengthening existing co-ops and enabling stable, member-governed operations, the program helps keep monthly housing charges affordable and sustains supply for young people and families.

resources.name: National Housing Co-Investment Fund and Seed Funding (Atlantic – Halifax Office)
resources.description: CMHC’s Co-Investment Fund and Seed Funding streams finance the creation, repair, and sustainability of co-operative housing projects in Nova Scotia, offering low-cost loans and contributions that lower development and operating costs. This support enables resident-owned co-ops to expand and preserve affordable units, with CMHC’s Halifax team assisting proponents through application, underwriting, and delivery to stabilize supply for families and young people.

solutions.text: Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Support Program: Create community-led toolkits, model plans and neighbor outreach to encourage homeowners to add basement suites or garden suites, increasing gentle density and rental options.

resources.name: Backyard Suites (HRM)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality permits backyard (garden) suites and secondary/basement suites and provides a homeowner-focused information hub with guides, checklists, and application templates to help residents add gentle density on existing lots. Planning staff and 311 support offer outreach and one-on-one assistance to homeowners and neighbors, clarifying design standards, permitting steps, and good-neighbor practices so more homeowners can confidently create new rental options.

resources.name: Secondary and Backyard Suites Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings provides a toolkit-style set of resources—plain-language guides, application checklists, and sample site-plan templates—to help homeowners add secondary (basement) and backyard suites under its updated planning rules. Planning staff conduct public information sessions and provide direct support to property owners, reducing approval barriers and encouraging community acceptance of small-scale infill that expands local rental supply.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Backyard and Secondary Suites Guide
resources.description: The Town of Wolfville offers homeowner guidance and permitting support for secondary and backyard suites, including explanatory materials that outline where suites are allowed, key design standards, and step-by-step application requirements. Staff provide outreach and pre-application advice to help residents and nearby neighbors understand impacts and benefits, enabling gentle density and new rental options in established neighborhoods.

resources.name: Secondary & Backyard Suites Information and Permitting
resources.description: The Town of Bridgewater supports homeowners in creating secondary/basement and backyard (garden) suites by publishing how-to information, application checklists, and clear design and zoning standards. Through planning counter support and community outreach, the town helps residents navigate approvals and address neighbor concerns, accelerating small-scale, rental-producing housing additions on existing properties.

solutions.text: Vacant Property Reuse Initiative: Map and repurpose vacant or underused buildings (commercial or institutional) by assembling volunteer teams, local trades and small grants to convert them into affordable units.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership Program (Builds & Renovations)
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia acquires donated, surplus, or underused properties and rehabilitates or completes them into affordable homeownership units. Volunteer build teams work alongside local trades and suppliers, leveraging donated materials and small grants to convert vacant or distressed buildings into safe, energy‑efficient homes sold with affordable, no‑profit mortgages. This approach directly reuses existing building stock to add supply faster and at lower cost than new construction.

resources.name: Surplus Property Disposal for Affordable Housing
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality identifies vacant or underutilized municipal buildings and lands and makes them available to non‑profit and co‑operative providers for affordable housing. Through streamlined disposition, nominal leases/sales, and complementary grants and fee relief, the program lowers project costs so partners can convert existing structures into affordable rental units using local contractors and community partners. By reusing public assets, the initiative accelerates delivery and sidesteps bottlenecks associated with greenfield construction.

resources.name: Supportive Housing (Property Acquisitions and Conversions)
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia partners with the Province and community organizations to acquire and repurpose hotels and other vacant or underused buildings into supportive and deeply affordable housing across the province. The agency oversees rapid retrofit projects—funded by provincial dollars and federal programs such as the Rapid Housing Initiative—by contracting local trades to convert existing properties into code‑compliant homes with on‑site supports. Reusing built assets delivers units quickly and cost‑effectively while expanding the affordable housing supply.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1300, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: New Dawn Affordable Housing
resources.description: New Dawn acquires, rehabilitates, and manages older residential and mixed‑use buildings in Sydney to create and preserve affordable rental homes for low‑ and moderate‑income residents. Projects focus on renovating vacant or underused properties with local contractors and community partners, supported by grants and patient, community‑based financing. This adaptive‑reuse model adds units and extends the life of existing buildings at lower cost and with shorter timelines than new construction.

solutions.text: Local Approvals Task Force: Form a community–municipal working group to identify common planning barriers, streamline minor permit processes, provide peer support for applicants and advocate faster local approvals.

resources.name: Development Industry Liaison Group (DILG)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s DILG is a standing working group that brings municipal planning, engineering, and building officials together with development and community representatives to identify bottlenecks in the approvals pipeline and co-design process improvements. Through issue-tracking, shared checklists, and targeted pilots for items like minor variances and accessory units, the group streamlines routine permit steps, offers peer-to-peer guidance for applicants, and advocates for faster, more predictable local approvals.
resources.address: 5251 Duke Street, 3rd Floor (Duke Tower), Halifax, NS B3J 1A7

resources.name: Halifax Housing Task Force (Special Planning Areas Initiative)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing
resources.description: The Province’s task force for HRM coordinates provincial and municipal decision-makers to fast-track housing in designated Special Planning Areas, resolving interdepartmental barriers and setting service standards for timely approvals. By convening a focused approvals table and engaging local stakeholders on site-specific issues, it streamlines review steps for qualifying projects and accelerates local development permissions to address housing supply and affordability.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Business Navigators
resources.description: Business Navigators provide one-on-one guidance to entrepreneurs, builders, and housing providers on permits, licenses, and approvals across provincial and municipal levels, helping applicants complete high-quality submissions for faster processing. The team coordinates joint calls with local permitting staff, maintains plain-language checklists for minor permits, and escalates systemic barriers—functioning as peer support and an advocacy channel to streamline local approvals.

resources.name: Pre-Application and Development Review (One-Window Coordination)
resources.organization: Cape Breton Regional Municipality – Planning & Development
resources.description: CBRM’s Planning & Development team convenes pre-application meetings with planning, engineering, fire, and building officials to identify issues early and set clear submission requirements, reducing rework and delays. This coordinated, one-window review approach streamlines minor permits (e.g., home occupations, signage, accessory structures) and provides applicants with direct staff support, leading to quicker, more predictable local approvals.

solutions.text: Modular and Prefab Construction Hub: Support a local cooperative or small business hub for modular/prefab building components, lowering construction time and cost while creating local construction jobs and training.

resources.name: Interhabs Panelized Home Packages
resources.description: Interhabs designs and manufactures panelized wall, floor, and roof systems at its Hubbards facility, then ships them to sites for rapid assembly. This off-site fabrication shortens build schedules, reduces on-site labour and carrying costs, and supports local jobs; Interhabs also collaborates with local trades and apprentices, building regional capacity in modular/panelized construction.
resources.address: 10160 St Margarets Bay Road, Hubbards, NS B0J 1T0

resources.name: Truefoam Building Envelope Systems
resources.description: Truefoam manufactures prefabricated building envelope components—such as EPS insulation products and insulated concrete form (ICF) systems—used by modular and panelized builders across Nova Scotia to enclose structures quickly and efficiently. By supplying locally made components, offering technical support and training for installers, and maintaining a manufacturing workforce in Dartmouth, Truefoam helps lower construction time and costs while strengthening the local prefab ecosystem.

resources.name: NSCC Centre for the Built Environment — Off-site Construction Training
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) — Ivany Campus
resources.description: NSCC’s Centre for the Built Environment houses carpentry and construction technology programs that build building components and modules in shop settings for community and industry partners, mirroring real-world prefab workflows. This hands-on training develops the local workforce for modular and panelized construction, reducing on-site timelines for employers and creating clear pathways from education to jobs in Nova Scotia’s off-site construction sector.

solutions.text: Community Construction Training & Apprenticeships: Partner with trades, schools and non-profits to run short-cycle training and apprenticeship programs that both employ youth and supply skilled labor for local housing projects.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY places high-school students in paid summer work terms with residential builders and construction trades across Nova Scotia, giving youth hands-on site experience and exposure to apprenticeship pathways. By partnering with contractors, unions, schools, and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, BFY builds a pipeline of entry-level talent that supports local housing construction and helps relieve skilled-labour bottlenecks.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia – Build Program
resources.description: Habitat NS partners with schools, training providers, and trade professionals to host supervised build sites where students, apprentices, and emerging tradespeople gain practical hours while constructing affordable homes. These community builds directly add to local housing supply and create short-cycle, real-world training and employment experiences for youth seeking careers in the construction trades.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program (Construction Trades)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency registers and supports apprentices in construction trades such as carpentry, construction electrician, and plumber/pipefitter, combining paid on‑the‑job training with in‑class technical instruction. By coordinating employers, unions, colleges, and youth entrants, the program builds a steady pipeline of skilled workers who can be mobilized on residential and community housing projects across the province.
resources.address: 2021 Brunswick Street, 4th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 2S9

resources.name: Carpentry (Certificate)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Ivany Campus
resources.description: NSCC’s Carpentry certificate is a pre-apprenticeship program that prepares students for entry-level roles on residential and light commercial construction projects, including framing, finishing, and site safety. Through industry partnerships and work placements with local homebuilders, graduates transition quickly into paid apprenticeships, directly expanding the skilled workforce needed for Nova Scotia’s housing construction.

resources.name: Trades & Construction Programs
resources.description: The East Preston Empowerment Academy delivers short-cycle trades readiness and entry-level construction training—often in partnership with NSCC, unions, and local employers—to help African Nova Scotian youth and adults gain in-demand skills. Participants move into paid work placements and apprenticeships with residential builders, supporting inclusive workforce growth while contributing to local housing projects.
resources.address: 190 Brooks Drive, East Preston, NS B2Z 1H3

solutions.text: Employer-Assisted Housing Partnerships: Encourage local employers, especially growing firms and institutions, to form partnerships that offer rental blocks, down-payment assistance, or guaranteed leases for young workers.

resources.name: Cabot Cape Breton Staff Accommodation
resources.description: Cabot Cape Breton provides dedicated staff housing near its Inverness resorts to ensure seasonal and early‑career employees have reliable, affordable places to live. The employer secures and manages rental blocks and dorm‑style units, effectively guaranteeing leases tied to employment and reducing competition in the local rental market—an employer‑assisted housing model that helps attract and retain young workers.

resources.name: Fox Harb'r Resort Employee Housing
resources.description: Fox Harb'r Resort offers on‑site and nearby employee accommodations to support recruitment and retention, particularly for young and seasonal workers in hospitality and golf operations. By operating dedicated staff housing and master‑leasing local units during peak seasons, the employer reduces housing barriers and provides guaranteed, stable rentals aligned with the employer‑assisted housing approach.
resources.address: 1337 Fox Harbour Road, Fox Harbour, NS B0K 1Y0

resources.name: Faculty and Staff Housing
resources.description: Acadia University maintains a portfolio of university‑owned houses and apartments reserved for employees, including new faculty and staff relocating to Wolfville. By providing employer‑controlled rental options and prioritized leases for employees, Acadia implements an employer‑assisted housing model that stabilizes access to housing for young hires and supports talent attraction.

resources.name: Recruitment Housing Supports for Health Professionals
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health (Office of Healthcare Professionals Recruitment)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health, through its recruitment office, coordinates temporary and longer‑term housing for newly hired clinicians and allied health workers by partnering with landlords, hotels, and developers to secure blocks of units and, where needed, guarantee leases. This employer‑assisted approach reduces housing bottlenecks that can deter young professionals from accepting positions across the province.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

solutions.text: Shared-Equity Homeownership Programs: Create community-backed shared-equity models where non-profit partners or municipalities take a modest equity stake to lower purchase prices for first-time buyers, with resale rules that preserve affordability.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership Program (Shared-Equity Model)
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia sells homes to qualifying first-time buyers using a shared-equity structure: the homeowner takes on an affordable first mortgage while Habitat holds a non-interest-bearing second mortgage that represents an equity stake. Upon resale, a shared-appreciation formula applies so the home remains affordable for the next buyer, preserving community affordability while lowering the initial purchase price.

resources.name: North End Community Land Trust – Permanently Affordable Homeownership
resources.description: The North End Community Land Trust advances a community land trust model in Halifax’s North End, separating land from buildings to lower the upfront cost for buyers and keep homes affordable over time. Buyers own their homes while the CLT retains the land via a long-term ground lease with resale restrictions and a shared-equity formula, ensuring any appreciation is partially reinvested to preserve long-term affordability for first-time and moderate-income households.

solutions.text: Rent-to-Own and Lease-Option Pilots: Launch small-scale rent-to-own pilots facilitated by local housing organizations to help renters build equity and transition into ownership without predatory financing.

resources.name: Rent-to-Own Mini Home Program
resources.description: Killam Apartment REIT offers a rent-to-own option for manufactured (mini) homes in several Nova Scotia land-lease communities. Residents move into a new or pre-owned mini home under a lease-option agreement where a portion of monthly payments is credited toward the eventual purchase, with a clearly defined buyout option at the end of the term. This creates an accessible, non-predatory pathway for renters to build equity and transition into ownership while living in the home.
resources.address: 3700 Kempt Road, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3K 4X8

resources.name: Eastern Woodland Housing Program – Rent-to-Own (RTO)
resources.description: The Native Council of Nova Scotia’s Eastern Woodland Housing Program includes a Rent-to-Own stream that helps off-reserve Indigenous households move from renting to ownership. Participants enter lease-option agreements with a fixed purchase price; a portion of each monthly payment is accrued as equity toward a down payment, paired with homebuyer education and support to reach mortgage readiness. This structured, community-led approach enables families to build equity and assume title without resorting to high-cost or predatory financing.
resources.address: 129 Truro Heights Road, Truro Heights, NS B6L 1X1

solutions.text: Tiny Home and Micro-Village Projects: Develop community-supported tiny-home clusters on municipally or donor-owned land as affordable, fast-to-build options with shared amenities and strong local management.

resources.name: Pallet-Shelter Micro-Villages (Supportive Housing Sites)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality has established multiple pallet-shelter micro-villages on municipally owned land in Halifax and Dartmouth, each providing private insulated cabins alongside shared washroom/shower facilities, power, and heat. The sites are operated with local service partners and include on-site, 24/7 management and supports, creating fast-to-build, low-cost housing that relieves pressure on the rental market while longer-term housing is developed.

resources.name: River Street Sleeping Cabin Community
resources.description: The Town of Kentville created a sanctioned sleeping-cabin community on municipal land on River Street, delivered in partnership with a local non-profit operator to provide managed, supportive tiny-home style cabins. The cluster model delivers rapid, affordable dwellings with shared amenities and on-site supports, helping residents stabilize and transition toward longer-term housing while easing local affordability and supply pressures.

resources.name: Bridgewater Sleeping Cabin Village
resources.description: The Town of Bridgewater has supported a managed sleeping-cabin village on town property as part of its homelessness response, providing a cluster of small, insulated cabins with shared washroom/shower facilities and coordinated on-site supports through a community partner. By enabling a tiny-home micro-village on public land and streamlining servicing and oversight, the initiative quickly adds deeply affordable units with strong local management.

solutions.text: Local Impact Investment & Crowdfunding: Establish community investment vehicles or crowdfunding campaigns to finance affordable housing projects, offering local residents a way to invest in and benefit from supply increases.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Economic Development Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: New Dawn’s provincially registered CEDIF raises RRSP/TFSA-eligible capital from Nova Scotians, allowing local residents to invest directly in community development. New Dawn channels this community investment into local ventures and community real estate, including the development and preservation of affordable and supportive housing units in Cape Breton, thereby expanding housing supply while returning financial and social benefits to local investors.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia – Home Build Community Fundraising
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia runs ongoing public fundraising campaigns that enable Nova Scotians to contribute directly to the construction of affordable homeownership units across the province. These community crowdfunding efforts pool small and large local donations to finance land, materials, and build costs, translating resident contributions into new, permanently affordable housing supply for working families.

resources.name: Sunflower Court Capital Campaign
resources.description: Adsum for Women & Children led a community capital campaign to help finance Sunflower Court, a supportive and affordable housing development in Lakeside that adds new units for women, gender-diverse people, and families. Through broad-based local crowdfunding and philanthropy, residents could directly back construction costs, accelerating delivery of new, deeply affordable homes and expanding non-market supply in HRM.

solutions.text: Inclusionary Zoning Advocacy: Mobilize community groups to advocate municipal policies that require or incentivize affordable units in new developments, with clear local targets and developer supports.

resources.name: Our HRM Alliance
resources.description: Led by the Ecology Action Centre, Our HRM Alliance convenes residents, NGOs, and planners to press Halifax Regional Municipality and other NS municipalities to embed inclusionary housing tools—such as density bonusing and affordable set-asides—into planning frameworks like the Centre Plan and secondary planning strategies. The coalition mobilizes public input, proposes local affordability targets, and advocates paired developer supports (e.g., expedited approvals, fee rebates, and green/infrastructure incentives) to secure affordable units in new developments.

resources.name: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service (Housing and Tenants’ Advocacy)
resources.description: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service organizes tenants and community groups and provides legal/policy expertise to advocate municipal measures that require or incentivize affordable units in private developments. Through submissions to council and planning processes, they push for measurable affordability targets, inclusionary mechanisms in land-use bylaws, and complementary developer supports such as density bonusing agreements and fast-tracked approvals.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Federation of Municipalities – Housing Advocacy
resources.description: NSFM represents Nova Scotia’s municipalities and advocates for provincial and municipal policy tools that enable inclusionary zoning and affordable housing requirements in new developments. They develop recommendations and brief decision-makers on setting local affordability targets while promoting practical developer supports (e.g., density bonusing, fee waivers, and grant programs) to make inclusionary approaches feasible.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1304, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: YWCA Halifax – Housing and Public Policy Advocacy
resources.description: YWCA Halifax engages in municipal consultations and community coalitions to advance inclusionary housing measures that secure affordable homes for women and families within new private developments. They mobilize community voices, recommend clear affordability targets, and advocate developer supports such as incentive grants and streamlined approvals so inclusionary requirements are effective and implementable.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

solutions.text: Temporary Pop-up and Transitional Units: Use community spaces, modular units or converted shipping containers to create short-term transitional housing while permanent supply is planned and delivered.

resources.name: Halifax Modular Supportive Housing Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality purchased and installed prefabricated modular units on municipal land to create rapid, short-term supportive housing for people experiencing homelessness. These pop-up transitional communities provide private rooms with shared facilities and on-site supports while permanent, longer-term housing supply is planned and built. The initiative increases immediate capacity quickly, easing pressure on the rental market and construction pipelines.

resources.name: The Overlook Supportive Housing
resources.description: Shelter Nova Scotia converted an existing hotel into transitional supportive housing, rapidly creating dozens of self-contained rooms that can be operated immediately while permanent affordable units are developed. This adaptive reuse leverages an existing community space to provide short-term, bridge housing with on-site supports and case management. It exemplifies a fast, lower-cost way to add units and stabilize residents as they move toward longer-term housing.

resources.name: Temporary Pallet Shelter Village (Halifax)
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre operates a temporary village of Pallet modular cabins in Halifax, offering private, heated sleeping units with shared amenities and wraparound supports. These rapidly deployable structures act as transitional housing to bring people indoors quickly while longer-term Indigenous-led and mainstream housing projects are advanced. The model uses modular, movable units that can be installed on available community sites to meet urgent demand.

resources.name: Sydney Pallet Shelter Community
resources.description: In partnership with the Province, the Ally Centre of Cape Breton supports a Pallet shelter community in Sydney that provides modular, quickly assembled cabins as short-term bridge housing. Residents access on-site services, harm reduction, and housing navigation while permanent housing options are arranged. The approach creates immediate, pop-up capacity using modular units to address acute housing shortages in Cape Breton.

solutions.text: University and College Housing Partnerships: Work with post-secondary institutions to convert surplus rooms or co-develop mixed-use student-youth housing that remains available to graduates and early-career residents.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Summer Accommodations (Stay with Us)
resources.description: Dalhousie opens surplus residence rooms and suites to non-students each summer, offering short-term, furnished rentals to interns, co-op students, researchers, and early‑career workers. By converting underused student housing into affordable, flexible-term accommodation, the program directly expands supply for young people relocating to Halifax for work or internships and supports employer recruitment.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Summer Accommodations
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University rents residence rooms to the broader community during the summer, with options suited to interns, recent graduates, and early‑career professionals on short work placements. This converts surplus campus housing into budget-friendly, move‑in‑ready units that help ease rental pressure and support youth talent staying in or moving to Halifax.

resources.name: MSVU Summer Accommodations & Conference Services
resources.description: Mount Saint Vincent University makes residence spaces available to the public in the off‑academic season, providing affordable, furnished stays for co-op students, interns, and early‑career workers. By tapping surplus residence capacity, MSVU adds short-term, youth‑oriented housing options on a transit‑served campus minutes from Halifax’s core.

resources.name: Acadia University Summer Accommodations
resources.description: Acadia converts residence rooms to public rentals in the summer, welcoming interns, visiting researchers, and new graduates needing flexible, short-term housing in the Annapolis Valley. This model turns underutilized student housing into affordable supply for young workers, supporting regional employers and easing pressure on the local rental market.

solutions.text: Neighborhood Matchmaking Platform: Create a local online/offline service that connects homeowners with spare rooms, potential renters, student tenants or co-living matches to quickly increase available rentals.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Off-Campus Living
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Off-Campus Living service operates an online listing platform and advising service that connects local landlords and homeowners offering spare rooms or shared accommodations with students and other renters. Through tools like room/roommate matching and guidance on leases and tenant rights, the program accelerates placement into existing housing stock and supports co-living arrangements that increase available rentals in Halifax neighborhoods.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Language Centre Homestay Program
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University – The Language Centre
resources.description: The SMU Language Centre’s Homestay Program matches international and domestic students with vetted Halifax host families who have spare rooms, providing room-and-board arrangements and cultural support. This structured host–student matchmaking quickly mobilizes underused bedrooms in local homes and offers an affordable, community-based rental option aligned with co-living principles.

resources.name: Cape Breton University Homestay Program
resources.description: CBU’s Homestay Program connects community homeowners willing to rent spare rooms with CBU students, creating affordable placements and shared living arrangements. By recruiting, screening, and supporting host families, the university activates existing housing capacity across the Sydney area and provides a rapid, neighborhood-based rental matchmaking service.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

resources.name: Acadia Language Centre Homestay
resources.description: Acadia University’s Language Centre places students with local host families in Wolfville and surrounding communities, pairing homeowners who have spare bedrooms with student renters. The program’s screening, matching, and ongoing support formalize co-living arrangements and quickly expand rental availability by leveraging existing homes.

solutions.text: Community Design Charrettes and Zoning Workshops: Run participatory design sessions with residents and planners to reimagine underused parcels, test gentle-density models and build community consensus for zoning updates.

resources.name: Shape Your City Halifax – Planning & Development Engagement
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality runs ongoing public design charrettes, open houses, and workshop series under Shape Your City to inform updates to the Centre Plan, Regional Plan, and related land-use by-laws. These sessions bring residents, planners, and stakeholders together to reimagine underused parcels, test gentle-density options (e.g., secondary/backyard suites and small multiplexes), and build consensus that feeds directly into zoning changes to expand housing supply and affordability.

resources.name: Kings 2050 – Community Engagement on Municipal Planning Strategy & Land Use By-law
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings – Planning & Development
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings facilitates design workshops, charrette-style sessions, and statutory public participation to shape its Municipal Planning Strategy and Land Use By-law. Engagement focuses on enabling gentle-density in growth centers (e.g., accessory dwelling units, infill, mixed-use zoning), using resident input to refine policies and streamline approvals that add attainable rental and entry-level ownership options.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Bridgewater Downtown & Waterfront Plan – Public Design Workshops
resources.description: The Town of Bridgewater’s planning team conducts hands-on public design workshops and charrettes to guide the Downtown & Waterfront Plan and related zoning updates. These sessions test gentle-density infill, adaptive reuse of underutilized parcels, and mixed-use forms, translating community preferences into by-law amendments that support more housing choice and revitalization.

resources.name: Public Participation Program (PPP) – Eastern District Planning Commission
resources.description: EDPC coordinates public participation programs for its member municipalities, hosting community design workshops, charrettes, and open houses during plan and by-law reviews. These events invite residents to co-design neighbourhood forms, explore accessory suites and small-scale multi-unit options, and shape zoning that unlocks gentle-density and faster approvals across rural and small-town communities in eastern Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 606 Reeves Street, Unit 1, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 2R7

solutions.text: Home Repair and Accessibility Grant Pool: Organize pooled small grants and volunteer labor to repair and upgrade older rental units, bringing more existing housing stock to market and improving long-term habitability.

resources.name: HomeWarming
resources.organization: Clean Foundation and Efficiency Nova Scotia
resources.description: HomeWarming provides no-cost energy-efficiency upgrades like insulation, draft-proofing, and minor repairs to income-qualified households across Nova Scotia, funded by partners including Efficiency Nova Scotia and Nova Scotia Power and delivered by Clean Foundation. By pooling public and utility funds and coordinating qualified contractors, the program upgrades aging homes to be safer, warmer, and more durable—preserving existing housing stock and reducing energy costs so units remain viable in the market over the long term.

resources.name: Affordable Multi‑Unit Residential Buildings Program
resources.description: Efficiency Nova Scotia offers incentives and technical support to non-profit providers and landlords of affordable rental buildings to complete energy and building-system upgrades (e.g., insulation, heating, ventilation, lighting, and controls). These grants and rebates reduce operating costs and fund critical retrofits that improve comfort and safety, helping keep older rental units habitable and affordable and bringing underperforming units back into active use.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: Non-Profit Organization Grant Program for Affordable Housing
resources.description: HRM’s grant program provides capital funding to registered non-profit housing organizations for projects that create, renovate, or convert affordable rental units, including life-safety, code, and accessibility upgrades. By directing small grants to repair and rehabilitate existing buildings, the program helps bring vacant or deteriorated units back to market more quickly and sustains the long-term habitability of older rental stock.

resources.name: Home Repair Program (HRP)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing (Housing Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The province’s Home Repair Program provides forgivable loans and grants to eligible low‑income households to address health, safety, structural, and accessibility issues in aging homes. By pooling public funds to tackle critical repairs and upgrades, the program keeps existing housing safe and habitable—preserving the province’s older housing stock and easing pressure on the overall housing market.

solutions.text: Tenant Support and Eviction Prevention Services: Provide community-based legal clinics, rent-banking, mediation and tenant education to reduce displacement and keep young residents stably housed while broader supply solutions are deployed.

resources.name: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service (Tenant Law Clinic)
resources.description: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service is a community-based legal clinic that provides free legal information, advice, and representation to low‑income tenants, including at Residential Tenancies hearings, to prevent evictions and illegal rent practices. The clinic also offers outreach and tenant education workshops on rights and responsibilities, and engages in landlord mediation and negotiation to help clients maintain stable housing while broader housing supply solutions are pursued.

resources.name: Settlement Services – Housing Support
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides housing navigation for newcomers to Nova Scotia, including one‑on‑one counselling to secure and keep rentals, tenant education on leases, repairs, and Residential Tenancies rules, and budgeting for rent and utilities. Staff assist with landlord communication and mediation, and connect clients to rent supplements and emergency financial supports to address arrears or avoid eviction, stabilizing tenancies as supply solutions develop.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Housing Support Program
resources.description: Adsum’s Housing Support Program helps women, gender-diverse people, and families at risk of homelessness to maintain their tenancies through landlord mediation, negotiation of repayment plans, and accompaniment to Residential Tenancies processes when needed. The program provides tenant education on rights and responsibilities and assists clients in accessing rent relief, damage deposit and arrears assistance, and other emergency funds to prevent eviction.

resources.name: Housing Support & Eviction Prevention
resources.description: Shelter Nova Scotia offers eviction prevention and housing stabilization supports, including case management, landlord mediation, and help developing repayment plans to resolve rent arrears or tenancy conflicts. Staff provide tenant education, budgeting support, and connections to emergency assistance for rent and utilities, reducing displacement and helping people remain housed while longer-term housing supply measures advance.

solutions.text: Community Land Bank: Form a locally governed land bank to acquire, hold and steward properties for phased redevelopment into affordable housing, prioritizing projects that support youth retention.

resources.name: Surplus Municipal Land for Affordable Housing Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality identifies, acquires, and assembles surplus municipal properties and strategically disposes of them to non-profits and community partners for affordable housing development. By acting as a municipal land bank, HRM lowers upfront land costs, enables phased redevelopment on community-prioritized sites, and supports projects that help retain and attract young workers and families by increasing rental and entry-level housing options.

resources.name: Provincial Land for Housing Initiative
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia stewards provincially owned lands and coordinates their redevelopment into mixed-income and affordable housing, often in phases and in partnership with community, municipal, and non-profit developers. Functioning like a province-wide land bank, the initiative reduces land and carrying costs, accelerates approvals on strategic sites, and targets housing supply that supports workforce and youth retention across the province.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 301, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Land Acquisition and Homebuilding Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia acquires and holds donated or discounted land and surplus properties, then redevelops them in phases into affordable homeownership units for low- to moderate-income families. By stewarding land for long-term community benefit and reducing development costs, the program expands attainable housing options that help young families and early-career workers put down roots in Nova Scotia.

obstacles.title: Thin job density and limited career ladders
obstacles.description: Insufficient concentration of high-quality roles and mid-to-senior pathways in both emerging sectors and established trades reduces long-term prospects and advancement.

solutions.text: Local Industry Cluster Working Groups: Form cross-sector working groups (businesses, post-secondary, chambers, municipalities) that coordinate recruitment, shared training, joint marketing and investment to increase concentration of high-quality roles and build clear career ladders.

resources.name: Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE convenes ocean technology companies, post-secondary institutions (e.g., NSCC and Dalhousie), government, and investors at a single waterfront campus to coordinate sector growth. Through shared facilities, joint industry-academic projects, talent events, and vendor showcases, it drives collaborative recruitment, shared training, and joint marketing that deepen the ocean-tech job base and create clearer career pathways within the cluster.

resources.name: Ocean Technology Council of Nova Scotia (OTCNS)
resources.organization: Ocean Technology Council of Nova Scotia
resources.description: OTCNS is the industry association for Nova Scotia’s ocean-technology cluster, bringing together businesses, academia, and government to coordinate workforce development, supply-chain connections, and export promotion. It leads cluster-wide initiatives such as student and newcomer outreach, sector marketing (e.g., partnering on conferences and trade missions), and collaborative training that strengthen recruitment pipelines and build progressive career ladders across the marine technology ecosystem.

resources.name: Farm and Workforce Development
resources.description: This Nova Scotia Federation of Agriculture initiative coordinates farmers, commodity groups, post-secondary partners (e.g., Dalhousie Faculty of Agriculture, NSCC), and municipalities to tackle sector-wide recruitment and skills development. It offers shared training, HR tools, and career promotion for agriculture that grow the density of quality on-farm and agri-food roles while mapping clear advancement paths from entry-level to supervisory and management careers.
resources.address: 60 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: Irving Shipbuilding Centre of Excellence (NSCC)
resources.description: Hosted at NSCC, the Centre of Excellence works with Irving Shipbuilding, suppliers, community organizations, and government to align training and recruitment with the National Shipbuilding Strategy. It develops coordinated talent pipelines (including outreach to underrepresented groups), delivers shared curricula and upskilling, and connects learners to apprenticeships and high-quality marine trades and technology roles with clear progression pathways.

solutions.text: Community Incubator and Accelerator Hubs: Create locally run incubators (physical and virtual) offering mentorship, shared services, seed microgrants and investor showcases to help startups scale from one-person operations into firms with mid- and senior-level roles.

resources.name: Volta (Innovation Hub & Volta Cohort)
resources.description: Volta is a startup incubator and community hub that provides founders with office space, mentorship, shared services, and structured programming to grow beyond solo operations. It runs investor-facing events and the Volta Cohort pitch program, which offers seed investment and exposure to funders, helping companies hire into new mid- and senior-level roles as they scale. Volta’s physical and virtual supports create a pipeline from idea to growth-stage firms, strengthening local career ladders.

resources.name: COVE and Startup Yard at COVE
resources.description: COVE is an ocean-technology commercialization hub that offers shared labs, prototyping shops, wharf access, and an incubator (Startup Yard) with mentorship and business advisory services. It convenes investor showcases and industry demo days, and partners with regional seed programs to help founders secure early capital and scale their teams. By enabling ocean tech startups to grow from one- or two-person ventures into firms with technical and managerial roles, COVE directly builds local job density and career pathways.

resources.name: CEED Incubation & Entrepreneur Development Programs
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides incubator-style programming, advisory, and shared services (including co-working and workshops) for new and growing businesses across Nova Scotia. It connects entrepreneurs with mentorship and access to early-stage capital such as CEED’s microloans and partner microgrant opportunities, and it hosts pitch events that put founders in front of investors. These supports help ventures professionalize, create management capacity, and add mid- and senior-level roles as they expand.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Innovation Hubs
resources.description: IGNITE operates rural innovation hubs that provide co-working space, maker resources, mentorship, and accelerator-style programming to help founders move from idea to scalable companies. It regularly hosts investor networking, pitch events, and partners on seed-funding and microgrant opportunities that give entrepreneurs the early capital and exposure they need. By supporting growth in communities like Yarmouth, IGNITE helps startups add professional roles and build local career ladders.

resources.name: Navigate Startup House
resources.organization: Navigate Startup House (Cape Breton Partnership & Cape Breton University)
resources.description: Navigate offers an incubator-style co-working space, mentorship, and programming for Cape Breton founders, connecting them to advisors, shared services, and regional partners. It organizes community pitch events and links entrepreneurs to seed microgrants and investor networks to accelerate early growth. These supports help companies evolve from solo ventures into employers that can add mid-level and senior positions in the local economy.

solutions.text: Apprenticeship and Employer Consortiums: Partner small employers and trades schools to create pooled apprenticeship slots, shared training schedules and employer rotation programs that ensure steady pipeline and defined journeyperson/career progression.

resources.name: ACRC (Carpenters Local 83) Apprenticeship & Training Centre
resources.organization: Atlantic Canada Regional Council of Carpenters, Millwrights and Allied Workers (Local 83)
resources.description: The Atlantic Canada Regional Council (ACRC) administers group-sponsored apprenticeship for carpenters and millwrights, coordinating placements with dozens of small and mid-sized signatory contractors across Nova Scotia. Apprentices are dispatched through the union hiring hall to rotate among employers, follow shared block-release training schedules in partnership with NSCC, and progress on a clearly defined pathway to Red Seal journeyperson certification.

resources.name: NSCC Apprenticeship Technical Training
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College delivers standardized, block-release in-class technical training for apprentices from many employers across the province, in coordination with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and industry partners. By pooling cohorts from multiple small firms and aligning shared training schedules, NSCC supports employer rotation models and a consistent curriculum that leads apprentices toward defined competencies and journeyperson certification.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: NSCC in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding Inc. and community/union partners
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding recruits cohort-based intakes (e.g., women, Mi’kmaw, African Nova Scotian participants) and provides coordinated pre-apprenticeship and technical training at NSCC aligned to shipbuilding trades. Delivered by a consortium including NSCC, Irving Shipbuilding, trade unions, and community partners, it pools apprenticeship opportunities, synchronizes training schedules, and offers a clear progression into apprenticeships and onward to Red Seal certification.

resources.name: Women Unlimited Program (Trades & Technology)
resources.description: Women Unlimited delivers cohort-based pre-apprenticeship programs and partners with NSCC, unions, and a network of construction and industrial employers to place participants into entry-level and apprenticeship roles. By coordinating training timetables with schools and pooling employer placements—often using union hiring halls for rotation—the program builds a steady pipeline into the skilled trades with structured supports and a defined path to journeyperson status.

solutions.text: Micro-credential and Modular Upskilling Programs: Develop short, stackable local credentials aligned with employer needs (digital skills, advanced trades, supervisory skills) so workers can advance into mid-level and senior roles without leaving the community.

resources.name: NSCC Microcredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College offers short, stackable micro-credentials co-designed with employers in areas such as digital skills, advanced manufacturing and trades, and frontline supervision. Learners earn industry-recognized digital badges that can be combined to ladder into certificates or diplomas, enabling working adults to upskill into mid-level and senior roles without leaving their communities.

resources.name: Dalhousie Open Learning & Career Development Microcredentials
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Open Learning & Career Development unit provides micro-credentials and digital badges in employer-aligned fields like data analytics, project management, leadership, and emerging technologies. Courses are modular and stackable, delivered online or hybrid, allowing workers across Nova Scotia to build pathways from entry-level to supervisory and managerial roles while remaining in their communities.

resources.name: Cape Breton University Micro-credentials
resources.description: Cape Breton University offers short, skills-focused micro-credentials aligned with regional employer needs in sectors such as clean energy, tourism, healthcare administration, and digital business tools. Credentials are stackable and often count toward broader certificates or degree pathways, providing residents—especially in rural areas—with flexible upskilling routes to advance into mid-level and leadership roles.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

resources.name: NSCAD Extended Studies Micro-credentials
resources.description: NSCAD University’s Extended Studies delivers micro-credentials in creative and digital fields—such as UX/UI design, digital illustration, animation, and production tools—built with input from industry partners in screen, design, and interactive media. These short, stackable courses award digital badges that can accumulate into advanced certificates, helping creatives in Nova Scotia move into more senior technical and supervisory roles without relocating.

solutions.text: Regional Hiring Consortium and Job-Sharing Platform: Build a community-run platform where neighbouring small employers post part-time, fractional and shared roles to create denser, more stable local employment pathways and opportunities for job progression.

resources.name: COVE Job Board and Member Opportunities
resources.description: COVE operates a multi-employer job and contract board for Nova Scotia’s ocean-tech cluster, where SMEs and startups post internships, part-time, contract, and shared-project roles. By centralizing opportunities from neighbouring small employers, the platform creates denser local pathways and makes it easier for talent to progress between firms as their careers advance.

resources.name: CANS Job Board
resources.description: The Construction Association of Nova Scotia hosts a sector-wide job board where many small and mid-sized contractors post apprenticeships, seasonal, part-time, and project-based roles. This consortium-style platform enables job seekers to find continuous work across multiple employers and facilitates job sharing across projects, strengthening local career ladders in the skilled trades.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Volta Jobs
resources.description: Volta aggregates postings from resident and community startups across Halifax and Nova Scotia, including internships, co-ops, part-time, and contract roles common in early-stage companies. By pooling opportunities from numerous small employers into one community-run platform, it helps candidates stitch together fractional roles and advance within the regional startup ecosystem.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Work in Cape Breton
resources.description: Work in Cape Breton is a regional job platform that curates postings from many small and medium employers across Cape Breton–Unama’ki, highlighting full-time, part-time, seasonal, and contract roles. By concentrating opportunities across sectors into a single community-driven hub, it supports job sharing and smoother progression between employers, helping build stable local career pathways.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

solutions.text: Mentorship and Career Ladder Networks: Set up formal mentorship programs linking youth and early-career workers with mid- and senior-level local professionals, including reverse-mentoring and structured progression plans.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program pairs internationally trained youth and early‑career professionals with mid‑ to senior‑level local mentors in their field to build networks, learn sector norms, and receive career guidance. The program uses structured matching, agreed goals, and regular check‑ins to support progression toward licensure, job readiness, and advancement, with two‑way learning that can include reverse‑mentoring on technology and cultural insights.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Volta Office Hours
resources.description: Volta’s Office Hours connect students, founders, and early‑career tech talent with seasoned executives, investors, and subject‑matter experts for one‑on‑one mentorship and career navigation. These recurring sessions create structured guidance and network bridges that help participants progress from entry‑level roles or early ventures to more senior responsibilities, while also enabling reverse‑mentoring as young innovators share emerging tools and market insights.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Craft Apprenticeship and Mentorship Program
resources.description: Craft Nova Scotia’s program formally matches emerging craftspeople with master artisans for multi‑month, on‑the‑job mentorship using learning plans, milestones, and portfolio development. The model builds clear career ladders in the trades and arts by guiding mentees from foundational skills to professional practice, while encouraging two‑way knowledge exchange (e.g., reverse‑mentoring on digital marketing or new tools).
resources.address: 1061 Marginal Road, Suite 140, Halifax, NS B3H 4P7

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program creates formal mentorship relationships between apprentices and certified journeypersons across dozens of skilled trades. With signed training agreements, logbooks, competency targets, and progressive wage and responsibility steps, it provides a structured progression plan from entry to Red Seal certification, embedding career ladders and knowledge transfer on the job.

resources.name: JA Company Program
resources.description: JA’s Company Program engages high school youth in building a real venture under the guidance of volunteer mentors from the local business community, providing hands‑on exposure to roles across marketing, finance, and operations. The structured program cycle and leadership opportunities create early career ladders in entrepreneurship and related fields, while mentors open professional networks that support long‑term advancement.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 309, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Municipal Procurement for Local Career Development: Adopt municipal procurement clauses that prioritize local suppliers who commit to local hiring, apprenticeships or career-ladder guarantees, using public spend to grow quality roles.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Social Procurement Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality (HRM) integrates social value criteria into its procurement process, using a Supplier Social Value Questionnaire and scoring to reward bidders that commit to local hiring, apprenticeships, co-op placements, and workforce development for equity-seeking groups. By embedding these requirements and evaluation points in RFPs and contracts across construction, services, and goods, HRM uses public spending to grow quality local roles and career ladders in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Cogswell District Redevelopment – Community Benefits and Workforce Development
resources.description: As part of HRM’s Cogswell District Redevelopment, procurement and contract requirements include social value and community benefits expectations such as local employment, apprenticeship utilization, and on-the-job training opportunities with contractors and subcontractors. This project operationalizes HRM’s social procurement approach at scale, channeling a major municipal infrastructure investment into concrete career pathways and advancement for Nova Scotians.

resources.name: CBRM Social Procurement and Local Benefits in Tenders
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Municipality (CBRM) incorporates social value considerations into its tendering and RFP processes, encouraging bidders to outline plans for local hiring, apprenticeship participation, and training as part of project delivery. By evaluating proposals on these workforce development commitments alongside price and quality, CBRM leverages municipal procurement to expand good jobs and career-ladder opportunities in the region.

resources.name: Town of Bridgewater Sustainable Procurement Policy
resources.description: The Town of Bridgewater’s procurement framework integrates social and economic value, asking suppliers to demonstrate local workforce development approaches—such as employing Nova Scotia apprentices, creating co-op or internship placements, and committing to training and advancement—especially in infrastructure and clean energy projects. This policy uses municipal purchasing power to cultivate stable, quality roles and clearer advancement pathways for local residents.

solutions.text: Community-owned Cooperatives and Social Enterprises: Support worker-owned cooperatives and social enterprises in key sectors (food, fisheries, renewables, creative industries) to create locally rooted organizations with intentional promotion paths.

resources.name: Just Us! Coffee Roasters Co-op
resources.description: Just Us! is a worker-owned coffee roasting and retail cooperative that anchors fair-trade food sector jobs in rural Nova Scotia.
