As a worker co-op, employees are members who participate in governance and can progress from entry-level café or production roles into roasting, quality control, logistics, and management, building clear internal promotion pathways while keeping ownership and profits local.

resources.name: New Dawn Centre for Social Innovation
resources.description: Operated by New Dawn Enterprises, this social enterprise hub provides affordable workspace, programming, and wraparound supports for locally rooted organizations and startups in Cape Breton, fostering job creation and growth in community services, creative industries, and emerging sectors. By clustering enterprises and offering mentorship and leadership opportunities, it creates ladders for young people to move from entry-level roles to supervisory, management, and founder positions within a community-owned development ecosystem.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-operative
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre is a member-owned co-operative venue that incubates creative industry careers by providing production space, technical training, and paid opportunities for artists and arts workers. Members can advance from participant to producer, technical lead, and board leadership, creating intentional promotion pathways while keeping cultural infrastructure community-owned and locally governed.

resources.name: Scotian Gold Co-operative Limited
resources.description: Scotian Gold is a grower-owned agricultural co-operative that operates packing, storage, and distribution facilities for Nova Scotia’s apple industry, sustaining year-round, locally rooted jobs in the food sector. The co-op offers on-the-job training and advancement from seasonal and entry-level roles into skilled positions in processing, quality assurance, warehousing, and logistics supervision, creating clear career ladders in a community-owned enterprise.

solutions.text: Sector Career Pathway Roadmaps: Produce and distribute clear, community-specific career maps for priority sectors showing entry points, mid-level roles, skills/wage expectations and local employers to make advancement visible and attainable.

resources.name: Explore Careers Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: Explore Careers Nova Scotia is a provincial portal that publishes sector and occupation profiles with clear entry points, progression to mid- and senior-level roles, required skills/education, regional wage ranges, and local labour market outlooks. The site connects users to Nova Scotia employers and job postings and is promoted through Nova Scotia Works centres and schools, making sector career roadmaps visible and actionable for youth across the province.

resources.name: Apprenticeship Pathways
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency provides trade-specific career pathway diagrams that map the steps from entry-level apprentice to journeyperson and into advanced roles (e.g., foreperson, estimator, inspector), including required hours, certifications, and typical wage progression. It also links candidates to local employers through the Apprenticeship Job Board and industry partners, distributing these roadmaps online and through NSCC and Nova Scotia Works to make advancement in the skilled trades transparent and attainable.

resources.name: COVE Ocean Careers
resources.description: COVE’s workforce initiative curates ocean-sector career pathways that outline entry-level roles, in-demand technical skills, and progression into mid- and senior-level positions across marine technology, shipbuilding support, ocean data, and related fields. It complements these maps with a directory of Nova Scotia ocean employers and events that connect talent to industry, helping learners and jobseekers see concrete advancement options within the province’s blue economy.

resources.name: Screen Nova Scotia – Get Started in Film & TV
resources.description: Screen Nova Scotia’s ‘Get Started’ resources map out departments and roles in the screen industry, showing entry pathways (e.g., production assistant), progression to specialized mid-level and senior roles, required certifications/skills, and guidance on rates and unions. The site links directly to Nova Scotia training providers, guilds, and local production companies, creating an accessible career roadmap for emerging workers in the province’s film and television sector.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 802, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

resources.name: Skills for Hire Atlantic
resources.description: Skills for Hire Atlantic provides role-based pathways into tech (e.g., software development, data, cybersecurity), outlining entry-level positions, the skills and certifications required to advance, and typical wage expectations sourced from regional labour market data. Developed and delivered in Nova Scotia through Digital Nova Scotia and partners, it pairs these roadmaps with employer engagement, job boards, and mentorship to connect participants to local tech firms and visible advancement routes.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 309, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Youth Entrepreneurship Microgrants and Clinics: Offer small start-up grants plus free legal, accounting and marketing clinics through community partners to help young entrepreneurs create scalable businesses that can hire locally as they grow.

resources.name: Accelerate Program
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia’s Accelerate Program provides non-dilutive, milestone-based funding (small startup grants) to help early-stage companies validate and grow, with many founders being young entrepreneurs. Participants also receive structured training and free clinics through partner experts—covering legal, IP, accounting, and marketing—to build scalable businesses that can hire locally as they expand.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 1101, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

resources.name: Spark Nova Scotia
resources.description: Spark Nova Scotia is a province-wide startup competition that awards non-dilutive cash prizes (microgrants) to early-stage founders, including young entrepreneurs, to advance their business ideas. The program also provides mentorship and workshops delivered with community partners—offering guidance on legal structures, accounting/finance basics, and go-to-market strategy—to help ventures become scalable local employers.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 1101, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

resources.name: Ready2Launch
resources.description: Ready2Launch is Dal Innovates’ summer accelerator for student and recent graduate founders, providing non-dilutive startup funding (typically $10,000 microgrants) alongside intensive training and mentorship. The program connects teams with pro bono or partner-supported legal, IP, accounting, and marketing advisors, helping young entrepreneurs build investment-ready, job-creating companies in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Entrepreneurship Programs & Clinics
resources.description: IGNITE operates rural innovation hubs that host free clinics, office hours, and workshops with legal, accounting, and marketing partners to support early-stage founders, many of whom are youth. Working with Invest Nova Scotia and regional partners, IGNITE also helps deliver funding opportunities such as Spark (non-dilutive microgrants), enabling young entrepreneurs to launch and scale companies that create local jobs.

resources.name: Student Entrepreneurship Program (SEP)
resources.organization: CBDC NOBL (Community Business Development Corporation Northern Opportunities for Business Limited)
resources.description: CBDC’s Student Entrepreneurship Program provides non-repayable microgrants to help high school and post-secondary students launch summer and early-stage ventures, typically covering startup costs like permits, marketing, and initial inventory. Participants also receive free business advisory support and access to consultant clinics (e.g., accounting, marketing, and legal) through CBDC’s network, directly aligning with the solution’s mix of micro-funding plus practical clinics to help youth build scalable, job-creating businesses.
resources.address: 35 Commercial Street, Suite 208, Truro, NS B2N 3H9

resources.name: Spark Zone (Nova Scotia Sandbox)
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University — Sobey School of Business Entrepreneurship Centre
resources.description: Spark Zone supports student and recent-grad founders with seed microgrants for prototyping and market validation, along with structured workshops and one-on-one mentorship. Through partner-led clinics and office hours (e.g., legal basics, bookkeeping and tax, branding and digital marketing), the program pairs small startup funding with free professional support so youth can validate ideas, form proper business structures, and position ventures to scale and hire locally.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Nova Scotia Sandbox)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University — Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs offers student teams small project and prototyping microgrants to de-risk early development while providing free expert clinics and mentorship on topics like IP, contracts, incorporation, financial modeling, and go-to-market. This mix of micro-funding and professional advisory support helps youth entrepreneurs build viable, technology-enabled businesses that can grow and create local jobs in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6050 University Avenue, Room 426, Halifax, NS B3H 1W5

resources.name: Volta Cohort and Expert Office Hours
resources.description: Volta provides non-dilutive startup grants through its Volta Cohort program (typically $25,000 awards) to early-stage founders, including students and young entrepreneurs, to help validate and scale ventures that can create local jobs. It also offers free legal, accounting, and marketing clinics via regular ‘Office Hours’ with partner firms and mentors, giving youth-led teams access to professional advice while building investment-ready, locally hiring companies.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 700, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

resources.name: CEED Startup Programs and Business Clinics
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: The Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED) runs startup programs and pitch-based microgrant opportunities that help young and first-time founders access small amounts of seed funding to launch and test business ideas. CEED complements this with free or low-cost legal, accounting, and marketing clinics delivered with community partners and advisors, enabling youth entrepreneurs to set up properly, refine go-to-market strategies, and grow firms that hire locally.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Entrepreneurship Programs and Partner Clinics
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic supports youth and early-stage founders in rural Nova Scotia with microgrant opportunities tied to regional pitch events and partner-funded competitions, helping cover startup and prototyping costs. It also hosts free clinics and mentoring sessions with legal, accounting, and marketing partners, equipping young entrepreneurs with practical expertise to build scalable ventures that can create jobs in their home communities.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

solutions.text: Co-working Spaces with Sector 'Pods': Develop affordable co-working facilities that include sector-specific pods (tech, creative, trades-adjacent services) to concentrate talent, foster collaboration and accelerate company growth into multi-role employers.

resources.name: Volta
resources.description: Volta is Atlantic Canada’s largest startup hub, offering affordable co-working, dedicated offices, and community amenities for technology founders and teams in downtown Halifax. By concentrating software, hardware, and digital creative companies across multiple floors and curating programming (mentorship, corporate innovation outposts, and community events), Volta functions as a tech-focused pod that fosters collaboration and peer hiring pipelines. This clustering increases job density and helps startups grow into multi-role employers with mid-to-senior career paths.

resources.name: Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE is a purpose-built ocean-technology campus offering shared co-working offices, shop space, prototyping labs, and on-water infrastructure for companies and researchers. The facility acts as an ocean sector pod that colocates startups, established suppliers, marine trades, and R&D teams, enabling daily collaboration, shared equipment, and industry partnerships. This concentration of ocean talent and services accelerates company scaling and creates diverse roles across engineering, operations, manufacturing, and field work.

resources.name: The PIER – Port Innovation, Engagement & Research
resources.description: The PIER is a supply-chain and ocean gateway innovation hub at the Halifax Seaport that provides flexible co-working, meeting rooms, and testbeds for logistics, shipping, port-tech, and marine-related firms. By clustering shippers, carriers, tech vendors, researchers, and workforce partners in one space, it operates as a sector-specific pod that breaks down silos and speeds up solution development and vendor–employer connections. This coordinated environment increases high-quality roles and advancement paths in operations, analytics, and product development across the maritime value chain.

resources.name: The Labs at the Life Sciences Research Institute (LSRI)
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia’s The Labs at the Life Sciences Research Institute offers affordable shared wet labs, co-working offices, and specialized equipment for health, biotech, and medical device startups. As a life-sciences pod, it colocates companies with mentors, clinical and academic partners, and shared core facilities, lowering barriers to R&D while building a dense talent network. The setup helps firms grow from founder-led teams to multi-disciplinary employers (R&D, QA/RA, manufacturing, and commercialization), strengthening career ladders in the sector.

solutions.text: Returning-Resident Attraction and Reintegration Program: Create a community-led program that maintains alumni networks, provides relocation support, matches returnees to local mid-level jobs and promotes pathways for rapid advancement on return.

resources.name: Halifax Connector Program
resources.description: The Halifax Connector Program matches job-ready returnees, recent graduates, and newcomers with established professionals in their field for curated, one-on-one networking meetings that often lead to interviews and job offers. In addition to building alumni-style professional networks, Halifax Partnership provides relocation guidance and introduces candidates directly to employers with mid-level openings and clear advancement pathways, helping returnees reintegrate quickly into the local labour market.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Cape Breton Connector Program
resources.description: This program connects returnees, new graduates, and newcomers with business and community leaders across Cape Breton to grow their professional networks and uncover hidden job opportunities. Working alongside local employers and sector partners, it facilitates matches to mid-level roles and links participants to community resources, easing relocation and supporting career progression in the region.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: A volunteer-led network of local Welcome Groups that support individuals and families moving or returning to Cape Breton with practical relocation help (community orientation, housing and services navigation) and warm social introductions. By building trusted community and professional ties for returnees—and making connections to local employers and mentors—the network accelerates reintegration and supports pathways to advancement in both established trades and emerging sectors.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works – Halifax Peninsula (TEAM Work Cooperative)
resources.description: As part of the province-wide Nova Scotia Works system, TEAM Work provides individualized job matching, employer connections, and labour market navigation for people returning to Nova Scotia, including virtual pre-arrival support. Services include resume coaching targeted to mid-level roles, referrals to wage-subsidy and upskilling programs that speed advancement, and direct outreach to local employers to build sustainable career ladders.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

resources.name: Volta Talent & Community Programs
resources.description: Volta connects experienced professionals—including Nova Scotians returning from away—with scaling tech companies through curated introductions, a regional job board, and career events that surface mid-level and leadership-track roles. Staff and the founder community provide practical relocation and ecosystem navigation support, helping returnees integrate rapidly and advance within high-growth firms in Halifax and across the province.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

solutions.text: Local Talent Scholarships with Return-to-Service: Fund scholarships (post-secondary or technical) that include agreements or incentives for recipients to work in the community for a defined period, creating predictable pipelines into local career ladders.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Learner Bursary Program (Return-of-Service)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health offers bursaries to students in programs such as nursing, licensed practical nursing, continuing care assistant, diagnostic imaging, and laboratory sciences. Funding is tied to a formal return-to-service agreement that requires recipients to work at a Nova Scotia Health facility for a defined period after graduation, creating a predictable pipeline into local roles and career progression within the provincial health system.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: Shannex Health-Care Student Scholarships (Return-of-Service)
resources.description: Shannex provides scholarships and education support for students in programs like Continuing Care Assistant (CCA), Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN), and Registered Nurse (RN). Awards typically include a commitment to work at Shannex communities in Nova Scotia for a set term after graduation, giving learners a funded path into local, in-demand roles and a clear on-ramp to career ladders in seniors’ care.
resources.address: 100 Baker Drive, Suite 200, Dartmouth, NS B2W 4M1

resources.name: MODG Medical Student Bursary (Return-of-Service)
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Guysborough
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Guysborough (MODG) supports medical learners with bursaries that require a signed return-of-service commitment to practice in the community for a defined period after training. By linking financial support to local practice, the program builds a stable pipeline of physicians into rural primary care and specialist roles, strengthening long-term local career pathways.

solutions.text: Job Shadowing Weeks and Rotational Placements: Organize community-wide job-shadow and short rotational placement weeks where young people experience mid- and senior-level roles across employers, building networks and reducing barriers to advancement.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Job Shadowing (Observerships)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health facilitates structured job-shadow (observership) experiences that allow students and jobseekers to spend short periods following clinicians, administrators, and technical staff across hospital departments. These observational placements, which can span multiple days, expose participants to mid- and senior-level roles and help them build professional networks, directly reducing barriers to advancement in health careers.

resources.name: ISANS Job Shadowing Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS matches newcomer youth and early-career professionals with host employers for short, structured job-shadow placements, typically ranging from a day to a week, to observe mid- and senior-level roles in their fields. By coordinating placements across multiple employers and sectors, the program builds networks, provides local references, and helps participants understand advancement pathways in Nova Scotia workplaces.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Management Career Services Job Shadow Experience
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Faculty of Management (Management Career Services)
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Management Career Services runs a Job Shadow Experience that pairs students with alumni and employer hosts for half- to full-day shadows inside their organizations. Students observe managers and senior professionals, ask questions about career paths, and grow networks across multiple employers during dedicated job-shadow periods, aligning with the goal of improving access to mid- and senior-level career ladders.

resources.name: Government of Nova Scotia Graduate Development Program (Rotational Internships)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Public Service Commission’s Graduate Development Program places recent graduates in paid rotational assignments across multiple departments over 18–24 months. These rotations provide exposure to mid- and senior-level public-sector work, mentorship, and a province-wide network, mirroring the solution’s short rotational placements that build career ladders and reduce barriers to advancement for young professionals.

obstacles.title: Wage competitiveness versus rising living costs
obstacles.description: Average wages lag national benchmarks while essentials (housing, food, transportation) rise, eroding quality of life and competitiveness with larger provinces.

solutions.text: Community Land Trusts for Affordable Housing: Create or expand locally governed community land trusts that buy and hold land for permanently affordable rental and ownership housing, prioritizing young workers and families and stabilizing long-term housing costs.

resources.name: Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia acquires land and builds homes that are sold to low- and moderate-income families through affordable, geared-to-income mortgages. By keeping land and homes within a community-governed nonprofit structure and applying resale and shared-equity covenants, Habitat preserves long-term affordability and shields these homes from speculative price escalation—functionally aligning with community land trust principles to stabilize housing costs for young workers and families.

resources.name: New Dawn Affordable Housing
resources.description: New Dawn Enterprises is a community development organization that acquires, develops, and holds residential properties in Cape Breton for below-market, long-term affordable rental housing. By keeping land and buildings in community ownership under a nonprofit board, New Dawn removes properties from speculative markets and uses long-term stewardship to maintain affordability—an approach that mirrors community land trust goals of permanent community control and cost stabilization for working families and seniors.

resources.name: Adsum Affordable & Supportive Housing (including Sunflower Court)
resources.description: Adsum for Women & Children develops and stewards permanently affordable and supportive housing—such as Sunflower Court—by acquiring and holding land and buildings under nonprofit, community-based governance. This model keeps housing off the speculative market and ensures long-term affordability for women, gender-diverse people, and families, directly addressing rising housing costs with a community-controlled approach consistent with community land trust principles.

solutions.text: Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Support Program: Organize workshops, design templates, and a local contractor directory to help homeowners add secondary suites or garden suites, increasing affordable rental supply while giving owners rental income.

resources.name: Backyard Suites – Homeowner Workshops, Design Catalogue and Builder Directory
resources.description: Backyard Suites is a Nova Scotia-based nonprofit that helps homeowners add secondary suites and garden suites by running free/low-cost workshops and webinars that explain zoning, permitting, and budgeting. They publish a design catalogue with standardized backyard/secondary suite plans suited to local bylaws and maintain a directory of local designers, builders, and contractors so homeowners can quickly find qualified teams. This end-to-end support lowers barriers to creating ADUs, adding gentle density and new long-term rentals while generating income for owners.

resources.name: Secondary and Backyard Suites (HRM Planning & Development)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality provides a dedicated program page, guidance documents, and step-by-step permitting checklists to help residents design and legally establish secondary suites and backyard suites. Planning staff offer support through 311 and at municipal service centres, and HRM has hosted public information sessions during policy updates to help homeowners navigate requirements. By clarifying design standards and streamlining approvals, the municipality makes it easier for homeowners to add compliant ADUs that expand the long-term rental supply.

resources.name: Secondary and Backyard Suites – Homeowner Guidance (Municipality of the County of Kings)
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings – Planning & Inspections
resources.description: The County of Kings enables secondary and backyard suites in its land-use bylaw and provides homeowner-facing guidance, application forms, and sample drawings to support typical suite layouts. Planning staff offer pre-application consultations and help residents navigate building code, permitting, and inspections. These practical templates and hands-on support help homeowners create ADUs or garden suites that add rental options while providing owners with supplemental income.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs) – Information and Permitting Support (Town of Truro)
resources.description: The Town of Truro permits accessory dwelling units and provides homeowner information packages, checklists, and direct assistance from Planning staff to design and permit secondary or backyard suites. By outlining design and code requirements and guiding applicants through approvals, Truro reduces uncertainty and accelerates homeowner-driven ADU projects. This municipal support increases gentle density and long-term rental availability while helping owners generate rental income.

solutions.text: Living Wage Employer Network and Certification: Form a local coalition of employers, non-profits, and unions to define a regional living wage, provide a certification program, and celebrate businesses that commit to pay wages that cover local essentials.

resources.name: Living Wage Atlantic Employer Certification
resources.description: Living Wage Atlantic is a regional certification and recognition program that supports Nova Scotia employers to adopt and publicly commit to paying the locally calculated living wage. The program provides certification, a public employer registry, and promotional campaigns that celebrate certified Living Wage Employers, while convening employers, community organizations, and unions in Nova Scotia to expand adoption and strengthen wage standards.
resources.address: 139 Prince Edward Street, Saint John, NB E2L 3S3

resources.name: Living Wage Policy – Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings adopted a living wage policy that sets a wage floor benchmarked to the regional living wage and applies it to municipal employment and procurement practices. By publicly promoting the policy and encouraging local businesses and non-profits to follow suit, the municipality helps build a local network of living wage employers and celebrates organizations that meet or exceed the standard.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

solutions.text: Local Salary Benchmarking and Transparency Hub: Run a community-managed, anonymized salary benchmarking service and jobs board so local employers and jobseekers can compare compensation against national/Provincial norms and negotiate fairer pay.

resources.name: Digital Nova Scotia Job Portal & Tech Sector Compensation Survey
resources.description: Digital Nova Scotia operates a province-focused tech job portal that aggregates roles from local employers and encourages the posting of salary ranges, improving transparency for jobseekers. They also publish anonymized, Nova Scotia–relevant compensation and benefits surveys for the ICT sector, benchmarking local pay data against Atlantic, provincial, and national norms so employers and candidates can negotiate fair, competitive wages.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: CANS Job Board and Compensation & Benefits Survey
resources.description: The Construction Association of Nova Scotia (CANS) hosts a public job board for the province’s construction sector, centralizing local opportunities and encouraging clear, competitive postings. CANS also conducts anonymized compensation and benefits surveys across member firms, producing wage benchmarks by trade and role that are used to set fair pay and compare Nova Scotia rates with Atlantic/provincial and national construction norms.
resources.address: 260 Brownlow Avenue, Unit 3, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1V9

resources.name: Dalhousie Management Career Services (MCS) – Job Board & Salary Reporting
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Management – Management Career Services
resources.description: Dalhousie’s MCS runs the myCareer job board for co-op and graduate roles with Nova Scotia employers and encourages inclusion of compensation ranges to support informed applications. MCS also compiles anonymized salary data from student and new-grad placements by program and industry, publishing benchmarking reports that help employers align offers with provincial/national standards and help candidates negotiate fair pay.
resources.address: Rowe Management Building, 6100 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: KBRS/Meridia Atlantic Canada Salary Guides & Job Board
resources.organization: KBRS (Knightsbridge Robertson Surrette) / Meridia Recruitment Solutions
resources.description: KBRS and its recruitment division Meridia publish anonymized Atlantic Canada salary guides and role-specific compensation studies drawing on employer surveys and placement data, with Halifax/Nova Scotia benchmarks to compare against wider Canadian norms. They also maintain a regional job board for professional and executive roles, often including pay bands, to improve transparency and support fair, market-aligned negotiations.
resources.address: Suite 1800, Purdy’s Wharf Tower II, 1969 Upper Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3R7

solutions.text: Paid Apprenticeships and Micro-Internship Partnerships: Partner with tradespeople, small businesses and colleges to create short paid apprenticeships and micro-internships that build skills, provide income, and connect young people to local career paths.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program places registered apprentices in paid, on‑the‑job training with certified journeypersons across dozens of trades. It partners with small businesses, union and non‑union employers, and Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) to deliver earn‑while‑you‑learn pathways that build skills, provide income, and lead to Red Seal certification and local careers.

resources.name: NSCC Apprenticeship Training
resources.description: NSCC delivers the in‑class technical training component for registered apprentices while partnering with employers across Nova Scotia to support paid, work‑integrated learning in the trades. These college‑employer partnerships help learners earn income on job sites, build marketable skills in short training blocks, and transition directly into sustainable local careers.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding recruits cohorts (including Mi’kmaq and African Nova Scotian learners) into paid pre‑apprenticeship and apprenticeship streams that combine NSCC training with on‑the‑job, paid work terms at the Halifax Shipyard. The program partners industry, colleges, unions, and community groups to provide mentorship from journeypersons, income while training, and direct pathways into high‑demand local trades careers.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship
resources.description: This program places youth and students in 9–15 week paid internships with municipalities, non‑profits, and small businesses across Nova Scotia’s clean economy. These short, paid micro‑internships build practical skills, provide income during training, and connect young people with local employers and career paths in environmental services and emerging green sectors.

resources.name: Co-operative Education Program
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University coordinates paid co‑op work terms with private sector, non‑profits, and government employers across Nova Scotia. These structured, short‑term paid placements function as micro‑internships that help students earn income, gain job‑ready experience, and build connections to local career opportunities in business, technology, and community services.

solutions.text: Youth Entrepreneurship Microgrants and Incubator: Provide small startup grants, mentorship, co-working space and low-cost business services for young entrepreneurs to launch local ventures that keep earnings in the community.

resources.name: CEED Entrepreneurship Programs and Co-working
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED offers training, mentorship, and co-working space to help new and young entrepreneurs start and grow businesses in Nova Scotia. Through programs like Launch and Grow as well as its microloan funds, CEED lowers startup costs with affordable services and financing, and connects participants to grants and advisory supports. This directly advances youth entrepreneurship by pairing hands-on coaching with space and early-stage capital to keep ventures and incomes in the community.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 216, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Incubators (Yarmouth & Pictou County)
resources.description: IGNITE operates rural innovation hubs that provide co-working space, maker resources, mentorship and startup programming for students and young founders in Western and Northern Nova Scotia. The hubs regularly host youth-focused bootcamps and partner-led microgrant competitions (such as Spark Nova Scotia regional heats), enabling small startup grants alongside advisory support and low-cost workspace. This helps young entrepreneurs launch viable local ventures without leaving the province.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: Start-Up Yard is an oceantech incubator offering shared offices, labs, prototyping facilities, and intensive mentorship for early-stage founders, including student and youth-led teams. Through programs delivered with partners (e.g., Ocean Startup Project challenges), participants can access non-dilutive seed funding/microgrants, technical expertise, and business services at low or no cost. This combination reduces barrier-to-entry and keeps new high-potential companies and earnings in Nova Scotia’s coastal communities.

resources.name: Business Is Jammin’ (Youth Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: Business Is Jammin’ delivers entrepreneurship education, coaching and mentorship for Black youth across Nova Scotia, and supports youth-led ventures with startup resources. Programs include camps and accelerators that provide seed funding or small microgrants for participants to test business ideas, along with connections to BBI’s advisory services and networks. By pairing capital with guidance and community-based support, BIJ helps young entrepreneurs build sustainable local businesses.
resources.address: 1660 Hollis Street, Suite 700, Halifax, NS B3J 1V7

resources.name: Spark Nova Scotia (Early-Stage Startup Competition)
resources.description: Spark Nova Scotia awards non-dilutive cash prizes (microgrants) and provides intensive mentorship and workshops to early-stage founders in regions outside Halifax, including many first-time and youth entrepreneurs. Winners receive startup funds to validate ideas and access a network of advisors and low-cost business services through Invest Nova Scotia and partners. The program directly enables young people to launch and grow ventures locally, strengthening communities and retaining talent.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

solutions.text: Community Childcare Cooperatives: Establish parent-run or worker cooperative childcare programs that reduce fees, increase availability, and enable more young parents to participate in the workforce.

resources.name: Needham Preschool Co-operative
resources.description: A parent-run, non-profit cooperative preschool in Halifax’s North End where member families share governance and volunteer classroom support to keep fees affordable. By pooling parent time and resources, the co-op expands access to early learning and childcare hours, helping young parents balance work or study with dependable, community-based care.

resources.name: Sackville Heights Cooperative Nursery School
resources.organization: Sackville Heights Cooperative Nursery School Society
resources.description: A community-based, parent-governed cooperative nursery school offering play-based early learning with family volunteer participation to reduce operating costs and tuition. The co-op model increases local childcare availability and helps parents remain in or return to the workforce by providing reliable, affordable part-day care within the community centre.
resources.address: 45 Connolly Road, Lower Sackville, NS B4E 1S8

solutions.text: Community Transit Solutions and Subsidized Passes: Work with municipal partners to negotiate bulk discounted transit passes, community shuttle programs, or volunteer ride-shares focused on connecting workers to employment hubs affordably.

resources.name: Low Income Transit Pass Program
resources.description: Halifax Transit’s Low Income Transit Pass Program provides eligible residents with a 50% discount on adult monthly passes for buses and ferries. By reducing monthly commuting costs, it helps workers afford reliable transportation to employment hubs across the municipality. This is a direct municipal subsidized-pass initiative that addresses rising transportation costs and supports workforce participation.

resources.name: Rural Transit Funding Program
resources.description: HRM’s Rural Transit Funding Program provides annual operating assistance and per-trip subsidies to community transit providers such as BayRides and MusGo Rider. These community shuttle and door-to-door services connect residents in rural areas to jobs, training, and mainline Halifax Transit routes at affordable fares, filling gaps where conventional transit is limited. The program exemplifies municipal partnership to expand community transit solutions that reduce commuting costs for workers.

solutions.text: Food Co-ops, Bulk Buying and Community Kitchens: Develop community-run food cooperatives, bulk-buy programs and shared cooking facilities to lower household grocery costs and build food security for young families and low-wage workers.

resources.name: The Loaded Ladle
resources.description: The Loaded Ladle is a student-run cooperative that prepares and serves free or pay-what-you-can plant-based meals from a shared community kitchen at Dalhousie University. By bulk-purchasing ingredients and organizing collective cooking, it reduces the cost of nutritious meals for students and young workers while building food skills and food security.

resources.name: Community Market & Kitchen Programs
resources.organization: The North Grove (Dartmouth Family Centre & Dartmouth North Community Food Centre)
resources.description: The North Grove operates a community market and community kitchen programs that provide low-cost produce, shared meals, and cooking skill-building for residents in Dartmouth North. By bulk-buying and offering affordable produce and meals prepared together in a shared kitchen, the programs help young families and low-wage workers stretch grocery budgets and strengthen local food security.

resources.name: WFM2Go
resources.description: WFM2Go is the Wolfville Farmers’ Market Co-operative’s online ordering and community distribution program that aggregates products from dozens of local producers for weekly pickup or delivery. By coordinating bulk-style, consolidated orders through a co-op structure, it reduces overhead and transportation costs, helping households access fresh staples at competitive prices while keeping food dollars local.

resources.name: Bulk Food Buying Club
resources.organization: Home of the Guardian Angel (Chebucto Family Centre)
resources.description: The Chebucto Family Centre’s Bulk Food Buying Club pools participants’ funds to purchase staple foods and produce at wholesale prices, with shares divided by volunteers for pickup. The centre also hosts community kitchen sessions and family cooking programs, directly lowering grocery costs and building cooking confidence for young families and low-wage households.

solutions.text: Energy Retrofits and Community Renewable Projects: Organize group purchasing for home energy retrofits, and develop community-owned solar or district energy projects that reduce utility bills for households and small businesses.

resources.name: Solar City
resources.description: Solar City is a Halifax Regional Municipality program that organizes and finances residential solar installations through a local improvement charge, leveraging pre-qualified vendors and standardized pricing to lower up-front costs. By aggregating demand and offering on-bill financing, the program functions like a group-purchase model for home energy retrofits (solar PV and solar hot water), helping households reduce electricity and heating bills.

resources.name: Home Energy Assessment
resources.description: Efficiency Nova Scotia’s Home Energy Assessment connects homeowners with an energy advisor who identifies cost-effective retrofits (insulation, air sealing, heat pumps, and more) and unlocks substantial rebates and financing options. The program directly supports comprehensive home energy retrofits that cut energy consumption and utility bills for households across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: HomeWarming
resources.description: HomeWarming provides no-cost energy assessments and home upgrades (such as insulation, draft-proofing, and other efficiency measures) to income-qualified homeowners, lowering heating needs and monthly energy costs. Delivered by Clean Foundation and EfficiencyOne with utility support, the program implements whole-home retrofit solutions that reduce energy burden for those most affected by rising living costs.

resources.name: Clean Energy Financing (PACE) – Town of Bridgewater
resources.description: Bridgewater’s Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) program finances home energy retrofits—including insulation, heat pumps, and solar PV—with repayment through the property tax bill, making upgrades accessible with no large up-front costs. By coordinating eligible measures and vetted contractors, the program scales retrofit activity across the community and helps residents lower their utility bills.

resources.name: Antigonish Community Solar Garden
resources.description: Operated by the Town of Antigonish Electric Utility, the Community Solar Garden enables residents and small businesses to subscribe to locally generated solar energy and receive bill credits for their share of the output. This community-owned renewable project expands access to clean power without requiring rooftop installations, directly reducing electricity costs for participants.

solutions.text: Shared Workspaces, Broadband Hubs and Remote Work Support: Create affordable co-working spaces with high-speed internet, meeting rooms and mail services so remote workers and freelancers can access higher-paying remote jobs while living locally.

resources.name: The Commons Halifax Coworking
resources.description: The Commons Halifax provides affordable coworking memberships with high-speed internet, meeting rooms, phone booths, and a virtual office option that includes business address and mail handling. These services enable freelancers and remote workers to operate professionally and reliably from Halifax while connecting to employers and clients across Canada and beyond. By reducing overhead and offering robust connectivity, the space helps residents pursue higher-paying remote work without leaving Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Volta Community Membership & Coworking
resources.description: Volta operates a large innovation hub in downtown Halifax that offers coworking desks, private offices, high-speed internet, meeting rooms, and mail services for companies and independent professionals. Flexible memberships and shared amenities make it easier for remote workers and startups to access national and international opportunities while living locally. This directly supports wage competitiveness by connecting Nova Scotians to higher-paying remote roles and clients.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: CEED Hub Coworking
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED’s Hub provides affordable coworking space with high-speed internet, meeting and boardrooms, printing, and a professional business address with mail handling for members. In addition to space, CEED offers entrepreneurship training and advisory support, helping freelancers and remote workers stabilize income and scale client work from Nova Scotia. These supports reduce operating costs and enable access to higher-paying remote contracts and jobs while remaining in the province.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Time Banks and Skill-Swap Networks: Set up a localized time-bank system where residents exchange hours of service (childcare, tutoring, maintenance), reducing cash expenses and strengthening community support.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: A member-run lending library providing access to tools and hands-on skill-share workshops and fix-it nights where residents teach one another home repair, maintenance, and DIY skills. Members can offset fees through volunteer hours and contribute skills to peer-led sessions, creating a local skill-swap network that reduces out-of-pocket costs for repairs and maintenance.

resources.name: Bike Again! Community Bike Shop
resources.description: A volunteer-driven, do-it-yourself bicycle repair program where community members learn from experienced volunteers during open shop nights and workshops. Participants can exchange volunteer time for access, skills, and occasionally refurbished bikes, building a practical skill-swap network that lowers transportation costs for residents.

resources.name: Repair Café Halifax (Halifax Public Libraries)
resources.description: A recurring series where residents bring broken household items and work side-by-side with volunteer fixers to diagnose and repair them for free. By exchanging time and know-how instead of money, the events cultivate ongoing peer-to-peer skill-sharing and reduce replacement and repair costs for community members.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Work Trade and Skill-Share Programs
resources.description: Community-based programs offering work-trade opportunities where volunteers exchange hours of service for workshop access or program participation in areas like carpentry, energy efficiency, and sustainable living. Regular skill-share events and work parties facilitate resident-to-resident learning, strengthening a local time-and-skill exchange that reduces cash barriers.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

resources.name: Annapolis Valley Regional Library Repair Café (Berwick Library)
resources.description: Library-hosted repair cafés and how-to workshops connect residents with volunteer fixers to co-repair small appliances, clothing, and household items at no cost. These peer-led, time-based exchanges help community members learn practical skills and avoid replacement expenses, building a sustainable local skill-swap network.

solutions.text: Community Investment Funds and Worker Co-ops: Establish a local revolving investment fund or community bond program to finance worker cooperatives, affordable housing or small business growth that keeps returns and jobs local.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: New Dawn raises capital from Nova Scotia residents through Community Economic Development Investment Fund (CEDIF) share offerings and invests it in Cape Breton–based businesses and community projects. By channeling local savings into local enterprises and affordable housing developments, the fund keeps returns and decision-making in the community while creating and retaining jobs. This directly supports wage growth and quality of life by financing locally rooted ventures that circulate profits and employment within Nova Scotia.

resources.name: FarmWorks Investment Co-operative Limited (CEDIF)
resources.description: FarmWorks is a provincially recognized CEDIF that raises community investment to provide patient, revolving loans to Nova Scotia food and agriculture businesses. The fund finances startups and expansions that strengthen local supply chains, create rural employment, and keep profits circulating in the province. By mobilizing resident investors and recycling repayments into new loans, FarmWorks exemplifies a community investment model that boosts small business growth and local resilience.

resources.name: CEED Microloan and Impact Financing
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED operates revolving microloan and impact financing programs that provide accessible capital to new and growing small businesses in the Halifax region. As loans are repaid, funds are recycled to the next cohort of entrepreneurs, keeping resources and job creation local. Paired with training and mentorship, this community-focused financing improves the viability of small enterprises that can raise wages and strengthen quality of life in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Just Us! Coffee Roasters Worker Co-operative
resources.description: Just Us! is a worker-owned co-operative that roasts and distributes fair-trade coffee while anchoring good jobs and profits in Nova Scotia. Worker-owners share governance and surplus, demonstrating how the co-operative model can improve job quality and keep economic returns local. As a mature worker co-op, it shows how community-minded ownership can contribute to wage security and cost-of-living resilience for young workers in the province.

solutions.text: Financial Counseling, Rent-to-Own Pathways and Housing Navigation: Offer free or low-cost financial coaching, tenant/first-time-buyer workshops and community-led rent-to-own pilot programs to help young people plan and secure stable housing without excessive cost burden.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Rent to Own Program
resources.organization: Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing (Housing Nova Scotia)
resources.description: A provincial initiative that helps eligible renters transition to homeownership by allowing a portion of their monthly rent to be credited toward a future down payment. Delivered through Housing Nova Scotia and partner developers, the program provides a structured pathway to owning a home without the immediate burden of a full down payment, aligning with rent-to-own pathways in the solution.

resources.name: ISANS Financial Literacy and Housing Support for Newcomers
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS offers free financial literacy coaching, budgeting and banking workshops, and information sessions on tenant rights and renting in Nova Scotia. Settlement counsellors also provide housing navigation support, helping young newcomers understand leases, find affordable rentals, and plan for future homeownership, directly implementing the financial coaching and tenant education aspects of the solution.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service – Tenant Rights & Housing Law Workshops
resources.description: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service delivers public legal education workshops on tenant rights, leases, and dispute resolution, and provides legal support to renters navigating the housing system. These workshops equip young tenants with practical knowledge to secure and maintain housing, reducing cost burdens through prevention of unlawful fees and evictions while offering navigation through complex tenancy issues.

resources.name: Money Matters & Housing Information Sessions (Halifax Public Libraries)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts free Money Matters financial literacy workshops and periodic tenant/first-time homebuyer information sessions in partnership with community experts. These sessions provide budgeting, credit-building, and housing education that help young people plan for stable housing and navigate the rental and homebuying process at low or no cost.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia – Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat Nova Scotia provides an affordable path to homeownership through education sessions, homeowner selection support, and a geared-to-income mortgage model that lowers monthly housing costs. By combining homebuyer readiness workshops, financial coaching, and an attainable ownership pathway, the program helps young families move from unstable or high-cost rentals to stable, affordable homes.

obstacles.title: Education-to-employment alignment and credential recognition
obstacles.description: Gaps between training programs and employer needs, limited co-ops/apprenticeships, and slow recognition of out-of-province/international credentials delay entry into fulfilling work.

solutions.text: Local Employer–Education Advisory Councils: Form neighbourhood or municipal advisory councils that meet quarterly to align curricula, co-op placements and local labour needs; include employers, teachers, community orgs and youth to shape training priorities and feedback loops.

resources.name: Program Advisory Committees (PACs)
resources.description: NSCC operates Program Advisory Committees for nearly all programs and campuses, bringing together local employers, faculty, students/alumni, and community partners to provide continuous feedback on program content and delivery. These committees meet regularly to align curricula with local labour needs, shape co-op and work‑integrated learning opportunities, and ensure rapid updates to training based on employer input—functioning as local employer–education advisory councils with feedback loops.

resources.name: Trade Advisory Committees (TACs)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency convenes Trade Advisory Committees made up of employers, journeypersons, educators/training providers, and apprentices to review training standards and advise on program requirements. These committees meet to align apprenticeship curricula with industry demand, expand and coordinate co-op/apprenticeship placements, and streamline recognition of credentials and prior learning—directly implementing employer–education advisory mechanisms that keep training responsive to local labour markets.

resources.name: Industry Advisory Board (Faculty of Computer Science)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Faculty of Computer Science engages an Industry Advisory Board of local and regional employers who meet with faculty leadership to advise on curriculum, emerging skill needs, and experiential learning. The board helps shape co-op pathways, recommends program updates, and builds feedback loops between students, educators, and employers—operating as a local employer–education advisory council that keeps training aligned with Halifax’s tech labour market.

solutions.text: Community Micro-Internship Program: Create short (2–8 week) paid micro-internships hosted by local businesses and non-profits to give youth hands-on experience, build portfolios, and establish employer relationships without full long-term commitment.

resources.name: Level UP Micro-Internships
resources.description: Level UP provides paid, project-based micro-internships of approximately 80 hours that students complete over 2–8 weeks for Canadian SMEs and non-profits. Students in Nova Scotia are matched with local and national employers to deliver real deliverables (e.g., marketing plans, data analysis), earning a stipend while building portfolios and employer relationships—directly aligning classroom learning with workforce needs.
resources.address: 200-128 West Pender Street, Vancouver, BC V6B 1R8

resources.name: Intrapreneurship Program
resources.description: Venture for Canada’s Intrapreneurship Program places post-secondary students in 6–8 week, 80–100 hour paid project placements with startups and small businesses, including companies based in Nova Scotia. These short, employer-defined projects give youth hands-on experience, help them build portfolios and references, and strengthen education-to-employment alignment without requiring a full-term work placement.
resources.address: 171 East Liberty Street, Suite 100, Toronto, ON M6K 3P6

resources.name: Summer Work Student Exchange (SWSE)
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth (local partner for YMCA of Greater Toronto’s SWSE)
resources.description: SWSE offers 6-week, paid summer work experiences for youth with host employers such as municipalities and non-profits in communities across Nova Scotia. Participants earn wages while completing short, supervised roles that build practical skills and employer connections—functioning as community-based micro-internships that ease the transition from learning to work.

resources.name: Canada Summer Jobs (CSJ) – Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Employment and Social Development Canada (Service Canada)
resources.description: Canada Summer Jobs funds thousands of short-term, paid placements (often 6–8 weeks) with local businesses and non-profits across Nova Scotia. These roles operate like micro-internships, giving youth hands-on work experience, portfolio-building projects, and employer relationships while helping organizations address immediate skill needs.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1005, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Volunteer Skills Mentorship Network: Match tradespeople, entrepreneurs and professionals with young people for mentoring, job-shadowing and small projects; use community centres and libraries as coordination hubs.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program pairs internationally trained workers and recent graduates with established professionals in Nova Scotia for one‑on‑one mentoring, networking, and workplace exposure. Participants receive guidance on local credential expectations, informational interviews, and opportunities for job shadowing or short projects—coordinated through ISANS and partner community venues—directly aligning training with employer needs.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1H8

resources.name: Cape Breton Connector Program
resources.description: The Cape Breton Connector Program matches job‑ready recent graduates and newcomers (including youth) with volunteer Connectors—local business owners, tradespeople, and professionals—who provide one‑on‑one career mentoring and warm introductions to their networks. Through guided connections and community meetups hosted by the Partnership and local partners, participants secure informational interviews, job‑shadow opportunities, and short project leads that bridge education and training to real employment in Cape Breton.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship
resources.description: Clean Leadership places high‑school, post‑secondary, and recent graduate interns with environmental employers across Nova Scotia to work on real, supervised projects. Each intern is matched with a workplace mentor (engineers, technicians, project managers) who provides coaching, job shadowing, and career navigation support—creating hands‑on small‑project experiences that translate classroom learning into in‑demand green‑sector skills.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio
resources.description: The Lou Duggan Creative Studio at Halifax Central Library operates as an accessible community hub where local makers, tradespeople, entrepreneurs, and creative professionals volunteer to lead hands‑on workshops and mentor teens and young adults in practical, career‑relevant skills (e.g., digital fabrication, design, media, and craft). Library staff coordinate schedules, equipment, and outreach, enabling job‑shadow‑style learning and small portfolio projects that connect youth to industry practices in a welcoming public space.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Local Recognition & Bridging Committees: Set up community panels (including licensed practitioners) to advise on recognizing out-of-province and international credentials, identify gaps, and recommend local bridging courses or supervised work placements.

resources.name: Practice Ready Assessment Nova Scotia (PRA-NS)
resources.organization: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Nova Scotia (CPSNS) in partnership with Nova Scotia Health
resources.description: PRA-NS assesses international medical graduates through a structured process led by licensed physicians who review credentials, evaluate competencies, and conduct supervised clinical field assessments in Nova Scotia communities. The program identifies individual gaps and recommends targeted bridging, mentorship, and supervised practice placements to align candidates with provincial standards, expediting recognition and entry to work.
resources.address: Suite 400, 175 Western Parkway, Bedford, NS B4B 0V1

resources.name: Internationally Educated Nurse (IEN) Registration Pathway
resources.description: NSCN’s IEN pathway uses a registration committee composed of licensed nurses and public representatives to assess out-of-province and international credentials, determine equivalency, and identify competency gaps. The pathway directs applicants to bridging options such as competency assessments, additional coursework, orientation modules, and supervised practice experiences with local employers to ensure safe, timely integration into Nova Scotia’s workforce.

resources.name: Professional Practice Program (PPP)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ PPP connects internationally trained professionals with supervised work placements and mentorships hosted by local employers and licensed practitioners. Employment specialists collaborate with regulatory bodies and industry partners to review credentials, pinpoint gaps, and recommend bridging courses, workplace language training, and on-the-job experience that align candidates with Nova Scotia’s standards and employer needs.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Candidacy Mentorship Program (CMP)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Social Workers (NSCSW)
resources.description: NSCSW’s registration process, overseen by its Board of Examiners, evaluates out-of-province and international applicants’ education and experience, identifies gaps, and assigns conditions to licensure. The Candidacy Mentorship Program provides supervised, structured practice under licensed social workers, functioning as a bridging mechanism to build competencies required for full registration and meaningful employment in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1888 Brunswick Street, Suite 700, Halifax, NS B3J 3J8

solutions.text: Community-Funded Bridging Scholarships: Establish a locally administered fund to cover exam fees, short bridging course tuition, licensing costs and tool purchases for newcomers and returning residents to speed credential recognition.

resources.name: Atlantic Immigrant Career Loan Fund (AICLF)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: AICLF provides low-interest microloans to internationally trained newcomers so they can pay for credential recognition costs like licensing and certification exam fees, short bridging or upgrading courses, professional assessments, and required tools. By removing upfront financial barriers and pairing financing with career advising, the fund accelerates credential recognition and helps newcomers enter in-demand jobs faster.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Skills Development Program
resources.organization: Employment Nova Scotia, Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: Skills Development provides individual funding for eligible jobseekers to cover short, industry-recognized training aligned to employer needs, including course tuition, certification and licensing exam fees, and essential equipment or tools. Delivered through Nova Scotia Works centres across the province, it functions like a bridging scholarship that reduces time and cost barriers to gaining or recognizing credentials for rapid entry into work.

resources.name: NSCC Student Awards (Make Way Campaign)
resources.description: NSCC’s donor-funded Student Awards provide bursaries and scholarships that students can use to pay for bridging and upgrade courses, certification and licensing exam fees, and required tools or safety gear—especially in trades, health, IT, and community services. These community-funded awards directly reduce financial barriers to credential completion and recognition, helping learners transition quickly from training to employment.

resources.name: ISET Employment & Training Program
resources.description: Through the Indigenous Skills and Employment Training (ISET) program, the Mi'kmaw Native Friendship Centre provides financial assistance for short courses, certification and licensing exams, safety tickets, and work-related tools and equipment. Administered locally, this support acts as a bridging scholarship that helps Indigenous clients obtain or recognize credentials and move faster into skilled employment in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Skills-to-Work Portable Micro-credentials: Partner with community colleges and libraries to create bite-sized, locally recognised digital badges (e.g., CNC basics, childcare first steps, web dev fundamentals) that employers commit to accepting as evidence of skill.

resources.name: NSCC MicroCredentials and Digital Badges
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College offers short, stackable micro-credentials that issue portable digital badges in areas such as CNC operations, early childhood education fundamentals, and web development basics. Developed with industry partners and aligned to local labour-market needs, these bite-sized credentials are recognized by employers across Nova Scotia as evidence of specific, job-ready skills, helping learners transition more quickly from training to work.

resources.name: Dalhousie Microcredentials and Digital Badges
resources.organization: Dalhousie University — Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development delivers micro-credentials with digital badges in areas like data analytics, cybersecurity, project management, and web development fundamentals. Courses are co-designed with employers and professional associations, producing portable badges (shareable on resumes and LinkedIn) that validate discrete, work-relevant competencies and speed education-to-employment alignment.

resources.name: Professional and Continuing Studies Micro-credentials
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University — Professional and Continuing Studies
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University’s Professional and Continuing Studies offers short, stackable micro-credentials that confer digital badges in business, data and analytics, leadership, and digital skills. Programs are informed by employer input and regional workforce needs, enabling learners to quickly earn locally recognized badges that signal verified, job-ready skills to hiring managers.

resources.name: CBU Continuing Education Micro-credentials
resources.description: Cape Breton University offers micro-credentials through Continuing Education in fields such as health and community services, business technology, and energy sector fundamentals, issuing portable digital badges upon completion. Designed with local industry partners and community employers, these targeted credentials address specific skill gaps and provide rapid, recognizable proof-of-skill for hiring.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

solutions.text: Neighbourhood Co-op and Apprenticeship Hubs: Coordinate local businesses to share co-op and apprenticeship placements across firms and seasons so small employers can host learners without bearing all supervision costs.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth
resources.organization: Construction Association of Nova Scotia (in partnership with Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and Nova Scotia Department of Education & Early Childhood Development)
resources.description: A summer co-op program that recruits, safety-trains, and places Nova Scotia high school students with a network of construction employers across the province. By centrally handling screening, onboarding, and paperwork, it allows small and mid-sized contractors to host learners with reduced supervision and administrative burden, and it can coordinate placements over multiple seasons and worksites so experience is shared across firms.
resources.address: 260 Brownlow Avenue, Unit 3, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1V9

resources.name: NSCC Work-Integrated Learning (Co-op, Internships, and Applied Learning)
resources.description: NSCC’s WIL team coordinates co-op and internship placements across hundreds of small and medium-sized employers in communities throughout Nova Scotia. The college screens candidates, manages term timing (fall/winter/summer), and provides evaluation frameworks, enabling employers to share talent across seasons and companies while minimizing supervision, recruitment, and administrative costs.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Co-operative Education
resources.description: Dalhousie’s co-op offices (e.g., Management Career Services and SITE Co-op) centrally recruit and match students with employers for 4–8 month work terms across fall, winter, and summer. By handling job postings, candidate vetting, site visits, and performance evaluations, they make it practical for small businesses to host learners and share placements across firms and seasons without carrying the full supervision and administrative load.

resources.name: COVE Internship Program
resources.description: COVE coordinates internship and co-op opportunities across its ocean technology cluster, matching students with multiple resident and partner companies. The hub centralizes recruitment, onboarding, and shared programming, which helps small marine and tech firms host interns and, where appropriate, arrange rotations or successive terms so experiential learning is distributed across employers.

resources.name: Study and Stay Nova Scotia
resources.description: This program supports international students to build careers in Nova Scotia by coordinating employer connections, mentorship, and paid work experiences across a consortium of local businesses. EduNova’s centralized model reduces hiring friction for small employers and enables shared placement opportunities and staged work terms across firms, accelerating education-to-employment alignment.
resources.address: 1888 Brunswick Street, Suite 807, Halifax, NS B3J 3J8

solutions.text: Community Assessment Centres for Competency Validation: Run local assessment events where experienced volunteers and instructors evaluate practical skills of job-seekers (including internationally trained) and provide competency certificates tied to local employer needs.

resources.name: Trade Qualifier (TQ) and Practical Assessment Pathway
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency runs local practical assessments and examinations that allow experienced workers, including internationally trained tradespeople, to have their on-the-job skills evaluated by certified assessors and instructors. Successful candidates receive a Certificate of Qualification (and, where applicable, Red Seal endorsement) that is recognized by Nova Scotia employers, directly validating competencies and accelerating entry into in-demand jobs.
resources.address: 2021 Brunswick Street, 10th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 2S9

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) and Challenge Assessments
resources.description: NSCC delivers campus-based RPL that uses portfolio reviews, challenge exams, and skills demonstrations assessed by faculty to verify learners’ practical competencies. These assessments can grant course credit or microcredentials tied to industry standards and local employer needs, shortening training time and providing college-backed competency validation for job seekers, including internationally trained professionals.

resources.name: Nursing Community Assessment Service (NCAS) – Nova Scotia Pathway
resources.description: Through NSCN, internationally educated nurses complete NCAS multi-method competency assessments (computer-based testing, simulation, and OSCE-style stations) at local test sites to validate readiness for practice in Nova Scotia. The results produce an evidence-based report that informs licensing and targeted bridging, effectively certifying practical competencies aligned with employer and health-system needs to speed workforce entry.

resources.name: Early Childhood Education Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE)
resources.description: NSCECE runs an RPL pathway where experienced and internationally trained child-care workers are assessed by instructors through portfolio reviews, interviews, and practical demonstrations against provincial ECE competencies. Successful candidates receive credit and advanced standing toward recognized ECE credentials used by employers and the province for hiring and classification, directly validating community-based skills for faster employment.

solutions.text: Employer Pledge: Skills-First Hiring Pilot: Recruit a coalition of local employers to pilot skills-first hiring practices — trial résumeless screening, work sample tests and competency-based interviews — and share results with the community.

resources.name: Employer Support Services (ESS)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Employer Support Services convene a broad network of Nova Scotia employers and help them adopt skills-first hiring practices. The team provides tools and coaching for competency-based interviews, pre-screens and presents candidates using skills profiles (minimizing résumé dependence), and facilitates On-the-Job Training (OJT) placements that function as structured work-sample tests. ISANS regularly shares outcomes and employer case studies through events and publications, encouraging wider community uptake of skills-first approaches.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Employer Engagement Services (Job Development & Work Trials)
resources.description: TEAM Work Cooperative partners with a coalition of Halifax-area employers to fill roles through skills-first methods. Job Developers present résumé-lite candidate profiles that foreground competencies, coordinate paid work trials/working interviews so employers can assess real work samples, and coach hiring teams on structured, competency-based interviewing. The organization shares employer success stories and practical lessons through its employer network and events, helping normalize skills-first hiring in the community.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

resources.name: Industry Project Challenges and Hackathons
resources.organization: ShiftKey Labs, Faculty of Computer Science, Dalhousie University
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs collaborates with Nova Scotia employers to co-design real-world challenge sprints and hackathons where participants complete projects that serve as work-sample tests. Hiring managers observe and evaluate these deliverables and frequently follow up with structured, competency-based technical interviews—reducing reliance on traditional résumés. Outcomes are showcased at demo days and through public channels, encouraging more employers to adopt skills-first hiring practices.
resources.address: 6050 University Avenue, Room 426, Halifax, NS B3H 1W5

solutions.text: Shared Maker Spaces and Tool Libraries: Establish or expand community maker spaces and tool libraries that allow young people and newcomers to practise trade and tech skills, build portfolios and access equipment for training or small business starts.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
