resources.description: A member-based lending library offering hundreds of hand, power, and garden tools to the public, along with safety orientations and skill-building workshops. By reducing cost barriers to equipment and providing training, it enables youth and newcomers to practise trade and fabrication skills, prototype projects, and build portfolios or small business ideas without needing to purchase their own tools.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Creation Space)
resources.description: A public makerspace within Halifax Central Library offering 3D printers, sewing machines, vinyl cutters, and digital design tools, alongside free programs and staff support. It provides accessible, low-cost opportunities for young people and newcomers to learn tech and craft skills, develop prototypes or creative portfolios, and gain hands-on experience aligned with employment and entrepreneurship.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: The Garage Makerspace (LCLC Library Branch)
resources.description: A community makerspace featuring 3D printing, laser cutting, sewing machines, electronics, and multimedia tools, housed in the library at the Lunenburg County Lifestyle Centre. Through workshops, drop-in access, and staff guidance, it helps youth and newcomers build technical competencies, create prototypes and portfolios, and explore entrepreneurship or trades pathways using shared equipment.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Yarmouth Makerspace & Prototyping Lab
resources.description: IGNITE provides community-accessible prototyping tools (e.g., 3D printers, electronics, and fabrication equipment) plus mentorship and entrepreneurship programming for startups and youth. The makerspace enables hands-on learning, product development, and portfolio building for newcomers and young people, supporting training-to-employment alignment and small business starts across the region.

resources.name: The Deanery Project – Woodshop & Maker Facilities
resources.description: A rural community innovation hub with a fully equipped woodshop and maker facilities offering workshops in woodworking, sustainable design, and repair skills. By providing shared tools, training, and project-based learning, the Deanery helps youth and newcomers gain practical trade skills, build portfolios, and prototype ideas that can lead to employment or micro-enterprises.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

solutions.text: Community-led Language & Workplace Culture Orientation: Offer practical workplace English/French and local workplace customs courses in community centres to help internationally trained people and youth integrate quickly into local jobs.

resources.name: English in the Workplace (EIW)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ English in the Workplace (EIW) delivers customized, practical language classes focused on job-specific communication, safety terminology, and Nova Scotia workplace norms. Instructors partner with employers and internationally trained workers to build the English needed for meetings, customer service, documentation, and teamwork, while covering local workplace expectations and culture. Offered on-site at workplaces and in community settings, EIW accelerates entry and retention in local jobs.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: English Language Learning (ELL)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ ELL program hosts free conversation clubs, tutoring, and newcomer workshops in branches across the municipality, providing accessible, community-based language learning. Many sessions build everyday and workplace English, including resume and interview language, customer-service interactions, and Canadian workplace culture and customs. By connecting newcomers and youth with volunteer facilitators and peers in library community spaces, the program supports quicker integration into local jobs.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Continuing Education – French for the Workplace (Français en milieu de travail)
resources.description: Université Sainte-Anne’s continuing education stream offers practical French for the Workplace courses that help professionals, newcomers, and youth build job-related bilingual skills. Training emphasizes real workplace scenarios such as customer service, email and phone etiquette, meetings, and sector-specific vocabulary, along with insights into Acadian and Nova Scotian workplace culture. Delivered on campus, in community locations across Nova Scotia, or online, the program strengthens the bilingual capacity needed for local employment.

resources.name: English Language Learning (ELL) Program
resources.description: Chebucto Connections offers free small-group English classes and conversation circles at its community hub in Spryfield, making language learning accessible where people live. Sessions focus on everyday and workplace English, communication styles, scheduling, safety, and rights at work, and often connect participants to local employers and services. This community-led approach helps internationally trained residents and youth quickly gain the language and cultural fluency needed to secure and keep local jobs.
resources.address: 531 Herring Cove Road, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3R 1X3

solutions.text: Local Hiring & Skills Fair Series: Host regular themed hiring fairs and micro-workshops (trades week, tech week, arts & culture week) where employers commit to on-the-spot interviews, short trials and co-op offers targeted to youth and newcomers.

resources.name: ISANS Job Fairs & Employer Information Sessions
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS regularly hosts job fairs, sector-specific recruitment events, and employer info sessions that connect newcomers with hiring managers who conduct on-the-spot interviews and speed networking. Events often include short skills workshops (e.g., resume tailoring, Canadian workplace expectations) and pathways to co-ops or work trials, directly addressing credential recognition and faster entry to meaningful work for immigrants.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: NSCC Career and Employment Services – Career Fairs & Employer Showcases
resources.description: Across NSCC campuses, Career and Employment Services runs themed career fairs and employer showcases (e.g., trades, ICT, health) where recruiters provide on-the-spot interviews, co-op recruitment, and apprenticeship sign-ups for students and recent grads. Events are paired with micro-workshops like portfolio reviews, interview prep, and credential/skills mapping to ensure alignment between training and employer needs.

resources.name: Dalhousie Co-op & Career Services – Sector Career & Co-op Fairs
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Bissett Student Success Centre
resources.description: Dalhousie hosts sector-focused hiring and co-op fairs (engineering, computer science, business, health, arts) where employers conduct same-day screening and interviews and recruit for co-op, internship, and entry-level roles. These events integrate micro-workshops (resume clinics, pitch coaching, credential guidance) to bridge education-to-employment gaps and accelerate youth transitions into work.

resources.name: Hire Me Halifax
resources.description: Hire Me Halifax is a recurring hiring event where students, recent graduates, and newcomers pitch their skills to local employers, followed by rapid networking and on-the-spot interview opportunities. The program includes short prep workshops (pitch building, resume and LinkedIn tune-ups) and connects candidates to immediate roles, internships, and project placements across sectors.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Youth Entrepreneurship Incubator: Run a community incubator that provides mentorship, shared workspace, microgrants and market access for youth starting local enterprises, helping translate informal skills into sustainable businesses.

resources.name: CEED (Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development)
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED supports young founders with training, one‑on‑one mentorship, and cohort-based programming that helps turn informal skills into sustainable businesses. Its Halifax hub and partner network provide collaborative workspace and market access opportunities (pop-ups, vendor events), while CEED also connects youth to seed funding or microgrants through programs and pitch events, aligning learning with real business creation.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: JA Nova Scotia Company Program
resources.description: High school youth form teams to create and operate real ventures over a semester with guidance from volunteer business mentors. Students receive startup capital, meet in shared spaces, sell at trade fairs and pitch events, and gain market access and practical credentials—translating skills into viable enterprises and bridging education-to-employment.

resources.name: The Spark Zone
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University (Nova Scotia Sandbox Program)
resources.description: Part of Nova Scotia’s Sandbox network, the Spark Zone provides student and youth entrepreneurs with mentorship, coaching, and co‑working space at Saint Mary’s University and partner campuses. It offers seed funding through sandbox microgrants and pitch competitions and connects teams with industry partners and showcases, helping youth validate ideas and access markets.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs
resources.description: A Nova Scotia Sandbox at Dalhousie University that incubates student-led tech ventures with mentorship from industry and faculty and access to collaborative lab/co‑working space. It provides small project funding and pitch prizes and creates pathways to customers through pilot projects and showcases, helping youth convert technical and informal skills into market-ready businesses.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic
resources.description: IGNITE operates community innovation hubs that offer shared workspaces, prototyping resources, mentorship, and entrepreneur‑in‑residence support in rural Nova Scotia. Its youth-focused cohorts and challenges provide seed funding through pitch events and give market access via community showcases and local industry partners, helping young people launch and grow local enterprises.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

solutions.text: Community Champions for Credential Navigation: Train volunteer navigators to help residents understand credential recognition pathways, prepare applications, connect to bridging courses and accompany applicants to meetings with regulatory bodies.

resources.name: ISANS Community Connections: Professional Mentorship
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS recruits and trains volunteer mentors who act as navigators for internationally educated and out‑of‑province professionals, helping them understand licensure and credential recognition pathways in Nova Scotia. Volunteers support clients to prepare applications and portfolios, connect them to ISANS’ bridging options (e.g., occupation‑specific language, employment bridging, and orientation to licensure workshops), and can accompany clients to meetings with regulatory bodies or prospective employers. Staff licensing advisors create individualized action plans while volunteer mentors provide ongoing, practical navigation and advocacy to speed entry into field‑appropriate work.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YREACH – YMCA Settlement & Community Integration
resources.description: YREACH operates across Nova Scotia and trains local volunteers as community connectors and mentors who help newcomers and interprovincial movers navigate credential recognition processes. Volunteers and settlement staff assist clients in understanding licensing requirements, assembling documentation, preparing applications, and making referrals to bridging courses and apprenticeship/co‑op pathways; they can also accompany clients to regulatory body appointments or information sessions. This hands‑on navigation reduces delays into employment and aligns training and prior education with Nova Scotia workforce needs.

solutions.text: Local Credit-for-Experience Programs: Partner with regional colleges to create formal processes where verified community work experience, portfolios or employer references convert to course credit or advanced standing toward certificates.

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) awards academic credit toward certificates and diplomas by assessing prior learning gained through work, community experience, military training, and industry credentials. Learners can submit portfolios, employer references, and proof of competencies or complete challenge assessments to demonstrate they meet course outcomes, resulting in course credit or advanced standing that shortens time to completion.

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) — Faculty of Open Learning and Career Development
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Open Learning and Career Development
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Faculty of Open Learning and Career Development provides RPL to grant advanced standing within professional and continuing education certificates. Through structured portfolio assessment, competency mapping to course outcomes, and validation via employer references or documented work products, experienced learners can bypass specific courses and accelerate completion of their credentials.

resources.name: Advanced Standing (Portfolio Review) for Studio and Design Courses
resources.description: NSCAD University recognizes substantial prior studio practice and community-based creative work by granting advanced standing or transfer credit through formal portfolio review. Applicants submit portfolios and documentation of practice that assess equivalency to course learning outcomes, enabling them to receive credit toward certificates or progress more quickly in degree programs.

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education
resources.description: The Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE) offers an RPL pathway that converts verified workplace experience into credit toward the Early Childhood Education diploma. Candidates compile a portfolio with employer references, supervisor evaluations, and evidence of competencies aligned to course outcomes, and may complete assessments to challenge courses, reducing the number of courses required for completion.

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL)
resources.description: Cape Breton University recognizes prior learning gained through employment, community leadership, and professional training by awarding credit toward selected certificates and degrees. Using portfolio assessments and course challenge evaluations mapped to learning outcomes, CBU grants advanced standing so learners with demonstrated competencies can shorten their pathway to credentials.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

obstacles.title: Talent retention and return pathways
obstacles.description: Established out-migration patterns, weak alumni engagement, and scarce incentives or clear pathways for return make it hard to keep or bring back young talent.

solutions.text: Local Alumni Network & Directory: Create a community-run digital directory and regular meetup series for local alumni (students, former workers, emigrants) to stay connected, share job leads, mentor youth, and coordinate return initiatives.

resources.name: Dalhousie Alumni & Friends
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Alumni & Friends network maintains an online alumni community and communications hub that keeps graduates connected to each other and to opportunities in Nova Scotia. The office organizes regular events and meetups in Halifax and across the province, and runs mentorship and career engagement initiatives that link students and recent grads with alumni for job leads and guidance—supporting those considering a return to live and work in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Alumni Association
resources.description: The SMU Alumni Association sustains a digital alumni hub and communications channels to connect graduates, share career opportunities, and coordinate volunteer mentorship for current students. It hosts frequent local gatherings and professional networking events in Halifax and Nova Scotia, helping alumni who have moved away remain engaged and making it easier to return and rejoin the province’s community and economy.

resources.name: NSCC Alumni Relations
resources.description: NSCC Alumni Relations provides an online alumni community and communications platform for graduates of Nova Scotia Community College to stay connected and access resources. Through local campus-based alumni events, mentorship programs connecting alumni with students and recent grads, and frequent sharing of job leads in established trades and emerging sectors, the network supports talent retention and encourages alumni to build or continue careers in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Cape Breton University Alumni Association
resources.description: The CBU Alumni Association maintains a robust alumni network with digital communications that highlight opportunities on Cape Breton Island and across Nova Scotia. It organizes homecoming and regional meetups, and activates alumni to mentor students and share job leads—helping former residents and graduates stay connected and making it easier for them to return and contribute to the local economy and community life.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

resources.name: StFX Alumni Association
resources.description: StFX’s Alumni Association offers an online alumni community and directory, along with active Nova Scotia chapters that host regular gatherings and professional networking events. Alumni volunteer as mentors and speakers to support students and recent graduates, share job leads, and keep the Antigonish community ties strong—facilitating pathways for StFX grads who wish to return to or remain in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Returner Microgrant Program: Establish community-funded microgrants to help young people cover relocation costs, short-term housing, or startup expenses when returning to the area, administered by a local nonprofit or chamber of commerce.

resources.name: Micro-Grant Program
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business offers periodic micro-grants that provide non-repayable funds to women and gender-diverse entrepreneurs to cover early-stage costs like equipment, prototyping, market testing, and short-term operating expenses. Administered by a local nonprofit at Mount Saint Vincent University and supported by community partners, these grants help reduce the immediate financial barriers of launching or re-establishing a business in Nova Scotia, including for young returnees who are coming back to start up.

resources.name: Rural Innovation Fund
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic’s Rural Innovation Fund provides small, non-dilutive grants to rural innovators and early-stage founders to validate ideas, build prototypes, and cover critical startup expenses. Delivered by a community-based nonprofit with hubs in rural Nova Scotia, the fund helps returning young people reduce the upfront costs of launching ventures back home, creating clearer pathways to return and contribute to local economies.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty Placemaking Grants
resources.description: Downtown Halifax Business Commission awards micro-grants for small-scale placemaking projects (e.g., pop-ups, storefront activations, murals) that help people test ideas and activate underused spaces. These community-funded grants lower early project costs for returning young creatives and entrepreneurs, enabling them to quickly establish a presence and integrate into the local economy through visible, low-barrier initiatives.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 2A2

resources.name: Neighbourhood Grants
resources.description: United Way Halifax offers small, community-funded grants to residents and grassroots groups to run local projects that build belonging, services, and social enterprises. For young people returning to the region, these micro-grants can offset immediate costs of launching community initiatives or pilot programs, creating welcoming on-ramps to re-engage and put down roots.
resources.address: 46 Portland Street, 7th Floor, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 1H4

solutions.text: Local Mentorship Circles: Organize sector-specific mentorship circles pairing established local professionals with recent graduates and returners for career coaching, networking, and introductions to employers.

resources.name: Volta Mentors
resources.description: Volta Mentors connects early-career talent and returning Nova Scotians with seasoned local founders, product leaders, and technologists through structured office hours, peer circles, and targeted workshops. By organizing sector-focused mentorship sessions and making curated introductions to employers and investors, the program provides career coaching, networking, and warm referrals that help participants build careers and stay in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: NSCC Alumni Mentorship Program
resources.description: The NSCC Alumni Mentorship Program pairs students and recent graduates with established alumni working in their specific trades and sectors across Nova Scotia. Through guided mentorship circles, one-on-one coaching, and alumni-led networking events, the program facilitates career advice and warm introductions to local employers—supporting both retention of graduates and pathways for returners.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program matches internationally trained professionals and recent graduates with established local professionals in the same field for several months of guided mentorship. Through sector-specific mentoring circles, networking events, and curated employer introductions, participants gain local insights, build professional networks, and access job opportunities that encourage them to stay and thrive in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Cape Breton Connector Program
resources.description: The Cape Breton Connector Program connects recent graduates, newcomers, and returning professionals with experienced local leaders—'Connectors'—in their industry. It organizes curated one-on-one meetings and small networking circles that provide career coaching, expand professional networks, and generate warm introductions to employers, strengthening local retention and return pathways in Cape Breton.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

solutions.text: Community Employer Pledge: Encourage small businesses, nonprofits and public employers to sign a pledge to prioritize hiring and training local youth and returners, advertise positions locally, and offer internships with clear pathways to permanent roles.

resources.name: Graduate to Opportunity (GTO)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: GTO provides wage incentives to Nova Scotia employers who hire recent post-secondary graduates into full-time permanent positions, encouraging businesses and nonprofits to prioritize local youth and new grads. Employers commit to creating meaningful entry-level roles with training and mentorship, posting opportunities locally and building clear pathways that help graduates stay and grow their careers in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Innovate to Opportunity (ITO)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: ITO helps Nova Scotia employers hire master’s and PhD graduates into innovation and R&D roles by providing multi-year salary support tied to training and retention plans. Employers are encouraged to recruit locally, advertise roles within Nova Scotia, and establish structured onboarding that creates a clear pathway from early-career placement to long-term employment—supporting the retention and return of highly skilled talent.

resources.name: Co-operative Education Incentive (CEI)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: CEI offers wage subsidies to Nova Scotia employers to hire local post-secondary students for paid co-op terms that meet defined learning outcomes and supervision standards. By requiring structured, career-relevant placements and promoting local job postings through campus channels, CEI encourages employers to train youth in-province and convert successful internships into ongoing or permanent roles.

resources.name: Employer Engagement and Wage Subsidy Services (Nova Scotia Works)
resources.organization: TEAM Work Cooperative (Nova Scotia Works Centre)
resources.description: TEAM Work Cooperative’s Nova Scotia Works centre partners with small businesses, nonprofits, and public employers to advertise jobs locally, host targeted hiring events, and access wage subsidies for youth and early-career candidates. Employers enter placement agreements that emphasize local recruitment, on-the-job training, and clear progression from internships or subsidized roles to regular employment, supporting talent retention and return in the community.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Co-working & Remote Worker Hubs: Convert underused municipal or community spaces into affordable co-working hubs with high-speed internet and meeting rooms to attract remote workers and support new startups returning to town.

resources.name: Volta Co-Working & Innovation Hub
resources.description: Volta provides affordable co-working memberships, dedicated offices, meeting rooms, and enterprise-grade internet in downtown Halifax, alongside startup programming and community events. By offering professional infrastructure and a collaborative environment, it functions as a practical hub for remote workers and new or returning founders to build companies and careers in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship) Campus
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE transformed a former Canadian Coast Guard facility on the Dartmouth waterfront into a shared campus with co-working offices, labs, hot desks, and bookable meeting rooms with high-speed connectivity. This repurposed community asset brings together startups, remote professionals, and established ocean firms, creating an affordable, collaborative environment that attracts talent and supports venture creation in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: North Queens Business Hub
resources.description: The North Queens Business Hub is a municipally operated co-working centre in Caledonia that repurposes community space to provide affordable desks, private offices, reliable high-speed internet, and meeting rooms. It is designed to attract remote workers and support local entrepreneurs—including those moving back to rural Queens County—by giving them professional infrastructure close to home.

resources.name: Halifax Central Library – Co-Working and Meeting Spaces
resources.description: Halifax Central Library offers free high-speed Wi‑Fi, extensive open work areas, study rooms, and bookable meeting spaces that many entrepreneurs and remote workers use as a no-cost co-working hub. As a municipal community space in the city core, it lowers barriers for startups and returning talent by providing professional-grade connectivity and collaboration spaces without membership fees.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Returner Job & Skills Fair: Host regular local job fairs specifically marketed to alumni and returners that combine employer booths, skills-upgrade workshops, and on-the-spot interviews or hiring.

resources.name: NSCC Career Fairs & Industry Days
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College hosts regular, multi-campus career fairs and industry days that are actively promoted to current students and alumni, including graduates returning to Nova Scotia. These events combine employer booths with skill-building supports like resume reviews, interview prep, and short workshops, and many participating employers conduct same-day screenings or on-the-spot interviews to expedite hiring.

resources.name: SMU Career & Networking Fair
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University Career & Experiential Learning
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University’s Career & Experiential Learning Centre runs recurring Career & Networking Fairs open to students and alumni, including grads who are considering a return to Nova Scotia. The fairs feature employer booths alongside resume and LinkedIn clinics, interview skills workshops, and opportunities for employers to conduct on-the-spot interviews or make quick hiring decisions.

resources.name: ISANS Job Fair
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS organizes an annual job fair that connects jobseekers—including newcomers and Nova Scotians returning from away—with employers across sectors. The event blends employer expo booths with pre-fair skill-upgrade sessions (resume tailoring, interview preparation, and workplace-readiness workshops) and facilitates on-the-spot screening and interviews to accelerate hiring.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Job Junction Hiring Fairs & Employer Showcases
resources.description: Nova Scotia Works – Job Junction hosts frequent hiring fairs and employer showcases that are open to all jobseekers, including alumni and individuals returning to the province. These in-person events pair employer booths with resume reviews and interview coaching, and many participating companies schedule same-day interviews or make rapid hiring decisions on site.
resources.address: 6950 Mumford Road, Suite 109, Halifax, NS B3L 4W1

solutions.text: Apprenticeship and Micro-credential Pathways: Partner with community colleges and local firms to create short, stackable training and apprenticeship programs aligned with regional industry needs and guaranteed interviews on completion.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based apprenticeship and training pathway led by Irving Shipbuilding with Nova Scotia Community College and community partners that prepares underrepresented Nova Scotians for in-demand shipbuilding trades. Participants complete targeted, stackable training at NSCC and on-the-job learning with the Halifax Shipyard, aligning skills directly to industry needs. Graduates receive guaranteed interviews with Irving Shipbuilding and, in many cohorts, conditional employment opportunities upon successful completion.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY is a pre-apprenticeship pathway that partners high school students with construction employers for paid summer placements, delivered by the Construction Association of Nova Scotia with NSCC and industry. Participants earn stackable, industry-recognized safety micro-credentials (e.g., WHMIS, Fall Protection, First Aid) and are matched to employers through structured interviews, aligning training to immediate labour market needs. Successful participants gain hours toward apprenticeship, references, and often return offers that keep emerging talent in Nova Scotia’s construction sector.
resources.address: 260 Brownlow Avenue, Unit 3, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1V9

resources.name: NSCC Microcredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College offers short, stackable micro-credentials co-designed with employers in sectors such as oceans, energy, digital, and health, enabling learners to upskill quickly and build pathways into further study or employment. Programs emphasize applied projects and work-integrated learning, with employer partners participating in capstones, hiring events, and interviews for completers to accelerate entry into regional jobs. These credentials can stack toward certificates/diplomas or complement apprenticeships, creating clear, flexible pathways that help retain and attract talent in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Boat Builder and Marine Service Technician Apprenticeship
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Boatbuilders Association coordinates registered apprenticeship pathways in partnership with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and local boatyards, aligning hands-on training to employer demand. Apprentices complete stackable short courses (e.g., composites, marine systems, safety) that build toward trade certification while gaining paid experience with sponsoring firms. NSBA facilitates employer connections and recruitment events so completers can interview directly with hiring boatyards, strengthening retention in Nova Scotia’s marine sector.
resources.address: 2698 Agricola Street, Suite 201, Halifax, NS B3K 4C9

solutions.text: Welcome & Relocation Toolkit: Produce a practical toolkit (housing tips, childcare options, employer contacts, community groups, school info) for returners and distribute it through the alumni network, realtors, and employers.

resources.name: Welcome to Nova Scotia Guide and Settlement Toolkits
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS produces and updates a comprehensive Welcome to Nova Scotia guide and settlement toolkits that cover housing search tips, tenant rights, childcare options and waitlists, school registration steps, community groups, and employer connections. Their settlement practitioners share these resources in print and online, and distribute them through employer partners and community referrers, helping newcomers and returning Nova Scotians navigate relocation quickly and confidently.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Newcomer Services – Welcome to Halifax Package
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries provides a practical Welcome to Halifax package that consolidates rental and housing resources, childcare and school enrollment information, community organization directories, and job-search supports. The toolkit is available at branches and through outreach with partners (e.g., ISANS and YMCA YREACH) and local employers, ensuring returners and new residents can easily access relocation essentials.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Relocation and Immigration (New Employee Settlement Toolkit)
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s HR team maintains a relocation and settlement toolkit for new and returning employees that includes guidance on housing markets and neighborhoods, childcare options, school registration, spouse/partner employment, and community connections. Hiring units share these materials directly with recruits and alumni returning to Nova Scotia, aligning employer recruitment with a clear pathway to settle and thrive in the province.

resources.name: RE/MAX Nova Relocation Services
resources.description: RE/MAX Nova offers relocation services that provide clients with tailored welcome packets featuring neighborhood and housing market insights, local school catchment details, childcare directories, and curated community group contacts. REALTORS distribute these toolkits to families moving or returning to the Halifax area and often coordinate with employer recruitment teams, enabling a smoother transition into housing, work, and community life.
resources.address: 7 Mellor Avenue, Unit 1, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0E8

solutions.text: Local Business Incubator and Micro-loans: Run a community incubator offering low-cost workspace, mentorship, and small loans for young entrepreneurs who want to launch or scale a business locally.

resources.name: CEED Microloan Program
resources.description: CEED’s Microloan Program provides accessible small business loans paired with training, coaching, and advisory services to help early-stage and young entrepreneurs get started. Through its co-working/incubation space, CEED also offers low-cost workspace and hands-on mentorship, directly aligning with the incubator-plus-micro-loan model to help founders launch and scale locally in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Volta Residency
resources.description: Volta’s Residency program provides subsidized office space, a collaborative community, and mentorship from experienced founders and advisors to accelerate early-stage startups in Halifax. Residents gain access to programming and connections to capital (including partners and initiatives like Volta Cohort), creating a clear pathway to build and scale companies locally and retain talent in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE is an incubator for ocean-technology ventures that offers co-working and prototyping space, shared labs, and tailored mentorship from industry experts. The program connects founders to early-stage funding opportunities and investor networks while anchoring them in Nova Scotia’s blue economy, helping young entrepreneurs build and grow companies locally.

resources.name: Ulnooweg Business Financing
resources.description: Ulnooweg’s Business Financing program provides micro and small business loans to Indigenous entrepreneurs across Nova Scotia, complemented by one-on-one advisory support, mentorship, and training. By pairing accessible capital with ongoing guidance, the program supports young and emerging founders to start and expand businesses in their home communities, strengthening pathways to stay or return.
resources.address: 172 Truro Heights Road, Millbrook, NS B6L 1X1

solutions.text: Youth Civic Leadership & Decision-Making Seats: Create youth advisory seats on municipal boards and community planning groups so young people influence local priorities and feel invested in staying or returning.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: The HRM Youth Advisory Committee is an official advisory board to Halifax Regional Council made up of young people who provide input on municipal policies, planning, and services. Members advise Council and liaise with other boards and committees, ensuring youth perspectives shape local priorities and municipal decisions. By creating formal youth seats within city governance, the committee builds youth civic leadership and attachment that supports talent retention and return.

resources.name: Teen Advisory Group (TAG) – Halifax Central Library
resources.description: TAG is a standing youth committee at Halifax Central Library where teens co-design programs, spaces, and community initiatives, and provide recommendations directly to branch leadership. These advisory roles give young people meaningful, ongoing influence over a key community institution’s plans and services. By embedding youth voice in local planning and decision-making, TAG fosters belonging and civic leadership that can encourage youth to stay or return.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: IWK Youth Advisory Council
resources.description: The IWK Youth Advisory Council engages youth in structured decision-making roles with hospital leadership and program teams, reviewing policies, service changes, and facility design to ensure youth needs inform organizational decisions. Although focused on health services, the council gives young people formal influence over a major public institution that shapes community quality of life. This youth leadership pathway strengthens civic connection and investment in Nova Scotia, supporting retention and return.

solutions.text: Family Support & Childcare Cooperatives: Develop community-run childcare co-ops, flexible afterschool programs and caregiver networks to lower barriers for young families considering returning.

resources.name: YMCA Before & After School Program (Halifax/Dartmouth)
resources.description: The YMCA provides licensed before- and after-school child care with extended hours, PD day care, and school break programs across HRM. By offering flexible, affordable care close to schools and workplaces, it lowers day-to-day barriers for working and returning young families, supporting talent retention and return to Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Veith House After School Program
resources.description: Veith House runs a community-based after-school program that offers supervised care, homework support, recreation, and healthy snacks for school-aged children on a sliding-fee scale. This flexible, locally run option helps caregivers balance work or training with family needs, reducing childcare barriers that can deter young families from staying or returning to Halifax.

resources.name: South Shore Family Resource Association Family Home Child Care Agency
resources.description: This licensed agency recruits, approves, and supports a network of regulated home-based childcare providers across Lunenburg and Queens Counties, offering full-time, part-time, and non-standard hour options. The community-run model expands flexible, neighbourhood-level childcare capacity, making it easier for young families to work or return to the South Shore.

resources.name: VCDA Family Home Child Care Agency
resources.description: Valley Child Development Association operates a licensed family home child care agency that screens, trains, and supports approved home childcare providers throughout the Annapolis Valley. By coordinating a distributed network with flexible placements and subsidy navigation, it lowers childcare hurdles for young families considering staying in or returning to the region.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides on-site childminding so newcomers can attend language classes, employment training, and settlement workshops, while also connecting caregivers to local family supports. This practical, no-cost care reduces immediate barriers for young newcomer families to establish work and community ties in Nova Scotia, supporting long-term retention and return.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Returner Showcases and Success Stories: Regularly highlight returning residents who have built businesses or careers locally through profiles, events and social media to normalize and promote return pathways.

resources.name: Invest Nova Scotia — Stories
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia regularly publishes founder and company profiles, including many 'boomerang' Nova Scotians who returned to build businesses in the province. These stories are amplified through newsletters, events, and social media to normalize coming home and show tangible return pathways in sectors like tech, oceans, and advanced manufacturing.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 701, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

resources.name: Volta Stories & Founder Features
resources.description: Volta highlights startup founders and teams through written profiles, videos, and stage time at community events, often featuring Nova Scotians who moved away and returned to launch or scale companies in Halifax. By showcasing these returner success stories across its website and social channels, Volta promotes clear examples of how to come back and plug into the local tech and startup ecosystem.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, 7th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic — Entrepreneur Spotlights
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic profiles founders, professionals, and students who have chosen to return to rural Nova Scotia (Western and Northern regions) to build companies and careers. Through social media spotlights, blog features, and pitch/event platforms, IGNITE normalizes return pathways and connects returners with mentors, partners, and local opportunities.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

resources.name: SMUEC Entrepreneur Profiles & Events
resources.description: The Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre regularly publishes alumni and client success stories that include Nova Scotians who returned home to start ventures or advance careers, and features them at events like pitch competitions and the Starting Point conference. These profiles and showcases provide visible examples of return journeys and practical entry points into Halifax’s entrepreneurial network.

solutions.text: Alumni-to-Employer Matching Platform: Build a lightweight local platform to match alumni skills with employer needs, track return intentions, and advertise short-term project or contract work to ease re-entry.

resources.name: Career & Co-op – myCareer Platform
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Career & Co-op runs myCareer, a matching platform that connects students and alumni with Nova Scotia employers. Employers post full-time, part-time, co-op, internship, contract, and project-based roles while alumni create profiles showcasing skills for targeted outreach. The team also tracks graduate outcomes and location preferences through surveys, informing strategies to engage alumni who intend to return and easing re-entry with short-term opportunities.

resources.name: Career & Experiential Learning (Employer & Alumni Job Portal)
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University’s Career & Experiential Learning operates an employer–talent portal serving both students and alumni, aligning graduate skills with employer needs across Nova Scotia. The platform routinely features term, contract, co-op, and project-based postings that reduce barriers for alumni returning to the province. Staff maintain employer relations and monitor graduate destinations to strengthen talent retention and return pathways.

resources.name: Student and Graduate Employment (NSCC Job Matching)
resources.description: NSCC’s Student and Graduate Employment service runs a province-wide job board and matching support for NSCC students and alumni. Employers post apprenticeship, seasonal, contract, and short project roles, and graduates create profiles so their skills can be quickly matched to local industry needs. NSCC also conducts graduate follow-up surveys that track employment and mobility, informing efforts to re-engage alumni who plan to return to Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Career Services (Alumni & Employer Connections)
resources.description: Mount Saint Vincent University’s Career Services provides an online portal and advising that connect employers with both student and alumni talent. The service highlights part-time, contract, and project-based opportunities and facilitates introductions that ease re-entry for alumni relocating back to Nova Scotia. Graduate destination data and ongoing alumni engagement help identify and support those with intentions to return.

solutions.text: Housing Pilot Programs: Implement small-scale housing solutions like community land trusts, rent-to-own pilots or subsidized transition units to provide affordable, short-term housing for returners.

resources.name: Phoenix Youth Apartments
resources.description: Phoenix Youth Apartments provides subsidized, time-limited, staff-supported apartments for youth ages 16–24 who are transitioning to independent living, including those returning to Halifax for school or work. Residents pay rent geared to income and receive wraparound supports, creating a short-term, affordable landing pad that stabilizes housing while they build education and employment pathways—an example of subsidized transition units.

resources.name: SHYM (Supportive Housing for Young Mothers)
resources.description: SHYM offers up to two years of supportive, affordable housing for pregnant and parenting youth, combining rent-geared-to-income units with onsite life-skills, education, and employment supports. As subsidized transitional housing, SHYM provides a safe, short-term base for young families re-establishing themselves in Nova Scotia, helping them stabilize, pursue training or work, and plan for longer-term housing.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: The Sunflower – Supportive Housing
resources.description: Adsum’s Sunflower development adds small-scale, deeply affordable supportive units for women, gender-diverse people, and families, with rent-geared-to-income and onsite supports. These service-enriched, subsidized units function as transitional and stable housing that helps residents reconnect with school or work and move toward permanent housing—aligning with the solution’s focus on pilot-style, small-scale transition housing.

resources.name: Supported Housing for Women
resources.organization: Elizabeth Fry Society of Mainland Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Elizabeth Fry Society of Mainland Nova Scotia operates subsidized, time-limited apartments and housing supports for women and gender-diverse people leaving incarceration or homelessness. This transitional model provides affordable, stable housing with case management so participants can return to the community, pursue education or employment, and transition to longer-term housing—demonstrating the subsidized transition unit approach.
resources.address: 6169 Quinpool Road, Suite 302, Halifax, NS B3L 4P8

solutions.text: Community-sponsored Professional Re-entry Fellowships: Offer time-limited fellowships placing returners in public-sector, cultural or nonprofit roles with mentorship and networking to rebuild local experience and visibility.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship Program
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s paid, time-limited internships place youth and early-career professionals with municipalities, Mi’kmaw communities, nonprofits, and community organizations across Nova Scotia to deliver environmental and community-impact projects. Hosts provide day-to-day mentorship while Clean Foundation coordinates professional development workshops and cohort networking, helping returners rebuild local experience, references, and visibility in the province’s public and nonprofit sectors.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Municipal Internship Program
resources.organization: Association of Municipal Administrators Nova Scotia (AMANS)
resources.description: This one-year, paid program places emerging professionals with municipal governments across Nova Scotia in roles such as administration, planning, and economic development. Interns receive mentorship from senior municipal leaders and access AMANS’ province‑wide network, providing a structured, time-limited public‑sector placement that helps returners establish current local experience and professional connections.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1304, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Artist-in-Residence Program
resources.organization: Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21
resources.description: The Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21 offers time-bound artist residencies that include a stipend, access to museum resources, curatorial mentorship, and public engagement opportunities. By situating artists within a prominent public cultural institution, the residency provides visibility and networking that can help returning creatives re-enter Nova Scotia’s arts ecosystem and build local professional momentum.

resources.name: Artist Residency Program
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts runs structured, time-limited residencies that provide studio space, housing, mentorship from experienced arts professionals, and public programming opportunities. These nonprofit cultural placements help returning and emerging artists rebuild local profiles and networks through exhibitions, open studios, and community engagement across rural Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

resources.name: Artist-in-Residence and Emerging Artist Programs
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design offers time-limited residencies and incubator-style placements that provide studio access, mentorship, business skills development, and exhibition opportunities within a nonprofit cultural hub. These programs help returning and early-career craft artists re-establish local experience and visibility while building professional networks across the Island’s creative sector.

obstacles.title: Infrastructure and mobility gaps
obstacles.description: Patchy rural broadband, limited public transit, costly or sparse intercity and air connections hinder access to jobs, education, and cultural life across the province.

solutions.text: Community Broadband Cooperative: Form a locally owned broadband co-op to plan, fund, build, and operate high-speed internet for unserved or underserved neighbourhoods. Actions include member recruitment, feasibility studies, bulk purchasing of equipment, volunteer installation days, and applying jointly for provincial and federal connectivity grants.

resources.name: Chebucto Community Net
resources.description: Chebucto Community Net is a volunteer-driven, member-supported nonprofit internet service in Halifax that provides affordable access, email, and hosting to residents and community groups. It implements a locally owned broadband model by organizing members, pooling resources to purchase connectivity wholesale, running community Wi‑Fi/DSL services, and leveraging grants and volunteer effort to extend service and digital literacy to underserved users.
resources.address: Room 006, Chase Building, 6136 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: Valley Community Fibre Network (VCFN)
resources.description: VCFN is a community-owned, open-access dark fibre backbone in the Annapolis Valley jointly established by local municipalities and Acadia University. It advances the community broadband solution by coordinating regional planning, aggregating demand for bulk infrastructure purchases, and partnering with ISPs and communities to extend last‑mile broadband to underserved rural areas using municipal, provincial, and federal funding.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative (INSI)
resources.description: INSI is the province’s connectivity program delivered by Build Nova Scotia that partners with municipalities, community groups, co‑ops, and ISPs to plan and finance rural broadband builds. It supports the community cooperative approach by helping with feasibility work, enabling bulk procurement of infrastructure, and channeling provincial and federal connectivity funds to community‑led projects that connect unserved and underserved communities.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 301, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

solutions.text: Library and Community Hub Connectivity Nodes: Upgrade libraries, municipal halls, and community centres as public connectivity hubs with reliable broadband, extended hours, private work pods, and printing services so residents can access remote work, education, telehealth, and government services without needing home internet.

resources.name: Open Libraries (Self-Service Extended Hours) – Sheet Harbour Public Library
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Open Libraries program extends access to the Sheet Harbour branch beyond staffed hours, letting cardholders enter the building to use high-speed Wi‑Fi, public computers, printers, and study spaces. This creates a reliable connectivity hub where residents can work remotely, take online classes, attend telehealth appointments in private rooms, and access digital government services even if they lack home internet.

resources.name: People’s Place: Antigonish Town & County Library
resources.description: People’s Place operates as a community hub with robust broadband, free public Wi‑Fi and computers, printing/scanning, and multiple bookable meeting and study rooms for quiet, private use. Evening and weekend hours, along with staffed support, enable residents to do remote work, complete online education, hold telehealth appointments, and access digital government services without needing home internet.

resources.name: McConnell Library (Sydney)
resources.description: As the central branch of the Cape Breton Regional Library, McConnell Library provides high-speed Wi‑Fi, numerous public computers, printing/photocopying, and bookable study and meeting rooms suited for quiet work or telehealth calls. Extended evening and weekend hours make it a dependable connectivity node for students, job seekers, remote workers, and residents needing online government or health services.

resources.name: Margaret Hennigar Public Library (Bridgewater)
resources.description: Located within the Lunenburg County Lifestyle Centre, this branch offers reliable broadband with free Wi‑Fi, public computers, and printing, plus quiet and collaborative rooms that can be reserved for remote work, online classes, and virtual medical appointments. The centre’s extended facility hours increase access for residents who lack home internet or need after-hours connectivity.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

resources.name: Digby Library & Cultural Centre
resources.description: This modern rural library hub provides free high-speed Wi‑Fi, public computers, and printing/scan/fax services, along with bookable study spaces for privacy during remote work or telehealth sessions. By offering dependable connectivity and on-site support, it enables residents to participate in online education, employment, healthcare, and government services despite patchy home broadband.

solutions.text: Rural Digital Champions and Training: Recruit and train local volunteers to run digital skills workshops, help neighbours set up home internet, assist with remote-work tools, and host regular 'connectivity clinics' to increase adoption and make broadband investments more impactful.

resources.name: Tech Help (Halifax Public Libraries)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries runs free Tech Help drop-ins and digital literacy workshops at branches across HRM, including rural communities like Musquodoboit Harbour and Sheet Harbour. Staff and trained volunteer tech tutors help residents set up devices and home Wi‑Fi, learn remote‑work tools (email, Zoom, cloud apps), and troubleshoot connectivity issues at regular clinics—boosting broadband adoption and effective use.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Cyber-Seniors and Tech Help (Cape Breton Regional Library)
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library’s Cyber-Seniors and Tech Help sessions pair local youth and trained volunteers with older adults and other learners to build foundational digital skills. Through scheduled one-on-one coaching and drop-in clinics at rural branches, they help residents with device setup, home internet and Wi‑Fi questions, and remote‑work tools like Zoom and email—turning broadband availability into everyday adoption.

resources.name: Tech Help / Tech Time (Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library)
resources.description: PARL offers Tech Help/Tech Time at branches such as People’s Place Library, where staff and community volunteers host regular device clinics and digital-skills workshops. They assist patrons with getting online at home, setting up smartphones and laptops, choosing service options, and learning remote‑work tools (Zoom, Teams, cloud storage), acting as neighbourhood digital champions across rural Pictou and Antigonish counties.

resources.name: One-on-One Tech Help and Digital Literacy (Annapolis Valley Regional Library)
resources.description: AVRL provides one-on-one Tech Help appointments and beginner classes offering personalized digital coaching across rural Annapolis, Kings, and Hants County communities. Librarians and volunteer mentors guide residents through internet setup basics, Wi‑Fi routers, online safety, and telework tools, while recurring drop-ins serve as connectivity clinics that increase broadband take-up and meaningful use.

resources.name: Tech Help and Digital Literacy Programs (Eastern Counties Regional Library)
resources.description: Eastern Counties Regional Library delivers Tech Help and digital literacy programming throughout Guysborough, Inverness, and Richmond counties using small-group workshops and one-on-one support. Staff and volunteer tech coaches run regular drop-ins to troubleshoot connectivity, help with device setup and home Wi‑Fi questions, and train people on video calls, email, and online services—supporting rural broadband adoption and confidence.
resources.address: 390 Murray Street, Unit 145, Mulgrave, NS B0E 2G0

solutions.text: Community Wi-Fi Mesh Pilot: Deploy low-cost mesh Wi-Fi networks to cover village centres and dense clusters of households using community-managed nodes. Organize hardware donations, volunteer tech teams, and simple subscription or donation models for maintenance.

resources.name: Halifax Public Wi‑Fi (HRM)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality maintains a network of outdoor wireless access points that blanket key public spaces and transit‑heavy corridors with free connectivity. The system links multiple nodes across plazas and streetscapes to create mesh-style coverage, and is managed locally by the municipality and its technology partners, aligning with a community-managed approach to extend access where people gather.

resources.name: Halifax Waterfront Free Wi‑Fi
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia operates free public Wi‑Fi along the Halifax waterfront boardwalk, using a chain of outdoor access points mounted on buildings and poles to create continuous coverage in busy pedestrian areas. The network is locally managed and maintained with regional contractors, providing a community-scale mesh-style solution that supports residents, workers, and visitors in a key civic hub.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Lunenburg Free Public Wi‑Fi
resources.description: The Town of Lunenburg provides community Wi‑Fi across portions of the Old Town and waterfront by installing outdoor access points on municipal assets and partnering locations, creating a mesh-style blanket of service in the town centre. The municipality manages the network locally and sustains it through town resources and partnerships with local businesses, aligning with the community‑managed mesh model.

resources.name: Downtown Halifax Free Wi‑Fi
resources.description: The Downtown Halifax Business Commission has supported the deployment of free public Wi‑Fi in sections of the downtown core, placing multiple outdoor nodes on member businesses and streetscape fixtures to extend coverage across busy blocks. This community‑led approach leverages local hosts and sponsorships to manage and maintain a mesh-style network that keeps the district connected for residents, students, and visitors.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

solutions.text: On-Demand Microtransit Service: Launch a community-run on-demand minibus or shuttle service using a simple booking app or phone line to connect rural areas to towns during peak commuting hours and key services. Start with a volunteer or part-time driver pool and scale with rider fees and municipal contributions.

resources.name: Bridgewater Transit On Request
resources.description: Bridgewater Transit On Request is an on-demand minibus service that supplements the town’s fixed-route system during lower-demand periods. Riders book trips by phone or via simple online tools, and trips are dynamically routed to connect neighbourhoods and nearby rural areas with key destinations like downtown, health services, and employment hubs. The service scales through rider fares and municipal funding from the Town of Bridgewater, implementing a microtransit model aligned with community needs.

resources.name: Access-A-Bus (Paratransit)
resources.description: Access-A-Bus is Halifax Transit’s demand-responsive, door-to-door minibus service for eligible riders, scheduled by phone booking. It operates across urban, suburban, and rural parts of the Halifax Regional Municipality, connecting people to essential services, education, and employment when fixed-route options are limited. The program exemplifies on-demand microtransit funded primarily by the municipality with modest rider fares.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Eastern Shore
resources.description: MusGo Rider Eastern Shore is a community-run, on-demand shuttle service that provides pre-booked, door-to-door transportation for rural communities along Nova Scotia’s Eastern Shore. Riders schedule trips by phone or online to reach towns, medical appointments, education, shopping, and work, with shared rides dispatched to optimize routes. The co-operative uses paid part-time drivers and sustains operations through rider fares, municipal contributions via HRM, and provincial support—directly aligning with the microtransit model.

solutions.text: Volunteer Driver and Rideshare Network: Coordinate a vetted volunteer driver program for seniors, students and low-income residents needing access to medical appointments, schools, and employment. Combine with a community ride-matching platform to promote carpooling for daily commutes and events.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Eastern Shore Community Transportation
resources.description: Community-run, door-to-door transportation along the Eastern Shore that prioritizes rides for seniors, students, and low-income residents to medical appointments, school, work, and essential services. MusGo Rider coordinates a network of vetted volunteer drivers and shared trips to keep fares affordable, effectively implementing a volunteer driver program and informal ride-matching for rural communities with limited public transit.

resources.name: Strait Area Transit
resources.description: A community transit co-operative serving Richmond County, Port Hawkesbury, and surrounding areas with pre-booked, door-to-door and route-based service to medical appointments, employment, school, and shopping. By coordinating shared rides and utilizing community drivers, the service fills mobility gaps in rural areas and mirrors a volunteer-driver style network that reduces isolation and transportation costs.
resources.address: 604 Reeves Street, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 2R7

resources.name: Transport de Clare
resources.description: A non-profit community transportation service in the Municipality of Clare that provides pre-booked, door-to-door rides for medical appointments, education, work, and daily needs. The service coordinates shared trips and community drivers to keep fares low, functioning as a volunteer-style driver network that improves access in rural areas where public transit is limited.

resources.name: SmartTrip Halifax – Ridematching
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality hosts a free online ridematching platform that connects commuters for carpools to workplaces, campuses, and events, helping residents in areas with limited transit share rides. By matching drivers and riders and supporting employer and campus carpool programs, the platform implements the ride-matching component of the solution to reduce transportation barriers and costs.

solutions.text: Community Carshare and EV Charging: Establish a locally managed carshare fleet including electric vehicles housed at community hubs, with member booking, maintenance volunteers, and shared costs. Work with municipality to install public EV chargers at key locations to reduce travel costs and emissions.

resources.name: Communauto Atlantic Carsharing (Halifax)
resources.description: Communauto Atlantic operates a station-based carshare service across Halifax Regional Municipality, including electric and hybrid vehicles parked at community hubs such as parkades, libraries, and university campuses. Members book vehicles through an app, pay shared costs instead of owning a car, and use on-street carshare spaces provided through municipal partnerships—reducing transportation costs and emissions while filling mobility gaps.

resources.name: Halifax Public EV Charging Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality has installed public Level 2 EV chargers at municipal facilities—including parkades, libraries, and recreation centres—and continues expanding the network as part of its HalifACT climate plan. By placing chargers at key community hubs and working with network operators, the municipality reduces range anxiety and operating costs for residents and shared-mobility providers, supporting lower-emission travel across the city.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Power EV Fast-Charging Network
resources.description: Nova Scotia Power operates a province-wide network of public DC fast chargers and Level 2 stations, developed in partnership with municipalities, site hosts, and the Province. Strategically located along 100-series highways and in town centres, the network enables intercity EV travel and lowers transportation emissions and costs—benefiting residents, visitors, and carshare fleets that rely on accessible rapid charging.
resources.address: 1223 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

resources.name: Plug In Nova Scotia
resources.description: Plug In Nova Scotia supports communities, municipalities, and businesses to plan, fund, and install public EV charging at high-use community locations, and maintains a provincial charging map and outreach programs. By helping towns and community groups place chargers at hubs like arenas, libraries, and main streets, the initiative reduces travel barriers and emissions while complementing shared-mobility options such as carsharing.

solutions.text: School and Community Bus Sharing Program: Negotiate shared use of school buses and municipal vehicles outside school hours for community transit needs, weekend connections, and events. Create schedules that serve commuters and link remote neighbourhoods to transit hubs.

resources.name: CCRCE School Bus Charters
resources.organization: Chignecto Central Regional Centre for Education
resources.description: Chignecto Central Regional Centre for Education offers after-hours and weekend charters of its school buses to community groups, municipalities, and event organizers. This enables shared use of the existing school-bus fleet to provide community shuttles for events and to create custom pickup schedules that connect outlying rural communities to regional hubs such as hospitals, colleges, and intercity bus stops when regular public transit is limited.

resources.name: SSRCE Bus Charter Program
resources.organization: South Shore Regional Centre for Education
resources.description: South Shore Regional Centre for Education makes its school buses available for charter outside school hours, allowing municipalities, nonprofits, and community organizers to move residents to weekend activities and special events. By coordinating routes and times, communities use these charters to link rural neighbourhoods across Lunenburg and Queens counties to town centres and transit connection points when fixed-route options are sparse.

resources.name: AVRCE School Bus Charter Service
resources.organization: Annapolis Valley Regional Centre for Education
resources.description: Annapolis Valley Regional Centre for Education provides charter access to its school buses during evenings and weekends, supporting community transit needs such as shuttles for festivals, sports, and seasonal work. Local partners use these buses to set up scheduled trips that connect small communities in the Annapolis Valley with regional hubs (e.g., hospitals, campuses, and intercity bus terminals), filling mobility gaps where public transit is limited.

solutions.text: Employer Transit Partnerships: Encourage local employers to pool resources to subsidize shuttle routes, offer transit passes, stagger shifts, and support remote-work days. Small businesses can collectively underwrite a commuter shuttle that benefits multiple workplaces.

resources.name: Halifax Transit Employer Pass (EPass) Program
resources.description: EPass is a partnership program where employers in the Halifax region collaborate with Halifax Transit to offer their employees discounted monthly transit passes via payroll deduction. By pooling employee demand across participating workplaces, the program reduces commuting costs and encourages mode shift to public transit; employers can also align shift schedules with transit service to improve access for staff. This directly supports the solution by enabling employer-backed transit benefits that make commuting more reliable and affordable for young workers.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Employee Transit EPass
resources.description: Dalhousie University participates in Halifax Transit’s EPass program, providing eligible staff with discounted monthly transit passes through an employer partnership and payroll deduction. The university’s commuting and sustainability efforts promote transit use and flexible work practices where operationally feasible, helping to stagger travel and reduce peak-hour strain. This implements the solution by using employer resources to underwrite transit access and support scheduling approaches that improve mobility for employees.

solutions.text: Intercommunity Transit Coalition: Form a coalition of towns, chambers of commerce, post-secondary institutions and community groups to lobby for improved intercity bus and rail service. Collect ridership data, common-schedule proposals, and co-financing offers to present to regional transit providers and funders.

resources.name: Transportation Program
resources.description: Ecology Action Centre’s Transportation program convenes municipalities, chambers of commerce, student associations, and community groups across Nova Scotia to advocate for stronger intercity bus and passenger rail service with coordinated schedules and seamless connections. The team produces research and ridership-demand analyses and facilitates joint proposals that integrate university term-time travel and rural mobility needs. EAC regularly submits briefs to the Province, VIA Rail, and carriers, packaging co-funding commitments and data-backed schedules on behalf of local coalitions.

resources.name: Dalhousie Transportation Collaboratory (DalTRAC)
resources.description: DalTRAC conducts province-wide travel surveys and ridership modelling (e.g., NovaTRAC) that underpin intercommunity transit planning in Nova Scotia. Working with towns, campuses, chambers, and NGOs, the lab co-develops common-schedule options and connectivity maps for intercity bus and potential rail, and shares actionable datasets with service providers and funders. Its applied studies help coalitions quantify demand and build evidence-based schedule and co-financing proposals for regional transit improvements.

resources.name: Transportation and Infrastructure Advocacy
resources.description: NSFM’s advocacy brings together elected officials from towns and rural municipalities with chambers of commerce, post-secondary institutions, and community transit groups to press for improved intercity bus links and passenger rail in Nova Scotia. They compile municipal ridership needs, align common schedule asks across regions, and coordinate letters of support and cost‑sharing commitments. NSFM presents unified proposals to the Province, federal partners, and carriers such as Maritime Bus and VIA Rail to secure service enhancements.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1304, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Kings Transit Authority (Inter-Municipal Regional Bus Service)
resources.description: Kings Transit Authority is a joint municipal service funded by multiple towns and counties in the Annapolis Valley that coordinates regional routes and schedule connections, including links to intercity carriers serving the Valley. The authority gathers ridership data and works with partners such as Acadia University, local chambers, and municipalities to adjust timetables and advance funding proposals. As an intermunicipal coalition, it demonstrates the co-financing and schedule-integration approach that enables broader intercommunity bus networks.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

solutions.text: Local Air Service Advocacy Group: Create a community task force to engage regional airports and carriers to explore cost-effective seasonal or route-based air services. Offer passenger guarantees, coordinated marketing, and municipal support to make routes viable.

resources.name: Air Service Development
resources.description: Halifax Stanfield’s Air Service Development team works directly with airlines, municipalities, provincial partners, and destination marketers to identify and launch viable seasonal and year-round routes. They coordinate cooperative marketing, provide market data and demand forecasts, and help structure community-backed risk‑sharing tools (such as minimum revenue guarantees supported by public and private partners) to de‑risk new or returning services, aligning closely with the proposed advocacy-task-force model.

resources.name: Air Service Development
resources.organization: Sydney Airport Authority Inc. (J.A. Douglas McCurdy Sydney Airport)
resources.description: Sydney Airport partners with Cape Breton municipalities, business groups, and tourism organizations to attract and sustain seasonal and route‑based air services. The airport convenes a community task‑force approach—combining coordinated marketing campaigns, market intelligence, and community-backed risk‑sharing (including revenue guarantees where appropriate) to make routes to and from Cape Breton viable and affordable.
resources.address: 280 Silver Dart Way, Sydney, NS B1L 1B2

resources.name: Halifax Gateway
