resources.description: Halifax Gateway is a multi‑stakeholder initiative that brings together the airport, port, carriers, exporters, tourism agencies, and all orders of government to expand air connectivity to and from Nova Scotia. The partnership packages municipal and private support, joint marketing funds, and route performance analytics to engage carriers on seasonal and strategic routes—directly mirroring the solution’s community task‑force model with coordinated marketing and de‑risking tools to launch and sustain air services.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Community Freight and Consolidation Hub: Set up a local consolidation point for deliveries and bulk orders to lower shipping costs for businesses and residents. Organize coordinated delivery days, group purchasing to reduce frequency and price of long-distance freight, and a volunteer driver pool for last-mile distribution.

resources.name: WFM2Go Online Market & Delivery
resources.description: WFM2Go is an online ordering and weekly delivery service operated by the Wolfville Farmers' Market that aggregates products from dozens of local producers at a central hub. Orders are packed at the market and sent out on coordinated delivery days to a network of community pickup sites across the Valley and HRM, reducing redundant trips for vendors and customers. By consolidating freight and scheduling distribution, it lowers per-delivery costs and improves access to local goods for residents and small businesses.

resources.name: Maritime Bus Parcel Service (Halifax Terminal)
resources.description: Maritime Bus uses its intercity bus network to move consolidated parcel freight between Nova Scotia communities and beyond. Parcels are aggregated at terminals like the Halifax hub and ride on scheduled buses to regional depots for customer pickup, reducing the frequency and cost of separate courier trips. This hub-and-spoke system functions as community freight consolidation with coordinated delivery days tied to the bus timetable.

resources.name: Feed Nova Scotia Food Distribution Network
resources.description: Feed Nova Scotia operates a province-wide consolidation and distribution hub that receives large volumes of donated food at its Dartmouth warehouse. It packs and ships pallets and totes on scheduled routes to more than 140 member food banks and meal programs, which then coordinate local pickup times and volunteer-supported last-mile distribution to residents. The centralized hub and route scheduling reduce transportation costs for community agencies and ensure consistent, consolidated deliveries across rural and urban areas.

resources.name: Truro Farmers' Market Online Ordering & Delivery
resources.description: The Truro Farmers' Market runs an online ordering platform and weekly curbside pickup that aggregates goods from multiple vendors into single customer orders. Orders are consolidated at the market building and distributed on set pickup days, with volunteers and staff coordinating fulfillment and occasional home delivery for those with mobility challenges. This model reduces individual vendor trips, pools purchasing, and provides a local hub for efficient last-mile distribution.

solutions.text: Active Transportation Improvements: Mobilize neighbourhood groups to map priority walking and cycling routes, volunteer for maintenance, and work with councils to build safe bike lanes, e-bike charging stands, and secure bike parking — enabling shorter, low-cost local trips and better connections to transit.

resources.name: Halifax Active Transportation Program
resources.organization: Halifax Regional Municipality – Transportation & Public Works
resources.description: Halifax’s Active Transportation Program plans, designs, and builds safe walking and cycling routes as part of the Integrated Mobility Plan, including protected bike lanes, multi-use pathways, wayfinding, and end-of-trip amenities. The program works with neighbourhood groups through consultations and route mapping, coordinates volunteer engagement for counts and feedback, and installs bike racks and corrals to support secure bicycle parking and better connections to Halifax Transit.

resources.name: Blue Route – Nova Scotia’s Provincial Cycling Network
resources.description: The Blue Route identifies, signs, and develops priority on-road and trail cycling corridors across Nova Scotia, linking communities and transit nodes to enable safer, lower-cost local and regional trips. Cycling Nova Scotia partners with municipalities and residents to map routes, audit conditions, and plan improvements, while supporting communities to add secure bike parking and other end-of-trip amenities along the network.
resources.address: 5516 Spring Garden Road, 4th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 1G6

resources.name: Our Transportation Program
resources.description: Ecology Action Centre’s transportation team mobilizes neighbourhoods to co-create active transportation plans, host community route-mapping walks and rides, and advocate for safe bike lanes that connect to transit. They collaborate with municipalities to pilot street re-designs, open-streets events, and the installation of bike racks and repair stations, building local capacity for volunteer maintenance and everyday cycling.

resources.name: Bike n Bus
resources.description: Halifax Transit’s Bike n Bus program equips buses with front-mounted bike racks and adds bicycle parking at major terminals and ferry landings, making it easier to combine cycling with public transit for seamless local trips. The program complements HRM’s bikeway network by enabling first/last‑kilometre connections and provides guidance to riders on safe routes to and from transit hubs.

solutions.text: Pop-Up Transit and Event Shuttles: Organize temporary shuttle services for festivals, market days, school terms, and peak travel periods linking remote hamlets to town centres. Use these pilots to demonstrate demand and build cases for permanent routes.

resources.name: Halifax Transit Special Event Shuttles
resources.description: Halifax Transit regularly operates temporary shuttle and park‑and‑ride services for major festivals and peak event periods (e.g., Natal Day, Canada Day on the Halifax Common), linking suburban park-and-ride lots and outlying communities to central event sites. These pop-up routes and added trips help residents from farther-flung HRM communities access cultural activities without needing a car, demonstrating demand for expanded service during peak times.

resources.name: Kings Transit Authority — Special Event and Festival Shuttles
resources.description: Kings Transit Authority provides added trips and temporary shuttle-style services during peak valley events such as the Annapolis Valley Apple Blossom Festival, connecting rural communities along the Valley corridor to town centres like Kentville and Wolfville. These pop-up services make it easier for residents of smaller communities to attend parades, concerts, and markets, while helping the agency test demand and refine cases for more permanent routing or frequency increases.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

resources.name: StFX Students’ Union Airport Shuttle
resources.description: During peak travel periods at the start and end of academic terms, the StFX Students’ Union organizes shuttle buses for students traveling between Antigonish and regional transport hubs, including airport connections. These time-limited services function as pop-up transit, reducing mobility barriers for a rural university town and illustrating demand patterns that can inform ongoing transportation planning.

solutions.text: Community Mobility Fundraising and Grant Support: Create a local fund and a volunteer grant-writing team to support transit and broadband projects. Pool donations, apply for government infrastructure programs, and provide match funding to unlock larger grants.

resources.name: Annapolis County Rural Internet Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Annapolis
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Annapolis established a dedicated broadband fund and convened a community advisory group to plan, write, and submit applications to government programs such as the Universal Broadband Fund and the Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative. By pooling municipal dollars with contributions from local partners and using these funds as matching support, the project unlocked larger provincial and ISP investments to extend high‑speed internet to underserved rural communities.
resources.address: 752 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

resources.name: Colchester High-Speed Internet Initiative
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: The Municipality of Colchester created a local financing mechanism and assembled staff and community partners to prepare competitive grant applications for federal and provincial broadband programs. The municipality’s matching contributions—supplemented by community and industry partners—were used to leverage larger infrastructure grants and private investment, accelerating last‑mile connectivity in rural parts of Colchester County.

resources.name: East Hants Rural Internet Project
resources.description: East Hants organized a community‑driven broadband initiative that pooled municipal funds and support from local stakeholders, and developed grant proposals to federal and provincial programs to close service gaps. The locally raised match funding unlocked larger awards and vendor investments, enabling new infrastructure builds and upgrades that improve access to education, jobs, and services in rural communities.

resources.name: Lunenburg County Internet Improvement Initiative
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg advanced rural connectivity by setting aside local funds and collaborating with volunteers and industry partners to prepare applications to provincial and federal broadband programs. By providing municipal match funding and coordinating partner contributions, the initiative leveraged larger grants and ISP co‑investment to expand reliable high‑speed service across underserved communities.

solutions.text: Neighbourhood Speedtest Mapping Campaign: Organize residents to run and publish regular internet speedtests on a shared map to document connectivity gaps. Use results to pressure ISPs and governments for upgrades and to prioritize community broadband investments.

resources.name: Colchester County Internet Speed Test Campaign (CIRA Internet Performance Test)
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: The Municipality of Colchester mobilizes residents to run the CIRA Internet Performance Test and aggregates the results on a public map to pinpoint neighbourhoods and rural roads with poor service. The mapped evidence is used to engage ISPs and the Province for upgrades and to target municipal broadband investments, directly aligning with a neighbourhood speedtest mapping campaign.

resources.name: Kings County Internet Speed Test Mapping Campaign
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: Kings County invites households to regularly complete internet speed tests (via the CIRA Internet Performance Test) and visualizes the results to reveal service gaps across its communities. Staff and councillors use the crowd-sourced map to advocate with ISPs and senior governments and to prioritize rural broadband expansion areas.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: MODL Community Internet Speed Test and Mapping
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg runs an ongoing call for residents to submit home internet speed tests and compiles the results into maps highlighting connectivity gaps throughout the district. The data-driven map supports negotiations with ISPs and funding partners and helps the municipality prioritize where to invest in broadband infrastructure.

resources.name: Pictou County Internet Speed Test Mapping (CIRA IPT)
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Pictou
resources.description: Pictou County engages residents to run standardized internet speed tests using the CIRA Internet Performance Test and publishes results in a shared map to document underserved neighbourhoods. The county uses this community-sourced evidence to pressure providers, inform funding applications, and direct community broadband upgrades.

solutions.text: Remote Work Hubs with Employer Partnerships: Set up coworking spaces in underused municipal buildings or partner with local businesses to host satellite workplaces. Offer high-speed internet, meeting rooms, and childcare co-ops to make remote work viable and reduce long commutes.

resources.name: The Commons Halifax
resources.description: The Commons Halifax operates multi-location coworking spaces that provide high-speed internet, bookable meeting rooms, phone booths, and flexible desks, enabling remote employees and freelancers to work close to home. They host company satellite teams and partner with local employers and startups through events and memberships, reducing commute times while connecting talent to the local business ecosystem.

resources.name: Volta
resources.description: Volta is a large innovation hub and coworking space that offers high-speed internet, meeting rooms, and private offices for companies and remote teams. Through partnerships with employers, accelerators, and community organizations, Volta hosts satellite workplaces and professional programming that let people work locally while accessing mentoring and employer networks—cutting long commutes and strengthening Halifax’s tech ecosystem.

resources.name: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: COVE provides shared workspaces, labs, and meeting rooms on the Dartmouth waterfront with enterprise-grade connectivity, enabling ocean-sector companies and remote technical teams to operate locally. Its resident-company model and industry partnerships effectively create employer-linked satellite workplaces, letting people work near home while engaging with a network of firms, suppliers, and innovation supports.

resources.name: CEED Coworking & Meeting Spaces
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED’s facility offers affordable coworking desks, high-speed internet, and bookable meeting rooms alongside entrepreneurship programs, enabling remote workers and small teams to work from a central Halifax hub. By connecting members with employer partners, mentors, and training, CEED functions as a practical remote-work site that reduces commuting and strengthens local career pathways.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Local Mobility Innovation Challenges: Host hackathons or challenge grants inviting students, entrepreneurs and civic groups to prototype low-cost mobility solutions—apps for ride-matching, scheduling tools for microtransit, or cargo-bike delivery pilots—then incubate promising ideas locally.

resources.name: Downtown Halifax E-Cargo Bike Pilot
resources.description: The Downtown Halifax Business Commission piloted an e-cargo bike delivery service that let local merchants test low-cost, low-emission last‑mile deliveries within the downtown core. By coordinating participating businesses with local couriers and tracking performance data, the program prototyped an alternative to urban van deliveries and created a pathway to scale cargo‑bike logistics locally, directly aligning with the solution’s call for cargo‑bike delivery pilots.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

resources.name: ANTIGo On-Demand Transit
resources.description: ANTIGo is the Town of Antigonish’s app-enabled, on-demand microtransit service that pools ride requests and dynamically routes vehicles to improve coverage and reduce wait times. By deploying a scheduling platform for microtransit and iterating based on rider data, ANTIGo operationalizes the solution’s focus on prototyping and incubating low‑cost mobility tools that expand access to jobs, campus, and services for residents without cars.

resources.name: TnGo Truro Transit (On-Demand Zones)
resources.description: TnGo operates fixed routes alongside app/phone‑bookable on-demand service areas that use dynamic scheduling to cover lower‑density neighborhoods cost‑effectively. This approach prototypes and deploys microtransit scheduling tools locally, mirroring the solution’s emphasis on low‑cost mobility innovation that improves access to work, education, and services in a small‑city/rural context.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs Hackathons and Innovation Challenges
resources.organization: ShiftKey Labs, Faculty of Computer Science, Dalhousie University
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs, Dalhousie University’s computer science sandbox, regularly hosts hackathons and design challenges where students and entrepreneurs prototype civic tech—including mobility solutions like ride‑matching concepts, real‑time transit tools using HRM open data, and rural booking/scheduling ideas. Promising teams receive mentorship and connections into Nova Scotia’s startup ecosystem, helping incubate local prototypes into pilots that can be tested with municipalities or community groups.

solutions.text: Coordinated Tourism and Transport Packages: Work with regional tourism operators to create combined transport and activity packages that boost off-peak intercity connections. Use package guarantees to attract seasonal carriers and justify additional routes.

resources.name: Bay Ferries Travel Packages (Fundy Rose & The CAT)
resources.description: Bay Ferries partners with hotels, resorts, and tourism operators in Digby, Yarmouth, and across Atlantic Canada to bundle ferry passage on the Fundy Rose and the seasonal CAT with accommodations and curated activities (e.g., golf, cultural sites, whale watching). These coordinated travel packages stimulate shoulder‑season demand and provide predictable passenger volumes that help sustain seasonal carriers and justify additional sailings, strengthening intercity connectivity to and from southwestern Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 94 Wyse Road, Suite 201, Dartmouth, NS B3A 1N7

resources.name: Ambassatours Gray Line Multi‑Day Nova Scotia Tours
resources.description: Ambassatours Gray Line runs escorted, multi‑day coach packages—such as Best of Nova Scotia and Celtic Colours departures—that combine intercity transportation with accommodations, attraction admissions, and event tickets. By aggregating demand and coordinating guaranteed group allotments with regional tourism partners, they add shoulder‑season departures and extend routes into rural communities, boosting off‑peak connections between Halifax, the Annapolis Valley, and Cape Breton.
resources.address: 1751 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S5

resources.name: Magic Winery Bus – Wolfville
resources.description: The Magic Winery Bus offers seasonal hop‑on, hop‑off service in the Annapolis Valley that bundles transportation with tasting experiences at multiple wineries via pre‑arranged partner stops. By coordinating schedules and reservations with participating vineyards, the program creates guaranteed demand that justifies dedicated shuttle routes in shoulder seasons, improving regional mobility between Wolfville and rural wineries through transport‑plus‑experience packages.

obstacles.title: Healthcare and mental-health access
obstacles.description: Primary care shortages, long wait times, and uneven mental-health supports undermine family formation, stability, and confidence in staying long term.

solutions.text: Community-run after-hours clinics: Neighborhoods partner with local nurses, nurse practitioners, and volunteer physicians to staff periodic evening/weekend clinics in community centres or churches to handle urgent-but-non-emergency care and reduce ER/waitlist pressure.

resources.name: Mobile Primary Care Clinic – New Minas Baptist Church
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health (in partnership with New Minas Baptist Church)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health operates periodic evening and weekend mobile clinics at New Minas Baptist Church to provide urgent-but-non-emergency care for community members, including those without a family doctor. Staffed by nurse practitioners, registered nurses, and local physicians, these pop-up clinics in a church setting handle same-day concerns (e.g., minor infections, prescription refills), diverting patients from emergency departments and easing primary care waitlists.
resources.address: 9453 Commercial Street, New Minas, NS B4N 3G3

resources.name: Mobile Primary Care Clinic – East Preston Recreation Centre
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health (in partnership with East Preston Recreation Centre)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health runs recurring mobile clinics at the East Preston Recreation Centre, often on evenings and weekends, to address non-emergency health needs close to where people live. The clinics are staffed by nurse practitioners, nurses, and physicians and are designed to provide timely care in a community centre setting, reducing strain on emergency rooms and improving access for unattached patients.
resources.address: 24 Brooks Drive, East Preston, NS B2Z 1H3

resources.name: Mobile Outreach Street Health (MOSH) – After-Hours Outreach Clinics
resources.description: MOSH, a program of the North End Community Health Centre, delivers after-hours outreach clinics in shelters, drop-ins, and community spaces—often including faith-based venues—across Halifax. Teams of nurses, nurse practitioners, and volunteer physicians provide urgent, non-emergency primary care, wound care, and prescription support on-site, preventing avoidable ER visits and connecting people to ongoing services.

resources.name: Cobequid Community Health Centre – Urgent Care (Evenings/Weekends)
resources.description: Cobequid’s urgent care service offers extended-hour, same-day assessment and treatment for non-life-threatening concerns, staffed by physicians and nurses. By providing accessible after-hours care in a community health centre, it diverts many urgent-but-non-emergency cases from regional emergency departments and helps alleviate wait times for primary care.
resources.address: 40 Freer Lane, Lower Sackville, NS B4C 0A2

solutions.text: Volunteer patient transport network: A coordinated volunteer driver program provides rides to medical and therapy appointments for residents with transportation barriers, using a simple booking system and vetted drivers from the community.

resources.name: Wheels of Hope Transportation Service (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Canadian Cancer Society’s Wheels of Hope recruits, screens, and coordinates volunteer drivers to provide rides for people in Nova Scotia who need transportation to cancer-related medical and therapy appointments. Clients book trips through a centralized system, and vetted volunteers use their own vehicles to reduce missed appointments and ease barriers for those without reliable transportation, especially in rural areas.

resources.name: Hospice Halifax Volunteer Driver Program
resources.description: Hospice Halifax coordinates trained and screened volunteers to drive hospice clients to medical treatments, therapies, and program activities when transportation is a barrier. Rides are arranged through the organization’s volunteer services team, providing a dependable, no-cost option that helps patients maintain access to care and supports.

solutions.text: Local telehealth hubs: Libraries, community centres, or co-working spaces host private, Wi‑Fi‑equipped booths where residents can join virtual appointments, with staff available to assist with technology and interpretation.

resources.name: Book a Room
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries offers free, bookable private rooms, Wi‑Fi, and on-site computers/headsets that residents use to join virtual medical and mental‑health appointments. Library staff provide one‑on‑one technology assistance (e.g., setting up Zoom/Teams, testing microphones/cameras) and can connect patrons with newcomer/interpretation supports available through partner services, effectively operating as community telehealth hubs.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Interpretation & Virtual Appointment Support
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides private meeting rooms, Wi‑Fi, and device access at its settlement centre so clients can join virtual healthcare and counselling appointments. Staff assist with scheduling and connecting to platforms like VirtualCareNS, and professional interpreters (in person, phone, or video) can join sessions to ensure language access—delivering the core elements of a telehealth hub for newcomers.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Meeting Rooms and Public Computer Access
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library’s McConnell Library branch offers free, bookable study/meeting rooms, reliable Wi‑Fi, and public computers with webcams/headsets that patrons use for virtual doctor and counselling visits. Library staff provide basic tech help to get connected and maintain a quiet, private environment—functioning as a local telehealth access point for residents without suitable home internet or space.

solutions.text: Peer mental-health support networks: Trained community volunteers run peer-led support groups and one-on-one peer mentoring for common issues (anxiety, postpartum concerns, addiction recovery), offering low-barrier, locally trusted supports.

resources.name: Peer Support Services (Mental Health & Addictions Program)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Mental Health & Addictions Program provides one-on-one peer mentoring and group-based peer support delivered by trained peer supporters with lived experience of mental health or substance use challenges. These free, low-barrier supports help people manage issues like anxiety, depression, and addiction recovery, offering trusted, community-rooted help alongside the formal health system.
resources.address: 5909 Veterans' Memorial Lane, Halifax, NS B3H 2E2

resources.name: Laing House Peer Support
resources.description: Laing House offers youth-driven peer support for people aged 16–29 living with mental illness, using trained peer mentors and member-led groups to reduce isolation and build coping skills. Through drop-in programming, peer circles, and one-on-one mentoring, youth with lived experience support their peers in navigating anxiety, depression, and related challenges in a welcoming, stigma-free setting.
resources.address: 1225 Barrington Street, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3J 1Y2

resources.name: Grief and Bereavement Support
resources.description: Hospice Halifax provides free bereavement support groups and one-on-one peer support facilitated by trained volunteers and peer mentors for adults coping with loss. These peer-led groups create a safe, low-barrier space to share experiences, reduce isolation, and build practical coping strategies that address grief-related anxiety and mental health stressors.

solutions.text: Community mental-health first aid training: Regular, subsidized training sessions teach residents, youth workers, teachers, and employers how to recognize crises, provide initial support, and connect people to professional services.

resources.name: Psychological First Aid
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross delivers Psychological First Aid training that equips community members, volunteers, educators, and employers to recognize signs of distress and mental-health crises, provide calm, supportive initial assistance, and connect individuals to professional and community resources. Courses are offered in person and online across Nova Scotia, making practical skills like active listening, safety planning, and referral pathways accessible to residents and workplaces.

resources.name: Mental Health First Aid (MHFA) – Community and Workplace Training
resources.description: Safety Services Nova Scotia offers accredited Mental Health First Aid courses that train participants to identify emerging mental-health problems and acute crises (such as panic attacks or suicidal ideation), provide initial support using a proven action plan, and guide people to appropriate professional services and community supports. Sessions are scheduled year-round for employers and the public, helping build province-wide capacity to respond early and reduce wait-time impacts by facilitating timely referrals.
resources.address: 201 Brownlow Avenue, Unit 9, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1W2

resources.name: Mental Health First Aid (MHFA) – Continuing Education
resources.description: NSCC’s Continuing Education regularly hosts Mental Health First Aid courses (including Standard and Adults Who Interact with Youth) at campuses and online, training teachers, youth workers, employers, and community members to recognize symptoms, respond safely, and connect individuals to professional care and community resources. By integrating MHFA into accessible, short-format offerings, NSCC expands practical crisis-recognition and referral skills across Nova Scotia’s communities and workplaces.

resources.name: In the Know – Mental Health Literacy for Agriculture
resources.description: Farm Safety Nova Scotia delivers the ‘In the Know’ program to farmers, farm families, and ag-sector employers, building skills to recognize mental distress, start supportive conversations, and connect people to professional services and local resources. The sector-specific training reduces stigma and equips rural communities with practical first-aid style responses and referral pathways, improving early support where access to care can be limited.
resources.address: 60 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

solutions.text: School-based mental-health ambassadors: High schools and post-secondary institutions establish student ambassador programs that promote mental-health resources, run peer-help initiatives, and help younger students navigate services.

resources.name: DSU Peer Support
resources.description: The Dalhousie Student Union’s Peer Support program trains student volunteers to provide confidential, non-judgmental peer listening and resource navigation for fellow students. As on-campus mental-health ambassadors, they run outreach tables and workshops, promote services like counselling and crisis supports, and offer warm referrals that help classmates—especially first-years—find the right help quickly.

resources.name: Stay Connected Mental Health Project — Student Navigator Program
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Student Health & Wellness (in partnership with IWK Health)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Stay Connected initiative equips Student Navigators—trained peer leaders—who promote mental-health resources on campus, host awareness events, and guide students in accessing counselling, crisis lines, and community services. Developed with IWK Health, the program embeds ambassadors across faculties and student groups to proactively connect students (including first-years) to the supports they need and reduce wait-time barriers.

resources.name: Jack.org Acadia University Chapter
resources.description: This student-run chapter leads peer-to-peer mental health education at Acadia, delivering Jack Talks, campus campaigns, and training that reduce stigma and increase literacy. Chapter members act as mental-health ambassadors by signposting campus and community supports, collaborating with counselling services, and mentoring younger students to navigate help effectively.

resources.name: Jack.org Citadel High School Chapter
resources.description: The Citadel High chapter organizes student-led campaigns and Jack Talks that normalize conversations about mental health and connect peers with supports like school counsellors, Nova Scotia Health services, and Kids Help Phone. Senior student leaders act as ambassadors by running peer-help initiatives and guiding younger students to appropriate resources inside and beyond the school.

solutions.text: Community health navigator program: Locally based navigators help residents understand waitlists, book appointments, complete forms, apply for subsidized services, and follow up—reducing missed appointments and improving continuity of care.

resources.name: Community Navigator
resources.description: Chebucto Connections’ Community Navigator provides one-on-one support to help residents access primary care and mental-health services by explaining waitlists, arranging referrals, and booking appointments. Navigators also assist with completing forms (e.g., MSI, Fair Pharmacare), applying for subsidized programs, and following up after visits—reducing missed appointments and improving continuity of care for families in Spryfield and surrounding communities.
resources.address: 531 Herring Cove Road, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3R 1X3

resources.name: Settlement Services – Health and Social Service Navigation
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS settlement counsellors act as navigators for newcomers, helping them register for MSI, find a family doctor, understand specialist waitlists, and book medical and mental-health appointments. They also provide form-filling support, connect clients to language and interpretation for care, help apply for income and medication subsidies, and follow up to ensure people can attend and adhere to care plans.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Family Navigator (Mental Health and Addictions)
resources.description: The IWK Family Navigator helps youth and families understand and access mental-health and addictions services, clarifying referral pathways and expected wait times and assisting with scheduling. Navigators connect families to appropriate community supports, help with paperwork required for services or school-based accommodations, and provide follow-up to reduce missed appointments and support ongoing care.

resources.name: Community Health Teams – Navigation and Connections
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health (Central Zone) – Community Health Teams
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Community Health Teams offer health navigation that links people to primary care, mental-health programs, chronic disease supports, and community resources. Staff help residents book appointments and classes, complete forms for benefits and subsidies (e.g., Fair Pharmacare), and provide follow-up and self-management coaching to improve continuity of care and reduce no-shows.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 402, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Employer-supported mental-health coalition: Local employers form a coalition to share best practices, fund on-site or virtual counselling access for employees, offer flexible schedules for appointments, and jointly subsidize mental-health resources.

resources.name: Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP)
resources.description: Health Association Nova Scotia operates a shared EFAP that pools the purchasing power of many health and community care employers across the province to provide 24/7 confidential counselling (virtual, phone, and in-person) for employees and their immediate family members. The association convenes HR and workplace leaders to share best practices, implement the National Standard for Psychological Health and Safety, and encourage flexible scheduling so staff can attend appointments. By jointly procuring and subsidizing mental-health services, member organizations reduce costs and expand access for their workforces.

resources.name: Farmer Assistance Program (FAP)
resources.organization: Farm Safety Nova Scotia (a program of the Nova Scotia Federation of Agriculture)
resources.description: Funded collectively by Farm Safety Nova Scotia and member farms through the Nova Scotia Federation of Agriculture, the FAP provides confidential, short-term counselling and crisis support to farm owners, workers, and their families via phone, video, and in-person sessions. The program pairs access to counselling with industry-wide training (e.g., Mental Health First Aid) and peer learning so employers can share effective practices and support flexible time for appointments during peak seasons. This sector-wide approach lowers barriers to mental-health care and creates a coordinated employer-supported safety net in agriculture.
resources.address: 7 Atlantic Central Drive, East Mountain, NS B6L 2Z2

resources.name: Chambers Plan (Employee Assistance Program for Members)
resources.description: Through the Halifax Chamber of Commerce, small and medium-sized employers join the national Chambers of Commerce Group Insurance Plan to access an Employee Assistance Program that includes 24/7 counselling (virtual and in-person), work-life services, and mental-health resources. By pooling hundreds of local employers, the plan spreads costs and makes clinically supervised support affordable while the Chamber’s events and peer networks help businesses share policies like flexible scheduling for appointments. This coalition model enables member employers to jointly subsidize and sustain ongoing mental-health supports for their teams.

solutions.text: Healthcare student placement and retention partnerships: Community groups collaborate with regional colleges and universities to host clinical placements, offer homestays, and create mentorship and incentive packages that encourage new graduates to stay or return.

resources.name: Longitudinal Integrated Clerkship (LIC) – Nova Scotia Distributed Sites
resources.description: Dalhousie Medicine’s LIC places third‑year medical students for extended, community‑based clinical rotations in Nova Scotia sites, where they learn in family medicine and specialty settings alongside local preceptors. The program partners with community hospitals, clinics, and municipal groups to embed learners, provide mentorship, and connect them with local supports, creating strong ties that encourage graduates to stay or return to practice in the host communities.

resources.name: Learners & Academic Partnerships (Student Placements)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health coordinates clinical placements for nursing, medicine, and allied health students across hospitals and community sites in all zones of the province. Working directly with Nova Scotia universities/colleges and local preceptors, the program organizes placements, onsite mentorship, and transition‑to‑practice connections that support recruitment and long‑term retention of new graduates in the communities where they train.

resources.name: Students and New Grads – Clinical Placements and Employment Pathways
resources.description: Shannex partners with Nova Scotia institutions (e.g., NSCC, Dalhousie, CBU) to host practicums and co‑ops for nursing, continuing care, and allied health learners in long‑term care and home care settings across the province. The program provides preceptors, structured mentorship, scholarships, and clear pathways to local employment, encouraging students to remain in Nova Scotia communities after graduation.
resources.address: 261 Joseph Zatzman Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1M7

resources.name: North Nova Family Medicine Teaching Site – Community Support for Learners
resources.description: In collaboration with Dalhousie Family Medicine and Nova Scotia Health (Northern Zone), the Aberdeen Health Foundation supports the North Nova teaching site by funding education resources and community‑based initiatives that welcome medical learners. Through local mentorship, integration activities, and practical supports that ease placements in Pictou County, the initiative strengthens ties that encourage residents and new physicians to establish long‑term practice in the region.
resources.address: 835 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3S6

solutions.text: Community wellness hubs with integrated services: Existing community spaces are reimagined as hubs that combine primary-care pop-ups, counselling rooms, social prescribing programs (food/fitness/support groups), and referral coordination in one place.

resources.name: North End Community Health Centre
resources.organization: North End Community Health Centre Society
resources.description: A community-based health hub offering team-based primary care alongside on-site mental health counselling, social work, harm reduction, and dental services. It functions as a one-stop access point that also hosts group programs (nutrition education, peer support, and wellness activities) and actively coordinates referrals to housing, income supports, and specialized health services—embodying an integrated community wellness model.

resources.name: Community Navigator Program (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: Halifax Central Library serves as a community wellness hub where on-site Community Navigators and partner agencies provide counselling, health navigation, and referrals in private rooms, while Public Health and community partners run pop-up clinics (e.g., vaccinations, testing, and primary care navigation). The branch layers social prescribing through free fitness, arts, and support groups, linking people to food programs and community services from one accessible location.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Phoenix Centre for Youth (PCFY)
resources.description: PCFY operates a youth-focused hub that combines on-site health services (nurse practitioner clinics), mental health and addictions counselling, basic needs supports, and referrals under one roof. It offers social prescribing through life-skills, cooking and wellness groups, and coordinates connections to housing, education/employment, and specialized care so youth can access comprehensive supports in a single, welcoming space.

resources.name: Ally Centre of Cape Breton
resources.description: This drop-in health and social service hub integrates primary care (nurse practitioner/physician clinics), harm reduction, STI testing, mental health counselling, and peer support for people facing barriers to care. It also provides meals and practical supports, and staff coordinate referrals to housing, detox/treatment, and community services—delivering comprehensive, low-barrier wellness in one place.

resources.name: Cobequid Community Health Centre – Primary and Community Wellness Services
resources.description: A multi-service community health centre offering primary and urgent care, outpatient clinics, mental health and addictions services, and chronic disease education under one roof. Community Health Teams host group programs, health coaching, and navigation on-site, while staff coordinate referrals across Nova Scotia Health and community partners—functioning as an integrated wellness hub for Lower Sackville and area.
resources.address: 40 Freer Lane, Lower Sackville, NS B4C 0A2

solutions.text: Micro-grants for local mental-health initiatives: A community-run micro-grant fund supports grassroots projects (peer groups, outreach events, culturally specific counselling pilots) that improve access and build locally relevant supports.

resources.name: Community Health Boards Wellness Funds
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health – Community Health Boards
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Community Health Boards distribute small, community-led grants that support local projects improving health and well-being, including mental health. Funds often back peer-support groups, rural outreach events, and culturally specific counselling pilots, helping communities create accessible, locally relevant mental-health supports that complement formal care and reduce barriers like wait times.

resources.name: Community Grants Program
resources.organization: Mental Health Foundation of Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Mental Health Foundation of Nova Scotia provides micro-grants to grassroots organizations across the province to launch and expand mental-health and addictions initiatives. These grants enable peer-led support circles, culturally grounded counselling pilots, and community outreach for youth and underserved groups, directly improving local access and tailoring services to community needs.

resources.name: HRM Community Grants Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality offers small project grants to non-profit groups for community initiatives, including mental-wellness programming. Funding can support neighborhood peer groups, mental-health outreach events, and culturally responsive supports that strengthen inclusion and reduce isolation, enabling locally led responses that complement overburdened clinical services.

solutions.text: Crisis respite and tele-response volunteer program: A volunteer-staffed crisis respite and phone/video check-in program offers short-term, non-clinical support during mental-health crises and connects callers to professional services as needed.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Sexualized Violence Help Line
resources.organization: South House Sexual and Gender Resource Centre
resources.description: A province-wide, 24/7 phone and online chat service staffed by trained volunteer responders who provide immediate, non-clinical emotional support to people impacted by sexualized violence. Volunteers offer crisis de-escalation, safety planning, and short-term respite via phone/text, and connect callers to professional services such as SANE programs, counseling, legal supports, and community resources across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Friendly Calls (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Friendly Calls pairs trained Red Cross volunteers with adults for regular, scheduled telephone check-ins that provide social connection, active listening, and short-term, non-clinical support during periods of stress or crisis. Volunteers can identify emerging mental-health concerns and, with consent, connect participants to professional services and community resources or escalate to emergency/crisis services when needed.

resources.name: Good2Talk Nova Scotia
resources.description: Good2Talk provides 24/7 phone and text support for post-secondary students in Nova Scotia, offering immediate, non-clinical crisis support and problem-solving. Using professional counsellors and trained volunteer crisis responders (for text), the service offers short-term respite and connects students to campus services, community mental-health resources, and provincial crisis supports as needed.
resources.address: 439 University Avenue, Suite 300, Toronto, ON M5G 1Y8

resources.name: Peer Support Nova Scotia (Virtual Peer Support)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health – Mental Health & Addictions Program
resources.description: Peer Support Nova Scotia offers phone and video-based one-to-one peer support and group sessions delivered by trained peer supporters, providing short-term, non-clinical support and de-escalation for people experiencing mental-health challenges. Peer supporters help callers explore coping strategies and, when appropriate, make referrals and warm hand-offs to Nova Scotia Health’s clinical services and other community resources.

obstacles.title: Childcare availability and affordability
obstacles.description: Scarce spaces and high costs constrain workforce participation for young parents and reduce the province’s attractiveness for early-career families.

solutions.text: Community Childcare Co-operatives: Neighbourhood families form non-profit co-ops to pool resources, share caregiving responsibilities and manage one or more licensed childcare spaces with sliding-scale fees and volunteer support, keeping costs down and increasing local capacity.

resources.name: Co-operative Development Services
resources.description: Nova Scotia Co-operative Council (NSCC) provides hands-on support to groups of parents and neighbours who want to organize, incorporate, and operate non-profit childcare co-operatives. Their advisors help communities pool resources, design sliding-scale fee structures, recruit volunteer boards, and set up back-office systems so co-ops can manage licensed spaces sustainably and affordably.
resources.address: 111 Ilsley Avenue, Unit 208, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1S8

resources.name: Community-based Co-operative Development Training
resources.organization: Coady Institute, St. Francis Xavier University
resources.description: Coady Institute at St. Francis Xavier University equips community groups with practical training and coaching to start and govern non-profit co-operatives, including parent-led childcare co-ops. The program supports families to share caregiving responsibilities through co-operative governance, prepare sustainable business plans for licensed spaces, and leverage grants and volunteer capacity to keep fees affordable.

resources.name: Social Enterprise Advisory for Community Childcare Co-ops
resources.description: Common Good Solutions mentors community groups to launch and scale mission-driven enterprises, including neighbourhood childcare co-operatives that use sliding-scale fees and parent volunteer support. Their advisors help co-ops model revenues and costs, navigate licensing and staffing, and establish governance structures so families can co-manage quality, affordable local childcare spaces.

solutions.text: Employer-Community Partnership Childcare: Local businesses partner with municipalities and community groups to convert underused space into shared childcare rooms, with employers subsidizing spots for employees and offering flexible scheduling tied to community needs.

resources.name: Kids & Company – Halifax Purdy’s Wharf Child Care Centre
resources.description: Kids & Company operates an on-site child care centre in the Purdy’s Wharf office complex, partnering with downtown employers through corporate membership programs that subsidize and guarantee child care spaces for employees. The centre repurposes commercial building space into licensed child care rooms and offers extended hours and back-up care options that align with the variable schedules of participating businesses, implementing an employer–community model in the urban core.
resources.address: 1969 Upper Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3R7

resources.name: YMCA Child Care at NSCC Ivany Campus
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth in partnership with Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC)
resources.description: The YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth partners with Nova Scotia Community College to operate licensed early learning and child care within campus facilities, converting institutional space into shared child care rooms for students, staff, and the surrounding community. This employer–community partnership provides priority access for NSCC employees and learners and offers hours aligned to class and shift schedules, reducing barriers to workforce participation in the Dartmouth waterfront business district.

resources.name: Peter Green Hall Children’s Centre
resources.organization: Peter Green Hall Children’s Centre Society
resources.description: Peter Green Hall is a non-profit child care centre embedded on the Dalhousie/King’s campus, using repurposed university space to deliver licensed care for university staff, faculty, students, and nearby community families. The centre works closely with institutional employers to prioritize spaces and align scheduling with academic and campus work patterns, demonstrating a community–employer model that expands access to affordable, centrally located care.

solutions.text: Pop-up and Micro Childcare Hubs: Short-term, licensed pop-up hubs run in community centres, libraries or faith buildings during peak demand periods (e.g., school holidays, shift hours) to expand accessible care without permanent construction.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS operates federally regulated Care for Newcomer Children rooms that provide short-term, on-site child care while parents attend language, employment, and settlement programs. These micro childcare hubs are set up in existing community space at ISANS and run only during program hours, expanding access precisely when demand peaks without requiring any new construction.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1H8

resources.name: YMCA Care for Newcomer Children (CNC) – Halifax
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth – Centre for Immigrant Programs
resources.description: The YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs offers short-duration, on-site child care through the federally regulated CNC model so parents can attend newcomer language and employment services. Using existing rooms at the community facility as micro childcare hubs during class times, the program flexibly adds capacity when needed without building permanent centres.

resources.name: EXCEL Before & After and In-Service Day Programs
resources.description: EXCEL runs school-age care in HRCE schools and expands to full-day programs on in-service days and during March Break at multiple school sites. By activating temporary, site-based hubs in existing classrooms and gymnasiums only during peak demand, EXCEL increases affordable care availability without any new construction.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

solutions.text: Training and Apprenticeship Pathways for ECE Workers: Local colleges and community organizations create subsidized early childhood education (ECE) training, paid apprenticeships and micro-credentials targeted at residents, including bursaries and wraparound supports to grow the local workforce.

resources.name: Early Childhood Educator Tuition Support Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: The province’s Tuition Support Program subsidizes tuition for residents training to become Early Childhood Educators (ECEs) or upskilling to higher certification levels at recognized Nova Scotia institutions. By offsetting education costs and enabling workplace-based study while employed in licensed child-care centres, it creates clear earn-while-you-learn pathways that function like apprenticeships. The program directly supports growing the local ECE workforce and improving childcare availability by helping more educators qualify faster.

resources.name: Early Childhood Educator Bursary Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: This provincial bursary provides financial assistance to ECE students enrolled in approved programs across Nova Scotia, reducing barriers such as tuition, textbooks, and related training expenses. The bursary complements workplace-based training and practicum placements, making it easier for residents to pursue ECE credentials while maintaining employment in child-care settings. Together with institutional student services and placement supports, it offers wraparound assistance that strengthens recruitment and retention of local ECEs.

resources.name: Early Childhood Education Diploma (Workplace Program)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE)
resources.description: NSCECE’s workplace-based ECE diploma allows students employed in licensed centres to complete subsidized training while continuing to earn, blending on-the-job learning with flexible coursework. The college partners with employers and the province’s tuition support and bursary programs, and provides advising, tutoring, and practicum coordination as wraparound supports. NSCECE also offers short professional development courses recognized by employers, helping workers stack skills and micro-credentials aligned to sector needs.
resources.address: 6208 Quinpool Road, 3rd Floor, Halifax, NS B3L 1A3

resources.name: Early Childhood Education (ECE) Diploma
resources.description: NSCC delivers full-time, part-time, and flexible ECE diploma pathways at campuses across Nova Scotia, including recognition of prior learning for experienced workers. The program integrates work-integrated learning and collaborates with employers so many students can earn while they study, and it aligns with provincial tuition support and bursary programs to reduce costs. NSCC also offers targeted short courses and stackable learning options that function as micro-credentials to upskill the existing workforce.

resources.name: Early Childhood Education Diploma (Distance/Workplace Delivery)
resources.description: Jane Norman College offers ECE diploma programs with distance and workplace delivery options designed for rural and working learners, enabling paid, on-the-job training alongside academic coursework. The college coordinates practicums with licensed centres, provides advising and student supports, and leverages provincial tuition support and bursary programs to lower costs. These pathways create accessible, subsidized training and earn-while-you-learn opportunities that expand the local pool of qualified ECEs.

solutions.text: Intergenerational Care Networks: Programs connecting seniors and families — using seniors as paid or volunteer assistants in supervised childcare settings — provide meaningful work for older residents and reliable, lower-cost care for families.

resources.name: MSVU Child Study Centre – Intergenerational Learning
resources.organization: Mount Saint Vincent University Child Study Centre
resources.description: The Child Study Centre is a licensed early learning and child care program on the Mount Saint Vincent University campus. Through an ongoing partnership with the on‑campus Caritas Residence for seniors, older adults regularly join classroom routines as volunteer helpers—reading with children, supporting art and nature activities, and sharing life skills—under the supervision of certified ECE staff. This intergenerational model enriches care and leverages seniors’ time to support families with dependable, high‑quality child care.

resources.name: Windsor Elms Village – Intergenerational Program
resources.description: Windsor Elms Village hosts recurring intergenerational playgroups in partnership with local licensed child care centres and family resource programs. Older residents volunteer as "grandfriends," assisting early childhood educators with circle time, reading, music, and crafts in supervised sessions that bring children and seniors together. The program adds caring adult support to childcare activities while giving seniors meaningful roles and social connection.

resources.name: Maggie’s Place – Childcare Volunteer Program
resources.description: Maggie’s Place provides free and low‑cost early years and parent programs with on‑site child‑minding, recruiting screened volunteers—including many retirees—to assist early childhood staff during infant/toddler and preschool sessions. Senior volunteers help with play, reading, snacks, and transitions under staff supervision, improving adult‑to‑child ratios and reliability of care while parents attend programs that support employment, education, and family well‑being. This intergenerational approach offers meaningful roles for older adults and expands affordable care options for families.

resources.name: East Preston Family Resource Centre – Childminding & Intergenerational Volunteering
resources.description: EPFRC runs parent and early childhood programs with supervised child‑minding and welcomes older adult volunteers to assist ECE staff with playgroups and family programs. Retirees and community Elders support reading circles, cultural storytelling, and play activities in a structured, staff‑led setting, broadening capacity and making care more accessible to families. This intergenerational model provides purposeful engagement for seniors while helping families access reliable, lower‑cost care during programs.

resources.name: Northwood – Intergenerational Programming with Child Care Partners
resources.description: Northwood’s Halifax campus collaborates with nearby licensed child care centres and pre‑primary classrooms to host regular intergenerational sessions where residents volunteer alongside ECEs during songs, reading, and play. Activities are supervised by childcare staff, with seniors providing additional support and social enrichment that helps maintain ratios and reliability for families. The program offers meaningful, structured roles for older adults while strengthening affordable early learning opportunities.

solutions.text: Shared Care Schedules and Timebanks: Neighbourhoods set up formal timebanking or schedule-sharing platforms where parents swap childcare hours, supported by basic training, background checks and a community coordinator to ensure safety and equity.

resources.name: Neighbourhood Babysitting Exchange
resources.organization: Dartmouth Family Centre & Dartmouth North Community Food Centre
resources.description: Dartmouth Family Centre facilitates a member-based babysitting exchange where parents swap childcare hours using a shared schedule and hour-for-hour credits. A staff coordinator supports onboarding, provides safety and basic childcare training, and helps families complete Vulnerable Sector Checks to ensure trust and equity among participants.
resources.address: 107 Albro Lake Road, Dartmouth, NS B3A 3Y2

resources.name: Spryfield Sitter Circle
resources.organization: Home of the Guardian Angel (Chebucto Family Centre)
resources.description: Chebucto Family Centre hosts a sitter circle where local parents exchange childcare by the hour through a shared calendar and time-credit system, reducing costs while expanding access to flexible care. The centre’s team coordinates orientations, supports background checks, and offers basic first-aid and child-safety workshops so families can participate with confidence.

solutions.text: Community Sponsorship and Micro-Grant Funds: Local charities, foundations and business consortia create micro-grant pools to subsidize childcare fees for low-income young parents and to seed community-led childcare initiatives.

resources.name: Strong Communities Financial Assistance – Child Care
resources.description: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth provides donor-funded financial assistance that reduces or covers fees for its licensed child care programs for families with low incomes, including young parents. Local businesses and individual sponsors contribute to this assistance pool, directly subsidizing child care so parents can work, study, or seek employment.

resources.name: Neighbourhood Grants
resources.description: United Way Halifax offers small, quick-turnaround grants to grassroots groups and charities to run community-led solutions such as parent co-ops, pop-up child-minding, and expanded after-school care in under-served neighbourhoods. In addition, donor-sponsored funds administered through partner agencies can offset or cover child care fees for low-income parents so they can access work, education, or training.
resources.address: 46 Portland Street, Suite 130, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 1H4

resources.name: Community Grants
resources.description: The Community Foundation of Nova Scotia stewards donor-advised, field-of-interest, and community funds that award small grants to charities across the province to start or expand child- and family-serving programs, including cooperative and community-led child care. Through locally sponsored funds, partner charities can provide bursaries that reduce or fully subsidize child care fees for young parents, improving affordability and enabling workforce participation.

resources.name: HRM Community Grants Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Community Grants Program provides annual project micro-grants to non-profits for start-up costs, equipment, and program delivery. Community groups can use these funds to pilot or expand neighbourhood child care, after-school, and child-minding initiatives—seeding community-led solutions—and some projects incorporate fee subsidies to ensure low-income families can participate.

solutions.text: After-hours and Shift-friendly Childcare: Community centres and employers collaborate to operate licensed after-hours childcare to serve shift workers and students, with community volunteers and part-time ECE staff to keep costs manageable.

resources.name: Family Home Child Care Agency
resources.organization: Family Matters, Annapolis County Family Resource Centre
resources.description: Family Matters operates a provincially licensed Family Home Child Care Agency that recruits, approves, and supports home-based educators who can offer flexible, non‑standard hours, including evenings and weekends, for families in Annapolis County and surrounding areas. This network model enables shift‑friendly childcare close to homes, workplaces, and community hubs, helping parents who work rotating shifts or attend night classes. By coordinating part‑time ECE staff and community‑based providers under one licensed framework, the agency keeps costs manageable while maintaining quality and safety standards.

resources.name: Kids & Company Halifax – Bayers Road
resources.description: Kids & Company operates a licensed childcare centre that partners with employers to provide flexible enrollment options, back‑up care, and extended hours to better accommodate shift workers and students with non‑standard schedules. Their employer‑supported model allows families to access care earlier in the morning or later into the evening when demand warrants, aligning staffing with part‑time ECEs to expand coverage while controlling costs. This collaboration with workplaces helps maintain workforce participation for parents who work outside typical 9–5 hours.

solutions.text: Shared Ride and Childcare Transport Co-ops: Neighbourhood-run transport cooperatives coordinate safe group travel to childcare sites and schools, reducing access barriers for families in rural or transit-poor parts of the province.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Cooperative Transportation Service (Youth and Family Rides)
resources.description: MusGo Rider is a community-owned transportation co-operative serving Nova Scotia’s Eastern Shore, coordinating pre-booked, shared door-to-door rides. Families use MusGo’s vetted drivers and group scheduling to get children to daycares, schools, and after-school programs when school buses or public transit are unavailable, reducing access and affordability barriers in rural areas. The co-op model allows neighbours to pool demand and keep costs low through shared trips and volunteer-supported operations.

resources.name: Kids & Company School Transportation (Dartmouth – Burnside)
resources.description: Kids & Company’s Dartmouth centre organizes shared pick‑up and drop‑off to its childcare programs from multiple nearby schools, using dedicated vans and coordinated routes. By bundling family demand and operating group transport to licensed childcare, the centre lowers logistical barriers for working parents in an area with limited pedestrian-friendly access, aligning with the shared-ride childcare transport model. Staff manage schedules, safety checks, and car-seat requirements so children travel together reliably between schools and care.

resources.name: BGC Halifax After-School Transportation
resources.description: BGC Halifax coordinates daily bus and van routes that collect children from multiple schools and bring them to clubhouses for licensed after‑school care and programming. This shared ride system pools neighbourhood demand so families have dependable, low-cost transport between schools and childcare sites, especially benefiting households without a vehicle or flexible work hours. Centralized routing, trained drivers, and group supervision ensure safe, consistent travel that eases access and affordability pressures on parents.

solutions.text: Flexible Fee Models and Sliding-scale Policies: Community-run centres adopt transparent sliding-scale fee structures, sibling discounts and pay-what-you-can days, supported by local fundraising to sustain operations while increasing affordability.

resources.name: BGC Greater Halifax After School and Day Camp Programs (Sliding-Scale Fees)
resources.description: BGC Greater Halifax (formerly Boys & Girls Clubs) operates community-based after-school care and day camps that keep fees low and offer subsidies so cost is not a barrier. They implement a sliding-scale approach and family discounts where possible, and explicitly fundraise through donations and community events to cover reduced fees—ensuring no child is turned away for inability to pay.

resources.name: The North Grove Early Years Programs (Free and Pay-What-You-Can)
resources.description: The North Grove offers free early learning and child development programs, along with no-cost on-site childminding that enables parents to attend skills training, appointments, or employment supports. Programs operate at no fee or pay-what-you-can and are sustained by a blend of public funding, donations, and local fundraising—directly embodying flexible, transparent fee practices to reduce childcare barriers.

resources.name: Veith House After-School and Summer Programs (Sliding-Scale/PWYC)
resources.description: Veith House, a long-standing community centre in Halifax’s North End, delivers after-school care and summer day camps for children and youth. Fees are offered on a sliding-scale and pay-what-you-can basis, with support for families (including sibling discounts) made possible through grants, donations, and local fundraising—expanding access to affordable, community-run care.

resources.name: Halifax Affordable Access Program (Recreation, Camps and After-School)
resources.description: The municipality’s Affordable Access Program provides income-based discounts—up to full subsidy—for recreation programming delivered at community-run centres, including day camps and some before/after-school childcare options. This transparent sliding-scale model reduces or eliminates fees for low-income families, with the municipality underwriting discounts and community partners supporting access through ongoing fundraising.

resources.name: South Shore Waldorf School Flexible Tuition (Early Childhood & Aftercare)
resources.description: The South Shore Waldorf School, a non-profit community school, offers early childhood programs and aftercare that use a transparent Flexible Tuition model and sibling discounts to match fees to family circumstances. Parent-led fundraising and donor support help sustain operations while keeping fees accessible, aligning with sliding-scale and community-supported affordability principles.

solutions.text: On-site Childcare Pilot Grants for Small Businesses: Municipalities offer small grants and technical support for small businesses and co-working spaces to pilot on-site childcare pods, demonstrating feasibility and encouraging wider adoption.

resources.name: Community Grants Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Community Grants Program provides small operating and project grants to non-profit organizations, including those that partner with small businesses and co-working hubs. These grants and staff advisory support can be used to pilot on-site childcare pods by funding minor renovations, equipment, and start-up costs in shared workspaces, helping demonstrate feasibility and encouraging broader adoption.

resources.name: Early Learning and Child Care Start-Up and Expansion Supports
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: Nova Scotia’s Department of Education and Early Childhood Development offers start-up and space-creation funding alongside technical support to establish or expand licensed childcare, including guidance on licensing, facility standards, and operator partnerships. Small businesses and co-working spaces can partner with eligible non-profit operators to pilot on-site childcare pods using these grants and advisory services, showcasing viable employer- or site-based childcare models.

resources.name: Grants to Organizations (GTO) Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings provides project and capital grants to community organizations, including those collaborating with local employers and co-working spaces. Funding and municipal staff guidance can be used to pilot on-site childcare pods—covering fit-up, equipment, and early operational costs—helping test childcare solutions embedded in workplaces and shared business hubs.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

solutions.text: Volunteer Mentor Networks for New Parents: Experienced parents and local ECE professionals volunteer through community programs to provide drop-in support, parenting workshops and short-term relief care to reduce stress and allow workforce participation.

resources.name: Family Support & Parenting Programs
resources.organization: Dartmouth Family Centre & Dartmouth North Community Food Centre
resources.description: Dartmouth Family Centre offers drop-in parent-and-tot programs, peer-led support groups, and parenting workshops facilitated by trained ECE staff with support from community volunteers and experienced parent mentors. The centre provides on-site child-minding during workshops and appointments, offering short-term relief care so parents can attend training, job interviews, or work-related sessions—directly reducing stress and supporting workforce participation.
resources.address: 107 Albro Lake Road, Dartmouth, NS B3A 3Y2

resources.name: Supportive Housing for Young Mothers (SHYM)
resources.description: YWCA Halifax’s SHYM program pairs young mothers with volunteer mentors and provides parenting education workshops facilitated by ECE-trained staff and community professionals. The program includes short-term on-site child-minding and practical supports so participants can attend school, training, or work-related activities, easing childcare pressures and strengthening their ability to participate in the workforce.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: Family Support and Parent Education
resources.description: New Ross Family Resource Centre delivers drop-in playgroups, peer mentoring, and parenting workshops led by ECE professionals, with support from community volunteers and experienced parents. The centre offers short-term child-minding during programs and appointments, creating relief care that helps parents manage stress and maintain employment or pursue training opportunities.

resources.name: Family Matters Parenting Programs
resources.organization: Family Matters – Annapolis County Family Resource Centre
resources.description: Family Matters provides parent-and-baby drop-ins, home visiting, and structured parenting workshops facilitated by ECE-trained staff and supported by community volunteers and peer mentors. On-site child-minding and short-term relief care during sessions enable parents to attend trainings, appointments, and job-readiness activities, directly addressing childcare barriers to workforce participation.

solutions.text: Local Recruitment Campaigns and Wage Supplements: Community coalitions run recruitment drives highlighting local career ladders in childcare, offering small wage supplements or signing bonuses funded by local businesses and foundations to retain staff.

resources.name: ECE Compensation Framework and Retention Bonus
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: Nova Scotia’s Department of Education and Early Childhood Development implements a province-wide ECE compensation framework that raises base pay (a wage supplement via a public wage grid) and provides periodic retention bonuses to stabilize staffing in licensed child care. Alongside these financial incentives, the department runs ongoing recruitment efforts that highlight clear local career ladders (e.g., Level 1–3 certifications, diploma-to-degree pathways) to attract new entrants and upskill existing staff. Together, the wage top-ups/bonuses and recruitment messaging directly support centres’ ability to retain educators and keep spaces open and affordable for families.

resources.name: NSCECE Career Services and Employer Partnerships
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education leads community-facing recruitment drives—info sessions, job fairs, and a province-wide job board—that promote clear career pathways in childcare from entry roles to Level 3 ECEs. Through employer partnerships with licensed centres across the province, NSCECE helps operators advertise roles (including hiring incentives like signing bonuses or enhanced starting wages where offered) and matches local candidates to vacancies, improving retention. This coordinated outreach and employer linkage implements the solution’s focus on local recruitment campaigns tied to tangible financial incentives for staff.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works – Job Junction Employer Services (Childcare Recruitment and Wage Incentives Support)
resources.description: Job Junction, a Nova Scotia Works centre, helps licensed childcare operators plan and run local recruitment campaigns—crafting job postings, hosting/employer-attending hiring events, and screening candidates—to quickly fill educator roles. It also connects childcare employers to available wage subsidies and hiring incentives administered through Nova Scotia Works and provincial programs, which function as wage supplements or signing bonuses to attract and retain staff. The combined outreach and incentive navigation directly advances the solution’s approach to bolstering the childcare workforce through targeted recruitment plus financial supports.
resources.address: 6950 Mumford Road, Suite 1306, Halifax, NS B3L 4W1

solutions.text: Shared Space Licensing Support Program: A community-led service assists churches, schools and community halls with licensing, minor renovations and health/safety compliance so they can more quickly and affordably open licensed childcare capacity.

resources.name: YMCA Child Care – Community Partnerships & New Site Development
resources.description: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth partners with schools, churches and community halls to open licensed child care in shared spaces. The YMCA team manages the provincial licensing process, coordinates minor renovations (e.g., washrooms, secure access, fire safety) and implements health and safety protocols so new spaces can come online faster and at lower cost.

resources.name: Community Use of Schools – Licensed Child Care Partnerships
