resources.description: HRCE facilitates long-term, shared-space agreements that allow non-profit operators to deliver licensed child care within school facilities. The division coordinates facility fit-up and compliance (e.g., dedicated rooms, secure entrances, playground standards) and works with operators and provincial licensing officials to help sites meet health and safety requirements quickly.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Community Grant Program (Facility Infrastructure & Safety Upgrades)
resources.description: The Municipality of East Hants provides capital grants and staff advisory support to help community halls, churches and non-profits complete minor renovations and safety upgrades needed for licensed child care (e.g., exits, accessibility, washrooms, fire safety). This funding and guidance lowers start-up costs and accelerates the conversion of shared community spaces into licensed child care capacity.

resources.name: YMCA Child Care – Community Site Development
resources.description: YMCA of Cape Breton collaborates with schools, parishes and community organizations to establish licensed child care programs in existing community facilities. The YMCA team navigates licensing requirements, oversees minor renovations for code and health/safety compliance, and provides staff training and operating systems to bring new spaces online efficiently.

solutions.text: Community Childcare Innovation Lab: A local multi-stakeholder lab (residents, municipal staff, employers, ECE experts) tests low-cost models—co-ops, pop-ups, blended funding—and documents best practices for scaling across neighbourhoods.

resources.name: NSCECE Lab School Child Care Centres
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education
resources.description: The Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education operates lab school child care centres that function as real-world practice sites where ECE faculty, students, families, and community partners co-design and test evidence-informed, low-cost approaches to early learning and care. The centres pilot scheduling flexibility, inclusive programming, and operational efficiencies, then document practices through training, toolkits, and professional learning communities so models can be replicated by neighbourhood providers across the province—aligning with a community childcare innovation lab approach.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides on-site, no-cost Care for Newcomer Children so parents can participate in language, employment, and settlement programs, co-locating child care with services and coordinating with staff, families, and employer partners to test flexible, pop-up, and part-time care options. The program adheres to national CNC standards while documenting procedures, safety protocols, and scheduling models that are shared with partners and replicated across sites—mirroring a multi-stakeholder lab that pilots and scales low-cost, community-embedded childcare solutions.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Chebucto Family Centre Childcare
resources.description: The Chebucto Family Centre offers free on-site childcare and mobile/pop-up child-minding during community programs so parents can attend employment, education, and health services, coordinating with residents, local service providers, and municipal partners in Spryfield. Staff test low-cost staffing models, flexible hours, and co-location strategies, then share program guides and learnings through family resource networks to help other neighbourhoods adopt similar approaches—advancing a community childcare innovation lab model.

obstacles.title: Barriers to entrepreneurship and access to capital
obstacles.description: Thin local angel/VC networks, risk-averse lending, limited commercialization supports, and costly spaces slow startup formation and small business growth.

solutions.text: Community Microgrant Program: Create a locally funded microgrant pool (supported by businesses, philanthropists, and municipal seed funding) to provide small, quick capital awards for startups, pilot projects, and prototypes that demonstrate local economic or social impact.

resources.name: Volta Community Grants
resources.description: Volta provides small, fast-turnaround grants to support grassroots events, pilot programs, and early-stage prototype activities that strengthen Nova Scotia’s startup ecosystem. Funded by corporate sponsors and community partners, these microgrants lower upfront costs for founders and community builders to test ideas, run meetups or hackathons, and demonstrate local economic and social impact.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty Placemaking Grant Program
resources.description: Downtown Halifax Business Commission’s Gritty to Pretty program offers microgrants for public art, storefront activations, pop-ups, and other placemaking pilots that improve the downtown experience and drive foot traffic for local businesses and startups. Backed by member businesses and sponsors, the program provides quick, small-scale capital to test concepts that generate tangible social and economic impact in the urban core.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

resources.name: Facade Improvement Grant Program
resources.description: The Downtown Dartmouth Business Commission provides matching microgrants to small businesses and property owners to improve storefronts, signage, and activate vacant spaces—lowering the capital barrier for new ventures, pop-ups, and expansions. Funded by a business improvement district and partners, the program quickly injects small amounts of capital that catalyze local economic activity and support entrepreneurship.

resources.name: HRM Community Grants Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Community Grants Program offers small, one-time project grants to nonprofits and community groups to pilot new services, social enterprise initiatives, and community economic development projects. As a municipal microgrant stream with a streamlined application, it provides quick capital to test ideas and prototypes that deliver local social and economic impact across the region.

solutions.text: Local Angel Co-op Network: Form a cooperative of local high-net-worth individuals, retired entrepreneurs, and professionals who pool capital and expertise to make small early-stage investments and mentor founders in the community.

resources.name: FarmWorks Investment Co-operative Limited (CEDIF)
resources.description: FarmWorks is a province-wide community investment co-operative that pools capital from Nova Scotia residents to make patient, early-stage investments in local food and agriculture ventures. Members include experienced entrepreneurs and professionals who provide mentorship, business advice, and networking to portfolio companies, aligning closely with a local angel co-op model that combines funding and hands-on support for founders.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Economic Development Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: New Dawn’s CEDIF pools capital from local investors in Cape Breton to finance early-stage and growth businesses, keeping investment and decision-making in the community. Alongside financing, New Dawn connects entrepreneurs with seasoned local business leaders and professionals for mentorship and governance support, delivering the co-operative angel approach of capital plus expertise.

resources.name: Community Impact Investment Fund (CIIF)
resources.description: The CIIF, administered by the Nova Scotia Co-operative Council with Atlantic credit unions, aggregates funds from local individuals and institutions to provide patient, early-stage capital to small and growing businesses and social enterprises across Nova Scotia. Beyond financing, CIIF leverages a network of retired entrepreneurs, industry professionals, and credit union advisors to mentor founders, mirroring an angel co-op that pairs pooled community capital with hands-on guidance.
resources.address: 111 Ilsley Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1S8

solutions.text: Community Loan Fund via Credit Unions: Partner with regional credit unions to create a community loan fund offering low-interest, flexible loans, microfinance, and credit-building tools targeted at startups, sole proprietors, and underrepresented entrepreneurs.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Small Business Loan Guarantee Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Co-operative Council (in partnership with Nova Scotia Credit Unions)
resources.description: Province-wide financing delivered exclusively through Nova Scotia credit unions, this program provides low-interest, flexible loans and lines of credit to startups and small businesses, including sole proprietors. Administered by the Nova Scotia Co-operative Council with a provincial loan guarantee, it reduces lender risk and expands access to capital for underrepresented and early-stage entrepreneurs, directly aligning with a community loan fund model via credit unions.
resources.address: 111 Ilsley Avenue, Unit 208, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1S8

resources.name: Immigrant Business Loan Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS connects newcomer entrepreneurs with financing through Nova Scotia credit unions under the Small Business Loan Guarantee framework, helping immigrants start or expand businesses with accessible, relationship-based lending. The program pairs loans and credit-building tools with advisory support and training, lowering barriers to capital and improving credit profiles for underrepresented founders.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: CUA Microloan and Credit-Builder Solutions for Entrepreneurs
resources.description: As a Halifax-based credit union, CUA offers microloans and credit-building products that support startups and sole proprietors with flexible underwriting and community-focused lending. CUA also participates in the province’s credit union–delivered Small Business Loan Guarantee Program, enabling low-interest financing and credit development for diverse and early-stage entrepreneurs.

solutions.text: Pop-up Incubators and Shared Workspaces: Use vacant storefronts, municipal buildings, or school facilities to host temporary co-working hubs and pop-up shops that reduce rent barriers, provide short-term affordable space, and expose entrepreneurs to customers and mentors.

resources.name: Salt Yard – Halifax Waterfront Pop-Up Retail
resources.description: Salt Yard provides seasonal, turnkey micro-retail kiosks (converted shipping containers) on the Halifax waterfront, offering short-term, lower-cost space for emerging brands and makers. By activating high-foot-traffic public land with temporary storefronts, the program reduces rent barriers and exposes entrepreneurs to customers, events, and peer support.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 301, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty: Storefront Activation Grants
resources.description: This grant program funds the temporary activation of vacant downtown storefronts as pop-up shops, studios, and galleries, helping entrepreneurs test concepts and reach customers without long-term leases. It offsets short-term fit-up and activation costs, connects property owners and tenants, and brings foot traffic back to underused spaces.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

resources.name: Alderney Landing Farmers’ Market & Pop-Up Vendor Program
resources.description: Located in a municipally connected cultural facility, Alderney Landing hosts weekly and seasonal markets that offer affordable, short-term vendor tables and pop-up retail booths for small businesses and artisans. These temporary spaces reduce overhead and provide immediate customer exposure, often serving as a launchpad toward permanent storefronts.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Nova Scotia Sandbox Program)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs is a university-based innovation sandbox that offers free or low-cost co-working style space, meeting rooms, and programming in a campus facility. By using school infrastructure to host hackathons, mentorship sessions, and project sprints, it lowers space costs and provides an accessible hub where early-stage entrepreneurs can collaborate and build prototypes.

resources.name: Downtown Truro Pop-Up Shop Program
resources.description: This initiative activates vacant storefronts by brokering short-term leases for emerging retailers and makers, letting them test markets with minimal overhead in Truro’s core. The program supports entrepreneurs with promotion and landlord connections, using temporary space to reduce risk and build a path toward permanent tenancy.

solutions.text: Peer Mentorship and Apprenticeship Circles: Organize mentor circles pairing established local business owners and tradespeople with startups and young entrepreneurs for regular advice, skill exchange, and informal commercialization guidance.

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic
resources.description: CDL–Atlantic is a mentorship-driven venture program at Dalhousie University that pairs science- and technology-based startups with experienced entrepreneurs, angel investors, and industry leaders in small, objective-focused sessions. Founders meet regularly with rotating mentor circles to receive commercialization guidance, refine go-to-market strategies, and build investor readiness—directly addressing gaps in local capital access and advisory support.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: Start-Up Yard is COVE’s ocean-technology incubator and accelerator that organizes ongoing mentorship cohorts led by seasoned ocean-industry executives, engineers, and entrepreneurs. Through regular advisory circles, Entrepreneurs-in-Residence, and partner-led clinics, startups exchange skills with tradespeople and suppliers, validate products with end users, and receive practical commercialization and funding navigation support.

resources.name: Centre for Women in Business – Advisory and Mentorship
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business, Mount Saint Vincent University
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business runs peer mentorship cohorts and advisory circles that connect established women business owners and subject‑matter experts with early-stage and growth-focused entrepreneurs. Participants meet regularly for guided problem-solving, skill-sharing, and market entry planning, receiving informal yet structured commercialization advice and connections to financing and procurement opportunities.

resources.name: ISANS Business Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Business Mentorship Program matches newcomer entrepreneurs with established Nova Scotia business owners for multi‑month mentoring relationships and group learning. Mentors provide regular advice on local regulations, suppliers, customer development, and financing, while peer cohorts enable skill exchange and networking that accelerate commercialization and small-business growth.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Regular Pitch Nights and Demo Days: Host monthly or quarterly community pitch events where founders present to local investors, customers, and service providers; combine with 'buy local' showcases to generate feedback, visibility, and immediate sales opportunities.

resources.name: Volta DemoCamp and Cohort Pitch Competition
resources.description: Volta runs recurring DemoCamp events where startups publicly demo products and gather feedback from a room of peers, customers, and community members, alongside biannual Volta Cohort pitch competitions judged by investors and service providers. These events give founders stage time to pitch, gain visibility, connect with local angels/VCs, and often include networking and showcase elements that help generate immediate customer interest and sales leads.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: SMUEC Startup Showcase & Pitch
resources.description: The Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre hosts cohort showcase and pitch nights where founders present to investors, mentors, customers, and service providers from the Halifax community. These public events act as demo days that highlight local ventures and frequently incorporate open networking and marketplace-style interactions that encourage on-the-spot customer validation and sales opportunities.

resources.name: IGNITE Rural Pitch Competitions and Demo Nights
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic organizes regular community pitch events and program demo nights across its rural hubs, giving founders from Western and Northern Nova Scotia opportunities to present to local investors, buyers, and ecosystem partners. These gatherings often feature networking and community showcases at the Yarmouth and New Glasgow hubs, creating immediate pathways for customer introductions, pilot sign-ups, and local sales.

resources.name: Ready2Launch Demo Day
resources.organization: Norman Newman Centre for Entrepreneurship, Dalhousie University
resources.description: Launch Dal’s Ready2Launch accelerator culminates in a public Demo Day where student and research-based startups pitch to investors, industry partners, and the broader community. The event showcases prototypes and go-to-market plans, creating a forum for immediate feedback, introductions to local service providers, and early customer engagement and sales traction.

resources.name: Ocean Startup Challenge Demo Day
resources.description: The Ocean Startup Project hosts Demo Day and pitch events for its Challenge cohorts, where ocean-tech founders pitch to investors, government partners, and potential customers from the marine industry. Held at COVE and related venues, these sessions blend live demos and exhibitor-style showcases that drive partner engagement, procurement conversations, and early sales for local ocean ventures.

solutions.text: Business Bootcamps and Commercialization Clinics: Run low-cost workshops and short incubator programs (delivered by volunteers, universities, and local businesses) covering customer discovery, pricing, grant navigation, regulatory compliance, and prototyping support.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard is COVE’s incubator for ocean-technology companies, offering structured accelerator-style bootcamps and commercialization clinics. Programming led by industry volunteers and advisors covers customer discovery with marine stakeholders, pricing and go-to-market, regulatory and safety compliance for marine operations, and guidance on grants and procurement. Companies also access prototyping and testing supports through COVE’s facility and ocean test infrastructure.

resources.name: Volta Academy
resources.description: Volta Academy is a free, cohort-based training series for early-stage founders that delivers practical workshops and clinics on customer discovery, pricing, sales, and investment/grant navigation. Sessions are taught by volunteer mentors, local business leaders, and service providers, with office hours that address legal, accounting, and regulatory questions. Participants connect to prototyping resources and community partners through Volta’s startup hub.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs is Nova Scotia’s ICT Sandbox hosted at Dalhousie University, offering no-cost workshops, bootcamps, and hackathons that help students and founders validate markets and build prototypes. Programming regularly covers customer discovery, lean startup methods, pricing and business models, privacy/regulatory considerations, and how to find and apply for grants, often delivered by volunteer industry mentors and faculty. The lab provides hands-on prototyping support and mentorship to accelerate commercialization.

resources.name: Rural Innovation Centre
resources.description: The Rural Innovation Centre at the Acadia Entrepreneurship Centre delivers hands-on bootcamps and commercialization clinics for startups and small businesses across the Annapolis Valley. Its low-cost programs focus on customer discovery, pricing and financial modelling, grant and procurement navigation, and regulatory readiness, supported by volunteer mentors and university experts. Entrepreneurs can also access prototyping and maker resources through Acadia and local partners.

solutions.text: Community Equipment and Maker Spaces: Establish co-op maker spaces and equipment libraries where entrepreneurs can access tools, fabrication equipment, film/editing suites, and rehearsal space on a pay-per-use or membership basis to lower capital costs.

resources.name: Media Studio & Creative Labs (Central Library)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Central Library provides free and low‑cost access to a Media Studio, editing suites, 3D printers, and other creative tools. Entrepreneurs and creators can book recording booths, video editing stations, and maker equipment on a per‑use basis, removing the need to purchase costly gear. Orientation and staff support help new users get up to speed quickly, lowering barriers to entry.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: CFAT Membership and Equipment Rentals
resources.description: Centre for Art Tapes (CFAT) operates a membership‑based media arts centre offering affordable rentals of cameras, audio gear, lighting kits, and access to editing/animation suites. Members pay reduced rates for equipment and facilities on a per‑use basis, significantly lowering capital costs for film, video, and media entrepreneurs. Training and mentorship programs further support commercialization and project delivery.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co‑op – Space Rentals
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co‑op offers affordable rehearsal, production, and performance space rentals with access to professional lighting, sound, and staging equipment. As a member‑owned cooperative, it provides discounted rates and community‑oriented booking that enable performing artists and creative startups to prototype and present work without high upfront facility costs. This pay‑per‑use model supports entrepreneurship in the arts and cultural sectors.

resources.name: Open Studio & Sewing Lounge
resources.description: The Lunenburg Makery provides a community studio with shared equipment such as sewing machines, textile tools, and workspace for craft and design projects. Entrepreneurs and makers can access the space through workshops, drop‑in sessions, and memberships, reducing the need to invest in their own equipment. This shared, pay‑as‑you‑go model supports small creative businesses and product prototyping in a low‑cost environment.

solutions.text: Small Business Guarantee Pool: Set up a risk-sharing guarantee backed by municipal or philanthropic funds to provide partial guarantees for bank loans to promising local startups, lowering lender risk and improving borrowing access.

resources.name: Credit Union Small Business Loan Guarantee Program (Nova Scotia)
resources.organization: CUA (Credit Union Atlantic) – participating Nova Scotia credit union
resources.description: This program provides loans to startups and small businesses through participating Nova Scotia credit unions, backed by a government guarantee that covers a substantial portion of the lender’s risk. By sharing risk with lenders, it enables approval of loans that might otherwise be declined, improving access to capital for promising local entrepreneurs and early-stage ventures.

resources.name: Canada Small Business Financing Program (CSBFP)
resources.organization: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
resources.description: CSBFP is a federal loan guarantee that shares risk with banks and credit unions across Nova Scotia by guaranteeing a significant portion of eligible small business loans. This reduces lenders’ exposure and encourages financing for startups and growing firms to acquire equipment, make leasehold improvements, and fund expansion—directly addressing risk-averse lending barriers.

resources.name: Livestock Loan Guarantee Program (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: This sector-specific guarantee shares risk with financial institutions on loans to eligible farmers for breeding livestock purchases and related needs. By backing a portion of the loan, the program lowers lender risk and improves credit access for agricultural entrepreneurs, enabling growth of small farm businesses across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7 Atlantic Central Drive, East Mountain, NS B6L 2Z2

resources.name: Export Guarantee Program (EGP)
resources.description: EDC’s EGP provides a partial guarantee to a company’s financial institution, enabling increased working capital and term lending for export-ready SMEs in Nova Scotia. By sharing the credit risk with banks, the program unlocks capital for growth, market entry, and scaling, aligning with the risk-sharing guarantee model to support entrepreneurial expansion.

solutions.text: Local Crowdfunding Platform and Match Fund: Launch a regional crowdfunding portal complemented by a community matching fund that amplifies successful campaigns and encourages local residents to invest in neighbourhood ventures and cultural projects.

resources.name: Community Grants Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Community Grants Program provides matching funds to non-profit and community groups for community facilities, culture, and neighborhood projects. Groups frequently leverage local crowdfunding and grassroots fundraising to meet their required contribution, and HRM matches eligible dollars, effectively amplifying successful community campaigns and encouraging residents to invest in local ventures and cultural initiatives.

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty Placemaking Program
resources.description: Gritty to Pretty funds murals, public art, and streetscape improvements in downtown Halifax and often requires or encourages applicants to bring forward community-raised dollars, including via local crowdfunding. By providing grant dollars that match or top up what residents and businesses contribute, the program acts as a community matching fund that boosts neighborhood cultural projects and catalyzes local investment.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 2A2

resources.name: FarmWorks Investment Co-operative (CEDIF)
resources.description: FarmWorks raises capital from Nova Scotians through Community Economic Development Investment Fund (CEDIF) share offerings, pooling many small local investments to finance food and agriculture enterprises across the province. This community investment model functions like localized crowdfunding for neighborhood ventures, and provincial CEDIF tax credits help de-risk and effectively ‘match’ resident contributions by amplifying the value of community investment.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: New Dawn’s CEDIF enables Cape Breton residents to invest directly in local enterprises and community projects through regulated share offerings, aggregating many small contributions into growth capital for neighborhood ventures. By mobilizing broad-based local investment and leveraging provincial CEDIF tax credits that increase the financial benefit to community investors, it operationalizes a community-powered capital pool akin to regional crowdfunding with an amplification mechanism.

solutions.text: Municipal Low-Rent and Flexible Lease Programs: Advocate for municipal policies that offer reduced rent, rent-to-own paths, or short-term flexible leases for startups in key corridors, plus incentives for landlords who host new local businesses.

resources.name: Volta Residency (Flexible Office and Desk Space)
resources.description: Volta provides early-stage startups with affordable, month-to-month desk and private office rentals in downtown Halifax, lowering upfront space costs and commitment risk. This flexible leasing model directly addresses the barrier of costly spaces by offering reduced-rate, short-term arrangements in a key urban corridor, helping founders test and scale without long leases.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Alderney Landing Farmers’ Market Vendor Program
resources.description: Alderney Landing offers low-cost, short-term vendor stalls for new and growing food, craft, and creative businesses on the Dartmouth waterfront. These flexible, seasonal and weekly rentals reduce fixed overhead and allow startups to enter a prime corridor, pilot offerings, and build customer bases before moving to longer-term commercial leases.

resources.name: Craft Business Incubator Studios
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design provides subsidized studio spaces and shared retail exposure for craft entrepreneurs, with flexible terms that lower entry costs. By combining reduced-rent workspace in a visible downtown Sydney location with business supports, the program helps artisans test markets and grow toward independent retail or longer-term leases.

resources.name: COVE Tenant Program (Flexible Office, Lab, and Workshop Space)
resources.description: COVE offers ocean-technology startups and SMEs flexible licenses for offices, labs, and workshops on the Dartmouth waterfront, reducing the need for long-term commercial commitments. Shared infrastructure and scalable space options lower occupancy costs and risk, enabling companies to launch and grow in a key innovation corridor.

solutions.text: Community Procurement and 'Buy Local' Pledges: Mobilize institutions, non-profits, and residents to commit to buying from local startups and small businesses; coordinate procurement opportunities and procurement-ready training for local suppliers.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Procurement (Supplier Engagement & Tenders)
resources.description: HRM’s Procurement division posts public tenders and runs supplier engagement such as 'How to Do Business with HRM' sessions and reverse trade shows to help local SMEs navigate municipal purchasing. Through social value and community-benefit practices, it encourages participation from local and diverse suppliers and connects them with procurement opportunities, advancing buy-local outcomes in public spending.

resources.name: Procurement Assistance Canada – Atlantic Region (Supplier Outreach)
resources.organization: Public Services and Procurement Canada (Procurement Assistance Canada – Atlantic Region)
resources.description: Procurement Assistance Canada (Atlantic) provides free seminars, one-on-one advisory, and meet-the-buyer events in Nova Scotia to help startups and small businesses register on CanadaBuys, find opportunities, and prepare competitive bids. By building procurement-readiness and brokering connections to federal buyers located in the province, it channels public purchasing toward local SMEs.

resources.name: CANSnet Tenders and Procurement Readiness Training
resources.description: CANS provides Nova Scotia construction SMEs with coordinated access to public and private tenders through CANSnet and its plan room, along with training on estimating, bidding, and contract compliance. It also hosts meet-the-buyer and networking events with general contractors and public owners, directly connecting local suppliers to procurement opportunities and improving their capacity to win work.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

resources.name: BBI Supplier Diversity & Procurement Readiness Program
resources.description: BBI offers workshops and coaching on procurement processes, bid preparation, and supplier diversity certifications (e.g., CAMSC/CCAB) to help Black-owned startups and SMEs in Nova Scotia become procurement-ready. It convenes meet-the-buyer sessions with public institutions and corporate purchasers, encouraging anchors to include local Black-owned businesses in supply chains and facilitating direct connections to contracting opportunities.

resources.name: CWB Procurement Readiness and Supplier Diversity Program
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business at Mount Saint Vincent University
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business equips women-owned firms with procurement training on selling to government and large organizations, RFP response support, and introductions to supplier diversity programs (e.g., WEConnect/WBE Canada). It organizes matchmaking and buyer roundtables in Nova Scotia that encourage institutions to source from local women-led startups and SMEs, aligning purchasing with buy-local objectives.

solutions.text: University–Community Commercialization Partnerships: Encourage local post-secondary institutions to offer commercialization clinics, student internships, and licensing pathways that help community ventures prototype, validate markets, and access research expertise.

resources.name: Dal Innovates
resources.description: Dal Innovates provides commercialization clinics, mentorship, and programs like market discovery and customer validation that help researchers and community ventures turn ideas into prototypes and investable businesses. Through its ties to Dalhousie’s research community and tech-transfer supports, it connects ventures with faculty expertise, student talent, and guidance on pathways for IP development and licensing, while facilitating internships and experiential projects that accelerate go-to-market learning.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre (SMUEC)
resources.description: SMUEC delivers startup coaching, market validation programming, and commercialization clinics for founders from both the university and the wider community. It places students in consulting roles and internships with local ventures to perform research, prototype testing, and go-to-market analysis, while connecting companies to faculty advisors and campus resources that advance commercialization and investment readiness.

resources.name: NSCC Applied Research and Innovation
resources.description: NSCC partners community and industry clients with college faculty and students to design prototypes, run applied tests, and validate markets using campus labs and technical facilities across Nova Scotia. Through capstone projects, internships, and funded applied-research engagements, ventures gain hands-on support to de-risk commercialization and access practical expertise that accelerates product development and industry adoption.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Nova Scotia Sandbox)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs is a university–community sandbox that connects students with startups and nonprofits to build MVPs, run user tests, and conduct customer discovery, effectively serving as a commercialization clinic for digital products. It offers mentorship, workshops, and industry projects that provide ventures with access to Dalhousie Computer Science expertise and student internships, helping teams prototype rapidly and validate markets before seeking investment.

obstacles.title: Cumbersome regulation and permitting
obstacles.description: Inconsistent municipal processes, long permitting timelines, and complex compliance increase costs and uncertainty for builders, employers, and creators.

solutions.text: Community Permit Navigation Hubs: Set up volunteer-run or municipally partnered hubs where residents and small developers receive in-person help filling applications, understanding fees, and preparing supporting documents to reduce mistakes and re-submissions.

resources.name: Planning & Development Permit Applications Centre
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Permit Applications Centre provides in-person guidance at service counters for development and building permits. Staff help applicants complete forms, clarify fees, verify required drawings and supporting documents, and offer pre-application guidance to reduce errors and re-submissions.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, 2nd Floor, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Permit Centre – Planning & Development
resources.description: CBRM’s Permit Centre offers face-to-face assistance to residents, small builders, and businesses seeking development and building permits. Planning technicians and building officials work with applicants to fill out applications, explain fee schedules, and confirm required plans and documents so submissions are complete and avoid repeat visits.

resources.name: Planning & Development Services (Permits & Inspections)
resources.description: The Municipality of East Hants provides an in-person permits and inspections counter where staff guide homeowners and small developers through development, building, and occupancy permit applications. Staff review checklists, confirm zoning requirements, and help assemble supporting documents and fee payments to minimize mistakes and processing delays.

resources.name: Planning & Development / Building Inspection Office
resources.description: The Town of Truro’s Planning & Development and Building Inspection Office provides walk-in support to residents and contractors for permit applications. Staff assist with completing forms, identifying required drawings and approvals, and explaining fees and timelines, helping ensure submissions are complete and reducing re-submission rates.

obstacles.title: Inclusion, equity, and belonging deficits
obstacles.description: Experiences of racism, discrimination, and accessibility barriers—particularly impacting Mi’kmaq, African Nova Scotians, newcomers, 2SLGBTQ+, and disabled people—erode the promise of a welcoming province.

solutions.text: Community-led Reconciliation Councils with Mi'kmaq Nations: Form local reconciliation councils co-chaired by Mi'kmaq elders and community members to guide land-acknowledgement practices, cultural education, co-developed events, and shared decision-making on community planning and public spaces.

resources.name: Municipal Friendship Accord (Truro–Colchester–Millbrook First Nation)
resources.organization: Town of Truro; Municipality of the County of Colchester; Millbrook First Nation
resources.description: The Town of Truro, Municipality of Colchester, and Millbrook First Nation signed a Municipal Friendship Accord and formed a joint advisory body to put reconciliation into practice. The group, jointly led by Millbrook representatives and municipal officials, guides land-acknowledgement use across civic functions, co-develops cultural education and community events, and collaborates on planning decisions for parks and other public spaces.

resources.name: Paqtnkek–Antigonish Friendship Accord (Joint Implementation Committee)
resources.organization: Paqtnkek Mi’kmaw Nation; Town of Antigonish; Municipality of the County of Antigonish
resources.description: Paqtnkek Mi’kmaw Nation, the Town of Antigonish, and the Municipality of the County of Antigonish maintain a Friendship Accord with a joint implementation committee that brings Elders and community leaders together with municipal councillors. The committee steers respectful land-acknowledgement practices, co-develops public programs and events, and supports shared decision-making on community planning and public spaces to build an inclusive region.

resources.name: Bras d’Or Lakes Collaborative Environmental Planning Initiative (CEPI)
resources.organization: Unama’ki Institute of Natural Resources (CEPI Secretariat)
resources.description: CEPI is a community-led council co-chaired by Mi’kmaq and non-Indigenous partners, hosted by the Unama’ki Institute of Natural Resources, that applies Two-Eyed Seeing to stewardship and planning for the Bras d’Or Lakes. It convenes Mi’kmaq Elders, municipal leaders, and residents to co-develop education and cultural programming, promote land-acknowledgement and Mi’kmaw place names, and make shared decisions affecting public shorelines and community spaces.

resources.name: Kejimkujik–Mi’kmaq Cooperative Management
resources.organization: Parks Canada in partnership with the Mi’kmaq of Nova Scotia
resources.description: Parks Canada collaborates with the Mi’kmaq of Nova Scotia through cooperative management and an advisory circle at Kejimkujik National Park and National Historic Site. Mi’kmaq Elders and community representatives help shape land-acknowledgement protocols, co-develop interpretive programs and cultural events, and share in decisions about trails, place names, and the design and use of public spaces in the park.
resources.address: 3005 Kejimkujik Main Parkway, Maitland Bridge, NS B0T 1B0

solutions.text: African Nova Scotian Heritage and Economic Development Program: Support neighbourhood-based initiatives that preserve history (oral histories, monuments, heritage trails) while funding small-business support, entrepreneurship workshops, and mentorship targeted to African Nova Scotian residents.

resources.name: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Black Cultural Society of Nova Scotia
resources.description: A provincial museum and community hub that preserves and shares African Nova Scotian history through exhibits, archives, oral history projects, and heritage programming in Cherry Brook/Preston. The Centre also supports community economic activity by hosting markets, networking events, and skills workshops in partnership with local business-support organizations, creating vendor and mentorship opportunities for African Nova Scotian entrepreneurs.
resources.address: 10 Cherry Brook Road, Cherry Brook, NS B2Z 1A8

resources.name: Black Loyalist Heritage Centre
resources.description: A museum and interpretive site that documents and preserves the stories of Black Loyalists through exhibitions, guided tours, oral histories, and a heritage campus in historic Birchtown. In addition to heritage preservation, the Centre stimulates local African Nova Scotian entrepreneurship by partnering with artisans and small businesses (gift shop consignment, cultural markets) and by hosting community learning events that build heritage tourism and microenterprise skills.
resources.address: 119 Old Birchtown Road, Shelburne, NS B0T 1W0

resources.name: AKOMA Community Development and Heritage Initiative
resources.description: AKOMA stewards the former Nova Scotia Home for Colored Children site, advancing heritage preservation through storytelling, commemorations, and planned interpretive features that honour Preston-area African Nova Scotian history. In parallel, AKOMA is developing a social enterprise campus (event space, community hub, and commercial opportunities) and delivers training, vendor opportunities, and mentorship that support small-business growth and employment for African Nova Scotians in the Preston communities.

resources.name: Africville Museum and Community Programming
resources.description: Located on the historic site of Africville, the museum preserves African Nova Scotian history through exhibits, artifacts, oral histories, commemorations, and a heritage trail experience in Africville Park. The organization also strengthens local economic development by collaborating with Black vendors and cultural producers during community events and festivals, creating pathways for entrepreneurship, mentorship, and skills-building linked to heritage tourism.

solutions.text: Community Accessibility Audits and Micro-Grants: Train local volunteers to run accessibility audits for public buildings and small businesses, and provide community micro-grants to implement priority accessibility upgrades (ramps, signage, hearing loops).

resources.name: Community ACCESS-Ability Program (CAP)
resources.organization: Department of Communities, Culture, Tourism and Heritage (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Community ACCESS-Ability Program provides cost-shared grants to municipalities and non-profit organizations to remove barriers in community facilities. Funding supports priority upgrades such as ramps, automatic doors, accessible washrooms, tactile/wayfinding signage, and assistive listening systems, often identified through community accessibility audits conducted by municipal Accessibility Advisory Committees and local volunteers. This pairs community-led assessments with micro-grant capital funding to implement the most urgent fixes.

resources.name: Business ACCESS-Ability Grant Program
resources.organization: Department of Communities, Culture, Tourism and Heritage (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: This grant program helps Nova Scotia small and medium-sized businesses fund accessibility improvements in the built environment and communications. Eligible projects include ramps, lifts, door openers, tactile/Braille signage, website accessibility, and assistive listening systems like hearing loops; applicants are encouraged to assess barriers and consult people with disabilities so micro-grant investments are guided by audit findings. The program directly enables businesses to act on accessibility audit priorities with cost-shared funding.

resources.name: Accessibility Directorate Grants (Capacity Building for Accessible Communities)
resources.organization: Accessibility Directorate, Department of Justice (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Accessibility Directorate provides grants to public sector bodies (e.g., municipalities, libraries, post-secondary institutions) to build capacity to meet Nova Scotia’s Accessibility Act. Funding is commonly used to train staff and community volunteers to conduct accessibility audits, complete barrier assessments of buildings and services, and create prioritized implementation plans that lead to small, high-impact upgrades. This directly supports the solution’s audit-and-train approach and connects communities to other micro-grant streams for capital improvements.

resources.name: CNIB Accessibility Consulting (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: CNIB’s Halifax team provides on-site accessibility assessments and advisory services for public buildings and small businesses using recognized standards (e.g., CSA, CNIB’s Clearing Our Path). They train staff and volunteers on inclusive customer service and wayfinding and deliver actionable audit reports that prioritize fixes like tactile signage, lighting/contrast improvements, and hearing assistive technologies. CNIB also advises clients on leveraging Nova Scotia grant programs (e.g., Access-Ability) to implement recommended upgrades, aligning audits with micro-grant-funded action.

solutions.text: Peer-led Newcomer Settlement Hubs: Establish volunteer-run hubs where newcomers can get help with paperwork, language-conversation groups, job-search coaching, connections to cultural mentors, and access to donated household items to ease settlement.

resources.name: Community Connections Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections Program creates peer-led welcome hubs where trained volunteers host conversation circles, mentor matches, and social events that help newcomers build language confidence and local networks. Settlement staff and volunteers assist with forms and paperwork, while employment specialists provide job-search coaching and resume support; the program also connects clients to donated household items and furniture through community partners to ease the first months of settlement.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Community Connections & Settlement Support
resources.description: The Halifax Refugee Clinic operates a volunteer-driven hub where trained volunteers and staff help refugee claimants and other newcomers with paperwork, system navigation, and access to services. They host conversation groups and provide one-on-one mentoring and job-search coaching, and maintain a donation room of clothing and household essentials to help clients get established.
resources.address: 5590 North Street, Suite 204, Halifax, NS B3K 1N2

resources.name: Newcomer Services and English Conversation Groups (Central Library)
resources.description: Halifax Central Library serves as a community-led newcomer hub, hosting volunteer-run English Conversation Groups, newcomer social meetups, and information sessions that help with everyday paperwork and system navigation. Staff and partners offer resume and job-search workshops and connect participants with cultural mentors and local donation networks (including periodic winter-gear and household starter drives) to reduce barriers to settling in.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: This region-wide initiative builds peer-led welcome hubs by training volunteer Community Connectors who meet newcomers for coffee chats, host conversation meetups, and mentor families as they navigate forms, services, and daily life. The network links newcomers to job-search support via the Connector Program and community partners, and coordinates access to donated furnishings and household goods through local drives and partner organizations.

solutions.text: Inclusive Hiring Pledges for Local Employers: Create a community-backed pledge program that helps small and medium employers adopt inclusive hiring practices, remove biased job requirements, embed accessibility accommodations, and display a public commitment to equity.

resources.name: Employer Support Services (Inclusive Workplaces)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS works directly with Nova Scotia employers to build inclusive hiring practices for immigrants and refugees. They provide training on bias-free recruitment, review job postings to remove unnecessary credential barriers, advise on accommodations and equitable onboarding, and facilitate diverse candidate recruitment. Employers demonstrate a public commitment to equity by partnering with ISANS for hiring initiatives and being profiled as immigrant-inclusive workplaces through ISANS networks.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Come to Work (Atlantic Region)
resources.description: CNIB’s Come to Work program partners with employers who commit to accessible, inclusive hiring for people who are blind, Deafblind, or have low vision. The program helps employers remove biased job requirements, conduct accessibility reviews, and implement accommodations throughout recruitment and onboarding, while training HR teams on inclusive practices. Participating employers are recognized through CNIB’s networks and events, signalling a public, community-backed commitment to accessibility and equity.

resources.name: 50 – 30 Challenge
resources.organization: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
resources.description: The 50–30 Challenge is a national pledge program that invites Nova Scotia businesses and non-profits to publicly commit to achieving gender parity and greater representation of underrepresented groups in leadership. Participants receive free tools and guidance to adopt inclusive hiring and promotion practices, reduce biased requirements, and embed accessibility considerations across HR policies. Signatory organizations are listed publicly, making their commitment visible to employees, applicants, and the broader community.

solutions.text: 2SLGBTQ+ Safe Spaces and Drop-in Centres: Fund and volunteer for community drop-in centres that provide peer support, mental-health referrals, sex-positive education, and emergency housing lists for 2SLGBTQ+ youth and adults facing discrimination or family rejection.

resources.name: Youth Project Drop-In and Support Programs
resources.description: The Youth Project operates a safe, affirming drop-in space and peer-led groups for 2SLGBTQ+ youth across Nova Scotia. Staff provide one-on-one peer support, mental-health referrals, sex-positive education and supplies, and maintain up-to-date resource lists for emergency housing and crisis supports for youth facing family rejection or homelessness.

resources.name: South House Drop-In and Peer Support
resources.organization: South House Sexual and Gender Resource Centre
resources.description: South House runs a low-barrier, safer-space drop-in and resource centre where 2SLGBTQ+ people can access peer support, community, and referrals. The centre offers sex-positive education, safer-sex supplies, and helps navigate affirming mental-health services and emergency housing or shelter options in the HRM.

resources.name: Ally Centre of Cape Breton Drop-In
resources.description: The Ally Centre operates an inclusive, LGBTQ-affirming drop-in that provides peer support, harm reduction, and case management for people facing discrimination or housing insecurity. Staff connect community members with mental-health and addictions services and maintain current information on local emergency shelter and housing resources in Cape Breton.

resources.name: South Shore Sexual Health Centre Drop-In
resources.description: This sex-positive, 2SLGBTQ+-affirming centre provides confidential drop-in support, education, and safer-sex supplies for youth and adults. Staff offer peer support and navigation, make referrals to mental-health and primary care providers, and keep resource lists for emergency shelter and housing supports across the South Shore.

solutions.text: Cultural Competency and Anti-Racism Trainings: Deliver regular, locally tailored workshops co-designed with Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer, 2SLGBTQ+, and disability advocates for schools, businesses, and community groups to reduce bias and improve intercultural interaction.

resources.name: Intercultural Competency Training
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides Intercultural Competency Training for employers, schools, and community organizations across Nova Scotia, offering regular workshops on anti-racism, unconscious bias, and inclusive communication. Sessions are locally tailored and co-developed with newcomer clients, settlement staff, and community partners to address real scenarios in workplaces and classrooms, improving intercultural interaction and reducing bias.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Cultural Competency Training
resources.description: The Mi'kmaw Native Friendship Centre delivers Cultural Competency Training for public servants, businesses, educators, and service providers, led by Elders and Knowledge Keepers. Workshops are grounded in Mi'kmaw history, treaties, and urban Indigenous experiences, and are customized for local contexts to build cultural safety, challenge stereotypes, and strengthen respectful relationships.

resources.name: Education & Outreach Program (Anti-Black Racism and African Nova Scotian History Workshops)
resources.organization: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia’s Education & Outreach Program offers anti-Black racism and African Nova Scotian history workshops to schools, municipalities, police, and businesses. Sessions are co-created with African Nova Scotian historians, community leaders, and youth, and use local case studies to reduce bias and foster equitable, culturally competent practices.
resources.address: 10 Cherry Brook Road, Cherry Brook, NS B2Z 1A8

resources.name: Education & Training Program
resources.description: The Youth Project’s Education & Training Program delivers 2SLGBTQ+ inclusion workshops to schools, workplaces, and community groups across Nova Scotia. Trainings are designed with 2SLGBTQ+ youth and educators, covering terminology, pronouns, inclusive policies, and strategies to prevent homophobia and transphobia, thereby improving intercultural interaction and belonging.

solutions.text: Community Mentorship Circles for Youth: Create mentorship programs pairing youth from marginalized groups with local professionals, tradespeople, and artists to build networks, career pathways, apprenticeships, and confidence to stay or return home.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program pairs immigrant and refugee newcomers, including youth and recent graduates, with established local professionals in their fields for guided, goal-based mentoring. Through informational interviews, job shadowing, and networking, mentees build professional connections and clearer career pathways in Nova Scotia, supporting inclusion and increasing the likelihood they stay and thrive locally.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Youth & Cultural Programming (Elders and Community Mentorship)
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre offers youth programs that connect Indigenous youth with Elders, knowledge keepers, artists, and local employers to build skills, cultural identity, and career readiness. Through circles, workshops, and mentorship activities, participants gain networks across trades, arts, and community services, strengthening confidence and pathways to education, employment, and leadership in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Youth Social Enterprise & Mentorship
resources.description: Hope Blooms engages predominantly African Nova Scotian youth in a community-led social enterprise, pairing them with local chefs, entrepreneurs, gardeners, and artists who mentor in business, culinary, agriculture, and creative skills. Youth co-design and run real ventures, develop networks with professionals, and access scholarships—building confidence and career pathways that anchor them in Nova Scotia’s economy and community.

resources.name: MentorAbility Nova Scotia
resources.description: MentorAbility NS, coordinated locally by TEAM Work Cooperative, arranges short-term career mentorships that connect youth and adults with disabilities to employers and professionals in sectors like skilled trades, IT, hospitality, and the arts. Participants explore occupations through job shadowing and guided networking, building confidence, inclusive connections, and clearer pathways to work and apprenticeships in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Employment Programs (EmploymentWorks and Transition Supports)
resources.description: Autism Nova Scotia’s employment programs, including EmploymentWorks, pair autistic youth and young adults with workplace mentors and local employers for skill-building, job sampling, and networking. These mentorship experiences help participants identify strengths, navigate career pathways, and transition into Nova Scotia’s workforce with the supports and community connections needed to thrive.
resources.address: 5945 Spring Garden Road, Unit 101, Halifax, NS B3H 4R4

solutions.text: Accessible Transportation Initiatives: Coordinate volunteer rides, subsidized local transit passes, and targeted mobility services for people with disabilities, elders, and low-income residents to increase access to jobs, services, and cultural events.

resources.name: Access-A-Bus
resources.description: Access-A-Bus is Halifax Transit’s door-to-door, shared-ride service for people with permanent disabilities who cannot use conventional transit. It provides pre-booked, accessible transportation to workplaces, medical appointments, services, and cultural events, directly addressing mobility barriers and increasing inclusion for disabled residents and elders.

resources.name: Affordable Access Program – Low Income Transit Pass
resources.description: The Affordable Access Program offers a 50% discounted Halifax Transit monthly pass to eligible low-income residents, including seniors and people receiving income assistance. By reducing the cost barrier to public transit, the program enables more reliable access to jobs, education, health services, and cultural activities, supporting equity and participation across diverse communities.

solutions.text: Local Inclusive Festivals and Arts Grants: Sponsor neighborhood festivals and small grants that prioritize programming by Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer, 2SLGBTQ+, and disabled artists to celebrate diversity and create cross-cultural engagement.

resources.name: Cultural Festivals and Events Funding Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s grant program provides operating and project funding to non-profit organizers of public cultural festivals and events across HRM. Its assessment criteria emphasize diversity, accessibility, and inclusion, which channels sponsorship to festivals that feature and are led by Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer, 2SLGBTQ+, and disabled artists, creating neighborhood-based, cross-cultural engagement.

resources.name: Eyelevel Artist-Run Centre
resources.description: Eyelevel presents exhibitions, pop-ups, and neighborhood arts events and regularly issues paid calls and microgrants that prioritize Mi’kmaq and other Indigenous, African Nova Scotian, newcomer, 2SLGBTQ+, and disabled artists. By directing small grants and presentation platforms to equity-deserving creators and hosting free or low-cost programs in accessible spaces, Eyelevel advances inclusive local festivals that foster cross-cultural connections.

resources.name: Bus Stop Theatre Community Access Program
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op operates a community venue that subsidizes or waives rental fees and provides in-kind support for grassroots festivals and events led by underrepresented artists. Partnering with Mi’kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer, 2SLGBTQ+, and disability communities, the program effectively offers small, targeted grants and platforms for inclusive neighborhood festivals that celebrate diversity and invite cross-cultural participation.

resources.name: Pier 21 Artist-in-Residence and Cultural Events
resources.organization: Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21
resources.description: The Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21 commissions and presents newcomer artists through its artist-in-residence and hosts public cultural festivals and programs that center immigrant and refugee voices. By providing paid opportunities, workshops, and accessible, often free, cross-cultural events—including programming that features 2SLGBTQ+ newcomers and artists with disabilities—the museum supports inclusive arts that build community understanding.

resources.name: Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre – Community Cultural Programming
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre organizes urban Indigenous cultural gatherings such as Mawio’mi, arts markets, and seasonal festivals that feature Mi’kmaq artists and knowledge keepers. These inclusive, neighborhood-based events often collaborate with African Nova Scotian, newcomer, 2SLGBTQ+, and disability groups, offering paid performance and vendor opportunities that foster accessibility and cross-cultural engagement.

solutions.text: Community Language and Interpretation Networks: Organize volunteer interpreter pools and community language classes (including Mi'kmaq language learning support) to lower communication barriers for newcomers and strengthen cross-cultural exchange.

resources.name: Language Interpretation & Translation Services (LITS) and English Language Programs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides trained interpreters and translators in dozens of languages to help newcomers and service providers communicate clearly in legal, health, education, and community settings. Alongside LITS, ISANS delivers English classes and volunteer-led conversation circles that build everyday language skills and foster cross-cultural exchange—directly reducing communication barriers and strengthening inclusion.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Mi’kmaw Language & Cultural Programs
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre offers Mi’kmaw language classes, cultural workshops, and community gatherings that invite both Indigenous and non-Indigenous participants to learn and practice the Mi’kmaw language. These programs revitalize Mi’kmaw language use and create welcoming, cross-cultural spaces where newcomers and local residents can connect and build belonging.

resources.name: English Language Learning & Conversation Groups
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts free, volunteer-facilitated English conversation groups and language learning programs across branches, giving newcomers low-barrier opportunities to practice speaking and build community connections. Branches also feature Mi’kmaw language and cultural programming throughout the year, supporting inter-cultural understanding and a more welcoming environment.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Mi’kmaw Language Revitalization Initiative
resources.description: Mi’kmaw Kina’matnewey supports Mi’kmaw language revitalization through curriculum development, teacher training, community classes, and digital resources used across Nova Scotia’s Mi’kmaw communities. These efforts strengthen access to Mi’kmaw language learning for youth and adults while fostering cross-cultural understanding between Indigenous and newcomer communities.

solutions.text: Disability Employment Support and Skills Labs: Host community-run skills labs offering resume help, workplace accommodation planning, assistive tech demos, and employer roundtables to improve hiring and retention of people with disabilities.

resources.name: Come to Work
resources.description: CNIB’s Come to Work program supports job seekers with sight loss through resume and interview coaching, job matching, and mentorship. It also runs accessible technology training and demonstrations (e.g., screen readers, magnification, and workplace accessibility tools) to prepare candidates and advise employers on effective accommodations. The team regularly engages employers through information sessions and roundtables to improve inclusive hiring and retention practices.

resources.name: The WorkBridge (Nova Scotia Works for Persons with Disabilities)
resources.description: The WorkBridge provides tailored employment services for people with disabilities, including career counseling, resume and cover-letter support, interview preparation, and job development. Staff collaborate with clients and employers on accommodation planning and coordinate assistive technology trials through community partners to ensure successful onboarding and retention. The program also hosts employer engagement events and roundtables to connect inclusive employers with talent and share best practices in accessibility.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

resources.name: Employment Services
resources.description: ILNS Employment Services offers skills labs and workshops focused on resume building, interview practice, job search strategies, and workplace readiness for persons with disabilities. The team supports individualized accommodation planning and provides orientations to assistive technologies (such as speech-to-text, screen readers, and accessible productivity tools) in their resource space. ILNS also conducts employer outreach, information sessions, and roundtables to advance inclusive hiring and retention across sectors.
resources.address: 4 Duke Street, Suite 104, Bedford, NS B4A 2Z7

resources.name: New Leaf Enterprises (Employment and Skills Development)
resources.description: New Leaf Enterprises provides hands-on skills labs (such as food service, production, and social enterprise work) alongside resume support, job readiness training, and coaching for adults with disabilities. Staff work directly with employers on job carving and accommodation planning, and they familiarize participants and workplaces with adaptive tools used in training to support on-the-job success. The program regularly invites employers for tours and discussion sessions to build inclusive hiring pipelines and sustained retention.

solutions.text: Neighbourhood Restorative Justice and Conflict Resolution: Set up restorative circles and mediation services facilitated by trained community volunteers to address interpersonal discrimination incidents and rebuild trust without defaulting to punitive systems.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Restorative Justice Program (NSRJP)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Restorative Justice Program diverts youth and eligible adult matters from the formal justice system into community-based restorative processes. Community justice agencies across the province recruit and train volunteer facilitators to run restorative circles, conferences, and mediations that address harms, including interpersonal discrimination, support accountability, and rebuild relationships. This non-punitive approach centers those affected, encourages dialogue, and connects parties with culturally relevant supports.

resources.name: Indigenous Justice Program (Restorative Circles)
resources.description: The Indigenous Justice Program at the Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre provides restorative circles, peacemaking, and mediation for urban Indigenous community members. Elders, Knowledge Keepers, and trained community volunteers facilitate talking circles that address incidents of interpersonal harm and discrimination, focusing on healing, accountability, and relationship repair rather than punishment. The program connects participants with supports and uses culturally grounded practices to rebuild trust.

resources.name: Restorative Approach in Schools
resources.description: HRCE implements a system-wide Restorative Approach that uses dialogue circles, conferencing, and mediation to address incidents such as racism, bullying, and exclusion in schools. Trained school-based facilitators engage students, families, and, when appropriate, community volunteers and Elders to repair harm, rebuild trust, and strengthen belonging without defaulting to punitive discipline. The approach emphasizes accountability, inclusion, and culturally responsive practices that reflect Mi’kmaq, African Nova Scotian, 2SLGBTQ+, newcomer, and disability communities.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Restorative Circles and Conflict Transformation Programs
resources.description: Tatamagouche Centre delivers community-based restorative circles, conflict transformation, and anti-racism dialogue programs across Nova Scotia. The Centre trains and mobilizes facilitators and volunteer circle-keepers to convene mediated circles in neighbourhoods and organizations after incidents of harm or discrimination, focusing on healing, accountability, and relationship repair. Its programs partner with Mi’kmaq, African Nova Scotian, and newcomer communities to ensure culturally grounded, non-punitive responses that rebuild trust.
resources.address: 259 Loop of Hwy 6, Tatamagouche, NS B0K 1V0

solutions.text: Bias Incident Reporting and Rapid Response Network: Create a community-managed reporting tool and volunteer rapid-response teams that document incidents, offer supports to affected people, and coordinate with service providers to prevent escalation.

resources.name: Hate Crime Unit and Victim Services
resources.description: Halifax Regional Police operates a Hate Crime Unit that receives and investigates hate- and bias-motivated incidents, including online reporting and direct intake, and maintains detailed documentation to track and analyze incidents. Trained Volunteer Victim Services teams are deployed to provide immediate, trauma-informed support and referrals, and HRP coordinates with community agencies and service providers to address safety needs and prevent escalation.

resources.name: Nova Scotia RCMP – Hate/Bias Incident Reporting and Response
resources.organization: Royal Canadian Mounted Police, Nova Scotia (H Division)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia RCMP accepts reports of hate-motivated incidents across the province and documents them for investigation and trend monitoring, coordinating responses through local detachments. Members work with Victim Services and partner organizations to provide supports, safety planning, and referrals, helping affected individuals while liaising with community stakeholders to prevent further harm.

resources.name: Client Support for Hate, Harassment and Discrimination
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides a safe, multilingual intake for newcomers to report experiences of racism, discrimination, or hate, and staff document incidents within case files to guide action. Settlement counsellors and specialized staff deliver rapid response supports (navigation, safety planning, mental health referrals) and coordinate with police, the Nova Scotia Human Rights Commission, schools, and employers to resolve issues and prevent escalation.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Access to Justice and Human Rights Support
resources.description: reachAbility runs free legal clinics and advocacy services where people facing discrimination and accessibility barriers can report incidents, have them documented, and receive rapid legal information and support. With volunteer lawyers and advocates, the program assists with human rights complaints, accommodations, and coordinated problem-solving with service providers to reduce conflict and prevent escalation.

resources.name: Human Rights & Equity Services – Report and Support
resources.description: Dalhousie’s HRES offers an online Report and Support portal where students, staff, and faculty can confidentially report incidents of racism, discrimination, and harassment; staff document cases and provide timely, trauma-informed intake. Case managers coordinate with campus security, counselling, academic/workplace accommodations, and external services (police, Nova Scotia Human Rights Commission, community agencies) to support those affected and prevent escalation.
resources.address: Henry Hicks Building, 6299 South Street, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

solutions.text: Elder–Youth Knowledge Exchanges: Facilitate programs where Mi'kmaq elders, African Nova Scotian storytellers, and community elders mentor youth—sharing cultural practices, local history, trades skills, and leadership development to strengthen belonging.

resources.name: Nikani Awtiken (Culturally Relevant Leadership Program)
resources.description: Nikani Awtiken is a land-based leadership program where Mi’kmaq Elders and Knowledge Keepers mentor Indigenous youth through cultural teachings, Mi’kmaw language, traditional ecological knowledge, and leadership development. Youth learn hands-on skills (e.g., canoeing, plant medicines, crafts) while building identity, confidence, and community belonging through direct intergenerational exchange.

resources.name: Rites of Passage
resources.organization: Association of Black Social Workers (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Rites of Passage program pairs African Nova Scotian youth with community Elders and storytellers using an Africentric framework to teach cultural history, identity, life skills, and leadership. Through circles, workshops, and mentorship, youth gain guidance from respected community members, strengthening belonging and resilience against racism while exploring education, trades, and career pathways.
resources.address: 6406 Quinpool Road, Suite 201, Halifax, NS B3L 1A8

resources.name: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia (Youth & Community Programs)
resources.organization: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Centre hosts intergenerational programs where African Nova Scotian Elders, historians, and artists share oral histories, cultural practices, and leadership lessons with youth through talks, workshops, and heritage events. These exchanges cultivate pride, strengthen identity and belonging, and connect youth to mentors and community networks across arts, entrepreneurship, and community service.
resources.address: 10 Cherry Brook Road, Cherry Brook, NS B2Z 1A8

resources.name: Membertou Heritage Park (Mi’kmaq Cultural Workshops & Youth Programs)
resources.description: Membertou Heritage Park offers Elder-led cultural workshops and youth experiences featuring Mi’kmaw language, drumming, storytelling, and traditional crafts such as beadwork and basketry. Youth learn directly from Elders and Knowledge Holders, reinforcing intergenerational ties, cultural continuity, and leadership grounded in Mi’kma’ki.

resources.name: Halifax Public Libraries (Indigenous and African Nova Scotian Community Programs)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries runs free, accessible intergenerational programs—such as Mi’kmaw cultural teachings and storytelling circles, and African Heritage Month youth workshops—led by Elders, historians, and community mentors. These events connect youth with cultural knowledge, oral history, arts and trades skills, and leadership opportunities, fostering belonging across diverse communities.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Affordable, Accessible Community Housing Co-ops: Support the creation of small-scale housing co-ops and shared-living models governed by residents, with units designed for accessibility and with priority allocation for marginalized local residents.

resources.name: The Village at Akoma Affordable Housing
resources.description: Akoma Holdings is redeveloping the former Nova Scotia Home for Colored Children lands into a community that includes affordable, accessible housing designed to reflect African Nova Scotian culture and needs. The project prioritizes African Nova Scotian residents, seniors, and families and incorporates barrier-free units and shared community spaces that support co-living and belonging. Resident engagement and advisory processes guide design and tenancy, aligning with resident-governed, equity-focused housing models.

resources.name: Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre Housing & Wije’winen Initiatives
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre leads Indigenous-governed affordable and supportive housing initiatives in Halifax, including the planned Wije’winen Living facility with accessible units and communal, culturally grounded spaces.
