This blended-finance approach built sustainable local capital while protecting long-term access to performance space.

resources.name: Keep the HAT On / Angels of the Theatre
resources.description: Highland Arts Theatre runs ongoing crowdfunding-style campaigns built on thousands of small monthly donations to sustain productions and keep tickets accessible. These citizen contributions are regularly paired with corporate sponsorships and public cultural grants, creating a resilient funding base for a year-round arts venue. The model directly channels local investment into creative programming and capital needs in downtown Sydney.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Fund (CEDIF) for Eltuek Arts Centre
resources.description: New Dawn Enterprises uses its CEDIF program to issue community investment shares to Nova Scotians, raising local, RRSP-eligible capital for social infrastructure projects like the redevelopment of the former Holy Angels into Eltuek Arts Centre. These community share offerings are complemented by support from public and philanthropic partners, blending citizen investment with institutional funds to finance studios, galleries, and incubator spaces. The result is a durable, community-owned arts hub that anchors Sydney’s creative economy.

resources.name: Chester Playhouse Rebuild Capital Campaign
resources.description: Following a devastating fire, the Chester Playhouse launched a community capital campaign that crowdfunded donations from residents, artists, and alumni to rebuild and modernize the theatre. Local gifts were leveraged alongside major contributions from the Municipality of the District of Chester, the Province of Nova Scotia, and business sponsors, closing the financing gap for construction and equipment. This community-driven funding model restored a key cultural space and strengthened long-term support for local arts.

solutions.text: Cultural Tourism and Local Experience Packages: Develop walking tours, seasonal cultural weekends, and artist studio visits marketed regionally. Small businesses, B&Bs, and creatives collaborate to create packages that generate revenue and profile for local culture.

resources.name: Cape Breton Artisan Trail
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: A curated island-wide studio and gallery route connecting visitors with working artisans for demonstrations, workshops, and direct-from-artist purchases. The trail is marketed regionally and through visitor information centres and accommodations, encouraging multi-stop itineraries that highlight local craft traditions. By driving traffic to small studios and galleries, it creates revenue for creatives and raises the profile of Cape Breton’s culture.

resources.name: Ross Creek Arts Weekends & Open Studios
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: Ross Creek hosts seasonal arts weekends, public open studios, and cultural workshops with local artists, often paired with food experiences and recommendations for nearby B&Bs and accommodations. These bookable, hands-on experiences are marketed across the province and invite visitors to engage directly with artists and rural culture. The programming generates income for creatives and local small businesses while strengthening the region’s cultural tourism offerings.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

resources.name: Guided Heritage & Food Tours of Lunenburg
resources.description: Lunenburg Walking Tours offers guided walking experiences led by local storytellers that connect architecture, boatbuilding heritage, and folk art with stops at independent shops, galleries, and eateries. The tours are promoted to regional visitors and frequently coordinated with local businesses and inns, encouraging package-style experiences for guests. This approach channels spending to small enterprises and elevates Lunenburg’s cultural profile.

resources.name: Lunenburg Art Walk
resources.description: A seasonal evening art walk where galleries, studios, and maker spaces across Old Town Lunenburg open late for exhibitions, artist demos, and live cultural programming. The event provides a self-guided walking tour format with maps and promotions that draw regional visitors into multiple venues in one night. It boosts sales for local artists and creative businesses while showcasing the town’s cultural assets.

resources.name: Artist-in-Residence & Creative Getaway Weekends
resources.description: White Point packages accommodations with hands-on workshops, artist talks, live music, and culinary experiences led by Nova Scotian creators throughout the year. These bookable cultural weekends are promoted to regional visitors and engage local artisans, musicians, and producers as paid facilitators. The model directly supports creatives and nearby small businesses while offering immersive local culture to guests.
resources.address: 75 White Point Beach Resort Road, White Point, NS B0T 1G0

solutions.text: Digital Platform for Local Creatives: A community-managed online marketplace and events calendar where artists sell work, list classes, and promote shows. Low fees and local promotion increase reach and provide data to inform programming decisions.

resources.name: The Designer Craft Shop (Online)
resources.organization: Craft Nova Scotia / Centre for Craft Nova Scotia
resources.description: A community-managed e-commerce platform operated by a member-based craft council, The Designer Craft Shop’s online store showcases and sells the work of Nova Scotia craftspeople year-round while also listing exhibitions and workshops hosted at the Centre for Craft Nova Scotia. By combining an online marketplace with an events/classes calendar and strong local promotion, it helps artists reach buyers, fill classes, and promote shows. As a non-profit, it keeps artist costs manageable and uses sales and attendance data to inform future programming and marketing.

resources.name: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design Online Store & Course Calendar
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: This platform features a curated online shop for Cape Breton artisans alongside an events and course calendar where artists list classes, exhibitions, and community programming. The Centre promotes makers locally and island-wide, helping creatives sell work and fill workshops with user-friendly registrations. Program participation and sales insights are tracked and used by the Centre to refine offerings and support sustainable careers for local artists.

resources.name: ARTSPLACE Gallery Online Shop & Events Calendar
resources.organization: Annapolis Region Community Arts Council (ARTSPLACE Gallery)
resources.description: ARTSPLACE, a community-run gallery in Annapolis Royal, maintains an online shop for member artists and an actively updated calendar of exhibitions, classes, and arts events. The digital platform increases reach for rural creatives, enabling artwork sales and registrations for workshops and shows with strong local promotion. As a non-profit, ARTSPLACE uses sales and attendance data to guide future programming and keep fees accessible for emerging and established artists.
resources.address: 396 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

resources.name: Ticket Halifax
resources.description: Ticket Halifax is a locally run ticketing and event-listing platform where artists and arts organizations can promote shows, readings, classes, and festivals and sell tickets directly to audiences. Integrated with The Coast’s local media channels, it provides strong regional promotion and artist-friendly tools, helping creatives reach new attendees. Organizers receive sales and attendance reports they can use to make data-informed programming and scheduling decisions.

solutions.text: Cross-sector Incubators: Arts + Tech + Trades: Create incubation programs that pair artists with tech, design, and tradespeople to prototype products and services (e.g., digital media, set fabrication, craft-tech). Shared mentorship and maker resources support small creative enterprises.

resources.name: FILM 5
resources.description: FILM 5 is an intensive incubator for emerging filmmakers that pairs writers, directors, and producers with experienced mentors across cinematography, sound, editing, and art departments. Participants receive training, mentorship, access to equipment and post-production resources, and production budgets to prototype short films—bringing artists together with technical and trades professionals to create market-ready work. This cross-sector model directly supports small creative enterprises in digital media and screen production.
resources.address: Suite 101, 5663 Nora Bernard Street, Halifax, NS B3K 1B6

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio
resources.description: The Lou Duggan Creative Studio is a public makerspace at Halifax Central Library offering 3D printing, sewing machines, electronics, vinyl cutting, and digital media tools with workshops and staff mentorship. Artists, technologists, and craftspeople collaborate to prototype products and installations—from wearable tech and craft-tech to set pieces—using shared equipment and guidance. As an accessible, no-cost resource, it lowers barriers for small creative enterprises to test, iterate, and launch ideas.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Halifax Makerspace
resources.description: Halifax Makerspace is a member-run fabrication hub providing access to woodworking, metalworking, electronics, 3D printing, CNC, and laser tools alongside peer mentorship and project nights. It brings together artists, designers, engineers, and tradespeople to co-develop prototypes and small-batch products such as interactive installations, set elements, and craft-tech goods. The shared tools, cross-disciplinary community, and informal coaching function as an incubator for early-stage creative enterprises.
resources.address: Unit 102, 6050 Almon Street, Halifax, NS B3K 1T8

resources.name: Studio Access Program
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: The Studio Access Program provides makers with access to well-equipped studios in textiles, ceramics, metals/jewellery, and print, along with instruction and professional development. By connecting artists with skilled technicians and craftspeople, participants prototype and produce craft-tech and design products, often integrating digital design workflows. Shared resources and mentorship help creative entrepreneurs move from concept to market within a supportive cross-sector environment.

solutions.text: Inclusive, Multicultural, and Intergenerational Programming: Design events and spaces that reflect linguistic, cultural, and age diversity—community storytelling nights, cultural exchange workshops, and intergenerational arts projects—to broaden participation and make the arts welcoming for all residents.

resources.name: Programs & Events at Halifax Public Libraries
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries offers free, all-ages cultural programming across branches—multilingual storytimes, newcomer cultural exchange workshops, Indigenous and African Heritage Month events, and intergenerational arts and music activities. By providing accessible venues and diverse programming, the Library creates welcoming spaces that reflect linguistic, cultural, and age diversity, helping counter underinvestment by ensuring communities can gather, create, and share stories without financial barriers.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Cultural Programming
resources.description: The Mi'kmaw Native Friendship Centre hosts intergenerational cultural programming including drumming circles, language and craft workshops, storytelling with Elders, and community feasts that welcome Indigenous and non-Indigenous participants. These activities create inclusive, multicultural spaces where youth, adults, and Elders connect through the arts, strengthening community belonging and cultural exchange in the urban core.

resources.name: Community Programs and Cultural Events
resources.organization: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia delivers exhibits, storytelling nights, heritage month events, and arts workshops that celebrate African Nova Scotian culture while inviting the broader public to participate. Programming intentionally bridges generations—featuring youth and Elders—to share lived experiences and creative expression, fostering cross-cultural understanding and sustained community engagement.
resources.address: 10 Cherry Brook Road, Cherry Brook, NS B2Z 1A8

resources.name: Programs and Events at the Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21
resources.organization: Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21
resources.description: Pier 21 hosts family programming, community storytelling, and cultural performances that bring together newcomers and long-time residents to share immigration stories and artistic traditions. These intergenerational, multicultural events create welcoming spaces for dialogue and creative exchange, helping sustain an inclusive arts ecosystem that supports community vibrancy.

resources.name: Free Family Art Sunday
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts hosts Free Family Art Sunday, a recurring, no-cost, intergenerational program where people of all ages create art together, often featuring themes and guest artists from diverse cultural backgrounds. By removing financial barriers and centering inclusive, community-led creation, the program offers rural residents a welcoming space for cultural exchange and shared storytelling through the arts.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

solutions.text: Adopt-a-Venue and Maintenance Volunteer Programs: Local groups sponsor and maintain community venues—cleaning, repairs, volunteer staffing—in exchange for programming time. This reduces operating costs and deepens community stewardship of cultural assets.

resources.name: Member Volunteer and Work-Trade Program
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op engages members and community groups to take on front-of-house shifts, cleaning and minor repairs, and technical support for events. In return, volunteers receive access to rehearsal/production time and discounted rentals, directly exchanging stewardship and maintenance for programming opportunities. This lowers operating costs while giving local creators predictable, affordable venue access.

resources.name: Ross Creek Volunteer Program & Work-Exchange
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: Volunteers help with facility upkeep, gardens and trails, set/prop building, and event staffing at the Ross Creek Centre for the Arts. In exchange, participants earn access to workshops, studio/rehearsal space, or program credits—linking hands-on venue maintenance to time in the arts facilities. The program strengthens community ownership of the campus and reduces operating costs for year-round cultural programming.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

resources.name: Volunteer & Work-Trade Program
resources.description: The Deanery Project invites local volunteers and partner groups to adopt aspects of the site—supporting building repairs, trail and facility maintenance, and event hosting. In return, groups and individuals can access studios, meeting/performance spaces, and workshop/residency credits, effectively trading stewardship for programming time. This community-powered model preserves the venue and expands affordable cultural and learning opportunities.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

resources.name: Member Work-Sharing and Gallery Stewardship Program
resources.description: ART 1274 Hollis operates as an artist-run cooperative where members staff the gallery, handle cleaning and display maintenance, and assist with minor repairs and event setup. In exchange, member artists receive guaranteed exhibition space and opportunities to schedule talks or pop-up programming, directly linking volunteer stewardship to programming access. This co-op model keeps operating costs low and ensures the venue is sustained by the artists who use it.

obstacles.title: Climate risk and community resilience
obstacles.description: Coastal erosion, storms, and flooding threaten housing, infrastructure, and resource-based livelihoods, raising costs and uncertainty for young residents.

solutions.text: Living shorelines and saltmarsh restoration: Community-led projects to restore saltmarshes, create tidal wetlands, and install living shorelines (native vegetation, coir logs, rock sills) to reduce erosion, absorb storm surge, and provide habitat for fisheries.

resources.name: Making Room for Wetlands
resources.organization: TransCoastal Adaptations: Centre for Nature-Based Solutions, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: Making Room for Wetlands is a Saint Mary’s University TransCoastal Adaptations initiative that restores and reconnects saltmarshes and tidal wetlands across Nova Scotia to reduce coastal erosion and flooding. The program partners with communities, landowners, and municipalities to implement nature-based solutions such as managed realignment, tidal flow restoration, and living shorelines that use native vegetation, coir logs, and low-profile rock sills. It also provides technical guidance and training so local groups can plan, install, and monitor these projects for long-term resilience and fisheries habitat benefits.

resources.name: Mahone Bay Living Shoreline Project
resources.description: The Town of Mahone Bay implemented a living shoreline along vulnerable sections of its waterfront to reduce erosion and buffer storm surge impacts on roads, homes, and community assets. The project uses native salt-tolerant plants, coir logs, and low rock sills to stabilize the shoreline while enhancing habitat for coastal species. It was delivered with community engagement and ongoing monitoring to demonstrate nature-based coastal protection that supports working waterfronts and local quality of life.
resources.address: 493 Main Street, Mahone Bay, NS B0J 2E0

resources.name: Coastal Action Living Shorelines Program
resources.description: Coastal Action plans and installs living shorelines at erosion hotspots on Nova Scotia’s South Shore, using native vegetation, coir rolls, brush layering, and low rock sills to reduce wave energy and stabilize banks. The program engages waterfront landowners, municipalities, and volunteers in hands-on restoration, and monitors shoreline change and habitat response over time. By building tidal wetland and saltmarsh edge habitat, it protects community infrastructure and supports local fisheries and biodiversity.

resources.name: Living Shorelines Nova Scotia
resources.description: Clean Foundation delivers community-based living shoreline and saltmarsh restoration projects that use coir logs, native plantings, and small rock sills to stabilize coasts and absorb storm surge. The program partners with coastal communities to host volunteer planting days, train practitioners, and create demonstration sites that show effective, nature-based erosion control. These projects reduce climate risks to homes and infrastructure while improving nearshore habitat for fish and other wildlife.

solutions.text: Dune and beach nourishment programs: Local initiatives to rebuild and maintain dunes and beaches using community labour, volunteers, and partnership funding to protect coastal properties and recreational assets.

resources.name: Living Shorelines Program
resources.description: Ecology Action Centre’s Living Shorelines projects restore and build up coastal dunes and beaches by installing sand fencing, reshaping blowouts, and planting native marram (American beach) grass. The program mobilizes volunteers, youth groups, and local partners for hands-on planting and monitoring days, using partnership funding to protect shoreline roads, properties, and recreational beach assets from storms and erosion.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Provincial Parks Coastal Dune Restoration
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources and Renewables – Provincial Parks
resources.description: Nova Scotia Provincial Parks leads ongoing dune restoration and beach nourishment at provincial beaches by installing sand fencing, rebuilding dune profiles with windblown sand, and organizing community planting of native beach grasses. The work is delivered with volunteers, municipalities, NGOs, and local businesses, using partnership funding to strengthen natural barriers that protect nearby communities, park infrastructure, and recreational amenities from erosion and storm surge.

resources.name: Coastal Restoration and Dune Stabilization
resources.description: ACAP Cape Breton runs community-based coastal restoration that includes dune stabilization and nourishment on Cape Breton beaches, using sand fencing and transplanting of beach grasses to rebuild degraded dunes. The initiative engages volunteers and partners with provincial parks staff, municipalities, and local sponsors to reduce storm and flood risks to adjacent roads, homes, and recreational spaces while maintaining public access.

resources.name: TransCoastal Adaptations – Living Shorelines and Dune Restoration
resources.organization: TransCoastal Adaptations: Centre for Nature-Based Solutions, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: Based at Saint Mary’s University, TransCoastal Adaptations designs and implements nature-based shoreline projects across Nova Scotia, applying dune and beach nourishment where appropriate by installing sand fencing and planting native dune vegetation. Projects are delivered with municipal and provincial partners, NGOs, and community volunteers, leveraging blended funding to buffer community assets and recreational beaches from erosion and coastal storms.

solutions.text: Green stormwater infrastructure in towns: Install rain gardens, bioswales, permeable paving, and tree canopies in neighbourhoods to reduce flooding, recharge groundwater, and improve urban resilience.

resources.name: Urban Forest Master Plan (UFMP)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Urban Forest Master Plan expands and maintains street tree canopies in neighbourhoods across the city to intercept rainfall, slow runoff, and cool streets. By prioritizing plantings along streets, parks, and right‑of‑ways—especially in areas prone to flooding—the program reduces stormwater entering sewers and improves urban resilience to heavy rain and heat.

resources.name: Cogswell District Project – Green Stormwater Infrastructure
resources.description: HRM’s Cogswell District redevelopment integrates green stormwater infrastructure into new complete streets and public spaces, including bioretention planters (rain gardens), tree-lined medians, stormwater planters, and permeable surfaces. These features capture and filter runoff before it reaches Halifax Harbour, reduce localized flooding, and enhance groundwater recharge and climate resilience in a dense urban district.

resources.name: Stormwater Credits Program (Non-Residential)
resources.description: Halifax Water’s Stormwater Credits Program provides financial incentives for properties that install on-site green stormwater infrastructure such as permeable pavement, rain gardens/bioretention, green roofs, and cisterns. By rewarding projects that reduce and treat runoff before it enters public drainage systems, the program accelerates the adoption of nature-based solutions that mitigate flooding and improve watershed health.
resources.address: 450 Cowie Hill Road, Halifax, NS B3P 2V3

resources.name: Depave Paradise – Nova Scotia
resources.description: Led locally by the Ecology Action Centre, Depave Paradise mobilizes volunteers to remove unnecessary asphalt from schoolyards, community centers, and parking lots in Nova Scotia and replace it with rain gardens, native plant beds, trees, and permeable surfaces. These retrofits reduce stormwater runoff and urban flooding while creating greener neighbourhood spaces that absorb rain and improve climate resilience.

solutions.text: Community emergency preparedness teams: Train and equip local volunteer response teams for evacuation coordination, sandbagging, temporary shelters, and communications during storms and floods.

resources.name: Joint Emergency Management (JEM) Teams
resources.organization: Halifax Regional Municipality Emergency Management Office
resources.description: Halifax’s JEM Teams are neighborhood-based volunteer emergency preparedness groups organized and supported by the municipal Emergency Management Office. Volunteers receive training, exercises, and equipment to operate comfort centres and temporary shelters, assist with evacuation coordination and wellness checks, support sandbagging and debris management, and provide community communications during storms and floods. The program integrates volunteers into incident command alongside first responders to enhance localized resilience and rapid response.

resources.name: Disaster Management Volunteer Program (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross recruits, trains, and deploys volunteer teams across Nova Scotia to run reception centres and temporary shelters, register evacuees, and coordinate emergency supplies during floods and severe storms. Volunteers are equipped and certified in shelter management, logistics, psychological first aid, and emergency communications, and they work directly with municipal EMOs and first responders to support evacuations and immediate needs. The Nova Scotia office also stages cots, blankets, hygiene kits, and communications equipment to enable rapid, community-based response.

resources.name: Halifax Search and Rescue (HSAR)
resources.description: HSAR is a volunteer ground search and rescue organization that also supports storm and flood operations across HRM and Nova Scotia. In addition to search missions, HSAR trains and equips volunteers for evacuation assistance, door-to-door wellness checks, sandbagging, and field communications using VHF/UHF radios and incident command protocols during weather emergencies. The team conducts regular exercises with EMO and maintains mobile command, generators, and community preparedness outreach to strengthen local resilience.

resources.name: Kings County Regional Emergency Management Organization (REMO)
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: Kings REMO coordinates municipal emergency preparedness, training, and volunteer engagement across communities in Kings County. The program helps organize and equip community comfort centres and volunteer teams for evacuation support, sandbagging, and local communications during floods and storms, and integrates these volunteers with municipal services and partner agencies like the Red Cross. Ongoing exercises and public education build neighborhood-level capacity to respond and recover quickly.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

solutions.text: Resilient housing retrofit assistance: Local programs offering grants, bulk procurement, or volunteer labour to raise foundations, flood-proof basements, improve drainage, and retrofit homes to withstand extreme weather.

resources.name: Adopt-A-Drain
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Adopt-A-Drain mobilizes volunteers to keep nearby storm drains clear of leaves and debris, reducing overland flooding during heavy rain events. By improving neighborhood drainage, the program helps protect basements and foundations from water intrusion and complements homeowner flood-proofing measures.

resources.name: Rainscaping Program
resources.description: Coastal Action’s Rainscaping Program helps homeowners install low-impact stormwater solutions—such as rain gardens, bioswales, downspout disconnections, and rain barrels—to reduce runoff and localized flooding. The organization provides site assessments, designs, education, and often coordinates volunteer planting days or cost-shared installations when funding is available, directly improving property drainage and flood resilience.

resources.name: Green Stormwater Infrastructure (GSI) Program
resources.organization: ACAP Cape Breton (Atlantic Coastal Action Program – Cape Breton)
resources.description: ACAP Cape Breton supports residents in implementing green stormwater infrastructure—like rain gardens, permeable landscaping, and rain barrels—to manage runoff and reduce basement and yard flooding. The program offers workshops, property-level guidance, and community volunteer events to install and maintain these features, strengthening household and neighborhood resilience to extreme rainfall.

resources.name: Rain Garden & Stormwater Management Program
resources.description: Clean Annapolis River Project works with homeowners to design and implement site-specific stormwater solutions—rain gardens, swales, and downspout redirection—that mitigate flooding and erosion. Through technical advice, educational resources, and occasional cost-share support or donated materials, the program enables practical drainage retrofits that protect foundations and reduce flood risk.
resources.address: 314 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

solutions.text: Managed retreat planning and land-swap initiatives: Community-driven planning that identifies high-risk parcels, offers fair relocation incentives or land-swaps, and converts vulnerable sites to open space or coastal buffers.

resources.name: Truro Floodplain Property Acquisition Program
resources.description: The Town of Truro has undertaken a voluntary buyout and relocation program for properties repeatedly impacted by flooding along the Salmon River and McClures Brook floodplains. The program identifies high-risk parcels through flood-risk mapping, offers fair-market compensation and relocation assistance to willing homeowners, and converts acquired lands to open space and flood storage areas, creating green buffers that reduce future risk.

resources.name: Making Room for Wetlands
resources.organization: TransCoastal Adaptations: Centre for Nature-based Solutions, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: TransCoastal Adaptations works with municipalities and communities to plan managed retreat by identifying at-risk coastal parcels and enabling dike realignment, voluntary land acquisition, and conservation easements that restore salt marshes. By converting vulnerable sites into natural buffers and providing technical support for relocation and land-swap options, the initiative reduces flood and erosion risk while expanding protective coastal habitat.

resources.name: 100 Wild Islands Legacy Campaign
resources.description: This Nova Scotia Nature Trust initiative secures vulnerable coastal parcels and islands along the Eastern Shore through purchases and conservation easements, removing development pressure and converting high-risk areas into permanent natural buffers. Working with local residents and landowners, the campaign protects shorelines and salt marshes that absorb storm surge and sea-level rise, supporting community-led resilience and space for nature while reducing long-term risk.
resources.address: 81 Prince Albert Road, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 1M1

resources.name: Pugwash River Estuary Conservation Project
resources.organization: Nature Conservancy of Canada (Nova Scotia Program)
resources.description: The Nature Conservancy of Canada’s project in the Pugwash River estuary acquires and protects flood- and erosion-prone coastal lands, converting them to conserved wetlands and shoreline buffers. Through community partnerships and voluntary land securement, the initiative removes development from high-risk parcels and restores natural systems that mitigate storm surge and flooding—key components of managed retreat.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 217, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Community microgrids and resilient power hubs: Develop neighborhood-scale backup power (solar + storage) and designated community hubs to keep critical services running during outages and support local businesses.

resources.name: HalifACT Resilience Hubs
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s HalifACT initiative is creating a network of community resilience hubs at libraries, recreation centres, and other public buildings. These hubs are being equipped with on-site solar photovoltaics and battery storage to maintain essential services—such as device charging, communications, refrigeration, and warming/cooling—during grid outages, while supporting nearby residents and small businesses. By combining solar + storage and designated hub operations, the program implements neighborhood-scale backup power and microgrid-ready sites that strengthen climate resilience to storms and flooding.

resources.name: Smart Grid Nova Scotia
resources.description: Nova Scotia Power’s Smart Grid Nova Scotia program deploys distributed energy resources in communities, including behind-the-meter battery systems that can pair with rooftop solar to provide backup power during outages. By aggregating these resources into a virtual power plant alongside smart EV chargers and controllable loads, the program delivers neighborhood-scale resilience and peak demand management, reducing storm impacts and keeping critical services online. The approach demonstrates how solar + storage can operate as a community microgrid backbone and support resilient power hubs across the province.
resources.address: 1223 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

solutions.text: Diversify coastal livelihoods and skills training: Offer local training and startup support for aquaculture, green trades, ecotourism, and digital/remote work to reduce economic reliance on vulnerable resource sectors.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard is an ocean-technology incubator that provides workspace, prototyping and testing facilities on the Dartmouth waterfront, mentorship, and market access for early-stage companies. By accelerating ventures in aquaculture tech, marine monitoring, coastal protection, and related blue-economy sectors, it equips local founders with skills, networks, and investment readiness. This diversifies coastal livelihoods by creating new ocean-focused businesses and high-quality technical jobs in coastal communities.

resources.name: Clean Leaders
resources.description: Clean Leaders is a paid green-jobs training and employment program that places youth with host organizations across Nova Scotia for hands-on work in areas like shoreline restoration, energy-efficiency upgrades, invasive species management, and community climate projects. Participants gain certifications and practical experience that translate into careers in the green trades and environmental services. By building a skilled local workforce for climate adaptation and energy efficiency, the program strengthens coastal resilience and expands non-extractive livelihood options.

resources.name: Ocean Technology Advanced Diploma (Ivany Campus)
resources.description: This NSCC program trains students in marine sensors, data systems, robotics/ROVs, and field operations for ocean industries, with applied research and industry work placements. Graduates support innovation in aquaculture, marine environmental monitoring, and coastal infrastructure, and many roles can be performed in distributed or digital-first teams. The program builds in-demand technical talent that enables blue-economy growth and diversifies employment opportunities in coastal communities.

resources.name: Plan to SucCEED (Entrepreneurship Training)
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: Plan to SucCEED is a practical business-planning program that helps aspiring and early-stage entrepreneurs develop viable business models, marketing plans, and financial forecasts. CEED pairs training with coaching and access to financing, supporting startups across rural and coastal Nova Scotia in sectors like eco- and cultural tourism, fisheries value-add, trades services, and online/remote businesses. This enables residents to launch sustainable local enterprises that reduce dependence on volatile resource sectors.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Volta Residency Program
resources.description: Volta’s Residency provides founders with mentorship, programming, and a collaborative workspace to build scalable technology companies, including ocean-tech, climate solutions, and remote-first digital businesses. Through workshops, advisor networks, and access to capital partners, the program helps entrepreneurs acquire the skills and support needed to grow in Nova Scotia. By enabling tech and digital ventures that can operate from coastal communities, it expands diversified, location-flexible employment for young people.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

solutions.text: Community flood insurance pools and emergency funds: Create locally managed insurance cooperatives or reserve funds to lower premium volatility, speed recovery, and cover gaps where private insurance is unavailable.

resources.name: Canadian Red Cross Personal Disaster Assistance Program (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Personal Disaster Assistance Program provides immediate and short‑term emergency financial assistance, lodging, and essentials to households affected by floods, coastal storms, and other disasters across Nova Scotia. By quickly delivering funds and material support—especially for uninsured or underinsured residents—it acts as a rapid, community‑based recovery mechanism that fills insurance gaps and reduces the volatility and hardship families face after climate‑related events.

resources.name: Mayor's Relief Fund (Cape Breton Regional Municipality)
resources.description: The Mayor's Relief Fund is a locally managed fund that provides financial assistance to CBRM residents facing urgent needs after severe weather, flooding, and other emergencies. It helps cover essential costs that insurance may not address—such as temporary accommodations, basic household needs, and emergency repairs—thereby speeding recovery and stabilizing households impacted by climate‑driven events.

resources.name: Emergency Assistance Program
resources.description: The Mi'kmaw Native Friendship Centre offers emergency financial assistance, shelter supports, and basic‑needs help to urban Indigenous individuals and families who are displaced or impacted by storms and flooding. This rapid‑response support functions as a community emergency fund, bridging gaps when private insurance is unavailable or delayed and helping residents recover more quickly from climate‑related housing and livelihood disruptions.

solutions.text: Citizen science and coastal monitoring networks: Organize volunteers to monitor beach erosion, water levels, storm damage, and species shifts, feeding real-time data to municipalities and provincial planners.

resources.name: CoastSnap Nova Scotia
resources.organization: TransCoastal Adaptation Centre for Nature-Based Solutions (Saint Mary’s University)
resources.description: CoastSnap Nova Scotia installs fixed smartphone photo stations at popular beaches and headlands (e.g., Lawrencetown, Rainbow Haven), where volunteers take repeat photos that precisely track shoreline change, dune movement, and storm impacts over time. The images are processed by researchers to produce datasets and time-lapse analyses of beach erosion and water level effects, which are shared with municipal planners and provincial adaptation initiatives to inform coastal management and nature-based solutions.

resources.name: Coastal and Marine Program
resources.description: Coastal Action’s Coastal and Marine Program engages community volunteers in nearshore monitoring, including eelgrass and invasive green crab surveys, beach and dune condition checks, and post-storm shoreline assessments across the South Shore. The resulting habitat, species, and shoreline condition data are shared with local municipalities and provincial partners to guide restoration priorities, living shoreline projects, and coastal climate adaptation planning.

resources.name: Sydney HarbourWatch
resources.organization: ACAP Cape Breton (Atlantic Coastal Action Program – Cape Breton)
resources.description: HarbourWatch mobilizes volunteers and community partners to collect regular coastal water-quality measurements (e.g., bacteria, temperature) and document storm-related impacts around Sydney Harbour and nearby beaches. Data are published promptly and provided to the Cape Breton Regional Municipality and provincial agencies to inform public advisories, infrastructure planning, and coastal resilience actions.

resources.name: Community Aquatic Monitoring Program (CAMP)
resources.organization: Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) – Maritimes Region
resources.description: CAMP supports citizen science monitoring of estuaries across Nova Scotia by training local groups and students to sample fish and invertebrate communities, track seasonal changes, and record environmental conditions that reflect warming waters, storm impacts, and habitat shifts. The standardized datasets feed into Fisheries and Oceans Canada analyses and are shared with provincial and municipal partners to inform coastal habitat management and climate adaptation decisions.

solutions.text: Habitat restoration to stabilize shorelines: Restore eelgrass beds, oyster reefs, and kelp where appropriate to dampen wave energy, trap sediment, and support food systems important to local fishers.

resources.name: Eelgrass Monitoring and Restoration Project
resources.description: Coastal Action restores eelgrass (Zostera marina) in South Shore coves using methods like green crab removal and eelgrass transplanting to rebuild meadows lost to erosion and invasive species. Restored eelgrass beds attenuate wave energy and trap sediments, helping stabilize vulnerable shorelines while improving nursery habitat for lobster and finfish that support local fisheries.
resources.address: 37 Tannery Road, Unit 8, Lunenburg, NS B0J 2C0

resources.name: Oyster Habitat Restoration
resources.description: This initiative rebuilds native oyster reef habitat in Mahone Bay by deploying shell cultch and reef structures that provide substrate for oyster settlement and growth. Re-establishing oyster reefs dampens waves and encourages sediment deposition, which stabilizes shorelines and boosts water quality and habitat that benefit inshore fisheries and local harvesters.
resources.address: 37 Tannery Road, Unit 8, Lunenburg, NS B0J 2C0

resources.name: Green Crab Management and Eelgrass Restoration (Bras d’Or Lake)
resources.description: UINR works with Mi’kmaq communities to trap and remove invasive European green crab and to transplant eelgrass in degraded bays of the Bras d’Or Lake. By restoring eelgrass meadows that bind sediments and reduce wave energy, the program protects coastal shorelines and enhances critical nursery habitats for culturally and economically important species like lobster and trout.

resources.name: Green Crab Mitigation and Eelgrass Habitat Restoration (Annapolis Basin)
resources.description: CARP partners with researchers and volunteers to reduce green crab impacts and pilot eelgrass restoration in the Annapolis Basin and nearby estuaries. Rebuilt seagrass beds help attenuate waves and trap sediment, stabilizing shorelines while improving water quality and habitat that supports local shellfish and finfish harvesters.
resources.address: 314 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

solutions.text: Partnerships with Mi'kmaq and Indigenous knowledge holders: Co-design adaptation projects that integrate traditional ecological knowledge, stewardship practices, and Indigenous-led conservation for culturally appropriate resilience.

resources.name: Mi'kmaw Conservation Group
resources.description: A program of The Confederacy of Mainland Mi'kmaq, the Mi'kmaw Conservation Group co-designs aquatic and coastal restoration projects with Mi'kmaq communities, Elders, and knowledge holders across Nova Scotia. It integrates traditional ecological knowledge with western science to restore fish habitat, stabilize shorelines, monitor climate impacts, and train Indigenous Guardians—building culturally grounded resilience to erosion, flooding, and storms.

resources.name: Collaborative Environmental Planning Initiative (CEPI)
resources.description: CEPI brings Mi'kmaq Elders and knowledge holders together with governments, researchers, and communities to co-develop a watershed plan for the Bras d'Or Lake (Unama'ki) grounded in Two-Eyed Seeing (Etuaptmumk) and Netukulimk. By embedding Mi'kmaw stewardship practices into habitat restoration, shoreline buffering, and community education, CEPI advances climate adaptation that strengthens ecosystem and community resilience.

resources.name: Netukulimk (Mi'kmaq Rights Initiative)
resources.description: The Netukulimk program at Kwilmu'kw Maw-klusuaqn (Mi'kmaq Rights Initiative) partners with Mi'kmaq communities, governments, and proponents to integrate traditional ecological knowledge into land, water, and marine planning across Nova Scotia. Through Mi'kmaq Ecological Knowledge Studies, collaborative policy development, and community-led stewardship, it ensures adaptation projects are co-designed and culturally appropriate—supporting resilience of coastal livelihoods and infrastructure.

resources.name: Kespukwitk Conservation Collaborative
resources.description: This southwest Nova Scotia partnership—named for the Mi'kmaw Kespukwitk district—co-designs conservation and climate adaptation projects with Mi'kmaq communities alongside NGOs and governments. By weaving Mi'kmaw knowledge with science in salt marsh restoration, species-at-risk recovery, and coastal planning, the collaborative builds nature-based resilience to flooding, storms, and erosion while creating local stewardship and youth opportunities.
resources.address: 9 Mount Merritt Road, Kempt, NS B0T 1B0

solutions.text: Community advocacy for coastal setbacks and zoning: Local coalitions can lobby municipal councils for updated setback rules, stricter permitting in hazard zones, and incentives for resilient development patterns.

resources.name: Coastal Protection Campaign
resources.description: Ecology Action Centre’s coastal team leads public campaigns and community coalitions that push for stronger municipal coastal setback bylaws, no-build buffers in hazard zones, and climate-smart permitting. They provide residents with research, templates, and guidance to appear before councils, and have been a key advocate for implementing Nova Scotia’s Coastal Protection Act alongside municipal land-use updates that incentivize resilient development away from erosion and flood-prone shorelines.

resources.name: Coastal & Marine Program
resources.description: Coastal Action convenes South Shore communities, local officials, and planners to translate shoreline monitoring and flood/erosion science into municipal policy asks, including coastal setbacks and hazard-zone restrictions. Through workshops and roundtables, they help residents prepare submissions to councils and advocate for bylaws and incentives that steer development to safer areas while promoting nature-based shoreline resilience.

resources.name: TransCoastal Adaptations: Centre for Nature-Based Solutions
resources.description: This Saint Mary’s University initiative partners with coastal communities and municipalities to co-develop policies that incorporate sea-level rise and erosion risk into land-use bylaws, including buffers and coastal setback language. It equips community groups with training, tools, and evidence to advocate at council for stricter permitting in hazard zones and incentives for resilient, nature-based development patterns.

resources.name: Community Climate Adaptation & Resilience Program
resources.description: Clean Foundation supports Nova Scotia communities with risk assessments and public engagement that feed into municipal planning, helping residents and youth advocate for coastal setbacks, floodplain protections, and no-build zones. They facilitate community meetings, translate technical risk maps into zoning recommendations, and encourage councils to adopt incentives that direct growth to safer, serviced locations.

resources.name: Climate Change and Coastal Planning Advocacy
resources.description: NSFM represents municipalities and advances policy positions on climate adaptation, sharing best practices on coastal flood and erosion risk, and urging consistent land-use planning tools such as coastal setbacks and development restrictions in hazard zones. Through member resolutions, guidance documents, and meetings with provincial and municipal leaders, they help councils adopt resilient zoning and incentive structures that reduce coastal risk.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1304, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Youth engagement and resilience education: Schools and youth groups run hands-on programs (shoreline restoration, emergency drills, green trades apprenticeships) to build skills and retention of young residents.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship (CLSI)
resources.description: CLSI places Nova Scotia youth (ages 15–30) in paid summer internships with municipalities, Indigenous communities, NGOs, and businesses to work on climate adaptation and environmental projects. Participants gain hands-on skills through activities like shoreline and salt marsh restoration, stormwater mapping, community outreach, and resilience planning—building practical experience that supports youth retention and green career pathways.

resources.name: Coastal and Marine Program
resources.description: Coastal Action engages youth and schools across the South Shore in hands-on coastal stewardship, including eelgrass and salt marsh restoration, beach cleanups, and coastal habitat monitoring. Through classroom visits and field-based activities, young people learn practical resilience skills tied to storms, flooding, and erosion while contributing directly to healthier shorelines.
resources.address: 37 Tannery Road, Unit 2, Lunenburg, NS B0J 2C0

resources.name: Coastal Adaptation Program
resources.description: EAC’s Coastal Adaptation team partners with schools, youth groups, and communities to deliver workshops and field activities on living shorelines, nature-based solutions, and flood/erosion risk. Youth participate in shoreline assessments, planting and stabilization projects, and local resilience planning, gaining skills that translate into community leadership and green career pathways.

resources.name: Emergency Preparedness Education (Atlantic)
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross delivers emergency preparedness education to Nova Scotia schools and youth groups, including workshops, drills, and training on severe weather, flooding, and power outages. Youth practice creating family emergency plans and kits and learn response skills (first aid and community readiness) that strengthen local resilience to climate-related disasters.

resources.name: Youth Build Volunteer Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia engages youth volunteers on supervised build sites to learn construction safety, energy-efficient building practices, and climate-resilient home design. These hands-on experiences expose young people to green trades careers while directly improving community resilience through safe, durable, and efficient housing.

solutions.text: Small-scale nature-based flood retention: Create ponds, wetlands, and upstream retention basins in watersheds to slow runoff, reduce peak flows, and provide recreational and biodiversity benefits.

resources.name: Halifax Water Stormwater Service
resources.description: Halifax Water plans, builds, and maintains stormwater infrastructure across the municipality, including naturalized stormwater ponds, constructed wetlands, and upstream detention basins that slow runoff and reduce peak flows in urban watersheds. These nature-based assets improve water quality, decrease flood risk for neighbourhoods and roads, and often provide green spaces and habitat for wildlife.
resources.address: 450 Cowie Hill Road, Halifax, NS B3P 2V3

resources.name: Salt Marsh Restoration & Managed Realignment Program
resources.organization: TransCoastal Adaptations: Centre for Nature-based Solutions, Saint Mary's University
resources.description: This program designs and implements nature-based coastal flood mitigation by restoring salt marshes and undertaking managed dyke realignments that re-establish tidal wetlands. The resulting wetlands act as natural retention and storage areas that attenuate storm surge and riverine flood peaks, while enhancing biodiversity and creating recreational and educational opportunities through accessible coastal sites.

resources.name: Annapolis River Wetlands & Floodplain Restoration
resources.description: CARP restores and enhances wetlands, floodplains, and headwater ponds throughout the Annapolis River watershed to slow runoff, reduce peak flows, and build climate resilience for nearby communities and farms. Projects include constructing or enhancing small wetlands, reconnecting floodplains, and riparian replanting that improves habitat and provides community recreation and education opportunities.
resources.address: 314 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

resources.name: Watershed Restoration & Wetland Conservation
resources.description: Coastal Action undertakes watershed-scale restoration on Nova Scotia’s South Shore, creating and enhancing small wetlands and naturalized stormwater detention features that reduce flooding and improve water quality. By working with municipalities, landowners, and community groups, the program installs nature-based retention projects and restores upstream habitats that support biodiversity and provide public green spaces.

obstacles.title: Fragmented innovation and commercialization ecosystem
obstacles.description: Siloed supports, weak industry–postsecondary collaboration, and procurement barriers slow the translation of research and ideas into local jobs and firms.

solutions.text: Community Innovation Hub Network: Establish a distributed network of small, locally-run hubs (in libraries, community centres, colleges) that provide coworking, mentorship, prototyping equipment, and commercialization guidance to connect entrepreneurs, students, and industry.

resources.name: Volta
resources.description: Volta is a downtown innovation hub that provides flexible coworking space, mentorship, startup programming, and investor/corporate connections for entrepreneurs and students. By convening founders, industry partners, and postsecondary talent through workshops, accelerator programs, and events, it helps translate ideas into companies and careers—directly addressing ecosystem fragmentation and commercialization gaps.

resources.name: Startup Yard at COVE
resources.description: Startup Yard at COVE is an ocean technology incubator offering shared labs, prototyping facilities, and waterfront test infrastructure alongside business mentorship and commercialization support. It connects startups, students, and researchers with established marine industry partners at COVE, helping ventures validate products, navigate procurement, and scale within a collaborative, industry–postsecondary hub.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: The Lou Duggan Creative Studio is a public makerspace inside Halifax Central Library that offers tools like 3D printers, sewing and crafting equipment, and digital media resources, along with staff support and workshops. As a free, community-run hub, it provides accessible prototyping, skills development, and collaboration space that connects youth, students, and local entrepreneurs—linking creativity to early-stage commercialization pathways and community partners.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Dalhousie University Sandbox)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs is a university-based innovation sandbox that provides collaborative workspace, prototyping support, mentorship, and industry-linked challenges for students and early-stage teams. Through hackathons, applied projects, and commercialization coaching within the Dal Innovates network, it bridges students, startups, and employers—advancing a distributed hub model that strengthens talent pipelines and accelerates market adoption of new ideas.

resources.name: Perennia Innovation Centre
resources.description: The Perennia Innovation Centre is a pilot-scale food and beverage facility that offers shared processing suites, labs, and technical advisory services to help entrepreneurs prototype, validate, and commercialize products. Operating as a regional hub in rural Nova Scotia, it connects startups and students with industry experts and buyers, enabling applied R&D, scale-up, and market readiness within a supportive, community-accessible environment.
resources.address: 199 Dr. Bernie MacDonald Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2H5

solutions.text: Local Industry–Postsecondary Partnership Program: Facilitate ongoing, community-hosted projects where local firms and postsecondary classes co-design applied research, apprenticeships, and capstone projects with shared outcomes and public showcases.

resources.name: NSCC Applied Research
resources.description: NSCC Applied Research connects Nova Scotia companies and community organizations with faculty and student teams to co-design applied R&D, product development, and process-improvement projects embedded in courses, co-ops, and capstones. Projects are scoped to shared outcomes—such as prototypes, feasibility studies, and implementation plans—and regularly culminate in campus or community demo days and showcases that engage employers and inform hiring.

resources.name: Dalhousie Engineering Capstone Design Program
resources.description: Through industry-sponsored capstone projects, multidisciplinary student teams collaborate with Nova Scotia firms and community partners over two academic terms to design, build, and test real solutions. Results are presented at the Faculty’s public Capstone Design Expo/Conference, creating direct pathways to internships, employment, and commercialization for local partners.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Nova Scotia Sandbox)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs is a university–industry sandbox that brings local tech companies together with postsecondary students to co-create prototypes, data experiments, and software solutions through challenge sprints, applied research, and mentorship. Teams publicly demo outcomes at hackathons and showcase nights, and many projects evolve into co-ops, apprenticeships, or startup ventures with regional employers.

resources.name: Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE convenes ocean-sector companies with postsecondary programs (e.g., NSCC and Dalhousie) to co-design applied projects, field trials, and work-integrated learning in a real-world harbour campus. The centre regularly hosts challenge events and public demonstrations where student–industry teams share results, accelerating technology adoption, talent pipelines, and local procurement in the blue economy.

resources.name: Verschuren Centre Industry Partnerships and Pilot Facility
resources.organization: Verschuren Centre for Sustainability in Energy and the Environment, Cape Breton University
resources.description: The Verschuren Centre partners with Nova Scotia SMEs and scale-ups to run pilot-scale applied research with student researchers and co-op placements embedded in industry projects across cleantech, biotech, and advanced materials. Projects are jointly scoped with companies and faculty, culminating in validated pilots and open houses/industry showcases that link students to jobs and help firms commercialize in-province.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

solutions.text: Neighbourhood Demo Days and Marketplaces: Organize regular events where local innovators, makers, and students present prototypes and businesses to community members and small buyers, generating feedback, early sales, and local visibility.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE Demo Day
resources.description: COVE’s Start-Up Yard runs regular Demo Days where ocean technology startups and student teams showcase working prototypes and business concepts to community members, small buyers, industry partners, and government. These open demo-market events generate real-world feedback, early sales conversations, and pilot opportunities, helping bridge the gap between research, commercialization, and local procurement.

resources.name: Volta DemoCamp Halifax
resources.description: Volta hosts DemoCamp and community showcase nights where founders, makers, and students give live product demos (no slides) to the public, local businesses, and investors. By convening diverse stakeholders to see and test early-stage products, these events deliver rapid feedback, create visibility, and spark early customer and partnership leads for Nova Scotia ventures.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs Hackathons & Demo Nights
resources.organization: ShiftKey Labs, Faculty of Computer Science, Dalhousie University
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs runs student-centered hackathons and demo nights where teams present functioning prototypes to local companies, mentors, and community members at Dalhousie. These showcases connect postsecondary talent with real users and small buyers, accelerating feedback loops, pilot projects, and pathways from campus innovation into the regional economy.
resources.address: 6050 University Avenue, Room 426, Halifax, NS B3H 1W5

resources.name: NSCAD Student Art Sale
resources.description: NSCAD’s recurring Student Art Sale is a public marketplace where students present and sell new work—including design objects, functional prototypes, and creative products—directly to community members and local retailers. The event provides immediate user feedback, early revenue, and commissioning opportunities, helping emerging creatives validate offerings and connect with local buyers.

resources.name: Alderney Landing Community Markets & Maker Fairs
resources.description: Alderney Landing hosts weekly farmers’ and artisan markets plus seasonal maker fairs that feature local innovators, student creators, and early-stage micro-businesses. These neighbourhood marketplace events give vendors affordable tables to test products, gather feedback from residents, and make early sales—building local visibility and links to small retailers and community buyers.

solutions.text: Community Procurement Champions: Create volunteer or municipal roles to help small local firms and social enterprises navigate public and institutional procurement processes and to advocate for procurement policies favouring local innovators.

resources.name: Procure with Halifax (Vendor Engagement & Social Procurement)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Corporate Procurement team runs vendor information sessions, office hours, and guides that help small local firms understand how to register, find tenders, and submit compliant bids to the municipality. HRM also incorporates social value into procurements and engages with community and industry partners to reduce barriers—acting as a municipal procurement champion that both coaches suppliers and advocates for procurement practices that create opportunities for local innovators and social enterprises.

resources.name: Procurement Assistance Canada – Atlantic Region
resources.description: Procurement Assistance Canada (formerly OSME) provides free seminars, one-on-one advising, and outreach across Nova Scotia to help small and diverse businesses navigate federal procurement, register as suppliers, and identify relevant opportunities on CanadaBuys. Acting as procurement champions, they mentor local firms and social enterprises on how to bid effectively and engage federal buyers, while advocating for inclusive, SME-friendly procurement practices within federal institutions operating in the province.

resources.name: Supplier Diversity Program
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business, Mount Saint Vincent University
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business helps women-owned companies—including social enterprises—become procurement-ready by offering training on selling to public institutions, connections to buyer networks, and support for supplier diversity certifications (e.g., through WBE Canada). By coaching firms through procurement processes and championing inclusive procurement policies with public and institutional buyers, the program functions as a community procurement champion for women-led innovators in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: CANS Tendering & Procurement Support (CANSnet)
resources.description: The Construction Association of Nova Scotia supports local contractors and trades with training on public tendering, access to project and bid information through CANSnet, and one-on-one guidance to navigate procurement requirements for government and institutional projects. CANS also advocates with public owners for fair, transparent procurement policies that strengthen opportunities for Nova Scotia firms—acting as an industry-based procurement champion that helps local businesses win work and build capacity.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

solutions.text: Shared Commercialization Services: Form cooperative services (legal templates, IP clinics, accounting, marketing) available at low cost to startups and researchers, lowering the barrier to spin out local ventures.

resources.name: Volta Office Hours
resources.description: Volta runs recurring Office Hours that connect startups with pro bono or low-cost experts in law, IP, accounting, and marketing. By centralizing these shared commercialization services in a single hub, Volta lowers the transaction cost for founders and researchers to get templates, advice, and due-diligence support needed to form companies and pursue customers.

resources.name: The Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: The Start-Up Yard at COVE provides ocean technology ventures with shared commercialization services, including IP and legal clinics through partner networks, accounting and finance mentoring, and go-to-market support. These coordinated services reduce barriers for researchers and founders to spin out companies, validate products, and access procurement opportunities in marine and defense markets.

resources.name: CEED Consulting
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED Consulting offers affordable, project-based commercialization support to startups and SMEs, including market research, marketing plans, customer discovery, and basic financial modeling delivered by trained teams. By providing accessible, standardized services and templates, CEED helps founders turn ideas into validated business models and reduces the cost of early legal, marketing, and accounting readiness.

resources.name: Product Development & Innovation Services
resources.description: Perennia’s Product Development & Innovation Services give agri-food startups access to shared labs, regulatory and labeling guidance, shelf-life testing, and packaging/marketing support on a fee-for-service basis. This one-stop, sector-specific commercialization support lowers the barrier for researchers and entrepreneurs to move prototypes to market-ready products and launch local ventures.
resources.address: 199 Dr. Bernie MacDonald Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2H5

resources.name: Office of Commercialization and Industry Engagement (OCIE)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s OCIE provides researchers and spinout teams with shared commercialization services such as IP assessment, patenting and licensing support, standard research and collaboration agreements, and startup formation guidance. By centralizing templates, legal/IP clinics, and industry matchmaking, OCIE reduces friction and cost in translating research into Nova Scotia-based companies.

solutions.text: Local Seed and Microgrant Funds: Pool community donations, municipal seed money, and business sponsorships into small, fast-turnaround grants or microloans to help teams move from idea to prototype or pilot.

resources.name: Early Stage Commercialization Fund (ESCF)
resources.description: ESCF provides small, fast-turnaround, non-dilutive funding to help researchers and early-stage companies in Nova Scotia move promising ideas toward prototypes and pilots. By bridging the gap between lab results and market validation, the fund acts as a local seed mechanism that accelerates commercialization and encourages collaboration with industry partners.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

resources.name: Awesome Foundation Halifax Microgrants
resources.description: The Halifax chapter awards $1,000 no-strings-attached microgrants, pooled from monthly contributions by local volunteer trustees, to quickly fund prototypes, pilots, and early-stage community and creative projects. This community-backed seed funding model enables small teams to test ideas rapidly without lengthy application processes, strengthening local innovation across arts, tech, and social impact.

resources.name: CEED Microloan Program
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED offers microloans to new and early-stage entrepreneurs to cover startup costs like prototyping, equipment, and pilot projects, with quick decisions and wraparound coaching. As a community-based nonprofit supported by public and private partners, CEED’s microfinancing fills the early capital gap and helps founders move from idea to first customers in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: CBDC Blue Water Micro Loan Program
resources.organization: CBDC Blue Water (Community Business Development Corporation)
resources.description: CBDC Blue Water provides microloans to rural and small community entrepreneurs in Halifax County East, enabling quick access to early capital for validation activities such as prototypes, pilots, and initial market tests. As a community development finance organization supported by public partners, it channels local and government-backed funds into small, fast-turnaround financing that helps teams progress from concept to traction.
resources.address: 61 Stella Drive, Unit 103, Porters Lake, NS B3E 0G4

resources.name: Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta Cohort is a seed program that provides early-stage startups with $25,000 in funding and in-kind resources through a fast, competitive process supported by public and private partners. The program helps founders build MVPs, run pilots, and validate market fit, addressing early capital gaps and strengthening the regional innovation pipeline.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

solutions.text: Mentor Circles Linking Youth and Industry: Set up sector-specific mentor circles where experienced local professionals advise students and young entrepreneurs in regular sessions, building relationships and pathways to jobs.

resources.name: Volta Mentors
resources.description: Volta’s mentor network connects student founders and early-stage entrepreneurs with seasoned founders, investors, and sector experts through recurring office hours, advisory circles, and workshops. These small-group and 1:1 sessions provide sector-specific guidance on product, commercialization, and hiring, and often include facilitated introductions to employers and partners. By building sustained relationships between youth-led startups and industry, the program creates clear pathways to jobs, internships, and company growth in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS pairs internationally trained students and young professionals with established Nova Scotia professionals in the same sector for a structured, multi-month mentorship. Mentors and mentees meet regularly, participate in group networking events, and work on industry-specific goals such as interview prep, credential navigation, and introductions to employers. This builds trusted relationships that translate into work placements and jobs, strengthening industry–postsecondary connections across the province.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 2005, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic
resources.organization: Creative Destruction Lab (hosted at Dalhousie University)
resources.description: CDL–Atlantic runs cohort-based, sector-focused mentorship streams where founders—often graduate students and young researchers—meet in regular roundtable sessions with accomplished entrepreneurs, operators, and investors. These mentor circles deliver targeted guidance on customer discovery, sales, and scaling, and facilitate introductions to industry partners and pilot opportunities. The program accelerates the translation of research into companies and jobs, tightening links between universities and industry in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Nova Scotia Sandbox) – Mentorship and Office Hours
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science – ShiftKey Labs
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs hosts recurring mentor office hours, industry-led workshops, and project cohorts that connect postsecondary students with professionals from Nova Scotia’s ICT sector. In these small-group sessions, mentors provide practical, sector-specific advice on product development, UX, and commercialization, and often link students to co-ops, internships, and jobs. The sandbox model directly bridges postsecondary talent with industry needs, reducing ecosystem fragmentation.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE provides ocean-technology founders and student innovators with access to a network of experienced marine industry mentors through recurring cohort meetings, advisory boards, and Ocean Connector events. These sector-specific mentor circles help teams validate use-cases, navigate procurement with marine operators, and connect with internships and technical talent. By aligning students and young entrepreneurs with ocean-industry leaders, the program turns ideas into pilots, jobs, and growing firms in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: School-to-Work Innovation Curriculum: Partner community businesses and colleges with local schools to deliver project-based learning, entrepreneurship modules, and short work placements tied to local economic needs.

resources.name: Options and Opportunities (O2) – Halifax Regional Centre for Education
resources.description: O2 is a high school pathway that connects students with local employers and post-secondary partners to complete project-based coursework and for-credit co-op placements aligned with Nova Scotia’s labour needs. HRCE schools deliver O2 with community businesses, NSCC dual-credit opportunities, and entrepreneurship-focused modules, helping students translate classroom learning into real work experience and business creation.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Co-op and Work-Integrated Learning (WIL)
resources.description: NSCC partners with hundreds of Nova Scotia employers to embed co-ops, practicums, and applied industry projects directly into college programs across sectors like oceans, ICT, health, and skilled trades. Students gain short work placements and team-based, client-driven projects, while entrepreneurship courses and supports help them prototype ideas and commercialize solutions tied to local economic needs.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Nova Scotia Sandbox Program)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs connects Dalhousie students with startups, tech firms, and public-sector partners to tackle real-world problems through hackathons, client projects, and mentorship. These project-based experiences simulate workplace delivery, build commercialization and entrepreneurship skills, and frequently lead to short-term internships or co-ops with Nova Scotia companies.

resources.name: The Spark Zone (Nova Scotia Sandbox Program)
resources.description: The Spark Zone brings students from Saint Mary’s University and partner institutions together with local businesses and non-profits to deliver client-focused, project-based innovation. It offers entrepreneurship training, mentorship, and funding to help student teams prototype solutions and often arranges short placements or ongoing roles with partner organizations addressing regional economic priorities.

solutions.text: Maker and Skills Workshops: Offer accessible community workshops (fabrication, coding, digital media, trades refresher) to upskill residents and provide a pipeline of talent for local commercialization projects.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: Halifax Central Library’s Lou Duggan Creative Studio is a public makerspace offering 3D printers, sewing machines, Cricut/vinyl cutters, and digital media tools alongside free or low-cost workshops for all ages. By teaching hands-on fabrication, coding, and digital production skills, it enables residents to prototype ideas, build creative portfolios, and support micro-enterprises. The Studio’s community-driven programming and partnerships create a practical pathway from skills-building to participation in local innovation and commercialization projects.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science (ShiftKey Labs)
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs, part of Nova Scotia’s Sandbox network, runs open workshops, hackathons, and bootcamps in software development, UX design, product prototyping, and entrepreneurship. These hands-on sessions upskill students and community members in coding and digital media while linking them to mentors and industry partners. The lab provides a direct pipeline to commercialization by connecting participants with local startups and applied projects that translate skills into jobs and ventures.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic
