Alumni chapters and volunteers also sponsor local meetups and panels, combining mentor-matching with practical sponsorship of opportunities that help grads establish themselves locally.

resources.name: SMU Alumni Mentoring (Ten Thousand Coffees)
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University’s Ten Thousand Coffees platform connects students and recent graduates with alumni for career conversations, job shadowing, and introductions within Halifax’s business and nonprofit communities. Alumni sponsors use the network to surface internships and early-career roles, implementing the mentor-matching and sponsorship elements that encourage graduates to stay and grow in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Starting Point Conference & Pitch Competition
resources.description: Starting Point is Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre’s annual conference and pitch competition for students and recent graduates, offering mentorship from alumni founders and judges plus cash awards to launch or grow ventures locally. The short-term grants and ongoing coaching provide financial help paired with career and business support, incentivizing grads to build in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Self-Employment Benefits (SEB) – Annapolis Valley
resources.description: Delivered by Acadia Entrepreneurship Centre, the SEB program provides eligible new founders—including recent graduates—with income support and intensive business coaching while they start a company in the Annapolis Valley. Drawing on Acadia’s mentor network (including alumni advisors), it blends financial assistance with mentorship to help graduates root their enterprises in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Childcare Co-ops and Subsidy Pool: Community-run childcare co-operatives and an associated subsidy pool lower childcare costs for young families, reducing overall household expenses and supporting decisions to form homes locally.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Child Care Subsidy Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: The provincial Child Care Subsidy provides income-tested assistance to help families afford licensed child care across Nova Scotia. By acting as a centralized subsidy pool tied to the Canada-Wide Early Learning and Child Care agreement, it directly lowers monthly fees for eligible households and enables community-operated centres (including co-ops and non-profits) to serve more young families, reducing cost pressures that can delay home formation or drive out-migration.

resources.name: YMCA Child Care (Greater Halifax/Dartmouth)
resources.description: The YMCA operates multiple not-for-profit, community-based licensed child care centres across HRM that accept the Nova Scotia Child Care Subsidy and Canada-Wide fee reductions. This model pools public subsidies with a community-run governance structure to keep parent fees lower, making it easier for young families to remain in Nova Scotia while managing student debt and household costs.

resources.name: Mount Saint Vincent University Child Study Centre (Early Learning Program)
resources.description: MSVU’s Child Study Centre is a university-affiliated, community-serving, licensed early learning program that accepts provincial child care subsidies under the Canada-Wide ELCC framework. As a not-for-profit centre with parent/community engagement, it leverages the public subsidy pool to reduce fees for families, supporting students and young workers to settle locally without prohibitive child care expenses.

solutions.text: Shared Workspaces and Remote-Job Hubs: Community-operated coworking hubs with high-speed internet, mentoring and job placement services let residents access higher-paying remote work without relocating, improving incomes while keeping roots local.

resources.name: Volta Community Membership & Coworking
resources.description: Volta operates a large community coworking hub that provides high-speed internet, shared desks, meeting rooms, and programming for people building tech-enabled careers from Halifax. Through mentorship, workshops, and connections to employers and programs (e.g., pitch events, founder meetups, and talent networking), it helps residents access remote and hybrid roles or build remote-ready startups without relocating, improving incomes while keeping roots in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Yarmouth Innovation Hub
resources.description: IGNITE’s Yarmouth hub offers community-operated coworking with high-speed internet, meeting rooms, and maker/innovation spaces for entrepreneurs, freelancers, and remote workers in Southwest Nova. Through mentorship, accelerator-style programming, and employer/community partnerships, the hub supports residents to secure remote work and grow businesses from home communities, reducing pressure to relocate despite student debt burdens.

resources.name: Navigate Startup House
resources.description: Navigate provides a coworking space with reliable high-speed internet, desks, and meeting facilities in Sydney, alongside coaching, mentorship, and regular skills and employer-connection events. By helping entrepreneurs, freelancers, and grads plug into remote-friendly opportunities and networks while staying in Cape Breton, it advances higher-earning pathways that ease student debt pressures without requiring relocation.

resources.name: Acadia Entrepreneurship Centre – LaunchBox
resources.description: LaunchBox is a university-affiliated coworking and startup hub that offers high-speed internet, shared workspace, mentorship, and experiential training for students and recent graduates in the Annapolis Valley. Its programming connects participants with remote-ready skills, advisors, and employer and investor networks so they can access remote roles or build location-independent ventures in Nova Scotia, supporting income growth while remaining local.

solutions.text: Return-to-Community Welcome Grants: Small cash grants or relocation bonuses funded by municipalities, community foundations and local businesses for people who return to Nova Scotia after completing education elsewhere, used for housing deposits, moving costs or startup expenses.

resources.name: Office of Healthcare Professionals Recruitment – Incentives and Relocation Support
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia – Office of Healthcare Professionals Recruitment
resources.description: The Office of Healthcare Professionals Recruitment (OHPR) offers cash incentives and relocation assistance to physicians, nurses, and other health professionals who choose to live and work in Nova Scotia, including Nova Scotians returning after training or practice elsewhere. Funds are disbursed as signing bonuses and moving/relocation allowances that can be used for moving costs, temporary housing, and other settling-in expenses, directly aligning with a return-to-community welcome grant model.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Recruitment – Relocation Assistance and Signing Bonuses
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health provides relocation allowances and signing bonuses to qualified candidates who accept positions across the province, including Nova Scotians returning after completing education or training out of province. These funds function as welcome grants that can be applied to moving expenses, short-term housing deposits, and other start-up costs of resettling in a Nova Scotia community.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: Municipality of Colchester – Community Physician Recruitment Incentive Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: The Municipality of Colchester offers financial incentives and relocation support to physicians who establish practice locally, often in collaboration with community partners and businesses. The incentive acts as a welcome grant, helping returning Nova Scotians cover moving costs, housing deposits, and other early expenses involved in settling back into the community.

resources.name: Town of Amherst – Physician Recruitment and Retention Incentive
resources.description: The Town of Amherst provides financial incentives and relocation assistance to recruit and retain physicians, with support from municipal funds and local community partners. These incentives operate like welcome grants that can be used for moving expenses, initial housing needs, and other start-up costs—particularly valuable for Nova Scotians returning after medical education or residency outside the province.
resources.address: 98 Victoria Street East, Amherst, NS B4H 1X6

solutions.text: Community Income Share Agreement (ISA) Pool: A locally governed ISA program where community investors fund education or training for residents in exchange for modest, time-limited income shares, aligning repayment with local job prospects and reducing upfront debt.

resources.name: Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP) – Nova Scotia Student Assistance
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Student Assistance (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: RAP lets Nova Scotians repay student loans based on their actual income, with payments reduced or paused when earnings are low and government covering the difference. By tying repayment to income earned in local jobs rather than fixed schedules, it implements the solution’s core mechanism of income-contingent, time-limited repayment and reduces upfront financial pressure that can drive graduates to leave the province.
resources.address: 2021 Brunswick Street, 4th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 2S9

resources.name: Nursing Education Tuition Relief and Return-of-Service Incentives
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Health and Wellness / Nova Scotia Health
resources.description: Nova Scotia funds portions of nursing education and offers grants in exchange for a time-limited return-of-service in provincial health care. This shifts costs from upfront tuition to an obligation tied to local employment and earnings, echoing a community ISA by aligning “repayment” with working in Nova Scotia and easing debt burdens that might otherwise push graduates to higher-paying markets elsewhere.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: Early Childhood Education (ECE) Education Funding Program – Return-of-Service
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: The province provides tuition funding and bursaries for ECE students who commit to work in Nova Scotia’s child care sector for a defined period. Instead of carrying upfront debt, participants fulfill a time-limited service obligation tied to local jobs and earnings, implementing the solution’s income-aligned, community-backed approach to reducing financial barriers to training.

resources.name: Practice Ready Assessment Program – Return-of-Service (PRAP-NS)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health / Nova Scotia Department of Health and Wellness
resources.description: PRAP-NS supports internationally trained physicians to enter practice in Nova Scotia, with placements that include return-of-service commitments in designated communities. By replacing large upfront costs with a time-bound obligation linked to employment and income in the province, it mirrors the ISA model’s alignment of repayment with local job outcomes, helping retain talent and reduce financial barriers.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

solutions.text: Crowdfunded Business and Home Starter Platform: A local crowdfunding platform that connects community investors with young entrepreneurs and first-time buyers offering small grants, loans or equity investments plus community validation and mentorship.

resources.name: Community Economic Development Investment Fund (CEDIF) Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Finance and Treasury Board
resources.description: Nova Scotia’s CEDIF program enables local residents to pool small investments into community-run funds that provide loans or equity to local businesses and projects. By channeling community capital and oversight through regionally managed funds, it functions as a local crowdfunding framework that backs young entrepreneurs with patient financing and community validation, often paired with mentorship from fund managers and advisors.

resources.name: FarmWorks Investment Co-operative Limited (CEDIF)
resources.description: FarmWorks raises capital from Nova Scotia residents through CEDIF share offerings and channels it into loans and equity-like investments for food and agriculture entrepreneurs across the province. This community-investment model acts like local crowdfunding—hundreds of small investors support emerging businesses while FarmWorks provides mentorship, networking, and ongoing guidance that helps founders start and grow in their home communities.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: New Dawn raises capital from Cape Breton residents via CEDIF share offerings and reinvests those funds as loans and equity in local enterprises and community projects, including housing. This model connects community investors directly with local founders, providing capital alongside mentorship and community validation that helps young people start businesses and put down roots in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia – Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat Nova Scotia mobilizes community donors, volunteers, and partner organizations to finance and build affordable homes for first-time buyers, then provides education and ongoing support to ensure successful homeownership. While structured as charitable community funding rather than investor returns, it functions as a community-backed home starter pathway that reduces upfront costs and debt burdens for young families, pairing financing with mentorship and homeowner readiness training.

solutions.text: Local Loyalty and Tax-Relief Incentives: Community-led incentive packages—such as discounts from local businesses, property-tax deferral programs run by municipalities, or rebate vouchers from chambers of commerce—help reduce early household costs for young residents committing to stay.

resources.name: Low Income Property Tax Exemption
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality provides an annual property tax exemption for eligible low-income homeowners, reducing or eliminating the amount of residential property tax owed. By lowering recurring housing costs, this municipal tax-relief incentive helps young residents and new families who meet income thresholds to stabilize finances early on and build roots in the community instead of relocating.

resources.name: Low Income Property Tax Exemption Program
resources.description: The Town of Bridgewater offers a low-income property tax exemption that reduces annual property tax bills for qualifying households. This tax-relief incentive eases early housing costs—especially helpful for younger homeowners and families—making it more affordable to stay in Bridgewater and invest in local life and careers.

resources.name: Low Income Property Tax Exemption
resources.description: Wolfville’s low-income property tax exemption provides an annual reduction in residential property taxes for eligible property owners. By lowering essential housing expenses, the program functions as a local tax-relief incentive that helps younger residents and families meet early household costs and encourages them to remain in the community.

resources.name: Downtown Truro Dollars
resources.description: Downtown Truro Dollars is a community-led gift card and voucher program redeemable at participating local businesses, often promoted with bonus-value sales and employer/community giveaways. These vouchers act like localized rebates/discounts that reduce day-to-day expenses for residents—useful for young people setting up households—while directing spending to Truro’s independent businesses and strengthening local ties.

resources.name: More Opportunity for Skilled Trades (MOST) Tax Refund
resources.organization: Department of Finance and Treasury Board, Government of Nova Scotia
resources.description: MOST provides an annual refund of provincial income tax paid on the first $50,000 of eligible earnings for qualified workers under 30 in designated occupations. By significantly reducing early-career tax burdens for young residents who live and work in Nova Scotia, it functions as a targeted tax-relief incentive that makes it more affordable to stay and build a life in the province.

obstacles.title: Housing Affordability and Supply Constraints
obstacles.description: Rising rents, limited rental stock, aging homes, and slow approvals/zoning limit accessible, stable housing for students, newcomers, and young families across urban and rural communities.

solutions.text: Community Land Trusts (CLTs): Create locally governed CLTs that buy and hold land for permanently affordable housing; community members help steward properties, set resale rules, and prioritize students, newcomers, and young families.

resources.name: Housing Trust of Nova Scotia
resources.description: A province-wide, community-governed trust that acquires and holds land and buildings to provide permanently affordable rental housing. It implements core CLT principles by removing properties from speculation, using long-term ownership and affordability covenants, and partnering with post-secondary institutions and newcomer-serving agencies to prioritize students, newcomers, and young families.
resources.address: 5516 Spring Garden Road, Suite 202, Halifax, NS B3J 1G6

resources.name: Kjipuktuk (Halifax) Community Land Trust
resources.description: A resident-led initiative creating a community land trust in Halifax to acquire land and steward permanently affordable homes. The trust’s governance model centers local residents and partner organizations to set ground-lease terms and resale/lease restrictions, focusing on stable housing options for students, newcomers, and young families in high-cost neighbourhoods.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia – Community Land and Affordability Stewardship
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia secures land and develops affordable homes, using resale restrictions and long-term affordability instruments (such as shared equity and covenants) that maintain affordability over time. While primarily an affordable homeownership program, its approach mirrors CLT principles by separating speculative land value from housing costs and engaging community volunteers and partners to steward properties for families, newcomers, and younger households entering the housing market.

solutions.text: Co‑housing and Shared‑Living Developments: Support resident‑led co‑housing projects where households share common spaces and resources to reduce individual costs; organize local workshops and seed funding to help groups form.

resources.name: Co-operative Development Services
resources.description: Nova Scotia Co-operative Council provides hands-on support to groups forming housing co-operatives, including facilitation, governance training, and incorporation. They help resident-led groups plan shared-living/co‑op housing with common amenities and connect them to seed funding and technical assistance (e.g., CMHC Seed Funding), directly enabling the formation of co‑housing-style, resident-governed developments that reduce per-household costs.

resources.name: The Rebuilding (Supportive Housing)
resources.description: Shelter Nova Scotia’s Rebuilding program provides shared, supportive housing with common kitchens and living spaces, lowering individual housing costs while offering stability and on-site supports. The communal model creates a co‑living environment that helps residents transition from homelessness into longer-term, community-oriented housing.

resources.name: Community Living and Sustainable Housing Workshops
resources.description: The Deanery Project hosts regular workshops and hands-on training on community living, natural building, and sustainable design that help resident groups explore and plan shared-living/co‑housing models. By convening local teams, offering facilitation, and demonstrating shared infrastructure and common spaces on-site, they equip Nova Scotians to launch practical, lower-cost co‑living initiatives.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

resources.name: Community Housing and Supportive Housing Programs
resources.description: Adsum provides community and supportive housing options for women, gender-diverse people, and families that include shared common areas and on-site supports, reducing individual housing costs and increasing stability. Their resident-centered, communal living approach aligns with shared‑living principles by pooling resources and creating safe, supportive homes across the Halifax area.

solutions.text: Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Campaign: Run neighborhood outreach and technical assistance to help homeowners build basement suites, garden suites, and in‑law units; pair volunteers with tradespeople for low‑cost renovations and guide approvals.

resources.name: Secondary Suites and Backyard Suites
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality provides clear guidance, checklists, and one-on-one support to help homeowners add basement suites, garden suites, and in-law units. Planning & Development staff advise on zoning, permits, and inspections and maintain an online hub that streamlines the approvals process so homeowners can create safe, legal accessory units that add rental supply.

resources.name: Planning & Inspections – Secondary and Garden Suites
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings – Planning & Inspections
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings permits secondary and garden suites in many zones and offers pre-application guidance, plan review, and coordinated building/inspection services. Planners and building officials help homeowners navigate code requirements (egress, fire separation, parking) and approvals so residents can add compliant accessory units on existing properties across rural and small-town communities.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Home Repair Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia’s Home Repair Program provides subsidized repairs and renovations for eligible homeowners, coordinating permits and licensed trades while mobilizing trained volunteers to reduce project costs. While not ADU-specific, the program can support work that helps create or bring secondary suites up to code where permitted (e.g., fire separation, egress windows, electrical and accessibility upgrades), expanding safe and affordable rental options.

resources.name: HomeWarming
resources.organization: Clean Foundation and Efficiency Nova Scotia
resources.description: HomeWarming delivers free energy-efficiency assessments and upgrades for income-qualified homeowners, coordinating contractors for insulation, air sealing, ventilation, and heating improvements. These upgrades can be paired with secondary-suite projects to make basement or garden units comfortable, code-ready, and lower-cost to operate; program navigators reduce complexity by guiding homeowners through assessments, scopes of work, and scheduling.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 1110, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

solutions.text: Local Rental Co‑ops and Tenant‑Owned Models: Form rental cooperatives where members democratically manage buildings and share expenses; provide training, template bylaws, and small grants to start local co‑ops.

resources.name: Co-operative Housing Development and Member Services (Atlantic Support)
resources.organization: Co‑operative Housing Federation of Canada (CHF Canada)
resources.description: CHF Canada supports existing and emerging rental housing co‑operatives in Nova Scotia with governance training, board education, and operational best practices so residents can democratically manage their buildings and share costs. It provides model bylaws, policies, and toolkits tailored to co‑ops, helping local groups incorporate and run member‑controlled rental housing. CHF Canada also partners on national programs that channel development support to new co‑ops in the Atlantic region, connecting Nova Scotia groups to resources that make tenant‑owned models viable.
resources.address: 66 Slater Street, Suite 400, Ottawa, ON K1P 5H1

resources.name: Sector Transformation and Community‑Based Tenant Initiative Funds
resources.description: The Centre provides small grants, capacity‑building, and coaching to community housing providers and tenant groups in Nova Scotia to start, strengthen, or convert to co‑operative housing. Through practical toolkits, peer learning, and project funding, it helps local groups draft bylaws, set up democratic governance, and complete early‑stage planning needed to launch rental co‑ops. This directly advances tenant‑owned and co‑operative models that keep rents affordable and stable in Nova Scotia communities.
resources.address: 1188 Saint‑Antoine Street West, Suite 402, Montreal, QC H3C 1B4

resources.name: Co‑operative Development Services (Housing Co‑ops)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Co‑operative Council helps community groups across the province form and grow co‑operatives, including rental housing co‑ops, by providing incorporation support, model bylaws, and board governance training. Its advisors guide feasibility, member recruitment, and business planning, and connect new housing co‑ops to credit union financing and community investment resources that reduce start‑up barriers. This on‑the‑ground development assistance enables tenant‑owned, democratically managed rental options in urban and rural Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 90 Research Drive, Suite 101, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

solutions.text: Vacant/Underused Building Reuse Program: Map and mobilize community action to convert vacant storefronts, schools, and warehouses into affordable rental units or mixed‑use housing; coordinate volunteer rehab teams and crowdfunding for renovations.

resources.name: Habitat Nova Scotia Homebuilding & Rehabilitation Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia mobilizes community volunteers, donors, and in‑kind supporters to build and rehabilitate homes for families, often acquiring or revitalizing underused properties rather than building only on greenfield sites. Through volunteer rehab teams and community fundraising (including ReStore proceeds and local campaigns), they convert aging or vacant housing into safe, affordable homes, directly increasing the supply of attainable rental and ownership options across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Barrington Street Heritage Conservation District Incentive Program
resources.description: This Halifax Regional Municipality program provides grants and technical support to restore and adapt heritage buildings along Barrington Street, encouraging owners to reactivate long‑vacant upper floors as residential apartments above ground‑floor commercial uses. By offsetting code, life‑safety, and rehabilitation costs, it enables the adaptive reuse of underused storefronts and upper stories into mixed‑use housing, adding units in a walkable urban core without new land consumption.

resources.name: Downtown Amherst Upper Storey Residential Conversion Grant
resources.description: The Town of Amherst supports property owners to convert vacant or underused upper floors of downtown commercial buildings into code‑compliant residential apartments. Grants help finance interior rehab (egress, sprinklers, accessibility, and energy upgrades), accelerating the reuse of existing storefront buildings for mixed‑use housing and increasing affordable rental supply in the downtown.
resources.address: 98 Victoria Street East, Amherst, NS B4H 1X6

resources.name: Downtown Building Improvement and Residential Conversion Program
resources.description: Yarmouth’s program provides matching grants and guidance to building owners to rehabilitate façades and convert vacant or underutilized upper floors in the downtown into residential units above active ground‑floor retail. By lowering renovation costs and streamlining improvements, the initiative brings new apartments to market in existing buildings, supporting mixed‑use main‑street vitality and more affordable rental options.

resources.name: New Dawn Properties – Affordable Housing Redevelopment
resources.description: New Dawn acquires, rehabilitates, and repurposes underused properties in Sydney and surrounding Cape Breton communities, adding and preserving affordable rental units within mixed‑use and residential buildings. Leveraging community investment tools (such as CEDIFs), donations, and local contractor networks, New Dawn’s projects transform aging or vacant structures into quality homes, aligning adaptive reuse with grassroots financing and community participation.

solutions.text: Volunteer Renovation and Skills‑Share Network: Organize skilled trades volunteers, apprentices, and community groups to renovate aging homes affordably—pairing people in need of lower rents with labor and materials donations.

resources.name: Volunteer Build Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia mobilizes skilled tradespeople, apprentices, and community volunteers to construct and, when feasible, rehabilitate homes, with families contributing sweat equity and materials donated by partners. By leveraging volunteer labour and donated or discounted building supplies, they significantly reduce project costs and increase access to safe, stable, and affordable housing, directly aligning with a skills‑share and renovation network approach.

resources.name: HomeWarming
resources.organization: Clean Foundation (in partnership with Efficiency Nova Scotia)
resources.description: HomeWarming provides free energy‑efficiency home upgrades (insulation, draft‑proofing, and related repairs) to eligible low‑income Nova Scotians, focusing on aging homes to lower utility costs and improve comfort. Delivered by Clean Foundation and Efficiency Nova Scotia, the program coordinates trained crews and materials at no cost to residents, effectively renovating existing homes affordably and complementing volunteer/community efforts to keep housing costs down.
resources.address: 126 Portland Street, Suite 202, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 1H8

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library – Tool Lending and DIY Skills‑Share
resources.description: The Halifax Tool Library lends a wide range of renovation and repair tools and hosts volunteer‑led workshops where skilled tradespeople and experienced DIYers teach practical home‑repair skills. By reducing equipment costs and mobilizing a skills‑share network, they enable residents, students, and community groups to complete low‑cost repairs and small‑scale renovations on aging housing, supporting affordability and extending the life of existing rental stock.

solutions.text: Tiny Home and Modular Pilot Projects: Support small‑scale pilots for tiny homes or modular units on community land or church lots to quickly add affordable units; document best practices and help replicate successful models.

resources.name: Halifax Modular Supportive Housing Initiative
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality (HRM) has deployed modular supportive housing communities on municipal sites to rapidly add safe, private units for people experiencing homelessness. By using pre-fabricated modular buildings and partnering with service providers for on‑site supports, HRM shortened approval and construction timelines and created a scalable template for other communities. HRM publicly shares project updates and siting/servicing practices to inform similar pilots across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Kentville Micro Shelter Village
resources.description: Open Arms developed a small village of micro‑shelters (tiny homes) on community land in Kentville to provide heated, lockable cabins and shared facilities as a bridge to permanent housing. The pilot demonstrates how quickly deployable, low‑cost units can expand local supply and improve stability for people in housing crisis. Open Arms shares build details, operating policies, and partnership approaches with churches, municipalities, and community groups to help replicate the model elsewhere in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: The Sunflower (Rapid Modular Supportive Housing)
resources.description: Adsum’s Sunflower project added deeply affordable, supportive units in the Halifax area using rapid, modular construction methods and streamlined site work. The approach accelerated delivery for women, gender‑diverse people, and families while controlling costs and documenting lessons on design, procurement, and operations. The project offers a practical roadmap for other Nova Scotia communities exploring small‑scale modular builds to expand affordable housing supply quickly.

solutions.text: Local Employer‑Assisted Housing Partnerships: Encourage local employers (colleges, hospitals, small businesses) to co‑fund rental units or offer rent guarantees for employees; communities can broker agreements and host matching events.

resources.name: Cabot Cape Breton Associate Housing
resources.description: Cabot Cape Breton provides employer-assisted housing for associates in Inverness, offering subsidized rooms and shared apartments in company-managed accommodations near the resort. By directly co-funding and master-leasing local rentals, the employer secures units and effectively guarantees rent on behalf of employees. This reduces housing barriers for seasonal and year-round staff in a tight rural market, aligning with local employer-assisted housing partnerships.

resources.name: Fox Harb'r Resort Team Member Housing
resources.description: Fox Harb'r Resort operates on-site and nearby team member housing, providing furnished, subsidized accommodations to seasonal and permanent staff. The resort invests in and manages these units, functioning as a rent guarantor and co-funder to expand access to safe, proximate housing for employees. This employer-backed model supports recruitment and retention in a rural area with limited rental supply.
resources.address: 1337 Fox Harbour Road, Wallace, NS B0K 1Y0

resources.name: White Point Beach Resort Staff Accommodation
resources.description: White Point Beach Resort offers employer-arranged staff accommodations within walking distance of the property for seasonal and year-round roles. The resort co-funds and manages dorm-style and shared rental units, lowering upfront housing barriers and providing predictable costs for employees. By securing and stewarding units, White Point acts as an employer-assisted housing partner in a community with constrained rental options.
resources.address: 75 White Point Beach Resort Road, White Point, NS B0T 1G0

solutions.text: Shared‑Equity Homeownership Programs: Set up community-run shared‑equity schemes where a nonprofit or municipality takes an equity stake to lower purchase prices for first‑time buyers while preserving long‑term affordability.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership (Shared-Equity Model)
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia builds and sells homes to qualified first-time buyers and lowers the entry price by providing an affordability subsidy structured as a shared‑equity/second mortgage. The organization retains an equity interest or uses a shared‑appreciation covenant so that, upon resale, a portion of appreciation is returned to Habitat or the home can be repurchased, preserving long‑term affordability for the next buyer. This model reduces upfront costs and monthly payments for young families and newcomers while keeping homes affordable over time.

resources.name: Kjipuktuk (Halifax) Community Land Trust
resources.organization: Affordable Housing Association of Nova Scotia (AHANS)
resources.description: The Kjipuktuk Community Land Trust, supported by the Affordable Housing Association of Nova Scotia, acquires and stewards land so that households can purchase homes at reduced prices while the trust retains ownership of the land via long‑term ground leases. This community land trust structure is a proven shared‑equity model: it lowers the purchase price for first‑time buyers and uses resale formulas to keep homes permanently affordable, ensuring the subsidy benefits multiple generations of local residents.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 309, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Neighbourhood Zoning Advocacy Coalitions: Form community groups to work with councils on faster approvals, gentle density zoning (laneway housing, duplexes), and reducing red tape—preparing model policy proposals and grassroots outreach.

resources.name: Our HRM Alliance
resources.description: Our HRM Alliance is a coalition of community groups convened by the Ecology Action Centre that advocates for compact, complete communities across Halifax. The alliance works directly with HRM Council and planning staff during Regional Plan/Centre Plan processes to legalize gentle density (e.g., secondary suites, backyard/laneway suites, duplexes) and streamline as-of-right approvals. It prepares joint policy submissions, develops model bylaw language and outreach toolkits, and mobilizes residents to speak at hearings and contact councillors to reduce red tape and speed approvals.

resources.name: Downtown Dartmouth Planning & Housing Advocacy
resources.description: The Downtown Dartmouth Business Commission (DDBC) collaborates with HRM Council and planning staff on Centre Plan and bylaw amendments to support mixed-use growth and gentle density in established neighbourhoods. DDBC submits policy letters and recommendations that call for faster approvals, as-of-right infill, and reduced red tape, including support for secondary suites, backyard suites, and duplex conversions. It also hosts public forums, walking tours, and member outreach to build grassroots support for zoning reforms that add housing while strengthening main streets.

resources.name: Policy & Red Tape Reduction for Housing
resources.description: The Halifax Chamber of Commerce runs an active policy program that advocates for permitting reform and zoning changes to increase housing supply. Through policy papers, deputations to HRM Council and the Province, and its Red Tape Reduction initiative, the Chamber champions faster, predictable approvals and bylaw amendments to enable gentle density such as secondary and backyard/laneway suites and small-scale infill. It convenes industry and community stakeholders, shares model policy recommendations, and organizes outreach to build broad support for streamlining development rules.

resources.name: CBRM Forward (Municipal Planning Strategy & Land-Use By-law Review)
resources.description: CBRM Forward is Cape Breton Regional Municipality’s multi-year review of its planning strategy and land-use by-laws, built on extensive neighbourhood engagement. The initiative proposes bylaw changes to allow accessory dwelling units, duplexes, and context-sensitive infill, and to expand as-of-right approvals that speed up housing delivery and cut red tape. It equips resident groups and local organizations with draft policies, open houses, and feedback tools to co-develop practical zoning solutions with Council and staff.

solutions.text: Local Short‑Term Rental Management and Regulation: Develop community-led regulations and registries for short‑term rentals to protect long‑term housing stock; offer pathways for hosts to convert to longer leases with incentives.

resources.name: Short-Term Rentals (STR) Licensing and Land-Use Rules
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality regulates short-term rentals through a licensing program and land-use bylaw amendments that generally limit whole-home STRs in residential areas to a host’s primary residence, require registration numbers on listings, and enable municipal enforcement. These community-led rules protect long-term rental supply by curbing commercial STRs in neighbourhoods, and HRM provides guidance to owners on transitioning units into compliant long-term rentals, including pointing to landlord registration and tenant-matching resources. Together, the licensing and zoning framework create a clear pathway for operators to move from short stays to stable leases.

resources.name: Tourist Accommodations Registration (Short-Term Rental Registry)
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia — Service Nova Scotia
resources.description: Nova Scotia’s provincewide registry requires all short-term and tourist accommodation operators to register annually and display a registration number on listings, creating a centralized, enforceable record of STR activity. The registry supports municipalities in managing and enforcing local bylaws to protect long-term housing stock by identifying unlicensed or non-compliant STRs. It also provides clear compliance guidance and links to residential tenancies information so hosts can convert units to longer-term leases when they choose.

resources.name: Short-Term Rental Accommodation Program (Licensing and Zoning Limits)
resources.description: The Town of Lunenburg licenses short-term rentals and restricts whole-home STRs to specific zones and conditions, prioritizing primary residences and maintaining a local registry for compliance. By limiting commercial-style STRs in residential areas, the program protects the town’s long-term rental supply and neighbourhood character. Staff provide guidance to property owners on bringing units into compliance or transitioning them into longer-term leases aligned with local housing needs.

resources.name: Off-Campus Living (Landlord and Listing Support)
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Off-Campus Living program offers landlords free listings, tenant-matching support, and guidance on 8–12 month leases, creating a practical pathway for STR hosts to shift to stable, longer-term student rentals. The program reduces vacancy risk and administrative burden by connecting owners with a steady pool of renters and providing resources on leases, standards, and dispute prevention. These supports act as non-monetary incentives that make conversion from short stays to long-term housing more attractive.

solutions.text: Community Housing Trust Fund: Build a locally governed revolving fund financed by donations, business contributions, and municipal seed money to buy, rehab, or guarantee affordable housing projects.

resources.name: Community Housing Growth Fund (Nova Scotia)
resources.organization: Affordable Housing Association of Nova Scotia
resources.description: Administered by a Nova Scotia-based non-profit, this fund provides pre-development, acquisition, repair/rehab, and development financing to community housing providers. By combining provincial seed funding with locally governed decision-making and offering a mix of grants and repayable loans, it functions like a community housing trust fund—helping non-profits buy or rehabilitate properties while loan repayments revolve back into future affordable housing projects.
resources.address: 2625 Joseph Howe Drive, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3L 4G4

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: New Dawn raises RRSP-eligible community investment capital from local residents and businesses to finance community development projects, including acquisition, rehabilitation, and development of housing and mixed-use properties in Cape Breton. The capital is locally governed and repaid over time, allowing funds to revolve into subsequent projects—directly mirroring a community housing trust fund model that mobilizes private and philanthropic dollars for long-term affordable housing solutions.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia – Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat NS builds and sometimes rehabilitates homes for qualifying families using donated funds, business contributions, and in-kind municipal support (such as land or fee relief). Homeowners pay an affordable, no- or low-interest mortgage to Habitat, and those repayments revolve back into the fund to build additional homes—operating as a locally governed revolving housing fund that expands affordable homeownership supply over time.

resources.name: Halifax Affordable Housing Grant Program
resources.description: This municipally seeded fund supports non-profits, co-operatives, and community groups to acquire, rehabilitate, or develop affordable housing in HRM, often leveraging private and philanthropic contributions. Governed locally by the municipality, the program acts as a catalyst fund—bridging financing gaps in land servicing, renovation, and project readiness so community-led affordable housing projects can proceed.

solutions.text: Tenant Support, Mediation and Education Hubs: Create local hubs offering renters’ rights education, dispute mediation, and move‑in/move‑out assistance to reduce evictions and maintain housing stability for vulnerable residents.

resources.name: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service – Tenancy Law and Housing Support
resources.organization: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service (Schulich School of Law, Dalhousie University)
resources.description: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service provides tenants’ rights education, summary legal advice, and representation for low‑income tenants in Residential Tenancies disputes. Staff and law students deliver public legal education workshops, help renters prepare for move‑in/move‑out (e.g., condition reports, security deposits), and mediate or advocate in landlord‑tenant issues to prevent evictions and improve housing stability.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Residential Tenancies Program
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia – Service Nova Scotia
resources.description: This provincial program educates tenants and landlords about their rights and responsibilities and provides standardized forms, guides, and resources to support fair tenancies. It offers dispute resolution (including mediation by a Residential Tenancies Officer and hearings) to address issues like repairs, rent, and security deposits—reducing evictions and helping maintain stable housing across the province.
resources.address: 300 Horseshoe Lake Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 0B7

resources.name: YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs – Housing & Settlement Support
resources.description: The YMCA supports newcomers with tenant‑rights orientation, workshops on leases and repairs, and one‑on‑one coaching to navigate Nova Scotia’s rental system. Settlement staff help mediate misunderstandings with landlords, assist with lease signings and move‑in checklists, and connect clients to community resources to prevent evictions and build housing stability.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Open Arms – Housing Support Program
resources.description: Open Arms provides housing navigation, tenant education, and practical move‑in assistance (e.g., liaising with landlords, securing essentials) for individuals and families in the Annapolis Valley. Housing Support Workers offer coaching on renters’ rights and responsibilities and mediate landlord‑tenant issues to prevent evictions and sustain tenancies.

resources.name: Truro Homeless Outreach Society (Hub House) – Housing Outreach & Tenancy Support
resources.description: THOS provides tenant‑focused outreach that includes renters’ rights education, help completing Residential Tenancies forms, and guidance through dispute processes. Staff work with clients and landlords to resolve conflicts, negotiate payment plans, and support move‑in/move‑out logistics—reducing evictions and improving housing stability in Colchester County.

solutions.text: Downsizing Incentives for Seniors: Coordinate community programs that help seniors downsize—providing packing assistance, home modification for safe transitions, and matching smaller units with families—freeing family‑sized homes.

resources.name: ReStore Donation Pickup (Downsizing Support)
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia’s ReStore offers free pickup of furniture, appliances, and household goods that seniors no longer need when decluttering and downsizing. By removing the cost and logistics of clearing out large items, the service helps seniors transition more quickly and safely into smaller homes or apartments; donated goods are resold to fund affordable housing, indirectly increasing supply for families.

resources.name: Home Care and Transition Support
resources.description: Northwood’s Home Care team provides in‑home support, light housekeeping, and personal assistance, and their care coordinators help older adults plan and manage transitions, including organizing, packing, and connecting with vetted moving services when downsizing to apartments or supportive housing. By smoothing the move from family homes to smaller, safer units—and ensuring needed safety equipment and modifications are in place at the new residence—Northwood helps free up larger homes for families while keeping seniors supported.

resources.name: Senior Supports and Navigation
resources.description: The Dartmouth Seniors Service Centre coordinates practical supports that help older adults downsize and relocate, including referrals to trusted movers, cleaners, and organizers, assisted transportation, and help completing housing applications and transition paperwork. By organizing community-based assistance for packing, decluttering, and safe move planning, the Centre reduces barriers for seniors moving to smaller, more suitable homes—freeing up family‑sized housing in the community.

solutions.text: Housing‑Trades Training and Build Days: Partner community colleges and trades programs to run supervised build days where students gain experience constructing affordable units, while the community supplies sites and materials.

resources.name: Team Build Days
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia organizes supervised build days on active affordable home sites where volunteers, students, and apprentices work alongside certified tradespeople. They frequently partner with local colleges and trades programs so students gain hands-on construction experience while Habitat and community partners provide the build site, materials, and project management—directly aligning with student training build days that deliver new affordable units.

resources.name: NSCC Carpentry Community Build Projects
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College integrates real-world construction projects into its carpentry and trades curricula, where students complete supervised builds for community partners such as Habitat for Humanity and local housing/shelter organizations. These projects function as structured build days and multi-week practicum sites—students construct components or complete tiny homes/units under instructor supervision while community partners provide sites and materials, resulting in additional affordable or supportive housing stock.

obstacles.title: Wage and Career Competitiveness
obstacles.description: Average wages and benefits often lag larger provinces, with higher rates of precarious or seasonal work, making it harder to retain talent.

solutions.text: Local Living Wage Campaign: Community-led advocacy to encourage municipalities, local institutions and larger employers to adopt a living wage policy; includes public education, employer toolkits, and phased implementation plans to raise average wages.

resources.name: United Way Halifax Living Wage Advocacy
resources.description: United Way Halifax advances a living wage in the region by conducting and sharing local living-wage research with community partners, educating the public and employers, and convening roundtables that encourage major institutions and businesses to adopt living wage policies. They provide guidance and resources to employers on how to phase in living wage practices (e.g., through procurement standards and contracted services), helping raise average wages and reduce precarious work across the municipality.
resources.address: 46 Portland Street, Suite 100, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 1H3

resources.name: HRM Living Wage Requirement for Service Contracts
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality has adopted a living wage requirement for many externally contracted services, embedding living wage standards into municipal procurement to ensure contracted workers are paid at or above the local living wage. The municipality informs vendors and community partners about the policy and its phased implementation, using procurement guidelines and education to encourage wider employer adoption and lift overall wage floors across the region.

solutions.text: Small-Business Benefits Consortium: A cooperative of local small businesses that pools resources to offer affordable group health, dental and retirement options, negotiated with insurers to lower per-employee costs and make jobs more competitive.

resources.name: Chambers of Commerce Group Insurance Plan (Chambers Plan) — via Halifax Chamber of Commerce
resources.description: The Halifax Chamber of Commerce provides access to the Chambers of Commerce Group Insurance Plan (Chambers Plan), a pooled benefits program designed for small and mid-sized employers. By aggregating employees from thousands of participating member businesses, the plan spreads risk and negotiates group rates for health, dental, life, disability, employee assistance, and group retirement savings options. This collective purchasing power lowers per-employee costs and helps small firms in HRM compete with larger employers on total compensation.

resources.name: CANS Group Benefits Program
resources.description: The Construction Association of Nova Scotia (CANS) offers a pooled group benefits program that enables member firms—many of them small and medium-sized contractors—to access health, dental, life, and disability coverage, with optional retirement savings solutions. Leveraging the association’s scale, CANS negotiates competitive premiums and plan features through industry benefit partners, giving smaller employers access to benefits typically reserved for larger organizations. This consortium model reduces per-employee costs and strengthens members’ ability to recruit and retain skilled workers.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: CFIB Member Benefits (Health, Dental & Retirement Plans) — Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Canadian Federation of Independent Business (CFIB) connects Nova Scotia member SMEs to pooled group health, dental, life/disability, and retirement solutions arranged through CFIB’s national benefits partners. By bundling thousands of independent employers, CFIB spreads risk and secures group pricing and plan designs that individual small firms could not obtain on their own. These benefits help local businesses enhance total compensation and improve talent attraction and retention.

solutions.text: Seasonal-to-Year-Round Transition Program: Community initiative helping seasonal employers diversify services, cross-train staff and partner with complementary businesses so workers can move between roles and maintain year-round income.

resources.name: Workplace Innovation and Productivity Skills Incentive (WIPSI)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: WIPSI provides cost-shared funding to Nova Scotia employers to train and upskill their workforce, enabling seasonal businesses to cross-train staff in new roles (e.g., digital marketing, operations, quality, and trade skills) and diversify services beyond peak seasons. Employers can also collaborate with training providers and partner firms to design customized, multi-skill training so workers can shift between complementary roles across businesses, helping maintain year-round employment and income.

resources.name: Perennia Food & Beverage – Product Development and Food Safety Training
resources.description: Perennia helps seasonal producers and processors develop value-added food and beverage products and adopt year-round processing practices, reducing reliance on short harvest windows. Through product development support, HACCP/food safety training, and connections to pilot-processing resources and co-packers, Perennia enables employers to diversify services and cross-train seasonal staff for roles in processing, quality, and packaging, creating pathways to steady, year-round work.
resources.address: 199 Dr. Bernie MacDonald Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2H5

resources.name: NSCC Customized Training for Employers
resources.description: NSCC partners with groups of employers—especially in tourism, aquaculture, and trades—to design short, targeted training that equips seasonal workers with multiple, stackable skills (e.g., hospitality-to-culinary, maintenance-to-electrical fundamentals, digital operations). By coordinating cohorts across complementary businesses and communities, NSCC helps employers share talent and move workers between roles across the shoulder and off-seasons, supporting transitions to year-round income.

resources.name: Aquaculture Workforce Development & Training
resources.description: The Aquaculture Association of Nova Scotia coordinates industry-led training and certifications that allow seasonal farm staff to move into hatchery, processing, maintenance, or logistics roles during off-peak periods. By facilitating partnerships among farms, hatcheries, and processors and supporting cross-training (e.g., equipment operation, food safety, and quality), the program helps create multi-skilled teams and shared staffing models that stabilize year-round employment in coastal communities.
resources.address: 11 Thornhill Drive, Unit 110, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1R9

solutions.text: Community Apprenticeship & Co-op Network: A locally coordinated platform that connects young people with apprenticeships, co-op placements and paid internships across trades, arts and tech, supported by mentorship and employer matching.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency administers apprenticeship training across the province, registering apprentices and employer sponsors and coordinating on-the-job learning with technical training. It implements the solution by matching young people with paid apprenticeship placements in skilled trades, ensuring mentorship by certified journeypersons, and providing supports and incentives that help employers hire and retain apprentices.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency; Construction Association of Nova Scotia; Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: Building Futures for Youth places Nova Scotia high school students in paid summer jobs with construction employers, where they gain hands-on experience and mentorship from skilled journeypersons. The program implements the solution by coordinating employer matching, paid placements and pathways to apprenticeship hours, helping youth explore skilled trades and transition into long-term careers.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

resources.name: NSCC Co-operative Education & Work-Integrated Learning
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College connects students in trades, technology, and creative programs with co-op, internships, and applied projects through employer partnerships across the province. It advances the solution by coordinating employer matching for paid work terms, embedding mentorship and career coaching, and fostering industry-ready skills that improve wage and career outcomes.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Management Career Services (Co-op)
resources.organization: Rowe School of Business, Dalhousie University
resources.description: Management Career Services at Dalhousie’s Rowe School of Business coordinates paid co-op and internship placements in business, analytics, and technology-related roles with a large employer network. The program implements the solution by providing employer matching, job development, and mentorship/coaching to support students’ transition into high-quality work in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Youth Entrepreneurship Microgrants and Incubator: Local microgrant fund plus low-cost incubator space and mentorship to help young founders launch ventures, covering startup costs, business training and connections to local supply chains.

resources.name: Volta
resources.description: Volta is Atlantic Canada’s largest innovation hub, providing low-cost co-working and residency space, mentorship, and founder training to help early-stage (often youth-led) startups launch and grow. Through its Volta Cohort program, it awards $25,000 in non-dilutive funding to selected founders, functioning as a microgrant to offset startup costs while pairing teams with experienced advisors. Volta also connects companies to local supply chains and customers through corporate partnerships, community events, and investor networks.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic
resources.description: IGNITE operates rural innovation hubs that provide free or low-cost workspace, maker labs, and structured mentorship to help youth and community founders turn ideas into businesses. It partners with Invest Nova Scotia’s Spark Nova Scotia competition to bring non-dilutive microgrant funding to early-stage founders in Western and Northern Nova Scotia, covering initial startup and prototyping costs. IGNITE’s industry partnerships and programming connect young entrepreneurs to local suppliers and customers across sectors like oceans, energy, and agriculture.

resources.name: Dal Innovates
resources.description: Dal Innovates is Dalhousie University’s venture-building platform offering student and recent graduate founders access to incubation space, mentorship, and experiential training. Its Ready2Launch program provides non-dilutive seed funding (e.g., team stipends/microgrants) alongside intensive coaching to help youth-led startups validate markets and build initial products. Participants work from the Emera IDEA Building and are connected to local research labs, industry partners, and regional startup supports to integrate into Nova Scotia’s supply chains.

resources.name: Ocean Startup Project
resources.organization: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship) in partnership with regional organizations
resources.description: The Ocean Startup Project is a pan-Atlantic initiative headquartered at COVE that accelerates ocean-tech founders with non-dilutive microgrant funding through programs like the Ocean Startup Challenge (seed awards) and Discovery programs (stipends), plus structured mentorship. Startups gain access to workspace, testing infrastructure, and peer networks at COVE’s incubator, helping teams reduce early costs and accelerate commercialization. The program connects young founders to Nova Scotia’s ocean economy supply chains in sectors such as shipbuilding, fisheries, aquaculture, and offshore energy.

solutions.text: Shared Workspaces and Maker Spaces: Community-run co-working and maker facilities that lower overhead for freelancers and small teams, providing equipment, workshops and networking to make independent careers viable.

resources.name: Volta
resources.description: Volta is a community-run innovation hub that provides co-working desks, private offices, meeting rooms, and shared amenities for startups, freelancers, and small teams. It lowers overhead by bundling workspace and infrastructure with mentorship, workshops, and networking events, helping independent careers and early-stage companies gain traction in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: COVE is an ocean-technology hub offering shared offices, labs, prototyping facilities, and waterfront testing infrastructure to startups and small teams. By providing specialized equipment, programming, and frequent industry networking events, it reduces capital costs for entrepreneurs and enables sustainable, independent careers in Nova Scotia’s blue economy.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: The Lou Duggan Creative Studio is a public makerspace offering access to equipment like sewing machines, vinyl cutters, and multimedia tools, along with free and low-cost workshops. Operated by Halifax Public Libraries, it provides community-accessible space and skills training that reduce barriers for creatives, freelancers, and small ventures to prototype, learn, and connect.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: The Lunenburg Makery
resources.description: The Lunenburg Makery is a community makerspace and studio that provides shared equipment for textiles, craft, and design, along with classes, workshops, and studio time. By offering affordable access to tools, space, and a peer network, it lowers overhead for independent artisans and creative entrepreneurs looking to build viable careers in the region.

solutions.text: Community Land Trusts & Affordable Housing Initiatives: Locally governed housing projects that remove speculative pressure, offering affordable rental and rent-to-own options so younger workers can live near jobs without unsustainable housing costs.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia – Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia builds and sells homes to qualifying low- and moderate-income households using affordable, geared-to-income mortgages and shared-equity models that function similarly to rent-to-own. By placing resale restrictions and affordability covenants on homes, Habitat removes speculative pressure and preserves long-term affordability, enabling younger workers and families to live near employment across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Housing
resources.description: New Dawn Community Housing develops, owns, and manages affordable rental units in Cape Breton, providing below-market and rent-geared-to-income options for individuals and families. As a locally governed, community-based non-profit, New Dawn keeps its properties permanently outside the speculative market, stabilizing rents and enabling working-age residents to live near jobs and services in the Sydney area.

resources.name: YWCA Halifax – Affordable and Supportive Housing
resources.description: YWCA Halifax develops and operates affordable and supportive housing for women, gender-diverse people, and families, including programs that provide below-market rents and on-site supports. As a community-governed non-profit landlord, YWCA Halifax holds housing in the non-market sector, reducing speculative pressures and helping young workers and parents secure stable homes near transit, services, and employment.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

solutions.text: Childcare Cooperatives and Employer-Supported Childcare: Community-operated childcare co-ops and employer-supported programs to reduce childcare costs and increase workforce participation among parents, making local jobs more accessible.

resources.name: Peter Green Hall Children’s Centre
resources.organization: Peter Green Hall Child Care Society
resources.description: Peter Green Hall is a parent-run, non-profit child care co-operative that offers full-day early learning and care. Families participate in governance and operations to help keep fees affordable, directly aligning with the childcare co-op model that reduces costs and supports parents’ ability to work or study in Halifax’s urban core.

resources.name: MSVU Child Study Centre
resources.description: The on-campus Child Study Centre provides early learning and childcare with priority access for Mount Saint Vincent University students, faculty, and staff, functioning as an employer-supported model that makes work and study more feasible for parents. By situating childcare at the workplace and integrating with the university’s Child and Youth Study program, it helps reduce commuting and scheduling barriers while maintaining quality, research-informed care.

resources.name: Halifax Playschool Co-operative
resources.description: Halifax Playschool is a parent co-operative preschool where families share in administration and volunteer duties to keep program costs lower. This community-operated model provides accessible early learning that supports parents who are working, studying, or transitioning back to the workforce by offering reliable, affordable care hours.

resources.name: Port Wallis Co-operative Nursery School
resources.organization: Port Wallis Co-operative Nursery School Society
resources.description: Port Wallis is a non-profit, parent-run nursery school that reduces costs through cooperative governance and family participation. By offering affordable, community-based early learning in Dartmouth, it helps parents balance employment or training with childcare, increasing their ability to participate in the local workforce.

solutions.text: Local Hiring Pledge & 'Hire Local' Campaign: A public commitment program where businesses pledge to prioritize local hiring and provide clear career pathways and wages; the campaign elevates participating employers and encourages consumer support.

resources.name: Game Changers Youth Retention Initiative
resources.description: Game Changers mobilizes Halifax-area employers to publicly commit to hiring and retaining local youth and recent graduates through co-ops, internships, apprenticeships, and entry-level careers. Employers sign a visible commitment and are promoted through events, media, and partner channels, encouraging community and consumer support for businesses investing in local talent and offering clear career pathways and wages.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Hire Me Cape Breton
resources.description: Hire Me Cape Breton is a public campaign that showcases local talent and invites employers to commit to interviewing and hiring Cape Breton residents, especially students and young professionals. Participating employers are profiled and promoted, signalling their pledge to hire locally and to offer meaningful roles with clear pathways, which strengthens retention and encourages community members to support these businesses.

resources.name: Living Wage Employer Certification (Atlantic Living Wage Network – Nova Scotia)
resources.organization: United Way Halifax (Atlantic Living Wage Network – Nova Scotia)
resources.description: This certification invites Nova Scotia employers to publicly commit to paying at least the local living wage and to transparent wage policies, directly addressing wage competitiveness and job quality. Certified employers are listed and promoted, helping consumers identify and support organizations that provide quality local jobs and clear pay pathways, and encouraging more businesses to follow suit.
resources.address: 7001 Mumford Road, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3L 2H8

resources.name: Game Changers: Youth Retention Action Plan
resources.organization: Halifax Partnership and Halifax Chamber of Commerce
resources.description: Game Changers is a public commitment and awareness campaign that calls on employers to pledge to hire and retain young talent locally, create quality entry-level roles, and outline clear career pathways and wages. The initiative elevates participating employers through recognition, events (e.g., Hire Me Halifax), and storytelling that encourages peers and the community to support businesses investing in local youth and recent graduates—directly addressing wage and career competitiveness and talent retention in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Hire Me Cape Breton
resources.description: Hire Me Cape Breton is a region-wide campaign and talent platform that invites employers to commit to hiring locally by connecting with a public pool of Cape Breton candidates (students, graduates, and returnees) and posting quality jobs with clear growth paths. The campaign spotlights participating employers across media and community channels, building their reputation as local hirers and encouraging community support while reducing reliance on seasonal and precarious work.

resources.name: Employer Support Services (Inclusive Hiring & Employer Recognition)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Employer Support Services help Nova Scotia businesses publicly commit to inclusive, local hiring by recruiting from newcomer and graduate talent pools, adopting fair recruitment and wage practices, and building clear onboarding and advancement pathways. Through employer spotlights, hiring events, and partnerships (e.g., Connector activities), ISANS elevates participating employers and encourages community support for businesses that prioritize local talent and quality jobs.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Game Changers: Youth Retention Action Plan
resources.description: Game Changers mobilizes Halifax employers to publicly commit to hiring and advancing local students and recent graduates through co-ops, internships, and entry-level roles, building clear career pathways in Nova Scotia. Participating employers are profiled and promoted through the campaign, encouraging community and consumer recognition for businesses that prioritize local hiring and quality jobs, helping address wage and career competitiveness.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Living Wage Employer Program – Halifax
resources.description: This certification program recognizes employers that publicly commit to paying at least the local living wage and to transparent compensation practices, improving wage competitiveness for workers in Halifax. Certified employers are listed and promoted, providing visible recognition that encourages residents and purchasers to support them, and signaling clear wage and career commitments that help attract and retain young talent.
resources.address: 46 Portland Street, 7th Floor, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 1H4

resources.name: Hire Me Cape Breton
resources.description: Hire Me Cape Breton is a public-facing campaign that showcases local job seekers and elevates employers who commit to recruiting locally and creating progression opportunities within their organizations. By featuring participating employers across digital channels and events, it encourages community and consumer support for businesses prioritizing local hiring and helps address retention challenges by connecting Cape Bretoners to quality jobs close to home.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

solutions.text: Skills Partnerships with Colleges and Training Providers: Collaborative local training programs co-designed by community, employers and colleges to provide in-demand certificates, short courses and stacking credentials tailored to regional industry needs.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding Inc. and community partners
resources.description: A collaborative training pathway co-designed by Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC), Irving Shipbuilding, and community partners to prepare underrepresented Nova Scotians for shipbuilding trades. Participants complete tailored pre-apprenticeship and trade training (e.g., welding/metal fabrication) at NSCC with industry-informed curriculum, paid work terms at Halifax Shipyard, and clear progression into Red Seal apprenticeships. This delivers in-demand, stackable credentials linked directly to local employer needs, improving career prospects and wages.

resources.name: NSCC Microcredentials and Customized Training
resources.description: NSCC partners with employers, sector councils, and communities across Nova Scotia to co-design short courses, microcredentials, and customized training aligned to regional labour market needs. These stackable credentials provide targeted upskilling and pathways into certificates, diplomas, and apprenticeships, improving job readiness and advancement in key sectors. Programs are delivered locally at NSCC campuses and online, helping young people access in-demand skills that support higher-wage, stable careers.

resources.name: Skills for Hire Atlantic
resources.description: An employer-informed, cohort-based digital skills program developed by Digital Nova Scotia with industry partners to address immediate hiring needs in fields like web development, cybersecurity, and data. The curriculum is co-designed with tech employers and delivered with training providers to issue microcredentials and job-readiness supports, creating pathways into higher-wage tech roles in Nova Scotia. Graduates gain stackable, industry-recognized credentials that align directly with local demand.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Ocean Technology Advanced Diploma (delivered with COVE industry partners)
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship (COVE) in partnership with Nova Scotia Community College
resources.description: A specialized NSCC program built with input from ocean-technology employers and delivered in collaboration with the Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship (COVE). Learners gain stackable, industry-aligned competencies in areas such as marine instrumentation, ocean data, and field operations, with access to COVE’s industry testbeds and employer networks for work-integrated learning. The partnership ensures training directly matches regional ocean-sector needs, supporting strong local career pathways.

solutions.text: Mentorship and Career Pathways Program: A community-run mentorship network linking students and early-career workers with local professionals for guidance, job-shadowing, and structured career maps that show routes to higher wages.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program links students, recent graduates, newcomers, and early-career professionals with established local ‘Connectors’ for one-on-one career conversations and warm introductions to their networks. Participants receive guidance on local hiring practices, role expectations, and wage trajectories, and are often referred to informational interviews and short job-shadow opportunities. This structured networking model creates clear career pathways into higher-quality, higher-wage roles in Halifax’s key sectors.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
