resources.description: ISANS pairs internationally trained and early-career professionals with mentors working in their field in Nova Scotia for several months of guided coaching and career navigation. Mentees gain Canadian workplace insights, expand professional networks, and receive tailored steps toward licensure, skills upgrading, and higher-wage job readiness, with optional workplace visits or job-shadowing when available. The program provides a structured pathway that turns mentorship into concrete career outcomes.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: VANS Mentorship Program
resources.description: Visual Arts Nova Scotia’s Mentorship Program matches emerging artists with established professional artists for a multi-month, goal-focused mentorship. Participants build portfolios, learn business practices (pricing, contracts, grants), and map step-by-step pathways to sustainable incomes in the arts, often including studio visits and shadowing of professional workflows. The program connects early-career creatives with local professionals to translate mentorship into viable, higher-earning career routes.

resources.name: Mentoring and Growth Programs
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business, Mount Saint Vincent University
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business provides structured mentoring circles and one-to-one matches that connect women entrepreneurs and early-stage founders with experienced business leaders across Nova Scotia. Programming includes business planning, sales and export readiness, and growth roadmaps that outline steps to scale revenue and improve wages for founders and their teams. Through ongoing mentor guidance and targeted workshops, participants access clear career and business pathways tied to higher earnings.

resources.name: Mentor Connect
resources.description: SMU’s Entrepreneurship Centre connects students and early-career innovators with local business mentors for structured mentoring, goal setting, and introductions to the Halifax business community. Participants develop actionable career and venture roadmaps, receive guidance on skill gaps and wage growth pathways, and are connected to experiential learning and occasional shadowing opportunities with local firms. The program helps translate mentorship into tangible steps toward higher-quality employment and entrepreneurship.

solutions.text: Social Enterprises and Worker Co-ops: Support for community-based social enterprises and worker-owned cooperatives that prioritize stable, fair-paying jobs in sectors like food, tourism, craft and services, reinvesting profits locally.

resources.name: Just Us! Coffee Roasters Co-op
resources.description: A worker-owned cooperative that roasts and sells Fair Trade coffee and operates a café in Grand Pré. It creates stable, fair-paying jobs in the food and service sector and shares ownership and profits with workers, reinvesting earnings into local operations and community initiatives to strengthen rural employment.

resources.name: LakeCity Works
resources.description: A non-profit social enterprise that designs and manufactures wood furniture and custom projects while employing people living with mental illness. It offers paid employment, skills training, and benefits in the craft/manufacturing sector, and reinvests revenues to expand supports and create more inclusive, stable jobs locally.

resources.name: New Dawn Enterprises
resources.description: A community development corporation in Cape Breton that operates multiple social businesses, including home care, meals, real estate, and an arts centre. It provides stable, fair-paying jobs in care, food, and services while reinvesting surpluses into local entrepreneurship, housing, and cultural infrastructure to retain and attract talent.

resources.name: Wolfville Farmers' Market
resources.description: A community-owned cooperative market that hosts local food, craft, and service vendors year-round and operates the WFM2Go online market and distribution service. It sustains livelihoods for small producers, creates local logistics and market management jobs, and reinvests surpluses into vendor development, youth opportunities, and community food programs.

resources.name: DASC Works (Social Enterprise of Dartmouth Adult Services Centre)
resources.description: A social enterprise that provides contract assembly, packaging, fulfillment, confidential shredding, and wood products while employing adults with intellectual disabilities. It delivers paid, supported employment and skills development in services and light manufacturing, reinvesting earned revenues into wages, training, and the creation of more inclusive local jobs.

solutions.text: Seasonal Worker Stabilization Fund: A local fund that provides income smoothing or short-term top-ups during off-season periods, funded by municipal seed money, business contributions and community donations, to reduce precarity.

resources.name: Home Energy Assistance Top-up (HEAT) Fund
resources.description: The HEAT Fund provides one-time financial assistance to help low-income households cover home heating costs during the winter, a period when many Nova Scotians working in seasonal industries face reduced income. Administered by The Salvation Army and funded by Nova Scotia Power, the Province of Nova Scotia, and community donations, the program effectively acts as a short-term top-up that stabilizes household finances in the off-season and reduces precarity.

resources.name: Heating Assistance Rebate Program (HARP)
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia (Service Nova Scotia)
resources.description: HARP offers an annual rebate to eligible low- and moderate-income Nova Scotians to offset winter heating costs, smoothing expenses when household earnings often dip due to seasonal work slowdowns. By injecting a predictable, time-limited cash benefit during the cold season, the program functions as a targeted top-up that reduces financial strain and helps stabilize budgets between peak work periods.

resources.name: Employment Insurance (EI) Fishing Benefits
resources.organization: Service Canada / Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC)
resources.description: EI Fishing Benefits provide income support to self-employed fishers during periods when they cannot fish, offering a structured benefit based on earnings that bridges off-season income gaps. Operating across Nova Scotia’s coastal communities, this program directly smooths income between seasons, reducing precarity for workers in one of the province’s most seasonal industries.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Supplemental Unemployment Benefit (SUB) Program
resources.organization: Service Canada / Employment and Social Development Canada (ESDC)
resources.description: The SUB Program allows Nova Scotia employers and unions to register plans that top up employees’ EI benefits during temporary layoffs or seasonal shutdowns without reducing EI entitlement. In practice, these employer- or union-funded top-ups stabilize workers’ income in the off-season, aligning directly with an income-smoothing approach that reduces financial precarity.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Job-Sharing and Flexible Work Initiatives: Promotion of job-sharing models, part-time portability and compressed workweeks among local employers to retain skilled workers seeking flexibility while maintaining earnings and benefits.

resources.name: NSTU Job Share Arrangements
resources.description: Through collective agreements with regional centres for education, the Nova Scotia Teachers Union enables job-sharing arrangements where two qualified educators split one full‑time assignment while maintaining pro‑rated salary, pension, and benefits. NSTU provides guidance and templates to help employers and members set up job shares and flexible schedules, supporting retention of skilled teachers who need reduced or flexible hours without sacrificing career progression.
resources.address: 3106 Joseph Howe Drive, Halifax, NS B3L 4L7

resources.name: Flexible Work Program
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Flexible Work Program allows eligible employee groups to participate in alternate work arrangements, including job sharing, compressed workweeks (e.g., 9‑day fortnights), and flexible start/finish times. HR policies and manager toolkits support structuring these arrangements so employees can maintain earnings and benefits while adapting hours, helping the university attract and retain talent in Nova Scotia’s competitive labour market.

resources.name: NSGEU Collective Agreements – Flexible Work Provisions
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Government and General Employees Union (NSGEU)
resources.description: NSGEU negotiates and supports implementation of flexible work provisions across Nova Scotia’s public sector, including compressed workweeks (earned day off/9‑day fortnight), job‑sharing options, and pro‑rated benefits portability for part‑time employees. The union assists employers and members with setting up, monitoring, and troubleshooting these arrangements, enabling workers to maintain earnings and benefits while adjusting hours, which improves retention in hard‑to‑staff roles.
resources.address: 255 John Savage Avenue, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0J3

resources.name: Employer Support Services (Inclusive & Flexible Work Practices)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS advises Nova Scotia employers on inclusive HR strategies that include creating job‑share roles, offering part‑time positions with benefits, and implementing flexible or compressed schedules to attract and retain immigrant talent. Through workshops, one‑to‑one consulting, and practical toolkits, ISANS helps organizations redesign jobs and policies to embed flexibility while maintaining productivity and employee benefits.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Transportation and Commuter Solutions: Community transport cooperatives, subsidized transit passes or ride-share programs that expand access to higher-paying jobs across the region and reduce commuting barriers for workers.

resources.name: Low Income Transit Pass Program
resources.description: Halifax’s Low Income Transit Pass Program provides a 50% discount on Halifax Transit monthly passes for eligible low-income residents. By lowering commuting costs, it enables workers to reach employment opportunities across the region, directly reducing transportation barriers to better-paying and more stable jobs.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, 2nd Floor, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Employer Transit Pass Program (EPass)
resources.description: EPass offers discounted Halifax Transit passes to employees of participating organizations via payroll deduction, making daily commuting more affordable. The program supports workforce retention and access to higher-paying jobs by reducing commuting costs and improving reliable regional mobility for workers.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Cooperative – Community Transportation Service
resources.description: MusGo Rider provides door-to-door, pre-booked community transit across the Eastern Shore and surrounding rural areas, serving trips to work, training, and childcare. As a cooperative offering affordable fares, it connects residents to employment hubs where higher-paying jobs exist, reducing the need for private vehicle ownership and overcoming rural commuting barriers.

resources.name: Kings Transit Authority – Regional Bus Service
resources.description: Kings Transit operates fixed-route regional buses linking communities across Kings and Annapolis Counties with employment centres such as New Minas, Kentville, and Wolfville. By providing reliable, affordable regional transit and monthly pass options, it expands access to jobs and reduces transportation costs for workers who commute across the Valley.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

obstacles.title: Limited Mid-Career Progression and Firm Scale
obstacles.description: A small number of head offices and scale-ups constrains advancement pathways, senior roles, and R&D-intensive jobs that keep young professionals long-term.

solutions.text: Local Scale-Up Peer Network: Create a community-run network where leaders of small firms meet regularly to share growth strategies, talent challenges, and partnership opportunities, enabling informal benchmarking, referrals, and joint bids that increase firm scale.

resources.name: COVE Ocean Connector
resources.organization: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: COVE’s monthly Ocean Connector gatherings convene leaders of small and scaling ocean-technology firms to share growth strategies, talent needs, and upcoming market opportunities. By co-locating dozens of SMEs at the COVE campus and facilitating regular peer meetups, the initiative enables informal benchmarking, referrals, and collaborative project development—often leading to partnerships and joint bids that help companies scale.

resources.name: Volta CEO Roundtables & Community Events
resources.description: Volta hosts recurring peer roundtables and community events that bring together founders and senior leaders of small technology firms to discuss growth tactics, hiring challenges, and market expansion. These forums create a trusted space for leaders to exchange playbooks, make referrals, and identify partnership opportunities, which can translate into collaborative go-to-market efforts and larger joint pursuits.

resources.name: CEED Mastermind Groups for Entrepreneurs
resources.description: CEED facilitates peer-based mastermind groups where small-business owners meet regularly to troubleshoot scaling challenges, compare metrics, and share recruitment and retention strategies. The structured, recurring format fosters accountability and a pipeline of referrals and collaborations, enabling firms to partner on opportunities and grow beyond the constraints of going it alone.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic (CDL-Atlantic)
resources.organization: Creative Destruction Lab at the Rowe School of Business, Dalhousie University
resources.description: CDL-Atlantic runs a cohort-based program at Dalhousie University where founders of early-stage, high-growth firms meet regularly in sessions and bootcamps to set objectives, compare approaches, and share scaling and talent strategies alongside mentors. The cadence of in-person sessions and cohort interactions fosters founder-to-founder referrals and partnerships, including collaborative commercialization efforts that can accelerate scale.

solutions.text: Shared R&D and Makerspace Hubs: Establish communal lab, workshop, or prototyping spaces where multiple small businesses, entrepreneurs, and tradespeople can access equipment, test ideas, and collaborate on R&D without the individual capital burden.

resources.name: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: COVE is a shared ocean-technology hub that provides startups and small firms access to communal labs, workshops, electronics benches, and on-water test facilities on the Dartmouth waterfront. Companies co-locate to use specialized equipment, prototype new products, and collaborate with peers, researchers, and industry partners without bearing full capital costs. This shared R&D environment accelerates product development and supports scaling ocean-tech ventures in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – New Glasgow Innovation Hub
resources.description: IGNITE’s New Glasgow hub operates a makerspace and prototyping facility with 3D printers, laser cutters, electronics benches, and fabrication tools available to entrepreneurs, tradespeople, and small businesses. The shared space enables low-cost R&D, rapid prototyping, and product testing alongside mentorship and collaboration with other innovators. This model lowers barriers to experimentation and supports companies to scale within the region.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Yarmouth Innovation Hub
resources.description: IGNITE’s Yarmouth hub provides a communal makerspace and applied R&D environment where entrepreneurs and small firms can access shared equipment such as 3D printers, CNC tools, and electronics workstations. Users prototype, iterate, and test ideas without the cost of owning specialized gear, while collaborating with mentors and peers. The hub strengthens rural innovation capacity and supports business growth in Southwestern Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library – Community Workshop
resources.description: The Halifax Tool Library operates a membership-based tool lending library and a community workshop with shared woodworking and DIY fabrication equipment. Entrepreneurs, tradespeople, and makers can access tools, workspace, and training to build prototypes and test product ideas at a fraction of the cost of purchasing their own equipment. This shared model reduces capital barriers and fosters collaboration among local makers and small businesses.

resources.name: Halifax Central Library – Creation Spaces
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Creation Spaces offer publicly accessible makerspace resources including 3D printers, audio-visual studios, and digital design tools. Entrepreneurs and creatives can prototype products, develop content, and experiment with new technologies in a shared, low-cost environment supported by staff training. By lowering equipment and skills barriers, the library’s communal labs enable early-stage R&D and collaboration across disciplines.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Mid-Career Leadership Fellowship: Run a local fellowship for professionals transitioning into senior roles that bundles mentoring, short secondments at partner firms, leadership training, and a capstone project to accelerate promotion-readiness within the community.

resources.name: Leadership Halifax
resources.description: Leadership Halifax is a cohort-based civic leadership program for mid-career professionals that runs over several months and builds the competencies needed for senior roles in the region. Participants receive structured leadership training, are paired with community and industry mentors, and complete a team-based community impact project that acts as a capstone. The program also includes site visits and leader shadowing with partner organizations, providing short real-world exposures that mirror secondments and accelerate promotion-readiness in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Advanced Management & Mentorship Program (AMMP)
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: AMMP is a flagship, multi-month leadership development and mentorship program for women entrepreneurs and managers that blends executive-level training with intensive one-on-one and peer mentoring. Participants build a strategic growth plan as a capstone, apply tools to real business challenges, and receive guidance from seasoned leaders across partner firms. By combining mentoring, applied learning, and exposure to regional business networks, AMMP functions as a mid-career leadership fellowship that strengthens promotion- and scale-readiness within Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program connects internationally trained, mid-career professionals with experienced Nova Scotia leaders for structured mentoring focused on leadership, networking, and navigating Canadian workplaces. Through employer partners, participants access short workplace exposures and work placements that function like secondments, applying new skills in real settings and building local references. Combined with targeted training and individualized development plans, the program accelerates readiness for supervisory and senior roles in the province.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Indigenous Women in Community Leadership (IWCL)
resources.organization: Coady Institute, St. Francis Xavier University
resources.description: IWCL is a nationally recognized fellowship delivered from Nova Scotia that supports Indigenous women—often mid-career community and organizational leaders—through intensive leadership education and individualized mentorship with senior Indigenous leaders. Participants design and implement a community-based capstone project with partner organizations, and many engage in short project shadowing or host-community residencies that mirror secondments. This applied, mentored model builds promotion-ready leadership capacity that remains rooted in Nova Scotia and across Mi’kma’ki.

resources.name: Executive Certificate in Leadership
resources.organization: Dalhousie University — Rowe School of Business Executive Education
resources.description: Dalhousie Executive Education’s modular certificate helps mid-career managers transition into senior roles through intensive leadership training, coaching/mentoring, and peer learning. Participants complete an applied action-learning project (a practical capstone implemented in their organization) and engage with local industry leaders and case partners, building cross-sector exposure and promotion-readiness within the Nova Scotia ecosystem.

resources.name: Emerging Leaders Program
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University — Sobey School of Business, Executive and Professional Development
resources.description: A cohort-based program designed for high-potential, mid-career professionals, the Emerging Leaders Program combines executive leadership training with coaching and mentorship from experienced practitioners. Learners complete an applied capstone project tied to a real organizational challenge and engage with guest executives and local partners, mirroring the fellowship model that accelerates readiness for senior roles.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program & Workplace Experience
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS supports internationally trained, mid-career professionals by pairing them with industry mentors, delivering targeted leadership and workplace-readiness training, and arranging short, structured workplace experience placements with Nova Scotia employers. These time-bound placements function like secondments, allowing participants to deliver tangible projects for host firms (a capstone-style outcome) while expanding networks that speed advancement into leadership roles.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Canadian Women in Ocean Industries Leadership (CWOIL) Mentorship Program
resources.description: CWOIL advances mid-career women in the ocean economy through structured mentorship with senior industry leaders, cohort-based leadership development, and curated exposure to partner companies via industry engagements and site visits. Participants craft a personal leadership plan and often undertake applied projects or showcase outcomes with mentor guidance, strengthening pathways to senior roles across Nova Scotia’s ocean sector.

resources.name: Greater Heights of Growth
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business, Mount Saint Vincent University
resources.description: This 12‑month cohort program equips women business owners and senior leaders with executive education, one‑on‑one coaching, and structured peer mentorship to scale their organizations and step into higher leadership. Each participant develops and executes a growth plan as a capstone project and connects with advisors and partner firms in Nova Scotia’s ecosystem, mirroring a fellowship model that accelerates promotion‑readiness.

solutions.text: Fractional Executive Pool: Organize a cooperative of part-time CFOs, CTOs, CMOs and HR leads available to multiple small businesses so firms can access senior skills at affordable rates while creating pathways for mid-career managers to gain executive experience.

resources.name: Outsourced and Virtual CFO Services
resources.description: MNP provides fractional CFO and controller services to small and mid-sized businesses, assigning senior finance leaders on a part-time basis so multiple firms can access executive-level financial strategy and oversight without hiring full-time. This directly implements the fractional executive pool model by deploying experienced CFOs across several clients concurrently, while creating pathways for mid-career finance professionals to build executive experience in diverse industries.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 1200, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Experts-in-Residence (EiR) Program
resources.description: Volta’s EiR program connects startups and scaling companies with seasoned executives in finance, product/technology, marketing, and people operations who work with multiple firms on a part-time basis. By providing hands-on advisory and interim leadership across a portfolio of resident companies, the program functions as a fractional executive pool and offers mid-career managers a pathway to gain executive-level experience across different growth-stage businesses.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard Advisors and Executives-in-Residence
resources.description: COVE’s Start-Up Yard engages a bench of senior advisors and executives-in-residence who support multiple ocean-tech SMEs with part-time leadership in areas such as technology/product (CTO-level guidance), commercialization/marketing (CMO-level), and finance. This shared-talent model lets firms access top-tier expertise affordably and gives mid-career professionals structured opportunities to serve as fractional executives across several ventures.

solutions.text: Community Investment and Angel Co-op: Form a local investor group or co-op that pools community capital to provide seed and growth funding to promising local companies, tied to mentorship and community employment commitments to retain mid-career talent.

resources.name: FarmWorks Investment Co-operative Limited
resources.description: FarmWorks is a community-owned investment co‑operative (CEDIF) that pools capital from Nova Scotia residents to provide patient, growth-oriented financing to food and agriculture businesses across the province. Alongside capital, it offers hands-on mentorship and advisory support from experienced operators, encouraging local procurement and job creation as firms scale in place. By anchoring funding and guidance in the community, FarmWorks helps create and retain mid-career management and technical roles in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Small Business Loan Guarantee Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Co-operative Council (in partnership with Nova Scotia Credit Unions and Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Delivered through Nova Scotia credit unions, this program pools community-sourced capital and leverages a provincial guarantee to provide start-up and growth financing to Nova Scotia companies. Credit union advisors and the Nova Scotia Co-operative Council provide ongoing mentorship and business counseling, with financing targeted to firms operating and hiring locally. The combination of community-backed capital and advisory support helps companies expand headcount and create senior roles that retain mid-career talent.

resources.name: Nova Scotia First Fund (Venture Capital)
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia’s early-stage venture capital fund provides seed and pre-seed equity to Nova Scotia startups, often alongside local angels and community investors. Portfolio companies receive access to mentors, commercialization programming, and partner hubs, with investment focused on firms headquartered and growing employment in the province. By tying capital to mentorship and local scale-up pathways, the fund helps create senior technical and leadership roles that keep mid-career professionals in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Build Ventures Fund
resources.description: Build Ventures is an Atlantic Canadian venture capital fund based in Halifax that pools capital from regional institutions and governments to make seed and Series A investments in high-growth companies. The fund provides board-level guidance, mentorship, and deep networks to help companies scale from Nova Scotia while building teams locally. By combining growth capital with active support and an East Coast base, it fosters the creation and retention of mid-career and senior roles in the region.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta Cohort provides pre-seed funding to early-stage Atlantic Canadian startups alongside intensive mentorship, founder education, and investor connections. The program’s capital is contributed by regional partners and is tied to programming that helps companies gain traction and hire locally from Nova Scotia’s talent base. This community-backed funding plus mentorship builds local scale-up pathways and leadership opportunities that encourage mid-career professionals to stay in the province.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

solutions.text: Apprentice-to-Management Pathways: Partner trades, post-secondary institutions and employers to design clear staged career maps that move apprentices into supervisory and business roles, including sponsored training and shared placement opportunities across firms.

resources.name: Supervisory Training Program (STP)
resources.description: CANS’ Supervisory Training Program (STP) delivers a structured series of modules that help experienced apprentices and journeypersons move into foreperson, superintendent, and project management roles. Delivered in partnership with member employers and industry/post-secondary instructors, it builds leadership, scheduling, cost-control, and communication skills that firms require for front-line management. Employers frequently sponsor participants and send cohorts from multiple companies, creating clear, staged career maps from tools-based roles into supervision across the construction sector.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.organization: Construction Association of Nova Scotia (CANS) in partnership with Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC)
resources.description: Building Futures for Youth connects high school students with paid summer placements across a wide range of construction trades, coordinated with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and NSCC. Students earn pre-apprenticeship hours, safety tickets, and mentorship with host employers, then transition into registered apprenticeship and technical training after graduation. By brokering shared placements across many firms and mapping clear steps from high school to apprenticeship and onward to journeyperson/supervisory roles, BFY operationalizes an apprentice-to-management pipeline for the sector.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Irving Shipbuilding Inc. Centre of Excellence in partnership with Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC)
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based training-to-employment initiative pairing NSCC technical training (e.g., welding, metal fabrication) with sponsored work terms and hiring opportunities at Irving Shipbuilding. Co-designed with industry and community partners (including Women Unlimited and Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre), it lays out a staged career path from pre-apprenticeship through apprenticeship to lead hand and supervisory roles in the shipyard. Irving and partners co-fund tuition, learner supports, and placements, creating a clear, supported progression into long-term, higher-responsibility positions.

resources.name: Leadership for Safety Excellence (LSE) & Supervisor Development
resources.description: Construction Safety Nova Scotia delivers Leadership for Safety Excellence and related supervisor development courses that prepare journeypersons and senior apprentices to step into foreperson and site supervisor roles. Offered province-wide and recognized by many contractors for advancement, the training covers due diligence, hazard management, communication, and team leadership. These stackable certificates are used by employers as part of staged career maps to move tradespeople into management tracks while improving productivity and safety performance.

solutions.text: Inter-Company Secondment Program: Coordinate short-term rotations among local firms and nonprofits to broaden mid-career professionals' experience, reduce skill gaps, and expose them to leadership responsibilities without leaving the community.

resources.name: Sponsored Employee (Loaned Representative) Program
resources.description: United Way Halifax’s Sponsored Employee (Loaned Representative) Program seconds mid-career employees from local companies to United Way for a campaign term, where they manage workplace campaigns, liaise with dozens of employers, and lead community initiatives. This structured, time-bound secondment exposes professionals to cross-sector leadership and project management responsibilities while keeping them embedded in the local community, directly aligning with an inter-company secondment model that broadens experience and reduces skill gaps.
resources.address: 46 Portland Street, 7th Floor, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 1H4

resources.name: Civic Innovation Outpost
resources.organization: Volta (in partnership with Halifax Regional Municipality)
resources.description: The Civic Innovation Outpost embeds Halifax Regional Municipality staff at Volta to collaborate with local startups and community partners on real municipal challenges. Through these short-term, cross-organizational placements, mid-career public servants gain private-sector exposure and leadership experience while startups learn to navigate public-sector constraints—functioning as a local, inter-organization secondment that builds skills without requiring permanent job changes.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Interchange Canada
resources.description: Interchange Canada facilitates temporary assignments between the federal public service and external organizations, including Nova Scotia-based companies, municipalities, universities, and nonprofits. Local employers can host or send mid-career professionals on defined-term secondments, creating structured rotations that build leadership capacity and cross-sector skills while keeping talent in the province.

solutions.text: Municipal Procurement for Growth: Advocate for local governments and anchor institutions to structure procurement that favors scaling local SMEs and requires partnerships or capacity-building plans that create senior roles and R&D collaborations.

resources.name: HRM Social Procurement Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality integrates social and local economic benefit criteria into its procurement, weighting RFPs to encourage participation by local SMEs and diverse suppliers. The program includes supplier engagement sessions and contract clauses that support subcontracting, skills development, and capacity-building partnerships, helping local firms scale and create more senior roles tied to delivering on municipal contracts.

resources.name: Halifax Anchor Collaborative
resources.description: Led by Halifax Partnership, this collaborative brings together major local anchors (HRM, Nova Scotia Health, post-secondary institutions, the Port of Halifax, and others) to align procurement practices that grow local supplier participation and scale SMEs. The group facilitates vendor outreach, joint problem statements, and partnership requirements in bids, fostering capacity-building and R&D collaboration pathways that create higher-skill roles and retain talent.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Innovation Hub – Innovation Procurement Pathway
resources.description: The Innovation Hub works with clinical teams and procurement to issue challenge-based opportunities, co-develop pilots with local SMEs, and create a pathway from validated pilots to procurement and scale within the health system. By requiring collaborative projects with researchers and health leaders and offering vendor development supports, it builds SME capacity, drives R&D partnerships, and creates senior technical and management roles in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: The PIER – Port Innovation, Engagement & Research
resources.description: Operated by the Halifax Port Authority, The PIER is a living lab where port operators and logistics anchors run challenge-driven pilot projects that can lead to procurement of solutions from local SMEs. The program actively facilitates industry–SME–research partnerships and provides testbeds and mentorship that build supplier capacity, accelerate commercialization, and create senior and R&D-intensive roles tied to anchor procurement in the ocean and logistics sectors.

solutions.text: Peer Mentorship Circles: Set up facilitated peer groups of mid-career professionals across sectors to exchange problem-solving, career planning, and leadership coaching, increasing retention by improving career satisfaction and networks.

resources.name: Peer Roundtables
resources.description: The Halifax Chamber of Commerce runs facilitated, cross-sector Peer Roundtables where small groups of business leaders and managers meet regularly to troubleshoot challenges, share leadership practices, and plan career and business growth. These confidential circles create structured peer mentorship that builds networks and supports mid-career retention by improving satisfaction and clarity on advancement pathways in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 32 Akerley Boulevard, Unit 100, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1N1

resources.name: Mastermind Groups
resources.description: CEED facilitates ongoing mastermind-style peer groups that bring together entrepreneurs and managers from diverse industries to exchange problem-solving approaches, set growth goals, and receive leadership coaching from advisors and peers. These structured circles help mid-career professionals build strong networks and stay engaged in Nova Scotia’s business community, directly aligning with the peer mentorship circle model.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Peer Mentoring Circles
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business hosts facilitated peer mentoring circles and mastermind cohorts for women entrepreneurs and leaders across sectors, focusing on real-time problem-solving, growth planning, and leadership development. By connecting mid-career professionals in small, consistent groups, the program strengthens networks and supports long-term career satisfaction and retention in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: Seton Academic Centre, Room 202, 166 Bedford Highway, Halifax, NS B3M 2J6

resources.name: Founders Peer-to-Peer Sessions
resources.description: Volta convenes recurring peer-to-peer founder circles and facilitated discussions where startup leaders share practical solutions on hiring, scaling, and leadership, while receiving coaching from experienced mentors and peers. These small-group sessions operate as mentorship circles that deepen networks and improve mid-career satisfaction for tech professionals choosing to build their careers in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: Suite 100, 1505 Barrington Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Ocean Connector and Peer Roundtables
resources.description: COVE brings together mid-career professionals from ocean-focused firms for facilitated knowledge-sharing through its Ocean Connector series and member peer roundtables, enabling collaborative problem-solving on commercialization, R&D, and leadership challenges. These circles strengthen cross-company networks and provide coaching and career clarity that help retain skilled professionals within Nova Scotia’s blue economy.

solutions.text: Community-Owned Scale-Up Accelerator: Launch a locally governed accelerator focused on scaling existing firms (not just startups) offering business development, market access, talent matching, and investor introductions tailored to mid-career role creation.

resources.name: Scale-up Hub Program (Boston/Atlanta/UK)
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia’s Scale-up Hub places Nova Scotia technology companies in key international markets and provides sales coaching, business development support, and curated introductions to customers, partners, and investors. It targets firms that already have traction and are ready to scale exports, helping them accelerate revenue growth and expand leadership capacity. By enabling growth at established firms, the program drives the creation of mid-career roles in sales, product, and operations that are anchored in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 701, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic
resources.description: CDL–Atlantic is an objectives-based program hosted at Dalhousie University that helps science and technology companies scale through mentorship from experienced entrepreneurs and a global network of angel and venture investors. The program emphasizes market access, sales discipline, and investor readiness for companies beyond the idea stage, catalyzing rapid growth. As participating firms scale, they build out mid-career management and specialist roles in Nova Scotia to execute commercialization and expansion plans.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard and Ocean Technology Cluster Services
resources.description: COVE provides a full-stack ocean technology cluster in Dartmouth with shared infrastructure, prototyping and testing facilities, accelerator programming, and direct access to buyers in defense, energy, and marine industries. Its programs support both startups and scaling SMEs with business development, pilot opportunities, and investor and partner introductions to grow exports. This growth pathway anchors mid-career engineering, project management, and business development roles within Nova Scotia’s ocean economy.

resources.name: SmartBusiness Program
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s SmartBusiness program is a business retention and expansion (BRE) service that proactively engages established firms to identify growth barriers and connect them to export development, financing, R&D, and market opportunities. Working closely with partners like the Connector Program and post-secondary institutions, it brokers talent matches for hard-to-fill mid-career roles and opens doors to new customers and investors. By helping existing companies scale in-place, the program strengthens advancement pathways and senior job creation in the region.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Worker Ownership & Cooperative Conversions: Support transitions of viable small firms to employee ownership or cooperatives, creating broader senior-role opportunities and incentives for long-term commitment by embedding leadership within the workforce.

resources.name: Small Business Loan Guarantee Program (Co-operative and Employee Buyout Financing)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Co-operative Council (in partnership with Nova Scotia Credit Unions and the Province of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: This province-wide financing program, delivered through Nova Scotia credit unions and coordinated by the Nova Scotia Co-operative Council, provides loan guarantees that enable co-operatives and employee/management groups to acquire and grow viable small businesses. By making capital accessible for succession deals and co‑operative start-ups, the program helps owners transition their firms to worker ownership or co‑op structures, embedding leadership and long-term commitment within the workforce.
resources.address: 90 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: Registry of Joint Stock Companies – Co-operatives (Incorporation and Compliance)
resources.organization: Service Nova Scotia (Registry of Joint Stock Companies)
resources.description: The Registry provides the legal pathway, forms, and guidance required to incorporate worker and multi‑stakeholder co-operatives in Nova Scotia, and to transition existing firms into co‑operative entities. By enabling compliant co‑op governance and registration, the Registry directly supports owners and employees who choose employee ownership or co‑operative conversions as a succession strategy.

resources.name: International Centre for Co-operative Management (Executive Education and Advisory)
resources.organization: Sobey School of Business, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: Housed at Saint Mary’s University, the Centre delivers specialized executive education, research, and advisory services for co-operatives and credit unions, including support for organizations exploring or managing conversions to employee ownership and co‑op models. By building management capacity among employee-owners and emerging leaders, ICCM helps ensure that succession to worker ownership creates robust leadership pipelines and long-term, locally anchored firms.

solutions.text: Cross-Sector Cluster Projects: Organize community-led projects that bring businesses, universities, arts and nonprofits together on major local problems (food systems, clean tech, cultural tourism), generating R&D-intensive roles and multi-disciplinary senior positions.

resources.name: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: COVE convenes multi-partner ocean technology projects that unite companies, Dalhousie/NSCC researchers, government labs, and nonprofit organizations to tackle challenges in fisheries, offshore energy, and marine monitoring. Through joint R&D, shared testbeds, and the Start-Up Yard accelerator, it generates advanced engineering and data roles and creates senior, cross-disciplinary positions (program directors, commercialization leads, technical project managers) that anchor ocean-sector talent in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Verschuren Centre for Sustainability in Energy and the Environment
resources.organization: Verschuren Centre for Sustainability in Energy and the Environment at Cape Breton University
resources.description: The Verschuren Centre leads industry-academic-nonprofit consortia to design and scale clean-tech solutions in bioeconomy, decarbonization, and circular manufacturing, leveraging pilot-scale facilities and community partnerships. By coordinating collaborative R&D and scale-up projects with companies, Cape Breton University and other institutions, and NGOs, it creates R&D-intensive roles (process engineers, applied scientists) and senior multidisciplinary positions (project leads, industry liaisons) that grow Nova Scotia’s clean-tech cluster.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

resources.name: Perennia Applied Research & Innovation
resources.description: Perennia coordinates cross-sector food systems initiatives that bring together farmers and processors, Acadia/NSCC researchers, retailers, community food organizations, and government to advance product development, food safety, aquaculture innovation, and controlled-environment agriculture. These cluster projects produce applied R&D roles (food scientists, aquaculture technologists) and senior, multi-disciplinary positions (technical directors, quality and commercialization leads) that strengthen Nova Scotia’s agri-food economy.
resources.address: 45 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Innovation Hub
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Health Innovation Hub connects clinicians with startups, global medtech firms, universities, and nonprofits to co-develop and validate medical technologies and digital health solutions in real care settings. By running collaborative R&D, clinical evaluations, and procurement pilots, it creates R&D-intensive roles (clinical research specialists, data scientists) and senior cross-functional positions (program directors, commercialization managers) that grow healthtech capacity in the province.

resources.name: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design – Creative Sector Development
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: CBCCD leads creative economy and cultural tourism collaborations that bring artisans and cultural organizations together with tourism operators, Cape Breton University/NSCC, municipalities, and Indigenous partners to co-create market-ready cultural products and experiences. These cross-sector initiatives generate design, curation, and product-development roles and senior project leadership that blend arts, business, and community development—building a sustainable cultural tourism cluster in Nova Scotia.

obstacles.title: Entrepreneurship Barriers and Access to Capital
obstacles.description: Risk-averse lending, thin angel/VC networks, collateral requirements, and complex procurement impede startups and small business growth.

solutions.text: Community Microloan Program: Local credit unions, foundations and municipalities pool capital to offer small, low-interest, flexible-term loans to early-stage entrepreneurs who lack traditional collateral; coupled with light-touch underwriting and local mentorship to improve repayment and business outcomes.

resources.name: CEED Startup & Growth Loans
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides micro and small business loans (typically $5,000–$20,000) tailored for early-stage entrepreneurs who may not qualify for traditional bank financing. The loans feature flexible terms and are paired with CEED’s mentorship, training, and business advisory services, creating a light-touch underwriting approach that helps reduce collateral barriers and improve business outcomes for Nova Scotia founders.

resources.name: Black Business Financing (Loan Program)
resources.description: BBI offers accessible financing, including micro and small business loans, for Black entrepreneurs across Nova Scotia, often accommodating limited collateral and providing competitive, flexible terms. Capital is coupled with hands-on business counselling, mentorship, and training through BBI’s advisory team and programs, directly addressing risk-averse lending barriers and improving repayment and growth outcomes.

solutions.text: Community Loan Guarantee Pool: A locally funded guarantee reserve underwritten by municipal government, philanthropic organizations and anchor businesses that backstop a portion of small business loans, reducing lender risk and unlocking credit for startups without heavy collateral.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Credit Union Small Business Loan Guarantee Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Co-operative Council (in partnership with Nova Scotia Credit Unions and the Province of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: A province‑wide loan guarantee program delivered through participating credit unions and administered by the Nova Scotia Co‑operative Council. The Province of Nova Scotia backstops a significant portion of each approved small business loan, reducing lender risk and enabling startups and SMEs without substantial collateral to secure financing for working capital and growth. This directly implements a community-backed guarantee pool that unlocks credit by sharing risk between public partners and local lenders.
resources.address: 111 Provost Street, Suite 400, New Glasgow, NS B2H 2P9

resources.name: Immigrant Entrepreneur Loan Stream (Small Business Loan Guarantee Program)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS supports immigrant and refugee entrepreneurs to access loans delivered by Nova Scotia credit unions under the provincial Small Business Loan Guarantee Program. By leveraging the province’s loan guarantee, lenders can approve newcomers who may lack Canadian credit history or collateral, while ISANS provides advisory support to strengthen business plans. This reduces lender risk and expands access to startup and growth capital for immigrant-founded ventures.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1W1

resources.name: Nova Scotia Social Enterprise Loan Guarantee Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Co-operative Council (in partnership with Nova Scotia Credit Unions and the Province of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: A targeted loan guarantee program for co‑operatives and nonprofits, administered by the Nova Scotia Co‑operative Council and delivered through participating credit unions. The province guarantees a portion of each loan, lowering lender risk so mission-driven organizations can finance equipment, working capital, and expansion without heavy collateral. This community guarantee mechanism mobilizes public and co‑operative sector partners to unlock capital for social enterprises across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 111 Provost Street, Suite 400, New Glasgow, NS B2H 2P9

resources.name: Small Business Loan Guarantee Program (Community Credit Union Delivery)
resources.organization: Community Credit Union of Cumberland Colchester
resources.description: Community Credit Union of Cumberland Colchester is a participating lender in Nova Scotia’s Small Business Loan Guarantee Program. Using the provincial guarantee to backstop a portion of each approved loan, the credit union can extend financing to startups and small businesses that might not meet traditional collateral or credit thresholds. This local delivery of a community guarantee pool reduces lender risk and unlocks credit for entrepreneurs in Colchester and Cumberland counties.

solutions.text: Local Angel Network and Syndicate: A community-run angel group that aggregates local investors to co-invest in promising startups, runs regular pitch nights, and syndicates investments so individual risk is lower and transaction costs are reduced for entrepreneurs.

resources.name: Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta Cohort is a biannual investment program and pitch event that pools capital from partners to make standardized $25,000 investments into early-stage Atlantic Canadian startups. By convening local and regional investors at its pitch nights and facilitating follow-on co-investment, the program functions like a syndicate that lowers individual investor risk and streamlines diligence. The standardized terms and centralized process reduce transaction costs for founders raising their first outside capital.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic
resources.organization: Creative Destruction Lab at the Rowe School of Business, Dalhousie University
resources.description: CDL-Atlantic runs an objectives-based program where vetted startups repeatedly pitch and work with a community of accredited angels and venture investors drawn from across Atlantic Canada. These investors often form syndicates to co-invest in participating companies, sharing due diligence and spreading risk, while CDL’s structured sessions and templates lower transaction costs. Regular pitch and selection meetings create a consistent pipeline for local co-investment.

resources.name: BioPort Atlantic – BioInnovation Challenge (Investor Showcase)
resources.organization: BioNova (Nova Scotia Life Sciences Industry Association)
resources.description: BioPort Atlantic, produced by BioNova, hosts the BioInnovation Challenge and investor showcase where life sciences startups pitch to panels of angels and VCs. The event intentionally aggregates regional investors to enable co-investment syndicates and provides standardized pitch materials and feedback that reduce fundraising friction and costs for founders. By curating deal flow and coordinating investor participation, it helps de-risk early checks for individual angels.

resources.name: Startup Yard at COVE – Investor Showcases
resources.description: Startup Yard at COVE is an ocean-technology incubator that runs demo days and investor showcases where cohort companies pitch to a community of local and regional angels, strategic investors, and funds. These events facilitate syndication and co-investment among attending angels, with shared vetting and standardized presentations reducing individual risk and transaction costs. By convening the ocean-tech investor community in Nova Scotia on a recurring basis, it functions as a practical local angel syndication platform.

solutions.text: Community Investment Cooperative: A cooperative vehicle enabling residents to invest small amounts into a diversified portfolio of local startups and small businesses, giving entrepreneurs access to patient, local equity while keeping returns and ownership benefits in the community.

resources.name: FarmWorks Investment Co-operative Limited (CEDIF)
resources.description: FarmWorks is a provincially registered Community Economic Development Investment Fund that pools small investments from Nova Scotia residents and reinvests the capital in a diversified portfolio of local food and beverage enterprises. By providing patient, relationship-based loans and quasi-equity to farms, processors, restaurants, and food startups across the province, it channels community ownership and returns back to Nova Scotians while expanding access to growth capital for entrepreneurs.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Development Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: New Dawn’s CEDIF allows Cape Breton residents to invest modest amounts in a community-managed fund that backs local small and medium-sized businesses. The fund provides patient, locally governed capital that helps entrepreneurs overcome traditional financing barriers, while dividends and potential tax benefits keep wealth and ownership rooted in the community.

resources.name: Black Business Community Investment Fund (BBCIF)
resources.description: The BBCIF is a Community Economic Development Investment Fund sponsored by the Black Business Initiative that aggregates small investments from Nova Scotians to finance Black-owned startups and growing small businesses. It deploys patient, community-based capital—often unavailable through conventional lenders—while enabling residents to share in the returns and strengthen local ownership.
resources.address: 1660 Hollis Street, Suite 910, Halifax, NS B3J 1V7

solutions.text: Procurement Set-Asides and Simplified Bids for Locals: Municipalities and public agencies create small-contract set-asides and simplified procurement tracks for startups, social enterprises and local SMEs, with streamlined requirements and faster payment terms to increase local participation.

resources.name: Social Procurement Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Social Procurement Program integrates social value and supplier diversity into municipal purchasing while using simplified processes for low-value buys. By unbundling larger projects into smaller contracts and using informal quote processes under threshold values, HRM opens opportunities for local startups, social enterprises, and SMEs. The program recognizes diverse and social suppliers and uses electronic funds transfer and prompt-payment practices to improve cash flow for small vendors, increasing local participation.

resources.name: Supplier Diversity Program (Nova Scotia Procurement)
resources.organization: Service Nova Scotia and Procurement, Government of Nova Scotia
resources.description: Nova Scotia’s Supplier Diversity Program expands access to provincial contracts by recognizing certified diverse and social enterprise suppliers and enabling designated or set-aside opportunities where permitted by trade agreements. The province also uses simplified, low-value procurement methods (direct purchases and quick quotes) that reduce paperwork and compliance burdens for local SMEs and startups. Electronic invoicing and prompt-payment measures (including prompt payment in construction) help accelerate cash flow for small vendors participating in public procurements.

resources.name: Procurement and Social Value Purchasing
resources.description: CBRM’s procurement function uses simplified purchasing for low-value contracts through informal quotes and standing offers that are accessible to local SMEs, startups, and community-based suppliers. Building on a social procurement approach, the municipality reserves small opportunities (e.g., catering, community events, and service micro-contracts) for certified diverse or social enterprise suppliers where applicable, reducing barriers to entry. The municipality prioritizes electronic payments and efficient invoicing to support faster payment cycles for small local vendors.

resources.name: Procurement Assistance Canada (Atlantic Region) and PSIB Support
resources.description: Procurement Assistance Canada’s Atlantic Region office helps Nova Scotia SMEs and startups navigate federal procurement by offering training, one-on-one advisory support, and guidance on simplified purchasing methods (e.g., low-dollar-value buys, standing offers, and supply arrangements). The office promotes and supports the federal Indigenous procurement target and set-aside opportunities under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB), and advances faster payment practices for small suppliers on federal contracts. These measures reduce bidding complexity and open targeted small-contract pathways for local firms across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: Queen Square, 45 Alderney Drive, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 2N6

solutions.text: Procurement Matchmaking and Supplier Navigation Service: A Chamber of Commerce or economic development office runs a hands-on service that matches startups to upcoming public and private contracts, and provides bid-writing help, templates and one-to-one navigators to demystify procurement.

resources.name: CANSnet Project Leads & Bid Support
resources.description: CANSnet aggregates public and private construction tenders across Nova Scotia and the region, providing members with daily project leads, bid documents, and a staffed plan room to navigate opportunities. The Construction Association of Nova Scotia offers training on estimating and tendering, access to standardized forms/templates, and one-on-one assistance that helps startups and SMEs understand requirements and prepare competitive bids—functioning as a practical procurement navigation and matchmaking service for the construction sector.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Procurement Assistance Canada – Atlantic Region (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Procurement Assistance Canada (PAC) provides free one-to-one advising, webinars, and workshops that help Nova Scotia startups and small businesses register in CanadaBuys, find upcoming federal contract opportunities, and understand how to prepare compliant bids. Advisors demystify procurement with templates, checklists, and plain-language guidance, and they run matchmaking/outreach events that connect local suppliers with federal buyers and prime contractors.

resources.name: Supplier Development and Supply Chain Engagement
resources.description: Irving Shipbuilding’s supplier development team connects Nova Scotia SMEs with opportunities in the National Shipbuilding Strategy supply chain, maintaining a supplier portal and hosting outreach and matchmaking sessions with buyers and tier-one contractors. The team offers direct navigation support on pre-qualification, standards, and documentation, and provides guidance on responding to solicitations—helping firms understand requirements and position stronger bids for complex private-sector contracts linked to public programs.

resources.name: Supplier Information Sessions & Procurement Outreach
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality (HRM) runs supplier information sessions and buyer–supplier outreach that explain how to do business with the municipality, upcoming procurement plans, and how to navigate HRM’s competitive processes. Procurement staff provide guidance, templates/resources, and one-on-one support and debriefs to help startups and small businesses understand requirements, improve bid quality, and connect with the right municipal buyers.

solutions.text: Local Startup Accelerator and Pre-Seed Fund: A community accelerator (run by university, non-profit or consortium) that provides a short program combining small pre-seed grants, shared workspace, investor introductions and industry mentorship tailored to regional economic strengths.

resources.name: Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta Cohort is a Halifax-based accelerator program that provides early-stage startups with non-dilutive pre-seed funding (e.g., $25,000 awards), mentorship, and structured programming. Winners receive access to shared workspace at Volta, investor introductions through pitch events and the Volta network, and guidance from industry mentors aligned with Atlantic Canada’s strengths in ICT, ocean tech, and health innovation.

resources.name: Invest Nova Scotia Accelerate
resources.description: Accelerate is a cohort-based program that offers milestone-driven, non-dilutive pre-seed funding (often up to tens of thousands of dollars), expert mentorship, and commercialization support tailored to sectors like oceans, clean tech, life sciences, and ICT. Companies gain access to shared resources, advisors, and investor connections through Invest Nova Scotia’s network, helping overcome early capital barriers and build traction.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 1101, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard is an ocean-technology incubator/accelerator that provides shared workspace, prototyping facilities, tailored mentorship, and industry partnerships focused on Nova Scotia’s blue economy strengths. Through COVE and partner initiatives like the Ocean Startup Project’s Challenge, participating teams can access non-dilutive pre-seed grants alongside investor and customer introductions to accelerate commercialization.

resources.name: Launch Dal – Ready2Launch
resources.description: Ready2Launch is Dalhousie University’s accelerator for student and researcher-led startups, offering a focused summer program with stipends/pre-seed funding, venture-building mentorship, and access to shared workspace on campus. Teams receive guidance from experienced founders and sector mentors, along with investor and partner introductions through demo days and Dal’s regional innovation network.

solutions.text: Investor-Readiness Bootcamps and Mentor Network: Volunteer entrepreneurs, investors and service providers run regular bootcamps and a mentorship registry to help founders craft investor-ready pitches, financial models and governance structures, increasing their ability to attract capital.

resources.name: Volta Academy & Mentor Network
resources.description: Volta Academy delivers recurring cohorts and workshops that train founders to craft investor-ready pitches, develop financial models, and understand governance best practices. Its Mentor Network and Office Hours connect startups with volunteer entrepreneurs, investors, and service providers for ongoing coaching and feedback, directly increasing their readiness to attract capital.

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic
resources.description: CDL-Atlantic runs an intensive, objectives-driven program where founders meet regularly with experienced entrepreneurs, angel investors, and venture capitalists to refine their business models, financial plans, and governance. Through repeated mentorship sessions and investor-facing meetings, companies become investment-ready and receive curated introductions to capital providers.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard Accelerator
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE provides ocean-tech founders with structured bootcamps and sprints focused on pitch development, financial modeling, commercialization, and governance/regulatory readiness. A built-in mentor network of industry executives, investors, and service providers offers hands-on guidance and investor introductions, helping companies become capital-ready.

resources.name: CEED Startup & Growth Programs
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED delivers practical bootcamps and workshops that cover business planning, cash flow and financial modeling, and investor pitch preparation. Through CEED’s network, participants access volunteer mentors and professional service providers who offer ongoing advice on governance and fundraising, directly supporting investor readiness.

resources.name: BioInnovation Challenge & Mentor Program
resources.description: BioNova’s BioInnovation Challenge pairs early-stage life sciences companies with seasoned mentors and provides intensive pitch coaching, financial planning support, and IP/governance guidance. The associated mentor network includes investors and industry experts who help founders refine investment materials and connect with potential capital sources.

solutions.text: Collateral Alternatives and Peer Guarantee Schemes: Community programs that accept non-traditional security—future receivables, inventory, intellectual property—or organize peer/group guarantee schemes where local businesses or residents jointly vouch for a loan to reduce formal collateral needs.

resources.name: CEED Impact Loan
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED’s Impact Loan provides startup and growth financing to early-stage and emerging entrepreneurs while focusing on character, cash flow, and viability rather than hard collateral. The program commonly uses alternative security such as promissory notes and general security over future receivables or inventory, reducing or replacing the need for traditional fixed-asset collateral. This approach directly addresses collateral barriers and expands access to capital for Nova Scotia founders.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Loan Guarantee Program for Women
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business helps women entrepreneurs access the Nova Scotia Small Business Loan Guarantee Program delivered through credit unions, where the province provides a guarantee (up to 90%) that substitutes for traditional collateral. This enables lenders to rely more on business viability, cash flow, and assets like receivables/inventory rather than requiring hard collateral from the borrower. The program is paired with advisory support to strengthen applications for those with limited collateral histories.

resources.name: Small Business Loan Guarantee Program
resources.description: Valley Credit Union delivers the province-wide Small Business Loan Guarantee Program, offering term loans and lines of credit backed by a provincial guarantee of up to 90%. The guarantee reduces or replaces collateral requirements, allowing the credit union to accept alternative security (e.g., general security over inventory and receivables) and to lend based on projected cash flows. This expands access to capital for startups and small businesses that lack significant fixed assets.

solutions.text: Locally Focused Crowdfunding and Investor Days: Organize community equity crowdfunding rounds and regular 'Investor Days' where local residents, alumni and diaspora can invest small amounts or pledge support for local startups, bundled with marketing to build local customer-investor relationships.

resources.name: FarmWorks Community Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: FarmWorks operates a provincially registered CEDIF that raises RRSP-eligible capital from Nova Scotia residents in small denominations during recurring public offerings, and then lends that capital to local food and agriculture businesses across the province. They host public information sessions and entrepreneur showcases where community members meet founders, sample products, and decide to invest or pledge customer support—effectively turning each raise into a locally focused crowdfunding round that builds customer–investor relationships.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: New Dawn organizes CEDIF share offerings that enable Cape Breton residents and diaspora to invest modest amounts in a pooled community fund financing startups and growing businesses on the Island. Each offering is paired with open investor information nights and venture spotlights at the New Dawn Centre for Social Innovation, serving as community 'Investor Days' that connect entrepreneurs with prospective customer–investors and supporters.

resources.name: Community Economic Development Investment Funds (CEDIF) Program
resources.organization: Province of Nova Scotia, Department of Finance and Treasury Board
resources.description: Nova Scotia’s CEDIF Program provides the legal and administrative framework for community equity crowdfunding by allowing groups to raise capital from Nova Scotians (often with low minimum investments) in exchange for shares, supported by an equity tax credit. The program enables recurring, publicly marketed community offerings and investor information sessions, making it practical for residents and alumni to invest directly in local startups and small businesses while building long-term customer–investor relationships.

resources.name: COVE Demo Day: Investor & Industry Showcase
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE’s annual Demo Day is an investor and industry showcase where ocean-technology startups and scaleups present live demos and pitches to local residents, alumni, corporate partners, and investors. The event functions as a regional 'Investor Day' that catalyzes follow-on investments (e.g., through angels or NS-compliant equity crowdfunding vehicles) and customer pilots, creating direct relationships between community backers and emerging companies.

solutions.text: Social Procurement and Impact Investor Partnerships: Local foundations, social enterprises and impact investors coordinate to earmark funding and procurement to locally owned, high-impact businesses—blending grants, concessionary capital and procurement preferences to de-risk investment.

resources.name: Atlantic Social Procurement Initiative (ASPI)
resources.description: ASPI builds the capacity of public buyers and anchor institutions in Nova Scotia to include social value, local hiring, and supplier diversity criteria in procurement, while coaching social enterprises to become procurement-ready. Led from Nova Scotia, the initiative convenes municipalities, post‑secondary, health authorities, and community funders to align purchasing with impact and connect enterprises to social finance partners, blending demand-side procurement signals with patient capital to de-risk investment in local, high‑impact businesses.
resources.address: 100 Ochterloney Street, Suite 201, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 1C5

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Social Procurement Program
resources.description: HRM’s procurement framework incorporates social value by awarding points for local economic development, workforce inclusion (e.g., apprenticeships and diversity hiring), and community benefits in bids. By signalling preference for local and diverse suppliers and running supplier outreach with community partners, the program creates predictable demand that enables foundations and impact lenders to co-invest alongside public contracts, reducing risk for high-impact, locally owned businesses.

resources.name: Black Business Loan Program
resources.description: The program provides financing and advisory support to Black-owned businesses across Nova Scotia, using flexible, relationship-based lending that complements grants and other concessionary capital. Through supplier diversity partnerships and procurement-readiness events, BBI connects clients to public- and private-sector buyers, effectively pairing capital with procurement opportunities to de-risk growth for investors and create stable revenue for local, high‑impact firms.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 309, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Lender–Startup Dialogue Workshops: Facilitated workshops where local lenders, credit unions and startups exchange perspectives, share case studies, and co-develop pragmatic lending criteria and pilot products that balance risk management with startup realities.

resources.name: Volta Funding Panel & Office Hours Series
resources.description: Volta regularly convenes funding panels and lender office hours that bring together BDC, credit unions, commercial banks, and startup founders to discuss real financing cases and underwriting expectations. These facilitated sessions let lenders explain risk frameworks while founders share traction data and collateral challenges, leading to practical checklists, feedback loops on lending criteria, and pilots such as revenue-based or milestone-tied credit options tailored to early-stage companies.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: CEED Access to Financing Workshops & Panels
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED hosts recurring workshops and roundtable panels that connect entrepreneurs with lenders from CBDCs, BDC, credit unions, and commercial banks to unpack real financing scenarios and eligibility criteria. Facilitators guide lenders and founders through case studies to align expectations, co-create bank meeting readiness checklists, and surface opportunities for pilot lending products that reflect startup cash-flow realities.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Business Support Series: Meet Your Funders
resources.description: The Halifax Chamber’s Business Support Series includes "Meet Your Funders" sessions that bring startups and small businesses face-to-face with BDC, ACOA, CBDCs, and local credit unions. Moderated discussions and Q&A allow lenders to explain risk appetites and documentation needs while founders provide feedback on barriers, helping co-develop pragmatic criteria and pathways to pilot lending approaches suitable for early-stage ventures.
resources.address: 32 Akerley Boulevard, Unit 100, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1N1
