resources.name: CWB Meet the Funders & Banker Breakfasts
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business runs "Meet the Funders" and Banker Breakfast-style sessions where founders engage directly with credit unions, BDC, and commercial lenders to compare underwriting expectations and explore tailored financing paths. Through facilitated dialogue and case-based discussion, lenders and entrepreneurs co-create practical readiness tools and refine lending approaches for women-led startups and SMEs.
resources.address: 166 Bedford Highway, McCain Centre, 2nd Floor, Halifax, NS B3M 2J6

solutions.text: Shared Equipment, Maker Spaces and Co-Labs: Community-run maker spaces, shared production facilities and university co-labs reduce upfront capital requirements by giving startups access to tools, testing labs and short-term production capacity at affordable rates.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE provides ocean-technology startups with affordable access to shared machine shops, electronics benches, prototyping tools, labs, and waterfront test facilities, including wharf access. By offering flexible bays, shared equipment, and common services under one roof, it reduces upfront capital needs for building, testing, and short-run production of marine hardware and systems.

resources.name: Perennia Innovation Centre (Food & Beverage Pilot Facility)
resources.description: Perennia’s Innovation Centre operates a federally inspected pilot plant, commercial-scale processing lines, and analytical labs that food and beverage startups can rent by the day or project. Access to shared production equipment, packaging capabilities, and quality testing allows entrepreneurs to prototype, validate, and produce small batches without purchasing costly machinery.
resources.address: 45 Innovation Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2H5

resources.name: Life Sciences Research Institute (LSRI) – Startup Labs & Offices
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia manages shared wet labs, specialized equipment, and startup offices at the LSRI for early-stage life sciences companies. Flexible leases and common lab infrastructure (e.g., tissue culture rooms, shared instrumentation, and safety systems) reduce capital requirements so biotech and medtech ventures can prototype and validate products cost-effectively.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: The Halifax Tool Library is a community-run lending library offering thousands of shared tools and a small workshop for members at low cost. Makers, tradespeople, and early-stage entrepreneurs can borrow equipment for prototyping, repairs, or short production runs, avoiding the expense of buying seldom-used tools.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: The Lou Duggan Creative Studio is a public makerspace with 3D printers, sewing machines, Cricut cutters, and digital media tools that individuals and small teams can book at little or no cost. Early-stage founders use the shared studio to prototype products, create packaging, and produce marketing assets without investing in their own equipment.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Alumni and Diaspora Investment & Mentorship Network: A program that engages Nova Scotia alumni and former residents abroad to invest, mentor, source customers and open market channels for local startups—leveraging emotional ties to mobilize capital and business connections.

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Creative Destruction Lab (CDL) Atlantic
resources.description: CDL-Atlantic is a seed-stage program at Dalhousie University that pairs high-potential Atlantic Canadian startups with a curated group of world-class mentors, angel investors, and venture capitalists. The mentor roster includes many Dalhousie/Atlantic alumni and expatriate Canadians who provide investment, hands-on mentorship, and warm introductions to international customers and partners—directly aligning with a diaspora-driven investment and market-access model.
resources.address: Rowe School of Business, 6100 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta Cohort is an early-stage funding and support program that invests in Atlantic Canadian startups and surrounds them with a broad mentor network. Through Volta’s community of alumni founders, advisors, and supporters—including Nova Scotians living elsewhere—the program facilitates mentorship and warm introductions to investors and potential customers, helping companies open sales channels at home and abroad.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE is an ocean-technology incubator that connects Nova Scotia companies with a global network of industry mentors, pilots, and buyers. The program actively engages experienced ocean-sector leaders—including Nova Scotia alumni and expats working internationally—to mentor founders, co-invest, and broker customer introductions and pilot projects, accelerating market entry and growth.

resources.name: Invest Nova Scotia – Accelerate
resources.description: Accelerate provides funding, coaching, and a structured accelerator for early-stage startups, complemented by access to Invest Nova Scotia’s investor and advisor networks. Drawing on Nova Scotia’s alumni and diaspora communities through mentors, visiting advisors, and partner events, the program helps founders secure investment and unlock customer relationships and distribution channels in external markets.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 1101, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

solutions.text: Pro Bono Legal, Accounting and Procurement Clinics: Volunteer professional clinics offering free or low-cost help with term sheets, procurement bids, incorporation, contracts and financial projections so startups can present stronger, less risky propositions to investors and buyers.

resources.name: Volta Office Hours
resources.description: Volta offers recurring, free one-on-one office hours with volunteer legal, accounting and IP partners to help founders review term sheets, structure incorporations, draft/interpret contracts, and refine financial models. These clinics reduce risk and strengthen investor- and buyer-facing materials so startups can negotiate investment, close sales, and compete for procurement opportunities with greater confidence.

resources.name: Procurement Assistance Canada – Atlantic Region (Supplier Advisory Services)
resources.description: Procurement Assistance Canada’s Atlantic team provides free seminars and one-on-one advisory to help Nova Scotia startups and SMEs become procurement-ready and submit stronger bids for Government of Canada contracts. Services include guidance on registering as a supplier, navigating tender platforms, understanding RFP requirements, and improving bid strategies and debriefs so companies can compete more effectively.

resources.name: ISANS Business Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides free, one-on-one business counselling for immigrant entrepreneurs, including support with business registration/incorporation, contract basics, business planning and developing financial projections and cash-flow statements. They also host clinics and workshops with volunteer professionals (lawyers, accountants, and procurement advisors) to help clients prepare stronger, lower-risk proposals for lenders, investors, and public-sector buyers.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Centre for Women in Business – Ask an Expert Clinics
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business hosts pro bono and subsidized ‘Ask an Expert’ clinics where volunteer lawyers, accountants, and procurement specialists meet with women and non-binary entrepreneurs to review contracts, discuss incorporation/structuring, and strengthen financial projections. These sessions help founders de-risk their ventures, understand term sheets, and navigate supplier registration and public-sector bids.
resources.address: 166 Bedford Highway, 3rd Floor McCain Centre, Halifax, NS B3M 2J6

resources.name: Common Good Solutions – Social Enterprise Incubator and Advisory
resources.description: Common Good Solutions provides low-cost and often grant-subsidized advisory and clinic-style supports to social enterprises across Nova Scotia, including help with incorporation (e.g., CIC or non-profit), contract review, and building financial models and projections. They also coach clients on social procurement opportunities and bid preparation so enterprises can present stronger, more competitive proposals to institutional buyers.

obstacles.title: Transportation and Regional Connectivity Gaps
obstacles.description: Sparse intercity transit, limited rural options, car dependency, and costly or infrequent air links reduce mobility for work, study, and culture.

solutions.text: Community Shuttle Cooperatives: Form a locally governed shuttle cooperative that runs scheduled routes between towns and key hubs (markets, schools, hospitals). Members contribute time, money, or governance; revenue from fares and local business sponsorships covers operating costs.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Co-operative Ltd. — Eastern Shore
resources.description: Member-owned rural transit co-operative providing scheduled and demand-responsive shuttle services along the Eastern Shore, linking communities to key hubs such as Halifax hospitals, NSCC campuses, and major shopping/market areas. Residents become members, elect a local board, and support operations through modest membership fees and fares, while additional revenue is raised via local business sponsorships and community partnerships—closely aligning with the community shuttle cooperative model.
resources.address: 67 Park Road, Musquodoboit Harbour, NS B0J 2L0

resources.name: MusGo Rider Co-operative Ltd. — Musquodoboit Valley
resources.description: Locally governed co-operative operating community shuttles that connect Musquodoboit Valley residents with schools, clinics/hospitals, and commercial centres on scheduled and pre-booked runs. The co-op structure engages members in governance and cost-sharing, with fare revenue and local sponsorships helping to sustain reliable rural mobility in a low-density region.

resources.name: Colchester Transportation Cooperative Limited (CTCL)
resources.description: A community-owned transportation co-operative serving Truro and Colchester County with scheduled shuttle trips and coordinated rural routes to employment, education, health, and shopping hubs. CTCL’s co-op model invites local membership and governance, while operational costs are supported by fares, community fundraising, and sponsorships—delivering the community shuttle cooperative approach in practice.

resources.name: Kings Point-to-Point Transit
resources.description: A community-based non-profit that operates scheduled and demand-responsive shuttles connecting towns across Kings County to key hubs such as hospitals, colleges, workplaces, and markets. While not a formal co-op, it follows the spirit of the solution by engaging local governance, coordinating routes between rural communities and service centres, and sustaining operations through fares, donations, sponsorships, and community partnerships.
resources.address: 14 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

resources.name: Strait Area Transit
resources.description: A community-governed non-profit that delivers fixed-route and shuttle services across the Strait area, linking rural communities to Port Hawkesbury and other hubs for work, study, healthcare, and shopping. It advances the solution’s aims by coordinating inter-community routes and sustaining operations with fare revenue, local sponsorships, and community support, improving regional connectivity for youth and families.
resources.address: 16 Paint Street, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 3J8

solutions.text: Volunteer Driver Networks: Organize vetted volunteer drivers to provide door-to-door rides for seniors, students, and low-income residents for work, medical appointments, and training—coordinated through a simple phone line or web form.

resources.name: Wheels of Hope Transportation Service
resources.description: Wheels of Hope matches vetted volunteer drivers with cancer patients who need door-to-door rides to and from medical appointments and treatments across Nova Scotia. Rides are coordinated through the Canadian Cancer Society’s phone intake and online request process, reducing transportation barriers for low-income and rural residents while ensuring safe, reliable access to care.
resources.address: 5826 South Street, Suite 1, Halifax, NS B3H 1S6

resources.name: Senior Wheels Transportation Program
resources.description: Senior Wheels recruits and screens volunteer drivers to provide affordable, door-to-door transportation for seniors and adults with mobility challenges in the Sackville area. Trips for medical appointments, shopping, and other essential needs are booked through a central phone line, coordinating community volunteers to fill local transportation gaps.
resources.address: 45 Connolly Road, Middle Sackville, NS B4E 1S6

solutions.text: Community Ride‑Share and Carpool Platforms: Launch a hyperlocal carpool matching service (app, Facebook group, or bulletin boards) for regular commutes, events, and school runs, with recognized carpool lanes, priority parking, and employer promotion.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Carpool Program
resources.description: Dalhousie encourages students, staff, and faculty to share rides for daily commutes and events, and designates on‑campus priority carpool stalls for vehicles with two or more registered Dal commuters. The university supports hyperlocal carpool matching through campus communication channels (student portal groups and department lists) and promotes carpooling via its Sustainability Office and Parking Services, aligning with employer-backed incentives like preferred parking.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Carpool Program
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University issues carpool permits for groups of two or more commuters sharing a vehicle and provides reserved, priority carpool parking spaces in campus lots/garages. SMU promotes ride-sharing through Parking Services and sustainability communications and facilitates informal matching via campus channels and student groups to help connect riders for regular commutes and special events.

resources.name: NSCC Carpooling and Preferred Parking
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College campuses encourage carpooling by setting aside preferred carpool stalls for vehicles with multiple NSCC commuters and by promoting shared rides for routine commutes and cross‑campus travel. Campuses use student portals and social media groups to help match riders locally, and promote carpooling as part of their sustainable transportation options to reduce single‑occupancy trips across urban and rural campuses.

solutions.text: Microtransit and Book‑Ahead Demand Services: Run community-managed book-ahead or on-demand minibuses to serve low-density routes on flex schedules—paid by ride, subscription, or municipal subsidy—reducing the need for private cars.

resources.name: Access-A-Bus (Halifax Transit Paratransit)
resources.description: Access-A-Bus provides shared, book-ahead door-to-door service using minibuses for eligible riders across the Halifax Regional Municipality. Trips are scheduled in advance and dispatched dynamically, offering demand-responsive mobility on low-density routes where fixed-route service is less practical, with fares subsidized by the municipality.

resources.name: MusGo Rider (Eastern Shore and Valley-Sheet Harbour)
resources.description: MusGo Rider operates community-managed, pre-booked door-to-door transit along Nova Scotia’s Eastern Shore, using minibuses and vans to connect dispersed rural communities. Riders schedule trips in advance for work, medical, education, and daily needs, with fares set per ride and services supported by local and provincial funding—functioning as true microtransit in low-density areas.

resources.name: Kings Point-to-Point Transit
resources.description: Kings Point-to-Point Transit offers book-ahead, door-to-door shared rides throughout Kings County, coordinating flexible routes based on daily demand. Using accessible minibuses and vans, it fills gaps between towns and rural areas, reducing car dependency by providing affordable, subsidized rides for employment, appointments, and community activities.

resources.name: Strait Area Transit
resources.description: Strait Area Transit runs demand-responsive community transit across the Strait region (including Inverness, Richmond, and Port Hawkesbury), where riders pre-book shared trips on accessible minibuses. The service flexes routing to match daily requests, providing affordable mobility across low-density communities and inter-town connections with support from municipal and provincial partners.
resources.address: 227 Reeves Street, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 2R7

solutions.text: Shared Vehicles and E‑Bike Libraries: Establish community carshare and e-bike lending programs with pickup hubs in villages and campuses; combine membership fees and local grants to make short trips affordable and reduce barriers to mobility.

resources.name: E‑Cargo Bike Library
resources.description: Halifax Tool Library operates a member-based e‑cargo bike lending program that allows residents to borrow electric-assist cargo bikes for errands, school runs, and short urban trips. Bikes are booked and picked up at the Tool Library hub, lowering the cost barrier to trying e‑mobility and reducing car-dependent trips. The program is supported by memberships and local grants/sponsorships, aligning with the solution’s model of community lending to expand affordable mobility options.

resources.name: PARL E‑Bike Lending Program
resources.description: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library lends e‑bikes to cardholders through select branch pickup hubs, enabling residents to try electric cycling for short trips between towns and within communities. The program includes basic safety gear and orientation, and is supported by local partnerships and provincial grants to keep use affordable. By leveraging existing library branches as hubs, it directly implements the e‑bike library model to reduce transportation barriers in rural and small-town Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 182 Dalhousie Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 5E3

resources.name: South Shore Public Libraries E‑Bike Loan Program
resources.description: South Shore Public Libraries offers e‑bikes for short-term loan at multiple branches, using libraries as convenient community pickup hubs for residents across Lunenburg and Queens counties. Backed by community partners and local grants, the program lets users try e‑bikes at little to no cost, encouraging practical, low-emission trips to work, school, and services. This directly advances the e‑bike library component of the solution by expanding affordable, shared mobility in smaller towns and rural areas.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

solutions.text: Mobility Hubs and Multi‑Modal Stations: Create local mobility hubs that combine bike racks, carshare parking, shuttle stops, real-time info boards, and lockers—developed in partnership with municipal planners, businesses, and volunteers.

resources.name: Alderney Ferry Terminal and Bus Terminal Mobility Hub
resources.description: Halifax Transit’s Alderney Ferry Terminal functions as a multi-modal hub, integrating frequent ferry service with an adjacent bus terminal, bike racks, and digital schedule information for seamless transfers between modes. Located within the Alderney Gate complex and next to the waterfront, the site ties together municipal transit, pedestrian connections, and nearby amenities, with coordinated planning between Halifax Transit, HRM facilities, and local businesses to improve last‑mile access.

resources.name: Scotia Square Transit Hub (Downtown Halifax)
resources.description: The downtown Scotia Square Transit Hub concentrates numerous Halifax Transit routes with sheltered platforms, real-time bus information displays, and direct indoor connections to shops and services via the pedway system. The complex includes extensive bike parking on surrounding blocks and carshare parking in the connected parkade, pairing municipal transit infrastructure with private partners to create a practical, all-in-one mobility node for commuters and students.

resources.name: Lunenburg County Lifestyle Centre (LCLC) Transit Hub
resources.description: Bridgewater Transit uses the LCLC as a main transfer point, linking local bus service with ample bike racks, parking, and indoor community amenities that support safe, convenient transfers. The hub is planned and operated by the Town of Bridgewater with partners at the LCLC and nearby businesses, providing posted schedules and wayfinding to connect residents to recreation, employment, and regional services.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

resources.name: Mayflower Mall Transit Transfer Hub
resources.organization: Cape Breton Regional Municipality – Transit Cape Breton
resources.description: Transit Cape Breton’s transfer hub at Mayflower Mall brings together multiple local routes at a single location with shelters, posted schedules, and pedestrian links to indoor amenities. The site offers bike parking on mall grounds and convenient taxi/shuttle pickup points, leveraging a partnership between the municipality and the mall operator to create a practical multi‑modal node for work, school, and shopping trips.
resources.address: 800 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6S9

resources.name: Halifax Stanfield Ground Transportation Centre
resources.description: Halifax Stanfield’s Ground Transportation Centre serves as a regional mobility hub, connecting Halifax Transit’s MetroX service with intercity shuttles, taxis, car rentals, and pedestrian access to the terminal. Coordinated by the airport authority with municipal and private operators, the hub provides wayfinding and real-time travel information in the terminal to streamline transfers between local, regional, and air travel.

solutions.text: Local Employer‑Education Transit Partnerships: Coordinate with employers, colleges, and hospitals to fund dedicated commuter routes, staggered shift transportation, or subsidized passes that keep workers and students connected to work/study.

resources.name: Halifax Transit UPass Program
resources.description: A formal partnership between Halifax Transit and participating post-secondary institutions (including Dalhousie, Saint Mary’s, NSCAD, Mount Saint Vincent, and the University of King’s College) provides a universal, prepaid transit pass for eligible students. Funded through student fees, the UPass offers unlimited access to Halifax Transit buses and ferries, reducing transportation cost barriers and dependence on cars. This directly implements subsidized passes that keep students connected to classes, co-ops, clinical placements, and part-time work across the region.

resources.name: Employer Transit Pass Program (EPass)
resources.description: Halifax Transit partners with public- and private-sector employers to offer discounted monthly transit passes to employees through payroll deduction. By lowering commuting costs and encouraging transit for daily travel, the program helps workers reliably reach job sites across the city without a car. This employer-funded subsidy model directly advances the solution by creating local employer–transit partnerships that keep workers connected to work on regular and shift schedules.

resources.name: Transit Cape Breton – CBU Universal Bus Pass (UPass)
resources.organization: Cape Breton Regional Municipality — Transit Cape Breton
resources.description: Transit Cape Breton and the Cape Breton University student community partner to provide a universal bus pass for CBU students, funded through student fees and aligned with expanded campus-oriented service. The collaboration has supported added capacity and campus-focused trips that move students reliably between Sydney, Glace Bay, and the university. This implements the solution by delivering subsidized, dedicated commuter access so students can reach classes, co-ops, and part-time jobs without needing a car.

resources.name: Acadia Students’ Union UPass (Kings Transit Partnership)
resources.description: The Acadia Students’ Union partners with Kings Transit Authority to provide a universal bus pass for full-time Acadia students, integrated into student fees. The pass offers unlimited travel on Kings Transit routes connecting Wolfville with regional hubs like New Minas and Kentville, enabling dependable trips to campus, co-ops, and local employment. This education–transit partnership directly advances the solution by subsidizing student mobility and linking learners to work and study across the Annapolis Valley.
resources.address: Students’ Union Building, 30 Highland Avenue, Wolfville, NS B4P 2R6

solutions.text: Community Advocacy Coalitions for Intercity Links: Form cross‑municipal citizen groups to lobby provincial and federal governments and private carriers for restored or new intercity bus and air services, presenting consolidated demand data and shared funding proposals.

resources.name: Transport Action Atlantic
resources.organization: Transport Action Atlantic (regional chapter of Transport Action Canada)
resources.description: Transport Action Atlantic is a volunteer, membership-based advocacy coalition spanning Nova Scotia and the other Atlantic provinces that champions better intercity public transportation. They convene citizens, municipal leaders, and operators to produce research and ridership estimates, then lobby provincial and federal governments and private carriers (e.g., VIA Rail, Maritime Bus) for restored or enhanced intercity bus and rail options, presenting consolidated regional demand and cost-sharing proposals.

resources.name: Ecology Action Centre – Transportation Program
resources.description: The Ecology Action Centre’s Transportation Program organizes coalitions of residents, youth, municipalities, and service providers to address intercity mobility gaps in Nova Scotia. Through surveys, community forums, and policy briefs, they compile demand and access data for intercity bus and regional air links and advocate to the Province of Nova Scotia, federal agencies, and private carriers for service restoration and funding partnerships that connect rural communities with urban hubs.

resources.name: NSFM Policy and Advocacy on Community and Intercity Transportation
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Federation of Municipalities coordinates cross‑municipal advocacy on rural and intercity transportation, aggregating data and priorities from member municipalities to present a unified case to the Province of Nova Scotia and the federal government. Through resolutions, submissions, and joint engagement with carriers, NSFM advances proposals for improved intercity bus coverage and regional air connectivity, including shared funding models that link multiple municipalities.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1304, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Rural Transit Fare Subsidy Funds: Establish a community-administered hardship fund to subsidize fares for low-income residents, students, and those needing medical travel; funded by donations, local business contributions, and fundraising events.

resources.name: QEII Patient Assistance Fund
resources.description: The QEII Patient Assistance Fund provides donor-funded support to cover essential costs for low-income patients receiving care at the QEII Health Sciences Centre, including transportation to and from medical appointments. By directly subsidizing travel expenses for individuals facing financial hardship, the fund functions as a community-administered hardship resource that reduces cost barriers to necessary medical travel, aligning with rural fare-subsidy objectives.
resources.address: 5657 Spring Garden Road, Suite 3005, Halifax, NS B3J 3R4

resources.name: IWK Patient and Family Assistance Fund
resources.organization: IWK Health Centre (supported by the IWK Foundation)
resources.description: The IWK Patient and Family Assistance Fund uses charitable donations to help families who face financial hardship with costs related to accessing pediatric and perinatal care, including transportation and travel for medical appointments. This community-supported fund acts as a hardship subsidy for travel, ensuring that families from rural and remote parts of Nova Scotia can afford necessary trips for care.

resources.name: Transportation Services (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Canadian Cancer Society’s transportation program provides subsidized or no-cost rides for people with cancer to attend treatments and related appointments, funded through community donations and corporate contributions. By removing transportation cost barriers—particularly for rural and low-income patients—it operates as a hardship-based fare subsidy that enables essential medical travel across Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Event and School Transport Pooling: Coordinate pooled transport for major community events, sports, and school extracurriculars to reduce single-occupant trips—organized by parent groups, community centres, or event committees.

resources.name: Tiger Patrol
resources.description: Tiger Patrol is the Dalhousie Student Union’s pooled evening shuttle for students, bundling ride requests and circulating to and from campus events, society meetings, practices, and nightlife. By consolidating multiple passengers into shared vans on set routes and on-demand within a defined zone, it reduces single-occupant car trips and improves safe access to extracurriculars and community life.

resources.name: ASU Safety Shuttle
resources.description: The Acadia Students’ Union operates the ASU Safety Shuttle to pool student transportation during evenings and weekends for campus events, rehearsals, practices, and downtown activities. Dispatch groups riders and runs circulating routes between residences, campus venues, and key Wolfville stops, cutting down on parent drop-offs and single-occupant trips while supporting active student life.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Eastern Shore
resources.description: MusGo Rider is a non-profit community transportation co-operative that coordinates shared rides across the Eastern Shore for work, school, and community life. For youth sports, after-school programs, and weekend events, dispatch combines bookings into pooled trips or group charters so teams and clubs travel together, replacing numerous single-occupant vehicle journeys with organized shared transport.
resources.address: 5228 Highway 7, Unit 2, Musquodoboit Harbour, NS B0J 2L0

resources.name: Student Matinee Program
resources.description: Neptune Theatre’s Student Matinee Program organizes group attendance for school classes and youth groups at daytime performances. The theatre coordinates bus access and scheduling and supports schools arranging shared buses, encouraging pooled transportation for cultural outings instead of individual car drop-offs, thereby reducing traffic and emissions while enabling extracurricular arts participation.

solutions.text: Local Mobility Information Platform: Create a single, community-run online and phone resource that aggregates schedules, ride-share opportunities, fares, and real-time updates for all local and regional transport options.

resources.name: Halifax Transit Rider Information and 311
resources.description: Halifax Transit provides a single, public-facing website and 311 phone line that consolidate bus and ferry routes, schedules, fares, service alerts, and real-time departure information. Riders can plan trips online and receive updates through integrated tools (including GTFS-realtime feeds and the Transit app), while 311 offers phone-based trip assistance and accessibility information. This functions as a centralized mobility information platform for the Halifax region, covering multiple local modes (bus and ferry) with web and phone access.

resources.name: Kings Transit Authority – Rider Information
resources.description: Kings Transit Authority operates a regional website and call centre that aggregate route maps, timetables, fares, and service notices for inter-municipal buses across the Annapolis Valley. Riders can access all local and regional service details in one place and call dispatch for assistance with trip planning and connections. This provides a centralized mobility information hub for multiple towns and rural communities in western Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

resources.name: CBRM Transit – Rider Info and Service Alerts
resources.description: Transit Cape Breton (CBRM Transit) maintains an online portal that consolidates bus routes, schedules, fares, and system-wide service alerts for the Cape Breton Regional Municipality. Contact numbers on the site provide phone support for route guidance and real-time service changes. This creates a single access point for local mobility information across the Sydney area and surrounding communities.

resources.name: Bridgewater Transit – Rider Information
resources.description: Bridgewater Transit offers a centralized website with route maps, stop lists, schedules, fares, and rider advisories for the Town of Bridgewater, with contact numbers for phone-based assistance. The platform consolidates all local transit information and links to real-time tools supported by the service. This delivers a community-run information hub that simplifies access to mobility details for residents and visitors on the South Shore.

solutions.text: Community Ferry and Water Taxi Initiatives: In coastal or island communities, develop community-run seasonal ferries or water taxis (chartered, volunteer-led, or cooperative) to improve connectivity for commuters and tourists.

resources.name: Sea Halifax – Harbour Water Taxi
resources.description: Sea Halifax operates a seasonal harbour water taxi that provides on-demand and short-hop connections between key Halifax and Dartmouth waterfront destinations. By offering flexible, small-vessel transport outside fixed bus routes, it improves first/last-mile connectivity for commuters and tourists and reduces car dependency around the harbour.
resources.address: 1751 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S5

resources.name: Halifax Transit Ferry Service (Alderney and Woodside Routes)
resources.description: Halifax Transit runs year-round passenger ferries linking downtown Halifax with Alderney Landing and Woodside in Dartmouth, providing fast cross-harbour commutes that complement bus and active-transportation networks. These ferries reduce road congestion and offer reliable, car-light access to jobs, education, and cultural venues for residents and visitors.

solutions.text: Shared EV Purchasing and Charging Network: Organize group procurement of electric vehicles for community fleets and install shared charging stations at community centres and hubs, supported by local fundraising and municipal incentives.

resources.name: HRM Electric Vehicle Charging Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality is installing and operating EV charging stations at municipal community hubs such as libraries, arenas, and recreation centres, while also procuring EVs for its corporate fleet using bulk purchasing and federal/provincial incentives. These publicly accessible chargers create a shared charging network that community fleets, carshare users, and residents can use, directly supporting the shift away from car dependency by enabling electric shared mobility across the region.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Power EV Fast-Charging Network
resources.description: Nova Scotia Power has deployed a provincewide network of DC fast and Level 2 charging stations located at community centres, libraries, arenas, and municipal lots, funded in part through federal ZEVIP and provincial/municipal contributions. By placing shared chargers at community hubs, the network supports community fleets, carshares, and residents to charge in common locations—an essential backbone for group EV adoption and intercommunity mobility in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1223 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

resources.name: Clean Foundation Community EV Charging (ZEVIP Delivery Program)
resources.description: As a Natural Resources Canada ZEVIP delivery organization in Atlantic Canada, Clean Foundation provides grants and technical support to municipalities and nonprofits across Nova Scotia to install Level 2 chargers at community buildings and hubs (e.g., community centres, rinks, libraries). By bundling multiple sites and coordinating procurement and installation—often alongside local fundraising and municipal incentives—the program builds shared charging networks that serve community fleets and residents.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Electric Community Transit Project
resources.description: MusGo Rider, a rural community transit co-operative on the Eastern Shore, has integrated battery-electric cars into its shared-ride fleet using provincial/federal incentives and community fundraising, and installed Level 2 chargers at community locations it serves. The EVs are dispatched for community trips and the chargers offer shared access when vehicles are not in service, demonstrating a group-procurement approach for a community fleet paired with a shared charging network based at local hubs.

solutions.text: Active Transportation Campaigns and Infrastructure Projects: Mobilize volunteers and local councils to build and maintain safe walking and cycling paths (including snow clearance), host bike-to-work days, and secure small grants for infrastructure that shortens local trips.

resources.name: Halifax Active Transportation Program
resources.description: HRM’s Active Transportation Program plans, builds, and maintains a connected network of sidewalks, multi‑use pathways, and all‑ages-and-abilities bikeways that shorten everyday trips to work, school, and services. The municipality provides year‑round maintenance, including winter snow clearing on priority sidewalks and protected bike lanes, and leverages provincial/federal grants to deliver small but high‑impact connections. The program also partners with community groups to support education and events that encourage walking and cycling.

resources.name: Halifax Bike Week
resources.description: Halifax Bike Week is an annual, week‑long series of events that mobilizes volunteers, businesses, and community groups to host bike‑to‑work days, commuter stations, group rides, and safety workshops. By making cycling visible and convenient, the campaign complements infrastructure projects and encourages residents to shift short local trips from cars to bikes. The municipality coordinates the program in partnership with local cycling organizations and employers to grow everyday riding.

resources.name: Switch: Open Street Sundays
resources.description: Switch temporarily opens streets to people and closes them to car traffic, creating safe, pop‑up walking and cycling routes that demonstrate how active transportation can work for everyday trips. The Ecology Action Centre coordinates volunteers, local councils, and businesses to deliver these events and often helps communities parlay successful pilots into small grants and permanent infrastructure improvements. The program also advances policies and practices—such as winter maintenance priorities—that support year‑round active mobility.

resources.name: Blue Route (Provincial Cycling Network)
resources.description: The Blue Route is a province‑wide cycling network developed by Cycling Nova Scotia that connects communities through on‑road bikeways and multi‑use paths designed for transportation as well as recreation. Working with municipalities and the Province, the program secures cost‑shared funding and delivers incremental projects—such as shoulder paving, protected lanes, and trail links—that create direct, safer routes for short and mid‑length trips. It also provides technical guidance to partners on design and maintenance to support year‑round usability.
resources.address: 5516 Spring Garden Road, 4th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 1G6

resources.name: Bridgewater Active Transportation Program
resources.description: The Town of Bridgewater implements its Active Transportation Plan by building and upgrading sidewalks, multi‑use paths, and safer street crossings that link neighbourhoods with downtown, schools, and the LaHave River trail—reducing the distance and time for local trips. The town hosts annual Bike Week activities, including bike‑to‑work events, and prioritizes winter snow clearing on key pedestrian and cycling corridors. Bridgewater routinely leverages provincial and federal grants (e.g., AT and Connect2‑style funding) to deliver small, high‑impact connections.

solutions.text: Remote Work Hubs and Travel Reduction Programs: Set up local co-working spaces in under-served communities to reduce commuting, supported by municipal wifi, hot-desking fees, and partnerships with employers to formalize remote work options.

resources.name: Volta Co-working and Innovation Hub
resources.description: Volta operates a large, downtown co-working hub with hot desks, dedicated desks, private offices, and meeting rooms supported by reliable high-speed internet and memberships/day passes. Through corporate partnerships and programming that enable remote and hybrid teams, it provides a professional, shared workplace so employees and founders can work locally and reduce daily commuting and intercity travel.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Regus – Purdy’s Wharf Co-working
resources.description: Regus offers flexible co-working with hot-desking, dedicated desks, private offices, and meeting rooms on a membership or day-pass basis, providing enterprise-grade connectivity and amenities. Corporate accounts let employers formalize remote and hybrid options, allowing staff to work from a professional hub close to home to cut car trips and cross-town commuting.
resources.address: 1959 Upper Water Street, Suite 1300, Halifax, NS B3J 3N2

resources.name: Regus – Metropolitan Place (Dartmouth) Co-working
resources.description: This Regus site in Dartmouth provides hot desks, dedicated desks, private offices, and meeting rooms with high-speed internet on flexible, fee-based plans. By giving workers on Halifax’s east side an accessible professional workspace and enabling employer-supported hybrid arrangements, it reduces bridge traffic and regional commuting.
resources.address: 99 Wyse Road, Suite 1100, Dartmouth, NS B3A 4S5

resources.name: Acadia LaunchBox Co-working & Startup Space
resources.description: LaunchBox provides free co-working space, meeting rooms, and reliable Wi-Fi for students and community entrepreneurs in the Annapolis Valley, with programs and partnerships that connect founders and local employers. By enabling remote work and startup activity in Wolfville, it reduces the need for long trips to urban centres and supports formalized remote/hybrid options close to home.

resources.name: Halifax Central Library – Public Wi-Fi & Workspaces
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Central branch offers free municipal Wi-Fi, extensive open seating, bookable study/meeting rooms, and quiet work areas suited to remote work and study. As a no-cost, community-based workspace with strong connectivity, it lets residents work locally and avoid unnecessary car trips, supporting flexible and hybrid work without a traditional commute.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Community‑Run Regional Air/Charter Advocacy: Coordinate businesses, tourism groups, and municipalities to subsidize seasonal or on-demand air services (charters) and negotiate with carriers for better schedules, using pooled demand and local marketing.

resources.name: Air Service Development Program
resources.description: Halifax Stanfield International Airport’s Air Service Development team works with Discover Halifax, Tourism Nova Scotia, Halifax Partnership, universities, and major employers to pool market data and demand signals, co-fund route marketing, and negotiate improved schedules and seasonal service with airlines. The airport also collaborates on group and on-demand charter opportunities tied to tourism seasons, conferences, and workforce mobility, effectively aligning community partners and marketing resources to sustain and expand air links.

resources.name: Sydney Air Service Development Partnership
resources.organization: J.A. Douglas McCurdy Sydney Airport Authority
resources.description: The J.A. Douglas McCurdy Sydney Airport Authority coordinates with Destination Cape Breton Association, the Cape Breton Partnership, Cape Breton Regional Municipality, and local tourism operators to pool demand, co-invest in marketing, and secure seasonal and year-round air services to key hubs. The partnership also facilitates charter options for events and workforce travel, using community-backed promotion and negotiated schedules to improve connectivity for Cape Breton residents, students, and visitors.
resources.address: 280 Silver Dart Way, Sydney, NS B1L 1A5

obstacles.title: Digital Infrastructure Inequities
obstacles.description: Rural and remote communities face slower, less reliable, and more expensive broadband, hindering remote work, online learning, and digital business.

solutions.text: Community Broadband Cooperative: Form a locally governed cooperative to plan, finance and operate broadband infrastructure (fiber, fixed wireless) so residents and businesses have ownership, lower long-term costs, and democratic control over service priorities.

resources.name: Chebucto Community Net (CCN)
resources.description: Chebucto Community Net is a member-governed, non-profit community internet service provider that offers affordable internet access, email, and web hosting to residents and community groups in the Halifax region. Operated by the Chebucto Community Net Society, CCN implements the community broadband model by keeping ownership and governance local, using a democratic membership structure to set service priorities and reinvesting revenues into community-oriented digital access and literacy. This community control helps maintain lower long-term costs and aligns service with local needs.
resources.address: Room 006, Chase Building, 6136 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: Valley Community Fibre Network (VCFN)
resources.description: The Valley Community Fibre Network is a community-owned, not-for-profit dark-fibre backbone linking municipalities, towns, educational institutions, and health facilities across the Annapolis Valley. Owned and governed by local public partners, it enables open-access leasing to local ISPs and businesses, lowering the cost of backhaul so rural last‑mile service can be extended affordably. By keeping infrastructure ownership and decision-making in the community, VCFN reflects the cooperative broadband model—prioritizing local needs and long-term, community-benefit reinvestment.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: East Hants Rural Internet Project
resources.description: The Municipality of East Hants leads a community broadband build that invests in local towers and fibre backbones to extend reliable, high-speed service to underserved rural communities. The municipality plans and finances core infrastructure and partners with service providers for last‑mile delivery while retaining public ownership and oversight to ensure affordability and community priorities. This locally governed approach mirrors a community broadband cooperative by centering community control, long-term cost management, and equitable access for residents and businesses.

resources.name: Pictou County Rural Broadband Initiative
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Pictou
resources.description: Pictou County coordinates planning and investment in community broadband infrastructure to connect rural areas with high-speed service, including fibre routes and wireless sites developed in partnership with the province and service providers. By using public stewardship and local decision-making to guide build‑out and service priorities, the County emphasizes community ownership principles to reduce long-term costs and improve reliability for residents, entrepreneurs, and farms. This initiative operationalizes the community broadband model by aligning infrastructure investment with democratically set local needs.

solutions.text: Municipal / Regional Broadband Partnership: Work with municipal councils and neighbouring communities to jointly contract ISPs or build municipally owned networks using shared rights-of-way, increasing bargaining power and enabling economies of scale.

resources.name: Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative (I4NS)
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia’s I4NS aggregates municipal demand and co-invests with internet service providers to extend broadband to rural and remote communities across the province. The program works directly with municipal councils and neighboring communities to map underserved roads, coordinate permitting and access to shared rights-of-way, and structure joint procurements that leverage regional scale. By bundling multiple communities into larger build packages, I4NS increases bargaining power and enables economies of scale for fibre and fixed wireless deployments.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 301, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Rural High-Speed Internet Project (East Hants)
resources.description: The Municipality of East Hants leads a multi‑phase rural broadband initiative that partners with ISPs to expand fibre and fixed wireless service to underserved communities. The municipality issues joint procurements, contributes capital funding, and leverages municipal rights‑of‑way and towers to reduce build costs and accelerate timelines. By coordinating work across multiple rural communities, the project increases bargaining power and achieves economies of scale for last‑mile connectivity.

resources.name: Guysborough County High-Speed Internet Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Guysborough (MODG)
resources.description: MODG’s county‑wide broadband program partners with regional ISPs to deliver fibre and fixed wireless to low‑density communities throughout Guysborough County. The municipality coordinates rights‑of‑way access, contributes capital to backbones and last‑mile builds, and bundles multiple rural communities into joint contracts to make projects economically viable. This regional approach increases negotiating leverage and leverages shared infrastructure to reduce per‑premise costs.

resources.name: MODL Internet Improvement Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg coordinates with neighboring municipalities and ISPs to extend fibre‑to‑the‑home and fixed wireless service to rural roads across Lunenburg County. Through cost‑sharing agreements, joint RFPs, and streamlined access to municipal rights‑of‑way, the program reduces deployment costs and shortens permitting timelines. By aggregating multiple communities into larger build areas, MODL increases bargaining power and enables scalable regional network expansion.

solutions.text: Public Wi‑Fi Hubs and Hotspots: Create free or low-cost public Wi‑Fi at libraries, community centres, municipal buildings and parks to ensure immediate basic access for students, jobseekers and entrepreneurs.

resources.name: Halifax Public Libraries – Free Wi‑Fi
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries provides free, open Wi‑Fi at all branches, including the Halifax Central Library, enabling immediate internet access without a library card. By offering reliable connectivity in a public community hub with study spaces and meeting rooms, the service supports students, jobseekers, and entrepreneurs who need to attend online classes, apply for jobs, conduct research, or run digital business tasks.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library – Free Public Wi‑Fi
resources.description: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library offers free public Wi‑Fi at all branch locations across Pictou and Antigonish Counties, including the New Glasgow Library. These library-based hotspots provide dependable, no-cost internet access in small towns and rural areas, helping residents complete schoolwork, search and apply for jobs, access government services, and support small-business and entrepreneurial activities.
resources.address: 182 Dalhousie Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 4M7

resources.name: Cape Breton Regional Library – Free Public Wi‑Fi
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library provides free Wi‑Fi at all branches, including the McConnell Library in Sydney, creating accessible internet hubs for community members. The service enables students, workers, and entrepreneurs to get online quickly for research, online learning, teleconferencing, job applications, and digital business needs, reducing the impact of limited home broadband in rural and remote communities.

resources.name: Annapolis Valley Regional Library – Free Wi‑Fi
resources.description: Annapolis Valley Regional Library offers free, open Wi‑Fi at every branch, including the Kentville Library, providing an immediate connectivity option for those without fast or affordable home internet. As community hubs with seating and workspaces, these branches support online classes, resume building and job applications, virtual meetings, and day-to-day digital tasks for local learners and small-business owners.

solutions.text: Community Mesh and Fixed Wireless Networks: Deploy low-cost mesh or community-managed fixed wireless links (on towers or tall buildings) to connect clusters of homes and businesses where wired fibre is not yet available.

resources.name: Eastlink Wireless Home Internet (Rural Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Eastlink deploys fixed wireless internet across rural Nova Scotia using a network of towers and rooftop or mast-mounted customer equipment to deliver broadband to clusters of homes where fibre is not yet available. By leveraging tall buildings, existing towers, and new rural sites, the service creates reliable last-mile links that support remote work, learning, and small business operations in underserved communities.

resources.name: Bell Wireless Home Internet – Nova Scotia
resources.description: Bell’s Wireless Home Internet provides fixed wireless broadband to rural and remote parts of Nova Scotia using LTE/5G radio links from local towers to outdoor antennas installed at customer premises. This approach extends high-speed connectivity to clusters of households and businesses that are beyond the current fibre footprint, improving access to digital services while fibre builds progress.
resources.address: 1601 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3P6

resources.name: Seaside Wireless Rural Internet
resources.description: Seaside Communications operates a rural fixed wireless network in Cape Breton and eastern Nova Scotia, using hilltop towers and relay sites to connect small and remote communities. Subscriber radios mounted on homes and businesses create point‑to‑multipoint links to these sites, delivering affordable broadband where wired options are limited and directly addressing digital infrastructure inequities.

resources.name: East Hants Rural Broadband Project
resources.description: The Municipality of East Hants coordinated the deployment of new wireless infrastructure (including multi-use towers on municipal and partner lands) to host ISP fixed wireless equipment serving rural communities. This project extends broadband to clusters of homes and businesses not yet reached by fibre, using tower-based radio links to improve speeds and reliability for residents and entrepreneurs.

solutions.text: Demand Aggregation Campaign: Organize residents and businesses to register demand and petition ISPs or funding programs, creating a clear business case for providers and prioritizing underserved routes.

resources.name: Rural Internet Project – Internet Interest Registry
resources.description: The Municipality of East Hants runs an ongoing Internet Interest Registry where residents and businesses submit their civic address and service needs. The municipality aggregates this demand data and shares it with Internet Service Providers and provincial programs to demonstrate viable build areas, helping providers prioritize underserved routes and secure funding for network expansion.

resources.name: Kings County Broadband Internet Project – Interest Form
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings collects expressions of interest from households and businesses seeking better internet service through a public interest form and surveys. Aggregated demand, mapped by road and community, is used to petition ISPs and align with provincial funding opportunities, supplying a clear business case to prioritize last-mile builds in unserved and underserved areas.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: MODL Internet Improvements – Internet Interest Form
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg (MODL) invites residents and businesses to register their need for reliable broadband via an Internet Interest Form. MODL compiles these registrations to create demand maps and road-by-road lists that are presented to ISPs and leveraged in partnership with provincial programs, accelerating provider commitments and prioritizing routes with concentrated demand.

resources.name: Inverness County Broadband Project – Internet Interest Registry
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Inverness
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Inverness operates a broadband interest registry and community outreach to capture where residents and businesses lack adequate service. The municipality aggregates and shares this demand with providers and provincial initiatives, strengthening the business case for investment and prioritizing underserved routes across rural communities.
resources.address: 375 Main Street, Port Hood, NS B0E 2W0

solutions.text: Local Broadband Mapping and Speed Testing: Collect and publish neighbourhood-level coverage and speed data (speedtests, service gaps) to inform planning, strengthen funding applications, and hold providers accountable.

resources.name: Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative — Internet Speed Test & Coverage Map
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia operates a province-wide speed test and coverage mapping platform that collects resident-submitted speed tests and availability reports and visualizes them at the community and neighbourhood level. The aggregated data identifies service gaps, informs planning and investment decisions, strengthens provincial and federal funding applications, and helps track provider commitments and performance over time.
resources.address: 1751 Lower Water Street, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3J 1S5

resources.name: Antigonish County Internet Speed Test
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Antigonish
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Antigonish invites residents to complete standardized internet speed tests and report service availability, then maps the results to the road and neighbourhood level. The municipality uses this evidence to pinpoint underserved areas, support funding proposals for rural broadband builds, and engage ISPs with concrete performance data to improve service and accountability.
resources.address: 285 Beech Hill Road, Antigonish, NS B2G 0B4

resources.name: East Hants Internet Speed Test and Broadband Mapping
resources.description: East Hants collects local speed test results and service reports from residents to build detailed connectivity maps across its rural communities. The dataset is used to identify service gaps, prioritize investment areas, and provide evidence for provincial/federal broadband funding applications, while also giving the municipality leverage to hold providers accountable for improvements.

resources.name: MODL Internet Project — Community Speed Testing and Mapping
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg runs an internet project that encourages residents to perform speed tests and submit availability details, compiling the results into neighbourhood-level maps and dashboards. These insights guide where the municipality targets new builds and partnerships, bolster grant applications, and provide a public benchmark to assess ISP performance and coverage claims.

solutions.text: Digital Literacy and Support Programs: Offer workshops, drop-in clinics and peer mentoring on digital skills, device setup, cybersecurity and remote work tools at libraries, schools and community centres.

resources.name: Tech Help
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries offers free Tech Help through drop-in clinics and bookable one-on-one sessions where staff and volunteers assist with device setup, email, videoconferencing (Zoom/Teams), cloud tools, and basic troubleshooting. They also run beginner-friendly digital literacy workshops covering online safety, privacy, and practical tools for remote work and learning, delivered across urban and suburban branches to increase access.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Tech Help @ the Library
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library hosts ongoing one-on-one tech tutoring and small-group workshops that help residents set up smartphones, tablets, and laptops; use email, video meetings, and cloud collaboration tools; and learn online safety basics. Delivered at branches like the McConnell Library, these drop-in and appointment-based services support remote work, online learning, and digital participation across rural and urban Cape Breton.

resources.name: Tech Help
resources.description: Cumberland Public Libraries provides free technology help sessions and workshops at branches such as the Four Fathers Memorial Library, guiding patrons through device setup, account creation, Zoom/Teams, and productivity tools. Staff and volunteers offer patient, one-on-one support and basic cybersecurity guidance, enabling residents—including those in rural communities—to engage in remote work, online learning, and e-services.

resources.name: Tech Help (One-on-One Technology Support)
resources.description: Annapolis Valley Regional Library runs one-on-one technology help and beginner workshops at branches like the Wolfville Memorial Library, covering smartphones, tablets, email, video calls, and cloud-based tools. Sessions emphasize practical digital skills and online safety, helping residents adopt remote work platforms and confidently access government, education, and health services online.

resources.name: Digital Skills for Life and Work
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers instructor-led digital literacy training for newcomers, including device setup, secure internet use, email, cloud storage, and videoconferencing platforms used for remote work and online services. Through workshops and hands-on coaching at their Mumford Road location, the program builds confidence with cybersecurity basics and practical tools required for job search, employment, and virtual community participation.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Device Access and Refurbishment Initiatives: Run donation and refurbishment programs to provide low-cost laptops, tablets and mobile hotspots to students, jobseekers and low-income households.

resources.name: Computers for Schools Plus (Nova Scotia)
resources.organization: Computers for Success Canada, delivered in Nova Scotia with Nova Scotia Community College
resources.description: Computers for Schools Plus (CFS+) in Nova Scotia refurbishes donated computers and related equipment from government, businesses, and the public, and redistributes them at low or no cost. Youth interns and technicians wipe, repair, and upgrade devices, which are then provided to schools, libraries, non-profits, and eligible individuals, supporting students, jobseekers, and low-income households with reliable hardware for online learning and work.

resources.name: ISANS Digital Access: Device Lending & Donations
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS accepts donated laptops and tablets, refurbishes and configures them, and provides devices to newcomers and refugees who face financial barriers to technology access. The program also maintains a lending pool of devices and connectivity supports so clients can attend online language classes, job search workshops, and settlement services, directly reducing digital inequities for low-income households.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: WiFi2Go (Mobile Hotspot Lending)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ WiFi2Go program lends portable Wi‑Fi hotspots so patrons without home internet can get online for school, job searching, telehealth, and essential services. The library system also lends Chromebooks, pairing devices with connectivity to lower barriers faced by students and low-income households across urban and rural branches.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Wi-Fi Hotspot Lending Program
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library lends mobile Wi‑Fi hotspots to cardholders, enabling internet access at home in communities where broadband is unreliable or unaffordable. By providing portable connectivity for remote learning, job applications, and online services, the program helps reduce digital access gaps for students, jobseekers, and low-income families across Cape Breton.

solutions.text: Local Co‑Working and Telework Hubs: Convert unused municipal or community spaces into affordable co‑working hubs with reliable internet, meeting rooms and mentorship to retain and attract young professionals.

resources.name: Volta
resources.description: Volta is Atlantic Canada’s largest innovation hub, offering affordable co-working desks and offices with reliable high-speed internet, shared meeting rooms, and event space. It pairs workspace with mentorship, programming, and investor/corporate connections, helping young professionals and founders work remotely, build companies, and stay in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: CEED Co-Working Space
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED operates a co-working hub that provides reliable fibre internet, bookable meeting rooms, and flexible desks alongside access to business advisors and entrepreneurship training. The space supports remote workers and early-stage founders with affordable infrastructure and mentorship, enabling youth to launch and grow ventures while remaining in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Yarmouth Innovation Hub
resources.description: IGNITE’s Yarmouth hub offers modern co-working space with dependable high-speed internet, meeting rooms, and collaboration areas for entrepreneurs, students, and remote professionals in a rural community. Through mentorship, workshops, and partnerships with industry and post-secondary institutions, it helps talent thrive locally and reduces the need to relocate for digital work.

resources.name: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: COVE repurposes a former federal marine facility into a collaborative waterfront campus that includes co-working space, labs, and shared meeting rooms with enterprise-grade connectivity. Startups and professionals gain access to mentorship, testing infrastructure, and industry networks, enabling telework and innovation in Nova Scotia’s ocean sector.

solutions.text: Partner with Colleges, Universities and Hospitals: Leverage anchor institutions for backbone connections, research partnerships, student placements and shared infrastructure to extend high-speed links into the community.

resources.name: Chebucto Community Net
resources.description: Chebucto Community Net is a non-profit community internet service that is hosted within Dalhousie University, leveraging the university’s backbone connectivity and facilities as an anchor institution to deliver reliable online access, email, and hosting to residents and community groups. By sharing university infrastructure and technical expertise, it extends high-speed connectivity and digital services beyond campus into the broader community. The organization also engages students and volunteers in operations and projects, creating experiential learning while supporting inclusive digital access.
resources.address: Room 006, Chase Building, 6136 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: eduroam at Halifax Public Libraries
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries partners with local post-secondary institutions and CANARIE’s research and education network to provide eduroam Wi‑Fi at library branches, allowing students, researchers, and staff from universities and colleges (e.g., Dalhousie, Saint Mary’s, NSCC) to securely connect using their campus credentials. This leverages the library’s high-capacity network and university authentication infrastructure to extend secure, high-speed access into community spaces beyond campus. The initiative demonstrates how anchor institutions share infrastructure to improve reliable connectivity for learners and researchers across the city and region.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Advocacy and Policy Campaigns: Mobilize residents, businesses and community groups to press municipal, provincial and federal governments for targeted investments, better regulation and service standards for rural broadband.

resources.name: Federation of Nova Scotia Municipalities
resources.description: The Federation of Nova Scotia Municipalities (NSFM) leads coordinated advocacy on broadband and cellular connectivity on behalf of the province’s towns and rural municipalities. NSFM mobilizes councils, local businesses, and residents to document service gaps, pass policy resolutions, and lobby provincial and federal governments for targeted investments, stronger service standards, and regulatory improvements that benefit rural and remote communities.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1304, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Nova Scotia Federation of Agriculture
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Federation of Agriculture (NSFA) advocates for reliable, affordable rural broadband as essential infrastructure for farms and rural enterprises. NSFA gathers data from producers, engages rural communities, and presses provincial and federal governments and regulators for targeted broadband investments, better service standards, and policies that close connectivity gaps impacting on-farm operations, remote learning, and rural businesses.
resources.address: 60 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: Municipality of the County of Cumberland – Rural Internet Advocacy
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Cumberland
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Cumberland mobilizes residents and businesses through surveys, speed tests, and public meetings to document internet gaps and advocate for solutions. Using this evidence, the municipality lobbies provincial and federal programs for targeted broadband investments and engages providers and regulators to improve service standards across rural communities.
resources.address: 1395 Blair Lake Road, Upper Nappan, NS B4H 3Y4

solutions.text: Community Seed Fund and Grant-Writing Team: Create a local fund and volunteer grant-writing group to match provincial/federal broadband grants and pay feasibility studies, engineering designs, or initial infrastructure costs.

resources.name: Fast-Track Internet for Lunenburg County
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg created a local broadband capital fund and partnered with internet service providers to leverage provincial and federal programs (e.g., the Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative and Universal Broadband Fund). A municipal project team coordinates grant applications, feasibility studies, and engineering designs, and uses seed funding to cover early make-ready work and initial infrastructure so projects can qualify for larger external grants.

resources.name: Colchester County Rural High-Speed Internet Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: Colchester County established a dedicated broadband investment fund to seed last‑mile and backbone projects and to match provincial/federal broadband grants. The County’s internal team and consulting partners prepare feasibility assessments, engineering designs, and grant applications, enabling rural communities to secure external funding while covering early-stage costs locally.

resources.name: Cumberland Rural Internet Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Cumberland
resources.description: The Municipality of Cumberland set up a community broadband fund to accelerate rural connectivity and provide matching dollars for provincial/federal programs. A municipal broadband working group coordinates with ISPs and community stakeholders to develop feasibility studies and engineering designs, and prepares competitive grant applications to unlock larger infrastructure investments.
resources.address: 1395 Blair Lake Road, Upper Nappan, NS B4H 3Y4

resources.name: Pictou County Rural Internet Project
resources.description: Pictou County created a local broadband financing program to act as seed/match funding for provincial and federal broadband grants and to cover the costs of preliminary engineering and feasibility work. The County convenes a project team that works with partner ISPs and community representatives to write grant proposals and sequence early infrastructure investments so rural areas can qualify for larger external funding.

solutions.text: Local ISP Incubation and Bidding Support: Help local entrepreneurs or regional ISPs with business planning, technical mentoring and cooperative buying of equipment so new providers can enter the market or expand services.

resources.name: Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative (INSI)
resources.description: INSI is the province’s broadband build-out program that partners with local and regional ISPs to extend high-speed service in underserved communities. Through open RFPs, technical due diligence, and project management support, the program helps smaller providers compete for projects, refine business plans, and navigate permitting and design. By aggregating demand and co-investing in shared backbone and last‑mile infrastructure, INSI effectively reduces equipment and deployment costs so local ISPs can enter new markets or scale service.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Business Development Program (Nova Scotia)
resources.organization: Atlantic Canada Opportunities Agency (ACOA) – Nova Scotia
resources.description: ACOA’s Business Development Program provides advisory services and funding that help SMEs—including local and regional internet providers—develop business plans, improve financial readiness, and prepare competitive bids for broadband expansion opportunities. The program can support technology adoption and, where applicable, collaborative projects that enable group purchasing of network equipment or shared infrastructure among community partners. This reduces barriers to entry and helps emerging ISPs scale sustainably in rural and remote areas.
resources.address: 5151 George Street, Suite 1400, Halifax, NS B3J 3E1

resources.name: Colchester County Rural Internet Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: The Municipality supports broadband expansion by working directly with local and regional ISPs on planning, permitting, and access to municipal assets such as tower sites and rights‑of‑way. Staff provide coordination and technical support during proposal development and procurement, helping smaller providers qualify for provincial/federal programs and expand into rural communities. The County also co-invests in shared infrastructure where feasible, lowering equipment and backhaul costs for participating ISPs.

resources.name: Rural Internet and Connectivity Support (Municipal Toolkit and Working Group)
resources.description: NSFM convenes municipalities and stakeholders to share procurement templates, policy guidance, and technical best practices that help communities partner with local ISPs on broadband builds. Through its working groups and resources, NSFM facilitates collaborative approaches—such as joint RFPs and shared infrastructure agreements—that make it easier for smaller providers to bid on projects and reduce equipment and deployment costs. This practical support helps rural Nova Scotia communities attract and scale locally rooted internet services.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1304, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Satellite and Alternative Connectivity Assistance: Coordinate community sign-up drives and technical support for reliable satellite, low-earth-orbit or other alternative services where terrestrial options are limited, and negotiate group discounts where possible.

resources.name: Starlink Equipment Rebate Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Guysborough
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Guysborough offers a rebate to help residents and small businesses in underserved rural areas cover the upfront cost of Starlink (LEO satellite) hardware, enabling reliable connectivity where wired options are limited. Municipal staff provide information sessions and one-on-one assistance to help people compare plans, complete sign‑ups, and coordinate installations, and they liaise with providers to consolidate local demand and improve service availability.
