resources.name: Rural Internet Equipment Rebate
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Cumberland
resources.description: Cumberland County supports households without adequate wired service by offering a rebate toward the purchase and installation of satellite/LEO equipment such as Starlink, helping overcome the cost barrier in remote areas. The program includes staff support to verify eligibility, guide residents through provider selection and sign‑up, and coordinate with vendors on coverage questions—streamlining uptake of alternative connectivity where terrestrial options are lacking.
resources.address: 1395 Blair Lake Road, Upper Nappan, NS B4H 3Y4

resources.name: Community LEO/Satellite Connectivity Solutions
resources.description: ROCK Networks works with Nova Scotia municipalities, Mi’kmaq communities, and local organizations to deploy low‑earth‑orbit (LEO) and other satellite solutions in hard‑to‑serve areas. They organize demand‑aggregation and community sign‑up support, provide turnkey installation and technical assistance, and negotiate group procurements or bulk pricing with satellite providers—accelerating reliable connectivity where fibre or cable builds are not feasible.
resources.address: 137 Venture Run, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0L9

resources.name: Community Internet Access and Alternative Connectivity Support
resources.description: Chebucto Community Net is a community‑run ISP that provides low‑cost access and personal technical support, helping Nova Scotians evaluate and sign up for alternative connectivity options—including satellite and fixed‑wireless—when wired service is not available. Through one‑on‑one assistance and volunteer-led clinics, they help residents choose appropriate plans, set up equipment and accounts, and troubleshoot connections, effectively coordinating grassroots sign‑up and support for alternative services.
resources.address: Room 006, Chase Building, 6135 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

solutions.text: Resiliency and Power Backup Projects: Install generator or battery backup at key public connectivity nodes (libraries, town halls, health centres) to keep communications and telework capabilities online during outages.

resources.name: HRM Comfort Centres Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality operates a network of comfort centres in libraries, community centres, and other municipal facilities that are equipped with standby generators or backup power. During storms and extended outages, these centres provide heat, device charging, and free public Wi‑Fi so residents can maintain communications and telework while their homes are without power. HRM prioritizes and maintains backup power at these public connectivity nodes to keep internet services available when the grid is down.

resources.name: CBRM Comfort Centres
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Municipality coordinates generator-equipped comfort centres in municipal buildings, libraries, and community/volunteer fire halls to support residents during power outages. These locations offer public Wi‑Fi, device charging, and space to work or study online, ensuring continuity of communications and telework in emergencies. The municipality maintains permanent generators or generator hookups at priority sites to keep connectivity available when utility power is lost.

resources.name: Colchester County Comfort Centres Network
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: The Municipality of Colchester designates and supports a network of comfort centres—often located in libraries, community centres, and fire halls—that have backup generators to remain operational during outages. These centres provide free public Wi‑Fi, charging stations, and a safe place for residents to stay connected for work, learning, and essential communications. The municipality invests in and maintains standby power at these public connectivity nodes to increase digital resiliency in rural and small communities.

obstacles.title: Skills Alignment and Work-Integrated Learning Gaps
obstacles.description: Training, co-ops, apprenticeships, and career guidance don’t always match employer demand across trades, tech, health, and creative sectors.

solutions.text: Community–Education–Employer Advisory Councils: Create local advisory councils (by town/region and by sector) that meet quarterly to align curriculum, co-op placements and apprenticeship spots with employer needs in trades, tech, health and the arts, and to coordinate funding and schedules across schools, colleges and employers.

resources.name: Program Advisory Committees (PACs)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College maintains Program Advisory Committees for each program and campus, composed of local employers, community representatives, and faculty. These sector-based councils meet regularly to advise on curriculum updates, equipment needs, and to coordinate co-op, work-integrated learning, and apprenticeship pathways so training aligns with regional labour market demand in trades, tech, health, and the arts. PAC input also informs program scheduling and partnerships, helping the college and employers align timelines and leverage funding for placements and apprentices.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.organization: Construction Association of Nova Scotia (in partnership with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and the Nova Scotia Department of Education & Early Childhood Development)
resources.description: BFY is a province-wide initiative that brings together high schools, the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, NSCC, and construction employers to place Grade 10–12 students in paid summer work terms linked to skilled trades careers. Regional employer–education committees recruit hosts, match students, and coordinate orientation, safety training, and placement schedules—creating a standing forum that aligns classroom learning with real apprenticeship pathways and employer needs. The program also links hours toward apprenticeship credit and helps align resources and funding between schools and industry.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Learners & Teachers (Interprofessional Practice & Learning)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Learners & Teachers team partners with universities and colleges to plan and schedule clinical placements across hospitals and community sites. Through discipline-specific provincial committees and ongoing employer–educator advisory meetings, they align curricula with practice requirements and coordinate placement capacity, timelines, and preceptor supports. This sector-based structure ensures health programs and employers jointly plan work-integrated learning so that student placements and graduate skills match system staffing needs.
resources.address: 7001 Mumford Road, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3L 4N9

resources.name: Faculty of Computer Science External Advisory Council
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Faculty of Computer Science convenes an external advisory council of industry leaders, community partners, and alumni to ensure programs reflect evolving needs in the tech sector. The council provides direct input on curriculum changes, co-op and internship design, and project-based learning, and helps coordinate employer participation and recruitment cycles with the academic calendar. This standing, sector-specific forum keeps employers, educators, and students aligned so work-integrated learning opportunities and graduate skills track real demand.

solutions.text: Community Apprenticeship Hubs & Micro‑Employer Consortia: Form community hubs that aggregate small and mid‑sized employers to sponsor shared apprenticeships and co‑op placements so smaller businesses can jointly host, mentor and rotate trainees across complementary worksites.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY is a province-wide construction co-op program that centralizes recruitment, safety training, and matching of high school students with member companies across the construction sector. By operating through a hub at CANS in partnership with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and school boards, BFY aggregates many small and mid-sized contractors to jointly host placements; where projects are short or seasonal, students can complete hours across different employers in the consortium. This shared model lowers the onboarding burden on small firms while giving youth multi-site experience across complementary trades.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: COVE Workforce and Industry Internship Programs
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE acts as an industry hub for Nova Scotia’s ocean technology cluster, coordinating internships, co-ops, and student projects with a network of small and mid-sized ocean companies. The hub model pools dozens of SMEs so they can jointly host and mentor learners, and in some cases sequence students across multiple firms to build complementary skills (e.g., marine electronics, robotics, and fabrication). COVE manages outreach, matching, and shared supports, enabling micro-employers to participate in work-integrated learning they could not support alone.

resources.name: NSCC Work-Integrated Learning (WIL) and Co-op
resources.description: NSCC operates a province-wide WIL hub that connects students from applied programs (IT, trades, health, creative industries, and more) to hundreds of SMEs and community organizations across Nova Scotia. The college aggregates small employers, structures shared or split co-op terms where needed, and handles screening, scheduling, and supervision frameworks so multiple micro-employers can sequentially host a single student to cover complementary tasks and competencies. This coordinated approach aligns training with employer demand while letting small firms participate in co-ops without bearing the full placement on their own.

resources.name: NSTHRC Apprenticeship and Tourism HR Programs
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Tourism Human Resource Council (operated by the Tourism Industry Association of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Tourism Human Resource Council coordinates apprenticeship pathways (e.g., Cook) and experiential learning partnerships across independent restaurants, hotels, and tourism operators, most of which are small employers. Acting as a sector hub, NSTHRC standardizes onboarding and training resources, connects learners to multiple kitchens and properties, and helps apprentices complete hours and competencies through placements that can span several member employers. This consortium model enables micro-employers to share mentorship and provide broader, rotating experience aligned with industry needs.

solutions.text: Local Work‑Integrated Learning Brokerage Service: Set up a community brokerage (municipal or non‑profit) that matches students with short placements, coordinates insurance and payroll, and handles onboarding paperwork so schools and employers face fewer barriers to offering placements.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship Program
resources.description: Clean Foundation brokers short-term paid internships by recruiting host organizations across Nova Scotia, matching high school and post-secondary students to roles in the clean economy, and providing orientation and training. The program streamlines onboarding paperwork and reporting, and in many cases acts as the employer of record to manage payroll, stipends, and insurance/WSIB-WCB coverage so schools and employers face fewer administrative barriers. This centralized coordination enables more employers to offer quality placements with reduced risk and overhead.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth
resources.description: This province-wide program brokers summer work placements for high school students in the construction sector by matching learners with vetted employers and coordinating safety training (e.g., WHMIS, Fall Protection) and required certifications. It centralizes onboarding paperwork and coordinates workers’ compensation coverage and risk management in partnership with schools and industry, significantly reducing administrative barriers for employers and educators. The brokerage approach enables short, skills-aligned placements that help students explore trades careers while meeting industry demand.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Learner Placement Services
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health centrally coordinates clinical and non-clinical student placements across hospitals and community sites, matching learners with supervisors and departments based on program needs. The service manages onboarding requirements (e.g., immunizations, background checks, confidentiality and OHS training) and ensures appropriate liability/insurance coverage through affiliation agreements, easing the administrative load on schools and host units. By brokering placements and standardizing paperwork, it expands access to work-integrated learning in the health sector.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: Management Career Services Co-op Program
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Management Career Services brokers co-op and internship placements by sourcing opportunities from employers, matching students, and supporting both parties through the full placement lifecycle. The office standardizes agreements, manages learning outcomes, provides employer toolkits, and coordinates required insurance and compliance paperwork with the university, reducing hiring friction for organizations of all sizes. This brokerage model enables short, skills-aligned placements across business, analytics, public administration, and tech-adjacent roles.

solutions.text: Sector Micro‑credential Pathways: Develop short, stackable micro‑credentials co‑designed by local employers and post‑secondary providers for in‑demand skills (e.g., marine tech, health aides, digital media) that count toward certifications or apprenticeships.

resources.name: NSCC MicroCredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College offers short, stackable micro-credentials co-designed with Nova Scotia employers across sectors such as oceans/marine technology, health care support, IT, and construction. These industry-validated badges can be combined to build pathways that ladder into NSCC certificates and diplomas or prepare learners for recognized industry certifications. In several trades-related offerings, the micro-credentials align with apprenticeship technical training and help learners progress toward certification where applicable.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Micro-credentials (Open Learning & Career Development)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development delivers employer-validated micro-credentials in areas like data and digital skills, project management, and ocean/health-adjacent fields, developed with input from industry partners. The badges are stackable and often count toward non-credit certificates or prepare learners for external professional certifications (e.g., PMI, CompTIA). Programs emphasize applied projects or work-integrated components to align training with in-demand skills in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Micro-credentials
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University offers micro-credentials in fields such as data analytics, digital marketing, and business operations that are developed with employer input to target regional talent needs. These short, stackable offerings issue digital badges that can be combined toward non-credit certificates and, in some cases, map into continuing education certificates or prepare candidates for external industry certifications. The focus on applied, project-based learning helps bridge work-integrated learning gaps for students and early-career professionals.

resources.name: Cape Breton University Micro-credentials
resources.description: Cape Breton University provides employer-aligned micro-credentials in areas such as healthcare support, tourism/hospitality, and digital skills to meet Cape Breton–Unama’ki labour market needs. The badges are stackable and can count toward CBU continuing education certificates or provide targeted preparation for sector-recognized certifications. Programs are delivered flexibly (online and in-community) and are designed with local industry partners to create clear talent pathways for young people in the region.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

solutions.text: School–Community Co‑op and Job‑Shadow Program: Expand school co‑op and job‑shadow programs by creating a community roster of host employers (including arts organizations and health clinics) and scheduling regular ‘career days’ with hands‑on demonstrations.

resources.name: Co-operative Education (High School)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Centre for Education’s Co-operative Education program places high school students with community host employers for credit-bearing work terms and job-shadow experiences. The program maintains a roster of employers across trades, technology, health, and the arts and regularly coordinates in-school career days and employer-led, hands-on demonstrations to align learning with current labour market needs.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Co-operative Education (High School)
resources.organization: Chignecto Central Regional Centre for Education (CCRCE)
resources.description: Chignecto Central Regional Centre for Education connects students with local businesses, health clinics, non-profits, and arts organizations for job-shadowing and co-op placements that earn academic credit. Educators and career practitioners actively build and manage an employer partner roster and host career exploration events with practical, hands-on demonstrations to help students understand real-world roles.

resources.name: Options and Opportunities (O2) and Co-operative Education
resources.organization: Annapolis Valley Regional Centre for Education (AVRCE)
resources.description: AVRCE’s O2 and Co-operative Education programs give students structured, community-based learning through job-shadow days and co-op placements with vetted local employers across sectors, including trades, healthcare, and creative industries. Staff maintain a living database of host employers and facilitate regular career days and skills showcases that feature hands-on activities aligned to local workforce demand.

resources.name: Co-operative Education (High School)
resources.organization: Cape Breton–Victoria Regional Centre for Education (CBVRCE)
resources.description: CBVRCE’s Co-operative Education program partners with Cape Breton–area employers to provide job-shadow and work placements that count toward graduation, helping students explore careers in trades, tech, health, and the arts. The program curates a regional roster of host employers and organizes school-based career fairs and interactive demonstrations to strengthen school–community ties.

resources.name: Co-operative Education and Work-Integrated Learning
resources.description: NSCC integrates co-op terms, internships, practicums, and service learning across many programs and campuses, placing students with a large network of host employers in technology, healthcare, trades, and creative sectors. Employer engagement and career services teams coordinate industry days, employer panels, and hands-on demonstrations while maintaining a province-wide roster of placement partners to align training with labour market needs.

solutions.text: Community Maker & Creative Studios with Employer Partnerships: Establish shared maker spaces and creative studios where students, entrepreneurs and employers collaborate on real projects — providing equipment, mentorship and a pipeline from learning to paid local work.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: The Lou Duggan Creative Studio provides community access to creative tools and spaces—such as digital fabrication tools, recording and media studios, and arts equipment—so people can learn by doing and build real projects. Library-led and partner-led workshops bring in local artists, entrepreneurs, and organizations to mentor participants and collaborate on community and small-business needs. This shared studio environment helps youth and aspiring creators develop portfolios and paid gigs, creating a bridge from learning to work in Nova Scotia’s creative economy.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: The PIER (Port Innovation, Engagement & Research)
resources.description: The PIER is a living lab and collaborative workspace at the Halifax Seaport where employers, startups, researchers, and students co-develop solutions for the ocean, logistics, and supply chain sectors. It provides shared labs, access to real industry data, and mentorship from port and marine companies to build prototypes and pilot projects. These employer-partnered projects lead directly to internships, contracts, and local jobs, creating a strong pathway from skills development to paid work.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs is a collaborative studio for digital product design and prototyping at Dalhousie University’s Faculty of Computer Science, where students and entrepreneurs build real solutions with mentorship and modern tools. The lab partners with local tech employers through hackathons, design sprints, and applied projects that tackle industry-defined challenges. These collaborations routinely translate into co-ops, paid contracts, and startup launches, aligning training with employer needs in Nova Scotia’s tech sector.

resources.name: NSCC Applied Research and Innovation – Makerspace and Prototyping Facilities (Ivany Campus)
resources.description: NSCC’s Applied Research and Innovation team operates makerspace and prototyping resources that support students, startups, and companies with fabrication, electronics, and digital design. Through capstone projects, employer-sponsored challenges, and applied research, students collaborate directly with local businesses to solve real problems and develop market-ready prototypes. This model provides equipment, mentorship, and a pipeline to paid work via internships, company contracts, and commercialization support.

resources.name: Centre for Craft Nova Scotia – Studios and Mary E. Black Gallery
resources.description: Centre for Craft Nova Scotia offers shared studios, specialized equipment, and professional development for makers, alongside the Mary E. Black Gallery which connects creators to markets and industry partners. Programs pair emerging artisans with mentors and link them to galleries, retailers, and community clients to co-develop products, exhibitions, and commissions. This creative studio ecosystem helps participants turn hands-on learning into sustainable, paid work and small business growth in the craft sector.

solutions.text: Mobile Training Units & Pop‑up Skills Labs: Deploy mobile training trailers or pop‑up labs that bring short technical and trade training to rural communities (e.g., welding, carpentry basics, digital skills), coordinated with local employers who pledge interviews for graduates.

resources.name: NSCC Customized Training (Mobile & On‑site Delivery)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College delivers short, employer‑aligned training by taking mobile and pop‑up labs to rural communities across the province. Using portable welding simulators, carpentry toolkits, and digital skills stations, NSCC sets up temporary training spaces in community halls, worksites, and First Nation communities, and aligns the curriculum with local employers’ needs. Programs are coordinated with employers who co‑host sessions and participate in on‑site recruiting and interview events for graduates through NSCC Career Services.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Rural Pop‑up Skills Labs
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic runs pop‑up skills labs and mobile workshops that bring hands‑on digital skills, prototyping, and entrepreneurship training to rural communities in Western and Northern Nova Scotia. Sessions are set up in community venues and employer worksites, often co‑designed with local companies that mentor participants and host hiring mixers or project showcases to connect graduates to interviews. The approach lowers access barriers and rapidly aligns short, practical training with immediate local talent needs.

solutions.text: Youth Mentorship & Employer Ambassador Network: Create a community volunteer network of employer ambassadors and near‑peer mentors who provide career coaching, mock interviews, workplace visits and ongoing mentorship linking youth to local job opportunities.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program matches newcomers, including youth and recent graduates, with volunteer mentors from Nova Scotia’s employer community for career coaching, informational interviews, and networking. Mentors act as employer ambassadors who provide sector-specific advice, resume feedback, mock interview practice, and introductions that help mentees access local job opportunities and workplace insights.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Learning and Employment Centre (LEC)
resources.description: Phoenix’s LEC provides youth with one-on-one career coaching, employer-led workshops, and mock interviews to build job readiness and confidence. Staff and volunteer mentors connect young people to local employers for workplace tours, informational interviews, and ongoing mentorship, acting as an employer ambassador network that aligns youth skills with real hiring needs.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Youth Programs
resources.description: IGNITE engages junior/high school and post-secondary youth with entrepreneurship bootcamps, employer panels, and mentorship from local founders and industry professionals across rural Nova Scotia. Through coaching, mock pitches/interviews, workplace tours, and near‑peer guidance from older student entrepreneurs, youth build skills and direct connections to local companies and start-up opportunities.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Industry Mentorship and Experiential Learning)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs connects computing and tech‑interested students with employer mentors through design sprints, hackathons, and industry‑led workshops at Dalhousie. Near‑peer mentors (senior students and recent grads) and employer ambassadors provide career coaching, mock technical interviews, and introductions or site visits with partner companies, directly linking youth to Nova Scotia’s tech job opportunities.

resources.name: Employment & Training Services (Youth and Adult)
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Employment & Training Services offer culturally grounded career coaching, skills workshops, and mentorship that connect Indigenous youth with local employers. Employer ambassadors and community mentors support mock interviews, job fairs, and workplace exposure, fostering ongoing relationships that help youth transition into trades, health, tech, and community service roles across Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Local Labour Market & Skills Dashboard: Maintain a simple community dashboard (managed by municipality or chamber) showing real‑time local openings, skill gaps, apprenticeship opportunities and training calendar so educators and learners can target learning to demand.

resources.name: Work in Halifax (Jobs & Labour Market Dashboard)
resources.description: Halifax Partnership maintains Work in Halifax, a community-facing portal that aggregates real-time local job postings across sectors and links to employer demand, in-demand occupations, and immigration pathways. Through its broader Halifax Index and labour market dashboards, the Partnership publishes up-to-date workforce indicators and skills insights, and promotes training, co-op, and apprenticeship opportunities via partner events so educators and learners can target learning to local demand.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Work In Cape Breton (Regional Job Board & Workforce Hub)
resources.description: Managed by the Cape Breton Partnership, Work In Cape Breton is a regional dashboard that posts real-time job openings and highlights priority sectors and in-demand skills on the Island. The Partnership complements the job board with labour market updates and a public events/training calendar (including apprenticeship info sessions and NSCC/industry programs), helping educators and jobseekers align learning and career choices with current employer needs.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Job Board & Labour Market Information
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: Nova Scotia Works provides a province-wide, continuously updated job board and a labour market information hub (including Explore Careers NS) that shows in-demand occupations, wages, and required skills. Local NS Works centres publish training and event calendars (including apprenticeship and employer information sessions), giving educators and learners a practical dashboard to align programs and upskilling with real-time local demand.

resources.name: Digital Nova Scotia Job Portal & Training Calendar
resources.description: Digital Nova Scotia operates a public job portal that lists current tech roles across the province and tags opportunities by skills and technologies, reflecting real-time employer demand. Its events and training calendar aggregates bootcamps, micro-credentials, and workshops co-created with industry, giving educators and learners a live dashboard of skill gaps and upskilling pathways aligned to Nova Scotia’s digital economy.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 701, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Return‑to‑Home Matching & Incentive Program: Offer a community‑run incentive and matching service for Nova Scotians living away — combining relocation micro‑grants, job matching with local employers, and peer support to encourage graduates and skilled workers to return.

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: The Connector Program matches recent graduates, returnees, and other skilled jobseekers with established business and community leaders (“Connectors”) who open doors to interviews, job leads, and wider professional networks. By actively introducing Nova Scotians living away to local employers and mentors, it provides practical job-matching and peer support that eases relocation decisions and aligns talent with in-demand roles across sectors.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Physician Recruitment and Retention Incentive Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Clare
resources.description: This community-led program offers significant signing bonuses and relocation supports to family physicians who choose to practise in Clare, and works with Nova Scotia Health and local clinics to match candidates to vacancies. The Municipality also provides settlement assistance and community connections, creating a peer-support environment that helps healthcare professionals return to Nova Scotia and integrate quickly into local life and work.

resources.name: Healthcare Professionals Recruitment – Incentives and Relocation Support
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia, Office of Healthcare Professionals Recruitment
resources.description: The Office of Healthcare Professionals Recruitment connects physicians, nurses, and allied health workers with opportunities across Nova Scotia Health and community practices, providing dedicated job-matching services and candidate support. It offers signing bonuses, relocation assistance, and return‑of‑service incentives, and engages community partners to support spouses and family integration—encouraging Nova Scotians living away to return while aligning critical health skills with employer demand.

solutions.text: Community Health & Care Training Pipeline: Partner local clinics, long‑term care facilities and colleges to create guaranteed practicum placements, fast‑track certificates for support roles, and mentorship pathways into nursing and allied health within the community.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Learners & Student Placements
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health partners with universities, colleges, and long-term care providers across the province to coordinate required clinical practicums, co-op terms, and preceptorships for nursing and allied health learners. The Learners & Student Placements team places students in hospitals, primary care, community health, and continuing care settings and supports mentorship and recruitment pathways so graduates transition directly into local roles, strengthening community-based care.

resources.name: IWK Health Student Placements & Clinical Education
resources.description: IWK Health coordinates clinical placements and preceptorships for nursing and allied health students in pediatric, perinatal, and women’s health, working closely with Dalhousie, NSCC, and other schools. The program provides structured mentorship and on-site learning in clinics and hospital units, creating a clear pipeline from education to employment within Halifax-area health services and community partners.

resources.name: Continuing Care Assistant (CCA) Accelerated Program
resources.description: NSCC’s accelerated CCA certificate delivers fast-tracked classroom learning combined with guaranteed clinical placements in long-term care and home care organizations across Nova Scotia. Developed with employers and Nova Scotia Health, the program embeds mentorship and work-integrated learning so graduates can move quickly into in-demand support roles and, if desired, bridge onward into LPN/RN or other allied health pathways within their communities.

resources.name: Healthcare Career Pathways for Newcomers (including IEN Bridging)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS supports internationally educated nurses and other internationally trained health professionals with career advising, exam preparation, mentorship, and employer connections, often in collaboration with Nova Scotia Health and long-term care agencies. The program helps participants secure supervised work experiences or observerships and guided practicum pathways, accelerating their integration into nursing and allied health roles that address local workforce needs.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Bootcamps & Short Intensives Co‑designed with Employers: Host short (2–12 week) community bootcamps in targeted areas (e.g., web dev, practical trades, digital media, hospitality service) taught jointly by educators and employers with hiring commitments for successful participants.

resources.name: CANS Construction Job Readiness Program
resources.description: A short, intensive training pathway that combines approximately five weeks of industry-led classroom instruction with a two-week work placement at member construction companies. The curriculum is co-designed with employers to build in-demand, entry-level trade and site skills, and participating companies host placements and frequently hire successful graduates. This directly aligns training to employer needs while creating a clear bridge to jobs in the skilled trades.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Skills for Hire Atlantic
resources.description: An 8–12 week, employer-informed bootcamp delivered in Nova Scotia that focuses on high-demand tech roles (e.g., web development, cybersecurity, data). Digital Nova Scotia co-designs curriculum with regional employers and uses industry instructors, while also organizing employer networking, interviews, and job-matching that help graduates transition directly into entry-level roles. The program tightly aligns training content and projects with current hiring needs across the province’s tech sector.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 601, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

resources.name: Screen Nova Scotia Production Training Program
resources.description: Short, employer-led bootcamps and intensives (typically from a few days up to several weeks) that train participants for in-demand film and TV crew roles such as grip, electric, locations, and set operations. The training is co-developed and delivered with unions/guilds and active production companies, and often leads directly to hiring hall lists, on-set placements, and entry-level job opportunities on Nova Scotia productions. This model ensures skills match current productions’ needs and builds a reliable pipeline of work-ready crew.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 448, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

resources.name: Palette Skills SalesCamp (Atlantic Canada)
resources.description: A 3–5 week intensive bootcamp focused on B2B tech and innovation sales, co-designed with hiring companies and taught by industry sales leaders. Cohorts delivered in Halifax include employer projects, coaching, and a hiring day with partner employers who commit to interviews and actively recruit graduates. The program rapidly equips participants with job-ready, employer-validated skills and connects them to concrete hiring pipelines in Nova Scotia’s growing tech and innovation sectors.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

solutions.text: Recognition & Bridging for International and Non‑traditional Credentials: Create community assessment and bridging programs to recognize immigrants' and non‑traditional workers' skills, offering short courses or supervised work placements to meet local certification requirements.

resources.name: Work-based Competency Assessment (WCA)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ WCA evaluates internationally trained and non-traditional workers directly in a workplace or simulated environment, documenting competencies against Nova Scotia occupational standards. Participants receive individualized plans for gap training, short courses, and employer-supervised placements to meet local certification or hiring requirements, effectively bridging prior experience to Nova Scotia credentials and jobs.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Nova Scotia Practice Ready Assessment Program (PRAP)
resources.organization: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Nova Scotia
resources.description: PRAP assesses internationally trained physicians in Nova Scotia through structured clinical placements with supervised practice and competency evaluation in real care settings. The program identifies any gaps and provides a pathway to meet provincial licensing requirements, directly bridging prior medical training to Nova Scotia’s certification standards.
resources.address: Suite 300, 1559 Brunswick Street, Halifax, NS B3J 2G1

resources.name: Qualifying Program (Internationally Trained Dentists)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Dentistry Qualifying Program provides advanced standing to internationally trained dentists, combining intensive short-course didactic upgrades with extensive, supervised clinical placements to meet Canadian competency standards. Graduates earn a DDS credential that satisfies Nova Scotia licensure requirements, directly bridging international credentials to local practice.

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) Pathway for Early Childhood Education
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE)
resources.description: NSCECE’s RPL Pathway assesses the prior work experience and learning of early childhood educators and related workers, mapping competencies to provincial diploma outcomes. Participants receive tailored gap training modules and required practicum placements to achieve Nova Scotia ECE classification, providing a clear bridge from non-traditional or international experience to local certification.

solutions.text: Youth Entrepreneurship & Social Enterprise Incubator: Establish a locally focused incubator that helps young founders turn ideas into viable businesses through training, shared workspace, mentorship, and links to local suppliers and markets—particularly for creative and tech ventures.

resources.name: Volta
resources.description: Volta is a startup hub that provides founders—especially in tech—with co-working space, structured training, and access to seasoned mentors and investors. Through its residency and community programs, it connects young entrepreneurs to local suppliers, customers, and talent pipelines, aligning real-world startup needs with employer demand and market opportunities in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED delivers hands-on entrepreneurship training, coaching, and mentorship along with access to co-working and peer networks that help young founders turn ideas into viable ventures. Its programs include supports for both for-profit and social enterprises and connect entrepreneurs to local markets, procurement opportunities, and service providers across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: The Spark Zone
resources.description: The Spark Zone is a university-led incubator that helps students and recent graduates in tech and creative sectors build startups through workshops, coaching, and project-based learning. It offers access to mentors, workspace, and industry connections, linking young founders with local suppliers, partners, and early adopters to align skills development with employer and market demands.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs is a Dalhousie University sandbox that incubates student-led tech ventures through experiential training, hackathons, mentorship, and access to collaborative workspace. It bridges classroom learning with employer needs by connecting teams to local tech companies, community partners, and potential customers, helping young founders validate and launch products in Nova Scotia.

obstacles.title: Credential Recognition and Labour Mobility Frictions
obstacles.description: Slow, inconsistent recognition for newcomers and interprovincial professionals/trades delays entry into the workforce and wastes skills.

solutions.text: Community Credential Navigation Clinics: Free drop-in clinics, run by trained volunteers, retired professionals and settlement workers, that help newcomers and interprovincial professionals translate documents, map foreign/other‑provincial credentials to Nova Scotia requirements, prepare applications, and track recognition progress.

resources.name: Licensing and Certification Support (Regulated Professions)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides one-on-one and small-group support to newcomers who need recognition of foreign or interprovincial credentials. Staff and trained volunteers help clients understand Nova Scotia’s licensing requirements, translate and organize documents, prepare regulator applications, and create step-by-step action plans with milestones to track recognition progress.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Newcomer Settlement & Employment Services
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth – Centre for Immigrant Programs
resources.description: The YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs offers free drop-in and appointment-based help for newcomers navigating credential recognition and labour mobility. Settlement workers and trained volunteers review and translate documents (via referrals), map foreign/out-of-province qualifications to Nova Scotia requirements, assist with application forms for regulatory bodies and training, and maintain action plans to track clients’ progress.

resources.name: Internationally Educated Nurse (IEN) Navigation Team
resources.description: NSCN’s IEN Navigation Team provides dedicated advisors who help internationally educated nurses translate and verify documents, map their education and experience to Nova Scotia nursing licensure pathways, and prepare complete applications. Advisors supply individualized checklists, connect applicants to bridging or assessment programs, and monitor milestones and timelines to track progress to licensure.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Employment Services (Credential Navigation for Trades & Professionals)
resources.description: TEAM Work Cooperative, a Nova Scotia Works centre, offers free guidance to interprovincial and internationally trained workers on credential recognition and labour mobility in Nova Scotia. Career practitioners help clients map credentials to provincial regulators or apprenticeship pathways, assemble and submit applications (e.g., trade qualification/Red Seal, professional licensing), and use individualized action plans to track each step through recognition.

solutions.text: Local Mentor Match Program: A community mentorship network pairing newcomers and interprovincial workers with local professionals or tradespeople to provide guidance on local workplace expectations, pathways to licensing, networking introductions, and practical advice for gaining local experience.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program matches immigrants, recent graduates, and interprovincial jobseekers with established local professionals and trades/employers for one-on-one introductions. Connectors share insights on local workplace expectations, regulatory pathways, and industry norms, and introduce participants to their networks for informational interviews. This guided networking accelerates credential navigation and helps participants gain local experience and references.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program pairs internationally trained professionals with volunteer mentors working in the same field in Nova Scotia. Mentors provide guidance on licensing and credential recognition, workplace culture, and sector-specific job search strategies, and facilitate networking introductions. This targeted, practical mentorship helps newcomers translate their credentials, build local experience, and connect to employment opportunities faster.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Bridging and Micro‑credential Courses with Community Colleges: Partnerships between municipalities, community organizations and colleges to offer short, targeted bridging courses and micro‑credentials that address gaps identified in recognition assessments (technical updates, provincial codes, language for the workplace), with flexible schedules and bursaries.

resources.name: NSCC MicroCredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College offers short, targeted micro-credentials co-designed with industry, municipalities and community partners to close specific skill gaps identified in recognition or prior learning assessments. Offerings include technical refreshers (e.g., provincial building/electrical code updates, safety certifications) and Canadian workplace communication, delivered in flexible formats (online, hybrid, evenings/weekends) across campuses. Many seats are subsidized through provincial funding and NSCC student awards/bursaries, helping newcomers and interprovincial professionals quickly bridge into Nova Scotia’s workforce.

resources.name: Early Childhood Education (ECE) Bridging Program for Newcomers
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (in partnership with Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education)
resources.description: ISANS partners with the Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE) to deliver a short bridging pathway that aligns internationally educated participants with Nova Scotia’s ECE requirements. The program combines targeted technical updates on provincial regulations and practice standards with occupation-specific English for the workplace and stackable micro-credentials (e.g., First Aid/CPR and sector compliance training), offered on flexible schedules. Participants can access bursaries/tuition supports available through provincial ECE funding and ISANS supports, enabling faster entry into regulated roles after recognition/assessment.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Trade Qualifier Supports and Red Seal Exam Preparation (with NSCC)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency partners with NSCC and industry to offer short, targeted upgrading, provincial code updates and Interprovincial (Red Seal) exam preparation that address gaps identified during credential recognition for experienced workers, newcomers and interprovincial tradespeople. Courses are delivered across the province and online with flexible scheduling to accommodate working learners. The Agency provides financial supports (e.g., travel and exam fee assistance and other bursaries) to reduce barriers, accelerating entry to the workforce once recognition requirements are met.

solutions.text: Employer-led Skills Recognition Panels: Local employer consortia and trade associations convene panels to evaluate transferable skills and provide conditional recognition or expedited hiring pathways (competency testing, on‑site assessments, trial placements) so qualified people can work while completing formal credentialing.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.description: Irving Shipbuilding partners with NSCC, Unifor, and community organizations to convene employer-led selection and assessment panels that evaluate applicants’ technical aptitudes and transferable skills through hands-on tests, interviews, and job-simulated tasks. Successful candidates receive conditional offers, paid work terms, and on‑the‑job assessments at the Halifax Shipyard while they complete formal training and certification, creating an expedited pathway from skills recognition to employment.

resources.name: Continuing Care Assistant (CCA) Recognition of Prior Learning and Work & Learn Pathways
resources.description: Health Association Nova Scotia coordinates employer-led RPL processes with long‑term care and home care members, where experienced workers and newcomers undergo competency reviews, on‑site skills demonstrations, and workplace assessments by employer assessors/preceptors. Candidates can be hired into paid ‘work and learn’ or trainee roles while completing any identified gaps, enabling conditional recognition and accelerated progression to full CCA certification and employment.
resources.address: 2 Dartmouth Road, Suite 301, Bedford, NS B4A 2K7

resources.name: Supervised Practice Experience for Internationally Educated Nurses (IENs)
resources.description: In partnership with Nova Scotia Health and employer sites across the province, the Nova Scotia College of Nursing enables IENs to receive conditional licensure and enter supervised roles where their competencies are assessed directly in the workplace. Through employer-supervised placements and performance evaluations aligned to regulatory standards, qualified nurses can work while they complete any outstanding credentialing requirements, creating an expedited pathway to full licensure and ongoing employment.

solutions.text: Community Apprenticeship and Paid Internship Placements: A coordinated program connecting small businesses and public institutions with newcomers and interprovincial professionals for paid, time‑bound apprenticeships or internships that count toward local licensing/experience requirements.

resources.name: On-the-Job Training (OJT) Wage Subsidy
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS connects immigrant jobseekers with Nova Scotia employers for paid, time-limited on-the-job training placements supported by a wage subsidy. Staff match candidates to small businesses and public institutions, and the supervised work experience gained can be applied toward required Canadian experience or documented hours for regulated professions and skilled trades where applicable, accelerating credential recognition and labour market entry.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Supervised Practice Experience Partnership (SPEP) for Internationally Educated Nurses
resources.description: SPEP places internationally educated nurses in paid, supervised roles within Nova Scotia Health and IWK Health for a defined period to demonstrate competencies in practice. The experience is formally recognized by the Nova Scotia College of Nursing toward licensing requirements, providing a structured pathway that converts supervised workplace experience into eligibility for Nova Scotia RN/LPN registration.
resources.address: 120 Western Parkway, Suite 300, Bedford, NS B4B 0V2

resources.name: START Program (Apprenticeship Employer Incentive)
resources.description: START provides financial incentives to small and medium-sized employers to create paid positions, including Registered Apprenticeship placements, for jobseekers in Nova Scotia. Apprentices hired through START accumulate recognized hours and competencies toward provincial/Red Seal trade certification, helping newcomers and interprovincial tradespeople secure time-bound, supervised employment that advances their licensing and work experience requirements.

solutions.text: Local Language and Workplace Culture Programs: Community-run language supports focused on industry-specific vocabulary and workplace culture orientation sessions, including mock interviews and workplace simulation, to reduce non‑technical barriers to hiring and recognition.

resources.name: Employment Language Training (ELT)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Employment Language Training offers sector-specific English courses (e.g., health care, engineering, business) that build technical vocabulary and practical communication for Canadian workplaces. Training includes workplace culture orientation, employer expectations, resume and cover letter language, and practice interviews and simulations to reduce non-technical barriers to hiring and speed workforce entry for internationally trained professionals.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Professional Practice Program (PPP)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ PPP provides short, mentored Canadian workplace practicums for internationally trained professionals, paired with pre-placement training in workplace culture, communication, and job search. Participants complete mock interviews, job-simulation tasks, and industry-focused coaching that help employers assess skills beyond credentials and support faster recognition and hiring.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Language Instruction for Newcomers to Canada (LINC) – Employment-Focused Workshops
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth – Centre for Immigrant Programs
resources.description: The YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs delivers LINC alongside employment-focused workshops that cover Canadian workplace culture, rights and responsibilities, and interview techniques. Instructors integrate job-search language and sector vocabulary and coordinate employer-led information sessions and mock interviews to help newcomers overcome non-technical barriers and transition into local jobs.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 201, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Language Instruction for Newcomers to Canada (LINC) – Workplace Readiness
resources.organization: YMCA of Cape Breton – Immigrant Services
resources.description: YMCA of Cape Breton Immigrant Services offers LINC and complementary workplace readiness programming, including sessions on Nova Scotia workplace norms, resume and interview clinics, and employer networking. Specialized workshops introduce industry-specific terminology (e.g., hospitality and health services) and provide simulated interview practice to help newcomers enter the labour market more quickly.

solutions.text: Digital Community Credential Repository: A secure, community-managed digital system where newcomers and interprovincial professionals can store verified copies of diplomas, transcripts, references and work samples to speed assessments by regulators and employers.

resources.name: NSCC MyCreds | MesCertif (Digital Credential Wallet)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College issues verified digital transcripts, diplomas, and certificates through the ARUCC MyCreds platform, giving learners a secure digital wallet to store and control their academic records. Graduates and newcomers can share tamper-evident documents directly with Nova Scotia regulators and employers, expediting assessments and reducing repeated verification. This functions as a trusted digital repository that supports faster credential recognition and labour mobility.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University MyCreds | MesCertif
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University participates in ARUCC’s MyCreds network to provide students and alumni with verified digital transcripts and credentials in a secure online wallet. Learners can store and share their official records instantly with Nova Scotia employers, professional regulators, and post-secondary partners, improving the speed and consistency of credential assessments. This digital repository reduces processing delays and supports interprovincial and international mobility.

resources.name: Nova Scotia College of Nursing – Applicant Portal & Digital Document Repository
resources.description: The Nova Scotia College of Nursing uses a secure online portal where internationally educated and interprovincial nurses submit, track, and manage verified educational credentials, registration verifications, references, and employment records. Documents are stored centrally and shared within the assessment workflow, enabling faster, more consistent licensure decisions and reducing duplicate submissions. This digital repository streamlines recognition for newcomers and mobile professionals entering Nova Scotia’s workforce.

resources.name: ISANS Client Portal and Employment Services – Digital Credential Portfolio
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides newcomers with a secure client portal to upload, store, and organize scanned and verified copies of diplomas, transcripts, licences, and work samples as part of employment and bridging services. Staff help clients validate documents and share curated credential packages with employers, training providers, and professional bodies across Nova Scotia, reducing delays and repeated handling. This community-delivered digital repository supports quicker assessments and smoother labour market entry.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Intermunicipal Skills Registry and Job Match Platform: A local online registry of qualified candidates with status indicators (recognized, provisionally recognized, awaiting assessment) that connects them to employers, apprenticeships and volunteer opportunities across towns and municipalities to improve matching and mobility.

resources.name: SkillsMatch Online Recruitment Tool and Database
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS operates a province-wide, online registry of immigrant and refugee talent in Nova Scotia that employers can search by occupation, location, and qualifications. Candidate profiles include clear status indicators such as licensing/credential recognition stage (fully recognized, in progress, or pending) and work authorization, and ISANS staff broker introductions to jobs, apprenticeships/placements, and volunteer or mentorship opportunities across municipalities. This directly reduces credential-recognition frictions and improves matching and mobility between communities.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: The Connector Program maintains a structured pool of job-ready newcomers and recent graduates and matches them with employers and industry leaders through curated introductions. Program staff track participants’ sectors, locations, and readiness (including work authorization and, where applicable, credential recognition progress) to target opportunities and facilitate movement to roles across Halifax and, through partner Connector programs in other regions, throughout Nova Scotia. This functions as a practical intermunicipal skills registry and match platform that shortens hiring cycles and supports labour mobility.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: NSCN Online Public Register
resources.description: The Nova Scotia College of Nursing provides a province-wide, publicly searchable registry showing each nurse’s licensure status (e.g., active, conditional, temporary) and practice class. Employers and health organizations across municipalities use this registry to instantly verify credential recognition and readiness to work, reducing delays and uncertainty in hiring and placements. While not a job board, it delivers the solution’s status-indicator component that underpins efficient job matching and mobility across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 120 Western Parkway, Suite 300, Bedford, NS B4B 0V2

solutions.text: Community-funded Bursaries for Licensing and Assessment Fees: A local fund, administered by settlement agencies or community foundations, to cover the costs of credential assessments, exams, licensing fees and required documentation for low- and moderate-income newcomers and interprovincial professionals.

resources.name: Atlantic Immigrant Career Loan Fund (AICLF)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: AICLF is a community-backed revolving fund that provides low-interest microloans to internationally trained newcomers so they can pay for credential assessments, licensing exams, professional association dues, short-term training, and required documentation. Administered in Nova Scotia by ISANS, the fund directly addresses cost barriers that delay credential recognition and labour market entry.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Internationally Educated Nurses (IEN) Financial Support Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health offers financial support to internationally educated nurses to cover costs such as credential assessments (e.g., NNAS), language testing, bridging/competency assessments (e.g., NCAS/OSCE), licensing application and exam fees (e.g., NCLEX), translation, and related documentation and travel. By removing these up‑front costs, the program accelerates licensure and workforce entry for newcomer nurses and interprovincial applicants.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: Practice Ready Assessment Program (Nova Scotia)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Department of Family Medicine (in partnership with Nova Scotia Health)
resources.description: Delivered by Dalhousie’s Department of Family Medicine in partnership with Nova Scotia Health, this program assesses internationally educated physicians for readiness to practice and provides structured support that can include coverage of assessment, licensing, and registration-related costs. By underwriting key fees and streamlining recognition, it reduces financial and administrative barriers so qualified IMGs can enter the Nova Scotia workforce more quickly.

solutions.text: Peer Professional Networks and Industry Circles: Sector-specific community networks (health, trades, tech, arts) that host regular peer review sessions, skills-sharing workshops and referral groups to help candidates demonstrate competencies and find local opportunities while awaiting formal recognition.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program matches internationally trained professionals with local, sector-specific mentors and convenes regular networking sessions and skills-sharing workshops. These peer circles and mentor meetups provide portfolio reviews, mock interviews, and targeted referrals, helping participants demonstrate competencies and access local opportunities while they work through credential recognition or licensing processes.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Ocean Connector
resources.description: COVE’s Ocean Connector is a monthly industry networking series that brings together ocean tech professionals, researchers, and companies for lightning talks, demos, and peer knowledge exchange. The events act as sector-specific circles where newcomers and interprovincial professionals can showcase skills, receive peer feedback, and gain referrals to project and employment opportunities while formal credential or security clearances are processed.

resources.name: Volta Residency
resources.description: Volta’s Residency program embeds founders and tech talent in a peer community with regular founder roundtables, skill-sharing workshops, office hours, and demo opportunities. These peer networks and referral pathways help participants validate competencies, build portfolios, and connect with local employers, advisors, and investors while they navigate recognition of prior experience or interprovincial mobility requirements.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: CANS Emerging Leaders
resources.description: CANS Emerging Leaders is a peer network for early- and mid-career construction professionals that hosts regular meetups, site tours, skills workshops, and mentoring events. By connecting tradespeople and project staff with employers and peers, the group creates referral channels and practical skill-sharing that help workers demonstrate competencies and secure roles while awaiting interprovincial trade certification or local credential recognition.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

resources.name: FILM 5 Training Program
resources.description: AFCOOP’s FILM 5 is a cohort-based program featuring peer review sessions, workshops with industry professionals, and production labs that culminate in public screenings and crew referrals. The program functions as an industry circle where artists and technical crew can demonstrate competencies through peer-evaluated projects, build local networks, and access opportunities while they work toward union membership or recognition of previous credits.
resources.address: 5663 Cornwallis Street, Suite 101, Halifax, NS B3K 1B6

solutions.text: Local Advocacy and Regulatory Navigation Coalition: A coalition of community organizations, employers, colleges and municipal leaders that collects local data on recognition delays, lobbies provincial regulators for streamlined processes, promotes mutual recognition agreements, and pilots local fast‑track protocols.

resources.name: Atlantic Physician Registry (Nova Scotia)
resources.organization: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Nova Scotia
resources.description: Administered by the provincial medical regulator, this program enables physicians in good standing in one Atlantic province to be recognized to practice across all four Atlantic provinces with a simplified, fast-track process. It operationalizes mutual recognition and reduces interprovincial licensing delays, while the College convenes health-system partners and shares mobility data with regulators to refine and streamline recognition processes.

resources.name: Practice Ready Assessment Nova Scotia (PRAN)
resources.organization: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Nova Scotia
resources.description: PRAN is a collaborative fast‑track pathway that assesses internationally educated physicians for readiness to practice in Nova Scotia and expedites licensure for high-need communities. Working with health authorities, employers, and post-secondary partners, it pilots streamlined local protocols and uses assessment data to inform provincial regulatory improvements, directly addressing credential-recognition delays.

resources.name: Immigrant Licensing & Certification Support and Policy Engagement
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides one-on-one licensing navigation, sector-specific bridging, and employer/college roundtables that surface real-time data on bottlenecks in credential recognition. Through multi-stakeholder working groups and policy submissions to provincial regulators, it advocates for streamlined processes and supports pilot fast‑track approaches with local employers and colleges to shorten time-to-licensure for newcomers.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1W8

resources.name: Cape Breton Local Immigration Partnership (CBLIP)
resources.description: CBLIP is a community coalition of municipalities, employers, post-secondary institutions, and service providers that coordinates research on newcomer employment barriers, including credential-recognition delays, and develops local action plans. It engages provincial regulators with evidence-based recommendations and works with employers and colleges to pilot local fast‑track supports (e.g., bridging and supervised work experience) to improve labour mobility in Cape Breton.

solutions.text: Community-hosted Competency Assessment Hubs: Pop-up or permanent hubs staffed by retired regulators, licensed practitioners and certified assessors who provide industry-recognized competency evaluations, portfolio assessments and supervised practical testing to accelerate local recognition decisions.

resources.name: Trade Qualifier and Practical Assessment (Skilled Trades)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency conducts competency-based evaluations for trade qualifiers and apprentices, including portfolio/experience review and supervised practical exams hosted in community shop facilities such as NSCC campuses. Licensed trades assessors and instructors observe candidates performing job tasks, validate Red Seal/industry standards, and provide documented results that accelerate certification and recognition decisions for newcomers and interprovincial workers.
resources.address: NSCC Akerley Campus, 21 Woodlawn Road, Dartmouth, NS B2W 2R7

resources.name: Practice Ready Assessment Nova Scotia (PRA-NS)
resources.organization: College of Physicians and Surgeons of Nova Scotia (with Nova Scotia Health)
resources.description: PRA-NS provides structured competency assessments for internationally trained physicians through supervised clinical practice in Nova Scotia communities. Licensed physician assessors evaluate candidates against provincial standards via observed clinical encounters, workplace-based assessments, and documented performance reviews, enabling faster, locally grounded licensing decisions.

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) and Challenge Assessments
resources.description: NSCC’s RPL services offer portfolio assessment, challenge exams, and demonstrations of skill to recognize competencies earned outside formal schooling, including international and interprovincial experience. Certified assessors review evidence and can arrange supervised practical evaluations in campus labs and shops, granting credit or advanced standing that shortens pathways to credentials recognized by local industry and regulators.

resources.name: Internationally Educated Applicants – Competency and Candidacy Assessment
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Social Workers
resources.description: The Nova Scotia College of Social Workers assesses internationally educated applicants through a competency-based review of portfolios and experience, followed by a supervised candidacy (mentored practice) that validates professional competencies in local settings. Registered social workers serve as assessors and mentors, providing structured evaluations that lead to timely recognition and licensing.
resources.address: 1888 Brunswick Street, Suite 700, Halifax, NS B3J 3J8

obstacles.title: Inclusion, Anti-Racism, and Reconciliation Gaps
obstacles.description: Systemic barriers faced by Mi'kmaq communities, African Nova Scotians, newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+ people, and persons with disabilities undermine a truly welcoming environment.

solutions.text: Community-led Reconciliation Action Plans: Form a local reconciliation working group with Mi'kmaq Elders, leaders, and youth to co-develop short- and long-term community actions (land stewardship, cultural education, monuments, protocols) with measurable timelines and annual public reporting.

resources.name: Task Force on the Commemoration of Edward Cornwallis and the Recognition and Commemoration of Indigenous History (Implementation)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality established a joint task force with Mi'kmaq leaders and knowledge keepers to co-develop concrete recommendations for how the city should address monuments, place names, and the public recognition of Mi’kmaq history. HRM is implementing these actions through an ongoing reconciliation process that includes renaming streets, updating protocols and signage, and advancing cultural education, with progress reported publicly to Council and the community.

resources.name: Wije’winen Centre (Urban Indigenous Reconciliation Hub)
resources.description: Led by the Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre, the Wije’winen Centre is being co-designed with Elders, community leaders, and Indigenous youth to deliver land-based stewardship programs, cultural education, ceremony spaces, and urban Indigenous services in Kjipuktuk/Halifax. The initiative functions as a community-led reconciliation plan with defined project phases and publicly shared updates and reports, creating protocols and measurable actions that advance relationships between Indigenous and non-Indigenous communities.

resources.name: NSCC Truth and Reconciliation Action Plan
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College’s plan is co-developed with Mi’kmaq Elders-in-Residence, Indigenous community partners, and students to set specific, time-bound actions across curriculum change, staff training, land acknowledgements, cultural spaces, and community protocols. NSCC tracks milestones and publishes institutional updates on progress, using annual reporting to demonstrate accountability and guide ongoing collaboration with Mi’kmaq communities across campuses.

resources.name: Unama’ki College Indigenous Strategy and Community Partnerships
resources.description: Unama’ki College at Cape Breton University works with Mi’kmaq Elders, community leaders, and youth across Unama’ki/Cape Breton to co-create actions on language revitalization, land stewardship, cultural education, and research protocols. The university embeds these commitments in strategy documents with targets and reports on progress through institutional updates and public communications, aligning campus and community efforts toward reconciliation with measurable timelines.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

solutions.text: Paid Indigenous and Equity-Focused Internships: Create paid internship and apprenticeship spots reserved for Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer, 2SLGBTQIA+, and disabled youth in local government, businesses, and non-profits to build skills and professional networks.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship (CLSI)
resources.description: CLSI offers 9–15 week paid environmental internships with municipalities, businesses, and non-profits across Nova Scotia. The program actively recruits Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer, 2SLGBTQIA+, and disabled youth through targeted outreach and dedicated supports, creating equity-focused paid placements that build skills, experience, and professional networks in the green economy.

resources.name: On-the-Job Training (OJT) and Work Placements
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS connects immigrants and refugees with paid, wage-subsidized work placements and internships in local government, businesses, and non-profits. These positions are reserved for newcomers and include employer mentorship and wraparound support, helping participants gain Canadian work experience, industry skills, and networks that lead to long-term employment.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: African Nova Scotian and Mi’kmaw Summer Student Museum Internship Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Museum (Department of Communities, Culture, Tourism and Heritage)
resources.description: This paid summer internship places African Nova Scotian and Mi’kmaw post-secondary students at Nova Scotia Museum sites and heritage organizations. The program reserves positions for these communities, providing hands-on experience, mentorship, and sector connections in museums, archives, and cultural institutions across the province.

resources.name: START Program – Apprenticeship Diversity Incentive
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration)
