resources.description: The START Program provides financial incentives to Nova Scotia employers to create paid apprenticeship spots for underrepresented groups, including Mi’kmaq and other Indigenous peoples, African Nova Scotians, newcomers, women in trades, and persons with disabilities. By offsetting wages and training costs, it facilitates equitable entry into skilled trades and helps apprentices build credentials and industry networks.

solutions.text: Local Anti-Racism and Inclusion Training: Offer regular, subsidized anti-racism, cultural safety, and accessibility trainings co-designed and delivered by community representatives and subject experts for employers, educators, first responders, and service providers.

resources.name: EDI and Anti-Racism Training for Employers and Service Providers
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers regular anti-racism, cultural humility, and inclusive workplace training tailored for employers, educators, and front-line service providers across Nova Scotia. Sessions are co-designed with newcomer community members and subject-matter experts, and are often subsidized through public funding so small organizations can participate.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: African Nova Scotian Anti-Racism Education and Training
resources.organization: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Black Cultural Centre provides anti-Black racism education, cultural safety workshops, and historical context sessions for schools, government, police/first responders, and employers. Programming is designed and delivered by African Nova Scotian community historians and practitioners, with partnership-supported and subsidized offerings to expand access.
resources.address: 10 Cherry Brook Road, Cherry Brook, NS B2Z 1A8

resources.name: 2SLGBTQIA+ Inclusion Workshops
resources.description: The Youth Project offers interactive training on creating safer, affirming spaces for 2SLGBTQIA+ people, tailored to educators, youth-serving staff, health providers, and community organizations. Workshops are developed and led with queer and trans youth and subject experts, and many sessions are low-cost or subsidized for schools and nonprofits.

resources.name: Indigenous Cultural Safety and KAIROS Blanket Exercise
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre facilitates Mi’kmaw cultural safety training, including the KAIROS Blanket Exercise and workshops on land acknowledgements, reconciliation, and working respectfully with urban Indigenous communities. Sessions are led by Elders, Knowledge Keepers, and experienced facilitators, and are offered regularly to employers, educators, and first responders, with options to tailor and subsidize delivery through partnerships.

solutions.text: Community Mentorship Circles: Establish mentorship programs pairing young people from underrepresented groups with local mentors in trades, arts, tech, and entrepreneurship, including peer support circles and career navigation workshops.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS matches newcomer youth and young professionals with local mentors from sectors such as trades, tech, arts, and entrepreneurship to build networks and workplace readiness. The program includes structured mentoring relationships, peer networking circles, and career navigation workshops that help participants understand credentialing, apprenticeships, and local labour market pathways—directly advancing inclusive mentorship for underrepresented young people.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1W8

resources.name: Hope Blooms Youth Entrepreneurship Program
resources.description: Hope Blooms empowers youth—many from African Nova Scotian and newcomer communities—with mentorship from local entrepreneurs, chefs, urban farmers, and creatives to run social enterprises and community food initiatives. Weekly circles, leadership sessions, and hands-on business workshops provide peer support and career navigation, helping participants gain skills in product development, marketing, financial literacy, and pathways to further education or trades.

resources.name: Imhotep’s Legacy Academy (ILA) Mentorship Programs
resources.description: ILA pairs African Nova Scotian students with university mentors and Black professionals in STEM to deliver after-school clubs, labs, and tutoring that build pipelines into tech, engineering, and trades-related pathways. Cohort-based sessions function as peer support circles, and career exploration workshops connect youth with scholarships, co-ops, apprenticeships, and postsecondary navigation resources.
resources.address: Killam Memorial Library, Dalhousie University, 6225 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: Youth & Employment Programs
resources.description: The Mi'kmaw Native Friendship Centre supports Indigenous youth with mentorship from Elders, culture-bearers, and local professionals across arts, culture, trades, and entrepreneurship. Programming includes peer circles, cultural mentorship, and employment readiness and career navigation workshops that connect youth with apprenticeships, certifications, and community-based opportunities—addressing systemic barriers faced by Mi’kmaq youth in urban Halifax.

resources.name: Media Arts Scholarship & Mentorship Program
resources.description: CFAT’s program pairs emerging media artists—prioritizing equity-deserving and underrepresented voices—with established mentors in film, audio, and digital arts. A cohort model fosters peer-support circles, while skill-building labs and professional development workshops provide career navigation into the creative industries, including portfolio development, grant writing, and industry networking.

solutions.text: Inclusive Procurement and Supplier Diversity: Adopt local procurement targets and supplier-diversity policies that prioritize businesses owned by Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotians, newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+, and people with disabilities, with outreach and procurement-readiness supports.

resources.name: Social Procurement Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality integrates social value and supplier diversity criteria into municipal tenders and RFPs. The program encourages participation from Mi'kmaw and African Nova Scotian businesses, as well as newcomer-, 2SLGBTQIA+-, and disability-owned suppliers, by including social value evaluation, local benefit requirements, and outreach to equity-deserving vendors. Procurement staff host information sessions and vendor onboarding supports to help diverse local firms become procurement-ready and compete for HRM contracts.

resources.name: Procurement Assistance Canada – Atlantic Region
resources.description: Procurement Assistance Canada (PAC) provides free one-on-one advice, workshops, and webinars that demystify selling to the federal government, with targeted outreach to Indigenous (including Mi’kmaw), Black, newcomer, 2SLGBTQI+, and disability-owned businesses. PAC helps diverse suppliers register, find opportunities, and bid effectively, and explains federal supplier diversity initiatives (e.g., the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business), directly supporting procurement-readiness and inclusive access to government contracts.

resources.name: Business Services – Entrepreneurship and Procurement Readiness
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS supports immigrant and refugee entrepreneurs with training, mentorship, and hands-on coaching to become procurement-ready. The team connects newcomer-owned businesses to public-sector buyers and supplier-diversity networks, hosts tendering and bidding workshops with provincial and federal procurement officials, and assists with certifications and compliance so they can compete for local and regional contracts.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Supplier Diversity Readiness and Procurement Training
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business, Mount Saint Vincent University
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business provides supplier diversity training, certification readiness (e.g., WBE Canada/WEConnect International), and buyer–supplier matchmaking for women-owned firms. Through workshops, advising, and events with institutional and corporate buyers, the Centre helps diverse women entrepreneurs—including racialized, newcomer, Indigenous, and 2SLGBTQIA+ women—navigate procurement processes and access supplier-diversity opportunities across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Supplier Development and Inclusive Procurement Support
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Economic Benefits Office (MEBO) connects Mi’kmaw-owned businesses and workers with major project procurement opportunities in Unama’ki (Cape Breton). MEBO delivers capacity-building workshops, safety/quality certifications, bid support, and buyer meet-and-greet events that strengthen procurement-readiness while advocating for Indigenous participation targets and inclusive procurement clauses with project proponents and public buyers.
resources.address: 90 San'tu Drive, Suite 5B, Membertou, NS B1S 0A5

solutions.text: Accessible Community Spaces Initiative: Audit and upgrade public buildings, event venues, parks, and transit stops for physical accessibility and sensory-friendly features, and publish accessibility maps and guides for residents and visitors.

resources.name: Access-A-Bus and Bus Stop Accessibility Improvements
resources.description: Halifax Transit operates Access-A-Bus, a door-to-door accessible transit service, and systematically upgrades bus stops, terminals, and ferries with features like accessible pads, low-floor buses, audible/visual stop announcements, and improved shelters. These efforts are guided by ongoing audits of stops and facilities to remove barriers and enhance wayfinding. The service publishes rider guides and clear information online so residents and visitors can plan accessible trips, directly aligning with the solution’s focus on upgrading transit stops and providing public guides.

resources.name: Downtown Halifax Accessibility Map
resources.description: This initiative catalogs accessible entrances, washrooms, curb ramps, parking, and barrier-free routes for businesses, public buildings, and venues throughout the downtown core, giving residents and visitors a practical guide to plan accessible outings. The Downtown Halifax Business Commission engages member businesses with on-site visits and resources to identify and complete upgrades like ramps, door openers, and better signage. By combining audits of local venues with a publicly available map and guides, the project directly implements the solution’s mapping and upgrade approach.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

resources.name: Autism-Friendly Communities
resources.description: Autism Nova Scotia partners with municipalities, libraries, recreation centres, museums, and businesses to assess physical and sensory barriers, deliver staff training, and implement sensory-friendly features such as quiet hours, visual schedules, social stories, and designated low-stimulus spaces. The program provides practical toolkits and community guides that highlight autism-friendly and accessible locations, helping families and visitors plan their participation in community life. This directly advances the solution’s goals by auditing spaces, upgrading environments, and publishing clear guides for the public.
resources.address: 5945 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3H 1Y4

resources.name: Sensory Friendly Mornings
resources.description: Discovery Centre hosts regular Sensory Friendly Mornings that lower lighting and sound, limit attendance, and provide quiet zones and sensory tools to create a more inclusive museum experience. The Centre publishes a sensory guide and social story to help visitors prepare, and it maintains accessibility features like elevators, ramps, and accessible washrooms throughout the venue. This program exemplifies the solution by upgrading a public venue for physical and sensory accessibility and sharing practical visitor guides.
resources.address: 1215 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

solutions.text: Microgrant Program for Diverse Entrepreneurs: Create small, low-barrier grants and wraparound supports (business coaching, legal aid, microloans) to help entrepreneurs from underrepresented groups start and scale local businesses.

resources.name: Business Development Services and Immigrant Business Loan
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides low-barrier microloans alongside wraparound supports for immigrant and refugee entrepreneurs, including one-on-one business advising, market research, and mentorship. The program also connects clients to legal and accounting clinics and delivers training on business planning, marketing, and regulations, helping newcomers overcome systemic barriers to start and scale local businesses.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Aboriginal Business and Entrepreneurship Development (ABED) Program
resources.description: NCNS delivers the federal ABED program in Nova Scotia for off-reserve and non‑status Indigenous (including Mi’kmaq) entrepreneurs, offering non‑repayable contributions (microgrants and grants) for planning, startup, and expansion costs. Participants receive culturally grounded, wraparound supports such as business coaching, help developing proposals and business plans, and referrals to legal and financial advisors to navigate systemic barriers and grow sustainable enterprises.
resources.address: 129 Truro Heights Road, Truro, NS B6L 1X1

solutions.text: Cultural Exchange and Celebration Series: Support regular community festivals, artist residencies, youth showcases, and story-sharing events that celebrate Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer, and 2SLGBTQIA+ cultures to build cross-cultural connections.

resources.name: Public Programs and Events
resources.organization: Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21
resources.description: The Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21 hosts year-round public programs, cultural celebrations, and oral history initiatives that share newcomer stories and lived experiences. Through community festivals, youth workshops, and storytelling events co-created with local partners, the museum creates opportunities for diverse communities to connect and learn from one another, directly supporting cross-cultural understanding.

resources.name: African Heritage Month Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia
resources.description: Coordinated by the Black Cultural Centre, African Heritage Month features province-wide community events, youth showcases, lectures, and performances that celebrate African Nova Scotian culture and history. These programs invite participation from people of all backgrounds, fostering story-sharing and cultural exchange that strengthen inclusion and anti-racism efforts across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 10 Cherry Brook Road, Cherry Brook, NS B2Z 1A8

resources.name: Mawio’mi on the Common (Halifax Powwow)
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre organizes the annual Mawio’mi on the Common and related cultural programming featuring Mi’kmaq drumming, dance, craft, and storytelling. The powwow welcomes the broader public and includes youth-focused activities, creating a shared space for reconciliation and cross-cultural celebration between Mi’kmaq communities and residents from diverse backgrounds.

resources.name: Community Connections Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections Program brings newcomers and local residents together through conversation circles, cultural events, and storytelling activities that build relationships across cultures. Regular group outings, youth-friendly workshops, and community celebrations help participants share traditions and create welcoming networks that include and respect diverse identities.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Pride Prom and Youth Arts Events
resources.description: The Youth Project hosts Pride Prom and year-round youth arts and storytelling events that showcase 2SLGBTQIA+ identities and experiences. Through open mics, creative workshops, and collaborations with schools, libraries, and community festivals, these programs create celebratory spaces for young people and promote cross-cultural connection and inclusion.

solutions.text: Local Diversity Advisory Council: Form a permanent advisory council with representation from Mi'kmaq communities, African Nova Scotians, newcomer groups, 2SLGBTQIA+ advocates, and disability organizations to advise municipal decisions, budgets, and services.

resources.name: Advisory Committee on the Inclusion and Equity (ACIE)
resources.description: A permanent advisory body to Halifax Regional Council that provides advice on policies, programs, budgets, and services to advance inclusion, anti-racism, and reconciliation. Membership includes representatives from Indigenous (Mi'kmaq) and African Nova Scotian communities, newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+ advocates, and persons with disabilities, aligning directly with the solution’s call for a multi-representative local diversity council.

resources.name: African Nova Scotian Advisory Committee
resources.description: A standing committee that advises Halifax Regional Council on strategies, policies, budgets, and municipal services affecting African Nova Scotian communities. By ensuring sustained representation and formal input from African Nova Scotians into municipal decision-making, it operationalizes the solution’s model of a diversity advisory body informing local governance.

resources.name: Accessibility Advisory Committee
resources.description: A permanent advisory committee mandated under Nova Scotia’s Accessibility Act that provides Halifax Regional Council with guidance on inclusive policies, public infrastructure, and municipal services. Composed primarily of people with disabilities and disability organization representatives, it directly fulfills the solution’s requirement for disability representation within a local advisory body shaping budgets and service delivery.

solutions.text: Culturally-Relevant Career Pathways in Schools: Partner schools, community organizations, and employers to integrate culturally-relevant career programming, co-op placements, and guest-mentorships that reflect diverse local histories and industries.

resources.name: Imhotep’s Legacy Academy (ILA)
resources.description: Imhotep’s Legacy Academy partners with public schools across Nova Scotia to deliver culturally responsive STEM programming led by African Nova Scotian university student mentors and professionals. Through after-school programs, in-school workshops, guest mentor talks, and paid summer research/industry placements, ILA connects students to local STEM industries and postsecondary pathways, highlighting African Nova Scotian histories and role models to build relevant career trajectories.

resources.name: In.Business: A Mentorship Program for Indigenous Youth
resources.organization: Cape Breton University – Purdy Crawford Chair in Indigenous Business Studies
resources.description: In.Business links Mi’kmaq and other Indigenous high school students with Indigenous business mentors through a blend of in-person and virtual activities organized with partner schools across Nova Scotia. The program integrates culturally grounded business content, mentor talks from local entrepreneurs and managers, and workplace/college visits to illuminate career pathways in regional industries and postsecondary business programs.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

resources.name: Women Unlimited Program
resources.description: Women Unlimited partners with NSCC campuses, school boards, unions, and employers to deliver career discovery, pre-apprenticeship training, and supported work placements for women and gender-diverse people in trades and technology. The program brings industry guest mentors into classrooms, builds culturally safe cohorts (including African Nova Scotian and Mi’kmaw participants), and facilitates co-op/placement experiences aligned with Nova Scotia’s industries such as shipbuilding, construction, and energy.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding – African Nova Scotian and Mi’kmaw Cohorts
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a multi-partner initiative that recruits, trains, and supports cohorts of African Nova Scotian and Mi’kmaw learners for shipbuilding trades, led by NSCC in collaboration with Irving Shipbuilding and community organizations. Students receive culturally relevant wraparound supports, mentorship from community and industry role models, and paid work-integrated learning/placements that connect directly to careers at the Halifax Shipyard and local suppliers.

resources.name: African Nova Scotian Student Support Worker Program
resources.description: The ANS Student Support Worker Program embeds culturally responsive staff in schools to guide African Nova Scotian students, connect them to co-op education and Options & Opportunities (O2) pathways, and bring Black professionals into classrooms as guest mentors. Working with community organizations and employers, the program organizes career exploration events, workplace visits, and mentorships that reflect African Nova Scotian histories and local industries, supporting transitions to trades, college, university, or entrepreneurship.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

solutions.text: Targeted Housing Supports: Develop local programs that prioritize affordable, accessible housing and rental supports for youth from marginalized communities, including transitional housing, rent supplements, and eviction-prevention assistance.

resources.name: Supported Housing for Young Mothers (SHYM)
resources.description: SHYM provides safe, affordable transitional housing and wraparound supports for mothers aged 16–24 and their children. The program combines on-site case management, life-skills and tenancy training, and rent‑geared‑to‑income units, while helping participants secure rent supplements or community housing as they transition to independence. Staff also focus on eviction prevention through budgeting support, mediation with landlords, and early intervention when tenancy issues arise.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: Phoenix Supportive Housing Program
resources.description: Phoenix’s Supportive Housing Program assists youth aged 16–24—including 2SLGBTQIA+ youth, African Nova Scotians, Indigenous youth, newcomers, and youth with disabilities—to access and maintain safe, affordable housing. Housing workers place youth in community apartments with rent subsidies or rent supplements where available, and provide intensive case management, tenancy education, and connections to income supports. The team emphasizes eviction prevention through landlord mediation, arrears planning, and ongoing coaching to sustain tenancies.

resources.name: Roots House Youth Shelter
resources.organization: Pictou County Roots for Youth Society
resources.description: Roots House offers emergency and short-term transitional housing for youth aged 16–24 in Pictou County and provides individualized housing navigation toward affordable, longer-term rentals. Staff help youth apply for rent supplements and community housing, secure damage deposits, and build budgeting and tenant-rights skills. The program prioritizes eviction prevention through early intervention, landlord mediation, and ongoing case management to stabilize housing.
resources.address: 603 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3S4

resources.name: Housing & Settlement Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS supports newcomer youth and families to find and keep safe, affordable rentals by providing one-on-one housing navigation, tenant-rights education, and workshops on the Nova Scotia rental market. Staff connect clients to rent supplement programs and other financial supports, and coordinate with landlords and partners to secure accessible units when needed. Eviction-prevention assistance includes budgeting help, advocacy, and early problem-solving when tenancy issues emerge.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Indigenous Housing Support Program
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre provides culturally grounded housing supports for urban Mi’kmaq and other Indigenous peoples, including youth, using Housing First and Rapid Rehousing approaches. Housing support workers help clients secure affordable apartments, access rent supplements where available, and navigate utilities and documentation. The program emphasizes eviction prevention through ongoing tenancy coaching, arrears planning, and landlord mediation to sustain stable housing.

solutions.text: Community Safety and Anti-Harassment Protocols: Work with community groups and businesses to adopt clear anti-harassment policies, reporting mechanisms, and rapid-response supports for incidents targeting race, Indigeneity, gender identity, or disability.

resources.name: SHIFT: Creating Safer Workplaces
resources.description: SHIFT provides free, confidential training and consulting to Nova Scotia employers and community organizations to prevent and respond to sexual and gender-based harassment. The project helps workplaces adopt clear anti-harassment policies, build accessible reporting mechanisms, and implement trauma-informed, rapid response supports for affected workers, including 2SLGBTQIA+ people.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: Welcoming Workplaces: Equity, Diversity & Inclusion Training
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Welcoming Workplaces offers anti-racism, anti-oppression, and human rights training and policy reviews for businesses and community groups. They work with employers to draft and implement anti-harassment and anti-discrimination policies, establish reporting and complaint processes, and connect newcomers who experience hate incidents with legal and support services.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Hate Crime Unit and Online Hate Incident Reporting
resources.description: Halifax Regional Police’s Hate Crime Unit investigates criminal incidents motivated by bias, including those targeting race, Indigeneity, religion, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, or disability. It maintains dedicated reporting options and community liaison programs, and provides rapid-response coordination with victims, businesses, and community groups to address and prevent harassment and hate-motivated incidents.

resources.name: Workplace Sexual Harassment Navigator Program
resources.organization: Legal Information Society of Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Workplace Sexual Harassment Navigator program offers free, trauma-informed legal information and navigation to workers and employers across Nova Scotia. It helps organizations develop and update anti-harassment policies, clear reporting and investigation procedures, and provides rapid supports to individuals experiencing harassment, including referrals and assistance with human rights and policing pathways.

resources.name: Inclusion in the Workplace: Anti-Discrimination & Policy Support
resources.description: reachAbility delivers disability inclusion training and policy support to employers and community organizations, focusing on eliminating discrimination and harassment against persons with disabilities. They assist workplaces to create accessible anti-harassment policies, confidential reporting channels, and effective accommodation and response protocols, and offer quick, barrier-free support to clients through legal information clinics and navigation services.
resources.address: 3845 Joseph Howe Drive, Suite 201, Halifax, NS B3L 4H9

solutions.text: Language and Cultural Revitalization Support: Fund community-led Mi'kmaq language classes, cultural camps, and school partnerships, and encourage inclusion of African Nova Scotian history and newcomer cultural content in local programming.

resources.name: Mi'kmaw Language Revitalization Program
resources.description: Mi'kmaw Kina'matnewey’s Mi'kmaw Language Revitalization Program supports community-led language classes, immersion initiatives, and land-based cultural camps across member Mi'kmaw communities. The program funds local instructors, develops curriculum and resources for Mi'kmaw community schools, and partners with schools to expand Mi'kmaw language offerings, strengthening intergenerational transmission and cultural pride.

resources.name: Mi'kmaw Language Program
resources.description: The Confederacy of Mainland Mi'kmaq’s Mi'kmaw Language Program delivers community-based Mi'kmaw language classes and creates learning resources in collaboration with Elders and fluent speakers. It facilitates cultural camps, teacher training, and school partnerships so that Mi'kmaw language and culture are embedded in local programming for children, youth, and families.

resources.name: Education & Public Programs
resources.organization: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia’s Education & Public Programs provide exhibits, school tours, curriculum-linked materials, and community events that foreground African Nova Scotian history and culture. By working with teachers, youth groups, and municipalities, the Centre ensures African Nova Scotian content is included in classrooms and local programming, fostering inclusion and anti-racism.
resources.address: 10 Cherry Brook Road, Cherry Brook, NS B2Z 1A8

resources.name: Education Research & ANS Curriculum Development
resources.description: The Delmore 'Buddy' Daye Learning Institute develops African Nova Scotian–centered curriculum resources, conducts research, and provides educator training to integrate ANS history and culture in schools. Through partnerships with school boards and community organizations, DBDLI equips teachers and youth programs to include accurate African Nova Scotian content in local learning and activities.
resources.address: 5450 Cornwallis Street, Suite 300, Halifax, NS B3K 1A9

resources.name: Community Connections
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections program links newcomers with local volunteers and groups, and organizes intercultural events and workshops in schools, libraries, and community hubs. These activities bring newcomer cultural content into local programming and help institutions co-design inclusive initiatives with immigrant communities, building welcoming spaces for youth and families.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Mental Health and Peer Support Services: Expand culturally-safe, low-cost mental health and peer-support services targeted to youth from marginalized backgrounds, including mobile outreach and crisis navigation assistance.

resources.name: Youth Outreach Program (YOP)
resources.description: Chebucto Connections’ Youth Outreach Program is a free, mobile outreach service for youth ages 16–24 facing barriers in Spryfield and surrounding communities. Outreach workers meet youth where they are (homes, schools, and community spaces) to provide peer-informed support, crisis de-escalation, and navigation to mental-health, housing, and income services. The program prioritizes marginalized youth, including African Nova Scotians, Mi’kmaq/Indigenous youth, newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+ youth, and youth with disabilities, and coordinates with emergency and clinical services when needed.
resources.address: 531 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1X3

resources.name: Wellness Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Wellness Program provides culturally safe mental-health supports for immigrants and refugees, including youth and young adults settling in Nova Scotia. Services include peer-support groups, psychoeducation, and one-on-one navigation to community and clinical mental-health services, as well as assistance with crisis planning and referrals to urgent care when necessary. The program is low- or no-cost and reduces barriers through interpretation, trauma-informed practice, and partnerships with schools and youth-serving agencies.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Community Support Program (Youth & Family Wellness)
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Community Support Program and youth services offer culturally grounded wellness supports for urban Indigenous youth and families in Kjipuktuk/Halifax. Staff and Elders facilitate peer circles, land-based and cultural activities, and one-to-one supports, while Indigenous Navigators help youth access mental-health care and crisis services across systems. Programming is free and delivered in a culturally safe environment that addresses systemic barriers faced by Mi’kmaq and other Indigenous youth in the city.

resources.name: Child & Youth Mental Health Programs
resources.description: Strongest Families Institute delivers free, evidence-based e-mental health programs for children and youth across Nova Scotia (for example, skill-based coaching for anxiety and behaviour concerns for ages 6–17). Trained non-clinical coaches provide scheduled telephone sessions and digital tools outside typical business hours, improving access for rural, low-income, and otherwise marginalized families; they also help families navigate to higher-intensity or crisis services when needed. The approach emphasizes cultural safety, family-centred support, and reduced stigma through confidential, at-home care.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 326, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Inclusive Hiring Toolkit for Local Employers: Develop and distribute a practical toolkit with inclusive job posting templates, accessible interview practices, bias-reduction checklists, and onboarding guidance tailored to small and medium local employers.

resources.name: Employer Support & Workplace Culture Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS equips small and medium employers with practical inclusive hiring tools, including sample inclusive job postings, interview accommodation guidance, and bias-reduction checklists tailored to recruiting and retaining immigrant and refugee talent. They provide employer consultations, templates and toolkits, and onboarding guidance to build culturally inclusive workplaces across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Employer Engagement Services
resources.description: Team Work Cooperative (a Nova Scotia Works centre) supports local employers with inclusive recruitment toolkits that feature equity-focused job posting templates, accessible interviewing practices, and practical bias-mitigation checklists. Their staff provide one-on-one employer advising and onboarding supports to help SMEs adopt inclusive policies and retain diverse hires, including youth, newcomers, and persons with disabilities.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 705, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Ready, Willing and Able – Nova Scotia Employer Supports
resources.organization: Autism Nova Scotia (provincial delivery partner for Ready, Willing and Able)
resources.description: Delivered in Nova Scotia by Autism Nova Scotia, Ready, Willing and Able partners with employers to implement inclusive hiring for autistic people and persons with intellectual disabilities using practical toolkits. Resources include inclusive job description and posting templates, interview accommodation guides, bias-awareness checklists, and structured onboarding supports with job coaching to ensure sustainable, inclusive workplaces.
resources.address: 5945 Spring Garden Road, Suite 103, Halifax, NS B3H 4R4

resources.name: Immigration Employer Support – Inclusive Hiring Resources
resources.description: Halifax Partnership provides employers with step-by-step resources to recruit and retain diverse talent, including newcomers and international students, through inclusive hiring guides and toolkits. Materials feature sample inclusive job postings, interview and assessment accommodations, bias-reduction checklists, and onboarding best practices tailored for small and medium-sized businesses in the Halifax region.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1103, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Community Data and Progress Dashboard: Co-create, with consent and privacy safeguards, a public dashboard tracking equity indicators (employment, wages, housing, service access) for Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotians, newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+, and people with disabilities to guide policy and accountability.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Quality of Life Initiative – Public Data Portal
resources.description: Engage Nova Scotia co-created a province-wide Quality of Life survey and public data portal with community partners, including Mi’kmaq and African Nova Scotian organizations, to measure equity-related indicators such as employment, wages, housing, belonging, discrimination, and access to services. The portal shares anonymized, disaggregated results (where sample sizes and privacy protections allow) for groups such as newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+ people, and persons with disabilities, enabling governments and community leaders to track progress and guide policy and accountability.

resources.name: Halifax Index
resources.description: The Halifax Index is an annual, public dashboard that tracks key indicators across the economy and quality of life, including labour market participation, wages, immigration, housing affordability, and inclusion metrics for Halifax. It provides open, methodologically transparent data that governments, employers, and community groups use to identify inequities and monitor progress on inclusive growth, aligning with the solution’s goal of public accountability on equity outcomes.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: 211 Nova Scotia – Public Data and Trends
resources.description: 211 Nova Scotia publishes anonymized, aggregated dashboard views of real-time community needs (e.g., housing, employment, food, settlement, mental health) drawn from calls and online contacts across the province. These public insights help governments and service providers identify access gaps for equity-deserving populations—including newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+ communities, and people with disabilities—while adhering to strict consent and privacy safeguards.

resources.name: Equity and Anti-Racism Data and Progress Reporting
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia – Office of Equity and Anti-Racism Initiatives
resources.description: The Office of Equity and Anti-Racism Initiatives coordinates the collection and governance of disaggregated equity data across the provincial government and publishes public-facing progress reporting tied to Nova Scotia’s equity and anti-racism priorities. This work advances a cross-government dashboard approach to track outcomes in employment, income, housing, and service access for Mi’kmaq communities, African Nova Scotians, newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+ people, and persons with disabilities, with strong consent, privacy, and community oversight practices.

obstacles.title: Health Care and Mental Health Access Shortfalls
obstacles.description: Primary care shortages, long wait times, and limited youth mental health and addictions services reduce quality of life and productivity.

solutions.text: Community-run evening and weekend primary care clinics: Local clinics staffed by rotating volunteer family doctors, nurse practitioners and medical students to provide walk-in and booked appointments outside typical hours, reducing wait times and improving access for working youth.

resources.name: Mobile Primary Care Clinics
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health operates rotating mobile primary care clinics that set up in community locations on evenings and weekends to serve people who struggle to access daytime appointments or who are unattached to a family practice. Clinics offer a mix of walk-in and pre-booked visits and are staffed by rotating teams of family physicians, nurse practitioners, and learners, expanding access outside typical hours and reducing wait times for non-urgent issues.

resources.name: North End Community Health Centre – Extended Hours Primary Care
resources.description: The North End Community Health Centre provides primary care with select evening and weekend clinics to better serve working residents and youth who cannot attend during standard hours. Care is delivered by a collaborative team of family doctors, nurse practitioners, and trainees from local health professional programs, offering both booked and limited same-day access to reduce delays and reliance on emergency departments.

resources.name: Spryfield Family Medicine Teaching Site – After-Hours Clinic
resources.description: Dalhousie Family Medicine’s Spryfield teaching clinic runs after-hours primary care sessions for its community and rostered patients, scheduling evening and select weekend appointments outside the regular workday. Services are provided by rotating family medicine residents and supervising physicians, with nurse practitioners involved, enabling both same-day/urgent bookings and short walk-in windows that improve timely access for working-age and youth patients.

resources.name: Family Focus Medical Clinics – After-Hours and Walk‑In Care
resources.description: Family Focus Medical Clinics provide extended evening and weekend primary care through a combination of booked and walk-in visits, allowing working youth and adults to access care beyond typical office hours. Clinics are staffed by rotating family physicians and nurse practitioners across multiple sites, which helps reduce wait times for non-urgent issues and diverts patients from emergency departments.

solutions.text: Peer-led youth mental health networks: Trained peer supporters and drop-in groups run by young people in collaboration with clinicians to provide early support, navigation, destigmatized conversation spaces and warm referrals to clinical services.

resources.name: DSU Peer Support Centre
resources.description: The Dalhousie Student Union’s Peer Support Centre provides drop-in, confidential, non-judgmental support from trained student peer supporters. Volunteers are equipped to listen, share resources, and make warm referrals to Dalhousie Student Health & Wellness clinicians and community services, creating early access points and navigation support. The student-run space reduces stigma by normalizing conversations about mental health among youth while collaborating with campus professionals.

resources.name: Peer Support and Mentoring Program
resources.description: Eating Disorders Nova Scotia offers free peer-led support groups, drop-ins, and one-to-one mentoring for youth and young adults, delivered by trained supporters with lived experience. The program partners with clinicians and programs at the IWK Health Centre and Nova Scotia Health for training, consultation, and coordinated care, providing warm referrals to clinical services when needed. By centering lived experience in welcoming spaces, it reduces stigma and helps youth navigate services early.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 309, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: 2SLGBTQIA+ Youth Peer Support Groups
resources.description: The Youth Project hosts peer-led support and drop-in groups for 2SLGBTQIA+ youth across Nova Scotia, facilitated by trained youth leaders and staff. Groups provide safe, affirming spaces for conversations about mental health, identity, and well-being, and staff collaborate with school-based supports and clinicians at the IWK and Nova Scotia Health to provide navigation and warm referrals. This peer-centered model reduces stigma and connects young people to appropriate care earlier.

resources.name: Youth Peer Support (Mental Health & Addictions)
resources.description: IWK Health integrates Youth Peer Support Specialists with lived experience into its Mental Health & Addictions services for adolescents and young adults. These peers co-facilitate groups and offer one-to-one support, helping youth navigate services and providing warm hand-offs to clinicians within IWK and to community partners. The model fosters early engagement, destigmatized conversations, and better connections to appropriate clinical care.

solutions.text: School- and campus-based mental health teams: Embed social workers, counsellors and telehealth pods in schools and post-secondary campuses so students get timely assessment, brief therapy and referral without leaving education settings.

resources.name: SchoolsPlus (School-Based Integrated Services)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: SchoolsPlus embeds multidisciplinary teams—including SchoolsPlus facilitators, social workers, mental health clinicians and community partners—directly in public schools across Nova Scotia. These teams provide on-site assessment, brief counselling/therapeutic intervention and coordinated referrals, and they help students access virtual care from school when needed, reducing wait times and barriers to service while keeping youth in their learning environments.

resources.name: School-Based Mental Health and Addictions Services
resources.organization: IWK Health, Mental Health & Addictions Program
resources.description: IWK Health places mental health clinicians within junior and senior high schools in the Halifax region to deliver timely assessment, brief therapy and direct referrals without students needing to leave school. The program collaborates with school teams and offers both in-person and virtual (tele-mental health) sessions to increase rapid access and continuity of care.

resources.name: Dalhousie Student Health & Wellness – Counselling & Psychological Services
resources.description: Dalhousie embeds counsellors, social workers and a stepped-care mental health team on campus to provide same-day/single-session counselling, brief therapy and coordinated referrals to community/psychiatric care as needed. Services are offered in-person and virtually, with private on-campus spaces available for telehealth appointments so students can access care without leaving the university setting.

resources.name: NSCC Ivany Campus Counselling Services
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Ivany Campus
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College provides on-campus counselling at the Ivany Campus, embedding counsellors within Student Services to deliver timely intake, brief therapy, crisis support and referrals to Nova Scotia Health or community providers. The service offers flexible access through in-person and virtual appointments, with private rooms available on campus for students who need a confidential space for telehealth sessions.

resources.name: Nancy Dingwall Health and Counselling Centre – Counselling Services
resources.description: Cape Breton University’s on-campus centre embeds a multidisciplinary team—including counsellors and health professionals—to provide mental health assessment, brief counselling and coordinated referrals for students. The centre offers both in-person and virtual counselling, enabling students to access tele-mental health from campus and receive timely support without leaving their educational environment.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

solutions.text: Community telehealth hubs: Privacy-equipped rooms in libraries, community centres and youth hubs with high-speed internet and trained facilitators to help residents connect with virtual primary care and mental health appointments.

resources.name: Book a Room (Private Study and Meeting Rooms for Virtual Care)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries offers free, bookable private rooms and study spaces with reliable high-speed internet where residents can attend virtual primary care or mental health appointments. Library staff provide basic tech help (e.g., setting up devices, using Zoom/Teams, connecting headsets) and can assist patrons in accessing Nova Scotia Health’s VirtualCareNS or other telehealth platforms, effectively functioning as community telehealth hubs.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Book a Room & Tech Help for Virtual Appointments
resources.description: The Truro Library provides bookable private rooms and public computers with broadband internet to support residents who need a quiet, confidential space for virtual medical or counseling appointments. Staff offer one-on-one technology assistance to help users connect with clinicians, navigate telehealth platforms, and ensure audio/video privacy, aligning with the community telehealth hub model.

resources.name: Library Meeting Rooms and Tech Help for Telehealth
resources.description: People’s Place Library in Antigonish makes private meeting rooms and study spaces available for virtual health and mental health appointments, supported by high-speed Wi-Fi and device access. Librarians provide tech coaching and can help patrons set up secure video calls, headphones, and telehealth logins, enabling youth and adults to connect with care when transportation or wait times are barriers.

resources.name: Private Rooms and Digital Assistance for Virtual Health Visits
resources.description: McConnell Library in Sydney offers bookable quiet rooms and computer workstations with high-speed internet where community members can attend virtual appointments with primary care providers or mental health clinicians. Staff can assist with video platform setup, device connection, and privacy accessories (e.g., headsets), making the branch a practical telehealth access point for Cape Breton residents.

solutions.text: Mobile health and mental health outreach units: Regularly scheduled vans or pop-up clinics that visit rural and underserved neighbourhoods to deliver primary care, counselling, harm reduction supplies and appointment booking support.

resources.name: Mobile Outreach Street Health (MOSH)
resources.description: MOSH is a mobile primary care and harm-reduction service that operates nurse- and physician-led outreach from a van across Halifax Regional Municipality. The team visits shelters, encampments, and underserved neighbourhoods to provide wound care, basic primary care, mental health support, and harm-reduction supplies (e.g., naloxone), and they help people book follow-up appointments and connect to ongoing care.

resources.name: Mainline Mobile Outreach (Needle Exchange Van)
resources.description: Mainline’s mobile outreach van follows regular routes across Halifax to reach people who use substances and others facing barriers to care. Staff distribute safer-use and harm-reduction supplies and naloxone, offer brief counselling and health education, and assist with referrals and appointment booking for detox, opioid agonist treatment, testing, and primary care.

resources.name: Ally Centre Street Outreach and Mobile Harm Reduction
resources.description: The Ally Centre operates street outreach and a mobile harm-reduction service throughout the Cape Breton Regional Municipality, including rural and underserved areas. The team distributes sterile equipment and naloxone, provides brief counselling and peer support, and connects clients to testing, addictions care, and primary care by arranging referrals and appointments; a street nurse offers basic primary care and wound care during pop-up visits.

resources.name: Mental Health Mobile Crisis Team (HRM)
resources.organization: IWK Health and Nova Scotia Health
resources.description: The Mental Health Mobile Crisis Team provides 24/7 telephone triage and mobile mental health outreach in Halifax Regional Municipality. Clinicians travel to homes and community locations to deliver on-site assessment, brief counselling, and safety planning, and they connect clients to ongoing services by coordinating referrals and follow-up appointments with community mental health and addictions programs.

solutions.text: Local clinician recruitment and retention partnerships: Community-driven incentive packages (mentorship, subsidized housing, relocation supports, integration into local social networks) developed with municipal and business partners to attract and keep providers.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Physician Recruitment
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health recruits family physicians, nurse practitioners, and mental health clinicians across the province and partners with municipalities, chambers of commerce, and community navigators to build local incentive packages. The program provides relocation assistance, community site visits, and spousal employment connections, while coordinating mentorship with local clinical teams to support retention. These community-driven supports help integrate providers into local social networks and reduce primary care and mental health access gaps.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: Physician Recruitment & Retention (South Shore)
resources.organization: Health Services Foundation of the South Shore
resources.description: The Health Services Foundation of the South Shore works with municipal partners, local businesses, and Nova Scotia Health to attract and keep physicians serving Lunenburg and Queens counties. The program funds and coordinates community-hosted visits, relocation support, temporary housing assistance, and family/spousal employment connections, and it pairs new clinicians with local mentors and welcoming committees. By bundling community incentives and social integration supports, it strengthens long‑term retention and improves access to primary and mental health services.
resources.address: 90 Glen Allan Drive, Bridgewater, NS B4V 3S6

resources.name: Antigonish Physician Recruitment Committee
resources.description: Hosted by the St. Martha’s Regional Hospital Foundation, this community-led committee partners with the Town and County of Antigonish, local employers, and Nova Scotia Health to recruit and retain physicians. It organizes customized community tours, helps with relocation and housing, facilitates spousal employment and school placements, and connects newcomers with local clinical mentors and social networks. These locally tailored incentive packages support long‑term retention and expand access to primary and mental health care in the region.

resources.name: Town of Lunenburg Physician Recruitment Initiative
resources.description: The Town of Lunenburg collaborates with local businesses, housing providers, and health-system partners to attract family physicians and other clinicians to the community. The initiative offers municipal incentive supports, assists with housing searches and relocation logistics, and connects providers and their families to community ambassadors, clubs, and social networks; it also facilitates mentorship linkages with local practitioners. These community-driven packages help new clinicians settle and stay, improving access to primary and mental health services on the South Shore.

solutions.text: Primary care cooperative (community-owned clinic): A community-governed clinic model that hires NPs and physicians on sustainable schedules, offers team-based care and prioritizes access for youth and underserved populations.

resources.name: North End Community Health Centre (Primary Care Clinic)
resources.description: A community-governed, non-profit primary care clinic that employs salaried family physicians, nurse practitioners, social workers, and allied health providers in team-based, sustainable roles. It prioritizes access for underserved populations—including youth, people experiencing homelessness, and racialized communities—through integrated primary care, mental health/addictions supports, and outreach (including the MOSH program), aligning with a community-owned clinic model.

resources.name: Clare Health Centre (Centre de santé de Clare)
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Clare
resources.description: A municipally owned, community-directed primary care clinic that recruits and supports family physicians and nurse practitioners working in a collaborative practice with sustainable schedules. It improves access for rural and francophone residents (including youth and families) by offering team-based primary care, chronic disease management, and navigation to mental health/addictions services in partnership with local providers.

resources.name: Eskasoni Health Centre (Primary Care and Wellness)
resources.description: A Mi’kmaw community-governed primary care centre that delivers culturally safe, team-based services with family physicians, nurse practitioners, nurses, and mental health/addictions counsellors. It prioritizes access for youth and families in Eskasoni through integrated primary care, youth wellness programming, and coordinated social supports, with providers working in salaried, sustainable roles within a community-owned model.

resources.name: Halifax Newcomer Health Clinic
resources.description: A team-based primary care clinic that employs physicians, nurse practitioners, nurses, and social workers to provide initial primary care and mental health supports to government-assisted refugees and other newcomers, with interpretation and trauma-informed services. It prioritizes access for an underserved population and transitions patients to long-term community practices, demonstrating sustainable, collaborative primary care scheduling and wraparound support.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2059, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Community paramedicine and home visit program: Expanded paramedic roles to provide in-home follow-up, chronic disease management and mental health checks, reducing ED visits and supporting continuity of care for vulnerable youth.

resources.name: EHS Community-Based Paramedicine (Mobile Integrated Health) Program
resources.organization: Emergency Health Services (EHS) Nova Scotia / Medavie Health Services Nova Scotia
resources.description: Community paramedics provide scheduled in-home visits for patients and families, including youth with chronic conditions, to perform assessments, vital-sign and medication reviews, and mental health/wellness checks. Working in partnership with primary care, Nova Scotia Health Mental Health & Addictions, and IWK Health, they coordinate referrals and share visit notes to support continuity of care. By delivering proactive follow-up and treating non-urgent needs at home, the program reduces avoidable 911 calls and emergency department visits.

resources.name: Extended Care Paramedic (ECP) Program
resources.organization: Emergency Health Services (EHS) Nova Scotia / Medavie Health Services Nova Scotia
resources.description: Advanced-care paramedics are dedicated to long-term care and supportive-living sites, delivering on-site assessment, point-of-care testing, wound care, catheter changes, and management of acute-on-chronic issues under standing orders and virtual physician support. They conduct follow-ups and wellness checks, liaising with family physicians and mental health teams when behavioral or psychiatric symptoms arise. Treating residents where they live prevents unnecessary transfers to hospital and maintains continuity with the person’s regular care team.

resources.name: EHS Palliative Care Paramedic Program
resources.organization: Emergency Health Services (EHS) Nova Scotia / Medavie Health Services Nova Scotia
resources.description: Specially trained paramedics make home visits to people with serious illness or enrolled in palliative care, providing symptom control (e.g., pain, breathlessness), anticipatory guidance, and after-hours support using individualized care plans developed with palliative and primary care teams. Visits include caregiver coaching, medication adjustments per protocol, and screening for distress or mental health needs with connection to grief and family/youth supports as appropriate. This delivers high-quality care at home, reduces emergency department use, and strengthens continuous, person-centered care.

solutions.text: Mental Health First Aid and suicide prevention training: Free or low-cost certified training for teachers, coaches, employers, faith leaders and volunteers so more community members can recognize crisis signs and make timely referrals.

resources.name: Suicide Prevention Gatekeeper Training (safeTALK and ASIST)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health, Mental Health and Addictions Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Mental Health and Addictions Program partners with community organizations to deliver safeTALK and ASIST suicide-prevention training across the province, often at no or low cost. These certified courses prepare teachers, coaches, employers, faith leaders and volunteers to recognize suicide risk, engage safely, and make timely referrals to crisis lines and local mental health services.

resources.name: Mental Health First Aid (MHFA) Training
resources.description: Safety Services Nova Scotia offers certified Mental Health First Aid courses for workplaces and community groups, with public and group sessions available at accessible rates. Training helps participants identify signs of mental health and substance-use crises, provide initial support, and connect people to professional and community resources.
resources.address: 201 Brownlow Avenue, Unit 9, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1W2

resources.name: Psychological First Aid (PFA) Training
resources.organization: Canadian Red Cross – Nova Scotia Office
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross Nova Scotia office delivers low-cost Psychological First Aid training (online and in-person) to volunteers, coaches, employers and faith communities. The course equips participants to recognize stress and mental health crisis signs, offer supportive communication, and refer individuals to appropriate local services and crisis supports.

resources.name: Teacher Mental Health First Aid and Suicide Prevention PD
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Teachers Union provides professional development that includes Mental Health First Aid and suicide-prevention sessions (e.g., safeTALK) for teachers and school staff across the province. These trainings build educators’ capacity to notice warning signs in students and colleagues, have supportive conversations, and make timely referrals to school-based and provincial mental health services.
resources.address: 3106 Joseph Howe Drive, Halifax, NS B3L 4L7

resources.name: Mental Health First Aid (Adults Who Interact with Youth and Standard)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Continuing Education
resources.description: NSCC Continuing Education offers public MHFA courses at campuses across Nova Scotia, with reduced rates for students and community partners. Facilitators certify participants to identify and respond to mental health and suicide-related crises and to refer individuals to appropriate community and clinical supports.

solutions.text: Employer-community youth wellness partnerships: Local employers partner with clinics and counselling services to offer flexible scheduling, on-site or virtual counselling access, employee assistance for young workers and supported return-to-work plans.

resources.name: CBI Health Return-to-Work and Mental Health Services (Halifax)
resources.description: CBI Health partners with local employers to deliver occupational rehabilitation and mental health supports that help employees, including young workers, access counselling and structured return-to-work plans. Services are offered in-person and virtually, and include coordination with employers for flexible scheduling, workplace accommodations, and graduated return-to-work after mental health leave. CBI clinicians also liaise with primary care and EAP providers to ensure seamless care between the workplace and community services.

resources.name: TEAM Work Cooperative Supported Employment (Nova Scotia Works)
resources.description: This Nova Scotia Works centre brokers partnerships between employers and community clinicians to support youth and young adults with mental health conditions in gaining and keeping work. They coordinate job development with flexible scheduling, connect clients to on-site or virtual counselling, and design supported return-to-work plans with employers following health-related absences. Ongoing job coaching and workplace accommodations are arranged in collaboration with therapists, EAPs, and managers.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 316, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Laing House Employment & Education Support
resources.description: Laing House works with youth aged 16–29 living with mental illness to re-enter work or school through employer partnerships and individualized wellness planning. Staff collaborate with local employers to arrange flexible schedules, workplace accommodations, and supported return-to-work pathways while connecting members to counselling and peer support available in-person or virtually. This wraparound model bridges community mental health care with employer practices so young workers can stabilize, succeed, and remain employed.

solutions.text: Harm reduction and addiction peer navigation services: Peer navigators and community harm reduction sites that distribute naloxone, provide safer-use information, linkage to treatment and nonjudgmental support to reduce barriers into care.

resources.name: Sharp Advice Needle Exchange
resources.description: Sharp Advice provides low‑barrier harm reduction services including distribution of sterile supplies, take‑home naloxone kits, and safer‑use education. Peer outreach workers with lived experience offer nonjudgmental support and navigation, helping people connect to detox, opioid agonist treatment, and mental health and social services, reducing barriers to care for youth and adults.

resources.name: Needle Distribution & Harm Reduction Program
resources.description: Northern Healthy Connections Society operates a community harm reduction site that distributes sterile equipment, provides take‑home naloxone kits and training, and offers safer‑use information. Peer outreach workers build trust, provide nonjudgmental support, and navigate clients to addiction treatment, primary care, and mental health services across Colchester and surrounding areas.

resources.name: Direction 180 Low-Threshold Opioid Agonist Treatment & Outreach
resources.description: Direction 180 provides low‑threshold opioid agonist treatment and harm reduction services, including naloxone distribution, safer‑use education, and mobile/community outreach that meets people where they are. Peer and outreach staff offer nonjudgmental support and practical navigation—assisting with appointments, referrals, and linkage to broader health and social services to reduce barriers into care.

solutions.text: Culturally safe and Indigenous-led services: Support Indigenous and newcomer-led counselling, traditional healing programs and multilingual navigators to ensure services are welcoming and effective for diverse youth.

resources.name: Health & Wellness Program
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Health & Wellness Program provides Indigenous-led counselling, Elder support, cultural programming, and traditional healing circles for urban Indigenous youth and families. By embedding Mi’kmaw culture, language, and ceremony in services, the program creates a culturally safe environment that improves access to mental health support and helps youth feel welcomed and understood.

resources.name: Health and Wellness Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Health and Wellness Program offers settlement counselling, mental health navigation, and group supports for immigrant and refugee youth and families, delivered by staff and volunteers who speak multiple languages. The program uses interpreters and cultural brokers to reduce barriers, ensuring newcomers can access timely, culturally responsive counselling and referrals.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Indigenous Patient Navigation Services (Central Zone)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health – Indigenous Health Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Indigenous Patient Navigation Services provide Indigenous youth and families with culturally safe support across the care journey, including advocacy, care coordination, and links to Elders and traditional healing. Navigators help youth access mental health and addictions services more effectively by bridging cultural gaps and addressing systemic barriers.

resources.name: Settlement Services
resources.description: YWCA Halifax’s Settlement Services provide trauma-informed counselling, case management, and referrals for newcomer women and youth, with access to interpretation and multilingual navigation. The program supports mental wellness by offering culturally responsive, gender-informed services that help youth connect to the right health and social supports quickly.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

solutions.text: Volunteer ride-share and transit voucher programs: Community-run transportation assistance (volunteer drivers, subsidy vouchers, scheduled shuttle routes) so young people can reliably reach clinics, counselling and follow-ups.

resources.name: Wheels of Hope (Transportation)
resources.description: The Canadian Cancer Society’s Wheels of Hope provides volunteer driver rides and travel cost subsidies so patients, including children and youth with cancer, can get to medical appointments, treatment, and related counselling. The program coordinates scheduled pickups and offers low- or no-cost transportation, directly addressing transportation barriers that can prevent timely care and follow-up.

resources.name: Transport de Clare – Community Transportation
resources.description: Transport de Clare offers pre-booked, door-to-door rides across the Municipality of Clare, using community drivers and accessible vehicles to get residents to health clinics, counselling, and follow-up appointments. With affordable, subsidized fares and scheduled routes when demand warrants, it functions as a community-run alternative to ride-share for rural youth and families who lack reliable transportation.

resources.name: Low Income Transit Pass Program
resources.description: Halifax Transit’s Low Income Transit Pass Program provides a 50% discount on monthly bus and ferry passes for eligible low-income residents, helping youth and families afford regular transportation to clinics and mental health services. By reducing fare costs and enabling consistent use of public transit, the program functions as a standing fare subsidy that supports reliable access to appointments and follow-ups.

solutions.text: Digital health navigation volunteers: Trained volunteers who help youth book appointments, set up telehealth apps, complete intake forms and follow up on referrals to reduce missed appointments and no-shows.

resources.name: Peer Support Program
resources.description: Laing House provides youth (ages 16–29) living with mental illness with peer-led support that includes practical health system navigation. Trained peer and adult volunteers help members book primary care and mental health appointments, set up and test telehealth tools on their phones or library computers, complete intake and referral forms, and follow up on next steps to reduce missed appointments and no-shows.
resources.address: 1225 Barrington Street, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3J 1Y2

resources.name: Settlement Volunteer Program (Health and Wellness Navigation)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS engages trained settlement volunteers and interpreters to help newcomer youth and families navigate the health system and digital care. Volunteers assist with booking appointments, creating accounts and installing telehealth apps, completing clinic intake/referral forms, and providing reminders or follow-ups so clients don’t miss care, reducing no-shows linked to language and digital barriers.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Book a Librarian – Tech Help
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries offers one-on-one tech help where staff and, in some branches, trained volunteers support youth and families to access digital health. They help patrons book medical and mental health appointments online, set up and practice using telehealth apps (e.g., Zoom for Healthcare), and complete e-forms and referrals; branches with private rooms and devices also provide guidance and reminders to reduce missed appointments.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Tech Help (One-on-One Digital Support)
resources.description: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library branches provide individualized tech help where staff and volunteers assist residents—including youth—to prepare for virtual care. Support includes creating accounts, installing and testing telehealth apps, booking appointments online, completing intake/referral forms, and offering follow-up instructions so clients arrive prepared and avoid missed visits.

solutions.text: Community wellness hubs integrating services and opportunities: Multi-use centres that combine counselling, primary care triage, job-search supports, skill-building workshops, arts programs and fitness options to address mental health upstream and connect youth to employment pathways.

resources.name: The North Grove
resources.description: The North Grove is a community hub in Dartmouth North that blends family support, social work and counselling, community meals, and food skills education with partner-delivered services. Staff help residents navigate and connect to primary care and mental health services, while running skill-building workshops in cooking, gardening, parenting, and digital literacy that reduce isolation and build readiness for work. Youth and young adults can access volunteer-to-employment pathways, creative activities, and accessible wellness and physical activity groups in one inclusive space.

resources.name: Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre is an urban Indigenous community hub offering wraparound supports under one roof, including cultural and clinical mental health services, youth programming, and family and housing supports. Its Employment & Training Centre provides job-search coaching, resume help, and links to training and employers, while staff triage and connect clients to primary care and addictions supports. Youth engage in arts, culture, and recreation programming that strengthen wellness upstream and create pathways into education and work.

resources.name: Chebucto Connections
resources.description: Chebucto Connections is a place-based community hub in Spryfield that integrates navigation and counselling support through partnerships with Community Health Team programming and other health services, alongside youth education-to-employment supports. The Pathways to Education program provides mentoring, tutoring, and career exploration, and staff connect youth to Nova Scotia Works job services and host skill-building workshops. The hub also offers community arts and recreation activities and helps residents access primary care and mental health resources, reducing barriers and wait-time impacts.
resources.address: 531 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1X3

resources.name: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia
resources.description: ISANS operates a multi-service settlement hub that integrates needs assessment and counselling, health and mental health navigation, language classes, and employment services for newcomers, including youth. Clients can access job-search support, career bridging and mentoring, entrepreneurship training, and digital skills workshops in the same centre where staff triage health concerns and link to primary and specialized care. ISANS also hosts community-building, arts and cultural activities and connects participants to local recreation and wellness opportunities to support wellbeing alongside employment pathways.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

obstacles.title: Childcare Availability and Early Learning Workforce
obstacles.description: Insufficient, unevenly distributed childcare—especially for infants, rural areas, and non-standard hours—constrains parents’ ability to work or train.

solutions.text: Community Childcare Co-ops: Parent-led cooperatives that pool time, skills and small local funding to open and run licensed micro-centres in towns and neighbourhoods, reducing costs and increasing local ownership.

resources.name: Wolfville Children’s Centre
resources.description: A community-founded, parent-governed non-profit that operates a licensed early learning and child care centre offering infant, toddler, preschool, and school-age care in a small, neighbourhood setting. Parents serve on the board and lead fundraising and volunteer efforts, pooling time and local resources to expand spaces and keep costs manageable—directly reflecting the co-operative, community-owned micro-centre model described.

resources.name: Lunenburg Day Care Centre
resources.description: A parent- and community-led non-profit society that runs a licensed early learning centre in the Town of Lunenburg, offering small-group childcare close to where families live and work. Families participate in governance, volunteering, and local fundraising to support staffing and facilities—embodying a cooperative, community-owned approach that lowers barriers and sustains a micro-centre in a rural setting.

solutions.text: After-hours and Weekend Care Hubs: Community-run hubs offering evening and weekend care on rotating schedules to serve shift workers, hospitality and seasonal industry employees.

resources.name: Valley Family Home Child Care Agency
