resources.description: A licensed family home child care network that recruits, approves, and supports multiple home-based educators across the Annapolis Valley, coordinating flexible placements for families. Several approved homes offer extended, evening, and weekend hours on a rotating basis, creating a community-run hub model that serves shift workers in agriculture, health care, retail, and seasonal industries.

resources.name: Cape Breton Family Place Family Home Child Care Agency
resources.organization: Cape Breton Family Place Resource Centre
resources.description: This licensed agency coordinates a network of approved family child care homes throughout Cape Breton, matching parents to caregivers who provide non-standard hours. By organizing evening and weekend care among multiple providers, it operates as an after-hours hub for hospitality, healthcare, and shift-based workers who need reliable childcare outside the typical weekday schedule.

solutions.text: Mobile Childcare Units: Van- or trailer-based early learning setups that visit rural areas, seasonal worksites and small communities on a regular schedule to provide short-term care and programming.

resources.name: Pop-Up to Play (Mobile Loose Parts Play)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE) – Resource Centre
resources.description: Pop-Up to Play is a mobile early learning program delivered from a van/trailer stocked with loose-parts materials that creates temporary play-and-learn environments in parks, community halls, and at partner worksites. The team travels to rural and underserved communities on a published schedule, offering supervised, short-duration, play-based sessions that give caregivers brief respite and connect families to early learning experiences where licensed childcare is limited.

resources.name: Outreach Playgroups
resources.description: ESFRA’s Outreach Playgroups are mobile, staff-led early learning sessions that travel by program van to small communities along the Eastern Shore, setting up play-based environments in libraries, community halls, and other local spaces. The pop-up format provides short-term care and programming on a regular schedule, allowing caregivers to attend appointments or services while children engage in developmentally rich activities close to home.
resources.address: 11 East Petpeswick Road, Musquodoboit Harbour, NS B0J 2L0

resources.name: Outreach Playgroups and Pop-Up Early Years Programming
resources.organization: Maggie’s Place Family Resource Centre – Colchester/East Hants
resources.description: Maggie’s Place operates mobile outreach playgroups that bring early learning materials and facilitators by van to rural sites across Colchester and East Hants. These pop-up sessions provide short-term, supervised programming in community venues on a rotating schedule, supporting families in areas with limited childcare access and enabling parents to participate in nearby programs or training.

resources.name: Mobile Outreach Playgroup
resources.organization: Family Matters – Lunenburg County Family Resource Centre
resources.description: Family Matters delivers mobile outreach playgroups that travel with equipment and learning materials to rural communities throughout Lunenburg County, setting up temporary early learning environments in local halls and community spaces. The program offers short-duration, play-based care and programming on a regular route, helping families in childcare deserts access early learning close to where they live and work.

solutions.text: School-based Before/After Programs: Use elementary school classrooms and gyms to host affordable before- and after-school care, coordinated by community organizations and municipal recreation departments.

resources.name: EXCEL Child Care (Before and After School Program)
resources.description: EXCEL provides affordable before- and after-school care directly in elementary schools across the Halifax region. Operated by the Halifax Regional Centre for Education, the program uses school classrooms and gymnasiums to deliver supervised care, physical activity, and enrichment, making it convenient for families and aligned with the school day.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: YMCA School Age Child Care (Before & After School) — Cape Breton
resources.description: The YMCA of Cape Breton partners with local elementary schools to offer school-based before- and after-school care. Programs operate within school classrooms and gym spaces under agreements with the regional education centre, providing accessible, low-cost supervision, healthy snacks, and active play that supports working families.

resources.name: YMCA School Age Child Care (Before & After School) — Pictou County
resources.description: The YMCA of Pictou County delivers before- and after-school care at partner elementary schools in the region. By using school classrooms and gymnasiums, the program provides convenient, supervised care with recreation and homework support, coordinated in collaboration with the local regional centre for education.
resources.address: 2756 Westville Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 5C6

resources.name: YMCA School Age Child Care (Before & After School) — Southwest Nova
resources.description: The YMCA of Southwest Nova Scotia operates school-based before- and after-school programs in partnership with elementary schools across Yarmouth, Digby, and Shelburne counties. Utilizing classrooms and gym spaces, the program offers affordable, licensed care that aligns with school schedules and supports parents working standard and extended hours.

solutions.text: Employer-Community Partnerships: Local businesses collaborate with municipalities and non-profits to offer onsite or nearby childcare slots, subsidy programs and flexible scheduling for employees.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Childcare Centre
resources.description: Campus-based, licensed childcare located on Saint Mary’s University grounds that partners with the university (employer) to offer convenient, nearby care for faculty and staff as well as students. The centre coordinates with campus schedules, offers priority access for SMU employees, and participates in provincial subsidy programs—helping employers retain staff by reducing childcare barriers and aligning hours with work and study needs.

resources.name: MSVU Child Study Centre (Early Learning Program)
resources.description: A non-profit early learning centre on the Mount Saint Vincent University campus that collaborates with the university to provide on-site childcare for employees and students. By situating care where people work and study, prioritizing campus families, and accepting government fee subsidies, it advances employer-supported childcare access and helps accommodate variable academic and work schedules.

resources.name: NSCC Kingstec Early Learning Centre
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Kingstec Campus
resources.description: Located at Nova Scotia Community College’s Kingstec Campus, this centre works with the college (employer) and local partners to provide on-campus childcare that supports staff and student parents. It offers full‑day licensed care close to workplaces and classrooms, aligns enrollment options with class/work timetables, and participates in provincial affordability programs—reducing childcare-related barriers to employment and training.

solutions.text: Local ECE Training and Apprenticeship Programs: Community colleges, businesses and centres create paid ECE apprenticeships and fast-track certification pathways tied to local hiring commitments.

resources.name: Work and Learn ECE Diploma Pathway
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE)
resources.description: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education runs flexible, accelerated diploma pathways that let participants remain employed in local child care centres while completing coursework. Through employer partnerships, students earn wages in licensed centres during their studies, complete practicum requirements on site, and fast-track to Level 3 classification—often with hiring commitments or immediate role upgrades from their sponsoring centres.

resources.name: Early Childhood Education (ECE) Diploma – Accelerated/Workplace Cohorts
resources.description: NSCC delivers ECE diploma programs across multiple campuses, including accelerated and blended options that align coursework with paid work in local child care centres. The college partners with employers—particularly in rural and under-served communities—to run workplace-based cohorts where learners earn income as assistants while training, complete required practicums on the job, and transition quickly into full ECE roles with local hiring commitments.

resources.name: Diplôme en éducation de la petite enfance (EPE) – Workplace/Community Cohorts
resources.description: Université Sainte-Anne offers a French-language ECE diploma tailored to Acadian and Francophone communities, combining online learning with work-integrated placements in local centres. Many students are employed in licensed child care or pre-primary settings while studying, and the university partners with regional providers who prioritize hiring graduates—expanding French-language childcare capacity in rural Nova Scotia through an earn-while-you-learn pathway.

solutions.text: ECE Wage Supplements and Bursaries: Community fundraising, local foundations and municipal top-ups provide wage supplements, signing bonuses and training bursaries to retain and attract early learning staff.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Early Childhood Educator Compensation Framework
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: Province-wide compensation framework that funds licensed child care operators to implement a standardized wage grid for classified Early Childhood Educators (ECEs). By providing government-funded wage increases and supplements directly to centres, the framework raises pay, supports retention, and helps attract qualified staff—addressing workforce shortages that limit childcare availability.
resources.address: One Government Place, 1700 Granville Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1X5

resources.name: Early Childhood Education Tuition Support Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: Provincial tuition support and bursaries for individuals entering or upgrading Early Childhood Education credentials in Nova Scotia. The program reduces financial barriers by covering eligible tuition and related costs, creating a pipeline of trained educators and helping retain existing staff through funded upskilling.
resources.address: One Government Place, 1700 Granville Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1X5

resources.name: NSCECE Student Bursaries and Scholarships
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education
resources.description: Donor- and community-funded bursaries and scholarships for students enrolled in Early Childhood Education programs at the Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education. These awards offset tuition, materials, and practicum-related costs, functioning as training bursaries that attract new ECEs and support current workers to complete credentials.

resources.name: NSCC Foundation Scholarships, Bursaries and Awards (Early Childhood Education)
resources.description: The NSCC Foundation administers donor- and partner-funded scholarships and bursaries, including awards targeted to Early Childhood Education students across Nova Scotia Community College campuses. By reducing education costs through community-backed funding, the program acts as a training bursary pipeline that helps recruit and retain the ECE workforce.

solutions.text: Shared Nanny and Care Pool: Neighborhood-based shared-nanny arrangements and parent-run scheduling platforms let families share vetted caregivers for staggered hours and non-standard shifts.

resources.name: CanadianNanny.ca – Nanny Share & Caregiver Marketplace
resources.description: CanadianNanny.ca is an online platform that allows Nova Scotia families to find and share vetted caregivers, explicitly supporting nanny-share arrangements where two or more households split a caregiver’s time and costs. Parents in Halifax, Cape Breton, and rural communities can post nanny-share jobs and filter caregivers by non-standard availability (evenings, weekends, overnights) to cover staggered shifts, then use in-platform messaging to coordinate schedules and logistics.
resources.address: 20 Leslie Street, Suite 203, Toronto, ON M4M 3L4

resources.name: Kijiji Halifax – Childcare & Nanny Share Listings
resources.description: Kijiji’s Halifax Childcare category is actively used by local parents to create and join neighborhood nanny shares, enabling families to pool resources and arrange shared caregivers for split shifts and off-peak hours. Listings and location filters help match nearby households and caregivers, while built-in messaging supports parent-run scheduling and coordination for flexible, non-standard care arrangements across the HRM and surrounding areas.
resources.address: 500 King Street West, Suite 200, Toronto, ON M5V 1L9

solutions.text: Intergenerational Care Programs: Partnerships between childcare programs and seniors' homes create mutual-care days where seniors support early learning activities and receive social engagement.

resources.name: Northwood Intergenerational Programs
resources.description: Northwood brings licensed childcare groups and pre-primary classrooms into its Halifax campus for scheduled mutual-care days where residents and young children read stories, sing, garden, and do crafts together. Recreation therapy staff and early childhood educators co-facilitate activities so seniors can actively support early learning while receiving meaningful social engagement, reducing isolation and strengthening community ties.

resources.name: Ocean View Intergenerational Playgroup and Visiting Program
resources.description: Ocean View Continuing Care Centre partners with local licensed childcare centres to host recurring playgroups and early-learning visits in common spaces at the residence and through reciprocal visits to childcare sites. Seniors participate alongside children and ECEs in reading circles, music and movement, and fine-motor craft activities, providing social connection for elders while enriching early learning experiences for children.
resources.address: 1909 Caldwell Road, Eastern Passage, NS B3G 1M3

resources.name: Windsor Elms Village Intergenerational Learning and Play Program
resources.organization: Windsor Elms Village for Continuing Care Society
resources.description: Windsor Elms Village collaborates with nearby early learning and childcare programs to run regular intergenerational sessions where residents and children engage in storytime, baking, art, and sensory play. Guided by recreation staff and early childhood educators, the program enables seniors to mentor and support children’s social, language, and motor development while enhancing residents’ purpose, belonging, and cognitive stimulation.

solutions.text: Pop-up Event Childcare Network: A trained volunteer and paid-provider roster that enables safe, temporary childcare at local training events, job fairs and community programs to remove attendance barriers.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides on-site, temporary childcare so parents can attend language classes, employment workshops, job-readiness training and information sessions. The CNC service uses trained, screened childcare staff who follow federal newcomer childcare standards, removing childcare as a barrier to participation in training and community programs.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC) — YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs
resources.description: The YMCA offers temporary, on-site childcare for newcomer parents while they attend language instruction, settlement orientations, employment readiness workshops and community programming. Childcare is delivered by trained, vetted staff under the CNC model, enabling safe, short-term care that lets adults fully participate in learning and labour-market activities.

resources.name: Child Minding for Programs
resources.organization: Home of the Guardian Angel (Chebucto Family Centre)
resources.description: Chebucto Family Centre offers free, temporary child minding during parenting classes, support groups and partner-led community sessions, so caregivers can attend training and programs without childcare barriers. Services are provided by trained staff and volunteers who follow safety and child-welfare protocols, effectively creating a pop-up childcare option tied to community events.

resources.name: Program Childcare and Child Minding
resources.description: Dartmouth Family Centre provides on-site, short-term child minding so parents and caregivers can participate in skills workshops, parenting education and community programs. Using trained staff and volunteers, the centre sets up safe, time-limited care aligned with program schedules, reducing attendance barriers for families.
resources.address: 107 Albro Lake Road, Dartmouth, NS B3A 3Y2

resources.name: Child Minding and Family Program Supports
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre offers temporary child minding to support participation in cultural programming, employment-readiness workshops and community events for urban Indigenous families. Care is delivered by trained staff and volunteers, providing safe, short-duration childcare that helps remove access barriers to training and community services.

solutions.text: Childcare Space Conversion Initiative: Community-led projects to convert underused municipal and commercial spaces—libraries, churches, empty storefronts—into licensed childcare rooms with shared governance.

resources.name: Ward 5 Neighbourhood Centre Early Learning & After School Programs
resources.description: Ward 5 operates licensed early learning and school-age programs from converted rooms within St. Mark’s Anglican Church in Halifax’s North End, turning underused parish and community hall space into childcare classrooms. The centre’s community board works with the church and local partners to share governance of the space, expanding access to affordable care in a walkable neighbourhood.

resources.name: New Ross Family Resource Centre Licensed Childcare
resources.description: The New Ross Family Resource Centre converted multi-purpose rooms in its community facility into licensed early learning spaces for infants, toddlers, and preschoolers, addressing rural childcare shortages. Governed by a local non-profit board and working with municipal and community partners, the centre exemplifies shared governance and community-led repurposing of existing space into regulated childcare.

resources.name: Sackville Heights Daycare & Learning Centre (at Sackville Heights Community Centre)
resources.description: Located in the repurposed Sackville Heights Community Centre—a former school—the daycare uses converted classrooms and common areas as licensed childcare rooms, expanding capacity without new construction. The community centre is overseen by a volunteer board and operates through tenant partnerships, providing shared governance and community-led management of underused municipal space for childcare.
resources.address: 45 Connolly Road, Middle Sackville, NS B4E 1K3

solutions.text: Transportation Linkages for Rural Families: Coordinated community shuttles and ride-share arrangements that connect rural families to central childcare hubs during peak hours.

resources.name: Fixed-Route Rural Service Connecting to Community Hubs
resources.description: Kings Transit Authority operates fixed-route buses across rural Kings and Annapolis Counties, timed around morning and afternoon commuter peaks. These routes link outlying communities to central towns like New Minas, Kentville, Wolfville, and Berwick—locations where licensed childcare centres and early learning programs are concentrated—allowing parents to use the bus as a reliable shuttle for childcare drop-off and pick-up. By providing predictable, peak-hour connections to these hubs, the service functions as a coordinated linkage between rural families and childcare access points.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

resources.name: Door-to-Door Community Transit (Grouped Ride-Share)
resources.description: BayRides provides pre-booked, door-to-door community transportation across the rural St. Margaret’s Bay area and groups riders traveling in similar directions. Dispatchers schedule morning and late-afternoon trips to central hubs in Upper Tantallon and nearby communities, making it practical for parents to reach licensed childcare and after-school programs during peak hours. This demand-responsive, shared-ride model operationalizes coordinated shuttles and ride-shares that bridge rural households to childcare hubs.
resources.address: 5284 St. Margarets Bay Road, Upper Tantallon, NS B3Z 2H9

resources.name: Community Ride-Share and Commuter Services
resources.description: MusGo Rider is a community-owned transportation co-operative that offers pre-booked, door-to-door rides and commuter services across the Eastern Shore and Musquodoboit Valley. The service coordinates shared trips for work and essential needs and will align pick-ups and drop-offs at daycare and early learning centres in regional hubs along Highway 7 during morning and afternoon peaks. By pooling trips and timing them with childcare hours, MusGo Rider delivers the coordinated shuttle and ride-share linkages rural families need to access childcare.
resources.address: 71 Park Road, Musquodoboit Harbour, NS B0J 2L0

solutions.text: Local Childcare Matching Platform: A community-managed online/mobile platform listing licensed centres, available spots, qualified caregivers, and shared-shift matches with ratings and scheduling tools.

resources.name: Find Regulated Child Care – Online Directory
resources.organization: Department of Education and Early Childhood Development, Government of Nova Scotia
resources.description: The province’s online directory lets families search licensed child care centres and family home programs across Nova Scotia by location, age group, language, and hours. Providers can update profiles and available spaces so parents can see current openings and contact programs directly, functioning as a local matching platform that improves access in rural areas and for non‑standard hours where offered.

resources.name: EXCEL Before and After School Program – Online Registration and Site Finder
resources.description: EXCEL’s web portal lists program locations at elementary schools across HRM, shows site‑by‑site capacity/status, and allows families to register, waitlist, and manage schedules by specific days. By centralizing openings and scheduling for licensed school‑age care, it matches parents with nearby spots and supports coverage around the school day to accommodate varied work hours.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: ECE Casual Relief Staff Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE)
resources.description: NSCECE operates a digital registry and dispatch service that connects licensed child care centres with qualified, vetted early childhood educators and assistants for shift coverage and short‑term placements. Centres post staffing needs and schedule coverage through the service, enabling rapid, on‑demand matching that helps programs maintain ratios and extend hours, which in turn expands reliable childcare availability for families.

resources.name: Care.com Nova Scotia – Child Care Marketplace
resources.description: Care.com’s Nova Scotia portal lists local babysitters, nannies, and in‑home caregivers with verified profiles, ratings/reviews, availability calendars, and in‑app messaging/booking tools. Families can filter by location, schedule (nights, weekends, part‑time), and qualifications to match with caregivers and coordinate shared‑shift or nanny‑share arrangements, complementing licensed centre options where spots are limited or hours are non‑standard.

solutions.text: Culturally Inclusive and Language-support Programs: Community groups develop culturally responsive childcare options and recruit multilingual ECE workers to serve diverse and newcomer families.

resources.name: ISANS Care for Newcomer Children (CNC)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides Care for Newcomer Children on-site while parents attend English classes, employment training, and settlement services. The program uses culturally responsive practices, offers toys and routines that reflect families’ cultures, and recruits multilingual early childhood staff and childminders so children can be comforted and supported in their home languages. This directly expands access to childcare for newcomer families and strengthens the culturally competent early learning workforce.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Aboriginal Head Start (AHS) – Early Childhood Development Program
resources.description: The Mi'kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s AHS program offers free, culturally grounded preschool for Indigenous children, integrating Mi'kmaw language, culture, Elders’ teachings, and family support. The centre hires Indigenous and culturally knowledgeable early childhood educators, creating a welcoming environment that affirms identity and supports language revitalization. This culturally responsive model provides accessible childcare and strengthens a workforce equipped to serve diverse families.

resources.name: Internationally Educated Early Childhood Educators (IEECE) Pathways and PLAR
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE)
resources.description: NSCECE supports internationally educated early childhood educators through advising, Prior Learning Assessment and Recognition (PLAR), and bridging courses that emphasize inclusive, culturally responsive practice. By helping multilingual newcomers obtain recognition and targeted training, the program expands the supply of qualified ECEs who can communicate with families in their home languages and deliver culturally attuned care. NSCECE also connects graduates with centres across Nova Scotia to meet community needs.

resources.name: YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs – Care for Newcomer Children (CNC)
resources.description: The YMCA provides Care for Newcomer Children while parents participate in settlement, employment, and youth/family programs. Staff reflect the diversity of clients and include multilingual educators trained in trauma-informed and culturally safe practices, ensuring children experience familiar languages and culturally relevant activities. This reduces childcare barriers for newcomer families and strengthens inclusive early learning capacity in HRM.

solutions.text: Advocacy and Municipal Support Task Force: A community task force that aggregates local needs data, advocates for zoning, licensing streamlining, municipal subsidies and public investment in childcare.

resources.name: Child Care Now Nova Scotia
resources.description: Child Care Now Nova Scotia is a provincial chapter of the national child care advocacy organization that coordinates parent, educator, and provider input to document local child care needs and gaps across communities in Nova Scotia. It uses that evidence to advocate with municipal councils and planners for zoning that permits child care centres in more neighbourhoods, streamlined permitting/licensing processes, and municipal investment tools (e.g., capital grants, fee relief, and land/space access) to expand non-profit child care. The chapter also works with provincial and federal partners to align municipal actions with broader public funding for infant care, rural services, and non-standard hours.

resources.name: Halifax Chamber of Commerce – Child Care Policy and Advocacy
resources.description: The Halifax Chamber of Commerce gathers member data and community feedback on workforce barriers, including child care shortages, and publishes policy positions that inform municipal decision-makers. Leveraging this evidence, the Chamber advocates to Halifax Regional Municipality for land-use and permitting changes that make it easier to open and expand child care centres, and for municipal supports such as tax/fee relief and public investment partnerships to increase spaces. It also collaborates with provincial partners to support ECE workforce growth in tandem with local zoning and licensing improvements.

resources.name: Halifax Partnership – Workforce and Policy Collaboration on Child Care
resources.description: Halifax Partnership convenes employers, post-secondary institutions, and government to collect and analyze local labour market data, identifying child care accessibility as a key constraint on workforce participation. Using these insights, it engages with HRM Planning & Development and council to encourage streamlined zoning/permitting for child care centres and to explore municipal investment mechanisms that help non-profit providers add infant, rural, and non-standard-hours spaces. The Partnership’s policy and investor tables help align municipal actions with provincial child care funding and ECE workforce strategies.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

obstacles.title: Cost of Living and Energy Affordability
obstacles.description: Inflation in food, insurance, transportation, and home energy erodes disposable income and the perceived value proposition of staying.

solutions.text: Community Energy Co-operatives (solar & wind): Local residents, businesses and municipalities pool funds to build small-scale renewable projects (rooftop/community solar, small wind) that supply electricity or credits to members, lowering energy bills and keeping revenue local while creating community governance and jobs.

resources.name: Mahone Bay Community Solar Garden
resources.organization: Town of Mahone Bay Electric Utility
resources.description: The Town of Mahone Bay Electric Utility operates a shared solar array where local residents and businesses can purchase subscriptions (panel capacity) and receive bill credits for the energy produced. By pooling community funds through subscriptions and municipal investment, the project lowers participants’ electricity costs, keeps energy dollars circulating locally, and supports community governance and local jobs in installation and maintenance.
resources.address: 493 Main Street, Mahone Bay, NS B0J 2E0

resources.name: Berwick Community Solar Garden
resources.description: The Berwick Electric Commission’s community solar garden allows customers to buy licenses to the output of one or more panels in a shared array and receive monthly bill credits, reducing household and business energy costs. The project is financed and owned locally by the municipal utility, enabling residents and the town to pool funds, retain revenue within the community, and create local employment for construction and operations.

resources.name: Antigonish Community Solar Garden
resources.description: The Town of Antigonish Electric Utility offers a community solar program where utility customers can purchase shares of a centralized solar array and receive energy credits on their bills proportional to their share. This model pools local capital with municipal ownership, reduces energy costs for participants, and ensures revenues and decision-making remain in the community while supporting local jobs.

resources.name: Ellershouse Wind Farm (Municipal Community Wind)
resources.description: Owned by the Alternative Resource Energy Authority (a partnership of the Towns of Antigonish, Berwick, and Mahone Bay), the Ellershouse Wind Farm supplies renewable electricity to the three community-owned utilities. By pooling municipal investment to develop and operate local wind generation, the project stabilizes and lowers wholesale power costs for residents, keeps revenues in Nova Scotia, and maintains public/community governance with local operations and maintenance jobs.
resources.address: 493 Main Street, Mahone Bay, NS B0J 2E0

solutions.text: Neighborhood Bulk-Buy Buying Groups: Organize community bulk purchases for groceries, heating fuel (bulk propane/wood pellets), and household staples to negotiate lower prices, reduce delivery costs, and support local suppliers through coordinated orders.

resources.name: Community Food Smart – Veith House Buying Club
resources.description: Veith House hosts a Community Food Smart bulk-buying club where neighbours pool their orders and money to purchase fresh produce at wholesale rates. Orders are coordinated monthly and delivered in bulk to the site for pick-up, reducing delivery costs and leveraging group buying power while prioritizing local suppliers where possible.

resources.name: Dartmouth North Community Food Centre – Affordable Markets & Food Boxes
resources.organization: Dartmouth Family Centre / Dartmouth North Community Food Centre
resources.description: The Dartmouth North Community Food Centre runs affordable community markets and food boxes by coordinating bulk purchases of produce from local farmers and wholesalers. By aggregating neighborhood demand and organizing centralized pick-ups, the program reduces per-unit and delivery costs for residents while channeling spending to local suppliers.

resources.name: Good Food Box – New Ross Family Resource Centre
resources.description: The New Ross FRC’s Good Food Box is a monthly community bulk-buy program that consolidates resident orders to purchase fresh produce at discounted, wholesale pricing. Volunteers pack boxes for pickup at the centre, reducing delivery costs for families and supporting local farmers and regional distributors through coordinated orders.

resources.name: Cape Breton Food Hub Co-op – Community Local Food Buying
resources.description: The Cape Breton Food Hub Co-op operates a member-based online ordering system that aggregates weekly orders from households and community sites across the island. By coordinating bulk orders from dozens of local producers and delivering to neighborhood pickup hubs, the Food Hub lowers distribution costs for residents and strengthens local supply chains.

solutions.text: Community Home Retrofit Program: A local program offering volunteer energy audits, group-negotiated contractor rates, bulk purchase of insulation/heat pumps, and coordinated scheduling so homeowners (especially renters and low-income households) can access affordable energy-efficiency upgrades.

resources.name: HomeWarming
resources.organization: Clean Foundation in partnership with Efficiency Nova Scotia and Nova Scotia Power
resources.description: HomeWarming provides free home energy assessments and no-cost efficiency upgrades (like insulation, air sealing, and heat pumps) to income-qualified Nova Scotia homeowners. The program manages procurement and a vetted installer network to secure competitive pricing and coordinates all scheduling, effectively delivering a community-style retrofit service that removes upfront costs and reduces energy bills for low-income households.

resources.name: Home Energy Assessment (HEA) and Rebates
resources.description: Efficiency Nova Scotia’s HEA program sends certified energy advisors to perform EnerGuide home energy audits and create prioritized upgrade plans. Through standardized rebates, a preferred-contractor network, and advisor-led coordination, homeowners can bundle upgrades like insulation and heat pumps at lower cost and with streamlined scheduling—closely mirroring a community retrofit approach.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: Affordable Housing Energy Efficiency Program
resources.description: Efficiency Nova Scotia works with non-profit and affordable multi-unit housing providers to deliver building-wide energy assessments and coordinated retrofits. By leveraging program incentives, a qualified-contractor network, and centralized project management, the program reduces per-unit costs for upgrades (e.g., insulation, heat pumps, and controls) and improves affordability for renters through lower energy bills.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: Clean Energy Financing Program (PACE)
resources.description: Bridgewater’s PACE program offers on-property, low-interest financing for home energy upgrades and pairs residents with energy advisors and approved contractors. The municipality coordinates assessments, contractor selection, and installation timelines—often batching projects—to help secure competitive rates on heat pumps, insulation, and other measures, making retrofits more affordable and accessible.

solutions.text: Tool Libraries and Repair Cafés: Shared tool lending libraries and regular community repair events let people borrow equipment and fix appliances or furniture, extending product life, cutting replacement costs, and passing on DIY skills across generations.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: A member-based lending library offering hundreds of hand, power, and garden tools that residents can borrow instead of buying. It directly lowers household costs and extends product life by enabling people to maintain and repair furniture, appliances, bicycles, and homes, while workshops and volunteer support pass on practical DIY skills across generations.

resources.name: Repair Café (Halifax Public Libraries)
resources.description: Free drop-in events where volunteer fixers help residents diagnose and repair small appliances, electronics, clothing, and household items. Hosted at branches like Halifax Central Library, these events extend product life, keep items out of landfill, save families money, and build hands-on repair skills through one-on-one guidance.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Repair Café St. Margarets Bay
resources.description: Community repair events where volunteers bring tools and expertise to help people fix household goods, small electronics, clothing, and furniture at no charge. By facilitating shared tools and mentoring, the cafés reduce replacement costs, extend the life of everyday items, and encourage intergenerational DIY skill-sharing.
resources.address: 3646 Hammonds Plains Road, Upper Tantallon, NS B3Z 4R3

solutions.text: Community Food Hubs, Gardens and Preserving Co-ops: Shared land gardens, community kitchens and bulk-preservation co-ops increase access to affordable fresh food, reduce grocery bills, stabilize seasonal prices, and create local food distribution channels.

resources.name: The North Grove Community Food Programs
resources.description: The North Grove operates a community food centre with on-site gardens, a greenhouse, a community kitchen, affordable produce markets, and bulk meal-making/preserving workshops. By providing shared growing space, tools, and kitchen facilities, they help residents grow and preserve food together, lower grocery bills, and build a neighbourhood-scale food distribution channel that increases year-round access to fresh, affordable food.

resources.name: Veith House Community Kitchen & Garden
resources.description: Veith House runs a community garden and a commercial-grade community kitchen offering collective cooking and food-preservation workshops. These shared spaces enable residents to grow food, batch-cook and can/freeze seasonal produce, and access low- or no-cost meals—reducing food costs while strengthening local food networks in Halifax’s North End.

resources.name: WFM2Go (Local Food Hub)
resources.description: WFM2Go is the Wolfville Farmers’ Market’s online food hub that aggregates products from dozens of local farms and food producers for weekly pickup across the Annapolis Valley and HRM. By coordinating bulk ordering and efficient distribution, it shortens supply chains, improves price stability across seasons, and expands access to fresh, local food at predictable costs—supporting household budgets and year-round availability.

resources.name: Bulk Buy & Community Kitchen (Spryfield)
resources.description: Chebucto Connections coordinates a neighbourhood Bulk Buy program and hosts community kitchen sessions that help residents pool funds to purchase wholesale produce and then batch-cook or preserve it together. Linked with nearby community gardens, this hub model lowers per-household food costs, stabilizes seasonal prices through bulk purchasing, and creates a reliable local distribution point for fresh food.
resources.address: 531 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1X3

solutions.text: Local Carshare, Ride-Pooling and E-Bike Libraries: Community-run carshare fleets, organized ride-pooling for shift workers, and e-bike lending programs reduce individual transport costs, lower dependence on personal vehicles, and improve mobility in rural and suburban areas.

resources.name: Communauto Atlantic (CarShare Halifax-Dartmouth)
resources.description: Communauto Atlantic operates a local carshare fleet across Halifax and Dartmouth, giving members affordable, app-based access to vehicles without owning a car. By placing cars in neighbourhood pods and offering hourly/daily rates, the service reduces transportation costs for residents and lessens dependence on personal vehicles, aligning with the solution’s community carshare approach.

resources.name: smartTRIP Halifax (Carpool and Vanpool Program)
resources.description: smartTRIP Halifax is the municipality’s transportation demand management program that helps workers form and join carpools and vanpools, including for early, late, and rotating shifts. By organizing ride-pooling through employers and public tools, it lowers commuting costs, reduces single-occupant trips, and improves access to jobs for residents who do not own cars.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Community Transit
resources.description: MusGo Rider is a non-profit cooperative that provides pre-booked, shared rides across the Eastern Shore and Musquodoboit Valley, pooling passengers headed in the same direction to keep fares low. The service supports shift workers, students, and seniors by coordinating door-to-door or hub-to-hub trips, reducing reliance on private vehicles in rural areas and improving mobility for essential travel.
resources.address: 14 West Petpeswick Road, Musquodoboit Harbour, NS B0J 2L0

resources.name: Annapolis County E-Bike Loan Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Annapolis
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Annapolis lends pedal-assist e-bikes to residents for short trial periods so they can test commuting, errands, and local trips by e-bike. By removing the upfront cost barrier and providing a low-cost mobility option, the program helps households reduce transportation expenses and dependence on personal vehicles.
resources.address: 752 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

solutions.text: Housing Co-operatives and Shared Living Models for Youth: Community-supported co-op housing, shared rental models and mentorship for co-living setups help young people access affordable, secure housing while building supportive neighbourhood networks.

resources.name: Portal Youth Host Homes & Supportive Housing
resources.description: The Portal provides supported housing options for youth ages 16–24 across the Annapolis Valley, including transitional apartments and a Host Homes model where screened community members share their homes with youth. These shared-living and roommate-style arrangements reduce housing costs and offer built-in mentorship and life-skills coaching, helping young people secure stable, affordable housing while building supportive neighbourhood networks.

resources.name: SHYFT House & Supportive Housing Program
resources.description: SHYFT offers emergency shelter and longer-term supportive housing for youth aged 16–24 through a shared-living house and nearby apartment units in Yarmouth. The program combines affordable, communal housing with case management, mentorship, and life-skills development, enabling young people to stabilize their housing, pool resources, and transition toward independent, sustainable living.

resources.name: Roots House Transitional Housing
resources.organization: Pictou County Roots for Youth Society
resources.description: Roots for Youth operates a youth shelter and transitional housing in New Glasgow that uses shared-living arrangements to keep rents low while providing on-site supports. Youth receive mentorship, housing navigation, and life-skills training, and are supported to move into roommate-based rentals or shared community housing, strengthening social connections and affordability.
resources.address: 603 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3S6

resources.name: Supportive Housing for Young Mothers (SHYM)
resources.description: SHYM provides affordable, supportive housing for mothers aged 16–24 through shared apartments and on-site staff support in Halifax. By combining co-living with mentorship in parenting, budgeting, and tenancy, the program lowers housing costs, builds peer support networks, and helps young families transition to stable, independent housing.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: Residential Group Care & Transition Programs
resources.description: HomeBridge operates shared residential programs for youth that provide safe, stable housing alongside wraparound supports and mentorship. In these communal living environments, young people build life skills, access education and employment supports, and develop the networks needed to transition to affordable shared rentals or independent housing.

solutions.text: Time Banks and Skill-Share Networks: Neighbors exchange hours of work (childcare, carpentry, tutoring) rather than money, reducing out-of-pocket expenses and strengthening mutual support systems that improve overall household affordability.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: A community-run lending library that provides access to hundreds of tools so residents can complete home, bike, and DIY repairs without purchasing equipment. The library also hosts volunteer-led repair cafés and peer-to-peer skill-share workshops where neighbors exchange time and know-how to fix household items and learn practical trades skills, directly reducing out-of-pocket expenses and strengthening mutual support.

resources.name: Halifax Makerspace
resources.description: A member-driven community workshop where people share equipment and teach each other fabrication, electronics, and repair skills. Through open nights, fix-it sessions, and peer mentoring, experienced volunteers trade their time to help neighbors repair appliances, bikes, and electronics, creating a practical skill-share network that lowers household costs while building community capacity.

resources.name: Repair Café Wolfville
resources.description: Regular community events where volunteer fixers help residents mend clothing, repair small appliances, sharpen tools, and tune up bikes at no cost. By exchanging time and skills instead of money, neighbors reduce repair expenses, keep items in use longer, and build mutual support networks that improve overall household affordability.

resources.name: Library of Things and Repair Café (Halifax Public Libraries)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries lends sewing machines, musical instruments, and other household gear through its Library of Things, and hosts volunteer-led Repair Café events at branches. These programs enable residents to access tools and community expertise without spending money, fostering a skills-for-time exchange where fixers and mentors donate hours to help neighbors reduce everyday costs.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Community-led Group Insurance & Financial Advisory Clinics: Regular community workshops and group-negotiated sessions with local brokers or credit unions help households compare and access more affordable home, tenant and auto insurance, and low-cost financial products targeted to young people.

resources.name: CPA Canada Financial Literacy Sessions at Halifax Public Libraries
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts recurring, free financial literacy workshops at branches in partnership with CPA Canada volunteers, local credit unions and, at times, licensed insurance advisors. Sessions help residents, including youth and newcomers, compare home, tenant and auto insurance options and understand ways to reduce premiums, while also introducing low- or no-fee youth banking products available locally. By convening community-led clinics, the Library connects people directly with advisors who can provide quotes, referrals and unbiased comparisons.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Financial Literacy for Newcomers (Banking and Insurance Basics)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers ongoing group workshops on budgeting, banking, credit and insurance basics for newcomers, often co-facilitated with local credit unions and insurers. These clinics help participants compare tenant, auto and home insurance products and access starter or low-cost financial products such as youth/student accounts and secured cards to begin building credit. ISANS staff also provide one-on-one referrals to partner advisors or brokers to complete applications and find discounts appropriate for newcomers and young families.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Each One, Teach One Community Financial Literacy Workshops
resources.description: Sydney Credit Union offers the Each One, Teach One program, bringing free financial education workshops to community venues and schools. Facilitated by trained credit union staff, sessions cover budgeting, credit, and understanding insurance, and they walk participants through comparing local tenant, home and auto insurance options available to members via credit union partners. Attendees are connected to low-fee youth accounts, student credit solutions and member-discounted insurance, improving affordability for young people and households.

resources.name: Community Insurance Education & Group Information Sessions
resources.description: BrokerLink’s Nova Scotia brokers host free community Insurance 101 sessions with neighbourhood groups and libraries, explaining how to compare and bundle tenant, home and auto insurance to reduce costs. Advisors provide on-the-spot quote checks, outline student and multi-policy discounts, and help groups explore affinity savings negotiated through employers, associations or credit unions. These broker-led clinics make it easier for young drivers and renters to access competitively priced insurance through an unbiased comparison.
resources.address: 85 Tacoma Drive, Unit 200, Dartmouth, NS B2W 3Y6

solutions.text: Local Transit Advocacy and Community Shuttle Services: Community-organized advocacy for better public transit routes and on-demand rural shuttles (cooperatively run or municipally partnered) reduce transportation costs and improve access to jobs and services.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Cooperative – Rural Transportation
resources.description: MusGo Rider operates a cooperative, on-demand community shuttle service across the Musquodoboit Valley and Eastern Shore, providing pre-booked, shared, door-to-door rides to work, school, medical appointments, and shopping. By coordinating affordable rural trips and partnering with municipalities and community agencies, it reduces transportation costs for residents and improves access to essential services and employment in areas with limited fixed-route transit.
resources.address: 67 Park Road, Musquodoboit Harbour, NS B0J 2L0

resources.name: Kings Transit Authority – Regional Bus Service
resources.description: Kings Transit provides fixed-route public transit connecting rural and small-town communities across Kings and parts of Annapolis Counties, linking residents to jobs, education, health care, and services in hub communities like Kentville, New Minas, and Wolfville. As a municipally partnered system with low fares and accessible buses, it reduces reliance on private vehicles and lowers transportation costs for workers, students, and families.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

resources.name: Halifax Transit – Regional Transit Network
resources.description: Halifax Transit operates the Halifax Regional Municipality’s integrated bus and ferry network, including suburban and rural express routes that connect outlying communities to employment and services in the urban core. By offering frequent, reliable, and multimodal public transit, the system lowers commuting costs, supports car-light living, and improves access to jobs, education, and community services for young people across the region.

resources.name: It’s More Than Buses – Transit Advocacy
resources.description: It’s More Than Buses is a volunteer-led advocacy group that campaigns for better public transit in HRM, promoting frequent service, better route design, and supportive infrastructure like bus lanes. Through community organizing, education, and engagement with decision-makers, they help shape improved transit policies and routes that reduce transportation costs and expand access to jobs and services, especially for young people and lower-income riders.

solutions.text: Community-Owned District Heating Pilots: Small-scale, locally governed district heating using biomass, wood-waste, or waste-heat sources can be piloted in dense neighbourhoods to lower winter heating costs and create local green jobs.

resources.name: Alderney 5 Renewable Thermal Energy System (A5)
resources.description: A5 is a municipally owned district energy system that uses Halifax Harbour seawater and heat-recovery chillers to provide shared heating and cooling to the Alderney Gate complex, including the library, market, and ferry terminal. By leveraging local ambient and waste-heat sources through a centralized thermal loop, the project reduces winter heating costs for multiple dense public buildings and supports local operations and maintenance jobs.

resources.name: Cogswell District Energy System
resources.organization: Halifax Regional Municipality – Cogswell District Redevelopment
resources.description: As part of the Cogswell District redevelopment, HRM is constructing a municipally governed, low-temperature district energy network designed to integrate waste-heat recovery (e.g., from sewer mains) and renewable thermal sources. This community-scale utility will connect mixed-use buildings in a dense downtown area to lower space-heating costs and build local capacity and green jobs in design, installation, and operations.

resources.name: Energize Bridgewater – Downtown District Energy Initiative
resources.description: The Town of Bridgewater is advancing a municipally owned district energy pilot to serve downtown buildings, evaluating biomass and wastewater-heat options as part of its Community Energy Investment Plan. By designing a shared thermal network focused on affordability and local fuel supply chains, the initiative aims to cut winter heating costs for residents and businesses while creating skilled trades and bioheat jobs in the community.

solutions.text: Youth Employment Hubs Focused on Green Retrofits and Trades: Community-run training and apprenticeship programs connect young people to paid work retrofitting homes and installing efficient heating systems, reducing labour costs for local projects while developing a local workforce.

resources.name: HomeWarming
resources.organization: Clean Foundation (in partnership with Efficiency Nova Scotia)
resources.description: HomeWarming provides free home energy assessments and energy-efficiency upgrades (such as insulation, air sealing, and related measures) to income-qualified Nova Scotians. Delivered by Clean Foundation in partnership with Efficiency Nova Scotia, the program coordinates a network of local contractors and entry-level installers, creating paid on-the-job opportunities and training pathways for young people in insulation, HVAC, and electrical trades while lowering home energy costs across the province.

resources.name: Clean Leaders (formerly NS Youth Conservation Corps)
resources.description: Clean Leaders is a provincially supported youth employment program that places Nova Scotians aged 15–30 in paid roles with municipalities, community groups, and businesses working on climate and energy projects. Many placements support residential energy outreach, audits, and retrofit initiatives, and participants receive training and certifications that connect them to apprenticeships and entry-level jobs with local contractors installing heat pumps and completing efficiency upgrades—building a community-based retrofit workforce.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY offers Grade 10–12 students safety training and paid summer placements with construction employers across Nova Scotia. Host employers include firms specializing in residential renovations, insulation, and HVAC/heat pump installation, giving youth hands-on experience and pathways into apprenticeship; this strengthens the local labour pool for home retrofits that cut energy bills and improve affordability.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

obstacles.title: Urban–Rural Opportunity Divide
obstacles.description: Jobs, amenities, and services concentrate in HRM while many rural areas face declining populations and fewer opportunities for youth.

solutions.text: Rural remote-work hubs and co-working spaces: Convert underused community buildings into reliable co-working hubs with high-speed internet, meeting rooms and event space so young remote workers and entrepreneurs can base themselves outside HRM while staying connected.

resources.name: Perennia Innovation Centre
resources.description: Perennia’s Innovation Centre in Bible Hill provides entrepreneurs and remote workers in the agri-food sector with flexible offices, coworking desks, meeting rooms, and production labs supported by reliable, high-speed connectivity. By offering an affordable, professional base outside HRM along with event and collaboration space, it enables rural founders and knowledge workers to operate and connect without relocating.
resources.address: 199 Innovation Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2H5

resources.name: Island Sandbox
resources.organization: Cape Breton University and NSCC Marconi Campus
resources.description: Island Sandbox is an entrepreneurship and innovation hub serving Cape Breton that provides open coworking areas, meeting rooms, programming, and events for startups, students, and community members. With dependable high-speed internet and shared amenities on CBU’s campus, it functions as a rural remote-work base where young founders and remote professionals can collaborate and stay connected without leaving the island.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

resources.name: Mahone Bay Centre Co-Working and Offices
resources.description: Housed in a renovated former school, the Mahone Bay Centre provides affordable offices, shared desks, meeting rooms, and community event space with high-speed internet for local entrepreneurs, remote workers, and nonprofits. By repurposing an underused community building into a collaborative workspace on the South Shore, it supports rural residents who work remotely or start businesses while remaining in their community.
resources.address: 45 School Street, Mahone Bay, NS B0J 2E0

solutions.text: Community broadband and connectivity co-op: Form local cooperatives to fund, build and maintain last-mile broadband in partnership with municipal and provincial programs, ensuring affordable, high-quality internet for students, creatives and remote workers.

resources.name: Rural Internet Project (MODL)
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg’s Rural Internet Project coordinates community-driven broadband expansion, pooling municipal funds with provincial and federal programs (including the Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative) to extend last-mile fibre and fixed-wireless service into underserved communities. By partnering with multiple ISPs and local stakeholders, the project prioritizes builds and secures affordable plans, directly addressing the rural–urban divide and enabling reliable connections for students, creatives, entrepreneurs, and remote workers.

resources.name: Pictou County Rural Broadband Project
resources.description: The Municipality of Pictou County leads a rural broadband initiative that maps underserved areas, co-funds new towers and fibre backbones, and partners with the provincial Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative and participating ISPs to deliver last-mile service to homes and businesses. This community-first, cost-sharing approach reduces deployment costs and keeps prices accessible, improving connectivity for youth, tradespeople, artists, and remote workers across small communities in the county.

resources.name: Colchester County Rural Internet Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: Colchester County coordinates community co-funding with the Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative and private providers to extend fibre and fixed-wireless last-mile service to rural homes and businesses. By investing in local towers, backhaul, and streamlined permitting, the county lowers build costs and enables affordable, reliable broadband for learning, telehealth, creative work, and remote employment in underserved areas.

resources.name: Chebucto Community Net (CCN)
resources.description: Chebucto Community Net is a non-profit, community-governed internet service that provides affordable home internet, email, and web services, reducing barriers to connectivity for residents who might otherwise be excluded. Working alongside public institutions and programs, CCN strengthens the community broadband ecosystem by ensuring low-cost options and digital inclusion supports for students, creatives, and remote workers in the Halifax region.
resources.address: Room 125, Chase Building, 6136 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4J2

solutions.text: Youth entrepreneurship micro-grant and mentorship program: Create a community-run micro-grant fund plus volunteer mentor network to help young people test business ideas, access micro-loans and receive practical guidance on scaling locally.

resources.name: CEED Micro Loan Program and Mentorship
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides small, flexible micro-loans alongside training and a volunteer mentor network to help young entrepreneurs in Nova Scotia validate ideas and grow locally. Through workshops, one-on-one coaching, and community mentors, participants receive practical guidance on business planning, sales, and scaling. This combination of micro-financing and mentorship directly supports youth to test ventures and build sustainable businesses, including those outside HRM via virtual delivery.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: CBDC Youth Loan (NOBL)
resources.organization: Community Business Development Corporation – NOBL (Northern Opportunities for Business Limited)
resources.description: CBDC NOBL’s Youth Loan program offers accessible micro-financing and ongoing business counselling to young entrepreneurs in rural northern Nova Scotia (Pictou, Antigonish, and Guysborough). Community-based investment committees and advisors provide mentorship on cash flow, marketing, and operations, helping youth pilot ventures close to home. This rural-focused micro-loan plus mentorship model addresses the urban–rural divide by enabling youth to start and scale businesses in their own communities.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

resources.name: Business Is Jammin’ Youth Entrepreneurship Programs
resources.organization: Black Business Initiative (BBI) – Business Is Jammin’
resources.description: Business Is Jammin’ (BIJ) delivers year-round programs that pair Black youth with business mentors and provide seed funding through pitch competitions and project micro-grants. Participants receive coaching on ideation, financial literacy, and go-to-market tactics, with mentors drawn from Nova Scotia’s business community. This hands-on mix of micro-grants and mentorship helps youth test ideas and build locally rooted enterprises across the province.
resources.address: 1660 Hollis Street, Suite 910, Halifax, NS B3J 1V7

resources.name: The Spark Zone (Student and Youth Entrepreneurship Sandbox)
resources.description: The Spark Zone supports students and recent graduates with mentorship from volunteer industry advisors and small seed funding for prototyping and validation. Operating as a university-community “sandbox,” it connects young founders to workshops, coaches, and partners to test business ideas and prepare for early growth in Nova Scotia. By lowering early-stage risk with micro-funding and guidance, it helps youth launch ventures and remain in the province.

solutions.text: Local apprenticeship and trades pipeline: Coordinate local employers, schools and tradespeople to offer paid youth apprenticeships, co-op placements and pre-apprenticeship training so young people can enter stable, well-paid trades without moving away.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding Inc. and community partners)
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based initiative that recruits youth from diverse communities and provides customized pre-apprenticeship trades training (e.g., welding and metal fabrication) at NSCC combined with paid work terms at Irving Shipbuilding. The program coordinates a full pipeline—community partners and schools for recruitment, NSCC for technical training, and journeyperson mentors on the job—so participants transition into registered apprenticeships and long-term shipbuilding careers in Halifax without leaving the province.

resources.name: NSCC Apprenticeship Training and Co-operative Education
resources.description: NSCC delivers in-school technical training for dozens of Red Seal and designated trades and coordinates co-op/work-integrated learning placements with employers across urban and rural Nova Scotia. By linking high schools, college programs, and local employers—often through dual credit pathways, pre-apprenticeship certificates/diplomas, and paid co-ops—NSCC helps young people start and progress in apprenticeships close to home.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Power Apprenticeship Programs
resources.description: Nova Scotia Power hires and trains paid apprentices in skilled trades such as powerline technician, electrician, and instrumentation across worksites throughout the province. The utility coordinates with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and NSCC for technical training and provides on-the-job mentorship by journeypersons, creating a stable, local pathway for youth to build well-paid trades careers without relocating.
resources.address: 1223 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

resources.name: Michelin Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Programs
resources.description: Michelin’s Nova Scotia plants sponsor and employ paid apprentices in industrial trades (e.g., industrial mechanic/millwright, industrial electrician), combining on-the-job training with in-school technical blocks through NSCC and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency. With operations in rural regions like Pictou County, the company provides local youth with a clear pathway into stable, well-paid skilled trades roles close to their communities.
resources.address: 1770 Granton Abercrombie Road, Granton, NS B2H 5C6

solutions.text: Shared maker spaces and mobile skills labs: Develop community maker spaces with tools for woodworking, metalwork, digital fabrication and coding, and run travelling skills clinics that bring hands-on training to remote villages.

resources.name: NSCC Mobile Trades Training Labs
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College operates mobile training labs that travel to rural and remote communities across the province to deliver hands-on trades training in areas like welding, metal fabrication, and carpentry. These fully equipped units bring shop-grade tools, safety infrastructure, and certified instructors on-site, reducing travel barriers for youth and adult learners and directly addressing the urban–rural training gap.

resources.name: Discovery on the Go
resources.description: The Discovery Centre’s mobile outreach program brings hands-on STEM experiences—such as robotics, coding, circuits, and maker-style design challenges—to schools, libraries, and community events throughout Nova Scotia, including rural and Mi’kmaw communities. By delivering interactive, skills-focused clinics outside of Halifax, the program functions as a traveling skills lab that helps youth explore technology and engineering pathways where local access may be limited.
resources.address: 1215 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio and Creation Spaces
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries operates shared public makerspaces—anchored by the Lou Duggan Creative Studio at Central Library—with equipment such as 3D printers, vinyl cutters, sewing machines, recording gear, and microcontrollers. These community-access spaces host free workshops in digital fabrication and coding, enabling youth and entrepreneurs to prototype, learn skills, and collaborate without needing to own expensive tools.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: SuperNOVA Outreach Programs
resources.description: SuperNOVA at Dalhousie University delivers mobile, instructor-led STEM programs—including robotics, coding, and engineering design workshops—to communities across Nova Scotia, with a focus on outreach in rural and underserved areas. By bringing equipment and facilitators to local schools and community hubs, SuperNOVA acts as a traveling skills clinic that lowers access barriers and sparks interest in tech and engineering careers.

solutions.text: School-to-community career pathways and mentorship networks: Partner schools with local businesses, non-profits and post-secondary institutions to provide career talks, job-shadowing, internships and mentorship programs highlighting local career options.

resources.name: Co-operative Education (Co-op) Program
resources.description: HRCE’s Co-op Program partners high schools with local businesses, non-profits, and post-secondary institutions to place students in supervised work experiences that earn academic credit. Students participate in career talks, job-shadowing and longer co-op placements with employer mentors, helping them explore local career options and build networks that ease the transition from school to work.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Imhotep’s Legacy Academy
resources.description: Imhotep’s Legacy Academy connects junior high and high school students of African heritage with university student mentors and STEM professionals for hands-on learning, career talks, and workplace/lab visits. By partnering schools with post-secondary institutions and local industry, the program builds mentorship networks and exposes youth to real Nova Scotia STEM career pathways.

resources.name: Work-Integrated Learning (Co-op and Internships)
resources.description: NSCC’s Work-Integrated Learning connects college programs and students with Nova Scotia employers across sectors for co-op terms, internships, apprenticeships, and applied projects. Campuses collaborate with local businesses and community organizations for employer talks, mentorship and placements—giving learners practical experience and clear pathways into local jobs, including in rural regions served by NSCC.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program matches post-secondary students and recent graduates with established local professionals for one-on-one informational interviews and facilitated introductions. Working closely with university and college career centers and community partners, it helps young people learn about local career paths, expand mentorship networks, and access job-shadowing or entry-level opportunities with Nova Scotia employers.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Pop-up retail incubators and market days: Activate vacant storefronts and public spaces with short-term pop-ups, night markets and seasonal markets that let young makers and food entrepreneurs test concepts and build customer bases.

resources.name: Downtown Truro Night Market
resources.description: The Downtown Truro Night Market turns sections of Prince Street into a pedestrian-only vendor district on select summer evenings, activating public space with short-term pop-up stalls, food trucks, and live music. It gives emerging makers, small food businesses, and youth-led startups low-cost, low-risk access to customers to test products, build brand awareness, and grow a following in a central rural hub.

resources.name: Alderney Landing Farmers’ Market
resources.description: This year-round weekend market activates the Alderney Landing waterfront facility with temporary tables and booths for local vendors, artisans, and food entrepreneurs. As a pop-up retail environment, it enables new and young businesses to pilot offerings, gather feedback, and build customer bases without the cost and risk of a permanent storefront, with additional seasonal markets increasing exposure.

resources.name: Wolfville Farmers’ Market
resources.description: The Wolfville Farmers’ Market operates weekly and seasonal markets that provide short-term stalls for local growers, makers, and food startups across the Annapolis Valley. By offering low-barrier vendor opportunities, themed pop-up events, and promotional support, it serves as a retail incubator where young and emerging entrepreneurs can test concepts, refine products, and build loyal customers.

resources.name: Truro Farmers’ Market
resources.description: The Truro Farmers’ Market hosts weekly market days and special pop-up events that give small-scale producers and makers from Colchester County and nearby rural communities access to short-term retail space. This format lets new food and craft entrepreneurs validate products, meet customers face-to-face, and grow revenue without a long-term lease, supporting rural opportunity outside HRM.

solutions.text: Local procurement and 'buy local' campaigns: Encourage municipal institutions, community organizations and residents to prioritize local suppliers, supporting rural producers, makers and service providers and keeping revenue in the region.

resources.name: WFM2Go (Online Farmers’ Market)
resources.description: WFM2Go is an online and mobile farmers’ market operated by the Wolfville Farmers’ Market that aggregates products from Nova Scotia farms and food producers and offers weekly pickup hubs across the Annapolis Valley, HRM, and nearby rural communities. By simplifying how households, community groups, and small businesses source from local suppliers, it keeps food dollars circulating in rural economies and creates dependable market access for small producers.

resources.name: Halifax Seaport Farmers’ Market
resources.description: The Halifax Seaport Farmers’ Market hosts dozens of Nova Scotia farmers, fishers, food producers, and artisans each weekend on the waterfront, offering a direct marketplace for locally grown and made products. By connecting urban residents and institutional buyers to rural vendors, the market advances buy-local purchasing and helps retain revenue within communities across the province.

resources.name: Craft Nova Scotia Shop at the Centre for Craft
resources.description: The Craft Nova Scotia Shop is a year-round retail gallery featuring only work by Nova Scotia artisans, complemented by seasonal markets and promotional campaigns. By curating and marketing locally made craft to residents, visitors, and institutional buyers, it channels consumer spending to rural and small-town makers and strengthens buy-local habits across the province.

resources.name: Truro Farmers’ Market
resources.description: The Truro Farmers’ Market operates year-round with farm products, prepared foods, and artisan goods from producers across Colchester County and northern Nova Scotia. Through regular markets and shop-local promotions, it encourages residents and community organizations to prioritize local suppliers, supporting rural livelihoods and keeping revenue within the regional economy.

resources.name: NSLC Local Product Promotion
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Liquor Corporation dedicates shelf space, in-store signage, and marketing campaigns to Nova Scotia–made beer, wine, cider, and spirits, making local options easy for consumers and hospitality buyers to find. By prioritizing provincial suppliers across its retail network, NSLC drives sustained demand for rural producers and helps keep beverage-sector revenue in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 93 Chain Lake Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 1A3

solutions.text: Agritech, value-added food hubs and co-ops: Create community food hubs and shared processing spaces where farmers and food entrepreneurs can add value (packaging, processing, distribution) and access shared marketing resources.

resources.name: WFM2Go (Wolfville Farmers’ Market Online Food Hub)
resources.description: WFM2Go aggregates products from dozens of Nova Scotia farmers and food entrepreneurs, packs orders at the Wolfville Farmers’ Market, and distributes to pickup sites across HRM and rural communities. By providing shared logistics, packaging, and a unified online storefront, it helps small producers add value and reach larger urban markets, narrowing the urban–rural opportunity gap for new and growing agri-food businesses.

resources.name: The Station Food Hub
resources.description: The Station operates a shared-use commercial kitchen, processing rooms, and cold storage that farmers and food entrepreneurs can rent to create value-added products, from prepared foods to co-packed items. It also coordinates aggregation and distribution to institutional and retail buyers, providing shared marketing and logistics that connect rural producers to larger markets and opportunities.

resources.name: Alderney Landing Community Kitchen
