resources.description: Alderney Landing’s licensed community kitchen is a rentable, fully equipped space where food entrepreneurs can develop, package, and scale value-added products without investing in their own facilities. Tied to the Alderney Landing Farmers’ Market and events, it offers built-in shared marketing and urban distribution channels that help rural and new producers access HRM customers.

resources.name: Truro Farmers’ Market Community Kitchen and Online Market
resources.description: The Truro Farmers’ Market operates a commercial kitchen and an online ordering platform that allow vendors to produce jams, baked goods, and other value-added foods in an inspected, shared facility and sell through centralized pickup. These shared processing and marketing services help small and rural producers reach broader audiences while reducing start-up costs and logistical barriers.

solutions.text: Community-owned renewable energy projects: Develop locally owned small-scale renewables (solar farms, wind co-ops, biomass) that create construction and maintenance jobs and return revenue to the community for youth initiatives.

resources.name: Antigonish Community Solar Garden
resources.organization: Town of Antigonish Electric Utility (Town of Antigonish)
resources.description: The Town of Antigonish Electric Utility owns and operates a community solar garden that allows local residents and businesses to subscribe to solar production from a municipally owned array. Construction and ongoing maintenance create local jobs, while revenues and energy savings stay with the town-owned utility and can be reinvested in local services and community programming, including supports that benefit youth. By enabling community ownership and participation, the project directly expands rural clean-energy opportunities and keeps economic benefits circulating locally.

resources.name: Berwick Community Solar Garden
resources.organization: Town of Berwick Electric Utility (Town of Berwick)
resources.description: The Town of Berwick’s electric utility operates a community solar garden where municipal customers can purchase or subscribe to output from locally sited solar panels. The project creates installation and maintenance jobs in the Annapolis Valley and keeps energy revenues within the community-owned utility, supporting local budgets and services that can include youth recreation and programming. This model expands access to renewables for renters and households without suitable roofs while retaining economic benefits in a rural town.

resources.name: Mahone Bay Solar Garden
resources.organization: Town of Mahone Bay Electric Utility (Town of Mahone Bay)
resources.description: Mahone Bay’s municipally owned electric utility developed a community solar garden that allows local electricity customers to take part in shared solar generation owned by the town. The initiative generates construction and technical jobs locally and channels revenues back through the community-owned utility to support affordability and municipal services that benefit residents, including youth. By keeping ownership and proceeds local, the project strengthens rural economic opportunities and resilience.
resources.address: 493 Main Street, Mahone Bay, NS B0J 2E0

resources.name: Ellershouse Wind Farm (Community Wind Partnership)
resources.description: The Alternative Resource Energy Authority (AREA)—a partnership of the Towns of Antigonish, Berwick, and Mahone Bay—owns the Ellershouse Wind Farm, supplying power to their municipal electric utilities. As a community-owned generation asset, it created local construction and operations jobs and returns revenue to the partner towns’ utilities, which can reinvest in local services, energy programs, and community priorities that include opportunities for youth. This cooperative municipal model demonstrates how rural communities can own clean energy infrastructure and keep the economic value local.

solutions.text: Rural transport solutions and ride-share networks: Organize community shuttle services, carpool networks or app-based shared rides to improve access to jobs, training and cultural amenities in regional centres without requiring car ownership.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Community Transit
resources.description: MusGo Rider operates community-based, door-to-door and pre-booked shared rides serving the Eastern Shore and Musquodoboit Valley, linking rural residents with Halifax and local hubs for work, education, health, and cultural activities. The co-operative coordinates ride-sharing using dispatch and scheduling to provide affordable transportation without requiring car ownership, directly addressing rural access to regional opportunities.
resources.address: 5228 Highway 7, Unit 2, Porters Lake, NS B3E 1J8

resources.name: Kings Transit Authority – Annapolis Valley Routes
resources.description: Kings Transit runs fixed-route community buses connecting rural and small-town communities across the Annapolis Valley (e.g., Wolfville, Kentville, Berwick, Greenwood/Middleton) to employment, NSCC campuses, services, and amenities in regional centres. By offering reliable, low-cost transit spanning dispersed communities, it functions as a rural shuttle network that reduces the need for private vehicle ownership.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

resources.name: Maritime Bus – Nova Scotia Intercity Service
resources.description: Maritime Bus provides scheduled intercity coach service connecting many Nova Scotia towns and rural areas with Halifax and other regional centres, enabling access to jobs, training, post-secondary institutions, and cultural amenities. The network acts as a shared shuttle option across the province, offering an alternative to car ownership for long-distance rural-to-urban travel.

solutions.text: Mobile health, career and social services: Coordinate regular mobile clinics and pop-up service days (health, mental-health supports, career counselling, childcare sign-ups) so young people in remote areas can access essential services locally.

resources.name: Mobile Primary Care Clinics
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health deploys mobile primary care clinics and pop-up community clinics across the province, including many rural and remote communities, to provide same-day care, prescription renewals, vaccinations, and referrals. By bringing clinicians and navigators directly to towns and community hubs, the clinics reduce travel barriers and ensure young people can access essential health services locally.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: Mental Health and Addictions Community Clinics (Walk-in/Pop-up)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health – Mental Health and Addictions Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Mental Health and Addictions Program hosts regular walk-in and pop-up clinics in community locations across rural Nova Scotia (such as libraries, community centres, and schools). These events offer brief counselling, addiction supports, assessment, and navigation without a referral, helping young people access mental-health services close to home.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Breast Screening Program – Mobile Mammography Coach
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health – Nova Scotia Breast Screening Program
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Breast Screening Program operates a mobile mammography coach that travels to small towns and rural communities to deliver on-site breast cancer screening. Scheduled visits reduce time and travel costs, increasing access to preventative health services for residents living outside urban centres.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Outreach Employment Services (YMCA Cape Breton)
resources.organization: YMCA of Cape Breton – Nova Scotia Works Employment Services
resources.description: YMCA Cape Breton delivers Nova Scotia Works employment services and runs regular outreach days in rural Cape Breton communities, offering career counselling, job search assistance, resume support, and connections to training and employers. These pop-up service days set up in partner sites and community hubs, bringing career services directly to youth and young adults who cannot easily travel to urban centres.

solutions.text: Arts, culture and creative residencies in rural places: Host artist residencies, music series and cultural festivals that spotlight local talent, attract visitors and give young creatives opportunities to build careers and networks close to home.

resources.name: Ross Creek Artist Residency Program
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts hosts multi-disciplinary artist residencies in a rural setting, providing studio space, accommodation, and community engagement opportunities alongside exhibitions and performances that draw visitors to the Annapolis Valley. The centre also mentors youth through camps and workshops, helping young creatives build networks, portfolios, and career pathways without leaving rural Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

resources.name: Artist-in-Residence at The Deanery Project
resources.description: The Deanery Project offers artist-in-residence opportunities on the Eastern Shore, pairing workspace and accommodations with hands-on outreach in local schools and community groups. It also presents concerts, film nights, and cultural events that attract visitors to a rural coastline while giving young creatives mentorship, collaboration, and presentation opportunities close to home.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

resources.name: Lunenburg Folk Harbour Festival & Concert Series
resources.description: This annual seaside festival and year-round concert series spotlight emerging and established Nova Scotian, Mi’kmaw, Acadian, and touring folk artists across intimate rural venues in Lunenburg. Workshops, community stages, and volunteer opportunities help young performers gain exposure and professional connections while the festival brings cultural tourism to the South Shore.

resources.name: deCoste Centre Year-Round Performance Series
resources.description: The deCoste Centre anchors a rural creative hub in Pictou with a year-round program of music, theatre, dance, and festivals that showcase local talent alongside touring artists, drawing audiences to the Northumberland Shore. Youth-focused events, school matinees, and community stages give emerging performers stage time and industry exposure without leaving their home region.

resources.name: Kings Theatre Performance and Artist Development Programs
resources.description: Kings Theatre presents concerts, film, and cultural festivals in the small town of Annapolis Royal, drawing visitors to the region while consistently featuring Nova Scotia artists. Through training opportunities, youth programming, and professional stage presentations, it helps young creatives build skills, audiences, and networks close to home.
resources.address: 209 St George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

solutions.text: Affordable housing co-ops and co-housing projects: Develop community-driven affordable housing models—co-ops, shared ownership and infill projects—that keep young households able to live and work locally.

resources.name: Treehouse Village Ecohousing
resources.description: Treehouse Village is a resident-developed cohousing neighbourhood that delivers multi-unit, energy-efficient homes with extensive shared amenities, lowering per-household costs and fostering mutual support. By using a community-led model on an infill site in Bridgewater, it enables people—including young families and workers—to secure attainable homes near jobs and services, helping them stay in rural Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia – Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat Nova Scotia builds and renovates homes across the province and partners with families through an affordable, geared-to-income mortgage, creating a shared-equity pathway to ownership. The program frequently delivers small-scale infill projects in rural towns and communities, keeping young households rooted locally by providing stable, attainable housing close to work and community life.

solutions.text: Partnerships with post-secondary institutions and micro-campuses: Work with colleges and universities to offer satellite courses, certificate programs and short intensive training locally (virtual and in-person blended models) tied to regional job needs.

resources.name: NSCC Strait Area Campus — Nautical Institute & Marine Training
resources.description: NSCC’s Strait Area Campus hosts the Nautical Institute and delivers diploma, certificate, and short-recertification courses aligned with regional industries such as marine transportation, fisheries, energy, and skilled trades. As a regional micro‑campus, it blends in‑person labs and simulations with online theory and flexible scheduling so rural learners can upskill locally in programs tied directly to coastal and industrial job needs.
resources.address: 226 Reeves Street, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 2A2

resources.name: Université Sainte-Anne – Formation continue and Regional Campuses
resources.description: Université Sainte-Anne operates multiple regional campuses (Church Point HQ with satellites in Halifax, Tusket, Petit-de-Grat, and Saint-Joseph-du-Moine) and a Continuing Education unit that brings post-secondary and micro-credential programming to Acadian and francophone communities. It delivers French-language workforce and community programs (e.g., health support, early childhood, tourism, public service, language upskilling) in blended online/in-person formats so learners can study close to home in alignment with local labour market needs.

resources.name: Extended Learning (Faculty of Agriculture)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Faculty of Agriculture delivers short courses, micro-credentials, and certificate programs for agriculture, agri-food, and environmental sectors across rural Nova Scotia. Using a blended model of online modules and on-farm or community‑site labs, the unit partners with producer groups and regional employers to offer satellite training that meets local workforce and innovation needs without requiring relocation to Halifax.

resources.name: Dalhousie Family Medicine Residency — South West Nova (Yarmouth) Site
resources.organization: Dalhousie University — Department of Family Medicine
resources.description: As part of Dalhousie’s distributed medical education model, the South West Nova site places family medicine residents at Yarmouth Regional Hospital while connecting them virtually to academic sessions and faculty across the province. This satellite training hub prepares physicians in and for rural communities, aligning hands-on clinical education with the region’s health workforce needs and enabling learners to train where they are most needed.

resources.name: Continuing & Distance Education (Off‑Campus and Online Cohorts)
resources.description: StFX coordinates off‑campus and online cohorts for certificates and degrees in areas such as education, health leadership, business, and adult education, often scheduled evenings/weekends to serve working adults. By partnering with regional employers and public systems, it delivers blended and satellite offerings to rural learners in northeastern Nova Scotia so they can earn credentials locally that match community and sectoral job demands.

obstacles.title: Climate Resilience and Environmental Risks
obstacles.description: Coastal erosion, storms, floods, and wildfires threaten homes, infrastructure, and sectors like fisheries and tourism, creating instability.

solutions.text: Living Shoreline and Saltmarsh Restoration: Community volunteers, local NGOs, and municipalities collaborate to restore dunes, saltmarshes, eelgrass beds, and oyster reefs to reduce wave energy, trap sediments, and slow coastal erosion while enhancing habitat.

resources.name: TransCoastal Adaptations – Living Shorelines and Salt Marsh Restoration
resources.organization: TransCoastal Adaptations: Centre for Nature-based Solutions, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: TransCoastal Adaptations (TCA) designs and implements living shoreline projects and salt marsh restoration across Nova Scotia in partnership with municipalities, community groups, and volunteers. Their teams install nature-based features such as coir logs, brush bundles, and native vegetation, and they restore tidal flow to degraded marshes to reduce wave energy, trap sediments, and build coastal resilience. TCA also provides training and monitoring to ensure projects enhance habitat for fish, birds, and invertebrates while protecting nearby infrastructure.

resources.name: Coastal Action – Eelgrass Restoration and Living Shorelines
resources.description: Coastal Action works with local municipalities (e.g., Town of Mahone Bay) and volunteers to restore eelgrass beds and build living shorelines that stabilize coasts and enhance marine habitat. Their projects include transplanting eelgrass, removing invasive green crabs that damage beds, and installing natural materials with native plantings to dampen waves and promote sediment accumulation. Ongoing monitoring and community engagement ensure long-term resilience and hands-on learning opportunities for youth and residents.

resources.name: UINR – Bras d’Or Lake Eelgrass and Oyster Habitat Restoration
resources.description: UINR partners with Mi’kmaq communities, local fishers, and government to restore eelgrass and enhance oyster habitat in the Bras d’Or Lake, improving shoreline stability and biodiversity. The team removes invasive green crabs, replants eelgrass in degraded areas, and deploys oyster spat collectors and reef enhancements to rebuild natural structure that calms waves and traps sediments. Community stewardship, youth training, and continuous monitoring support climate resilience and sustainable livelihoods.

resources.name: Ecology Action Centre – Coastal Restoration (Living Shorelines, Dunes, and Salt Marsh)
resources.description: The Ecology Action Centre coordinates community-based coastal restoration, including native dune grass plantings, living shoreline pilots with partners, and support for salt marsh conservation and restoration. By using natural features like coir logs, brush bundles, and native vegetation, EAC projects aim to reduce wave energy, encourage sediment capture, and protect public access and coastal infrastructure. Workshops and volunteer events engage youth and residents in hands-on stewardship and monitoring along Nova Scotia’s coasts.

solutions.text: Community FireSmart and Wildfire Preparedness: Neighbourhood-led FireSmart programs to create defensible space, clear fuels, run local inspections, and organize volunteer crews for fuel reduction around homes and critical infrastructure.

resources.name: FireSmart Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources and Renewables
resources.description: FireSmart Nova Scotia is the provincial program that helps neighbourhoods and property owners reduce wildfire risk through FireSmart home and community hazard assessments, workshops, and support to organize local fuel‑reduction activities like chipping days. The program trains community champions and works with municipalities and volunteer fire departments to create defensible space around homes and critical infrastructure, and to pursue FireSmart Canada Neighbourhood Recognition.

resources.name: Wildland-Urban Interface Fire Prevention Program
resources.organization: Halifax Regional Fire & Emergency (Halifax Regional Municipality)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Fire & Emergency delivers FireSmart-focused outreach in at-risk neighbourhoods, offering on-site property assessments, block-by-block inspections, and community workshops that teach residents how to create defensible space and reduce fuels. Working with local associations and volunteer stations, HRFE helps organize brush-clearing and debris disposal events and prioritizes fuel reduction near subdivisions and critical infrastructure using local risk mapping and seasonal burn restrictions.

resources.name: Kejimkujik Fire Management and FireSmart Program
resources.description: Parks Canada’s fire management program at Kejimkujik uses prescribed burning, mechanical thinning, and FireSmart landscaping to create defensible space around facilities, campgrounds, and cultural sites. The team partners with nearby communities and local fire departments to share FireSmart best practices, support volunteer fuel-reduction days along park boundaries and access roads, and reduce wildfire threats to adjacent homes and critical infrastructure.
resources.address: 3005 Kejimkujik Main Parkway, Maitland Bridge, NS B0T 1B0

solutions.text: Neighbourhood Emergency Response Teams (NERTs): Train local residents in basic emergency response, evacuation assistance, first aid, and shelter management so communities can respond quickly during storms, floods, or wildfire events.

resources.name: Joint Emergency Management (JEM) - Halifax
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s JEM program organizes neighborhood-based volunteer teams that prepare for and respond to local emergencies. Volunteers receive training and guidance in basic emergency response, evacuation assistance, comfort centre/shelter operations, and public preparedness education, enabling rapid, community-led action during storms, floods, or wildfires. JEM teams liaise with HRM Emergency Management, fire services, and NGOs to coordinate local resources and exercises.

resources.name: Canadian Red Cross - Emergency Management (Nova Scotia)
resources.organization: Canadian Red Cross, Nova Scotia Office
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross recruits and trains local volunteers across Nova Scotia to support emergency response, including opening and managing reception centres and shelters, conducting evacuations support and registration, and providing first aid and psychosocial services. They deliver community preparedness workshops and exercises so residents can organize and respond quickly to hurricanes, floods, and wildfire events. During activations, Red Cross teams work alongside municipal EMO/JEM groups to strengthen neighborhood-level response.

resources.name: Emergency Disaster Services (EDS) - Maritime Division
resources.description: The Salvation Army’s EDS program trains community volunteers in incident management, mobile feeding/canteen operations, logistics, and reception/shelter support to assist during disasters. In Nova Scotia, EDS teams deploy for severe storms, floods, and wildfires to help evacuees, support shelter operations, and provide emotional and spiritual care. This builds neighborhood-based capacity that complements municipal and provincial emergency management and accelerates community response and recovery.

resources.name: Medical First Responder (MFR) Units and Community First Aid Training - Nova Scotia
resources.organization: St. John Ambulance Nova Scotia Council
resources.description: St. John Ambulance Nova Scotia provides certified first aid/CPR and emergency first responder training to residents and operates volunteer Medical First Responder (MFR) units that support communities. These trained volunteers assist municipalities and NGOs at evacuation sites and comfort centres, delivering on‑site first aid and participating in local emergency exercises. By equipping neighbors with lifesaving skills and organized response capability, SJA strengthens rapid community action during storms, floods, or wildfire evacuations.
resources.address: 24 Garland Avenue, Unit 5, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0A1

solutions.text: Citizen Science Monitoring Networks: Set up volunteer monitoring for shoreline change, sea-level rise markers, water quality, and post-storm impacts to inform local planning and provide real-time data for municipalities and researchers.

resources.name: Atlantic Water Network
resources.description: Atlantic Water Network (AWN) coordinates and supports a province-wide citizen science network where volunteers monitor water quality in rivers, lakes, and coastal estuaries across Nova Scotia. AWN provides standardized protocols, training, and loaner equipment, and hosts data on Atlantic DataStream so municipalities and researchers can access near real-time results to track storm impacts, pollution events, and climate-driven change.

resources.name: Annapolis River Guardians
resources.description: Annapolis River Guardians is a long-running citizen science program that trains local volunteers to sample water quality (e.g., temperature, bacteria, nutrients, dissolved oxygen, conductivity) throughout the Annapolis River system, including tidal sections affected by sea-level change. The program conducts targeted sampling after major storms and shares its long-term dataset with municipalities and researchers to inform infrastructure planning, flood mitigation, and watershed management.
resources.address: 314 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

resources.name: TransCoastal Adaptations – Monitoring and Evaluation
resources.organization: TransCoastal Adaptations: Centre for Nature-Based Solutions, Saint Mary's University
resources.description: TransCoastal Adaptations equips community volunteers and municipal partners to track shoreline change at living shoreline and coastal restoration sites using fixed photo-posts, shoreline profiles, and water/sea-level markers. They coordinate post-storm assessments and share results with planners and researchers, creating a practical citizen science network that documents erosion, flooding, and recovery to guide on-the-ground climate adaptation decisions.

resources.name: MTRI Community-Based Water Monitoring
resources.organization: Mersey Tobeatic Research Institute Cooperative Ltd.
resources.description: Mersey Tobeatic Research Institute works with volunteers, lake associations, and watershed groups across southwestern Nova Scotia to monitor water quality and temperature and to document extreme-weather impacts on waterways that feed coastal areas. The institute provides training, field equipment, and shared data systems that municipalities and researchers use to detect climate trends and prioritize restoration and flood resilience actions.
resources.address: 9 Mount Merritt Road, Kempt, NS B0T 1B0

solutions.text: Community Flood Mapping and Risk Workshops: Host participatory mapping sessions where residents contribute local knowledge to refine flood and erosion maps, identify vulnerable assets, and co-design neighbourhood adaptation actions.

resources.name: Living Shorelines Nova Scotia
resources.organization: TransCoastal Adaptations: Centre for Nature-based Solutions, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: Living Shorelines Nova Scotia convenes community workshops in coastal towns across the province where residents annotate maps with local flood pathways, erosion hotspots, and at-risk infrastructure. TransCoastal Adaptations uses this local knowledge to refine flood and erosion risk maps and co-design neighbourhood-scale adaptation actions such as salt marsh restoration, dune enhancement, and shoreline setbacks.

resources.name: HalifACT: Acting on Climate Together
resources.description: Under HalifACT, the municipality hosts public climate risk mapping open houses and workshops where residents contribute flood histories, storm impacts, and vulnerable asset locations directly onto maps. These participatory sessions help refine municipal flood and coastal erosion maps and shape neighbourhood adaptation measures such as green infrastructure, coastal buffers, and emergency route planning.

resources.name: Coastal Flood Risk Mapping and Community Workshops
resources.organization: Applied Geomatics Research Group (AGRG), Nova Scotia Community College – Centre of Geographic Sciences
resources.description: AGRG partners with Nova Scotia municipalities to produce high-resolution coastal flood and erosion maps, then holds public open houses and map-groundtruthing sessions to capture residents’ on-the-ground observations. Community input is used to validate and refine hazard layers, identify vulnerable roads and facilities, and co-develop practical neighbourhood adaptation options and emergency response priorities.

resources.name: Resilient East Hants – Climate Change Adaptation Plan
resources.description: Resilient East Hants runs community risk workshops where residents and staff collaboratively map flood-prone areas, culvert bottlenecks, and assets like wells, roads, and public buildings. Insights from these participatory mapping sessions refine municipal flood risk maps and inform co-designed neighbourhood actions including drainage improvements, floodproofing priorities, and evacuation and communication plans.

solutions.text: Local Green Infrastructure Programs: Install and maintain rain gardens, bioswales, permeable driveways, and street-tree planting to reduce stormwater runoff, prevent local flooding, and improve urban resilience.

resources.name: Urban Forest Master Plan – Street Tree Planting Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Urban Forest Master Plan guides ongoing street-tree planting and maintenance across the public right-of-way to manage stormwater, reduce runoff, and cool streets. Using tree trenches, structural soils, and species suited to urban conditions, the program enhances infiltration and interception of rainwater while improving neighborhood resilience and livability.

resources.name: Depave Paradise – Halifax
resources.description: Led locally by the Ecology Action Centre, Depave Paradise organizes community events to remove unnecessary asphalt from schoolyards, parking lots, and other paved spaces and replaces it with rain gardens, permeable surfaces, and native trees. These installations absorb and filter stormwater, reduce runoff into sewers and waterways, and create greener community spaces that bolster urban climate resilience.

resources.name: Dalhousie Facilities Management – Green Infrastructure & LID Projects
resources.description: Dalhousie University integrates low-impact development into campus capital projects, including rain gardens, bioswales, permeable paving, and green roofs at multiple sites. These features capture and infiltrate rainfall on-site, alleviating pressure on municipal systems, reducing localized flooding risk, and improving water quality while providing hands-on learning opportunities for students.

resources.name: Cogswell District Project – Green Infrastructure & Complete Streets
resources.description: HRM’s Cogswell District redevelopment incorporates green stormwater infrastructure such as bioretention planters, rain gardens, tree-lined boulevards, and permeable surfaces within a new complete-streets network. Designed to slow, filter, and infiltrate stormwater where it falls, the project reduces runoff and flood risk in downtown Halifax while expanding urban canopy and active transportation spaces.

solutions.text: Homeowner Retrofit Assistance: Community-run advisory services and volunteer crews help homeowners elevate utilities, install flood barriers, and make low-cost floodproofing and insulation upgrades to reduce damage and energy costs.

resources.name: HomeWarming
resources.organization: Clean Foundation and EfficiencyOne (Efficiency Nova Scotia)
resources.description: HomeWarming provides free, income-qualified home energy assessments and upgrades for homeowners across Nova Scotia. Energy advisors visit homes, identify opportunities, and coordinate trusted contractors to install insulation, draft-proofing, and ventilation improvements at no cost, lowering bills and improving comfort. By tightening building envelopes and addressing moisture issues, the program helps households better withstand storms and cold snaps while reducing energy costs.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: Home Energy Assessment and Rebates
resources.description: Efficiency Nova Scotia offers one-on-one advisory services through EnerGuide home energy assessments and a suite of rebates for insulation, air sealing, and related upgrades. Certified energy advisors provide a tailored retrofit roadmap and connect homeowners with qualified contractors, enabling affordable, high-impact improvements. These envelope upgrades lower utility bills and increase comfort and resilience to extreme weather conditions.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: Stormwater and Flood Resilience for Homeowners
resources.description: Coastal Action provides homeowner workshops, site visits, and community volunteer events focused on practical stormwater management and flood resilience. The team advises residents on redirecting downspouts, installing rain barrels and rain gardens, and using nature-based shoreline protection, and in some cases coordinates volunteer planting or small installations. These low-cost measures help manage runoff, reduce flood damage risk, and complement insulation and moisture-control upgrades.
resources.address: 37 Tannery Road, Unit 3, Lunenburg, NS B0J 2C0

resources.name: Clean Energy Financing Program (PACE)
resources.description: Bridgewater’s PACE program helps homeowners plan and finance energy-efficiency retrofits such as insulation, air sealing, efficient windows/doors, and heat pumps. Staff provide advisory support, connect residents with qualified contractors, and offer low-interest, on‑property financing repaid via property tax. By making envelope and efficiency upgrades accessible and affordable, the program reduces utility costs and improves home resilience to severe weather.

resources.name: Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) Program
resources.description: Amherst’s PACE program provides advisory support and financing that enables homeowners to complete retrofits like insulation and air sealing that lower energy use and improve comfort. The municipality helps scope projects and connects residents to vetted contractors, then finances the work through property-assessed repayments. These upgrades cut utility bills and strengthen homes against extreme temperatures and storm-related stresses.
resources.address: 98 Victoria Street East, Amherst, NS B4H 1X6

solutions.text: Community-Owned Renewable Microgrids: Neighbourhood cooperatives develop solar arrays paired with battery storage to maintain power at shelters and critical services during outages caused by storms or wildfire smoke.

resources.name: Smart Grid Nova Scotia
resources.description: Smart Grid Nova Scotia is a Nova Scotia Power initiative that pilots distributed solar paired with battery storage and smart controls to improve community resilience. By deploying behind-the-meter batteries (e.g., at homes and community facilities) and integrating solar PV with islanding capability, the program maintains critical loads during storms and grid disruptions and reduces peak demand on feeders serving essential services.
resources.address: 1223 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

resources.name: The Deanery Project Community Microgrid
resources.description: The Deanery Project operates a community-run renewable microgrid that integrates on-site solar generation with battery storage to power buildings at its coastal education and arts centre. During regional outages caused by storms, the system can keep essential services (lighting, refrigeration, device charging, communications) running for visitors and neighbours, while the organization provides training and hands-on workshops to help other communities replicate cooperative, battery-backed solar resilience hubs.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1W0

solutions.text: Local Shoreline Setback and Managed Retreat Planning: Facilitate community conversations and small-scale pilot buyouts or voluntary relocation incentives, guided by local priorities, to reduce long-term risk in high-erosion zones.

resources.name: HalifACT – Coastal Hazard Setbacks and Adaptation Planning
resources.description: HalifACT is Halifax Regional Municipality’s climate action plan, which embeds coastal hazard mapping, sea-level rise allowances, and shoreline setback requirements into the Regional Plan and land-use by-laws. Through public engagement sessions and community planning processes, HRM works with residents and developers to direct new development away from high-erosion and flood-risk shorelines and to consider voluntary retreat of vulnerable structures over time. This implements local shoreline setback and managed retreat planning to reduce long-term risk.

resources.name: Coastal & Marine Program – Coastal Resilience and Living Shorelines
resources.description: Coastal Action partners with municipalities and shoreline property owners in Lunenburg County and beyond to assess erosion and flooding risks, host community workshops, and co-design adaptation options. Their coastal resilience and living shorelines projects recommend appropriate shoreline setbacks and, where feasible, relocating or moving infrastructure back from eroding coasts, demonstrating managed retreat at site scale. Findings inform local policies and empower voluntary, community-guided decisions to lower long-term hazard exposure.
resources.address: 37 Tannery Road, Unit 3, Lunenburg, NS B0J 2C0

resources.name: Climate Change and Adaptation Program (Mi’kmaw Communities)
resources.description: The Confederacy of Mainland Mi’kmaq supports member First Nations in Nova Scotia with community-driven climate risk assessments, coastal erosion mapping, and adaptation planning. The program convenes Elders, youth, and leadership to identify priority shoreline setbacks and, when necessary, plans for managed retreat of homes and critical services, helping communities access funding for voluntary relocations or structure moves. This embeds local priorities in decisions that reduce risk in high-erosion coastal zones.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Program – Coastal Land Conservation (Voluntary Buyouts)
resources.description: The Nature Conservancy of Canada acquires high-risk or ecologically significant coastal properties in Nova Scotia from willing sellers, creating permanent buffer zones where development is removed and shorelines can migrate naturally. By offering voluntary buyouts and converting vulnerable parcels to conservation lands, NCC helps communities implement managed retreat and de-facto setback areas along eroding coasts. They coordinate with local partners to target acquisitions that lower long-term exposure and support resilient coastal economies.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 381, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Oyster and Shellfish Reef Restoration for Coastal Protection: Fishers, local conservation groups, and Indigenous partners restore oyster reefs and other shellfish habitats that attenuate waves, reduce erosion, and support fisheries productivity.

resources.name: Bras d’Or Lakes Oyster Management and Enhancement Program
resources.description: UINR works with Mi’kmaq communities, local fishers, and DFO to restore and enhance native oyster reefs throughout the Bras d’Or Lakes by placing cultch (clean shell) to create reef substrate, conducting spat collection and reseeding, and running community oyster gardening and monitoring. These three‑dimensional oyster reefs help attenuate waves and stabilize vulnerable shorelines while improving water quality and supporting a culturally and economically important fishery, advancing nature‑based coastal protection and local livelihoods.

resources.name: South Shore Native Oyster Restoration Project
resources.description: Coastal Action partners with local fishers, Mi’kmaq partners, and government agencies to rebuild native oyster habitat in bays along Nova Scotia’s South Shore by deploying cultch, installing spat collectors, and reseeding to form living reef structures. The restored shellfish reefs dampen wave energy and reduce shoreline erosion, while community science and youth engagement link habitat restoration to stronger coastal resilience and revitalized inshore fisheries.
resources.address: 37 Tannery Road, Unit 3, Lunenburg, NS B0J 2C0

solutions.text: Tourism Sector Resilience Planning: Local tourism operators develop emergency plans, diversify offerings (off‑peak and inland experiences), and invest in resilient infrastructure and communication to keep businesses viable after events.

resources.name: Peggy’s Cove Infrastructure Improvements
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia led comprehensive, climate-resilient upgrades at Peggy’s Cove, including an accessible viewing platform, boardwalks, traffic-calming, and improved wayfinding designed to withstand storms and sea-level rise. These investments protect residents and visitors while maintaining safe access and communications after severe weather, helping nearby tourism operators remain open year-round and support off-peak visitation.
resources.address: 1751 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S5

resources.name: Cape Breton Highlands National Park – Climate-Resilient Visitor Infrastructure and Experience Management
resources.description: Parks Canada is reinforcing roads, bridges, trails, and visitor facilities in Cape Breton Highlands National Park to better withstand floods and storms, alongside emergency planning and real-time visitor communications for closures and alerts. The park promotes inland and shoulder-season activities across the highlands, diversifying tourism away from vulnerable coastal zones and helping regional operators sustain business after extreme weather.
resources.address: 37639 Cabot Trail, Ingonish Beach, NS B0C 1L0

resources.name: Tourism Strong – Crisis Preparedness and Business Continuity for Tourism Operators
resources.organization: Tourism Industry Association of Nova Scotia (TIANS)
resources.description: Tourism Strong provides Nova Scotia tourism businesses with practical emergency planning templates, funding links, and webinar training to build crisis response and business continuity plans for storms, floods, and wildfires. It also shares communication best practices and supports diversification into shoulder-season and inland offerings, helping operators maintain market presence and operations during and after disruptive events.
resources.address: 2089 Gottingen Street, Suite 201, Halifax, NS B3K 3B1

resources.name: Hike Nova Scotia – Year-Round Hiking Experience Development and Trail Stewardship
resources.description: Hike Nova Scotia partners with communities and operators to develop and promote inland hiking experiences and training (including winter and shoulder-season programs), broadening tourism beyond exposed coastal areas. Through hike leader certification, safety education, and sharing trail condition advisories, it strengthens visitor communications and preparedness—helping rural businesses remain viable after severe weather by drawing visitors to resilient, inland experiences.
resources.address: 5516 Spring Garden Road, 4th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 1G6

solutions.text: Youth Climate Leadership and Skills Programs: Schools, community centres, and trades programs provide youth with training in resilient construction, shoreline restoration, emergency response, and green entrepreneurship to build local capacity.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s paid internship program places youth (ages 15–30) with municipalities, community groups, and businesses across Nova Scotia to work on climate adaptation and green projects. Interns receive training and hands-on experience in areas such as shoreline restoration, flood risk mapping, wildfire risk reduction, and energy efficiency, building local capacity for climate resilience while developing green career skills.

resources.name: Centre for the Built Environment (Ivany Campus)
resources.description: NSCC’s Centre for the Built Environment is a living-lab facility where students in carpentry, building systems, and energy sustainability programs learn high-performance, storm- and flood-resilient construction and retrofitting. Through applied projects with communities and industry, youth gain practical skills in resilient building design, energy efficiency, and renewable integration that directly support climate-ready infrastructure in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Coastal Restoration & Education Program
resources.organization: Coastal Action (Blomidon Naturalists Society – Coastal Action)
resources.description: Coastal Action engages youth through school partnerships, internships, and volunteer stewardship to restore shorelines and coastal habitats on the South Shore. Participants learn coastal monitoring, native planting, salt marsh and eelgrass restoration, and living-shoreline techniques that reduce erosion and storm impacts, building local leadership and practical skills in nature-based climate resilience.
resources.address: 18 King Street, Unit 5, Lunenburg, NS B0J 2C0

resources.name: Hope Blooms Youth Social Enterprise Program
resources.description: Hope Blooms empowers youth to lead an urban agriculture and food-based social enterprise in Halifax’s North End, teaching climate-smart gardening, greenhouse operations, composting, and business skills. By producing healthy food and value-added products, participants gain green entrepreneurship experience while strengthening neighborhood resilience and community wellbeing.

resources.name: Youth Emergency Preparedness and Disaster Management Training
resources.organization: Canadian Red Cross – Nova Scotia Office
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross in Nova Scotia offers youth-friendly emergency preparedness education, first aid, and disaster management training, along with volunteer pathways on response teams. Young participants build skills in incident response, evacuation support, and recovery for climate-related events like floods, storms, and wildfires, enhancing local readiness and capacity.

solutions.text: Community Mutual Aid and Resilience Funds: Establish local emergency funds or insurance pools managed by community organizations to provide quick financial support for households and small businesses after climate disasters.

resources.name: Wildfire Recovery Appeal
resources.description: United Way Halifax manages a community-operated emergency fund that rapidly channels donations to households affected by climate-related disasters, such as the 2023 HRM wildfires. Working through local partner agencies, the appeal provides quick financial assistance (e.g., gift cards, basic needs, temporary shelter support) to stabilize families during evacuation and early recovery, embodying a pooled, community-managed resilience fund.
resources.address: 46 Portland Street, 7th Floor, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 1H4

resources.name: Emergency Relief Fund
resources.description: The North Grove operates a locally managed emergency fund that provides fast, flexible financial help to Dartmouth North households after storms, floods, and power outages. The fund issues grocery and essentials gift cards and helps cover urgent costs during evacuations or loss of income, functioning as a neighborhood-level mutual aid and resilience pool.

resources.name: Emergency Family Support Fund
resources.description: The Mi'kmaw Native Friendship Centre administers an emergency fund that offers rapid assistance—such as gift cards, temporary accommodation support, and replacement of essentials—to urban Indigenous and non-Indigenous families impacted by events like wildfires, hurricanes, and flooding. By pooling community donations and distributing aid quickly, the fund acts as a grassroots mutual aid mechanism that strengthens household resilience after climate disasters.

resources.name: Emergency Support for Newcomers Affected by Disasters
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides rapid-response financial assistance and material supports to newcomer households displaced or economically affected by climate events such as wildfires and floods. Through community-managed funds and coordinated donations, clients receive quick help with essentials (e.g., food, transportation, temporary lodging), enabling faster recovery and stability.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: NSCC Urgent Aid
resources.description: The NSCC Foundation’s Urgent Aid program is a standing, donor-supported emergency fund that provides fast microgrants to students facing sudden crises, including evacuations, lost income, and essential needs resulting from hurricanes, wildfires, and severe storms. Administered through campus and community channels for same-week disbursement, it functions as a community-managed resilience fund that helps young people quickly recover from climate-related shocks.

solutions.text: Indigenous-Led Knowledge Sharing and Co-Management: Partner with Mi'kmaq and other Indigenous knowledge holders to integrate traditional stewardship practices, seasonal planning, and co-management of lands, fisheries, and coastal protection projects.

resources.name: Unama'ki Institute of Natural Resources (UINR)
resources.description: UINR is an Indigenous-led organization representing the five Mi’kmaw communities of Unama’ki (Cape Breton) that co-manages the Bras d’Or Lake (Unama’ki) and adjacent coastal ecosystems. Through programs like AAROM, the Unama’ki Moose Management Initiative, and the Collaborative Environmental Planning Initiative, UINR integrates Mi’kmaw knowledge (Netukulimk, seasonal indicators) with Western science to guide fisheries stewardship, habitat restoration, and coastal protection in partnership with DFO, Parks Canada, municipalities, and universities. This delivers Indigenous-led knowledge sharing and practical co-management that strengthens resilience to storms, flooding, and wildfire risk.

resources.name: Mi’kmaq Conservation Group (MCG)
resources.description: MCG is the Netukulimk environmental program of The Confederacy of Mainland Mi’kmaq that supports Mi’kmaw communities across mainland Nova Scotia in aquatic stewardship and climate adaptation. As an AAROM organization, it partners with Mi’kmaw guardians, DFO, Nova Scotia Environment and Climate Change, and municipalities to restore tidal wetlands and rivers, monitor culturally important fisheries, plan for sea‑level rise, and implement nature‑based coastal protection using Mi’kmaw ecological knowledge and seasonal planning. This is Indigenous-led co-management that blends traditional stewardship with science to safeguard coasts, fisheries, and community infrastructure.

solutions.text: Volunteer Beach and Riparian Debris Removal: Regular community cleanups to remove driftwood, abandoned materials, and invasive debris that can worsen erosion, damage habitats, or increase fire risk when dry.

resources.name: Great Nova Scotia Pick-Me-Up (GNSPMU)
resources.description: The Great Nova Scotia Pick-Me-Up is a province-wide volunteer litter cleanup campaign that equips community groups with supplies and support to remove debris from beaches, riverbanks, trails, and neighbourhoods. By organizing shoreline and riparian cleanups, the program removes driftwood, plastics, and abandoned materials that can accelerate erosion, harm coastal and aquatic habitats, and elevate wildfire risk when dry.

resources.name: HRM Community Clean Up Program
resources.organization: Halifax Regional Municipality — Solid Waste Resources
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality provides free cleanup kits and coordinated collection for residents and groups who organize litter removals in public spaces, including beaches, lakeshores, and riverbanks. These volunteer cleanups prevent debris from degrading shorelines, reduce habitat damage and storm-related blockages, and lower fire risks posed by dry, combustible materials.

resources.name: Community Shoreline Cleanups along the Annapolis River
resources.description: Clean Annapolis River Project coordinates volunteer shoreline and riparian cleanups along the Annapolis River and its tributaries, removing litter, derelict materials, and invasive debris before they enter the Bay of Fundy. These efforts stabilize banks by preventing debris-induced erosion, protect fish and wildlife habitat, and reduce fire hazards from dry, combustible materials accumulating along the shore.
resources.address: 314 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

resources.name: Coastal Cleanup and Marine Debris Action
resources.description: Ecology Action Centre engages volunteers in coastal and harbour shoreline cleanups across Nova Scotia, often in partnership with community groups and schools. By removing driftwood accumulations, plastic waste, and derelict gear from beaches and riparian zones, these cleanups help reduce erosion impacts, protect marine and coastal biodiversity, and lower wildfire risk in dry seasons.

resources.name: Adopt-a-Spot / Community Clean-Up Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg supports volunteers to adopt and regularly clean local sites, including beaches, parks, trails, and riversides, providing supplies and coordinating debris collection. Routine removals of litter, driftwood piles, and abandoned materials protect sensitive shorelines from erosion, improve habitat quality, and reduce fire risks from dry debris accumulation.

solutions.text: Local Supply-Chain Resilience Initiatives: Businesses and community groups create local backup supply networks, shared storage, and mutual support agreements to keep essential goods and services available during disruptions.

resources.name: Feed Nova Scotia – Provincial Food Bank Network and Distribution
resources.description: Feed Nova Scotia operates a centralized warehousing and logistics network that supplies more than 140 member food banks, meal programs, and shelters across the province. By maintaining shared dry and cold storage, coordinating provincewide transportation, and facilitating mutual aid among member agencies, they keep essential food moving during storms, floods, and wildfires. Their hub-and-spoke system provides backup distribution routes and surge capacity to support communities when disruptions occur.

resources.name: Perennia Innovation Centre (Shared Food Processing and Storage)
resources.description: Perennia’s Innovation Centre provides shared, food-grade processing spaces along with cold and freezer storage that small and medium food businesses can use to produce, package, and store products. This shared infrastructure builds regional supply-chain resilience by creating backup processing and storage capacity, enabling producers to pivot and maintain supply when their own facilities are disrupted. Perennia also offers technical advisory and value-chain support that strengthens local networks among growers, processors, and distributors.
resources.address: 45 Innovation Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: WFM2Go – Community Food Hubs and Delivery
resources.description: WFM2Go is the Wolfville Farmers’ Market’s multi-producer online ordering and community hub delivery system that aggregates products from local farms and food makers for pickup at multiple sites across the region. By diversifying sales and distribution channels and using shared aggregation and cold storage at the market, WFM2Go helps maintain access to essential foods during weather-related disruptions. Its networked model distributes risk across many producers and hubs, creating local backup supply routes.

resources.name: Scotian Gold – Controlled-Atmosphere Storage and Grower Co-operative Distribution
resources.description: Scotian Gold operates one of the largest controlled-atmosphere storage and packing facilities in Atlantic Canada, coordinating apples and other produce from a network of Nova Scotia growers. Its shared storage and centralized distribution create year-round inventory buffers and redundancy that stabilize local supply when storms or transportation interruptions occur. As a grower co-operative, Scotian Gold formalizes mutual support among members to keep essential produce available to retailers and communities.

resources.name: FarmWorks – Local Food Business Investment and Network
resources.description: FarmWorks invests patient capital and provides mentorship to dozens of Nova Scotia food producers, processors, and distributors, helping them expand capacity and improve logistics. By financing local enterprises across the value chain and encouraging collaboration among them, FarmWorks strengthens regional backup supply networks and shared distribution options. This connected ecosystem of businesses enhances the province’s ability to keep essential goods available during climate-related disruptions.

solutions.text: Small-Scale Coastal Engineering Pilots: Community-directed pilot projects (e.g., submerged breakwaters, cobble beach nourishment) evaluated locally to protect high-value areas while minimizing ecological harm.

resources.name: Mahone Bay Living Shoreline Project
resources.description: The Town of Mahone Bay is piloting a living shoreline along its harbourfront to reduce storm surge and erosion while enhancing coastal habitat. The project combines community co-design with small-scale coastal engineering measures such as low-crested reef features, cobble berm nourishment, and salt-marsh plantings, and includes on-site monitoring to evaluate performance and ecological outcomes.
resources.address: 493 Main Street, Mahone Bay, NS B0J 2E0

resources.name: TransCoastal Adaptations Living Shorelines Demonstration Program
resources.organization: TransCoastal Adaptations: Centre for Nature-Based Solutions, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: TransCoastal Adaptations designs and implements community-directed living shoreline pilots across Nova Scotia to protect vulnerable coasts while maintaining natural processes. Projects test techniques like cobble beach nourishment, coir-fibre and brush-mattress stabilization, and low-crested rock sills/submerged breakwaters, with rigorous site monitoring to assess wave attenuation, erosion reduction, and habitat benefits.

resources.name: Ecology Action Centre – Coastal Adaptation & Living Shorelines
resources.description: The Ecology Action Centre partners with coastal communities to plan and deliver small-scale shoreline protection pilots that prioritize nature-based engineering. Initiatives include cobble and dune nourishment, coir log and brush-layer stabilization, and marsh bench creation, paired with community training and follow-up monitoring to minimize ecological harm and adapt designs to site conditions.

resources.name: Annapolis Royal Living Shoreline Demonstration
resources.description: Clean Annapolis River Project leads a living shoreline demonstration on the tidal Annapolis River waterfront to reduce erosion and buffer storm impacts. The site applies soft-engineering approaches—such as planted salt-marsh benches, cobble and rock toe protection, and biodegradable fibre rolls—developed with local stakeholders, and it is monitored to evaluate shoreline stability and habitat outcomes.
resources.address: 314 St George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

solutions.text: Public Education and Risk Communication Campaigns: Ongoing outreach in multiple languages about flood zones, evacuation routes, insurance options, and practical household preparedness steps to increase readiness across communities.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Emergency Management (hfxALERT and Preparedness Education)
resources.description: HRM’s Emergency Management leads public education on local hazards like coastal storms, flooding, and wildfires, and runs the hfxALERT notification system for timely risk and evacuation information. They publish preparedness guides, evacuation guidance when required, and seasonal campaigns on hurricane and winter storm readiness, helping residents understand risks, routes, and steps to prepare homes and emergency kits.

resources.name: Canadian Red Cross Emergency Preparedness Education – Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross delivers community presentations, workshops, and online resources in English and French (and with interpretation support as needed) to help households prepare for floods, hurricanes, and wildfires. Their outreach covers evacuation planning, emergency kits, how to register and receive assistance during disasters, and basic insurance considerations to reduce financial risk.

resources.name: Halifax Water Stormwater Education & Flood Prevention Resources
resources.description: Halifax Water provides public education on urban flood risks and practical steps homeowners can take to reduce flooding and sewer backup, including downspout disconnection, backwater valves, and lot grading. Their materials and customer outreach explain stormwater systems, advise residents to review insurance coverage for sewer backup/overland flooding, and share alerts and preparedness tips during heavy rain events.
resources.address: 450 Cowie Hill Road, Halifax, NS B3P 2V3

resources.name: Coastal Adaptation: Community Outreach on Sea-Level Rise & Storm Surges
resources.description: Ecology Action Centre works with coastal communities to communicate flood and storm-surge risks and to promote preparedness and resilient practices for homes and infrastructure. Through workshops, guides, and local engagement, they translate risk maps and climate projections into practical steps residents can take, including knowing high-risk zones, planning evacuation routes, and protecting property.

resources.name: Emergency Preparedness Workshops for Newcomers
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers newcomer-focused sessions that explain local hazards (flooding, hurricanes, winter storms, and wildfires), how to receive alerts, and what to do if evacuations are ordered. Workshops and translated materials cover household preparedness, 72‑hour kits, understanding tenant/home insurance basics, and how to find flood-risk and evacuation information in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

obstacles.title: Arts, Culture, and Nightlife Space Constraints
obstacles.description: Rising costs, restrictive bylaws, and venue closures limit affordable creation, rehearsal, and performance spaces that attract and retain young people.

solutions.text: Community Arts Hubs in Vacant Spaces: Coordinate with landlords and municipalities to temporarily repurpose empty storefronts, warehouses, and municipal buildings into low-rent co-creation hubs for rehearsals, small performances, and workshops; local volunteers and arts organizations manage scheduling and upkeep.

resources.name: RadStorm Halifax
resources.description: RadStorm is a volunteer-run, all-ages arts collective that has transformed a former storefront on Gottingen Street into an accessible, low-cost hub for rehearsals, small concerts, printmaking, and workshops. Community volunteers manage scheduling, upkeep, and programming, and artists can book space at sliding-scale rates. By leasing and activating an underused commercial space as a co-creation hub, RadStorm directly addresses the shortage of affordable arts venues.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op operates a cooperatively owned venue in a rehabilitated retail space, offering affordable rentals for rehearsals, small performances, film screenings, and community workshops. Scheduling and programming are managed by co-op members and local volunteers, with subsidy programs that keep rates low for emerging and independent artists. By sustaining an adapted storefront as community arts infrastructure, the Bus Stop exemplifies the conversion of commercial vacancies into co-creation hubs.

resources.name: Eltuek Arts Centre
resources.description: Eltuek Arts Centre was created through the adaptive reuse of the former Holy Angels Convent, transforming a previously empty institutional building into a multi-tenant arts hub in downtown Sydney. It provides subsidized artist studios, shared workrooms, galleries, and flexible rooms for rehearsals, small performances, and workshops, with community partners helping program and maintain the facility. By bringing a vacant building back into active use at accessible rates, Eltuek functions as a regional co-creation hub.

resources.name: Lunenburg Academy of Music Performance (LAMP)
resources.description: LAMP operates in the historic, municipally owned Lunenburg Academy, a former public school that has been repurposed into a year-round music and arts hub. It offers rehearsal rooms, performance spaces, and workshops/masterclasses for students and emerging artists at accessible rates, coordinated in partnership with the Town of Lunenburg and supported by community volunteers. This adaptive reuse of a civic building creates a low-barrier co-creation environment aligned with the community arts hub model.

resources.name: ARTsPLACE
resources.description: ARTsPLACE is an artist-run community arts centre that has converted a Main Street storefront into a collaborative hub with a gallery, studio spaces, and a classroom. Operated by the Annapolis Region Community Arts Council and volunteers, it offers low-cost rentals and subsidized access for rehearsals, pop-up performances, and skill-sharing workshops. By maintaining an adapted commercial space for community use, ARTsPLACE delivers an affordable co-creation venue in a rural town setting.
resources.address: 396 St George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

solutions.text: Shared-Use Agreements with Schools and Faith Groups: Negotiate formal, low-cost shared-use agreements so schools, churches, and community centers open gyms, auditoriums, and classrooms evenings and weekends for youth rehearsals and pop-up shows, with community groups handling staffing and basic maintenance.

resources.name: Spatz Theatre
resources.description: The Spatz Theatre is a public performance venue located inside Citadel High School in Halifax. Operated by the Spatz Theatre Society through a shared-use agreement with the school board, it rents the theatre to community and youth groups in the evenings and on weekends for rehearsals, festivals, and pop-up shows; the society provides technical staff, front-of-house, scheduling, and basic maintenance while keeping rates accessible.

resources.name: Bella Rose Arts Centre
resources.description: The Bella Rose Arts Centre is a performing arts venue housed at Halifax West High School. Managed by the Bella Rose Arts Centre Society under a joint shared-use model, it opens the auditorium after school hours and on weekends for youth theatre, dance recitals, and community performances, with the society supplying technical crews, front-of-house support, and affordable rental packages while coordinating basic maintenance.
resources.address: 283 Thomas Raddall Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 1R1

resources.name: The Stage at St. Andrew’s
resources.description: The Stage at St. Andrew’s is a community performance space operated by St. Andrew’s United Church in central Halifax. The church makes its sanctuary and hall available at low cost for rehearsals, small shows, and festivals in the evenings and on weekends, and its venue team handles bookings, on-site support, and routine upkeep so youth and community arts groups can focus on programming.

resources.name: Sackville Heights Community Centre Facility Rentals
resources.description: Sackville Heights Community Centre is a non-profit, community-run facility in a former school that offers a gym, multipurpose rooms, and studios. Through formal, low-cost rental policies, it opens these spaces after hours and on weekends for youth rehearsals, classes, and pop-up performances, while centre staff manage staffing, custodial services, and basic maintenance.
resources.address: 45 Connolly Road, Middle Sackville, NS B4E 1S6

solutions.text: Pop-Up and Micro-Venue Program: Organize an ongoing calendar of pop-up concerts, readings, and performances in parks, plazas, storefronts and unused lots using simple staging and noise-curfew strategies; rotate locations and Promoters to spread opportunity and foot traffic.

resources.name: Tunes at Noon
resources.description: Tunes at Noon is a free summer concert series that stages pop-up, small-scale performances in the Grand Parade plaza in downtown Halifax. Using minimal staging and daytime scheduling, the series aligns with municipal noise bylaws while drawing lunchtime foot traffic to nearby storefronts. It rotates a diverse lineup of local artists and partners to spread performance opportunities and activate public space.

resources.name: Salt Yard Sessions
resources.description: Salt Yard Sessions presents free, outdoor concerts on the Halifax waterfront using a modest pop-up stage and simple production to transform public boardwalk spaces into micro-venues. The series programs a rotating roster of local performers and curators, with set times designed to respect waterfront noise and public-use guidelines. By activating multiple waterfront spots and drawing steady audiences, it boosts nearby small businesses and showcases emerging talent.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Downtown Dartmouth Summer Sunshine Series
resources.description: The Summer Sunshine Series offers free, pop-up concerts in public spaces like Ferry Terminal Park and Sullivan’s Pond, turning parks and plazas into micro-venues with simple staging and sound. Performances are scheduled in early evening and weekend slots to align with municipal noise bylaws and maximize accessibility for families and youth. The series rotates locations and artists across the season, spreading opportunities for performers and driving foot traffic to downtown businesses.

resources.name: Truro BuskerFest
resources.description: Truro BuskerFest is an annual street-performance festival that brings pop-up stages and roaming acts to sidewalks, storefronts, and civic plazas throughout downtown Truro. Using mobile, low-footprint setups and scheduled showtimes, the event adheres to local street-use and noise rules while creating a vibrant, walkable circuit of micro-venues. The program disperses audiences across multiple blocks, boosting local commerce and giving emerging performers paid, high-visibility opportunities.

solutions.text: Cooperative Venue Ownership: Form community co-ops where artists and supporters buy or lease a building together, sharing capital, operating costs, governance and booking; co-op financial models reduce rent pressure and keep control local.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op
resources.description: A member-owned cooperative that operates a multi-use performance venue offering theatre, music, dance, and community events. Artists and community members collectively govern the space, share operating costs, and manage bookings, which stabilizes rents and keeps decision-making and cultural programming under local control.

resources.name: Acadia Cinema Cooperative / Al Whittle Theatre
resources.description: A community-owned cooperative that purchased and revitalized a historic cinema and live performance venue serving the Annapolis Valley. Member-owners share governance and financial stewardship, ensuring affordable access for filmmakers, musicians, and theatre groups while keeping venue ownership and programming decisions in the hands of the local community.

resources.name: The Old School Community Gathering Place
resources.organization: Old School Community Gathering Place Co-operative Limited
resources.description: A community co-operative that acquired a former school and converted it into affordable studios, rehearsal rooms, classroom/workshop areas, and an event/gallery space. Members and community shareholders share costs and governance, creating long-term, locally controlled creative infrastructure that reduces rent pressure for cultural users.

resources.name: ART 1274 Hollis Gallery
resources.description: An artist-run cooperative gallery where member artists jointly manage operations, share rent and marketing costs, and collectively curate exhibitions and events. This cooperative model sustains an affordable, centrally located venue for visual arts while keeping financial control and programming decisions with local creators.

resources.name: Peer Gallery Artists' Cooperative
resources.description: A cooperative of contemporary artists who jointly operate a year-round gallery, sharing lease costs, staffing, and curatorial decisions. By pooling resources and governing collaboratively, the co-op maintains a stable, affordable exhibition venue that supports local artists and community cultural programming.

solutions.text: Community Land Trust for Cultural Spaces: Establish a local land trust that acquires and holds property specifically for affordable cultural uses (studios, performance halls, maker spaces), preserving long-term affordability and insulating venues from real estate speculation.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Cooperative
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Cooperative owns and operates a multi-use performance venue on Gottingen Street in Halifax. By purchasing and holding the building in cooperative, community ownership, the organization preserves affordable rental rates for rehearsals, performances, and community events, effectively insulating the venue from real estate speculation and keeping cultural space accessible long-term.

resources.name: Eltuek Arts Centre
resources.description: Eltuek Arts Centre, operated by New Dawn Enterprises, owns and stewards the former Holy Angels Convent as a community arts facility in Sydney. By keeping the property in nonprofit ownership and leasing studios, workshops, and public spaces to artists and cultural groups at accessible rates, it preserves long-term, affordable cultural space and protects it from market pressures.

resources.name: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts is a nonprofit that owns a rural arts campus in the Annapolis Valley dedicated to creation, rehearsal, and performance. By holding land and facilities in community stewardship and offering subsidized studios, rehearsal halls, and maker spaces, it ensures enduring, affordable access for artists and youth while shielding the site from speculative redevelopment.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

resources.name: The Deanery Project
resources.description: The Deanery Project is a community nonprofit that owns a coastal site with studios, shop spaces, and event/performance areas in Lower Ship Harbour. By maintaining community ownership and providing low-cost access to maker spaces, workshops, and cultural programming, it preserves long-term affordability for cultural uses and protects the venue from speculative real estate pressures.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

solutions.text: Mobile Stage and Equipment Library: Create a community-owned mobile stage, PA systems and lighting that can be loaned or booked affordably for outdoor events, block parties and small indoor venues, lowering production barriers for organizers.

resources.name: Civic Events Mobile Stage and Equipment Bookings
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Civic Events team maintains a mobile stage (showmobile) and event gear that community groups can book for festivals, block parties, and outdoor performances at accessible rates. The program lowers production barriers by providing a ready-to-deploy stage along with PA support and event logistics guidance, helping organizers activate public spaces without needing to purchase expensive infrastructure.

resources.name: Event Equipment Lending Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings (Recreation Services)
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings lends community event equipment—such as portable PA systems, staging pieces, tents, and accessories—to local organizers for low or no cost. By supplying the core production elements needed for pop-up shows and small festivals, the program enables affordable, grassroots arts and culture events across towns and rural communities.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Recreation Equipment Loan Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg (MODL) Recreation
resources.description: MODL’s Recreation Department operates an equipment loan program that includes community event gear like portable sound systems, pop-up tents, and basic lighting to support neighborhood gatherings and small performances. This shared resource model reduces costs for organizers and helps activate parks and community spaces with arts and cultural programming.

resources.name: Yarmouth Recreation Equipment Loan Program
resources.organization: Yarmouth Recreation (Town of Yarmouth and Municipality of the District of Yarmouth)
resources.description: Yarmouth Recreation offers community groups access to event equipment, including a portable PA system and related accessories, that can be borrowed for local concerts, block parties, and cultural gatherings. By providing affordable access to sound and setup gear, the program helps emerging organizers and youth-led initiatives stage performances without prohibitive rental costs.

solutions.text: Nighttime Activation Micro-Grants: Set up small community micro-grant funds to help artists and grassroots promoters cover rental, licensing and soundproofing costs for night events that activate neighbourhoods and attract young audiences.

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty Placemaking Grants
resources.description: Gritty to Pretty provides small grants to artists, collectives, and community groups to animate Downtown Halifax with installations, lighting, and pop-up infrastructure that support evening and night programming. Funds can be used toward equipment and site rentals, permits/insurance, and modest build items that help mitigate noise spill (e.g., temporary acoustic treatments), directly lowering the cost barriers for grassroots promoters to run night events that attract young audiences.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

resources.name: Event Sponsorship Program
resources.description: This program offers micro-funding and in-kind support to organizers hosting concerts, markets, and cultural activations in Downtown Dartmouth, many of which take place in the evening. Sponsorships can offset venue or site rental, sound/lighting rentals, SOCAN/Re:Sound licensing, and municipal permit fees, helping artists and grassroots promoters deliver affordable night events that enliven the district.

resources.name: Event Partnership Program
resources.description: The Event Partnership Program provides small grants and logistical support to grassroots organizers to animate Downtown Truro with festivals, concerts, and night markets.
