resources.description: A single-door access point for at-risk and homeless youth that coordinates housing, mental health and addictions, employment, and education services across multiple agencies. Phoenix participates in community case conferencing and secure information-sharing (including HIFIS where applicable) to streamline referrals, track unmet needs among youth, and target rapid responses to emerging hot spots such as overdose risk or unsafe housing situations.

obstacles.title: Youth Voice and Civic Engagement Deficit
obstacles.description: Limited youth representation in decision-making and program design reduces policy relevance and trust in institutions.

solutions.text: Municipal Youth Councils with Decision Power: Establish or strengthen local youth councils that have clearly defined advisory and decision-making roles on municipal committees (planning, recreation, economic development) to ensure youth input shapes policies and budgets.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: A formal advisory body to Halifax Regional Council composed of youth members who provide input on municipal policies, services, and budget priorities impacting young people. The committee brings youth perspectives to standing committees (e.g., planning, recreation, and community development) through motions and recommendations that are recorded by the Municipal Clerk and considered by Council, ensuring youth voices shape municipal decisions.

resources.name: Cape Breton Regional Municipality Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: A municipal committee that engages youth from across CBRM communities to advise the Mayor and Council on issues such as recreation programming, transportation, and community planning. The committee channels youth input directly into Council and relevant municipal committees through formal recommendations and participation in consultations, helping to inform policies and budgets with lived youth experience.

solutions.text: Youth-led Participatory Budgeting: Allocate a portion of municipal or neighbourhood budgets for projects decided directly by youth through participatory budgeting processes, giving young people experience in prioritizing community investments.

resources.name: District 7 Participatory Budgeting (Halifax South Downtown)
resources.organization: Halifax Regional Municipality — Councillor Waye Mason (District 7)
resources.description: Each year, the councillor allocates a portion of the District 7 capital funds for projects that residents propose and vote on directly. The process includes targeted outreach to high schools and youth-serving organizations and invites youth to submit ideas and cast ballots, giving young people hands-on experience in prioritizing neighborhood investments like park upgrades, safety improvements, and community space enhancements.

resources.name: District 9 Participatory Budgeting (Halifax West Armdale)
resources.organization: Halifax Regional Municipality — Councillor Shawn Cleary (District 9)
resources.description: District 9 sets aside a share of its district capital funds and invites residents to decide which projects receive funding through a public vote. Youth are actively encouraged to participate through school and community outreach, with opportunities to propose and prioritize projects that matter to them—such as recreational amenities, active transportation, and arts initiatives—thereby practicing real-world budgeting and civic decision-making.

resources.name: Municipality of the County of Inverness Participatory Budgeting
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Inverness
resources.description: The Municipality dedicates a portion of its annual budget to community projects chosen by residents through participatory budgeting, with dedicated outreach to youth groups and schools to boost youth submissions and voting. By enabling young residents to help decide funding for local priorities—such as community recreation, cultural programming, and small infrastructure—this initiative directly builds youth voice in municipal investment decisions.
resources.address: 375 Main Street, Port Hood, NS B0E 2W0

solutions.text: Community Co-design Workshops: Host regular co-design sessions where youth and community stakeholders jointly develop programs and services (housing, transit, employment supports), using facilitation that centers youth voices, including rural and Mi'kmaq youth.

resources.name: Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Youth Advisory Committee convenes regular meetings and community engagement sessions where young people and municipal staff co-develop recommendations on issues like transit, housing, recreation, and employment supports. The committee’s facilitation model centers youth voice and actively seeks participation from diverse youth across urban, suburban, and rural HRM, including Mi’kmaq and other Indigenous youth, to inform municipal programs and services.

resources.name: Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: CBRM’s Youth Advisory Committee hosts youth-led forums and design workshops to gather input from young people and community stakeholders on local priorities such as transit access, housing needs, and employment opportunities. These sessions center youth perspectives from communities across Cape Breton, including rural areas and Mi’kmaq youth, and translate co-designed ideas into advice for municipal programs and policies.

resources.name: HeartWood Centre for Community Youth Development (Youth Engagement & Co-Design)
resources.organization: Community Sector Council of Nova Scotia
resources.description: HeartWood (now a program area of CSCNS) facilitates community co-design processes across Nova Scotia that bring together youth and local stakeholders to create or improve services, including transportation solutions, housing supports, and employment pathways. Using youth-centered facilitation methods, HeartWood runs workshops and design labs that prioritize the leadership of diverse youth—explicitly engaging rural communities and partnering with Mi’kmaq organizations to ensure Indigenous youth voices shape outcomes.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 309, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Wije’winen Project – Community Engagement & Youth Programming
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Wije’winen initiative conducts ongoing community engagement circles and co-design workshops with Mi’kmaq youth, Elders, and urban Indigenous community members to shape an integrated hub of services (including housing navigation, employment supports, and cultural programming). These sessions elevate youth leadership and ensure programs are co-created with and for Indigenous youth, while also inviting collaboration with non-Indigenous partners to improve services for the wider community.

solutions.text: Youth Civic Apprenticeships: Create short-term paid apprenticeships in local government, NGOs, and community organizations that place youth in policy, planning, and program-design roles to build skills and institutional knowledge.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship (CLSI)
resources.description: CLSI places high school, post-secondary, and recent graduate youth in paid summer and short-term roles with municipalities, Mi'kmaw communities, and NGOs across Nova Scotia. Interns support climate policy research, community planning, and program design/evaluation (e.g., municipal climate adaptation plans, waste-reduction strategies), directly building youth civic capacity and institutional knowledge while contributing to local decision-making.

resources.name: Student and Youth Employment (Co-ops & Internships)
resources.description: HRM hires students and recent graduates into paid co-op and internship positions across municipal departments, including Planning & Development, Public Works, and Government Relations & External Affairs. These placements engage youth in policy analysis, community planning, program and service design, and public engagement projects that inform municipal decisions and strategy.

resources.name: Internships and Co-op Placements
resources.description: The Ecology Action Centre hosts paid internships and co-op placements that embed youth in policy, planning, and program design across climate, transportation, coastal, and environmental justice initiatives. Interns co-develop community programs, contribute to policy submissions and planning processes, and support engagement with municipalities and provincial agencies—giving youth meaningful roles in shaping public-interest outcomes.

solutions.text: Intergenerational Dialogue Forums: Organize structured forums connecting youth, elders, business leaders, and elected officials to share perspectives on community priorities, build trust, and identify collaborative initiatives.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: HRM’s Youth Advisory Committee advises Regional Council and hosts engagement sessions, youth town halls, and roundtables that bring young people together with municipal councillors, staff, community elders, and local business voices to discuss priorities like housing, transit, and climate. These structured dialogues build trust across generations and turn youth input into concrete recommendations and collaborative initiatives considered by Council and departments.

resources.name: Connector Program (Connector Events and Meetings)
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program facilitates structured one‑to‑one meetings and networking events that match students and recent graduates with established business leaders and government officials. These forums enable youth to share goals and challenges, receive guidance from senior professionals, and co-create next steps—mentorships, job leads, and policy feedback—advancing community priorities and youth retention.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Ocean Connector Series
resources.description: COVE’s monthly Ocean Connector series convenes students and early‑career professionals alongside senior industry leaders, researchers, and government officials to explore challenges and opportunities in Atlantic Canada’s ocean economy. Through facilitated panels, Q&A, and structured networking, youth engage directly with decision‑makers, build intergenerational relationships, and identify collaborative projects that reflect community and sector priorities.

resources.name: Elders and Youth Programs and Community Talking Circles
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre convenes Elders and youth through talking circles, cultural programming, and community gatherings that often include service providers and municipal/provincial representatives. These structured forums foster trust and two‑way learning between generations, elevate Indigenous youth perspectives on community priorities, and catalyze collaborative initiatives with public and business partners.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Youth Conference and Employer Roundtables
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s Clean Leadership program brings high school and post‑secondary interns together with employers, municipal/provincial officials, and community organizations through kickoff conferences and regional roundtables. These structured intergenerational forums give youth a direct voice on local environmental priorities, build relationships with business and public leaders, and spark collaborative projects that strengthen communities and green career pathways.

solutions.text: Youth Seats on Boards and Commissions: Adopt policies that reserve youth representatives on municipal boards, school boards, arts councils, and community planning committees with mentorship and orientation to support effective participation.

resources.name: Youth Advisory Committee (HRM)
resources.description: The Halifax Regional Municipality’s Youth Advisory Committee reserves positions for youth (typically ages 13–24) to advise Regional Council on municipal policies, programs, and services affecting young people. Members receive orientation and staff support from the Municipal Clerk’s Office to participate effectively, and they can be asked to provide input to other HRM boards and committees, ensuring youth voices shape municipal decision-making.

resources.name: Mayor’s Youth Advisory Council (MYAC) – Kentville
resources.description: Kentville’s MYAC formally reserves seats for local youth to provide recommendations to Town Council on municipal priorities, programs, and community development. Town staff and councillors offer mentorship and orientation so youth members can participate confidently in meetings and, where appropriate, liaise with other town committees, embedding youth input in municipal decision-making.

resources.name: Mayor’s Youth Advisory Committee (MYAC) – Bridgewater
resources.description: Bridgewater’s MYAC reserves positions for youth to advise Council on issues that impact young people, including recreation, transportation, and community planning. The committee is supported by municipal staff who provide onboarding and ongoing mentorship, helping youth members engage effectively with Council and other municipal committees when youth perspectives are needed.

resources.name: Youth Advisory Council (YAC) – IWK Health
resources.description: The IWK Health Youth Advisory Council includes youth and young adults who advise on hospital programs, services, and policies, and may sit on related committees and working groups. Members receive orientation and are mentored by Patient and Family Engagement staff to ensure their contributions inform governance and quality-improvement decisions across the health centre.

solutions.text: Local Civic Tech Platforms: Develop simple local online platforms or apps where young people can propose ideas, give feedback on plans, track outcomes, and engage in consultations in accessible, youth-friendly formats.

resources.name: Shape Your City Halifax
resources.description: Shape Your City Halifax is the municipality’s online engagement hub where residents, including youth, can submit ideas, complete surveys and quick polls, drop map pins with comments, and participate in consultations on local projects. Each project page includes timelines, documents, and “What We Heard” reports so participants can track how input influenced decisions, making it a youth-friendly way to propose ideas and follow outcomes.

resources.name: Engage Bridgewater
resources.description: Engage Bridgewater is the Town’s digital civic engagement platform that hosts idea boards, surveys, Q&A, mapping tools, and project updates on topics such as active transportation, climate/energy projects, and public spaces. Youth can easily share ideas, vote or comment on others’ suggestions, and see “What We Heard” and status updates to track how their input shapes municipal decisions.

resources.name: Let’s Talk East Hants
resources.description: Let’s Talk East Hants is an online portal that invites residents to propose ideas, respond to surveys and quick polls, ask questions, and follow project milestones on municipal initiatives. The platform is mobile-friendly and accessible, and it regularly features projects relevant to youth (e.g., recreation, parks, facilities), providing clear updates and outcome summaries so young people can see how their feedback is used.

resources.name: Engage Wolfville
resources.description: Engage Wolfville is the Town’s civic tech platform for community input where users, including youth, can submit ideas, take surveys, join quick polls, and comment on plans ranging from recreation to housing and accessibility. Project pages feature timelines, documents, and “How We Used Your Input” updates, enabling participants to track outcomes and understand the impact of their contributions.

solutions.text: School–Community Service Learning: Partner schools with community agencies to offer credit-bearing service-learning projects where students work on real local issues and present recommendations to decision-makers.

resources.name: StFX Service Learning Program
resources.description: St. Francis Xavier University’s Service Learning integrates credit-bearing community projects into courses across disciplines. Students partner with local nonprofits, municipal departments, and Indigenous and rural organizations to tackle real issues (e.g., housing, public health, youth programming), producing briefs or project deliverables and presenting recommendations to community partners and local decision-makers.

resources.name: Service Learning and Community Engagement (SLCE)
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University’s SLCE program embeds community-engaged, for-credit projects within academic courses. Students collaborate with municipalities, nonprofits, and social enterprises to research community-defined challenges and deliver presentations, reports, and policy recommendations directly to partner leadership and public stakeholders.

resources.name: MSVU Service Learning
resources.description: Mount Saint Vincent University offers service learning courses that connect students with community agencies for for-credit, issue-focused projects. Learners complete reflective assignments and produce tangible outputs—such as program evaluations, communications strategies, or policy briefs—and present their findings and recommendations to partner organizations and relevant decision-makers.

solutions.text: Youth Policy Incubators / Labs: Support community-based policy labs where youth research local challenges, pilot interventions (transport, housing, arts spaces) and present evidence-based proposals to councils and funders.

resources.name: Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: Halifax’s Youth Advisory Committee (YAC) brings diverse young people together to identify local challenges—such as transit affordability, housing, public spaces, and arts—and to develop evidence-based recommendations for municipal decision-makers. The committee consults peers, conducts community outreach, and collaborates with municipal staff to scope and test small initiatives, then presents formal proposals and advice to Halifax Regional Council and its standing committees.

resources.name: Active School Travel Nova Scotia
resources.description: Active School Travel Nova Scotia supports student-led research on barriers to walking and wheeling to school, including data collection, route mapping, and walkability audits in communities across the province. Youth co-design and pilot interventions—like walking school buses and infrastructure improvements—with schools and municipalities, and present findings and proposals to councils and funders to inform safer, more equitable transportation policy.

resources.name: Bridgewater Youth Action Council
resources.description: The Bridgewater Youth Action Council engages local youth to research community priorities—such as public transit access, recreation and arts spaces—and to co-design solutions with town staff and partners. Members run consultations and small pilots, then present evidence-based proposals and budget requests to Town Council to influence policies and investments that affect young people.

solutions.text: Community Mentorship Networks: Form networks pairing youth with local mentors in government, business, and non-profits to build civic skills, expand networks, and create pathways into local leadership roles.

resources.name: Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Youth Advisory Committee brings together young people to advise Regional Council and staff on municipal policies, programs, and services. Youth members engage directly with councillors and municipal staff mentors, building civic literacy, policy insight, and leadership skills while expanding their networks in local government and community organizations.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship Program
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s paid summer internship places youth with host organizations across Nova Scotia—municipal governments, non-profits, and businesses—where site supervisors mentor interns through real community and environmental projects. The program includes professional development, project management training, and networking events that build civic skills and connect youth to leaders across sectors, creating pathways into local leadership and green careers.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS matches newcomer job seekers—including youth and recent graduates—with experienced professionals in government, business, and the non-profit sector for targeted, goal-oriented mentorship. Mentors provide sector knowledge, networking introductions, and workplace culture insights, helping young people build civic and professional skills while opening doors to leadership pathways in Nova Scotia communities.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Volta Academy
resources.description: Volta Academy is a mentorship-driven pre-accelerator that connects emerging and student entrepreneurs with seasoned mentors from local tech companies, investors, and public-sector partners. Through workshops, coaching, and pitch sessions, participants gain leadership, communication, and community problem-solving skills while expanding networks that can propel them into visible roles in Nova Scotia’s innovation ecosystem.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Cape Breton Connector Program
resources.description: The Cape Breton Connector Program introduces recent graduates and other early-career participants to established leaders in business, non-profits, and government who act as Connectors and open their networks. Through structured one-on-one meetings and warm introductions, youth build professional relationships, learn local civic and industry dynamics, and access pathways into leadership roles within the Cape Breton community.

solutions.text: Accessible, Inclusive Outreach Campaigns: Run multilingual, culturally appropriate outreach and pop-up engagement events (markets, sports fields, community centres) timed and located for youth participation, including rural tours and virtual options.

resources.name: Newcomer Youth and Family Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Newcomer Youth and Family Program engages immigrant and refugee youth through culturally responsive, multilingual outreach led by settlement staff and interpreters. The team sets up pop-up information tables and activities at schools, community centres, and local markets across HRM and partners in rural communities, while also offering virtual workshops and feedback sessions scheduled after school and evenings. These efforts create low-barrier opportunities for newcomer youth to share their perspectives on services and community issues, informing program design and local decision-making.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YREACH (YMCA Refugee and Immigrant Settlement Program)
resources.description: YREACH provides province-wide, multilingual outreach that meets youth and families where they are—hosting pop-up information sessions and youth-friendly activities at libraries, markets, sports fields, and community centres in both urban and rural Nova Scotia. Staff coordinate after-school and weekend events and offer virtual drop-ins/webinars to reduce barriers for youth participation, collecting feedback to connect young people’s needs and ideas to local services, schools, and municipalities. The program’s culturally appropriate approach helps newcomer and refugee youth feel welcome and heard in community planning and service design.

resources.name: Pop-Up Library
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Pop-Up Library brings library services and engagement activities to youth at community events, parks, markets, and recreation sites across HRM, complemented by virtual clubs and programs for teens. Staff provide accessible, culturally inclusive programming and resources (including multilingual materials and newcomer supports) and schedule sessions after school and on weekends to maximize youth participation. Pop-ups frequently include on-the-spot surveys, idea boards, and co-design activities that invite young people to shape future programs and inform community initiatives.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Bookmobile Service and Pop-Up Library
resources.description: The Cape Breton Regional Library’s Bookmobile and Pop-Up Library services reach youth in rural and underserved communities by setting up at festivals, arenas, school grounds, and community centres, with schedules aligned to after-school and weekend hours. The library pairs these on-the-road visits with virtual teen programs and digital access support, while partnering with local cultural and newcomer groups to ensure inclusive, culturally appropriate engagement. These mobile and online touchpoints invite youth to share feedback on programs and community needs, strengthening youth voice in local services.

solutions.text: Youth-Led Media and Storytelling: Fund youth-produced media projects (podcasts, zines, short films) that amplify young people’s experiences and policy priorities, increasing visibility and influencing public debate.

resources.name: CBC Creator Network – Atlantic Region
resources.description: CBC’s Creator Network commissions and funds short-form content from emerging and youth creators across Atlantic Canada, including Nova Scotia, providing honoraria, editorial mentorship, and national distribution. By resourcing young storytellers to produce videos, audio features, and digital series about issues that matter to them, the program directly amplifies youth perspectives and helps shape public conversations and policy discourse.

resources.name: ViewFinders: Atlantic International Youth Film Festival
resources.description: FIN’s ViewFinders festival showcases youth-made short films and offers workshops and school programs that support young filmmakers to tell stories about their communities, identities, and policy concerns. By exhibiting youth-produced films to public audiences and decision-makers, and by providing resources and recognition, ViewFinders elevates youth voices and influences public debate through film.
resources.address: 1496 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1R9

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: The Lou Duggan Creative Studio provides free access to podcasting equipment, audio booths, and digital media tools, along with teen-focused workshops and mentorship that enable young people to create podcasts, zines, and multimedia projects. By removing cost barriers and actively showcasing youth-produced content online and in-branch, the library amplifies youth experiences and perspectives to the broader public and civic leaders.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: CKDU 88.1 FM – Youth Programming and Training
resources.organization: CKDU 88.1 FM (Dalhousie Student Union Radio Society)
resources.description: CKDU, Halifax’s campus-community radio station, provides training, studio access, and on-air slots for youth and student producers to develop and broadcast original radio shows and podcasts on local issues. By equipping young people to create and distribute their own media, CKDU increases the visibility of youth perspectives and enables them to engage the public and policymakers through independent journalism and storytelling.

solutions.text: Transportation and Stipend Supports for Participation: Provide travel subsidies, childcare, honoraria, and snacks to reduce practical barriers that prevent youth — especially low-income and rural youth — from attending meetings and civic activities.

resources.name: Youth Advisory Committee (YAC)
resources.description: HRM’s Youth Advisory Committee advises Regional Council and staff on issues affecting youth and helps shape municipal policy and programs. To reduce participation barriers, HRM provides supports such as meeting honoraria, reimbursement for transit fares and travel, and childcare/dependent-care allowances, along with refreshments at meetings—enabling low-income and rural youth to attend and contribute consistently.

resources.name: IWK Youth Advisory Council
resources.description: The IWK Youth Advisory Council engages young people with lived experience to advise hospital leadership on policies, services, and patient experience. To remove practical barriers to participation, the council offers supports such as honoraria or gift cards, transit/parking reimbursement, and meals/snacks at meetings so youth can attend without financial strain.

resources.name: Phoenix Youth Advisory Council
resources.description: Phoenix engages youth with lived experience of homelessness and housing instability to inform program design and advocacy. The Youth Advisory Council reduces barriers by providing bus tickets or transit passes, meeting stipends/honoraria, and food/snacks; staff also help coordinate transportation for participants coming from outside the urban core so they can reliably take part in civic and organizational decision-making.

solutions.text: Evaluation and Feedback Loops with Youth: Create transparent mechanisms for reporting back to youth on how their input was used, including public dashboards and annual youth impact reports, to build trust and show real outcomes.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: The Youth Advisory Committee (YAC) is a formal advisory body to Halifax Regional Council that brings youth perspectives to municipal policy and program decisions. Agendas, minutes, staff reports, and Council responses are posted publicly on Halifax.ca, creating a transparent record of youth recommendations and the actions taken. Staff follow-up and motions tracking reported back to the committee show youth how their input was used and the outcomes achieved.

resources.name: IWK Health Youth Advisory Council (YAC)
resources.description: The IWK Youth Advisory Council engages youth patients and caregivers to shape hospital programs, services, and policies. IWK publishes annual corporate and patient-engagement reports and posts updates on initiatives influenced by youth input, closing the loop by explaining changes made and next steps. Staff also report back to the YAC on progress, providing a transparent mechanism that builds trust and demonstrates real outcomes from youth feedback.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Centre for Education Student Success Survey
resources.description: HRCE conducts an annual Student Success Survey to gather feedback from students on well‑being, engagement, and school climate. Results are shared publicly through online summaries and data visualizations, and schools communicate improvement plans that outline concrete actions taken in response to what students said. This creates an ongoing feedback loop that reports back to youth on how their input informs school planning and program changes each year.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

obstacles.title: Fragmented Governance and Data Silos
obstacles.description: Programs spread across governments and agencies with limited data sharing create navigation challenges and duplicated efforts.

solutions.text: Community Services Directory (crowd-sourced): Build and maintain a simple, searchable, crowd-sourced directory of local programs, supports and contact points (accessible online and as a printable booklet). Community organizations, libraries, schools and residents contribute updates, keeping information current and reducing duplication for youth and families navigating services.

resources.name: Cape Breton Connect
resources.organization: Cape Breton Regional Municipality (CBRM) Recreation Department
resources.description: Cape Breton Connect is a searchable, region-wide directory of sport, recreation, and community programs across Cape Breton. Community organizations and residents submit and update listings that are moderated by municipal recreation staff, keeping information current and reducing duplication. The site offers print-friendly listings that partners and libraries use to produce seasonal or local program booklets for families and youth.

resources.name: Highland Connect
resources.organization: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library (with regional recreation partners)
resources.description: Highland Connect is an online directory covering Antigonish, Guysborough, and Pictou counties that aggregates local programs, community groups, and recreation opportunities. Community organizations, libraries, and municipal recreation partners contribute and maintain listings, enabling a crowd-sourced approach to keep details accurate and comprehensive. The library supports residents by printing tailored, print-friendly listings and occasional booklet-style guides for easy offline navigation.

resources.name: South Shore Connect
resources.organization: Recreation Nova Scotia (with South Shore regional partners)
resources.description: South Shore Connect is a community-driven directory for programs, supports, and active living opportunities across Lunenburg, Queens, and Shelburne counties. Local organizations and residents submit program listings that are reviewed by regional partners, ensuring up-to-date, non-duplicative information that families can search by location and interest. Listings are print-friendly and are used by partners to create seasonal or topic-specific booklets for offline use.
resources.address: 5516 Spring Garden Road, Suite 407, Halifax, NS B3J 1G6

resources.name: Feed Nova Scotia – Find Food Directory
resources.description: Feed Nova Scotia’s Find Food directory maps food banks, meal programs, and community food supports across the province in a searchable, filterable tool. Member agencies and community partners regularly provide updates to keep hours, locations, and eligibility current, reducing duplication and helping families quickly navigate to the right support. The directory provides print-friendly location lists that outreach workers and libraries commonly print as take-home guides.

solutions.text: Shared Intake & Referral Toolkit: Co-create a lightweight shared intake and referral form and referral pathways that local organizations can adopt. Standardized intake reduces repeated paperwork for young people, speeds handoffs between agencies, and makes it easier to track who is being served without centralizing sensitive personal data.

resources.name: Halifax Coordinated Access (Reaching Home)
resources.description: United Way Halifax leads the community’s Coordinated Access system for people experiencing homelessness, using a standardized intake and assessment to add individuals to a shared By-Name List and refer them to the most suitable housing and support providers. Participating agencies agree to common data fields and referral protocols, which reduces duplicate paperwork and enables warm handoffs without centralizing more personal data than necessary.
resources.address: 7001 Mumford Road, Tower 1, Suite 1300, Halifax, NS B3L 2H8

resources.name: SchoolsPlus (Integrated Service Delivery for Students and Families)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: SchoolsPlus is a province-wide initiative that provides a single access point in schools to coordinate supports from education, mental health, justice, and community organizations using a shared consent and referral process. The common intake streamlines navigation for youth and caregivers, allowing partner agencies to receive standardized referral information and reduce repeated paperwork as students move between services.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works – Job Junction
resources.organization: Job Junction (Nova Scotia Works Employment Services Centre)
resources.description: As part of the Nova Scotia Works network, Job Junction uses a standardized client registration and needs assessment that is accepted across all Nova Scotia Works employment centres. This shared intake enables quick referrals to specialized services (e.g., training, wage subsidies, job development) at partner locations without redoing paperwork, while common data fields help track client progress across agencies.
resources.address: 3615 Dutch Village Road, Suite 120, Halifax, NS B3N 2T1

resources.name: ISANS Centralized Intake and Referral
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides a centralized intake and needs assessment for immigrants and refugees, collecting a standard set of information once and coordinating referrals to internal programs (language, employment, settlement) and external community partners. The shared intake and consent process streamlines access for youth and families new to Nova Scotia, allowing partner agencies to receive consistent referral packages and avoiding repeated forms while protecting client data.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Local Navigation Hubs with Youth Navigators: Establish physical and virtual community navigation hubs staffed by trained youth navigators or volunteers who guide young people to programs, help with referrals, and keep local partner organizations informed about recurring barriers and service gaps.

resources.name: SchoolsPlus Hub – Auburn Drive Family of Schools
resources.description: SchoolsPlus is a province-wide, school-based navigation hub where SchoolsPlus Facilitators and Community Outreach Workers help young people and families access and coordinate services. At the Auburn Drive hub, staff provide warm referrals to mental health, employment, housing, recreation, and other community programs, and they host partner agencies on-site and virtually. The hub also feeds recurring barriers and service gaps back to the Halifax Regional Centre for Education and provincial partners to reduce fragmentation.
resources.address: 300 Auburn Drive, Cole Harbour, NS B2W 6E9

resources.name: Community Navigator Program (Central Library)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Community Navigators provide on-site and virtual navigation support that helps youth and other community members access government programs, housing supports, ID, health services, education, and employment resources. At the Central Library, Navigators and teen services staff offer drop-in guidance and warm referrals, and keep local partners informed about recurring access barriers. This library-based hub model blends physical and virtual navigation to reduce silos and duplication across agencies.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works – TEAM Work Cooperative (Halifax Employment Centre)
resources.organization: TEAM Work Cooperative (Nova Scotia Works Employment Services)
resources.description: This Nova Scotia Works centre operates as a community navigation hub where career practitioners, including youth-focused staff, guide young people through job search, training, funding, apprenticeship, and wraparound supports. Staff provide one-on-one navigation and warm referrals to partner agencies (e.g., mental health, housing, education providers) and share insights on recurring barriers with the NS Works network and local partners. The centre offers in-person and virtual services to streamline access across fragmented programs.
resources.address: Suite 705, 6960 Mumford Road, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Connector Program — Students & Recent Graduates
resources.description: The Connector Program matches post-secondary students and recent graduates with volunteer ‘Connectors’ from industry to navigate Halifax’s employment and entrepreneurship ecosystem. Staff provide individualized guidance, make targeted referrals to programs and employers, and surface common barriers (e.g., hiring practices, credentialing, information gaps) to inform partners across business, government, and post-secondary. The program functions as a virtual and in-person navigation hub helping young people build careers and stay in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: Suite 1201, 1809 Barrington Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Community Data Cooperative (data trust): Form a voluntary cooperative of local nonprofits, schools and municipal partners to share aggregated, anonymized service-use data. The cooperative sets rules for access and use, enabling joint planning while keeping control in community hands and protecting privacy.

resources.name: Halifax Community Data Consortium (Community Data Program)
resources.description: Through the national Community Data Program, Halifax Regional Municipality convenes a local consortium of municipal departments, nonprofits, school and health partners, and post-secondary institutions to pool resources for access to custom, aggregated datasets (e.g., Statistics Canada and administrative data). Membership agreements, shared governance, and data-sharing protocols set clear rules for access and use, with standardized suppression to protect privacy. This cooperative model enables joint planning across organizations while keeping stewardship and control with community partners, reducing data silos and duplication.

resources.name: Health Data Nova Scotia (HDNS)
resources.description: HDNS acquires, de-identifies, links, and curates administrative datasets from Nova Scotia Health, IWK Health, and provincial departments for secure, governed use by researchers, planners, and community partners. Formal data-sharing agreements, a privacy-by-design access process, and disclosure control enable the use of aggregated, anonymized data for system planning and service improvement. This breaks down institutional silos while ensuring data ownership and decision-making remain with the contributing organizations—functioning like a data trust for the province’s health and social data.
resources.address: Sir Charles Tupper Medical Building, 5850 College Street, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: Maritime SPOR SUPPORT Unit (MSSU) – Nova Scotia Site
resources.organization: IWK Health Centre (in partnership with Dalhousie University and Nova Scotia Health)
resources.description: MSSU brings together health system decision-makers, clinicians, community organizations, patients, and academic partners to co-design and use de-identified, aggregated data for patient-oriented research and planning across Nova Scotia (and the Maritimes). Governed data access committees, privacy reviews, and standardized data-use agreements define how partners contribute to and use shared datasets while protecting confidentiality. This collaborative governance reduces fragmentation and enables coordinated, evidence-informed action that benefits youth and families.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Open Data Portal
resources.description: The provincial Open Data Portal publishes standardized, aggregated datasets from multiple departments under common licenses with robust disclosure controls to protect privacy. The platform enables nonprofits, municipalities, schools, and community partners to access consistent, privacy-protected data for joint analyses and planning, reducing duplication of effort. Departments retain stewardship and set rules for access and use, creating a trust-like governance framework that keeps control in public hands while enabling cross-sector collaboration.
resources.address: One Government Place, 1700 Granville Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1X5

resources.name: Halifax Index (Data Collaboration)
resources.description: The Halifax Index is an annual data collaboration that aggregates indicators contributed by municipal, provincial, federal, academic, and community partners under shared data-use and attribution agreements. Partners provide de-identified, aggregated measures that are governed for responsible use and public reporting, creating a common fact base for joint planning in workforce, youth retention, and quality-of-life strategies. This cooperative approach reduces information silos and supports coordinated action across sectors.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Quarterly Cross-Sector Roundtables: Host regular, neighbourhood-level roundtables where representatives from youth organizations, employers, post-secondary institutions, Indigenous partners and municipal staff share updates, align programs and agree simple next steps. Rotate meeting hosts and publish brief public notes to reduce duplication.

resources.name: Halifax Local Immigration Partnership (HLIP)
resources.description: HLIP convenes regular cross-sector collaboration tables where municipal staff, community youth-serving organizations, employers, post-secondary institutions, and Indigenous partners share updates and align local newcomer and youth-supporting initiatives. Meetings are hosted at rotating partner locations and HLIP circulates brief summaries and agreed next steps through its network and website updates, helping reduce duplication and bridge data silos across programs.

resources.name: Cape Breton Local Immigration Partnership (CBLIP)
resources.description: CBLIP brings together employers, youth organizations, post-secondary partners (e.g., NSCC/CBU), municipal staff, and Mi’kmaw and newcomer-serving organizations for ongoing coordination tables across Cape Breton–Unama’ki. These roundtables rotate among member-hosted venues and share concise meeting notes and action items, enabling partners to align programs, reduce overlap, and improve information flow supporting young people and newcomers entering local industries.

resources.name: Between the Bridges Community Tables (Dartmouth North)
resources.description: Between the Bridges uses a collective impact approach to host regular, neighbourhood-level roundtables where youth groups, employers, schools/NSCC, Indigenous partners, municipal staff, and residents coordinate actions on priorities like education-to-employment pathways. Meetings are held at rotating community locations and the initiative publishes short public updates and shared next steps, which reduces duplication and helps partners align services for local youth.

resources.name: Employer Engagement Forums & Sector Roundtables
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS convenes recurring sector-specific roundtables and employer forums that include businesses, youth employment practitioners, post-secondary co-op/WIL offices, municipal partners, and community/Indigenous organizations to coordinate hiring pathways and training. Sessions rotate among partner sites and ISANS shares concise takeaways and agreed next steps with participants, reducing program duplication and improving data-sharing for smoother youth and newcomer transitions into work.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Open Program Map and Calendar: Create an interactive map and shared calendar displaying where and when programs run (workshops, training, mentorship, events). Community groups update their entries; youth can filter by interest, location and accessibility, improving visibility and coordination.

resources.name: Halifax Public Libraries Events & Programs Calendar
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries maintains an interactive, system-wide events calendar where youth can filter by branch, age group (including teens), and interest (technology, arts, entrepreneurship, job skills, etc.). Community partners frequently deliver programs in library spaces and have their offerings listed through the Library’s centralized system, creating a shared, searchable schedule with dates, times, and locations that reduces duplication and helps youth navigate opportunities across the municipality.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Events Calendar
resources.organization: Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Works provides a province-wide events calendar listing workshops, training sessions, job fairs, and mentorship opportunities offered by a network of local NS Works Centres and partner organizations. Entries are maintained by community-based service providers across regions and can be filtered by topic and location, with linked details on where and when sessions run—helping youth and jobseekers navigate programs and avoid duplication across agencies.

resources.name: Volta Community Events Calendar
resources.description: Volta hosts an open community events calendar that aggregates workshops, mentorship sessions, meetups, and startup training from organizations across Nova Scotia’s tech and innovation ecosystem. Community partners submit events that are displayed with dates, locations, and registration details, enabling youth and early-career entrepreneurs to filter and discover opportunities in one place and improving coordination across the sector.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Events Calendar
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic maintains a shared events calendar for innovation communities in Western and Northern Nova Scotia, consolidating workshops, training, and mentorship events hosted by IGNITE and partner organizations. Listings specify date, time, and venue (Yarmouth, New Glasgow, or online) and are updated collaboratively by staff and community partners, helping youth filter by location and interest while reducing fragmentation across regional providers.
resources.address: 208 Main Street, Suite 2, Yarmouth, NS B5A 1C8

solutions.text: Volunteer Data Stewards Network: Train a network of volunteer data stewards drawn from libraries, community centres and colleges to help smaller organizations manage basic data tasks (cataloguing programs, anonymizing records, updating shared systems) and to support consistent data quality across the community.

resources.name: Tech Help Volunteers and Data Literacy Workshops
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries recruits and trains volunteer Tech Tutors and hosts free data/digital literacy workshops at branches such as Halifax Central Library. These volunteers act as data stewards for the community by helping individuals and small organizations clean spreadsheets, catalogue program information, and adopt privacy-conscious practices when sharing data. By supporting patrons and community groups to update and use shared tools consistently, the library helps improve data quality across local initiatives.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Volunteer Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Archives operates an ongoing Volunteer Program where trained volunteers transcribe, describe, and index records using standardized metadata and cataloguing practices. Volunteers receive guidance on handling sensitive information and contribute to searchable databases shared with libraries, museums, and community researchers across the province. This community steward model improves data quality and consistency in shared systems that many organizations rely on.

resources.name: Municipal Archives Volunteer Program
resources.description: Halifax Municipal Archives engages community volunteers to help process, describe, and digitize municipal records while applying consistent description and metadata standards in the Archives’ shared catalogue. Volunteers are trained in records handling, basic data cleanup, and privacy-aware description, supporting the responsible use of information across departments and by community users. By updating central systems used by multiple civic programs, volunteers function as data stewards who enhance data quality and reduce duplication.
resources.address: 81 Ilsley Avenue, Unit 11, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1L5

resources.name: MLIS Practicum and Community Projects
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, School of Information Management
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s School of Information Management places graduate students with libraries, archives, nonprofits, and small public agencies across Nova Scotia to undertake information and data management tasks. Students act as data stewards—cataloguing program information, designing metadata schemas, cleaning and anonymizing datasets, and implementing data management plans that connect to shared systems. This creates a province-wide network of trained practitioners who help smaller organizations improve data quality and interoperability.

resources.name: IT Data Analytics Capstone and Applied Research Projects
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Ivany Campus
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College’s IT Data Analytics program partners with local nonprofits, municipalities, and small businesses on student-led capstone and applied research projects. Under faculty supervision, students help community partners clean and integrate datasets, build dashboards, document data standards, and apply privacy best practices—then hand off processes that connect to shared community systems. Drawing from a college network across the province, this operates as a pool of data stewards who raise data quality for smaller organizations.

solutions.text: Community Privacy & Data-Sharing Agreement Template: Develop an easy-to-use template agreement and privacy guidelines that local organizations can sign to enable safe, limited data sharing for coordination. Include plain-language consent scripts for youth and families, and practical clauses about anonymization and retention.

resources.name: SchoolsPlus (HRCE)
resources.description: SchoolsPlus is a province-wide initiative that embeds community and government partners in schools to coordinate services for children, youth, and families. In the Halifax Regional Centre for Education, partner agencies sign standardized information-sharing and consent agreements so staff can share only the minimum necessary data to coordinate supports, using plain-language consent scripts with students and caregivers. The program follows provincial privacy guidelines and partner MOUs that include anonymization for reporting and clear data retention schedules.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Health Data Nova Scotia (HDNS)
resources.description: HDNS enables safe data sharing and linkage between public-sector and community partners for planning, service improvement, and evaluation. Partners use HDNS’s standardized data access and sharing agreements and privacy guidance that specify consent pathways, de-identification, limited-use provisions, and retention/secure destruction requirements. HDNS brokers anonymized datasets and supports partners in preparing plain-language consent materials approved by ethics boards to ensure transparent, privacy-protective coordination.
resources.address: Sir Charles Tupper Medical Building, 5850 College Street, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: Maritime SPOR SUPPORT Unit – Nova Scotia Site
resources.description: The MSSU (NS) supports cross-organization, patient-oriented projects by providing privacy-by-design expertise, standardized data-sharing/transfer agreement templates, and plain-language consent templates that enable limited, purpose-specific information exchange. Its guidance includes de-identification methods and retention/archiving clauses so health and community partners can coordinate services and evaluate outcomes while protecting youth and family privacy.
resources.address: Centre for Clinical Research, 5790 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 1V7

resources.name: ISANS Privacy and Information-Sharing Framework
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS coordinates settlement services with local partners (schools, health, employment, and community groups) using consent-based, limited data sharing to navigate clients to the right supports. The organization implements standardized data-sharing agreements and privacy guidelines with partner agencies and uses plain-language consent scripts with youth and families to permit only the minimum necessary information exchange for coordination. Policies include data minimization, anonymized reporting to funders, and clear retention schedules aligned with provincial and federal requirements.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Mi’kmaw Ethics Watch
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Ethics Watch oversees research and data practices involving Mi’kmaw communities and organizations in Nova Scotia, ensuring culturally governed privacy and data-sharing. It requires formal data-sharing and research agreements that include community consent processes, plain-language scripts, and clear provisions for anonymization, ownership, access, retention, and destruction—templates that local partners sign before any data exchange. This framework enables safe, coordinated information sharing for community and youth-focused initiatives while protecting privacy and sovereignty.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

solutions.text: Shared Outcomes Framework for Youth Programs: Co-design a small set of shared outcome measures (e.g., employment/education status, skill development, satisfaction) that local groups agree to report in an aggregated way. Shared metrics make collaborative planning easier and reduce duplicative reporting.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works (Province-wide Employment Services Network)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: Nova Scotia Works is a network of community employment centres funded and coordinated by the province that provides career and job services to youth and adults. The network operates under a shared performance management framework with standardized outcome measures (e.g., employment or education status upon exit, skills development milestones, and client satisfaction) captured in a common provincial system and aggregated for planning by the Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration. This shared metrics approach reduces duplicative reporting across providers and enables coordinated service planning for youth employment across communities.

resources.name: Pathways to Education — Spryfield
resources.organization: Chebucto Connections (in partnership with Pathways to Education Canada)
resources.description: Pathways to Education in Spryfield supports high school youth with academic, social, and financial supports delivered by Chebucto Connections. The program implements a national shared outcomes framework co-designed across Pathways sites, tracking standardized indicators such as attendance, credit accumulation, graduation, post-secondary enrollment, and participant satisfaction, which are aggregated and reported to Pathways to Education Canada and local partners. Using common metrics enables coordinated planning with schools and community agencies and reduces duplicative reporting to multiple funders.
resources.address: 531 Herring Cove Road, Unit C, Halifax, NS B3R 1X3

resources.name: SchoolsPlus (Halifax Regional Centre for Education)
resources.organization: Halifax Regional Centre for Education (Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development)
resources.description: SchoolsPlus brings health, mental health, social, and justice services into schools to support children, youth, and families across the Halifax region. As part of the province-wide SchoolsPlus model, HRCE uses a shared outcomes and reporting framework (e.g., service access, education engagement, referrals completed, and satisfaction) and common tracking tools across hubs, enabling aggregated reporting to the Department of Education and Early Childhood Development and regional partners. This shared measurement improves cross-agency coordination for youth and reduces duplicative reporting by community partners working with schools.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Youth Outreach Program (YOP) — Phoenix Youth Programs
resources.organization: Phoenix Youth Programs (funded by Nova Scotia Department of Community Services)
resources.description: Phoenix’s Youth Outreach Program engages marginalized youth through outreach, case management, and referrals to education, employment, housing, and health services. As a provincially funded YOP provider, Phoenix reports to the Department of Community Services using a shared set of outcome indicators across agencies (e.g., school engagement, employment/education status, housing stability, skills gains, and client satisfaction) within standardized reporting systems, enabling aggregate analysis and coordinated planning. This common outcomes approach reduces duplicative reporting for community providers and helps align efforts across the youth-serving system.

solutions.text: Youth Advisory Council on Service Integration: Create a council of young people from diverse backgrounds to review how services are organized, test navigation tools, advise on data-sharing practices and champion solutions. Their lived experience ensures community efforts stay youth-centered and practical.

resources.name: Youth Advisory Committee (Halifax Regional Municipality)
resources.description: The HRM Youth Advisory Committee is a diverse council of residents ages 15–24 that advises Regional Council on policies, programs, and services affecting youth. Members review how municipal services (recreation, transit, libraries, public safety) are organized and how youth navigate them, provide feedback on digital tools and cross-department referrals, and champion youth-centered solutions. They also advise staff on privacy and data-sharing considerations when partnerships span multiple municipal units and community agencies, helping to reduce fragmentation and improve service integration.

resources.name: IWK Youth Advisory Council
resources.description: The IWK Youth Advisory Council brings together youth with lived experience to advise IWK Health on policies, service design, and communication across pediatric and youth health and mental health services. The council tests wayfinding and navigation tools (e.g., websites, appointment and referral pathways) and offers guidance on consent, confidentiality, and data-sharing practices between IWK, Nova Scotia Health, schools, and community partners. Their input grounds integrated-care improvements in practical, youth-centered solutions that reduce duplication and make services easier to navigate.

resources.name: Superintendent’s Student Advisory Council (SSAC)
resources.description: The HRCE Superintendent’s Student Advisory Council convenes secondary students from across the region to advise education leaders on system navigation and student supports. Youth review how school, public health, mental health, and community services intersect, help test information portals and referral processes, and recommend clearer pathways for accessing help. Their insights inform cross-agency collaboration and responsible information-sharing, advancing coordinated, youth-centered services across the education system and its partners.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

obstacles.title: Provincial Brand and Talent Attraction Narrative
obstacles.description: Persistent outmigration narratives and modest external marketing undercut efforts to attract back alumni and newcomers seeking lifestyle and opportunity.

solutions.text: Community Storytelling Campaign: Collect and share short, locally produced stories (video, audio, written) of residents who built fulfilling lives here — alumni, entrepreneurs, tradespeople, artists. Distribute via social channels, local media, and a central website to replace negative narratives with authentic, place-based experiences.

resources.name: ACOA Success Stories
resources.description: The Atlantic Canada Opportunities Agency (ACOA) publishes written and video success stories highlighting Nova Scotia entrepreneurs, innovators, and community builders. Shared on a central website and across federal social media channels, these authentic profiles showcase opportunity and quality of life in Nova Scotia, countering outmigration narratives and supporting talent and business attraction.
resources.address: 5151 Terminal Road, 14th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 1A1

resources.name: Dal Alumni – Alumni Stories
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Advancement team regularly publishes alumni stories and profiles—often in video and written formats—on its website and Dal News, and amplifies them on social media. The stories feature graduates who have built fulfilling lives and careers in Nova Scotia as entrepreneurs, researchers, health professionals, and artists, reinforcing a positive, place-based narrative that encourages students and alumni to stay or return.

resources.name: SMU Alumni Profiles
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University curates and shares alumni profiles that spotlight Nova Scotia entrepreneurs, business leaders, community organizers, and creatives. Distributed via smu.ca, newsletters, and social media, these stories present authentic lived experiences in Halifax and across the province, helping to replace negative narratives with examples of fulfilling careers and community life.

resources.name: CBU Stories
resources.description: Cape Breton University publishes ‘CBU Stories’—written and video features on students, alumni, and community partners who live, work, and build careers in Cape Breton–Unama’ki. Shared on the CBU newsroom and social channels, these narratives highlight thriving paths in sectors like healthcare, trades, tourism, and culture, advancing a welcoming, opportunity-rich image of the region.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

resources.name: StFX Alumni Stories
resources.description: St. Francis Xavier University features alumni stories that showcase Nova Scotians building meaningful careers and community impact across Antigonish and the province, in written profiles, videos, and podcasts. Disseminated through the university’s website, newsletters, and social media, the series provides authentic, place-based narratives that support talent retention and return.

solutions.text: Alumni & Returner Ambassador Program: Recruit alumni and successful returners as volunteer ambassadors to host talks, panels, virtual Q&A sessions, and mentorship for students and prospective returnees. Promote ambassadors through schools, post‑secondary institutions, and industry groups to create visible role models.

resources.name: Dal Alumni Link
resources.description: Dal Alumni Link is Dalhousie University’s mentoring and networking platform that connects students and recent graduates with alumni for 1:1 mentorship, virtual Q&A sessions, and panel discussions. Alumni volunteers—including many who have returned to Nova Scotia—serve as visible ambassadors by sharing career paths and why they choose to live and work in the province, supporting talent attraction and retention.

resources.name: SMU Mentoring (Ten Thousand Coffees)
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University’s SMU Mentoring hub pairs students and emerging grads with alumni volunteers for informational interviews, office hours, and industry panels. Alumni—including successful returnees—act as ambassadors who share lived experiences and professional networks, promoting Nova Scotia’s opportunities and quality of life to help students stay or return.

resources.name: NSCC Alumni Mentorship
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College mobilizes its alumni network to mentor current students and recent graduates through career talks, classroom panels, and guided mentorship. Graduates who live and work in Nova Scotia—many as returnees—serve as role‑model ambassadors, providing practical advice and showcasing pathways to fulfilling careers in the province.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Connector Program engages volunteer ‘Connectors’—established professionals, employers, and community leaders, including many former newcomers and returnees—to meet with participants, host networking events, and make warm referrals. These ambassadors share their Nova Scotia success stories through info sessions and panels in partnership with post‑secondary institutions and industry groups, helping newcomers and returners envision careers and lives in the province.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Local Welcome Hubs: Set up neighborhood welcome hubs (physical or pop‑up) staffed by volunteers to provide information on housing, childcare, jobs, schools, and social activities for newcomers and returners. Hubs can host regular orientation events and networking mixers.

resources.name: Community Connections
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections program operates welcoming spaces at its Halifax office where trained staff and volunteers help newcomers navigate housing, childcare, employment, schooling, and community life. The program hosts regular orientation sessions, conversation circles, and networking mixers that connect newcomers and returnees with local services, employers, schools, and social activities—functioning as a local welcome hub.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 2005, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Newcomer Services (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Newcomer Services at the Central Library provide a walk-in welcome point where staff and volunteers offer information and referrals on housing, childcare, job search supports, school registration, and community activities. The library runs recurring newcomer orientations, settlement info sessions, English conversation groups, and social mixers—serving as a neighborhood welcome hub for both newcomers and returning residents.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: The Cape Breton Welcome Network is a volunteer-led network of community Welcome Groups coordinated by the Cape Breton Partnership that greets newcomers and returnees and connects them with local information on housing, schools, childcare, jobs, and recreation. These groups host regular welcome events, coffees, and mixers across communities—creating pop-up neighborhood hubs that help people build social networks and navigate services.

resources.name: YREACH (YMCA Newcomer Settlement Services)
resources.description: YREACH delivers settlement and welcoming services across Nova Scotia through local hubs in libraries, municipal buildings, and partner sites, with outreach staff and volunteers providing one-on-one navigation for housing, childcare, education, and employment. The program organizes newcomer orientations, information sessions, and networking events that connect newcomers and returning residents to community resources and social activities, effectively operating neighborhood welcome hubs province-wide.

solutions.text: Community Employer Showcase Series: Organize monthly employer open‑houses and sector showcases where local businesses, trades guilds, and startups present career paths, apprenticeships, and company culture to residents and alumni. Combine with on‑the‑spot recruitment and promotional materials highlighting local opportunity.

resources.name: TEAM Work Cooperative - Employer Information Sessions & Recruitment Events
resources.organization: TEAM Work Cooperative (Nova Scotia Works Halifax)
resources.description: TEAM Work Cooperative, a Nova Scotia Works employment centre, regularly hosts employer information sessions, sector spotlights, and in-house recruitment events where local companies and trades employers present career pathways, training/apprenticeship options, and workplace culture. These open-house style events invite residents, recent graduates, and alumni to meet hiring managers, apply on the spot, and receive take-home materials highlighting opportunities to build a career in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

resources.name: ISANS Employer Information Sessions & Recruitment Events
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS runs frequent sector-specific employer information sessions and hiring fairs that bring local businesses, trades, and startups together with jobseekers and alumni newcomers. Employers present career paths and company culture, conduct on-the-spot interviews, and share promotional materials about working and living in Nova Scotia, directly aligning with a community employer showcase model.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Volta Hiring Fair
resources.description: Volta’s hiring and talent events connect high-growth startups and tech employers with students, grads, and professionals through showcase booths, company pitches, and networking. Employers highlight roles, culture, and growth paths, and many accept applications or interview on the spot, supported by collateral that promotes the advantages of building a career in Nova Scotia’s innovation ecosystem.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Hire Me Halifax
resources.description: Hire Me Halifax is an annual showcase where employers meet emerging and returning talent through live pitches, employer booths, and targeted networking. The event spotlights local companies and sectors, facilitates immediate recruiting conversations, and equips attendees with materials about living and working in Halifax and Nova Scotia to counter out-migration narratives.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Micro‑grants for Returner Startups and Projects: Create a community-funded micro‑grant program to help returning residents launch small businesses or social enterprises. Grants paired with local mentorship, workspace access, and promotion to demonstrate viable pathways for people to come back and thrive.

resources.name: Awesome Foundation Halifax
resources.description: Awesome Foundation Halifax provides recurring $1,000 micro‑grants to individuals and small teams launching creative, entrepreneurial, or community-impact projects in HRM. Trustees select projects and provide informal mentorship and broad promotion through local networks and media, helping returning residents validate ideas, build early traction, and connect to local founders and spaces that can support their next steps.

resources.name: Municipal Community Grants Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Community Grants Program offers small project grants (typically up to $5,000) to community organizations and social enterprises to pilot or expand initiatives with local benefit. Staff guidance, municipal visibility, and connections to community facilities help awardees pair funding with mentorship and access to spaces or partners—creating a supportive on‑ramp for returning residents launching social ventures or community-focused startups.

resources.name: Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta Cohort provides early-stage startups with funding awards alongside residency perks such as workspace access at Volta, structured mentorship from experienced founders and advisors, and significant promotion through its pitch and demo events. For founders returning to Nova Scotia, this model mirrors a micro‑grant approach by pairing non-dilutive early capital (via its investment mechanism), a collaborative workspace, and strong local networks to accelerate getting established back home.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Ready2Launch
resources.description: Dal Innovates’ Ready2Launch is a summer accelerator that provides non‑dilutive seed funding, intensive mentorship, and access to university maker and co‑working spaces to help teams turn ideas into viable companies. The program’s funding plus expert guidance and visibility through showcases and partner networks gives returning alumni and newcomers a practical pathway to quickly validate and grow a venture in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Place‑based Festivals and Open Doors: Expand and market local festivals, arts walks, and industry open‑days that showcase community culture, food, creative economies, and quality of life. Use these events as recruitment touchpoints for alumni and newcomers to experience the community firsthand.

resources.name: Lunenburg Folk Harbour Festival
resources.description: A multi-day festival that activates Lunenburg’s waterfront and historic venues with concerts, workshops, artisan markets, and local food, putting the town’s culture and creative economy front and center. By welcoming visitors, returning alumni, and newcomers into community halls and seaside stages, the festival creates firsthand experiences of small-town quality of life that serve as powerful recruitment touchpoints.

resources.name: KitchenFest!
resources.organization: Colaisde na Gàidhlig | The Gaelic College
resources.description: An island-wide celebration of Gaelic music, dance, and food hosted in community halls, pubs, and cultural spaces across Cape Breton, opening doors to authentic local venues and traditions. The festival showcases vibrant rural life and creative opportunities, inviting visitors, diaspora, and potential newcomers to experience community spirit and lifestyle up close.
resources.address: 51779 Cabot Trail, St. Anns, NS B0E 1B0

resources.name: Craft Nova Scotia Summer Craft Market
resources.description: A curated, place-based marketplace at the Halifax Seaport that features dozens of Nova Scotia artisans, live demonstrations, and locally made food and goods, drawing residents and visitors into the city’s creative economy. By connecting attendees directly with makers and showcasing viable craft careers, the market functions as a welcoming recruitment touchpoint for alumni and newcomers exploring lifestyle and work in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Gran Fondo Baie Sainte‑Marie
resources.description: A signature cycling festival in the Municipality of Clare that pairs scenic routes with an expo, Acadian cuisine, and local music, immersing participants in the area’s culture and community life. The event showcases the region’s active lifestyle and hospitality, creating ideal recruitment moments where alumni and newcomers can engage with local organizers and learn about living and working in southwestern Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Paint the Town (Annapolis Royal)
