resources.organization: Annapolis Region Community Arts Council (ARTsPLACE Gallery)
resources.description: An annual plein‑air arts festival where artists spread out across Annapolis Royal to create works in real time, culminating in public auctions and street‑level cultural programming with local businesses. By animating the town with art, music, and food, the event invites visitors, alumni, and prospective residents to experience small‑town vibrancy and connect with the local arts community and opportunities.
resources.address: 396 St George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

solutions.text: Peer Mentorship & Skills Matching Network: Build a local platform (simple database or Facebook group) matching experienced residents with newcomers and young people for mentorship, skills tutoring, and job referrals. Highlight local career pathways and provide soft introductions to employers and tradespeople.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program matches recent graduates and newcomers with established business and community leaders (“Connectors”) who share sector insights and introduce them to 3–5 people in their networks. These warm introductions often include employers and tradespeople, helping participants learn about local career pathways and uncover job opportunities. The program functions as a practical, relationship-driven skills and networking platform that accelerates mentorship, referrals, and soft landings into Halifax’s job market.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program pairs internationally trained professionals with experienced local mentors in the same field for targeted guidance on licensing, sector expectations, and job search strategies. Mentors provide one-on-one support and warm introductions to employers and professional networks, helping participants navigate Nova Scotia’s career pathways. This structured matching model directly advances peer mentorship, skills tutoring, and job referrals for newcomers.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1W8

resources.name: CEED Entrepreneurial Support & Mentorship
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED connects aspiring and early-stage entrepreneurs—many of them youth and newcomers—to experienced local business advisors and mentors through coaching, cohort programs, and advisory sessions. Participants receive tailored skills development and soft introductions to lenders, suppliers, and employers, clarifying local entrepreneurship and trades-adjacent career pathways. This hands-on network functions as a practical matching platform that accelerates referrals, mentorship, and community-based job connections.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Volta Mentorship Program
resources.description: Volta’s mentorship program matches startup founders and emerging talent with experienced entrepreneurs, investors, and industry specialists for targeted guidance, skills development, and career navigation in tech and adjacent sectors. Through office hours, curated advisory sessions, and partner events, mentors provide warm introductions to employers, hiring managers, and service providers across Nova Scotia’s innovation ecosystem. This network highlights local tech career pathways and creates soft landings for youth and newcomers via relationship-based referrals.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

solutions.text: Housing & Shared Living Initiatives: Pilot community-led solutions such as co‑living houses, renovation-to‑rent programs, or incentive schemes for landlords to offer flexible short-term leases to returning alumni and early-career residents to lower relocation barriers.

resources.name: ISANS Housing Support and Landlord Engagement
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ housing team connects newcomers and early-career arrivals with private landlords, helps negotiate flexible start dates and shorter-term or furnished leases, and educates landlords on tenancy best practices. By brokering matches and reducing risk for landlords through references and settlement supports, the program expands access to transitional rental options that act as a soft landing for people relocating to Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Summer Accommodations
resources.description: SMU opens residence buildings to the public each summer, providing furnished rooms and suites with flexible short-term booking for interns, new hires, and returning alumni. These move-in-ready options function as a reliable landing pad while people search for long-term rentals, directly lowering relocation barriers for early-career residents in Halifax.

resources.name: Mount Saint Vincent University Summer Accommodations
resources.organization: Mount Saint Vincent University Conference & Event Services
resources.description: MSVU offers short-term residence stays each summer for individuals and groups—including co-op students, interns, and new professionals—providing furnished rooms with shared kitchens and common spaces. This co-living style, flexible housing serves as transitional accommodation for people relocating to Halifax, easing entry into the local rental market.

resources.name: Cape Breton University Summer Accommodations
resources.organization: Cape Breton University Residence & Conference Services
resources.description: CBU rents furnished residence rooms and suites on a short-term basis during the summer to students, visiting professionals, and people relocating to Cape Breton. These flexible, move-in-ready stays provide a low-commitment bridge while newcomers and returning alumni secure longer-term housing in the region.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

resources.name: HRM Backyard & Secondary Suites Initiative
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s planning framework permits and streamlines creation of secondary and backyard suites across the municipality, supported by clear guidelines and permitting. By enabling homeowners and small landlords to add self-contained units suited for co-living or flexible short-term rentals, the initiative expands community-led housing supply that lowers relocation barriers for early-career residents.

solutions.text: Community Placemaking and 'Welcome' Improvements: Invest volunteer time, small grants, and local business sponsorship into visible placemaking projects — murals, parks, bike routes, community gardens — and clear signage that make neighborhoods attractive and signal a welcoming, vibrant place to live.

resources.name: Neighbourhood Placemaking Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Neighbourhood Placemaking Program provides small grants, materials, and staff guidance for resident-led projects like street and intersection murals, pop-up parklets, community gardens, and welcoming wayfinding/signage. It leverages volunteer time and local partnerships to transform everyday public spaces into attractive, inclusive gathering places that signal vibrant, welcoming neighbourhoods to residents, alumni, and newcomers.

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty Placemaking Grants
resources.description: Gritty to Pretty funds public art and placemaking in Downtown Halifax through grants and sponsorships for murals, installations, lighting, and small-scale public realm upgrades. By pairing artists with property owners, volunteers, and local businesses, the program turns blank walls and overlooked spaces into welcoming landmarks that boost street life, pride of place, and the city’s appeal to young talent and visitors.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 1Z2

resources.name: Our Transportation (Active Transportation & Complete Streets)
resources.description: Ecology Action Centre advances people-first streets and active transportation across Nova Scotia through community-led projects, pop-up demonstrations, and support for permanent bikeways, trails, and wayfinding. It mobilizes volunteers, trains local champions, and collaborates with municipalities and businesses to create safe, attractive bike routes and pedestrian spaces that make communities more welcoming and connected.

resources.name: Urban Farm & Community Gardens
resources.organization: Urban Farm Museum Society of Spryfield
resources.description: The Urban Farm Museum Society of Spryfield stewards community gardens, an orchard, and public programming that activate local green spaces as welcoming, intergenerational gathering places. Through volunteer work bees, school partnerships, and local sponsorships, the farm adds garden beds, signage, and community art that showcase neighbourhood pride and invite people to connect outdoors.
resources.address: Captain William Spry Community Centre, 16 Sussex Street, Halifax, NS B3R 1N8

resources.name: Dartmouth North Community Food Centre
resources.organization: Dartmouth Family Centre & Community Food Centre
resources.description: The Community Food Centre transforms its site into a welcoming hub with community gardens, outdoor gathering spaces, and visible signage that invite residents to grow, share meals, and connect. Working with volunteers, local partners, and sponsors, it creates attractive public spaces and programming that strengthen neighbourhood identity and make Dartmouth North more inviting for families and newcomers.

solutions.text: Local Digital Relocation Portal: Create and maintain a simple, community-run web portal with practical relocation information (jobs, housing listings, childcare, service contacts, events, testimonials). Keep content updated by a rotating local editorial team and promote it to alumni networks.

resources.name: Move to Halifax (Talent & Relocation Portal)
resources.description: Halifax Partnership maintains a comprehensive digital relocation portal that aggregates job opportunities, neighbourhood and housing information, childcare and newcomer services, community events, and newcomer success stories. A local team curates and updates content and tools (including job links and settlement resources) and promotes the portal through employer networks and alumni/diaspora outreach to help prospective and returning residents make informed decisions.
resources.address: 5151 George Street, Suite 1277, Halifax, NS B3J 1M5

resources.name: Welcome to Cape Breton (Cape Breton Welcome Network)
resources.description: The Cape Breton Welcome Network runs a community-driven portal that offers practical relocation information for newcomers and returnees, including job board links, guidance on housing and childcare, service directories, local events, and newcomer testimonials. Content is maintained by regional coordinators and community hosts, and the site is actively promoted through employer partners, post-secondary alumni channels, and social media to attract people to live and work in Cape Breton-Unama’ki.

resources.name: Move to Truro
resources.description: The Town of Truro’s relocation hub provides newcomers and returnees with centralized, practical information on jobs, housing, childcare, local services, and community events, along with stories that showcase quality of life. Municipal staff keep the portal content current and share it through regional business and alumni networks to help prospective residents evaluate opportunities and settle smoothly in Truro and Colchester County.

resources.name: Moving to Bridgewater
resources.description: Bridgewater’s municipal website hosts a relocation section that consolidates key information for people considering a move, including links to local job opportunities, housing and rental guidance, childcare and family services, community contacts, and an events calendar. The page is maintained by local communications and community development staff and promoted via town channels and partner networks to reach alumni and newcomers exploring life on the South Shore.

solutions.text: Employer Branding Toolkit for Small Businesses: Develop an easy toolkit and templates local businesses can use to communicate workplace culture, benefits, career pathways, and remote-friendly roles. Host workshops to help employers produce job postings and short recruitment videos that sell living and working locally.

resources.name: Work in Halifax Talent Attraction Toolkit
resources.description: Halifax Partnership provides employers with ready-to-use talent attraction assets—messaging, images, videos, and market insights—that can be dropped into job postings, career pages, and social media to sell the lifestyle and opportunities of living and working in Halifax. The team hosts employer info sessions and webinars that coach small businesses on writing compelling postings and using short recruitment videos and social content to showcase workplace culture, benefits, and career pathways.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: ISANS Employer Support Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS equips Nova Scotia employers with practical toolkits, templates, and one-on-one advising to create inclusive job postings, onboarding materials, and workplace culture statements that resonate with candidates considering a move to the province. Through regular workshops and webinars, they guide small businesses on recruitment marketing and employer branding—including how to highlight benefits, career pathways, and remote-friendly roles—so postings and outreach better reflect living and working locally.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Tourism HR Nova Scotia – HR Toolkit for Tourism Operators
resources.organization: Tourism Industry Association of Nova Scotia (TIANS) / Tourism HR Nova Scotia
resources.description: Tourism HR Nova Scotia offers an HR toolkit with downloadable templates (job descriptions, postings, onboarding checklists) and step-by-step guides that help small tourism businesses strengthen employer branding and recruitment. They deliver workshops and webinars on crafting compelling job ads and short social video content that showcases workplace culture, benefits, and pathways from seasonal roles into long-term careers, all anchored in the appeal of living and working in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Business Workshops (Digital Storytelling & Recruitment Marketing)
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic runs frequent workshops that teach small businesses how to write effective, inclusive job postings and produce short, mobile-friendly recruitment videos and social content. Sessions emphasize showcasing workplace culture, flexibility (including remote-friendly roles), and the advantages of living and working in rural Nova Scotia, with staff providing light-touch coaching and templates so employers leave with ready-to-use materials.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3R7

resources.name: Cape Breton Partnership – Employer Attraction Resources and Workshops
resources.description: The Cape Breton Partnership provides employers with guidance and templates to craft job ads and career pages that highlight the Island Advantage—short commutes, affordability, and vibrant communities—alongside workplace culture and benefits. Through initiatives like the Cape Breton Welcome Network and Hire Me Cape Breton, they offer storytelling assets and video spotlights and host employer workshops on talent attraction and onboarding, helping small businesses market living and working locally.

solutions.text: Youth & Young Leader Civic Engagement Program: Create youth councils and paid internship projects that put young people in leadership roles shaping local policy, events, and marketing. Visible youth leadership helps change narratives about opportunity and makes the community more attractive to peers.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Youth Advisory Committee (YAC)
resources.description: A standing advisory committee of Regional Council composed of youth who advise on municipal policies, services, and strategic priorities affecting young people. Members help shape programs, communications, and events—often collaborating with staff on engagement campaigns—putting youth in visible leadership roles. This implements the solution by empowering youth to influence local policy and marketing narratives that attract and retain their peers.

resources.name: Town of Antigonish Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: The Youth Advisory Committee engages local high-school and post-secondary youth to advise Town Council on municipal policies, priorities, and youth-friendly initiatives. Participants co-design community events and outreach that highlight Antigonish as a great place for young people to live and lead. By formalizing youth voices in decision-making and public communications, the committee advances the solution’s aim of visible youth leadership that reshapes attraction narratives.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship (formerly NS Youth Conservation Corps)
resources.description: A paid, province-wide summer internship program placing youth with municipalities, Mi'kmaq communities, non-profits, and businesses to lead environmental and community projects. Interns take on meaningful roles—community engagement, policy research, communications, and event delivery—building leadership skills while producing visible results in their hometowns. These youth-led projects and marketing efforts counter outmigration narratives by showcasing real opportunities and impact across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: NextGen Cape Breton
resources.description: A regional network that empowers young adults to lead community-building initiatives, advise on retention strategies, and co-host public events that celebrate youth success in Unama'ki/Cape Breton. NextGen convenes youth voices with municipal and business leaders and amplifies youth-led marketing—storytelling, awards, and showcases—that present the island as a place to live, work, and lead. By elevating youth leadership in programming and promotion, it directly advances the solution’s brand- and talent-attraction goals.

resources.name: Halifax Public Libraries Teen Advisory Groups (TAG)
resources.description: TAGs are youth councils at library branches where teens plan programs, advise library staff on services and outreach, and lead peer-facing events and social content. Members shape local cultural programming and marketing that resonates with young audiences, making libraries and their communities more welcoming and vibrant. This creates visible youth leadership roles that contribute to a positive narrative about opportunity and belonging in Halifax.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

obstacles.title: Insufficient High-Quality Career Paths
obstacles.description: Limited availability of mid- to senior-level roles and clear advancement pathways, especially outside Halifax, pushes young talent to larger provinces.

solutions.text: Local Mentorship and Sponsorship Network: Create a community-run program pairing early- and mid-career talent with local senior leaders across sectors for ongoing mentorship, sponsorship, and career advocacy, including regular shadowing opportunities and sponsor-led promotion of mentees for leadership roles.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program pairs recent graduates and newcomers with established business and community leaders across sectors who share advice and proactively open their networks. Connectors commit to making targeted introductions that lead to informational interviews, job-shadowing opportunities, and referrals; many act as sponsors by advocating for participants and recommending them for leadership-track roles. This ongoing, relationship-based model builds clear local pathways into mid- and senior-level positions in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program matches internationally trained early- and mid-career professionals with senior leaders in their fields for structured, multi-month mentorship. Mentors provide career coaching, sector-specific guidance, and strategic introductions that often include workplace tours or job shadowing; many actively sponsor mentees by recommending them to hiring managers, associations, and leadership opportunities. The program strengthens local talent pipelines by turning mentoring relationships into concrete career advancement in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Professional Mentoring Program
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth – Centre for Immigrant Programs
resources.description: The YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs connects skilled newcomers with experienced Nova Scotia professionals for one-on-one mentoring, networking, and career advocacy. Mentors help mentees navigate local labour markets, arrange informational interviews and occasional shadowing, and champion them through warm introductions and references to employers. This sponsor-style support helps mentees secure progression into mid- and senior-level roles within the province.

resources.name: Mentoring Program
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business pairs women entrepreneurs and professionals with seasoned business leaders and sector experts for individualized mentoring and advisory support. Mentors provide ongoing guidance, open doors to customers, suppliers, boards, and investors, and often act as sponsors by making high-value introductions and endorsements for leadership roles. Participants may also observe mentor meetings or operations (shadowing) while receiving regular check-ins that accelerate career and business advancement in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 166 Bedford Highway, McCain Centre, 3rd Floor, Halifax, NS B3M 2J6

resources.name: Volta Mentorship Program
resources.description: Volta connects early- and mid-stage founders and tech professionals with Entrepreneurs-in-Residence and executive mentors for structured mentorship and advocacy. Through targeted matching, office hours, and introductions, mentors actively sponsor mentees by promoting them to investors, customers, and ecosystem leaders; mentees often gain shadowing opportunities during pitches, board meetings, and strategic sessions. This sponsor-led ecosystem approach helps emerging leaders progress into senior roles and build long-term careers in Nova Scotia’s innovation economy.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

solutions.text: Regional Leadership Fellowship: Launch a locally funded fellowship that rotates aspiring leaders through mid- to senior-level projects in multiple community organizations, businesses, and municipal offices to build experience, networks, and a clear leadership résumé outside Halifax.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship
resources.description: Clean Leadership places paid interns with municipalities, Mi’kmaw communities, nonprofits, and small businesses across Nova Scotia to deliver mid-level sustainability and community-impact projects. By embedding participants in host organizations throughout the province (often outside Halifax) and providing cohort-based leadership training, the program builds cross-sector experience, regional networks, and a strong early leadership résumé aligned with a rotating, community-embedded fellowship model.

resources.name: Pathy Foundation Fellowship
resources.organization: Coady Institute, St. Francis Xavier University
resources.description: Hosted at Coady Institute in Antigonish, this 12‑month leadership fellowship supports recent graduates to design and lead a community‑identified initiative in partnership with a local organization, often in rural and small‑town Atlantic Canada. Fellows receive intensive leadership training and mentorship at Coady and work embedded with community and cross‑sector partners, building networks and a leadership résumé outside Halifax similar to a regionally grounded leadership fellowship.

resources.name: Master of Public Administration (MPA) Co-op Program
resources.organization: School of Public Administration, Dalhousie University
resources.description: Dalhousie’s MPA Co-op rotates graduate students through multiple paid work terms with municipal governments, provincial agencies, and community organizations across Nova Scotia. These placements frequently occur in smaller centres, giving participants mid‑level project experience, cross‑sector exposure, and provincial networks that mirror the goals of a regional leadership fellowship.

resources.name: Acadia University Co-operative Education Program
resources.description: Acadia’s co-op program places students in several paid 4–8 month terms with businesses, nonprofits, and municipal offices across the Annapolis Valley and wider Nova Scotia. By rotating through distinct roles and sectors—often outside Halifax—participants develop practical leadership experience, regional networks, and clearer career pathways aligned with a regional leadership fellowship approach.

solutions.text: Skills Accelerator and Credential Microprograms: Coordinate community colleges, employers, and industry groups to offer short, stackable credentials and accelerated training focused on leadership, management, and specialized technical skills tailored to local industry needs.

resources.name: NSCC MicroCredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College collaborates with employers and industry associations to design short, competency-based micro-credentials in areas like leadership, supervision, digital skills, marine/oceans, construction, and advanced manufacturing. These stackable badges and certificates provide accelerated, job-aligned training that helps early- and mid-career workers progress into specialized and managerial roles across communities throughout Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Microcredentials (Open Learning & Career Development)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University — Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development offers industry-validated micro-credentials and intensive certificates in leadership, project management, data and digital, and sector-focused skills. Programs are designed with employer input and delivered in short, stackable formats to quickly upskill professionals for advancement into supervisory and mid-level roles across Nova Scotia’s key industries.

resources.name: Sobey Executive Education Certificates and Micro-credentials
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University — Sobey School of Business, Executive Education
resources.description: Sobey Executive Education delivers short, stackable programs in leadership, management, governance, finance, and strategy that can be combined into recognized certificates. Developed with and for employers in Atlantic Canada, these accelerated offerings build practical competencies that prepare emerging and mid-level managers for senior responsibilities within Nova Scotia organizations.

resources.name: Open Acadia Micro-credentials and Professional Certificates
resources.description: Open Acadia provides short, stackable micro-credentials and professional certificates aligned with regional needs in sectors such as agri-food, environmental management, community development, and business leadership. Programs are delivered in flexible, accelerated formats and developed with community and industry partners to help learners in rural and urban Nova Scotia move into specialized and supervisory roles.

solutions.text: Community-led Apprenticeship and Succession Plans: Work with trades, farms, and small businesses to establish structured apprenticeship-to-leadership pathways and public succession plans that guarantee mid- to senior-level progression for local hires.

resources.name: Registered Apprenticeship Program
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency’s Registered Apprenticeship Program partners with employers across the province to create structured training agreements, on‑the‑job mentorship with certified journeypersons, and block-release technical training at NSCC. It provides clear, competency-based pathways from entry-level apprentice to Red Seal certification and supports progression into lead hand, foreperson, and supervisory roles. The Agency also offers employer supports (e.g., START wage incentives and mentorship training) that help small businesses and trades shops develop internal succession plans and advance local hires into mid- and senior-level positions.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based, community-led program that prepares Nova Scotians—often from underrepresented communities—for entry into shipbuilding trades and long-term careers with progression opportunities. Delivered by NSCC with industry and community partners, it combines academic upgrading, essential skills, pre-apprenticeship training, and paid work terms that lead into registered apprenticeship and advancement toward Red Seal and supervisory roles at employers like Irving Shipbuilding. By mapping a transparent route from training to employment and leadership, it supports local talent to build sustainable, senior-level careers in a key Nova Scotia industry.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY places high school students in paid summer work experiences with construction employers across Nova Scotia, creating a direct on-ramp into apprenticeship with sponsoring companies after graduation. Administered by CANS with industry partners, the program establishes early, structured pathways into the skilled trades and links with additional CANS training (e.g., supervisor development and Gold Seal management certification) that help participants move from apprentice to foreperson, superintendent, and project leadership roles. This industry-led pipeline supports small and medium-sized firms’ succession needs while advancing local talent into mid- and senior-level positions.
resources.address: 260 Brownlow Avenue, Unit 3, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1V9

resources.name: Farm Transition Program
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Federation of Agriculture’s Farm Transition Program helps farm families develop written, step-by-step succession plans covering management transfer, ownership structure, and leadership development. Through workshops, advisory services, and tools (and by linking to programs such as FarmNEXT for new entrants), it supports mentorship-based, apprenticeship-style learning on farms so employees can progress into herdsperson/manager roles and ultimately take on successor-operator leadership. This structured succession approach keeps agricultural businesses locally owned and creates clear, senior-level career paths in rural communities.
resources.address: 7 Atlantic Central Drive, East Mountain, NS B6L 2Z2

solutions.text: Local Hiring and Advancement Charter: Adopt a voluntary community charter where employers commit to province-wide transparent hiring and promotion practices, targets for local mid/senior hires, and published career ladders, supported by a public recognition program.

resources.name: Employer Support & Workplace Culture Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS works directly with employers across Nova Scotia to design transparent, skills-based recruitment and promotion processes and to build equitable career ladders that help employees progress into mid- and senior-level roles. The program provides training, policy templates, and one-on-one HR advising, and it publicly profiles participating employers and promising practices—creating community recognition for organizations that commit to inclusive local hiring and advancement.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program (START, Apprenticeship & Journeyperson Certification)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program partners with employers province-wide to hire and advance local talent through registered apprenticeships that outline clear, competency-based pathways from entry-level to journeyperson and supervisory roles. Employers commit to transparent on-the-job training and progression standards, while the Agency publicly recognizes exemplary employers and mentors through awards and events—reinforcing community norms for quality career development and advancement.

resources.name: Irving Shipbuilding Centre of Excellence (ISCE)
resources.description: Hosted at NSCC, the ISCE publishes structured training-to-career pathways for shipbuilding and marine trades, enabling Nova Scotians to progress from entry-level to mid- and senior-skilled roles. In partnership with Irving Shipbuilding, graduates connect to local hiring commitments and internal promotion pathways, and employer partners and cohorts are publicly highlighted—advancing transparent career ladders and community recognition for employers investing in local advancement.

resources.name: Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Strategy and Equal by 30 Commitment
resources.description: EfficiencyOne (Efficiency Nova Scotia) publishes DEI goals and transparent hiring and promotion practices with leadership representation targets, reporting progress publicly to strengthen clear advancement pathways in the provincial clean‑energy sector. By signing the Equal by 30 pledge, the organization commits to gender-balanced leadership and pay transparency and is publicly recognized among employers advancing inclusive local hiring and advancement.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

solutions.text: Community Investment Fund for Scale-ups: Form a locally governed micro-VC or cooperative investment fund to provide growth capital and advisory support for promising local businesses, enabling them to create higher-level roles and retain talent.

resources.name: Invest Nova Scotia – Venture Capital
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia makes direct equity investments in high-potential Nova Scotia companies and provides hands-on support through experienced advisors, networks, and accelerator programming. By supplying growth capital and strategic guidance to help firms scale, the fund enables the creation of mid- and senior-level roles in the province and improves career pathways that help retain local talent.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 400, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

resources.name: Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta Cohort is an investment program that awards selected startups $25,000 in convertible note funding plus access to mentors, programming, and investor networks to accelerate growth. This locally run micro-investment initiative helps promising companies scale in Nova Scotia, translating early capital and advisory support into higher-skilled jobs and clearer advancement paths for young professionals.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Build Ventures Fund
resources.description: Build Ventures is an Atlantic Canada–based venture capital firm headquartered in Halifax that invests in scaling technology companies and provides board-level guidance and connections to help them grow. Its patient growth capital and advisory support enable Nova Scotia firms to expand locally, creating more mid- to senior-level roles that attract and retain talent in the province.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: The New Dawn Community Investment Fund pools local investor capital under Nova Scotia’s CEDIF framework to finance Cape Breton enterprises, providing patient growth capital alongside governance and mentorship from community leaders. As a community-owned investment vehicle, it helps promising local businesses scale, anchoring quality jobs and leadership opportunities on the Island and reducing outmigration.

solutions.text: Rural and Small-Town Co-working & Innovation Hubs: Establish community-run coworking sites with business advisory, mentorship, and part-time executive-in-residence programs to allow local entrepreneurs and remote divisions of larger firms to scale and hire senior staff locally.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Yarmouth Hub
resources.description: IGNITE operates rural innovation hubs that provide coworking desks, meeting rooms, and program space alongside structured mentorship, workshops, and business advisory supports. Through founder mentorship and advisor office-hours (including experienced entrepreneurs from industry), the hub helps startups and remote teams of established firms validate, scale, and recruit locally for mid- to senior-level roles. Its rural location enables companies to base leadership and technical talent in Southwest Nova Scotia rather than relocating to larger centres.

resources.name: Navigate Startup House
resources.organization: Cape Breton Partnership and Cape Breton University (Navigate Program)
resources.description: Navigate provides a community coworking and incubation space in Sydney with programming that includes mentorship, business advisory, and connections to Entrepreneurs-in-Residence–style expertise through its university and industry network. The hub supports founders and innovation-driven companies to grow from Cape Breton, helping them build senior roles locally and retain talent through clear advancement pathways. It also hosts events that bring together students, experienced professionals, and companies to create hiring pipelines outside of Halifax.

resources.name: North Queens Business Hub
resources.description: The North Queens Business Hub is a rural coworking centre offering high-speed internet, dedicated desks, meeting rooms, and on-site business support from municipal economic development staff and partner advisors. It regularly hosts mentorship sessions and advisory clinics (in partnership with CBDC and other agencies) that function like part-time executive-in-residence support for local entrepreneurs. By enabling remote workers and growth-minded small firms to operate from Caledonia with access to seasoned guidance, the hub helps create and sustain higher-level roles in the community.
resources.address: 9793 Nova Scotia Trunk 8, Caledonia, NS B0T 1B0

solutions.text: Sector Consortia for Career Pathways: Convene industry-specific consortia (e.g., fisheries tech, creative industries, clean energy) to map career ladders, standardize competencies, and coordinate cross-employer rotations so employees can gain the breadth needed for senior roles.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (NSAA)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency convenes trade-specific employer and labour committees to define competency standards, assessment methods, and progression from apprentice to journeyperson and supervisory roles. It standardizes training and credentials across employers and coordinates the completion of on‑the‑job hours, enabling apprentices to move between companies to gain the breadth of experience required for advanced roles. This directly implements sector-based career pathways and cross-employer rotations in established and emerging skilled trades across the province.

resources.name: Ocean Technology Council of Nova Scotia (OTCNS)
resources.organization: Ocean Technology Council of Nova Scotia
resources.description: OTCNS is the industry consortium for Nova Scotia’s ocean technology sector, bringing together employers, post-secondary partners, and government to map job families, define in-demand competencies, and align training. Through shared employer working groups and partnerships with NSCC and universities, the council builds clear career pathways and facilitates multi-employer mentorships, projects, and work-integrated learning so early‑career talent can gain experience across different firms. This coordinated approach helps workers progress toward senior technical and leadership roles in ocean industries.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Tourism Human Resource Council (NSTHRC)
resources.organization: Tourism Industry Association of Nova Scotia (TIANS)
resources.description: NSTHRC convenes tourism and hospitality employers across Nova Scotia to develop career ladders from entry-level roles to supervisory and management positions, using standardized occupational competencies aligned with national tourism standards. It coordinates multi-employer training cohorts (e.g., service excellence, supervisory skills) and works with operators to facilitate seasonal and project-based placements so workers can build experience across properties and regions. This sector-wide approach clarifies advancement pathways and builds the cross-employer experience needed for higher‑level roles.

resources.name: CANS Education & Training (Construction Career Pathways)
resources.description: CANS convenes a consortium of general and trade contractors, unions, and training providers to articulate construction career pathways and standardize core competencies for progression into foreperson, superintendent, and project management roles. Through shared training delivered to member firms and partnership initiatives like apprenticeship mobility and youth placements, workers can earn recognized credentials and gain cross‑employer experience on diverse projects. This coordinated, sector-led model helps talent advance into mid‑ and senior‑level roles across Nova Scotia’s construction industry.

solutions.text: Return-to-Region Talent and Alumni Program: Create a community-driven program that connects Nova Scotia alumni and former residents with local employers, offering return incentives like onboarding stipends, mentorship, and guaranteed mid-level role interviews.

resources.name: Halifax Connector Program
resources.description: The Halifax Connector Program actively connects recent graduates, skilled professionals, and former Nova Scotians returning to the region with established local employers and industry leaders through curated, one-on-one informational interviews. By facilitating direct introductions and mentorship, the program helps candidates access mid-level opportunities, build networks quickly, and transition back into Nova Scotia’s workforce—aligning with the solution’s emphasis on return pathways, mentorship, and interview access.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1200, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: ISANS Professional Mentoring Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentoring Program pairs internationally trained professionals and other new or returning residents with experienced local mentors and employer contacts to accelerate integration into Nova Scotia’s labour market. The program sets up targeted informational interviews, networking, and job search support that frequently lead to mid-level roles—implementing the solution’s mentorship and employer-connection components to help people establish or re-establish careers in the province.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: NSCC Career Services
resources.description: NSCC Career Services connects Nova Scotia Community College alumni—many of whom return to communities across the province after graduating—with local employers through regional job fairs, targeted employer days, and facilitated interview opportunities. Working with industry partners and community Connector initiatives, the service provides mentorship, networking, and employer introductions that help alumni secure mid-level roles and onboard effectively in communities outside Halifax.

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: The Connector Program matches returning Nova Scotians, recent graduates, and newcomers with established industry professionals who volunteer as Connectors. Through curated, warm introductions to hiring managers and sector leaders, participants expand their networks, secure informational interviews that often lead to job interviews, and access mentorship that helps them land and advance in mid-level roles in Halifax and across the province—directly aligning with the solution’s emphasis on employer connections and mentorship for returnees.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Graduate to Opportunity (GTO)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: GTO provides wage subsidies to Nova Scotia employers that create new, permanent full-time positions for recent graduates, including Nova Scotian alumni returning from other provinces. By offsetting early salary costs, the program functions as an onboarding incentive that helps employers—especially outside Halifax—hire for meaningful roles and invest in mentorship and early career progression, building clearer pathways into mid-level positions in the province.

resources.name: Innovate to Opportunity (ITO)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: ITO supports Nova Scotia employers to hire recent master’s and PhD graduates into innovation-focused roles, offering enhanced wage subsidies tied to structured skill development. This effectively acts as an onboarding stipend while requiring employers to define mentorship and growth plans, creating strong pathways into mid-level and specialized roles that attract and retain returning alumni across the province.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Recruitment and Retention Incentives
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health actively recruits former residents and alumni by offering relocation assistance, signing bonuses, and return‑of‑service incentives for in‑demand health professions. Dedicated recruiters connect candidates directly with hiring managers and local teams across urban and rural communities, and facilitate mentorship and community integration—implementing the solution through targeted employer connections and concrete return incentives into mid- and senior-level roles.

resources.name: Cape Breton Connector Program
resources.description: Focused on communities outside Halifax, the Cape Breton Connector Program links returning Cape Bretoners, new graduates, and newcomers with local business leaders who can open doors to employers. By brokering warm introductions, facilitating informational interviews, and providing mentorship, the program helps boomerang talent access mid-level opportunities and rebuild professional networks in the region—directly supporting return-to-region career pathways.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program links job-ready professionals—including returning Nova Scotians and university/college alumni—with established local employers and mentors through structured, one-on-one informational interviews and warm referrals. By mobilizing the province’s alumni and diaspora networks, it accelerates access to mid-level opportunities and helps returnees re-enter the labour market; staff also direct employers and candidates to provincial onboarding incentives and wage subsidies to ease a return move.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Cape Breton Connector Program
resources.description: The Cape Breton Connector Program matches returning Cape Bretoners and recent alumni with local business leaders for mentorship, networking, and facilitated introductions, opening doors to hidden-job-market opportunities across the island. It supports the solution by engaging the diaspora and alumni to encourage return-to-region hires, providing guided employer connections that often lead to interviews for mid-level roles, and by helping employers leverage available onboarding incentives.
resources.address: 285 Alexandra Street, Suite 102, Sydney, NS B1S 2E8

resources.name: Western REN CONNECTOR Program
resources.description: Western REN’s CONNECTOR Program serves Southwest Nova (Yarmouth, Digby, Clare) by introducing returning residents and alumni to local employers and industry leaders through curated informational interviews and referrals. This community-driven approach helps boomerang talent land mid-level roles outside Halifax and provides mentorship and navigation to employer incentive programs that can offset onboarding costs for returnees.
resources.address: 368 Main Street, Suite 203, Yarmouth, NS B5A 1E9

resources.name: NSCC Alumni Career Services
resources.description: NSCC Alumni Career Services connects college alumni—including those returning to Nova Scotia—with employers across the province through job postings, targeted networking events, and alumni-to-student mentorship that eases re-entry into local industries. By leveraging campus career teams in communities beyond Halifax, the program creates warm pathways to interviews for mid-level roles and helps employers and alumni tap into available onboarding supports and wage incentives.

solutions.text: Local Executive Training Scholarships: Raise funds (via chambers, foundations, and employers) to provide scholarships for local workers to attend short executive education and management programs, with commitments from participating employers to create advancement opportunities afterward.

resources.name: Canada–Nova Scotia Job Grant (CNSJG)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: CNSJG provides cost-shared tuition support for employer‑nominated employees to take short, third‑party training, including university executive education and management programs. Employers co-fund the training and, as part of the application, outline how the learning leads to a new or better job for the participant—effectively committing to advancement opportunities after completion.

resources.name: NSCC Customized & Corporate Training
resources.description: NSCC designs short, stackable leadership and management programs for employers across Nova Scotia, and helps companies leverage funding like the Canada–Nova Scotia Job Grant so employees can attend at low or no cost. Employers sponsor participants and commonly align completion with role expansion or promotion pathways, turning these subsidized seats into practical advancement opportunities—especially for teams outside Halifax.

resources.name: Rowe School of Business Executive Education
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Executive Education offers short, applied management and leadership programs and certificates that are eligible for employer co-funding and provincial training grants, effectively creating scholarship-like tuition relief for local workers. The unit actively works with employers across Nova Scotia to sponsor employees and align learning to internal succession plans, supporting concrete post-program advancement commitments.

resources.name: Sobey School of Business Executive and Professional Development (EPD)
resources.description: SMU’s EPD delivers short leadership, supervision, and management programs that employers in Nova Scotia routinely co-fund, often using the Canada–Nova Scotia Job Grant to subsidize tuition for workers. Cohorts are built with employer sponsorship and sector partnerships, and organizations typically link completion to expanded responsibilities or promotion tracks, operationalizing advancement commitments after training.

solutions.text: Job Rotation and Secondment Network: Coordinate a community-wide exchange program allowing mid-career employees to take temporary senior-role secondments across nonprofits, municipalities, and businesses to build leadership experience without relocating.

resources.name: Sponsored Employee (Loaned Representative) Program
resources.description: United Way Halifax partners with local employers to second mid-career employees for a full-time, time-limited placement (typically 12–16 weeks) to support campaign, corporate engagement, and community initiatives. These cross-sector secondments give participants real leadership responsibilities—managing stakeholder relationships, leading outreach projects, and delivering results—thereby building senior-level skills without requiring relocation and directly aligning with a community-wide exchange model.

resources.name: Interchange Canada Program
resources.description: Interchange Canada is a federal program that facilitates temporary assignments between the Government of Canada and other sectors, including provincial/municipal governments, nonprofits, academia, and businesses. In Nova Scotia, organizations use Interchange agreements to place mid-career professionals into time-bound senior advisory, project leadership, or policy roles (often 6–24 months), enabling cross-sector leadership development and career advancement without leaving the province.

resources.name: Public Service Commission Secondment and Exchange Program
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Public Service Commission supports formal secondments and acting assignments across provincial departments and with external partners such as municipalities, health authorities, universities, and community organizations. By brokering time-limited placements that give mid-career employees the chance to take on higher-responsibility roles, the program builds leadership capacity across sectors within Nova Scotia and advances career pathways without requiring relocation.

solutions.text: Transparent Local Career Maps and Promotion Clinics: Publish clear career maps for key local employers and industries and run regular community 'promotion clinics' where HR and managers give practical coaching on promotion criteria, resume building, and interview preparation for advancement.

resources.name: Employment and Bridging Programs (Practice Interviews & Industry Pathways)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS publishes clear, occupation-specific pathway information for regulated and in-demand professions in Nova Scotia (e.g., licensure steps and typical role progressions), helping newcomers and young workers understand how to advance. They also run recurring practice interview sessions, resume clinics, and employer/HR panels where hiring managers provide transparent coaching on promotion criteria, interview preparation, and advancement expectations with local employers.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: RBC Future Launch at Halifax Public Libraries (Career Clinics & Pathways Panels)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts free resume and interview clinics and sector-focused employer panels through RBC Future Launch, where HR professionals and managers offer practical coaching on how to progress to mid- and senior-level roles in Nova Scotia. The library also curates and shares local career pathway resources and role profiles online and in-branch, making advancement routes and required skills transparent for key local industries.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: COVE Ocean Talent Initiatives (Career Pathways & Employer Clinics)
resources.description: COVE develops and shares ocean-sector career pathway materials that outline role progressions and credentials across Nova Scotia’s blue economy. Through events like Ocean Connector, career fairs, and employer-led workshops, HR leaders and hiring managers provide hands-on coaching in resume building, interview preparation, and promotion criteria for advancement within local ocean-tech companies.

resources.name: NSCC Career Services (Career Mapping & Employer Promotion Clinics)
resources.description: NSCC Career Services publishes program-to-career maps and sector pathways that clarify typical advancement from entry-level to supervisory and management roles in Nova Scotia industries. They also host regular employer panels, mock interviews, and resume review clinics where HR professionals coach students and recent graduates on advancement requirements and how to competitively apply for promotions with local employers.

obstacles.title: Wage Competitiveness Gap
obstacles.description: Compensation and benefits often lag major Canadian markets, making it harder to retain or lure back skilled youth.

solutions.text: Community Living-Wage Campaign: A local coalition (nonprofits, businesses, unions, municipal reps) promotes adoption of a living-wage standard for community employers, creates a public registry of employers who commit, and helps small businesses phase in increases through recognition and shared resources.

resources.name: Supplier Living Wage (HRM)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality requires vendors delivering certain service contracts to pay, at minimum, a regionally calculated living wage. This policy operationalizes a local living-wage standard, signals recognition to compliant suppliers, and provides guidance and resources to help especially small and mid-sized vendors understand, plan for, and phase in wage increases. By leveraging municipal procurement, HRM drives broader adoption of living wages across the community and helps close local wage competitiveness gaps.

resources.name: Living Wage Employer Certification (Atlantic Canada)
resources.organization: Saint John Human Development Council (Living Wage Atlantic Canada)
resources.description: This regional program certifies employers in Nova Scotia who commit to paying a locally calculated living wage and publishes a public registry of certified employers. It offers recognition, communication materials, and implementation supports that help small and medium-sized businesses plan and phase in wage increases. Operating across Atlantic Canada, the program partners with Nova Scotia organizations and municipalities to promote adoption of a consistent living-wage standard.
resources.address: 139 Prince Edward Street, Saint John, NB E2L 3S3

resources.name: Town of Antigonish – Certified Living Wage Employer
resources.description: The Town of Antigonish is a certified Living Wage Employer, publicly committing to meet or exceed the Nova Scotia living-wage benchmark for municipal staff and eligible roles. By being listed on the regional registry and promoting the standard locally, the Town models adoption for other employers and uses its communications channels to recognize and encourage small businesses that are working toward certification. This municipal leadership helps normalize living-wage practices and strengthens local talent attraction and retention.

resources.name: Ecology Action Centre – Certified Living Wage Employer
resources.description: Ecology Action Centre (EAC) is a Halifax-based nonprofit that has adopted a certified living-wage policy, ensuring all staff receive at least the locally calculated living wage. EAC’s public commitment and inclusion in the living-wage employer registry help build momentum among community organizations and mission-driven small enterprises, while its outreach shares resources about implementing and sustaining living-wage practices. By recognizing and modeling this standard, EAC contributes to a community-wide shift toward more competitive, equitable compensation.

solutions.text: Local Wage Top-Up Fund: A community-managed micro-grant or matching fund that provides temporary top-ups or hiring subsidies to small employers who hire recent local graduates or apprentices, funded by local foundations, alumni donations, and municipal seed money.

resources.name: Graduate to Opportunity (GTO)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: Graduate to Opportunity provides a time-limited wage subsidy to Nova Scotia employers that hire recent post-secondary graduates into full-time roles. By covering a portion of the salary for the first years of employment (with higher support for small and medium-sized employers and equity-deserving hires), GTO functions as a wage top-up that helps close the compensation gap and encourages local hiring and retention of young talent.

resources.name: Innovate to Opportunity (ITO)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: Innovate to Opportunity offers multi-year wage subsidies to employers that create advanced, innovation-focused roles for recent master’s and PhD graduates. The program acts as a wage top-up to help smaller firms compete for highly qualified talent, supporting higher starting salaries and enabling graduates to build careers in Nova Scotia’s knowledge-intensive sectors.

resources.name: Co-operative Education Incentive (CEI)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: The Co-operative Education Incentive provides a wage subsidy to employers who hire eligible co-op students from Nova Scotia post-secondary institutions for work terms. By offsetting a significant portion of student wages, CEI functions as a short-term wage top-up that lowers hiring costs for small employers, builds local experience pipelines, and improves the likelihood that students transition into full-time roles in Nova Scotia after graduation.

resources.name: START Program (Employment Incentives for Employers)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: The START Program provides financial incentives and wage subsidies to Nova Scotia employers that hire unemployed Nova Scotians, including apprentices and newly trained workers. These temporary wage top-ups reduce the initial payroll burden for smaller businesses, helping them offer competitive compensation, create sustainable positions, and retain young people in the province.

solutions.text: Affordable Housing Partnerships: Collaborations between municipalities, non-profit housing organizations, and community land trusts to increase affordable rental and starter-home options for young workers, including rent-to-own pilots and prioritized units for early-career local hires.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia builds and sells energy-efficient homes to low- and moderate-income households using affordable, no- or low-interest mortgages, creating attainable starter-home options for early-career workers. The program operates through partnerships with municipalities (for land/permits), community donors, and employers, reducing development costs so monthly housing payments fit entry-level wages and help young families build equity.

resources.name: Wije’winen Housing Project
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre is developing the Wije’winen project, a mixed-use Indigenous community hub that includes affordable rental homes designed to be accessible to young Indigenous workers and families. The initiative is a partnership with municipal, provincial, and federal funders (including HRM and CMHC) and local non-profits, leveraging public land and community-led design to deliver below-market units integrated with wraparound services that reduce housing cost pressures for early-career residents.

resources.name: The Sunflower (Affordable Housing in Lakeside)
resources.description: Adsum’s Sunflower development provides 25 new affordable and supportive apartments created through a partnership among Adsum for Women & Children, the Halifax Regional Municipality, the Province of Nova Scotia, and CMHC’s Rapid Housing Initiative. The project increases the supply of deeply affordable rentals suitable for women and gender-diverse people—including many in early-career, lower-wage roles—by combining municipal land-use support, public capital, and non-profit stewardship to keep rents below market.

resources.name: Affordable & Supportive Housing Programs (including SHYM)
resources.description: YWCA Halifax operates affordable and supportive housing (such as Supportive Housing for Young Mothers, SHYM) that offers below-market rents and stability for women, gender-diverse people, and young families starting careers. Working with municipal and provincial partners for capital and rent supports, the YWCA’s non-profit model preserves long-term affordability and aligns unit sizes and rents with the realities of entry-level incomes.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: Phoenix Youth Housing
resources.description: Phoenix provides affordable and supportive apartments for youth aged 16–24 through partnerships with the Province of Nova Scotia, Halifax Regional Municipality, and community funders, helping young people transition into work or education. By keeping rents geared to income and coupling housing with employment readiness supports, the program directly addresses cost barriers faced by early-career workers and improves retention of young talent in the region.

solutions.text: Shared Benefits Pool: A cooperative benefits program where small employers band together to offer group dental, vision, or RRSP matching at lower cost, making total compensation more competitive without large payroll increases.

resources.name: Chambers of Commerce Group Insurance Plan (via Halifax Chamber Membership)
resources.description: The Chambers Plan is a national, not‑for‑profit pooled employee benefits program available locally through the Halifax Chamber of Commerce, allowing small employers to join a shared risk pool. By banding together, member companies access lower-cost health, dental, vision, life, disability, and optional group retirement solutions, improving total compensation without large payroll jumps. This cooperative model directly addresses wage competitiveness by making comprehensive benefits attainable for small firms.

resources.name: CANS Employee Benefits Program (Group Health & Dental)
resources.description: CANS offers member companies access to pooled group benefits—health, dental, vision, life and disability—delivered through association buying power across Nova Scotia’s construction sector. By aggregating many small and mid-sized employers into one benefits pool, CANS reduces premiums and stabilizes rates, with options to layer in retirement benefits like group RRSPs. This shared-benefits approach helps construction employers compete for talent without matching big-market wages.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Group Benefits Solutions for Health & Community Organizations
resources.description: Health Association Nova Scotia administers multi-employer group benefits for health and community organizations province-wide, including extended health, dental, vision, life and disability. Employers participate in a large shared-benefits pool that delivers economies of scale and more stable rates, with options to integrate group retirement plans. This cooperative structure enables smaller organizations to offer competitive total compensation to attract and retain staff.

solutions.text: Remote-Work Hubs & Broadband Support: Create or expand co-working spaces with reliable high-speed internet and office amenities so youth can access higher-paying remote jobs based elsewhere while contributing to the local economy and community life.

resources.name: Volta Co-Working & Innovation Hub
resources.description: Volta operates one of Atlantic Canada’s largest co-working hubs, offering hot desks, dedicated offices, meeting rooms, and enterprise-grade high-speed internet. By giving young professionals reliable workspace and connectivity in downtown Halifax, Volta enables them to secure and perform higher-paying remote roles with employers across Canada and beyond while remaining rooted in Nova Scotia’s community and economy.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: CO3 Coworking Space (South Shore)
resources.description: CO3 provides a professional co-working environment with fast, reliable Wi‑Fi, meeting rooms, private offices, and shared amenities in Bridgewater. The space supports remote workers, freelancers, and entrepreneurs so they can take on national and international contracts from the South Shore, directly addressing the wage gap by connecting local talent to higher-paying remote opportunities.

resources.name: Acadia LaunchBox (Nova Scotia Sandbox)
resources.description: Acadia LaunchBox offers co-working desks, high-speed internet, meeting space, and programming for students, recent grads, and early-stage founders in the Annapolis Valley. These amenities enable youth to build remote-ready ventures, freelance careers, and distributed work arrangements from Wolfville, allowing them to access higher-paying markets while remaining in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative (INSI)
resources.description: INSI is a province-wide broadband expansion program delivering high-speed internet to rural and underserved communities, led by Build Nova Scotia. By extending reliable connectivity to where youth live, the initiative makes full-time remote employment, hybrid work, and participation in co-working hubs feasible outside major centres—reducing the wage competitiveness gap by opening access to higher-paying remote jobs.
resources.address: 1751 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S5

solutions.text: Youth Entrepreneurship Accelerator: Local incubator providing low-cost workspace, mentorship, microgrants, and procurement connections so young entrepreneurs can scale businesses that pay sustainable wages and create local jobs.

resources.name: Volta
resources.description: Volta is Atlantic Canada’s largest startup hub, offering subsidized co-working and office space, structured mentorship, and founder support to help entrepreneurs scale companies and create local jobs. Through programs like Volta Residency and investor-readiness coaching, plus the Volta Cohort funding competition and regular founder–buyer meetups, it connects youth-led ventures to capital and procurement pathways with corporate and public-sector partners.
resources.address: Suite 100, 1505 Barrington Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE is an ocean-technology incubator providing affordable workspace, prototyping labs, and hands-on mentorship to early-stage founders, including youth and recent graduates. Its accelerator programming and industry network connect companies to pilot opportunities and supply chains with major ocean-sector buyers (ports, defense, and marine companies), helping ventures secure procurement and scale good-paying jobs in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: CEED (Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development)
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED supports aspiring and early-stage entrepreneurs with low-cost co-working, training, coaching, and access to mentors to accelerate business growth. It helps youth founders build sustainable ventures through practical programming, connections to micro-financing and grant opportunities, and introductions to local business networks and buyers that can lead to procurement and job creation in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: Suite 225, 7071 Bayers Road, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs is a Dalhousie University sandbox and incubator that gives student and youth founders free co-working space, mentorship from industry and faculty, and experiential programs to build and launch startups. It offers small project funding and frequent industry challenges that connect teams to potential customers and pilot/procurement partners in the local tech ecosystem, supporting ventures that can grow sustainable, well-paying jobs.

solutions.text: Apprenticeship and Wage Ladder Programs: Partnerships between tradespeople, community colleges, and employers to create clear paid apprenticeship pathways with staged wage increases, travel/childcare support, and public recognition for participating employers.

resources.name: Apprenticeship START Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration)
resources.description: The Apprenticeship START Program provides staged incentive payments to employers when they hire, retain, and advance registered apprentices at key milestones, helping create stable, paid apprenticeship positions with clear wage progression tied to apprenticeship levels. By offsetting wage costs and rewarding completion, it narrows the wage competitiveness gap and encourages employers to offer competitive, structured wage ladders. The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency also publicly recognizes outstanding employers and mentors through its annual Apprenticeship Awards of Excellence, raising the profile of participating firms.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY places Grade 10–12 students in paid summer jobs with construction employers, providing safety training, mentorship, and a direct bridge into registered apprenticeship pathways in the skilled trades. The program partners with industry, NSCC, and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency so participants can transition into apprenticeships that feature structured wage steps as they progress. Participating employers are profiled by the Construction Association of Nova Scotia, offering public recognition for firms investing in youth and apprenticeship development.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0A9

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Irving Shipbuilding Inc. (in partnership with NSCC and community partners)
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based training-to-employment and apprenticeship initiative that partners NSCC, Irving Shipbuilding, unions, and community organizations to recruit and prepare underrepresented Nova Scotians for well-paid marine trades careers. Graduates enter paid positions at the Halifax Shipyard with unionized, staged wage increases aligned to apprenticeship levels, while receiving wraparound supports (e.g., tutoring and assistance coordinated through community partners for transportation/childcare needs) during training. Irving publicly recognizes Pathways cohorts and employer partners, highlighting firms that commit to apprenticeship and inclusive hiring.

resources.name: UA Local 56 Joint Apprenticeship and Training Program
resources.description: UA Local 56 oversees registered apprenticeships for plumbers, pipefitters, welders, and related trades with a negotiated wage ladder that increases at each apprenticeship level and hours milestone. The union partners with NSCC and signatory contractors to provide paid on-the-job training, and collective agreements commonly include travel/subsistence provisions when work sites are away from home, helping reduce geographic barriers. Signatory employers are publicly listed and recognized by the union, demonstrating their commitment to apprenticeship and skilled workforce development.
resources.address: 24 Lakeside Park Drive, Lakeside, NS B3T 1L7

resources.name: Apprenticeship Technical Training (Block Release)
resources.description: NSCC delivers in-class technical training for registered apprentices across multiple trades on a block-release schedule coordinated with employers and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency. Successful completion of each training block formally advances an apprentice’s level, triggering corresponding wage increases on the job and reinforcing a transparent wage ladder. NSCC also connects apprentices to student services and bursaries and promotes industry partners that host apprentices, supporting retention and public recognition of participating employers.

resources.name: Apprenticeship Technical Training (NSCC)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College delivers the in-class technical training for many Red Seal and provincial trades in partnership with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and employers across the province. Apprentices alternate between paid on‑the‑job learning with their sponsor employer and NSCC block training; as they complete each level and required hours, standard apprenticeship wage ladders trigger staged pay increases. NSCC also offers student awards and bursaries that can help with travel and childcare during training periods, and publicly recognizes employer partners and apprentices through events and awards in collaboration with the apprenticeship system.

resources.name: Shipyard Trades Apprenticeship Program
resources.description: Irving Shipbuilding hires paid apprentices in trades such as welding, metal fabrication, pipefitting, and industrial/electrical at the Halifax Shipyard, aligning on‑the‑job training with NSCC and union partners for technical instruction. Apprentices progress through defined levels tied to Nova Scotia’s apprenticeship standards and collective agreements, receiving wage increases at each stage; the company provides supports like tools/PPE and covers travel or accommodations when apprentices attend off‑site training. Irving Shipbuilding also publicly celebrates apprentice milestones and participates in provincial apprenticeship recognition initiatives, raising the profile of participating employers and mentors.

resources.name: Powerline Technician Apprenticeship Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Power employs apprentices who earn while they learn under journeyperson supervision to become Powerline Technicians and related trade roles. The program uses a structured wage ladder that increases with each apprenticeship level and required hours completed, and partners with NSCC and industry training providers for technical courses; apprentices can access travel and living supports for training blocks and benefits that help with family and childcare planning. NS Power publicly recognizes apprentice achievements and training partners through corporate communications and industry events, highlighting employers and depots that invest in apprentices.
resources.address: 1223 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8
