resources.name: Carpenter Apprenticeship Program (Local 83/ACRC)
resources.organization: Atlantic Canada Regional Council of Carpenters, Millwrights and Allied Workers – Local 83
resources.description: Through the Carpenters Local 83 program under the Atlantic Canada Regional Council, apprentices are employed by signatory contractors and advance via a standardized wage progression (percentage of journeyperson rate) as they complete Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency levels and hours. The union training trust partners with NSCC for in‑class instruction and offers additional supports such as travel allowances for training, safety gear, and access to hardship funds that can offset childcare and transportation needs. The Council publicly recognizes signatory employers and outstanding apprentices through awards and communications, promoting firms that build robust apprenticeship pathways.
resources.address: 1000 Lucasville Road, Hammonds Plains, NS B4B 1P7

resources.name: Apprenticeship START Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration)
resources.description: Operated by the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, START incentivizes employers to hire and retain registered apprentices with milestone-based funding as apprentices progress through each level, reinforcing a clear wage ladder tied to the journeyperson rate. The program links apprentices, employers, and NSCC for block-release training, and offers supports such as travel and accommodation assistance (and access to childcare supports while in technical training) so apprentices can complete in-school components without undue financial burden. NSAA also publicly recognizes exemplary employers and mentors through its Apprenticeship Awards of Excellence, promoting employer participation and visibility.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.description: This Irving Shipbuilding initiative partners with Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) and community organizations (e.g., Women Unlimited, Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre) to create cohort-based, paid pathways into Red Seal trades at the Halifax Shipyard. Participants move from NSCC training into registered apprenticeships with unionized, staged wage increases as they complete hours and technical training, and receive wraparound supports that have included tuition assistance, mentoring, and help with transportation/childcare to improve retention. Irving publicly profiles partner employers and cohorts, celebrating milestones and completions to elevate employer engagement and recognition.

resources.name: NSCC Apprenticeship Technical Training (Akerley Campus)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Akerley Campus
resources.description: NSCC delivers in-school technical training for registered apprentices across multiple Red Seal trades in partnership with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and employers, embedding a transparent progression from Level 1 onward that aligns with staged wage increases on the job. Apprentices attend block-release training at Akerley and return to paid work with employers who apply wage ladders tied to trade levels; NSCC and NSAA make available travel/accommodation supports and bursaries that can help offset transportation or childcare costs during training. The college also participates in employer and apprentice recognition events with NSAA, highlighting employers that actively support apprenticeships.

solutions.text: Community Procurement & Buy-Local Campaign: Encourage municipalities, schools, and hospitals to prioritize local suppliers and youth-owned businesses through procurement policies and a visible campaign that shifts more revenue to local firms who can then pay better.

resources.name: HRM Social & Sustainable Procurement
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s procurement framework incorporates social value and sustainable procurement criteria that encourage participation from small, diverse, and locally based suppliers. The municipality hosts supplier information sessions and outreach that help Nova Scotia vendors—including youth-owned firms—understand upcoming opportunities and how to bid, thereby improving access to public contracts. By intentionally engaging local suppliers in municipal purchasing, HRM channels more public spending to Nova Scotia businesses so they can scale and offer more competitive wages.

resources.name: Farm to School Nova Scotia
resources.description: Farm to School Nova Scotia helps K–12 schools source and serve locally produced food, offering toolkits, grants, and connections to nearby farmers, fishers, and food businesses. The program supports initiatives like school salad bars and local food procurement pilots that direct institutional dollars into Nova Scotia’s agri-food sector, including emerging youth-led enterprises. This shifts steady, recurring revenue to local suppliers, strengthening their ability to create quality jobs and pay better wages.
resources.address: 33 Ochterloney Street, Suite 210, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 4P5

resources.name: Sustainable and Socially Responsible Procurement
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s procurement program advances sustainable and socially responsible purchasing, engaging small and local suppliers to participate in campus procurement where feasible under trade agreements. The university provides vendor guidance and pathways for local businesses—including startups and youth-owned firms—to register and compete for contracts in goods, services, and facilities. This institutional demand steers spending toward Nova Scotia companies, supporting growth and higher-quality employment for young people.

resources.name: Downtown Halifax Buy-Local Campaigns (e.g., Big Day Downtown)
resources.description: The Downtown Halifax Business Commission runs ongoing buy-local campaigns, events, and gift card programs that encourage residents, students, and employers to spend with locally owned businesses downtown. By driving consumer and organizational purchases to Nova Scotia firms—including youth-owned shops and service providers—the campaigns increase local revenue and business stability. This heightened demand helps local employers improve compensation and retain young talent in the region.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

solutions.text: Co-operative Business Development: Support worker-owned co-ops and social enterprises through legal clinics, training, and low-interest loans so workers share profits and decision-making, increasing effective compensation and retention.

resources.name: International Centre for Co-operative Management (Co-operative Management Education)
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University — Sobey School of Business, International Centre for Co-operative Management
resources.description: Based at Saint Mary’s University, this centre delivers specialized executive education, certificates, and graduate programs for leaders of co-operatives and social enterprises. By training managers and boards in governance, member engagement, and shared decision-making, it strengthens worker-owned co-ops’ capacity to distribute profits fairly and retain talent in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Credit Union Small Business Loan Guarantee Program (via East Coast Credit Union)
resources.description: East Coast Credit Union participates in Nova Scotia’s Credit Union Small Business Loan Guarantee Program, offering financing to co-operatives and social enterprises with the support of a provincial guarantee. This reduces borrowing costs and risk, enabling worker-owned co-ops to access affordable capital for start-up, expansion, or worker buyouts—supporting profit-sharing models that improve effective compensation and retention.

resources.name: CEED Microloans and Social Enterprise Support
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides training, coaching, and accessible microloans to new and growing enterprises, including co-operatives and social enterprises. By pairing hands-on business development training with affordable financing, CEED helps worker-owned ventures build sustainable revenue, share profits among members, and strengthen long-term retention.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Initio Technology & Innovation Law Clinic
resources.organization: Dalhousie University — Schulich School of Law
resources.description: Operated by Dalhousie’s Schulich School of Law, Initio provides free or low-cost legal services to startups and impact-focused organizations, including co-operatives and social enterprises. The clinic assists with incorporation, bylaws, governance, contracts, and IP, lowering legal barriers so worker-owned co-ops can formalize shared decision-making and direct more resources to member compensation and growth.

resources.name: Community Economic Development Investment Funds (CEDIF) Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Finance and Treasury Board
resources.description: Nova Scotia’s CEDIF program enables communities to raise patient, locally controlled capital to invest in co-operatives and social enterprises. By mobilizing community investors and offering an efficient pathway to equity financing, CEDIFs help fund worker co-op start-ups, expansions, and conversions—supporting shared ownership, profit distribution, and stronger compensation structures.

solutions.text: Transportation and Childcare Supports: Community-run transit solutions, ride-share cooperatives, and subsidized childcare pods reduce out-of-pocket costs for young workers, effectively raising disposable income and making local jobs more attractive.

resources.name: Low Income Transit Pass Program
resources.description: Halifax Transit offers a 50% discounted monthly transit pass to eligible low-income residents through the HRM Affordable Access Program. By cutting commuting costs for young workers and jobseekers, the program directly increases disposable income and makes local employment more viable and attractive.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC) and Transportation Supports
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides free, on-site childminding for parents attending language, employment, and entrepreneurship programs, and can offer transit support (e.g., bus tickets) for eligible participants. These services reduce out-of-pocket childcare and transportation costs for young newcomers, improving their ability to train, work, and stay in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Chebucto Family Centre Childcare & Parent Support
resources.organization: Home of the Guardian Angel (Chebucto Family Centre)
resources.description: The Chebucto Family Centre provides free on-site childcare while parents participate in employment readiness, skills workshops, and support programs. By functioning as a community-based, no-cost childcare option during program hours, it lowers childcare expenses for young families, helping them pursue work and training without added financial burden.

solutions.text: Local Skill-Stacking & Microcredential Programs: Partner with colleges and employers to offer short, employer-recognized credentials that raise starting wages (e.g., coding bootcamps, hospitality management), funded by employer sponsorships or community bursaries.

resources.name: NSCC Microcredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College offers short, stackable microcredentials across sectors such as IT, construction, health, and tourism that are co-designed and validated with employer partners. Learners earn digital badges and for-credit modules that can be stacked toward larger credentials, directly signaling in-demand skills to local employers and improving wage prospects. Many offerings are delivered through employer-sponsored cohorts or supported by donor- and community-funded NSCC Foundation bursaries, reducing cost barriers for early-career workers.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Microcredentials (Open Learning & Career Development)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University — Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Open Learning & Career Development unit delivers short, competency-based microcredentials and digital badges in areas such as data analytics, project management, cybersecurity, UX, and leadership, developed with input from industry advisory groups and employer partners. Credentials are employer-recognized, verifiable, and designed to stack with further professional learning, helping participants demonstrate job-ready skills that can command higher starting wages. Organizations frequently sponsor staff cohorts, and some learners access bursaries or government-funded seats to offset fees.

resources.name: Open Acadia Micro-credentials
resources.description: Open Acadia offers short, targeted micro-credentials and digital badges in fields such as business skills, data literacy, education, and community development, developed in collaboration with regional employers and sector partners. These stackable, flexible offerings give learners employer-recognized proof of competence that can be layered to advance careers and improve earning potential. Programs are often run with employer sponsorships or supported through university-administered bursaries and external funding, lowering financial barriers for participants.

solutions.text: Regional Alumni/Network Return Incentives: Leverage university and college alumni networks to create mentorship, relocation stipends, and job-matching services that reduce moving costs and bridge early-career wage gaps for returnees.

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program links recent graduates, returning Nova Scotians, and newcomers with established professionals (Connectors) for informational interviews and warm introductions that lead to jobs. It partners closely with local universities and alumni offices to tap alumni networks for mentorship and job-matching, helping returnees quickly rebuild networks and access hidden job markets. Program staff and employer partners also leverage provincial wage-support programs (e.g., Graduate to Opportunity/Innovate to Opportunity) to help bridge early-career wage gaps for young returnees.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 701, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Dal Alumni Link (Mentorship Program)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Office of Advancement (Alumni & Friends)
resources.description: Dal Alumni Link is a structured mentorship platform that connects Dalhousie students and recent graduates with alumni across sectors for guidance, introductions, and career navigation. By leveraging Dal’s global alumni network, the program supports graduates who want to return to Nova Scotia with local mentors, employer connections, and insight into roles posted through Dal’s career services. Staff regularly point returnees and employers to wage-support and early-career programs in Nova Scotia to make offers more competitive, complementing the mentorship and job-matching with practical return incentives.

resources.name: NSCC Alumni Connect and Graduate Employment Services
resources.description: NSCC leverages its province-wide alumni network to connect students and graduates with alumni mentors and industry contacts across communities, including those returning to Nova Scotia. Through Graduate Employment Services and the alumni network, returnees receive job-matching support, introductions to local employers in trades and emerging sectors, and practical guidance to reduce relocation friction. Advisors also help employers and grads use provincial wage-incentive programs (e.g., Graduate to Opportunity, START) to narrow early-career wage gaps and make coming back more affordable.

resources.name: Physician Recruitment Incentives and Alumni Outreach
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health actively engages Dalhousie University Faculty of Medicine alumni networks to recruit physicians back to communities across the province, pairing alumni outreach with dedicated job-matching to sites and mentors. The program offers relocation allowances and signing incentives/return‑of‑service options that directly offset moving costs and help bridge early‑career pay gaps, creating a clear return pathway for medical alumni. Recruiters coordinate introductions to local clinical leaders and provide settlement support to ensure a smooth transition for returnees.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

solutions.text: Community Recognition & Branding for Good Employers: A local 'Best for Youth' accreditation and marketing package that highlights employers offering above-average wages, career pathways, or strong benefits — helping them recruit talent and build customer goodwill.

resources.name: Tourism Employer of Choice (EOC) – Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Tourism Industry Association of Nova Scotia (TIANS)
resources.description: Supported in Nova Scotia by TIANS, the Tourism Employer of Choice program recognizes tourism and hospitality employers that meet rigorous standards in compensation, benefits, training, and career advancement. Certified employers receive a recognized designation and promotional support, enabling them to market themselves as top employers to youth and other jobseekers, improving recruitment and public goodwill.

resources.name: Lieutenant Governor’s Awards for Excellence in Nova Scotia Apprenticeship
resources.description: Administered by the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, these annual awards publicly recognize outstanding apprentices and the employers who provide exemplary on‑the‑job training, mentorship, and clear pathways to certification and advancement. The recognition elevates employers’ brands as career-building workplaces with strong practices and benefits, helping them attract and retain skilled young people.

resources.name: ISANS Immigrant Employment Awards
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS annually celebrates Nova Scotia employers that lead in recruiting, retaining, and advancing immigrant talent through equitable hiring, fair wages and benefits, and structured career pathways. Award recipients are profiled through ISANS and community channels, receiving recognition they can leverage in recruitment marketing to position themselves as inclusive, youth- and newcomer-friendly employers.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Time Banks and Community Currency: Local time-banking or complementary-currency systems allow young people to exchange services (childcare, tutoring, trades help) to reduce living costs and supplement monetary income while strengthening social ties.

resources.name: Bike Again! (Earn-a-Bike and Volunteer Shop Credits)
resources.description: Bike Again! is a community bicycle workshop where participants trade volunteer hours repairing bikes and mentoring new mechanics for access to tools, parts, training, and refurbished bicycles through an Earn-a-Bike model. The hours function like a complementary currency, letting young people exchange time and skills for transportation assets that reduce living costs while building peer-to-peer repair and tutoring networks.

resources.name: Volunteer Program and Community Market Credits
resources.description: The North Grove engages residents as volunteers in its kitchen, gardens, and community programs and provides credits/vouchers that can be used at its community market and food programs. These time-based credits operate as a local complementary currency, enabling young people to exchange hours of service for healthy food and supports, lowering cash expenses and strengthening neighborhood ties.

resources.name: CSA Workshare Program
resources.description: TapRoot Farms offers workshare positions where participants contribute set weekly hours on the farm in exchange for CSA shares or farm credits. This time-for-food exchange functions as a complementary-currency system that helps young people offset grocery costs, gain agricultural skills, and form supportive relationships within the local food community.
resources.address: 1736 Church Street, Port Williams, NS B0P 1T0

resources.name: Work-Trade and Skill-Exchange Program
resources.description: The Deanery Project hosts work-trade and skill-exchange placements where participants contribute hours in areas such as carpentry, energy systems, trail building, and program facilitation in return for training access, event participation, accommodations, or shop access. These structured time-based exchanges act as a complementary currency, allowing young people to substitute time and skills for cash costs while strengthening community connections on the Eastern Shore.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

solutions.text: Micro-Loan & Emergency Savings Programs: Community credit unions and foundations offer small low-interest loans, matched-savings, or emergency funds for young workers to handle relocation costs, training, or shortfalls, improving financial stability and retention.

resources.name: Small Business Loan Program
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides accessible micro- and small-business loans with coaching to help entrepreneurs cover start-up and training costs, purchase tools/equipment, and bridge short-term cash flow gaps. These low-interest loans directly support young workers and new founders who need modest financing to relocate for opportunities, gain certifications, or weather shortfalls, helping them build sustainable careers in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Black Business Loan Program – Microloan
resources.description: BBI offers microloans to Black entrepreneurs in Nova Scotia to finance early-stage business needs, training, certification, equipment, and working capital, paired with advisory support. By providing small, low-interest capital and mentorship, the program helps young Black professionals and founders manage relocation or start-up costs and remain employed locally, strengthening retention and economic inclusion.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 309, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Student Urgent Aid
resources.description: NSCC’s Student Urgent Aid provides fast, short-term emergency financial assistance to learners facing crises such as housing, food, transportation, certification fees, or program supplies. By stabilizing students during training and apprenticeship pathways, the fund helps young people persist to graduation and transition into Nova Scotia’s workforce, reducing attrition caused by financial shortfalls.

resources.name: HEAT Fund (Home Energy Assistance Top-up)
resources.organization: The Salvation Army Maritime Division (in partnership with Nova Scotia Power Inc.)
resources.description: The HEAT Fund provides one-time emergency financial assistance for home heating costs to eligible Nova Scotians, delivered by The Salvation Army in partnership with Nova Scotia Power. By covering urgent utility shortfalls, the fund prevents service disconnections and housing instability for working households, helping young workers remain housed and employed while managing seasonal or wage-related gaps.

obstacles.title: Housing Affordability and Supply Constraints
obstacles.description: Low vacancy rates, rising rents, and construction bottlenecks make settling and starting families difficult.

solutions.text: Community Land Trust (CLT): Form a locally governed CLT to acquire and hold land for permanently affordable housing, leasing homes to residents while keeping land ownership in community hands to prevent speculation.

resources.name: New Dawn Affordable Housing
resources.description: New Dawn acquires and holds land and buildings in community, non-profit ownership in Sydney and operates long-term, below-market rental housing. By keeping the land and assets in community hands and leasing homes to residents, New Dawn removes properties from speculation and safeguards permanent affordability—key elements of the community land trust approach.

resources.name: Antigonish Affordable Housing Society
resources.description: AAHS develops, owns, and stewards non-market rental housing on land it holds in perpetuity, including its Appleseed Court development. The Society retains land ownership while leasing homes to tenants at below-market rents, ensuring the property remains community-owned and protected from speculation—functionally implementing a community land trust model for permanent affordability.

resources.name: Adsum Housing
resources.description: Adsum acquires and holds property to create permanently affordable and supportive housing for women, gender-diverse people, and families. By keeping land in mission-locked community ownership and leasing homes to residents at non-market rates, Adsum prevents speculation and preserves affordability over the long term in line with community land trust principles.

resources.name: YWCA Halifax Housing
resources.description: YWCA Halifax owns and stewards affordable and supportive housing for women and gender-diverse people, retaining land and buildings under non-profit, community control. By leasing homes to residents at below-market rents and keeping assets mission-locked, the organization advances a community land stewardship model that curbs speculation and preserves long-term affordability akin to a CLT.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: Halifax Community Land Trust
resources.description: A locally governed, nonprofit community land trust working to acquire and steward land in Halifax for permanently affordable housing. It implements the CLT model by keeping land in community ownership and offering long-term, renewable ground leases to partner co-ops and nonprofit developers, ensuring resale restrictions and community stewardship prevent speculation and keep homes affordable in perpetuity.

resources.name: Housing Trust of Nova Scotia
resources.description: A province-wide nonprofit trust that acquires and holds residential properties and development sites to ensure long-term affordability for essential and moderate-income workers. By placing land and buildings under community stewardship with long-term ownership and affordability covenants, it removes housing from speculative markets and leases homes at below-market rents, aligning with core CLT principles of permanent community ownership.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Antigonish Affordable Housing Society – Community Stewardship Housing
resources.description: A community-led nonprofit that acquires land and develops multi-unit affordable housing in Antigonish, holding the land and buildings in community ownership for the long term. By retaining ownership and leasing homes to residents at affordable or geared-to-income rents, it removes sites from speculation and implements the CLT approach of permanent community stewardship and affordability.

resources.name: New Dawn Properties – Community Land Stewardship
resources.description: Cape Breton’s long-standing community development organization that purchases, rehabilitates, and holds residential properties for long-term affordable rental and community use. By keeping land and buildings in community hands and leasing homes to tenants, New Dawn prevents speculation and maintains lasting affordability, applying CLT-aligned principles of community ownership and perpetual stewardship.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Housing
resources.description: New Dawn Community Housing acquires and stewards land and buildings in community ownership to provide permanently affordable rental homes in Cape Breton. By holding title to the land and leasing homes to residents below market rates, the organization removes property from speculation and safeguards long-term affordability—key practices of a community land trust model.

resources.name: Sunflower Court (Affordable Community Housing)
resources.description: Developed and owned by Adsum for Women & Children, Sunflower Court increases the supply of permanently affordable rental homes while keeping the land and buildings under community non-profit ownership. Adsum leases homes to residents at affordable rates and stewards the property over the long term, preventing land speculation and aligning with core community land trust principles.

resources.name: Antigonish Affordable Housing Society – Affordable Rental Homes
resources.description: The Antigonish Affordable Housing Society acquires land and develops multi-unit, below-market rental housing that it retains in community non-profit ownership. By holding title to the land and leasing homes to low- and moderate-income residents, AAHS prevents speculation and ensures lasting affordability in line with a community land trust approach.

solutions.text: Housing Co-operatives: Establish resident-led co-ops that pool resources to build or buy multi-unit housing with shared governance and lower long-term costs for members.

resources.name: Co-operative Housing Federation of Canada – Atlantic Support for Nova Scotia Co-ops
resources.organization: Co-operative Housing Federation of Canada (CHF Canada)
resources.description: CHF Canada is the national federation that actively supports existing and emerging housing co-operatives in Nova Scotia through its Atlantic network. It delivers governance training, development assistance, refinancing and asset management tools that enable resident groups to pool resources to create, purchase, and sustain multi‑unit co‑op housing with democratic, member-led control—lowering long-term housing costs and increasing affordable supply.
resources.address: 225 Metcalfe Street, Suite 311, Ottawa, ON K2P 1P9

resources.name: Co-operative Development Services for Housing Co-ops in Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Co-operative Council helps resident groups form and grow housing co-operatives across the province by providing incorporation support, business planning, governance training, and pathways to financing and government programs. By organizing communities to pool capital and manage multi‑unit properties democratically, the Council enables co-ops that stabilize rents and expand affordable housing supply for young families and workers.
resources.address: 90 Research Drive, Suite 130, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

solutions.text: Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Promotion: Help homeowners add suites, garden apartments, or basement units by organizing design workshops, a local ADU guide, and a volunteer permit-navigation helpdesk.

resources.name: Backyard Suites
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality provides a detailed Backyard Suites guide, how-to webpages, and sample requirements that help homeowners understand where and how accessory dwelling units can be added on residential lots. Planning & Development staff offer counter and email support to navigate permitting, zoning, and inspections, and the municipality periodically hosts public information sessions to walk residents through design and approval steps.

resources.name: Secondary & Backyard Suites
resources.description: The Town of Wolfville promotes accessory dwelling units by providing clear guidance on secondary and backyard suites, including allowable locations, design considerations, and step-by-step permitting requirements. Planning staff offer pre-application consultations and permit-navigation assistance so homeowners can efficiently plan designs, prepare drawings, and obtain approvals for basement, garden, or backyard units.

resources.name: Secondary and Backyard Suites Information & Permitting
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings (Planning & Development)
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings supports ADU creation by publishing guidance on secondary and backyard suites and outlining zoning, lot standards, and design expectations. Its Planning & Development team provides one-on-one help at the permit desk and through pre-application meetings to streamline design choices, building code questions, and the development/permit application process.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Secondary Suites Guidance and Permitting
resources.description: The Town of Truro offers information for homeowners on adding secondary suites, including eligibility, design and building code considerations, and the steps to apply for development and building permits. Planning staff provide permit-navigation support and can review concept plans, helping residents convert basements or create accessory apartments that expand local rental supply.

solutions.text: Tiny Home and Laneway Housing Villages: Create pilot tiny-home or laneway housing projects on community or underused land to provide affordable, incremental housing options and test scaling approaches.

resources.name: Backyard Suites
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Backyard Suites program legalizes and guides the development of detached accessory dwelling units (laneway/tiny homes) on existing residential lots across HRM. By providing clear zoning, design standards, and permitting guidance, it enables homeowners to add small, self-contained units on underused backyard space, increasing gentle-density, expanding affordable rental options, and creating a scalable path to broader laneway housing adoption.

resources.name: Secondary Suites Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg’s Secondary Suites Program supports homeowners to create secondary and detached backyard suites, adding small, independent units on existing residential properties. Through incentives and streamlined approvals, the program pilots and scales incremental housing on underused land, delivering lower-cost options similar to laneway/tiny homes that can be replicated throughout the municipality.

solutions.text: Adaptive Reuse of Vacant Buildings: Coordinate community-led feasibility studies and fundraising to convert vacant commercial or institutional buildings into affordable rental or mixed-use housing.

resources.name: Halifax Rapid Housing Initiative (RHI)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality administers CMHC’s Rapid Housing Initiative locally, partnering with non-profits to convert vacant hotels and institutional/commercial buildings into permanent affordable or supportive housing. The program funds feasibility work, pre-development, and capital costs, while coordinating municipal approvals to speed adaptive-reuse projects that add affordable rental supply.

resources.name: AKOMA Village Redevelopment
resources.description: AKOMA is transforming the former Nova Scotia Home for Colored Children campus by adaptively reusing vacant institutional buildings and adding infill to create a mixed-use community with affordable rental housing. The community-led initiative has conducted feasibility and planning with residents of the Preston area and leverages blended financing, including philanthropy, community fundraising, and government programs like the Rapid Housing Initiative, to deliver conversions and renovations into livable units.
resources.address: 19 Wilfred Jackson Way, Dartmouth, NS B2Z 1A8

resources.name: New Dawn Properties – Adaptive Reuse and Affordable Housing
resources.description: New Dawn acquires and rehabilitates underused or vacant commercial and institutional buildings in the Sydney area, converting them into mixed-use spaces that include affordable rental units. Through community-led feasibility studies and the use of community investment (CEDIFs), grants, and philanthropic funding, the organization finances and delivers adaptive-reuse housing that adds to local supply while retaining heritage assets.

solutions.text: Community Renovation Corps: Organize volunteer+skilled trades teams to renovate derelict or underused units for affordable housing, paired with job training and resident-tenant placements.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership & Build Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia organizes teams of volunteers alongside Red Seal–certified trades to build and rehabilitate homes, including the renovation of donated or underused properties, and turns them into permanently affordable homes. They partner with local trades-training programs to provide hands‑on experience for learners on site, while their family selection and support process places qualified low- to moderate‑income households into stable, affordable homeownership—freeing up pressure on the rental market and directly increasing supply.

resources.name: Home Team (Property Maintenance & Unit Turnover)
resources.description: LakeCity Works’ Home Team is a social enterprise that employs and trains people living with mental illness to carry out repairs, renovations, and unit‑turnover work under the supervision of skilled trades. By refurbishing vacant or distressed units for non‑profits and landlords—painting, flooring, carpentry, accessibility upgrades—the team helps bring underused housing back online quickly and affordably while providing paid, on‑the‑job training that leads to long‑term employment in the trades.

resources.name: New Dawn Properties – Affordable Housing
resources.description: New Dawn acquires and rehabilitates older or underused buildings in Sydney to create and preserve affordable rental units, coordinating local skilled trades to complete upgrades and code‑compliance renovations. Working with community partners and housing waitlists, they place low‑ and modest‑income tenants in these revitalized units, and frequently provide opportunities for student placements and early‑career tradespeople to gain experience on live community housing projects.

solutions.text: Modular/Prefab Project Pool: Create a local consortium to commission modular or prefab units in bulk for faster, cheaper construction for non-profits and community builders.

resources.name: Modular Supportive Housing and Shelter Villages
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia leads a centralized, province-wide procurement and delivery program for modular and prefab supportive housing and shelter villages (including Pallet shelter communities). By aggregating demand from multiple communities and partnering with local non-profits to operate the sites, the agency bulk-orders standardized units and coordinates site work, driving down per‑unit costs and speeding timelines—exactly the pooled, consortium-style approach envisioned. This enables rapid deployment of new units for community operators across Nova Scotia while leveraging repeatable designs and vendor-of-record arrangements.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 301, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Nova Scotia Housing Hub
resources.description: The Housing Hub convenes municipalities, co-ops, and non-profits, and helps package multiple small affordable projects into shared, off‑site construction procurements. By pre-qualifying modular/panelized builders, standardizing designs, and coordinating bulk orders, the Hub reduces cost and risk for community developers and accelerates delivery—functioning as a local consortium that commissions modular units at scale. It also provides development support and financing pathways so community groups can tap into pooled purchasing power.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1110, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Sunflower Court (Rapid Housing modular build)
resources.description: Adsum for Women & Children delivered Sunflower Court as a rapid, factory‑built modular project, working with public partners to leverage standardized units and an accelerated schedule. The project exemplifies pooled procurement principles used in Rapid Housing—using prefabricated modules sourced in batches and coordinated site servicing—to lower costs and bring supportive homes online quickly for women and gender‑diverse people. This approach directly addresses supply bottlenecks by deploying repeatable modular designs for a non‑profit operator.

resources.name: Kentville Modular Shelter Village (Pallet shelters)
resources.description: The Portal operates a prefab shelter village in Kentville using Pallet units that were centrally procured and delivered through a provincial program. By relying on a bulk purchase of standardized prefab units and shared vendor relationships, the model cuts lead times and unit costs while enabling a local non‑profit to focus on services—mirroring a modular project pool. The result is rapid, lower‑cost capacity that relieves pressure on the housing system and supports young people and families locally.

solutions.text: Employer–Community Housing Partnerships: Facilitate partnerships between local employers and community organizations to develop workforce housing, employer-assisted rental pools, or guaranteed occupancy schemes.

resources.name: Cabot Cape Breton Staff Accommodation Program
resources.description: Cabot Cape Breton operates dedicated staff accommodation for seasonal and year-round employees and works with local landlords and the Municipality of the County of Inverness to secure additional rental blocks during peak periods. By reserving units for its workforce and coordinating with community partners, the resort provides guaranteed occupancy options that ease local housing pressures and strengthen recruitment and retention across hospitality, culinary, and maintenance roles.

resources.name: Keltic Lodge Staff Housing
resources.description: Keltic Lodge at the Highlands provides on-site and nearby staff housing and collaborates with local property owners in Ingonish to offer additional rooms for seasonal employees. This employer-assisted accommodation pool guarantees occupancy for workers, helping the lodge attract and retain staff in a rural area with limited rental supply while reducing commuting barriers and stabilizing its workforce.
resources.address: 383 Middle Head Peninsula, Ingonish Beach, NS B0C 1L0

resources.name: Employer Support & Landlord Outreach (Housing for Newcomer Workers)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS partners with Nova Scotia employers who are hiring newcomers to secure short- and long-term rentals by engaging property managers, community landlords, and settlement networks. By coordinating employer referrals, pre-arrival housing searches, and block bookings where available, the program functions as an employer-assisted rental pathway that stabilizes housing access for the workforce and their families.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YREACH – Employer-Supported Settlement & Housing Navigation
resources.description: The YMCA’s YREACH program works with employers across Nova Scotia to help internationally recruited staff secure housing, directly engaging local landlords, municipalities, and community groups to line up rentals. Through coordinated placements for cohorts of hires, landlord outreach, and arrival housing support, YREACH creates an employer-supported rental pool that reduces landlord risk and ensures timely, reliable occupancy for workers.

solutions.text: Local Down-Payment Assistance Fund: Set up a community-managed revolving fund or matched-savings program to help first-time buyers with down-payments tied to resale restrictions that preserve affordability.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia’s Affordable Homeownership Program builds and sells homes to qualifying first-time buyers with a mortgage geared to income, removing the upfront down-payment barrier. Habitat retains a shared-equity/second-mortgage interest and applies resale restrictions (such as right of first refusal and equity-sharing covenants), so when a family sells, the home remains affordable for the next buyer and any shared equity is reinvested to help more families. This community-managed approach functions as a revolving fund that preserves long-term affordability.

resources.name: Down Payment Assistance Program (DPAP)
resources.organization: Housing Nova Scotia (Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
resources.description: Administered by Housing Nova Scotia, the DPAP provides interest-free, repayable loans to eligible first-time homebuyers to cover a portion of the down payment, directly reducing upfront costs in a tight housing market. Because loans are repaid over time or on sale of the home, the funding recycles and can support additional buyers, operating as a revolving down-payment assistance fund. This targeted assistance complements broader affordability efforts by enabling earlier entry into homeownership for Nova Scotians.
resources.address: 14th Floor, 1741 Brunswick Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3X8

solutions.text: Shared-Equity and Rent-to-Own Programs: Pilot shared-equity or rent-to-own models where a community organization retains an equity share to lower upfront costs and keep homes affordable over time.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia builds and sells homes to qualifying families using a shared-equity model. Families purchase the home with an affordable, no-interest first mortgage and a deferred shared-equity second mortgage held by Habitat; upon resale, a portion of appreciation is retained or repaid to Habitat, keeping homes affordable for the next buyer and reducing upfront costs for first-time owners.

resources.name: North End United Housing Co-operative
resources.organization: North End United Housing Co-operative Limited
resources.description: North End United Housing Co-op provides limited-equity co‑operative housing where the co‑op (a community-owned, non-profit entity) retains ownership of the buildings and members purchase a low-cost share. Because the co-op holds the underlying equity and caps member shares, monthly housing charges stay below market and long-term affordability is preserved for future members, aligning with shared-equity principles.

resources.name: Cranberry Court Housing Co-operative
resources.description: Cranberry Court operates as a limited‑equity housing co‑operative in which the community co‑op owns the property and members buy a modest share instead of a full market-priced unit. By retaining equity collectively and controlling resale/share values, the co‑op lowers entry costs and maintains affordability over time, a practical implementation of a shared‑equity housing model.

solutions.text: Community Mortgage Guarantee Pool: Create a pooled guarantee or micro-lender standby from local investors and credit unions to reduce lending barriers for small-scale affordable developments and first-time buyers.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: The New Dawn Community Investment Fund pools capital from local Nova Scotia investors under the province’s CEDIF framework and deploys it as patient, often subordinated, loans or equity into community projects, including affordable and supportive housing in Cape Breton. By standing in behind senior lenders or co-investing alongside credit unions, the fund reduces risk and improves loan-to-value for small-scale housing developers and non-profits, unlocking conventional mortgage financing that might otherwise be out of reach. This community-backed standby capital functions like a guarantee pool, lowering barriers for projects that add affordable units and help young families stay in the region.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia provides affordable, geared-to-income mortgages and often uses deferred second mortgages or equity contributions funded by local donors and partners to bridge gaps for first-time buyers. This community-backed financing structure acts as a de facto guarantee/standby that reduces lender risk and down payment barriers, enabling households who would not qualify for conventional mortgages to become homeowners. By lowering financing hurdles, the program directly supports young families and essential workers to put down roots in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Loan Guarantee Program for On‑Reserve Housing in Nova Scotia
resources.description: The First Nations Market Housing Fund partners with Mi’kmaq communities in Nova Scotia to provide credit enhancement (guarantees) and capacity support that backstop lenders on mortgages and small-scale community housing projects on reserve. Its pooled guarantee effectively de‑risks loans made by credit unions and banks to eligible households and local developers, enabling construction and ownership where traditional collateral is limited. This model directly reduces lending barriers for first-time buyers and community-led affordable developments across participating Nova Scotia communities.
resources.address: 50 O'Connor Street, Suite 700, Ottawa, ON K1P 6L2

solutions.text: Bulk Purchasing Coop for Materials: Organize bulk-buying cooperatives for construction materials and trades services to lower costs for small builders, renovations, and non-profit housing projects.

resources.name: Solar City Program
resources.description: Halifax’s Solar City aggregates demand for solar installations and tenders standardized equipment and installation services to pre-qualified contractors, securing bulk pricing across many projects at once. By centralizing procurement and offering streamlined financing, the program reduces per-project material and labour costs for homeowners, small landlords, and community/non-profit buildings undertaking renovations—helping address affordability and construction bottlenecks.

resources.name: ReCover – Aggregated Deep Energy Retrofits
resources.description: ReCover bundles dozens of home and building retrofits into unified procurement packages, standardizing scopes and materials (e.g., insulation, air sealing, heat pumps, windows) to buy at scale and contract multi-trade teams. This bulk-buy model lowers unit costs and accelerates delivery for homeowners and community/non-profit housing providers in Nova Scotia, directly implementing bulk purchasing of materials and services to ease housing affordability and supply constraints.

resources.name: Provincial Rapid Housing and Modular Procurement
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia aggregates multiple affordable and supportive housing projects into province-wide tenders for modular units and related site works, leveraging volume to secure lower pricing on materials and coordinated trades. By bundling projects and centralizing procurement, the initiative reduces per-unit costs and shortens timelines for non-profit and public housing providers across the province.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 301, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Business Instant Savings (Distributor Point-of-Sale Rebates)
resources.description: Efficiency Nova Scotia negotiates province-wide agreements with distributors and contractors to provide immediate, point-of-sale discounts on retrofit materials and equipment (e.g., lighting, controls, HVAC/heat pumps). By pooling market demand and standardizing incentives, the program functions as a bulk purchasing mechanism that lowers upfront material and installation costs for small contractors, businesses, and non-profit housing providers undertaking renovations.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

solutions.text: Neighbourhood Infill and 'Missing Middle' Pilots: Work with residents and planners to identify sites for gentle density pilots (duplexes, triplexes, townhouses) and document best practices for broader adoption.

resources.name: Halifax Centre Plan (Packages A & B) – Established Residential 'Missing Middle' Policies
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Centre Plan updates enable gentle density in established neighbourhoods by permitting forms such as townhouses, triplexes, and low-rise infill in ER zones, with clear built-form standards to fit local character. The plan was co-developed with extensive public engagement to identify appropriate infill areas and includes a Design Manual and monitoring framework that document best practices and lessons learned for broader application across the city.

resources.name: HRM Secondary and Backyard Suites Program
resources.description: HRM’s municipality-wide program allows homeowners to add secondary suites and detached backyard suites as-of-right in most residential zones, creating incremental, gentle density within existing neighbourhoods. The initiative includes step-by-step guides, permit checklists, and public information sessions that document implementation practices and provide replicable standards to support wider adoption of infill housing types.

resources.name: Kings 2050 – Secondary/Garden Suites and Infill Housing Policies
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings – Planning & Development
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings updated its Municipal Planning Strategy and Land Use By-law through the Kings 2050 process to permit secondary and garden suites and to enable small-scale multi-unit infill (e.g., duplexes, townhouses) in serviced Growth Centres. The county identifies appropriate locations through community engagement and provides development guidance and application checklists that capture best practices for gentle density and neighbourhood-compatible design.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Town of Bridgewater Municipal Planning Strategy & Land Use By-law – Accessory Dwelling and Infill Housing
resources.description: Bridgewater’s planning framework permits accessory dwelling units (secondary and backyard suites) and supports small-scale infill like duplexes and townhouses in appropriate residential areas to incrementally add housing supply. The Town provides pre-application support and publishes planning documents and guidance that outline standards and processes, helping to document best practices for gentle density that can be replicated by local builders and homeowners.

solutions.text: Tenant Support and Mediation Services: Fund community-led tenant education, legal clinics, and mediation services to improve renter stability and reduce displacement.

resources.name: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service (Tenant Law Clinic)
resources.description: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service provides free legal advice, representation, and community legal education to low‑income tenants on matters such as evictions, repairs, security deposits, and Residential Tenancies hearings. Staff lawyers and law students negotiate with landlords, help prepare applications and evidence, and represent tenants in dispute resolution, directly advancing renter stability and preventing displacement.

resources.name: Residential Tenancies Program (Dispute Resolution & Mediation)
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia – Service Nova Scotia (Residential Tenancies Program)
resources.description: The provincial Residential Tenancies Program administers Nova Scotia’s Residential Tenancies Act and provides dispute resolution services, including mediation and adjudication between landlords and tenants. By offering accessible processes, information, and forms to resolve rent, repair, and eviction issues, the program helps stabilize tenancies and reduce preventable displacement across the province.
resources.address: 300 Horseshoe Lake Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 0B7

resources.name: Housing & Settlement Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides newcomers with tenant-rights education, housing navigation, and workshops on renting in Nova Scotia, including leases, repairs, and dispute options. Settlement counsellors also liaise with landlords to address issues early, support mediation, and connect clients to legal clinics, improving renter stability for young families and recent arrivals.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Housing Support Program
resources.description: The North End Community Health Centre’s Housing Support Program offers eviction-prevention services, tenant advocacy, and landlord–tenant mediation for individuals and families at risk of losing housing. Staff provide rights education, accompany tenants through Residential Tenancies processes, and coordinate with community and legal partners to help tenants maintain stable homes.

solutions.text: Home-Sharing and Intergenerational Matching: Run a local home-share program that matches homeowners with spare rooms to students, young families, or seniors to provide affordable housing and companionship.

resources.name: CBU Homestay Program
resources.description: Cape Breton University’s Homestay Program matches students with screened local homeowners who have a spare bedroom, creating an affordable housing option in a tight rental market. Hosts provide a furnished room (and often meals), while students contribute to household costs and companionship, building intergenerational connections and community ties.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

resources.name: The Language Centre (TLC) Homestay Program
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University – The Language Centre
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University’s Language Centre operates a Homestay Program that places international students with local host families and homeowners who have spare rooms. The program emphasizes safe, affordable accommodation and cultural exchange, fostering companionship and support while efficiently using underutilized housing space.

resources.name: English Language Studies Homestay
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s English Language Studies (ELS) facilitates homestay placements, connecting students with vetted Halifax-area homeowners who have available rooms. This home-sharing model provides affordable, supportive living arrangements that encourage daily interaction and cultural learning while easing pressure on the local rental supply.

resources.name: Acadia ELC Homestay Program
resources.description: The Acadia English Language Centre (ELC) Homestay Program in Wolfville matches language students with local homeowners offering a private room in their home. By pairing students with community hosts for affordable accommodation and daily interaction, the program advances intergenerational connections and makes immediate use of existing housing capacity.

solutions.text: Community Investment Bonds for Housing: Issue municipally or community-backed bonds that allow residents and local investors to finance affordable housing projects with modest returns.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Community Economic Development Investment Funds (CEDIF) Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Finance and Treasury Board
resources.description: The Province’s CEDIF program enables community groups to create pooled investment funds that raise capital from Nova Scotian residents through regulated share offerings—functionally similar to community bonds. Community housing organizations and co-operatives can use a CEDIF to finance land acquisition, construction, or renovation of affordable rental housing, offering local investors modest financial returns and provincial tax credits while keeping capital invested locally.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: New Dawn raises community investment capital from Nova Scotians through provincially regulated CEDIF share offerings and channels the proceeds into community infrastructure, including the development and operation of affordable and seniors’ housing in Cape Breton. The model gives local residents a way to finance new housing supply while earning modest returns (and CEDIF tax credits), directly aligning community savings with projects that expand and preserve below‑market rental options.

solutions.text: Local Trades Training and Apprenticeship Hubs: Partner with colleges and contractors to create community-based training programs that grow the local construction workforce and reduce labour bottlenecks.

resources.name: NSCC Apprenticeship Training (School of Trades & Transportation)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College delivers apprenticeship technical training and pre-apprenticeship programs in carpentry, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and other construction trades across multiple community campuses. NSCC partners with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and local contractors to provide work-integrated learning, employer-sponsored seats, and direct pathways to Red Seal certification, expanding the local construction workforce and easing labour bottlenecks that constrain housing supply.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY connects Grade 10–12 students with paid summer placements in construction trades, combined with safety training and mentoring, to accelerate entry into apprenticeship pathways. Delivered with industry and education partners (including CANS, schools, and NSCC), the program builds a local pipeline of new entrants for contractors, strengthening the community-based workforce needed to reduce construction delays and support more housing supply.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

resources.name: Halifax Electrical JATC (Joint Apprenticeship & Training Committee)
resources.organization: IBEW Local 625 and the Electrical Contractors Association of Nova Scotia (ECANS)
resources.description: The Halifax Electrical JATC, operated by IBEW Local 625 and signatory contractors, provides apprenticeship intakes, classroom instruction, and hands-on labs for electricians, and dispatches apprentices to local employers. This employer-union training hub directly links training to job placements on residential and commercial projects, growing the skilled workforce and helping contractors meet housing construction timelines.
resources.address: 14 McQuade Lake Crescent, Halifax, NS B3S 1B6

resources.name: UA Local 56 Training Centre Apprenticeship Programs
resources.description: UA Local 56’s Training Centre delivers apprenticeship and upskilling for plumbers, steamfitters/pipefitters, welders, and gasfitters in partnership with signatory mechanical contractors. By combining industry-led instruction, safety certifications, and coordinated apprentice placement, the centre serves as a community-based hub that expands the construction labour pool and reduces project bottlenecks affecting housing and infrastructure builds.

solutions.text: Energy-Efficiency Retrofit Programs: Coordinate subsidized retrofit projects for low-income rental and owner-occupied homes to lower utility costs and improve housing supply longevity.

resources.name: HomeWarming
resources.organization: EfficiencyOne (Efficiency Nova Scotia) and Clean Foundation
resources.description: HomeWarming provides free home energy assessments and fully subsidized efficiency upgrades for income-qualified owner-occupied homes across Nova Scotia. Measures such as insulation, air sealing, and equipment upgrades reduce household energy bills and improve comfort, while building-envelope improvements extend the lifespan of older homes—directly supporting affordability and the long-term viability of the housing stock.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: Affordable Multifamily Housing Program
resources.description: This program supports owners and managers of affordable rental and co‑operative housing to plan and complete energy-efficiency retrofits. Incentives and technical support for measures like insulation, heat pumps, and efficient lighting lower operating costs for landlords and tenants, while upgrades improve building durability—helping preserve and stabilize Nova Scotia’s affordable rental supply.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: Energy Assist
resources.description: Energy Assist offers no-cost in‑home energy assessments and immediate efficiency upgrades for income-constrained households, including renters and homeowners. By installing free measures such as LED lighting, weatherstripping, low‑flow devices, and smart thermostats—and by connecting clients to deeper retrofit programs like HomeWarming—it reduces utility costs right away and coordinates subsidized retrofits that enhance home longevity.
resources.address: 126 Portland Street, 6th Floor, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 1H8

resources.name: Home Repair Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia’s Home Repair Program helps low-income homeowners complete essential repairs and energy-efficiency upgrades, often using subsidized financing and volunteer labour to reduce costs. Typical projects—such as insulation, window and door replacements, and heating system improvements—lower utility bills and keep aging homes safe and serviceable, extending the life of the province’s housing stock.

solutions.text: Permit Navigation and Design Advisory Service: Offer a one-stop community service to help small developers and homeowners with zoning rules, design templates, and permit applications to speed approvals.

resources.name: Planning & Development — Customer Service Centre (Permits, Planning & Licensing)
resources.description: Halifax’s Planning & Development Customer Service Centre provides a single point of contact where homeowners and small builders can get zoning clarification, pre-application guidance, and help preparing complete permit submissions. Staff walk applicants through land-use bylaw requirements, checklists, and standard forms, and coordinate intake for development and building permits to reduce review times and speed approvals.

resources.name: Planning & Development — One-Window Permitting and Planning Services
resources.organization: Cape Breton Regional Municipality — Planning & Development
resources.description: CBRM’s Planning & Development office operates a one-window counter that advises residents and small developers on zoning and subdivision rules, and helps prepare and file development and building permit applications. The team provides step-by-step guidance, standard forms and checklists for common residential projects (e.g., decks, additions, accessory structures), and pre-application consultations that streamline submissions and accelerate approvals.

resources.name: Planning & Inspections — Integrated Permit and Development Services
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: Kings County offers an integrated Planning & Inspections service that functions as a one-stop shop for zoning questions, site plan reviews, and coordinated building/development permit intake. Planners and building officials provide pre-application meetings, standard application packages and checklists, and coaching to ensure complete submissions, helping small developers and homeowners move more quickly through approvals.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Planning & Development — Permit and Application Help Centre
resources.description: East Hants provides a centralized Planning & Development counter and online permitting portal where applicants receive zoning verification, guidance on lot and building code requirements, and templates/checklists for typical residential projects. Staff coordinate reviews and assist with complete application packages, reducing resubmissions and accelerating permit approvals for homeowners and small builders.

solutions.text: Community Land Use Charrettes and Visioning: Host participatory planning workshops to identify acceptable density increases, infill sites, and design principles that residents support and can advocate for with municipal governments.

resources.name: Shape Your City Halifax (Public Engagement Program)
resources.description: Shape Your City Halifax is HRM’s ongoing engagement program that runs design charrettes, visioning workshops, and corridor planning sessions for initiatives like the Centre Plan and local area plans. These facilitated sessions help residents identify acceptable density increases, infill opportunities, and built-form principles; the resulting maps and guidelines are used to update the Municipal Planning Strategy and Land Use By-law, strengthening community-backed advocacy for zoning changes that expand housing supply.

resources.name: Engage Bridgewater (Public Planning & Design Engagement)
resources.description: Engage Bridgewater combines an online platform with in-person design charrettes and neighborhood workshops to co-create the Town’s Downtown & Waterfront Master Plan and housing-related policy updates. Residents test building heights, missing-middle infill, and redevelopment scenarios, producing community-supported design directions that Council uses to amend zoning and guide infill approvals—directly advancing gentle density and new housing options.

resources.name: Community Planning Consultations and Design Workshops
resources.description: The Eastern District Planning Commission facilitates community visioning sessions, design workshops, and charrettes across its member municipalities (e.g., Port Hawkesbury, Inverness, Richmond, and Victoria Counties). These engagements map infill sites, discuss acceptable density and built form, and produce design principles that feed into local Municipal Planning Strategies and Land Use By-laws—equipping residents to advocate for policy changes that enable more housing.
resources.address: 606 Reeves Street, Unit 3, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 2R7

resources.name: Imagine Lunenburg: Comprehensive Community Plan Engagement
resources.description: Imagine Lunenburg is the Town’s community planning initiative that used public visioning, design charrettes, and mapping exercises to identify where and how to add housing through context-sensitive infill and higher-density forms. The community-derived design guidelines and policy directions inform the Town’s planning documents and bylaws, giving residents clear tools to support and advocate for zoning that increases housing supply while protecting Lunenburg’s character.

obstacles.title: Childcare Access and Affordability
obstacles.description: Shortages of licensed spaces, staffing challenges, and costs limit workforce participation for young parents.

solutions.text: Parent-led Childcare Co-operatives: Families organize and operate cooperative childcare pods that share caregiving responsibilities, rotating duties and pooling fees to create affordable, licensed or unlicensed options that meet local needs while pursuing provincial licensing where feasible.

resources.name: Child Care Co‑op Development Support
resources.description: Nova Scotia Co-operative Council provides hands-on assistance for parent groups to form and operate childcare co-operatives, including incorporation, bylaws, governance training, and financial planning. They help families organize cooperative childcare pods, pool fees, structure rotating duties, and navigate provincial licensing pathways with the Department of Education and Early Childhood Development.
resources.address: 90 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: Parent & Child (Early Years) Cooperative Program
resources.description: South Shore Waldorf School’s Parent & Child program offers a cooperative early-years model where families share responsibilities and fees to run small-group, play-based sessions facilitated by an educator. Parents rotate support roles and co-manage scheduling and logistics, creating affordable, community-rooted childcare pods that can bridge to more formal licensed care as demand and capacity grow.

resources.name: St. Margaret’s Bay Co-operative Nursery School
resources.organization: St. Margaret’s Bay Co-operative Nursery School Society
resources.description: A parent-led co-operative preschool where families participate in governance and classroom ‘duty days,’ sharing caregiving responsibilities and pooling fees to keep costs manageable. The co-op structure enables flexible, community-based childcare pods that align with provincial standards and can pursue licensing as capacity and staffing allow.
resources.address: 5374 St. Margarets Bay Road, Upper Tantallon, NS B3Z 2H9

solutions.text: Community Space Sharing for Childcare: Local churches, community centres, libraries and schools open underused rooms for licensed or informal childcare during business hours, with community groups coordinating scheduling, safety checks and minimal renovation funding.

resources.name: EXCEL Before and After School Program
resources.description: EXCEL provides licensed before- and after-school childcare in elementary schools across HRCE by using existing classrooms, gyms, and multipurpose rooms outside of instructional hours. The program coordinates scheduling with each host school, ensures safety checks and custodial access, and equips spaces with age-appropriate materials rather than building new facilities. This directly implements community space sharing by activating underused school rooms to expand affordable childcare access for working families.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Cape Breton Family Place – Outreach Playgroups & Child-Minding
resources.organization: Cape Breton Family Place Resource Centre
resources.description: Cape Breton Family Place coordinates free daytime playgroups and short-term child-minding in borrowed community spaces such as libraries, church halls, band offices, and recreation centres across the CBRM and surrounding communities. By booking rooms, handling safety protocols, and supplying portable toys and equipment, the team activates underused local spaces so families can access early learning and caregiver relief without needing a dedicated facility. This space-sharing model reduces barriers to participation and brings informal childcare supports closer to where families live.

resources.name: Veith House – Supportive Childcare & Family Programs
resources.description: Veith House opens its community centre rooms during business hours to provide supportive childcare and child-minding while parents attend employment supports, counseling, and skill-building programs on site. Staff and partners follow check-in procedures and safety policies, furnishing multipurpose spaces with portable early-years materials rather than undertaking major renovations. This approach exemplifies community space sharing by turning existing rooms into flexible, informal childcare environments that help parents access services and work.

resources.name: Halifax Public Libraries – Early Years Playgroups & Partner Programs
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries regularly hosts partner-led early years playgroups, caregiver-and-tot sessions, and occasional on-site child-minding for adult workshops by opening meeting rooms and program spaces during daytime hours. Library staff coordinate bookings and basic safety procedures while family resource centres deliver programming, allowing underused civic spaces to function as informal childcare and early learning hubs. This collaboration expands access to free, local supports for young families without needing new bricks-and-mortar childcare facilities.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Employer-Community Childcare Partnerships: Local employers partner with municipalities and non-profits to create onsite or near-site childcare hubs, offering subsidies, shared staffing, flexible schedules and priority placement for workers from small and medium businesses.

resources.name: Leeds Street Childcare Centre
resources.description: A non-profit childcare centre located on the NSCC IT Campus, it partners with the college (a major local employer) to provide on-site licensed childcare for students, staff, and nearby workers. By situating care at a transportation-accessible campus that serves many small and medium-sized employers in Halifax’s North End, it functions as a near-site childcare hub with schedules aligned to class and work hours and priority access for NSCC-affiliated families, effectively sharing staffing and space with a public institution.

resources.name: Akerley Child Development Centre
resources.description: Located at NSCC’s Akerley Campus in Dartmouth, this centre partners with the college to provide near-site licensed childcare supporting students, faculty, and staff, while also serving families working in nearby Burnside and Woodlawn business areas. The arrangement leverages shared facilities and training partnerships with NSCC’s early childhood education programs to stabilize staffing and align hours with class and shift schedules, creating practical access for employees of surrounding small and medium-sized businesses.

resources.name: Northwood Child Care Centre
resources.description: Within Northwood’s Halifax campus, this licensed childcare service operates alongside a large non-profit continuing care organization, creating an intergenerational and community hub model. It supports Northwood employees with priority access and flexible scheduling while also serving neighbourhood families, demonstrating an employer–non-profit partnership that shares space, resources, and staffing to expand affordable childcare access close to work.

resources.name: Greenwood Military Family Resource Centre (GMFRC) Childcare & Respite Services
resources.description: The GMFRC partners with the Department of National Defence to provide on-base and near-base childcare supports (including casual, emergency, and respite care) tailored to the irregular hours of military and civilian defence employees. As an employer–non-profit model, it offers priority access for CAF families, flexible scheduling, and coordinated community referrals, reducing barriers to workforce participation for young parents employed on or near 14 Wing Greenwood.

solutions.text: Time-Banking and Skill-Share Childcare Networks: Community members exchange hours of childcare through a time-bank platform: parents provide childcare when able and earn credits to be used when they need care, including supports for training and background checks.

resources.name: Northside TimeBank
resources.description: Northside TimeBank enables residents of the Northside (Cape Breton Regional Municipality) to exchange services using time credits, including parent-to-parent childcare swaps. The program outlines categories for child-related support and helps participating caregivers complete vulnerable sector and child-abuse registry checks, as well as access basic first-aid/CPR training, so families can earn hours by providing care and redeem those hours when they need childcare.
resources.address: 309 Commercial Street, North Sydney, NS B2A 1B9
