resources.name: St. Margaret’s Bay Time Bank
resources.description: Transition Bay St. Margarets hosts a community time bank where neighbours trade time for services such as babysitting and respite childcare, with one hour of care equaling one time credit. The initiative supports safer childcare exchanges by providing orientation, connecting volunteers to criminal record/vulnerable sector and child-abuse registry checks, and offering access to caregiver training so parents can confidently earn and redeem hours.
resources.address: 5229 St Margarets Bay Road, Upper Tantallon, NS B3Z 2H9

resources.name: Eastern Shore Time Bank
resources.description: The Deanery Project facilitates a rural time-banking network along Nova Scotia’s Eastern Shore that includes childcare and family support among its exchange categories. Members log hours for providing childcare and can redeem them when they need care, with the Deanery supporting caregiver orientation, child-safety workshops, and assistance with background checks (vulnerable sector/child-abuse registry) to promote safe participation.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

resources.name: The North Grove Skill-Share & Time Exchange
resources.description: The North Grove’s community skill-share and time-exchange activities allow families in Dartmouth North to swap childcare and other supports using time credits managed through the centre. Staff facilitate caregiver screening (vulnerable sector/child-abuse registry checks) and offer access to babysitter and first-aid training so parents can safely earn credits by watching children and redeem those credits when they need affordable care.

solutions.text: Community-run Training and Recruitment Pipeline: Municipalities, community colleges and local employers run funded training, micro-credentials and apprenticeships for early childhood educators (ECEs), offering scholarships, practicum placements and local hiring commitments.

resources.name: Early Childhood Education (ECE) Diploma Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE)
resources.description: NSCECE delivers a two-year ECE diploma with embedded practicums in its lab schools and partner licensed child care centres, creating a direct pipeline from training to local employment. The college supports students to access the provincial ECE tuition bursary and offers short-course upskilling and stackable credentials, aligning with community-run, funded training and local hiring commitments.

resources.name: NSCC Early Childhood Education Diploma (Full-time and Workplace Streams)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Akerley Campus
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College offers ECE diploma programs across the province, including a workplace stream that lets learners earn while they learn with employer partners, and practicums in licensed centres and Pre-Primary classrooms. NSCC participates in provincially funded tuition bursaries and provides micro-credentials and continuing education for ECEs (e.g., inclusion, leadership), matching the solution’s focus on funded training, micro-credentials, and local recruitment.

resources.name: Éducation à la petite enfance (ÉPE) – Diplôme
resources.description: Université Sainte-Anne delivers the francophone ECE diploma with supervised practicums in Acadian and francophone child care centres and Pre-Primary settings, feeding a local hiring pipeline for French-language services. Students can access provincial bursaries and scholarships, and the university partners with local employers for placements and recruitment, aligning with a community-run training and recruitment model.

resources.name: Pre-Primary Program – Early Childhood Educator Recruitment
resources.description: HRCE hires certified ECEs to deliver Nova Scotia’s Pre-Primary Program in schools across the Halifax region and regularly hosts practicum students from NSCC/NSCECE, providing supervised on-site learning and clear pathways into local jobs. As a major local employer, HRCE coordinates with community colleges and supports staff to access provincial training supports, anchoring the recruitment side of the community-run training pipeline.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

solutions.text: Sliding-scale and Sponsorship Funds: Local philanthropic groups, businesses and service clubs create a community childcare fund to provide sliding-scale subsidies or scholarships for families in precarious employment to access licensed care.

resources.name: YMCA Financial Assistance for Child Care
resources.description: The YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth operates licensed early learning and school-age child care programs and provides donor-funded financial assistance that reduces parent fees on a sliding scale. Supported by community philanthropy, corporate sponsors, and service-club donors through the YMCA Strong Communities campaign, this fund helps families in precarious or low-wage employment access licensed care by covering a portion of fees based on need.

resources.name: YMCA Child Care Fee Assistance
resources.description: The YMCA of Southwest Nova Scotia offers licensed child care and before-and-after school programs and maintains a community-supported fee assistance program to ensure affordability. Funded by donations from local businesses, service clubs, and individual philanthropists, the assistance is awarded on a sliding-scale to families facing financial strain or irregular employment, directly offsetting licensed child care costs.

resources.name: YMCA Strong Communities Child Care Assistance
resources.description: YMCA of Cape Breton provides licensed early learning and school-age child care and extends access through its Strong Communities donor-supported assistance. Using contributions from local philanthropists, businesses, and service organizations, the YMCA applies a sliding-scale assessment to reduce child care fees for families in precarious work situations, ensuring they can secure licensed care while maintaining employment.

solutions.text: Pop-up and Event Childcare Programs: Volunteer-led pop-up childminding at community events, town meetings and employment fairs gives parents the ability to attend work-related activities, training, and civic events while building confidence in local caregiving options.

resources.name: Public Engagement Childcare Support
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality provides free, on-site pop-up childminding at many public engagement sessions, planning meetings, and community consultations so parents and guardians can participate. These short-duration, event-based childcare supports are arranged for specific meetings across the municipality and delivered by vetted caregivers, reducing barriers to civic involvement for working and young parents.

resources.name: Chebucto Family Centre Childminding
resources.organization: Home of the Guardian Angel (Chebucto Family Centre)
resources.description: Chebucto Family Centre sets up on-site childminding so parents can attend workshops, employment-readiness sessions, partner-led job fairs, and community meetings hosted at or by the Centre. Using trained staff and volunteers, the Centre provides short-term, event-based care in safe play spaces, enabling young parents to focus on training and engagement activities while building trust in local caregiving supports.

resources.name: Childcare Support for Programs and Events
resources.organization: Antigonish Women's Resource Centre & Sexual Assault Services Association
resources.description: The Antigonish Women's Resource Centre & Sexual Assault Services Association provides free on-site childcare during group programs, training sessions, and community meetings, with support from trained volunteers. The organization also offers childminding at outreach and awareness events, helping parents—especially young and newcomer families—attend employment supports, workshops, and civic activities without childcare barriers.

solutions.text: Shared Transportation and Pickup Networks: Neighbourhood ride-share schemes and community volunteer drivers coordinate safe group pickups/drop-offs for children attending childcare, reducing barriers for families without private transportation.

resources.name: HRCE Student Transportation – Childcare/Alternate Drop-Offs
resources.description: HRCE’s student transportation program allows families to designate licensed childcare providers as alternate drop-off locations on eligible school bus routes. The board coordinates safe, shared school-bus rides and ensures children are escorted to the appropriate stop for their daycare or after‑school program, reducing the need for parents to drive. This provides predictable, supervised group transport that removes a major barrier for working families without private vehicles.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: YMCA of Cape Breton School-Age Child Care Transportation
resources.description: The YMCA of Cape Breton operates licensed school-age child care and coordinates daily group pickups from select local elementary schools to its programs using YMCA vans/buses and arranged school-bus drop-offs. Trained staff manage rosters, permissions, and hand‑offs to provide safe, reliable shared transportation for children. This reduces transportation barriers for working parents and ensures consistent access to after‑school care.

resources.name: BGC Greater Halifax – Spryfield After School Transportation
resources.description: BGC Greater Halifax runs licensed after-school programs that include coordinated daily pickups from multiple neighborhood schools to the Spryfield Club via club vans and arranged school-bus stops. Staff and drivers follow check‑in protocols and maintain communication with schools and families to ensure children are transported together safely. This shared pickup network provides dependable access to childcare for families who lack private transportation.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Eastern Shore – Youth & Family Community Transit
resources.description: MusGo Rider is a rural community transit co‑op that offers pre-booked, door‑to‑door shared rides across the Eastern Shore, including transportation for children and families to daycares, preschools, and after‑school programs. Drivers are screened and vehicles can accommodate car seats/boosters as needed; group ride scheduling and multi‑stop routing make childcare pickups and drop‑offs affordable and reliable. By providing supervised, shared transport in areas without conventional transit, MusGo Rider removes a key barrier to accessing childcare.
resources.address: 22404 Highway 7, Unit 2, Sheet Harbour, NS B0J 3B0

solutions.text: Home-based Provider Microgrants: Local governments and community foundations offer small grants for home childcare providers to meet licensing requirements, buy supplies, complete training, or upgrade safety features, increasing licensed local capacity.

resources.name: Family Home Child Care Start-Up Grant
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: The Department of Education and Early Childhood Development offers small, one-time start-up grants to individuals opening approved family home child care programs through licensed agencies. Funding helps new home providers meet approval/licensing requirements by covering costs such as mandatory training (e.g., first aid/CPR, food safety), safety equipment and minor home upgrades, and age-appropriate materials. By lowering start-up barriers, the grant increases the number of licensed home-based spaces in local communities.

resources.name: Licensed Child Care Space Creation and Minor Infrastructure Grant
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: This provincial grant provides small capital funds to create or expand regulated child care spaces, including those operated by approved family home child care providers working with agencies. Eligible expenses include safety and accessibility upgrades, minor renovations, and required equipment to meet provincial standards. The grant functions as a micro-capital boost that helps home providers add licensed capacity more quickly and affordably in underserved areas.

solutions.text: Intergenerational Childcare Partnerships: Day programs are co-located with seniors centres or assisted-living facilities to create intergenerational care opportunities where older adults support play and supervision, reducing staffing pressure while strengthening community bonds.

resources.name: Northwood Child Care Centre
resources.description: Located on Northwood’s Halifax Campus, this licensed early learning program is co-located within a long-term care community. Residents and senior volunteers regularly participate in shared playrooms, reading circles, music, and outdoor activities alongside early childhood educators, adding supportive adults to the environment and easing staffing pressure while fostering daily intergenerational connections.

resources.name: Aboriginal Head Start (AHS) Early Childhood Program
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s AHS provides culturally grounded early childhood education co-located with Elders and seniors programming in the same facility. Elders are present in classrooms to share language, stories, crafts, and land-based teachings, directly supporting play and supervision and creating daily intergenerational care that strengthens bonds and complements educator capacity.

resources.name: Little Eagles Aboriginal Head Start
resources.description: Little Eagles AHS operates at the Native Council of Nova Scotia’s headquarters, co-located with Elders and seniors programming that is integrated into the centre’s daily routine. Elders regularly join classrooms for storytelling, cultural activities, and outdoor play, providing additional supportive adults that help ease staffing demands while building strong intergenerational relationships.
resources.address: 129 Truro Heights Road, Truro Heights, NS B6L 1X1

resources.name: Town House Intergenerational Day Program and Child & Family Hub
resources.organization: Town House Glace Bay Citizens Service League
resources.description: Town House operates a seniors’ adult day program alongside child and family programs under one roof, enabling regular intergenerational sessions. Older adults support play-based activities such as music, art, and reading circles with children, adding caring adults to the environment to relieve pressure on early years staff while deepening community ties.
resources.address: 150 Commercial Street, Glace Bay, NS B1A 3C1

solutions.text: Community Childcare Navigators: Trained local navigators help young parents find and access childcare options, subsidies, training and emergency back-up care, and act as a liaison between families, providers and employers.

resources.name: Settlement Services (Child Care Navigation for Newcomers)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS settlement counselors act as navigators for newcomer parents, helping them locate licensed child care and family home care options, understand waitlists, and complete Nova Scotia Child Care Subsidy applications. They also connect clients to training and employment programs that offer on-site Care for Newcomer Children or other back-up arrangements, and coordinate with child care providers and employers to support parents’ work and training schedules.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Family Support Program (Childcare Navigation)
resources.organization: Dartmouth Family Centre & Dartmouth North Community Food Centre
resources.description: Family support workers at Dartmouth Family Centre provide one-on-one navigation to help parents find available child care spaces, apply for provincial subsidies, and access short-term or emergency child care resources through community partnerships. Staff liaise between families, child care providers, and employers/training programs to coordinate schedules, documentation, and smooth transitions back to work or school.

resources.name: Family Support & Young Parents Program
resources.organization: Home of the Guardian Angel (Chebucto Family Centre)
resources.description: Chebucto Family Centre’s family support team works with young and single parents to identify suitable licensed or family home child care, navigate subsidy applications, and connect to parenting programs and training opportunities that include child care supports. Staff act as liaisons with child care providers and employers to arrange schedules and troubleshoot gaps, including referrals to short-term back-up care when needed.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Employment Services (Childcare Barrier Navigation)
resources.description: Case managers at TEAM Work Cooperative’s Nova Scotia Works centre help jobseekers—especially young parents—address child care barriers by mapping local child care options, advising on subsidy eligibility, and making warm referrals to providers and family resource centres for back-up care. They coordinate with employers around interview and shift scheduling and advocate for flexible arrangements while parents secure stable child care.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

solutions.text: Local Awareness and Recruitment Campaigns: Community-led campaigns promote early childhood careers, highlight flexible ECE pathways, and recruit local talent (including immigrants and retired educators) into childcare roles using targeted outreach, job fairs and success stories.

resources.name: Early Childhood Educator Recruitment and Retention Strategy
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: Province-wide initiative that runs awareness and recruitment campaigns to attract people into early childhood educator (ECE) roles, highlighting the new wage grid, bursaries, and flexible training and classification pathways. The Department partners with communities, post-secondary institutions, and employers to support targeted outreach and host or sponsor job fairs and information sessions that bring local talent—including newcomers and career changers—into licensed child care roles.

resources.name: NSCECE ECE Career Fair & Community Outreach
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education
resources.description: NSCECE organizes ECE career fairs and community information sessions that connect local job seekers with licensed child care employers and promote early childhood careers. The college showcases flexible pathways (e.g., part-time study, recognition of prior learning, and accelerated options) and shares graduate success stories, directly recruiting new entrants—including newcomers and returning workers—into the ECE workforce.

resources.name: ISANS ECE Sector Recruitment Events & Pathways
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers targeted outreach to immigrants interested in early childhood education, offering sector-specific information sessions, credential guidance, and employer networking events. By partnering with child care centres and government programs, ISANS runs recruitment fairs and highlights newcomer success stories, helping fill local ECE vacancies and growing a diverse workforce in communities across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YMCA Child Care Hiring Fairs (Greater Halifax/Dartmouth)
resources.description: The YMCA hosts regular local hiring fairs and information nights to recruit early childhood educators and support staff for its licensed child care programs, with outreach that welcomes retirees, newcomers, and career changers. Campaigns promote ECE career opportunities, paid training and internal advancement pathways, and share staff success stories to attract community members into childcare roles.

resources.name: NSCC Early Childhood Education Outreach & Employer Connections
resources.description: NSCC promotes ECE careers through campus-based outreach, high school presentations, and community info sessions that explain multiple entry pathways (part-time, distributed learning, and prior learning assessment). Campuses host employer-linked job fairs and share learner success stories, directly connecting local talent to licensed child care employers across Nova Scotia.

obstacles.title: Healthcare Access and Wait Times
obstacles.description: Primary care shortages and long waits for mental health and specialized services undermine quality of life.

solutions.text: Community-run Nurse Practitioner Clinic: Pool local funds, space and volunteer administrative support to host a nurse practitioner-led clinic that provides primary care, chronic disease management and referrals on a regular schedule.

resources.name: North End Community Health Centre – Primary Care Clinic
resources.description: A community-governed, non-profit health centre that operates nurse practitioner-led primary care for unattached and marginalized residents in Halifax. Nurse practitioners provide comprehensive primary care, chronic disease management, and referrals to hospital and specialty services. The clinic sustains services through public funding, community donations, and volunteer support, aligning with the community-run model to improve timely access to care.

resources.name: Mobile Outreach Street Health (MOSH)
resources.description: An NP-led outreach program that delivers primary care on a regular schedule in shelters, drop-ins, and other community spaces across Halifax. Nurse practitioners manage chronic conditions, provide on-site primary care, and coordinate referrals and navigation to specialty and hospital services. Hosted by a community health centre and powered by local partnerships, donated resources, and volunteer involvement, MOSH exemplifies a community-run approach that brings care directly to people who face barriers to traditional clinics.

resources.name: Eskasoni Community Health Centre – Primary Care Services
resources.description: A community-run, band-governed health centre serving Eskasoni First Nation where nurse practitioners provide family primary care, chronic disease management, and culturally safe referrals to external specialists and hospitals. The clinic operates within a community-governed model that blends public funding with local resources and support, ensuring regular access to NP-led care close to home. This approach reduces wait times and improves continuity of care for community members.

solutions.text: Volunteer Primary Care Roster: Coordinate a local list of retired or part-time family physicians and nurse practitioners willing to take on a small panel of unattached patients, supported by community admin and outreach.

resources.name: North End Community Health Centre Primary Care Clinic
resources.description: A community-governed primary care clinic that provides longitudinal primary care to people who are unattached or face barriers to accessing the health system. The clinic coordinates a team of family physicians and nurse practitioners—many working part-time—who take on small caseloads, with community-based administration handling intake, scheduling, and outreach to sustain those panels.

resources.name: Mobile Outreach Street Health (MOSH)
resources.description: MOSH delivers primary care and harm reduction services to people experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity who are typically unattached to a family practice. It coordinates part-time physicians and nurse practitioners to provide ongoing care through mobile and community-based outreach, effectively managing small patient panels with administrative support from the North End Community Health Centre.

resources.name: Our Health Centre Primary Care Clinic
resources.description: Our Health Centre is a community-run hub that hosts family physicians and nurse practitioners—many in part-time roles—to expand access for local residents without a regular primary care provider. The centre’s administrative team coordinates intake from the provincial waitlist and local outreach, enabling providers to accept limited, manageable panels of unattached patients and supporting them with navigation and follow-up.

resources.name: Newcomer Health Clinic (Halifax)
resources.description: This Nova Scotia Health clinic provides interim primary care for refugees and other newcomers who are unattached, using a multidisciplinary team of family physicians and nurse practitioners who often work part-time. The clinic maintains small, time-limited patient panels and coordinates outreach and case management—often in partnership with settlement services—until patients can be transitioned to community family practices.

solutions.text: Shared Specialist Visit Days: Organize regular visiting specialist clinics (e.g., psychiatry, dermatology, endocrinology) in community health centres or libraries so residents can see specialists locally on scheduled days.

resources.name: Outpatient Specialty Clinics (Visiting Specialists) – Colchester East Hants Health Centre
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health coordinates rotating visiting specialist clinics (such as dermatology, endocrinology, rheumatology, and psychiatry) at the Colchester East Hants Health Centre. Specialists travel from larger centres to run clinics on scheduled days so Truro-area residents can access in-person specialty care locally without traveling to Halifax.

resources.name: Community Mental Health and Addictions – Visiting Psychiatrist Clinics (Eastern Shore)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Community Mental Health and Addictions program provides scheduled in-person psychiatrist days and related specialty consults at Eastern Shore Memorial Hospital. Psychiatrists travel to the community on set clinic dates, giving residents local access to assessments, medication management, and follow-up care that would otherwise require a trip to urban centres.

resources.name: Outpatient Visiting Specialist Clinics – Strait Richmond Hospital
resources.description: Strait Richmond Hospital hosts scheduled visiting specialist clinics—such as internal medicine, cardiology, and general surgery—coordinated by Nova Scotia Health. Specialists from regional hubs travel to the site on designated days, enabling residents of Richmond County and surrounding areas to see specialists locally for consults and follow-ups.

resources.name: IWK Pediatric Outreach/Satellite Clinics (Yarmouth Regional Hospital site)
resources.description: IWK Health runs pediatric outreach/satellite clinics where subspecialists (e.g., pediatric endocrinology, cardiology, and neurology) travel to regional sites like Yarmouth Regional Hospital on scheduled days. These in-person clinics bring specialist pediatric care closer to families, reducing travel to Halifax and improving timely access to expert consultations and follow-up.

solutions.text: Community Telehealth Hubs: Equip public spaces (municipal halls, libraries) with private booths, tablets and tech support to enable secure telehealth visits for residents lacking devices or connectivity.

resources.name: Community Zoom Rooms
resources.description: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library operates Community Zoom Rooms—bookable private spaces equipped with computers/tablets, webcams, headsets, and high-speed internet. Library staff provide on-site tech support to help residents connect securely to virtual healthcare providers, making it easier for people without reliable devices or connectivity to attend medical or mental health appointments.

resources.name: Zoom Rooms
resources.description: Annapolis Valley Regional Library offers Zoom Rooms—enclosed, bookable rooms with iPads or PCs, webcams, microphones, and robust Wi‑Fi, designed for secure virtual appointments. Staff can assist with setup and troubleshooting so community members can meet with clinicians via platforms like Zoom, Teams, or VirtualCareNS, even if they lack devices or home internet.

resources.name: Community Zoom Rooms
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library provides Community Zoom Rooms—private booths and rooms equipped with library devices, webcams, and headsets, plus on-site technical assistance. These spaces enable residents to conduct confidential telehealth visits and specialist consultations when they lack at-home connectivity or equipment.

resources.name: Zoom Rooms
resources.description: Western Counties Regional Library offers Zoom Rooms at select branches, providing quiet, private rooms with computers/tablets, webcams, and reliable internet for secure online appointments. Library staff help patrons get connected and navigate video platforms, making virtual medical and mental health care more accessible for those without devices or broadband at home.

solutions.text: Local Mental Health Peer Networks: Train and support peer counsellors and run peer-led support groups for youth, caregivers and specific conditions to reduce pressure on clinical services and provide timely support.

resources.name: Peer Support Services (Mental Health and Addictions Program)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health, Mental Health and Addictions Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health employs trained peer supporters with lived experience to provide one-to-one and group-based peer support across the province, including youth and family-focused offerings. Peer workers receive standardized training and supervision, and facilitate recovery-oriented, peer-led groups that offer timely emotional support and system navigation, helping reduce pressure on clinical teams and waitlists.
resources.address: 5909 Veterans' Memorial Lane, Halifax, NS B3H 2E2

resources.name: Family Peer Support Specialists (Child & Adolescent Mental Health and Addictions)
resources.description: At the IWK Health Centre, Family Peer Support Specialists use their lived experience to support parents and caregivers of children and youth accessing mental health and addictions services. They lead peer-led support groups and provide one-to-one peer coaching, helping families build coping skills and navigate services sooner, which eases demand on clinicians and improves timely access to support.

resources.name: Laing House Peer Support & Social Programs
resources.description: Laing House is a peer support organization for youth ages 16–29 living with mental illness that offers peer-led support groups, drop-in programming, and mentorship. Members are trained and supported to co-facilitate groups and activities, creating immediate, youth-driven support networks that complement clinical care and reduce isolation and pressure on formal mental health services.

resources.name: Peer Support & Social Groups for 2SLGBTQ+ Youth
resources.description: The Youth Project runs peer-led support and social groups for 2SLGBTQ+ youth across Nova Scotia, facilitated by trained staff and youth leaders with lived experience. These groups provide timely, identity-affirming peer support that addresses mental health stressors like isolation and stigma, offering an accessible alternative and complement to clinical services.

solutions.text: Community Health Navigator Program: Recruit and train navigators to help residents find providers, book appointments, enroll in services, and follow up on referrals, reducing missed appointments and accelerating care.

resources.name: Mobile Outreach Street Health (MOSH)
resources.description: MOSH is a street-based health program that helps people who are homeless or precariously housed navigate the health system. Its nurses and outreach team help clients find primary and specialty providers, book and accompany them to appointments, coordinate referrals, and follow up so care plans are completed—reducing missed appointments and speeding access to care.

resources.name: Health and Wellness Services (Health Navigation)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Health and Wellness team supports immigrants and refugees to navigate Nova Scotia’s health system. Staff help clients enroll in MSI, find family doctors and other providers, book medical and mental health appointments, arrange interpretation, and follow up on referrals to ensure services are accessed without delay.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Family Navigator Program (Mental Health and Addictions)
resources.description: The IWK Family Navigator helps families of children and youth with mental health and addictions concerns find and access the right care. Navigators assess needs, connect families to appropriate providers and community services, assist with appointment booking and referrals, and follow up to reduce wait-related drop-off and missed care.

resources.name: Cancer Patient Navigation Program (QEII Cancer Centre)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health, Cancer Care Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Cancer Patient Navigators guide individuals from diagnosis through treatment by coordinating appointments and referrals across oncology services. Navigators help patients understand their care plan, book tests and specialist visits, connect to supportive programs, and follow up to minimize missed appointments and accelerate timely care.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: Newcomer Health Clinic
resources.description: The Newcomer Health Clinic provides primary care and system navigation for government-assisted refugees and other newcomers when they arrive in Nova Scotia. The team helps patients get health cards, find ongoing primary care, book medical and mental health appointments, coordinate referrals, and follow up so transitions to community providers are seamless.

solutions.text: Mobile Clinic Days: Coordinate vans or pop-up clinics that bring primary care, immunizations and basic mental health screening to rural neighbourhoods on a rotating schedule.

resources.name: Mobile Primary Care Clinics (Province-wide)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health coordinates rotating pop-up and van-based primary care clinics that travel to communities across the province, with an emphasis on rural and underserviced areas. These clinics provide same-day assessment for common concerns, prescription renewals, basic testing, and on-site vaccinations (e.g., flu/COVID when available), and they include brief mental health screening with referrals to Mental Health & Addictions services, implementing the ‘Mobile Clinic Days’ model.

resources.name: Mobile Outreach Street Health (MOSH)
resources.description: MOSH operates mobile outreach vans and pop-up clinics that bring primary care, wound care, harm reduction, and mental health/addictions screening directly to shelters, encampments, and underserved neighbourhoods in the Halifax region. The team includes nurses, nurse practitioners, and outreach workers who provide on-site care, vaccinations (such as seasonal flu or hepatitis when available), and rapid mental health screening with navigation to ongoing services—delivering care where people live and gather in line with the ‘Mobile Clinic Days’ approach.

solutions.text: Centralized Community Booking Platform: Develop a user-friendly local appointment hub (phone + online) that aggregates available primary care and mental health slots from participating clinicians to reduce wait and travel.

resources.name: YourHealthNS
resources.description: YourHealthNS is Nova Scotia Health’s province-wide digital hub that consolidates appointment booking for a range of services, including primary care access clinics, mobile primary care clinics, and mental health and addictions walk-in options. Residents can search for nearby availability and self-book online, and the platform lists clinic-specific phone numbers for those who prefer to schedule by phone—centralizing access to open appointment slots across participating services to reduce wait times and unnecessary travel.

resources.name: VirtualCareNS
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health (in partnership with IWK Health and Maple)
resources.description: VirtualCareNS is a centralized online booking platform that connects Nova Scotians—especially those without a family doctor or nurse practitioner—to available virtual primary care appointments with participating physicians and nurse practitioners across the province. By aggregating clinician availability in one place and enabling remote visits, it shortens waits and eliminates travel; booking support is also available by phone through Nova Scotia Health access lines for people who need assistance.

resources.name: Mental Health & Addictions Program – Access & Intake (Nova Scotia Health)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Access & Intake service provides a single, province-wide entry point to mental health and addictions care, combining a toll‑free phone line (1‑855‑922‑1122) and online self-referral at mha.nshealth.ca. Intake navigators triage needs and directly book the first available appointment—virtual or at the nearest community clinic—by pulling from openings across participating clinicians and locations, reducing both wait times and travel for patients.

resources.name: IWK Mental Health and Addictions – Centralized Access and Intake
resources.description: The IWK’s Centralized Access and Intake offers a single point of contact for children, youth, and families to access mental health and addictions services, with referral and booking available by phone and through online forms. The service coordinates triage and schedules the first appointment with the appropriate clinician—either virtually or at community locations—by drawing from openings across IWK programs and partners, improving access and minimizing travel burden.

solutions.text: Community Paramedicine Expansion: Work with local EMS to expand community paramedicine visits for chronic disease monitoring, medication review and urgent-but-non-emergency care at home.

resources.name: EHS Extended Care Paramedic (ECP) Program
resources.organization: Emergency Health Services (EHS) Nova Scotia, delivered by Emergency Medical Care Inc. (Medavie Health Services Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Extended Care Paramedic program deploys specially trained paramedics to long-term care and community settings to assess and treat urgent-but-non-emergency issues on-site, helping residents avoid unnecessary emergency department transfers. ECPs perform point-of-care diagnostics, wound care, IV therapy, and medication reviews in consultation with physicians or nurse practitioners, supporting chronic disease management and timely care at home. This directly expands community paramedicine capacity to relieve pressure on primary care and hospital wait times.

resources.name: EHS Paramedics Providing Palliative Care at Home
resources.organization: Emergency Health Services (EHS) Nova Scotia, delivered by Emergency Medical Care Inc. (Medavie Health Services Nova Scotia)
resources.description: This program equips paramedics with advanced palliative competencies and access to individualized care plans so they can manage symptoms such as pain, dyspnea, and nausea in the patient’s home, in collaboration with local palliative and primary care teams. Paramedics conduct medication reviews, titrate therapies under standing orders, and honor care goals to minimize transfers and long waits in emergency departments. It exemplifies community paramedicine by delivering urgent, non-emergency care and supportive monitoring at home for people with advanced and chronic illnesses.

resources.name: EHS Special Patient Program (SPP)
resources.organization: Emergency Health Services (EHS) Nova Scotia, delivered by Emergency Medical Care Inc. (Medavie Health Services Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Special Patient Program enrolls individuals with complex or chronic conditions in advance and builds condition-specific care plans that responding paramedics can follow at home. When a 911 call occurs, paramedics access the patient’s protocol to provide targeted treatments, adjust medications in coordination with physicians, or arrange direct pathways that avoid emergency department delays. This proactive, community paramedicine model supports ongoing monitoring and urgent, non-emergent care in the home, improving access and continuity while reducing wait times.

solutions.text: School-based Mental Health Teams: Place counsellors and social workers in schools and provide youth mental health programming and early intervention to reduce later specialist demand.

resources.name: SchoolsPlus (Halifax Regional Centre for Education)
resources.description: SchoolsPlus in HRCE embeds SchoolsPlus facilitators and community outreach workers in hub schools and connects on‑site mental health clinicians from IWK Health/Nova Scotia Health to provide services where students learn. Teams offer early identification, brief counselling, group programming (e.g., anxiety management, coping skills), and coordinated referrals for youth and families. By delivering supports in schools and triaging to community services, the program reduces demand on specialist clinics and emergency care.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: SchoolsPlus (Chignecto Central Regional Centre for Education)
resources.organization: Chignecto Central Regional Centre for Education
resources.description: CCRCE’s SchoolsPlus program operates hub sites across Colchester, Cumberland, and Pictou counties with school-based teams that include facilitators, outreach workers, and partnered mental health clinicians. These teams provide on‑site counselling, skill‑building groups, and rapid connection to community services to support early intervention. Bringing mental health supports into schools reduces barriers to access and helps decrease later demand for specialized services.

resources.name: SchoolsPlus (South Shore Regional Centre for Education)
resources.organization: South Shore Regional Centre for Education
resources.description: SSRCE’s SchoolsPlus integrates school-based facilitators and community outreach workers with Nova Scotia Health/IWK clinicians to deliver mental health supports directly in Lunenburg and Queens County schools. Services include early assessment, brief counselling, group programs, and family navigation to community resources. The school‑embedded model provides timely help and reduces reliance on hospital-based and specialist services.

resources.name: SchoolsPlus Mental Health Clinicians (IWK Health)
resources.description: IWK Health places Mental Health & Addictions clinicians within SchoolsPlus hubs in HRM and surrounding areas to deliver school‑based assessment, brief therapy, and group programming. Clinicians collaborate with educators and school social workers to identify concerns early and connect youth to appropriate care pathways. Locating clinicians in schools improves access and helps reduce wait times for hospital‑based specialty services.

solutions.text: Peer-led Crisis & Warm Line: Establish a community-run non-clinical crisis/warm line staffed by trained peers for after-hours emotional support and triage to appropriate services.

resources.name: Peer Support Phone Service
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health – Peer Support Nova Scotia (Mental Health & Addictions Program)
resources.description: A non-clinical warm line staffed by trained peer supporters with lived experience of mental health and/or substance use, offering empathetic listening, validation, and problem-solving support. The service provides evening and weekend coverage to complement daytime services, helps callers de-escalate distress, and triages or connects people to appropriate community and health resources across Nova Scotia. It directly reduces pressure on emergency and clinical services by offering accessible, after-hours peer support.

resources.name: Caregiver Support Line
resources.description: A province-wide, non-clinical support line where trained peer support coordinators (many with lived caregiving experience) offer emotional support, active listening, and practical navigation to local services. While not crisis counselling, it functions as a warm line that helps caregivers manage stress, identify next steps, and connect to community resources, thereby easing reliance on overburdened clinical systems. The service provides timely, person-centered peer support that can prevent escalation to urgent care.

solutions.text: Community Training for Mental Health First Aid: Offer regular, subsidized mental health first-aid and suicide prevention training to teachers, employers, faith leaders and community volunteers to increase early help.

resources.name: Mental Health First Aid (MHFA) – Nova Scotia
resources.organization: St. John Ambulance Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island Council
resources.description: St. John Ambulance delivers accredited Mental Health First Aid courses across Nova Scotia for workplaces, schools, faith groups and community organizations. The training equips teachers, employers, faith leaders and volunteers to recognize signs of mental health problems or crisis (including suicide risk), provide initial support, and connect people to professional services—helping communities offer early help while reducing pressure on clinical waitlists.
resources.address: 72 Highfield Park Drive, Unit 121, Dartmouth, NS B3A 4X2

resources.name: Psychological First Aid (PFA) Training – Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross offers Psychological First Aid courses online and in-person that teach community members how to recognize distress, provide supportive listening, and link people to appropriate resources. Organizations can book group sessions for staff and volunteers, helping non-clinical gatekeepers offer early, culturally safe support and navigation for those experiencing mental health challenges or suicidal thoughts while awaiting formal care.

resources.name: In the Know – Mental Health Literacy for Agriculture
resources.organization: Farm Safety Nova Scotia (a program of the Nova Scotia Federation of Agriculture)
resources.description: Farm Safety Nova Scotia provides ‘In the Know,’ an evidence‑informed mental health literacy program tailored for farmers, farm families, and agricultural employers. Sessions build skills to recognize mental health and suicide risk, start supportive conversations, and connect peers to services—bringing practical, early-help training directly to rural workplaces and volunteer networks where access to care can be limited.
resources.address: 60 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

solutions.text: Ride & Access Volunteer Program: Create a volunteer driver network and transit vouchers to ensure residents can attend appointments on time and reduce missed care due to transport barriers.

resources.name: Wheels of Hope Transportation Service (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Canadian Cancer Society’s Wheels of Hope recruits and coordinates volunteer drivers to provide door-to-door rides for people attending cancer-related medical appointments across Nova Scotia. By scheduling reliable pick-ups and returns and covering travel logistics, the program ensures clients arrive on time and do not miss critical care due to transportation barriers—an exact fit with a volunteer driver network solution.

resources.name: Kings Point-to-Point Transit
resources.description: Kings Point-to-Point Transit provides pre-booked, door-to-door rides throughout Kings County, with a strong focus on transportation to medical, mental health, and specialist appointments. By coordinating community drivers and accessible vehicles and offering fare assistance through partner programs, they function as a practical ride network that reduces missed care caused by transportation gaps.
resources.address: 14 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

resources.name: Transportation Assistance (Bus Tickets and Vouchers)
resources.description: The North End Community Health Centre helps clients overcome cost and mobility barriers by providing transportation assistance—such as bus tickets and taxi vouchers—to get to primary care, mental health, and specialist appointments. Staff and outreach teams coordinate transport supports so patients can arrive on time and maintain continuity of care, directly implementing the transit-voucher component of the solution.

solutions.text: Local Specialist Referral Coordination: Volunteer or staff a community-based referral coordinator who follows up on waitlists, seeks cancellations and connects patients to alternate local resources.

resources.name: Mental Health & Addictions Access and Navigation
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health – Mental Health & Addictions Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s province-wide Access & Navigation service provides centralized intake and navigation for mental health and addictions. Navigators review referrals, triage to the most appropriate local clinic or program, and maintain contact to help clients manage wait times. They connect people with alternate local and virtual resources and can move clients into earlier appointments when cancellations occur.

resources.name: Mental Health & Addictions Central Referral Service (Children, Youth and Families)
resources.description: IWK Health’s central referral service coordinates access to child, youth and family mental health and addictions services across hospital and community partners. Intake clinicians and navigators contact families to screen and prioritize referrals, manage clinic waitlists, and offer appointments including short-notice cancellations. They also connect families to community and school-based supports to bridge care while waiting.

resources.name: Cancer Patient Navigation Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health – Cancer Care Program (Cancer Care Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Cancer Patient Navigation Program assigns local navigators to help people with suspected or confirmed cancer move through diagnostics and specialty care. Navigators coordinate referrals among primary care, diagnostic services, and cancer centres, monitor for cancellations or earlier openings, and troubleshoot delays. They also connect patients to local supports such as transportation, financial assistance, and psychosocial resources while awaiting appointments.

resources.name: Hip and Knee Central Intake and Orthopedic Assessment Clinics
resources.description: This program provides a single-entry referral pathway for hip and knee care across Nova Scotia. Coordinators and advanced practice clinicians triage referrals, manage surgeon and clinic waitlists across multiple sites, proactively contact patients about cancellations, and offer transfers to providers with shorter waits. They also connect patients to prehabilitation, physiotherapy, and community resources while they await specialist or surgical care.

solutions.text: Community-funded NP / Physician Incentives: Raise local incentives such as relocation support, temporary housing, childcare assistance or signing bonuses funded by municipalities, businesses and community groups to attract clinicians.

resources.name: Physician Recruitment Incentive Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg offers a community-funded signing bonus (publicly announced up to $150,000) to family physicians who establish practice locally, with funds approved by municipal council and supported by community partners. The program also assists with relocation logistics and community settlement (such as housing search and spousal employment connections), directly implementing community-backed incentives to attract clinicians.

resources.name: Physician Recruitment and Retention Program
resources.description: Region of Queens Municipality provides community-funded incentives, including substantial signing bonuses and tailored relocation support, to recruit and retain family physicians and other primary care providers. The program coordinates temporary housing options and community integration supports, using municipal funding and local partnerships to reduce barriers for clinicians moving to the area.
resources.address: 249 White Point Road, Liverpool, NS B0T 1K0

resources.name: Healthcare Recruitment Initiative
resources.description: The Municipality of Barrington delivers a community-backed recruitment initiative that includes a multi-year signing bonus for physicians, relocation assistance, and access to temporary housing arranged by the municipality. Funded by the municipality with support from local community partners, the program actively markets the area and provides on-the-ground settlement help to attract clinicians.

resources.name: Antigonish Physician Recruitment
resources.description: The Antigonish Physician Recruitment Committee, supported by municipal partners and the St. Martha’s Regional Hospital Foundation, offers community-funded incentives, including signing bonuses and relocation support, to attract family physicians. The team also assists with temporary housing, spousal/partner employment connections, and community and school/childcare navigation to make settling in Antigonish easier for clinicians.

solutions.text: Clinical Placement Partnerships with Universities: Partner with nearby nursing and medical schools to host student placements locally, expanding supervised workforce capacity and building future recruitment pipelines.

resources.name: Dalhousie Family Medicine Residency Program – Annapolis Valley Site
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Medicine, Department of Family Medicine
resources.description: This two-year residency site trains family medicine residents in partnership with Nova Scotia Health at Valley Regional Hospital and affiliated community clinics across the Annapolis Valley. Residents provide supervised primary care and hospital-based services, which expands local care capacity while building a pipeline of physicians who often choose to stay and practice in the region.

resources.name: Dalhousie Family Medicine Residency Program – North Nova Site
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Medicine, Department of Family Medicine
resources.description: Based at Colchester East Hants Health Centre and partnering community practices, this site hosts family medicine residents who deliver supervised primary care and inpatient services in Truro and surrounding areas. The placements increase immediate clinical capacity and foster long-term recruitment by immersing trainees in local teams and communities.

resources.name: Dalhousie Family Medicine Residency Program – South West Nova Site
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Medicine, Department of Family Medicine
resources.description: In collaboration with Yarmouth Regional Hospital and community clinics, this site places family medicine residents in supervised rotations across primary care, emergency, and inpatient settings. These partnerships both bolster day-to-day service capacity in rural communities and create strong recruitment pathways for graduates to remain in South West Nova.

resources.name: IWK Health – Clinical Learning and Practice Development
resources.description: IWK Health partners with Dalhousie University and other Atlantic Canadian schools to host nursing, medical, and allied health student placements across women’s, children’s, and mental health services. Through supervised clinical experiences, learners contribute to service delivery today while IWK builds a talent pipeline to recruit future clinicians to Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Community Pharmacy Clinical Services: Work with local pharmacies to expand services (vaccination, medication reviews, minor ailment prescribing where permitted) and advertise these options widely.

resources.name: Lawtons Pharmacy Services – Scotia Square
resources.description: Lawtons pharmacists at Scotia Square provide clinical services including publicly funded assessments and prescribing for many minor ailments permitted in Nova Scotia, routine and seasonal vaccinations (e.g., influenza and COVID-19), and comprehensive medication reviews for eligible patients. They implement the solution by expanding access to primary care through same-day pharmacist consultations and by widely promoting these options via their website and in‑store signage, helping reduce pressure on family practices and wait times.

resources.name: Shoppers Drug Mart Health & Pharmacy Services – Park Lane Mall
resources.description: This Shoppers Drug Mart location offers pharmacist-led clinical services such as vaccinations, medication reviews, and assessment/prescribing for common minor ailments under Nova Scotia’s scope of practice. By providing convenient walk-in and appointment-based care and promoting these services online and in stores, they help residents access timely care for non-urgent needs, alleviating strain on clinics and improving overall access.
resources.address: 5657 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 3R4

resources.name: Walmart Pharmacy Clinical Services – Bayers Lake
resources.description: Walmart Pharmacy in Bayers Lake provides vaccinations, medication reviews, and pharmacist assessments for minor ailments allowed in Nova Scotia, enabling prompt treatment without a physician visit. These services are prominently advertised through Walmart’s pharmacy webpages and in-store materials, expanding awareness and helping patients access primary care more quickly.
resources.address: 220 Chain Lake Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 1C5

resources.name: Costco Pharmacy Services – Halifax (Bayers Lake)
resources.description: Costco’s Halifax pharmacy offers immunizations (such as flu and COVID-19), medication reviews, and pharmacist management/prescribing for select minor ailments within Nova Scotia’s scope, providing an alternative access point for timely care. The pharmacy promotes these services via its online pharmacy portal and member communications, helping residents understand and use pharmacist-led care options.
resources.address: 230 Chain Lake Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 1C5

solutions.text: Culturally Safe and Indigenous-led Services: Support local Indigenous and cultural organizations to develop culturally safe primary and mental health services to improve access for under-served populations.

resources.name: Health & Wellness Program
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Health & Wellness Program provides culturally safe, Indigenous-led supports for urban Indigenous people, including mental health counselling, harm reduction, Elders’ support, and health navigation. The program also hosts visiting primary care clinics and outreach in partnership with local providers, ensuring care is grounded in Mi’kmaw culture, language, and ceremony to reduce barriers and improve timely access for underserved youth and families.

resources.name: National Native Alcohol and Drug Abuse Program (NNADAP)
resources.description: The Native Council of Nova Scotia delivers NNADAP and related community health services for off-reserve and non‑status Indigenous people across the province. Through culturally grounded addictions counselling, mental wellness programming, and navigation/referrals to family physicians, nurse practitioners, and other primary care, the program creates culturally safe access points that close gaps in mental health and primary care for Indigenous community members.
resources.address: 129 Truro Heights Road, Truro, NS B6L 1X1

solutions.text: Community Wellness Hubs: Convert available municipal or nonprofit space into multi-service hubs offering primary care screening, counselling, social supports, and healthy living programs in one place.

resources.name: Cobequid Community Health Centre
resources.description: A community-based, multi-service health hub that brings primary care, mental health and addictions services, public health, and wellness programs together under one roof. Residents can access primary care screening, counselling, lab services, and health promotion programming in a single, accessible location—reducing wait times and navigation barriers consistent with the community wellness hub model.
resources.address: 40 Freer Lane, Lower Sackville, NS B4C 0A2

resources.name: Western Kings Memorial Health Centre
resources.description: This centre functions as a local wellness hub by co-locating a collaborative family practice, mental health and addictions services, public health, and chronic disease management (e.g., diabetes education, nutrition). Community members can receive screening, counselling, social supports, and healthy living classes in one place, improving timely access to care and supports.

resources.name: Clare Health Centre (Centre de santé de Clare)
resources.description: A bilingual, community health centre that integrates a collaborative family practice with on-site lab services, chronic disease management, dietitian support, and mental health and addictions outreach. By offering coordinated primary care screening, counselling, and wellness programming in one community facility, it operates as a comprehensive wellness hub for residents of Clare and surrounding areas.
resources.address: 30 Hôpital Road, Meteghan Centre, NS B0W 2K0

resources.name: Sheet Harbour and Area Primary Health Care Centre
resources.description: A rural multi-service hub that co-locates collaborative family practice, mental health and addictions services, public health, and blood collection, with access to health promotion and navigation supports. The centre enables residents to obtain primary care screening, counselling, and healthy living programs in one accessible site, addressing access and wait-time challenges on the Eastern Shore.

solutions.text: Local Workforce Scholarships & Return Incentives: Fund scholarships, bursaries or guaranteed job placements for local students who commit to returning to practice in the community after training, focusing on nursing, counselling and allied health.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Learn and Stay Grant
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Advanced Education (Nova Scotia Student Assistance)
resources.description: The Learn and Stay Grant covers tuition and mandatory fees for Nova Scotia students in high-need health programs (e.g., registered nursing, licensed practical nursing, and paramedicine) in exchange for a formal return‑of‑service commitment to work in the province, often in the community where they trained. By tying financial support to a post‑graduation service obligation, the grant directly grows the local nursing and allied health workforce and helps reduce wait times in underserved areas.

resources.name: Nursing Incentives — Return-of-Service Bursaries and Tuition Support
resources.organization: Office of Healthcare Professionals Recruitment, Department of Health and Wellness (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: This provincial program provides bursaries and tuition supports for nursing students and new graduates (RNs, LPNs, and NPs) who sign return‑of‑service agreements to work in Nova Scotia, with priority for high‑need placements in primary care, mental health, and rural communities. The incentives combine financial aid with guaranteed job offers upon graduation, ensuring locally trained nurses return to practice in Nova Scotia to strengthen access and reduce wait times.

resources.name: Clinical Psychology Student Bursary – Mental Health & Addictions (Return‑of‑Service)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health, Mental Health & Addictions Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health offers bursaries to graduate clinical psychology students and residents who commit to a defined return‑of‑service in the Mental Health & Addictions Program after training, including placements in underserved zones. This model offsets training costs while guaranteeing roles in Nova Scotia, expanding access to counselling and psychological services and helping to shorten mental health wait times.

resources.name: Allied Health Student Bursary Program (Return‑of‑Service)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health provides bursaries for students in allied health fields—such as medical laboratory technology, diagnostic imaging, respiratory therapy, and pharmacy—who agree to return to work for a specified term after graduation, with emphasis on rural and high‑need sites. The funding is tied to service commitments and job placement, directly increasing diagnostic and therapeutic capacity that underpins shorter wait times and improved access to care.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

obstacles.title: Skills Mismatch and Training Alignment
obstacles.description: Education and apprenticeship pipelines do not consistently match emerging industry needs; limited work-integrated learning.

solutions.text: Community-Industry Skills Councils: Create local councils of employers, educators, training providers, labour and Indigenous and community representatives to identify emergent skills needs, co-design curricula and coordinate local apprenticeship and placement opportunities.

resources.name: Program Advisory Committees (PACs)
resources.description: NSCC’s Program Advisory Committees bring together employers, industry associations, labour, Mi’kmaw/Indigenous and community representatives with faculty to review labour market trends and emerging skills needs. These councils co-design and update curricula and micro-credentials, and help coordinate co-ops, clinical/practicum placements, and apprenticeship pathways with local employers across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: COVE Workforce Initiative
resources.description: COVE convenes ocean-sector employers, NSCC, Dalhousie, training providers, and community/Indigenous partners in working groups and advisory forums to identify critical skills gaps in the blue economy. Through these councils, COVE helps co-develop curriculum and short courses and brokers student co-ops, internships, and apprenticeship-style placements with member companies.

resources.name: Ocean Technology Council of Nova Scotia (OTCNS)
resources.organization: Ocean Technology Council of Nova Scotia
resources.description: OTCNS functions as a sector council for the ocean technology industry, organizing employer roundtables and HR working groups with post-secondary and training partners to define competency needs and align programs. The council informs curriculum updates at NSCC and universities and connects learners to employers through initiatives like industry-led projects, co-ops, and work placements.

resources.name: Faculty of Computer Science Industry Advisory Council
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Industry Advisory Council brings together tech employers, startups, public sector leaders, and faculty to identify emerging digital skills needs and advise on curriculum and program direction. The council collaborates with the faculty’s co-op and experiential learning teams to coordinate internships, capstone projects, and placements that align with Nova Scotia’s digital economy.

solutions.text: Expand Work-Integrated Learning Placements: Coordinate short-term co-ops, micro-internships and job-shadow placements with small businesses, nonprofits and public institutions so youth and career-changers gain real experience tied to local employer needs.

resources.name: Management Career Services (Co-op and Internship)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Management Career Services coordinates paid co-op work terms, internships and short project-based placements with small businesses, nonprofits and public-sector employers across Nova Scotia. Staff actively cultivate employer partnerships and match students to roles aligned with current business needs, giving youth practical, locally relevant experience and strengthening the talent pipeline in the province.
resources.address: Kenneth C. Rowe Management Building, 6100 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: NSCC Work-Integrated Learning (Co-op, Internship and Applied Learning)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College embeds co-ops, practicums, internships and job-shadow experiences across programs in trades, IT, health, business and creative industries. Employer engagement teams coordinate short-term placements with small businesses, community nonprofits and public institutions throughout Nova Scotia, aligning training with real job requirements and supporting both youth and career-changers.

resources.name: Acadia Co-operative Education
resources.description: Acadia’s Co-op program arranges paid work terms with employers in the private, public and nonprofit sectors—many across the Annapolis Valley and Halifax—so students gain experience directly tied to regional needs. The team brokers placements ranging from short-term terms to multi-term co-ops, enabling youth to build in-demand skills while supporting the capacity of local organizations.

resources.name: Clean Leaders
resources.description: Clean Leaders places youth (ages 15–30) in paid summer jobs and micro-placements with municipalities, community groups and small businesses working on environmental projects across Nova Scotia. The program coordinates host-site placements, provides job-readiness training and facilitates mentoring/job shadowing, delivering hands-on experience aligned to the province’s growing green economy.

resources.name: Co-operative Education Incentive (CEI)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: CEI is a provincial wage-subsidy program that helps Nova Scotia employers—including small businesses, startups and nonprofits—hire co-op students for 12–16 week work terms. By offsetting costs and working with post-secondary co-op offices to validate roles, the initiative expands the volume of short-term, work-integrated learning placements aligned with employer skill needs across the province.
resources.address: Maritime Centre, 1505 Barrington Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

solutions.text: Community Training Hubs: Establish multi-use local hubs (shared workshops, labs and classrooms) that deliver modular, evening and weekend courses and hands-on practice in trades and emerging tech, co-funded by municipalities and employers.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: The Halifax Tool Library is a community workshop and lending hub located inside Veith House. It delivers evening and weekend, modular workshops in woodworking, home repair, bicycle maintenance, and maker skills, giving residents hands-on practice using shared tools and shop space. The Library is sustained by member fees, municipal community grants, and local employer sponsorships, aligning training with practical trade skills and employer needs.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Lou Duggan Creative Studio is a multi-use maker lab with equipment like 3D printers, sewing machines, electronics benches, and media tools. The Studio hosts free and low-cost evening and weekend classes and drop-ins in digital fabrication, coding, and design, providing hands-on, modular learning for all ages. As a municipally funded space that partners with local employers and community groups for programming, it functions as a community training hub that builds tech and creative skills aligned with industry needs.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Yarmouth Innovation Hub & Makerspace
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic operates a community innovation hub and makerspace that provides shared labs, prototyping equipment, and classrooms in downtown Yarmouth. It runs modular workshops, bootcamps, and employer-partnered challenges in areas like 3D printing, robotics, electronics, and entrepreneurship—often scheduled on evenings and weekends to broaden access. The hub is supported by municipal partners and industry sponsors, directly connecting participants with employers and hands-on practice in emerging technologies.

resources.name: NSCC Continuing Education (Ivany Campus)
resources.description: NSCC’s Ivany Campus offers part-time Continuing Education and micro-credential courses in trades and emerging technologies using the college’s shops, labs, and classrooms. Many courses run evenings and weekends and are designed with employer advisory committees, giving learners hands-on, work-integrated practice aligned to local industry demand. NSCC programs are delivered with industry partnerships and public funders, with campuses collaborating with municipalities and employers to equip labs and deliver community-focused training.

solutions.text: Employer Apprenticeship Consortium: Form consortia where small employers pool resources to sponsor and mentor apprentices, share journeyperson supervision, and jointly apply for wage supports to expand on-the-job training capacity.

resources.name: Group Sponsor Model (Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency enables formal Group Sponsor agreements in which several small employers jointly register and sponsor apprentices, rotate placements, and share journeyperson supervision. This pooled approach centralizes administration and mentoring while helping employers collectively access wage supports (e.g., START) and other incentives to expand on‑the‑job training capacity. By aligning employers in a consortium, the program improves work‑integrated learning and better matches apprenticeship pathways to emerging industry needs across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: UA Local 56 Joint Apprenticeship & Training Program
resources.description: UA Local 56 operates a multi‑employer apprenticeship consortium for plumbing, steamfitting/pipefitting, and related Red Seal trades, indenturing apprentices centrally and dispatching them to many small signatory contractors. The joint training trust shares journeyperson supervision, coordinates mentorship and rotations across employers, and supports contractors and apprentices in securing provincial wage incentives and training supports. This multi‑employer model expands on‑the‑job training capacity and ensures skills development stays aligned with industry demand in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 14 McQuade Lake Crescent, Halifax, NS B3S 1B6

resources.name: Atlantic Canada Regional Council (Carpenters Local 83) – Joint Apprenticeship & Training
resources.organization: Atlantic Canada Regional Council of Carpenters, Millwrights and Allied Workers (Local 83 – NS)
resources.description: The ACRC’s Nova Scotia training centre runs a joint, multi‑employer apprenticeship system for carpenters and allied trades, placing apprentices with numerous small contractors under shared journeyperson supervision. Through centralized registration, rotation, and mentoring, the council pools employer resources and helps members leverage provincial wage supports to increase on‑the‑job training opportunities. This consortium model strengthens work‑integrated learning and keeps apprenticeship training responsive to current construction sector needs.
resources.address: 1000 Lucasville Road, Hammonds Plains, NS B4B 1P7

solutions.text: Local Labour Market Dashboard: Build a simple community-managed dashboard publishing timely local hiring trends, in-demand occupations and training pathways so residents, schools and employers can align programs to demand.

resources.name: Explore Careers Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration (Nova Scotia Works)
resources.description: Explore Careers Nova Scotia is a public labour market information dashboard that aggregates real-time job postings, occupational outlooks, wages, and regional hiring trends across the province. It connects in-demand occupations to training pathways by linking to relevant NSCC, university, and apprenticeship programs, helping residents, schools, and employers align education and work-integrated learning with current and emerging labour demand.
resources.address: One Government Place, 1700 Granville Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1X5

resources.name: Halifax Index and Labour Market Snapshot
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership publishes the Halifax Index and a monthly Labour Market Snapshot that function as a local dashboard tracking hiring trends, unemployment, sectoral demand, in-demand occupations, and population flows for the Halifax region. These open, regularly updated insights help educators, workforce programs, and employers coordinate training and recruitment to match real-time local needs, with links to employer initiatives and talent programs that create pathways into priority roles.
resources.address: 1969 Upper Water Street, Suite 2001, Halifax, NS B3J 3R7

solutions.text: Mentorship and Alumni Networks: Organize volunteer mentor programs that connect experienced local workers, tradespeople and returning alumni with youth and newcomers for career guidance, mock interviews and workplace visits.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program links recent graduates and newcomers with experienced local professionals for one-on-one informational interviews and networking introductions. Volunteer 'Connectors' share sector insights, review resumes, and introduce participants to at least three additional contacts, helping align skills with employer needs through real-world conversations and workplace exposure.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS matches internationally trained professionals and other newcomers with established local mentors working in their field for several months of guided mentorship. Mentors provide career guidance, mock interview practice, and networking support, often facilitating workplace visits or introductions that help mentees better understand Nova Scotia’s labour market and employer expectations.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Techsploration Program
resources.description: Techsploration connects young women and gender-diverse youth with volunteer role models from trades and technology sectors through school-based mentoring teams, workplace visits, and job-shadowing days. Participants receive hands-on exposure, career guidance, and mock interview-style interactions that bridge classroom learning with the skills and opportunities employers need across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 133 Troop Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2A7

resources.name: Dal Alumni Link (Mentoring Program)
resources.description: Dal Alumni Link pairs Dalhousie students and recent graduates with alumni mentors for career conversations, resume reviews, and industry-specific guidance.
