Through structured coffee chats and networking, mentors help mentees prepare for interviews, explore workplace expectations, and build connections that align academic training with Nova Scotia’s evolving job market.

resources.name: SMU Alumni Mentoring (Ten Thousand Coffees)
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University (Alumni Engagement & Career and Experiential Learning)
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University connects students and recent alumni with experienced SMU graduates for one-on-one mentoring, informational interviews, and career advice via the Ten Thousand Coffees platform. Volunteers provide sector insights, resume and interview preparation, and may facilitate workplace introductions that help learners align their skills with employer demands in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Stackable Micro-credentials and Badges: Partner local colleges and employers to offer short, industry-recognized modules and digital badges that stack toward certificates or credit, enabling faster alignment with evolving skills needs.

resources.name: NSCC Microcredentials and Digital Badges
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College offers short, industry-recognized micro-credentials that confer portable digital badges for discrete competencies co-designed with employer advisory partners across sectors such as ICT, oceans, and the skilled trades. Learners can stack multiple badges toward college micro-certificates and, in many cases, apply them as credit or recognition of prior learning toward certificates and diplomas. Offerings are frequently project-based or work-integrated and are updated rapidly to align with Nova Scotia employers’ evolving needs.

resources.name: Open Learning & Career Development Micro-credentials
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Open Learning & Career Development delivers micro-credentials and digital badges that verify job-ready skills co-designed with employers and professional associations in fields like data, health, and management. These short modules are stackable into micro-certificates and, where applicable, can be applied toward continuing education certificates or academic credit under Nova Scotia’s micro-credential framework. Programs emphasize applied projects and work-integrated elements to address regional skills gaps and accelerate alignment with employer demand.

resources.name: CBU Micro-credentials and Digital Badges
resources.description: Cape Breton University offers micro-credentials that award digital badges for short, skills-focused learning developed with local employers in sectors such as tourism, clean energy, and community health. Learners can stack badges into micro-certificates or apply them toward credit recognition in select programs, creating flexible pathways to credentials. The approach enables rapid upskilling and employer-aligned training that supports youth employment and retention across Cape Breton and rural Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Micro-credentials
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University provides micro-credentials through the Sobey School of Business and Continuing Education that issue digital badges for verified competencies valued by local industry partners. These short modules are stackable into micro-certificates or professional certificates, with some pathways recognized for academic credit or advanced standing. Programs emphasize applied projects and employer engagement to close skills gaps in business, technology, and entrepreneurship in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: School-Industry Experiential Days: Run regular career taster days, maker fairs and in-school project challenges where students work on real employer problems and see pathways into trades, tech, arts and community services.

resources.name: STEM Career Days and Industry Partner Programs
resources.description: The Discovery Centre hosts hands-on STEM career days, maker-style workshops, and employer-partnered exhibits that bring real workplace technologies and problems into a student-friendly environment. Partner organizations from sectors like energy, oceans, and digital tech lead interactive stations and challenges, helping students see clear pathways into trades, technology, arts-related design/STEAM, and community services.
resources.address: 1215 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

resources.name: Student Ocean Tech Experiences and H2O Conference Student Day
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE convenes employers and students for experiential ocean-technology programming, including student-focused days at the H2O: Home to Overseas Conference and on-site tours of the facility’s labs and test tank. Youth engage directly with ocean-tech companies through demos and problem-based activities, illustrating career pathways in marine trades, engineering, data/AI, and blue-economy community services.

resources.name: FIRST LEGO League Nova Scotia (Acadia Robotics)
resources.organization: Acadia University (Jodrey School of Computer Science)
resources.description: Acadia Robotics delivers FIRST LEGO League in Nova Scotia, where student teams tackle real-world themed challenges (e.g., energy, cities, health) through design, coding, and engineering. The program integrates mentorship from engineers and industry volunteers and hosts showcase days and tournaments, providing career taster experiences and clear pathways into technology, engineering, and related trades.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (in partnership with industry and education)
resources.description: BFY connects high school students with the construction sector through employer site visits, safety and skills bootcamps, and paid summer work placements that can count toward apprenticeship hours. The program aligns school learning with industry needs by letting youth work on real employer projects and experience trades careers first-hand, clarifying pathways into apprenticeship and skilled trades.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs Hackathons and Industry Innovation Challenges
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Computer Science (ShiftKey Labs)
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs hosts hackathons, design sprints, and innovation challenges where student teams collaborate with Nova Scotian employers and public-sector partners to solve real problems. These events serve as career taster days and project-based experiences that reveal pathways into software, data, health tech, oceans tech, and social innovation roles across the province.

solutions.text: Micro-grants for Employer-Based Training: Offer small community grants to help local businesses purchase training equipment, host trainees or subsidize mentor time—reducing barriers for employers to take on learners.

resources.name: Canada–Nova Scotia Job Grant (CNSJG)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Canada–Nova Scotia Job Grant provides cost-shared grants to employers to purchase short-term, third‑party training for new or existing employees, directly offsetting tuition, trainer fees, and training materials. By lowering out-of-pocket training costs for businesses, the program enables employers to align upskilling with real job requirements and take on learners with less risk, directly addressing skills mismatch and strengthening work‑integrated learning.

resources.name: Workplace Innovation and Productivity Skills Incentive (WIPSI)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: WIPSI funds employer-led training that improves productivity and innovation, covering eligible costs such as tuition, trainer fees, and training materials for groups of employees or sector cohorts. These micro- to mid-sized grants reduce the financial barrier for companies—especially SMEs—to deliver customized, on-the-job training, helping employers mentor staff and adopt skills that match evolving industry needs.

resources.name: Co-operative Education Incentive (CEI)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: CEI provides wage subsidies to employers to create paid co-op positions for post-secondary students, offsetting the costs of hosting trainees and supervising/mentoring them on the job. By reducing employer costs, CEI expands high-quality, work-integrated learning placements that connect education with real workplace skills in Nova Scotia firms.

resources.name: START Program (Employer Hiring Incentive)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The START program offers financial incentives to employers to hire and train unemployed or underemployed Nova Scotians, including wage subsidies and supports for on-the-job training and mentorship. These flexible employer-based funds reduce the cost of onboarding learners, helping businesses dedicate mentor time and align training with role-specific skill needs.

solutions.text: Newcomer and Indigenous Pathway Programs: Deliver targeted bridging programs that recognize foreign credentials, include cultural competency components and link Indigenous youth and newcomers to apprenticeship, mentorship and employer networks.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program pairs internationally trained newcomers with established professionals in their field to build networks, understand Canadian workplace culture, and accelerate entry into commensurate employment. Participants receive guidance on credential recognition and licensing pathways, while mentors and staff facilitate introductions to employers and sector associations, implementing the solution’s emphasis on mentorship, cultural competency, and employer linkages.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding for Indigenous Students
resources.description: This NSCC cohort-based pathway, developed with Mi’kmaw community partners and Irving Shipbuilding, provides academic upgrading, trades training and wraparound cultural supports that prepare Indigenous learners for careers in shipbuilding trades. The program includes work-integrated learning and direct connections to journeyperson mentors and employer networks at the Halifax Shipyard, creating clear pre-apprenticeship and apprenticeship pathways aligned to industry demand.

resources.name: Employment & Training Program
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Employment & Training Program supports Indigenous youth and adults with individualized employment planning, essential skills upgrading, certifications, and culturally grounded programming. Staff link participants to apprenticeships, mentorships, and local employer networks (often in partnership with NSCC, unions and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency), aligning training with labour market needs while embedding cultural competency and community support.

resources.name: Bachelor of Science, Nursing (Internationally Educated Nurses – IEN)
resources.description: CBU’s IEN program is a tailored bridging pathway that assesses prior nursing education and practice, provides gap training in Canadian standards and cultural safety, and prepares internationally educated nurses for Nova Scotia licensure. The curriculum integrates clinical placements and preceptorships with Nova Scotia Health, directly connecting newcomers to employer networks and mentored, work‑integrated learning that speeds entry into the local workforce.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

solutions.text: Remote Upskilling and Digital Access Centers: Provide community centres with reliable broadband, devices and coaching to enable residents to access online upskilling, virtual co-ops and remote work opportunities tied to local economic needs.

resources.name: Halifax Central Library – Digital Access and Learning Services
resources.description: Halifax Central Library provides free high‑speed Wi‑Fi, public computers, device lending, and one‑on‑one tech help so residents can access online training platforms, build digital literacy, and complete certifications. The library regularly hosts job-seeker workshops and employer/info sessions, and offers quiet, bookable spaces for virtual interviews and remote work, directly enabling online upskilling and pathways into local opportunities.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works – Job Junction
resources.description: Job Junction operates as a community employment centre with free computers, reliable broadband, printing, and private rooms to support online courses, virtual interviews, and remote job search. Career practitioners provide coaching on digital tools, resumes, and certifications, and connect clients to employer needs in the local labour market through virtual job fairs, workshops, and work‑integrated learning opportunities.
resources.address: 6950 Mumford Road, Suite 140, Halifax, NS B3L 4W1

resources.name: McConnell Library – Technology Access and Training
resources.description: The McConnell Library offers public computers, robust Wi‑Fi, and staff-led digital literacy support that help residents enroll in and complete online upskilling, industry-recognized courses, and other e-learning. It hosts tech help sessions and community workshops, and provides spaces for virtual meetings and interviews, enabling remote work readiness linked to Cape Breton’s evolving economy.

resources.name: Lunenburg Library – Digital Literacy and Job Support
resources.description: Lunenburg Library provides free broadband, public computers, and one‑on‑one tech coaching so residents can access online courses, develop digital skills, and complete remote training and certifications. Through partnerships and in‑library programs, it supports job seekers with resume help, digital tools, and spaces for virtual interviews, connecting learners to opportunities in South Shore’s local industries.

solutions.text: Youth Entrepreneurship and Social-Enterprise Incubator: Support local startups and social enterprises with shared workspace, business training and connections to trades and creative mentors so entrepreneurial pathways complement traditional employment routes.

resources.name: Volta
resources.description: Volta is a startup hub in downtown Halifax that provides shared co-working and office space, founder programming, and hands-on mentorship from experienced entrepreneurs and industry experts. Through workshops, accelerator-style training, and a broad mentor network spanning tech, creative, and business trades, it helps young founders build viable ventures. This directly supports entrepreneurial pathways alongside traditional employment by offering practical skills development and work-integrated learning opportunities.

resources.name: CEED Entrepreneurship Programs and Startup Incubator
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED delivers entrepreneurship training, coaching, and access to financing for new and growing ventures, including youth-led and social enterprises. Program cohorts meet at CEED’s Halifax facility, where participants receive business fundamentals training, mentorship from a network of advisors across trades and creative sectors, and connections to local partners. By combining experiential learning with practical startup supports, CEED aligns skills development with real market needs and nurtures entrepreneurial career pathways.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard is an ocean-technology incubator that offers shared office and workshop spaces, prototyping labs, and waterfront test facilities in Dartmouth. Its programs provide business training, mentorship, and industry connections with marine trades, ocean engineers, and established firms, helping youth-led and early-stage companies commercialize solutions. By pairing technical assets with entrepreneurial education and sector mentors, it bridges skills development with real jobs and supplier networks in an emerging industry.

resources.name: The Spark Zone (Nova Scotia Sandbox Program)
resources.description: The Spark Zone is a university-led sandbox that supports student and youth entrepreneurs with coaching, ideation-to-startup workshops, pitch training, and project-based mentorship across business, arts, and applied trades. It provides collaboration space on campus and connects participants with faculty experts and industry mentors to develop prototypes and launch ventures, including social innovation projects. This integrates work-integrated learning with entrepreneurship so young people can build careers through startups as well as traditional roles.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs is a student innovation hub at Dalhousie University that provides co-working space, hackathons, startup sprints, and mentorship to help youth build technology ventures. Participants receive practical training and connect with mentors from the tech sector and creative industries, often linking projects to co-op and work-integrated learning. This creates a pathway for young people to develop entrepreneurial skills and launch startups that complement traditional employment in Nova Scotia’s digital economy.

obstacles.title: Barriers to Entrepreneurship
obstacles.description: Scarce early-stage capital, fragmented mentorship networks, and complex regulations slow startup formation and scaling.

solutions.text: Community Seed & Microgrant Fund: A locally governed pool of small, early-stage grants and convertible micro-investments funded by municipalities, foundations, businesses and residents to help entrepreneurs prototype, validate ideas and cover early costs without restrictive terms.

resources.name: Spark Nova Scotia
resources.description: Spark Nova Scotia is a province-wide competition that awards non-dilutive seed grants to very early-stage founders to help them prototype, validate ideas, and cover initial business costs. Administered by Invest Nova Scotia and delivered with regional partners, Spark uses local judges and mentors to allocate small grants and wrap-around support that reduce barriers to starting up. By channeling public and private partner funds into flexible, equity-free microgrants, it directly implements a community-oriented seed fund model.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 1101, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

resources.name: Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta Cohort provides selected early-stage startups with $25,000 investments via a simple agreement for future equity (SAFE), plus mentorship and access to Volta’s community. The program is supported by regional corporate and public partners and uses local selection panels, creating a community-governed pool of convertible micro-investments. This structure helps founders in Nova Scotia cover prototyping and market validation costs without traditional restrictive lending terms.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Rural Innovation Fund
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic’s Rural Innovation Fund offers small, equity-free microgrants to rural innovators and entrepreneurs to test concepts, build prototypes, and validate market demand. Funded with support from municipal governments and local partners, the program is locally governed and pairs cash awards with mentorship and community connections. This directly embodies a community seed and microgrant fund that reduces early capital barriers outside major urban centres.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

resources.name: CEED Impact Loan
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED’s Impact Loan provides flexible microloans to early-stage entrepreneurs to cover startup costs such as prototyping, initial inventory, and early operations, alongside training and mentorship. Backed by public and community partners, CEED’s locally rooted approach emphasizes accessibility and supportive terms that reduce barriers to getting started. While structured as a loan rather than a grant, it functions as community-provided early capital aligned with the seed and microfund model.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Pooled Local Angel Network: A community-organized syndicate of local high-net-worth individuals and retired executives that co-invests in promising startups, with reduced minimums and sector focus on regional strengths (ocean tech, clean energy, forestry, creative industries).

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic (Oceans and Prime Streams)
resources.organization: Creative Destruction Lab (Dalhousie University – Rowe School of Business)
resources.description: CDL–Atlantic convenes a curated group of accomplished entrepreneurs, retired executives, and accredited angel investors who mentor and finance science- and technology-based startups. Through its Oceans stream, CDL–Atlantic catalyzes syndication among local angels who frequently co-invest in promising ocean tech and clean energy ventures, often structuring pooled investments that lower individual cheque sizes. This directly advances a community-organized angel syndicate model aligned with Nova Scotia’s regional strengths while reducing early-stage capital gaps and strengthening mentor networks.

resources.name: Volta Investor Connect
resources.description: Volta’s Investor Connect program builds and convenes a network of local angel investors and experienced executives to review curated deal flow, host investor-only pitch sessions, and coordinate syndication into Atlantic Canadian startups. By pooling local capital—often via group rounds or SPVs—the program helps reduce minimum cheque sizes for individual angels while channeling investment toward regional strengths such as ocean tech, cleantech, and creative digital industries. This directly implements a community-organized, pooled angel approach that addresses fragmented mentorship and scarce early-stage capital in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Community Bonds and Social Investment Vehicles: Municipalities and community organizations issue bonds or cooperative shares that direct resident capital to local social enterprises and startups, providing predictable, lower-cost early capital while keeping ownership local.

resources.name: Community Economic Development Investment Funds (CEDIF) Program
resources.organization: Department of Finance and Treasury Board, Government of Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Province of Nova Scotia’s CEDIF Program enables community-based organizations to raise capital from Nova Scotia residents by issuing community investment shares, often with provincial equity tax credits. This structure channels local savings into co-operatives, social enterprises, and startups, providing earlier, patient, and lower-cost capital while keeping ownership and decision-making rooted in the community.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Funds (CEDIFs)
resources.description: New Dawn raises capital from Cape Breton residents through community investment share offerings under Nova Scotia’s CEDIF framework and deploys it into local businesses, social-purpose real estate, and community ventures. By mobilizing resident ownership and offering targeted, patient financing, these funds reduce early-stage capital gaps for local enterprises while ensuring returns and governance remain in the community.

resources.name: Investment Shares Program
resources.description: As a financial co-operative, East Coast Credit Union issues member investment shares that strengthen local capital pools and are reinvested through lending to small businesses, social enterprises, and community projects across Nova Scotia. This cooperative share model channels resident capital into the regional economy, providing stable, relatively low-cost financing while maintaining local ownership and governance.

resources.name: Investment Shares Offering
resources.description: Sydney Credit Union, a community-owned financial co-operative, offers member investment shares that bolster its capital base for lending to local entrepreneurs, social enterprises, and community initiatives in Cape Breton. By inviting residents to invest through cooperative shares and recycling that capital locally, it provides predictable, community-controlled financing that supports startup formation and growth.

solutions.text: MentorMatch — Centralized Community Mentorship Platform: A simple directory and matching service, maintained by community partners, that connects entrepreneurs with vetted mentors across business skills, tech, trades and regulation compliance, including profiles, availability and short-term engagement options.

resources.name: Volta Mentorship & Office Hours
resources.description: Volta maintains a roster of vetted mentors and experts who provide office hours and targeted advisory sessions to startups across product, finance, legal/regulatory, marketing and growth. Founders are matched to appropriate mentors and can book short-term engagements, creating a centralized, low-friction way to access guidance and compliance know-how. This directly implements a community-maintained mentorship directory and matching service for entrepreneurs in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: ISANS Business Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS matches immigrant and newcomer entrepreneurs with experienced business mentors drawn from a curated pool covering sectors like trades, food services, retail, tech and professional services. The program pairs clients based on language, sector and regulatory needs (permitting, licensing, taxation), and facilitates structured, short-term mentorship engagements. This creates a centralized, community-run matching service that helps entrepreneurs navigate compliance and business growth in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: CEED Advisory & Mentorship
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides a centralized advisory and mentorship service that connects founders with vetted business advisors in finance, operations, marketing, sales and regulatory compliance. Through intake and matching, entrepreneurs are scheduled for focused, short-term 1:1 sessions and ongoing check-ins, reducing fragmentation in the mentor landscape. This community-partnered model functions as a practical directory and matching hub for entrepreneurs at all stages.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Centre for Women in Business Mentorship & Advisory
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business operates structured mentorship and advisory programs that match women and gender-diverse entrepreneurs with experienced mentors across sectors and disciplines. Staff curate mentor profiles and coordinate availability for short-term problem-solving sessions and longer-term guidance, including navigation of regulations, certification and procurement. This delivers a targeted, centralized matching service that strengthens inclusive entrepreneurial networks across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Mentor Network
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic maintains a mentor network that connects rural and urban Nova Scotian entrepreneurs with vetted industry and functional experts in tech, trades, oceans, and small business operations. Through intake and staff-facilitated matching, founders book short-term advisory sessions and office hours to tackle immediate challenges, including regulatory and compliance questions. This acts as a centralized, community-partnered mentorship hub serving multiple regions of the province.

solutions.text: Entrepreneur-in-Residence at Libraries and Campuses: Place experienced founders and business advisers part-time in public libraries, community centres and university campuses to offer drop-in coaching, workshops and referrals in accessible community locations.

resources.name: Dal Innovates — Entrepreneurs-in-Residence
resources.description: Dal Innovates places seasoned founders and sector experts on Dalhousie campuses (e.g., ShiftKey Labs, Emera ideaHUB and Launch Dal) to host weekly office hours, drop-in advising and hands-on workshops for students, researchers and community members. These EIRs offer one-on-one coaching, help navigate funding and regulatory pathways, and make referrals into Nova Scotia’s startup network, directly aligning with the entrepreneur-in-residence at campuses solution.

resources.name: SMU Entrepreneurship Centre — Entrepreneurs-in-Residence
resources.description: The Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre engages Entrepreneurs-in-Residence who maintain on-campus office hours and deliver frequent workshops for students, alumni and local founders. Advisors with lived startup experience provide drop-in coaching, business model feedback and referrals to funding, legal and accounting supports in an accessible campus setting.

resources.name: The Spark Zone — Mentors and Entrepreneurs-in-Residence
resources.organization: The Spark Zone (hosted by Saint Mary’s University with partner institutions)
resources.description: The Spark Zone embeds mentors and entrepreneurs-in-residence across partner university campuses to provide drop-in mentoring, problem labs and venture workshops for students and community innovators. By operating in accessible campus spaces, these practitioners offer on-the-spot coaching and connect founders to resources across Nova Scotia’s startup ecosystem.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE — Experts/Entrepreneurs-in-Residence
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE hosts experienced ocean-tech founders and advisors as experts-in-residence who hold office hours, deliver skills workshops and mentor early-stage companies on-site at the waterfront campus. These resident advisors provide practical coaching and make referrals to investors, prototyping resources and regulatory experts, bringing entrepreneur support directly into an accessible innovation campus.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic — Entrepreneurs/Experts-in-Residence and Office Hours
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic operates rural innovation hubs that host entrepreneurs/experts-in-residence with regular drop-in office hours, workshops and mentorship for founders at accessible community locations and partner NSCC campuses. Advisors offer coaching, help navigate funding and permitting, and provide warm referrals to professional services across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3R2

solutions.text: Regulatory Navigation Clinics: Monthly volunteer-run clinics with municipal officials, licensed accountants and lawyers to walk founders through permits, licensing, incorporation, zoning and compliance requirements in plain language and with checklists for local contexts.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Business Navigators
resources.organization: Service Nova Scotia, Government of Nova Scotia
resources.description: A free, province-wide service that provides one-on-one guidance to entrepreneurs on permits, licensing, registrations, zoning, and compliance across Nova Scotia. The team regularly delivers plain‑language regulatory navigation clinics and webinars with municipal planning staff, CRA liaison officers, and volunteer accountants/lawyers, using step‑by‑step checklists tailored to local contexts so founders can move from idea to compliant operation.

resources.name: ISANS Business Development – Legal and Accounting Clinics
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS hosts recurring business information sessions and volunteer‑run clinics where licensed lawyers and CPAs help immigrant and newcomer founders understand incorporation, registrations, permits, and ongoing compliance in plain language. Sessions are frequently co‑hosted with provincial Business Navigators and municipal officials to address zoning, licensing, and local requirements, and participants receive Nova Scotia–specific checklists and templates to navigate next steps.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: CEED Ask the Expert Clinics
resources.description: CEED offers regularly scheduled (often monthly) office hours and clinics where partner law firms and accounting professionals provide hands‑on guidance on incorporation, taxation, and regulatory compliance for startups and small businesses. These sessions are complemented by guest appearances from provincial Business Navigators and municipal planning staff for permits and zoning Q&A, and CEED supplies practical, Nova Scotia–specific checklists to help founders implement what they learn.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Volta Office Hours and Ask an Expert
resources.description: Volta runs recurring office hours and Ask an Expert sessions where volunteer lawyers and accountants meet with founders to cover incorporation options, IP, contracts, tax, and compliance in accessible language. In partnership with ecosystem and government partners, Volta hosts clinics on permits and licensing relevant to tech startups and provides actionable checklists and templates so companies can navigate municipal and provincial requirements.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

solutions.text: Community Makerspaces and Shared Prototyping Labs: Affordable shared workshops and fabrication labs equipped for low-cost prototyping (wood, metal, electronics, textiles) and staffed by trained volunteers to lower capital barriers for product-focused entrepreneurs and tradespeople.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio
resources.description: A free, bookable makerspace inside Halifax Central Library offering 3D printers, sewing machines, vinyl/Cricut cutters, and electronics kits alongside workshops and coaching. Library staff and trained volunteers help users learn equipment and complete low-cost prototypes, lowering capital barriers for artists, youth, and product-focused entrepreneurs.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: The Deanery Project Makerspace & Woodshop
resources.description: A community-run makerspace providing access to a woodshop, hand and power tools, textiles and craft studios, and flexible workspace for projects and prototypes. Staff and skilled volunteers offer training, mentorship, and low-cost access, enabling tradespeople, artists, and entrepreneurs to prototype products without significant up-front equipment costs.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Yarmouth Makerspace
resources.description: IGNITE’s Yarmouth hub includes a shared makerspace with 3D printers, laser cutter/CNC, electronics benches, and digital design tools for rapid prototyping. Entrepreneurs can access equipment, mentorship, and workshops facilitated by staff and community experts, reducing early-stage capital needs and accelerating product development.

resources.name: People’s Place Library Makerspace
resources.description: Antigonish’s public library offers a community makerspace with 3D printers, sewing machines, Cricut/vinyl cutters, and multimedia tools that can be reserved at low or no cost. Library staff and volunteers provide guidance and host skills workshops, helping local makers and youth prototype ideas and small-batch products without purchasing equipment.

solutions.text: Local Procurement Set-Asides and Buy-Local Campaigns: Municipal policies that reserve a percentage of procurement for local startups, makers and social enterprises plus promotion of buy-local procurement options to anchor early customers and revenue.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Social Procurement
resources.description: HRM has implemented a Social Procurement approach that embeds community benefit and local economic development into municipal purchasing. The program uses supplier outreach, smaller contract lots, and evaluation criteria that recognize social value to help local startups, makers, and social enterprises compete for city contracts—anchoring early customers and revenue. It also promotes opportunities for local vendors through vendor information sessions and a centralized procurement portal.

resources.name: Buy Halifax
resources.description: Buy Halifax is a sustained buy-local campaign that mobilizes businesses, institutions, and consumers to source goods and services from Nova Scotia companies. The initiative promotes local vendor directories, procurement-focused messaging, and partnerships that help anchor early sales for startups and social enterprises across the Halifax region. By elevating local options in purchasing decisions, it complements municipal procurement efforts to keep more spend within the community.

solutions.text: Regular Pitch Nights and Demo Days: Community-hosted pitch events that provide practice, local visibility, connections to investors and prize money or in-kind support (legal hours, coworking credits) to stimulate interest and funnel opportunities to investors and mentors.

resources.name: Volta Cohort Pitch Event
resources.description: Volta’s semi-annual Cohort Pitch Event gives early-stage startups a public stage to pitch to a panel of investors and mentors, building confidence and local visibility. Winners receive seed investment and in-kind supports such as workspace access and mentorship, while all participants connect with an active network of founders, advisors, and funders—directly addressing early capital and mentorship gaps.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: CEED Open Mic Pitch Night
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED hosts recurring open-mic pitch nights where founders practice concise pitches before a friendly audience of entrepreneurs, mentors, and potential investors. Events emphasize actionable feedback, visibility, and connections, with prizes or in-kind supports (e.g., training, advisory time, coworking access) offered by CEED and partners to help ventures progress from idea to investment-ready.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: IGNITE Pitch Competitions and Demo Days
resources.description: IGNITE runs regular rural innovation pitch events and cohort demo days in Western and Northern Nova Scotia, giving founders and students a platform to present solutions and practice investor-focused storytelling. Participants gain exposure to local mentors and investors, and events frequently award cash prizes or in-kind supports (legal hours, expert advisory, and workspace), catalyzing early traction outside major urban centres.

resources.name: DemoCamp Halifax
resources.organization: ShiftKey Labs (Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science)
resources.description: DemoCamp Halifax is a recurring community showcase where builders demo working products (no slides) to peers, mentors, and investors, followed by Q&A and networking. The format provides hands-on practice and real-time feedback while raising local visibility; sponsors and partners often offer prizes or in-kind support, and the event hubs founders into a broader mentorship and investor network.
resources.address: 6050 University Avenue, Goldberg Computer Science Building, Halifax, NS B3H 1W5

resources.name: RBC Student Pitch Competition
resources.description: Hosted by the SMU Entrepreneurship Centre, this annual competition provides coaching and practice sessions culminating in a public pitch event judged by entrepreneurs and investors. Finalists gain province-wide visibility and connections to mentors and funders, with cash prizes and in-kind supports helping student-led ventures overcome early-stage capital and network barriers.

solutions.text: Community Accelerator Focused on Regional Sectors: A short, low-cost accelerator run by local partners that combines mentorship, regulatory training, prototype support and investor exposure tailored to regionally important industries and inclusive cohorts (youth, Indigenous, newcomer entrepreneurs).

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard is COVE’s ocean technology accelerator offering cohort-based programming that pairs early-stage companies with industry mentors, regulatory and procurement guidance, prototyping facilities, and access to ocean test ranges. The program focuses on regionally critical sectors like fisheries, defence, offshore energy and marine transportation, helping founders validate, build prototypes, and navigate marine standards and certifications. It also connects companies to investors and buyers through demo days and partner events, and works with initiatives that broaden participation from youth, newcomer and Indigenous entrepreneurs.

resources.name: Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta Cohort is a short, competitive accelerator-style program that provides selected Atlantic Canadian startups with mentorship, investment-readiness training, and the opportunity to pitch for $25,000 investments, plus ongoing support through Volta’s hub. Run in partnership with local investors and service providers, it offers workshops on legal and regulatory fundamentals, investor relations, and go-to-market, and connects founders to a deep mentor network. Volta actively works with universities and community partners to encourage inclusive participation by youth, newcomer and underrepresented founders.

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic
resources.organization: Creative Destruction Lab at Dalhousie University
resources.description: CDL-Atlantic is a mentorship-driven accelerator at Dalhousie University that runs structured, short sprints for science and technology startups in streams such as Oceans, Prime and Health. Companies meet with experienced entrepreneurs, scientists, and active investors, receive guidance on regulatory pathways (e.g., ocean compliance or health approvals), and work toward clear, measurable milestones including investor readiness. The program is delivered with regional partners and attracts diverse founders, including international and newcomer entrepreneurs, while connecting them directly to angel and venture investors.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Rural Innovation Cohort
resources.description: IGNITE’s Rural Innovation Cohort brings early-stage founders from Nova Scotia’s rural communities together for a low-cost, mentor-led accelerator that is tailored to regional industries such as fisheries, aquaculture, cleantech and advanced manufacturing. Participants access makerspaces and prototyping labs, workshops on regulatory requirements and procurement with municipal/provincial partners, and regular pitch events that provide investor and buyer exposure. The program engages youth and underrepresented groups through partnerships with NSCC, community organizations and Indigenous and newcomer networks in Western and Northern Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Business Legal and Accounting Volunteer Clinic: Pro bono clinics staffed by local lawyers and accountants offering packaged services: incorporation, contract templates, tax basics and employment law primers to reduce complexity and cost for new ventures.

resources.name: Volta Office Hours: Legal and Accounting Clinics
resources.description: Volta hosts recurring, no-cost office hours where partner law firms and accounting firms meet one-on-one with founders to answer startup legal and finance questions. These pro bono clinics help new ventures choose and file incorporation structures, understand shareholder and contractor agreements, and learn bookkeeping, HST, payroll and tax basics—reducing early-stage complexity and costs.

resources.name: Centre for Women in Business Expert Advisory Clinics
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business, Mount Saint Vincent University
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business offers free or subsidized clinics connecting women-led startups with volunteer lawyers and CPAs for practical guidance. Sessions cover incorporation/registration options, contract templates and employment law primers, along with bookkeeping setup, HST and corporate tax basics—helping entrepreneurs navigate legal and accounting requirements at minimal cost.

resources.name: ISANS Business Services: Legal and Tax Clinics for Entrepreneurs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS partners with local law firms and CRA Liaison Officers to deliver no-cost legal and accounting clinics for immigrant entrepreneurs. Participants receive guidance on Nova Scotia business registration and incorporation, access to sample contract and policy templates, and practical primers on bookkeeping, HST, payroll and income tax to reduce startup barriers.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Navigate Startup House Advisor-in-Residence Clinics
resources.organization: Navigate (Cape Breton University & Nova Scotia Community College)
resources.description: Navigate provides free advisor-in-residence sessions and clinics that connect Cape Breton startups with local lawyers and accountants. Founders receive pro bono guidance on incorporation options, basic contract reviews, employment law considerations and small-business tax and bookkeeping essentials—streamlining early legal and accounting decisions.

solutions.text: Trades-to-Business Bridging Program: Training and mentorship for tradespeople who want to start small businesses — covering pricing, estimating, compliance, insurance and marketing — delivered by trade associations, colleges and local business mentors.

resources.name: CANS Education & Training
resources.description: The Construction Association of Nova Scotia (CANS) delivers year-round training specifically relevant to running trades businesses, including courses in estimating and bidding, project management, construction law and contract administration, and OH&S/compliance. Through workshops and peer networking with established contractors and suppliers, tradespeople gain practical skills in pricing jobs, understanding regulatory requirements and insurance needs, and marketing within the construction supply chain—bridging the gap from skilled worker to business owner.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: NSHBA Education & Training
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Home Builders’ Association offers business-focused training for builders and renovators, covering project estimating and pricing, building code and regulatory compliance, risk and insurance considerations, and business management and marketing. Members also access mentorship and peer learning through councils and events, helping skilled trades professionals transition into owning and growing residential construction and renovation companies.
resources.address: 3845 Joseph Howe Drive, Halifax, NS B3L 4H9

resources.name: CEED Business Development Programs
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides hands-on entrepreneurship training, one-on-one coaching, and mentorship that help tradespeople formalize and grow small businesses. Programming includes business planning, pricing and cash flow, marketing and sales, and guidance on permits, licensing and insurance—equipping carpenters, electricians, landscapers, and other trades to move confidently from the jobsite into business ownership.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: NSCC Entrepreneurship
resources.description: NSCC Entrepreneurship supports trades students and alumni with workshops, coaching, and mentor connections to start and scale small businesses. Offerings cover quoting and estimating, pricing and bookkeeping, regulatory compliance and insurance basics, and marketing and digital presence—providing a practical bridge from skilled trades training to successful self-employment across Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Youth Entrepreneurship Pipeline: School and community programs that teach business basics, run micro-grants and summer incubators for teens and young adults to build experience, networks and a culture of local entrepreneurship from an early age.

resources.name: Juniorpreneur & Youth Entrepreneurship Programs
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED delivers hands-on entrepreneurship education to youth through school workshops, after-school programs, and Juniorpreneur camps where teens form teams, create real products or services, and sell at pop-up markets. Programs include mentorship, pitch practice, and small seed funds or prizes, helping young people gain business basics, confidence, and early networks that reduce barriers to starting a venture in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 309, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: RBC Summer Up (Student Venture Incubator)
resources.organization: Arthur L. Irving Entrepreneurship Centre, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: RBC Summer Up is a paid summer incubator for post-secondary students and recent graduates that provides venture-building workshops, mentorship from local entrepreneurs, and seed funding to work on a startup full-time. By combining stipends/microgrants, business fundamentals training, and a mentor network, the program lowers capital and guidance barriers for young founders and builds an entrepreneurial pipeline in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Youth Entrepreneurship (School & Summer Programs)
resources.description: Acadia Entrepreneurship Centre partners with schools and communities across Nova Scotia to deliver in-class entrepreneurship modules, bootcamps, and summer programming where youth validate ideas, build business plans, and practice pitching. Through mentorship, experiential learning, and seed-funding opportunities tied to pitch events, the program equips teens and young adults with business basics and local networks to start ventures.

resources.name: 4-H Nova Scotia Entrepreneurship & Business Projects
resources.description: 4-H Nova Scotia offers project streams where youth plan and operate small ventures—learning budgeting, marketing, sales, and record-keeping—culminating in club achievement days and community markets. Many clubs run pitch nights or provide small startup budgets, giving practical experience, mentorship from volunteer leaders, and early revenue opportunities that build an entrepreneurial mindset from a young age.
resources.address: 60 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: Volta Academy
resources.description: Volta Academy is a multi-week, entry-level program that teaches early-stage founders—often students and young adults—the fundamentals of customer discovery, business models, and pitching, while connecting them with mentors in Nova Scotia’s startup ecosystem. Participants culminate with pitch events that provide exposure and access to small grants or prizes, building skills, networks, and early-stage capital to move ideas forward.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

solutions.text: Community Crowdfunding Platform with Matching: A locally branded crowdfunding portal that aggregates small contributions from residents, paired with matching funds from local government or foundations for projects that meet regional priorities and equity goals.

resources.name: Community Funds and Match Campaigns
resources.description: The Community Foundation of Nova Scotia operates an online giving portal where residents contribute small donations to place-based community funds and project-specific campaigns across the province. During periodic match campaigns, philanthropic partners provide dollar-for-dollar matching to eligible local projects that align with regional priorities such as rural vitality, youth opportunity, and equity for African Nova Scotian, Indigenous, and newcomer communities—effectively turning the platform into a community crowdfunding vehicle with matching funds.

resources.name: Matched Community Impact Campaigns
resources.description: United Way Halifax runs targeted, crowdfunding-style campaigns that pool small resident donations through their online giving pages and CanadaHelps project pages. Corporate and foundation partners frequently provide time-limited matching funds, doubling community contributions to priority initiatives focused on poverty reduction, youth opportunity, and equity for Black and Indigenous communities—mirroring a locally branded crowdfunding model that unlocks matching dollars for projects meeting regional goals.

solutions.text: Return-to-Region Incentives and Diaspora Engagement: A community effort to engage Nova Scotian alumni and the diaspora with incentives, mentorship roles, relocation support packages and introductions to local networks to attract founders back to the region.

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program links new and returning residents, recent graduates, and entrepreneurs with established business leaders to accelerate job searches and venture building. By facilitating one-on-one informational interviews and warm introductions to local networks, it provides mentorship roles and community connections that help alumni and diaspora founders re-establish in Halifax and access early customers, advisors, and capital.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Business Services for Immigrant Entrepreneurs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides pre-arrival and post-arrival settlement supports, business advising, and mentorship for entrepreneurs relocating to Nova Scotia, including guidance on regulations, access to financing, and introductions to local supplier, mentor, and investor networks. These services function as relocation support and network onboarding for founders—complementing diaspora and alumni return efforts by helping returning Canadians and newcomers quickly integrate and launch or scale ventures in the province.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE’s Start-Up Yard is an ocean-tech incubator that offers workspace, prototyping facilities, industry mentorship, and curated introductions to customers, investors, and partners in the regional supply chain. This soft-landing platform supports founders who relocate or return to Nova Scotia by providing practical setup support, mentor engagement, and rapid access to sector-specific networks—key components of return-to-region and diaspora attraction strategies.

solutions.text: Inclusive Entrepreneur Supports (Women, Indigenous, Newcomers): Targeted microgrants, mentorship circles, culturally appropriate programming and language supports developed with community leaders to lower barriers for historically underrepresented entrepreneurs.

resources.name: ISANS Business Services for Immigrant Entrepreneurs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS) provides newcomer entrepreneurs with one-on-one business advising, market research, and cohort-based training that includes mentorship circles and peer networking. Programs are delivered with multilingual supports and culturally responsive content co-designed with community partners, lowering barriers around language, regulations, and access to capital; ISANS also connects clients to microfinancing and grant opportunities through local partners.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Centre for Women in Business (CWB) – Mentorship and Growth Programs
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business, Mount Saint Vincent University
resources.description: CWB at Mount Saint Vincent University offers women-led cohorts, mentorship circles, and advisory groups that provide hands-on guidance from experienced entrepreneurs and sector experts. Through tailored programming, navigation of regulations, and connections to microgrant/financing partners, CWB reduces early-stage barriers for women founders across Nova Scotia, with supports designed to reflect women’s diverse lived experiences and business contexts.

resources.name: Black Business Initiative (BBI) – Entrepreneurial Support Programs
resources.description: BBI provides African Nova Scotian and Black entrepreneurs with culturally grounded business training, mentorship, and financing (including microloans and startup capital) tailored to community needs. Its advisory services, peer mentorship circles, and ecosystem partnerships help navigate regulations and connect founders to targeted capital and grants, directly addressing early-stage funding gaps and fragmented networks for historically underrepresented entrepreneurs.
resources.address: 1660 Hollis Street, Suite 810, Halifax, NS B3J 1V7

obstacles.title: Digital and Transportation Connectivity Gaps
obstacles.description: Rural broadband deficits, weak intercity transit, and limited active transport options constrain equitable access to jobs and services.

solutions.text: Community Broadband Co‑op: Form a locally governed cooperative to finance, build and manage high‑speed internet to underserved neighborhoods, pooling member fees, grants and volunteer labor to drive last‑mile connections.

resources.name: Chebucto Community Net
resources.description: Chebucto Community Net is a volunteer-driven, member-supported community internet service provider that has operated in Halifax since the early 1990s. As a locally governed non-profit, it pools member fees, grants, and volunteer expertise to deliver affordable internet access (including DSL) and digital services, directly aligning with a community broadband co‑op model for underserved residents.
resources.address: Room 006, Chase Building, 6136 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: Valley Community Fibre Network (VCFN)
resources.description: VCFN is a community-owned, not‑for‑profit open-access fibre backbone in the Annapolis Valley created by local municipalities and educational institutions to improve connectivity. Governed locally and financed through member contributions and public funding, it enables last‑mile ISPs and community projects to extend high‑speed service to rural and underserved areas—functionally implementing a cooperative, community broadband approach.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Annapolis County Rural High-Speed Internet Initiative
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Annapolis
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Annapolis leads a locally governed broadband build that combines municipal funding, provincial/federal grants, and partnerships with community stakeholders to reach rural residents. By coordinating community input, aggregating demand, and investing in shared infrastructure to support last‑mile providers, the initiative operationalizes a community broadband model that fills connectivity gaps for underserved communities.
resources.address: 752 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

solutions.text: Public Wi‑Fi Hubs in Community Spaces: Equip libraries, community centres, faith buildings and parks with reliable, free public Wi‑Fi and extended hours so residents can access jobs, training and services without home broadband.

resources.name: Halifax Central Library — Free Public Wi‑Fi and Computer Access
resources.description: Halifax Central Library provides free, high‑speed public Wi‑Fi throughout the building along with public computers, study spaces, and meeting rooms. With extended evening and weekend hours, it serves as a community hub where residents without home broadband can apply for jobs, complete online training, and access digital services.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Halifax North Memorial Public Library — Public Wi‑Fi & Digital Access
resources.description: This branch offers free public Wi‑Fi, computer workstations, and device charging in a welcoming, community‑oriented space. Its extended hours and programming support job seekers and learners who rely on library internet to access employment portals, online courses, and government services.

resources.name: McConnell Library (Sydney) — Free Public Wi‑Fi and Technology Access
resources.description: McConnell Library provides no‑cost Wi‑Fi and public computer access, enabling residents to connect for job searches, skills training, and essential online services. As a central community space with regular evening and weekend hours, it reduces connectivity barriers for people without reliable home internet.

solutions.text: Mobile Hotspot Lending Program: Create a library‑style program lending cellular Wi‑Fi hotspots and data plans to students, jobseekers and low‑income households for short‑term need.

resources.name: Borrow a WiFi Hotspot
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries lends portable cellular Wi‑Fi hotspots to cardholders for short-term use, providing home internet access where none exists. The devices use the mobile network to create a Wi‑Fi signal for students, jobseekers, and households without reliable broadband, directly addressing digital connectivity gaps across the municipality.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Wi‑Fi To Go
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library’s Wi‑Fi To Go program loans LTE mobile hotspots so patrons can get online at home or on the move. By bundling a hotspot with an active data plan for short-term loans, the program supports learners, jobseekers, and families in communities where fixed broadband is limited.

resources.name: Borrow the Internet (Wi‑Fi Hotspot Lending)
resources.description: Annapolis Valley Regional Library circulates portable Wi‑Fi hotspots that connect via the cellular network, enabling patrons without home internet to access online learning, job applications, telehealth, and essential services. The program mirrors a library checkout and includes the data plan, reducing barriers for low‑income and rural residents across the Valley.

resources.name: Internet To Go (Mobile Hotspots)
resources.description: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library’s Internet To Go service lends cellular hotspots that create a temporary home Wi‑Fi network anywhere with cell coverage. Offered as short-term loans with data included, it bridges connectivity gaps for students, jobseekers, and households in rural Pictou and Antigonish counties.

resources.name: Borrow the Internet (Hotspot Lending)
resources.description: South Shore Public Libraries lends mobile Wi‑Fi hotspot devices with active data plans to provide temporary internet access for patrons who lack reliable broadband. This library‑style lending directly supports students, jobseekers, and families in rural communities by removing cost and infrastructure barriers for short-term connectivity.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

solutions.text: Digital Skills and Support Volunteers: Organize volunteer tutors to run free workshops and one‑on‑one sessions on basic digital literacy, remote work tools, online job search and navigating government services.

resources.name: Tech Help (One-on-One and Drop-In)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries offers free one-on-one appointments and small-group workshops where staff and trained volunteers help patrons with computer and smartphone basics, email, video conferencing tools (e.g., Zoom), and cloud productivity apps. Sessions frequently support online job search and applications, resume uploading, and navigating government services such as Service Canada, CRA, and Nova Scotia online portals—directly addressing digital access barriers for residents across HRM.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Digital Skills Tutoring
resources.description: Dartmouth Learning Network provides free, volunteer-led one-on-one and small-group tutoring for adults to build essential digital skills, including computer fundamentals, email, document creation, and safe internet use. Tutors also support learners with online job search and applications, using remote work tools, and navigating government websites and digital forms—helping reduce digital barriers to employment and services.
resources.address: 73 Tacoma Drive, Suite 802, Dartmouth, NS B2W 3Y6

resources.name: Computer & Digital Skills for Newcomers
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers free digital literacy workshops and one-on-one support for immigrants and refugees to build confidence with computers, email, online safety, and productivity tools used in remote and hybrid work. Staff and trained volunteers help clients search and apply for jobs online and navigate essential government services (e.g., Service Canada, CRA, Nova Scotia services), ensuring newcomers can access employment and public programs.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Tech Help @ South Shore Libraries
resources.description: South Shore Public Libraries runs free drop-in and by-appointment tech help where staff and community volunteers guide residents through device setup, email, video meetings, and online file sharing. The sessions also focus on practical tasks like creating resumes, applying to jobs online, and accessing provincial and federal digital services—supporting rural residents to overcome connectivity and digital skill gaps.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

solutions.text: Community Co‑working and Maker Spaces: Convert an existing building into an affordable co‑working/maker space with high‑speed internet, meeting rooms and equipment to support entrepreneurs, remote workers and young creatives.

resources.name: Volta
resources.description: Volta is a startup hub that offers affordable co-working memberships, dedicated offices, meeting rooms, and event space with high-speed internet for founders, remote workers, and creative teams. By providing shared amenities, mentorship, and a collaborative environment in a centrally located building, it directly supports entrepreneurs and young creatives with space and connectivity that lower the barriers to launching and growing companies.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, 7th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE operates a collaborative ocean-technology campus offering shared offices, labs, workshops, and meeting rooms with enterprise-grade internet. It functions as an innovation-focused co-working and maker environment where startups and researchers access specialized equipment, prototyping facilities, and waterfront testing infrastructure—supporting entrepreneurs, remote technical teams, and young innovators.

resources.name: Halifax Central Library Creative Labs
resources.description: The Creative Labs at Halifax Central Library provide bookable studios, 3D printers, audio/video gear, and digital fabrication tools alongside high-speed Wi-Fi and numerous meeting and collaboration rooms. This publicly accessible maker/co-working environment enables entrepreneurs, remote workers, and young creatives to prototype ideas, produce media, and meet clients without the cost of private facilities.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library Makerspace
resources.description: The Halifax Tool Library runs a community makerspace and tool-lending library that gives members access to shared workshops, 3D printers, woodworking equipment, and project space with reliable internet. By lowering equipment and space costs, it enables makers, freelancers, and early-stage entrepreneurs to build products, learn new skills, and collaborate in an affordable, community-driven setting.

solutions.text: Local Micro‑Transit and Shuttle Services: Run community‑organized shuttle routes or flexible micro‑transit (volunteer drivers, small buses or contracted vans) timed for shift work, school and major employment centres.

resources.name: Access-A-Bus
resources.description: Access-A-Bus is Halifax Transit's door-to-door, pre-booked accessible micro-transit service using small buses/vans to transport eligible riders to work, school, medical appointments, and essential services. By providing flexible, scheduled rides across urban and suburban communities, it functions as a community-organized shuttle connecting people to employment centres and education on timelines that complement shift work and daily schedules.

resources.name: Bridgewater Transit
resources.description: Bridgewater Transit operates small community buses on routes that connect neighbourhoods with key employment hubs, retail areas, NSCC Lunenburg Campus, and the South Shore Regional Hospital. Launched to improve access for shift workers and students, the service provides frequent, reliable local shuttle-style connectivity that addresses rural and small-town transportation gaps.

resources.name: Pictou County Transit
resources.organization: Town of New Glasgow (in partnership with Pictou County municipalities)
resources.description: Pictou County Transit runs community-scale buses linking New Glasgow, Stellarton, Westville, and nearby communities to major employers, Aberdeen Hospital, retail centres, and NSCC. Its local shuttle-style routes and schedules improve access to jobs and education for youth and workers, supporting mobility where regional and intercity options are limited.
resources.address: 111 Provost Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 5E1

resources.name: Kings Transit Authority
resources.description: Kings Transit Authority provides regional local bus service across the Annapolis Valley, connecting rural towns and villages with employment areas, Acadia University, NSCC campuses, and essential services. Using smaller buses on community-oriented routes, it fills micro-regional transit gaps and offers scheduled access aligned with school and work-day travel needs.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

solutions.text: Volunteer Ride Share Network: Set up a coordinated volunteer driving program with vetted drivers and an easy booking system to help people reach jobs, medical appointments and training when transit is limited.

resources.name: Wheels of Hope Transportation Service
resources.description: The Canadian Cancer Society’s Wheels of Hope provides volunteer-driven rides to cancer-related medical appointments across Nova Scotia. Volunteers are screened and trained, and trips are coordinated through an easy booking system so people in rural and underserved areas can reliably reach treatment when public transit is limited.

resources.name: East Hants Community Rider
resources.description: East Hants Community Rider operates a door-to-door volunteer driver program that connects residents to employment, medical appointments, training, and essential services throughout rural East Hants. Riders book trips by phone or online, and vetted volunteer drivers use their vehicles to fill gaps where fixed-route transit does not operate.

solutions.text: Active Transportation Projects: Community‑led projects to install bike racks, repair stations, safe crosswalks and wayfinding, plus volunteer‑run bike repair clinics and local bike‑share pilots to increase cycling and walking options.

resources.name: Active Transportation Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Active Transportation Program plans and delivers infrastructure like protected bike lanes, safer crosswalks, multi-use pathways, bicycle parking and wayfinding signage across the city. The program also supports community partners during events such as Bike Week to host pop-up tune‑ups and safety clinics, helping residents adopt cycling and walking for everyday trips.

resources.name: Switch: Open Street Sundays
resources.description: Switch transforms local streets into car‑free community spaces where residents can walk and cycle safely, try pop‑up bike lanes and temporary crosswalks, and navigate pilot wayfinding. Ecology Action Centre coordinates volunteers and partner groups to offer free bike repair pop‑ups and skills demos at these events, building local capacity and momentum for permanent active transportation improvements.

resources.name: Blue Route (Provincial Cycling Network)
resources.description: Cycling Nova Scotia’s Blue Route initiative works with the Province and municipalities to develop connected bikeways and to implement standardized wayfinding and route signage across Nova Scotia. The organization provides technical guidance and community support that help local partners add bike parking and repair stations along priority corridors, expanding safe cycling options between and within communities.
resources.address: 5516 Spring Garden Road, 4th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 1G6

resources.name: Community Bike Repair Clinics and Tool Lending
resources.description: The Halifax Tool Library hosts volunteer‑run bicycle repair nights and mobile pop‑up tune‑ups, where trained volunteers help residents fix flats, adjust brakes, and keep bikes safe and road‑ready. By lending bike‑specific tools and offering hands‑on instruction, the program lowers barriers to cycling and supports neighborhood‑led maintenance that complements local active transportation infrastructure.

resources.name: X-Bikes (Campus Bike Share)
resources.description: StFX’s X-Bikes is a community‑oriented bike‑share that offers students and staff free or low‑cost access to bicycles for short‑term trips around Antigonish, with secure racks and on‑campus pick‑up/return points. The Sustainability Office maintains the fleet and hosts bike safety and maintenance workshops, helping to normalize everyday cycling and support first‑/last‑mile connectivity in the town.

solutions.text: Community Broadband Mapping and Needs Assessment: Collect household‑level data on connectivity through surveys and speed tests, produce maps to show gaps, and use findings to target local pilots and support funding applications.

resources.name: MODL Internet Speed Test and Connectivity Mapping
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg (MODL) runs an ongoing community Internet speed test and broadband needs assessment to collect household‑level data on connectivity. Using the CIRA Internet Performance Test and resident surveys, MODL maps speeds and service availability to pinpoint gaps. The resulting maps and datasets are used to target local pilot projects and strengthen applications to provincial and federal broadband funding programs.

resources.name: Chester Internet Speed Test and Broadband Gaps Map
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Chester
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Chester invites residents to complete home Internet speed tests and short surveys to gather address‑level performance data. Results are aggregated into interactive maps that reveal underserved pockets across the municipality. Chester uses these findings to prioritize underserved roads and communities for pilot builds and to support funding applications and negotiations with Internet service providers.

resources.name: Colchester Internet Speed Test and Broadband Needs Assessment
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: Colchester County runs a community broadband assessment that combines resident Internet speed testing with service availability surveys. The county compiles household‑level results into maps to identify unserved and underserved areas and quantify service gaps. These evidence‑based maps inform where to pilot expansions and bolster the county’s applications to programs like the Universal Broadband Fund and provincial initiatives.

resources.name: Kings County Internet Speed Test and Connectivity Survey
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings collects resident speed tests and survey responses to build a detailed picture of household‑level Internet performance across rural and suburban areas. Data are visualized on maps to reveal coverage and quality gaps, guiding where to focus pilot projects and community partnerships with providers. Kings County leverages these findings in funding applications and to advocate for targeted fibre and fixed‑wireless upgrades.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

solutions.text: Partnerships with Local Businesses for Connectivity: Encourage businesses to open Wi‑Fi access or host work pods, sponsor community internet infrastructure, or allow co‑working use of underused space during off hours.

resources.name: WorkSpace Atlantic – Bedford Coworking
resources.description: WorkSpace Atlantic is a local coworking provider that offers day passes, dedicated desks, private offices, and meeting rooms with high-speed Wi‑Fi in Bedford. By activating commercial space for flexible, bookable work pods and shared areas, it gives remote workers, students, and entrepreneurs reliable connectivity close to home. This advances the solution by enabling co-working use of local business space and providing community access to connectivity without long commutes.

resources.name: WorkEvolved Antigonish
resources.description: WorkEvolved is a downtown coworking studio that provides open desks, private pods, and meeting rooms with fast Wi‑Fi for individuals and teams. It partners with local organizations to host meetups and opens its space through day passes and memberships, allowing community use of underused downtown space outside traditional office hours. This implements the solution by giving residents professional connectivity and workspace without needing long travel or home broadband.
