resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Yarmouth Innovation Hub
resources.description: IGNITE operates a rural innovation hub in downtown Yarmouth with high-speed internet, bookable hot desks, meeting rooms, and maker spaces accessible to entrepreneurs, students, and remote workers. Through partnerships with municipalities and local industry, it runs community coworking days and programs that open the space to the public and provide connectivity. This directly addresses connectivity gaps by offering reliable Wi‑Fi and work pods in a shared, centrally located business space.

resources.name: COVE Co-Working and Shared Facilities
resources.description: COVE provides shared offices, collaboration zones, and co-working facilities with robust internet on the Dartmouth waterfront for ocean-sector startups and SMEs. Companies and researchers can access flexible desks and meeting rooms, including after-hours access for members, enabling high-bandwidth work without needing their own facilities. This implements the solution by leveraging a business campus to host work pods and provide connectivity in partnership with the ocean-industry community.

solutions.text: Pop‑up Transit and Weekend Routes: Pilot weekend or event‑based shuttle services connecting rural areas to downtowns, markets and training centres to demonstrate need and build ridership data for permanent service.

resources.name: CBU Express and Event Overflow Shuttles
resources.organization: Cape Breton Regional Municipality – Transit Cape Breton
resources.description: Transit Cape Breton launched express and overflow shuttle services to Cape Breton University during peak periods and on weekends, adding buses to connect surrounding communities with the Sydney downtown core and the CBU campus. These pop-up and expanded services respond to surges tied to semesters and events, demonstrating demand for permanent evening and weekend routes that link rural areas to a major training centre and urban amenities.

resources.name: Magic Winery Bus – Wolfville
resources.description: The Magic Winery Bus operates a seasonal weekend hop-on, hop-off shuttle linking downtown Wolfville with rural vineyards throughout the Annapolis Valley, creating convenient connections for residents and visitors between the town centre and outlying destinations. By concentrating service on weekends and special event days, the shuttle functions as a pop-up circulator that demonstrates demand for rural-to-downtown links and provides ridership data to inform longer-term mobility planning.

resources.name: South Shore Exhibition Park-and-Ride Shuttle
resources.description: Each summer during the South Shore Exhibition, the Town of Bridgewater coordinates free park-and-ride shuttles that move people from outlying lots into the downtown Exhibition grounds during peak evenings and weekends. This event-based service uses existing transit resources to test demand for evening and weekend mobility, connecting surrounding residential areas to the town’s main event district and informing decisions about more permanent service levels.

solutions.text: Local Advocacy and Funding Coalition: Form a cross‑sector coalition of residents, businesses, youth groups and municipalities to lobby provincial/federal programs, apply jointly for grants, and coordinate investment for long‑term connectivity improvements.

resources.name: Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative (IFNSI)
resources.description: IFNSI is a province-wide broadband expansion program that convenes municipalities, private internet service providers, community groups, and the Province to co-design and co-fund rural connectivity builds. It coordinates joint proposals to federal and provincial funds and negotiates regional projects, enabling communities and local governments to pool resources and advocacy to secure long-term, future‑proof internet access.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1800, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Connectivity and Transportation Advocacy
resources.description: NSFM convenes municipalities, businesses, chambers of commerce, and community and youth representatives to set shared priorities on rural internet, public transit, and active transportation. Through collective lobbying to provincial and federal programs and by facilitating intermunicipal collaboration and joint grant applications, NSFM helps coordinate long‑term investments that close digital and transportation gaps across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1304, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Transportation Program (Active Transportation and Transit)
resources.description: Ecology Action Centre’s transportation team builds cross‑sector coalitions of municipalities, youth groups, schools, local businesses, and residents to plan connected active transportation corridors and advocate for better community and intercommunity transit. They provide technical assistance and partnership brokering for joint applications to provincial and federal funding programs, coordinating multi‑year investments that improve equitable access to jobs and services.

obstacles.title: Inclusion and Belonging Challenges
obstacles.description: Systemic racism, discrimination, and barriers for Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotians, newcomers, and 2SLGBTQIA+ youth reduce retention and community vitality.

solutions.text: Community-led Cultural Safety and Anti-Racism Training: Run regular workshops co-designed and facilitated by Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer and 2SLGBTQIA+ leaders for schools, employers, service providers and community groups to reduce bias, improve service delivery and build culturally safe spaces.

resources.name: Intercultural Competency Workshops
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers intercultural competency and anti-racism workshops for employers, educators, service providers, and community groups across Nova Scotia. Sessions are co-designed and facilitated by newcomer and immigrant leaders who share lived experience, helping participants reduce bias, improve service delivery, and build culturally safe and welcoming workplaces and classrooms.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: 2SLGBTQIA+ Education & Training
resources.description: The Youth Project provides professional development and youth-led workshops to schools, employers, and service providers on creating safer, more inclusive spaces for 2SLGBTQIA+ people. Facilitated by 2SLGBTQIA+ educators and youth leaders, sessions cover topics like gender diversity, pronouns, inclusive policy, and reducing bias to improve services and campus/workplace culture.

resources.name: Mi'kmaw Cultural Awareness Training
resources.description: The Confederacy of Mainland Mi'kmaq offers Mi'kmaw cultural awareness and treaty education workshops for schools, municipalities, employers, and frontline service providers. Co-facilitated by Mi'kmaw Elders, knowledge keepers, and educators, the training addresses history, treaties, cultural protocols, and practical steps to create culturally safe spaces and reduce systemic bias.
resources.address: 57 Martin Crescent, Truro Heights, NS B6L 1N7

resources.name: Anti-Racism and African Nova Scotian Cultural Education
resources.organization: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia delivers educational workshops and outreach that help schools, employers, and community organizations understand African Nova Scotian history, culture, and the impacts of anti-Black racism. Led by African Nova Scotian educators and community leaders, the sessions build cultural safety, inform inclusive policies, and strengthen service delivery for Black communities.
resources.address: 10 Cherry Brook Road, Cherry Brook, NS B2Z 1A1

solutions.text: Youth Mentorship and Leadership Programs: Create local mentorship networks pairing young people from target communities with mentors in trades, technology, arts, entrepreneurship and community services to build skills, networks and pathways to meaningful careers.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program matches recent graduates, youth job seekers, and newcomers with volunteer Connectors—established professionals across sectors like technology, oceans, finance, public service, and trades-related industries—for informational interviews and network introductions. This mentorship-style networking builds social capital, increases belonging, and opens pathways to meaningful careers in Nova Scotia for underrepresented youth.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program pairs immigrant and refugee clients, including youth and recent graduates, with volunteer mentors working in their field to provide one-on-one guidance, industry insights, and introductions to professional networks. This structured mentorship helps newcomer youth overcome barriers to inclusion and employment by building skills, confidence, and routes into technology, health, business, and community services careers.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding and community partners
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based initiative that supports Mi’kmaq and African Nova Scotian learners to enter skilled trades careers in shipbuilding through academic upgrading, hands‑on trades training, wraparound supports, and mentorship from industry professionals. The program builds skills, relationships, and clear pathways to apprenticeships and employment, directly addressing systemic barriers to participation in the trades.

resources.name: Girls Get WISE
resources.organization: WISEatlantic (Women in Science and Engineering – Atlantic) at Mount Saint Vincent University
resources.description: Girls Get WISE offers mentorship-rich STEM camps, workshops, and events where girls and gender-diverse youth meet and learn from women working in science, technology, engineering, and related industries in Nova Scotia. By combining hands-on activities with direct role‑model engagement, the program builds skills, confidence, and networks that guide participants toward education and careers in technology and engineering.

resources.name: Phoenix Mentoring
resources.description: Phoenix Mentoring matches youth facing barriers—including 2SLGBTQIA+ youth and those experiencing homelessness—with trained adult mentors for consistent guidance, goal‑setting, and leadership development. In tandem with Phoenix’s Employment & Education services, mentors help young people explore career options, connect with employers and community service opportunities, and build the skills and networks needed to move into trades, arts, and service-sector roles.

solutions.text: Inclusive Hiring Supports for Local Employers: Offer toolkits, training and small incentives for businesses to adopt equitable hiring practices, implement anti-discrimination policies, create apprenticeship opportunities, and actively recruit Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer and 2SLGBTQIA+ talent.

resources.name: ISANS Employer Support Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides employers with practical toolkits, consultations and training on equitable and inclusive hiring, anti-discrimination policies, and culturally competent onboarding. Their team helps businesses recruit and retain newcomer talent through services like candidate matching, inclusive job description reviews, and workplace language support. This directly advances inclusive hiring practices and strengthens employer capacity to welcome immigrants and refugees in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Graduate to Opportunity (GTO)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: GTO offers salary incentives to Nova Scotia employers to create permanent, entry-level jobs for recent graduates, with a Diversity Bonus to encourage hiring from underrepresented groups such as Mi’kmaq, African Nova Scotians and other racially visible groups, persons with disabilities and recent immigrants. The program reduces employers’ risk and cost barriers so they can adopt more equitable hiring practices and bring diverse young talent into their teams. By pairing incentives with guidance on job quality and retention, GTO supports more inclusive workforce growth across the province.

resources.name: Employment & Training Program
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Employment & Training Program connects Indigenous job seekers with local employers and apprenticeships, and supports culturally safe, equitable hiring practices. The program offers employer outreach, recruitment support and advice on creating inclusive, anti-discriminatory workplaces that recognize Mi’kmaw culture and rights. By building partnerships and pipelines into skilled trades and other sectors, it helps employers actively recruit and retain Mi’kmaw talent.

resources.name: YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs – Employer Engagement
resources.description: The YMCA offers employer-focused workshops on inclusive recruitment, cross-cultural communication and anti-discrimination, along with customized support to adjust policies and practices for newcomer inclusion. They connect businesses with newcomer candidates, assist with job postings and screening, and advise on equitable onboarding and retention. These services help employers across Nova Scotia adopt inclusive hiring practices and expand their access to diverse immigrant talent.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 216, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works – Employer Services (TeamWork Cooperative)
resources.description: TeamWork Cooperative’s Nova Scotia Works Employer Services provide local businesses with inclusive hiring support, job-matching to diverse candidates and access to wage subsidies and incentives such as the provincial START program. They offer guidance and workshops on equitable recruitment, retention and anti-discrimination policies, and collaborate with community partners to source Mi’kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer and 2SLGBTQIA+ talent. This hands-on assistance helps employers operationalize inclusive hiring practices while reducing costs and risks.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

solutions.text: Culturally Appropriate Affordable Housing Initiatives: Develop community-based housing solutions such as co-ops, transitional housing and rent supports that prioritize youth at risk, newcomers and 2SLGBTQIA+ youth and incorporate cultural and safety needs identified by Mi'kmaq and African Nova Scotian communities.

resources.name: Wije’winen Housing and Indigenous Housing Support
resources.description: The Mi'kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Wije’winen initiative and Indigenous Housing Support team deliver culturally safe, community-based housing and Housing First supports for urban Indigenous people, including Mi’kmaq youth, families, and Two-Spirit/LGBTQ+ community members. They combine affordable units-in-development with tenancy advocacy, case management, and rent supplement navigation, ensuring housing that reflects Mi’kmaw cultural and safety needs while prioritizing those at highest risk of homelessness.

resources.name: Kinney Place – AKOMA Inclusive Affordable Housing
resources.description: Kinney Place provides new, deeply affordable apartments on the AKOMA lands, created by and for the African Nova Scotian community to address historical and systemic housing barriers. The development integrates culturally relevant design, on-site supports, and partnerships for rent supplements, creating safe, community-rooted housing options for youth, families, and elders that honor African Nova Scotian cultural identity and safety needs.

resources.name: Phoenix Youth Apartments & Housing Supports
resources.description: Phoenix operates a continuum of housing for youth aged 16–24, including emergency shelter, transitional apartments, and supported independent living, with inclusive services for 2SLGBTQIA+ youth and newcomers. Their teams provide culturally responsive, trauma-informed case management, life-skills development, and assistance accessing rent supports, helping at-risk youth stabilize and transition into long-term affordable housing.

resources.name: Supportive Housing for Young Mothers (SHYM)
resources.description: SHYM offers safe, affordable apartments with on-site transitional supports for mothers aged 16–24 and their children, welcoming newcomers and 2SLGBTQIA+ participants. Using a trauma-informed, culturally responsive model, SHYM connects residents to rent supplements, education, employment, and community resources, creating stable and culturally appropriate housing pathways for young families.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

solutions.text: Safe and Affirming Youth Drop-in Spaces: Fund and sustain accessible drop-in centres or designated hours in existing community hubs that provide culturally informed supports, peer groups, counselling referrals and programming for Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer and 2SLGBTQIA+ youth.

resources.name: The Youth Project (2SLGBTQIA+ Youth Drop-in and Programs)
resources.description: The Youth Project provides a safe, affirming drop-in space and designated program hours for 2SLGBTQIA+ youth ages 25 and under. It offers peer support groups, social programming, and workshops, and connects youth to gender-affirming counselling and health services, implementing culturally informed, trauma-aware supports that reduce isolation and foster belonging.

resources.name: Mi'kmaw Native Friendship Centre Youth Program and Drop-In
resources.description: The Mi'kmaw Native Friendship Centre operates culturally grounded youth drop-in and after-school programs that provide access to Elders, language and cultural activities, and peer groups for Mi'kmaq and other Indigenous youth, including Two-Spirit youth. Staff offer navigation and referrals to counselling, mental health, and social services, creating a safe, affirming hub that strengthens identity and belonging.

resources.name: Phoenix Centre for Youth
resources.description: Phoenix Centre for Youth is a low-barrier, walk-in drop-in centre for youth ages 16–24 that provides a safe, welcoming space, basic needs, recreation, and peer connection. Staff deliver culturally responsive supports and case management, including referrals to counselling, housing, employment, and health services, with an inclusive approach for African Nova Scotian, newcomer, and 2SLGBTQIA+ youth.

resources.name: YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs – Newcomer Youth & Teen Programs
resources.description: The YMCA’s Centre for Immigrant Programs offers newcomer youth drop-in and after-school hours featuring homework support, leadership development, and recreation in a safe, welcoming environment. Settlement staff use culturally informed practices and provide navigation and referrals to counselling and mental health services, supporting immigrant and refugee youth to build community and belonging.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 201, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Hope Blooms Youth Leadership and Community Hub
resources.description: Hope Blooms operates a community hub with daily after-school drop-in programming centered on an urban farm and community kitchen, offering mentorship, leadership, and entrepreneurship opportunities. Serving many African Nova Scotian and newcomer youth, the program provides culturally grounded supports, peer connection, and referrals to counselling and wraparound services through partner agencies.

solutions.text: Community Reconciliation and Cultural Exchange Events: Host regular public events — storytelling, music, food, workshops and shared ceremonies — led by Mi'kmaq and African Nova Scotian organizers to foster understanding, celebrate identity and create personal connections between communities.

resources.name: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia
resources.description: An African Nova Scotian–led museum and community hub that hosts regular public events such as storytelling circles, drumming and dance performances, intergenerational workshops, and community meals. The Centre frequently partners with Mi’kmaq organizers and local schools to co-present dialogues, shared ceremonies, and cultural exchanges that welcome the broader public, building relationships, understanding, and belonging across communities.
resources.address: 10 Cherry Brook Road, Cherry Brook, NS B2Z 1A8

resources.name: Africville Reunion Festival
resources.description: This annual gathering and the museum’s year-round programs bring together former residents, African Nova Scotians, and allies for music, food, storytelling, church services, and community celebrations on the historic Africville site. Led by African Nova Scotian organizers, these public events invite Mi’kmaq and other communities to share culture and history, fostering healing, reconciliation, and personal connections that counter systemic racism and strengthen belonging.

resources.name: Black Loyalist Heritage Centre
resources.description: The Centre offers ongoing public programming—exhibitions, guided storytelling tours, heritage days, music and dance showcases, and community feasts—celebrating the history and living culture of African Nova Scotians in Birchtown. Staff collaborate with Mi’kmaq knowledge keepers and regional partners for joint talks and cultural exchange events, using shared ceremonies and learning to build understanding and connections among youth, newcomers, and long-time residents.
resources.address: 119 Old Birchtown Road, Birchtown, NS B0T 1W0

resources.name: Wagmatcook Culture & Heritage Centre
resources.description: This Mi’kmaw-led cultural centre hosts regular public events—including traditional drumming and dance demonstrations, craft workshops, language sessions, and community feasts—guided by Elders and cultural practitioners. By welcoming schools, newcomers, and neighboring African Nova Scotian groups into shared ceremonies and teachings, the Centre nurtures reconciliation, celebrates identity, and builds lasting relationships across communities.

resources.name: Millbrook Cultural & Heritage Centre (Glooscap Heritage Centre)
resources.organization: Millbrook First Nation (Millbrook Cultural & Heritage Centre)
resources.description: The Centre delivers Mi’kmaw cultural programming—Elder-led storytelling, traditional arts workshops, seasonal celebrations, and educational talks—open to the public throughout the year. Through collaborations with African Nova Scotian organizations and local institutions, it convenes exchange events featuring music, food, and shared teachings that strengthen reconciliation and foster personal connections and belonging among diverse communities.

solutions.text: Expanded Settlement and Language Supports: Provide locally delivered language classes, job-readiness training, credential navigation help and newcomer orientation that are tailored to youth needs and connected to schools, employers and mentorship programs.

resources.name: Language Instruction for Newcomers to Canada (LINC)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers free, CLB-aligned English classes from literacy to advanced levels, offered in person and online, with youth-focused options and childminding to reduce barriers. Learners receive newcomer orientation, job-readiness workshops, and credential-recognition navigation, and are connected to mentors and employers through ISANS employment services and the Professional Mentorship Program—directly implementing locally delivered language and employment supports tailored to young newcomers.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: School Settlement Program
resources.organization: YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs (YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth)
resources.description: YMCA settlement staff work directly in HRCE schools to orient newcomer youth and families, provide individualized settlement plans, and connect students to English classes and tutoring. The program offers youth-focused workshops, leadership and job-readiness activities, and links to mentors and local employers through YMCA networks—anchoring language, orientation, and employment pathways where youth learn and live.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 208, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: English Language Learning & Newcomer Services
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts free English conversation groups, newcomer orientations, and homework clubs for teens and young adults at branches across HRM, often in partnership with ISANS. Staff and partners provide referrals for credential assessment and employment programs, and connect youth to volunteer and mentorship opportunities—making language learning and settlement supports accessible in community spaces closely tied to schools.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Connector Program (International/Newcomer & Recent Graduate Streams)
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program matches immigrant and international student youth with established professionals for one-on-one informational interviews, mentorship, and warm referrals that build local networks. Participants receive job-search coaching and direct employer connections across sectors, complementing language and settlement services by providing tailored, employer-linked pathways that improve retention and belonging.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Newcomer Settlement & Language Services (LINC)
resources.description: YMCA of Cape Breton provides locally delivered settlement orientation, youth activities, and federally funded LINC English classes in Sydney to help newcomer youth build language skills and navigate school and community life. Staff offer job-readiness support and connect participants with credential resources, mentors, and local employers across Cape Breton, integrating language, employment, and mentorship supports close to where youth live.

solutions.text: Inclusive School Curriculum and Anti-Bullying Programs: Work with school boards and community educators to incorporate Mi'kmaq and African Nova Scotian histories and contemporary contributions, and ensure 2SLGBTQIA+ inclusive materials and anti-bullying policies are taught and enforced.

resources.name: Treaty Education Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia (Department of Education and Early Childhood Development) in partnership with Mi'kmaw Kina'matnewey
resources.description: Treaty Education Nova Scotia integrates Mi'kmaq history, treaty relationships, language, and contemporary contributions into the P–12 curriculum across the province. Developed in partnership with Mi'kmaw Kina'matnewey, it provides lesson plans, teacher professional learning, and classroom resources used by regional centres for education to embed accurate Indigenous content and foster respect and belonging. By normalizing Mi'kmaw perspectives and countering stereotypes, the program supports safe, inclusive school climates.

resources.name: Safe and Inclusive Schools
resources.description: The Halifax Regional Centre for Education's Safe and Inclusive Schools team implements the Provincial School Code of Conduct, anti-bullying protocols, and 2SLGBTQIA+ inclusive practices in all HRCE schools. They train staff, support Gender and Sexuality Alliances, and provide SOGI-inclusive resources while working with student services and families to address incidents and promote belonging. This operationalizes inclusive curriculum and policy enforcement at the school level.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Education and Outreach (School Workshops and GSA Support)
resources.description: The Youth Project delivers 2SLGBTQIA+ education and anti-bullying workshops to students, teachers, and school staff across Nova Scotia, and supports the creation and sustainability of GSAs. Their school outreach provides age-appropriate, curriculum-aligned materials that address sexual orientation and gender identity, reduce homophobia and transphobia, and create safer classrooms. They collaborate with boards and educators to implement inclusive policies and classroom practices.

resources.name: Education and School Programs
resources.organization: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia offers curriculum-linked exhibits, tours, and teacher resources that highlight African Nova Scotian histories and contemporary achievements. Its education programs and outreach to schools help integrate accurate Black history into classrooms and support anti-racism and anti-bullying by building understanding and pride. The Centre partners with educators and community groups to strengthen inclusive learning environments province-wide.
resources.address: 10 Cherry Brook Road, Cherry Brook, NS B2Z 1A8

solutions.text: Community Advisory Councils with Lived-Experience Representation: Establish or expand municipal and organizational advisory councils that include youth and representatives from Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer and 2SLGBTQIA+ communities to guide local planning, services and funding decisions.

resources.name: Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: The Halifax Regional Municipality’s Youth Advisory Committee brings together diverse youth, including Mi’kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer and 2SLGBTQIA+ youth, to advise Regional Council on policies, programs and budget priorities that impact young people. By embedding lived-experience voices directly into municipal decision-making, the committee guides local planning and services to improve inclusion and belonging for diverse youth across HRM.

resources.name: African Nova Scotian Advisory Committee
resources.description: This standing advisory committee provides Halifax Regional Council with advice on issues affecting African Nova Scotian communities, including anti-Black racism, equitable access to municipal services, and culturally responsive programming. Composed of members with lived experience from African Nova Scotian communities, it informs municipal planning, service delivery and funding decisions to support inclusion and belonging.

resources.name: Diversity Advisory Committee
resources.description: The Town of Truro’s Diversity Advisory Committee brings residents with lived experience—such as Mi’kmaw and African Nova Scotian community members, newcomers, and 2SLGBTQIA+ residents—together to advise Council on inclusive policies, programs and events. Their recommendations shape municipal planning and services to reduce barriers and strengthen belonging in the community.

resources.name: Halifax Local Immigration Partnership – Immigrant Advisory Table
resources.description: The Immigrant Advisory Table convenes newcomers and former refugees to provide lived-experience advice to the Halifax Local Immigration Partnership on strategies, services and funding priorities that improve immigrant settlement and inclusion. Their input informs municipal, community and employer actions that strengthen belonging and retention for diverse newcomer communities.
resources.address: 1601 Lower Water Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3P6

resources.name: Chief’s Advisory Committee on Diversity
resources.description: Halifax Regional Police’s Chief’s Advisory Committee on Diversity engages leaders and community members from Mi’kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer and 2SLGBTQIA+ communities to advise on policing policies, training, and service delivery. This lived-experience council guides organizational planning and resource allocation to advance equitable, culturally competent public safety services.

solutions.text: Cultural Entrepreneurship and Arts Funding: Create micro-grants, incubators and exhibition/performance opportunities specifically for Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer and 2SLGBTQIA+ youth to build small businesses, cultural enterprises and creative careers rooted in community.

resources.name: ISANS Business Development Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides newcomers, including youth, with business planning support, training, mentorship and referrals to financing to start and grow small businesses and cultural enterprises. Through market-readiness workshops, networking and showcase events, newcomer creatives gain platforms to present work and build client bases—functioning as an incubator for community-rooted creative careers.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Media Arts Scholarship
resources.description: CFAT’s annual Media Arts Scholarship offers emerging artists a production stipend, mentorship, training and access to professional equipment, culminating in a public screening/exhibition. The program prioritizes equity-seeking communities—including Mi'kmaq, African Nova Scotian, newcomer and 2SLGBTQIA+ youth—providing micro-grant style support and an incubator environment that builds skills, portfolios and pathways to sustainable creative work.

resources.name: Community Access Program and Performance Opportunities
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op operates an affordable, community-run venue that prioritizes equity-seeking artists by offering subsidized space, technical support and presentation opportunities. Regular festivals and partner-led showcases provide 2SLGBTQIA+, Indigenous, African Nova Scotian and newcomer youth with platforms to perform, develop productions and earn revenue—key steps in building community-rooted cultural enterprises.

resources.name: Youth and Cultural Programs
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre delivers Indigenous youth programming that passes on Mi’kmaw arts and culture—such as beading, regalia-making, drumming and dance—alongside employment and entrepreneurship supports. Through markets, cultural celebrations and public performances, Mi’kmaq youth gain opportunities to sell work and showcase talent, growing small cultural enterprises and creative careers anchored in community.

resources.name: Programs and Events for African Nova Scotian Artists
resources.organization: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Black Cultural Centre presents exhibitions, concerts and heritage programming that showcase African Nova Scotian artists, often featuring youth performers and creators. Vendor markets and community events provide sales and stage opportunities that help young Black artists and cultural entrepreneurs build audiences, generate income and develop sustainable creative careers rooted in their communities.
resources.address: 10 Cherry Brook Road, Cherry Brook, NS B2Z 1A8

solutions.text: Culturally Informed Mental Health and Wellness Services: Develop locally accessible mental health supports that are trauma-informed and culturally specific, including peer-support groups, Indigenous healing practices, and counselling services sensitive to racialized and queer youth experiences.

resources.name: prideHealth
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health and IWK Health Centre
resources.description: prideHealth is a partnership of Nova Scotia Health and the IWK Health Centre that improves access to safe, gender‑affirming, and 2SLGBTQIA+‑competent care across Nova Scotia. It provides navigation, referrals to counselling and mental health services, and links to peer supports, using trauma‑informed and culturally responsive practices tailored to queer and trans youth.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Brotherhood and Sisterhood Initiatives
resources.description: These community‑based health programs offer culturally specific care for people of African descent, including primary care, mental health counselling, wellness groups, and peer navigation. Grounded in trauma‑informed practice and anti‑racism, they address barriers and racism‑related stress while strengthening belonging and health for African Nova Scotian youth and families.

resources.name: ISANS Wellness and Mental Health Programs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides trauma‑informed wellness and mental health supports for immigrants and refugees, including individual counselling with interpreters, group psychoeducation, and peer‑support circles. Services are culturally and linguistically responsive, helping newcomer youth and families heal from migration‑ and conflict‑related trauma while building community connections and belonging in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Phoenix Centre for Youth
resources.description: Phoenix Centre for Youth is a drop‑in and outreach hub for ages 16–24 that offers free counselling, case management, and peer‑support programming grounded in trauma‑informed and harm‑reduction principles. Staff provide culturally safe care for racialized and 2SLGBTQIA+ youth, helping young people access housing, health, and community resources that foster inclusion and wellbeing.

resources.name: CMM Mental Wellness Team
resources.description: The Confederacy of Mainland Mi'kmaq’s Mental Wellness Team delivers land‑based healing, cultural programming, and clinical counselling in Mi'kmaw communities across mainland Nova Scotia. Integrating Indigenous knowledge with trauma‑informed mental health care, the team facilitates circles, ceremonies, and peer supports alongside access to clinicians, supporting Mi'kmaq youth and families’ wellness and belonging.

solutions.text: Transport and Access Solutions for Rural and Underserved Areas: Organize community ride-shares, subsidized transit passes, bike-share programs and school-to-work shuttle services to reduce isolation and increase access to education, jobs and social programs for youth across regions.

resources.name: Low Income Transit Pass Program (LITP)
resources.description: Halifax Transit’s Low Income Transit Pass Program provides 50% discounted monthly bus and ferry passes to eligible low-income residents, including youth, newcomers, and marginalized communities. By lowering the cost barrier to reliable transportation across urban, suburban, and rural parts of the Halifax Regional Municipality, the program helps young people reach school, jobs, training, and community services, directly reducing isolation and improving inclusion.

resources.name: Welcoming Wheels
resources.description: Welcoming Wheels equips newcomer and low-income youth and families with refurbished bicycles, helmets, locks, lights, and safe-cycling training to support everyday mobility. By providing affordable, independent transportation for commuting to school, work, and social programs, the initiative reduces transportation barriers for underserved communities and fosters belonging and participation.

resources.name: Kings Transit Regional Bus Service
resources.description: Kings Transit operates a public bus network connecting rural and small-town communities throughout the Annapolis Valley, linking youth to schools, NSCC campuses, Acadia University, workplaces, and community services. With frequent stops across multiple municipalities and student fare options, the service expands affordable access to education, jobs, and social programs for youth in underserved areas.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

solutions.text: Support for Mi'kmaq-led Land Stewardship and Cultural Projects: Partner with local Mi'kmaq communities on stewardship, youth land-based learning, language revitalization and cultural economy projects that strengthen identity, create jobs and acknowledge Indigenous leadership in the region.

resources.name: Mi'kmaw Conservation Group (MCG)
resources.description: MCG is a Mi'kmaq-led stewardship program that restores rivers and coastal habitats, protects species at risk, and integrates Mi'kmaw ecological knowledge with Western science. It delivers youth land-based learning through community camps and field training, building skills in monitoring, habitat restoration, and traditional harvesting practices. The program creates seasonal and full-time jobs for Mi'kmaw community members as field technicians and coordinators, advancing Indigenous leadership in conservation across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Mi'kmaq Forestry Initiative (MFI)
resources.organization: Kwilmu’kw Maw-klusuaqn Negotiation Office (Mi’kmaq Rights Initiative)
resources.description: MFI is a Mi'kmaq-led, province-wide initiative that stewards Crown and community forest lands using Netukulimk principles, blending cultural values, biodiversity protection, and sustainable resource use. The program supports training and land-based learning for Mi'kmaw youth in areas like silviculture, forest monitoring, and non-timber forest products, while enabling community-driven forest enterprises. By centering Mi'kmaq governance in land management, MFI creates jobs and strengthens cultural identity through stewardship of traditional territories.

resources.name: Membertou Heritage Park
resources.description: Membertou Heritage Park is a Mi'kmaq-operated cultural centre and museum that offers guided cultural experiences, language-rich exhibits, and interpretive programming led by local knowledge keepers. It supports the cultural economy through an artisan marketplace and cultural tourism, creating employment for Mi'kmaw interpreters, artists, and youth. Land-based and seasonal activities connect visitors and community members to Mi'kmaw history and practices, reinforcing identity and Indigenous leadership in the region.

resources.name: Millbrook Cultural & Heritage Centre
resources.description: The Millbrook Cultural & Heritage Centre (formerly the Glooscap Heritage Centre) advances Mi'kmaw language and culture through exhibits, school programs, and community events that highlight traditional knowledge and stories. Its craft shop and cultural tourism offerings provide revenue and jobs for Mi'kmaw artists and cultural interpreters, strengthening the local cultural economy. Programming includes language content and opportunities for youth to engage with land-based cultural teachings, acknowledging Mi'kmaq leadership in heritage education.

solutions.text: Local Equity Data, Targets and Accountability: Collect community-level data on retention, employment and service access by identity groups (with privacy safeguards), set transparent equity targets, publish progress reports and use results to guide funding and program adjustments.

resources.name: Employment Equity Program and Workforce Census
resources.organization: Halifax Regional Municipality – Office of Diversity & Inclusion/ANSAIO
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality runs an Employment Equity Program that uses a confidential, voluntary workforce census to collect disaggregated data on representation, retention, and workplace experience across identity groups (including Mi’kmaq, African Nova Scotians, racialized communities, newcomers, people with disabilities, and 2SLGBTQIA+). The municipality sets representation and inclusion targets, publishes workforce diversity and progress reports, and uses results to adjust recruitment, training investments, and departmental plans to improve equitable access to municipal employment and services.

resources.name: Student Self-Identification and Equity Data Initiative
resources.description: HRCE implements voluntary student and staff self-identification and tracks outcomes like achievement, graduation, attendance, discipline, and access to supports by identity (e.g., Mi’kmaw and African Nova Scotian), with strict privacy safeguards. The centre sets measurable equity goals in its System Improvement Plan, publicly reports on progress, and reallocates resources (targeted programs, coaching, and community partnerships) to close gaps and strengthen retention and belonging for underrepresented youth.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Race-Based Data Collection in Policing
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Human Rights Commission leads a province-mandated initiative requiring Halifax Regional Police and Halifax District RCMP to collect standardized, privacy-protected race-based data on police interactions and publish community-level reports. The project sets clear equity objectives, identifies disparities affecting African Nova Scotian and Mi’kmaw communities, and guides policy, training, and resource allocation to reduce systemic discrimination and improve accountability.
resources.address: 5657 Spring Garden Road, Suite 305, Halifax, NS B3J 3R4

resources.name: Equity Data and EDI Accountability (Human Rights & Equity Services)
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Human Rights & Equity Services coordinates confidential self-identification and equity data across students, staff, and faculty to monitor recruitment, retention, and access to campus services by equity-deserving groups. The university sets transparent EDI targets, publishes annual progress updates, and uses results to guide funding decisions, targeted hiring and admissions initiatives, and program adjustments that enhance inclusion and belonging.

obstacles.title: Newcomer Attraction and Retention Hurdles
obstacles.description: Credential recognition, settlement supports, spousal employment, and social integration gaps limit long-term retention.

solutions.text: Local Credential Navigation Hub: A community-run centre that helps newcomers map their foreign credentials to local requirements, provides information on licensing bodies, connects them to bridging programs, and offers application assistance and document translation referrals.

resources.name: ISANS Career Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS Career Services functions as a comprehensive hub for internationally trained newcomers, providing one-on-one guidance to map foreign credentials to Nova Scotia’s workplace and regulatory requirements. Staff explain licensure pathways across regulated professions, assist with applications to assessment bodies and licensing regulators, and connect clients to bridging, mentorship, and sector-specific programs. They also provide referrals for certified translation and notarization of documents and host information sessions with regulatory bodies.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs (CIP)
resources.description: The YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs offers settlement and employment services that include credential and licensing navigation for newcomers. Settlement practitioners help clients map their education and experience to local standards, identify the correct licensing bodies, prepare and submit applications, and connect them to bridging programs, language training, and employer engagement opportunities. The centre also provides referrals for certified translation and helps organize required documentation.

resources.name: YMCA of Cape Breton Immigrant Services
resources.description: YMCA of Cape Breton Immigrant Services provides one-on-one settlement and employment counselling that guides newcomers through foreign credential recognition and local licensing pathways. Staff assist with understanding regulator requirements, filling out assessment and licensure applications, and connecting clients to bridging and upgrading programs and Nova Scotia Works supports. They also facilitate referrals for credential assessments and certified document translation to meet application standards.

resources.name: Internationally Educated Nurses (IEN) Pathway
resources.description: The IEN Pathway provides a structured navigation process for newcomers trained as nurses, mapping international education and experience to Nova Scotia’s nursing registration requirements. NSCN outlines licensure steps, reviews applicants’ credentials, supports documentation and assessment, and directs candidates to bridging or upgrading programs as needed. The pathway also advises on acceptable translations and how to obtain certified translations for required documents.

solutions.text: Community Bridging and Microcourse Programs: Short, locally delivered bridge courses and microcredentials (in partnership with colleges and employers) that translate international skills to local workplace standards and provide practical, employer-recognized certificates.

resources.name: Bridge to Work
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: Bridge to Work provides short, employer-led training and work placements that help internationally trained newcomers align their skills with Nova Scotia workplace standards. Participants complete targeted micro-courses and certifications (e.g., WHMIS, First Aid/CPR, safety, sector-specific training) and gain local experience and references through partnered employers—resulting in practical, employer-recognized credentials that translate prior international experience into local job readiness.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: NSCC Microcredentials
resources.description: NSCC offers short, stackable microcredentials co-designed with Nova Scotia employers to validate specific, job-ready competencies in fields such as IT, health, construction, and business. These locally delivered modules align learning to provincial workplace standards and award digital badges/certificates recognized by employers—enabling internationally trained individuals to quickly bridge skill gaps and demonstrate Canadian-standard competencies.

resources.name: Internationally Educated Nurse (IEN) Bridging Program
resources.organization: Registered Nurses Professional Development Centre (RNPDC), Nova Scotia Health
resources.description: RNPDC provides competency assessment and targeted bridge education that map internationally educated nurses’ prior training to Nova Scotia College of Nursing requirements. Through short courses, simulation labs, and supervised clinical placements, participants close identified gaps and earn completion documents recognized by the regulator and employers—directly translating international nursing skills to local practice standards.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

solutions.text: Employer–Community Mentorship Network: A volunteer mentor program pairing newcomers with local professionals in their field to provide guidance, references, interview practice, workplace culture coaching, and introductions to hiring managers.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program matches internationally trained newcomers with volunteer mentors who are established professionals in the same field. Mentors provide sector-specific guidance, mock interviews, resume and credential feedback, workplace culture coaching, and networking support, often introducing mentees to hiring managers and professional associations to accelerate labour market entry.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program links newcomers and recent graduates with volunteer ‘Connectors’—local employers and industry leaders—for one-on-one informational meetings and targeted introductions to at least three additional professionals in their field. Through this structured networking and light-touch mentorship, participants receive interview practice, workplace culture insights, and warm referrals to hiring managers and recruiters across the Halifax region.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Cape Breton Connector Program
resources.description: The Cape Breton Connector Program pairs newcomers and recent grads with volunteer business and community leaders who provide informational interviews, career guidance, and introductions to additional contacts in the same industry. This mentorship-style networking model helps participants practice interviews, understand local workplace norms, and secure referrals to hiring managers within Cape Breton’s employer community.

solutions.text: Spousal Employment Connector: A community-managed job-matching service and skills clinic focused on partners of newcomers, offering resume workshops, local labour-market orientation, short training, and connections to employers open to flexible or part-time roles.

resources.name: Employment Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides newcomers and their accompanying spouses/partners with customized job search support, including resume and cover letter workshops, interview practice, and local labour‑market orientation. The team offers short employment readiness training, mentoring, and job-matching with employer partners—including opportunities that are flexible or part-time—helping spouses build Canadian experience and connect quickly to work.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs – Employment Services (including YREACH)
resources.description: The YMCA supports newcomers and their spouses/partners with job search coaching, resume and cover-letter workshops, workplace culture and labour‑market orientation sessions, and referrals to short training. Staff connect clients to local employers open to hiring newcomers—including flexible and part-time roles—helping partners of immigrants gain first jobs, build networks, and integrate into the community.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 208, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Valley Connector Program
resources.description: The Valley Connector links newcomers, recent graduates, and accompanying spouses/partners with established business and community leaders who provide targeted introductions to employers and professional contacts. Through guided networking, labour‑market orientation, and curated connections, spouses can uncover flexible, part-time, and entry opportunities aligned with their skills while building a local network in the Annapolis Valley.
resources.address: 87 Cornwallis Street, Suite 201, Kentville, NS B4N 2E5

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works – Job Junction
resources.description: Job Junction provides free employment services to all job seekers, including spouses/partners of newcomers, offering resume and cover-letter workshops, interview preparation, labour‑market information, and individualized employment coaching. Their job developers maintain relationships with local employers and help match clients to suitable opportunities, including flexible and part-time roles that support families during the settlement period.
resources.address: 6950 Mumford Road, Suite 0120, Halifax, NS B3L 4W1

solutions.text: Newcomer Welcome and Buddy Families: Neighbourhood-based buddy or host-family programs that pair newcomers with established residents for social supports, cultural orientation, language practice, and informal networks to reduce isolation.

resources.name: Community Connections – Host & Family Match Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections program matches newcomer individuals and families with volunteer host families and local buddies who provide social support, neighborhood orientation, and informal networking. Matches meet regularly for activities like sharing meals, practicing English, and exploring community resources, helping reduce isolation and accelerating cultural and community integration.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YREACH Host Program (Community Connections)
resources.description: The YMCA’s YREACH Host Program pairs newcomers across Nova Scotia with volunteer host families and community mentors who introduce them to local services, social activities, and everyday Canadian life. Through regular meetups, language practice, and neighborhood orientation, the program builds newcomers’ informal networks and strengthens their sense of belonging.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 216, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: English Language Learning (ELL) Volunteer Tutoring & Conversation Groups
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries matches newcomers with trained volunteer tutors and conversation partners for one-on-one or small-group English practice and social connection at neighborhood branches. These pairings help newcomers build friendships, learn local norms, and navigate community resources while reducing isolation and strengthening informal networks.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: International Student Peer Mentorship Program
resources.description: Dalhousie’s peer mentorship program pairs new international students with experienced student mentors who offer cultural orientation, campus and city navigation, and social support. Regular meetups and events help newcomers practice English, make local connections, and integrate into community life—building informal networks that support long-term retention.

solutions.text: Community Childcare Co-op and Drop-in: A cooperative childcare or drop-in system organized by community groups to provide affordable, flexible childcare during job searches, training, or initial settlement periods.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides free, licensed on-site childminding so newcomer parents can attend language classes, employment services, and settlement appointments. The care is short-term and flexible to match program times, functioning as a community-based drop-in model that removes childcare barriers during job searches, training, and initial settlement.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC) Childminding
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth - Centre for Immigrant Programs
resources.description: The YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs offers supervised childminding for infants and children while parents participate in LINC classes, settlement services, and job readiness workshops. This no-cost, flexible, program-time care mirrors a community drop-in model, enabling newcomers to pursue training and employment supports without childcare costs.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Childminding and Family Drop-in
resources.description: The North Grove is a community hub that provides free childminding during adult programs such as skills-building, community kitchen, and partner-led employment or settlement sessions. Its drop-in family programming and short-term, flexible child care help parents participate in training, appointments, and job search activities, reflecting a community-organized childcare solution.

resources.name: Child-Minding and Family Support Programs
resources.organization: Home of the Guardian Angel (Chebucto Family Centre)
resources.description: Chebucto Family Centre offers on-site child-minding and family drop-in programs so parents can attend prenatal, parenting, life-skills, and partner-delivered employment supports. Coordinated by a community organization, the care is free and scheduled around program times, reducing barriers for job search and training in a cooperative, drop-in style.

solutions.text: Local Internship and Apprenticeship Pool: A community-coordinated pool of paid internships, work placements, and apprenticeships with local small businesses and public institutions specifically designated for internationally trained talent to gain local experience.

resources.name: Workplace Placement Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS coordinates a pool of paid work placements and internships with small businesses, nonprofits, and public-sector employers across Nova Scotia specifically for internationally trained newcomers. Through employer outreach, screening, and wage subsidies, the program matches clients with short-term paid roles that provide Canadian work experience, mentorship, and local references, often leading to permanent employment.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Newcomer Apprenticeship Supports (START and Employer Incentives)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency helps internationally trained tradespeople enter paid apprenticeships with local employers by assessing prior learning, supporting credential recognition, and actively matching candidates to apprenticeship opportunities. Through the START program and other employer incentives, NSAA offsets wages and training costs, creating a coordinated pool of paid placements that give newcomers Nova Scotia work experience and a pathway to certification.

resources.name: Federal Internship for Newcomers (FIN) – Atlantic Region
resources.description: FIN is a paid internship program that places qualified newcomers into federal departments, agencies, and partner organizations across Atlantic Canada, including Nova Scotia. The program provides Canadian work experience, on-the-job training, and mentorship through time‑limited paid placements, helping internationally trained professionals build local references and transition into long-term employment.

solutions.text: Social and Cultural Events Calendar: A centralized, community-run calendar and outreach program that promotes multicultural events, volunteer opportunities, sports and arts groups to help newcomers build social ties and a sense of belonging.

resources.name: ISANS Community Connections & Events Calendar
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS maintains an online events calendar and runs Community Connections programming that promotes multicultural gatherings, volunteer opportunities, and arts/sports-related activities for immigrants and refugees. Through outreach with partner groups and volunteer hosts, ISANS curates and publicizes community events and networking opportunities that help newcomers build friendships, practice language, and feel a sense of belonging in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Halifax Public Libraries – Events Calendar & Newcomer Programs
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries operates a system-wide online events calendar featuring multicultural celebrations, language conversation groups, arts workshops, and community meetups across its branches. Library staff conduct outreach with local partners to promote volunteer roles and community groups, acting as a centralized, community-run hub that connects newcomers to social, cultural, and recreational opportunities.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Cape Breton Regional Library – Community Events Calendar
resources.description: The Cape Breton Regional Library hosts a centralized online calendar for branch and community events, including English conversation groups, cultural showcases, music and arts programs, and newcomer social hours. Librarians and partners use the platform and in-branch outreach to highlight local festivals, volunteer opportunities, and recreation groups so newcomers can connect with people and activities in their communities.

resources.name: PARL Events Calendar & Newcomer Outreach
resources.description: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library (PARL) maintains a regional events calendar featuring conversation cafés, cultural celebrations, arts clubs, and community meetups across its branches. Staff collaborate with settlement agencies and municipalities to promote volunteer roles, local festivals, and sports/recreation groups, providing a centralized, community-run hub that helps newcomers build social networks and a sense of belonging.

solutions.text: Language Cafés and Conversation Circles: Free or low-cost community language meetups hosted at libraries, community centres, and cafes that combine practical language practice with local culture and job-search vocabulary sessions.

resources.name: English Conversation Group (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts free, drop-in English Conversation Groups at branches such as Halifax Central Library, where newcomers practice speaking with volunteer facilitators and other learners. Sessions often include everyday and workplace vocabulary, local news and culture topics, and practical language for job search and community life. This implements language cafés by offering informal, low-barrier practice in a welcoming public space.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Conversation Circles for Newcomers
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS runs Conversation Circles that connect trained volunteers with newcomers for weekly small-group speaking practice in person and online. Topics focus on Canadian workplace culture, resumes and interviews, and day-to-day life in Nova Scotia, building confidence, social connections, and employment readiness. The program functions like a language café—free, practical, and rooted in local culture and community networks.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: English Conversation Circle (McConnell Library, Sydney)
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library’s McConnell Library offers a free English Conversation Circle as a friendly meetup for adult learners, often supported by local settlement partners. Participants practice speaking, learn about local customs and services, and cover job-related vocabulary in an informal setting. Hosting the group at the public library keeps it accessible, social, and community-focused, aligning with the language café model.

resources.name: EAL Conversation Circle (Lunenburg Library)
resources.description: South Shore Public Libraries hosts English as an Additional Language (EAL) Conversation Circles at the Lunenburg Library. The drop-in sessions emphasize everyday communication, Nova Scotia culture, and workplace/job-search language, supported by volunteers and community partners. Meeting in a library ‘café-style’ environment keeps the program free, welcoming, and practical for newcomers seeking language and community connections.

solutions.text: Community Sponsorship and Settlement Circles: Neighbourhood sponsorship groups that assist with initial settlement needs—housing search, school registration, orientation to services—and provide a local support network through the first year.

resources.name: Community Connections
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections program recruits and trains volunteer welcome teams and mentors who form settlement circles around newcomer individuals and families. These volunteers help with practical first‑year needs—apartment searches, school registration, navigating health care and public services—and facilitate social integration through local activities and peer networks, directly implementing the neighbourhood support model described in the solution.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Private Sponsorship of Refugees (PSR) and BVOR Support
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: As a Sponsorship Agreement Holder, ISANS organizes and supports neighbourhood sponsorship groups that bring refugee families to Nova Scotia. The program trains and coaches sponsor teams to develop and carry out settlement plans, including securing housing, enrolling children in school, orienting families to transportation and health services, and building a community support network throughout the first year.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Refugee Sponsorship Program
resources.organization: Anglican Diocese of Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island
resources.description: The Anglican Diocese of Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island acts as a Sponsorship Agreement Holder, equipping parish- and community-based groups to sponsor refugees. Settlement committees in local parishes provide hands-on first‑year support—finding and furnishing housing, registering children in schools, arranging health coverage and appointments, and fostering community connections—functioning as settlement circles that ensure a supported start in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: YREACH Community Connections and Host Program
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth – YREACH (YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs)
resources.description: YREACH mobilizes local volunteers and community groups across Nova Scotia to form host circles that welcome and orient newcomers in their first year. Volunteers assist with housing searches, school registration, understanding transportation and health systems, and creating social links in neighbourhoods, complementing formal settlement services with a peer-based, community sponsorship approach.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 216, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Volunteer Work Experience Pathways: Structured volunteer-to-hire programs with local nonprofits and social enterprises that allow newcomers to gain Canadian references, local skills, and visibility within community employers.

resources.name: Community Connections (Volunteering)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections includes a volunteering stream that orients newcomers to Canadian volunteer culture, then brokers structured placements with local nonprofits and social enterprises. Staff match clients to roles aligned with their skills and career goals, ensure supervision and training plans are in place, and help participants translate their experience into Canadian references and resumes. This pathway increases newcomers’ visibility with community employers and has led many to interviews and hires with host agencies or partner organizations.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Volunteer & Peer Leadership Program
resources.description: The North Grove engages newcomers in structured volunteer roles across its community food centre, garden, and family programs, providing on-the-job training, supervision, and reference letters. Participants can progress into peer leader roles with added responsibilities, public-facing experience, and honoraria, creating clear steps from volunteering to paid opportunities on-site or with partner employers. This hands-on pathway helps newcomers build Canadian work experience, local networks, and verified references valued by community employers.

resources.name: ReStore Volunteer Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia’s ReStore offers structured retail, warehouse, merchandising, and customer service volunteer roles that include orientation, safety training, and skills coaching. Newcomers gain Canadian workplace experience and direct supervisor references, while learning point-of-sale, inventory, and logistics practices used by local employers. ReStore frequently considers experienced volunteers for paid store roles and provides references that help volunteers transition to employment in retail and logistics across HRM.

resources.name: Volunteer Program
resources.description: Feed Nova Scotia runs a structured volunteer program with roles in warehousing, food sorting, driving support, and administration, all of which include training, safety orientation, and performance feedback. Newcomers build local, verifiable experience and receive reference letters from supervisors; job postings are regularly shared with active volunteers, and the organization often hires from its volunteer pool for operational roles. These placements deliver Canadian references, practical skills, and day-to-day contact with employers and partners in the local food security network.

solutions.text: Local Recognition Badge System: A community-endorsed digital portfolio/badge program where local employers and training providers validate newcomer skills and microcredentials, making informal and foreign experience visible to recruiters.

resources.name: NSCC Microcredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College designs short, skills-focused microcredentials with local industry input and issues them as portable digital badges that employers can verify. The college also supports recognition of prior learning so internationally trained newcomers can have informal or foreign experience assessed and translated into locally recognized microcredentials, making their competencies visible to Nova Scotia recruiters.

resources.name: ISANS SkillsMatch
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: SkillsMatch is an online recruitment and skills-profiling platform that helps newcomers build verified digital portfolios highlighting qualifications, experience, and competencies. ISANS staff and employer partners validate credentials, references, and occupational readiness, creating an employer-endorsed profile that makes international and informal skills visible to Nova Scotia recruiters.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Micro-credentials & Digital Badges
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University offers microcredentials that are co-designed with industry to validate specific, in-demand competencies and are issued as shareable digital badges. These badges help newcomers translate prior and international learning into employer-recognized evidence that can be added to digital portfolios and shared with Nova Scotia recruiters.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Microcredentials (Open Learning & Career Development)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Open Learning & Career Development unit delivers microcredentials that document assessed competencies and are issued as digital badges that can be shared with employers. Developed in collaboration with local industry, these credentials help internationally trained learners build a verifiable, employer-recognized digital portfolio to support hiring and career progression in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Business Pledge for Inclusive Hiring: A municipal chamber-led initiative where local businesses commit publicly to fair hiring practices for internationally trained candidates, including interview adjustments, skills-based hiring, and trial work periods.

resources.name: Employer Support Services (Inclusive Hiring, Skills-Based Recruitment, and On‑the‑Job Training)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Employer Support Services help local businesses adopt inclusive, skills-based hiring practices for internationally trained candidates. The team provides coaching on equitable recruitment (including interview adjustments and bias-aware screening), connects employers to qualified newcomers via a skills-first job board, and facilitates On‑the‑Job Training wage subsidies that function as trial work periods to evaluate fit before permanent hire.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Halifax Connector Program (Inclusive Hiring and Employer Commitments to Newcomer Talent)
resources.description: The Halifax Connector Program engages employers to publicly participate as ‘Connectors,’ committing to meet internationally trained candidates and consider skills-first pathways into roles. Through employer outreach and guidance, the program encourages inclusive interview practices, promotes competency-based screening, and often leads to short-term projects or work trials that help businesses assess newcomer talent before long-term hiring.
resources.address: 1969 Upper Water Street, Suite 1300, Halifax, NS B3J 3R7

resources.name: Cape Breton Connector Program (Employer Inclusion and Newcomer Hiring Pathways)
resources.description: The Cape Breton Connector Program partners with local businesses that commit to inclusive, skills-focused hiring for internationally trained candidates by engaging as Connectors and mentors. The initiative promotes interview flexibility and practical, project-based or short trial placements to evaluate candidates’ skills on the job, helping employers build confidence to make fair, long-term hires.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

solutions.text: Spousal Entrepreneurship Support: Startup clinics, microgrants, and mentorship for newcomer spouses who want to start home-based or small-scale businesses, run by local economic development and immigrant-serving organizations.

resources.name: Business Development Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides one-on-one business counselling, market research support, workshops, and mentorship matching tailored to immigrant entrepreneurs, including spouses who want to launch home-based or small-scale ventures. The program helps clients validate business ideas, navigate licensing and taxation in Nova Scotia, connect with local networks, and access financing such as microloans through partner financial institutions—directly implementing startup clinics and mentorship that ease newcomer families’ path to self-employment.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Start-Up Classic
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED’s Start-Up Classic is a cohort-based program that guides early-stage entrepreneurs through business planning, marketing, and sales with hands-on workshops and clinics, plus access to experienced advisors and mentors. Newcomer spouses can use the program to formalize home-based or side-business ideas and may pursue CEED’s Micro Loan financing and advisory supports to get to first customers.
