resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Newcomer Program
resources.description: Futurpreneur’s Newcomer Program provides financing and up to two years of mentorship to immigrants launching businesses in Canada, including small and home-based ventures in Nova Scotia. The program tailors eligibility and support for those new to Canada, pairing participants with local mentors and resources to build networks and navigate the provincial business environment.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Connector Program (Entrepreneur Stream)
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program matches newcomer and spousal entrepreneurs with established business leaders for informational interviews, referrals, and networking that can lead to customers, advisors, and mentors. The program hosts regular networking and business ecosystem sessions, helping internationally trained spouses integrate quickly and turn small-scale business ideas into viable ventures in the Halifax region.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Housing Navigation and Shared Living Platform: Community-managed platform that helps newcomers find affordable housing options, roommate matching, and short-term stays while they secure permanent accommodation.

resources.name: ISANS Settlement & Housing Support
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides housing navigation for immigrants and refugees, helping clients understand the Halifax rental market, tenant rights, and how to find affordable rooms, apartments, and shared accommodations. Staff curate community listings, liaise with landlords and volunteers, and coordinate short-term stays for newly arrived newcomers (especially refugee arrivals) while permanent housing is arranged—functioning as a practical matching and navigation hub.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: YREACH (YMCA Immigrant Services)
resources.description: YREACH supports newcomers across Nova Scotia with housing search, landlord outreach, and connections to shared rentals and roommate opportunities through community networks and online tools. In many communities, staff also help arrange short-term host-home or temporary stays for clients while they secure longer-term accommodation, effectively operating a community-managed navigation and matching service.

resources.name: Off-Campus Living (Dalhousie University)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Off-Campus Living service hosts a centralized platform (via Places4Students) where students and other newcomers to Halifax can search affordable rentals, find roommates, and browse sublets or short-term stays. Advising and workshops help users understand leasing, shared-living arrangements, and tenant rights as they transition to longer-term housing.

resources.name: CBU Housing: Off-Campus Listings & Homestay Program
resources.description: Cape Breton University provides an off-campus housing portal with listings for rooms, shared rentals, and roommate matching, alongside a Homestay Program that places international students with local host families. These services give newcomers immediate short-term options and a guided path to secure affordable, longer-term accommodation in the community.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

solutions.text: Employer Awareness and Cultural Competency Workshops: Locally delivered training for hiring managers and HR staff on recognizing foreign qualifications, inclusive onboarding, and practical adjustments to integrate internationally trained employees.

resources.name: Employer Support Services – Workplace Culture & Inclusive Onboarding Training
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers employer-focused workshops such as Workplace Culture, Working with Newcomers, and Onboarding for Diversity that help hiring managers and HR teams recruit and retain internationally trained talent. Sessions cover recognizing and valuing foreign qualifications and experience, bias-aware hiring, and practical onboarding adjustments (e.g., mentorship, language supports, and clear competency mapping) to integrate newcomers effectively.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: YREACH Employer Engagement & Workplace Inclusion Workshops
resources.description: YREACH provides outreach and training to employers across Nova Scotia on hiring, onboarding, and retaining newcomers, including those recruited through the Atlantic Immigration Program. Workshops build cultural competency for HR and supervisors, explain how to interpret international credentials and work histories, and offer practical strategies for inclusive onboarding and day-to-day workplace accommodations.

resources.name: Intercultural Competence Training for Employers and Community Partners
resources.description: Dalhousie’s International Centre offers customized intercultural competence workshops that help employers and HR professionals build inclusive hiring and onboarding practices for internationally trained employees and co-op students. Training focuses on cross-cultural communication, bias-aware recruitment, team integration, and practical onboarding supports, with guidance on aligning international experience with job competencies.

solutions.text: Neighbourhood Welcome Kits and Orientation Tours: Volunteer-created welcome packages and guided tours that introduce newcomers to local services, transit, healthcare, schools, recreation, and neighbourhood social hubs.

resources.name: Community Connections Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections pairs newcomers with trained local volunteers who provide friendly, practical orientation to everyday life in Nova Scotia. Volunteers assemble welcome information packages and lead neighbourhood and transit tours that introduce newcomers to health clinics, schools, recreation centres, community hubs, and key local services—helping people build social networks and confidence to settle long-term.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YREACH (YMCA Newcomer Community Integration)
resources.description: YREACH provides settlement outreach across Nova Scotia, coordinating volunteers and staff to welcome newcomers with orientation sessions, guided community tours, and tailored welcome packages. These tours and kits highlight how to use local transit, access healthcare and schools, find recreation programs, and connect with neighbourhood social spaces—speeding up integration and boosting retention.

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: The Cape Breton Welcome Network mobilizes volunteer ‘Welcome Ambassadors’ who greet new residents, deliver community-specific welcome packages, and offer personalized orientation tours. These tours cover transit options, family health and school connections, recreation assets, and social hubs—helping newcomers quickly find their footing and feel at home in communities across Cape Breton.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

resources.name: Newcomer Services (Welcome Tours & Orientation) – Central Library
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Newcomer Services team offers welcome tours and one-on-one orientations at the Central Library, providing newcomers with information packages and personalized referrals to local services. Staff and trained volunteers introduce public transit resources, health and school system navigation tools, recreation programs, and neighbourhood community hubs—creating an accessible first stop for settling in HRM.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Newcomer Peer Support and Mental Health Groups: Locally available peer-led support groups and culturally sensitive mental health drop-ins to address settlement stressors, isolation, and family integration challenges.

resources.name: ISANS Wellness
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: Through its Wellness program, ISANS offers peer-led support groups (such as newcomer women’s circles and parenting groups), multilingual mental well-being workshops, and low-barrier wellness drop-ins facilitated by culturally competent staff and trained volunteers. These activities help newcomers process settlement stress, reduce isolation, and strengthen family integration while connecting participants to formal mental health care when needed.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YREACH (YMCA Settlement Services)
resources.description: YREACH operates province-wide, hosting peer-support circles, newcomer family meet-ups, and community drop-ins in libraries, schools, and YMCA sites, often co-facilitated by staff and volunteer mentors from diverse cultures. Sessions focus on social connection, coping skills, and navigation of services, addressing settlement stress and spousal/family integration while promoting mental well-being.

resources.name: Newcomer Health Clinic
resources.description: The Newcomer Health Clinic provides culturally safe primary and mental health care for refugees and other eligible newcomers, including trauma-informed screening, short-term counselling, and group orientation/wellness sessions supported by interpreters. The team collaborates with settlement partners to provide low-barrier wellness information and connects clients to peer-led supports and community drop-ins that reduce isolation and family stress.

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: Volunteer Community Connectors lead peer social groups, coffee chats, walking groups, and informal drop-ins that welcome newcomers across Cape Breton. These peer-led activities build trust, reduce isolation, and help families integrate, with staff providing culturally responsive referrals to mental health and settlement services when additional support is needed.
resources.address: 285 Charlotte Street, Suite 206, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

obstacles.title: Arts and Culture Ecosystem Fragility
obstacles.description: Precarious incomes, venue shortages, and limited touring and funding threaten creative careers that enrich community life.

solutions.text: Community Arts Microgrant Fund: A locally governed microgrant program funded by municipalities, businesses and community crowdfunding to provide small, fast-turnaround stipends for projects, short tours, or living expenses for artists between gigs.

resources.name: Arts Equity Funding Initiative (AEFI)
resources.description: Arts Nova Scotia’s AEFI provides small, accessible project grants to Indigenous, African Nova Scotian, immigrant, deaf and disability, 2SLGBTQIA+, and other equity-deserving artists and collectives. With simplified applications and multiple intakes, it functions as a microgrant stream that can quickly underwrite project costs, short tours/showcases, or gap expenses between gigs—stabilizing artists’ incomes and enabling fast-turnaround community arts activity.

resources.name: Music Nova Scotia Investment Program
resources.description: This program offers micro-funding to Nova Scotia musicians for artist development, marketing, touring/showcasing, and professional development, with multiple intakes each year and relatively quick decisions. By covering targeted, short-term costs—such as travel, accommodations, per diems, and promotional expenses—it provides fast-turnaround stipends that help artists bridge periods between gigs and sustain careers within the province.
resources.address: 2169 Gottingen Street, Suite 003, Halifax, NS B3K 3B5

resources.name: Halifax Community Grants Program – Arts & Culture Project Grants
resources.description: HRM’s Community Grants Program provides small project grants (often in the microgrant range) to community arts and culture initiatives, including artist stipends, pop-up events, workshops, and neighborhood arts activations. Although administered annually, it channels municipal funds to quickly resource grassroots projects that generate local creative activity, offering flexible support that can help cover modest project, touring, or honorarium expenses for artists.

solutions.text: Shared Venue & Timebank Network: A community-managed scheduling platform that lets venues, churches, schools and businesses share space and off-peak hours with performing and visual artists at low or barter-based cost.

resources.name: Bus Stop Theatre Co-op – Community Venue Rentals
resources.description: An artist-run cooperative operating a black-box theatre that offers affordable, sliding-scale rentals and member discounts for rehearsals, performances, film shoots, and workshops. Its community-managed booking calendar prioritizes independent and emerging artists, maximizing off-peak hours so creatives can access professional space without long-term overhead, directly alleviating venue scarcity and cost barriers.

resources.name: Halifax Public Libraries – Free Community Rooms and Paul O’Regan Hall Bookings
resources.description: Across its branches, Halifax Public Libraries provides free or low-cost meeting rooms, studios, and performance spaces—such as the Paul O’Regan Hall—bookable online by artists and community groups. By opening civic venues during off-peak hours for rehearsals, small performances, and exhibits, the library system functions as a shared-space network that reduces presentation costs and expands access for local creatives.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Alderney Landing – Theatre, Market, and Gallery Rentals
resources.description: A waterfront cultural hub offering accessible rentals of its theatre, market hall, outdoor plaza, and The Craig Gallery for performances, rehearsals, and exhibitions. Staff coordinate a centralized calendar and community/nonprofit rates to fill off-peak times, effectively sharing public and commercial spaces with artists at low cost to strengthen the local arts ecosystem.

resources.name: Eltuek Arts Centre – Studios and Shared Spaces
resources.organization: Eltuek Arts Centre (a New Dawn initiative)
resources.description: A multi-tenant arts centre that provides affordable studios, rehearsal rooms, and common areas to artists and community groups through an accessible booking process and sliding-scale options. By converting a former educational/convent complex into shared creative infrastructure and coordinating schedules across venues, Eltuek expands off-peak access and reduces overhead for Cape Breton artists.

resources.name: St. Andrew’s United Church Halifax – Sanctuary & Hall Rentals for the Arts
resources.description: This downtown church actively shares its acoustically renowned Sanctuary and adjacent halls with choirs, ensembles, festivals, and visual artists at community rates. Its booking office opens non-worship, off-peak hours to cultural uses, providing affordable performance and exhibition space that helps artists present work without prohibitive venue costs.

solutions.text: Artist Cooperative Studios and Maker Spaces: Convert vacant storefronts and underused municipal buildings into artist-run co-op studios and maker spaces with affordable monthly rents, shared tools and collective promotion.

resources.name: Bus Stop Theatre Co-op
resources.description: An artist-run cooperative venue that provides affordable rehearsal, creation, and performance space along with shared technical equipment and production support. By operating as a co-op in a converted storefront, it pools resources for members, coordinates collective promotion, and sustains a hub for local creators to develop and present work.

resources.name: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design – Shared Studios and Maker Facilities
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: This downtown arts hub offers shared, well-equipped studios (e.g., clay, textiles, jewellery/metal, print) with affordable access and rentals for artisans and emerging makers. It supports collective promotion through exhibitions, retail opportunities, and community programming, enabling artists to use shared tools and space to build sustainable creative careers.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: A public, municipal makerspace that provides free or low-cost access to shared tools like sewing machines, Cricut cutters, button makers, and other creative equipment, plus staff support and workshops. Located within the Halifax Central Library, it repurposes underused public space to enable collaborative making and community promotion of creative projects.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: The Deanery Project – Community Maker & Studio Spaces
resources.description: A rural, community-run centre offering affordable access to shared workshops and studios, including woodworking, textiles, and eco-design labs, along with residency and training programs. It repurposes community facilities to host collaborative making and collective promotion through events, exhibitions, and partnerships that support artists and makers.
resources.address: 751 West Ship Harbour Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

resources.name: The Make Space at People’s Place Library (Antigonish)
resources.description: A public library makerspace offering shared tools such as 3D printing, sewing equipment, and digital creation tools, with free or low-cost access and staff support. By integrating a makerspace into a municipal library building, it lowers barriers for youth and creatives to prototype, learn, and showcase work, advancing collective promotion and community-based making.

solutions.text: Regional Touring Hub and Artist Exchange: Community organizations coordinate a regional touring hub that bundles logistics, marketing and travel for small-scale touring productions so artists can reach neighbouring towns without unsustainable costs.

resources.name: deCoste Performing Arts Centre – Presenting Series
resources.description: deCoste acts as a regional hub on Nova Scotia’s North Shore by co-booking tours with neighbouring venues so small ensembles can route multiple dates in one trip. Staff coordinate shared marketing assets, advance technical riders, and bundle travel and accommodation planning with partner theatres, reducing per-stop costs and making community-scale touring sustainable.

resources.name: King’s Theatre Presents
resources.description: King’s Theatre builds touring circuits with partner presenters across the Annapolis Valley and South Shore, using block-booking to secure consecutive dates for small theatre, dance, and music productions. The team aggregates marketing, coordinates travel and accommodations, and advances logistics across multiple towns, enabling artists to reach neighbouring communities without prohibitive costs.
resources.address: 209 St George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

resources.name: Mermaid Theatre of Nova Scotia – Touring Productions
resources.description: Mermaid centrally manages routing, trucking of sets/puppets, travel and accommodations, and turnkey marketing kits for its small-scale family productions, enabling efficient multi-stop tours across Nova Scotia and beyond. As the anchor of the Mermaid Imperial Performing Arts Centre in Windsor, it also collaborates with nearby presenters to add neighbouring dates and share logistics, keeping tours affordable for artists and communities.

resources.name: Marigold Cultural Centre – Presenting Series
resources.description: The Marigold co-books with a corridor of North Shore venues to assemble weekend and weeklong tours for small touring productions, aligning dates so artists can play Truro and neighbouring towns on a single run. Staff bundle marketing campaigns, coordinate technical needs, and organize travel and accommodations with partner sites, lowering costs and expanding artists’ reach.

solutions.text: Pop-up & Mobile Venue Program: Organize pop-up performances, galleries and movie nights in parks, storefronts and community centres using portable staging so artists can test work and reach new audiences quickly.

resources.name: Outdoor Movies in Civic Square
resources.description: Downtown Truro Partnership presents free outdoor movie nights in Civic Square using an inflatable screen and portable A/V, transforming the public plaza into a temporary cinema. These pop-up events often pair with live performances and activations, letting local artists test work and reach new audiences in a low-barrier, highly visible setting.

resources.name: Salt Yard Sessions
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia’s Salt Yard Sessions is a free summer music series on the Halifax waterfront that deploys a seasonal outdoor stage and portable production to host frequent pop-up performances. By activating public spaces with quick-setup shows, it reduces venue barriers, helps artists reach passersby and tourists, and creates new audience pathways outside traditional venues.
resources.address: 1751 Lower Water Street, Suite 701, Halifax, NS B3J 1S5

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty Placemaking Program
resources.description: This program funds temporary public art and storefront activations that convert vacant downtown spaces into pop-up galleries and performance sites. By supporting mobile and short-term installations in parks, plazas, and storefronts, it enables artists to quickly present new work and connect with diverse audiences while strengthening the urban cultural ecosystem.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

resources.name: Mermaid Theatre Touring Productions
resources.description: Mermaid Theatre brings its acclaimed puppet theatre to schools, libraries, and community centres across Nova Scotia using transportable sets, lighting, and staging. These mobile performances convert multipurpose rooms into temporary theatres, allowing artists to share work rapidly with communities that may lack formal venues and helping build new, family-focused audiences.

solutions.text: Community-led Arts Residency Program: Short paid residencies hosted by libraries, schools, seniors’ homes and cultural centres that give artists income, workspace and opportunities to build local audiences and education partnerships.

resources.name: Halifax Public Libraries Musician-in-Residence
resources.description: A short, paid residency that places a local musician at the Halifax Central Library and across branches to create, rehearse, and deliver free public programs. The resident receives an honorarium and workspace while partnering with library staff to host concerts, workshops, and youth education sessions that build local audiences. By embedding an artist in a community hub, it provides income, venue access, and outreach opportunities aligned with the solution.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: NSCAD Community Studio Residency — New Glasgow
resources.organization: NSCAD University (in partnership with Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library)
resources.description: This fixed-term community residency places emerging artists in studio space at the New Glasgow Public Library to create new work and lead public programming. Residents collaborate with the library, local schools, and community partners to deliver workshops, talks, and exhibitions that grow local audiences and education connections. The program provides space, institutional support, and avenues for paid public engagement that stabilize artists’ income and deepen community ties.
resources.address: 182 Dalhousie Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 5E3

resources.name: Lunenburg School of the Arts Artist-in-Residence Program
resources.description: A 6–12 week residency that provides selected artists with a stipend, housing, and studio space in a small-town cultural centre. Residents present public talks, open studios, and community workshops—often including youth classes—building local audiences and education partnerships while advancing their practice. The program directly supports artist livelihoods and connects them with schools and the wider community.

resources.name: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts Artist Residency Program
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: Short, community-engaged residencies at a rural arts centre offering studio space, accommodation, and production support, with many residencies incorporating stipends or honoraria. Artists deliver public workshops, school outreach, and open studios that cultivate local audiences and hands-on learning opportunities. This model provides time, space, and income pathways for artists while strengthening arts access in the surrounding communities.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

resources.name: Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21 Artist-in-Residence
resources.organization: Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21
resources.description: An annual, paid residency hosted by a national cultural institution in Halifax that offers a stipend, workspace, and access to museum resources. The artist engages visitors, schools, and community groups through workshops, talks, and participatory projects that foster dialogue and audience development. By combining income support with public programming in a cultural centre, it advances the residency model outlined in the solution.

solutions.text: Creative Business Incubator and Mentorship: Local incubator offering business training, mentorship, co-working, grant-writing help and co-marketing for creative entrepreneurs to strengthen sustainable careers in the arts.

resources.name: FILM 5
resources.description: FILM 5 is Atlantic Filmmakers Cooperative’s flagship training and mentorship program for emerging writers, directors, and producers. It delivers intensive business and production training, one-on-one mentorship, grant-writing guidance, and access to industry experts, culminating in the production and public showcasing of short films that help artists market their work. By pairing skills development with networking, funding navigation, and exhibition opportunities, FILM 5 functions as an incubator that strengthens sustainable careers in the screen arts.

resources.name: Media Art Scholarship (MAS)
resources.description: The Media Art Scholarship is a structured mentorship and training program that supports emerging media artists through workshops, professional practice sessions, and one-on-one guidance. Participants receive instruction in project development, budgeting and grant writing, technical production, and strategies for presenting and promoting their work. By combining skills training with mentorship, access to facilities, and public exhibition, MAS operates as a creative incubator that helps artists build viable, long-term careers.

resources.name: Incubator Studios
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design’s Incubator Studios provide subsidized studio space, mentorship from experienced craftspeople and business advisors, and ongoing professional development workshops in topics like pricing, marketing, and grant applications. The Centre also offers retail gallery exposure and coordinated promotions that help creatives reach new customers and wholesale buyers. This combination of co-working style studios, business training, grant-writing support, and co-marketing directly incubates sustainable craft-based enterprises.

resources.name: The Chrysalis Project
resources.description: Neptune’s Chrysalis Project mentors emerging theatre artists through a season-long professional development and creation residency. Participants receive training in producing, marketing, and grant writing alongside artistic mentorship, plus opportunities to present work to audiences and industry peers through Neptune’s platforms. By blending mentorship, practical business skills, and co-marketing/showcasing, the program incubates creative entrepreneurs in the performing arts.

resources.name: Music Nova Scotia Investment Program and Professional Development
resources.description: Music Nova Scotia provides grant investment, mentorship, and year-round workshops that cover business planning, marketing, export readiness, and grant-writing for artists and music companies. Through showcases like Nova Scotia Music Week and coordinated industry outreach, it also creates co-marketing and networking opportunities that help artists build audiences and revenue. This integrated funding, training, and mentorship model operates as a sector-specific incubator for creative entrepreneurs in music.

solutions.text: Cultural Asset Mapping and Centralized Booking Platform: A community-driven map and online marketplace listing venues, equipment, artists and tech crews, making it easy to find partners, book shows and coordinate touring across the region.

resources.name: Screen Nova Scotia Production Guide
resources.description: Screen Nova Scotia operates a searchable online Production Guide listing film/TV crew, vendors, studios, and support services across the province. This directory functions as a cultural asset map for screen-based arts and enables producers to quickly find and hire technicians, facilities, and partners, streamlining bookings and coordination across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 802, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

resources.name: AFCOOP Equipment Rentals & Facilities
resources.description: AFCOOP maintains an online catalogue and booking system for film equipment, post-production suites, and production resources available to members and the community. By centralizing gear availability and facilitating reservations, AFCOOP lowers barriers for creators, connects them with technical resources and crew, and supports coordinated production activity across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 5663 Cornwallis Street, Suite 101, Halifax, NS B3K 1B6

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op Venue Rentals
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op provides a centrally listed venue with detailed technical specs, availability calendar, and an online rental request process. It also connects renters to in-house and local technicians, helping artists and touring productions find space, technical support, and partners in Halifax as part of a broader regional performance network.

resources.name: Craft Nova Scotia ‘Find a Maker’ Directory
resources.organization: Craft Nova Scotia (Centre for Craft Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Craft Nova Scotia’s online ‘Find a Maker’ directory maps craftspeople, studios, and galleries throughout the province, with profiles and contact details. This community-driven asset map helps presenters, event organizers, and retailers discover and book artisans for markets, exhibitions, and collaborations, strengthening the cultural economy across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1061 Marginal Road, Suite 140, Halifax, NS B3H 4P7

resources.name: VANS Artist Directory
resources.description: Visual Arts Nova Scotia hosts a province-wide Artist Directory that profiles visual artists by location, discipline, and services. This searchable map-like resource helps curators, community groups, and venues identify and contact artists for commissions, exhibitions, and community projects, functioning as a cultural asset map that fosters bookings and partnerships across the region.

solutions.text: Local Arts Patronage & Subscription Schemes: Community subscriptions, patron circles and neighbourhood 'arts passes' that pool small recurring contributions to guarantee baseline income for local companies and presenters.

resources.name: HAT Angels
resources.description: Highland Arts Theatre’s HAT Angels is a monthly patron program where community members pledge recurring contributions to underwrite Pay-What-You-Choose access and year-round productions. By pooling small monthly gifts, the program guarantees baseline income for artist fees, production costs, and venue operations, reducing volatility and keeping high-quality local theatre sustainable in Sydney.

resources.name: Neptune Theatre Season Subscriptions
resources.description: Neptune Theatre offers multi-show season subscriptions that secure upfront commitments from patrons, creating predictable earned revenue across the season. These pooled subscription funds provide a reliable baseline to plan productions, employ local artists and crews, and reduce financial risk for presenters in Halifax.

resources.name: Bus Stop Theatre Co-op Membership
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op runs a community and artist membership model with annual dues and optional sustaining contributions that support an affordable, artist-run venue. Pooled member revenues help cover core operating costs and lower rental barriers, ensuring indie companies and presenters have a dependable neighbourhood stage and baseline income opportunities.

resources.name: King’s Theatre Society Membership
resources.description: Community members in Annapolis Royal join the King’s Theatre Society through annual memberships and patron circles, pooling recurring support to stabilize programming and operations. These funds provide predictable cash flow to book artists, guarantee presenting fees, and keep a rural, community-serving venue active year-round.
resources.address: 209 St George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

resources.name: Folk Harbour Society Membership
resources.description: The Lunenburg Folk Harbour Society offers annual memberships and donor circles that aggregate community support for its summer festival and year-round concert series. This subscription-style base of recurring contributions provides reliable income to cover venue costs and artist guarantees, helping local and touring performers reach audiences in a financially stable way.

solutions.text: Community Ownership of Venues (Nonprofit Co-op): Mobilize residents, businesses and artists to form a nonprofit co-op that buys or licenses at-risk venues and operates them as community-minded performance and rehearsal spaces.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op
resources.description: A member-owned performing arts co-operative that operates a black box theatre in Halifax’s North End. After the venue was at risk of closure, the co-op worked with Halifax Regional Municipality, which purchased the property and granted the co-op a long-term community lease, securing community control of the space. It provides affordable rentals for performances and rehearsals, artist residencies, and co-operative governance that keeps the venue accessible to local creators.

resources.name: Lunenburg Opera House
resources.description: The Lunenburg Folk Harbour Society, a volunteer-driven charitable organization, purchased the historic Opera House to preserve an at-risk cultural venue and keep it in community hands. The Society operates the building as a community-oriented performance and rehearsal space with year-round programming and affordable access for artists and local groups. Memberships, donations, and partnerships sustain the venue as a shared cultural asset for the region.

resources.name: Highland Arts Theatre
resources.description: A non-profit theatre that transformed a decommissioned church into a community-owned performance venue in downtown Sydney. Through community fundraising and subscription-style donor programs, the organization secured and now operates the building as an accessible stage and rehearsal facility for local artists, youth, and touring productions. Its governance and rental policies prioritize community access, artist development, and sustainable operations.

resources.name: King’s Theatre
resources.description: Owned and operated by the King’s Theatre Society, this community non-profit preserves and runs a historic theatre in Annapolis Royal that was once at risk of closure. The Society programs film, music, and live theatre while making the stage available for community productions, artist residencies, and rehearsals at accessible rates. Memberships, donations, and local partnerships keep the venue accountable to residents and creators.
resources.address: 209 St George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

resources.name: deCoste Performing Arts Centre
resources.description: Operated by a charitable, community-based organization, the deCoste Centre preserves and runs a dedicated performing arts venue for northern Nova Scotia. The Centre provides a professionally equipped theatre that local groups and artists rent for performances and rehearsals, supported by memberships, donors, and municipal partnerships. Ongoing community capital campaigns strengthen the long-term, community-controlled stewardship of the venue.

solutions.text: Shared Equipment Library and Technical Resource Pool: A loanable inventory of sound, lighting, instruments and set-building tools maintained by a community hub to lower production costs for small shows and tours.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: A nonprofit lending library that provides members with short-term access to hundreds of hand and power tools for woodworking, construction, and fabrication. Theatre makers and touring artists can borrow saws, drills, sanders, and other set-building tools at low cost, reducing technical and production expenses for small shows.

resources.name: Sun Life Musical Instrument Lending Library
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries maintains a circulating collection of musical instruments (e.g., guitars, keyboards, violins, ukuleles, and more) that can be borrowed with a library card. By removing the upfront cost of instruments for rehearsals and performances, it helps emerging musicians and small productions lower costs and build capacity.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Equipment Rentals
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op maintains a community-accessible inventory of technical gear including PA systems, microphones, mixers, projectors, lighting fixtures, and staging components. Artists and grassroots producers can rent equipment at community rates for pop-up events and small tours, reducing barriers to presenting work across venues.

resources.name: Costume & Prop Rentals
resources.organization: Two Planks and a Passion Theatre
resources.description: Two Planks and a Passion Theatre offers an extensive, catalogued collection of costumes, props, and small set pieces for rent to schools, community groups, and independent productions. This shared inventory lets companies stage or tour shows without the high cost of building or buying materials, supporting rural and urban productions alike.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

solutions.text: Paid Youth Apprenticeships and Internships in the Arts: Local arts organizations partner with schools and businesses to offer paid placements that teach production, marketing and business skills, keeping young people connected to creative careers.

resources.name: Neptune Theatre Apprenticeship Program
resources.description: Neptune Theatre provides paid apprenticeships in areas such as stage management, technical production, costumes, and marketing/communications. Working alongside professional staff on live productions and campaigns, apprentices gain hands-on production, audience development, and arts-business skills. The program collaborates with post-secondary theatre programs and industry sponsors to create pathways that keep young creatives working and training in Nova Scotia’s theatre sector.

resources.name: Young Canada Works Internships at the Art Gallery of Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Art Gallery of Nova Scotia partners with the federal Young Canada Works program and local universities to offer paid student and graduate internships in curatorial, education, visitor experience, and marketing/communications. Interns receive hands-on training in exhibition production, program delivery, and arts administration while contributing to a major public gallery. These placements build practical production, outreach, and business skills that prepare youth for sustainable careers in the arts.

resources.name: RBC Emerging Artist Program (Apprenticeships)
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts (with Two Planks and a Passion Theatre)
resources.description: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts, in collaboration with resident company Two Planks and a Passion Theatre, offers paid emerging-artist apprenticeships supported by the RBC Emerging Artists Project. Apprentices work on professional theatre productions and arts centre operations, learning production management, stagecraft, marketing/communications, and community engagement under mentorship from experienced practitioners. The program partners with funders and post-secondary programs to create real work-integrated learning that keeps young people connected to creative careers in rural Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

resources.name: Young Canada Works and Co-op Internships
resources.organization: Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21
resources.description: The Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21 provides paid internships for youth and students through Young Canada Works, Canada Summer Jobs, and co-op partnerships with local universities and colleges. Interns contribute to public programming, exhibitions, digital media, and marketing/communications, gaining practical production and business skills within a national cultural institution. These placements connect young people to meaningful arts and heritage careers in Nova Scotia while building sector capacity.

solutions.text: Festival Collaboration and Off-Season Programming: Neighboring festivals and presenters coordinate dates, routing and shared performers to extend artist income beyond single events and create year-round opportunities.

resources.name: Folk Harbour Presents (Year-Round Concert Series)
resources.description: Run by the Lunenburg Folk Harbour Society, this ongoing concert series brings touring folk and roots artists to Lunenburg outside of the summer festival season. The program aligns dates with nearby presenters along the South Shore and Annapolis Valley to route shared performers on consecutive nights, extending engagements beyond a single event and providing artists added off-season income while building year-round audiences.

resources.name: deCoste Presents and Regional Block-Booking Tours
resources.description: deCoste Performing Arts Centre programs a robust fall–spring series and participates in regional block-booking networks to co-book touring artists with neighbouring venues. By coordinating dates and sharing performers with other Nova Scotia presenters, the centre helps artists string together multi-stop routes, adding shoulder dates around festivals and generating steady, year-round opportunities for performers and local crews.

resources.name: King's Presents Touring Series & Festival Shoulder Dates
resources.description: King’s Theatre builds year-round programming that often dovetails with regional festivals and nearby presenters to create efficient touring routes. By aligning schedules and sharing artists on back-to-back dates with partner venues, the series gives performers added shows beyond single events and maintains off-season work opportunities for artists, technicians, and local suppliers.
resources.address: 209 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

resources.name: Chester Playhouse Presents & Routing Partnerships
resources.description: Chester Playhouse curates concerts and theatre outside peak festival months and coordinates with nearby presenters to route touring artists through multiple South Shore communities. Through co-booking and date alignment, the Playhouse helps artists add consecutive shows before/after regional festivals, extending income beyond single engagements and fostering sustainable, year-round cultural activity.

solutions.text: Community Standards for Fees and Transparent Contracts: A locally agreed guideline for minimum artist fees, clear contracts and prompt payment practices adopted by presenters and venues to stabilize incomes and professionalize the sector.

resources.name: Payment of CARFAC Artist Fees and Standard Exhibition Contracts
resources.description: As a provincially funded public art museum, the Art Gallery of Nova Scotia pays artists using the CARFAC-RAAV minimum fee schedule for exhibitions, commissions, and public programs. The gallery uses clear, standardized written agreements that outline rights, timelines, and payment schedules, and follows public-sector prompt payment practices. This sets a local benchmark for presenters and venues to adopt professional fee standards and transparent contracting, stabilizing artist incomes.

resources.name: Exhibition Program: CARFAC Fees and Transparent Contracts
resources.organization: Craft Nova Scotia (Mary E. Black Gallery)
resources.description: Mary E. Black Gallery pays exhibiting artists and craft practitioners according to CARFAC-recommended minimums and uses clear loan/exhibition contracts that specify fees, deliverables, and payment timelines. Calls for submissions explicitly state professional fee payment and contractual terms, signaling sector-wide expectations for fair compensation. By modeling these practices, the gallery helps normalize minimum fees and transparent agreements among Nova Scotia presenters.
resources.address: 1061 Marginal Road, Suite 140, Halifax, NS B3H 4P7

resources.name: Use of Canadian Theatre Agreement and Standard Artist Contracts
resources.description: Neptune Theatre operates under professional agreements such as the Canadian Theatre Agreement (with Canadian Actors’ Equity Association) and Playwrights Guild of Canada contracts, which set minimum fees and standardized terms for performers, directors, designers, and playwrights. The company employs formal contracts and reliable payroll schedules, ensuring prompt and transparent payment. This adoption of recognized standards advances professionalization and income stability for theatre artists in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: CARFAC Fee Advocacy and Contract Resources
resources.description: Visual Arts Nova Scotia disseminates the CARFAC-RAAV Minimum Fee Schedule and provides professional development and contract resources that help artists and presenters adopt clear, written agreements and fair pay practices. Through advocacy, training, and sector support, VANS encourages venues, festivals, and galleries to budget for minimum fees and to formalize terms and payment schedules. This leadership strengthens local norms around fair compensation and transparent contracting across the visual arts ecosystem.
resources.address: 1113 Marginal Road, Suite 201, Halifax, NS B3H 4P7

resources.name: Standard Presenter Contracts and Professional Fee Policy
resources.description: King’s Theatre engages touring and local artists using standardized performance agreements that detail deposits, technical riders, cancellations, settlements, and prompt payment, and it pays professional fees in line with industry minimums (e.g., AFM/Equity/CADA benchmarks). As a year-round rural presenter, it models transparent contracts and fair compensation for artists appearing on its stage. This consistent practice helps normalize fee standards among venues and presenters across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 209 St George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

solutions.text: Skills Exchange and Timebank for Creative Services: A neighbourhood timebank where artists and arts workers trade services—graphic design, childcare, carpentry, marketing—reducing cash outlays and strengthening mutual support.

resources.name: AFCOOP Work Trade Program
resources.description: AFCOOP lets members earn credits by volunteering on committees, events, and equipment centre shifts, which can be exchanged for equipment rentals, workshops, and memberships. This time-for-access model functions like a timebank for creative services, reducing cash costs for filmmakers while strengthening a peer support network across Nova Scotia’s film community.

resources.name: CFAT Active Member Program (Volunteer Work Exchange)
resources.description: CFAT’s Active Member model requires/encourages members to contribute volunteer hours that translate into discounted access to media arts equipment, editing suites, and training. By trading time and skills for creative resources, artists lower their out-of-pocket costs and build reciprocal support within the media arts community.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library (Volunteer-for-Membership & Skillshare)
resources.description: The Halifax Tool Library operates a community lending library for tools used in set-building, exhibits, crafts, and repairs, and offers options to offset membership fees with volunteer hours. Members also participate in peer skill-shares, effectively exchanging time and knowledge for access to tools and workshop space—reducing costs and fostering mutual aid among artists and makers.

resources.name: Anchor Archive Zine Library (Work-Trade & Skillshare)
resources.description: Anchor Archive offers community access to a zine library and publishing resources, with volunteers able to trade shifts and skills for memberships, print access, and program participation. This work-trade approach acts as a neighbourhood skills exchange for writers, designers, and printmakers, strengthening mutual support while lowering cash barriers for creative production.

obstacles.title: Rural–Urban Opportunity Divide
obstacles.description: Services, investment, and jobs concentrate in HRM while many rural communities face shrinking services and aging infrastructure.

solutions.text: Community Broadband Co‑op: Form a locally governed cooperative to fund, build and manage high‑speed internet access so residents, remote workers and businesses can participate fully in the digital economy.

resources.name: Riverport Internet (FTTH Network)
resources.description: Riverport Internet is a community-owned fibre-to-the-home network created by the locally governed Riverport Electric Light Commission. The utility finances, builds, and operates high-speed internet for residents and businesses in Riverport and surrounding Lunenburg County, reinvesting surpluses locally. This directly implements a community broadband model by putting infrastructure ownership and decision-making in the hands of the community, enabling remote work and local entrepreneurship.

resources.name: Chebucto Community Net
resources.description: Chebucto Community Net is a member-supported, locally governed non-profit internet provider that offers affordable internet access, email, and web services to individuals and community groups. Run by a volunteer board and sustained through community membership, it exemplifies a community-driven approach to connectivity and digital inclusion. This model advances the co‑op-style solution by keeping governance and service priorities close to the people who use the network.
resources.address: Room 006, Chase Building, 6136 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: East Hants Rural Broadband Project
resources.description: The Municipality of East Hants leads a community broadband initiative that funds and builds local network infrastructure to extend high-speed internet to underserved rural areas. Guided by local council and resident input, the project uses municipal investment and partnerships to deliver last‑mile connections for homes and businesses. This community-governed approach mirrors a broadband co‑op by aligning ownership, oversight, and service delivery with local needs.

resources.name: Connected Colchester – Rural Internet Initiative
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: Connected Colchester is the County’s community-driven broadband program that invests in fibre and fixed wireless infrastructure to reach rural residents and businesses. The municipality owns and manages network assets and partners with service providers to deliver last‑mile service, ensuring local oversight and reinvestment. This implements the community broadband model by using local governance to close the rural–urban connectivity gap.

solutions.text: Local Remote‑Work Hubs: Convert existing municipal buildings or vacant storefronts into shared workspaces with reliable internet, meeting rooms and business supports to attract remote workers and freelancers.

resources.name: WorkEvolved Antigonish
resources.description: WorkEvolved converts a historic Main Street storefront into a modern coworking hub offering hot desks, private offices, meeting rooms, and reliable high‑speed internet. It attracts freelancers, remote employees, and startup founders in rural Nova Scotia and provides programming and networking that connect members to business supports and the broader Antigonish entrepreneurship community.

resources.name: New Dawn Centre for Social Innovation – Coworking & Startup Space
resources.description: New Dawn repurposed an existing downtown Sydney building into a social innovation centre with coworking areas, private offices, event space, and boardrooms supported by enterprise‑grade internet. It serves remote workers, freelancers, and early‑stage companies, and houses entrepreneurship programming (including Navigate Startup House partners) that provides mentorship, workshops, and community connections.

resources.name: The Academy – Co‑Work & Business Hub
resources.description: The Academy transformed a former school into a mixed‑use community complex that includes coworking spaces, meeting rooms, and small offices with reliable Wi‑Fi for remote workers and entrepreneurs. It anchors business supports on‑site and hosts events and training that help local freelancers and startups connect with resources in rural Annapolis Royal.
resources.address: 590 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

solutions.text: Youth Apprenticeship & Trades Partnerships: Partner schools, employers and unions to create paid local apprenticeships, internships and co‑op placements that keep youth training and working in the community.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY places Nova Scotia high school students in paid summer jobs with local construction employers, while also delivering safety training and helping students earn co-op education credits. Run in partnership with industry, schools, and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, the program connects youth to real worksites in their own communities, creating direct pathways into registered trades apprenticeships and long-term local employment.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC), in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding Inc.
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based program that partners NSCC with Irving Shipbuilding, unions, and community organizations to train Nova Scotians—often from underrepresented groups—for skilled trades careers at the Halifax Shipyard. Participants complete technical training at NSCC and transition into paid, unionized positions and apprenticeships with local employers, keeping youth training and working in Nova Scotia’s shipbuilding sector.

resources.name: Women Unlimited
resources.description: Women Unlimited partners with NSCC campuses, unions, and employers to recruit and support women into trades and technology through career exploration, essential and technical skills training, and connections to paid work placements and apprenticeships. By coordinating with local industry and training providers across Nova Scotia, the program helps participants secure employment and apprenticeship opportunities close to home, strengthening community-based skilled trades capacity.

solutions.text: Microgrant Program for Startups and Social Enterprises: Establish small locally managed grants and wraparound mentorship to help entrepreneurs test businesses, cultural projects and value‑added farm initiatives.

resources.name: Spark Nova Scotia
resources.description: Spark Nova Scotia is a province-wide startup competition that awards non-dilutive microgrants (up to tens of thousands of dollars) alongside mentorship, workshops, and advisory support to help founders validate and launch early-stage companies, especially in Western, Northern, and Cape Breton regions. By combining seed funding with hands-on coaching and a regional delivery model through partners, it enables entrepreneurs to test business ideas close to home and reduces the rural–urban opportunity gap.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Scotiabank Entrepreneur-in-the-Making
resources.description: This NSCC program provides student and recent graduate entrepreneurs with microgrants (typically $1,000–$3,000) and wraparound mentorship, including one-on-one coaching, workshops, and connections to campus innovation resources across Nova Scotia. It supports testing and launching small businesses, social enterprises, and creative projects in communities served by NSCC’s rural and urban campuses, helping young people start up where they live.

resources.name: FILM 5
resources.description: FILM 5 is a training and production program that pairs emerging filmmakers with mentorship, workshops, and small production grants to develop and produce short films and creative content. By combining micro-funding with intensive coaching and industry connections, it functions as a microgrant-and-mentorship model for cultural entrepreneurs across Nova Scotia, enabling them to prototype creative ventures and build sustainable careers.
resources.address: 5663 Cornwallis Street, Suite 204, Halifax, NS B3K 1B6

resources.name: Community Grants
resources.description: Ulnooweg Indigenous Communities Foundation offers small grants to Indigenous communities and organizations in Nova Scotia to advance community economic development, culture, and youth-led initiatives, with many projects operating in rural areas. Through the Ulnooweg Development Group’s advisory services, recipients gain wraparound mentorship and business supports that help launch social enterprises, cultural projects, and value-added food initiatives at a community scale.
resources.address: 172 Truro Heights Road, Truro Heights, NS B6L 1X1

solutions.text: Community Investment Fund / Local Loan Pool: Pool community capital (residents, pensioners, businesses) to provide low‑interest loans or match funding for local business expansions, housing repairs and social infrastructure.

resources.name: Clean Energy Financing Program (PACE)
resources.description: The Town of Bridgewater’s PACE program provides low-interest, long-term financing for homeowners to complete energy-efficiency and home-renewal upgrades (e.g., heat pumps, insulation, solar). The municipality pools local capital and issues financing that is repaid via property tax bills, creating a revolving local loan pool that funds housing repairs and keeps savings and benefits in the community—directly aligning with the community investment/loan-pool solution.

resources.name: Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) – Clean Energy Financing
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg (MODL)
resources.description: MODL’s PACE program offers homeowners affordable, pay-as-you-save financing for energy-efficiency and home upgrades, repaid on-property tax accounts. By using municipal capital to create a local revolving loan pool, the program finances essential housing improvements and reduces household costs, supporting community infrastructure and keeping dollars circulating locally in rural Lunenburg County.

resources.name: CEED Impact Loan
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED’s Impact Loan provides accessible, flexible financing to startups and growing small businesses, pairing capital with advisory support and mentorship. Operating as a community-based revolving loan fund, it pools resources to extend affordable loans for business expansion and job creation—helping entrepreneurs access opportunity across Nova Scotia and addressing financing gaps outside traditional urban centres.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Ulnooweg Lending Services
resources.description: Ulnooweg provides patient, flexible loans and business support to Mi’kmaq and other Indigenous entrepreneurs throughout Nova Scotia and Atlantic Canada. As an Indigenous-led development finance organization, it stewards a dedicated community loan pool that channels capital into new and expanding local enterprises, strengthening community-owned businesses, services, and social infrastructure in rural and remote regions.

solutions.text: Mobile Service Delivery (Health, Library, Business Supports): Organize scheduled mobile clinics, libraries and business advisory vans to bring essential services, training and supports to smaller settlements on a regular route.

resources.name: South Shore Public Libraries Mobile Library
resources.description: A fully equipped bookmobile that follows a regular route to rural communities across Lunenburg and Queens counties, offering borrowing, holds pickup, Wi‑Fi, printing, and programs. By bringing core library services and digital access directly to small settlements, it reduces travel barriers and ensures rural residents receive the same services as urban branches.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

resources.name: Annapolis Valley Regional Library Bookmobile
resources.description: The AVRL Bookmobile travels on a published schedule to rural stops throughout Annapolis and Kings counties, providing borrowing, holds pickup, new library cards, and community programming. This mobile service brings literacy resources and digital connectivity to residents in smaller communities, closing access gaps created by distance from urban branches.

resources.name: Mobile Primary Care Clinics
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health operates mobile primary care clinics that rotate through communities across the province on scheduled dates, offering same‑day care for non‑urgent concerns, prescription renewals, immunizations, and preventive services. By bringing clinicians and equipment to rural locations, the program reduces travel for residents and supplements local capacity where primary care access is limited.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Breast Screening Program – Mobile Mammography
resources.description: The provincial breast screening program operates mobile mammography coaches that visit small towns and community health centres on a regular route, providing no‑fee screening mammograms close to where people live. This mobile model increases early detection access in rural areas by removing long travel times to urban imaging centres.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

solutions.text: Rural Housing Retrofit & Renovation Program: Coordinate volunteer teams, trades training placements and small grants/loans to renovate vacant homes, create affordable rentals and make housing suitable for young families and seniors.

resources.name: HomeWarming
resources.organization: Clean Foundation (in partnership with EfficiencyOne/Efficiency Nova Scotia)
resources.description: HomeWarming provides free home energy assessments and upgrades (like insulation, air sealing, and draft-proofing) to eligible low-income homeowners across Nova Scotia, with a strong reach into rural communities. The program coordinates certified local contractors and community partners to deliver retrofits that lower energy bills and make homes safer and more comfortable for seniors and families, enabling them to remain in their communities.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership and Build Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia mobilizes volunteer build crews alongside professional trades and student placements to construct and rehabilitate homes for families, often transforming underused or existing properties into safe, affordable housing. By coordinating volunteer teams and partnerships with trades programs, it reduces project costs and creates hands-on training opportunities while making homes suitable for young families in rural and small-town communities.

resources.name: SWITCH Bridgewater (Property Assessed Clean Energy Financing)
resources.description: SWITCH Bridgewater offers low-interest, on-property-tax financing for home energy retrofits such as heat pumps, insulation, and window upgrades, enabling homeowners—including seniors on fixed incomes—to complete improvements now and repay over time. The program works with qualified local contractors and helps households in a rural town reduce energy costs, upgrade aging housing, and improve comfort and safety to support aging in place and family needs.

resources.name: New Dawn Properties – Affordable Rental Development and Rehabilitation
resources.description: New Dawn acquires, rehabilitates, and manages rental properties in Cape Breton, creating and preserving affordable rental options for residents in rural and small urban communities. By investing in building upgrades and working with local trades, the initiative brings older or underutilized buildings back into productive use and provides safe, suitable housing for seniors and families close to services and employment.

solutions.text: Local Procurement Pledge: Encourage municipalities, hospitals and community organizations to prioritize local suppliers and contractors to retain public spending in the local economy.

resources.name: Supplier Development Program (Reverse Trade Show and Supplier Outreach)
resources.description: The Province’s Supplier Development Program connects public-sector buyers with Nova Scotia vendors through reverse trade shows, webinars, and one-on-one support, helping local firms understand and compete for public contracts. By actively recruiting rural and small suppliers and guiding them through tendering requirements, the program broadens local participation in municipal, health, and institutional procurement, keeping more public spending within Nova Scotia while complying with trade agreements.

resources.name: CBRM Procurement and Supplier Engagement
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Municipality runs an open tendering program and hosts vendor information sessions to encourage Cape Breton-based suppliers and contractors to bid on municipal work. By structuring procurements that are accessible to local SMEs and highlighting community benefits where permitted, CBRM channels municipal spending to local firms across the island while maintaining full compliance with trade agreements.

resources.name: Sustainable Procurement Policy
resources.description: Bridgewater’s Sustainable Procurement Policy guides municipal purchases to consider local economic impact and supplier development alongside price and quality. By encouraging bids from South Shore businesses and using evaluation criteria that reward community benefits and service responsiveness, the town keeps more public dollars circulating in the regional economy.

resources.name: Local Contractor Engagement and Bid Depository
resources.description: CANS provides a bid depository, tender intelligence, and owner outreach that link public-sector buyers with qualified Nova Scotia contractors and trades. By advocating procurement practices that facilitate local participation and by equipping firms—urban and rural—to access municipal, healthcare, and institutional projects, CANS helps retain construction spending within Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Institutional Market Access and Local Procurement Support
resources.description: Perennia works with food and agriculture producers and institutional buyers to increase the amount of Nova Scotia food in public sector kitchens (e.g., hospitals, long-term care, and schools). Through market-readiness coaching, product development, and buyer–supplier matchmaking, the program helps institutions source from local suppliers, keeping food procurement dollars in rural communities.
resources.address: 199 Innovation Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2H5

solutions.text: Community Transportation Network: Create a community-run ride‑share, shuttle or volunteer driver program that links villages to regional hubs for work, services and events, improving access without large capital outlay.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Cooperative
resources.description: MusGo Rider is a community-run, door-to-door shared-ride service that connects rural communities along the Eastern Shore and Musquodoboit Valley to regional hubs like Musquodoboit Harbour, Dartmouth, and Halifax for work, medical appointments, shopping, and events. Operating as a cooperative with a mix of volunteer and paid drivers, it provides scheduled, pre-booked rides at low cost, effectively functioning as a community shuttle that expands access without large capital infrastructure.

resources.name: Kings Point-to-Point Transit
resources.description: Kings Point-to-Point provides accessible, pre-booked, door-to-door transportation across Kings County, linking rural villages to regional hubs such as Kentville, Wolfville, and New Minas for employment, education, healthcare, and shopping. By using a small fleet and coordinated shared rides, the non-profit offers a shuttle-style service that fills gaps in rural mobility and reduces the need for personal vehicles or major transit infrastructure.
resources.address: 14 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

resources.name: Strait Area Transit
resources.description: Strait Area Transit operates community-based fixed and on-demand routes across the rural Strait region, connecting small communities in Inverness and Richmond counties with the hub of Port Hawkesbury for jobs, services, and events. The cooperative’s shared-ride shuttles provide affordable mobility options that bridge the rural–urban divide without requiring heavy capital investment in large-scale transit systems.
resources.address: 902 Reeves Street, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 2E1

solutions.text: Maker Spaces and Applied Skills Labs: Develop community workshops equipped with tools, 3D printers and mentorship where entrepreneurs, students and hobbyists can prototype products and learn technical skills.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Lou Duggan Creative Studio is a public makerspace offering 3D printers, laser cutting, sewing machines, electronics, and digital media tools. Library staff and volunteer mentors run free and low‑cost workshops and one‑on‑one help so entrepreneurs, students, and hobbyists can learn applied skills and prototype ideas. As an accessible community workshop, it reduces barriers to hands‑on learning and supports youth and creators from across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: RBC Innovators’ Lab
resources.description: Located inside the Discovery Centre, the RBC Innovators’ Lab is a hands‑on makerspace equipped with 3D printers, laser cutters, microcontrollers, and fabrication tools. It delivers public workshops, youth programs, and mentorship that teach design, coding, and prototyping skills, supporting students, creators, and early‑stage entrepreneurs. By providing open access to tools and expertise, it enables Nova Scotians to build and test products locally.
resources.address: 1215 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

resources.name: Make & Break Space (New Glasgow Library)
resources.description: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library’s Make & Break Space is a community makerspace at the New Glasgow Library with 3D printing, robotics, electronics, and crafting tools. Librarians and community volunteers host workshops and provide guidance so youth, students, and small‑business owners can prototype, tinker, and build practical skills. Serving a rural region outside HRM, it expands access to applied learning and creative technology in Pictou County.
resources.address: 182 Dalhousie Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 4C7

resources.name: The Creative Lab (Truro Library Makerspace)
resources.description: Colchester-East Hants Public Library’s Creative Lab at the Truro Library offers a public makerspace with 3D printers, sewing and vinyl-cutting equipment, and digital media tools. Staff-led programs and drop‑in support help learners and entrepreneurs prototype products, learn design software, and develop technical skills. As a hub in central Nova Scotia, it improves access to hands‑on learning for youth from surrounding rural communities.

solutions.text: Local Food and Value‑Added Processing Co‑op: Support farmers and fishers to pool resources for processing, branding and marketing value‑added products (preserves, smoked fish, craft foods) to increase local incomes.

resources.name: Wolfville Farmers’ Market Cooperative
resources.description: A producer-owned cooperative that aggregates and markets products from farms and fishers through the weekly market and its WFM2Go online platform. It offers a certified community/commercial kitchen and shared marketing channels so small producers can create preserves, baked goods, and other value‑added products and reach customers across the Valley and HRM—pooling resources to increase local incomes.

resources.name: Scotian Gold Cooperative Limited
resources.description: A grower‑owned cooperative that pools the harvest of apple growers for centralized storage, packing, and branding under the Scotian Gold label. The co-op also provides value‑added processing (e.g., juices and sliced products) and coordinates national marketing and distribution, capturing more value for member farms and sustaining rural jobs in the Annapolis Valley.

resources.name: Victoria Co-operative Fisheries Ltd.
resources.description: A fisher‑owned cooperative in Neil’s Harbour that operates processing facilities for lobster, crab, and other species, investing collectively in equipment, packaging, and quality control. By branding and marketing value‑added seafood (cooked/frozen and processed products) to domestic and export markets, the co-op helps member fishers capture more of the seafood value chain and supports year‑round rural employment.
resources.address: 10 Wharf Road, Neil's Harbour, NS B0C 1N0

resources.name: Perennia Food and Beverage Innovation Centre
resources.description: Perennia provides shared pilot‑scale processing facilities, product development, and food safety services that multiple farms, fisheries, and small food businesses can access. Producers can develop and co‑pack value‑added items (preserves, beverages, ready‑to‑eat foods), receive branding and labelling guidance, and prepare for market entry—effectively pooling specialized processing capacity that would be costly to build individually.
resources.address: 199 Innovation Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

solutions.text: Cultural and Creative Economy Events Series: Organize festivals, markets, artist‑in‑residence programs and cultural showcases that build place identity, attract visitors and provide income for local creators.

resources.name: Lunenburg Folk Harbour Festival
resources.description: This annual multi-day music festival fills Lunenburg’s historic waterfront and venues with concerts, workshops, and community events, showcasing folk, roots, and traditional artists. It attracts visitors from across Nova Scotia and beyond, strengthening place identity in a UNESCO World Heritage town. By paying performers and creating vendor and workshop opportunities, it provides direct income for local creators and culture workers.

resources.name: Customs House Artisan Incubator
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: This year-round craft and design hub offers studio space, residencies, retail gallery sales, exhibitions, and public workshops in downtown Port Hawkesbury. It draws visitors to rural Cape Breton through markets and cultural showcases while building a local creative cluster. The program generates income for artisans via training-to-market pathways and retail sales, directly implementing a creative economy solution outside HRM.
resources.address: 402 Granville Street, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 2M9

resources.name: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts Artist-in-Residence Program
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: Ross Creek hosts Canadian and international artists at its rural arts campus, providing studios, accommodation, and community engagement opportunities. Residencies culminate in open studios, talks, pop-up shows, and performances that attract cultural visitors to the North Mountain/Annapolis Valley region. The program strengthens local identity through creative exchange and offers paid opportunities and sales for artists.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

resources.name: Parrsboro Creative Artist-in-Residence (AIR)
resources.description: Parrsboro Creative’s AIR brings artists to the Bay of Fundy community for themed residencies that include public workshops, exhibitions, and pop-up markets at the Art Lab. These events activate Main Street, draw visitors to the UNESCO Cliffs of Fundy Geopark area, and showcase local culture. The program provides income streams for creators through sales, teaching, and presentation fees while reinforcing rural place identity.

resources.name: Summer Sounds on the Pictou Waterfront
resources.description: This outdoor concert series presents Nova Scotia musicians and cultural performances on the Pictou waterfront throughout the summer, often alongside local food and craft vendors. It brings residents and tourists downtown, animating public space and strengthening a distinctive small-town cultural identity. By offering paid gigs and vendor stalls, it creates direct income for performers and makers in a rural setting.

solutions.text: Mentorship Circles – Youth to Business Leaders: Match young residents with local business owners, tradespeople and community leaders for regular mentorship, skills sharing and entrepreneurship coaching.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program matches recent graduates and young professionals with established business leaders for one-on-one informational interviews and ongoing networking. These connections help youth build local relationships, learn industry expectations, and access coaching that can lead to jobs or entrepreneurial opportunities, directly aligning with mentorship circles between youth and business leaders.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Volta Academy
