The program also includes education resources that help owners plan cost-effective flood-proofing and maintenance.
resources.address: 450 Cowie Hill Road, Halifax, NS B3P 2V3

resources.name: Coastal Adaptation Program
resources.description: Ecology Action Centre partners with coastal municipalities and communities to plan and implement nature-based shoreline protection and stormwater solutions that reduce flood and erosion risks. The team runs workshops and produces homeowner guides on practical, low-cost flood-proofing measures and recovery steps, including how to document damage and engage with insurers after severe storms. They also advocate for provincial and municipal policies and funding that support cost-shared, climate-resilient retrofits for households and small businesses.

resources.name: Living Shorelines Program
resources.organization: TransCoastal Adaptations: Centre for Nature-Based Solutions, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: TransCoastal Adaptations works with Nova Scotia municipalities, community groups, and funders to co-design and install living shorelines that reduce erosion and coastal flooding at community and private sites. The program provides homeowner training, technical guidance, and demonstration projects that show affordable, nature-based retrofits, while advocating for broader cost-sharing and subsidy models to scale adoption. Their collaborations help align municipal planning, insurer-supported resilience funding, and resident education to lower future claims and damages.

resources.name: Disaster Management – Emergency Preparedness (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross delivers flood and storm preparedness education across Nova Scotia, including Ready workshops, home readiness checklists, and community outreach in partnership with municipalities. They support residents after events with guidance on documenting losses and navigating insurance and assistance programs, improving claims preparedness. By promoting practical, low-cost measures and coordinating with local governments, the program strengthens community resilience and reduces the impact of climate-related disasters.

resources.name: Stormwater Management Program
resources.description: Coastal Action collaborates with South Shore municipalities and local partners to plan and deliver green infrastructure—such as rain gardens, rain barrels, and permeable surfaces—that mitigate localized flooding. The program offers public workshops and site-specific guidance to homeowners on affordable flood-proofing actions and maintenance, while advocating for municipal incentives and cost-sharing that make retrofits more accessible. These measures reduce runoff and property damage, helping to lower community risk and potential insurance claims.
resources.address: 37 Tannery Road, Unit 2, Lunenburg, NS B0J 2C0

solutions.text: School and Community Climate Education & Career Fairs: Run education programs and career fairs connecting students with local green employers, apprenticeships and hands-on projects so young people see clear local career paths in resilience, trades and clean-tech sectors.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship Program
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s Clean Leadership program places high school, college, and university students in paid summer internships with municipalities, NGOs, and private-sector employers in the clean economy. Interns work on hands-on projects in energy efficiency, climate adaptation, waste reduction, and natural infrastructure, while participating in professional development that highlights local career pathways. This directly implements the solution by connecting youth to real green employers and projects, often complemented by school-based climate education and career talks delivered by Clean’s educators.

resources.name: Get Connected Career Fair
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Career Services
resources.description: NSCC’s annual Get Connected career fairs link students in trades, technology, environmental engineering, energy sustainability, and ocean tech with Nova Scotia employers and apprenticeship recruiters. Many participating companies work in clean growth, climate resilience, and electrification, offering on-site interviews, networking, and demonstrations. This directly supports the solution by providing school-based career fairs that open clear pathways into local green and resilient trades and clean-tech roles.

resources.name: H2O: Home to Overseas Conference – Student & Early Career Day
resources.description: Hosted by COVE, the Student & Early Career Day during the H2O Conference connects high school and post-secondary students with ocean-technology and blue-economy employers focused on coastal resilience, marine renewables, and climate monitoring. The event features employer booths, career panels, and hands-on demos of ocean tech used to address climate risks. It implements the solution by acting as a community career fair that directly links youth to local clean-tech employers and experiential opportunities.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth
resources.description: Building Futures for Youth places Nova Scotia high school students in paid summer work experiences with local construction employers, including roles in energy-efficient building, sustainable materials, and resilient infrastructure. The program includes safety training, mentorship, and exposure to Red Seal apprenticeship pathways. It implements the solution by combining school-to-work education with direct connections to employers in trades that are central to climate resilience and the clean economy.
resources.address: 260 Brownlow Avenue, Unit 5, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1V9

obstacles.title: Fragmented Governance and Slow Execution
obstacles.description: Siloed municipal–provincial–federal programs, lengthy approvals, and risk-averse procurement impede timely, coordinated action.

solutions.text: Tri-level Community Roundtables: Organize regular municipal–provincial–federal roundtables hosted by local communities to coordinate priorities, align timelines, and resolve bottlenecks for youth-focused projects (job programs, housing, training). Community groups provide agendas, local data, and shared project lists so governments can streamline approvals.

resources.name: Cape Breton Local Immigration Partnership (CBLIP)
resources.description: CBLIP convenes recurring community-led roundtables that bring together the Cape Breton Regional Municipality, Nova Scotia departments (e.g., Labour, Skills and Immigration; Community Services; Housing), and federal partners (IRCC, Service Canada/ESDC, ACOA) alongside youth-serving organizations and employers. Through working groups, shared project pipelines, and locally generated data on newcomer and youth needs, these tables align timelines and funding streams for youth-focused employment, housing, and training initiatives, helping governments streamline approvals and remove bottlenecks.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

resources.name: Halifax Local Immigration Partnership (HLIP)
resources.description: HLIP hosts multi-level roundtables and action teams where community groups set agendas and present local data to municipal (HRM), provincial (Labour, Skills and Immigration; Community Services; Housing) and federal (IRCC, Service Canada/ESDC) partners. These coordinated tables focus on youth attraction and retention, newcomer and youth employment pathways, and housing access, producing shared project lists and coordinated implementation plans that help align funding windows and accelerate approvals for youth-focused programs.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Game Changers (Youth Employment Initiative)
resources.description: Game Changers mobilizes employers and convenes recurring community-led roundtables with HRM, Nova Scotia departments (Labour, Skills and Immigration; Education and Early Childhood Development), and federal partners (Service Canada/ESDC) to coordinate youth hiring, work-integrated learning, and job-readiness supports. Using employer demand data and a shared project pipeline, the tables align timelines across programs, reduce duplication, and streamline approvals so youth can access jobs, mentorship, and training more quickly.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Between the Bridges (Dartmouth North)
resources.description: Between the Bridges facilitates community-hosted, cross-government roundtables in Dartmouth North that bring HRM, Nova Scotia departments (Community Services; Labour, Skills and Immigration; Housing), and federal agencies (Service Canada/ESDC, IRCC) together with local youth-serving groups. The initiative uses neighbourhood-level data and co-created agendas to maintain a shared list of youth-focused projects (employment pathways, skills training, and housing supports), aligning timelines and funding streams to speed up approvals and remove implementation bottlenecks.

solutions.text: Community Project Accelerator for Local Pilots: Create a community-run accelerator that fast-tracks small pilots (social enterprise, skills labs, maker spaces) by bundling approvals, offering short-term space, and providing mentorship; use successful pilots as proof-of-concept to shorten higher-level approvals.

resources.name: COVE Start-Up Yard
resources.description: COVE’s Start-Up Yard is an ocean-tech incubator that provides short-term office, lab, and wharf access so companies can rapidly pilot and demo solutions in real coastal conditions. As a neutral convener, it connects founders with regulators, naval and port buyers, and service providers to navigate permissions, safety plans, and standards—effectively bundling approvals and site access. Evidence from these pilots serves as proof-of-concept that de-risks projects and shortens subsequent municipal, provincial, and federal approvals.

resources.name: Volta Residency
resources.description: Volta Residency offers subsidized, flexible workspace and structured mentorship to accelerate early-stage ventures, including social enterprises, by giving them a home base for short-term pilots. Through its advisor network and government/industry partners, Volta helps teams navigate permitting, funding programs, and procurement pilots—reducing friction across siloed processes. Startups use pilot outcomes and demo-day traction as proof-of-concept to speed decisions by larger public and private approvers.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Perennia Innovation Centre
resources.description: Perennia’s Innovation Centre provides short-term access to pilot-scale food processing suites, labs, and specialized equipment, paired with mentorship from food scientists and regulatory advisors. The team helps ventures meet HACCP/CFIA requirements and coordinates inspections and documentation, effectively bundling regulatory steps so compliant pilot batches can launch quickly. Pilot data and samples then serve as proof for retailers and regulators, accelerating approvals and broader market entry.
resources.address: 199 Dr. Bernie MacDonald Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2H5

resources.name: Emera ideaHUB Incubation
resources.description: Emera ideaHUB is a hardware-focused incubator that provides short-term prototyping space, fabrication tools, and engineering mentorship to fast-track product pilots. It guides startups through certification and safety-testing pathways and connects them with industry and public-sector partners for field trials—streamlining fragmented steps that typically delay execution. Validated pilots from the HUB serve as proof-of-concept that helps compress timelines for institutional approvals and procurement.

resources.name: Halifax Innovation District (Waterfront Testbeds and Pilots)
resources.organization: Build Nova Scotia (in partnership with Halifax Partnership)
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia activates public spaces on the Halifax waterfront as living labs, providing short-term pilot locations and pop-up space for mobility, data, and smart-city solutions. By coordinating with landowners and municipal/provincial partners, it streamlines site permissions and logistics—bundling key approvals so pilots can launch quickly. Results from these demonstrations are used to inform policy, de-risk procurement, and accelerate higher-level approvals for broader rollout.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 301, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

solutions.text: Inter-municipal Shared Services Consortium: Form a local consortium where adjacent municipalities pool administrative services (planning, procurement, legal) to reduce duplicated approvals and speed execution of regional youth and economic projects.

resources.name: Eastern District Planning Commission
resources.description: An inter-municipal planning and development authority that provides shared planning, subdivision approval, building inspection, and development permitting for multiple municipalities in eastern Nova Scotia. By centralizing professional planning, standardized bylaws, and permitting processes across member municipalities, the Commission reduces duplicated approvals and accelerates execution of regional economic and community projects that benefit youth and local employers.
resources.address: 606 Reeves Street, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 2R7

resources.name: Municipal Joint Services Board (Antigonish)
resources.organization: Municipal Joint Services Board (Town of Antigonish and Municipality of the County of Antigonish)
resources.description: A formal shared-services consortium between the Town of Antigonish and the Municipality of the County of Antigonish that consolidates functions such as procurement, occupational health and safety, information technology, and records management. This pooled administrative capacity standardizes policies and purchasing, cuts red tape between adjacent jurisdictions, and speeds delivery of joint initiatives that support local businesses, training partners, and youth employment projects across the region.
resources.address: 285 Beech Hill Road, Antigonish, NS B2G 0B4

resources.name: Kings Transit Authority
resources.description: An inter-municipal transit authority funded and governed by multiple Kings County municipalities that centralizes service planning, fleet procurement, and operations to deliver cross-boundary public transit. By pooling administrative and purchasing functions, it reduces duplication among member municipalities and provides faster, region-wide mobility that connects youth to education, apprenticeships, and jobs, strengthening the regional economy.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

solutions.text: Local Procurement Cooperative: Develop a community-led cooperative to aggregate buying power for common goods and services (training programs, equipment for makerspaces), producing standardized contracts and vendor lists that meet higher-level procurement rules but are faster to use.

resources.name: Council of Atlantic University Libraries (CAUL-CBUA) Consortial Purchasing
resources.organization: Council of Atlantic University Libraries / Conseil des bibliothèques universitaires de l’Atlantique (CAUL-CBUA)
resources.description: CAUL-CBUA coordinates consortial procurement for Atlantic university libraries, negotiating shared licenses for e-resources, discovery platforms, and related services. By aggregating member demand and using standardized contracts that comply with public-sector procurement rules, it creates vetted vendor lists and faster purchasing paths for post-secondary institutions in Nova Scotia—reducing approval cycles and enabling quicker access to learning and training resources for students and researchers.
resources.address: Killam Memorial Library, 6225 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: Novanet Consortium – Shared Procurement and Systems for Academic Libraries
resources.description: Novanet is a consortium of Nova Scotia academic libraries that jointly procure core systems (integrated library services, discovery layers) and license e-resources through collective agreements. This aggregated buying power produces standardized vendor contracts and a common vendor roster, speeding compliance-heavy purchases for multiple campuses and ensuring students and faculty gain timely access to shared infrastructure and content.
resources.address: Patrick Power Library (c/o Novanet Office), 923 Robie Street, Halifax, NS B3H 3C3

resources.name: APSEA Centralized Procurement for Specialized Education Supports
resources.description: The Atlantic Provinces Special Education Authority centrally sources specialized equipment, assistive technologies, and contracted services for learners who are blind/visually impaired or deaf/hard of hearing across the Atlantic region. By consolidating demand and maintaining standardized, compliant contracts and supplier lists, APSEA accelerates purchasing and deployment of training tools and equipment to schools and communities in Nova Scotia, overcoming fragmented procurement processes.

solutions.text: Community Grant Matching and Risk Fund: Set up a locally governed matching fund that tops up provincial or federal grants and absorbs initial project risk, encouraging faster uptake by risk-averse procurement officers and making proposals more attractive.

resources.name: Solar City Program (Property Assessed Clean Energy Financing)
resources.description: HRM’s Solar City is a municipally governed financing program that advances up-front capital for solar installations and recovers it via a Local Improvement Charge on property tax bills. The program allows projects to stack HRM financing with provincial and federal rebates (e.g., Efficiency Nova Scotia incentives and Canada Greener Homes), effectively topping up those funds so projects can proceed at full scope. By carrying and securing the early capital on the municipal tax roll, HRM mitigates initial project risk and accelerates uptake among risk-averse decision makers and procurement processes.

resources.name: Clean Energy Financing Program (PACE)
resources.description: The Town of Bridgewater’s Clean Energy Financing program provides a locally managed pool of capital that homeowners can combine with federal or provincial incentives to complete deeper energy retrofits. Bridgewater fronts the cost and recovers it through a property-linked Local Improvement Charge, reducing lender risk and procurement friction for early-stage work. This matching and stacking design de-risks projects and speeds execution by aligning with external program timelines and covering gaps those programs don’t fund.

solutions.text: Youth Advisory Councils Embedded in Municipal Decisions: Establish youth advisory councils that are formally consulted on municipal approvals for projects affecting young people; their endorsements help speed political buy-in and identify priorities that reduce rework.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: The HRM Youth Advisory Committee is a formal advisory body established by Halifax Regional Council to bring youth perspectives directly into municipal decision-making. Council and municipal staff consult the committee on policies, planning, and projects that affect young people—such as recreation facilities, transit, and public spaces—so its recommendations can inform approvals, build political buy-in, and prioritize youth needs early to reduce rework across departments.

resources.name: Kentville Youth Council
resources.description: The Kentville Youth Council engages local youth to advise the Town of Kentville on municipal initiatives that impact young people. Working with Town staff and presenting to Council, the group provides input on program design, park and facility planning, and community events—creating a formal channel where youth endorsements shape approvals, accelerate political support, and align cross-department priorities to minimize rework.

solutions.text: Digital Collaboration and Approvals Hub: Build a community-maintained online hub that centralizes project proposals, required permits, timelines, contact persons across government levels, and status updates to reduce back-and-forth and shorten decision cycles.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Environmental Assessment Registry
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Environment and Climate Change
resources.description: The Environmental Assessment (EA) Registry is a province-wide online hub that centralizes major project proposals, all submitted studies, agency review comments, public notices, key milestones, and final decisions. It publishes clear timelines, identifies responsible contacts, and tracks status updates in one place, helping project proponents, municipalities, provincial regulators, and—when required—federal partners coordinate efficiently and reduce back-and-forth during approvals.

resources.name: Halifax Permits, Planning, Licensing & Compliance (PPL&C) Customer Portal
resources.description: HRM’s digital portal lets residents and businesses submit development proposals and building/plumbing/electrical permit applications, upload drawings, pay fees, and monitor review status across municipal departments. It consolidates required permits, target timelines, review comments, and case officer contacts into a single online workspace, cutting email loops and in-person visits and accelerating coordinated decision-making.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Utility and Review Board e-Filing System
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Utility and Review Board
resources.description: The NSUARB e-Filing portal centralizes applications, evidence, schedules, and decisions for approvals and appeals involving energy, water utilities, transportation, and municipal planning matters. Parties and the public can access case timelines, procedural updates, and contact information in one place, improving transparency and coordination among municipalities, provincial regulators, utilities, and other stakeholders.
resources.address: 3rd Floor, 1601 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3P6

resources.name: Nova Scotia Procurement Portal (e-Tendering)
resources.description: The provincial procurement portal centralizes tenders, submission requirements, deadlines, addenda, and buyer contacts for procurements across departments, agencies, school boards, health authorities, and broader public sector entities. By providing a single digital workspace for notices, Q&A, and status updates, it reduces fragmented communication and shortens procurement decision cycles that often slow project delivery.

solutions.text: Standardized Local Agreement Templates: Publish community-vetted templates (MOUs, service agreements, partnership charters) that meet municipal and provincial needs so local organizations and governments can sign and implement projects faster.

resources.name: HRM Procurement Standard Terms & Contract Templates
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality publishes standardized solicitation documents, terms and conditions, and form-of-agreement templates for goods, services, and construction. These vetted templates reduce negotiation time and uncertainty for vendors and community partners, enabling the municipality to execute projects and partnerships faster while complying with provincial procurement requirements.

resources.name: NSFM Resource Library – Model Policies and Inter-Municipal Agreement Templates
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Federation of Municipalities maintains a resource library that includes model policies, sample MOUs, and inter-municipal service agreement templates developed with input from municipal administrators and sector partners. Municipalities adapt these standardized documents to quickly formalize shared services, regional collaborations, and partnerships with community organizations, cutting legal drafting time and aligning with provincial legislation.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1304, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Clean Leadership – Standardized Host Organization and Participant Agreements
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s Clean Leadership program places youth with municipalities, non-profits, and businesses across Nova Scotia using standardized host organization agreements and participant MOUs. These templates define roles, insurance, supervision, and reporting, allowing municipal and community partners to sign quickly and launch projects on a consistent provincial framework.

resources.name: Cape Breton Regional Enterprise Network (REN) – Standard Partnership & Governance Agreements
resources.description: The Cape Breton Partnership administers the Cape Breton REN under standardized inter-municipal and provincial partnership agreements that set governance, cost-sharing, and performance frameworks. Using the REN model agreements enables multiple municipalities and the Province of Nova Scotia to join under a common charter, speeding set-up and renewals so local economic development projects can proceed without bespoke negotiations.

resources.name: Halifax Water – Standardized Developer Servicing & Connection Agreements
resources.description: Halifax Water publishes standardized servicing requirements, specifications, and agreement forms used by developers and community housing groups for water and wastewater projects within HRM. By relying on consistent legal and technical terms, these templates shorten review cycles and approvals, enabling faster project starts while aligning municipal utility and provincial regulatory expectations.
resources.address: 450 Cowie Hill Road, Halifax, NS B3P 2V3

solutions.text: Procurement Capacity-Building for Local Vendors: Run training and mentorship for small local vendors and social enterprises on government procurement rules to increase the pool of qualified bidders and reduce procurement delays caused by vendor deficiencies.

resources.name: Doing Business with HRM – Supplier Information Sessions
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Procurement team hosts recurring information sessions and one-on-one guidance to help small businesses and social enterprises understand municipal procurement rules, bidding requirements, and how to respond to tenders. By teaching vendors how to register, locate opportunities, and submit compliant bids, the program builds supplier capacity and reduces delays caused by incomplete or non-compliant submissions.

resources.name: Procurement Assistance Canada (Atlantic Region) – Supplier Seminars and Advisory
resources.organization: Public Services and Procurement Canada – Procurement Assistance Canada (Atlantic Region)
resources.description: Procurement Assistance Canada provides free training, webinars, and one-on-one advisory to help small and diverse suppliers in Nova Scotia sell to the Government of Canada, including how to use CanadaBuys, understand security requirements, and prepare compliant bids. This hands-on capacity-building helps local vendors navigate federal procurement rules and reduces delays related to vendor deficiencies.
resources.address: Queen Square, 45 Alderney Drive, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 2N6

resources.name: Province of Nova Scotia – Supplier Engagement and Reverse Trade Show
resources.description: Nova Scotia’s Procurement division runs supplier engagement activities, including training sessions on how to bid on provincial tenders, common compliance pitfalls, and how evaluations work, along with an annual Reverse Trade Show connecting vendors with public-sector buyers. These initiatives mentor SMEs and social enterprises on procurement rules and processes, expanding the pool of qualified bidders and streamlining procurements.

resources.name: Indigenous Procurement Readiness and PSIB Support
resources.description: Ulnooweg provides advisory, workshops, and mentorship to Indigenous entrepreneurs on selling to public-sector buyers, including navigating the federal Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB), developing capability statements, and forming bid teams. This builds vendor readiness to meet procurement requirements and improves bid quality, reducing delays and increasing successful participation in public contracts.
resources.address: 172 Truro Heights Road, Truro Heights, NS B6L 1X1

resources.name: ISANS Business Services – Selling to Government Workshops
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers workshops and advisory for immigrant-owned SMEs on how to do business with municipal, provincial, and federal governments, often in partnership with public procurement teams. Training covers finding opportunities, understanding tender documents, and preparing compliant bids, which directly builds procurement capacity and reduces errors that can delay contract awards.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Municipal Regulatory Sandbox Program: Launch a community-driven sandbox allowing pilot regulatory flexibility for innovative youth employment and business models on a time-limited basis, with clear evaluation criteria so successful models can be scaled without lengthy approvals.

resources.name: Halifax Right-of-Way Patio and Parklet Program (Sidewalk Café Licence)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality issues seasonal, time-limited permits that let businesses temporarily use the public right-of-way for patios and parklets, with streamlined approvals and clear operating criteria. Introduced and expanded through quick-response pilots, the program functions as a municipal regulatory sandbox—testing flexible rules, evaluating safety/economic outcomes, and then standardizing successful approaches—so youth-led restaurants, cafes, and creative vendors can launch or expand employment and business models without lengthy approvals.

resources.name: Town of Wolfville Sidewalk Café and Parklet Program
resources.description: Wolfville provides a seasonal permitting framework that relaxes standard right-of-way rules to allow temporary patios and parklets, enabling small and youth-owned businesses to pilot new offerings quickly. The town evaluates pilots on safety, accessibility, and community benefit, and uses results to refine policy—an applied regulatory sandbox that shortens approval timelines and supports local employment in hospitality and cultural sectors.

resources.name: Town of Lunenburg Temporary Outdoor Seating Policy
resources.description: Lunenburg’s policy enables time-limited permits for temporary outdoor seating in the public realm, easing typical right-of-way restrictions so businesses can test expanded service models during the season. This sandbox-style approach includes defined standards and review points, allowing successful pilots to inform lasting bylaw and process changes that support faster execution and local youth employment.

resources.name: CBRM Temporary Outdoor Patio Permit Program
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Municipality offers expedited, seasonal patio permits that allow businesses to temporarily occupy sidewalks and curb lanes, reducing red tape to test new service and hiring models. The municipality monitors safety, accessibility, and economic impact, using findings to adjust policy—functioning as a regulatory sandbox that accelerates recovery, supports youth jobs, and coordinates cross-department approvals.

solutions.text: Joint Risk-Sharing Agreements: Negotiate simple local agreements where community organizations and municipalities share defined financial or delivery risks for priority projects, lowering barriers for conservative procurement processes.

resources.name: Zatzman Sportsplex Operating Agreement
resources.description: The Zatzman Sportsplex is operated by the Dartmouth Sportsplex Community Association under a service agreement with Halifax Regional Municipality (HRM). The agreement shares risk by assigning day-to-day programming and revenue risk to the community non-profit while HRM retains major capital responsibilities and provides a defined operating subsidy tied to service levels. This joint, performance-based arrangement enables faster decision-making and delivery than traditional procurement while clearly allocating financial and delivery risks.

resources.name: Canada Games Centre Society–HRM Operating Agreement
resources.description: The Canada Games Centre is managed by the Canada Games Centre Society through a long-term operating agreement with HRM that defines performance targets, subsidy frameworks, and responsibilities. Operational delivery and program revenue risks are borne by the Society, while HRM assumes major capital upkeep, creating a clear, shared-risk framework. This structure allows the Centre to deliver priority community recreation services quickly and flexibly, reducing barriers associated with conservative municipal procurement.
resources.address: 26 Thomas Raddall Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 0E2

resources.name: Lunenburg County Lifestyle Centre Joint Services & Operating Agreements
resources.description: The Lunenburg County Lifestyle Centre (LCLC) is co-owned by the Town of Bridgewater and the Municipality of the District of Lunenburg and operated by the Lunenburg County Lifestyle Centre Society under defined service and funding agreements. These agreements outline how operating deficits/surpluses, programming delivery, and asset responsibilities are shared, allocating financial and delivery risks between the municipalities and the community operator. The joint model streamlines execution of priority recreation projects and programming compared to traditional procurement-only approaches.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

resources.name: Pictou County Wellness Centre Inter-Municipal & Operating Agreements
resources.description: The Pictou County Wellness Centre is governed through inter-municipal agreements among local governments and an operating agreement that assigns day-to-day delivery to the facility organization, with municipalities sharing defined funding responsibilities. The agreements clarify who carries operating risk (programming, revenues, service outcomes) versus capital and long-term asset risks, creating a shared-risk model. This enables timely delivery of priority recreation and community services without relying solely on slow, risk-averse procurement processes.
resources.address: 2756 Westville Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 5C6

resources.name: Halifax Partnership Service Agreement with HRM
resources.description: Halifax Partnership delivers economic development for the municipality under a multi-year service agreement co-funded by HRM and private/institutional investors, with defined performance metrics and reporting. The agreement shares risk by tying municipal funding to outcomes while leveraging investor contributions, allowing the Partnership to execute priority projects and initiatives more nimbly than traditional procurement. This public–private, joint-risk approach lowers barriers to coordinated action across employers, community organizations, and the municipality.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Community Impact Dashboard and Scorecard: Maintain an accessible dashboard tracking outcomes (jobs created, youth retained, housing units) for community-led initiatives to provide evidence that accelerates funder approvals and aligns multi-level government decision-making.

resources.name: Halifax Index
resources.description: An annual, publicly accessible dashboard that consolidates indicators on employment, labour force participation, population flows and youth retention, housing starts, and affordability in Halifax. The Index functions as a community impact scorecard used by community groups, businesses, and municipal–provincial–federal partners to align decisions and support funding applications with clear evidence on jobs, youth attraction/retention, and housing outcomes.

resources.name: Strategic Performance Snapshot (Municipal Performance Dashboard)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality maintains an interactive performance dashboard tracking planning and development metrics, including permit volumes, processing timelines, and affordable housing units enabled. By publishing standardized, up-to-date indicators, the Snapshot serves as a cross-government scorecard that helps community-led proposals and municipal projects demonstrate outcomes, accelerating approvals and coordinating efforts with provincial and federal housing and infrastructure programs.

resources.name: Our Impact (Energy Efficiency Program Results Dashboard)
resources.description: Efficiency Nova Scotia publishes ongoing impact metrics—homes and buildings upgraded, energy savings, participation by households and businesses, and jobs supported through efficiency projects—via public dashboards and scorecards. These accessible outcomes help communities and nonprofits evidence the benefits of local retrofits, while enabling alignment and faster approvals from provincial and federal funders for climate, affordability, and housing-related initiatives.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: ISANS Impact Dashboard
resources.organization: Immigration Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS publicly reports outcomes such as newcomer employment, job placements, entrepreneurship support, and retention in Nova Scotia through an impact dashboard and annual scorecards. These standardized metrics provide clear evidence for community-led workforce and settlement initiatives, helping municipal–provincial–federal funders assess results quickly and coordinate programs that contribute to youth and talent retention and job creation across the province.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

obstacles.title: Talent Perception and Outmigration Narratives
obstacles.description: Persistent beliefs that success requires leaving Atlantic Canada weaken local aspiration and reduce return migration.

solutions.text: Local Success Story Campaign: Collect and share multimedia profiles of residents succeeding in diverse fields (trades, tech, arts, entrepreneurship, community services) through schools, social media, local radio and newspapers to normalize local achievement and highlight viable careers without leaving.

resources.name: NSCC Stories (Alumni and Student Profiles)
resources.description: NSCC Stories publishes video, photo, and written profiles of students, apprentices, and alumni in trades, technology, arts, business, and community services across campuses in Nova Scotia. The college distributes these stories through its website, social media, and outreach to schools and career programming, normalizing local achievement and showcasing viable career paths that can be built without leaving the province.

resources.name: Halifax Partnership Stories and Game Changers
resources.description: Halifax Partnership features multimedia profiles of local entrepreneurs, new graduates, youth hires, and employers through its Stories and Game Changers initiatives. These profiles are shared via the Partnership’s website, social media, newsletters, and community events, promoting the narrative that talent can thrive in Halifax and Nova Scotia and highlighting concrete, local career opportunities across sectors.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Centre for Women in Business Member Spotlights
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business, Mount Saint Vincent University
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business regularly publishes Member Spotlights and founder features that highlight women-led companies in fields ranging from ocean tech and trades to creative industries and services. Shared across its website, social media, and partner networks (including post-secondary and community organizations), these stories provide relatable local role models and reinforce that successful enterprises can be built in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Cape Breton Partnership – Our Stories
resources.description: The Cape Breton Partnership’s Our Stories showcases video and written profiles of residents—entrepreneurs, tradespeople, innovators, and community leaders—who are building careers and businesses on the Island. By circulating these profiles through its website, social media, media partners, and outreach to schools and employment programs, the initiative counters outmigration narratives and highlights tangible local pathways to success.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

resources.name: ISANS Client Success Stories
resources.organization: Immigration Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS publishes Client Success Stories profiling newcomers who have launched businesses, entered the trades, and advanced in technology and community services across Nova Scotia. These stories are shared through the ISANS website, social media, and community outreach (including school and youth-settlement programming), helping normalize local achievement and demonstrating real pathways to build a life and career in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Returnee Mentorship & Networking Program: Create a community-run mentorship network that pairs young people with local professionals and returnees for career guidance, internships and informal support, increasing visibility of local pathways and making return migration feel more feasible.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program pairs internationally trained professionals and recent graduates with established local professionals in their field for 12–24 weeks of one-to-one mentoring, networking introductions, and labour‑market guidance. By opening doors to informational interviews, job shadowing, and industry events, it increases visibility of Nova Scotia career pathways and builds the social capital that helps newcomers and returnees see a viable future in the province.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Mentorship at Volta
resources.description: Volta connects aspiring and early‑stage founders, students, and young professionals with a network of experienced entrepreneurs and sector experts through mentor office hours, workshops, and community meetups. These structured and informal interactions provide career guidance, local internship and co‑op leads, and connections to returnee founders and professionals, making Nova Scotia’s tech and startup pathways more visible and attainable.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Ocean Connector (Networking Series) and Workforce Initiatives
resources.description: COVE’s Ocean Connector series and workforce initiatives bring students, recent graduates, and early‑career talent together with ocean‑sector companies, engineers, and returning Nova Scotia professionals for monthly networking, talks, and hiring connections. By facilitating warm introductions, mentorship, and internship pathways in a high‑growth local industry, COVE helps young people discover in‑province career options and strengthens the networks that support staying or returning.

resources.name: Business Advisory & Mentorship
resources.description: CEED provides one‑to‑one business advisory, mentorship, and peer networking that match aspiring and early‑stage entrepreneurs—including students, recent grads, and returnees—with seasoned local business owners and coaches. Through ongoing guidance, referrals, and ecosystem events, participants gain professional contacts, practical career and venture advice, and exposure to local opportunities that make building a life and career in Nova Scotia more feasible.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Community Internship & Apprenticeship Consortium: Coordinate a consortium of small businesses, non-profits and tradespeople to offer short-term paid internships and apprenticeships, with shared placement management and promotion to students and recent grads to build local experience and ties.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship
resources.description: Clean Foundation coordinates paid summer internships by recruiting a network of host employers across Nova Scotia’s public, private, and non-profit sectors to place high-school, college, and university students in environmental roles. The program centrally manages outreach, matching, and training, so small businesses and community organizations can participate easily, while students gain locally relevant work experience and ties that encourage them to stay or return to Nova Scotia.

resources.name: COVE Internship Program
resources.description: COVE convenes ocean-technology companies, start-ups, and research organizations to offer coordinated, paid internships for students and recent graduates. By centrally promoting opportunities and matching talent with multiple small and mid-sized ocean firms, COVE helps participants build hands-on experience and local industry networks that strengthen their commitment to careers in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Management Career Services (Co-op)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Management Career Services runs a coordinated co-op system that sources and manages paid work terms with hundreds of employers, including SMEs, non-profits, and social enterprises across Nova Scotia. The centralized promotion, recruitment, and placement process lowers barriers for small organizations to host talent and helps students build local experience and professional connections.

resources.name: Co-operative Education and Work-Integrated Learning
resources.description: NSCC coordinates co-op, internships, and apprenticeship pathways across its campuses, partnering with small businesses, tradespeople, and community organizations to offer paid, short-term placements. The college centrally manages employer engagement and student matching, giving learners practical experience and local ties while enabling employers to access emerging talent across Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: ‘Stay & Return’ Microgrant Fund: Establish a locally administered microgrant program that provides seed funding for startups, creative projects or community ventures by youth and returnees, lowering barriers to launching locally and creating visible success examples.

resources.name: Community Grants Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Community Grants Program provides small project grants (typically up to $5,000) to non-profits for community initiatives, including youth-led and creative ventures. By offering accessible seed funding for local projects and startups, it lowers barriers to launching in-place and creates visible examples of success that reinforce the viability of staying or returning to Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty Placemaking Grants
resources.description: Gritty to Pretty offers micro to mid-sized grants for public art, storefront animation, and placemaking projects in Downtown Halifax, supporting local artists, creatives, and entrepreneurs to prototype and launch ideas. These highly visible, low-barrier seed funds help youth and returnees showcase talent locally, building narratives of success and belonging in Nova Scotia’s urban core.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

resources.name: Neighbourhood Grants
resources.description: United Way Halifax’s Neighbourhood Grants provide small, rapid microgrants to resident-led projects that strengthen community connections and improve local quality of life. By supplying seed funding for young leaders and local returnees to start community ventures or creative initiatives, the program reduces startup friction and creates tangible, public wins that encourage people to stay or come back to Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Skills Showcases & Career Pathway Fairs: Host regular community events that spotlight concrete career pathways (trade demonstrations, portfolio reviews, tech demos, social enterprise booths) so youth and families can see day-to-day work and realistic income/progression locally.

resources.name: CANS Construction Career Expo
resources.description: The Construction Association of Nova Scotia hosts a large, hands-on career expo where students and families can try welding simulators, carpentry stations, surveying tools, and other trade demos while meeting local employers and apprentices. Exhibitors explain apprenticeship pathways, day-to-day work, safety training, and wage progression in Nova Scotia’s construction sector, directly countering the idea that you must leave the province to build a well-paid career.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Volta Hiring Fair
resources.description: Volta’s recurring hiring fair brings Halifax-based startups and scale-ups together with students and jobseekers for product demos, portfolio reviews, and on-the-spot interviews. Companies showcase real roles in software, product, design, sales, and operations, and share local salary bands and growth paths—making the region’s tech careers visible and attainable without leaving Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: ISANS Employer Showcases and Job Fairs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS runs regular sector-specific showcases and career fairs that connect jobseekers—including youth and families—with Nova Scotia employers in health care, hospitality, IT, manufacturing, and more. Events feature employer booths, info sessions on local credentials and career ladders, and practical guidance on wages and progression, helping attendees see clear, local pathways to meaningful work.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Youth Job & Volunteer Fairs
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts youth-focused job and volunteer fairs—often at the Central Library and other branches—where local employers, trades, social enterprises, and community groups run booths and skills demos. Libraries pair these expos with resume clinics and portfolio reviews, giving teens and families a clear view of day-to-day work and entry points into local career pathways.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: NSCC Open House & Program Showcases (Akerley Campus)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Akerley Campus
resources.description: NSCC’s Akerley Campus opens its shops, labs, and kitchens for interactive showcases where faculty, students, and industry partners demonstrate trades, culinary, transportation, and technology programs. These events outline local employment outcomes, apprenticeship routes, and wage progression, helping youth and families visualize concrete, Nova Scotia–based career pathways.

solutions.text: Local Hiring Pledges & Employment Directory: Encourage local employers to sign a public hiring pledge to prioritize regional candidates where possible and maintain a centralized directory of local job, apprenticeship and contract opportunities to counter the narrative 'you must leave to get work.'

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Job Board
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: Nova Scotia Works operates the province’s centralized, public job board that aggregates Nova Scotia-only employment, apprenticeship, co-op, and contract postings from employers across the province. By making local opportunities easy to find in one place and engaging employers to post roles locally, it directly counters the idea that residents must leave to get work and supports hire-local practices.

resources.name: Halifax Connector Program & Work in Halifax Job Portal
resources.description: The Halifax Connector Program matches local and returning talent with volunteer business leaders (Connectors) who commit to meet and introduce them to their networks, reinforcing a community-wide norm to hire locally. In tandem, the Partnership’s job portal and campaigns spotlight Halifax-based opportunities, creating a visible directory of regional roles and encouraging employers to prioritize candidates who want to build careers in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Cape Breton Job Board
resources.description: The Cape Breton Job Board is a region-specific directory that lists jobs, apprenticeships, and contract opportunities exclusively in Cape Breton—Unama’ki. By centralizing local postings and working with employers to feature island-based roles, it makes it easier for residents and returnees to find work at home and encourages businesses to recruit and retain local talent.

resources.name: Volta Jobs Board
resources.description: Volta’s Jobs Board curates openings from Halifax and Nova Scotia startups, providing a centralized directory of local tech and innovation roles. Through its member programming and employer engagement, Volta encourages companies to source talent locally and showcase opportunities that allow emerging professionals to build careers without leaving the province.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: ISANS Job Board & Employer Engagement
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS maintains a Nova Scotia–focused job board and works directly with employers through recruitment events and advisory services to fill roles with local talent, including internationally trained residents who have chosen Nova Scotia. By promoting local candidate pipelines and highlighting provincial opportunities in one place, ISANS helps employers commit to recruiting in-province and counters outmigration narratives.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Alumni & Diaspora Engagement Network: Build and maintain a community-managed database and regular programming for alumni and diaspora to share remote mentoring, investment, seasonal work, and returning opportunities—turning outward migration into a resource rather than a loss.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program matches new graduates, newcomers, and job seekers with established professionals (Connectors) who open their networks, provide informational interviews, and share opportunities. The program actively maintains a large database of Connectors—including Nova Scotia alumni and diaspora living away or recently returned—and runs regular programming to facilitate mentoring, referrals, and pathways to local jobs, thereby turning outward migration into a resource.
resources.address: 1969 Upper Water Street, Suite 1301, Halifax, NS B3J 3R7

resources.name: Ten Thousand Coffees (Dalhousie University)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Office of Advancement (Alumni Engagement)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Ten Thousand Coffees mentoring community connects students and recent grads with a global network of Dal alumni, enabling remote mentoring, career advice, and introductions. By engaging Dal’s diaspora—alumni living across Canada and abroad—the platform maintains a living database of mentors and hosts ongoing virtual meetups and programs that highlight career paths in Nova Scotia and support returning or investing back in the province.

resources.name: Ten Thousand Coffees (Nova Scotia Community College - NSCC Connects)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) Alumni Relations
resources.description: NSCC’s mentoring community on Ten Thousand Coffees connects students and recent graduates with NSCC alumni across industries for virtual coffee chats, career conversations, and project-based guidance. This alumni database and ongoing programming draw in NSCC’s diaspora—graduates working outside Nova Scotia—to mentor remotely, flag seasonal and full-time opportunities, and help peers navigate pathways to return or contribute to local enterprises.

resources.name: Ten Thousand Coffees (Saint Mary’s University)
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University engages its alumni network to mentor students and young alumni through structured, ongoing matches and virtual events hosted on its alumni networking and mentoring platform. By tapping SMU’s global diaspora, the community maintains a searchable database of mentors and regularly promotes Nova Scotia career, startup, and returning-to-work opportunities, reframing outmigration as a source of mentorship, investment, and pathways home.

solutions.text: Visible Pathways in Schools and Youth Programs: Partner schools, community centres and trade boards to integrate local career mapping into curricula and extracurriculars, run job-shadow days and invite local role models to show students practical routes to fulfilling local careers.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.organization: Construction Association of Nova Scotia (CANS) in partnership with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency
resources.description: Building Futures for Youth connects Grade 10–12 students with paid summer co-op placements in Nova Scotia’s construction sector, pairing them with local employers and certified tradespeople. Working with school co-op offices, the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, and industry partners, the program integrates career mapping, safety training, job-shadowing, and mentorship to show clear, practical pathways from high school into local skilled trades careers.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

resources.name: Options and Opportunities (O2) Program
resources.description: O2 is a high school program that embeds career development into the curriculum through individualized career planning, co-op education, and community-based learning. Delivered in partnership with local employers and community organizations, it provides students with job-shadow days, workplace experiences, and exposure to local role models across trades, technology, health, arts, and community services, making visible the many pathways to fulfilling careers in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: WISEatlantic – Girls Get WISE and School Outreach
resources.organization: Women in Science and Engineering – Atlantic (hosted by Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: WISEatlantic partners with schools and community groups across Nova Scotia to deliver hands-on STEM workshops, career panels, and mentorship opportunities led by local scientists, engineers, and technologists. Through Girls Get WISE retreats and in-school sessions, students meet role models, learn about regional post-secondary pathways and employers, and see practical routes into rewarding STEM careers without leaving the province.

solutions.text: Housing & Family Support Initiatives: Support community-led solutions like co-operative housing, affordable rental pools and shared childcare cooperatives to reduce relocation pressures for families and make staying or returning more viable financially and socially.

resources.name: Community Housing Acquisition Program (CHAP)
resources.organization: Housing Nova Scotia (Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
resources.description: CHAP provides funding to non-profit and co-operative housing providers to acquire existing rental properties and preserve them as permanently affordable, community-owned housing. By expanding and stabilizing affordable rental pools across Nova Scotia, the program reduces financial pressure on families and strengthens locally governed housing options. This community-led approach helps young people and families stay or return by ensuring secure, affordable homes in their communities.

resources.name: Co-operative Development Services
resources.description: This province-wide service helps communities form and grow co-operatives—including housing co-ops and parent-led childcare co-ops—through feasibility support, governance training, business planning, and access to financing tools. By empowering residents to create member-owned solutions, it directly advances co-operative housing and shared childcare that lower costs and build local wealth. These community-led models strengthen social ties and make it more viable for families and young people to remain in or return to Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 90 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: New Dawn Properties
resources.description: New Dawn manages a portfolio of affordable and mixed-income rental housing in Cape Breton, keeping units community-owned and reinvesting revenues locally. This creates a stable, affordable rental pool that supports families, workers, and newcomers, while complementing employment and community services operated by the organization. By expanding secure, community-led housing options, New Dawn helps reduce the need to relocate and makes it easier for people to stay or return to Nova Scotia.

resources.name: YWCA Halifax Early Learning & Child Care Centre
resources.description: YWCA Halifax operates licensed early learning and child care that is accessible and tailored to local family needs, alongside wraparound supports for women and families. Affordable, reliable childcare reduces costs and enables parents to work, train, or study locally, decreasing pressure to relocate. Combined with YWCA’s supportive and affordable housing initiatives, this community-led ecosystem helps families build stable lives in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: Aboriginal Head Start Program
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre delivers an Indigenous-led early childhood education program that provides free, culturally grounded childcare, nutrition, and family supports. Parent involvement and community leadership lower barriers to childcare, strengthen cultural identity, and build social networks that make staying or returning more feasible. Together with the Centre’s housing and support services, it reduces relocation pressures for Indigenous families in Halifax.

solutions.text: Public Celebrations & Local Awards: Create annual awards, festivals and public showcases that celebrate local entrepreneurs, skilled tradespeople, artists and community leaders to raise local pride and counteract the idea that success only happens elsewhere.

resources.name: Halifax Business Awards
resources.description: An annual gala that publicly recognizes outstanding local entrepreneurs, innovators, exporters, and community-minded businesses across Halifax. By celebrating homegrown success stories on a high-profile stage, the awards elevate local role models and demonstrate that ambitious careers and thriving companies are built in Nova Scotia, countering the narrative that success requires leaving.

resources.name: Game Changers Awards
resources.description: This annual celebration honors employers, community leaders, and young professionals who are creating meaningful career opportunities and retaining talent in Halifax. The public recognition showcases local pathways to success and highlights companies investing in youth and newcomers, reinforcing that Nova Scotia offers rewarding careers and community impact.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Immigrant Entrepreneurship Showcases and Awards
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS hosts public showcases and recognition events during Small Business Week and throughout the year that feature immigrant-owned businesses and founders. By celebrating newcomer entrepreneurs’ achievements, these events raise local pride, expand networks, and make visible the diverse success stories happening in Nova Scotia today.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Craft Nova Scotia Holiday Craft Market and Summer Show
resources.organization: Craft Nova Scotia (Centre for Craft Nova Scotia)
resources.description: These juried annual festivals at the Halifax Seaport publicly showcase the work of Nova Scotian artisans and fine craft producers, celebrating skilled tradespeople and creative entrepreneurs. By drawing large local audiences to discover and buy locally made goods, the shows elevate artisan careers and reinforce that creative, trade-based livelihoods thrive in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Peer-Led Entrepreneurship Circles and Incubator: Set up low-cost, peer-run incubator groups that provide mentorship, shared workspace, legal/accounting clinics and access to local seed funding to help aspiring entrepreneurs and creators launch viable local ventures.

resources.name: Volta Residency and Community Membership
resources.description: Volta operates a downtown incubator that offers founders low-cost shared workspace, a peer community of entrepreneurs, and structured mentorship from experienced operators and advisors. It regularly hosts legal and accounting office hours and clinics with partner firms, and runs the Volta Cohort program that provides early-stage seed funding and investor readiness support—directly aligning with peer-led incubator circles that help local ventures launch and scale in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: Start-Up Yard is an oceans-focused incubator that provides entrepreneurs with shared workspace, prototyping facilities, and access to a peer network of founders and sector mentors. The program delivers expert advisory sessions—often including legal and accounting guidance—and connects companies to local seed funding pathways and investors through partners like Invest Nova Scotia and ACOA, helping founders build viable ventures without leaving the province.

resources.name: CEED Entrepreneurship Programs & Impact Loan
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides peer-based entrepreneurship programs, coaching, and a collaborative workspace environment that fosters learning circles among founders. It offers practical clinics and workshops with legal and accounting professionals and administers the CEED Impact Loan (micro-seed funding) to help new and growing Nova Scotia businesses access the early capital they need to launch and create local jobs.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Community Ambassadors & Returnee Welcome Program: Develop a volunteer ambassador program that greets returning residents, helps them navigate services (housing, childcare, licensing), introduces them to local networks and promotes rapid integration into community and economic life.

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: The Cape Breton Welcome Network organizes local volunteer Welcome Groups that greet newcomers and returning residents to communities across Cape Breton–Unama’ki. Volunteers act as community ambassadors, offering practical guidance on housing, childcare, healthcare, and licensing, and introducing returnees to social and professional networks through events, meetups, and one-on-one connections to speed up integration into community and economic life.

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: The Connector Program matches job-ready newcomers, recent graduates, and returning Nova Scotians with established professionals who volunteer as Connectors, facilitating warm introductions to their networks. By rapidly building social and professional ties, sharing local job market insights, and hosting networking events, the program helps returnees navigate services and integrate quickly into Halifax’s community and economy.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Newcomer Services at Halifax Central Library
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Newcomer Services provide a welcoming, walk-in hub where staff greet people new to the city—including returning Canadians—offer one-on-one information and referrals, and help navigate practical needs such as housing, childcare, schooling, and documentation. Through conversation groups, orientation sessions, and community events, they connect returnees to local networks and resources that accelerate social and economic integration.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Settlement & Employment Services (ISANS)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides comprehensive settlement navigation and employment support that greets newcomers with needs assessments, orientation, and guidance on housing, childcare, healthcare, and professional licensing. Mentorship, networking, and employer-connection programs act as community ‘ambassadors,’ introducing participants to local professionals and opportunities so they can integrate rapidly into Nova Scotia’s social and economic life.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

obstacles.title: Limited availability of high-quality, future-ready jobs
obstacles.description: A small domestic market, seasonal employment, and slow productivity growth limit stable, well-paying roles in emerging sectors, making it harder to compete with larger provinces for talent.

solutions.text: Community Business Incubator: Create a locally-run incubator that offers low-cost space, mentorship, and business services for startups and small enterprises in tech, creative industries, and value-added resource processing to help founders move from concept to revenue.

resources.name: Volta Residency
resources.description: Volta’s Residency provides subsidized office and co-working space, access to in-house mentors, and back-office services (including legal/accounting clinics, marketing workshops, and founder peer circles) for early-stage startups in tech and creative industries. The program connects founders with advisors, investors, and corporate partners, helping teams validate ideas, build go-to-market plans, and move from concept to recurring revenue in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE is an ocean-technology incubator offering affordable office, lab, and workshop space with shared prototyping equipment and waterfront test facilities. Companies receive mentorship from industry experts, commercialization support, and supply-chain connections, enabling founders in blue economy and value-added marine sectors to progress from prototype to market revenue.

resources.name: CEEDspace
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEEDspace is a low-cost co-working and incubation hub that provides desks and offices, mentorship, and hands-on business advisory for startups and small enterprises across sectors, including tech and creative industries. Through training programs, coaching, and connections to financing, CEED helps founders validate ideas, acquire first customers, and build sustainable revenue in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Innovacorp Enterprise Centre (Life Sciences Research Institute)
resources.description: The Innovacorp Enterprise Centre at the Life Sciences Research Institute offers flexible, subsidized wet labs and office space for life sciences and biotech startups, along with shared equipment and on-site advisory. Operated by Invest Nova Scotia, it connects founders to mentors, commercialization programming, and funding pathways, helping teams move efficiently from R&D to regulated product sales and export revenue.

resources.name: Navigate Startup House
resources.organization: Navigate (a joint initiative of Cape Breton University and Nova Scotia Community College – Marconi Campus)
resources.description: Navigate Startup House provides affordable co-working space, meeting rooms, and maker resources in Cape Breton, paired with mentorship, workshops, and business advisory services. As a university–college partnership, it supports tech, creative, and resource-based ventures in developing business models, accessing markets, and growing revenue without leaving the region.

solutions.text: Cooperative Enterprise Development: Support formation of worker and producer co-ops (e.g., fisheries, food processing, crafts, tourism) that keep profits local, stabilize seasonal income, and provide democratic, stable employment.

resources.name: International Centre for Co-operative Management
resources.organization: Sobey School of Business, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: Based at Saint Mary’s University, the International Centre for Co-operative Management delivers executive education, applied research, and advisory services tailored to co-operatives and credit unions. By equipping founders and managers with governance, strategy, and finance skills specific to worker and producer co-ops, the Centre directly supports the creation and strengthening of democratic enterprises that retain profits locally and stabilize employment across seasons.

resources.name: Just Us! Coffee Roasters Co-op
resources.description: Just Us! is a worker-owned co-operative that roasts, packages, and retails fair-trade coffee and related products in the Annapolis Valley and beyond. As a democratic workplace that reinvests locally, it provides year-round jobs in food processing and hospitality, stabilizing income in a region with strong seasonality while modeling how worker co-ops keep profits in the community.

resources.name: Scotian Gold Co-operative Limited
resources.description: Scotian Gold is a producer co-operative owned by apple growers that provides shared packing, storage, marketing, and distribution infrastructure in the Annapolis Valley. By pooling resources and returning profits to member-farmers, the co-op strengthens local supply chains, creates steady year-round employment in grading and storage, and helps stabilize seasonal farm incomes.

solutions.text: Microgrant and Microloan Funds: Operate community microgrant and revolving microloan programs to help entrepreneurs, social enterprises, and tradespeople scale operations, purchase equipment, or bridge seasonal gaps.

resources.name: CEED Impact Loan
resources.description: CEED’s Impact Loan is a revolving microloan fund that provides early-stage and growing entrepreneurs with flexible financing typically ranging from about $5,000 to $25,000. The fund helps small businesses and social enterprises purchase equipment, cover working capital, or bridge seasonal cash-flow gaps, and is paired with coaching and training to increase the likelihood of sustainable growth and job creation.

resources.name: ISANS Business Loan Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Business Loan Program offers microloans to immigrant and refugee entrepreneurs to start or grow small businesses in Nova Scotia, often in partnership with local credit unions. Funds can be used to buy tools and equipment, inventory, or to bridge seasonal and start-up cash-flow needs, and the financing is complemented by business training and mentorship to support long-term success.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Ulnooweg Indigenous Business Financing
resources.description: Ulnooweg provides flexible micro and small-business loans to Mi’kmaq and other Indigenous entrepreneurs across Nova Scotia through a revolving fund model. Financing supports equipment purchases, working capital, and bridge loans for seasonal sectors like fisheries and tourism, and is paired with advisory services to help entrepreneurs and tradespeople scale operations and create quality local jobs.
resources.address: 172 Truro Heights Road, Truro Heights, NS B6L 1X1

solutions.text: Local Procurement and Buy-Local Campaigns: Mobilize municipalities, institutions, and residents to prioritize local suppliers and contractors, creating predictable demand that supports year-round jobs and small business growth.

resources.name: Love Local Cape Breton
resources.description: Love Local Cape Breton is an island-wide buy-local campaign that promotes Cape Breton–Unama’ki businesses through a searchable directory, marketing toolkits, and seasonal promotions. By encouraging residents, employers, and municipal partners to source goods and services from local vendors, it channels everyday and institutional spending toward local suppliers, helping create steadier, year-round demand and supporting small business growth.

resources.name: Downtown Halifax Dollars
resources.description: Downtown Halifax Dollars is a local gift card/currency accepted by participating independent businesses, making it easy for residents, employers, and event organizers to keep spending within the local economy. The program works with member businesses and institutional purchasers to channel procurement (e.g., staff rewards, client gifts, event prizing) to local suppliers, driving predictable demand that supports year-round jobs.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

resources.name: Downtown Dartmouth Dollars
resources.description: Downtown Dartmouth Dollars is a community currency and shop-local campaign that directs household and organizational spending to independent retailers, services, and restaurants in Downtown Dartmouth. By engaging residents, employers, and partners for bulk purchases and promotions, it helps local suppliers capture more year-round procurement, stabilizing revenue and employment beyond the peak tourist season.

resources.name: Meet Your Farmer (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Meet Your Farmer is a province-wide initiative that connects consumers and buyers with Nova Scotia farmers through producer directories, storytelling, and events like Open Farm Day. The campaign encourages households, retailers, and institutions to procure local food, strengthening supply relationships and increasing predictable demand for Nova Scotia producers throughout the year.
resources.address: 7 Mellor Avenue, Unit 1, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0E8

solutions.text: Community Skills Hubs and Maker Spaces: Set up local skills hubs offering short courses, workshops, shared tools and prototyping equipment so residents can gain digital, trades, and creative skills and test new business ideas affordably.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
