resources.description: A member-supported lending library and workshop that provides access to hundreds of hand and power tools, along with safety orientations and skills workshops in woodworking, home repair, and fabrication. It implements the solution by lowering the cost of entry for residents and entrepreneurs to prototype products, learn trades and maker skills, and carry out small-scale production without purchasing expensive equipment. The shared shop, classes, and community mentors help people test business ideas and build practical capabilities.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: A free, public makerspace at Halifax Central Library offering 3D printers, sewing machines, Cricut cutters, design software, and hands-on workshops for youth and adults. It functions as a community skills hub by teaching digital fabrication, design, and creative production skills while giving access to shared tools to prototype products, signage, and art. Entrepreneurs and learners can experiment affordably, build portfolios, and explore self-employment paths.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE is an oceans-sector innovation hub that provides shared workshops, prototyping labs, machine shop access, and test infrastructure alongside regular training sessions and industry events. It implements the solution by giving startups, students, and skilled tradespeople access to specialized tools and collaborative spaces to build and iterate marine technologies without the overhead of owning equipment. The hub’s programming connects talent to mentors and companies, building in-demand technical skills and pathways to jobs.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Yarmouth Innovation Hub & Maker Lab
resources.description: IGNITE runs a rural innovation hub in Yarmouth that combines coworking with a community maker lab featuring 3D printers, electronics benches, and prototyping equipment, plus startup workshops and youth programs. By offering shared tools, training, and mentorship, the space helps residents learn digital and trades-adjacent skills and prototype new products and business ideas at low cost. This hands-on environment supports entrepreneurship and helps retain talent in Southwest Nova Scotia.

resources.name: James McConnell Memorial Library – Creation Station
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library’s Creation Station provides community access to 3D printing, Cricut/vinyl cutting, sewing machines, and digital media tools, with free orientations, drop-in help, and workshops. It serves as a community skills hub by teaching practical digital fabrication and creative skills and offering shared equipment so people can prototype products, crafts, and signage for small ventures. The library lowers barriers for youth and adults to explore technology, learn-by-doing, and develop employable skills.

solutions.text: Apprenticeship and Trades Mentorship Networks: Connect experienced tradespeople with young people through paid apprenticeships, mentorships, and employer consortiums to expand pathways into stable, well-paid skilled trades.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program matches apprentices with employer sponsors and journeyperson mentors across more than 70 skilled trades. The Agency coordinates paid on‑the‑job training with in‑school technical training, administers employer incentives, and supports youth apprenticeship pathways—expanding mentored, sustainable routes into stable, well‑paid trades careers.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY places Nova Scotia high school students in paid summer jobs with construction employers and pairs them with experienced tradespeople for on‑site mentorship. Participants receive safety training, earn co‑op credits, and can transition directly into registered apprenticeships through employer partners—broadening entry pathways into stable, well‑paid skilled trades.
resources.address: 260 Brownlow Avenue, Unit 3, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1V9

resources.name: Women Unlimited Program
resources.description: Women Unlimited prepares and supports women to enter and succeed in skilled trades and technology through cohort‑based training, career exploration, and industry mentorship. The program connects participants to employers for paid work placements and apprenticeship opportunities, building inclusive, mentored pathways into long‑term, well‑paid trades careers in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Trades Bridging & Apprenticeship Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS helps internationally trained tradespeople enter Nova Scotia’s apprenticeship system by assessing skills, providing gap training and mentoring, and connecting clients with local employers. Through supervised work experiences and employer introductions, participants transition into registered apprenticeships and progress toward Red Seal certification, strengthening the province’s mentored trades talent pipeline.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Season-to-Year-Round Tourism Initiatives: Develop off-season cultural, outdoor, and conference programming and package experiences with local producers to spread tourism revenues across more months and create steady jobs.

resources.name: Halifax Convention Centre
resources.description: Halifax Convention Centre brings national and international meetings, conventions, and trade shows to Nova Scotia throughout the year, including the winter and shoulder seasons. By attracting off‑season business events and featuring Nova Scotia food and beverage partners in its culinary offerings, the Centre spreads visitor spending beyond summer and sustains stable jobs in hospitality, event services, and related local suppliers.

resources.name: Cape Smokey (Four-Season Mountain Resort)
resources.description: Cape Smokey is developing a true four-season destination on Cape Breton Island with alpine skiing, a year-round gondola, hiking, and festivals that reduce reliance on the summer window. The resort programs winter and shoulder‑season outdoor experiences and collaborates with Nova Scotia food and beverage producers for on‑mountain dining and events, extending tourism revenues and employment across more months.
resources.address: 38696 Cabot Trail, Ingonish Beach, NS B0C 1L0

resources.name: White Point Beach Resort
resources.description: White Point Beach Resort operates year‑round on the South Shore and creates off‑season packages such as winter coastal escapes, wellness retreats, and February Lobster Crawl experiences with local fishers, artists, and culinary producers. By programming themed weekends and events outside peak summer, the resort drives steady occupancy, supports local suppliers, and maintains stable hospitality and recreation jobs.
resources.address: 75 White Point Beach Resort Road, White Point, NS B0T 1G0

resources.name: Lunenburg Folk Harbour Winter Concert Series
resources.description: Run by the Lunenburg Folk Harbour Society, this concert series brings live music to downtown Lunenburg during the tourism off‑season. By activating local venues and coordinating with nearby restaurants and accommodations for patron offers, it encourages winter and shoulder‑season visits that circulate revenue to small businesses and provide ongoing gigs for artists and technical crews.

solutions.text: Remote Work Hubs and Attraction Programs: Convert underused community spaces into co-working hubs with strong internet and amenities, and run local campaigns to attract remote workers and digital entrepreneurs seeking quality of life.

resources.name: Volta
resources.description: Volta operates a large co-working and innovation hub in downtown Halifax that provides hot desks, private offices, meeting rooms, and reliable high-speed internet, along with programming and mentorship for startups and digital entrepreneurs. By offering professional workspace and amenities in a central location and fostering a supportive community, Volta enables remote workers and founders to base themselves in Nova Scotia while accessing networks and resources that help them grow.

resources.name: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: COVE has transformed a former Canadian Coast Guard site on the Dartmouth waterfront into a collaborative campus with co-working space, labs, meeting rooms, and robust connectivity for ocean-tech firms and professionals. The hub’s flexible workspaces, programming, and soft-landing supports attract remote workers and digital entrepreneurs in the blue economy who are seeking quality of life in Nova Scotia while staying connected to global markets.

resources.name: The PIER at the Seaport
resources.description: The PIER is a port-focused innovation hub and living lab at the Halifax Seaport that offers hot desks, collaboration zones, event space, and secure, high-speed connectivity for companies and professionals working in logistics, supply chain, and ocean sectors. By providing modern co-working infrastructure in a repurposed waterfront space and convening industry partners, it attracts remote professionals and startups who want to work from Nova Scotia while tapping into an active cluster.

resources.name: Work From Nova Scotia (Talent Attraction Campaign)
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia’s Work From Nova Scotia initiative promotes the province as a destination for remote workers by highlighting quality of life, Atlantic Time Zone advantages, cost-of-living, and access to co-working hubs across urban and rural communities. The campaign and concierge-style support help remote employees and digital entrepreneurs relocate, connect with local ecosystems, and quickly integrate into Nova Scotia’s communities and economy.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Community Investment and Social Finance Pools: Create local investment vehicles (community bonds, pooled equity) that let residents invest in regionally important projects—renewables, housing, childcare, or business expansions—that generate jobs and returns.

resources.name: New Dawn Innovation Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: The New Dawn Innovation Fund is a Community Economic Development Investment Fund (CEDIF) that enables Nova Scotia residents to invest directly in Cape Breton enterprises and community projects. By pooling local equity through share offerings that qualify for provincial tax credits, the fund channels capital into job-creating ventures across sectors such as housing, community services, and small business growth—delivering potential returns to investors while strengthening the regional economy.

resources.name: CUA Investment Shares
resources.description: CUA (Credit Union Atlantic) offers member investment shares that pool local capital for lending to small businesses, community organizations, and priority projects in the Halifax region. These shares give residents a way to invest in their own economy—financing initiatives such as business expansions, affordable housing developments, and community infrastructure—while earning dividends tied to local economic performance.

resources.name: Community Credit Union Investment Shares
resources.organization: Community Credit Union of Cumberland Colchester
resources.description: Community Credit Union of Cumberland Colchester issues member investment shares that aggregate resident capital to finance loans for local businesses, non-profits, and community projects. This social finance pool keeps money circulating in the region—supporting business expansions, community facilities, and services like childcare—while providing members with potential dividends and a direct stake in regional job creation.

solutions.text: Partnerships with Colleges and Universities: Work with regional post-secondary institutions to co-design micro-credentials, co-op placements, and applied research projects that address local employers' needs and keep graduates local.

resources.name: NSCC Microcredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College co-designs stackable micro-credentials with local employers and sector councils to rapidly validate in-demand skills in areas like digital, clean tech, healthcare, and trades. These short, competency-based credentials are aligned to regional labour needs and often link to work-integrated learning and applied research with partner companies, helping students gain local experience and encouraging them to stay in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: DeepSense
resources.description: DeepSense connects ocean-sector companies with Dalhousie University researchers and students to co-develop applied AI/ML and data analytics solutions to real industry problems. Through funded collaborative projects, internships, and co-op placements, it builds employer-informed experience for students while helping local firms innovate, strengthening the talent pipeline that keeps graduates working in Nova Scotia’s blue economy.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Nova Scotia Sandbox)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs is a university–industry innovation sandbox at Dalhousie’s Faculty of Computer Science that partners with regional employers and startups to co-create prototypes, run challenge sprints, and support student-led applied projects. It facilitates pathways to co-ops and paid projects with local companies, giving students practical experience that matches employer needs and encourages them to launch careers in Nova Scotia’s tech sector.

resources.name: Co-operative Education Program
resources.description: CBU’s Co-operative Education program collaborates with local employers and faculty to design for-credit, paid work terms that align academic learning outcomes with real workplace requirements. By connecting students to companies across Cape Breton and Nova Scotia in sectors like energy, technology, public service, and tourism, the program builds job-ready skills and often leads to post-graduation employment in the region.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

solutions.text: Value-Added Local Supply Chains: Coordinate producers, processors, and retailers to develop value-added products (e.g., specialty foods, transformed seafood, artisan goods) that capture more local value and year-round employment.

resources.name: Perennia Food and Beverage Innovation
resources.description: Perennia provides product development, food safety, and market-readiness services that help Nova Scotia producers and processors create value-added foods and transformed seafood. By connecting growers, processors, and retailers—through pilot processing support, shelf-life testing, packaging, and commercialization advice—Perennia helps move raw commodities into higher-value products and supports year-round employment.
resources.address: 45 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: Scotian Gold Cooperative Ltd.
resources.description: Scotian Gold is a growers’ co-operative that coordinates member apple producers with year-round storage, packing, grading, and marketing to deliver value-added apple products to regional and national retailers. By integrating producer supply, advanced processing, and retail distribution under one umbrella, the co-op captures more value locally and provides stable, skilled jobs in the Annapolis Valley.

resources.name: Acadian Seaplants Limited
resources.description: Acadian Seaplants sources seaweeds from Nova Scotia harvesters and transforms them into value-added products for food, agriculture, and personal care markets. The company integrates raw material supply, processing, quality assurance, and global sales, strengthening local supply chains and supporting year-round employment in production, R&D, and logistics.

resources.name: Fisherman’s Market International Inc.
resources.description: Fisherman’s Market works directly with Nova Scotia fishers, operates in-province processing (filleting, smoking, freezing), and sells through retail, wholesale, and export channels. By coordinating producers, processors, and retailers to offer value-added seafood products, the company keeps more value in the province and maintains year-round jobs in processing, sales, and distribution.

resources.name: Acadian Maple Products
resources.description: Acadian Maple aggregates sap and syrup from Nova Scotia maple producers and operates processing, bottling, and product development to create value-added maple foods (e.g., maple butter, candies, sauces). With on-site retail and wholesale distribution that connects local producers to stores and tourism markets, it increases local value capture and supports steady, year-round employment.
resources.address: 13578 Peggy's Cove Road, Upper Tantallon, NS B3Z 2Z6

solutions.text: Green and Blue Economy Projects: Promote community-led renewable energy, energy-efficiency retrofits, and sustainable aquaculture projects that create skilled local jobs while advancing climate resilience.

resources.name: HomeWarming
resources.organization: Clean Foundation (in partnership with Efficiency Nova Scotia and Nova Scotia Power)
resources.description: HomeWarming provides no-cost home energy assessments and efficiency upgrades (such as insulation, air sealing, and heat pumps where appropriate) to income-qualified Nova Scotians. The program hires local, certified contractors to complete retrofits, creating skilled trades jobs across the province while lowering energy bills and emissions to improve climate resilience for vulnerable households.

resources.name: Efficiency Nova Scotia — Home Energy Assessment
resources.description: This program delivers comprehensive home energy audits, personalized upgrade roadmaps, and rebates for efficiency retrofits, engaging a province-wide network of contractors and energy advisors. By accelerating building upgrades and electrification-ready measures, it cuts energy costs and emissions while supporting sustained, high-quality employment in Nova Scotia’s clean energy trades.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: Solar City Program (Halifax Regional Municipality)
resources.description: Solar City offers property-assessed clean energy (PACE) financing and support for installing solar photovoltaic and solar hot water systems on homes and businesses in HRM. By enabling community-led renewable energy projects delivered by local installers, the program drives skilled green jobs and increases local energy resilience.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: Start-Up Yard is an ocean-tech incubation and acceleration program providing workspace, prototyping and testing facilities, mentorship, and market access for companies developing solutions in sustainable aquaculture, marine monitoring, and low-carbon marine operations. It strengthens Nova Scotia’s blue economy by growing export-ready firms and creating skilled local jobs in climate-resilient ocean industries.

resources.name: Acadian Seaplants – Sustainable Seaweed Aquaculture
resources.description: Acadian Seaplants operates seaweed cultivation and processing facilities using science-based, environmentally responsible practices that support sustainable aquaculture growth. The company provides year-round skilled employment in rural and coastal communities, contributing to Nova Scotia’s blue economy while supplying low-impact marine biomass that supports climate resilience and circular bioeconomy markets.

solutions.text: Entrepreneurship Mentorship and Peer Networks: Establish peer-led networks and mentorship circles for early-stage entrepreneurs offering peer learning, shared problem solving, and connections to customers and funders.

resources.name: Volta Residency Program
resources.description: Volta’s Residency Program places early-stage tech founders in a shared downtown hub where they participate in founder roundtables, peer-to-peer workshops, and community events that encourage shared problem-solving. Residents are matched with Entrepreneurs-in-Residence and volunteer mentors, and tap into a network of alumni and advisors for ongoing guidance. Volta also hosts investor office hours, pitch events, and corporate partner introductions that help founders connect with customers and funders.

resources.name: CEED Mastermind Program
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED’s Mastermind Program convenes small, peer-led circles of early-stage entrepreneurs who meet regularly to troubleshoot business challenges, exchange practical know-how, and hold each other accountable. Each group is facilitated by experienced CEED advisors and mentors who provide targeted coaching and connections to subject-matter experts. CEED complements the circles with networking and showcase events that link participants to lenders, grant programs, and potential customers across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic (Entrepreneurship Hub)
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic operates innovation hubs that host recurring founder meetups, peer labs, and themed working groups where early-stage entrepreneurs collaborate and solve problems together. Through its mentor network and Entrepreneurs-in-Residence, IGNITE provides one-on-one and group mentorship and facilitates introductions to industry partners, buyers, and funding programs. Regular pitch nights, demo days, and investor-readiness sessions connect founders to customers and funders while keeping them rooted in their communities.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE is an ocean-technology incubator where cohorts of early-stage founders work side-by-side, share test facilities, and participate in peer learning through founder circles and technical roundtables. Each company is paired with Entrepreneurs-in-Residence and a roster of volunteer mentors who provide commercialization, engineering, and market-entry guidance. COVE’s industry consortium enables curated introductions to customers and funders through demo days, buyer forums, and partnerships with investors and public programs.

solutions.text: Cultural and Creative Sector Supports: Invest in festivals, artist residencies, makers markets, and workspace for artists and cultural entrepreneurs to grow creative industries that boost local screens, music, and tourism jobs.

resources.name: Craft LAIR (Local Artist In Residence) at the Centre for Craft Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Craft Nova Scotia / Centre for Craft Nova Scotia (Mary E. Black Gallery)
resources.description: Craft Nova Scotia’s Craft LAIR provides rotating residencies that give emerging and established craft artists dedicated studio/showcase space at the Mary E. Black Gallery and Centre for Craft. The program pairs workspace with public engagement and professional development, and the organization also produces juried craft markets that connect makers to buyers and tourists. Together, these supports help craft entrepreneurs grow sustainable businesses and jobs in Nova Scotia’s creative economy.
resources.address: 1061 Marginal Road, Suite 140, Halifax, NS B3H 4P7

resources.name: Ross Creek Artist-in-Residence Program
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: The Ross Creek Centre for the Arts hosts multidisciplinary artist residencies that provide studio space, accommodation, and community engagement opportunities in rural Nova Scotia. Residencies, workshops, and seasonal festivals on site support artists’ professional growth while drawing cultural tourists to the Annapolis Valley. This combination of workspace, programming, and audience development helps create and sustain creative-sector jobs across theatre, visual arts, and related services.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

resources.name: Artist-in-Residence (AIR) Program
resources.description: Lunenburg School of the Arts’ AIR program offers studio facilities, mentorship, and public engagement to selected artists in the UNESCO Old Town of Lunenburg. By providing workspace and community programming alongside public exhibitions and talks, the residency helps artists develop their practice and market presence. The program contributes to cultural tourism and local creative jobs by activating galleries, shops, and hospitality businesses around resident artists’ work.

resources.name: Studios, Residency, and Market Programs
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design operates public studios (textiles, clay, metal/jewellery, print, and more), a retail gallery, and creative residencies that attract visiting and local artists to make and sell work. Its exhibitions, training, and maker-focused markets connect artisans to customers and visitors year-round, strengthening the island’s craft and cultural tourism economy. These supports translate into sustainable self-employment and employment in production, retail, and cultural events.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op (Affordable Arts Workspace & Festival Hub)
resources.organization: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-operative Limited
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op provides affordable rehearsal and performance space for theatre, music, dance, and screen-related events, and serves as a key venue for festivals like Halifax Fringe and Mayworks. By offering accessible workspace and technical support, it enables artists and creative entrepreneurs to produce shows, earn income, and build audiences. This year-round venue activates the local creative economy by generating gigs for artists, technicians, and producers while drawing patrons to the neighbourhood.

solutions.text: Local Talent Retention Programs: Coordinate community-based incentives—mentorship, networking events, housing supports, and career pathways—for recent grads and returnees to make staying or coming back more attractive.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program links recent graduates and newcomers with established business and community leaders for targeted, one-on-one introductions that grow professional networks and uncover job opportunities. Through curated matches and regular networking events across priority sectors, it provides mentorship and clear career pathways that encourage young people and returnees to build their futures in Halifax and stay in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1104, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS pairs internationally trained professionals and recent graduates with local mentors in their fields to build networks, understand the Nova Scotia labour market, and receive job search support that accelerates career entry. As a settlement organization, ISANS also offers wraparound services such as housing search assistance, language and employment supports, and employer connections—reducing barriers and making it more attractive for newcomers and returnees to settle and work in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Volta Residency
resources.description: Volta Residency provides early-stage founders and tech talent with subsidized workspace, access to seasoned mentors and advisors, and frequent community events that connect them to investors and industry partners. By lowering startup costs and embedding recent grads in Nova Scotia’s innovation ecosystem, the program creates strong entrepreneurial and career pathways that help retain local talent.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Rural Innovation Hubs
resources.description: IGNITE operates rural innovation hubs that offer mentorship, coaching, and regular networking events connecting students, recent graduates, and returnees with local employers and entrepreneurs in communities like Pictou County and Yarmouth. Its programs help participants develop ventures and secure meaningful local roles—strengthening community ties and making it more appealing to stay or return to rural Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 38 Provost Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 2A3

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre (SMUEC) – Talent & Venture Programs
resources.description: SMUEC connects students and recent graduates with local employers through paid consulting projects, internships, and work-integrated learning, while also offering mentorship, startup coaching, and networking events (including through its RBC Talent Hub initiatives). These supports create concrete career and entrepreneurial pathways in Halifax, increasing the likelihood that young people build their futures in Nova Scotia.

obstacles.title: Housing affordability and supply constraints
obstacles.description: Rising rents and home prices, construction bottlenecks, and limited diverse housing options (including student and mid-market rentals) push young people to leave or avoid returning.

solutions.text: Community Land Trust (CLT): Establish a locally governed CLT to buy and hold land for permanently affordable ownership and rental housing, ensuring long-term affordability and community control over development priorities.

resources.name: Affordable Housing Land Disposition (Surplus Land for Affordable Housing)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality identifies surplus municipal parcels and makes them available to non-profit and co‑operative housing providers through long-term ground leases or transfers with affordability covenants. By retaining public ownership interests or registering perpetual affordability requirements on title, the program mirrors a community land trust approach—separating land from buildings to lock in long-term affordability and community oversight of development outcomes.

resources.name: Community-Owned Lands and Housing Development at AKOMA
resources.description: AKOMA stewards a large, historically Black community site in Dartmouth and partners with non-profit and public funders to build affordable and supportive housing on land held by the community. By keeping land in community ownership and leasing sites for housing with long-term affordability requirements, AKOMA implements the core CLT model—securing permanent affordability and ensuring that development reflects community priorities and governance.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership with Long-Term Affordability Controls
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia acquires land and constructs homes that are sold to qualifying families using ground leases, shared-equity/second-mortgage instruments, and resale restrictions that preserve affordability across owners. This structure separates land value from the home price and embeds lasting affordability conditions—functionally aligning with CLT principles to keep housing permanently affordable while ensuring community-focused stewardship of the asset.

solutions.text: Housing Co-operatives and Co-housing: Support creation of member-run co-ops and co-housing projects where residents share governance and costs, increasing affordable mid-market and student housing options while building social capital.

resources.name: Treehouse Village Ecohousing
resources.description: Treehouse Village Ecohousing is a resident-developed cohousing community in Bridgewater that uses shared governance and common facilities to reduce individual housing costs while fostering strong social connections. Homes are designed to be energy-efficient and mid-market, with a common house and shared amenities that lower per-household expenses and support intergenerational living. The project directly implements the co-housing model by organizing residents as a member-run community that plans, owns, and manages the property together.

resources.name: Housing Nova Scotia – Co-operative Housing Support
resources.organization: Housing Nova Scotia (Nova Scotia Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
resources.description: Housing Nova Scotia supports the creation and sustainability of member-run housing co-operatives by providing policy oversight, financing programs, and technical assistance that help new and existing co-ops plan, build, and maintain affordable homes. This work expands the supply of mid-market and affordable rental options, including opportunities suitable for students and young workers. By strengthening governance and long-term viability of co-ops, the program helps communities self-organize stable, community-led housing.

resources.name: International Centre for Co-operative Management (Co-operative Management Education)
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University, Sobey School of Business
resources.description: Based at Saint Mary’s University, this centre delivers graduate and executive programs tailored to co-operative and mutual leaders, including housing co-ops. Training in governance, finance, and member engagement equips Nova Scotia communities to start and effectively manage member-run housing co-operatives and co-housing projects. By building leadership capacity and sector-specific skills, it accelerates the creation and success of affordable, community-governed housing.

resources.name: Coady Institute – Co-operative Development and Community-Led Housing Support
resources.organization: Coady Institute, St. Francis Xavier University
resources.description: Coady Institute provides education, coaching, and applied research to communities across Nova Scotia to form and strengthen co-operatives, including member-run housing and co-housing initiatives. Through community-based development practice, Coady helps groups design participatory governance, financial plans, and member engagement processes needed to launch and sustain affordable co-operative housing. This support enables youth, students, and local residents to co-create mid-market housing with strong social capital.

solutions.text: Accessory Dwelling Units (ADU) Drive: Run community workshops, design guides, and a local permit-navigation service to help homeowners add legal basement suites, laneway houses, and granny flats that expand rental supply quickly and affordably.

resources.name: Secondary and Backyard Suites
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Secondary and Backyard Suites initiative legalizes and guides the creation of basement apartments and detached backyard suites on most residential lots. The Planning & Development team provides homeowner design guides, checklists, and sample drawings to streamline development and building permits. Staff offer pre-application consultations and counter service, and the municipality runs public information sessions when rules are updated—helping residents add legal ADUs quickly and affordably.

resources.name: Secondary and Garden Suites
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings enables accessory dwelling units—both attached secondary suites and detached garden suites—across urban and rural areas through its Land Use By-law. The municipality publishes step-by-step homeowner guides, application checklists, and site plan templates, and Development Officers provide one-on-one permit navigation to review designs and code requirements. Open houses and Q&A sessions during policy updates help residents understand how to create legal ADUs that expand the local rental supply.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Secondary Suites and Garden Suites
resources.description: The Town of Wolfville’s program permits secondary suites within existing homes and detached garden suites to increase gentle-density rental options. Planning staff provide a homeowner how-to and permit checklist, and they meet with applicants to navigate zoning, heritage, servicing, and building code steps. Through public workshops and engagement tied to housing policy updates, the Town equips residents to design and permit legal ADUs that serve students, young workers, and families.

resources.name: Backyard and Secondary Suites
resources.description: The Town of Lunenburg allows accessory apartments and detached backyard suites with design guidance that respects the town’s heritage context. The Town provides application forms, checklists, and siting/design guidance, while Development Services staff offer pre-application reviews and permit-navigation support for homeowners. Community information meetings during by-law updates help residents understand how to build compliant, long-term rental ADUs that add to the local housing supply.

solutions.text: Adaptive Reuse of Vacant Buildings: Organize local inventories and partnerships to convert underused commercial, institutional, and industrial spaces into student and mid-market rental units, with community-led feasibility studies and fundraising.

resources.name: Public Lands and Assets for Housing (Adaptive Reuse and Redevelopment)
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia inventories surplus and underused public assets and leads partnerships to convert them into housing, including the adaptive reuse of existing buildings. Through calls for proposals and pre-development support, they work with municipalities, post-secondary institutions, non-profits, and private developers to transform vacant or underutilized commercial and institutional properties into mixed-income and student-oriented rentals, backed by feasibility work and capital stack assembly.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: HRM Affordable Housing Initiatives and Rapid Housing Conversions
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality identifies underused municipal and privately owned sites suitable for housing and supports partners to convert non-residential buildings (e.g., hotels, offices, and institutional spaces) into rental housing through land contributions, expedited approvals, and coordination of federal/provincial funding. These initiatives organize local inventories, enable community-led feasibility studies, and help finance adaptive reuse projects that expand affordable and mid-market rental supply, including options benefitting students.

resources.name: AKOMA Community Development – Former NS Home for Colored Children Redevelopment
resources.description: AKOMA is leading a community-driven redevelopment of the former Nova Scotia Home for Colored Children campus, which includes the adaptive reuse of existing cottages and institutional buildings into affordable and mid-market rental units. The project advances housing supply through partnerships with government and community organizations, detailed feasibility and planning, and active fundraising to deliver culturally grounded, mixed-income housing options.

resources.name: YWCA Halifax Affordable Housing and Space Conversion
resources.description: YWCA Halifax has converted an existing commercial/office property into safe, affordable rental homes for women and families alongside program space, demonstrating adaptive reuse that brings new housing online faster than new construction. The organization leverages community fundraising, partnerships, and public funding to complete feasibility, design, and renovation, adding mid-market and deeply affordable units in a mixed-use building.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: New Dawn Properties – Adaptive Reuse and Mixed-Income Rentals
resources.description: New Dawn repurposes vacant and underused buildings in Sydney and surrounding communities into rental housing and community-serving spaces, emphasizing mixed-income affordability. Their development approach includes community-led feasibility studies, capital fundraising, and partnerships with local institutions and employers to meet demand for student and mid-market rentals while preserving and adapting existing commercial and institutional assets.

solutions.text: Modular and Prefab Community Builds: Partner with community colleges, local builders, and trades programs to deliver modular or prefabricated housing projects that reduce construction time and costs while providing training and local jobs.

resources.name: Modular Supportive Housing Initiative
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia leads delivery of modular supportive housing sites in partnership with the Province and community housing operators, using prefabricated units to rapidly add safe, dignified homes. The initiative reduces construction time and costs by manufacturing units offsite and assembling them quickly, while engaging local contractors and apprentices for site work, utility connections, and finishing—creating training opportunities and local jobs.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: NSCC Kingstec Tiny Home Project
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Kingstec Campus
resources.description: Through this ongoing community-build initiative, NSCC Kingstec carpentry and related trades students design and construct transportable tiny homes and modular units in partnership with local non-profits and municipalities. The homes are prefabricated in campus shops to shorten build schedules and lower costs, then delivered and installed with support from local builders—providing hands-on training for students and creating jobs for local trades.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia Panelized Build Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia accelerates affordable home construction using panelized and prefabricated building methods, assembling wall systems and components offsite for faster onsite builds. The affiliate partners with NSCC trades programs and local contractors for volunteer and student build days, creating practical training opportunities and local employment while reducing total project time and costs.

resources.name: CBU Modular Student Housing Project
resources.description: Cape Breton University is expanding student residence capacity using modular construction to address housing shortages quickly and cost-effectively. Prefabricated units are manufactured offsite and installed on campus with local trades handling foundations, utilities, and finishing—supporting local jobs while easing pressure on the regional rental market for young people.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

solutions.text: Shared-Equity and Down-Payment Assistance Pools: Create a community-backed shared-equity fund or revolving down-payment assistance that helps young buyers access homes while preserving affordability through resale restrictions or equity-sharing agreements.

resources.name: Down Payment Assistance Program (DPAP)
resources.organization: Housing Nova Scotia (Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
resources.description: The Province of Nova Scotia’s DPAP provides interest-free, repayable loans to eligible first-time homebuyers to cover a portion of their down payment. Because loans are repaid over time and recirculated, the program functions as a revolving down-payment assistance pool that expands access to ownership for moderate-income buyers and helps preserve affordability through purchase price and income limits.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia builds and sells homes to partner families using an affordable, geared-to-income mortgage paired with a deferred/secondary mortgage that captures the difference between market value and the affordable price. This shared-equity approach and resale restrictions (such as right of first refusal and equity-sharing on sale) help families access homeownership now while preserving long-term affordability and recycling value back into the program for future homeowners.

solutions.text: Mid-Market Rental Co-investment: Form local investment consortia (municipalities, employers, credit unions, non-profits) to develop mid-market rental buildings targeted at young professionals and students, with community oversight to set rents and tenancy priorities.

resources.name: NSCC Student Housing Initiative
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College is delivering new and expanded student residences on multiple campuses, co-funded with the Province and local partners to offer quality, mid‑market rental options for students. As a community‑governed public institution, NSCC provides oversight of rents and allocates spaces based on student need, easing pressure on local markets and aligning with a co‑investment model that targets young people.

resources.name: Affordable Housing Grant Program
resources.description: HRM’s capital grant program funds non‑profit and co‑operative developers to build or preserve affordable and mid‑market rental housing, explicitly encouraging projects that stack municipal funds with provincial, federal (e.g., CMHC), philanthropic, and private/social finance. Funded projects enter agreements that maintain community oversight of affordability targets, rents, and tenant selection priorities—supporting consortium‑style development geared to workers, young professionals, and students.

resources.name: New Dawn Rental Housing
resources.description: New Dawn develops, owns, and manages mixed‑income rental apartments in Cape Breton using blended financing from public programs and community investors, creating stable mid‑market options for local workers and students. As a community‑controlled non‑profit with a local board, New Dawn provides oversight on rents and tenancy priorities to meet regional workforce and youth housing needs, embodying the co‑investment and governance features of the solution.

resources.name: Wije’winen Housing (within the Wije’winen Centre)
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Wije’winen development in Halifax includes a significant number of affordable and mid‑market rental units integrated with cultural, health, and employment services, financed through multi‑partner contributions (municipal, provincial, federal, and philanthropic/social finance). Indigenous‑led community governance ensures transparent oversight of rents and tenant priorities—such as Indigenous youth, students, and early‑career workers—directly aligning with a co‑investment, community‑guided rental model.

solutions.text: Trades Apprenticeship Housing Projects: Link construction of affordable units to apprenticeship and skills-training programs, letting local youth gain experience while building housing for their peers and community members.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia Build Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia builds affordable homes across the province and actively partners with trades-training providers to staff build sites with students and apprentices under licensed supervision. Through collaborations with NSCC campuses, high school skilled-trades programs, and union training centers, youth gain practical experience and apprenticeship hours while constructing real, entry-cost homes for local families—directly linking skills development to increased affordable housing supply.

resources.name: Carpentry - Certificate
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Pictou Campus
resources.description: NSCC’s Carpentry Certificate program at the Pictou Campus integrates community build projects with Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia and local contractors, where students help construct complete homes or major building modules. Learners earn supervised practical experience and apprenticeship hours on real affordable housing builds, directly connecting hands-on skills training with the delivery of new, modest-cost homes in the community.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY places Grade 10–12 students in paid summer work terms with residential construction employers and community builders, giving youth on-site experience toward apprenticeship pathways. Many host employers work on new home construction and community projects, including builds undertaken by non-profit housing providers such as Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia, thereby pairing early trades training with the creation of additional affordable and mid-market housing supply.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0A9

solutions.text: Tenant Support and Stabilization Services: Provide community-run tenant information, mediation, legal clinics, and rent-banking to prevent evictions, stabilize households, and make renting safer and more attractive for young people.

resources.name: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service – Tenants’ Rights and Advocacy
resources.organization: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service (Dalhousie University Schulich School of Law)
resources.description: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service provides free legal representation, summary advice, and community legal education to low‑income tenants on issues such as evictions, repairs, illegal rent increases, and security deposits. The clinic helps stabilize households by negotiating with landlords, mediating disputes, and representing tenants at Residential Tenancies hearings—directly preventing evictions and making renting safer for young people.

resources.name: Housing and Tenant Support for Newcomers
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS offers tenant information workshops and one‑on‑one support to help newcomers understand leases, tenant rights and responsibilities, and Nova Scotia’s Residential Tenancies processes. Settlement counselors assist with landlord communication and early mediation, connect clients to legal help when needed, and support applications for benefits and rent supplements—preventing evictions and improving rental stability for young adults and families new to the province.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Housing Support and Tenancy Sustainment
resources.description: Welcome Housing & Support Services provides eviction‑prevention and tenancy‑sustainment assistance, including landlord mediation, tenant education, budgeting support, and navigation of benefits like rent supplements. Staff help tenants address arrears by connecting them to emergency financial aid through community partners and negotiating realistic repayment plans—reducing displacement and keeping renting viable for youth and other low‑income renters.

resources.name: Youth Housing Support and Rehousing Program
resources.organization: Pictou County Roots for Youth Society
resources.description: Roots for Youth helps young people secure and keep safe rentals through tenant education, housing navigation, and landlord mediation. The program works to prevent evictions by helping with budgeting, lease understanding, and access to emergency assistance for rent or utilities through local partners, stabilizing youth tenancies and making renting more achievable for those starting out.
resources.address: 603 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3S7

solutions.text: Vacant-Home Renovation Volunteer Program: Coordinate volunteers, trades apprentices, and local contractors to renovate abandoned or vacant homes for affordable rental or ownership, reducing blight and increasing supply.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia – Build Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia mobilizes community volunteers, construction apprentices, and local contractors to build and, when suitable properties are acquired, rehabilitate existing or long-vacant houses into safe, affordable homes for qualifying families. Volunteers work alongside journeypersons and apprentices on site, reducing project costs and returning neglected properties to productive use as affordable homeownership units, directly increasing housing supply and reducing neighborhood blight.
resources.address: 81 Wright Avenue, Unit 12, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1H4

resources.name: Build Right Nova Scotia – Habitat for Humanity Volunteer Build Days
resources.organization: Build Right Nova Scotia (Nova Scotia Building Trades / NS Construction Labour Relations Association)
resources.description: Build Right Nova Scotia coordinates union tradespeople and apprentices from member locals to volunteer on Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia build and rehab projects across the province. By supplying skilled volunteer labour and mentoring apprentices on-site, they help renovate existing dwellings when Habitat acquires properties needing repair, accelerating the turnaround of vacant or deteriorated houses into affordable homes.
resources.address: 100 Ilsley Avenue, Unit N, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1L3

resources.name: NSCC Service Learning Construction Projects (Carpentry and Trades)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Ivany Campus
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College integrates real-world service learning into its carpentry and construction trades programs by partnering with community housing nonprofits (including Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia) on renovation and retrofit projects. Under instructor supervision and alongside local contractors and volunteers, students help bring older or previously vacant homes up to code for affordable rental or ownership, adding supply while earning practical hours toward apprenticeship pathways.

solutions.text: Local Zoning and Policy Advocacy Collective: Form resident-led working groups to advocate for zoning reforms (allowing gentle density, duplexes, triplexes, and ADUs), faster approvals, and inclusionary policies that support diverse housing types.

resources.name: Our HRM Alliance
resources.description: The Our HRM Alliance is a resident- and community-organization coalition convened by the Ecology Action Centre that advocates for compact growth and inclusive, complete communities in Halifax Regional Municipality. It organizes resident working groups, policy campaigns, and submissions to Council to advance zoning reforms that allow gentle density (e.g., duplexes, triplexes, and ADUs), enable inclusionary tools, and create faster, more predictable approvals under the Centre Plan and subsequent bylaw updates.

resources.name: Municipal Affairs Committee (Housing & Development Advocacy)
resources.description: The Halifax Chamber’s Municipal Affairs Committee convenes local residents, small businesses, and industry stakeholders to shape and advocate for policies that speed up permitting and enable as-of-right gentle density, ADUs, and missing-middle housing in HRM. Through position papers, deputations, and regular meetings with municipal and provincial decision-makers, the committee advances inclusionary and pro-housing zoning policies that broaden the mix of attainable homes.
resources.address: 32 Akerley Boulevard, Suite 100, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1N1

resources.name: Housing for All Cape Breton
resources.description: Housing for All Cape Breton is a New Dawn–led initiative that brings residents, community groups, and builders together in working sessions and public forums to push for municipal land-use changes in CBRM that allow gentle density (duplexes, triplexes, and ADUs) and streamline approvals. The coalition prepares recommendations and submissions to Council and planning staff and mobilizes citizen voices to support inclusionary and diverse-housing policies across serviced neighbourhoods.

resources.name: Wolfville Planning Advisory Committee (Housing & Land Use)
resources.description: The Town of Wolfville’s citizen-appointed Planning Advisory Committee functions as a resident-led working group that reviews and recommends zoning and land-use bylaw changes, including town-wide permissions for secondary/garden suites (ADUs), expanded two-unit zones, and reduced barriers to missing-middle infill. By advising Council and leading public consultations, the PAC helps accelerate approvals and embed inclusionary, pro-density policies that expand housing options for students and mid-market renters.

solutions.text: Employer-Assisted Housing Partnerships: Encourage large local employers (universities, hospitals, employers) to pool land or funding to create rental units or offer rental subsidies/guarantees for early-career staff and students.

resources.name: Staff Accommodation Program
resources.description: Cabot Cape Breton develops and operates dedicated on-site and nearby staff accommodations to house seasonal and early‑career employees at subsidized rates. By directly supplying rental units and master‑leasing additional rooms as needed, the employer reduces pressure on the local market and ensures new hires can accept roles despite housing shortages—an employer-assisted approach aligned with the proposed solution.
resources.address: 19 Broad Cove Road, Inverness, NS B0E 1N0

resources.name: Employee Housing
resources.description: Fox Harb’r Resort provides purpose-built and employer-managed housing for staff, including seasonal and early‑career workers, offering affordable, convenient accommodations tied to employment. This employer-assisted model lowers living costs and commuting barriers, functioning like a rental subsidy/guarantee by reserving units for employees and stabilizing workforce recruitment and retention in a tight housing market.
resources.address: 1337 Fox Harbour Road, Fox Harbour, NS B0K 1Y0

resources.name: Staff Housing Program
resources.description: White Point Beach Resort operates employer-provided staff housing for team members, including students and early‑career hires in hospitality roles. By setting aside rental units and coordinating affordable accommodations during peak seasons, the resort directly addresses local housing constraints and provides a practical employer-assisted pathway that enables young workers to live close to work.
resources.address: 75 White Point Beach Resort Road, White Point, NS B0T 1G0

resources.name: Staff Accommodation
resources.description: Keltic Lodge at the Highlands offers employer-managed housing for its workforce, including co‑op students and early‑career hospitality professionals. The lodge sets aside rooms and residences for employees, effectively creating dedicated rental supply and reducing living-cost barriers so new recruits can accept placements within Cape Breton Highlands National Park.
resources.address: 383 Keltic In Road, Ingonish Beach, NS B0C 1L0

resources.name: Medical Learners & Recruitment Housing
resources.organization: Health Services Foundation of the South Shore
resources.description: The Health Services Foundation of the South Shore supports and coordinates dedicated housing for medical learners (students and residents) and newly recruited clinical staff in partnership with Nova Scotia Health. By funding and reserving furnished rental units near South Shore Regional Hospital at below‑market or cost-recovery rates, the program functions as employer-assisted housing that lowers entry barriers for early‑career clinicians and helps stabilize local care teams.
resources.address: 90 Glen Allan Drive, Bridgewater, NS B4V 3S6

solutions.text: Micro-mortgage and Community Loan Programs: Work with local credit unions to offer small, flexible mortgages, shared-equity loans, or guarantee schemes tailored to young buyers and renters, lowering barriers to entry into local housing markets.

resources.name: Down Payment Assistance Program (DPAP)
resources.organization: Housing Nova Scotia (Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
resources.description: DPAP provides interest-free, repayable loans to eligible first-time homebuyers to cover a portion of the required down payment, directly reducing one of the biggest barriers to entering the housing market. By pairing with insured mortgages offered by local credit unions and other lenders, the program functions as a community-backed loan/guarantee mechanism that makes small, flexible mortgages viable for younger and moderate-income buyers in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia offers an affordable homeownership pathway using a community-backed, zero-interest (or geared-to-income) mortgage model and shared-equity/second-mortgage structures. This lowers upfront costs and monthly payments for qualifying families, effectively operating as a micro-mortgage/community loan approach that removes traditional credit and down payment barriers for young and moderate-income households.

resources.name: First Home Mortgage
resources.organization: Community Credit Union of Cumberland Colchester
resources.description: Community Credit Union of Cumberland Colchester provides flexible first-time homebuyer mortgages, including small-dollar loans suitable for modest properties and the option to use mortgage insurance for low down payments. As a local credit union, it works with members to tailor terms, and can pair mortgages with programs like DPAP or federal shared-equity incentives, reducing barriers for younger buyers entering Nova Scotia’s housing market.

resources.name: First-Time Homebuyers Mortgage
resources.description: Sydney Credit Union offers mortgages geared to first-time buyers, enabling small, flexible loans with low down-payment options through mortgage insurance and personalized underwriting. The credit union can combine its lending with programs like the provincial Down Payment Assistance Program or the federal shared-equity incentive to reduce upfront and monthly costs, helping young households access homeownership in Cape Breton and surrounding communities.

solutions.text: Neighborhood Infill Design Charrettes: Host community design sessions to identify context-sensitive 'missing middle' infill opportunities and co-create plans that increase density in ways that local residents support and maintain neighborhood character.

resources.name: Shape Your City Halifax – Centre Plan Public Engagement
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Centre Plan used hands-on community design workshops and charrette-style sessions to co-create built-form rules that enable gentle, context-sensitive infill (e.g., townhouses, triplexes, backyard/secondary suites) in established neighbourhoods and along transit corridors. Residents collaborated with planners to map suitable sites, test building transitions, and refine design guidelines so added density fits heritage streetscapes and local character. This collaborative process directly supports ‘missing middle’ housing to expand supply and affordability with strong neighbourhood buy-in.

resources.name: Plan New Minas – Community Design Charrette and Secondary Plan
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings led an intensive, multi-day design charrette for the New Minas Growth Centre to co-design mixed-use, ‘missing middle’ infill along Commercial Street and adjacent neighbourhoods. Participants worked with planners to visualize building types, heights, and transitions, and to identify infill opportunities that add housing while respecting existing character. The resulting Secondary Planning Strategy and land-use bylaw updates open new pathways for context-sensitive density, helping address housing supply and affordability.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Future Lunenburg – Community Design Workshops
resources.description: Future Lunenburg is the Town’s comprehensive planning and bylaw modernization initiative that employed public design workshops and charrette-style exercises to identify gentle infill opportunities compatible with the community’s UNESCO-designated heritage fabric. Residents helped test ‘missing middle’ housing options—such as accessory suites, duplexes, and courtyard homes—and co-develop design guidelines to ensure new density complements historic streetscapes. The adopted policies expand diverse housing choices with community support, advancing affordability while safeguarding neighbourhood character.

solutions.text: Housing Matching and Resource Platform: Develop a community-run online platform that matches students, young workers, and landlords for shared rentals, lists affordable units, coordinates sublets, and shares information on tenant rights and supports.

resources.name: Off-Campus Living
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Off-Campus Living program hosts an online housing hub (via Places4Students) where landlords list rooms, apartments, and shared rentals, and students can filter by price, location, and amenities. The platform supports sublet postings and provides guidance on tenant rights, budgeting, and community supports, helping match students and young renters with affordable housing options.

resources.name: Off-Campus Housing
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University operates an off-campus housing portal (powered by Places4Students) that connects students with local landlords offering rooms, apartments, and shared accommodations, including short-term and sublet listings. The site aggregates rental resources and links to Nova Scotia tenant-rights information and support services, functioning as a matchmaking and information platform for affordable options.

resources.name: Housing Services – Off-Campus Listings
resources.description: NSCC’s Housing Services page centralizes off-campus listings through a partner platform (e.g., Places4Students) where landlords can post units and students can search for affordable rentals and shared accommodations. It also provides links to tenant-rights information, local housing supports, and practical guidance, enabling matching, sublet coordination, and informed renting for learners across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Off-Campus Housing
resources.description: Mount Saint Vincent University offers an online off-campus housing resource (linked with Places4Students) that lets landlords advertise rooms, apartments, and shared rentals, and enables students to search by budget, proximity, and amenities. The resource includes sublet listings and directs users to tenant-rights information and community supports, helping young renters secure safe, affordable housing.

obstacles.title: Skills mismatch and weak work-integrated learning
obstacles.description: Training and post-secondary programs do not always align with employer needs; insufficient co-ops, apprenticeships, and applied learning reduce job readiness and retention.

solutions.text: Community-Employer Cooperative Placements: Local businesses, non-profits and municipal programs partner with high schools and colleges to create paid short-term co-op placements focused on community projects (parks, digitization, events). The community helps recruit hosts, subsidizes wages through a pooled fund, and promotes placements to students to increase accessible, locally-relevant work experience.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship Program (CLSI)
resources.description: CLSI places high school, NSCC, and university students in 9–15 week paid internships with municipalities, Mi’kmaq communities, non-profits, and local businesses to deliver community-focused environmental projects (e.g., park stewardship, coastal cleanups, waste audits, community events). Clean Foundation recruits and supports host organizations, administers wage subsidies through a pooled funding model backed by government and partners, and promotes placements to students across Nova Scotia—creating accessible, locally relevant work experience aligned with community needs.

resources.name: Co-operative Education Incentive (CEI)
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia — Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: CEI provides wage subsidies to Nova Scotia employers—including small businesses, municipalities, and non-profits—to hire post-secondary co-op students for short-term, paid work terms that build practical skills. By offsetting wages and coordinating with campus co-op offices, CEI helps create more placements tied to local priorities (such as community events, digitization projects, and public service initiatives) while improving alignment between training and employer needs.

resources.name: Halifax Municipal Archives – Young Canada Works Internships
resources.description: The Halifax Municipal Archives regularly hosts paid student interns—funded through Young Canada Works and other wage-subsidy programs—to digitize, describe, and make accessible municipal records that support community history and civic engagement. The Archives partners with local colleges and universities to recruit students and structure short-term placements that deliver tangible community outcomes (e.g., digitization and public exhibits), directly aligning learning with municipal and community needs.
resources.address: 81 Ilsley Avenue, Unit 11, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1L5

resources.name: Management Career Services Co-op Program
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Management Career Services coordinates paid co-op and internship terms with local businesses, non-profits, and municipal departments in areas like event management, data/digitization, marketing, and public administration. The office promotes opportunities to students, supports employer recruitment, and helps organizations access wage subsidies (e.g., CEI and federal SWPP), thereby expanding short-term, community-relevant placements that strengthen job readiness and align skills with employer needs.
resources.address: 6100 University Avenue, Suite 2100, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

solutions.text: Sector Advisory Councils: Form neighborhood or regional advisory councils of employers, educators, and community reps (health, fisheries, tech, creative industries) that meet quarterly to align curricula, identify in-demand skills, and design local internships or micro-apprenticeships tailored to Nova Scotia’s labour needs.

resources.name: NSCC Program Advisory Committees
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) maintains employer-led Program Advisory Committees for each program area that bring together industry, educators, and community representatives to review curricula and emerging skill needs. These councils meet regularly to align coursework with Nova Scotia’s labour market, from health and fisheries to tech, trades, and creative industries. Through these partnerships, NSCC co-designs co-ops, internships, and micro-credentials to improve job readiness and local retention.

resources.name: Student-to-Sea Program
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE’s Student-to-Sea program convenes ocean-technology employers, post-secondary institutions, and students to identify in-demand skills and shape experiential learning in Nova Scotia’s blue economy. Industry partners advise on competencies and help refine curricula while co-designing paid internships, co-ops, and short work placements with COVE and schools. This sector-backed approach ensures students gain practical, locally relevant experience aligned with employer needs.

resources.name: OTCNS Workforce and Skills Initiatives
resources.organization: Ocean Technology Council of Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Ocean Technology Council of Nova Scotia (OTCNS) is an employer-led sector council that works with NSCC, Dalhousie, and training providers to align curricula with ocean-tech workforce needs. Through industry advisory roundtables, working groups, and events, OTCNS surfaces in-demand skills and feeds them back to educators while brokering student internships and project-based placements with member companies. This coordinated, sector-level mechanism improves work-integrated learning and job readiness across Nova Scotia’s ocean industries.

solutions.text: Community Micro-Credential Programs: Libraries, community centres and colleges co-develop short, stackable micro-credential courses (e.g., basic coding, boat handling, hospitality customer service) that respond to employer-identified gaps and are publicly promoted by local chambers and community groups.

resources.name: NSCC MicroCredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College delivers short, stackable micro-credential courses co-designed with local employers and sector councils to close specific skill gaps in areas such as basic coding, ocean/marine operations, hospitality service, construction, and healthcare. Learners earn digital badges that can stack toward further credentials, and offerings are delivered both on campus and at community locations, aligning training with job-ready competencies and supporting work-integrated learning promoted through employer and community networks.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Microcredentials (Open Learning & Career Development)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University — Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Open Learning & Career Development unit offers employer-validated, stackable micro-credentials in high-demand fields such as coding, data analytics, project management, and sustainability. Programs are co-developed with industry and community partners, issued as portable digital badges, and often build into further study, directly addressing employer-identified gaps and enhancing applied, work-integrated learning pathways for Nova Scotia’s workforce.

solutions.text: Local Apprenticeship Sponsorships: Municipalities, chambers, and regional development agencies create incentive packages (wage top-ups, tool grants, housing stipends) to encourage small and medium enterprises to take on apprentices in trades and emerging sectors, reducing employer risk and improving retention.

resources.name: Apprenticeship Services (Cape Breton Partnership)
resources.description: The Cape Breton Partnership delivers the federally funded Apprenticeship Service that provides cash incentives to small and medium-sized employers to hire and retain first-year apprentices in Red Seal trades, with higher supports for equity-deserving apprentices. By offsetting wages and offering hands-on support to set up high-quality apprentice placements with local SMEs, the program lowers employer risk and strengthens retention—directly implementing the solution’s wage top-ups and employer sponsorship approach.

resources.name: Apprenticeship Employer Incentives & Apprentice Award Trust
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency offers employer-focused incentives (e.g., START wage subsidies delivered through Nova Scotia Works) to encourage SMEs to register and train apprentices, and manages financial supports that reduce costs tied to apprenticeship. Through the Apprentice Award Trust and other supports, apprentices can receive help with tools and required equipment, and the Agency provides travel and accommodation assistance for technical training—advancing the solution by bundling wage top-ups and tool supports to boost job readiness and retention.

resources.name: START Program (Employer Wage Incentive for Apprentices)
resources.description: Delivered locally by Nova Scotia Works centres, the START program provides wage subsidies and training supports to employers who hire and develop apprentices in trades, helping SMEs create permanent, full-time apprenticeships. These customized incentive packages can include wage top-ups and funds for essential gear or training, directly reducing employer risk and aligning on-the-job learning with local industry needs.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

resources.name: Apprenticeship Services (Marine Trades)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Boatbuilders Association supports employers in the marine trades to sponsor apprentices and access Apprenticeship Service incentives that offset wages for first-year apprentices, with enhanced supports for equity-deserving groups. By pairing cash incentives with employer coaching on onboarding and training plans, the initiative helps SMEs de-risk apprenticeship hiring and improves completion and retention in niche and emerging marine sectors.

solutions.text: Community Mentorship & Retiree Networks: Establish volunteer mentorship programs that connect experienced retirees and industry professionals with youth and new workers for structured job shadowing, coaching and skill-transfer sessions hosted at community centres or virtually.

resources.name: Halifax Partnership Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program links recent graduates, immigrants, and early-career job seekers with established local professionals who volunteer as 'Connectors' for structured one-on-one meetings and warm introductions. Through scheduled conversations, informational interviews, and networking (in person at community locations or virtually), participants receive coaching, labour-market insights, and referrals that often lead to workplace visits or short job-shadow experiences—helping align skills with employer needs and improving job readiness.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS matches newcomer and early-career professionals with experienced local mentors—often including retirees—for 3–6 month mentorships focused on Canadian workplace practices, sector expectations, and career navigation. Mentors provide coaching, skills-transfer guidance, and facilitated networking; many pairs arrange workplace visits or short job-shadowing, with meetings hosted at community sites or online to directly improve job readiness and alignment with employer needs.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic
resources.description: IGNITE operates community innovation hubs that connect youth and new founders with a volunteer network of industry mentors, including retired experts, for regular coaching, skills workshops, and project-based learning. Mentoring happens on-site at the hubs or virtually, giving participants hands-on, job-shadow-style exposure to real work environments and direct skills transfer that bridges training with current employer and industry needs.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs is a university innovation sandbox that pairs students and early-career technologists with volunteer mentors from the ICT sector for structured coaching, code reviews, career advising, and industry-led sessions.
