Activities are hosted in the lab space or virtually, enabling practical skills transfer, portfolio-building, and connections that can lead to workplace visits, job shadowing, co-ops, or entry-level roles—strengthening alignment between learning and employer needs.
resources.address: 6050 University Avenue, Room 426, Halifax, NS B3H 1W5

solutions.text: School-to-Work 'Try-It' Days: Coordinate monthly job-shadow and hands-on trade/industry days where local employers open workplaces to students and job seekers for short, low-commitment experiences that build awareness and realistic expectations about local careers.

resources.name: Workplace Tours & Job Shadow Days
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS coordinates recurring employer-led workplace tours and short job-shadow opportunities that let newcomers and young job seekers experience local occupations first-hand. These low-commitment, hands-on visits help participants understand day-to-day roles, workplace culture, and skill requirements, directly addressing skills mismatch by aligning expectations and building job readiness.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Try-A-Trade Mobile Construction Experience
resources.description: NSCSC’s mobile Try-A-Trade program brings hands-on trade stations and employer partners to communities and coordinates site tours with local contractors and fabrication shops. By letting students and job seekers try tools, meet tradespeople, and observe real workplaces, the initiative provides short, practical exposures that build awareness of construction careers and align training interests with industry needs.
resources.address: 2695 Dutch Village Road, Suite 205, Halifax, NS B3L 4G8

resources.name: CANS Construction Career Expo (Try-A-Trade)
resources.description: CANS hosts a large hands-on career expo and related employer-led demonstrations where participants can try trade tasks, speak with contractors, and explore apprenticeship pathways. The events function as “try-it” industry days that simulate job-shadow experiences, helping youth and job seekers form realistic expectations about construction careers and connect directly with hiring employers.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

resources.name: Options and Opportunities (O2) Program
resources.description: O2 integrates regular workplace visits, short job-shadow days, and community-based learning with local employers across trades, technology, and service sectors. These experiential opportunities give high school students hands-on exposure to real job sites and expectations, improving alignment between classroom learning and employer needs and strengthening pathways to co-ops, apprenticeships, and entry-level roles.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

solutions.text: Community Makerspaces & Simulation Labs: Fund and host local makerspaces or pop-up simulation labs (e.g., hospitality setups, marine tech benches, multimedia studios) where students and local jobseekers can practice applied skills in partnership with employers who help design real-world tasks.

resources.name: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship)
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE operates shared prototyping labs, electronics benches, and marine test facilities on the Dartmouth waterfront where students and jobseekers gain hands-on experience with ocean technologies. Employers co-located at COVE co-design real project tasks, offer internships, and run challenge-based learning that mirrors real maritime operations, directly addressing skills alignment and work-integrated learning.

resources.name: Emera ideaHUB
resources.description: The Emera ideaHUB is Dalhousie’s hardware incubation and prototyping facility that provides machine shop access, electronics benches, and fabrication labs for students and startup teams. Industry mentors and employer partners co-develop real product challenges and support capstone/co-op projects, giving participants applied, work-ready skills aligned with local manufacturing and tech needs.

resources.name: Fresh Twenty One (NSCC Akerley Campus Training Restaurant)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Akerley Campus
resources.description: Fresh Twenty One is NSCC Akerley’s on-campus training restaurant and culinary/hospitality simulation lab where students run a full-service operation open to the public. Local employers collaborate on menus, service standards, and kitchen workflows, and recruit via co-ops and practicums—ensuring graduates practice real-world tasks that match hospitality industry needs.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – New Glasgow Innovation Hub & Makerspace
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic’s New Glasgow hub offers a community makerspace with 3D printers, electronics workstations, and multimedia tools that support prototyping and hands-on learning for youth, students, and jobseekers. Regional employers co-host challenges, workshops, and mentorship that translate local business needs into real build-and-test projects, improving job readiness and alignment with industry.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

solutions.text: Local Placement Matching Platform: Develop a simple community-run online platform or bulletin (managed by a chamber or community org) that matches students, recent graduates and adult learners with local co-ops, part-time roles, internships and project-based placements.

resources.name: COVE Careers (Ocean Sector Job Board)
resources.description: COVE maintains a sector-focused online careers board that aggregates internships, co-ops, early-career, and project-based roles across Nova Scotia’s ocean technology and marine industries. By curating local postings and facilitating connections between employers and students/recent graduates (often in collaboration with post-secondary partners), it functions as a community-run bulletin that matches talent to real placements and applied projects.

resources.name: Halifax Chamber of Commerce Job Board
resources.description: The Halifax Chamber operates a public job board where member employers list co-ops, internships, part-time roles, and project-based opportunities in the Halifax region. As a chamber-run community bulletin, it helps students, recent graduates, and adult learners discover local placements that build job readiness and align training with employer needs.
resources.address: 32 Akerley Boulevard, Unit 1, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1N1

resources.name: Volta Careers (Startup and Scaleup Job Board)
resources.description: Volta’s online careers page lists roles from resident startups and partner companies, including internships, co-ops, part-time, and project-based placements. By centralizing postings from the local innovation community, it provides a practical matching platform that connects students and new grads with hands-on work-integrated learning experiences in Nova Scotia’s tech ecosystem.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: ISANS Job Board
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS hosts a job board and employer connections that feature a range of local opportunities, including internships and work placements suited to newcomers, recent graduates, and adult learners. The platform, paired with staff facilitation and bridging programs, acts as a community-driven matching hub helping candidates connect with Nova Scotia employers for practical, job-ready experience.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Community-Funded Wage Subsidy Pool: Create a locally administered subsidy program (supported by municipal grants, foundations and business contributions) to top-up wages for placements in high-need sectors, lowering cost barriers for employers to host trainees.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship (CLSI)
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s CLSI program places youth and post-secondary students in paid environmental and clean-economy roles with municipalities, nonprofits, and businesses across Nova Scotia. The program provides wage subsidies that top up intern pay using a blend of public and private funding, lowering employer costs to host trainees in high-need sustainability and climate-related sectors and creating high-quality work-integrated learning opportunities.

resources.name: Work Start (Wage Subsidy Program)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Work Start program offers wage subsidies to Nova Scotia employers who hire immigrants and refugees for work-experience roles, helping align newcomer skills with local labour needs. By reimbursing a portion of wages for a defined placement, the program reduces cost barriers for employers to host trainees and facilitates work-integrated learning that supports retention in high-need sectors.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Co-operative Education Incentive (CEI)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: CEI provides wage subsidies to Nova Scotia employers to hire co-op students for work terms aligned with their academic programs, strengthening work-integrated learning. By covering a portion of student wages, the program reduces employer costs and expands the number of quality placements in high-need fields such as technology, business, and applied sciences.

resources.name: Graduate to Opportunity (GTO)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: GTO offers a two-year wage subsidy to Nova Scotia employers who hire recent post-secondary graduates into entry-level roles, with enhanced supports for underrepresented groups and rural placements. This top-up reduces the upfront cost of onboarding new talent and encourages employers to create career-launch positions in emerging and established sectors, improving school-to-work transitions.

resources.name: Apprenticeship START
resources.description: Apprenticeship START provides wage incentives to Nova Scotia employers that hire, register, and retain apprentices—especially in high-demand trades and underrepresented communities. By offsetting wages and related costs during the training period, the program lowers employer barriers to hosting trainees and expands hands-on learning pathways that align with labour market needs.

solutions.text: Employer-Led Curriculum Labs: Host short-term curriculum design sprints where clusters of local employers and instructors co-create modules, case studies and assessment tasks reflecting real local projects, then pilot them in community colleges and high schools.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding (Irving Shipbuilding Centre of Excellence)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding Inc.
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding brings Irving Shipbuilding engineers, trades supervisors, and NSCC instructors together to co-design program modules, shop assignments, and assessment rubrics aligned to real production work at the Halifax Shipyard. The employer-led curriculum is iterated through short design workshops before being delivered and refined with student cohorts at NSCC, improving job readiness and direct pathways to apprenticeships.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Nova Scotia Sandbox Program)
resources.organization: Faculty of Computer Science, Dalhousie University
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs runs rapid, employer-led design sprints and hackathons where local tech companies and Dalhousie instructors co-create challenge briefs, case studies, and marking rubrics that map to course outcomes in computer science and related programs. Faculty then pilot these employer-authored modules as graded assignments or capstones, ensuring students practice with problems, tools, and evaluation standards used by Nova Scotia employers.

resources.name: DeepSense Industry Data Challenges
resources.organization: DeepSense (hosted by Dalhousie University with industry and government partners)
resources.description: DeepSense convenes ocean-sector employers with faculty to translate real company data problems into classroom-ready case datasets, project briefs, and assessment criteria. These employer-authored modules are piloted in Dalhousie and NSCC courses and sprints, giving students hands-on analytics experience on local ocean data while aligning learning outcomes with industry practices and tools.
resources.address: Steele Ocean Sciences Building, 1355 Oxford Street, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: Connector in the Classroom (Connector Program)
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s Connector in the Classroom works with instructors at NSCC and local universities to co-develop course-embedded modules where students research sectors, interview employers, and complete labour‑market projects using employer-designed templates and rubrics. These short, employer-led activities are piloted as graded assignments that build local networking, communication, and job-readiness aligned to Nova Scotia employers’ expectations.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Youth Entrepreneurship Incubators: Run community incubator programs that pair aspiring young entrepreneurs with local mentors, business services and small grants so they build real ventures that create local jobs and teach transferable skills in marketing, finance and operations.

resources.name: JA Company Program
resources.description: JA Nova Scotia’s Company Program is an after‑school youth entrepreneurship incubator where high school students form real companies, guided by volunteer mentors from the local business community. Participants receive hands-on training in marketing, finance, and operations, access business services and workshops, and compete for small seed funds and awards that help launch and grow their ventures—building job-ready skills while creating real products and services.

resources.name: Navigate Startup House Incubation
resources.organization: Navigate (Cape Breton University & Nova Scotia Community College)
resources.description: Navigate provides a youth-friendly incubator environment for students and recent graduates in Cape Breton to develop startups, pairing them with experienced mentors, advisors, and peer networks. The program offers workspace, workshops on marketing, finance, and operations, and connections to local business services and funding opportunities, enabling young founders to build real ventures and jobs in the region.

resources.name: IGNITE Youth & Startup Programming
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic runs entrepreneurship programming that engages youth and early-stage founders across rural Nova Scotia, connecting them with mentors, business advisors, and prototyping resources. Through bootcamps, workshops, and incubator-style support, participants build companies, access local services, and are connected to small grants and funding competitions—developing practical skills in marketing, finance, and operations while creating community-rooted ventures.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3R2

resources.name: The Spark Zone
resources.description: The Spark Zone is a university-based incubator that supports student and youth entrepreneurs with mentorship, venture coaching, and access to business services through a network of industry partners. It helps teams validate ideas, develop go-to-market strategies, and manage finances and operations, and provides access to small project funds and pitch opportunities—advancing real ventures that can create local employment.

resources.name: Volta Academy & Residency
resources.description: Volta operates an incubator in downtown Halifax that supports early-stage and student/youth-founded startups with mentorship, programming, and access to professional services. Through Volta Academy and its Residency, founders build capabilities in marketing, finance, and operations and can compete for non-dilutive micro-grants (e.g., Volta Cohort awards) to accelerate venture creation and job growth in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Community-Based Recognition of Prior Learning: Non-profits and colleges collaborate to assess and formally recognize skills gained through community work, volunteering, informal employment and Indigenous learning, converting experiences into credits, micro-credentials or trade hours to speed job readiness.

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL/PLAR)
resources.description: NSCC assesses learning gained outside formal education—such as community volunteering, caregiving, Indigenous land-based learning, and informal employment—through portfolios, interviews, demonstrations, and challenge assessments. Successful assessments convert prior experience into course credits, exemptions, or micro-credentials, shortening programs and speeding job readiness; NSCC often works with Nova Scotia Works and community partners to help learners document competencies and align them to program outcomes.

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) for Newcomers
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS helps immigrants and refugees document and validate skills developed through community work, volunteering, and informal or overseas employment via portfolio development and competency assessments. Staff liaise with colleges, universities, and regulatory bodies in Nova Scotia to translate this learning into course credits, micro-credentials, or recognized trade experience, accelerating pathways to employment and licensure.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Prior Learning and Trade Qualifier Assessment
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency evaluates prior trade-related learning and experience—including competencies gained in community and informal work—through its Prior Learning Assessment and Trade Qualifier pathways. Verified experience can be credited toward apprenticeship hours or grant advanced standing, with the Agency coordinating with NSCC and community employment organizations to confirm competencies and arrange targeted gap training.
resources.address: 145 Hobsons Lake Drive, Suite 400, Halifax, NS B3S 0H9

resources.name: Prior Learning Assessment and Recognition (PLAR)
resources.description: CBU awards academic credit for demonstrable learning acquired through employment, community service and volunteering, military experience, and Indigenous knowledge. Using portfolio assessment, interviews, and challenge processes aligned with course outcomes—and supported by third-party attestations from community supervisors—CBU converts prior experiential learning into credits to reduce time to completion and improve job readiness.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

resources.name: Prior Learning Assessment and Recognition (PLAR)
resources.description: MSVU recognizes learning gained through volunteer roles, community leadership, caregiving, and workplace experience by assessing documented portfolios and, where appropriate, challenge exams or interviews. Successful candidates receive transfer credit or course exemptions, and the university engages with local employers and community agencies to ensure assessed competencies align with labour-market and program outcomes.

solutions.text: Transport & Housing Supports for Placements: Local governments and community organizations provide targeted supports (transit passes, short-term housing or host-family stipends) to remove logistic barriers that prevent students and apprentices from taking up placements in nearby towns or regional employers.

resources.name: Learner Housing Program (Clinical Placements)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health provides free or subsidized short‑term housing in communities across the province for health‑profession students completing clinical placements away from home. The program helps learners accept placements with regional hospitals and clinics by reducing travel and accommodation barriers, and may also offer travel support or mileage reimbursement tied to placement requirements.
resources.address: 7001 Mumford Road, Suite 300, Halifax, NS B3L 2H8

resources.name: Work-Integrated Learning (WIL) Travel Bursary
resources.description: NSCC’s WIL Travel Bursary provides targeted financial assistance to students who must travel or temporarily relocate to complete required co-ops, practicums, and applied learning placements. Funds can cover transportation (e.g., fuel, mileage, transit passes) and short-term accommodation so students can accept placements with employers in nearby towns or rural regions.

resources.name: Co-op Access Bursary (Rowe School of Business)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Management Career Services (Rowe School of Business)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Management Career Services offers a Co-op Access Bursary that reduces non-tuition costs that can block students from taking work terms, including relocation, temporary housing, and transportation. By offsetting expenses like bus passes, mileage, and short-term rentals, the fund enables students to pursue placements with employers throughout Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Co-op Access Bursary
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University – Co-operative Education Office
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University provides a Co-op Access Bursary to help students cover the extra costs of accepting work terms outside their immediate community, such as transportation and short-term accommodation. This targeted support removes logistical barriers so students can take placements with regional employers across Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Community Project-Based Learning Partnerships: Schools, colleges and employers collaborate on semester-long projects that deliver tangible community outcomes (revitalizing a waterfront, building digital services for a non-profit) so learners gain applied skills while employers evaluate and recruit participants.

resources.name: NSCC Applied Research and Innovation
resources.description: NSCC’s Applied Research and Innovation unit partners faculty and students with Nova Scotia employers, non-profits, and municipalities on term-based projects that solve real operational challenges—building prototypes, digital tools, and process improvements. These collaborations are embedded in courses and capstones across programs, giving learners hands-on experience while partners co-supervise and evaluate work. Employers use these projects to identify talent and often recruit students directly from the teams.

resources.name: Service Learning Program
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University embeds for-credit, semester-long community projects into courses across disciplines, where students collaborate with non-profits, social enterprises, and public-sector partners on needs such as program evaluations, digital services, and community planning. Projects are jointly scoped with community hosts and faculty, producing tangible deliverables while developing students’ professional skills. Partners mentor students and provide feedback that informs hiring and ongoing collaboration.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Nova Scotia Sandbox Program)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science (Nova Scotia Sandbox Program)
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs connects students from Dalhousie, NSCC, and other schools with companies and community organizations to tackle real product challenges over multi-week and semester-length sprints, resulting in prototypes, MVPs, and digital services. Industry mentors co-design project scopes and provide iterative feedback, enabling employers to evaluate participants’ skills on authentic work. Many projects lead to internships, co-ops, or startup opportunities stemming from the delivered solutions.

resources.name: DeepSense Student Projects
resources.description: DeepSense runs 12–16 week applied data and AI projects where student teams collaborate with ocean-sector companies to build analytics dashboards, machine learning models, and decision-support tools using real industry datasets. Projects are co-supervised by company partners and academic mentors, producing tangible deliverables that address specific business problems. Employers assess students’ capabilities through the project cycle and frequently hire participants into internships and full-time roles.

obstacles.title: Youth outmigration and insufficient return pathways
obstacles.description: Graduates and early-career workers depart for larger cities, and alumni lack clear incentives, networks, and pathways to return or work remotely from Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Community-led Alumni Network: Create a local alumni platform run by community groups and post‑secondary partners that connects graduates with job leads, mentorship, social events, and return opportunities specific to Nova Scotia communities.

resources.name: Dalhousie Alumni & Friends (Dal Alumni Hub)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s alumni network connects students and recent graduates with alumni mentors and industry contacts through the Dal Alumni Hub and regular networking events across Nova Scotia. Working with local employers, Career & Co-op offices, and community partners, the network surfaces job leads, mentorship, and volunteer opportunities, and invites Dal alumni to re-engage with Nova Scotia communities through chapter events and return-to-Nova-Scotia programming.

resources.name: NSCC Alumni Association
resources.description: The NSCC Alumni Association fosters a province‑wide community of graduates that stays connected to local campuses and employers through mentorship, events, and an active alumni communications network. In partnership with NSCC Career Services and regional industry partners, the association shares job leads, hosts career and social events in communities across Nova Scotia, and supports grads who return to the province or shift between regions to work or start businesses.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Alumni Association
resources.description: SMU’s alumni association connects graduates with mentors, employer networks, and local chapters that host social and career events throughout Nova Scotia. Through collaborations with community organizations and the university’s career and co‑op offices, the association promotes job leads, mentorship matches, and return opportunities for Huskies who want to build their careers and lives in Nova Scotia communities.

resources.name: Cape Breton University Alumni Association
resources.description: CBU’s alumni association sustains a community‑led network that links graduates with Cape Breton employers, entrepreneurship supports, and mentorship opportunities through local events and partnerships. By collaborating with community partners and campus career services, it circulates regional job leads, hosts homecoming and networking activities, and encourages alumni to return or remain in Cape Breton to contribute to the island’s growing economy.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

solutions.text: Returner Fellowship and Micro-grant Program: Offer small community-funded fellowships or relocation micro‑grants to cover moving costs, short-term housing, or project seed funding for former residents who want to return and work locally or start ventures.

resources.name: Healthcare Recruitment Incentives (Relocation Assistance)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health provides signing bonuses and relocation assistance to healthcare professionals who move to Nova Scotia, helping cover moving expenses and, in some cases, temporary accommodation. These incentives directly function as relocation micro-grants that reduce the financial barriers for former Nova Scotians to return and work locally, aligning with the goal of bringing talent back to the province.

resources.name: Physician Recruitment and Retention Incentive Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Inverness
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Inverness offers financial incentives, including relocation and settlement support, to physicians who choose to establish or resume practice in the county. These community-funded incentives operate as targeted micro-grants that help cover moving costs and initial housing needs, encouraging former residents in the medical profession to return and serve locally.
resources.address: 375 Main Street, Port Hood, NS B0E 2W0

resources.name: Physician Recruitment Incentive Program
resources.description: The Town of Amherst provides financial incentives and relocation assistance to physicians who relocate to practice in the community, including those returning home to Nova Scotia. By offsetting moving expenses and initial setup costs, the program acts as a micro-grant mechanism that lowers barriers for returners to re-establish careers locally.
resources.address: 98 Victoria Street East, Amherst, NS B4H 1X6

resources.name: Family Physician Recruitment and Retention Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings offers recruitment incentives that include relocation and settlement assistance to family physicians who choose to practice in Kings County. These funds serve as community-backed micro-grants covering moving and initial living costs, creating a clear and financially supported pathway for medical professionals—especially former residents—to return and work locally.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

solutions.text: Local Mentorship Circles: Organize sector-specific mentorship circles (tech, trades, arts, entrepreneurship) pairing young people and alumni with local business leaders for skills guidance, networks, and exposure to local career paths.

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program matches recent graduates and early-career professionals with established business leaders (“Connectors”) for targeted, sector-specific networking conversations. Through curated introductions and small-group meetups, participants gain guidance on local career paths, expand professional networks, and learn about opportunities to stay and build a career in Nova Scotia. This directly implements mentorship circles by pairing youth and alumni with leaders across industries like tech, finance, and trades-related sectors to accelerate local attachments and retention.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Volta Mentors
resources.description: Volta’s mentor network connects early-stage founders, students, and emerging tech talent with experienced entrepreneurs, product leaders, and investors for office hours, workshops, and small peer circles. Participants receive practical skills guidance, introductions to local companies, and insights into building careers and ventures in Nova Scotia’s tech ecosystem. These recurring mentorship circles strengthen local networks and help young people see clear, compelling pathways to stay and grow in the province.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: CEED Mentorship & Advisory Services
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides entrepreneurs and youth founders with access to Entrepreneurs-in-Residence, advisory sessions, and peer mentorship cohorts that bring small groups together around shared sector challenges. Through these mentorship circles, participants receive guidance from seasoned local business leaders in areas such as trades, retail, and services, while building networks that support staying and scaling in Nova Scotia. Alumni frequently return as mentors, reinforcing durable local career pathways.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Peer Mentoring Groups
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business hosts structured peer mentoring circles that connect women entrepreneurs and early-career professionals with experienced business leaders across Nova Scotia. These small, sector-focused groups meet regularly to exchange practical advice, make local connections, and identify supply-chain and talent opportunities. The program strengthens retention and return pathways by showing how to launch and grow businesses locally while leveraging an alumni-style network of mentors.
resources.address: 166 Bedford Highway, Suite 208, Halifax, NS B3M 2J6

resources.name: Start-Up Yard Mentorship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE’s Start-Up Yard connects ocean-tech students, recent graduates, and early-stage founders with mentors from Nova Scotia’s marine, defense, and offshore industries through cohort-based programming, office hours, and industry roundtables. Participants receive technical and business guidance, introductions to local suppliers and employers, and exposure to regional career paths in the blue economy. These sector-specific mentorship circles help young talent build futures in Nova Scotia rather than leaving for larger markets.

solutions.text: Employer Return & Remote-work Pledge: Encourage local employers to adopt a community pledge to proactively recruit alumni, advertise flexible/remote roles, and provide clear pathways for returning Nova Scotians to rejoin organizations remotely or in person.

resources.name: Work From Nova Scotia
resources.description: Work From Nova Scotia is a province-wide initiative that encourages employers to support remote and hybrid work arrangements so talent can live and work in Nova Scotia. The program promotes remote-friendly job postings, connects employers to relocation supports and co-working ecosystems, and targets alumni and former residents looking to return. By inviting employers to commit to flexible hiring and advertise remote roles, it creates clear pathways for returning Nova Scotians to rejoin organizations from within the province.
resources.address: 1969 Upper Water Street, Suite 1300, Halifax, NS B3J 3R7

resources.name: Connector Program – Halifax
resources.description: The Connector Program engages employers and community leaders (“Connectors”) who commit to meeting recent graduates, newcomers, and alumni and making three warm introductions to their networks. This pledge-like commitment accelerates hiring, encourages employers to proactively recruit emerging talent, and has increasingly supported hybrid and remote roles. It creates tangible return pathways for Nova Scotians by linking them directly to decision-makers who can champion flexible opportunities at local organizations.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 701, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: ISANS Connector Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Connector Program works with employers across Nova Scotia to identify talent needs and facilitates one-to-one networking between employers and skilled candidates, including internationally educated alumni and returning residents. Employers are encouraged to adopt inclusive, flexible, and remote-friendly hiring practices and to share opportunities through the program’s network. This builds clear pathways for candidates to rejoin or enter Nova Scotia organizations, whether in person or working remotely from within the province.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: NSCC Employer Services & Alumni Job Connections
resources.description: NSCC partners with employers to post jobs (including remote and hybrid roles), design flexible work-integrated learning, and create direct pipelines for NSCC graduates and alumni to return to or remain in Nova Scotia. Employer outreach and advisory services help organizations implement remote onboarding and retention practices, while alumni platforms make it easy to advertise return-friendly opportunities. Together, these measures operationalize a community commitment to proactively recruit alumni and provide clear return pathways into Nova Scotia workplaces.

solutions.text: Community Co-working & Childcare Hubs: Convert underused municipal spaces into affordable co‑working hubs with reliable broadband and drop‑in childcare to enable remote work, entrepreneurship, and hybrid job arrangements for returning young families.

resources.name: Lunenburg County Lifestyle Centre – Library & Playcare as Work-and-Care Hub
resources.description: The Lunenburg County Lifestyle Centre (LCLC) is a civic complex that houses the Margaret Hennigar Public Library alongside recreation facilities, creating a practical community co‑working environment with free high‑speed Wi‑Fi, quiet work tables, study rooms, and printers. Parents can work in the library or book meeting rooms while making use of the Centre’s on‑site child‑minding/playcare services for short stays, effectively pairing workspace and care under one roof. By leveraging a shared municipal space to offer broadband-enabled work areas and drop‑in childcare, LCLC advances remote work, entrepreneurship, and hybrid job arrangements for young families.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

resources.name: Canada Games Centre – Community Co-working with On-site Child Minding
resources.description: The Canada Games Centre is a Halifax Regional Municipality facility that provides free Wi‑Fi throughout the building, open lounge seating, and rentable meeting rooms that function as accessible co‑working spaces. Its affordable, short‑term child‑minding service lets parents focus on calls, meetings, or laptop work while children are safely cared for nearby. This integrated work‑and‑care setup in a municipal hub supports remote workers, entrepreneurs, and returning young families seeking flexible arrangements.
resources.address: 26 Thomas Raddall Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 0E2

resources.name: Zatzman Sportsplex – Wi‑Fi Work Areas with Drop‑in Childcare
resources.description: Zatzman Sportsplex is a municipally supported recreation complex offering public Wi‑Fi, open seating/concourse areas, and rentable community rooms suitable for remote work and meetings. Its staffed, short‑stay child‑minding (Tot Spot/Playcare) enables parents to work on site while children are nearby in safe care. By activating an existing civic space as a combined workspace and childcare hub, the Sportsplex lowers barriers for entrepreneurs and hybrid workers in Dartmouth.

resources.name: Rath Eastlink Community Centre – Work-Friendly Commons with Child Minding
resources.description: The Rath Eastlink Community Centre provides facility‑wide Wi‑Fi, community lounge areas with tables and power outlets, and bookable rooms that serve as ad hoc co‑working spaces. Its drop‑in child‑minding offering allows parents to concentrate on remote work, meetings, or training sessions while children are cared for on site. This co‑location of broadband-enabled workspace and childcare in a regional civic facility helps entrepreneurs and hybrid workers in Colchester County balance work and family.

solutions.text: Local Internship and Apprenticeship Exchanges: Partner schools, businesses, and trades to create paid local internships and apprenticeship placements tied to community projects, ensuring early‑career workers gain experience without leaving the region.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s flagship youth employment program places high school and post-secondary students in 9–16 week paid summer internships with municipalities, nonprofits, and local businesses across Nova Scotia. Interns work on community-focused environmental and climate projects, with training and mentorship coordinated in partnership with schools and host employers—helping early‑career workers gain experience and connections without leaving the province.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY partners Nova Scotia high schools with construction employers to deliver paid summer work terms for Grade 10–12 students on local construction sites. Run with industry and apprenticeship partners, placements are safety-certified and aligned to apprenticeship pathways, giving youth hands‑on, community‑based experience and hours toward trade certification—creating a clear route to stay and build a career in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 110, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Co-operative Education & Work-Integrated Learning (WIL)
resources.description: NSCC’s WIL programs coordinate paid co-ops, internships, and practicums with employers and community organizations across Nova Scotia in trades, technology, business, health, and community services. Staff broker placements tied to real local projects and provide employer and student supports, ensuring learners build career experience and networks while remaining in their home communities.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Co-operative Education
resources.description: SMU Co-op connects undergraduate and graduate students with paid work terms at Nova Scotia companies, nonprofits, and public-sector organizations in fields such as business, tech, and the arts. The program partners with faculty and local employers to design learning outcomes and community-linked projects, creating clear local career pathways that encourage students and alumni to stay in or return to Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Skills Bridging & Micro-credential Programs: Work with community colleges and employers to offer short, low-cost micro-credentials and bridging courses aligned with local industry needs so alumni can update skills before returning.

resources.name: NSCC Microcredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College offers short, competency-based microcredentials co-designed with employers in sectors like IT, healthcare, oceans, trades, and clean energy. These stackable, low-cost badges and bridging courses help recent graduates and alumni quickly update in-demand skills, often delivered online or in hybrid formats to support those looking to return to Nova Scotia or move into local roles.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Micro-credentials (Open Learning & Career Development)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development provides micro-credentials and digital badges aligned with employer needs in areas such as data, project management, ocean tech, and professional communication. Programs are short, flexible, and developed with industry advisors to bridge learners into Nova Scotia’s growth sectors and help alumni refresh skills for local opportunities.

resources.name: MSVU Extended Learning Micro-credentials
resources.organization: Mount Saint Vincent University – Extended Learning
resources.description: Mount Saint Vincent University’s Extended Learning offers short, stackable micro-credentials and digital badges in workforce-relevant topics such as leadership, non-profit management, business communication, and education technology. Created with community and employer input, these offerings provide accessible upskilling pathways that help alumni and early-career professionals align with Nova Scotia’s labour market needs.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Professional & Continuing Studies Micro-credentials
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University – Professional & Continuing Studies
resources.description: SMU’s Professional & Continuing Studies delivers focused micro-credentials and short courses in areas like business analytics, project management, and digital skills, shaped with input from industry partners. The flexible, career-oriented format helps graduates and returning alumni bridge into high-demand roles in Nova Scotia’s economy.

solutions.text: Community Entrepreneurship Incubator: Establish a municipally supported incubator offering mentoring, legal/business clinics, low-cost office space, and pitch funds to help young entrepreneurs launch locally rooted businesses.

resources.name: Volta Residency
resources.description: Volta’s Residency program provides subsidized office space, mentorship, founder education, and regular office-hour clinics with legal, accounting, and marketing partners to help startups build and scale in Nova Scotia. It also connects entrepreneurs to pitch opportunities such as Volta Cohort (which offers early-stage investment), helping young founders access capital and launch locally rooted businesses that encourage graduates to stay or return to Halifax.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE is an ocean-sector incubator offering shared offices, labs, prototyping facilities, and hands-on mentorship from industry advisors to help founders validate and commercialize products in Nova Scotia. The program runs workshops, partner office hours, and pitch events that connect entrepreneurs to customers and funding, enabling young innovators to build globally competitive, locally anchored ocean-tech companies.

resources.name: Navigate Startup House
resources.organization: Navigate (Cape Breton University & Nova Scotia Community College)
resources.description: Navigate Startup House provides free or low-cost co-working space, meeting rooms, mentorship, and business workshops for emerging entrepreneurs in Cape Breton. Operated by CBU and NSCC, it hosts advisor sessions and pitch events while connecting founders to local networks and funding pathways—creating a clear, community-based launchpad that helps young people start and grow businesses without leaving Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Craft Business Incubator
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: The Craft Business Incubator supports creative entrepreneurs with affordable studio space, tailored business training, and mentorship to turn craft practices into sustainable local enterprises. Through workshops, one-on-one advising, market development support, and a collaborative workspace, it functions as a community incubator that enables young creatives to launch and stay rooted in Cape Breton.

solutions.text: Local Housing Solutions Task Group: Form a neighbourhood task group to pilot affordable housing options for young workers and returners — e.g., co‑housing, rent-to-own schemes, and time-limited starter units using community land trusts or partnerships.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia partners with local volunteer build committees, municipalities, and employers to deliver attainable starter homes for working families. By organizing neighbourhood-level teams to acquire land, build, and select partner families, the program mirrors the task‑group approach and creates clear pathways for young workers and returners to put down roots in Nova Scotia. Its affordable, no‑interest mortgages and sweat equity model function as a practical alternative to rent‑to‑own while preserving long-term affordability.

resources.name: New Dawn Properties – Affordable Rental & Community Revitalization
resources.description: New Dawn Properties leads community‑driven housing in Sydney by assembling partnerships with the municipality, local businesses, and lenders to convert and build mixed‑income units. Their projects add smaller, attainable rental apartments and live‑work spaces suited to early‑career workers and returning graduates, while keeping properties under community stewardship to protect long‑term affordability. New Dawn convenes project‑specific neighbourhood and stakeholder groups—effectively local housing task groups—to pilot starter units and shared‑amenity housing tailored to workforce needs.

resources.name: Affordable Housing Strategy & Working Group
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: MODL’s Affordable Housing Strategy and cross‑departmental working group coordinate residents, non‑profits, and employers to pilot options like secondary suites, small‑lot/cluster housing, and infill starter units across Lunenburg County. The municipality supports neighbourhood task teams with planning tools, by‑law updates, and partnerships (including with Habitat for Humanity) to bring attainable homes to market for local and returning workers. These initiatives create community‑led pathways to housing that help young people establish themselves locally.

resources.name: Affordable Housing Grants and Partnerships
resources.description: HRM’s initiative funds and enables non‑profit and co‑operative housing providers to deliver new affordable units, including small starter apartments, secondary suites, and co‑living/co‑housing‑style projects near jobs and transit. Through grants, surplus land agreements, and enabling by‑law changes, the municipality supports neighbourhood‑scale task groups and partner organizations to pilot models that keep housing within reach for young workers and returnees. The program advances partnership‑based pathways into stable, affordable housing across Halifax.

solutions.text: Relocation & Welcome Packages: Create standardized community welcome packages for returners that include housing leads, childcare and schooling info, community events calendar, healthcare access details, and employer contacts.

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: The Cape Breton Welcome Network provides standardized welcome packages and one-on-one navigation for people moving to or returning to Cape Breton. Packages include local rental and real-estate leads, childcare and school contacts, community event listings, steps for accessing healthcare (MSI and local clinics), and curated introductions to employers via the Cape Breton Connector Program, making relocation smoother and more informed.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

resources.name: Settlement & Community Integration (Newcomer Orientation)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers comprehensive newcomer and returnee orientation that functions as a standardized welcome package for anyone relocating to Nova Scotia. Their materials and consultations cover housing leads and tenant guidance, childcare and school enrollment (HRCE/CSAP), community events and networks, healthcare access (MSI, family practice registry), and employment connections through job services and partner Connector programs.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Newcomers Guide and Welcome Services
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality maintains an official Newcomers Guide and online welcome kit that consolidates key relocation information for new and returning residents. The package points to local housing search tools, childcare and school registration, municipal/community event calendars, healthcare access (health cards and family practice registry), and employer networking through the Halifax Partnership Connector Program.

solutions.text: Pop-up Industry Showcases: Host regular local showcases where businesses, cultural groups, and trades demonstrate career paths, apprenticeships, and remote-work roles to alumni and students considering return.

resources.name: NSCC Career Fairs & Industry Showcases
resources.description: Across Nova Scotia Community College campuses, Career Services hosts recurring job fairs, employer spotlights, and sector showcases where local businesses, trades, cultural organizations, and public-sector employers present interactive demonstrations. Students and alumni explore apprenticeships, co-ops, full-time and remote-work roles in areas like ICT, oceans, health, creative industries, and skilled trades. These pop-up, on-campus showcases directly connect talent with employers and make it easier for grads and returnees to see viable career paths in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Hire Me Halifax
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s recurring talent showcase brings employers and emerging professionals together in a pop-up event format where participants pitch themselves and meet hiring teams from local companies. The event highlights career paths in tech, finance, oceans, creative sectors, and trades, including remote and hybrid roles suitable for alumni considering a return to Nova Scotia. By convening employers and talent in one room, it creates clear, low-barrier pathways for young people to build careers in the province.
resources.address: 1969 Upper Water Street, Suite 1300, Halifax, NS B3J 3R7

resources.name: Volta DemoCamp and Industry Night Series
resources.description: Volta regularly hosts DemoCamp and Industry Nights where startups and scale-ups demo products, discuss hiring needs, and connect with students, recent grads, and returning professionals. These community pop-ups expose attendees to career paths in Nova Scotia’s tech ecosystem—from co-ops and junior roles to remote-first positions in software, product, and marketing—and enable direct conversations with founders and hiring managers. The showcases help retain and attract young talent by making local and remote opportunities immediately visible and accessible.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Employer Showcases and Job Fairs
resources.description: As a Nova Scotia Works service provider, TEAM Work Cooperative runs recurring pop-up employer showcases, sector information sessions, and multi-employer job fairs at its centre and partner venues. Local businesses, trades, and community organizations demonstrate career pathways, apprenticeships, and remote/hybrid roles to jobseekers, students, and alumni. These events create direct pipelines to employment and apprenticeships that support graduates to stay in or return to Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Youth & Alumni Advisory Council: Form a council of current youth and alumni to advise municipal leaders and institutions on policies and programs that would make returning and staying more attractive.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: The Halifax Regional Municipality Youth Advisory Committee is a standing committee of Regional Council composed of youth members who advise Council and municipal staff on policies, services, and programs affecting young people. By bringing forward recommendations on issues like transit, housing, recreation, and employment, the committee ensures youth voices shape decisions that make Halifax a more attractive place to stay, study, work, and return to after graduation.

resources.name: NSCC Alumni Council
resources.description: The NSCC Alumni Council is a representative body of graduates from campuses across Nova Scotia that advises NSCC Alumni Relations and college leadership on alumni engagement and student-to-alumni transition initiatives. Through mentorship, networking, and employer connections focused on Nova Scotia’s labour market, the council informs programs and policies that help graduates build careers in the province and encourage alumni to return or work remotely from Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Dalhousie Alumni Association (Board of Directors)
resources.description: The Dalhousie Alumni Association, led by a volunteer board of alumni, serves as an advisory and governance partner to the university on alumni relations, career development, and community engagement. By shaping mentorship networks, regional events, and initiatives that connect students and graduates with Nova Scotia opportunities, the association helps create clear pathways and incentives for alumni to remain in or return to the province.

resources.name: Acadia University Alumni Association
resources.description: The Acadia University Alumni Association engages an elected council of alumni that advises the university on programs that strengthen alumni–community ties, career supports, and experiential learning connections. Their input informs policies and initiatives—such as mentorship, employer networking, and regional engagement—that make it easier for Acadia graduates to build fulfilling lives in Nova Scotia and for alumni elsewhere to reconnect and return.

resources.name: Cape Breton University Alumni Association
resources.description: The Cape Breton University Alumni Association, through its alumni board and committees, collaborates with university leadership to guide alumni programming, mentorship, and partnerships with local employers and community organizations. By advising on initiatives that showcase Cape Breton career pathways and remote-work options, the association supports efforts to retain graduates in the region and to attract alumni back to Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

solutions.text: Community Procurement & Hiring Preferences: Local governments and anchor institutions adopt procurement and hiring practices that prioritize nearby small businesses and returning talent, creating demand for local skills and jobs.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Sustainable Procurement Program
resources.description: HRM’s procurement policy embeds social and sustainable procurement criteria in tenders, enabling evaluation points for local economic development, supplier diversity, apprenticeships, and community benefits. By weighting social value, the municipality steers contracts toward Nova Scotia small businesses and vendors that commit to local hiring and training, creating demand for local skills and clearer pathways for youth and returning talent to find work at home.

resources.name: Build Nova Scotia Procurement & Community Benefits
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia integrates community benefits and social value considerations into procurements for provincial infrastructure, waterfronts, and connectivity projects, encouraging use of local supply chains, apprentices, and diverse Nova Scotian suppliers. These practices channel public spending to nearby small businesses and require workforce development outcomes, opening steady roles for graduates and returning professionals in trades, tech, and professional services.
resources.address: 1751 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S5

resources.name: Procurement Assistance Nova Scotia (PANS) – Supplier Development & Supplier Diversity
resources.organization: Procurement, Service Nova Scotia (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: PANS helps Nova Scotia small and diverse businesses compete for public contracts through training, one-on-one advisory support, and reverse trade shows that connect local suppliers with government, health, and post-secondary buyers. The program also advances inclusive procurement tools (e.g., supplier diversity measures and social value criteria), operationalizing community-focused procurement that grows demand for local firms and supports hiring and apprenticeship opportunities for youth and returning talent.

resources.name: Hire Me Cape Breton
resources.description: This regional talent initiative spotlights Cape Bretoners (including those living away and recent grads) through candidate profiles and employer outreach, encouraging local employers and anchor institutions to prioritize interviewing and hiring returning talent. By building a direct pipeline between regional employers and returnees, the program supports hiring practices that keep and bring back skilled youth, strengthening the local workforce and the small-business supply base that often fulfills public and institutional contracts.

solutions.text: Peer-led Returner Buddy Program: Match returning alumni with local ‘buddies’ who help with practical re-integration — navigating services, networking, and social connections — for their first 3–6 months back.

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program matches recent graduates, newcomers, and returning professionals with established local “Connectors” for guided, one-on-one networking. Connectors make warm introductions, share insider knowledge on local services and community life, and help participants plug into professional and social circles during their first months back. This peer-led matching directly supports returnees with practical re-integration over a defined period, often aligning with a 3–6 month transition window.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Dalhousie University Ten Thousand Coffees (Dal Alumni Link)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University (Alumni & Friends / Office of Advancement)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Ten Thousand Coffees hub (Dal Alumni Link) matches alumni and students for one-on-one mentorship and coffee chats based on goals, interests, and location. Alumni returning to Nova Scotia can be paired with local alumni “buddies” who provide introductions to sector networks, guidance on navigating Halifax services and opportunities, and invitations to community events, supporting re-integration over the first several months back. The flexible, peer-led format functions like a returner buddy system that accelerates social and professional reconnection.

resources.name: SMU Mentoring (Ten Thousand Coffees)
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University’s Ten Thousand Coffees hub connects students and alumni for targeted, one-on-one conversations and mentoring. Alumni who are returning to Halifax can match with local SMU alumni “buddies” who share sector connections, help navigate local services and campus/community resources, and provide social introductions over a period of months. This peer-led, time-flexible model mirrors a returner buddy approach to smooth practical re-integration.

resources.name: Acadia Alumni & Students (Ten Thousand Coffees)
resources.description: Acadia University’s Ten Thousand Coffees hub facilitates one-on-one matches between alumni and students for mentorship and networking in the Annapolis Valley. Alumni moving back to Nova Scotia can request local matches with Wolfville-area alumni who act as “returner buddies,” offering introductions, guidance on navigating services and housing, and connections to community and industry events over the first months. The structured, peer-led setup supports practical re-integration and rebuilding of local networks.

solutions.text: Transport and Connectivity Improvements: Community-driven campaigns to improve local transit links, ride‑share networks, and last‑mile solutions combined with advocacy for affordable, high-speed home internet to support remote workers.

resources.name: Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative (INSI)
resources.description: INSI is a province-wide broadband expansion program delivering affordable, high‑speed internet to underserved and rural communities through partnerships with ISPs and municipalities. By closing last‑mile gaps with fibre and fixed‑wireless projects, it enables remote work and learning and supports young people who want to remain in or return to Nova Scotia while staying connected to employers and markets.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 301, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: East Hants Rural High-Speed Internet Project
resources.description: The Municipality of East Hants is expanding access to reliable, high‑speed home internet across rural communities by coordinating last‑mile builds and leveraging provincial and federal funding. This improves connectivity for remote workers, entrepreneurs, and students, helping young residents live and work locally while maintaining ties to broader employment networks.

resources.name: Communauto Atlantic – Halifax Carshare
resources.description: Communauto Atlantic operates a member‑based carshare network in Halifax that complements public transit and active transportation, giving residents flexible, affordable access to vehicles without the cost of ownership. By strengthening last‑mile options and enabling car‑light living, it helps young professionals and students connect to jobs, co‑working spaces, and services across the region.

resources.name: Halifax Transit (Bus and Ferry Network)
resources.description: Halifax Transit provides region‑wide bus and ferry services, with ongoing network improvements that enhance frequency, coverage, and connections between suburban and rural communities and urban job centers. Strengthened local transit links and multimodal integration support last‑mile mobility for youth and early‑career workers, making it easier to live in Nova Scotia while accessing work and education.
resources.address: 520 Ragged Lake Boulevard, Halifax, NS B3S 1R7

resources.name: Bridgewater Transit
resources.description: Bridgewater Transit connects neighborhoods, workplaces, and services across Bridgewater and links to surrounding communities on the South Shore, improving access to jobs, training, and healthcare without needing a personal car. As a locally managed system, it strengthens last‑mile connectivity and supports youth retention by making daily mobility more reliable and affordable.

solutions.text: Cultural & Social Anchor Events: Fund and promote festivals, maker fairs, speaker series, and creative co-ops that showcase the region’s lifestyle and talent, strengthening cultural ties that attract alumni back for social and economic life.

resources.name: Public Programs & Events at the Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21
resources.organization: Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21
resources.description: Pier 21 runs year-round public programs—talks, film screenings, cultural celebrations, and exhibitions—that showcase stories, arts, and foodways from communities across Nova Scotia and beyond. By activating a landmark waterfront venue with speaker series and cultural festivals, they create anchor events that celebrate local talent and heritage, strengthening ties that draw alumni and newcomers to reconnect with Halifax’s social and economic life.

resources.name: Bus Stop Theatre Co-op – Community Arts & Festival Hub
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op is a community-owned venue that hosts festivals, artist showcases, speaker series, and creative residencies featuring local performers, filmmakers, and makers. By providing an affordable, collaborative stage for cultural events, it anchors a vibrant scene on Gottingen Street that highlights Nova Scotia talent and gives alumni a reason and a network to return, participate, and build careers.

resources.name: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design – Exhibitions, Markets & Workshops
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: CBCCD presents exhibitions, maker workshops, artist talks, and craft markets that spotlight Cape Breton artisans and creative entrepreneurs. These programs function as cultural anchor events, connecting local talent with audiences and alumni, fostering creative co-ops, and encouraging return pathways by showcasing viable creative livelihoods and a distinctive Island lifestyle.

resources.name: Lunenburg School of the Arts – Workshops, Talks & Exhibitions
resources.description: The Lunenburg School of the Arts offers hands-on maker workshops, visiting-artist talks, and community exhibitions that highlight regional craft, design, and fine arts. By convening creators and audiences in a historic town setting, it provides anchor programming that showcases local culture, strengthens creative networks, and entices alumni and remote workers to return or relocate.

resources.name: Halifax Public Libraries – Programs & Events
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts free author talks, music and film series, entrepreneurship and tech meetups, and community festivals at branches like the Central Library. These inclusive, well-promoted cultural and speaker events act as social anchors that showcase local talent and provide welcoming spaces for students, alumni, and early-career professionals to connect and build community in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

obstacles.title: Health and mental health access gaps
obstacles.description: Primary care shortages, long wait times, and limited youth-focused mental health services undermine quality of life and the ability to sustain work and study.

solutions.text: Community Mental Health Peer Support Groups: Organize locally run, age-specific peer support groups for youth and young adults facilitated by trained community volunteers to provide regular, low-barrier emotional support, crisis coping skills, and referral pathways.

resources.name: Laing House Peer Support Program
resources.description: Laing House is a youth-driven organization for ages 16–30 living with mental illness. It runs regular peer-led support groups and drop-in circles facilitated by trained youth and volunteers with lived experience, offering low-barrier emotional support, skill-building (e.g., WRAP, coping and crisis planning), and warm referrals to clinical care and community resources.

resources.name: Youth Project Peer Support Groups
resources.description: The Youth Project offers province-wide peer support groups and weekly drop-ins for 2SLGBTQIA+ youth ages 12–25. Groups are facilitated by trained staff and community volunteers with lived experience, providing a low-barrier space for emotional support, coping skills, safety planning, and referrals to mental health, housing, and school-based services.

resources.name: Peer Support Nova Scotia (Youth and Young Adult Groups)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health, Mental Health & Addictions Program
resources.description: Peer Support Nova Scotia is a provincial program within Nova Scotia Health that delivers peer-led support groups and one-to-one peer support across communities, including age-specific groups for young adults. Trained peer supporters use recovery-oriented practices to teach coping and crisis self-management skills and provide clear pathways to Nova Scotia Health Mental Health & Addictions services and other community resources.

resources.name: Dalhousie Student Union Peer Support Centre
resources.description: The Dalhousie Student Union Peer Support Centre provides free, low-barrier peer support for students (primarily young adults) through trained volunteer peer supporters and periodic peer-led group sessions. The centre focuses on active listening, stress and crisis coping strategies, and connects students to on-campus counselling, 24/7 crisis lines, and community mental health services.

solutions.text: School-Community Mental Health Hubs: Create on-site or neighborhood hubs co-located with schools or community centres where counsellors, social workers and youth workers hold regular drop-in hours, run workshops, and connect students to services.

resources.name: SchoolsPlus (HRCE)
resources.description: SchoolsPlus places community outreach workers, social workers, and partnering mental health clinicians directly in schools to offer drop-in support, group programming, and workshops. Operating as school-based hubs, they coordinate services and connect students and families to health, mental health, and social supports both on-site and through community partners.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Youth Health Centre at Citadel High School
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Youth Health Centre provides on-site, drop-in access for students to a Public Health Nurse and partners who offer confidential counselling, sexual and mental health education, and navigation to services. The centre hosts classroom sessions and workshops, and connects students to community and clinical supports such as IWK Mental Health & Addictions and Nova Scotia Health services.

resources.name: NSCC Counselling Services – Ivany Campus
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Ivany Campus
resources.description: Co-located within the college’s Student Services hub, NSCC counsellors and social workers provide same-day and short-term counselling, group workshops (e.g., stress management, coping skills), and mental health navigation. They connect students to community resources and provincial health services, functioning as an on-campus hub for wellness supports.

resources.name: Dalhousie Student Health & Wellness – Counselling Services
resources.description: Located within the university’s health and wellness centre, clinicians provide single-session and short-term counselling, workshops, and group programs, with drop-in options during peak times. The team connects students to specialized community mental health providers and provincial services, creating a campus-based hub that integrates counselling, primary care, and referral pathways.

solutions.text: Volunteer Telehealth Access Stations: Set up private booths in libraries, community centres or youth centres with high-speed internet and staff/volunteer navigators to help youth access telemedicine and virtual mental health appointments.

resources.name: Tele-Health Visit Room (People’s Place Library)
resources.description: People’s Place Library offers a bookable private room equipped with high-speed internet, a computer, webcam, and headset so residents—including youth—can attend VirtualCareNS and other virtual mental health or primary care appointments. Library staff act as navigators by helping patrons set up devices, access secure platforms (e.g., Zoom for Healthcare), and troubleshoot connectivity, effectively serving as a volunteer-supported telehealth access station in the community.

resources.name: Telehealth Connection Space (Rosa M. Harvey Middleton & Area Library)
resources.description: The Middleton library provides a dedicated, private space with reliable broadband, a computer, camera, and headset for community members to attend virtual health and counseling sessions. Staff help users—particularly teens and young adults—book the room, log into VirtualCareNS or other mental health services, and ensure privacy and tech readiness, mirroring a volunteer telehealth access station model.

resources.name: Virtual Care Room (Margaret Hennigar Public Library)
resources.description: At the Bridgewater branch, patrons can reserve a quiet, private room outfitted with high-speed internet and meeting technology to connect with physicians, therapists, and youth mental health providers online. Library staff and volunteers assist with account setup, secure video links, and basic troubleshooting, lowering access barriers for youth who lack private space or connectivity at home.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

resources.name: Telehealth/Zoom Booths (Truro Public Library)
resources.description: The Truro Public Library offers bookable private rooms and computer stations with webcams and stable broadband suitable for telemedicine and virtual counseling sessions. Staff provide on-site navigation support—helping youth and other patrons join VirtualCareNS or IWK mental health appointments securely—functioning as a community-based telehealth access point.

solutions.text: Youth Mental Health First Aid Training: Offer regular free or low-cost Mental Health First Aid courses for teachers, coaches, employers, parent groups and youth leaders so more people can recognize crises and provide immediate support and referrals.

resources.name: Mental Health First Aid (Adults Who Interact with Youth)
resources.description: Dalhousie Student Health & Wellness regularly delivers Mental Health First Aid training to faculty, staff, and student leaders who work closely with youth and young adults. The course builds skills to recognize signs of mental health problems and crises, provide initial help, de-escalate situations, and connect students to appropriate campus and community supports and referrals, implementing the solution by expanding the number of informed helpers in schools and youth settings.

resources.name: Mental Health First Aid Training (Standard and Supporting Youth)
resources.organization: St. John Ambulance Nova Scotia & Prince Edward Island Council
resources.description: St. John Ambulance NS/PEI Council offers low-cost Mental Health First Aid courses to the public and workplaces across Nova Scotia, including versions tailored for adults who interact with youth. Participants learn to identify common mental health concerns, respond to crises with evidence-based de-escalation techniques, and link individuals to professional care and community resources, directly increasing the capacity of teachers, coaches, employers, parents, and youth leaders to provide immediate support and referrals.
resources.address: 72 Highfield Park Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3A 4X2

solutions.text: Local Provider Recruitment and Retention Campaigns: Local businesses, municipalities and community groups coordinate sign-on bonuses, housing supports, mentorship, and community welcome packages to attract and retain family physicians, nurse practitioners and counsellors.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Recruitment and Retention Incentives
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health runs province-wide recruitment and retention for family physicians, nurse practitioners, and other primary care providers, offering sign-on bonuses, relocation assistance, and return-of-service incentives. Local zone recruiters coordinate site visits, community tours, and mentorship connections, and work with municipalities and community groups to provide welcome packages and help with housing and spousal employment, directly addressing access gaps in primary care and mental health.

resources.name: Cape Breton Healthcare Recruitment and Community Navigator
resources.description: The Cape Breton Partnership’s healthcare recruitment initiative supports the attraction and retention of family physicians, nurse practitioners, and allied health professionals by providing a dedicated community navigator who assists with housing searches, school placements, spousal employment, and settlement. Working with local municipalities, businesses, and Nova Scotia Health, they organize welcome packages, community introductions, and mentorship connections to ensure providers and their families are supported and remain in the region.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

resources.name: Recruitment Antigonish (Physician Recruitment and Retention)
resources.organization: Recruitment Antigonish (St. Martha’s Regional Hospital Foundation)
