resources.description: Recruitment Antigonish coordinates with community partners to attract and retain family physicians and other primary care providers, offering personalized community tours, welcome packages, and spousal/settlement support including housing and school navigation. The program partners with Nova Scotia Health to align sign-on and relocation incentives and pairs new clinicians with local mentors and hospital leaders to build lasting ties to the community.

solutions.text: Community-run Sliding-scale Counselling Fund: Establish a community-managed fund (supported by donations, municipal grants, and fundraisers) to subsidize short-term counselling for youth who face cost barriers to private therapy.

resources.name: Mental Health Counselling
resources.description: The Youth Project offers free counselling for 2SLGBTQIA+ youth, reducing cost barriers to timely mental health support. Services are sustained through community donations, grants, and fundraising, effectively operating as a community-managed subsidy that makes short-term counselling accessible when private therapy is unaffordable.

resources.name: Community Mental Health and Wellness Counselling
resources.description: North End Community Health Centre provides no-cost and low-barrier counselling to youth and families who face financial obstacles, ensuring short-term, timely support. Backed by donations, municipal/provincial funding, and community fundraising, the program functions like a community-managed subsidy that covers costs so youth do not have to pay private therapy rates.

resources.name: Counselling Program
resources.organization: Home of the Guardian Angel (Chebucto Family Centre)
resources.description: Chebucto Family Centre offers free and pay-what-you-can counselling for youth, parents, and families, directly addressing financial barriers to mental health services. The program is funded through donations, grants, and community fundraisers, allowing the centre to subsidize short-term counselling rather than requiring clients to pay full private therapy fees.

resources.name: Counselling and Support Services
resources.description: Every Woman’s Centre provides free, confidential counselling and support to women and girls, including youth, eliminating cost as a barrier to accessing short-term mental health care. Services are supported by grants, community donations, and fundraising, which together operate as a community-managed subsidy in place of private therapy fees.

solutions.text: Mobile Outreach Clinics and Pop-up Wellness Days: Operate periodic mobile clinics or pop-up wellness events in underserved neighbourhoods offering primary care checkups, mental health screening, crisis intervention, and information about local resources.

resources.name: Mobile Outreach Street Health (MOSH)
resources.description: MOSH operates mobile outreach nursing and pop-up clinics in Halifax, visiting shelters, encampments, and community sites to provide low-barrier primary health care, wound care, harm reduction supplies, and vaccinations. Staff include nurses and allied health providers who conduct basic health and mental health screening, offer crisis intervention when needed, and connect people to local resources, primary care providers, and social supports—directly aligning with mobile clinics and pop-up wellness events in underserved areas.

resources.name: Mobile Primary Care Clinics
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health runs periodic Mobile Primary Care Clinics that pop up in communities across the province to offer same-day primary care assessments, prescription refills, testing, and referrals for people without timely access to a family practice. These events frequently include navigation support to mental health and addictions services and provide information on local resources, functioning as rotating, low-barrier wellness days in underserved areas.

resources.name: Street Outreach and Mobile Health Services
resources.description: The Ally Centre of Cape Breton delivers street outreach and mobile health supports, including nurse-led pop-up clinics that provide primary care basics, harm reduction, STI/HIV/Hep C testing, and vaccinations in Sydney and surrounding communities. Staff provide mental health check-ins, crisis intervention, and resource navigation, linking people—especially underserved and at-risk populations—to local primary care, mental health, housing, and social services.

resources.name: Mental Health Mobile Crisis Team (MHMCT)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health, Mental Health and Addictions Program
resources.description: The provincial Mental Health Mobile Crisis Team offers 24/7 telephone support and, when appropriate, sends a mobile team of mental health clinicians for on-site crisis intervention in the community. The team conducts risk and mental health assessments, de-escalates crises, and provides information and referrals to local resources—functioning as a mobile, rapid-response component that complements pop-up wellness and outreach models.

solutions.text: Youth Navigation and Peer Advocacy Program: Train youth navigators and peer advocates to help peers schedule appointments, complete intake forms, follow up on care, and advocate with providers and schools to reduce drop-offs from the care pathway.

resources.name: Youth Health Centres
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s school-based Youth Health Centres provide confidential, youth-friendly navigation to health and mental health services across the province. Coordinators help students book appointments, complete referrals and consent/intake forms, and coordinate follow-up with families and providers. They also advocate within schools and the health system to reduce barriers and prevent drop-offs from care.
resources.address: 7 Mellor Avenue, Unit 5, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0E8

resources.name: Phoenix Centre for Youth
resources.description: The Phoenix Centre for Youth offers drop-in and outreach support that helps young people navigate health and mental health services. Staff and peer mentors assist with scheduling appointments, transportation and reminders, completing intake and benefits forms, and following up on care plans. They also advocate with providers, schools, and community partners to keep youth engaged in care.

resources.name: The Youth Project – Individual Support & System Navigation
resources.description: The Youth Project provides one-on-one support to 2SLGBTQIA+ youth across Nova Scotia, helping them access affirming health and mental health care. Staff and trained peer leaders assist with booking appointments, completing referrals and consent forms, and coordinating follow-up. They also advocate with schools and healthcare providers to ensure inclusive supports and reduce care drop-offs.

resources.name: School Settlement Services (SWIS) – Youth Navigation
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ School Settlement Services place settlement workers in schools to help newcomer youth and families navigate provincial health and mental health systems. They assist with registering for MSI, booking appointments, completing intake and consent forms (with language support), and coordinating follow-up. Workers also advocate with school staff and healthcare providers so students remain connected to needed care.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Peer Support Nova Scotia (Mental Health & Addictions)
resources.description: Peer Support Nova Scotia trains and employs peer support specialists, including youth and young adult peers, within Nova Scotia Health’s Mental Health and Addictions program. Peers help individuals prepare for and attend appointments, complete intake paperwork, set recovery goals, and navigate services. They also collaborate with providers and community partners to advocate for clients and maintain continuity of care.

solutions.text: Employer-Community Mental Health Partnerships: Local employers partner with community organizations to provide flexible scheduling for appointments, workplace mental health supports, and co-funded counselling hours for young employees and apprentices.

resources.name: Supported Employment (Nova Scotia Works – TEAM Work Cooperative)
resources.organization: TEAM Work Cooperative (Nova Scotia Works Halifax Peninsula)
resources.description: TEAM Work Cooperative’s Supported Employment program helps youth and adults, including apprentices and early‑career workers, secure and keep jobs by partnering directly with local employers. Staff coordinate flexible work arrangements around medical and counselling appointments and provide on‑the‑job coaching, while linking participants to community mental health services for short‑term counselling and ongoing supports. Employers receive guidance on accommodations and mental health practices that improve retention of young employees.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

resources.name: Onboarding Employer Support Services (OESS)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ OESS partners with Nova Scotia employers to recruit and retain newcomer youth and early‑career workers, offering workplace cultural training, policy guidance, and support plans that include flexible scheduling for health and settlement appointments. Through ISANS Wellness and counselling services, young employees can access short‑term, culturally responsive mental health supports, while employment specialists coordinate with managers to reduce work‑study‑health conflicts. Employers gain a direct connection to community clinicians and navigators who help address mental health barriers that affect attendance and performance.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Farm Family Support Center (We Talk. We Grow.)
resources.organization: Farm Safety Nova Scotia (Nova Scotia Federation of Agriculture)
resources.description: Farm Safety Nova Scotia operates the Farm Family Support Center, providing 24/7 confidential counselling and mental health navigation for farm owners, employees, apprentices, and their families across the province. Employers participate through their farm membership, effectively co‑funding counselling hours and crisis support delivered by community mental health professionals, while training like In the Know (with CMHA) equips supervisors to build supportive, flexible scheduling practices during peak stress periods. This employer‑community partnership brings immediate counselling access and workplace mental health supports to young workers in agriculture.
resources.address: 7 Atlantic Central Drive, East Mountain, NS B6L 2Z2

resources.name: ISET Employment & Training with Wije’winen Health Centre Supports
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s ISET Employment & Training program partners with local employers to place Indigenous youth and apprentices in jobs while coordinating flexible schedules that respect medical, counselling, and cultural commitments. Participants can access mental health and wellness services through the Centre’s Wije’winen Health Centre, with staff collaborating alongside employers to implement accommodations and on‑site supports that sustain work and learning. This integrated, community‑employer model improves retention by pairing culturally safe counselling with practical workplace adjustments.

solutions.text: Community Digital Resource Directory: Maintain an up-to-date, searchable online and print directory of local primary care providers, youth mental health services, crisis lines, peer supports, and how to access them (including languages and eligibility).

resources.name: 211 Nova Scotia – Online Community and Social Services Directory
resources.description: 211 Nova Scotia maintains a continuously updated, searchable online directory of community and government services across the province, including primary care options, youth mental health services, crisis lines, and peer supports. The listings include how to access services, eligibility criteria, hours, and language availability, and the service is accessible online and via 24/7 phone/text to help residents navigate local resources.

resources.name: Find Services (Nova Scotia Health Service and Facility Directory)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Find Services directory is a province-wide, searchable listing of health services and facilities, including primary care clinics, urgent treatment centres, emergency departments, and mental health and addictions services. Each entry provides service descriptions, access steps (walk-in, referral, self-referral), hours, locations, and contacts, helping people identify the right local option and how to use it.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: Help NS (Mental Health & Addictions Service Navigator)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health – Mental Health and Addictions Program
resources.description: Help NS is Nova Scotia Health’s dedicated digital navigator for mental health and addictions, offering a searchable, province-wide directory of supports for all ages with a focus on youth pathways. It provides clear information on eligibility, how to access services (self-referral, central intake, walk-in, virtual), crisis line contacts, and links to community and peer supports, ensuring residents can quickly find appropriate local care.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: Find a Social Worker (Private Practice Directory)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Social Workers
resources.description: The Nova Scotia College of Social Workers maintains a searchable directory of registered private-practice social workers across the province, many specializing in youth mental health. Listings include practice areas, languages, locations (in-person/virtual), and contact details, enabling residents to identify appropriate counselling and mental health supports and understand how to access them.
resources.address: 1888 Brunswick Street, Suite 700, Halifax, NS B3J 3J8

solutions.text: Stigma-Reduction Campaigns Led by Youth: Fund and support youth-led public education campaigns, storytelling projects and arts events that normalize help-seeking, share lived experience, and highlight available local services.

resources.name: Jack.org Dalhousie University Chapter
resources.description: This student-led chapter organizes Jack Talks (youth-delivered mental health presentations), on-campus campaigns, and storytelling events that normalize help-seeking, challenge stigma, and share lived experience. Their activities highlight local supports by directing peers to Dalhousie Student Health & Wellness, provincial crisis lines, and community services, making mental health resources more visible and approachable.

resources.name: Jack.org Acadia University Chapter
resources.description: Led by Acadia students, this chapter runs youth-driven mental health awareness campaigns, Jack Talks, and events during Mental Health Week that encourage open dialogue and help-seeking. They host resource-sharing activities and speaker sessions that connect youth to local options such as the Acadia Student Resource Centre, regional health services in the Annapolis Valley, and national helplines.

resources.name: The Spot (Youth Arts Drop-In at Halifax Central Library)
resources.organization: Youth Art Connection in partnership with Halifax Public Libraries
resources.description: The Spot is a free, youth-led arts drop-in where young people create music, visual art, zines, and performances that share lived experience and promote mental wellness. Public showcases and library-based events reduce stigma and normalize help-seeking, while Youth Art Connection facilitators and library staff connect participants and audiences to local mental health and community services.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: MacPhee Centre for Creative Learning – Youth-Led Arts Programs
resources.description: The MacPhee Centre co-designs creative programs with youth and hosts public exhibitions, zines, and performances that openly address mental health, identity, and belonging. These youth-led storytelling and arts events reduce stigma and include resource-sharing that points participants toward local counselling, peer supports, and community services across HRM and Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Phoenix Youth Programs – Arts and Advocacy Initiatives
resources.description: Phoenix supports youth to create and publicly share art, media, and personal narratives about mental health and recovery through showcases and community events. These youth-led storytelling activities reduce stigma, normalize help-seeking, and directly connect both participants and audiences to Phoenix’s counselling, housing, and mental health navigation services and to partner agencies.

solutions.text: Integrated Wellness Hubs with Holistic Supports: Convert or designate community spaces where primary care, mental health counselling, addiction services, housing and employment supports coordinate care and warm referrals under one roof.

resources.name: North End Community Health Centre
resources.description: A community-based primary care clinic that integrates family medicine, mental health counselling, harm reduction and addictions supports, and social work in one location. The centre’s team (including MOSH outreach) provides housing navigation and income/employment support through onsite case management and coordinated, warm referrals to partner agencies, enabling seamless wraparound care under one roof.

resources.name: Phoenix Centre for Youth (including Phoenix Youth Health Clinic)
resources.description: A drop-in hub for youth that combines primary healthcare (through an onsite youth health clinic), mental health and addictions counselling, and practical supports like identification, income assistance, and basic needs. Housing support workers and employment/education staff coordinate care plans and make warm referrals from the same space, helping young people stabilize, access work or school, and maintain wellness.

resources.name: Our Health Centre (Chester Community Health Hub)
resources.description: A collaborative community health hub that co-locates family physicians/nurse practitioners with Nova Scotia Health mental health and addictions services, public health, and allied health providers. The centre hosts community partners for social, housing, and employment navigation and uses shared care planning and warm handoffs so residents can access primary care, counselling, addiction supports, and practical life supports in one place.

resources.name: Ally Centre of Cape Breton
resources.description: A harm-reduction and health hub offering low-barrier primary care clinics, STI testing, and mental health/addictions supports alongside outreach, case management, and peer services. Staff provide housing stabilization support and connect participants to education and employment programs through onsite navigation and warm referrals, integrating wellness and social determinants of health under one roof for people in Sydney and surrounding communities.

solutions.text: Partnerships with Post-secondary Health Programs: Partner with regional universities, colleges and training programs to place nurse practitioner, social work and psychology students in supervised community clinics to expand access while offering learning opportunities.

resources.name: Dalhousie Social Work Community Clinic
resources.organization: Dalhousie University School of Social Work
resources.description: A partnership between Dalhousie University’s School of Social Work and Veith House, this community clinic places Master of Social Work students in supervised practice to deliver free counselling, case management, and system navigation. By embedding student clinicians in a community setting under registered social workers’ supervision, the clinic expands access to mental health and social care for youth and families while providing hands-on training.

resources.name: North End Community Health Centre
resources.description: NECHC is a community health centre that serves residents of Halifax’s North End with primary care, mental health, and outreach services. As a teaching site, it partners with regional post-secondary programs (including Dalhousie University’s Nurse Practitioner and Social Work programs) to place supervised learners in its clinics and mobile/outreach services, increasing appointment capacity and timely access for underserved and youth populations.

resources.name: Bayers Road Community Mental Health & Addictions Clinic
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health, Mental Health & Addictions Program (Central Zone)
resources.description: This outpatient clinic provides assessment, therapy, and group programs for mental health and addictions in Halifax. In partnership with Dalhousie University and other post-secondary institutions, the clinic hosts clinical psychology residents/practicum students and social work interns who deliver services under licensed supervision, which increases service capacity and shortens wait times for community mental health care.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 109, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: IWK Mental Health & Addictions Program
resources.description: IWK provides hospital- and community-based mental health and addictions care for children, youth, and families across Nova Scotia. In collaboration with Dalhousie University and affiliated post-secondary programs, IWK places clinical psychology residents and social work students within supervised interdisciplinary teams at its clinics, expanding youth-focused counselling and assessment while offering high-quality training.

solutions.text: Transportation and childcare assistance for appointments: Create community volunteer driver programs, bus-pass subsidies and on-site childcare options so youth and families can attend health and mental health appointments without logistical barriers.

resources.name: Wheels of Hope (Transportation Services)
resources.description: The Canadian Cancer Society’s Wheels of Hope provides volunteer driver transportation for people, including youth and families, to get to and from medical and cancer-related appointments across Nova Scotia. By offering door-to-door rides and coordinating travel logistics, the program removes transportation barriers so clients can reliably attend primary care, specialist, and mental health/psychosocial oncology appointments.
resources.address: 5826 South Street, Suite 1, Halifax, NS B3H 1S6

resources.name: Low Income Transit Pass Program
resources.description: Halifax Transit offers a 50% discounted monthly bus pass to eligible low-income residents, reducing the cost of travel for youth and families. This subsidy helps people reliably reach health and mental health appointments at clinics, the IWK, and community providers by removing the financial barrier to public transit.

resources.name: Family Support and Early Years Programs
resources.description: The North Grove is a family resource centre that provides on-site child-minding through its Early Years and Family Support programs so parents can attend programs, meet with visiting health partners, or connect with counseling and navigation services at the centre. Staff can also provide bus tickets and help families arrange and get to off-site medical and mental health appointments, reducing transportation and childcare barriers to care.

resources.name: Phoenix Centre for Youth
resources.description: Phoenix Centre for Youth offers drop-in support, case management, and mental health navigation for youth ages 16–24, including practical help such as bus tickets, accompaniment, and reminders to attend medical and counseling appointments. By removing transportation barriers and supporting youths’ logistics around care, Phoenix helps young people access primary care, community mental health, and specialized services.

resources.name: Childminding and Settlement Supports
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides on-site childminding so newcomer parents can attend health navigation meetings, mental health workshops, and settlement appointments at the centre. ISANS also helps eligible clients with bus passes or tickets and appointment coordination, enabling newcomer youth and families to reach primary care and mental health services without transportation or childcare barriers.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Culturally Safe and Indigenous-led Supports: Support local Indigenous and cultural organizations to deliver culturally appropriate mental health services, traditional healing circles and liaison roles to ensure services are accessible and trusted.

resources.name: Mi'kmaw Native Friendship Centre – Health & Wellness Programs
resources.description: The Mi'kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Health & Wellness programs provide culturally grounded mental health supports for urban Indigenous youth and families, including access to Elders, smudging and talking/healing circles, and land‑based activities. As an Indigenous-led hub, the Centre delivers services in a Mi’kmaw cultural context and partners with clinics to offer trauma‑informed counselling and addictions support that youth can trust. Staff also act as liaisons and navigators, helping clients access mainstream mental health services and reduce wait‑time barriers.

resources.name: Native Council of Nova Scotia – Health and Social Programs
resources.description: The Native Council of Nova Scotia’s Health and Social Programs support off‑reserve and non‑status Indigenous people with culturally appropriate mental wellness services, harm‑reduction supports, and referrals. Guided by Elders and Indigenous staff, the Council hosts culture‑based wellness workshops and circles while connecting youth and families to traditional healers when requested. Program coordinators also serve as liaisons with provincial services to coordinate care and advocate for culturally safe access.
resources.address: 129 Truro Heights Road, Truro, NS B6L 1X1

resources.name: The Confederacy of Mainland Mi’kmaq – Mental Wellness & Cultural Support
resources.description: The Confederacy of Mainland Mi’kmaq delivers community‑based Mental Wellness and Cultural Support services across member Mi’kmaw communities, blending counselling with Elder support, drumming, and healing circles. Their Indigenous‑led team partners with local health centres to provide trauma‑informed, land‑based, and language‑inclusive approaches to mental health and addictions. CMM also trains service providers in cultural safety and helps clients navigate provincial systems to ensure respectful, timely care.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health – Indigenous Patient Navigator Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Indigenous Patient Navigator Program provides Mi’kmaw and Indigenous patient navigators who support clients in accessing mental health and addictions care across the province. Navigators coordinate appointments, advocate for cultural safety, and connect patients with Elders and traditional practices during hospital or community‑based care. The program acts as a liaison between Indigenous communities and mainstream services to reduce barriers, build trust, and shorten pathways to support.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

obstacles.title: Underdeveloped entrepreneurship and scale-up ecosystem
obstacles.description: Early-stage capital, mentorship, commercialization supports, and access to procurement are uneven, slowing startup creation and the growth of youth-led firms.

solutions.text: Community Mentorship Network: Create a local roster of volunteer mentors — entrepreneurs, retired executives, tradespeople — offering regular office hours, peer circles, and one-on-one coaching tailored to youth-led startups.

resources.name: Volta Mentors
resources.description: Volta operates a community of volunteer mentors—founders, investors, and seasoned executives—who hold regular office hours, workshops, and one-on-one advisory sessions for early-stage founders. Youth-led startups can book mentor office hours, join peer founder circles through Volta programming, and receive tailored coaching to validate ideas, build traction, and prepare for funding.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Business Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Business Mentorship Program matches newcomer and immigrant entrepreneurs with volunteer business mentors for structured, one-on-one coaching and goal setting over several months. The program convenes regular check-ins and group learning sessions, creating peer support circles and practical office hours that help youth and early-stage founders build networks, refine business models, and navigate Nova Scotia’s market.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Startup Yard Incubator
resources.description: Startup Yard at COVE provides ocean-technology startups with access to a roster of experienced mentors and Entrepreneurs-in-Residence who hold regular office hours and deliver one-on-one coaching. Cohort-based programming creates peer founder circles and tailored commercialization support—ideal for youth-led ocean and blue-economy ventures seeking market validation and partnerships.

resources.name: Advisory Services and Mentorship
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED offers ongoing one-on-one advisory sessions with experienced entrepreneurs and facilitators, plus scheduled office hours and cohort-based programs that foster peer learning circles. These services deliver practical coaching, accountability, and connections tailored to early-stage and youth-led startups across sectors.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Business Advisory & Mentorship
resources.description: Ulnooweg provides Indigenous entrepreneurs with personalized business advisory services, connecting clients to a network of volunteer mentors, industry experts, and peer circles across Atlantic Canada. Through regular check-ins, coaching sessions, and workshops, youth-led and early-stage Indigenous ventures receive tailored guidance on planning, financing, and scaling.
resources.address: 172 Truro Heights Road, Truro Heights, NS B6L 1X1

solutions.text: Community Seed Microfund: Establish a small, locally governed microgrant or microloan fund (crowdfunded and sustained by donations) to finance prototypes, pilot projects, and early customer discovery for youth-led ventures.

resources.name: Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta Cohort is a seed funding program that provides $25,000 investments and wraparound mentorship to early-stage Atlantic Canadian startups. It operates like a community seed fund by supporting founders (including youth-led teams) to build prototypes, run pilot projects, and validate early customer demand before larger capital. Funding is paired with programming, workspace access, and connections to mentors and investors to accelerate early customer discovery.

resources.name: Spark Nova Scotia
resources.description: Spark Nova Scotia awards non-dilutive seed funding to idea-stage and early-stage founders across the province to help them develop MVPs, test prototypes, and conduct initial market validation. The program functions as a community-driven seed grant competition that de-risks early experimentation for emerging startups, including youth-led ventures, and connects them with mentors and commercialization supports. Awards are regionally delivered to expand access to early capital outside major urban centers.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 1101, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

resources.name: ISANS Immigrant Business Loan Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides microloans and business advisory support to newcomer entrepreneurs to help finance startup costs, prototypes, initial inventory, and early customer discovery. This microfinance approach fills a critical early capital gap for youth and first-time founders, pairing financing with coaching and mentorship to increase the likelihood of successful pilots and market entry. Loans are community-oriented and designed to be accessible for early-stage ventures.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: NSCC Make Way Entrepreneurship Fund
resources.description: The NSCC Make Way Entrepreneurship Fund provides small, donor-supported microgrants to NSCC students to kickstart ventures, build prototypes, and run pilot projects. By offering early, flexible capital alongside campus-based mentorship and entrepreneurial training, the fund enables youth-led teams to test ideas and engage in early customer discovery before pursuing larger financing. This community-backed model mirrors a local seed microfund sustained by philanthropy.

solutions.text: Affordable Co‑working and Maker Spaces: Convert underused community buildings into low-cost co‑working hubs with shared office infrastructure, workshops and prototyping equipment, and startup support services.

resources.name: Volta
resources.description: Volta is Atlantic Canada’s startup hub in downtown Halifax offering affordable co-working desks, private offices, meeting rooms, and shared office infrastructure for early-stage companies. It delivers mentorship, workshops, and connections to investors and procurement partners that fill key gaps in commercialization support. By lowering space and infrastructure costs and providing wraparound startup services, Volta advances accessible co-working and entrepreneurship for young founders.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE operates within COVE’s collaborative ocean-tech campus, providing shared offices, labs, workshops, and a machine shop that enable rapid prototyping and testing on the Dartmouth waterfront. The program offers mentorship, commercialization guidance, and direct connections to industry and procurement pathways in the ocean economy. By giving founders access to specialized maker infrastructure and startup support services at a single, affordable site, it removes barriers to building and scaling new ventures.

resources.name: The Hub Central Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Hub Central Nova Scotia is a community-operated co-working space in downtown Truro offering low-cost desks, meeting rooms, and shared office amenities for freelancers, startups, and non-profits. It convenes peer mentorship, training events, and links to regional small-business support organizations that help early-stage founders navigate growth. By transforming main-street space into an accessible entrepreneurship hub, it delivers affordable co-working and community-based support services for youth-led ventures.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library & Makerspace
resources.description: The Halifax Tool Library operates a community makerspace and tool-lending service that provides affordable access to workshops, fabrication tools, and prototyping equipment. Members can borrow tools, use shared shop space, and take skills-based classes to build and test product ideas without the capital expense of owning equipment. This shared maker infrastructure complements the co-working ecosystem by enabling early-stage entrepreneurs and trades-oriented youth to prototype and iterate quickly at low cost.

solutions.text: Municipal Procurement Set‑Asides: Work with municipal councils to create streamlined procurement tracks or set-asides for youth-led and local small businesses to supply services and goods to towns and counties.

resources.name: Social Procurement Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Social Procurement Program embeds social value into municipal purchasing by recognizing and encouraging bids from local small and diverse suppliers, including youth-led enterprises. The program uses evaluation criteria that award points for local economic impact and supplier diversity, hosts vendor information sessions to simplify access, and, where permitted by trade agreements, employs targeted competitions or set-asides (e.g., for Indigenous and diverse suppliers) and unbundles contracts to sizes accessible to startups and small firms.

resources.name: Social Value Procurement Policy
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Municipality’s Social Value Procurement Policy integrates community benefit and local economic development goals into purchasing, creating clearer pathways for local small businesses to compete for municipal work. Through social value weighting, supplier outreach, and opportunities sized for small vendors—and by using set-asides permitted under trade agreements for diverse suppliers—the policy helps youth-led and early-stage firms enter municipal supply chains.

resources.name: Social Procurement Strategy
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings’ Social Procurement Strategy leverages municipal buying to grow local capacity by prioritizing bids that deliver community benefits and by engaging small, locally owned suppliers. The strategy introduces simplified, small-value competitions, encourages unbundling of larger contracts, and recognizes diverse and social enterprises—practical mechanisms that open municipal opportunities to youth-led startups and scaling small businesses across the county.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

solutions.text: Anchor Institution Supplier Programs: Organize local hospitals, universities and school boards to run supplier-development initiatives that connect youth-led firms to procurement opportunities, pilot contracts and mentorship.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Innovation Hub
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Health Innovation Hub partners with startups, including youth-led ventures, to pilot health technologies and services within hospital settings across the province. Through innovation-friendly procurement pathways, test/pilot projects, and mentorship from clinicians and health system leaders, the Hub helps firms validate solutions and navigate purchasing processes. This directly connects emerging companies to real procurement opportunities and de-risks first contracts with a major anchor institution.

resources.name: Province of Nova Scotia Reverse Trade Show (Public Sector Buyers)
resources.description: This annual supplier-development event brings together procurement teams from universities, school boards, health authorities, municipalities, and provincial departments to meet suppliers, including youth-led firms and student-founded startups. It offers supplier education, one-on-one matchmaking with buyers, and guidance on bidding and vendor qualification, creating pathways to pilot projects and contracts. By coordinating multiple anchor institutions in one forum, it directly implements an anchor-based supplier-development approach.

resources.name: Irving Shipbuilding Supplier Development & Supply Chain Program
resources.description: Irving Shipbuilding actively develops Nova Scotia’s supplier base for the National Shipbuilding Strategy through supplier onboarding, capability assessments, and outreach to local SMEs and startups. The program connects firms to RFQs and pilot work packages, offers mentorship from procurement and engineering teams, and helps companies meet quality and compliance requirements to scale within a major anchor’s supply chain. This creates tangible procurement pathways and learning opportunities for youth-led firms in advanced manufacturing and ocean industries.

resources.name: COVE Buyer Engagement, Supply Chain Events, and Pilot Demonstrations
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE convenes anchor buyers (e.g., Royal Canadian Navy, Port of Halifax, offshore energy operators, and universities) with ocean-tech SMEs and startups through industry days, buyer–supplier roundtables, and on-water demonstration opportunities. These activities provide mentorship from anchor partners, help firms refine offerings to procurement needs, and enable pilot projects that de-risk adoption. The result is a practical supplier-development pathway that connects youth-led ocean-tech companies to contracting and scale-up opportunities with major regional anchors.

solutions.text: Volunteer Startup Clinics: Host regular pop-up clinics staffed by volunteer lawyers, accountants, marketers and product experts who provide short, practical advice to early-stage founders.

resources.name: Volta Office Hours
resources.description: Volta hosts recurring Office Hours where early-stage founders can book short, focused one-on-one meetings with volunteer experts from law, accounting, marketing, product, and sales. These pop-up style clinics are offered in partnership with local professional firms and mentors who donate their time to provide practical, actionable advice, helping startups validate ideas, manage risk, and navigate growth. This directly implements the solution by delivering regular, no-cost access to specialized expertise for Nova Scotia founders.

resources.name: Advisory Clinics and Ask-an-Expert Sessions
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business runs ongoing advisory clinics and ask-an-expert sessions where lawyers, accountants, marketers, and seasoned entrepreneurs volunteer time to meet with women and gender-diverse founders for brief, practical consultations. These pop-up clinics provide targeted guidance on incorporation, contracts, bookkeeping, branding, and go-to-market strategy, enabling early-stage ventures to make informed decisions quickly. The program embodies the volunteer startup clinic model by mobilizing professional expertise for short, accessible appointments.

resources.name: SMUEC Ask the Experts and Pro Bono Startup Clinics
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre (SMUEC) organizes recurring ask-the-expert and pro bono startup clinics where partner lawyers, accountants, and marketing/product professionals volunteer to deliver short, one-on-one consultations to founders. These sessions focus on immediate challenges like company structure, IP considerations, financial setup, and customer discovery, giving entrepreneurs clear next steps. By convening volunteer professional service providers for quick advisory meetings, SMUEC directly implements the volunteer startup clinic approach.

resources.name: CEED Ask-an-Expert Business Clinics
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED offers periodic ask-an-expert business clinics where volunteer professionals from legal, accounting, marketing, and product backgrounds provide brief, tactical consultations to new and growing entrepreneurs. These drop-in and bookable sessions help founders address pressing questions—such as basic contracts, tax setup, pricing, and customer validation—without cost barriers. The format mirrors pop-up volunteer clinics, delivering rapid, practical advice that strengthens Nova Scotia’s early-stage startup ecosystem.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Community Accelerator / Bootcamp: Run a local accelerator focused on regional strengths (ocean tech, clean energy, creative industries) offering cohort training, mentor matching and a community demo day.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard is an ocean-technology accelerator that runs cohort-based programming for early-stage companies, offering intensive workshops, prototyping support, and structured mentor matching with leaders from the marine industries. The program hosts community-facing demo and pitch days at COVE that connect founders with investors, customers, and procurement partners, directly aligning with the accelerator/bootcamp model focused on Nova Scotia’s ocean-tech strength.

resources.name: Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta Cohort selects promising Atlantic Canadian startups for an accelerator-style program providing founder education, mentorship, and weekly coaching. Each cohort culminates in a public pitch event where companies present to investors and the community for funding and support, creating a clear demo-day pathway that strengthens the local scale-up ecosystem.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 130, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic
resources.organization: Creative Destruction Lab (hosted at Dalhousie University, Rowe School of Business)
resources.description: CDL-Atlantic runs objective-based, cohort accelerators in streams such as Oceans, Prime, and Energy, matching ventures with a curated roster of experienced entrepreneurs, scientists, and investors. Teams progress through structured sessions and milestones, culminating in investor-facing presentations and showcases, directly addressing mentorship, commercialization, and capital access gaps for Nova Scotia startups.

resources.name: Accelerate Program
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia’s Accelerate is a milestone-driven accelerator for early-stage technology companies in sectors including oceans and clean tech. Cohorts receive training workshops, mentor matching, and non-dilutive support, and participate in program showcases and investor connections that function like demo days to speed commercialization and scale-up in the province.

solutions.text: Investor‑Readiness Workshops: Deliver regular workshops and pitch-practice sessions run by local investors and experienced founders to improve business plans, financials and investor outreach skills.

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic
resources.organization: Creative Destruction Lab (CDL) at the Rowe School of Business, Dalhousie University
resources.description: CDL-Atlantic runs a multi-month, objectives-based program where startups work directly with angel investors and successful founders to become investment-ready. Ventures receive rigorous feedback on business models, financial projections, and fundraising strategies, and participate in pitch coaching and practice sessions ahead of investor meetings. The program culminates in targeted investor exposure, improving founders’ outreach skills and confidence.
resources.address: Rowe School of Business, 6100 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.description: Start-Up Yard is COVE’s ocean-technology incubator offering investor-readiness workshops, founder roundtables, and structured pitch-practice sessions with local ocean-industry executives, angels, and experienced entrepreneurs. Companies refine their business plans, pricing and unit economics, and investment materials with hands-on coaching. The program includes investor days and tailored introductions that strengthen founders’ outreach and fundraising skills.

resources.name: CEED Startup Program
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED’s cohort-based Startup Program delivers practical workshops on business model design, financial planning, and capital readiness, led by Entrepreneurs-in-Residence and guest mentors from the local investor and founder community. Participants develop and rehearse investor pitches, receive detailed feedback on decks and financials, and learn effective investor outreach tactics. This hands-on approach accelerates investor readiness and improves fundraising outcomes.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Volta Academy
resources.description: Volta Academy is a workshop series that helps founders strengthen business plans, financial projections, and fundraising narratives through sessions facilitated by experienced founders and local investors. The program includes pitch-practice labs, office hours, and feedback cycles to refine decks and delivery. It culminates in opportunities to pitch to the community and investor networks, building confidence and improving investor outreach.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

resources.name: Accelerate Program
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business’s Accelerate Program supports women-identifying founders with investment-readiness workshops focused on financials, growth planning, and capital strategy. Participants practice their pitches with experienced founders and local investors who provide direct feedback on clarity, traction, and ask. The program also guides outreach planning and data room preparation to improve fundraising efficiency.
resources.address: 166 Bedford Highway, Rosaria Student Centre, Room 202, Halifax, NS B3M 2J6

solutions.text: Entrepreneurship in Schools and Colleges: Partner schools, community colleges and universities to integrate hands-on entrepreneurship projects, internships with local startups, and youth-run student ventures.

resources.name: Dal Innovates
resources.organization: Dalhousie University (Norman Newman Centre for Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: Dal Innovates integrates entrepreneurship into undergraduate and graduate education through venture-building bootcamps, customer discovery programs, and industry-led challenges connected to courses and research. Students form teams to build real ventures, receive mentorship from local founders and investors, and connect to co-op and internship opportunities with Halifax startups—providing hands-on commercialization experience and early-stage support.

resources.name: Spark Zone (Nova Scotia Sandbox)
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre (lead for the Spark Zone)
resources.description: The Spark Zone, led by Saint Mary’s University with partner institutions (NSCC, NSCAD University, and Mount Saint Vincent University), embeds hands-on entrepreneurship through innovation challenges, startup sprints, and mentor-led incubator programming. Students launch and operate ventures, work on projects for local SMEs, and access internships and placements with partner startups—linking classroom learning to real commercialization pathways.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Nova Scotia Sandbox)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs is the Dalhousie Faculty of Computer Science sandbox that connects students with tech startups through hackathons, applied projects, and an incubator where student teams build and test real products. It collaborates with courses and capstones and facilitates mentorship and co-op/internship pathways with Halifax’s tech ecosystem, giving students hands-on commercialization experience.

resources.name: Launchbox (Acadia Entrepreneurship Centre)
resources.description: Launchbox integrates entrepreneurship into Acadia University through workshops embedded in classes, venture challenges with local businesses, and a student incubator that supports youth-run ventures. The program pairs students with mentors and internship opportunities across the Annapolis Valley, providing practical commercialization supports and networks outside Halifax.

resources.name: Cultiv8 Innovation Sandbox
resources.description: Cultiv8 embeds entrepreneurship within the Dalhousie Faculty of Agriculture by engaging students in agri-food innovation challenges, prototyping, and student-run ventures linked to regional producers. The sandbox partners with courses and clubs, arranges internships with local agri-tech startups and farms, and offers mentorship and pre-seed support tailored to rural founders.
resources.address: 62 Cumming Drive, Bible Hill, NS B2N 5E3

solutions.text: Community Demo Days and Pitch Competitions: Organize frequent, low-barrier showcase events where youth-led teams present prototypes to the public, local investors and civic leaders to build visibility and feedback.

resources.name: Volta Cohort Pitch Competitions and Community Showcases
resources.description: Volta runs recurring pitch competitions and showcase nights where early-stage and youth-led teams present prototypes to an audience of investors, mentors, and civic and industry leaders. These low-barrier events provide public visibility, real-time feedback, and potential funding introductions, directly implementing community demo days and pitch formats to strengthen Nova Scotia’s startup pipeline.

resources.name: CEED Pitch Competitions and Program Demo Days
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: The Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED) hosts regular pitch nights and cohort Demo Days where founders, including youth and student teams, showcase early prototypes to the public, mentors, and funders. These events are designed to be accessible entry points, offering feedback from judges and community stakeholders and building visibility for emerging ventures across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Pitch Nights and Community Showcases
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic regularly organizes open pitch nights and showcase events in rural hubs where youth-led and early-stage teams demo products to local investors, municipal leaders, and community partners. These gatherings provide low-barrier exposure, feedback, and networking that connect founders with mentorship and capital, strengthening Nova Scotia’s broader innovation ecosystem.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs DemoCamp Halifax and Student Showcases
resources.organization: ShiftKey Labs, Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs at Dalhousie University hosts DemoCamp Halifax and student showcase events where learners and youth-led teams present working prototypes to the public, industry mentors, and investors. These sessions are purposely low-barrier and feedback-oriented, giving emerging entrepreneurs visibility, constructive critique, and connections that help move ideas toward commercialization.

resources.name: SMUEC RBC Student Pitch Competition and Venture Demo Days
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre (SMUEC) runs pitch competitions and program Demo Days (including the RBC Student Pitch Competition) where student and youth-led teams publicly present ventures to investors, mentors, and civic leaders. These events create accessible platforms for feedback, validation, and exposure, directly supporting early-stage entrepreneurs in Nova Scotia to refine and scale their ideas.

solutions.text: Shared Equipment and Resource Library: Create a community-run inventory of specialized tools, lab time, software licenses and business resources that startups can borrow to reduce upfront costs.

resources.name: Startup Yard at COVE
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE) in partnership with Invest Nova Scotia
resources.description: An ocean-technology incubator that provides shared prototyping labs, electronics benches, machine shop access, high-bay workshop space, and on-water testing infrastructure. Startups access equipment, work bays, and common software and meeting facilities on a shared basis, functioning as a resource library that lowers upfront capital costs and accelerates commercialization.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Yarmouth Makerspace
resources.description: IGNITE operates community makerspaces that give entrepreneurs access to 3D printers, laser cutters, electronics benches, and collaborative work areas. Members can book equipment, space, and technical support instead of purchasing their own, acting as a shared resource library that reduces prototyping costs and speeds product development for early-stage companies.

resources.name: Perennia Innovation Centre (Food & Beverage Pilot Facility)
resources.description: A provincially supported pilot plant and lab that rents time on specialized food processing equipment, test kitchens, and analytical laboratories to startups and scale-ups. Companies can book equipment, lab time, and technical staff as needed, operating as a shared equipment library that eliminates large capital purchases during early growth.
resources.address: 75 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: Halifax Central Library Creators’ Labs and Studios
resources.description: Public creation spaces offering bookable 3D printers, sewing machines, audio/video recording studios, digitization gear, and digital media workstations with professional software. Entrepreneurs can prototype products, produce marketing assets, and access specialized tools without owning them, serving as a shared resource library that lowers barriers for early-stage ventures.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Verschuren Centre – Pilot Facilities & Shared Labs
resources.organization: Verschuren Centre for Sustainability in Energy and the Environment
resources.description: An applied research and commercialization centre providing access to shared pilot-scale biomanufacturing, materials, and clean-tech laboratories, along with specialized analytical equipment and technical staff. Startups can rent lab time, equipment, and process development support on demand, replacing large upfront capital expenditures with pay-as-you-need access.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

solutions.text: Retiree and Alumni Engagement Program: Mobilize retired professionals and university alumni as mentors, advisors or small-scale angel investors through structured programs and reverse-mentoring opportunities.

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic
resources.organization: Creative Destruction Lab (hosted at Dalhousie University, Rowe School of Business)
resources.description: CDL–Atlantic at Dalhousie University is a mentorship-driven program that pairs early-stage tech ventures with a curated group of Fellows, Associates, and Advisors—many of whom are retired executives, seasoned entrepreneurs, and alumni investors. Through structured goal-setting sessions and ongoing advisory meetings, these mentors provide strategic guidance and often make small-scale angel investments, while also engaging in reverse-mentoring by learning from young founders about emerging technologies and markets.
resources.address: Rowe Management Building, 6100 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: SMU Mentoring (Ten Thousand Coffees)
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University’s SMU Mentoring program uses the Ten Thousand Coffees platform to match students and recent grads with alumni mentors, including retired professionals and founders, for career and entrepreneurship guidance. The structured matching and conversation guides foster advisory relationships and two-way learning—creating reverse‑mentoring opportunities where experienced alumni learn from youth about new technologies, markets, and startup culture.

resources.name: CEED Advisory Services & Mentor Network
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED connects aspiring and early-stage founders with a network of volunteer advisors and mentors that includes retired executives, seasoned entrepreneurs, and alumni of Nova Scotia’s startup ecosystem. Through structured advisory sessions, accelerator-style programming, and mentorship circles, these experts provide hands-on guidance and investor readiness support—often opening doors to small-scale angel capital and facilitating reverse‑mentoring dialogues with youth-led ventures.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Invest Nova Scotia – Accelerate Program and Mentor Network
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia’s startup programming pairs founders with a mentor network of experienced entrepreneurs, retired industry leaders, and alumni of successful Atlantic Canadian startups. Mentors provide structured guidance on commercialization, scaling, and capital strategy, and frequently connect teams to early-stage angel investors—while reverse‑mentoring occurs as seasoned advisors gain fresh insights from youth-led companies in new sectors.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

resources.name: Halifax Partnership Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program links young talent and newcomers—including student founders and recent grads—with volunteer Connectors drawn from the local business community, many of whom are retired professionals and university alumni. Through structured, one‑on‑one meetings and warm introductions, Connectors advise on opportunities, markets, and procurement pathways, and often become ongoing mentors—creating reciprocal learning and reverse‑mentoring as they engage with emerging industries and youth-led ventures.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Inclusive Youth Entrepreneurship Supports: Design targeted training, peer networks and microgrants for Indigenous, racialized, immigrant and rural youth to remove systemic barriers and grow diverse founders.

resources.name: Business Is Jammin’ (BIJ)
resources.description: Business Is Jammin’ is the youth initiative of the Black Business Initiative that delivers entrepreneurship education, mentorship and experiential learning for Black youth across Nova Scotia. BIJ runs camps, after‑school programs and pitch competitions that pair skill-building with coaching and small seed awards, and connects participants to BBI advisors and financing as they grow ventures. This directly tackles systemic barriers by creating culturally relevant peer networks and early capital pathways for racialized youth founders.
resources.address: 1741 Brunswick Street, Suite 600, Halifax, NS B3J 3X8

resources.name: ISANS Business Services for Immigrant Entrepreneurs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides newcomer youth and adults with entrepreneurship training workshops, one‑on‑one business counselling, and market‑readiness programs to launch and grow businesses in Nova Scotia. The program builds peer networks through cohort-based courses and networking events, and helps clients access startup financing and microloans through partner credit unions and community lenders. These supports reduce barriers immigrant youth face in navigating regulations, markets and early-stage capital.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: CEED LEAP Program
resources.description: LEAP is CEED’s entry-level, cohort-based entrepreneurship training for idea- to early-stage founders, including youth and underrepresented groups, delivered through facilitated sessions, mentoring and hands-on business planning. Participants gain access to CEED’s entrepreneur community, coaches and events, and can apply to CEED’s Microloan Program for early capital to test and scale. This blend of targeted training, peer networks and micro-financing strengthens Nova Scotia’s startup pipeline for diverse young founders.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: IGNITE Youth Entrepreneurship Programming
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic engages rural high school and post-secondary students with workshops, hackathons, mentorship and access to makerspaces in its hubs, building practical startup skills close to home. It convenes peer networks of rural innovators and partners on pitch events such as Invest Nova Scotia’s Spark competition that award non-dilutive seed funding to early-stage teams. These activities help rural youth overcome distance and capital gaps through training, community and micro-grant opportunities.

resources.name: RBC Alliance of Young Women Entrepreneurs (AYWE)
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: AYWE is a cohort-based program that supports women aged 19–39 with entrepreneurship training, mentorship and a strong peer network across Nova Scotia. It emphasizes inclusive access for racialized, newcomer and rural participants through hybrid delivery and tailored advising, and connects founders to funding pathways and supplier diversity opportunities. By equipping young women with skills, networks and capital connections, AYWE advances a more diverse pool of Nova Scotia founders.

solutions.text: Local Angel Network or Syndicate: Help community investors form a local angel group or syndicate to pool capital, perform due diligence, and provide early-stage funding with local knowledge and patient capital.

resources.name: Ulnooweg Indigenous Investment Fund (UIIF)
resources.description: UIIF pools capital to provide flexible, patient, early-stage financing to Indigenous entrepreneurs in Nova Scotia and across Atlantic Canada. The fund brings together community-aligned investors, conducts due diligence with local knowledge through Indigenous governance, and syndicates financing to help startups and growth-stage ventures access capital that traditional lenders often do not provide.
resources.address: 165 Willow Street, Suite 201, Truro, NS B2N 4Z9

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Funds (CEDIF)
resources.description: New Dawn raises capital from community investors in Cape Breton through Nova Scotia’s CEDIF structure and deploys it into local startups and enterprises using patient, community-guided investment strategies. By pooling residents’ capital, organizing investor oversight, and performing due diligence on prospective investees, the funds operate as a local investment syndicate that supplies early-stage financing informed by deep local knowledge.

solutions.text: One‑Stop Business Navigation Hub: Create a single-access point (physical + online) where founders can learn about permits, funding sources, mentorship, incubation and procurement opportunities in the region.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Business Navigators
resources.organization: Province of Nova Scotia (Service Nova Scotia and Internal Services)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Business Navigators provide a single-window service to help entrepreneurs understand permits, licenses, zoning, and other regulatory requirements, while also pointing them to relevant funding programs and procurement portals. Founders can access advisors online and by phone, and can get in-person support through Service Nova Scotia offices, effectively creating a one-stop navigation hub that connects to mentorship and incubation partners across the province.
resources.address: Maritime Centre, 1505 Barrington Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Invest Nova Scotia
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia serves as a 'single front door' for business growth and innovation supports, centralizing access to funding programs, export services, mentorship networks, and incubation facilities (formerly through Innovacorp). Its team and online portal guide founders to the right programs and partners, and provide navigation to regulatory and procurement resources, functioning as a province-wide one-stop hub for startups and scaling firms.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 701, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

resources.name: SmartBusiness Program
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s SmartBusiness Program assigns account managers who act as navigators for companies and founders, connecting them with municipal/provincial permitting, incentives and grants, mentorship, and supplier/procurement opportunities. With a downtown office and online intake, the program provides a single-access point that streamlines how startups discover and engage with supports across the region.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: CEED – Entrepreneurship Hub
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED operates a physical entrepreneurship hub and online portal that give founders a centralized place to access training, mentorship, advisory services, micro-financing, and connections to government funding and procurement readiness resources. Staff provide one-on-one navigation support and referrals to incubation programs and regulatory guidance, functioning as a practical, one-stop gateway for starting and growing a business in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Volta Startup Hub
resources.description: Volta is a central hub for Atlantic Canadian startups that combines physical space with an online community to connect founders to mentorship, investment readiness, workshops, and corporate/government partners. Through its programs and on-site staff, Volta helps companies navigate funding options, incubation pathways, and procurement/supplier introductions, creating a practical one-stop access point for startup support in the region.
resources.address: Maritime Centre, 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 1300, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

obstacles.title: Transportation and digital connectivity shortfalls
obstacles.description: Limited public transit within and between communities, and uneven rural broadband/cell coverage, reduce access to jobs, education, and services.

solutions.text: Community on‑demand microtransit shuttle: A locally managed, app/phone-booking minibus service that provides flexible routes between neighborhoods, schools, employment hubs and transit terminals — run by a mix of paid drivers and trained community volunteers with municipal scheduling support.

resources.name: Access‑A‑Bus
resources.description: Access‑A‑Bus is Halifax Transit’s door‑to‑door, pre‑booked shuttle service that provides demand‑responsive trips for eligible riders, connecting homes and neighborhoods with schools, employment sites, medical services, and Halifax Transit terminals. Trips are scheduled through municipal dispatch, with paid drivers operating minibuses and coordinating transfers to the fixed‑route network—an implementation of on‑demand microtransit that fills gaps where conventional routes are limited.

resources.name: Kings Point‑to‑Point Transit
resources.description: Kings Point‑to‑Point Transit provides door‑to‑door, demand‑responsive transportation across Kings County, with rides booked by phone and scheduled flexibly to link rural and small‑town residents to schools, jobs, health care, and Kings Transit hubs. The non‑profit service employs paid drivers and community volunteers to expand coverage, functioning as a local microtransit shuttle that fills first/last‑mile gaps between neighborhoods and key destinations.
resources.address: 14 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

resources.name: MusGo Rider Eastern Shore
resources.description: MusGo Rider operates pre‑booked, demand‑responsive community shuttles along Nova Scotia’s Eastern Shore, providing flexible routing between rural neighborhoods, schools, workplaces, services, and Halifax Transit connection points. Using a mix of paid staff and trained community volunteers, the co‑operative delivers affordable microtransit with dispatch/scheduling support and partnerships that extend mobility where fixed‑route transit and broadband access are limited.

solutions.text: Volunteer driver and ‘Wheels for Work’ program: Organize volunteer drivers and a low-cost ride voucher system to transport people to jobs, training and health appointments; prioritize youth employment pathways and partner with employers for reimbursed rides.

resources.name: BayRides Community Transportation
resources.description: BayRides provides pre-booked, door-to-door rides across the St. Margaret’s Bay area for work shifts, training/education, medical appointments and daily needs at low, flat fares. The service helps youth and other residents reach jobs and programs where no regular transit exists, and can arrange third‑party billing or fare support with community agencies and employers to reduce out‑of‑pocket costs.
resources.address: 201-5288 St. Margaret’s Bay Road, Upper Tantallon, NS B3Z 2H9

resources.name: Transportation Services (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross operates volunteer driver programs in Nova Scotia that provide affordable, pre-booked rides to essential appointments and services, including medical visits and community supports. By mobilizing screened volunteers and offering low-cost transportation, the program fills transit gaps for rural and peri‑urban residents and can be coordinated with employers and service providers to ensure people can reliably reach training and other scheduled commitments.

resources.name: Wheels of Hope (Volunteer Driver Program)
resources.description: Wheels of Hope matches cancer patients in Nova Scotia with volunteer drivers who provide no‑cost or low‑cost rides to treatment and related medical appointments, ensuring people can access care despite long distances or limited transit. The volunteer model and mileage reimbursement keep rides affordable and predictable, directly addressing transportation barriers to critical health services for youth and adults alike.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Transportation Assistance
resources.description: TEAM Work Cooperative’s Nova Scotia Works centre provides employment services that include transit support such as bus tickets and limited taxi/ride vouchers for eligible clients to attend interviews, training, and the first days of work. Staff coordinate with youth jobseekers and, when applicable, employers or funding partners to reduce transportation barriers on the path to employment.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

solutions.text: Community ride‑share/cooperative taxi service: A member-owned ride-share or taxi co‑op that keeps fares local, hires community drivers (including youth), and provides reliable late‑night and weekend service where commercial operators won’t go.

resources.name: MusGo Rider Co-operative
resources.description: MusGo Rider is a member-owned community transportation co-operative providing pre-booked, door-to-door rides along the Eastern Shore and Musquodoboit Valley where conventional transit and taxis are limited. It hires local community drivers and keeps fares circulating locally, offering reliable service for work, school, medical, and social trips, including coverage outside typical commuter hours to improve access for youth and residents in rural areas.
resources.address: 7900 Highway 7, Unit 5, Musquodoboit Harbour, NS B0J 2L0

resources.name: BayRides Community Transit
resources.description: BayRides operates a community-owned, demand-responsive ride service in St. Margaret’s Bay, filling gaps where no fixed-route transit or late-night taxis operate. By employing local drivers and reinvesting fares in the service area, it provides affordable, door-to-door transportation for work, education, appointments, and evening/weekend needs, helping youth and residents stay connected to jobs and community life.
resources.address: 5284 St. Margarets Bay Road, Upper Tantallon, NS B3Z 2H9

resources.name: Kings Point-to-Point Transit
resources.description: Kings Point-to-Point Transit offers community, door-to-door rides across Kings County, serving rural and small-town areas with limited taxi and bus options. As a local non-profit, it employs community drivers, keeps fares in the region, and provides reliable trips for employment, training, healthcare, and social activities, with scheduling that extends beyond standard business hours to improve mobility for youth and workers.
resources.address: 14 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

solutions.text: E‑bike and bike‑share with repair hubs: Small, community-run e‑bike and conventional bike-sharing programs plus volunteer repair clinics to enable short-distance commuting, reduce car dependence, and make active transport affordable and accessible.

resources.name: DSU Bike Centre
resources.description: The DSU Bike Centre is a volunteer-run community bike workshop offering DIY repair bays, tools, parts, and skills workshops for students and the broader community. By providing low-cost repairs, refurbished bikes, and maintenance education, it enables affordable short-distance commuting and reduces car dependence in Halifax.

resources.name: Public Bicycle Repair Stands
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality maintains a network of outdoor, self-service bike repair stands equipped with tools and air pumps at libraries, transit terminals, and along key cycling routes. These 24/7 repair hubs make on-the-spot maintenance accessible, helping residents keep bikes roadworthy for everyday errands and short commutes.

resources.name: E-Bike Lending Program
resources.description: South Shore Public Libraries offers community e-bike lending at select branches, allowing residents to borrow e-bikes, helmets, and locks for short-term use. The program introduces people to e-bikes as a practical option for errands and commuting, expanding access to affordable, car-light transportation in areas with limited transit.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library Bike Repair Clinics
resources.description: The Halifax Tool Library runs skills workshops and periodic volunteer-led bike repair clinics, and provides access to bike-specific tools and repair stands through its lending program. By lowering the cost of maintenance and teaching hands-on repair skills, it supports safe, affordable cycling for short trips and daily commutes.

solutions.text: Inter‑community commuter bus partnerships: Jointly funded scheduled buses connecting smaller towns with regional employment centers, colleges and hospitals — organized by several communities pooling resources and coordinating timetables to match shifts and classes.

resources.name: Kings Transit Authority (Annapolis Valley Inter‑Municipal Service)
resources.description: Kings Transit runs fixed-route, inter-community buses linking small towns across the Annapolis Valley with regional hubs such as Kentville and Wolfville, including direct access to Acadia University, NSCC Kingstec Campus, Valley Regional Hospital, and major employment areas. It implements the solution through a joint funding and governance model with multiple municipalities (County of Kings and the Towns of Kentville, Wolfville, Berwick, and Annapolis Royal) pooling resources, and by coordinating timetables to align with class times and common shift changes to improve access to jobs, education, and services.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

resources.name: Pictou County Transit
