solutions.text: Apprenticeship Pipelines and Employer Training Partnerships: Partner schools, colleges and local employers to expand apprenticeships, paid internships, and rapid re-skilling programs that connect young people to well-paying local trades and industries.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program registers apprentices and employers, coordinates paid on-the-job training with certified journeypersons, and delivers technical training in partnership with NSCC. It offers employer incentives and supports that expand apprenticeship seats and promote rapid upskilling in in-demand Red Seal and provincial trades, helping young people earn while they learn and transition into well-paying local careers.

resources.name: NSCC Apprenticeship Technical Training
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College delivers in-class technical training for registered apprentices across a wide range of trades in coordination with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and local employers. Programs are aligned to regional labour demand and often integrate work-integrated learning and employer partnerships, enabling apprentices and career changers to upskill quickly and progress toward certification while maintaining paid employment.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY places Nova Scotia high school students in paid summer work terms with local construction employers, providing safety training, mentorship, and hands-on experience in skilled trades. The program is a partnership with industry and education (including NSAA and the Department of Education) that builds an apprenticeship pipeline by helping youth accrue hours, explore trades careers, and transition into post-secondary or apprenticeship pathways.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Nova Scotia Power Apprenticeship Programs
resources.description: Nova Scotia Power recruits and trains apprentices for skilled trade roles such as Powerline Technicians and Industrial Electricians through paid, employer-sponsored apprenticeships. Working with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and training providers, these programs combine structured on-the-job learning with technical coursework to build a local talent pipeline for stable, well-paying energy sector careers.
resources.address: 1223 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Irving Shipbuilding Inc. (in partnership with NSCC and community partners)
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a collaborative training-to-employment initiative that recruits diverse Nova Scotians, provides foundational and trade-specific training at NSCC, and transitions graduates into paid apprenticeships at the Halifax Shipyard. Partnering with community organizations and local industry, the program offers wraparound supports and an earn-while-you-learn model that accelerates entry into well-paying shipbuilding trades.

solutions.text: Community Food Co-ops and Bulk Buying Clubs: Establish or expand food co-ops and bulk-buying groups to lower household grocery costs, support local producers, and keep more income available for savings and investment.

resources.name: Bulk Buy Food Box
resources.description: Chebucto Connections runs a community bulk-buying club that pools residents’ orders to purchase fresh produce and pantry staples at wholesale prices, then packs and distributes monthly food boxes. By aggregating demand and sourcing from local suppliers where possible, the program lowers household grocery costs while supporting Nova Scotia producers and keeping more community spending local.
resources.address: 531 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1X3

resources.name: Good Food Market
resources.description: The North Grove’s Good Food Market offers affordable, community-priced produce and staples sourced through bulk procurement, allowing families to buy fresh food below typical retail pricing. Operating as a not-for-profit, the market functions like a community buying club—reducing mark-ups, prioritizing local suppliers, and helping households stretch grocery budgets while strengthening the local food economy.

resources.name: WFM2Go Online Local Food Ordering
resources.description: WFM2Go is the Wolfville Farmers’ Market’s online ordering and distribution program that consolidates weekly customer orders from dozens of Nova Scotia farmers and food producers into a single pickup or delivery. By aggregating purchases and logistics, it reduces transaction and distribution costs, offers value bundles and seasonal boxes, supports local producers, and helps households manage grocery spending through planned, bulk-style orders.

solutions.text: Community Revolving Loan Fund / Social Finance Hub: Launch a local revolving loan fund that provides low-interest, flexible loans for housing repairs, small businesses, or emergency needs—capitalized by municipal seed funding, donations, and impact investors.

resources.name: CEED Microloan Financing
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides flexible microloans and growth loans to new and expanding small businesses in Nova Scotia, with mentoring and training to improve repayment and success. As borrowers repay, CEED re-lends the capital to new entrepreneurs, operating effectively as a revolving social finance fund that lowers barriers to entrepreneurship for young people and newcomers.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Small Business Loan Guarantee Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Co-operative Council (in partnership with Nova Scotia Credit Unions and the Province of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: This program channels affordable, flexible loans to startups and existing small businesses through Nova Scotia’s credit unions, backed by a provincial guarantee administered by the Nova Scotia Co-operative Council. The revolving portfolio enables ongoing re-lending as loans are repaid, mobilizing community deposits and public backing to expand access to capital for entrepreneurs facing cost-of-living and credit constraints.
resources.address: 90 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: Solar City Program (PACE Financing)
resources.description: Halifax’s Solar City provides low-interest, property-assessed clean energy (PACE) loans for residential solar and efficiency upgrades, repaid via the property tax bill. The fund is municipally capitalized and revolves as repayments flow back, directly supporting housing-related improvements that cut utility costs and ease cost-of-living pressures.

resources.name: Clean Energy Financing Program (CEFP)
resources.description: Bridgewater’s CEFP offers low-interest, on-bill/PACE-style financing for home energy retrofits—such as heat pumps, insulation, and airtightness—so homeowners can make necessary repairs and efficiency upgrades with no upfront cost. The program uses municipal capital and recycles repayments to fund future projects, operating as a revolving loan fund that reduces household energy expenses and improves housing quality.

solutions.text: Career Mentorship and Local Hiring Network: Create a region-wide alumni and professional mentoring network and local-hiring platform that connects graduates with employers, internship opportunities, and wage-advancing career paths.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program matches recent graduates and job seekers with established business and community leaders for one-on-one, career-focused conversations and warm introductions to their networks. By facilitating informational interviews and referrals to hiring managers, it accelerates local hiring, opens doors to internships and full-time roles, and helps newcomers and young professionals build wage-advancing career paths in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Dal Alumni Link and myCareer
resources.organization: Dalhousie University (Bissett Student Success Centre & Alumni Engagement)
resources.description: Dal Alumni Link pairs students and recent graduates with alumni mentors across sectors for guidance on career planning, networking, and wage growth pathways. Complementing this, Dalhousie’s myCareer platform connects employers with students for co-ops, internships, and graduate roles, creating a province-wide mentorship and hiring network that helps graduates transition into well-paying careers in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: NSCC Career Services & Co-op Education
resources.description: NSCC’s Career Services and Co-op teams run a province-wide employer network, job boards, and work-integrated learning that connect students and graduates to internships, co-ops, and full-time roles across industries. They also facilitate mentorship and industry engagement events that help learners build professional networks and progress into sustainable, higher-wage career paths within Nova Scotia.

resources.name: COVE Internship Program
resources.description: COVE’s Internship Program places students and recent graduates with ocean-technology companies for paid, career-building work experiences and structured mentorship from industry professionals. Through employer partnerships, talent events, and hands-on projects at the waterfront innovation hub, participants gain direct pathways into high-demand roles and wage-advancing careers in Nova Scotia’s growing ocean sector.

resources.name: Apprenticeship Program
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency registers apprentices and helps connect them with employer sponsors for paid, on-the-job training under certified mentors (journeypersons), paired with technical instruction. This structured mentorship and hiring model leads to trade certification (often Red Seal), enabling significant wage progression and stable, long-term careers in Nova Scotia’s skilled trades.

solutions.text: Subsidized Remote Work Hubs and Broadband Access: Develop subsidized coworking hubs and invest in community broadband to enable remote work, reduce commuting costs, and allow workers to live in lower-cost communities while accessing higher-paying jobs.

resources.name: Rural Internet Project (Municipality of Colchester)
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: The Municipality of Colchester is investing municipal and senior-government funds to expand high-speed broadband through a mix of fibre and fixed wireless in underserved rural communities. By subsidizing last‑mile infrastructure and partnering with internet service providers, the project brings reliable home and hub connectivity that enables residents to work remotely, access online training, and run small businesses from lower‑cost areas. This directly reduces commuting expenses and opens access to higher‑paying remote jobs across Canada.

resources.name: High-Speed Internet Project (Municipality of the District of Lunenburg)
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: MODL’s High-Speed Internet Project co-funds broadband expansion with provincial/federal programs and ISPs to deliver reliable service to rural households and businesses across Lunenburg County. The initiative fills service gaps with new fibre and wireless builds, creating the connectivity foundation people need to work from home or shared hubs in their communities. By improving local broadband, it supports remote employment, reduces commuting, and lets young residents stay or return to more affordable communities.

resources.name: Work and Study Spaces with Free Wi‑Fi (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: Halifax Central Library provides free high‑speed Wi‑Fi, quiet work areas, bookable meeting rooms, and public computers, functioning as a no‑cost coworking hub for freelancers, students, and remote employees. These subsidized spaces lower barriers to remote work by offering reliable broadband, desks, printing, and private rooms for virtual meetings in a central, transit‑accessible location. This helps reduce commuting costs and supports residents who want to live affordably while accessing higher‑paying remote opportunities.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Resource Centre (TEAM Work Cooperative)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Works Resource Centre at TEAM Work Cooperative offers free, publicly funded access to high‑speed internet, computers, printing, and private rooms for virtual interviews and remote meetings. Staff provide digital skills workshops and support navigating remote job platforms, helping clients transition into remote roles without the cost of a private office. This subsidized hub reduces commuting and work‑related expenses while connecting people to higher‑wage opportunities that can be done from anywhere in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

solutions.text: Time-Banks and Care Exchange Programs: Set up time-banks where community members exchange hours of service (childcare, tutoring, elder care) to reduce out-of-pocket costs and strengthen local support networks.

resources.name: HomeShare Atlantic
resources.description: HomeShare Atlantic matches older adults who have spare rooms with students or young workers who provide a set number of weekly help hours (companionship, light chores, errands) in exchange for low-cost housing. This is a care-exchange model that substitutes time and support for cash, directly lowering housing expenses for young people while strengthening intergenerational support networks across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Spryfield Urban Farm Volunteer Program
resources.description: Through resident-led gardening and program support at the Spryfield Urban Farm, neighbours contribute volunteer hours to grow food, host workshops, and provide on-site supports such as childcare during sessions. This informal time-exchange reduces out-of-pocket costs for participants (fresh produce, shared meals, learning opportunities) and builds local support networks in the Spryfield community.
resources.address: 531 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1X3

resources.name: The North Grove Volunteer Program
resources.description: The North Grove engages community members to contribute time in its community kitchen, gardens, and family programs, including peer-to-peer skill sharing and on-site supports during programming. By enabling people to exchange time and skills for access to meals, produce markets, and family supports, the program functions as a local care-exchange that reduces cash costs and strengthens mutual aid in Dartmouth North.

resources.name: Work Exchange Program
resources.description: Tatamagouche Centre’s Work Exchange Program allows participants to trade volunteer hours in hospitality, groundskeeping, and program support for credits toward program fees and accommodations. This time-for-value approach lowers financial barriers for students and young adults while building community ties through shared work and learning in rural Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 259 Loop of Highway 6, Tatamagouche, NS B0K 1V0

solutions.text: Advocacy Coalitions for Local Tax, Rent and Transit Relief: Form citizen and business advocacy groups to press municipal and provincial governments for targeted property tax relief, rent stabilization measures, transit subsidies, and employer tax incentives tied to living wages.

resources.name: Alternative Provincial Budget – Nova Scotia (APB)
resources.organization: Canadian Centre for Policy Alternatives – Nova Scotia
resources.description: The APB is a multi-sector coalition process led by researchers and community partners that publishes a full shadow budget for Nova Scotia, including concrete proposals for targeted property tax relief for low-income households and non-profits, permanent rent stabilization and anti-renoviction measures, transit fare reductions and subsidies, and incentives for employers to adopt living wages. The coalition uses the APB to coordinate advocacy with municipal councils and the provincial government, equipping citizen and business groups with policy-ready recommendations to press for tax, rent, and transit affordability reforms.

resources.name: Community Legal Education and Law Reform Program
resources.description: This program organizes tenants and community partners to advocate for rent stabilization, stronger security of tenure, and fair housing standards in Nova Scotia. Beyond individual casework, Dalhousie Legal Aid Service leads and supports coalitions that make submissions to municipal councils and the Nova Scotia Legislature, pressing for permanent rent caps, renoviction protections, and related affordability measures that align with the solution’s call for citizen advocacy on rent relief.

resources.name: Transportation Program
resources.description: EAC’s Transportation Program convenes residents, social service agencies, and employers to advocate for affordable, accessible public transit across Nova Scotia. The coalition engages Halifax Regional Council and the Province to expand low-income transit passes, improve fare equity and service funding (including rural and community transit), and promote employer-supported transit benefits—directly implementing the solution’s call for organized advocacy on transit subsidies tied to cost-of-living relief.

resources.name: Public Policy and Advocacy
resources.description: United Way Halifax convenes community organizations, residents, and employers to advance policy solutions that reduce poverty, including support for living-wage adoption, affordable transit, and municipal affordability programs. Through coalition-building and direct engagement with HRM and the Province, the initiative presses for measures such as expanded low-income transit access, practical tax relief for low-income households, and incentives that encourage employers to pay living wages—advancing the solution’s multi-pronged approach to cost-of-living relief.

solutions.text: Financial Literacy, Matched-Savings and Home-Readiness Programs: Offer community workshops and matched-savings accounts focused on budgeting, credit repair, and down-payment accumulation to help young people prepare for homeownership and entrepreneurship.

resources.name: Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia prepares first-time, low-to-moderate income homebuyers through homeowner-readiness training that covers budgeting, credit management, and the true costs of homeownership. Applicants complete financial literacy workshops and develop savings plans for closing and home-related costs while working toward an affordable mortgage, directly supporting down-payment accumulation and long-term financial stability.

resources.name: Financial Literacy for Newcomers & Business Development Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS offers workshops and one-on-one coaching on budgeting, banking in Canada, credit building/repair, and savings tools (e.g., FHSA/TFSA) to help newcomers plan for milestones like first-time homeownership. Its Business Development team delivers training on cash flow, pricing, and financing options for start-ups, helping young entrepreneurs build financial capability and accumulate the capital needed to launch and grow businesses.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Start-Up and Scale-Up Training
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED delivers practical entrepreneurship programs that teach budgeting, bookkeeping, cash-flow planning, and credit readiness, along with mentorship to support launching and growing a business. Participants build savings plans and learn to access financing—skills that directly support asset-building for start-up costs and, by strengthening credit and money management, help position young people for future homeownership.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Business Is Jammin’ (Youth Financial Literacy & Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: Business Is Jammin’ engages Black youth across Nova Scotia with workshops on budgeting, saving, and credit, alongside hands-on entrepreneurship training and mentorship. The program builds financial capability early—supporting savings discipline for future goals like down payments—and connects participants to BBI’s business advisory services and financing pathways when they are ready to start or expand ventures.
resources.address: 1660 Hollis Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 1V7

obstacles.title: Childcare scarcity and family support gaps
obstacles.description: Insufficient, unaffordable childcare—especially in rural areas and for non-standard hours—forces difficult trade-offs between work, study, and caregiving.

solutions.text: Community Childcare Co-ops: Families and local volunteers pool time, skills, and small fees to run licensed or informal cooperative childcare sites, rotating caregiving duties to expand affordable options and build trust within neighbourhoods.

resources.name: Family Playgroup
resources.description: The North Grove hosts a parent-led Family Playgroup where caregivers co-create schedules and rotate supervision roles, creating an informal childcare co-op model. By pooling time and skills—and using volunteer childminding during select programs—the playgroup expands low-cost, trust-based care options for neighbourhood families, including those with limited access to formal childcare.

resources.name: Parent & Tot Playgroup
resources.description: Maggie’s Place runs a cooperative Parent & Tot Playgroup where families share facilitation and rotate light caregiving duties during sessions, helping to create affordable, community-based care. The centre also organizes volunteer-supported childminding during certain parent programs, enabling caregivers to study, work, or attend services while relying on a trusted neighbourhood co-op network.

solutions.text: Shared Caregiver Network & Registry: A community-maintained directory of vetted caregivers, babysitters, and respite workers (including background-check facilitation and references) so families can quickly find reliable help for non-standard hours.

resources.name: Support Worker Registry
resources.description: Autism Nova Scotia’s Support Worker Registry connects families with a vetted pool of respite and support workers across the province. Workers are screened and listed with experience, references, and availability, helping families quickly find reliable help for evenings, weekends, and other non-standard hours.
resources.address: 5945 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3H 1X4

resources.name: YMCA Licensed Family Home Child Care
resources.description: The YMCA operates a licensed family home child care network that recruits, approves, and monitors home-based caregivers, maintaining a directory of providers who have completed background checks, child abuse registry checks, and first aid/CPR. Families are matched to approved caregivers who can offer flexible schedules, including early mornings, evenings, and weekends to meet non-standard hour needs.

resources.name: Northwood Home Care (In-Home Support Services)
resources.description: Northwood maintains a large roster of screened, trained home support workers and respite staff, matching families with caregivers based on availability and needs. Their coordinated scheduling and vetted personnel enable reliable in-home respite and care during evenings, overnights, and weekends, helping families secure support outside standard hours.

resources.name: Home Support and Caregiver Respite Services
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross in Nova Scotia provides a coordinated roster of screened home support workers and respite staff, facilitating background checks and training to ensure safe, reliable in-home care. Families can be matched with vetted caregivers available for flexible and non-standard hours, enabling quick access to respite and support when licensed child care is unavailable.

solutions.text: After-Hours Pop-Up Childcare Hubs: Use community centres, libraries or school gyms to host evening and weekend childcare shifts staffed by trained local providers, enabling parents working non-standard hours to attend to shifts or study.

resources.name: Parents’ Night Out & Child Minding
resources.description: The Canada Games Centre runs evening and weekend child-minding and Parents’ Night Out programs where trained recreation staff supervise children in the gym, pool viewing areas, and multi-purpose rooms. By using the community centre’s facilities after hours, they provide flexible, short-duration childcare so parents working non-standard shifts or attending classes can access safe care nearby.
resources.address: 26 Thomas Raddall Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 0E2

resources.name: Kids Night Out
resources.description: Zatzman Sportsplex offers Kids Night Out sessions on select evenings and weekends where certified program leaders run supervised activities in the gym and community rooms. Hosted in a public recreation facility, these pop-up childcare blocks give parents working late shifts or studying after hours dependable care in a convenient community hub.

resources.name: PlayCare & Parents’ Night Out (John W. Lindsay YMCA)
resources.description: The YMCA provides evening and weekend PlayCare and Parents’ Night Out programs where trained staff offer supervised play in community spaces at the John W. Lindsay YMCA. These scheduled, after-hours childcare blocks let parents cover non-standard work shifts or attend study sessions while children are safely engaged on site.

resources.name: Parents’ Night Out
resources.description: St. Margaret’s Centre hosts Parents’ Night Out events staffed by trained recreation leaders who run games, crafts, and gym time for children in the evening. Using the community centre’s multi-purpose rooms and arenas as pop-up childcare spaces, the program helps families manage weekend or after-hours work and study schedules.
resources.address: 12 Westwood Boulevard, Upper Tantallon, NS B3Z 1H3

solutions.text: Timebanking for Caregiving: A local timebank where community members exchange hours of childcare, elder care, or household help — enabling families to earn childcare credits by helping others and redeem them when they need care.

resources.name: Halifax North TimeBank
resources.description: A neighborhood timebank hosted through Veith House that lets residents exchange hours of childcare, elder check-ins, meal prep, and household help. Members log the time they give and receive as credits in a shared ledger, so families can earn childcare hours by helping others and redeem those credits when they need care, including during non-standard hours.

resources.name: St. Margarets Bay Time Bank
resources.description: A community timebank for the St. Margarets Bay area coordinated by Transition Bay St. Margarets, facilitating exchanges of childcare, senior support, and household tasks. Families earn time credits by providing care or help to neighbors and redeem those credits when they need childcare or respite, strengthening support in rural communities with limited childcare options.
resources.address: 11 Station Road, Head of St. Margarets Bay, NS B3Z 1R2

resources.name: Eastern Shore Time Exchange
resources.description: A timebank-style service exchange supported by The Deanery Project that matches residents to swap hours of childcare, elder care visits, rides, and home help. Participants track hours as a community currency, enabling parents and caregivers to bank time by assisting others and draw on those credits for flexible, affordable care.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

solutions.text: Employer–Community Childcare Partnerships: Local employers partner with community groups to fund shared childcare slots, offer flexible scheduling, or provide on-site care during peak shift times for employees and trainees.

resources.name: Kids & Company Corporate Child Care Program – Halifax Quinpool
resources.description: Kids & Company partners with Nova Scotia employers to reserve guaranteed and backup child care spaces for employees, offering flexible and extended hours that support shift-based work and training schedules. Employers purchase corporate memberships so their staff can access priority placement, backup care days, and multi-location access, directly reducing childcare barriers for workers and trainees in Halifax.

resources.name: Halifax & Region Military Family Resource Centre – Child Care Services
resources.organization: Halifax & Region Military Family Resource Centre
resources.description: The H&R MFRC, funded in partnership with the Department of National Defence, delivers licensed child care, casual care, and respite care tailored to the non‑standard schedules of Canadian Armed Forces members and trainees. By coordinating with base units and offering flexible programming and extended hours during exercises or deployments, the MFRC exemplifies an employer–community partnership that ensures reliable care aligned with peak shift times.
resources.address: 100 True South Road, Halifax, NS B3K 5X5

resources.name: MSVU Child Study Centre (On‑Campus Early Learning)
resources.description: Located on the Mount Saint Vincent University campus, the Child Study Centre provides licensed early learning aligned with the university’s academic schedules, supporting student parents, trainees in practicums, and university employees. As a campus-based partnership between the university (employer/training institution) and the centre, it offers convenient on‑site care and priority access that reduces childcare barriers to work and study.

resources.name: ISANS – Care for Newcomer Children (CNC)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides on‑site Care for Newcomer Children during language classes, employment‑readiness training, and onboarding support programs, enabling parents to participate fully in training and job placement activities. Funded through settlement partnerships and coordinated with employer-linked programs, this model delivers flexible, on‑site childcare for trainees and new hires, directly addressing childcare scarcity during program hours.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Mobile Childcare Units for Rural Areas: Convert vans or trailers into safe, portable childcare spaces that visit smaller communities on a schedule, offering supervised play, early learning activities, and respite for caregivers.

resources.name: MODL Rec Van
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg – Recreation Department
resources.description: The MODL Rec Van is a mobile recreation unit that brings a stocked van and trailer of toys, craft kits, books, mats, and outdoor gear to smaller communities across the District on a rotating schedule. Staff set up safe, temporary play and early-learning zones and supervise group games and activities, providing short respite for caregivers while children engage in structured and free play close to home—functioning as a portable, childcare-like space for rural families.

resources.name: Annapolis County Recreation Play Trailer
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Annapolis – Recreation Services
resources.description: Annapolis County Recreation operates a mobile play trailer that travels to villages and rural parks on a published schedule, carrying mats, shade, toys, books, and simple early-learning materials. Trained leaders set up and supervise a safe, pop‑up play environment so children can participate in guided and free play while caregivers receive short-term respite—delivering a portable childcare-style experience where formal childcare is scarce.
resources.address: 752 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0

resources.name: Colchester Mobile Recreation Van
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester – Recreation Services
resources.description: Colchester Recreation’s Mobile Recreation Van visits rural communities throughout the county with a van full of portable play and learning equipment. Staff create a temporary, supervised play space for children—featuring games, crafts, and early-learning activities—offering families a nearby, scheduled option that supports child development and provides short-term caregiver respite in areas with limited childcare.

solutions.text: School-Based Before/After Care Programs: Extend community-run programming in school facilities to provide affordable supervised care for school-aged children before and after classes, coordinated by parent volunteers and local educators.

resources.name: EXCEL Before and After School Program
resources.description: EXCEL is a school-based, fee-subsidized before-and-after school program that operates in dozens of elementary schools across the Halifax region. Using school gyms and classrooms, trained leaders provide supervised care, play, and enrichment before classes start and after dismissal, coordinated with school administrators and families. This directly implements the solution by extending community programming in school facilities to offer reliable, affordable wraparound care for school-aged children.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: YMCA School Age Child Care (SACC) — In-School Programs (HRM)
resources.description: The YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth partners with local elementary schools to deliver licensed, school-based before-and-after care right in classrooms and gyms across HRM. Programs run before the first bell and after dismissal, combining homework support, recreation, and healthy snacks, and accept provincial subsidies to keep care affordable. This implements the solution by coordinating with educators and parent communities to extend supervised care within school facilities.
resources.address: 1575 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3J 0H5

resources.name: Service de garde scolaire (Before/After School Care) at École Beaubassin
resources.description: Le Petit Voilier provides on-site before-and-after school care at CSAP schools such as École Beaubassin, using school classrooms to offer bilingual, play-based supervision for children in Primary–Grade 6. Staff coordinate with school personnel and parents to align hours with bell times and professional development days, easing family logistics. This is a direct example of community-run programming delivered in school facilities for accessible, supervised care.
resources.address: 34 Larry Uteck Boulevard, Bedford, NS B4A 0K6

resources.name: Extended Day Program (Before and After School)
resources.description: Sacred Heart School of Halifax operates an Extended Day program within its elementary school facilities, offering supervised care before classes and into the early evening after dismissal. Led by school staff, the program includes homework support, structured play, and snacks, providing predictable, affordable wraparound care for families. This uses existing school spaces to extend the day and meet childcare gaps for school-aged children.
resources.address: 5820 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3H 1X8

solutions.text: Community Microgrants for Family Care Startups: A local fund that provides small grants and mentorship to residents who want to start licensed home daycares, drop-in centres, or innovative childcare pilots in under-served areas.

resources.name: Family Home Child Care Start-Up Grant
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: A provincial funding stream that provides small start-up grants to residents who become approved Family Home Child Care providers through licensed agencies. The grants help cover safety upgrades, equipment, and materials required to meet provincial standards, while agency staff offer hands-on mentorship with business setup, training, and licensing. This model specifically strengthens child care in under-served communities, including rural areas and for non-standard hours.

resources.name: Child Care Capacity Fund
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development
resources.description: A provincial grant program that supports communities, non-profits, municipalities, and Family Home Child Care agencies to create or expand child care options in areas with limited supply. Funding can be used for innovative pilots such as flexible or extended-hours care, outreach and recruitment of new home-based providers, and small start-up supports, with technical assistance and mentorship embedded through partnering agencies. The fund helps seed new spaces and strengthen community-led solutions targeting gaps in access and affordability.

resources.name: YMCA Family Home Child Care (HRM)
resources.description: A provincially licensed Family Home Child Care agency that recruits and mentors residents to open approved home daycares across the Halifax Regional Municipality. The YMCA provides step-by-step coaching on meeting provincial standards, supports business planning and training, and connects new providers to provincial start-up grants and ongoing quality supports. By focusing on communities with shortages and accommodating non-standard hours where possible, it expands access to regulated care for families that need it most.

solutions.text: Intergenerational Care Programs: Link seniors and elders with childcare programming where older adults volunteer in early learning activities, providing social connection and supervised care while strengthening community bonds.

resources.name: Kids View Child Care Centre
resources.description: Kids View Child Care Centre is a licensed early learning program located on the Grand View Manor long-term care campus. Children and older adult residents participate in daily shared activities such as reading, music, gardening, and art, creating structured intergenerational contact under staff supervision. By embedding childcare alongside seniors’ care, the program provides dependable childcare for local families while fostering social connection and community bonds between generations.

resources.name: Aboriginal Head Start (AHS) – Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s AHS program offers culturally grounded early childhood education where Elders and Knowledge Keepers regularly join classrooms to share Mi’kmaw language, stories, songs, and traditions. This intentional intergenerational approach links seniors with young children in supervised learning environments, strengthening cultural identity and social connection while providing reliable early learning and care for urban Indigenous families.

resources.name: Eskasoni Aboriginal Head Start
resources.description: Eskasoni’s Head Start provides community-based early learning for preschoolers that actively integrates Elders into daily programming. Elders support language revitalization and cultural teachings through storytelling, crafts, and land-based activities, creating meaningful intergenerational relationships in a supervised setting that also offers families consistent early childhood care.

solutions.text: Volunteer Emergency Childcare Pool: A vetted roster of community volunteers who can provide short-notice childcare for emergencies, single parents, or students facing last-minute schedule changes.

resources.name: South House Childcare Collective
resources.organization: South House Sexual and Gender Resource Centre
resources.description: A volunteer-run childcare collective that maintains a roster of vetted community volunteers who can provide free, short-notice child-minding for caregivers. It supports single parents, students, and community members who face last-minute schedule changes, appointments, or emergencies—implementing the solution by coordinating screened volunteers to deliver rapid, flexible childcare in home or community settings when available.

resources.name: IWK Volunteer Sibling Support (Emergency Child-Minding)
resources.description: The IWK Health Centre deploys screened volunteers to provide on-the-spot childcare for siblings in the Emergency Department and outpatient clinics, allowing caregivers to focus on urgent medical needs without arranging last-minute childcare. This functions as a vetted, scheduled volunteer pool that responds to emergencies and short-notice situations, directly aligning with the solution’s goal of rapid, reliable community child-minding.

resources.name: Chebucto Family Centre – Short-Notice Childcare/Child-Minding Support
resources.description: Chebucto Family Centre coordinates trained staff and volunteers to offer short-term, on-call child-minding so parents and students can attend appointments, classes, or handle urgent needs. By organizing a trusted local pool of child-minders and matching families quickly when capacity allows, the centre operationalizes a community-based, emergency childcare roster that fills gaps in access and affordability.

solutions.text: Childcare Provider Training & Apprenticeship Hub: Local workshops and paid apprenticeships to train residents (including teens and newcomers) as early childhood educators, building a pipeline of qualified providers within the community.

resources.name: Early Years Professional Development Centre (PDC)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education
resources.description: NSCECE’s Early Years Professional Development Centre delivers in-person and online workshops, short courses, and coaching to early childhood educators and home child care providers across Nova Scotia. By bringing training to urban and rural communities and upskilling assistants and newcomers already working in centres, it functions as a local training hub that strengthens the pipeline of qualified providers, including for programs operating during non-standard hours.

resources.name: Early Childhood Education (ECE) Diploma Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education
resources.description: NSCECE’s diploma combines classroom learning with intensive practicums in its Lab Schools and partner licensed child care centres, giving students mentored, hands-on experience. Many learners work in paid roles in centres while they study, and the college partners with employers to recruit graduates—building a steady pipeline of qualified educators for communities across the province.

resources.name: Early Childhood Education (ECE) Program
resources.description: NSCC’s ECE program is offered at multiple campuses and via flexible delivery, pairing coursework with work-integrated learning placements in licensed child care and pre-primary settings. NSCC collaborates with employers on work-and-learn pathways so students can be employed while completing credentials, helping rural and urban centres grow their own talent and address childcare shortages.

resources.name: Diplôme en éducation de la petite enfance (ÉPE)
resources.description: Université Sainte-Anne offers a French-language early childhood education diploma that includes practicum placements in francophone and bilingual licensed centres throughout Nova Scotia. The program supports Acadian communities and francophone newcomers with local training and work experience, expanding the pool of qualified bilingual educators needed to run inclusive childcare programs.

resources.name: Valley Family Child Care Agency
resources.description: The Valley Family Child Care Agency recruits, trains, approves, and mentors home-based childcare providers, offering orientation, safety training, ongoing professional development, and regular support visits. By helping local residents—including newcomers and parents re-entering the workforce—set up regulated family home child care, it creates community-based childcare capacity and a pathway into the profession.

solutions.text: Community Transport for Childcare Access: Coordinate volunteer driver programs or shuttle services that bring children to central childcare hubs from surrounding rural neighborhoods, reducing travel barriers for families.

resources.name: YMCA School Age Program (Transportation from Select Schools)
resources.description: The YMCA’s School Age Program in Halifax/Dartmouth provides daily bus/van pick‑up from designated elementary schools to central YMCA child care hubs, functioning as a coordinated shuttle so families don’t need to arrange their own transport. By consolidating children from multiple neighborhoods into safe, supervised routes, the program reduces travel barriers for parents with work or study commitments and ensures children reach licensed after‑school care reliably.

resources.name: YMCA School Age Program Transportation (Yarmouth)
resources.description: The YMCA of Southwest Nova Scotia coordinates shuttle-style pick‑ups from participating schools in Yarmouth County to the YMCA’s central child care/after‑school hubs. This organized transport reduces distance and scheduling barriers—particularly for families in outlying rural areas—by ensuring children have a dependable ride to licensed care at the end of the school day.

resources.name: Pre-primary Program Transportation (Annapolis Valley)
resources.organization: Annapolis Valley Regional Centre for Education (AVRCE)
resources.description: AVRCE provides school bus transportation for four‑year‑olds to centralized pre‑primary early learning classrooms, operating a hub‑and‑spoke model across rural communities in the Annapolis Valley. By coordinating dedicated routes for young children, the service functions as a community shuttle that connects families to early learning/childcare access points while caregivers work or study.

solutions.text: Sliding-Scale Sliding-Window Drop-In Centres: Community-run drop-in centres with flexible hours and a sliding-fee model to serve families with fluctuating incomes and shift work schedules, allowing short-term use by the hour.

resources.name: Child Minding
resources.description: The Canada Games Centre offers on-site, drop-in child minding that can be booked in short time blocks (typically by the hour) for children while caregivers attend activities, study, or use the facility. Hours include mornings, evenings, and weekends, and fees are low-cost with income-based financial assistance available through the Centre’s subsidy programs, effectively creating a sliding-fee model that supports families with fluctuating incomes and non-standard schedules.
resources.address: 26 Thomas Raddall Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 0E2

resources.name: Child Minding
resources.description: Zatzman Sportsplex provides flexible, hourly child-minding so caregivers can access programs, wellness services, or community resources on-site. It operates during daytime and evening hours, with affordable per-hour pricing and access to municipal low-income fee assistance, aligning with a sliding-scale, short-duration care model that supports shift-working families.

resources.name: Respite Childcare and Child-Minding
resources.organization: Maggie’s Place Family Resource Centre – Colchester
resources.description: Maggie’s Place offers short-term, appointment-based and occasional drop-in child-minding so parents and caregivers can attend work appointments, interviews, classes, or support programs. Services are offered at low or no cost (pay-what-you-can), scheduled in brief blocks that function like hourly care, and include some evening programming—delivering a community-run, sliding-fee, sliding-window model tailored to families with variable incomes and schedules.

solutions.text: Parent Cooperative Study & Work Spaces with Onsite Care: Shared community spaces where parents can study or work while children are nearby in a supervised room; participants rotate supervision or contribute small fees to retain affordable care.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC) and Onsite Childminding
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides onsite, supervised childminding adjacent to classrooms and computer work areas so parents can attend language classes, employment workshops, or quietly work on resumes and coursework. Care is free for eligible clients and delivered by trained staff in nearby rooms, allowing parents to study or work while remaining close to their children—an affordable, practical version of a co-located work/study space with childcare.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Family and Early Years Programs with Onsite Child-Minding
resources.organization: The North Grove (formerly Dartmouth Family Centre & Dartmouth North Community Food Centre)
resources.description: The North Grove operates a community hub where parents can access computers, Wi‑Fi, study/meeting areas, and employment or education supports while early-years educators and volunteers supervise children in adjacent play-based rooms. Programs are free or low-cost, letting parents work or study nearby without the financial burden of traditional childcare—directly implementing a shared community work/study space with onsite care.

resources.name: Parenting & Family Support with Onsite Childcare
resources.organization: Chebucto Family Centre (a program of Chebucto Connections)
resources.description: Chebucto Family Centre offers free and low-cost programs, drop-in supports, and access to computers/quiet space for parents, with onsite child-minding provided in a nearby playroom by staff and volunteers. This setup allows parents to study, job search, or meet with service providers while their children are safely supervised next door—an affordable, community-based approach that embodies the cooperative work/study with onsite care model.

resources.name: Onsite Early Learning and Program Child-Minding
resources.description: YWCA Halifax provides onsite licensed early learning and program child-minding at the same location where participants take employment, education, and entrepreneurship programs, enabling parents to work on coursework or business tasks while children are supervised in nearby rooms. Fees are subsidized or free for program participants, offering an accessible, co-located work/study environment with affordable care.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

solutions.text: Community Advocacy & Information Campaigns: Organize local campaigns to map childcare gaps, share stories, and lobby municipal or provincial bodies for flexible licensing, wage supports, and rural-focused funding—amplifying community needs.

resources.name: Systemic Advocacy — Affordable, Accessible Child Care
resources.description: YWCA Halifax leads public campaigns and storytelling efforts that highlight the lived experiences of caregivers and early childhood educators facing a shortage of affordable, flexible child care. Through coalition-building, policy briefs, and meetings with municipal and provincial decision-makers, they advocate for flexible licensing, ECE wage supports, and dedicated rural funding to close access gaps. They also share community-informed research and resources to help map where care is most needed and amplify community priorities.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: Early Childhood Collaborative Research Centre (ECCRC) — Child Care Access & Policy Engagement
resources.description: ECCRC conducts province-wide research and community consultations to map child care access gaps, including in rural and underserved communities, and documents family and provider experiences through surveys and knowledge-mobilization reports. The centre translates these findings into actionable recommendations and policy briefs for municipal and provincial leaders, advocating for flexible licensing, ECE wage and retention supports, and targeted rural investment. Public webinars, briefs, and media outreach help circulate evidence and community stories to inform decision-making.

resources.name: Policy, Advocacy & Research — Child Care Access for Newcomers
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS gathers settlement data and newcomer family stories to identify child care barriers such as cost, limited spaces, and lack of non-standard-hour care, and shares these insights with municipalities and the Province. Through submissions, briefings, and public education, ISANS advocates for flexible licensing options, culturally responsive care, workforce wage supports, and rural-focused funding that reflect immigrant community needs. Information sessions and employer/community partnerships further map local gaps and mobilize support for practical policy changes.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Family Resource & Referral Centres: One-stop local centres offering information on childcare options, subsidy applications, parenting supports, and connections to mental health or housing services to reduce hidden barriers to work and study.

resources.name: Maggie’s Place Family Resource Centre – Colchester
resources.description: Maggie’s Place operates as a one-stop family resource hub offering parenting programs, drop-ins, and navigation support for families. Staff provide information on licensed childcare options, help families apply for the Nova Scotia Child Care Subsidy, and connect parents to mental health, housing, and income supports to reduce barriers to work and study.

resources.name: Dartmouth Family Centre – Family Support Programs
resources.organization: Dartmouth Family Centre & Dartmouth North Community Food Centre
resources.description: The Dartmouth Family Centre provides a centralized place for families to access parenting supports, early years programming, and referrals. Staff assist with locating licensed childcare, navigating and completing childcare subsidy applications, and connecting families to housing, food security, and mental health services so caregivers can pursue employment or education.
resources.address: 107 Albro Lake Road, Dartmouth, NS B3A 3Y2

resources.name: ISANS Settlement Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides settlement case management and family support that help newcomers identify childcare options, understand eligibility, and complete Nova Scotia Child Care Subsidy applications. As a one-stop referral point, staff connect families to mental health care, housing support, and employment services, reducing hidden barriers that prevent parents from working or studying.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre – Family and Community Services
resources.description: The Centre offers wraparound family and community supports, including help finding culturally safe childcare, assistance completing benefits and subsidy applications, and parenting and early childhood programming. Staff provide warm referrals to housing supports, mental health care, and other community services, functioning as a one-stop hub to reduce barriers for Indigenous families pursuing work or education.

solutions.text: Shared Employer Childcare Consortia: Clusters of small employers pool resources to jointly fund a local childcare program or hire a caregiver who serves employees across multiple workplaces, making care affordable and sustainable.

resources.name: Kids & Company Corporate Child Care – Dartmouth (Burnside)
resources.description: Kids & Company partners with multiple employers through corporate memberships that collectively fund guaranteed child care access and back-up care for employees across different workplaces. In Dartmouth’s Burnside area, small and mid-sized employers pool membership fees to secure priority spaces and extended-hours options for staff, effectively creating a shared employer childcare consortium that reduces costs and stabilizes availability.

resources.name: Kids & Company Corporate Child Care – Halifax (Mumford)
resources.description: Through multi-employer corporate memberships, Kids & Company enables clusters of small employers to co-fund access to local child care, including reserved spots and emergency back-up care that serve employees from numerous workplaces. The Halifax site supports a consortium model by aggregating employer contributions to maintain stable capacity and flexible care options, helping retain workers who face childcare scarcity or non-standard hours.

solutions.text: Event-Based Childcare and Family-Friendly Scheduling: Ensure community events, training sessions, and open houses routinely offer childcare or child-friendly scheduling (including family tickets) so parents can participate in civic and economic life.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides on-site Care for Newcomer Children during adult language classes, employment workshops, and community information sessions so parents can fully participate. By pairing training and events with free, licensed child care and offering sessions at family-friendly times, the program removes a major barrier to civic and economic participation for newcomer parents.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1H8

resources.name: Child Minding
resources.description: The Canada Games Centre offers supervised, low-cost child-minding so parents can attend adult fitness classes, registered programs, or special community events held at the facility. The centre also schedules family-friendly program times and offers family admission options, enabling parents to participate without arranging separate childcare.
resources.address: 26 Thomas Raddall Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 0E2

resources.name: Childcare Supports for Programs
resources.description: YWCA Halifax integrates free on-site childminding and childcare supports into many of its employment, leadership, and community programs so caregivers can attend training and workshops. Sessions are frequently scheduled at family-friendly times (school-day or early evening), and events are designed to be inclusive of parents and children when appropriate.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: Barrier-Free Community Events (Childcare Provided)
resources.description: The Ecology Action Centre routinely offers free childcare and family-friendly scheduling for public meetings, workshops, and training sessions to reduce barriers to participation. By advertising childcare availability and hosting all-ages programming, EAC enables parents to engage in civic dialogue and community action without needing separate childcare arrangements.

obstacles.title: Climate vulnerability and coastal risk
obstacles.description: Storm surges, flooding, heat, and insurance pressures threaten homes, infrastructure, and coastal economies, undermining long-term stability and investment.

solutions.text: Living shorelines and salt‑marsh restoration: Volunteer-driven projects to restore salt marshes, eelgrass beds and natural shorelines that reduce erosion and storm surge impacts while improving fish habitat; partnerships with conservation groups and municipalities to implement and maintain sites.

resources.name: Living Shorelines Nova Scotia (LSNS) Network
resources.organization: TransCoastal Adaptations: Centre for Nature‑based Solutions, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: LSNS convenes community groups, volunteers, municipalities, and scientists to design and implement nature-based shoreline projects across Nova Scotia. The network organizes volunteer planting of native salt-marsh vegetation, installs low-impact stabilization features (e.g., coir logs, brush bundles, shell/rock sills), and monitors sites to reduce erosion and storm-surge impacts while improving fish habitat. It also provides training and guidance to municipal partners to select, build, and maintain living shoreline and salt‑marsh restoration sites.

resources.name: Coastal Action Living Shorelines & Eelgrass Restoration
resources.description: Coastal Action leads on-the-ground living shoreline projects and eelgrass restoration in Lunenburg County and surrounding coastal communities. The team engages volunteers in planting salt‑marsh species and transplanting eelgrass, and works with municipalities and waterfront landowners to install nature-based erosion controls that buffer storm surges and enhance nearshore fish habitat. Long-term site monitoring and maintenance are done in partnership with local governments and community groups.
resources.address: 37 Tannery Road, Unit 2, Lunenburg, NS B0J 2C0

resources.name: Bras d’Or/Unama’ki Eelgrass Restoration and Green Crab Mitigation
resources.description: UINR coordinates community-led restoration of eelgrass beds in the Bras d’Or (Unama’ki) by removing invasive European green crab and transplanting eelgrass with volunteers and Mi’kmaw Guardians. These efforts rebuild critical nursery habitat, stabilize sediments, and improve shoreline resilience to waves and storms. UINR partners with federal agencies, researchers, and municipal stakeholders to plan sites, train volunteers, and monitor ecological outcomes.

resources.name: Mahone Bay Living Shoreline Project
resources.description: This municipal pilot demonstrates a nature-based shoreline along the Town of Mahone Bay waterfront to reduce flooding and storm-surge impacts. Working with conservation partners, the Town has installed coir logs, rock/shell sills, and native salt‑marsh plantings and hosts community volunteer days for planting and site upkeep. The project protects public infrastructure while enhancing coastal habitat for fish and invertebrates.
resources.address: 493 Main Street, Mahone Bay, NS B0J 2E0

solutions.text: Community flood mapping and early‑warning network: Local mapping of flood-prone streets and assets using community workshops and citizen science; install community sirens, text/phone alert lists and low-cost sensors to give residents advance warning of storm surges and extreme tides.

resources.name: hfxALERT (Halifax Mass Notification System)
resources.description: hfxALERT is Halifax Regional Municipality’s opt‑in text, phone, and email notification system used to warn residents about coastal storm surges, flooding, extreme weather, evacuations, and road closures. Through the Halifax Coastal Strategy and HalifACT engagement processes, HRM has also produced coastal hazard and flood‑risk maps with community input, which help target alerts to flood‑prone streets and critical assets and improve local readiness.

resources.name: Truro Alerts (Voyent Alert!)
resources.description: The Town of Truro maintains floodplain and risk mapping for the Salmon River and downtown, developed through studies and public open houses to identify flood‑prone streets and assets. Truro Alerts (powered by Voyent Alert!) delivers targeted text/phone/email warnings based on real‑time river level sensors and Environment Canada forecasts, giving residents advance notice of high water, storm surges, and potential evacuations.

resources.name: Coastal Flooding and Storm Surge Monitoring (Lunenburg County)
resources.description: Coastal Action works with coastal communities such as Mahone Bay, Lunenburg, and Chester to map flood‑prone areas using community workshops, king‑tide photo surveys, and low‑cost water‑level loggers in harbours and streams. The program shares results with residents and municipal emergency managers to inform preparedness and support local early‑warning protocols ahead of storm surges and extreme tides.

resources.name: Water Monitoring Equipment Hub
resources.description: Atlantic Water Network lends low‑cost sensors (e.g., water‑level loggers and rain gauges) and provides training to Nova Scotia community groups and municipalities to monitor flood‑prone rivers, brooks, and coastal inlets. The community‑generated data support local flood‑risk maps and help partners develop or refine early‑warning practices that notify residents of rising waters and storm surges via municipal alert systems.

solutions.text: Neighbourhood resilience hubs and emergency shelters: Designate and retrofit trusted community buildings (libraries, schools, churches) as resilience hubs with backup power, water, cooling or warming capacity, emergency supplies and local coordination plans for evacuations and temporary sheltering.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Comfort Centres and Warming Centres
resources.description: HRM designates trusted community buildings (e.g., libraries, recreation centres, and community halls) to operate as comfort centres and warming/cooling centres during storms, prolonged power outages, heat waves, or winter emergencies. These sites provide charging, potable water, Wi‑Fi, washrooms, and climate-controlled space, with many locations equipped with backup generators, and coordinate with partners for evacuation support and temporary sheltering when needed.

resources.name: Cape Breton Regional Municipality Comfort Centres and Warming Centres
resources.organization: Cape Breton Regional Municipality Emergency Management
resources.description: CBRM maintains a network of designated comfort centres in community halls, fire stations, churches, and recreation facilities that open during severe weather, floods, and extended outages. Many sites have backup generators and provide warming/cooling, water, washrooms, device charging, information updates, and coordination with provincial EMO and the Canadian Red Cross for evacuation and shelter needs.

resources.name: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg Comfort Centres
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg Emergency Management Organization
resources.description: MODL identifies and supports a network of comfort centres across rural communities, often in community halls and fire stations, many equipped with backup generators through municipal/provincial funding. These centres open for warming or cooling, water access, charging, and information sharing, serving as local coordination hubs that can support evacuations and connect residents to emergency sheltering when necessary.

resources.name: Kings REMO Comfort Centres
resources.description: The Kings Regional Emergency Management Organization (serving the County of Kings and the Towns of Berwick, Kentville, and Wolfville) coordinates designated comfort centres in community facilities with backup power. These hubs provide warming/cooling space, device charging, Wi‑Fi, water, and local situation updates, and they integrate with municipal plans for evacuations, reception centres, and temporary sheltering during major events.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Canadian Red Cross Emergency Shelters and Reception Centres – Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross partners with municipalities and provincial EMO to open and operate emergency shelters and reception centres in community buildings such as schools, churches, arenas, and community centres. They provide cots, blankets, hygiene supplies, registration and family reunification, and volunteer teams, complementing local comfort centres by offering short-term sheltering and coordinated evacuation support during storms, floods, and other disasters.

solutions.text: Home and small‑business retrofit program: Community-led initiatives and pooled contractor lists to help homeowners and local businesses install flood barriers, backflow valves, elevate utilities, improve insulation and cooling, and access provincial retrofit grants or low‑interest loans.

resources.name: Home Energy Assessment
resources.description: Efficiency Nova Scotia’s Home Energy Assessment provides an EnerGuide evaluation and a tailored upgrade plan, then connects homeowners with a network of qualified contractors and rebates for insulation, air sealing, and high-efficiency heat pumps for cooling. The program helps households stack provincial incentives with the federal Greener Homes Loan to finance deeper retrofits, directly advancing the solution’s goals around improving insulation/cooling and accessing grants or low‑interest loans.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: Small Business Energy Solutions
resources.description: This turnkey program helps small businesses complete on-site assessments and install upgrades like heat pumps, HVAC controls, and other efficiency measures through vetted contractors, with significant incentives to lower upfront costs. By delivering practical retrofit support and connecting businesses to provincial rebates and financing options, it advances the solution’s focus on improving cooling and energy performance for local enterprises.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: HomeWarming
resources.organization: Clean Foundation (in partnership with EfficiencyOne/Efficiency Nova Scotia)
resources.description: HomeWarming provides free energy-efficiency retrofits for income-qualified Nova Scotians, including insulation, draft-proofing, and, where appropriate, efficient heating/cooling upgrades through local contractors. The program reduces vulnerability to heat and energy cost pressures and helps homeowners navigate available supports, aligning with the solution’s retrofit and community-led delivery approach.
resources.address: 126 Portland Street, 2nd Floor, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 1H8

resources.name: Stormwater Credit Program
resources.description: Halifax Water’s Stormwater Credit Program provides bill credits and technical guidance for non-residential properties that install on-site stormwater controls (e.g., permeable pavement, cisterns, detention/retention features). By incentivizing retrofits that reduce runoff and localized flooding for small businesses and institutions, it directly supports the solution’s flood‑protection aims and leverages local contractors to implement measures.
resources.address: 450 Cowie Hill Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1A1

resources.name: Clean Energy Financing Program (PACE) - Bridgewater
resources.organization: Town of Bridgewater (in partnership with PACE Atlantic CIC)
resources.description: Bridgewater’s PACE program offers low-interest, long-term financing repaid via the property tax bill for eligible home retrofits such as insulation, air sealing, heat pumps, and other efficiency improvements. Delivered with a community focus and supported by an approved contractor network, it helps residents access financing and trusted installers to complete upgrades that improve cooling and energy resilience.

solutions.text: Local insurance cooperatives and advocacy: Form municipal or community insurance pools, co-ops or advocacy groups to negotiate affordable premiums, promote risk-reducing measures among members and lobby provincial/federal bodies for supportive insurance policy and subsidies.

resources.name: School Insurance Program (SIP)
resources.description: SIP is a not-for-profit, member-owned risk pool that provides comprehensive insurance and risk management services for Nova Scotia’s public education system. By pooling risk across all school regions, negotiating coverage and reinsurance collectively, and delivering inspections, training, and loss-prevention programs, SIP keeps premiums stable and reduces losses from floods, severe storms, and other hazards. It also collaborates with provincial partners on policy and funding that strengthen community resilience, aligning with the solution’s focus on community pools, risk reduction, and advocacy.

resources.name: Insurance Bureau of Canada — Atlantic Office
resources.description: IBC’s Atlantic Office leads regional advocacy for fair, accessible property and casualty insurance and climate-resilient policy in Nova Scotia. It works with municipalities and provincial/federal governments on flood mapping, coastal protection, mitigation funding, and public–private insurance solutions, while promoting community risk‑reduction measures that help households and businesses lower premiums. This directly advances the solution’s advocacy component by mobilizing policy change and subsidies to address climate and coastal risk.
resources.address: 1969 Upper Water Street, Suite 1703, Halifax, NS B3J 3R7

resources.name: AgriInsurance Program (Nova Scotia)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Crop and Livestock Insurance Commission
resources.description: Delivered by the Nova Scotia Crop and Livestock Insurance Commission, AgriInsurance is a provincially administered risk‑pooling program that provides subsidized, actuarially sound coverage to farmers for weather‑related losses. The program negotiates coverage and reinsurance on behalf of producers, promotes on‑farm risk‑reduction practices through assessments and standards, and partners with provincial and federal bodies to design premium subsidies and disaster‑assistance policy. It exemplifies a community-scale insurance pool model that mitigates climate risk and stabilizes premiums.
resources.address: 74 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

solutions.text: Distributed renewable energy and microgrids: Community solar arrays and battery storage sited at schools, co‑ops and municipal facilities to provide critical power during outages and reduce vulnerability of essential services; training local technicians for maintenance.

resources.name: Amherst Solar Garden
resources.description: The Town of Amherst operates a community-scale solar garden on municipal land that offsets electricity use for civic facilities such as water and wastewater infrastructure, arenas, and administrative buildings. By siting generation locally on a former landfill and tying it into municipal operations, the project reduces exposure to storm-related disruptions on long transmission lines and establishes a platform for future battery storage and microgrid capabilities to keep essential services powered during outages.
resources.address: 98 Victoria Street East, Amherst, NS B4H 1X6

resources.name: Berwick Community Solar Garden
resources.description: Berwick Electric Commission’s community solar garden feeds clean power directly into the town’s municipally owned distribution utility, reducing peak demand and stabilizing energy costs for public services and community subscribers. The project localizes generation at municipal facilities, supporting resilience planning and laying the groundwork for pairing with battery storage to form a microgrid that can keep critical services (e.g., water, public works) operating during severe weather events.

resources.name: Smart Grid Nova Scotia (Battery Storage and DER Pilot)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Power’s Smart Grid Nova Scotia pilot deploys distributed energy resources, including residential battery systems and smart inverters, to create feeder-level resiliency and enable islanding for participating customers during outages. By integrating local storage with rooftop solar and advanced controls, the program demonstrates community-scale microgrid functionality that reduces vulnerability to storms and helps maintain critical loads while also training local electricians and contractors through installation and maintenance partnerships.
resources.address: 1223 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

resources.name: Energy Sustainability Engineering Technology (ESET) and Solar/Battery Training
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Ivany Campus
resources.description: NSCC’s ESET program and related micro-credentials train local technicians to design, install, and maintain solar PV, battery energy storage, and microgrid control systems used in schools, municipal facilities, and community co‑ops. Graduates gain hands-on skills with distributed renewable systems and commissioning procedures that are essential for keeping community microgrids reliable during outages and for supporting long-term operations and maintenance across Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Green infrastructure and stormwater management: Install rain gardens, bioswales, permeable pavements and roadside infiltration strips in town centres and neighbourhoods to reduce urban flooding, improve water quality and create green public spaces.

resources.name: Depave Paradise Nova Scotia
resources.description: Community-led events remove unnecessary asphalt from schoolyards, parking lots, and sidewalks and replace it with rain gardens, bioswales, and permeable landscaping that soak up and filter stormwater. By converting hard surfaces into green infrastructure, the program reduces localized flooding, improves water quality, and creates attractive, usable public spaces in neighbourhoods across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Cogswell District Project – Green Infrastructure and Stormwater Management
resources.description: This downtown redevelopment integrates low impact development features—such as bioretention planters (rain gardens), tree trenches with soil cells, permeable plaza surfaces, and roadside infiltration areas—to capture, slow, and treat stormwater at the surface. The design reduces urban flooding and pollutant loads to the harbour while creating new parks, complete streets, and green public spaces in Halifax’s core.

resources.name: Sawmill River Daylighting Project
resources.description: By replacing a buried culvert with a naturalized open-channel waterway through downtown Dartmouth, this project uses green infrastructure to attenuate peak flows, reduce flood risk, and improve water quality and fish passage. Streetscape upgrades add greenscaping and stormwater features that function like bioswales, creating a linear public green space that manages runoff before it reaches the harbour.
resources.address: 450 Cowie Hill Road, Halifax, NS B3P 2V3

resources.name: Campus Green Infrastructure & Stormwater Management
resources.description: Dalhousie designs, builds, and maintains rain gardens, bioswales, permeable paving, and green roofs—particularly on the Sexton and Studley campuses—to intercept and infiltrate runoff, reduce peak flows, and filter pollutants. These installations demonstrate practical low impact development techniques, reduce strain on municipal systems, and provide green spaces used for teaching, research, and public enjoyment.

solutions.text: Urban heat reduction and tree canopy program: Community tree-planting drives, cool-roof incentives and shade installations at parks and bus stops to cut extreme-heat risks for residents, particularly seniors and youth, and improve neighbourhood liveability.

resources.name: Urban Forestry Program (Urban Forest Master Plan Implementation)
resources.organization: Halifax Regional Municipality (Parks & Recreation – Urban Forestry)
