This approach accelerates spousal employment by tapping a curated employer network and facilitating flexible, skills-aligned opportunities.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Cape Breton Connector Program
resources.description: The Cape Breton Connector Program connects newcomer spouses and partners with local employers and volunteer connectors across key sectors in the region. Through targeted networking events, employer outreach, and warm referrals, it helps internationally trained candidates understand hiring needs and secure interviews, internships, or flexible roles. The program strengthens retention by coordinating with settlement staff and maintaining active employer contacts to match talent with openings.

resources.name: Connector Program (Truro & Colchester)
resources.organization: Truro & Colchester Partnership for Economic Prosperity
resources.description: This regional Connector Program builds a community network of employers, HR volunteers, and settlement partners to introduce newcomer spouses and other job seekers to hiring managers in Truro and Colchester. It offers employer briefings, curated networking meetings, and warm referrals that lead to interviews, project work, and internships aligned to candidates’ skills. By actively brokering employer connections and maintaining contact lists of opportunities, the program improves spousal employment and long-term newcomer retention.
resources.address: 35 Commercial Street, Suite 208, Truro, NS B2N 3H9

solutions.text: Skills Bridging and Micro-credential Workshops: Offer short, locally-delivered bridging courses and micro-credentials (e.g., Canadian workplace expectations, licensure navigation, digital skills, customer service) via community colleges, libraries, or business associations to help internationally-trained newcomers meet local job requirements quickly.

resources.name: ISANS Employment & Bridging Programs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers short, targeted employment-readiness workshops and bridging programs for internationally trained newcomers, including Canadian workplace culture, licensing navigation for regulated professions, sector-specific language training, and digital skills. Many offerings are micro-courses delivered with employer and post-secondary partners, helping clients gain locally relevant competencies and quickly meet Nova Scotia job requirements.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: NSCC MicroCredentials
resources.description: NSCC offers short, stackable micro-credentials in areas such as digital essentials, customer service, workplace communication, and industry-specific skills, issued as digital badges recognized by Nova Scotia employers. Delivered locally across campuses and online, these micro-credentials help internationally trained newcomers bridge prior experience to local expectations and rapidly signal job-ready skills to employers.

resources.name: Newcomer Services at Halifax Public Libraries
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries provides free, locally delivered workshops for newcomers, including digital literacy classes, resume and interview clinics, and sessions on Canadian workplace expectations. Frequently offered in partnership with ISANS and Nova Scotia Works, these short courses help internationally trained residents build practical skills and local knowledge that align with employer needs.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Professional Mentorship and Credential Navigation: Establish volunteer mentorship programs linking newcomers with senior professionals in their field to review resumes, simulate interviews, advise on credential recognition pathways, and provide industry introductions. Partner with professional associations to demystify licensing processes.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS pairs internationally trained newcomers with volunteer mentors who are senior professionals in the same field to review resumes, conduct mock interviews, and provide targeted industry advice. Mentors help mentees understand credential recognition and licensing pathways for regulated professions in Nova Scotia, and ISANS collaborates with regulatory bodies and professional associations to offer accurate guidance and referrals.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: The Connector Program introduces newcomers and international students to volunteer ‘Connectors’—established local professionals—who provide informational interviews, resume feedback, and three targeted industry introductions to expand networks and improve job readiness. Through partnerships with employers and professional networks, the program demystifies local hiring expectations and helps participants navigate sector norms and, when relevant, pathways toward credential recognition.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Neighbourhood Welcome Teams: Organize local volunteer welcome teams (residents, service clubs, faith groups) to do home visits, neighbourhood orientation walks, and introductions to schools, recreation, and local businesses, helping newcomers build informal social networks quickly.

resources.name: Community Connections
resources.organization: Immigration Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections program matches newcomers with volunteer hosts and welcome teams who provide informal settlement support. Volunteers offer neighbourhood orientation walks, coffee/home visits, and introductions to local schools, libraries, recreation programs, faith and community groups, and nearby businesses—helping newcomers quickly build social networks and feel at home.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: This island-wide volunteer network organizes local Welcome Groups and Ambassadors who meet newcomers, host community tours and walks, and connect families to schools, recreation, service clubs, and local businesses. By facilitating friendly, place-based introductions and ongoing check-ins, the network helps newcomers build informal social ties and integrate into Cape Breton communities.

resources.name: YREACH Host Program
resources.description: YREACH’s Host Program recruits and trains local volunteers across Nova Scotia to welcome and orient newcomers and their families. Hosts arrange meetups, neighbourhood walks, and introductions to schools, recreation, community services, and local businesses, providing practical guidance and social connections that support long-term settlement and retention.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 201, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Language Cafés and Conversation Circles: Run informal, drop-in language cafés hosted by libraries, cafés, or community centres where newcomers practice English (or French), share culture, and meet locals through conversation partners, story nights, and job-language sessions tailored to workplace vocabulary.

resources.name: English Conversation Group — Halifax Central Library
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts drop-in, volunteer-led English Conversation Groups where newcomers practice speaking in a welcoming, café-style setting. Sessions include themed discussions, story-sharing nights, and practical everyday and workplace vocabulary, connecting participants with local volunteers and other residents to build confidence and community ties.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Conversation Circles and English for Work
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS runs informal Conversation Circles that pair newcomers with volunteers and peers to practice English, share culture, and expand local networks in small, friendly groups. Complementary English-for-work offerings focus on job-search and workplace vocabulary (emails, interviews, safety, and customer service), helping participants gain the language needed for employment while integrating socially.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: English Conversation Group — McConnell Library (Sydney)
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library’s McConnell Library offers a weekly, drop-in English Conversation Group facilitated by community volunteers. Newcomers and international students practice speaking in a relaxed, café-style environment, discuss local life and services, and build connections with residents; occasional themed sessions highlight practical and work-related language.

resources.name: Café Français — French Conversation Sessions
resources.description: Alliance Française Halifax hosts informal Café Français meetups where learners and newcomers practice French with native speakers and advanced learners. Held at the centre and local cafés, these sessions emphasize everyday conversation, cultural exchange, and practical vocabulary useful for work and community life, helping participants build social connections in French.

solutions.text: Local Employer Pledge and Small-Business Incentives: Encourage a voluntary local employer pledge to hire and fairly assess internationally-trained candidates, paired with community incentives such as free job-posting on municipal boards, recognition awards, or local procurement preferences for champion employers.

resources.name: Employer Support Services (Inclusive Hiring & Job Posting)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS works directly with Nova Scotia employers to improve inclusive recruitment and fair assessment of internationally trained candidates through training, coaching, and tools on bias-aware screening and credential evaluation. Employers can post jobs to reach immigrant talent, participate in mentorship and bridging programs, and receive public recognition as employer partners, aligning with incentives and visibility for champion employers.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program invites local employers and business leaders to pledge time to meet internationally trained newcomers and international students, helping them access hidden job markets and fair consideration. Participating employers are publicly recognized as Connectors and gain visibility through the Partnership’s channels and events, creating a community incentive for inclusive hiring.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 701, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Social Procurement Program
resources.description: HRM’s Social Procurement Program embeds evaluation points for social value, including inclusive employment practices and hiring from equity-deserving groups such as newcomers, into municipal purchasing. This creates a local procurement preference for employers who commit to fair assessment and integration of internationally trained candidates, rewarding champion employers in competitive bids.

resources.name: Halifax Business Awards – Diversity, Equity & Inclusion Award
resources.description: The Halifax Business Awards include a DEI category that recognizes employers demonstrating inclusive recruitment, advancement, and workplace practices, including fair assessment of internationally trained candidates. Winners and finalists receive public recognition, media exposure, and promotion through the Chamber’s platforms, creating a strong community incentive for local businesses to champion inclusive hiring.
resources.address: 32 Akerley Boulevard, Unit 1, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1N1

solutions.text: Peer Buddy Program for Social Integration: Match newcomer families with established local ‘buddies’ (families, students, seniors) for regular social activities, child playdates, and cultural exchange. The program reduces isolation, supports childcare needs, and accelerates community belonging.

resources.name: Community Connections (Host and Buddy Program)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections program matches newcomer individuals and families with local volunteer buddies (families, students, and retirees) for regular meetups, playdates, and cultural exchange. Volunteers help newcomers practice English, discover neighbourhood resources, and join community events, reducing isolation and accelerating social integration and belonging.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YREACH Community Connections and Host Volunteers
resources.description: YREACH connects newcomers across Nova Scotia with local volunteer hosts who meet for coffee, family-friendly outings, and cultural exchange, and who introduce schools, childcare, and community resources. These buddy-style matches provide informal social support and language practice that reduce isolation and help newcomer families build local networks.

resources.name: International Student Peer Mentorship Program
resources.description: Dalhousie’s program pairs incoming international students with trained upper-year student buddies who meet regularly, attend campus and city activities together, and provide practical settlement support. This peer-buddy approach builds social ties, cultural exchange, and a sense of belonging that supports newcomer retention in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: International Student Ambassador (Peer Buddy) Program
resources.description: NSCC’s International Student Ambassador Program connects new international students with returning student ambassadors who act as peer buddies for regular meetups, study groups, and community activities. Ambassadors help newcomers navigate services, housing, and local culture across NSCC campuses, reducing isolation and fostering long-term community attachment.

solutions.text: Community Entrepreneurship Incubator: Launch a local incubator providing business mentorship, micro-grants, co-working space, and start-up workshops aimed at immigrant entrepreneurs and returning Canadians. Focus on low-cost startup guidance, market access, and mentorship from local business leaders.

resources.name: ISANS Business Development Services for Immigrant Entrepreneurs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides one-on-one business counselling, market research support, and a suite of start-up workshops tailored for newcomers starting or buying a business in Nova Scotia. The program connects immigrant entrepreneurs with local mentors and networks, offers access to shared work and meeting spaces, and helps clients navigate micro-financing and small funding opportunities through partner programs—delivering the mentorship, low-cost guidance, and market access central to the incubator solution.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: CEED – Startup Incubator & Co-working
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED delivers practical entrepreneurship training, mentorship from experienced local business leaders, and co-working space to help early-stage founders build and grow in Nova Scotia. Through programs that include business planning workshops, coaching, and access to financing (including microloans and partner funding), CEED lowers the cost and risk of starting up—supporting immigrant entrepreneurs and returning Canadians with hands-on guidance and a supportive peer network.

resources.name: Volta – Startup Hub & Incubator
resources.description: Volta provides founders with co-working space, community membership, and access to seasoned mentors and corporate partners, along with structured workshops and founder education (e.g., Volta Academy). Its flagship Volta Cohort program offers non-dilutive early funding awards and intensive mentorship, giving newcomers and returning Canadians a pathway to launch and scale locally with market connections, low-cost workspace, and targeted start-up support.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

solutions.text: School–Settlement Liaisons: Place trained settlement liaisons in schools to support newcomer children and their parents with school registration, language supports, extracurricular access, and connections to community programs—improving family attachment to the community.

resources.name: School Settlement Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS places specialized settlement staff in and alongside public schools to help newcomer students and their caregivers navigate registration, orientation, and ongoing communication with educators. Staff coordinate interpretation, connect families to English language learning, and link children to extracurriculars and community programs—functioning as school–settlement liaisons that strengthen family attachment to the community.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YREACH – School-Based Settlement Support
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth – Centre for Immigrant Programs (YREACH)
resources.description: Through the YREACH program, the YMCA places settlement practitioners in schools and regularly visits classrooms across Nova Scotia to assist newcomer families with school registration, orientation, and access to English support. Staff also bridge students to after-school activities, youth programs, and local community services, acting as dedicated liaisons between schools, families, and the wider community to support long-term integration and retention.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 3005, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Newcomer Welcome Centre and EAL Services
resources.description: HRCE operates a Newcomer Welcome Centre that assesses students’ language needs, supports school registration and placement, and liaises with families and educators to ensure appropriate English as an Additional Language (EAL) supports. The Centre connects families with in-school and community partners (such as ISANS and YMCA YREACH), and helps students access extracurriculars and community resources—serving a school-based hub role that mirrors settlement liaison functions.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

solutions.text: Community Cultural and Welcome Events: Host regular multicultural festivals, welcome dinners, and newcomer spotlights organized by neighbourhood associations to celebrate diversity, create visible inclusion, and provide low-barrier opportunities for newcomers to meet employers, service providers, and neighbours.

resources.name: Newcomer and Community Welcoming Programs (Central Library and branches)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts regular newcomer welcome fairs, multicultural celebrations, language conversation circles, and community spotlights that bring together newcomers, employers, and local service providers in accessible public spaces. Events at the Central Library and branches are free and family-friendly, lowering barriers to participation while showcasing diverse cultures and helping residents build social networks. By partnering with settlement agencies and municipal partners, these gatherings create visible inclusion and practical connections that support settlement and retention.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: YREACH Community Welcome Events
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth – Centre for Immigrant Programs (YREACH)
resources.description: The YMCA’s YREACH program organizes community welcome dinners, potlucks, multicultural nights, and newcomer spotlights across Nova Scotia communities, often in partnership with local municipalities, schools, and employers. These low-barrier events celebrate culture, introduce newcomers to neighbours and local services, and create opportunities to meet potential employers in an informal setting. By taking place in towns and neighbourhood hubs, YREACH enhances social integration and supports long-term newcomer retention.

resources.name: Nova Multifest
resources.description: Nova Multifest is an annual, free multicultural festival at Alderney Landing that features cultural performances, newcomer spotlights, international cuisine, and community exhibitor booths. The festival provides a welcoming, celebratory space for newcomers to connect with neighbours, local employers, and service providers while showcasing the diversity of the region. Its open, family-friendly format reduces barriers to participation and helps build social ties that support settlement and retention.

resources.name: Community Events and Newcomer Welcome Programming
resources.organization: Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21
resources.description: The Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21 hosts newcomer-focused community days, cultural celebrations, and citizenship ceremonies that bring together newcomers, employers, community organizations, and neighbours. These events highlight immigrant stories, celebrate cultural heritage, and provide information tables and networking opportunities with local services. By offering inclusive, public-facing programs at a central waterfront venue, Pier 21 creates visible inclusion and practical connections that aid settlement and retention.

solutions.text: Affordable Short-term Housing and Host Match: Develop a community-run temporary housing and host-family matching program (leveraging volunteers and local landlords) to give newcomers time to secure permanent housing and employment without immediate housing stress.

resources.name: Resettlement Assistance Program (RAP)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ RAP provides immediate, short-term accommodation for government-assisted refugees upon arrival in Nova Scotia, while staff help clients secure permanent housing and connect to employment and settlement services. The program coordinates with local hotels and landlords and leverages community partners to ensure affordable temporary placements, then supports transitions to long-term rentals through housing navigation, orientation, and landlord engagement. This directly implements the solution by relieving newcomers’ immediate housing stress and giving them time to stabilize and find work.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YREACH Host Homes (Ukrainian Response)
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth – YREACH (YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs)
resources.description: Through YREACH, the YMCA has coordinated a host-home and short-term accommodation network across Nova Scotia to match displaced Ukrainians and other newcomers with screened local hosts and participating landlords. Hosts provide free or low-cost temporary housing while YMCA settlement staff assist families with housing searches, employment navigation, and community connections, enabling a supported transition to permanent housing. The model leverages volunteers and community housing assets to reduce immediate housing pressure and improve newcomer retention.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Homestay Program
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Homestay Program matches newcomers (primarily international students and language learners) with vetted local host families who provide short-term room, meals, and community orientation. This host-match model eases immediate housing stress for new arrivals while they secure longer-term accommodation and employment or co-op placements, and it builds local social networks that support settlement and retention in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: The Language Centre Homestay Program
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University – The Language Centre
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University’s Language Centre operates a Homestay Program that places newcomers (especially ESL students) with screened host families for short-term, affordable accommodation and local integration support. By providing a stable landing place and community connections while participants arrange longer-term housing and employment-related activities, the program implements a practical host-family matching approach that reduces initial housing barriers.

obstacles.title: Post-secondary sustainability and research capacity limits
obstacles.description: Financial pressures on institutions, program cuts, and constrained research funding reduce innovation, talent pipelines, and the province’s appeal to students.

solutions.text: Community-sponsored micro-scholarships: Local businesses, service clubs, and residents pool small donations to create targeted micro-scholarships for students pursuing in-demand programs, trades, or research projects to improve access and retention.

resources.name: Scholarship & Bursary Funds
resources.description: The Community Foundation of Nova Scotia (CFNS) hosts scholarship and bursary funds that local businesses, service clubs, and residents establish and support through pooled contributions—often small gifts. These community-backed funds create targeted micro-scholarships for Nova Scotia students in in-demand areas such as skilled trades, health care, and applied research, improving access and retention. By administering and stewarding these funds province-wide, CFNS channels grassroots philanthropy into sustained student support.
resources.address: Suite 806, 1888 Brunswick Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3J8

resources.name: Make Way – The Campaign for NSCC (Student Awards & Bursaries)
resources.description: NSCC Foundation’s Make Way campaign mobilizes community donors—local employers, service clubs, alumni, and residents—to fund hundreds of small, targeted student awards and urgent-aid bursaries across Nova Scotia campuses. Many awards range from a few hundred to a few thousand dollars and are directed to high-demand programs and Red Seal trades, often sponsored by local companies. This pooled, community-driven micro-scholarship model removes financial barriers, boosts completion rates, and strengthens the province’s skilled workforce pipeline.

resources.name: Donor-Funded Bursaries and Awards
resources.description: Dalhousie University aggregates gifts from alumni, local businesses, and community members to sustain numerous small bursaries and scholarships for students. Many awards are targeted to in-demand programs and research areas—such as Engineering, Computer Science, and Health—providing micro-scholarships that reduce financial strain and help students persist. The centralized awards office administers these community-supported funds to enhance access and retention for Nova Scotia learners.

resources.name: Donor-Funded Scholarships & Bursaries
resources.description: Cape Breton University (CBU) partners with residents, community groups, and regional employers to fund many small scholarships and bursaries through pooled donations. These awards are often targeted to priority fields for the region—such as nursing, engineering technology, business, and community services—helping students afford studies and remain in Cape Breton. By channeling grassroots philanthropy into micro-scholarships, CBU strengthens local talent pipelines and student retention.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

solutions.text: Municipal internship and co-op partnerships: Municipalities and local employers coordinate to offer paid internships and co-op placements with clear pathways to employment, giving students practical experience and keeping talent in the region.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Student and Co-op Employment
resources.description: HRM partners with local post-secondary co-op offices to offer paid co-op and internship placements across municipal departments such as Planning & Development, Transportation & Public Works, ICT, Finance, and Recreation. These structured work terms are aligned with academic requirements, include mentorship and on-the-job training, and often lead to subsequent terms or entry-level municipal roles. By creating clear pathways to employment, the program helps retain young talent and strengthens local municipal capacity.

resources.name: Cape Breton Regional Municipality Student and Co-op Opportunities
resources.description: CBRM works with Cape Breton University, NSCC, and other institutions to hire paid co-op students and interns into municipal areas like engineering, planning, finance, IT, and recreation. Placements follow co-op agreements, provide supervision and mentorship, and frequently lead to additional terms or post-graduation hiring within the municipality. This coordinated approach gives students practical municipal experience and supports talent retention in Cape Breton.

resources.name: Municipality of East Hants Student and Co-op Employment Program
resources.description: The Municipality of East Hants offers paid co-op and internship roles across departments such as Planning & Development, Public Works, and Finance in partnership with university and NSCC co-op offices. Students complete defined work terms with mentorship and applied projects that align with academic outcomes, and successful participants are considered for seasonal or permanent roles. This creates a clear pathway from education to local municipal careers, keeping skilled graduates in the region.

resources.name: Municipality of the County of Kings Co-op and Student Employment
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: The County of Kings recruits paid co-op students and interns from Acadia University, Dalhousie, NSCC, and other institutions for placements in engineering, GIS, planning, IT, and community services. Terms are structured with campus co-op offices, include mentorship and real municipal project work, and often lead to subsequent placements or entry-level roles after graduation. The program links education with municipal practice to retain young professionals in the Annapolis Valley.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship
resources.description: Run by Clean Foundation, this province-wide program places paid student interns with host organizations—including municipalities across Nova Scotia—for 9–15 week terms focused on environment, climate, and community projects. Clean Foundation coordinates with municipal hosts and campus co-op offices, provides training and professional development, and many interns transition to longer-term roles with their host or other regional employers. The program creates structured, paid pathways that connect students to municipal and community careers while building local capacity.

solutions.text: Community-run maker spaces and labs: Neighborhoods, libraries, and community centres host shared maker spaces and basic research labs (tools, equipment, mentorship) so students and entrepreneurs can prototype ideas affordably.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Lou Duggan Creative Studio is a free, bookable makerspace offering tools like 3D printers, sewing machines, electronics kits, and digital media equipment. Library staff and community mentors run workshops and provide 1:1 guidance so youth, students, and entrepreneurs can learn skills and prototype ideas without high upfront costs. By lowering barriers to equipment and mentorship, it directly supports grassroots innovation and talent development in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: McConnell Library Makerspace / Innovation Lab
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library’s McConnell Library hosts an Innovation Lab with 3D printing, vinyl cutting, robotics, coding kits, and audio/visual tools that community members can book or access through guided programs. Staff-led workshops and drop-in sessions provide mentorship and practical skills, enabling students and early-stage entrepreneurs to test ideas and build prototypes affordably. The space strengthens local innovation capacity outside of post-secondary institutions.

resources.name: People’s Place Library Makerspace (Antigonish Town & County Library)
resources.description: The People’s Place Library offers a community makerspace with 3D printing, crafting/sewing tools, and STEAM kits, alongside staff-supported programs for all ages. These resources let youth, students, and small business founders experiment, iterate, and prototype without needing to purchase expensive equipment. By pairing tools with skills training and mentorship, the library fosters local creativity and entrepreneurship.

resources.name: Margaret Hennigar Public Library Creative Lab
resources.description: South Shore Public Libraries’ Creative Lab in Bridgewater provides shared equipment such as 3D printers, Cricut/vinyl cutters, sewing machines, and multimedia tools for community use. Through free or low-cost bookings, workshops, and staff support, the lab helps students, makers, and entrepreneurs prototype products and learn practical skills. This community-run space expands innovation opportunities beyond campus settings and supports local talent development.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

solutions.text: Local-business curriculum co-design: Employers and post-secondary faculty collaborate to co-design short modules and applied projects that align programs with local labour needs and improve graduate job-readiness.

resources.name: Program Advisory Committees (PACs)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College convenes Program Advisory Committees made up of local employers and faculty who regularly review and co-design curriculum elements, short modules, and applied course projects. Through these employer-informed updates and project briefs, programs are aligned to current regional labour needs, ensuring graduates build job-ready skills that match Nova Scotia’s economy.

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Nova Scotia Sandbox)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs partners with tech employers and Dalhousie faculty to co-create hands-on learning modules, industry challenge sprints, and course-integrated projects for computer science students. Companies define real problems and tools, while instructors embed these applied projects within coursework, directly aligning student learning outcomes with local digital and ICT workforce needs.

resources.name: COVE Skills and Workforce Development Programs
resources.description: COVE works with ocean-technology companies and faculty at institutions such as NSCC and Dalhousie to co-design short training modules, challenge projects, and applied research experiences. These employer-defined projects are delivered in collaboration with instructors and embedded in coursework or work-integrated learning, directly preparing students for in-demand roles in Nova Scotia’s ocean economy.

resources.name: Community Business Projects (Course-Embedded Consulting)
resources.description: The Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre collaborates with local employers and Sobey School faculty to design course-embedded consulting projects and micro-modules. Businesses co-develop project briefs and deliverables with instructors, enabling students to tackle real client challenges while faculty map these applied experiences to learning outcomes and local labour market needs.

solutions.text: Alumni mentorship and networking programs: Regional alumni groups mentor current students, host career panels, and create networking events to strengthen career pipelines and raise the province’s profile among graduates.

resources.name: Dal Alumni Link
resources.description: Dal Alumni Link connects current Dalhousie University students with alumni for one-to-one mentoring, career advice, and informational interviews. Alumni volunteers also participate in career panels and host networking events in Halifax and regional hubs, strengthening career pipelines in Nova Scotia and showcasing opportunities that encourage graduates to stay or return.

resources.name: X Connect (StFX Ten Thousand Coffees)
resources.organization: St. Francis Xavier University Alumni Association
resources.description: X Connect is St. Francis Xavier University’s alumni–student mentoring and networking platform, pairing students and recent grads with alumni for career conversations, mentorship, and industry insights. The program also mobilizes regional alumni to host career panels and mixers in Nova Scotia, building professional networks that support local talent pipelines and elevate the province’s profile among graduates.

resources.name: SMU Mentoring (Ten Thousand Coffees)
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University’s mentoring initiative connects students with alumni for guided mentoring matches, coffee chats, and career exploration. Alumni chapters and volunteers regularly lead panels, employer spotlights, and networking events in Halifax and across Nova Scotia, helping students transition into local industries and reinforcing the province as a compelling place to build a career.

resources.name: NSCC Alumni Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) Alumni Relations
resources.description: The NSCC Alumni Mentorship Program engages college alumni to mentor current students through career chats, mock interviews, classroom panels, and campus networking events across Nova Scotia. By activating sector-specific alumni networks and hosting employer-connected meetups, the program strengthens pathways into local trades and emerging industries while promoting Nova Scotia as a destination to live and work after graduation.

solutions.text: Community research priorities and funding pools: Local stakeholders identify priority research topics (e.g., ocean tech, clean energy, fisheries) and contribute to matching funds or prize grants that attract external research dollars.

resources.name: Net Zero Atlantic
resources.description: Net Zero Atlantic convenes industry, government, academia, and community stakeholders to define Atlantic Canada’s clean energy research priorities (e.g., offshore wind, grid decarbonization, marine renewables). It administers competitive, multi-partner research calls and feasibility studies that require partner co-funding, pooling provincial and industry dollars to leverage larger federal and private investments and attract external research funding into Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 5151 George Street, Suite 940, Halifax, NS B3J 1M5

resources.name: Ocean Frontier Institute (OFI)
resources.organization: Ocean Frontier Institute at Dalhousie University
resources.description: OFI is a pan-Atlantic research partnership led by Dalhousie University that works with industry, government, Indigenous and coastal communities to set priority ocean research themes (e.g., sustainable fisheries, ocean climate, technology). Through programs such as its Seed Fund and targeted calls, OFI requires partner cash/in-kind contributions and leverages federal and international programs (CFI, NSERC, others), pooling local resources to attract substantial external research dollars aligned with Nova Scotia’s priorities.

resources.name: DeepSense
resources.description: DeepSense matches ocean-sector companies with academic researchers and students to tackle industry-defined data and AI challenges in areas like fisheries, marine transportation, and ocean tech. Projects typically braid company contributions with Mitacs/NSERC and in‑kind high-performance computing credits (IBM/partners), effectively creating a local co-funding pool that attracts external research dollars while building Nova Scotia’s talent pipeline.

resources.name: Atlantic Fisheries Fund (Nova Scotia Stream)
resources.organization: Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) in partnership with the Province of Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Atlantic Fisheries Fund is a federal–provincial, cost‑shared program that supports innovation, infrastructure, and science partnerships across fisheries and aquaculture, with priorities set in consultation with regional stakeholders. Nova Scotia proponents must provide matching funds, enabling community and industry dollars to leverage large federal contributions and bring externally sourced research and development funding into the province.

resources.name: Atlantic Innovation Fund (AIF)
resources.description: AIF invests in large, collaborative R&D projects in Atlantic Canada’s priority sectors, including ocean technology and clean growth, with proposals shaped by regional industry and research partners. Its co‑investment model requires significant leveraging from provincial, institutional, and private sources, pooling local funds to attract substantial federal dollars to Nova Scotia’s universities, colleges, and firms.
resources.address: 1801 Hollis Street, Suite 2030, Halifax, NS B3J 3N4

solutions.text: Adopt-a-program sponsorships: Companies, non-profits, and community foundations sponsor at-risk certificate or diploma programs (equipment, student bursaries, instructor support) to prevent cuts and maintain diversity of offerings.

resources.name: Make Way: The Campaign for NSCC (Program and Equipment Funds)
resources.description: Make Way channels corporate, non-profit, and community foundation donations directly to specific NSCC certificate and diploma programs to fund equipment upgrades, student bursaries, and program enhancements. By letting donors ‘adopt’ program areas, campuses can keep smaller or at-risk offerings current and viable, supporting instructor capacity and safeguarding a diverse range of training options across the province.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Irving Shipbuilding Inc. (in partnership with Nova Scotia Community College and community partners)
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is an industry-sponsored training initiative in which Irving Shipbuilding partners with NSCC and community organizations to deliver shipbuilding-related trades programs. Irving funds student supports (tuition, tools/PPE, bursaries) and invests in program delivery and equipment, helping NSCC maintain and expand specialized trades offerings while creating a steady talent pipeline for Nova Scotia’s shipbuilding sector.

resources.name: CANS Construction Education and Research Foundation
resources.description: The CANS Foundation mobilizes donations from construction companies and industry partners to support construction-related certificate and diploma programs at NSCC. Funds flow into program-specific equipment purchases, shop and lab improvements, and student awards, which sustain instructor capacity and keep a broad mix of trades programs available across Nova Scotia despite budget pressures.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0A9

resources.name: Women Unlimited (Trades & Technology Program Sponsorships with NSCC)
resources.description: Women Unlimited partners with NSCC campuses and industry sponsors to co-deliver cohort-based pathways into trades and technology certificate/diploma programs. Corporate and philanthropic partners help underwrite student bursaries, tools/PPE, and targeted instructional capacity, effectively ‘adopting’ cohorts and programs to keep them running, diversify enrolment, and ensure graduates transition into sponsored work placements and apprenticeships.

solutions.text: Volunteer guest instructors and practicum hosts: Retired professionals and skilled tradespeople offer guest lectures, short courses, or supervise practica to expand program capacity and bring real-world expertise into classrooms.

resources.name: Corporate Residency MBA (CRMBA)
resources.organization: Rowe School of Business, Dalhousie University
resources.description: Dalhousie’s CRMBA pairs graduate business students with corporate partners for an eight-month residency in which industry supervisors coach students on real projects and professional practice. The Rowe School also embeds guest lectures, case coaching, and workshops from Executives and Entrepreneurs in Residence—often retired or semi-retired leaders who volunteer time—expanding instructional capacity with applied, real‑world expertise.

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab – Atlantic (CDL-Atlantic)
resources.organization: Creative Destruction Lab Atlantic at Dalhousie University
resources.description: Hosted at Dalhousie University, CDL-Atlantic engages experienced entrepreneurs, investors, and retired executives as volunteer Fellows and Associates who deliver intensive objective-setting sessions, office hours, and targeted feedback to early-stage science and tech ventures. These mentors act as guest instructors and practicum supervisors through CDL-linked courses and for-credit internships, bringing deep industry expertise into a university setting and expanding experiential learning capacity.

resources.name: Entrepreneurs‑in‑Residence (EIR) and Mentor Network
resources.description: The SMU Entrepreneurship Centre engages experienced entrepreneurs and industry professionals—including many retirees—as Entrepreneurs‑in‑Residence and volunteer mentors who deliver talks, short courses, and office hours for students and founders. The Centre also supervises applied consulting projects and placements with business hosts, giving students practicum-style, real‑world experience guided by practitioners.

resources.name: Co‑operative Education and Work‑Integrated Learning (WIL)
resources.description: NSCC’s WIL programs partner with employers, alumni, and skilled tradespeople across the province to host practicums, co‑ops, and clinical placements supervised by on‑site professionals. Many practitioners also volunteer as guest speakers and shop demonstrators, expanding instructional capacity and bringing up‑to‑date, hands‑on expertise directly into classrooms and labs.

solutions.text: Regional talent retention campaigns: Community groups run campaigns showcasing local career paths, quality of life, and success stories to encourage students to stay or return and to attract out-of-province students.

resources.name: Study and Stay Nova Scotia
resources.description: Study and Stay Nova Scotia is a province-wide retention initiative that supports international students to build careers and lives in Nova Scotia after graduation. It combines mentorship, career coaching, employer connections, and alumni ambassador storytelling that highlights real local career paths, lifestyle advantages, and success stories—encouraging students to stay or return and attracting out-of-province learners to consider Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1888 Brunswick Street, Suite 701, Halifax, NS B3J 3J8

resources.name: Work in Halifax (Talent Attraction & Retention Campaign)
resources.description: Work in Halifax is Halifax Partnership’s ongoing talent attraction and retention campaign that markets local career opportunities, cost-of-living advantages, and quality-of-life benefits to students and young professionals. Through storytelling profiles of graduates and returnees, student-focused events, and employer spotlights, the campaign showcases clear career paths in emerging and established sectors to encourage students to stay or return to Nova Scotia and to draw in out-of-province students.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Connector Program (Nova Scotia)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers the Connector Program in Nova Scotia to link internationally trained students and recent graduates with established local professionals for career conversations and introductions. Alongside networking events and success-story features that highlight real career pathways and the welcoming lifestyle in Nova Scotia, the program functions as a regional retention effort by helping students see concrete futures in the province and encouraging them to stay or return.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Community-run micro-grants for student research: Local foundations and businesses offer small competitive grants for student-led applied research and entrepreneurial projects to seed innovation and provide hands-on experience.

resources.name: RBC Student Pitch Competition (Starting Point Conference)
resources.description: Hosted annually by the Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre, the RBC Student Pitch Competition provides small cash awards to student-led startups and applied projects through a competitive pitch process. Funded by corporate partners and local sponsors, these micro-grants help students validate ideas, build prototypes, and gain hands-on entrepreneurial and research experience in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Protocase Student Sponsorship Program
resources.description: Cape Breton-based manufacturer Protocase provides in-kind micro-grants (manufacturing credits, materials, and services) to post-secondary student teams for engineering design, prototyping, and applied research. This business-led support seeds student innovation by reducing barriers to building and testing real-world solutions, giving participants practical, hands-on project experience.

resources.name: DSU Grants & Sponsorships (Student Project Grants)
resources.description: The Dalhousie Student Union administers small, competitive grants to student societies and individuals to launch student-led initiatives, including innovation-focused projects, prototyping, and community-based research collaborations. These micro-grants provide locally governed seed funding that helps students gain experience managing budgets, executing applied projects, and sharing results within the Halifax community.

resources.name: Student Initiative Fund
resources.description: The Acadia Students’ Union’s Student Initiative Fund offers micro-grants to Acadia students and societies to pilot student-led projects such as entrepreneurship events, prototype testing, and applied research with community partners in the Annapolis Valley. Administered locally by the student union, the fund provides seed capital and experiential learning opportunities that help students turn ideas into action.

solutions.text: Shared facilities consortium: Multiple institutions, municipalities, and businesses coordinate shared access to expensive equipment and labs to increase research capacity without duplicative costs.

resources.name: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.organization: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: COVE is a collaborative ocean-technology hub on the Dartmouth waterfront that provides shared access to specialized workshops, prototyping labs, testing equipment, marine docks, and subsea test ranges. It brings together businesses, universities/colleges, and government agencies to co-locate and share costly infrastructure, coordinating access and services to expand R&D capacity without duplicating facilities across institutions.

resources.name: The PIER at the Seaport
resources.description: The PIER is a port innovation living lab operated by the Halifax Port Authority that offers shared testbeds, data platforms, and workspace for logistics, ocean tech, and supply-chain collaborators. Municipal partners, universities, and private companies pilot and evaluate technologies with access to port operations and shared infrastructure, reducing the need for each partner to build separate labs and increasing collective research capacity.

resources.name: Verschuren Centre for Sustainability in Energy and the Environment
resources.description: The Verschuren Centre operates pilot-scale bioprocessing, materials, and clean-tech labs that companies and researchers can access on a fee-for-service or collaborative basis. By providing shared, industrial-grade equipment (e.g., bioreactors, downstream processing, and analytical instrumentation) and expert technical staff to multiple institutions and businesses, it enables scale-up R&D while avoiding duplicative capital expenditures and strengthening regional research capacity.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

resources.name: Ocean Frontier Institute (OFI)
resources.description: OFI is a multi-university partnership led from Dalhousie University that coordinates large shared ocean-research assets—such as gliders, moorings, specialized laboratories, and access to research vessels—across academia, government, and industry. By pooling infrastructure and managing cross-institutional access and scheduling, OFI expands research and training capacity in Nova Scotia while minimizing duplicative investment by individual organizations.

solutions.text: Trades apprenticeship accelerators: Employers and community colleges create accelerated apprenticeship cohorts with employer commitments, wraparound supports, and community awareness campaigns to rebuild trade pipelines.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding Inc.)
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based trades accelerator delivered by NSCC with hiring commitments from Irving Shipbuilding. It combines accelerated technical training, paid work experience, and mentorship with strong wraparound supports for participants from underrepresented communities (e.g., African Nova Scotian, Indigenous, women), leading directly into apprenticeship at the Halifax Shipyard. The program also conducts targeted outreach with community partners and employers to rebuild the shipbuilding trades pipeline in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: UA Local 56 Joint Apprenticeship and Training Program
resources.organization: United Association Local 56 (Plumbers, Pipefitters, and Welders)
resources.description: UA Local 56 operates an employer-backed apprenticeship pathway for plumbers, pipefitters, and welders in Nova Scotia, organizing cohort-style intakes aligned to contractor demand. The program delivers accelerated/upgrading technical training and safety certifications at its training centre, places apprentices with signatory employers, and provides mentorship and supports that help apprentices progress to Red Seal. UA Local 56 also undertakes outreach and awareness activities with schools and communities to promote careers in the piping trades.
resources.address: 32 Joseph Zatzman Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1N3

resources.name: NSCC Apprenticeship Technical Training (In-School)
resources.description: NSCC delivers the in-school technical training blocks and several condensed, cohort-based pathways in high-demand trades (e.g., carpentry, automotive service, welding) in partnership with employers and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency. Campuses coordinate employer commitments for placements and apprenticeship sponsorships while student services provide wraparound supports such as tutoring, Indigenous and newcomer advising, and financial aid navigation. The college also runs province-wide outreach and awareness initiatives to attract youth and career-changers to the skilled trades, strengthening the talent pipeline.

solutions.text: Community-driven curriculum for culture and arts: Local arts organizations partner with colleges to support arts programming through venue access, joint performances, and community studios, enhancing cultural education and retention of creative talent.

resources.name: Dalhousie–Symphony Nova Scotia Orchestral Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Fountain School of Performing Arts, Dalhousie University
resources.description: At Dalhousie’s Fountain School of Performing Arts, music students participate in an orchestral mentorship program with Symphony Nova Scotia. Through side-by-side rehearsals, masterclasses, and joint performances at the Rebecca Cohn Auditorium, students train with professional musicians in a professional venue integrated into their curriculum. This partnership expands access to high-calibre performance spaces and instruction, strengthening cultural education and helping retain emerging talent in the province.

resources.name: NSCC Creative Arts & Design – Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design Partnership
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design (in partnership with Nova Scotia Community College – Marconi Campus)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College delivers its Creative Arts & Design programming in partnership with the Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design, using the Centre’s professional studios, gallery, and community workshops in downtown Sydney. Students learn from practising artisans, present exhibitions in public venues, and access shared equipment and maker spaces that directly connect coursework to the local creative economy. The model embeds a community arts organization into college delivery, enriching curriculum, expanding venue access, and supporting the development and retention of creative practitioners in Cape Breton.

resources.name: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts – University Partnerships, Residencies, and Co-ops
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts / Two Planks and a Passion Theatre
resources.description: The Ross Creek Centre for the Arts and resident company Two Planks and a Passion Theatre host post-secondary students from NSCAD University, Acadia University, Dalhousie, and others for credited internships, residencies, and capstone placements. Students use Ross Creek’s studios, production shops, and outdoor/indoor stages for joint productions and exhibitions alongside professional artists. These community-embedded experiences broaden arts curricula, provide venue and studio access, and help keep early-career artists connected to Nova Scotia’s cultural sector.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

solutions.text: Civic advocacy and citizen funding initiatives: Residents organize advocacy coalitions and participatory budgeting efforts to lobby for sustained post-secondary funding and to direct local taxes or bonds to strategic educational investments.

resources.name: District 7 Participatory Budgeting (Halifax)
resources.description: District 7 uses a participatory budgeting process where residents propose and vote on how to allocate a portion of the District Capital Fund to community projects. This channels local tax dollars into strategic educational and youth-serving investments (such as makerspaces, literacy and arts programming, and campus-adjacent improvements) and builds civic advocacy by empowering residents to directly shape public spending priorities that support learning and talent development.

resources.name: Dalhousie Student Union – Government Relations and Advocacy
resources.description: The DSU is the elected student government at Dalhousie University that leads campaigns, budget submissions, and coalitions to advocate for increased and sustained public funding for universities and student financial support. By mobilizing students and community partners, the DSU advances civic advocacy to influence provincial policy on tuition, operating grants, and research capacity, strengthening Nova Scotia’s post-secondary system and talent pipeline.

resources.name: Cape Breton University Students’ Union – Advocacy for Accessible, Well-Funded PSE
resources.description: CBUSU represents students at CBU and coordinates advocacy at municipal and provincial levels for stable operating funding, research support, and affordable tuition. Through campaigns, consultations, and partnerships with other student associations, CBUSU amplifies resident voices to protect programs and research capacity, helping sustain a vibrant post-secondary ecosystem in Cape Breton.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

resources.name: NSGEU Post-Secondary Education Advocacy
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Government and General Employees Union (NSGEU)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Government and General Employees Union represents thousands of workers across universities and NSCC and runs public campaigns, submissions, and coalitions pressing for sustained public investment in post-secondary education and research. By organizing members and engaging the broader community, NSGEU advances civic advocacy that opposes cuts, protects programs, and strengthens research capacity across the province.
resources.address: 255 John Savage Avenue, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0J3

obstacles.title: Perception and branding of opportunity in Nova Scotia
obstacles.description: National narratives emphasize limited opportunity and lower pay, overshadowing strengths in lifestyle and emerging sectors and weakening talent attraction.

solutions.text: Community storytelling and alumni testimonial campaign: Collect and share short videos, written profiles and social posts from local residents and returnees highlighting real career paths, quality of life, and pay trajectories to counter national narratives with concrete local stories.

resources.name: ISANS Client Success Stories
resources.organization: Immigration Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS regularly collects and shares written profiles, videos, and social content highlighting immigrants and returnees who have built careers and lives in Nova Scotia. These stories showcase concrete career paths, credentials recognition, wage progression, and quality-of-life benefits, directly countering national narratives by amplifying real local experiences across sectors.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: NSCC Alumni Profiles
resources.description: NSCC curates alumni profiles and video testimonials that trace graduates’ career journeys in Nova Scotia—from trades and healthcare to tech and creative industries. The stories emphasize practical outcomes like job titles, career progression, and lifestyle advantages in communities across the province, using social and web channels to inspire young people to stay, study, work, and return.

resources.name: COVE News & Stories
resources.description: COVE publishes founder and workforce spotlights, video interviews, and written features that profile ocean-sector professionals and companies growing in Nova Scotia. By highlighting concrete roles, career pathways, and the province’s quality of life, these stories help rebrand Nova Scotia as a global blue-economy hub and demonstrate real opportunities for youth and returnees.

resources.name: CBU Alumni Stories
resources.description: Cape Breton University showcases alumni testimonials and profiles that chart career outcomes and life in Cape Breton and greater Nova Scotia. The campaign uses web features and social media to share authentic narratives about jobs, entrepreneurship, community impact, and lifestyle, helping prospective and current students see viable futures—professionally and personally—within the province.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1M 1A2

solutions.text: Local opportunity map and living-cost calculator: Publish an interactive map and simple calculator showing job openings by sector, average wages, housing costs, commute times and amenities by town to present an accurate, place-specific picture of opportunity and affordability.

resources.name: Job Bank – Cost of Living Calculator and Job Map
resources.description: Job Bank provides an interactive job search with map-based results for Nova Scotia communities and detailed occupation profiles with local wages and employment outlooks by region. Its Cost of Living Calculator estimates monthly expenses for specific NS towns and cities, allowing users to compare job openings by sector alongside localized wage and affordability information to form a clear, place-specific view of opportunity.
resources.address: 140 Promenade du Portage, Gatineau, QC K1A 0J9

resources.name: Explore Careers Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: Explore Careers Nova Scotia is the province’s official labour market portal offering interactive occupation profiles with wages, employment outlooks, and job openings mapped and filtered by region across the province. It complements job and wage data with regional comparisons and links to housing and cost-of-living resources, helping users weigh opportunity and affordability by specific Nova Scotia towns and communities.

resources.name: Work in Halifax (Job Board and Halifax Index)
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s Work in Halifax portal aggregates local job openings and sector information, while the Halifax Index publishes housing, affordability, wages, and quality-of-life indicators for communities across HRM. By connecting real-time jobs with wage benchmarks and cost-of-living insights, it offers a place-specific picture of opportunity and affordability that counters perceptions of limited prospects.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Work Here Cape Breton
resources.description: Work Here Cape Breton is an island-wide portal that features a job board highlighting openings by sector and location, alongside community profiles that describe housing, amenities, and lifestyle. It links to cost-of-living resources and provides localized wage and affordability context so candidates can assess job opportunities against what it costs to live in different Cape Breton towns.

solutions.text: Employer showcase nights and open business tours: Organize monthly events where local employers, startups and trades businesses host tours, demos and Q&A sessions so students and job-seekers can see real roles, pay ranges and career ladders in person.

resources.name: Onsite Recruitment and Information Sessions (ORIS) and Workplace Tours
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS runs ongoing employer-led ORIS events where companies host information sessions and Q&A at ISANS and on their worksites, often including facility tours and demonstrations. These sessions let jobseekers see real roles, typical wage ranges, and advancement pathways directly from hiring managers. By providing in-person exposure to local employers across sectors, the program delivers the kind of showcase nights and open business tours described in the solution.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Ocean Connector
resources.description: COVE’s monthly Ocean Connector series and regular facility tours bring ocean-technology employers together with students and jobseekers for live demos, employer panels, and Q&A. Attendees tour tenant labs and workshops at the waterfront campus to see roles in engineering, trades, and operations first-hand, with discussion of career paths and skills in demand. These recurring showcases directly implement employer showcase nights and open business tours, countering outdated perceptions by highlighting cutting-edge local opportunities.

resources.name: Women Unlimited Program
resources.description: Women Unlimited integrates frequent employer showcase evenings and structured worksite tours with trades and industrial partners across Nova Scotia. Participants meet hiring managers and journeypersons for demonstrations and candid Q&A about entry requirements, apprenticeship wages, and career ladders. This hands-on exposure lets women see real jobs and progression opportunities in person, aligning directly with the solution’s employer showcase nights and open business tours.

resources.name: Recruitment and Information Sessions (RIS)
resources.description: Through its Nova Scotia Works centre, TEAM Work Cooperative hosts recurring Employer Recruitment & Information Sessions (RIS) and coordinates workplace tours with local businesses. Employers deliver demonstrations, explain job duties, typical pay ranges, and progression opportunities, and answer participant questions in person. These events function as showcase nights and on-site visits that connect students and jobseekers directly with hiring employers and real career pathways.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Regional talent ambassador program: Train recent graduates and local professionals to act as ambassadors—speaking at schools, online, and at recruiting events—to promote Nova Scotia careers, answer questions about pay and lifestyle, and connect prospects with employers.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program mobilizes local business and community leaders as trained 'Connectors' who meet with recent graduates and newcomers to discuss career paths, wages, and lifestyle in Nova Scotia. Connectors make introductions to employers and other professionals, attend recruiting events, and speak with students and jobseekers, effectively acting as regional talent ambassadors who promote Halifax and Nova Scotia as places to build fulfilling careers.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Cape Breton Connector Program
resources.description: The Cape Breton Connector Program engages established local professionals as volunteer ambassadors who meet one-on-one with emerging talent, share insights about industries, salaries, and living in Cape Breton, and introduce them to employers in their networks. Through school visits, information sessions, and networking events, the program actively promotes regional career opportunities and helps candidates build connections that lead to jobs in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

resources.name: Immigrant Ambassadors
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Immigrant Ambassadors are trained newcomers and local professionals who share their stories, speak at schools and community events, and participate in outreach to highlight Nova Scotia’s quality of life and career opportunities. They answer practical questions about working and living in the province and often help connect prospective residents and graduates with ISANS employment services and employer networks, serving as authentic ambassadors for Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Community-run internship and co-op directory: Create and maintain a searchable directory of paid internships, co-ops and short-term placements offered by local businesses, with clear compensation info and application guidance to make opportunities visible and accessible.

resources.name: Digital Nova Scotia Job Board
resources.description: Digital Nova Scotia maintains a searchable job board for the province’s tech and digital sector that routinely features paid internships, co-ops, and short-term placements with local companies. Listings are tagged by role type (including internship/co-op), often include compensation details, and provide clear application instructions, making opportunities visible and accessible to students and early‑career talent while showcasing Nova Scotia’s growing tech ecosystem.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Volta Jobs Board
resources.description: Volta, Halifax’s startup hub, hosts a province-focused, searchable jobs board that includes paid internships and co-op placements at Nova Scotia startups and scaleups. Each listing includes application guidance and employer links, and many postings indicate compensation, helping students and new grads quickly find pathways into the local innovation economy.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 802, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

resources.name: COVE Ocean Sector Job Board
resources.description: COVE curates a searchable job board dedicated to Nova Scotia’s ocean and marine technology sector, regularly featuring paid internships, co-ops, and project-based placements with local firms and research organizations. Positions include role details, application steps, and, when provided by employers, salary information—spotlighting opportunities in an emerging sector and guiding applicants through the process.

resources.name: Management Career Services (myCareer) Co-op and Internship Portal
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Management Career Services operates the myCareer portal, a structured directory of paid co-op, internship, and short-term placements with Nova Scotia employers. Postings specify employment terms (including compensation when provided) and include clear application instructions and timelines, while MCS offers guidance on resumes, interview prep, and application strategy to improve access and outcomes.
resources.address: 6100 University Avenue, Suite 2100, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

solutions.text: Wage transparency and living-wage pledge toolkit: Develop a volunteer-supported toolkit for small employers to publish salary bands, commit to local living-wage standards where possible, and explain benefits/perks to improve recruitment and perceptions about pay.

resources.name: Employer Support: HR Toolkit & Inclusive Hiring
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides hands-on support and practical toolkits to help small and medium-sized employers create transparent job postings, including clear salary ranges and explanations of total compensation (benefits, perks, and pathways). Their employer advisors and workshops guide organizations to benchmark wages against local standards, reference Nova Scotia living-wage research, and adopt fair, competitive pay practices that improve recruitment and retention.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Employer Playbook: Talent Attraction & Retention Resources
resources.description: Halifax Partnership offers employer-focused guides and advisory support that encourage posting salary bands, communicating benefits/perks, and using clear, candidate-friendly language to position Halifax roles competitively. Their resources draw on local labour market insights and promote aligning offers with Nova Scotia living-wage research, helping small employers build transparent, credible compensation narratives that strengthen the region’s talent brand.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: HR for Startups Program & Volta Job Board Support
resources.description: Volta provides mentorship, workshops, and peer learning for startups on building compensation frameworks, publishing salary ranges, and articulating total rewards to candidates. Through programming and its job board support, Volta encourages transparent pay practices and connects founders to Nova Scotia living‑wage research and practical templates, enabling small employers to adopt clear salary bands and benefits explanations that improve hiring outcomes.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Mezzanine Level, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Employer Guide & Job Posting Standards (Co-op and Career)
resources.description: Dalhousie Management Career Services provides employers with guides, templates, and advising that encourage including salary ranges in job postings and clearly outlining total compensation to attract student and early‑career talent. Their standards and coaching help small organizations implement transparent pay practices and benchmark wages using local data, aligning offers with Nova Scotia cost‑of‑living insights and living‑wage research where feasible.
resources.address: Rowe Management Building, 6100 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

solutions.text: Return-to-Nova-Scotia welcome packs and concierge: Offer a community-curated welcome package for returnees with relocation checklists, housing leads, childcare and schooling info, employer contacts, and a volunteer concierge buddy to ease transition and showcase lifestyle benefits.

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: The Cape Breton Welcome Network mobilizes local volunteer Hosts and community groups to greet newcomers and returnees, offering a community-curated welcome that includes local guides, events, and introductions to services. They provide practical settlement support—such as information on housing options, schools and childcare, and employer contacts—while pairing people with a friendly local ‘concierge’ to ease transitions and highlight Cape Breton’s lifestyle benefits.

resources.name: Community Connections
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections program pairs newcomers with local volunteer mentors and families, creating a concierge-style buddy system that helps people navigate housing, schooling, childcare, and community life. Settlement staff also provide orientation sessions, checklists, and targeted referrals to employers and services—delivering a comprehensive welcome package that showcases Nova Scotia’s opportunities and quality of life.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YREACH (YMCA Reaching Out Across Communities)
resources.description: YREACH provides pre- and post-arrival settlement support across Nova Scotia, including personalized orientation, relocation checklists, and referrals for housing, childcare, schooling, health care, and community services. Through its regional network, staff and volunteers act as local concierges—connecting newcomers and returnees to employers, community groups, and events to build social ties and highlight local lifestyle advantages.

resources.name: Physician Recruitment – Relocation and Community Navigation
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s Physician Recruitment team provides concierge-style relocation support for incoming and returning physicians and their families, including community tours, school and childcare information, housing leads, and spousal employment assistance. They coordinate introductions to local practices, health teams, and community contacts, effectively offering a tailored welcome package that accelerates settlement and showcases Nova Scotia’s quality of life.
resources.address: 90 Lovett Lake Court, Halifax, NS B3S 0H7

solutions.text: Youth entrepreneurship microgrants and pop-up marketplaces: Provide small startup grants, mentorship and temporary retail/market space for young entrepreneurs to test ventures locally and demonstrate that viable businesses and earnings grow in the region.

resources.name: Business Is Jammin’ (Youth Entrepreneurship Programs & Pop-Up Markets)
