resources.organization: Business Is Jammin’ (a program of the Black Business Initiative)
resources.description: Business Is Jammin’ runs entrepreneurial programs for Black youth across Nova Scotia, combining mentorship, skills training, and real-world selling opportunities. Through pitch events that award small seed grants and youth-focused pop-up markets/showcases, participants test products in local venues, gain customers, and build confidence that viable businesses and earnings are possible at home in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 309, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Junior Achievement Nova Scotia – Company Program
resources.description: JA’s Company Program mentors high school students to ideate, launch, and run small businesses over a semester, supported by volunteer business mentors. Students receive startup resources and seed capital mechanisms (such as sponsored shares) and sell through public trade fairs and pop-up marketplaces in community venues—giving them hands-on retail experience and proof that entrepreneurship can thrive in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 201, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Halifax Public Libraries – Youth/Teen Pop-Up Markets
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts youth and teen entrepreneur pop-up markets at branches like the Central Library, offering free or low-cost vendor space, staff support, and promotional reach. These markets let young makers and startups test products, pricing, and branding with real customers, often paired with entrepreneurship workshops and mentorship from local partners.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: New Glasgow Farmers Market – Market Sprouts Youth Vendor Program
resources.description: Market Sprouts gives youth dedicated vendor opportunities within the New Glasgow Farmers Market, including guidance from market staff and seasoned vendors. By providing a high-traffic, supportive pop-up setting and low-barrier table access, young entrepreneurs can validate products, build customer relationships, and see a clear path to earning locally.
resources.address: 620 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3S2

solutions.text: School-industry partnership and career pathways: Establish formal partnerships between local schools, community colleges and employers to co-design curricula, apprenticeships and pathways that lead directly to in-demand local jobs with transparent earnings progression.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding Inc. and Unifor Canada
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based training initiative that brings NSCC together with Irving Shipbuilding, Unifor, and community partners to recruit and train underrepresented Nova Scotians for skilled trades at the Halifax Shipyard. Employers co-design curriculum and shop training, provide mentors, paid work terms, and guaranteed interviews so learning maps directly to in-demand roles. Graduates transition into registered apprenticeships with defined certification levels and wage steps, offering a transparent progression into stable marine trades careers.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (NSAA)
resources.description: NSAA manages apprenticeship training across Nova Scotia by formally linking high schools, NSCC, and employers to develop talent pipelines in more than 70 trades. It works with industry advisory groups to align curricula and on-the-job training, registers youth apprentices, and enables students to earn both high-school/apprenticeship credits through real job placements. Apprentices advance through provincially regulated levels with published wage scales and certification milestones, ensuring transparent earnings progression into in-demand local jobs.

resources.name: P-TECH Nova Scotia (Pathways in Technology Early College High School)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) with Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development, IBM Canada, and regional school boards
resources.description: P-TECH Nova Scotia creates a seamless pathway from high school through an NSCC diploma into entry-level IT roles with partners like IBM and local employers. High schools, NSCC faculty, and industry jointly define competencies, coursework, mentorship, and paid work-integrated learning so students graduate job-ready for regional tech roles. The model emphasizes clear role expectations and stacked credentials that map to transparent entry-level wages and advancement opportunities in Nova Scotia’s digital economy.

resources.name: Science, Information Technology, and Engineering Co‑op (SITE Co‑op)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s SITE Co‑op program connects students with paid 4–8 month work terms at Nova Scotia employers in ICT, oceans, clean tech, and advanced manufacturing. Employer advisory input and ongoing supervisor evaluations inform program outcomes and technical curricula, while co‑op coordinators align job-ready skills with local demand. Graduates build direct pathways into full-time roles—often with the same employers—benefiting from documented salary bands and clear early-career progression after co‑op.

solutions.text: Remote-worker hubs with cultural programming: Develop or promote affordable co-working hubs that bundle reliable internet, social events, childcare drop-ins and local experience days to attract remote workers who value Nova Scotia's lifestyle while maintaining external pay.

resources.name: Volta (Community & Coworking)
resources.description: Volta is a large, downtown Halifax coworking and innovation hub that offers reliable internet, desks, meeting rooms, and community membership options well-suited to remote workers. It implements the solution by bundling workspace with frequent social and cultural programming—such as networking mixers, founder talks, pitch nights, and community meetups—that connect remote professionals to Nova Scotia’s tech, arts, and startup scenes while they maintain external employment. Its central location enables easy access to local culture, events, and amenities that showcase the province’s lifestyle.

resources.name: Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE is a waterfront innovation campus in Dartmouth providing shared workspaces, labs, and high-speed connectivity for ocean-sector companies, startups, and remote professionals. It advances the solution by pairing quality coworking infrastructure with regular community programming—industry talks, demo days, meetups, and public engagement events—that immerse remote workers in Nova Scotia’s blue-economy culture and local experiences on the harbour. The campus fosters cross-sector networking and lifestyle appeal while enabling people to keep external clients or employers.

resources.name: CO3 Coworking Space
resources.description: CO3 is a community-oriented coworking hub on the South Shore that offers flexible desks, private offices, meeting rooms, and robust internet for freelancers and remote employees. It implements the solution by combining affordable workspace with regular social and learning events—networking coffees, workshops, and collaborations with local organizations—that connect members to Bridgewater’s creative and entrepreneurial culture. The space attracts remote workers seeking community and lifestyle advantages while continuing to work for employers elsewhere.

resources.name: New Dawn Centre for Social Innovation – Coworking
resources.description: Located in Sydney, the New Dawn Centre provides coworking and shared offices alongside a hub of social enterprises, nonprofits, and cultural groups, with reliable internet and meeting spaces for remote professionals. It delivers the solution by embedding remote work infrastructure within an active community venue that regularly hosts cultural programming, community gatherings, and learning events—linking remote workers to Cape Breton’s arts, social impact, and local experience opportunities. This integrated setting helps attract and retain talent drawn by Nova Scotia’s lifestyle while maintaining external pay.

solutions.text: Sector spotlight festivals and hands-on workshops: Host regular pop-up festivals that spotlight tech, creative industries and skilled trades with hands-on workshops, employer booths and live demonstrations to showcase opportunities and local pay realities.

resources.name: H2O: Home to Overseas Conference & Exhibition
resources.organization: Ocean Technology Council of Nova Scotia (OTCNS)
resources.description: H2O is Atlantic Canada’s flagship ocean technology conference featuring an industry exhibition, employer booths, in-water demos, and technical workshops that spotlight local ocean tech careers and companies. It implements the solution by creating a festival-like showcase where youth and jobseekers can try equipment, meet hiring employers, and attend sessions that discuss career paths and pay realities in Nova Scotia’s thriving ocean sector.

resources.name: COVE Ocean Connector & Demo Day Series
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE hosts recurring Ocean Connector meetups and Demo Days where resident companies and researchers provide hands-on demonstrations of marine tech, tours of labs and test facilities, and networking with employers. These events function as sector spotlights by showcasing real projects, skills, and local job opportunities—including discussions about roles, career routes, and compensation—helping young people see viable futures in Nova Scotia’s blue economy.

resources.name: CANS Construction Job Fair
resources.description: This annual expo brings together construction and skilled trades employers with interactive displays, equipment demos, and on-the-spot recruitment for roles across Nova Scotia. By offering a hands-on, sector-focused fair with employer booths and information on apprenticeships, certifications, and typical local wages, it directly addresses perceptions about opportunity and pay in the trades.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: NSCC Province-wide Open House
resources.description: NSCC’s open house events at campuses across the province feature shop and lab tours, live demonstrations, and hands-on workshops across technology, creative programs, and skilled trades. Industry partners and college advisors host booths and info sessions that outline local job pathways and typical wages, offering a practical, sector-spotlight experience that helps students and young adults envision careers in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Collective employer branding and recruitment collateral: Form a community marketing cooperative that produces consistent recruitment materials (videos, job templates, benefits lists) that small businesses can use to present professional, positive branding about roles and compensation.

resources.name: ISANS Employer Support Services
resources.organization: Immigration Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: Immigration Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS) provides a coordinated suite of employer branding and recruitment resources that small and medium-sized businesses can adopt, including job description templates, inclusive hiring guides, onboarding checklists, and ready-to-use outreach materials. Through workshops and customized advising, ISANS helps employers co-brand collateral and communicate clear roles, benefits, and compensation to attract talent, reinforcing a consistent, positive message about career opportunities in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Study and Stay Nova Scotia – Employer Resources
resources.description: EduNova’s Study and Stay Nova Scotia program includes employer-facing tools such as job posting templates, interview guides, onboarding checklists, and shareable lifestyle-and-work videos designed for SMEs recruiting international students and recent graduates. These materials provide a consistent, province-positive brand that employers can customize, helping to counter perceptions of limited opportunity while clearly presenting roles, benefits, and career paths in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1888 Brunswick Street, Suite 701, Halifax, NS B3J 3J8

resources.name: Tourism HR Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Tourism Industry Association of Nova Scotia (TIANS)
resources.description: Tourism HR Nova Scotia, a division of TIANS, offers a centralized recruitment toolkit for tourism and hospitality employers, including standardized job description templates, compensation and benefits guides, and ready-made marketing collateral that businesses can co-brand. By equipping hundreds of small operators with consistent, professional recruitment materials and sector-wide messaging, the program strengthens collective employer branding and supports talent attraction across the province.

resources.name: Talent at COVE
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE’s Talent at COVE platform supports ocean-sector employers with shared recruitment assets—employer profile templates, sector brand messaging, and promotional videos highlighting Nova Scotia’s blue economy and lifestyle—that small firms can use to present professional job postings. By centralizing collateral and storytelling for the ocean tech community, it creates a consistent, positive brand for roles and compensation, improving SMEs’ reach and credibility with prospective talent.

solutions.text: Local media partnerships for positive narratives: Partner with regional radio, newspapers and podcasters to produce series about thriving local careers, sector growth stories and breakout employers to shift external narratives toward strengths and opportunities.

resources.name: Land and Sea — Nova Scotia stories
resources.description: Land and Sea is CBC Atlantic’s long-running regional series, with frequent Nova Scotia episodes that profile innovators in fisheries, farming, tourism, ocean tech, crafts, and other growth sectors. By broadcasting in-depth, locally produced stories about entrepreneurs, skilled tradespeople, and standout employers across TV, radio, and digital, the show creates positive narratives about real career pathways and sector momentum in the province. Community, industry, and education partners regularly work with CBC producers to surface story leads, aligning closely with the goal of using local media to highlight strengths and opportunity.

resources.name: Pursuing the Edge (podcast)
resources.description: Pursuing the Edge is IGNITE Atlantic’s podcast that showcases founders, employers, and professionals building careers in oceans, agri-food, clean tech, digital, and creative industries across rural and small-urban Nova Scotia. Each episode spotlights tangible career pathways, breakout employers, and sector growth stories, reframing provincial narratives toward opportunity and impact. Produced locally and distributed broadly, the podcast partners with businesses and ecosystem organizations to tell authentic success stories that attract and retain talent.

resources.name: Build Right Nova Scotia campaign
resources.organization: Build Right Nova Scotia (an initiative of Mainland Building Trades and the Construction Association of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Build Right Nova Scotia is a province-wide public-awareness initiative from the construction industry that runs multi-channel partnerships with local radio, TV, and newspapers to highlight the skilled trades. Through interviews, profiles, and campaign series about major projects, employers, apprentices, and career ladders, it positions construction as a rewarding, future-proof path in Nova Scotia. By collaborating with media outlets to share positive career narratives, the campaign counters perceptions of limited opportunity and lower pay.

resources.name: Invest Nova Scotia Stories
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia produces and places sector growth and employer success stories that highlight thriving careers in oceans, ICT, clean tech, agri-food, and advanced manufacturing. Working with regional media and content partners, these stories appear as articles, videos, and sponsored features that spotlight breakout employers and real pathways for youth and newcomers. The series reframes provincial perception by consistently amplifying strengths, quality of life, and opportunity across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 701, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

solutions.text: Mentorship circles linking students with local leaders: Create recurring mentorship groups that connect youth with experienced local professionals for career advice, internships, networking and realistic discussions about pay, growth and lifestyle choices.

resources.name: WISEatlantic Mentor Café
resources.organization: WISEatlantic (Women in Science and Engineering – Atlantic), Mount Saint Vincent University
resources.description: WISEatlantic hosts recurring Mentor Café events that bring high school girls and post-secondary students together with women working in STEM across Nova Scotia. In small-group roundtables, mentors share candid insights on local career paths, salaries, work-life balance, and growth opportunities, and help students build networks for job shadowing and internships. These sessions create ongoing mentorship circles that highlight real opportunities in the province’s STEM sectors.

resources.name: Volta Academy
resources.description: Volta Academy is a multi-week, cohort-based program for students and aspiring founders that includes workshops and mentor roundtables led by local founders, investors, and industry experts. Participants receive realistic guidance on startup life, compensation, career paths, and pathways into internships or co-ops with Nova Scotia tech companies. The cohort model builds recurring mentorship circles and strong local networks that demystify opportunities in the region.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: COVE Ocean Connector
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE’s monthly Ocean Connector series and student-focused events convene ocean-sector leaders with students and early-career talent. Through recurring panels, small-group networking, and mentorship, participants learn about roles, wages, and career growth in Nova Scotia’s blue economy and make contacts for co-ops and internships. These gatherings function as mentorship circles linking youth with local engineers, entrepreneurs, and researchers.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Career & Experiential Learning – Mentoring Program
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University, Career & Experiential Learning
resources.description: SMU’s mentoring program connects students with alumni and Halifax-area professionals through structured mentoring cohorts, office hours, and networking events. Mentors provide practical advice on career pathways, compensation expectations, and lifestyle choices in Nova Scotia, and often facilitate internships and workplace learning. The program fosters recurring mentorship circles that help students build confidence and strong local connections.

solutions.text: Community land trust and affordable housing pilots: Support local housing initiatives—community land trusts or co-op housing pilots—that make living locally economically viable and allow pay comparisons to focus on net standard of living rather than headline salaries.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia builds and sells homes to eligible low- and moderate-income families using an affordability model (no-interest, geared-to-income mortgages and volunteer-built homes) that substantially lowers monthly housing costs. By creating stable, attainable homeownership, the program makes it economically viable for families to live and work locally, supporting the solution’s focus on improving net standard of living rather than competing on headline salaries.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Housing
resources.description: New Dawn Community Housing acquires, develops, and operates non-market rental housing in Cape Breton, maintaining below-market rents and long-term community ownership. By expanding affordable, community-controlled housing options in Sydney and surrounding areas, it helps residents stay rooted locally and improves overall affordability, directly aligning with the solution’s aim to make local living economically viable.

resources.name: YWCA Halifax Housing Programs
resources.description: YWCA Halifax provides affordable and supportive housing for women, gender-diverse people, and families (including programs like supportive housing for young mothers), combining safe units with wraparound services. These non-market and supportive options reduce housing costs and stabilize tenancies, enabling residents to build sustainable lives locally and reinforcing the solution’s emphasis on affordability as a driver of quality of life.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: Riverside Estates Affordable Housing
resources.description: Operated by the Antigonish Affordable Housing Society, Riverside Estates provides non-market, energy-efficient rental apartments with rents geared to income, created through community partnerships and local fundraising. By adding permanently affordable units under community stewardship, the initiative reduces cost-of-living pressures and supports residents to remain in Antigonish, directly implementing the solution’s community-based affordable housing approach.

solutions.text: Skills-bridging bootcamps funded by local employers: Coordinate short, employer-backed training programs to upskill local candidates for emerging roles with clear job-placement commitments and published starting wages so prospects see attainable, paid pathways.

resources.name: Irving Shipbuilding Centre of Excellence (ISCoE) at NSCC
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding Inc.)
resources.description: ISCoE coordinates employer-funded, cohort-based training delivered by Nova Scotia Community College to prepare Nova Scotians for in-demand shipbuilding roles (e.g., welding, metal fabrication) with Irving Shipbuilding as the hiring employer. Through initiatives like Pathways to Shipbuilding, Irving funds seats and provides conditional job offers to successful graduates at the Halifax Shipyard, while unionized starting wages and progression rates are publicly posted via collective agreements—creating a clear, paid pathway from training to employment.

resources.name: Women Unlimited – Career Discovery and Employer-Sponsored Pathways
resources.description: Women Unlimited designs short, cohort-based pre-apprenticeship programs in partnership with Nova Scotia employers (e.g., Irving Shipbuilding, Nova Scotia Power, construction and trades employers) that include employer sponsorship, paid work terms, and conditional hiring or apprenticeship seats upon completion. Because placements are tied to employers with published starting wages—often set through collective agreements—participants see transparent, attainable routes into well-paid, in-demand roles.

resources.name: Shannex Continuing Care Assistant (CCA) Training Program
resources.description: Shannex funds tuition and provides paid, employer-backed training and work-integrated learning for aspiring Continuing Care Assistants, with successful graduates offered employment at Shannex communities across Nova Scotia. Starting CCA wages are publicly posted in Shannex job listings and provincial wage tables, giving candidates a transparent view of earnings while moving through a short, skills-bridging pathway directly into a guaranteed role.
resources.address: 1226 Hollis Street, Suite 400, Halifax, NS B3J 1T6

obstacles.title: Housing Affordability and Availability
obstacles.description: Rents and home prices have outpaced local earnings, vacancy rates are low, and construction capacity is constrained. A lack of diverse, attainable options—especially for students, newcomers, and young families—pushes people to leave or delays life milestones.

solutions.text: Community Land Trust (CLT): Form a nonprofit CLT to acquire and hold land permanently, separating land ownership from housing ownership so homes can be sold or leased at permanently affordable rates for students, newcomers and young families.

resources.name: Habitat Homeownership Program (Ground Lease/Shared-Equity Model)
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia builds and sells homes to qualifying low- and moderate-income families using shared-equity and long-term affordability covenants; in some projects, the organization retains land ownership or uses ground leases to separate land from the home, ensuring resale restrictions keep homes permanently affordable. By holding the underlying land in nonprofit stewardship and limiting appreciation on the structure, Habitat preserves affordability for future student households, newcomers, and young families who might otherwise be priced out.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Housing (Long-term Land Stewardship)
resources.description: New Dawn Enterprises acquires and holds land and buildings in community ownership and delivers below-market rental housing across Sydney and Cape Breton, preserving affordability over the long term. By keeping land and assets under nonprofit control and leasing units at attainable rates, New Dawn implements core community land trust principles—separating speculative land value from housing costs—to ensure stable, affordable homes for young families, newcomers, and working residents.

solutions.text: Housing Co-operatives: Support formation and expansion of housing co-ops where residents collectively own and manage buildings, lowering costs through shared governance and long‑term stability.

resources.name: Co-operative Development Services
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Co-operative Council provides hands-on support to groups forming or expanding housing co-operatives across the province. Services include feasibility and business planning, incorporation under the Nova Scotia Co-operatives Act, board/governance training, and links to financing through credit unions—helping resident-owned co-ops lower costs via shared governance and long-term stability.

resources.name: Atlantic Region Member Services
resources.organization: Co-operative Housing Federation of Canada (CHF Canada)
resources.description: CHF Canada supports existing and emerging housing co-operatives in Nova Scotia with governance training, asset management guidance, refinancing tools, and policy support. By strengthening resident-owned co-ops and enabling new co-op development, CHF Canada helps keep rents affordable through collective ownership and long-term, mission-driven management.

resources.name: Program Administration and Support for Federal Co‑op Housing (Atlantic)
resources.description: The Agency for Co-operative Housing administers federal operating agreements and related supports for housing co-ops in Nova Scotia, providing compliance oversight, financial analysis, and guidance on maintaining affordability. Its work helps resident-controlled co-ops remain stable, reinvest in buildings, and keep rents lower over the long term through the co-operative model.

solutions.text: Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) Support Program: Provide toolkits, design templates, permitting navigation, small grants or low‑interest loans and vetted contractor lists to help homeowners create legal secondary suites and laneway homes.

resources.name: Secondary and Backyard Suites
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality provides homeowners with step-by-step guidance to create legal secondary suites and backyard (laneway) suites, including zoning lookups, permit checklists, sample drawings, and inspection requirements. Planning staff offer pre-application consultations and permitting navigation to streamline approvals, and HRM’s design resources (including outcomes from a backyard suites design competition) help residents choose code-compliant layouts and engage qualified contractors.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, 2nd Floor, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Secondary Suites (County of Kings)
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings – Community Development Services
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings supports homeowners to add legal secondary suites by providing clear guidance on where suites are permitted, what building and fire code standards apply, and how to navigate development and building permits. Planning staff help residents assess feasibility on their lot, prepare compliant plans, and move through approvals, effectively serving as a permitting navigator and technical resource.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Secondary and Backyard Suites (Town of Bridgewater)
resources.description: The Town of Bridgewater enables and guides the creation of secondary and backyard suites through homeowner-facing resources that explain zoning permissions, design considerations, and permit/inspection steps. Town planning staff provide pre-application advice and permitting navigation to help residents develop code-compliant rental suites, expanding attainable housing options in existing neighbourhoods.

solutions.text: Modular and Tiny-Home Pilot Projects: Develop community pilot sites for modular and tiny homes as transitional or workforce housing, using local land, shared amenities and cooperative ownership models to speed delivery and reduce costs.

resources.name: Modular Supportive Housing (HRM)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality deployed modular, small-footprint housing clusters on municipal land to provide rapid, transitional housing for people experiencing homelessness. The sites use prefabricated sleeping units with shared amenity trailers (washrooms, showers, common spaces) and are operated with nonprofit partners to deliver wraparound supports, demonstrating a pilot approach to tiny-home/modular villages that can be scaled to meet workforce and transitional needs.

resources.name: Community Micro‑Shelter Villages
resources.organization: Out of the Cold Community Association
resources.description: Out of the Cold Community Association operates small, modular micro‑shelter (tiny‑cabin) villages in HRM, providing secure sleeping cabins paired with shared amenities and common areas. The organization delivers onsite case management, meals, and community supports that help residents stabilize and transition to longer‑term housing or employment—an active, real‑world pilot of tiny‑home style transitional housing on local land.

resources.name: Modular Student Housing Expansion
resources.description: Cape Breton University added modular residence buildings on campus land to quickly increase bed capacity for students, easing pressure on the local rental market. The prefabricated units connect to shared amenities (laundry, kitchens, lounges) and are managed cooperatively within the university’s residence system, demonstrating how modular construction can deliver attainable, community‑oriented housing for the student workforce.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

resources.name: Millbrook Tiny Homes Initiative
resources.description: Millbrook First Nation has advanced a cluster of small and tiny homes on band‑owned land to create attainable housing for singles and young adults within the community. The homes are modest, quickly assembled units arranged with shared spaces and services, using a band‑governed, community‑centric model that lowers costs and speeds delivery—aligning with tiny‑home pilot concepts for transitional and workforce housing.

solutions.text: Vacant Building and Underused Land Conversion Initiative: Map vacant properties and idle commercial buildings and coordinate volunteer, nonprofit and municipal efforts to convert them into multi‑unit rentals, student housing or mixed-use community hubs.

resources.name: Surplus Property for Affordable Housing Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality identifies and inventories underused and surplus municipal properties, then prioritizes them for affordable and mixed-income housing through requests for proposals and partnership agreements. The program enables conversions of idle buildings or lots into multi-unit rentals and community-oriented spaces by working with nonprofits, co-ops, and developers, and by aligning with federal/provincial programs like the Rapid Housing Initiative. This directly advances the solution by mapping public assets and coordinating municipal and nonprofit efforts to transform them into housing and mixed-use community hubs.

resources.name: Land for Housing Initiative
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia leads a province-wide effort to identify, assemble, and prepare underused or surplus provincial lands and buildings for housing, issuing calls to partners to deliver mixed-income and attainable units. The initiative coordinates municipalities, nonprofits, and developers to repurpose idle properties, expedite servicing, and convert suitable buildings to residential or community-use purposes. This implements the solution by mapping public assets and driving adaptive reuse and infill that can include student housing and multi-unit rentals.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Homebuilding & Revitalization Program
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia acquires donated or underused land and buildings and mobilizes volunteers, trades, and community partners to construct or rehabilitate multi-unit townhomes and duplexes for moderate-income families. By converting idle or derelict properties and building on surplus or donated parcels in partnership with municipalities and donors, the program increases attainable rental and ownership options. This aligns with the solution by coordinating volunteers and nonprofits to transform underused sites into multi-unit housing.

resources.name: New Dawn Properties – Building Reuse & Affordable Housing
resources.description: New Dawn identifies vacant or underused buildings in Sydney and the CBRM area and redevelops them into affordable rentals and community hubs, often combining housing with arts, social enterprises, and services. Projects have included the adaptive reuse of legacy buildings and coordination with public programs (e.g., CMHC and provincial partners) to finance conversions and create inclusive, mixed-use spaces. This implements the solution by mapping local underutilized assets and converting them into multi-unit housing and community-serving facilities.

solutions.text: Employer-Assisted Housing Partnerships: Encourage local employers, colleges and hospitals to offer rental guarantees, down‑payment assistance, or employer‑owned rental units tied to local hiring and retention strategies.

resources.name: Cabot Cape Breton Staff Housing
resources.description: Cabot Cape Breton provides employer-managed staff accommodations for seasonal and year-round team members working at its Cabot Links and Cabot Cliffs properties. By reserving and operating dedicated housing for employees, the company removes upfront rental barriers and stabilizes tenures tied to hiring and retention, directly reflecting an employer-assisted housing model.

resources.name: Fox Harb’r Resort Employee Housing
resources.description: Fox Harb’r Resort operates on-site and nearby staff accommodations for team members, offering furnished rooms and shared units with rent often managed through payroll deduction. This employer-provided housing is explicitly tied to recruitment and retention, ensuring new hires can secure attainable accommodations in a tight rural market—an example of employer-assisted housing.
resources.address: 1337 Fox Harbour Road, Fox Harbour, NS B0K 1Y0

resources.name: Keltic Lodge Staff Accommodation Program
resources.description: Keltic Lodge at the Highlands provides employer-run staff housing for seasonal and returning employees working in the resort and hospitality operations. By maintaining dedicated staff residences and reserving rooms for workers each season, the employer reduces competition in the local rental market and directly links housing access to workforce recruitment and retention.
resources.address: 383 Keltic In Road, Ingonish Beach, NS B0C 1L0

resources.name: Dalhousie Medicine Distributed Medical Education – Learner Accommodations
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Distributed Medical Education unit coordinates and funds accommodations for medical students and residents during rural and regional clinical placements across Nova Scotia, often reserving apartments or securing rooms in partnership with local hospitals and communities. These university- and hospital-facilitated housing arrangements act as rental guarantees and dedicated units tied to training and recruitment pipelines, lowering housing barriers so learners can live and work in high-need areas.

solutions.text: Community Housing Investment Fund / Microloan Pool: Create a locally governed revolving fund that provides microloans, down‑payment assistance or gap financing for first‑time buyers, renovations to create rental units, and community-led developments.

resources.name: First-time Home Buyers Down Payment Assistance Program (DPAP)
resources.organization: Housing Nova Scotia (Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
resources.description: Province-wide program that provides repayable loans to eligible first-time buyers to cover a portion of the required down payment, closing the gap between savings and mortgage qualification. Structured as a revolving fund, repayments return to the program to assist additional households, directly implementing down-payment assistance to improve affordability and access to ownership.
resources.address: 14th Floor, Barrington Tower, 1894 Barrington Street, Halifax, NS B3J 2A8

resources.name: Secondary and Backyard Suite Incentive Program
resources.organization: Housing Nova Scotia (Department of Municipal Affairs and Housing)
resources.description: Provides forgivable loans to homeowners to create secondary/basement or backyard suites that must be rented at attainable rates for a set period. This gap financing reduces upfront renovation costs and increases local rental supply within existing neighborhoods, directly implementing the solution’s focus on renovations that add rental units.
resources.address: 14th Floor, Barrington Tower, 1894 Barrington Street, Halifax, NS B3J 2A8

resources.name: Affordable Housing Grant Program
resources.description: Offers pre-development and capital grants to non-profit and co-operative housing providers to build or preserve affordable homes across the municipality. By de-risking projects and closing funding gaps, the program functions as local gap financing that enables community-led developments to proceed and leverages additional public and private investment.

resources.name: Affordable Homeownership Program
resources.description: Enables low- to moderate-income families to become first-time homeowners through affordable, no-interest mortgages and no required down payment, removing key barriers to ownership. Mortgage repayments flow into Habitat’s locally governed Fund for Humanity, which is reinvested to build additional homes—operating as a community revolving fund aligned with the solution’s gap-financing and community-led development approach.

solutions.text: Local Construction and Retrofit Training Program: Partner with trades schools and nonprofits to train residents in construction, modular assembly, energy retrofit and suite conversions, expanding local capacity while creating jobs.

resources.name: NSCC Carpentry (Certificate) — Ivany Campus
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College’s Carpentry program provides hands-on training in residential construction and renovation, including framing, building envelope, code compliance, and finishing. Graduates are job-ready for roles that expand local housing capacity—such as building new units, completing suite conversions, and assisting with retrofit projects—directly addressing labour shortages while creating local employment.

resources.name: NSCC Energy Sustainability Engineering Technology (Diploma) — Ivany Campus
resources.description: This NSCC program trains technologists in building science, energy auditing, HVAC systems, and efficiency retrofit design. Graduates help plan and deliver home energy retrofits and performance upgrades—skills essential for modernizing housing, lowering operating costs, and supporting projects like secondary suite conversions that require energy and code upgrades.

resources.name: EfficiencyOne Academy (Energy Efficiency Workforce Training)
resources.description: EfficiencyOne Academy provides training pathways for energy-efficiency professionals and contractors—including Energy Advisor preparation, building science fundamentals, and courses for heat pump, insulation, and air-sealing work. By equipping local residents and trades with retrofit skills, the Academy expands Nova Scotia’s capacity to deliver home upgrades and efficient suite conversions while creating good local jobs.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: Constructing Futures
resources.description: YWCA Halifax’s Constructing Futures is a pre-apprenticeship program that trains women and gender diverse people for careers in construction trades through hands-on learning, essential safety certifications, and employer placements. Participants gain practical skills relevant to residential building and renovation—including work that supports energy retrofits and secondary-suite conversions—helping grow the local construction workforce and improve housing supply.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

solutions.text: Shared Housing and Roommate Matching Platform: Run a community-managed platform that matches students, newcomers and young workers to compatible shared-house options, supports co‑leasing and provides information on tenants' rights.

resources.name: Dalhousie University Off-Campus Living
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Off-Campus Living hub connects students with shared-house and room-for-rent listings through its partner platform (Places4Students), including a roommate finder to match compatible housemates. It also offers guidance on leases and co-tenancy (e.g., sample roommate agreements, budgeting tools) and links to Nova Scotia Residential Tenancies resources so renters understand their rights and responsibilities.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Off-Campus Housing
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University, Student Affairs & Services
resources.description: SMU’s Off-Campus Housing service uses a housing platform (Places4Students) with room and shared-accommodation listings and a roommate-matching feature to help students find compatible living situations. The site and Student Affairs resources provide renter education, including tips on co-leasing arrangements and clear links to Nova Scotia tenant rights and dispute-resolution information.

resources.name: Mount Saint Vincent University Off-Campus Housing
resources.organization: Mount Saint Vincent University, Residence Life
resources.description: MSVU’s Off-Campus Housing page connects students to shared housing and room rentals via a partner listing platform (Places4Students) and campus-managed resources, including roommate search tools. It provides checklists and guidance on co-tenancy (e.g., roommate agreements, lease tips) and directs renters to Nova Scotia Residential Tenancies for up-to-date rights information.

resources.name: St. Francis Xavier University Off-Campus Housing
resources.organization: St. Francis Xavier University, Student Life
resources.description: StFX supports students seeking shared accommodation in Antigonish through an off-campus listing service and a roommate finder powered by Places4Students. Student Life resources explain leases, co-signing and co-tenancy considerations, and link to Nova Scotia Residential Tenancies to ensure renters understand their rights and responsibilities.

resources.name: Acadia University Off-Campus Housing
resources.description: Acadia’s Off-Campus Housing service uses Places4Students to list rooms and shared houses in and around Wolfville and includes roommate-matching features to find compatible housemates. It offers renter education, including sample agreements and guidance on co-leasing, and directs students to Nova Scotia tenant-rights resources for informed renting.

solutions.text: Inclusionary Zoning and Planning Advocacy: Organize community campaigns to work with municipalities to adopt inclusionary zoning, density bonuses and reduced parking rules to increase the supply of affordable units near services and transit.

resources.name: Our HRM Alliance
resources.description: A civic coalition advocating for sustainable, affordable growth in the Halifax Regional Municipality, the Alliance organizes campaigns, public education, and submissions to Council to shape land‑use policy. It has supported tools like density bonusing to secure affordable housing, promoted inclusionary housing mechanisms, and backed reduced parking requirements in growth centres to enable more homes near services and transit.

resources.name: Centre Plan Density Bonusing Program
resources.description: Part of HRM’s Regional Centre Plan, this program enables additional building height or floor area in exchange for public benefits, including contributions toward affordable housing. It also modernizes land-use rules in transit‑rich, service‑rich areas—paired with relaxed parking standards in key corridors—to increase housing supply and support compact, walkable communities.

resources.name: Housing and Planning Policy Advocacy
resources.description: NSFM represents municipalities province‑wide and advocates for legislative tools that enable inclusionary zoning, more flexible density bonusing, and the authority to reduce or remove parking minimums near transit. Through policy papers, government relations, and member working groups, it helps local governments adopt planning reforms that unlock affordable housing supply in serviced, transit‑accessible areas.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1105, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Municipal Planning Services and Bylaw Updates
resources.description: EDPC provides planning services to several Nova Scotia municipalities, leading community consultations and drafting Municipal Planning Strategies and Land‑Use Bylaws that can incorporate density bonusing for affordable units and reduced parking requirements in town centres. By aligning zoning with transit and services, EDPC helps councils adopt reforms that enable more diverse, attainable housing in the right places.
resources.address: 606 Reeves Street, Unit 3, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 2R7

resources.name: Built Environment Program
resources.description: EAC’s Built Environment work mobilizes residents and partners to support compact, transit‑oriented communities, advocating for inclusionary housing tools, density bonuses, and parking reform in municipal plans. The team organizes campaigns, produces policy briefs, and collaborates with municipalities to remove zoning barriers and increase affordable housing near services and frequent transit.

solutions.text: Tool Library and Building Materials Reuse Hub: Operate a tool‑lending library and salvaged materials center so DIY landlords and residents can affordably renovate existing stock or build accessory suites.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: A community tool‑lending library that provides affordable access to hundreds of hand and power tools for home repair, woodworking, renovation, and landscaping. By letting residents and small landlords borrow tools instead of buying, it lowers the cost of maintaining and upgrading existing housing and supports DIY creation of secondary suites.

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia ReStore
resources.description: A building materials reuse store that sells donated and salvaged home improvement items—such as doors, windows, cabinets, lighting, plumbing fixtures, and lumber—at discounted prices. This keeps usable materials out of landfills while enabling cost‑effective renovations and repairs for homeowners, renters, and DIY landlords adding or upgrading suites.

solutions.text: Landlord-Tenant Support and Mediation Services: Expand community legal clinics, tenant education, proactive inspection programs and mediation services to stabilize tenancies, reduce turnover and prevent evictions.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Residential Tenancies Program
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia — Service Nova Scotia
resources.description: The provincial Residential Tenancies Program provides information, early dispute resolution, and formal hearings between landlords and tenants under the Residential Tenancies Act. Tenancy officers offer mediation/conciliation services, help parties resolve issues before they escalate, and issue orders when necessary—stabilizing tenancies and preventing avoidable evictions.

resources.name: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service – Housing and Tenancy Advocacy
resources.organization: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service, Schulich School of Law, Dalhousie University
resources.description: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service is a community legal clinic that provides free legal representation, summary advice, and community outreach to low‑income tenants. The clinic educates renters on their rights and responsibilities, negotiates with landlords, and represents clients in Residential Tenancies proceedings to resolve disputes, reduce turnover, and prevent evictions.

resources.name: ISANS Housing & Settlement Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides newcomers with housing orientation, tenant‑rights education, and one‑on‑one support to find and keep safe, affordable rentals. Staff liaise with landlords, help interpret leases and resolve issues early, and connect clients with legal and community resources—supporting stable tenancies and reducing the risk of eviction for immigrants and refugees.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Minimum Standards for Residential Occupancies (By-law M-200) – Compliance & Inspections
resources.description: HRM’s Municipal Compliance team enforces the Minimum Standards for Residential Occupancies (By‑law M‑200) and conducts inspections to address unsafe or substandard rental conditions. Through complaint response and targeted inspection campaigns, the municipality compels repairs, educates landlords and tenants on standards, and mitigates conflicts that can lead to displacement or eviction.

solutions.text: Community Vacancy Registry and Vacancy Tax Advocacy: Collect local data on vacant units through a community registry and campaign for municipal vacancy taxes or incentives to bring units back into the rental market.

resources.name: Short-term Rental Regulations and Registration (HRM)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality requires short-term rental operators to register and complies with provincial tourist accommodation registration, while restricting entire-home short-term rentals to primary residences in most residential zones. This creates a transparent, local registry of units being used as short-term rentals and enables targeted enforcement to reduce commercial STRs, helping shift vacant or underused dwellings back into the long-term rental market.

resources.name: Short-Term Rentals Licensing & Registry (Town of Lunenburg)
resources.description: The Town of Lunenburg licenses and registers short-term rental accommodations and limits non–owner-occupied STRs to specific areas. By maintaining a detailed registry of STR units and enforcing zoning/licensing rules, the Town collects local data on dwellings removed from the long-term market and creates incentives for owners to return units to year-round rental.

resources.name: Short-Term Accommodations Registration Program (Town of Wolfville)
resources.description: Wolfville requires short-term accommodation operators to register and comply with primary-residence and zoning rules, producing a municipal inventory of STR units. This registry-based approach allows the Town to identify housing diverted to tourism use and apply policies that encourage conversion of those units back to long-term rental, improving availability for students, newcomers, and young families.

resources.name: Municipal Tax Tools Advocacy (including Vacant Homes Tax Authority)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Federation of Municipalities advocates for enabling legislation to expand municipal tax tools, including the authority to consider a vacant homes tax and incentives that would bring underutilized housing back into the rental market. Through policy papers and government engagement, NSFM supports data-informed municipal strategies to track underused properties and implement fiscal measures to increase housing supply.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1304, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Campus–Community Housing Partnerships: Encourage colleges and universities to co-develop housing with municipalities and community groups—leasing excess campus space, building mixed-use student-family housing, or offering transitional housing programs for graduates.

resources.name: Stay at Dal (Summer Accommodations)
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Stay at Dal program opens residence rooms and suites to the general public, community groups, and seasonal workers during the summer months. By leasing otherwise idle campus housing in the off-peak academic season, the program provides short-term, transitional options for newcomers, interns, and recent graduates while easing pressure on Halifax’s tight rental market.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Summer Accommodations
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University leases residence rooms to the public and community organizations in the summer, making use of unoccupied campus space to offer affordable short-term stays. This supports transitional housing needs for recent graduates, new hires, and visiting workers, and helps reduce spillover demand in Halifax’s constrained rental market.

resources.name: MSVU Family & Mature Student Housing
resources.description: Mount Saint Vincent University provides on-campus apartment-style units for students who are parents or living with partners/children, integrating family-friendly housing with access to campus services. By expanding diverse, attainable options beyond traditional dorms, this mixed-use student–family housing model supports retention of students and young families in the community.

resources.name: NSCC Student Housing – Ivany Campus Residence
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College is expanding on-campus residence capacity at Ivany Campus, supported by the Province of Nova Scotia, to provide more beds near transit and employment hubs. Purpose-built student housing helps meet demand for trainees in trades, technology, and health programs while easing pressure on surrounding rental markets through a campus–community approach.

obstacles.title: Wage Growth and Job Quality Gap
obstacles.description: Average wages lag larger Canadian markets and many entry-level roles are part-time, seasonal, or lack benefits. This weakens retention and makes it harder for young people to build stable, fulfilling careers.

solutions.text: Community Living Wage Campaign & Employer Recognition: Organize a local living wage campaign to calculate a Nova Scotia-specific living wage, encourage employers to adopt it, and create a public recognition program (seal or directory) that highlights businesses paying living wages and offering stable hours and benefits.

resources.name: Living Wage Employer Program – Halifax
resources.description: United Way Halifax convenes the local living-wage campaign and partners with researchers to calculate the Halifax-area living wage, then recruits employers to adopt it. The program recognizes participating businesses with a public listing and a Living Wage Employer seal, encouraging payment of at least the local living wage along with predictable scheduling and basic benefits to improve job quality and retention.
resources.address: 46 Portland Street, 7th Floor, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 1H4

resources.name: Living Wage in Procurement Policy
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality embeds a locally calculated living-wage standard into its social procurement and contracting for services (such as cleaning and security), requiring vendors on covered contracts to pay at least the living wage. By integrating these requirements into tenders and publicly posting awarded contracts and supplier rosters, HRM effectively recognizes compliant employers and incentivizes wider adoption of living-wage practices that support more stable hours and better job quality.

solutions.text: Employer Consortium for Quality Entry-Level Jobs: Form a local consortium of businesses, nonprofits and post‑secondary institutions that commits to improving entry-level roles (predictable schedules, minimum hours, basic benefits, paid training), shares best practices, and leverages collective purchasing to reduce employer cost barriers.

resources.name: Chambers of Commerce Group Insurance Plan (Halifax Chamber of Commerce)
resources.description: Through the national Chambers Plan delivered locally by the Halifax Chamber, small and mid‑sized employers pool together to purchase affordable health, dental, life, and disability benefits—making it feasible to offer basic benefits to entry‑level staff. The Chamber also convenes employers, post‑secondary partners, and nonprofits at roundtables and events to share HR best practices (e.g., predictable scheduling, onboarding, retention), directly supporting the improvement of job quality in entry‑level roles.

resources.name: CANS Group Benefits Plan and Education & Training
resources.description: The Construction Association of Nova Scotia (CANS) acts as an employer consortium that reduces the cost barrier to offering benefits by providing a pooled Group Benefits Plan for member firms, helping even smaller contractors extend health and dental coverage to entry‑level hires. CANS also coordinates industry‑recognized training and certifications in partnership with NSCC and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, sharing best practices in onboarding, safety, and workforce scheduling to stabilize and upskill entry‑level roles across the sector.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Irving Shipbuilding Inc., in partnership with Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) and community partners
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is an employer‑led consortium with Irving Shipbuilding, NSCC, unions, and community organizations that provides paid pre‑apprenticeship education and wraparound supports, leading to entry‑level, unionized roles at the Halifax Shipyard. The program improves job quality by linking paid training to full‑time positions with benefits and predictable shifts, while partners coordinate curricula and share practices that strengthen onboarding, retention, and career progression for new workers.

resources.name: Farm and Workforce Development Program
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Federation of Agriculture convenes farm employers, post‑secondary institutions, and sector partners to strengthen entry‑level roles through HR toolkits, onboarding templates, and industry‑aligned training that make farm jobs safer, more predictable, and skills‑based. By coordinating employer cohorts and sharing best practices—along with linking employers to wage and training supports—the program helps farms improve job quality and retention for new and seasonal workers across the province.
resources.address: 60 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

solutions.text: Pooled Benefits Cooperative for Small Employers: Create a municipally supported cooperative that allows small businesses and social enterprises to join a pooled plan for health, dental and retirement benefits — making benefits affordable for part-time and early-career workers.

resources.name: Chambers of Commerce Group Insurance Plan (via Halifax Chamber of Commerce)
resources.description: The Chambers Plan is a not-for-profit, pooled employee benefits program that enables small businesses, nonprofits, and social enterprises to access affordable health, dental, life, disability, and employee assistance benefits. Employers join the Halifax Chamber of Commerce to participate, leveraging the national pool of tens of thousands of employees to stabilize premiums and improve coverage options for part-time and early‑career workers—directly addressing job quality and retention challenges.
resources.address: 32 Akerley Boulevard, Unit 1, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1N1

resources.name: Health Association Nova Scotia Group Benefits Solutions
resources.description: Health Association Nova Scotia administers pooled group benefit plans (health, dental, life, LTD, and EFAP) for a wide range of health, community, and nonprofit employers across the province, including many small organizations. By aggregating purchasing power and risk across participating employers, the program delivers stable, affordable benefits—helping smaller workplaces offer competitive coverage to part-time and early‑career staff and improving recruitment and retention.

solutions.text: Local Apprenticeship & Co-op Wage Top-Ups: Establish community-funded top-up grants for apprenticeships, co-ops and internships so young people earn a competitive wage during training, reducing the trade-off between learning and financial stability.

resources.name: Co-operative Education Incentive (CEI)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: The CEI provides wage subsidies to Nova Scotia employers to hire post-secondary co-op students for 12–16 week work terms. By reimbursing a portion of student wages, the program effectively tops up pay so students can earn competitive income while completing work-integrated learning in Nova Scotia. This reduces the financial trade-off for students and encourages employers to offer higher-quality placements.

resources.name: Apprenticeship START Program
resources.description: The Apprenticeship START Program provides wage incentives and completion bonuses to employers who hire and mentor apprentices in designated trades. These funds offset payroll costs so employers can pay apprentices competitive wages throughout their training, directly implementing a wage top-up model that supports retention and progression. The program also helps expand apprenticeship opportunities across small and rural employers.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship
resources.description: Clean Leadership places youth and post-secondary students in paid summer internships with organizations working on environmental and clean economy projects. Clean Foundation subsidizes a significant portion of each intern’s wages, enabling hosts to offer competitive pay while providing structured training and mentorship. This wage top-up approach helps students gain experience without sacrificing financial stability.

resources.name: COVE Internship Program
resources.description: COVE’s Internship Program funds a portion of wages for post-secondary students and recent graduates placed with ocean-technology companies across Nova Scotia. By reimbursing employers for a share of each intern’s salary, COVE helps organizations offer competitive compensation during on-the-job training. The program strengthens the talent pipeline while reducing the wage gap that can deter youth from early careers in the sector.

solutions.text: Microgrants and Seed Funding for Youth Entrepreneurship: Provide small grants, low-interest loans and mentorship for young entrepreneurs to help cover living costs while launching sustainable ventures, enabling longer development time and better-paid outcomes.

resources.name: CEED Microloan Program
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED’s Microloan Program provides low-interest financing (typically up to tens of thousands) and wraparound training and mentorship for new and early-stage entrepreneurs in Nova Scotia. Funds can be used for startup expenses and short-term personal runway while founders validate their business, and CEED supports them with workshops, one-on-one coaching, and peer networks—extending development time and improving the odds of sustainable, better-paid outcomes.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta Cohort provides $25,000 in non-dilutive seed funding to early-stage startups in Atlantic Canada, along with structured mentorship, founder programming, and access to a supportive community. By offering micro-seed capital plus guidance, the program enables young entrepreneurs in Nova Scotia to cover essentials during the launch phase, focus on product-market fit, and build ventures that create higher-quality, better-paid jobs.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Accelerate (Startup Funding & Mentorship)
resources.description: Accelerate is a milestone-driven program that provides non-dilutive funding (often $40,000–$50,000 per company), expert advisory, and intensive programming to help early-stage startups grow in Nova Scotia. This seed support—paired with mentorship and access to the province’s startup infrastructure—helps young founders extend runway for development and hiring, improving the pathway to sustainable revenue and quality employment.

resources.name: Indigenous Business Loans & Advisory
resources.description: Ulnooweg provides flexible, low-interest business loans and hands-on advisory services to Indigenous entrepreneurs across Atlantic Canada, including youth in Nova Scotia. Financing can be used for startup and working capital—often easing living-cost pressures in the launch phase—while mentorship and capacity-building supports help founders develop sustainable ventures that create quality jobs in their communities.

solutions.text: Seasonal Work Smoothing & Shared Employment Bank: Develop a regional job-matching and shared-employment bank that helps seasonal workers move between employers across sectors, and provides short-term placement subsidies so workers maintain income year-round.

resources.name: START Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration (Employment Nova Scotia)
resources.description: START provides wage incentives to Nova Scotia employers to hire unemployed or underemployed Nova Scotians, including support for short-term and staggered placements. Employment service providers use START to move seasonal workers into off-season roles with other employers and sectors, helping them maintain income and build year-round work histories.

resources.name: Job Creation Partnerships (JCP)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration (Employment Nova Scotia)
resources.description: JCP funds time-limited, community-based work projects that give eligible jobseekers paid, work-like experience with host employers. In seasonal communities, these placements are used between peak seasons to keep workers attached to the labour force and develop transferable skills, while employers receive cost-shared wage support—smoothing income for workers across the year.

resources.name: TourismTalent.com – Nova Scotia Job Board
resources.organization: Tourism Industry Association of Nova Scotia (TIANS)
resources.description: TourismTalent.com is TIANS’ provincial job-matching platform that aggregates hospitality and tourism jobs across Nova Scotia and promotes rapid, multi-employer hiring. Seasonal workers use the site to move between employers and sub-sectors (accommodations, events, food service, attractions) as demand shifts, functioning as a shared-employment bank and complementing wage-subsidy programs that fund short-term off-season roles.

resources.name: AgJobsNS – Farm and Workforce Development
resources.description: AgJobsNS is the Nova Scotia Federation of Agriculture’s province-wide employment hub for farm and agri-food employers. It enables seasonal workers to find consecutive placements with different farms and agri-businesses (e.g., greenhouse, harvest, processing) to string together year-round income, and supports employers in accessing wage-subsidy programs to fund short-term off-season roles.
resources.address: 7 Atlantic Central Drive, East Mountain, NS B6L 2Z2

solutions.text: Municipal Procurement Standards for Job Quality: Require that municipal contracts and grants prioritize bidders who offer stable hours, living wages and employee benefits, using local purchasing power to raise standards across the community.

resources.name: Sustainable Procurement Program and Supplier Code of Conduct
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Sustainable Procurement framework embeds social value and workforce standards into purchasing, allowing RFPs and contracts to weight criteria such as fair wages, benefits, stable scheduling, apprenticeship/training plans, and inclusive hiring. Its Supplier Code of Conduct sets minimum labour expectations and enables contract clauses and evaluation points that favour bidders demonstrating strong job quality practices. By leveraging municipal purchasing power across goods, services, and construction, HRM steers awards toward employers that raise job standards in the community.

resources.name: Cogswell District Redevelopment – Social Procurement & Community Benefits
resources.description: For the multi-year Cogswell District Redevelopment, HRM embedded community benefits and social procurement requirements into the major construction contract, including workforce development targets, apprenticeship hours, and opportunities for underrepresented groups alongside adherence to HRM labour standards. These provisions incentivize contractors and subcontractors to provide stable, well-compensated jobs with benefits consistent with industry and collective agreement norms, and to document their employment practices through contract reporting. The project uses a high-value municipal procurement to prioritize bidders with strong job quality commitments and to model higher standards for future municipal projects.

solutions.text: Local Wage Transparency Portal: Build a community-run online portal that lists local job quality metrics (wages, hours, benefits, advancement opportunities) to empower jobseekers, encourage competition on quality, and spotlight employers improving terms.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Online Job Board
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: Province-wide job portal that aggregates local employment opportunities and standardizes key job quality fields such as wage/salary, job type (full-time/part-time/seasonal), hours per week, and benefits when provided by employers. By using structured posting templates and filters, it encourages employers to disclose compensation and working conditions, helping jobseekers compare quality across local roles and spotlighting employers that offer stronger terms.
resources.address: 5151 Terminal Road, 7th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 2T8

resources.name: ISANS Job Board
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: Community-run job board curated by the Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia that posts local opportunities with clear indicators for wages/salaries, schedule (FT/PT/term), and benefits when available. ISANS staff work directly with employers to improve posting transparency and highlight inclusive, higher-quality jobs, enabling newcomers and young jobseekers to assess job quality and advancement potential.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Volta Jobs Board
resources.description: Startup community jobs portal showcasing roles from Halifax and Atlantic Canadian tech companies, with postings that often include salary ranges, equity/benefits, work arrangement, and role level. Volta promotes transparent, high-quality postings among its member companies and spotlights employers improving compensation and workplace practices, enabling jobseekers to compare quality metrics across local tech opportunities.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

resources.name: TEAM Work Cooperative – Hot Jobs
resources.description: A Nova Scotia Works employment centre that publishes a continuously updated local ‘Hot Jobs’ listing with wage or salary details, hours, contract length, and benefits when provided by employers. Staff collaborate with local businesses to include transparent job quality metrics and tag roles by full-time/part-time/seasonal status, helping jobseekers compare opportunities and recognize employers offering better terms.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

solutions.text: Childcare & Transit Supports Tied to Employment: Expand community-run affordable childcare (including extended-hour options) and targeted transit subsidies for early-career workers to remove barriers that make part-time or low-paid jobs the only feasible option.

resources.name: Low Income Transit Pass Program
resources.description: Halifax Transit provides a 50% discount on adult monthly transit passes for eligible low-income residents through the municipality’s Affordable Access Program. By cutting commuting costs for people in entry-level, part-time, or seasonal jobs, the program directly supports early-career workers to access a wider range of shifts and work locations without prohibitive transportation expenses. This targeted transit subsidy helps reduce a key barrier that can keep workers stuck in only the closest or most limited job options.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC) and Transportation Support
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS offers on-site, no-cost Care for Newcomer Children during language, employment, and settlement programming so parents can build skills and pursue jobs without childcare barriers. The organization also provides transit support (such as bus tickets for eligible clients) to attend classes, interviews, and early employment activities. Together, these services remove two major hurdles—childcare and transportation—for newcomers in early career stages, enabling steadier entry into the workforce.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YWCA Spryfield Early Learning and Child Care Centre
resources.description: YWCA Halifax operates a community-based, licensed child care centre that offers affordable care with extended-hour options like early drop-off and late pick-up to support working families. By providing reliable, accessible care close to home, the centre helps parents accept full shifts, training, or non-standard hours instead of limiting themselves to part-time roles. This directly advances the solution by expanding community-run, affordable childcare aligned with employment needs.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: East Preston Family Resource Centre – Early Learning & Child Care
resources.description: EPFRC provides licensed early learning and child care, along with before- and after-school programs, designed around the schedules of working families in East Preston and nearby communities. With community-led governance and affordable, inclusive programming, the centre enables parents to maintain steady employment, training, or shift work rather than defaulting to part-time options. This expands access to locally run, affordable childcare that removes a central barrier to job quality and retention.
resources.address: 190 Brooks Drive, East Preston, NS B2Z 1J5

solutions.text: Career Pathway Partnerships with Wage Guarantees: Create sector-specific partnerships (healthcare, tech, trades, arts) between schools, employers and community orgs that guarantee wage steps on completion of linked training so young people can see and reach real earnings growth.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding Inc.
resources.description: A sector partnership between NSCC, Irving Shipbuilding, unions, and community organizations that recruits and trains cohorts (e.g., welding and metal fabrication) for careers at the Halifax Shipyard. Learners complete NSCC technical training with paid work terms at the shipyard; successful graduates are hired into unionized roles with a defined wage grid and apprentice-to-journeyperson step increases set by the collective agreement. This creates a transparent, guaranteed earnings ladder linked to credential milestones, directly addressing wage growth and job quality for young workers.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Early Childhood Educator (ECE) Wage Grid and Career Pathways
resources.organization: Department of Education and Early Childhood Development (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: A province-wide initiative that mandates minimum hourly wages for ECEs based on credential level (e.g., Entry, Level 1–3), ensuring automatic wage increases when workers complete recognized training or upgrading. The department funds education, recognition of prior learning, and bridging supports with NSCC and other partners so educators can move up the grid, making earnings growth predictable and tied to specific training milestones. This creates a clear, guaranteed wage pathway within the early learning sector and improves retention and job quality.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration)
resources.description: The provincial apprenticeship system registers apprentices with employer sponsors across trades, combining NSCC technical training and paid on‑the‑job experience. Apprenticeship agreements document wage progression tied to training levels and hours, and in many unionized settings minimum apprentice wages are fixed as a percentage of the journeyperson rate—providing clear, guaranteed step increases as apprentices advance. This sector‑specific, employer‑school partnership offers youth a transparent earnings ladder and stable, skilled careers in high‑demand trades.
