resources.description: Kings County has conducted resident and business broadband surveys and maintained an online interest registry to quantify take-up for improved service in underserved areas. The county uses these aggregated commitments to demonstrate clear demand to providers and to strengthen proposals for provincial and federal broadband funding, guiding where and when ISPs deploy infrastructure.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Colchester County High-Speed Internet Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: Colchester County operates demand aggregation through address-level pre‑registration and community surveys, including speed tests, to document need and willingness to subscribe. The compiled pledge lists and mapped demand help the county work with ISPs to plan build phases and support funding applications by clearly demonstrating anticipated take-up rates in rural communities.

solutions.text: Volunteer Digital Stewards and Installation Teams: Train local volunteers to help neighbours install routers, set up Wi‑Fi extenders, configure secure home networks and maintain local wireless hotspots. This lowers barriers for older residents and those with limited technical skills.

resources.name: Chebucto Community Net (including Chebucto Wireless)
resources.description: Chebucto Community Net is a volunteer-run community internet organization that provides low-cost access and hands-on help to residents and community groups in the Halifax area. Volunteers act as digital stewards by assisting users with configuring home routers, setting up secure Wi‑Fi networks, and troubleshooting connectivity; they have also supported community wireless hotspots through the Chebucto Wireless initiative. This neighbor-to-neighbor model lowers technical barriers for older adults and people with limited tech skills.
resources.address: Room 006, Chase Building, 6136 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: WiFi to Go and Technology Tutoring
resources.description: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library lends portable Wi‑Fi hotspots through its WiFi to Go program and runs volunteer-led technology tutoring at branches across rural communities. Trained volunteers provide one-on-one help to set up home internet equipment, configure routers and Wi‑Fi extenders, and secure home networks, while also helping patrons activate and use loaned hotspots. This combination of hotspot access and volunteer digital stewards reduces connectivity and skills gaps for residents, including seniors.
resources.address: 182 Dalhousie Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 4C7

resources.name: Borrow the Internet and Tech Help
resources.description: South Shore Public Libraries offers Borrow the Internet hotspot lending and free, volunteer-supported Tech Help sessions throughout Lunenburg and Queens counties. Library staff train community volunteers (tech tutors) who sit down with residents to install and configure home routers, extend Wi‑Fi coverage, and set up secure passwords and updates, and they provide hands-on help to get mobile hotspots working at home. This practical support helps older adults and newcomers get reliable, secure home connectivity.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

resources.name: Borrow a Wi‑Fi Hub and Tech Help by Appointment
resources.description: Colchester-East Hants Public Library lends Wi‑Fi hotspot devices and provides one-on-one technology help sessions supported by trained staff and volunteers. Residents can receive step-by-step assistance to connect and secure home networks, set up routers and Wi‑Fi extenders, and troubleshoot connectivity issues, including help getting loaned hotspots working. By pairing connectivity tools with community tech stewards, the library lowers barriers for people with limited technical skills in rural and small-town communities.

solutions.text: Local Matching Funds and Community Crowdfunding: Create a municipal or community-level fund (fed by local government, businesses and citizen donations) to match provincial/federal grants or ISP investments, making projects more financially viable and accelerating buildout.

resources.name: Colchester County Rural Internet Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: The Municipality of Colchester created a multi‑year Rural Internet Project that dedicates municipal capital to co-fund broadband builds with provincial programs (e.g., Internet for Nova Scotians) and private ISPs. By offering local matching funds to complement federal/provincial grants and ISP investment, the county improves project viability in low-density areas and accelerates fibre and fixed‑wireless buildouts for rural residents and businesses.

resources.name: MODL Internet Expansion Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg (MODL) runs an Internet Expansion Program that commits municipal funds to cost-share projects with the provincial Internet for Nova Scotians initiative and partnering ISPs. These local matching contributions de‑risk private builds and unlock higher-level grants, enabling last‑mile fibre and fixed‑wireless coverage to reach underserviced roads and communities more quickly.

resources.name: Pictou County Rural Broadband Initiative
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Pictou
resources.description: Pictou County has established a municipal broadband initiative that sets aside local funding to partner with Build Nova Scotia and ISPs on fibre-to-the-home and fixed‑wireless expansions. The county’s contributions function as matching dollars to leverage provincial/federal programs and private capital, making rural builds financially feasible and reducing timelines for connectivity improvements.

resources.name: Inverness County Broadband and Cellular Expansion Program
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Inverness
resources.description: Inverness County operates an ongoing program that blends municipal funds with federal/provincial grants and ISP investment to extend broadband and improve cellular service across rural communities. By providing local matching contributions and coordinating community partnerships where appropriate, the county accelerates fibre routes and tower builds that otherwise would be uneconomic in sparsely populated areas.
resources.address: 375 Main Street, Port Hood, NS B0E 2W0

solutions.text: Shared Infrastructure Agreements (Poles, Conduits and Towers): Coordinate municipalities, utilities and landowners to enable shared access to poles, conduits and tower sites. Community groups can broker or manage agreements so multiple providers can cost-effectively extend service into rural areas.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Power Joint Use Program (Pole Attachments)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Power’s Joint Use program manages third‑party attachments to NSP-owned distribution poles across the province. Through standardized joint-use agreements, engineering make-ready, and tariffed attachment rates overseen by the Nova Scotia Utility and Review Board, the program enables internet and wireless providers to share existing pole infrastructure instead of building new. This coordinated access to poles along established rights‑of‑way lowers costs and accelerates rural broadband extensions by aligning utilities, municipalities, and landowner permissions.
resources.address: 1223 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

resources.name: Bell Wholesale – Support Structure Access
resources.description: Bell Wholesale provides regulated access to Bell-owned poles, strand, and underground conduits throughout Nova Scotia under CRTC-approved support-structure tariffs. Carriers and ISPs can sign support-structure agreements to attach fiber/coax or place sub-ducts in existing conduit, coordinating with utilities and municipalities to share common routes. This shared infrastructure model reduces construction costs and enables multi‑provider builds into smaller and rural communities.

resources.name: Municipal Access Agreements (MAA) and Utility Right‑of‑Way Permitting
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality administers Municipal Access Agreements and right‑of‑way permits that allow telecommunications providers to occupy municipal corridors and, where available, municipal duct banks. The standardized agreements coordinate with other utilities and city departments so multiple providers can share corridors, poles, and conduit routes with consistent technical and restoration requirements. By reducing duplication and clarifying access terms, the MAA framework supports cost‑effective, shared infrastructure deployments that help extend networks from urban hubs to surrounding rural areas.

resources.name: Mahone Bay Electric Utility – Joint Use of Poles
resources.description: The Town of Mahone Bay Electric Utility owns local distribution poles and manages Joint Use of Poles agreements with telecommunications carriers. The utility coordinates pole surveys, make‑ready work, and attachment licensing so multiple providers can share the same pole lines rather than build parallel infrastructure. This shared access arrangement lowers capital costs and enables additional providers to reach nearby rural areas, directly supporting expanded broadband coverage.
resources.address: 493 Main Street, Mahone Bay, NS B0J 2E0

solutions.text: Community Cell Boosters and Small‑Cell Deployments: Identify strategic community-owned locations (halls, water towers, municipal buildings) where small cellular nodes or signal boosters can be installed to improve mobile coverage. Organize permits, site stewardship and cost-sharing among users.

resources.name: Cellular Connectivity Project
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia leads a province-wide program to identify cellular coverage gaps and deploy solutions such as small cells and signal boosters on community-owned and public assets (e.g., community halls, fire stations, water towers, and municipal buildings). The program coordinates permitting, access to sites, and cost-sharing through public–private partnerships with carriers and integrators to improve mobile service in rural and underserved areas.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 1101, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

resources.name: Small Cell Wireless Infrastructure Guidelines
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality provides a standardized permitting framework that allows carriers and partners to mount small-cell equipment on municipal assets like streetlights, traffic poles, and other public right-of-way structures. By streamlining site selection, stewardship, and attachment agreements, the guidelines enable community-sited micro cells that densify coverage and fill service gaps in neighbourhoods and along corridors.

resources.name: Joint Use – Telecommunications Attachments
resources.description: Nova Scotia Power’s Joint Use program enables wireless providers and community partners to attach small-cell radios, repeaters, and related equipment to utility poles and other NSP assets across the province. The program manages engineering standards, safety, and permitting, providing a practical pathway for community-level deployments that enhance cellular coverage in rural and hard-to-serve areas.
resources.address: 1223 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

resources.name: Nova Communications Cellular Booster Solutions
resources.description: ROCK Networks (Nova Communications) designs and installs carrier-approved cellular signal boosters (e.g., Cel-Fi systems) and small-cell solutions in community halls, municipal buildings, health clinics, and other public facilities across Nova Scotia. They work with local stakeholders to survey sites, secure approvals, and deploy equipment, creating shared, community-sited improvements that extend reliable mobile coverage for residents, businesses, and emergency services.

solutions.text: Mobile Wi‑Fi Outreach (School Buses, Libraries-on-Wheels): Deploy Wi‑Fi-equipped vehicles or library-bus services that park at neighbourhood hub points on scheduled days to provide internet access, device lending and digital help for remote learners and residents without home service.

resources.name: South Shore Public Libraries Mobile Library
resources.description: A Wi‑Fi-enabled mobile library that travels to rural communities across Lunenburg and Queens Counties on a published schedule, parking at local hubs to provide free internet access. Staff offer on-the-spot digital help and lend library materials and devices (where available), helping residents and remote learners who lack reliable home service get online, complete coursework, and access e-services.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

resources.name: Cape Breton Regional Library Bookmobile
resources.description: The Bookmobile brings library service and free Wi‑Fi to underserved communities in Cape Breton, parking at regular neighborhood stops so people can connect to the internet near their homes. Visitors can borrow books and other materials, get basic tech support from staff, and use onboard connectivity for tasks like online learning, telehealth, and job searches.

resources.name: Cumberland Public Libraries Bookmobile
resources.description: A mobile library service that parks at scheduled stops throughout Cumberland County to deliver free Wi‑Fi access alongside borrowing services. The team helps patrons with digital tasks—such as accessing online classes, setting up devices, and navigating government services—while lending materials and, where available, take-home hotspots or devices.

solutions.text: Community Telework Hubs and Makerspaces: Convert underused community spaces into co-working and makerspace hubs with fast internet, meeting rooms and equipment. Offer affordable day passes or memberships to support remote workers, entrepreneurs and students.

resources.name: Alderney Gate Library Creative Lab
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Alderney Gate branch provides a Creative Lab alongside high-speed Wi‑Fi, public computers, and bookable meeting and study rooms. The lab and shared spaces function as a community telework and makerspace hub, offering equipment like 3D printers and digital media tools so remote workers, entrepreneurs, and students can create, collaborate, and meet locally at low or no cost.

resources.name: Perennia Innovation Centre (Shared Labs and Co‑working)
resources.description: The Perennia Innovation Centre in Bible Hill offers shared offices, hot desks, labs, and bookable boardrooms with enterprise-grade internet for agri-food and rural entrepreneurs. By providing affordable workspace, specialized equipment, and meeting facilities in a community-accessible hub, it enables startups and professionals to work, prototype, and collaborate without needing urban facilities.
resources.address: 199 Innovation Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: People’s Place Library Makerspace
resources.description: Antigonish’s People’s Place Library includes makerspace tools (e.g., 3D printing and crafting equipment), free high-speed Wi‑Fi, public workstations, and bookable rooms for study or meetings. This turns a central community space into a practical telework and maker hub where youth, students, and small business owners can access technology and collaborative areas at no or low cost.

resources.name: Margaret Hennigar Public Library Creative/Maker Services
resources.description: Located within the Lunenburg County Lifestyle Centre, the Margaret Hennigar Public Library offers high-speed Wi‑Fi, public computers, bookable rooms, and maker/creative tools such as 3D printing and digital crafting equipment. These services effectively convert a community facility into a co-working and makerspace environment that supports remote work, entrepreneurship, and hands-on learning for residents.
resources.address: 135 North Park Street, Bridgewater, NS B4V 9B3

solutions.text: Local Digital Skills and Remote Work Training: Partner with schools, community colleges and NGOs to run workshops on basic digital skills, cybersecurity, remote-work best practices and online entrepreneurship so residents can take full advantage of improved connectivity.

resources.name: Tech Help and Digital Literacy Workshops
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries offers free drop-in Tech Help, device clinics, and scheduled workshops on computer basics, internet use, online safety/cybersecurity, and using remote-work tools like Zoom and Teams. By providing hands-on instruction and one-on-one support, the library helps residents build the digital skills needed for remote work, online learning, and entrepreneurship, especially as connectivity improves across the province.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Digital Literacy for Newcomers and Online Business Training
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers digital literacy classes that cover computer basics, safe internet practices, and how to use common online collaboration tools, alongside employment workshops tailored to finding and succeeding in remote jobs. Its Business Development Services provide training and coaching for online entrepreneurship—including e-commerce, digital marketing, and running a business remotely—so newcomers can leverage improved connectivity to work and start ventures from anywhere in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Continuing Education: Digital Literacy and Cybersecurity Microcredentials
resources.description: NSCC offers continuing education courses and short microcredentials in digital literacy, cybersecurity fundamentals, and workplace technology, delivered in-person across multiple campuses and online. The college also integrates remote-work readiness—covering collaboration platforms, digital professionalism, and online safety—so learners can participate in remote employment and online entrepreneurship as broadband access expands in rural communities.

resources.name: Workshops & Training for Online Entrepreneurship
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides practical training and coaching for aspiring and existing entrepreneurs across Nova Scotia, including workshops on e-commerce, digital marketing, online sales tools, and running remote-first businesses. By helping small business owners adopt digital tools and secure online practices, CEED equips residents to launch and grow ventures from connected rural communities.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Telehealth and Remote-Service Kiosks: Set up private, internet-enabled kiosks at clinics, community centres or libraries where residents can connect to telehealth providers, employment services or government portals with on-site assistance as needed.

resources.name: TeleHealthNS – Yarmouth Regional Hospital Site
resources.description: TeleHealthNS provides private, internet-enabled rooms equipped with secure video conferencing so patients can connect with specialists and primary care providers without having to travel long distances. At the Yarmouth Regional Hospital site, hospital staff help patients check in, set up the connection, and ensure clinical peripherals (e.g., digital stethoscopes, cameras) work during the appointment—delivering exactly the kind of assisted telehealth kiosk experience needed in rural areas.

resources.name: TeleHealthNS – Roseway Hospital Site
resources.description: The Roseway Hospital hosts a TeleHealthNS room where residents can attend virtual appointments with remote clinicians using secure video technology, reducing travel time and improving access to care. On-site staff assist with scheduling, connection setup, and any peripherals required, functioning as a staffed telehealth kiosk within the community hospital.

resources.name: TeleHealthNS – Inverness Consolidated Memorial Hospital Site
resources.description: TeleHealthNS operates a dedicated telehealth room at the Inverness Consolidated Memorial Hospital, providing a private, internet-enabled space for patients to connect with distant providers. Clinical and administrative staff offer on-site assistance before and during sessions, effectively delivering a kiosk-style service that bridges broadband and distance barriers in rural Cape Breton.

resources.name: Access Nova Scotia – Bayers Lake Service Centre (Self‑Serve Kiosks)
resources.organization: Access Nova Scotia (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Access Nova Scotia service centres provide self-serve computer kiosks and dedicated terminals where residents can complete provincial government transactions and access online services, with staff available to help on-site. These kiosks function as remote-service points for government portals—supporting tasks like licensing, registrations, and benefits applications for people who may lack reliable broadband at home.
resources.address: 300 Horseshoe Lake Drive, Halifax, NS B3S 0B7

solutions.text: Bulk Purchasing Programs for Home Connectivity and Devices: Organize cooperative buying programs so households can purchase routers, extenders, antennas or low-cost ISP plans in bulk to lower per-unit costs and speed adoption. Local businesses or the municipality can coordinate procurement and distribution.

resources.name: Borrow the Internet (Mobile Wi-Fi Hotspots)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries bulk-procures mobile Wi‑Fi hotspot devices and associated data plans from carriers, then coordinates system-wide distribution so households can take home reliable internet at no cost. By aggregating demand and centrally purchasing connectivity equipment, the library lowers the per-unit cost of home connectivity and rapidly expands access for residents who lack broadband, including those in suburban and rural parts of HRM.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Borrow the Internet (Hotspot Lending Program)
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library purchases mobile hotspots and data in bulk and lends them to households across Cape Breton, coordinating procurement and distribution through local branches. This centralized, high-volume buying model reduces per-device costs and enables families—especially in rural communities—to establish home connectivity for remote work, learning, and telehealth.

resources.name: Borrow the Internet (Hotspots and Devices)
resources.description: Pictou-Antigonish Regional Library coordinates a bulk purchase of mobile Wi‑Fi hotspots (and complementary loaner devices) and distributes them through its branches for home use by residents. By aggregating demand and managing procurement centrally, the program lowers per-unit costs and accelerates adoption of home connectivity in rural communities across Pictou and Antigonish counties.
resources.address: 182 Dalhousie Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 4M5

resources.name: Community Internet Services and Equipment Support
resources.description: Chebucto Community Net is a non-profit community ISP that aggregates local subscribers to offer low-cost internet plans and provides guidance and access to compatible modems/routers sourced at scale. By coordinating member sign‑ups and facilitating bulk procurement of home connectivity equipment at cost, Chebucto reduces per-household expenses and supports wider adoption of reliable home internet in the Halifax area.

solutions.text: Local Business Digitalization and E‑commerce Clinics: Provide tailored support for local shops, trades and artists to establish online storefronts, digital payment systems and remote-client workflows so improved internet directly boosts local economic opportunities.

resources.name: Small Business Advisory Services & Training (Digital and E‑commerce)
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business provides one-on-one advisory, peer cohorts, and hands-on workshops that help women-owned small businesses build or improve online storefronts, set up digital payment systems, and implement online booking and client management tools. Advisors work with retailers, trades and creatives across Nova Scotia—including rural communities—to choose platforms (e.g., Shopify, Squarespace, Square), integrate shipping and inventory, and develop digital marketing and remote-service workflows so improved connectivity translates into sales and new clients.

resources.name: Business Support & Digital Adoption Workshops
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic runs practical clinics, office hours, and workshops that guide local shops, trades and artists through standing up e-commerce sites, configuring digital payments and POS, and adopting online booking and collaboration tools. Their teams in Western and Northern Nova Scotia deliver tailored, step-by-step support—often in partnership with local stakeholders—to help rural entrepreneurs translate better broadband into online sales, remote client services, and streamlined digital workflows.

resources.name: Craft Lab: Business Skills and E‑commerce
resources.organization: Craft Nova Scotia (Centre for Craft Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Craft Nova Scotia’s Craft Lab offers training and mentorship that help artisans and makers set up and optimize online sales channels (Shopify, Etsy, and direct web stores), configure digital payment gateways, and manage shipping and customer service remotely. Sessions and clinics focus on practical steps—from product photography and listings to inventory, fulfillment, and marketing—so that improved internet access directly supports sustainable online revenue for creative businesses across the province.

resources.name: Agri‑food Business Advisory & E‑commerce Training
resources.description: Perennia provides ongoing advisory services and workshops to help food producers and processors establish online ordering systems, integrate secure digital payments, and design delivery/pickup logistics suited to rural operations. Specialists work with businesses to choose platforms, manage labeling and compliance for online sales, and build remote customer workflows—enabling Nova Scotia’s agri‑food entrepreneurs to convert improved broadband into practical e‑commerce growth.
resources.address: 199 Dr. Bernie MacDonald Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2H5

solutions.text: Advocacy and Coordinated Government Engagement: Form a citizen-led broadband advisory group to compile local evidence, prioritize projects, and engage municipal, provincial and federal decision-makers and funding streams with a unified voice and clear project proposals.

resources.name: MODL Internet Connectivity Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of Lunenburg
resources.description: The Municipality of the District of Lunenburg leads a coordinated Internet Connectivity Project that brings residents, community representatives, municipal staff, and ISPs together to map service gaps, run speed-test campaigns, and prioritize underserved areas. The project prepares unified proposals and co-funding packages to engage provincial and federal programs (such as the Internet for Nova Scotia Initiative and Universal Broadband Fund), ensuring a single, community-backed voice advocates for local builds.

resources.name: Colchester Rural Internet Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Colchester
resources.description: Colchester County’s Rural Internet Project convenes a community advisory approach to collect on-the-ground connectivity data, survey residents and businesses, and map priority build zones across rural communities. Using this evidence, the County engages ISPs and aligns proposals with provincial and federal funding streams to advance shovel-ready projects, advocating with a unified local voice for improved broadband and cellular service.

resources.name: Inverness County Cellular and Internet Connectivity Project
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Inverness
resources.description: Inverness County established a Connectivity Committee and coordinator role to gather local speed data, document service gaps, and prioritize communities most in need of upgrades. The County then works directly with provincial partners and federal funding programs, submitting coordinated proposals with ISPs so the region speaks with one voice and moves high-impact broadband projects forward.
resources.address: 375 Main Street, Port Hood, NS B0E 2W0

resources.name: St. Mary’s Connectivity Committee
resources.organization: Municipality of the District of St. Mary’s
resources.description: The District of St. Mary’s convenes a citizen-and-municipal Connectivity Committee to gather local feedback, run connectivity surveys, and maintain an evidence-based inventory of underserved areas. This committee collaborates with ISPs and engages provincial and federal decision-makers to align funding applications and advocate for prioritized rural broadband and mobile projects across the municipality.

obstacles.title: Barriers to Entrepreneurship and Access to Capital
obstacles.description: Early-stage financing is scarce and risk tolerance is low, especially outside Halifax. Entrepreneurs face limited mentorship, procurement hurdles, and challenges finding affordable space.

solutions.text: Local Angel and Micro-Investor Network: Residents, retired entrepreneurs and small investors form a regional angel network that pools modest capital for early-stage startups outside Halifax, with shared due-diligence and low-minimum contribution tiers to spread risk.

resources.name: FarmWorks Investment Co-operative Limited (CEDIF)
resources.description: FarmWorks is a provincially registered Community Economic Development Investment Fund that pools small investments from Nova Scotia residents (with low minimum share amounts) and deploys that capital into loans and quasi-equity for early-stage and growing food, farm, and beverage enterprises across rural communities. A volunteer investment committee conducts shared due diligence and provides mentorship and networking to reduce risk for individual investors while increasing the flow of early-stage capital outside Halifax. This directly advances local entrepreneurship by filling financing gaps for startups and small businesses in communities throughout the province.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: Operated by New Dawn Enterprises in Cape Breton, this CEDIF aggregates modest investments from local residents and channels them into loans and investments for early-stage and expanding businesses on the island. The fund uses a formal review process and board-led due diligence to evaluate opportunities and spread risk across a portfolio, while also connecting entrepreneurs to mentorship and space through New Dawn’s broader ecosystem. By mobilizing local savings into community ventures, it provides non-Halifax startups with accessible growth capital and support.

resources.name: Community Economic Development Investment Funds (CEDIF) Program
resources.organization: Department of Finance and Treasury Board, Government of Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Province of Nova Scotia’s CEDIF Program enables residents to pool capital through community-led funds that invest in local businesses and startups, often with low minimum contributions and provincial tax incentives. These funds use shared governance and due diligence processes—typically via volunteer investment committees—to evaluate deals and manage portfolios, allowing small investors to diversify while channeling early-stage financing to ventures across rural and small urban communities. The program provides the legal and regulatory framework that underpins many local angel-style and micro-investment initiatives operating outside Halifax.

solutions.text: Community Investment Co-op: Create a co-op that allows local people to buy shares and provide patient, mission-driven equity or loan capital to neighbourhood businesses and social enterprises, keeping returns and control local.

resources.name: FarmWorks Investment Co-operative Limited (CEDIF)
resources.description: FarmWorks is a community investment cooperative that raises capital from Nova Scotians through CEDIF share offerings and deploys it as patient, relationship-based loans to local farms, food producers, and food-related enterprises across the province. By enabling residents to buy shares and recycle returns locally, FarmWorks keeps ownership and decision-making in the community while filling early-stage financing gaps for neighbourhood businesses and social enterprises in the food system.

resources.name: Black Business Community Investment Fund Limited (BBCIFL)
resources.description: BBCIFL is a Community Economic Development Investment Fund that allows Nova Scotians to purchase shares and channel patient, mission-aligned capital into Black-owned and operated businesses throughout the province. The fund complements advisory supports from the Black Business Initiative and helps overcome early-stage financing barriers by keeping investment, returns, and control within local communities.

resources.name: New Dawn Community Investment Fund (CEDIF)
resources.description: New Dawn raises capital from local residents through periodic CEDIF share offerings and invests in community enterprises and social purpose projects in Cape Breton, such as affordable housing, community infrastructure, and mission-driven businesses. By inviting community members to buy shares and share in the returns, the fund keeps capital circulating locally and provides flexible, patient financing that addresses gaps faced by early-stage and impact-focused ventures.

solutions.text: Mentorship Circles and Peer Learning Groups: Organize regular, facilitated mentorship circles pairing experienced local business owners with new entrepreneurs for skill-building, peer accountability and practical problem solving.

resources.name: Creative Destruction Lab - Atlantic (CDL-Atlantic)
resources.organization: Creative Destruction Lab - Atlantic at Dalhousie University
resources.description: CDL-Atlantic runs a cohort-based program where early-stage ventures meet regularly in facilitated small-group sessions with experienced entrepreneurs, operators, and investors to set objectives and solve real business challenges. The program’s structured mentor panels and follow-up meetings create peer accountability among founders while providing practical, hands-on guidance from seasoned business leaders.

resources.name: Centre for Women in Business - Peer Mentoring Groups
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business convenes facilitated peer mentoring circles that bring together women entrepreneurs with experienced business owners to share strategies, troubleshoot challenges, and build skills. Groups meet regularly to set goals, hold each other accountable, and work through real-time business problems with guidance from trained facilitators and mentors.
resources.address: 166 Bedford Highway, Seton Academic Centre, 3rd Floor, Halifax, NS B3M 2J6

resources.name: Volta Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Groups
resources.description: Volta hosts recurring, facilitated peer-to-peer groups for startup leaders (e.g., founders, CTOs, marketers) where experienced operators and mentors guide discussions on current business bottlenecks. Participants workshop live issues, exchange playbooks, and set action items, creating peer accountability and practical problem solving within a trusted circle.

resources.name: ISANS Business Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS connects immigrant entrepreneurs with established local business owners and facilitates group learning sessions alongside one-on-one mentorship. Cohorts meet regularly to develop skills, address real business challenges, and track progress, ensuring peer accountability and practical, Nova Scotia-specific advice from experienced mentors.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Accelerate
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia’s Accelerate program delivers a cohort-based experience where startups receive ongoing mentorship from seasoned entrepreneurs and subject-matter experts while participating in regular peer sessions. Founders set milestones, report on progress, and collaborate in facilitated workshops, fostering peer accountability and practical problem solving within a supportive circle.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 810, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

solutions.text: Pop-up Markets and Shared Retail Rotations: Coordinate rotating pop-up stalls in vacant storefronts, community halls and seasonal markets to give startups affordable customer testing space and exposure without long-term leases.

resources.name: Salt Yard and Salt Yard Too Pop-Up Retail (Halifax Waterfront)
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia curates seasonal pop-up retail kiosks and container shops along the Halifax Waterfront, offering short-term, low-cost licenses to rotating local makers, food startups, and artists. The program provides turnkey, high-foot-traffic stalls without long-term leases, enabling entrepreneurs to test products, validate demand, and gain exposure in a shared retail environment.
resources.address: 1751 Lower Water Street, Suite 601, Halifax, NS B3J 1S5

resources.name: Alderney Landing Farmers’ Market
resources.description: Located in a community cultural centre on the Dartmouth waterfront, the Alderney Landing Farmers’ Market offers affordable, short-term table rentals to a rotating mix of food producers, artisans, and startups. Through weekly markets and seasonal pop-up events, it provides entrepreneurs with low-commitment retail exposure and direct customer feedback without the need for a permanent storefront.

resources.name: Halifax Brewery Market
resources.description: The Halifax Brewery Market operates weekly inside the historic Alexander Keith’s Brewery complex, offering rotating stall space to small-scale food businesses, crafters, and social enterprises. With flexible vendor terms and seasonal special markets, it serves as a shared retail platform where entrepreneurs can pilot products and build customer bases without long-term leases.
resources.address: 1496 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1R9

resources.name: New Glasgow Farmers Market
resources.description: This year-round community market provides affordable, short-term booths for rotating local vendors, including food startups and artisans from across Pictou County. Its indoor/outdoor seasonal setup and special pop-up events give entrepreneurs a low-risk way to test products, reach new customers, and scale toward permanent retail as demand grows.
resources.address: 620 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3S2

solutions.text: Community-run Coworking and Makerspaces: Convert underused municipal or church space into low-cost coworking, fabrication and kitchen-share spaces with tiered pricing, equipment access and business drop-in support.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries operates the Lou Duggan Creative Studio inside the Central Library, offering free or low-cost access to equipment like 3D printers, sewing machines, audio/visual gear, and design tools. As a municipally run, bookable makerspace with workshops and staff support, it gives entrepreneurs and youth hands-on fabrication resources, meeting rooms, and programming that lower startup costs and provide practical, drop-in guidance.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: The Deanery Project – Community Workshops and Shared Spaces
resources.description: Located on a repurposed former church property, The Deanery Project provides community-run workshop spaces (woodworking, bikes, crafts), a rentable community kitchen, and collaborative work areas at affordable rates. It supports micro-entrepreneurs and creative startups with equipment access, skills training, and program-based mentorship, embodying a low-cost, rural coworking and makerspace model.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

resources.name: The Old School Community Gathering Place – Shared Kitchen and Workspaces
resources.organization: The Old School Community Gathering Place Society
resources.description: Housed in a revitalized former school, The Old School offers a certified commercial kitchen for rent, multipurpose studios, and offices that function as coworking-style spaces with community-friendly pricing. It enables food producers, artisans, and small service businesses to launch and grow with affordable space, equipment access, and locally organized programming and support.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: Operating from the community-run Veith House, the Halifax Tool Library provides low-cost memberships that give entrepreneurs and makers access to thousands of hand and power tools, plus skill-building workshops. By eliminating upfront equipment costs and offering a drop-in, borrow-what-you-need model, it directly supports small trades, home-based businesses, and early-stage makers.

resources.name: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship)
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE operates a large, repurposed waterfront facility that provides shared offices, coworking, machine and fabrication shops, and test infrastructure for ocean-focused startups and SMEs. With membership-based access, programming, and industry mentorship, it lowers space and equipment barriers while connecting companies to procurement and commercialization opportunities.

solutions.text: Local Procurement Consortia: Form buyer consortia of schools, health centres and municipalities to aggregate demand and create predictable contracts that make it easier for small local suppliers to win work.

resources.name: Collaborative Procurement and Standing Offers (MASH Sector Access)
resources.organization: Province of Nova Scotia – Procurement (Service Nova Scotia and Internal Services)
resources.description: Nova Scotia’s Procurement division runs collaborative procurements and provincewide standing offers that can be used by provincial departments, Nova Scotia Health, IWK, regional centres for education, municipalities, and other MASH entities. By aggregating demand across these public buyers and awarding multi‑year, often regionalized contracts, the program creates predictable volumes that make it easier for small local suppliers to compete and win work through a single, streamlined agreement.

resources.name: Canadian Collaborative Procurement Initiative (CCPI) – Atlantic Region
resources.description: CCPI enables Nova Scotia’s municipalities, academic institutions, schools, and hospitals (MASH) to use federal standing offers and supply arrangements, pooling demand with other public buyers to secure stable pricing and service levels. This buyer consortium model reduces duplication of tenders and opens a clear pathway for qualified local small and medium suppliers to access predictable, consolidated contracts and receive call‑ups from multiple institutions.

resources.name: Provincial Supply Chain (Procurement) for Health Services
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health operates a shared provincial supply chain and procurement function that consolidates purchasing for hospitals and health facilities across the province, often coordinating with IWK and group purchasing while also running provincial RFPs and standing offers. By combining the demand of many sites and using regional lots and multi‑year agreements, the program creates predictable institutional contracts that small Nova Scotia suppliers can service without marketing to each facility separately.
resources.address: 90 Lovett Lake Court, Beechville, NS B3T 0H1

solutions.text: Microgrant and Seed Match Programs: Community foundations, businesses and municipalities jointly fund small microgrants and match public seed funding for pre-revenue pilots, commercialization, and market validation.

resources.name: Early Stage Commercialization Fund (ESCF)
resources.description: ESCF provides non-dilutive microgrants to university and college researchers in Nova Scotia to build prototypes, conduct customer discovery, and validate market potential before revenue. By covering early technical and market-validation costs and pairing teams with mentors, the program fills the seed-capital gap and de-risks commercialization so projects can attract follow-on investment or matching funds from public and private sources.

resources.name: Productivity and Innovation Voucher Program
resources.description: This voucher program gives small, non-dilutive grants (vouchers) to Nova Scotia SMEs to purchase R&D, prototyping, testing, and market-assessment services from local universities and colleges. It operates as a seed-stage catalyst by offsetting early validation and pilot costs, often leveraging company contributions and institutional resources—effectively matching public support with private effort to accelerate commercialization.

resources.name: Ocean Startup Challenge
resources.description: The Ocean Startup Challenge awards non-dilutive microgrants and wraps them with mentorship and programming to help pre-revenue ocean-technology founders build MVPs and validate markets across Atlantic Canada, including rural Nova Scotia. Funded by public agencies and corporate partners, it blends community and industry backing with seed-sized grants to reduce early risk and position startups for matched funding and scale-up.

resources.name: Ready2Launch
resources.description: Ready2Launch provides non-dilutive seed funding stipends and intensive mentorship to student and researcher-led teams to run pilots, develop prototypes, and complete customer validation. Backed by public and private partners, the program functions as a microgrant and seed-stage bridge that helps founders de-risk early commercialization and unlock additional matched funding or investment.

solutions.text: Landlord-Entrepreneur Partnerships: Encourage local landlords to offer flexible short-term, revenue-share or graduated-rent leases for startups, supported by a community mediation/guarantee fund to reduce risk.

resources.name: Halifax Waterfront Vendor Opportunities
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia curates seasonal kiosks, pop-up huts, and flexible retail/food spaces along the Halifax Waterfront, offering short-term license agreements designed for early-stage entrepreneurs. Terms are structured to lower upfront costs and risk (e.g., seasonal, short-duration agreements with right-sized fees), and Build Nova Scotia acts as a landlord-intermediary that provides high-foot-traffic locations and coordination support—functioning much like a community partner that de-risks space access for startups.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 301, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty: Storefront and Window Activation Grants
resources.description: This Downtown Halifax Business Commission program funds and brokers short-term activations in vacant storefronts and windows, pairing property owners with entrepreneurs, artists, and small retailers. The grants offset risk for landlords and startups (e.g., basic fit-out, insurance, and activation costs), enabling flexible, time-limited pop-up or graduated-rent arrangements that let new ventures test markets before committing to long-term leases.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

resources.name: Downtown Truro Pop-Up Shop Program
resources.description: Downtown Truro Partnership works with local landlords to place startups and micro-retailers in short-term, low-cost pop-up spaces (including seasonal container shops) so they can test products and build a customer base. The program facilitates flexible leases, helps negotiate terms, and provides promotional support—reducing risk for property owners while giving entrepreneurs an affordable pathway toward permanent tenancy.

solutions.text: Volunteer Professional Clinics: Local lawyers, accountants and marketers provide pro-bono clinics and office hours to help founders with incorporation, contracts, bookkeeping and tendering at no or low cost.

resources.name: Volta Office Hours
resources.description: Volta hosts recurring, free or low-cost office hours where local lawyers, accountants, and marketing professionals volunteer time to meet one-on-one with founders. These clinics help startups with incorporation and shareholder agreements, bookkeeping and financial modeling, and practical issues like contract review and procurement readiness.

resources.name: Business & IP Centre (BIPC) Halifax – Experts in Residence and Clinics
resources.description: BIPC Halifax provides free expert advice sessions and drop‑in clinics where volunteer professionals (including IP and business lawyers, accountants, and marketing advisors) guide entrepreneurs through incorporation, contracts, bookkeeping, market research, and brand strategy. The Centre also hosts procurement and tendering workshops with partner experts to help founders navigate selling to government.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Advisory Services and Ask‑an‑Expert
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business offers free and low‑cost advisory sessions and Ask‑an‑Expert clinics where volunteer professionals (lawyers, accountants, and marketing specialists) provide one‑on‑one guidance to entrepreneurs. Founders receive practical help with choosing a legal structure and drafting contracts, setting up books and cash‑flow systems, and preparing for procurement and tender opportunities.
resources.address: 166 Bedford Highway, 3rd Floor Rosaria Student Centre, Halifax, NS B3M 2J6

resources.name: Start‑Up Yard Experts‑in‑Residence and Office Hours
resources.description: Start‑Up Yard at COVE runs expert office hours and clinics where partner lawyers, accountants, and procurement advisors donate time to support ocean‑sector founders. These sessions cover incorporation, IP and contract basics, bookkeeping and financial reporting, and how to qualify for and respond to tenders with large buyers and government.

resources.name: Expert Office Hours and Clinics
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic hosts free expert office hours and themed clinics where local lawyers, accountants, and marketers volunteer their time to advise rural founders. Entrepreneurs receive hands‑on help with incorporation and contracts, bookkeeping setup and tax basics, and practical guidance for navigating government procurement and tendering processes.

solutions.text: Regional Pitch Nights and Demo Days: Host regular, locally-run pitch events and demo days where entrepreneurs present to community investors, customers and mentors in an accessible, low-pressure format.

resources.name: Volta Cohort Pitch Event and DemoCamp Halifax
resources.description: Volta hosts recurring pitch nights and demo events where early-stage founders present to local angels, venture funds, customers, and mentors in a supportive, low-pressure setting. Flagship events like the Volta Cohort Pitch and DemoCamp Halifax are open to the community and provide structured feedback, visibility, and connections to funding—directly tackling early financing gaps and mentorship access.

resources.name: Startup Yard at COVE Demo Day
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: Startup Yard at COVE runs accelerator cohorts that culminate in public Demo Days at the COVE campus, where ocean-technology startups pitch to regional industry partners, investors, and mentors. These demo events are designed to be accessible and collaborative, giving founders practical exposure to customers and capital in a low-pressure format while strengthening Nova Scotia’s ocean economy.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Community Pitch Nights
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic hosts recurring community pitch nights and showcases in rural hubs like Yarmouth and Pictou County, giving entrepreneurs a friendly stage to share ideas with local mentors, potential customers, and community investors. Events are frequently free and open to the public, lowering barriers to participation and helping founders outside Halifax gain early feedback, visibility, and connections to capital.

resources.name: CEED Cohort Pitch Nights and Demo Days
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED’s entrepreneurship programs regularly culminate in pitch nights and demo showcases where participants present to a room of local mentors, lenders, and community supporters. These gatherings emphasize constructive feedback and relationship-building in an accessible, low-pressure environment, helping founders validate ideas, meet customers, and unlock early-stage financing pathways.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Community-backed Loan Guarantee Scheme: Pool a small guarantee fund through local stakeholders that reduces lender risk for microloans to early-stage businesses, unlocking credit from local credit unions and banks.

resources.name: Credit Union Small Business Loan Guarantee Program
resources.description: Valley Credit Union delivers the province-wide Credit Union Small Business Loan Guarantee Program, where a pooled guarantee fund backed by the Province of Nova Scotia and administered with the Nova Scotia Co-operative Council reduces lender risk for start-ups and small businesses. Entrepreneurs apply at the credit union, which can approve microloans and working capital with a government-backed guarantee (often up to 90%), unlocking credit that would otherwise be unavailable—especially in rural communities outside Halifax.

resources.name: Credit Union Social Enterprise Loan Guarantee Program
resources.description: New Ross Credit Union participates in the Credit Union Social Enterprise Loan Guarantee Program, which pools a community-backed guarantee fund with provincial support to de-risk lending to early-stage and growing social enterprises. By using the guarantee to cover a significant portion of potential losses, the credit union can extend microloans and operating lines that enable impact-focused organizations to access affordable financing they wouldn’t secure from conventional lending alone.

solutions.text: Shared Procurement and Tendering Portal: Build a regional platform where small suppliers can find and collaborate on tenders, share certifications, and band together to meet larger contract requirements.

resources.name: CANSnet Projects & Documents (Electronic Plan Room)
resources.description: CANSnet is the Construction Association of Nova Scotia’s province‑wide electronic plan room where owners, architects, and contractors post public and private construction tenders, drawings, addenda, and award information. Small suppliers and subtrades use the portal to find opportunities, maintain company profiles that showcase capabilities and certifications, and connect with general contractors and other subs to form bid teams for larger projects—directly supporting collaboration to meet bigger contract requirements.
resources.address: 260 Brownlow Avenue, Unit 3, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1V9

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Procurement (Bonfire Supplier Portal)
resources.description: HRM centralizes municipal tenders on its Bonfire portal, where vendors register once, upload certifications and compliance documents, and subscribe to commodity codes to receive opportunities. The portal enables suppliers—including smaller firms—to discover tenders, submit jointly as consortiums or joint ventures when permitted, and share required documentation in one place, lowering administrative barriers and encouraging collaboration to meet larger-scope contracts.

resources.name: Health Association Nova Scotia – Group Purchasing & Strategic Sourcing
resources.description: HANS operates a shared purchasing program for health and community organizations across Nova Scotia, using an e-bidding portal to post solicitations and manage supplier registrations and certifications. By aggregating demand and standardizing documentation in one platform, the program makes it easier for small and regional suppliers to find opportunities and team up or subcontract to deliver multi-site, larger contracts they could not meet alone.

resources.name: COVE Member Directory & Opportunities
resources.organization: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: COVE provides an industry platform and member directory that connects ocean-technology SMEs with procurement calls, pilot opportunities, and larger industry projects across Atlantic Canada. Through curated opportunities, matchmaking, and member profiles that highlight capabilities and certifications, COVE helps smaller suppliers find tenders and form collaborative consortia to pursue larger marine and defense contracts.

solutions.text: Youth and Student Entrepreneurship Partnerships: Partner schools and colleges with community businesses to run internships, short incubators and student-led pop-ups that keep young talent engaged locally and test business ideas.

resources.name: Volta Academy
resources.description: Volta Academy is a skills-based program that connects university and college students with founders, mentors, and local companies to validate ideas through customer discovery, rapid prototyping, and pitch events. By partnering with post-secondary institutions and the startup community, it offers short, cohort-based incubator experiences and facilitates student-led pop-ups and demo nights that test business ideas and build local entrepreneurial talent.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs (Nova Scotia Sandbox)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs is a university–industry sandbox that brings Dalhousie students together with community businesses to co-create technology solutions through hackathons, design sprints, and applied projects. It runs short pre-incubation programs and mentorship that help student teams test and validate ideas, and it brokers internships and project placements with Nova Scotia companies to keep emerging talent engaged locally.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre (SMUEC)
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University – Sobey School of Business
resources.description: SMUEC partners with Nova Scotia businesses and public-sector organizations to place students in paid consulting projects, internships, and work-integrated learning that solve real operational challenges. It also delivers short incubators, venture discovery programming, and student-led pop-ups and pitch events, giving young entrepreneurs hands-on opportunities to test ideas and build companies in the province.

resources.name: Acadia Entrepreneurship Centre
resources.description: The Acadia Entrepreneurship Centre connects students with local businesses and municipalities across the Annapolis Valley to run entrepreneurship bootcamps, summer venture programs, and applied projects. Through short incubators, mentorship, and student pop-up markets, it helps young entrepreneurs validate products and services while creating pathways to internships and employment with community partners.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Youth & Student Innovation Programs
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic partners with regional schools, NSCC campuses, and local businesses to run youth innovation challenges, maker-space programming, and short incubators that help students develop and test business ideas. It facilitates student-led pop-ups, pitch nights, and project placements with rural companies, keeping young talent engaged in Southwest and Northern Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

solutions.text: Local Crowdfunding Campaign Support: Provide community workshops, coaching and in-kind marketing to help founders run successful rewards- or equity-crowdfunding campaigns that mobilize area supporters.

resources.name: Volta Community Programming and Mentorship
resources.description: Volta delivers ongoing workshops, Lunch & Learns, and founder mentorship that regularly cover alternative financing, including how to plan and execute rewards- and equity-crowdfunding campaigns (e.g., choosing platforms like Kickstarter/Indiegogo or equity portals such as FrontFundr, structuring rewards, and campaign storytelling). Their advisors provide one-on-one coaching on campaign strategy and outreach, and Volta amplifies local founders’ campaigns through its newsletters, events, and social channels, offering in-kind marketing support to mobilize community backers.
resources.address: Suite 100, 1505 Barrington Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Centre for Women in Business – Training & Advisory
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business, Mount Saint Vincent University
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business provides workshops and one-on-one advisory that help women and gender-diverse founders plan and run crowdfunding campaigns, including guidance on platform selection, reward tiers, pre-launch audience building, and compliance considerations for equity crowdfunding. The Centre also offers in-kind promotional support by featuring member campaigns in its networks and social channels, and connects entrepreneurs with mentors and peers for feedback to improve campaign success.

resources.name: Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre – Coaching & Student Consulting
resources.organization: Saint Mary’s University Entrepreneurship Centre (SMUEC), Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: SMUEC offers training and advisory services that include crowdfunding education for startups and social enterprises, covering campaign planning, messaging, budgeting, and digital marketing tactics to activate local supporters. Through staff advisors and student consulting teams, founders receive practical help producing campaign assets (e.g., pitch pages and outreach plans) and can access in-kind promotion via SMUEC events and partner networks, strengthening both rewards- and equity-crowdfunding efforts.

solutions.text: Equipment Libraries and Shared Tool Pools: Set up community tool and equipment lending libraries for makers, tradespeople and food producers to lower startup capital needs and encourage collaboration.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: A membership-based lending library offering hundreds of hand and power tools for woodworking, home repair, gardening, and light trades. By letting people borrow instead of buy, it lowers upfront equipment costs for makers and tradespeople and fosters collaboration through workshops and a volunteer-run community hub.

resources.name: The Station Food Hub (Shared-Use Commercial Kitchen)
resources.description: A shared-use commercial kitchen and food processing facility that provides food entrepreneurs with access to certified kitchen space, specialized equipment, and storage. By renting time on equipment like dehydrators, canners, and packaging tools, producers can test, launch, and scale products without large capital investments.

resources.name: Perennia Food and Beverage Innovation Centre
resources.description: A provincially supported pilot plant and applied research facility that gives food and beverage startups access to commercial-grade processing equipment and technical expertise. Entrepreneurs can book equipment and space to develop, test, and produce products, reducing the need to purchase costly machinery up front.
resources.address: 45 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Creation Space)
resources.description: A free, bookable makerspace at Halifax Central Library providing access to shared equipment such as 3D printers, sewing machines, Cricut cutters, and multimedia tools. This shared equipment pool enables creators and early-stage entrepreneurs to prototype, produce, and learn new skills without buying expensive tools.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Procurement Literacy and Tender Readiness Workshops: Offer recurring workshops teaching small businesses how to register for government procurement, write bids, and meet compliance so they can compete effectively.

resources.name: Procurement Assistance Canada – Atlantic Region
resources.description: Procurement Assistance Canada (PAC) delivers recurring seminars and one-on-one advisory sessions that teach small businesses how to sell to the federal government. Workshops cover registering on CanadaBuys (SAP Ariba), finding and interpreting tenders, bid-writing tips, security clearances, and compliance requirements so firms can submit competitive bids.

resources.name: Supplier Development Program
resources.description: The Province of Nova Scotia’s Supplier Development Program offers ongoing ‘Procurement 101’ and tender-readiness sessions that walk businesses through registering as a provincial supplier, navigating the Nova Scotia Tenders portal, and understanding insurance, safety, and other compliance requirements. It also hosts bid-writing guidance and buyer-supplier engagement events (e.g., reverse trade shows) to help small firms compete for provincial and public sector contracts.

resources.name: HRM Supplier Information Sessions
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality (HRM) runs supplier information sessions and vendor outreach that explain how to register, search opportunities, and submit proposals through HRM’s e-procurement portal. The sessions cover bid compliance (insurance, safety, and contract terms) and provide practical guidance to help small businesses prepare stronger responses to municipal tenders.

resources.name: Business Services – Procurement and Tendering Workshops
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers recurring workshops and coaching that help immigrant-owned small businesses learn how to sell to government, often in partnership with PAC and Nova Scotia Procurement. Sessions cover registration on procurement portals, understanding RFx requirements, and bid-writing and compliance basics, with follow-up one-on-one advising to get entrepreneurs tender-ready.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Procurement Readiness and Supplier Diversity Workshops
resources.description: BBI offers targeted training and events that prepare Black-owned businesses to compete for public-sector contracts, including sessions on registering with CanadaBuys and the Nova Scotia tenders portal, writing compliant bids, and meeting insurance and safety requirements. Programs frequently feature buyer panels and partnerships with PAC and supplier-diversity organizations to connect participants directly with procurement opportunities.
resources.address: 1660 Hollis Street, Suite 910, Halifax, NS B3J 1V7

obstacles.title: Regulatory and Permitting Friction
obstacles.description: Slow, complex, and overlapping approvals for housing, renewables, and business expansion delay projects and raise costs. Occupational licensing barriers can deter mobility and innovation.

solutions.text: Community Permit Helpdesk: A volunteer-run desk (physical or online) that helps residents and small builders prepare complete permit applications, explain timelines, and liaise with municipal contacts to reduce errors and re-submissions.

resources.name: Planning & Development Permit Applications Centre
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Permit Applications Centre provides front-counter and online guidance to residents and small builders on building, development, and occupancy permits. Staff review submissions for completeness, explain timelines, fees, and required documentation, and coordinate with internal municipal contacts to reduce errors and re-submissions.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 2005, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Planning & Development Customer Service
resources.organization: Cape Breton Regional Municipality (CBRM) Planning & Development
resources.description: CBRM’s Planning & Development office assists homeowners, contractors, and small builders in preparing complete permit applications for building and development projects. Staff provide checklists, explain process timelines and inspection steps, and liaise with municipal departments (e.g., fire, engineering, bylaw) to troubleshoot issues and prevent re-submissions.

resources.name: Planning and Inspections Counter Services
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings – Planning & Inspections
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings offers in-person and online assistance to residents and small builders to navigate building, development, and subdivision permits. Staff help applicants assemble complete packages, clarify zoning and code requirements, outline timelines and inspection stages, and coordinate with inspectors and planners to minimize delays and re-work.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: SmartBusiness Program
resources.description: SmartBusiness provides one-on-one navigation support to help companies and entrepreneurs understand and complete municipal and provincial permitting and licensing requirements. Advisors help prepare application materials, explain approval timelines, and directly connect clients with the appropriate HRM and provincial contacts to resolve bottlenecks and reduce re-submissions.
resources.address: 5151 George Street, Suite 1215, Halifax, NS B3J 1M5

resources.name: Business & Entrepreneurship Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS supports newcomers who are starting or expanding a business by guiding them through permits, licences, and regulatory steps at the municipal and provincial levels. Advisors help clients prepare complete applications, explain timelines and compliance requirements, and liaise with municipal permitting offices and provincial regulators to reduce errors and delays.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Pre‑Approved Local Design Library: Develop a set of common, pre‑approved designs for tiny homes, accessory units, renewable installations and small commercial fitouts that municipalities can endorse to speed approvals for repeatable projects.

resources.name: Solar City Program
resources.description: Halifax’s Solar City program streamlines residential and small commercial solar by using standardized, pre‑engineered system designs and pre‑qualified contractors, which the municipality has vetted to simplify permitting and interconnection. By offering permit-ready documentation and coordinating with Nova Scotia Power, Solar City functions as a local library of approved renewable installation designs that speeds approvals and reduces repeat review for repeatable projects.

resources.name: Net Metering Interconnection – Pre‑Certified Equipment and Standard Packages
resources.description: Nova Scotia Power’s net metering program maintains standardized interconnection requirements and accepts pre‑certified inverters and equipment, enabling installers to use repeatable, utility‑approved solar PV packages with standard single‑line diagrams. This acts as a pre‑approved design library for small renewable systems, cutting review time and simplifying municipal and utility approvals for common rooftop installations.
resources.address: 1223 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

resources.name: Backyard Suites (Accessory Dwelling Units) – Standardized Design and Permit Package
resources.description: HRM’s Backyard Suites program provides a standardized application package with typical drawings, siting rules, and design criteria that allow repeatable, code‑compliant ADU layouts to be reviewed and approved more quickly. By publishing consistent templates and accepted design parameters across the municipality, it operationalizes a pre‑approved approach that reduces friction for accessory units and accelerates permit turnaround for common designs.

solutions.text: Permitting Ambassadors Program: Train local volunteers to act as permitting ambassadors who pre‑review applications, coach applicants on local rules, and accompany them to planning meetings to smooth communication with officials.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Business Navigators
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Business Navigators provide one-on-one, concierge-style guidance to help entrepreneurs understand permits, licences, and regulatory requirements at the municipal and provincial levels. Advisors pre‑review applications for completeness, coach applicants on local rules and sequencing, and coordinate or join calls/meetings with officials to resolve issues and speed approvals—functioning effectively as permitting ambassadors.

resources.name: Pre-Application Consultations (Planning & Development)
resources.description: HRM’s Planning & Development offers pre‑application consultations where planners review concepts and draft submissions, identify required permits/approvals, and coach applicants on how to comply with local bylaws and planning policies. Staff then coordinate with internal departments and accompany files through planning meetings and committee processes to smooth communication and reduce delays.

resources.name: ISANS Business Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Business Services provide immigrant and newcomer entrepreneurs with tailored guidance on Nova Scotia permits, licences, zoning, and sector-specific regulations. Business counsellors pre‑review application packages and plans, coach clients on local rules and documentation, and liaise with (and, when needed, accompany clients to) meetings with municipal and provincial officials to keep applications moving.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: CEED Business Advisory Services
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED advisors help startups and growing businesses navigate permitting and compliance for activities such as occupancy, signage, home‑based operations, and renovations. They pre‑review forms and supporting documents, coach clients on municipal and provincial rules, and prepare or join clients for conversations with planning and inspection officials to reduce friction and avoid rework.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Local Fast‑Track Pilot Projects: Organize community-backed pilot projects (e.g., a cluster of modular homes or community solar) and negotiate a municipal fast‑track review and clear checklist to prove a repeatable, low‑risk approval path.

resources.name: Solar City Program
resources.description: Halifax’s Solar City is a municipally run PACE program that delivers rooftop solar through pre-qualified contractors, standardized designs, and HRM-managed permits. The program uses a one-window intake and published checklists to streamline reviews and inspections, effectively fast-tracking hundreds of small distributed projects and proving a repeatable, low-risk approval path for solar across the municipality.

resources.name: Energize Bridgewater – Community Solar Garden Pilot
resources.description: The Town of Bridgewater’s community solar garden pilot organizes a municipal-led, subscription-based solar project to demonstrate a replicable model for clean energy. By coordinating interconnection early, using standardized municipal approvals and a clear participant checklist, the pilot fast-tracks reviews and establishes a low-risk template other Nova Scotia communities can adopt.

resources.name: Antigonish Community Solar Garden
resources.description: The Town of Antigonish Electric Utility operates a community solar garden that lets residents subscribe to locally produced solar power. The municipality standardized procurement and permitting steps and provides clear customer enrollment materials, creating a fast, predictable process that serves as a pilot for repeatable, low-risk municipal community solar approvals in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Halifax Housing Accelerator Fund – Fast-Track Development Approvals
resources.description: Under its Housing Accelerator Fund action plan, HRM is piloting faster, clearer approvals through measures like pre-approved designs (e.g., accessory/backyard suites), published checklists, digital permitting, and prioritized review lanes for affordable and modular projects. These steps reduce permitting friction, establish guaranteed timelines, and create a repeatable, low-risk pathway for multi-site housing pilots to scale.

solutions.text: Regulatory Literacy Workshops: Host free, recurring workshops for youth and local entrepreneurs on zoning, permitting, building codes and occupational licensing, including step‑by‑step guides and Q&A with municipal staff.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Business Navigators
resources.organization: Service Nova Scotia (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: A free provincial service that delivers recurring webinars and outreach sessions to help entrepreneurs understand permits, licenses, zoning, and regulatory steps for starting or expanding a business in Nova Scotia. Business Navigators provide step-by-step guidance, checklists, and live Q&A with government staff, including direction on municipal development permits, provincial occupational licensing, and building-code touchpoints.

resources.name: Halifax Permits Information Sessions
resources.description: HRM Planning & Development hosts recurring public information sessions and webinars to walk homeowners, youth builders, and local entrepreneurs through zoning, development and building permit processes, and code compliance. Sessions include step-by-step demonstrations of the Halifax Permits portal and open Q&A with municipal staff to clarify application requirements, timelines, and inspections.

resources.name: ISANS Entrepreneurship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: This free program for newcomer entrepreneurs in Nova Scotia runs ongoing workshops that cover business registration, municipal licensing, home-based business zoning rules, and sector-specific permits.
