Sessions often feature guest speakers from municipal and provincial offices for live Q&A and provide step-by-step guides to navigate permitting and occupational licensing.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Small Business Series (Halifax Public Libraries)
resources.description: A free, recurring workshop series hosted at library branches that helps youth and aspiring entrepreneurs understand the regulatory steps to start and grow a business in Nova Scotia. Sessions regularly include partners such as Nova Scotia Business Navigators and municipal staff, offering checklists for permits and licenses, practical how-tos, and live Q&A on zoning, building permits, and occupational licensing.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Community Legal Clinic for Permits and Licensing: Create a pro‑bono clinic where volunteer planners and lawyers help residents appeal decisions, interpret bylaws, complete complex applications and navigate occupational licensing hurdles.

resources.name: Business Navigators
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia — Service Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Business Navigators program provides free one-on-one help to entrepreneurs and organizations in Nova Scotia to understand and meet regulatory requirements. Navigators explain which permits, licences and certifications are needed, help complete applications, and coordinate with departments to resolve bottlenecks. This directly reduces permitting friction and licensing barriers by giving residents a clear path through complex, overlapping approvals.

resources.name: Licensing and Certification Support for Regulated Professions
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides specialized advising for internationally trained professionals and immigrant entrepreneurs to navigate occupational licensing and certification in Nova Scotia. Staff help clients interpret regulatory requirements, map licensing steps, prepare documentation and applications, and connect with regulatory bodies and bridging programs. By demystifying licensing and compliance, ISANS lowers barriers and speeds entry into trades and professions.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1H9

resources.name: Free Legal Clinic at the Halifax Law Courts
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Courts (in partnership with Pro Bono Nova Scotia)
resources.description: This clinic offers brief, pro bono legal advice from volunteer lawyers to self-represented people in civil and family matters, including administrative law issues. Lawyers help participants understand bylaws and regulations, prepare or review forms and affidavits, and discuss options to appeal or seek judicial review of government and municipal decisions. The service equips residents to navigate complex permitting or licensing processes and challenge adverse rulings.
resources.address: 1815 Upper Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 1S7

resources.name: Planning & Development Customer Service (Permits and Inspections)
resources.description: HRM’s Planning & Development counter provides front-line support and pre-application guidance for building, development, and occupancy permits. Staff help residents and businesses interpret zoning and land-use bylaws, identify required approvals, and complete complex applications, and can outline next steps and applicable appeal routes. This hands-on navigation reduces regulatory friction for housing, renewables, and business expansion projects within Halifax.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, 2nd Floor, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Shared Compliance Resource Hub: Maintain an open online repository of checklists, form templates, local policy summaries, common permit examples and vetted contractor contact lists to reduce time spent hunting information.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Business Navigators
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia — Office of Regulatory Affairs and Service Effectiveness
resources.description: A government service that centralizes regulatory and permitting guidance for entrepreneurs and project proponents through an online hub of step‑by‑step guides, checklists, and links to required forms across departments and municipalities. Navigators curate and share tailored checklists, templates, and relevant policy summaries, and connect clients with the correct inspectors or program officials, reducing time spent hunting for information and expediting approvals.

resources.name: Halifax Permits, Licences & Applications (Planning & Development)
resources.description: HRM’s Planning & Development portal consolidates building, development, and business permitting resources, offering application forms, detailed checklists, sample drawings, and plain‑language guides to local policies and codes. By maintaining a single online repository and a centralized permit counter, it functions as a shared compliance hub that streamlines what applicants need and how to submit it, reducing regulatory friction for housing and business projects.

resources.name: Efficiency Nova Scotia — Find a Contractor and Program Resources
resources.description: Efficiency Nova Scotia maintains an open library of program guides, eligibility checklists, measure lists, and application forms for residential, commercial, and renewable energy upgrades. Its vetted “Find a Contractor” directory helps applicants quickly identify qualified contractors, while the consolidated templates and step‑by‑step resources reduce paperwork errors and speed compliance with rebate and permitting requirements.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency — Resources for Apprentices and Employers
resources.description: The Agency hosts a centralized repository of trade profiles, application forms, logbook templates, exam outlines, and employer guides that clarify steps to certification and licensing across skilled trades. By providing standardized templates and plain‑language summaries of requirements in one place, it functions as a compliance resource hub that reduces occupational licensing friction and supports workforce mobility.

solutions.text: Employer‑Sponsored Bridging Courses: Partner local employers and training providers to offer short, low‑cost bridging courses and apprenticeships that meet licensing competencies or prepare candidates for exams.

resources.name: Internationally Educated Engineers (IEE) Bridging Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ IEE Bridging Program helps internationally educated engineers address competency gaps and prepare for licensure with Engineers Nova Scotia. The program combines exam preparation, workplace communication and Canadian standards training with employer-linked mentorships and work placements, effectively bridging candidates into regulated roles that meet licensing requirements.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) and Irving Shipbuilding Inc.
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based pre-apprenticeship and bridging program that prepares participants for Red Seal trades at the Halifax Shipyard. NSCC delivers targeted technical training and certifications aligned to employer needs while Irving Shipbuilding provides paid work terms and sponsorship into apprenticeships, ensuring graduates meet trade competencies and are exam-ready.

resources.name: Internationally Educated Nurses (IEN) Bridging and Support
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health partners with educators and the Nova Scotia College of Nursing to offer bridging education, supervised practice experiences, and exam preparation for IENs pursuing RN/LPN licensure. The employer-sponsored model provides paid work opportunities and covers or offsets required bridging courses and clinical placements so candidates can meet licensing competencies and write the NCLEX/CPNRE.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: Registered Apprenticeship Training (RAT)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency coordinates employer-sponsored apprenticeships that combine paid on-the-job training with short blocks of technical training at NSCC to meet trade competencies. The program aligns learning with Red Seal standards, offers exam preparation resources, and incentivizes employers to hire and train apprentices, directly reducing licensing barriers.

resources.name: Energy Advisor Training Pathway
resources.description: Efficiency Nova Scotia partners with service organizations and employers to deliver training and mentoring that prepare candidates to pass Natural Resources Canada’s Energy Advisor exams. The pathway includes exam prep, job-matching with approved service organizations, and on-the-job bridging support so trainees can meet credentialing requirements and quickly move into paid roles.
resources.address: 230 Brownlow Avenue, Suite 300, Dartmouth, NS B3B 0G5

solutions.text: Licensing Fee Support & Micro‑Scholarships: Establish a community fund or bursary to cover exam and licensing fees for low‑income youth, newcomers and entrepreneurs starting social enterprises or trades careers.

resources.name: Atlantic Immigrant Career Loan Fund (AICLF) – Nova Scotia
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: AICLF provides low-interest micro-loans to internationally trained newcomers so they can pay costs required to gain licensure and work in their field, including credential assessments, exam and licensing fees, short-term training, and professional association dues. In Nova Scotia, ISANS delivers the program and provides coaching to help clients navigate regulatory bodies and use the funds strategically to remove licensing barriers.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Internationally Educated Nurses (IEN) Licensing and Bridging Support
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health offers navigation and financial supports that can cover required assessment, exam, and professional licensing fees for internationally educated nurses pursuing registration in Nova Scotia. The initiative reduces up‑front costs and streamlines the regulatory process so newcomers can enter the workforce more quickly in a high‑demand field.
resources.address: 90 Lovett Lake Court, Halifax, NS B3S 0H1

resources.name: Indigenous Skills and Employment Training (ISET) – Employment & Training
resources.description: The ISET program at the Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre provides individualized employment supports that can pay for mandatory certifications, exam fees, and occupational licensing costs for Indigenous clients, including youth entering trades or regulated occupations. By covering these up‑front expenses and offering case management, the program removes key financial barriers to employment and career mobility.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works – Certification & Employment Supports
resources.organization: TEAM Work Cooperative and WorkBridge Association (Nova Scotia Works Centre)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Works centres can provide funding for short‑term training and required certifications, including exam and licensing fees needed to start work in trades and other regulated occupations for eligible low‑income jobseekers and youth. Through individualized employment plans and access to provincial Skills Development and related supports, clients receive bursary‑style assistance that removes cost barriers to meeting regulatory requirements.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Local Micro‑Credential Recognition Agreements: Organize agreements among local employers to recognize community college micro‑credentials, employer‑verified skill badges or supervised apprenticeships as hiring qualifications while full licensing is pursued.

resources.name: NSCC MicroCredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College designs short, competency-based micro-credentials with local employers and issues them as digital badges that verify specific, job-ready skills. Employers engaged through NSCC program advisory committees and sector partnerships agree to recognize these micro-credentials in recruitment and advancement decisions, allowing candidates to be hired or promoted while they continue toward full diplomas, Red Seal certification, or professional licensing.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency – Apprenticeship Program and START Employer Incentive
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency registers formal apprenticeship agreements between employers and workers in more than 70 trades, enabling employers to hire and advance apprentices based on supervised on‑the‑job training while they work toward trade certification/Red Seal. The START incentive supports employers who hire and retain apprentices, effectively treating registered apprentice status as a recognized hiring qualification during the path to full certification.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based program delivered with NSCC and community partners that provides pre-apprenticeship training and industry-endorsed micro-credentials aligned to marine and metal trades. Irving Shipbuilding hires successful graduates into registered apprenticeship positions at the Halifax Shipyard, recognizing these micro-credentials and supervised training as entry qualifications while employees complete their trade certification.

resources.name: Dalhousie Open Learning & Career Development – Microcredentials and Digital Badges
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Faculty of Open Learning & Career Development
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Open Learning & Career Development unit offers employer-validated microcredentials and digital badges in areas such as data, project management, and ocean-related skills. Programs are co-designed with industry partners who agree to recognize the badges in hiring, upskilling, or advancement decisions, enabling learners to qualify for roles while they pursue full degrees, professional certifications, or licensing.

solutions.text: Cross‑Municipal Community Coalition: Form a coalition of neighbourhood associations and chambers of commerce across nearby municipalities to jointly advocate for aligned bylaws, standard forms and reciprocal permitting practices.

resources.name: Eastern District Planning Commission (EDPC)
resources.description: EDPC is a multi-municipal planning and development service that provides a single planning, building inspection, and permitting office for several municipalities in the Strait/Cape Breton region. By using common application forms, shared staff, and harmonized development procedures across member municipalities, it reduces cross-boundary red tape and effectively enables reciprocal permitting practices; EDPC also liaises with local business groups to keep processes aligned with regional needs.
resources.address: 606 Reeves Street, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 2R7

resources.name: Kings 2050 Inter‑Municipal Planning Initiative
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: Kings 2050 is a collaborative planning framework among the Municipality of the County of Kings and the Towns of Kentville, Wolfville, and Berwick to align municipal planning strategies, land-use bylaws, and growth management. The initiative standardizes definitions and development standards and has engaged local business and community associations to streamline permitting, making approvals more predictable and consistent across municipal boundaries in the Valley region.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: Nova Scotia Business Navigators
resources.organization: Service Nova Scotia and the Office of Regulatory Affairs and Service Effectiveness
resources.description: Business Navigators is a province-wide service that works directly with entrepreneurs, municipalities, and chambers of commerce to clarify and align permitting and licensing requirements. The team convenes cross‑municipal stakeholders, promotes common checklists and standard forms, and encourages reciprocal practices so businesses can start up or expand in multiple Nova Scotia municipalities with fewer regulatory barriers.

solutions.text: Community Data Collection & Case Studies: Collect and publish anonymized timelines, costs and bottlenecks from local projects to build evidence for municipal/provincial reform and to show where small fixes yield big time savings.

resources.name: Planning Applications – Status and Documents
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality maintains a public, continuously updated registry of planning and development applications that lists key milestones (submission, public meetings, decisions) and links to supporting documents. By publishing project-level timelines and statuses in one place, it lets residents, builders, and analysts identify recurring delays and bottlenecks across neighborhoods and application types, generating evidence that can inform small process fixes and broader municipal reform.

resources.name: Halifax Open Data Catalogue
resources.description: HRM’s Open Data Catalogue releases machine-readable datasets on building permits, planning, transportation, and service delivery that include dates, locations, and values sufficient to calculate processing times and spot backlogs. The portal enables independent analysis and case-study development on permitting and regulatory friction, helping the municipality and community partners quantify where incremental changes can save weeks or months on local projects.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Open Data Portal
resources.description: The provincial Open Data Portal publishes datasets on licensing, inspections, land use, and economic activity that can be combined to build anonymized timelines and cost profiles for projects across Nova Scotia. Researchers, municipalities, and industry groups use these datasets to create evidence-based case studies that reveal systemic bottlenecks in approvals and inform provincial and municipal process improvements.

resources.name: Major Projects Inventory (MPI)
resources.description: APEC’s Major Projects Inventory tracks capital projects in Atlantic Canada, including Nova Scotia, with estimated costs, schedules, and status updates that illuminate approval pathways and recurring hurdles. The dataset and accompanying analyses provide comparative timelines and evidence on where regulatory or permitting steps add delay, supporting policy recommendations and targeted fixes that can accelerate construction and deployment.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1105, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Business Navigators
resources.organization: Government of Nova Scotia – Office of Regulatory Affairs and Service Effectiveness
resources.description: Nova Scotia’s Business Navigators program helps entrepreneurs and builders navigate permits and licenses while systematically logging inquiries, wait times, and pain points across departments. The program publishes summaries of common bottlenecks and works with the Office of Regulatory Affairs and Service Effectiveness to turn those findings into case studies and quick regulatory fixes that reduce days and costs for projects province-wide.

solutions.text: Pre‑Zoned Community Land Bank: Create a community land trust that acquires and holds lots pre‑zoned for affordable housing, small businesses or renewable installations, reducing time spent rezoning and permitting.

resources.name: Surplus Municipal Lands for Affordable Housing (Administrative Order 50)
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality maintains a land inventory and disposes of surplus municipal properties specifically for affordable housing, often through discounted conveyances to non‑profit providers. Because many of these parcels are within the Centre Plan’s as‑of‑right zones, projects can proceed without lengthy rezonings, effectively acting as a municipal land bank of pre‑zoned sites that shortens approvals and lowers costs.

resources.name: Bridgewater Business Park
resources.description: The Town of Bridgewater assembles and services land in its Business Park and sells fully pre‑zoned industrial and commercial lots, providing shovel‑ready sites with clear as‑of‑right uses. This functions as a municipal land bank for small businesses, reducing rezoning and permitting friction so firms can build and expand more quickly.

resources.name: Truro Business Parks (Truro Business Park and Truro Industrial Park)
resources.description: The Town of Truro offers serviced, pre‑zoned lots in its business parks, with established development standards and as‑of‑right permissions that minimize the need for rezonings or development agreements. By banking and preparing land in advance, the program shortens approval timelines and reduces costs for startups and growing companies.

resources.name: Municipality of Kings Business Parks (Greenwich and Coldbrook)
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: The Municipality of the County of Kings acquires and services land in its Greenwich and Coldbrook business parks and offers pre‑zoned, shovel‑ready lots for industrial and commercial development. This land‑bank approach streamlines approvals and reduces permitting friction for small businesses by enabling as‑of‑right construction on prepared sites.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

solutions.text: Pop‑Up Regulatory Sandboxes and Maker Days: Work with municipal partners to host temporary events where rules are relaxed for experimentation (arts pop‑ups, micro‑construction demos, solar pilots) to test new models and demonstrate safe approaches.

resources.name: Seasonal Outdoor Patios and Parklets Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality streamlines temporary permits for sidewalk patios, curb-lane parklets, and pop-up seating so businesses and community groups can quickly test street-activation ideas. By coordinating traffic, accessibility, and safety requirements under a simplified approval, HRM temporarily relaxes normal right‑of‑way restrictions—functioning as a regulatory sandbox to pilot designs before longer-term changes.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, 2nd Floor, Tower 2, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty Placemaking Program
resources.description: Downtown Halifax Business Commission funds and coordinates temporary public art, pop‑ups, parklets, and small‑scale builds that activate underused spaces. The program works with HRM to navigate or ease event and encroachment permits for short-term installations, creating a pop‑up sandbox where teams can safely trial designs and operational models before pursuing permanent approvals.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

resources.name: Open Street Sunday – Downtown Dartmouth
resources.description: This recurring event temporarily closes key Downtown Dartmouth streets to vehicle traffic, enabling pop‑up markets, arts installations, and micro‑mobility demos with municipal traffic orders and special event permits. The day acts as a regulatory sandbox where businesses, community groups, and innovators trial street uses and safety setups that inform longer‑term permitting and design decisions.

resources.name: Halifax Solar City
resources.description: HRM’s Solar City program pilots and scales residential solar (PV, hot water, and thermal) with municipal on‑bill financing and pre‑qualified installers, streamlining approvals and inspections. By bundling permitting guidance and standardized safety requirements, the program functions as a municipal sandbox for renewable technology adoption and de‑risks broader deployment.

resources.name: H2O Conference In‑Water Technology Demonstration Day
resources.description: Hosted by COVE with municipal and federal partners, this annual demo day designates a controlled harbour zone where firms can deploy marine tech prototypes (e.g., ASVs, sensors) under event-specific permits and safety plans. The setup temporarily relaxes normal operating restrictions in a managed environment, creating a real‑world regulatory sandbox to validate technologies before commercial roll‑out.

solutions.text: Demonstration & Teach‑How Projects: Build one or two community demonstration projects (ex. a pre‑approved tiny home, community solar array, or co‑working retrofit) that serve as living templates and reduce uncertainty for future applicants.

resources.name: Solar City Program
resources.description: Halifax’s Solar City Program provides end-to-end support for residential and commercial solar projects, including standardized assessments, coordinated permitting, and vetted contractors. By delivering hundreds of installations across the municipality, it functions as a large-scale living demonstration that shows code-compliant designs, inspection pathways, and financing models that others can replicate. This reduces uncertainty for future applicants by publishing clear how-to guidance and streamlining approvals with municipal departments.

resources.name: Community Solar Garden Program
resources.description: AREA’s Community Solar Gardens in Antigonish, Berwick, and Mahone Bay are municipal-scale arrays that let residents subscribe to locally generated solar power. The projects serve as living templates by standardizing interconnection, permitting, subscription contracts, and utility billing practices across multiple jurisdictions. AREA shares lessons learned and model documents with other Nova Scotia communities, reducing regulatory and approval uncertainty for future community solar applicants.
resources.address: 493 Main Street, Mahone Bay, NS B0J 2E0

resources.name: The Deanery Project
resources.description: The Deanery Project is a hands-on sustainability and skills centre featuring demonstration buildings (small/tiny structures, natural materials), on-site solar, and efficiency retrofits. It offers workshops, tours, and maker-to-market programming that show step-by-step, code-aware approaches to constructing small dwellings and community energy systems. These living examples help residents, builders, and local officials see compliant pathways and reduce uncertainty around permitting and inspection for innovative projects.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

resources.name: Smart Energy Living Lab
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) Applied Research
resources.description: NSCC’s Smart Energy Living Lab is a campus-scale demonstration site with solar PV, battery storage, EV charging, building controls, and microgrid systems used for applied research and training. By piloting real-world integrations with utilities and authorities, the lab documents technical standards, safety protocols, and commissioning processes that de-risk wider deployment. The facility doubles as a teach-how hub for students, trades, and municipalities, clarifying approval pathways for future energy and retrofit projects.

resources.name: Eltuek Arts Centre
resources.description: Eltuek Arts Centre is a major adaptive-reuse project that transformed a former institutional complex into shared studios, offices, and community spaces. As a high-profile coworking and cultural retrofit, it demonstrates change-of-use approvals, heritage-sensitive design, and building code compliance for multi-tenant hubs. The centre hosts events and shares lessons with community groups and municipalities, offering a living example that reduces uncertainty for similar coworking and retrofit initiatives.

obstacles.title: Inclusion, Racism, and Systemic Barriers
obstacles.description: Discrimination and inequitable access to services affect Black Nova Scotians, Mi’kmaq communities, newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+ people, and persons with disabilities. Without culturally safe supports, social cohesion and talent retention suffer.

solutions.text: Community Anti-Racism & Inclusion Task Force: Create a citizen-led task force made up of representatives from Black, Mi’kmaq, newcomer, 2SLGBTQIA+, disability and youth communities to audit local institutions, propose policy changes, coordinate community education, and monitor progress on inclusion goals.

resources.name: Diversity Advisory Committee (DAC)
resources.description: The Town of Kentville’s citizen-led Diversity Advisory Committee includes residents and stakeholder representatives from equity-deserving communities who advise Council on anti-racism, equity, accessibility, and inclusion. The committee reviews municipal policies and services for systemic barriers, proposes policy and bylaw changes, supports community education and training on inclusion, and monitors progress on the Town’s inclusion goals through reports and recommendations.

resources.name: Diversity & Inclusion Advisory Committee
resources.description: Truro’s citizen-led Diversity & Inclusion Advisory Committee brings together community members and stakeholder representatives to identify and address systemic barriers affecting Black and Mi’kmaw residents, newcomers, 2SLGBTQIA+ people, persons with disabilities, and youth. The committee audits municipal programs and policies, recommends changes to hiring, procurement, public engagement, and service delivery, and coordinates/endorses public education initiatives while monitoring progress through regular reports to Town Council.

resources.name: Diversity and Inclusion Committee
resources.description: Bridgewater’s Diversity and Inclusion Committee is a resident-based advisory body that guides the Town’s Diversity & Inclusion Strategy and action plans. It reviews municipal policies and services for equity impacts, proposes policy improvements to address racism and systemic barriers, partners with local organizations to deliver community education on inclusion and anti-racism, and tracks progress for Council to ensure accountability.

resources.name: Diversity and Inclusion Committee
resources.description: The Town of Yarmouth’s Diversity and Inclusion Committee engages residents and stakeholder representatives, including voices from African Nova Scotian, Mi’kmaw, newcomer, 2SLGBTQIA+, disability, and youth communities, to advance a more inclusive municipality. The committee reviews Town policies and programs to identify barriers, recommends changes and best practices, helps coordinate public education and cultural awareness activities, and reports to Council on progress toward inclusion goals.

solutions.text: Culturally Safe Mental Health and Wrap‑Around Services: Support development and funding of community-run, culturally grounded counselling and wrap‑around services (mental health, housing navigation, childcare) run by or in partnership with affected communities to reduce barriers to help-seeking.

resources.name: ISANS Wellness and Counselling Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides trauma‑informed, culturally competent mental health and wellness support for immigrants and refugees, including short‑term counselling with interpreters and culturally specific group programming. As a community‑run newcomer organization, it offers wrap‑around settlement services such as housing navigation, employment counselling, and Care for Newcomer Children (childminding), reducing language and cultural barriers to help‑seeking.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Eskasoni Mental Health & Addictions Services
resources.description: Indigenous‑led and based in Eskasoni First Nation, this program delivers culturally grounded counselling that blends Mi’kmaq knowledge, language, Elders, and land‑based healing with clinical mental health and addictions care. It provides wrap‑around supports—crisis response, youth and family programming, and referrals for housing and social services—designed to reduce barriers by meeting community members where they are in a culturally safe environment.

resources.name: Primary Care, Mental Health and MOSH (Mobile Outreach Street Health)
resources.description: NECHC is a community‑governed health centre offering integrated primary care, counselling, social work, harm reduction, and the MOSH outreach team that brings care directly to people facing homelessness and poverty. The centre delivers culturally safe, low‑barrier services in partnership with affected communities—including African Nova Scotians, Indigenous people, newcomers, and 2SLGBTQIA+ residents—and provides wrap‑around navigation for housing, income, food, and addictions supports.

resources.name: Supported Housing for Young Mothers (SHYM)
resources.description: SHYM combines safe, affordable housing with on‑site case management, counselling, parenting programs, life‑skills, and connections to education and employment, with access to childcare supports. Operated by a community‑based women’s organization, the program is trauma‑informed and culturally responsive to diverse young mothers—including African Nova Scotian, Indigenous, newcomer, and 2SLGBTQIA+ youth—reducing barriers through co‑located, wrap‑around services.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

solutions.text: Indigenous-Led Partnerships and Cultural Revitalization: Partner with Mi’kmaq communities to co-design programs, support language and cultural revitalization projects, host jointly governed healing circles, and ensure Indigenous leadership in service delivery affecting their communities.

resources.name: Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre – Cultural, Language, and Healing Programs
resources.description: An Indigenous-led urban service hub that co-designs programs with Mi’kmaq Elders and community members, the Centre delivers Mi’kmaw language classes, cultural workshops, and land-based activities that strengthen identity and belonging. It partners with health, housing, and justice agencies to ensure culturally safe, Indigenous-governed services—such as healing circles and wraparound supports—are delivered to urban Indigenous peoples and allies in Halifax.

resources.name: Glooscap Heritage Centre & Mi’kmaq Museum – Culture and Language Revitalization
resources.organization: Millbrook First Nation (Glooscap Heritage Centre & Mi’kmaq Museum)
resources.description: Operated by Millbrook First Nation, the Centre leads Mi’kmaw cultural revitalization through exhibits, language and craft workshops, Elder-led teachings, and school partnerships. By collaborating with education, tourism, and community partners under Mi’kmaq governance, it co-designs programs that share Mi’kmaw knowledge and ensure Indigenous leadership in cultural education and community-facing services.

resources.name: Wagmatcook Culture & Heritage Centre – Elders-in-Residence and Community Programs
resources.organization: Wagmatcook First Nation (Wagmatcook Culture & Heritage Centre)
resources.description: This Mi’kmaq-led centre hosts Elders-in-residence, language learning, cultural camps, and community events that transmit L’nui’ta’simk (Mi’kmaw ways of knowing) to youth and families. It partners with schools, universities, and service providers to co-design culturally grounded programming and gatherings—supporting healing, intergenerational knowledge transfer, and locally governed service delivery.

resources.name: Unama’ki College – Mi’kmaw Language and Two-Eyed Seeing Initiatives
resources.description: Unama’ki College at Cape Breton University partners with Mi’kmaq communities to co-develop curricula, support Mi’kmaw language revitalization, and embed Elders, Knowledge Keepers, and Two-Eyed Seeing (Etuaptmumk) across programs. These Indigenous-governed partnerships ensure culturally safe services for students and communities, advance language learning, and strengthen community-led research and service delivery.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

solutions.text: Local Inclusive Hiring & Apprenticeship Hub: Establish a community hub that connects employers, unions, training providers, and underrepresented job seekers with inclusive apprenticeship pathways, bias‑aware hiring supports and employer mentorship to improve access to trades and emerging industries.

resources.name: ISANS Employment & Bridging Programs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers employment counselling, job matching, mentorship, and employer engagement to help immigrants and refugees access meaningful work in Nova Scotia. They provide bias-aware recruitment training for employers and connect underrepresented job seekers to apprenticeships, trades training, and emerging sectors through bridging programs in partnership with NSCC, Nova Scotia Works, and industry. This functions as a local hub linking employers, training providers, and diverse job seekers with culturally safe supports.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program creates structured, one-on-one networking between newcomers, recent graduates, and international students (Connectees) and local business leaders (Connectors). By facilitating warm introductions and employer mentorship across sectors, it reduces hiring bias and accelerates inclusive recruitment into emerging industries. The program complements apprenticeship and early-career pathways by linking talent to employers and ecosystem partners who can support training and progression.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 701, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth
resources.description: Building Futures for Youth places high school students in paid summer work with construction employers and unionized worksites, alongside industry-recognized safety and readiness training. The program coordinates employers, schools, and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship system so participants can transition into registered apprenticeships after graduation with employer mentorship. It actively promotes participation from underrepresented youth, strengthening inclusive pathways into the skilled trades.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works – TEAM Work Cooperative
resources.description: TEAM Work delivers Nova Scotia Works employment services with a strong focus on inclusive employment for people with disabilities, newcomers, and 2SLGBTQIA+ job seekers. Services include job development and matching, customized employment, wage subsidies, employer diversity training, and retention coaching that support bias-aware hiring and mentorship. The team brokers connections between job seekers, training providers, and employers in trades and growth sectors, supporting apprenticeship entry where appropriate.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding offers cohort-based, culturally responsive pathways for African Nova Scotian and Mi’kmaw learners to enter metal fabrication and related trades at NSCC, combining academic upgrading, technical training, and wraparound supports. Delivered with Irving Shipbuilding, unions, community partners, and the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, it includes paid work experience and employer mentorship leading to apprenticeship and long-term careers. This model exemplifies an inclusive hiring and apprenticeship hub aligning education, industry, and underrepresented communities in a high-growth sector.

solutions.text: Mentorship and Peer‑Support Networks for Youth: Create mentorship programs pairing young people from marginalized groups with local professionals, entrepreneurs and artists to provide career guidance, internships, work-shadowing and social supports that encourage staying or returning to the region.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program matches immigrant youth and young adults with established Nova Scotia professionals in their field for one‑on‑one guidance, networking, and Canadian workplace exposure. Matches meet regularly to review resumes, practice interviews, and set up informational interviews or job shadowing, often leading to internships or employment. This targeted mentorship helps newcomers overcome systemic barriers and build careers that keep them in the province.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program connects recent graduates, newcomers, and international students with local business and community leaders for brief one‑on‑one meetings that lead to at least three new referrals. These introductions create rapid access to professional networks, informational interviews, and potential work‑shadowing or internships across sectors. By helping underrepresented young talent get connected and feel welcomed, the program supports retention and return to the Halifax region.
resources.address: 1969 Upper Water Street, Suite 2001, Halifax, NS B3J 3R7

resources.name: Newcomer Youth Leadership Development (NYLD)
resources.organization: YMCA of Greater Halifax/Dartmouth – Centre for Immigrant Programs
resources.description: NYLD engages immigrant and refugee youth ages 13–24 in leadership training, peer‑support groups, and mentoring relationships with local professionals and post‑secondary ambassadors. Staff facilitate volunteer placements, workplace tours, and skill‑building that exposes participants to career pathways while offering culturally safe supports. The program helps newcomer youth develop social capital and opportunities that encourage them to stay and thrive in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 216, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Youth Services (Mentorship and Employment Readiness)
resources.description: MNFC’s Youth Services provide culturally grounded mentorship for Mi’kmaq and other Indigenous urban youth through Elder guidance, peer circles, and connections to Indigenous professionals, artists, and employers. Programs blend life‑skills and employment readiness with opportunities for job shadowing, training, and paid placements in community organizations. These supports reduce systemic barriers and build belonging so youth can pursue careers and contribute locally.

resources.name: PLANS (Promoting Leadership in Health for African Nova Scotians)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Faculty of Medicine – Global Health Office
resources.description: PLANS mentors Black youth interested in health and life sciences by connecting them with African Nova Scotian health professionals and university students. Through one‑to‑one mentoring, campus visits, summer programs, and clinical shadowing, PLANS offers targeted career guidance and networks that lead to post‑secondary study, internships, and local employment. The program strengthens representation in health careers and helps youth envision futures in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Accessibility Upgrades and Accessible Transit Initiatives: Mobilize community fundraising and municipal advocacy to improve physical accessibility in public spaces and increase affordable, accessible transit options so people with disabilities can fully participate in work and community life.

resources.name: Accessibility Strategy Implementation
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality is implementing a multi-year Accessibility Strategy that funds barrier-removal projects in public spaces—such as curb ramps, tactile and audible pedestrian signals, accessible beach mats, parks and trail upgrades, and improvements to recreation facilities and libraries. Guided by its Accessibility Advisory Committee and community consultations, HRM uses municipal advocacy and capital investments to make public infrastructure accessible so people with disabilities can fully participate in work and community life.

resources.name: Access-A-Bus
resources.description: Access-A-Bus is Halifax Transit’s door-to-door, shared-ride service for riders who cannot use conventional buses due to disabilities. By providing affordable, pre-booked, wheelchair-accessible transportation that connects people to jobs, education, health care, and community activities, it directly expands accessible transit options and supports full participation in daily life.

resources.name: Transit Bridgewater
resources.description: Transit Bridgewater operates accessible, low-floor buses on fixed routes with affordable fares and passes, improving mobility for residents with disabilities across the Town of Bridgewater. The municipality advances stop and shelter accessibility and collaborates with community partners and riders to expand inclusive service so people can reach work, school, and community services.

resources.name: Kings Transit Authority
resources.description: Kings Transit operates wheelchair-accessible, low-floor buses across Kings and Annapolis counties, linking rural and small-town communities with employment, education, and services. Through inter-municipal coordination and public funding, the system expands affordable, accessible transit options that reduce isolation and support inclusive participation in community life.
resources.address: 29 Crescent Drive, New Minas, NS B4N 3G7

resources.name: Community Wheels (East Hants Community Rider)
resources.description: Community Wheels is a non-profit community transit service providing pre-booked, wheelchair-accessible, door-to-door transportation throughout East Hants. Funded through a mix of fares, community fundraising, and government support, it removes transportation barriers for people with disabilities, enabling access to jobs, health care, and social activities in rural areas.

solutions.text: Newcomer Settlement & Language Access Collective: Form a community collective to coordinate language classes, credential recognition supports, legal navigation, buddy programs and culturally appropriate orientation so newcomers can integrate more quickly and contribute to local economies.

resources.name: ISANS Language Learning, Settlement, and Employment Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS) delivers integrated newcomer supports including LINC and English for Work classes, settlement orientation, and community connections that match newcomers with local volunteers for buddy/mentorship and conversation practice. They also provide employment services with credential recognition advising and bridging supports, plus interpretation/translation and navigation of public services—directly implementing a coordinated, culturally appropriate approach to faster integration and workforce participation.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YMCA YREACH Newcomer Settlement Program
resources.description: YREACH provides settlement navigation and culturally appropriate orientation for newcomers across Nova Scotia, helping with housing, schools, health care, community connections, and referrals to language classes. Staff coordinate with employers and service providers, link clients to credential recognition resources, and run community engagement and buddy-style connections in both urban and rural communities—functioning as a province-wide, collective-style hub for access and inclusion.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 216, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: English Language Learning for Newcomers
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries offers free English conversation groups, volunteer-led tutoring, digital literacy, and newcomer orientation sessions at branches, providing low-barrier language access and community integration. Libraries partner with local settlement agencies to host information clinics and culturally welcoming programs, acting as a neighborhood hub that connects newcomers to services, peers, and local volunteers for informal buddy support.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Halifax Refugee Clinic
resources.description: The Halifax Refugee Clinic provides free legal representation and legal navigation to refugee claimants and persons in need of protection, along with settlement support, referrals to language classes, and coordination of interpretation. By addressing complex legal barriers and linking clients to culturally safe services, the Clinic enables faster, safer integration and helps newcomers contribute to local communities and the economy.
resources.address: 5595 Fenwick Street, Suite 201, Halifax, NS B3H 4M2

solutions.text: 2SLGBTQIA+ Safe Spaces, Health Services and Youth Supports: Fund and host drop‑in centres, sexual health clinics, counselling and peer programs specifically designed for 2SLGBTQIA+ people and youth, co-designed and run with community members to ensure cultural safety and retention.

resources.name: The Youth Project — 2SLGBTQIA+ Youth Programs
resources.description: The Youth Project provides safer-space drop‑ins, peer support groups, one‑to‑one supportive counselling and referrals for 2SLGBTQIA+ youth (generally up to age 25) across Nova Scotia. Programs are co‑designed with queer and trans youth through advisory councils and peer facilitators, creating culturally safe supports that help young people feel welcome, connected, and more likely to stay in the province.

resources.name: prideHealth (2SLGBTQIA+ Health Navigation and Supports)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Health and IWK Health
resources.description: prideHealth is a partnership of Nova Scotia Health and IWK Health that improves access to culturally safe, 2SLGBTQIA+‑affirming health services across the province. The program offers navigation to primary care, sexual health, mental health, and gender‑affirming care, and collaborates with community groups and peer leaders to co‑design safer spaces, provider training, and outreach that reduce barriers to care.

resources.name: Halifax Sexual Health Centre (HSHC)
resources.description: HSHC is a community clinic offering inclusive, low‑barrier sexual and reproductive health care—STI testing and treatment, PrEP/PEP, contraception, pap tests, and gender‑affirming care navigation—delivered in a 2SLGBTQIA+‑affirming environment. Its client‑informed policies, peer‑inclusive education, and culturally safe practices make it a welcoming clinical access point for queer and trans people and youth.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 217, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: South House Sexual and Gender Resource Centre
resources.organization: South House Sexual and Gender Resource Centre
resources.description: South House operates a community‑run safer space with drop‑in hours, peer support, free safer‑sex supplies, referrals, and workshops centered on gender and sexual health for 2SLGBTQIA+ people and allies, including youth. Guided by a community board and peer facilitators, the centre co‑creates programming with local queer and trans communities to ensure culturally safe supports and social connection.

solutions.text: Community-Controlled Affordable Housing and Co‑ops: Support land trusts, housing co‑ops and nonprofit developments led by community members to create stable, culturally appropriate, and affordable housing options for young people and families from marginalized groups.

resources.name: Supportive Housing for Young Mothers (SHYM)
resources.description: SHYM provides safe, affordable apartments with on‑site supports for mothers aged 16–24 and their children. As a community‑led nonprofit development run by YWCA Halifax, it delivers stable, culturally safe housing paired with life‑skills, education, and employment supports, helping young families from marginalized groups build long‑term independence.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

resources.name: AKOMA Affordable Housing and Community Redevelopment
resources.description: AKOMA, an African Nova Scotian‑led nonprofit, is redeveloping the former Nova Scotia Home for Colored Children lands into a mixed‑use community that includes deeply affordable, culturally grounded housing. By stewarding community‑owned land and engaging Black community members in design and governance, AKOMA creates stable homes for African Nova Scotian youth and families and combats displacement.

resources.name: Housing Support Program and Transitional Housing
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre delivers culturally safe housing supports and Indigenous‑led transitional and supportive housing for urban Mi’kmaw and other Indigenous peoples. Through community‑driven services and the Wije’winen initiative that includes new affordable units, the Centre advances community‑controlled, culturally appropriate housing options in Halifax.

resources.name: Homeownership Program (Builds and Repairs)
resources.description: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia partners with community volunteers and qualifying low‑income families to build and rehabilitate affordable homes, sold with affordable, geared‑to‑income mortgages. This nonprofit, community‑driven development model adds stable, attainable housing for young families, newcomers, and others facing systemic barriers, helping them put down roots in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Microgrants and Start‑Up Support for Underrepresented Entrepreneurs: Provide small grants, business mentoring, shared workspaces and procurement supports targeting Black, Indigenous, newcomer, 2SLGBTQIA+ and disabled entrepreneurs to grow local businesses and jobs.

resources.name: Business Development Services for Immigrant Entrepreneurs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides newcomer and refugee entrepreneurs with one‑on‑one business advising, market research support, mentorship matching, and cohort-based training to start and scale ventures. The program connects clients to small financing options through partner microloan funds, helps them navigate government and corporate procurement processes, and links entrepreneurs with local shared workspaces and networks—directly aligning with micro-funding, mentoring, and ecosystem supports for underrepresented founders.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Black Business Financing and Entrepreneur Support
resources.description: BBI offers African Nova Scotian and Black entrepreneurs access to capital (including small loans), business advisory services, training, and mentorship, alongside programs that build capacity to compete for public and private procurement. Through initiatives like accelerators and supplier-readiness workshops, BBI helps founders validate ideas, access early-stage funding, and grow in supportive networks—addressing systemic barriers with culturally relevant supports.
resources.address: 1819 Granville Street, Suite 1150, Halifax, NS B3J 3R1

resources.name: Indigenous Entrepreneur Financing and Advisory
resources.description: Ulnooweg supports Mi’kmaq and other Indigenous entrepreneurs with tailored financing, business advisory, mentorship, and capacity-building, including guidance to access procurement opportunities and partnerships. By combining culturally grounded advisory with flexible capital and ecosystem navigation, the program advances Indigenous-owned start-ups and small businesses across Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Entrepreneurship Training, Micro-Financing and Coworking
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED delivers startup training cohorts, mentorship, and advisory services, and operates a shared workspace with meeting rooms to help founders build networks and reduce overhead. Its micro-financing programs and inclusive programming (including streams for youth, women, and newcomers) provide early capital and skills development that help underrepresented entrepreneurs launch and grow businesses.
resources.address: 6156 Quinpool Road, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3L 1A3

resources.name: Entrepreneurs with Disabilities Program (EDP)
resources.description: EDP offers tailored business coaching, training, and access to small-business financing for entrepreneurs with disabilities, delivered locally through the CBDC network. The program helps clients validate business plans, build financial readiness, and connect to community resources—providing mentoring and early-stage capital that lowers barriers for disabled entrepreneurs.
resources.address: 45 Alderney Drive, Suite 120, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 2N6

solutions.text: Employer Training: Inclusive Recruitment and Retention: Organize peer-led workshops for local employers covering anti‑bias recruitment, accommodations, culturally safe workplaces, flexible scheduling and retention strategies, with community members as co-trainers and auditors.

resources.name: Welcoming Workplaces (Employer Training)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Welcoming Workplaces provides employer training on equitable recruitment, bias‑aware interviewing, onboarding and retention, workplace accommodations, and intercultural communication. Sessions are co-facilitated by trained staff and immigrant community members who share lived experience; ISANS also reviews job postings and HR practices to audit for bias and advises on flexible scheduling and retention supports.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Indigenous Cultural Safety Training
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre delivers employer workshops that build culturally safe, anti-racist workplaces for Mi’kmaq and other Indigenous staff and clients. Training is led with Elders/Knowledge Keepers and urban Indigenous community facilitators, and includes reviews of recruitment language, accommodation practices (e.g., smudging and ceremonial leave), and policies to strengthen inclusive hiring and retention.

resources.name: Disability Confidence Training for Employers
resources.description: reachAbility trains employers to recruit and retain persons with disabilities through anti-bias hiring practices, duty-to-accommodate guidance, accessible job design, and flexible scheduling strategies. Workshops are peer-led by facilitators with disabilities and can include workplace accessibility audits and reviews of recruitment and onboarding materials to reduce barriers and improve retention.
resources.address: 3845 Joseph Howe Drive, Suite 201, Halifax, NS B3L 4H9

resources.name: Safer Spaces Training for Workplaces
resources.description: The Youth Project provides employer training to build 2SLGBTQIA+ inclusive recruitment, policies, and day-to-day practices. Sessions are co-led by queer and trans facilitators with lived experience, include reviews of job ads and onboarding materials for bias, and offer guidance on accommodations (e.g., affirmed names/pronouns, gender-affirming care) and retention strategies that create culturally safe workplaces.

solutions.text: Community Events and Storytelling to Build Social Cohesion: Host regular festivals, story circles, arts showcases and cross-cultural exchanges that celebrate diverse histories and lived experiences, building relationships across communities and improving sense of belonging for youth.

resources.name: Community Connections Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections Program organizes conversation circles, cultural potlucks, peer groups, and mentorship activities that bring newcomers and long-time residents together to share stories and build friendships. These cross-cultural events create welcoming spaces for youth to participate, practice language, and celebrate diverse histories, directly strengthening social cohesion and a sense of belonging.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Community Presents
resources.organization: Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21
resources.description: Community Presents is a public program at the Canadian Museum of Immigration that partners with cultural organizations to host performances, storytelling, film nights, and celebrations highlighting the lived experiences of immigrant, Indigenous, and diverse communities. The museum’s accessible, family-friendly events and youth workshops foster dialogue across cultures and generations, building relationships and belonging.

resources.name: Nova Multifest
resources.description: Nova Multifest is an annual multicultural festival at Alderney Landing featuring live music and dance, cultural showcases, storytelling, and cuisine from communities across Nova Scotia, including newcomer, African Nova Scotian, and Mi’kmaq cultures. The free, family-oriented event creates opportunities for youth to perform, volunteer, and engage in interactive activities that build cross-cultural understanding and a stronger sense of belonging.

resources.name: Community Meals and Events
resources.description: The North Grove hosts weekly community meals, intergenerational kitchen programs, and seasonal celebrations where neighbours cook, share stories, and showcase cultural traditions. These inclusive gatherings welcome youth and families from diverse backgrounds, strengthening relationships across differences and improving social cohesion in Dartmouth North.

resources.name: Community Arts and Storytelling Programming
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op provides an accessible stage for community showcases, spoken word nights, festivals, and cross-cultural collaborations featuring 2SLGBTQIA+, African Nova Scotian, Mi’kmaq, newcomer, and disability arts communities. By offering affordable space and youth-focused events, it enables young people to share their stories, build connections, and feel at home within Halifax’s diverse arts scene.

solutions.text: Local Anti-Discrimination Reporting and Rapid Response Protocol: Create accessible, community-managed reporting channels and a rapid response team (legal advice, advocacy, mediation) to address incidents of racism, discrimination or harassment and ensure survivors get culturally safe support.

resources.name: Discrimination Complaint Process and Dispute Resolution
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Human Rights Commission provides accessible channels to report racism, discrimination, and harassment through online, phone, and in‑person intake. Human rights officers offer early intervention, legal information, and restorative/mediation services to resolve incidents quickly, and they can advance cases to formal investigation and Board of Inquiry when needed. The Commission also engages African Nova Scotian, Mi’kmaq, and other communities to ensure culturally safe supports and navigation throughout the complaint process.
resources.address: 5657 Spring Garden Road, 3rd Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 3R4

resources.name: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service (Community Legal Clinic)
resources.organization: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service (Schulich School of Law, Dalhousie University)
resources.description: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service offers rapid-response legal information, advice, and representation to low‑income and marginalized clients facing discrimination in housing, employment, and services. The clinic assists with documenting incidents, drafting Nova Scotia Human Rights Commission complaints, negotiating with employers/landlords, and representing clients in mediation and hearings. Working closely with community partners and equity‑seeking groups, DLAS provides culturally safe advocacy and accompaniment to help survivors navigate reporting and obtain remedies.

resources.name: Settlement Services (Case Management & Navigation)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Settlement Services provide a confidential, community‑managed channel for newcomers to report experiences of racism, discrimination, or harassment to a trusted case manager. Staff offer rapid support by documenting incidents, safety planning, and making warm referrals for legal advice and mediation (e.g., Nova Scotia Human Rights Commission, legal clinics), as well as advocating with employers, schools, and landlords. Services are culturally safe and often multilingual, ensuring equitable access to supports and timely response.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Data, Accountability and Community Dashboard: Collect disaggregated local data (voluntary and community governed) on employment, education, housing and service access; publish a regular public dashboard and community scorecard to track progress and hold institutions accountable.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Workforce Diversity Census Dashboard
resources.description: HRM conducts a voluntary, self-identification workforce census and publishes an interactive public dashboard showing representation and pay equity for designated groups (e.g., women, African Nova Scotians, Mi’kmaq/Indigenous people, newcomers, persons with disabilities, and 2SLGBTQIA+ employees). The dashboard disaggregates local employment data and tracks progress against equity objectives, creating a community-facing scorecard that holds the municipality accountable for inclusive hiring, retention, and advancement.

resources.name: Homelessness in the Halifax Region Data Dashboard
resources.description: HRM publishes regularly updated statistics on homelessness, including by-name list trends, shelter occupancy, and housing placements, using local, community-collected data through coordinated access and HIFIS. By making these metrics public, the dashboard functions as a community scorecard that drives transparency and accountability across municipal, provincial, and community partners working to improve equitable access to housing and services.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Quality of Life Data Portal
resources.description: Engage Nova Scotia’s Quality of Life Initiative provides an interactive portal with county- and community-level results from one of Canada’s largest well-being surveys, disaggregated by demographics such as age, income, gender, ethnicity, disability, and newcomer status. The public dashboard and community scorecards help local leaders, service providers, and residents track progress on education, employment, housing, and access to services, and to hold institutions accountable for closing gaps affecting equity-deserving groups.
resources.address: 1526 Dresden Row, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3J 3K3

resources.name: Halifax Index
resources.description: The Halifax Index is an annual, publicly accessible dashboard that compiles local, disaggregated indicators on population, labour, education, housing, affordability, and inclusive growth. It provides a clear, data-driven scorecard that tracks progress over time and highlights equity gaps, enabling community stakeholders and institutions to be held accountable for inclusive economic outcomes across Halifax and the broader region.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Energize Bridgewater Community Energy & Poverty Dashboard
resources.description: Energize Bridgewater publishes a community-facing dashboard that tracks local energy poverty indicators, home retrofits, and access to energy-efficiency programs, with a focus on low-income and vulnerable households. By sharing disaggregated, place-based metrics and progress updates, the dashboard serves as a community scorecard that guides equitable housing and service interventions and holds municipal and utility partners accountable for reducing barriers to affordable, efficient housing.

obstacles.title: Retention of Students, Graduates, and Newcomers
obstacles.description: Insufficient job matching, spousal employment, community integration, and timely credential recognition undermine retention after graduation or arrival. Social networks and belonging are as critical as job offers.

solutions.text: Community Job & Skills Portal: A locally managed online board (run by municipalities, chambers and colleges) that matches students, graduates and newcomers with entry-level, part-time, remote and project-based roles, plus skills-tagging so employers can find candidates with transferable experience.

resources.name: Work in Halifax Job Board
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership’s Work in Halifax job board is a municipally managed portal that aggregates local employment opportunities across sectors, including entry-level, part-time, remote, and co-op/project roles. Job seekers can highlight their skills and experience to improve matching, and employers use keyword and skill-based filters to discover candidates with transferable capabilities; the portal links to newcomer and graduate-retention programming to support community belonging alongside job placement.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Work Here Cape Breton Job Portal
resources.description: Operated by the Cape Breton Partnership, Work Here Cape Breton lists jobs from employers across the island and invites students, recent graduates, and newcomers to connect with opportunities. The portal features entry-level, seasonal/part-time, remote, and project-based roles and uses searchable tags and filters so employers can find candidates with relevant and transferable skills, while also linking talent to settlement and community resources.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

resources.name: ISANS SkillsMatch
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS SkillsMatch is an online matching platform that connects immigrant job seekers with Nova Scotia employers based on detailed skills, credentials, and work experience. Employers can search candidate profiles and post roles, including entry-level and part-time/contract opportunities, while newcomers receive support with credential recognition and community integration—addressing both job matching and retention.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: myCareer (Dalhousie University)
resources.organization: Dalhousie University – Bissett Student Success Centre (Career & Leadership Development)
resources.description: myCareer is Dalhousie University’s online portal where students and recent graduates find co-ops, internships, part-time campus/community jobs, remote projects, and entry-level roles in Nova Scotia. Employers search talent by program, competencies, and skill tags to identify candidates with transferable experience, while the platform integrates events and networking that deepen students’ ties to the local community.

resources.name: Halifax Chamber of Commerce Job Board
resources.description: The Chamber’s member-driven job board is a community hub where local employers post opportunities across sectors, including junior, part-time, contract, and project-based roles suitable for students, new graduates, and newcomers. Listings are organized by industry and function with keyword and skill-based filters, helping employers surface candidates with transferable capabilities while connecting talent to the Chamber’s broader networking and mentorship ecosystem.
resources.address: 32 Akerley Boulevard, Suite 100, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1N1

solutions.text: Spousal & Partner Employment Network: A volunteer-supported program connecting partners of newcomers with targeted job leads, resume clinics, certification navigation, and employer introductions to reduce spousal underemployment.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program links job-ready newcomers, international students, and spouses/partners with volunteer ‘Connectors’ who open their professional networks, leading to targeted job leads, informational interviews, and employer introductions. Participants also receive one-on-one job search coaching (including resume and interview guidance) and referrals to credential recognition resources, directly addressing spousal underemployment and improving family retention in Halifax.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program matches internationally trained newcomers—including spouses and partners of principal applicants—with volunteer industry mentors who provide targeted job leads, resume feedback, and strategic networking support. The program integrates employer introductions with employment counselling and guidance on credential recognition and licensing pathways, helping partners transition into meaningful work faster and strengthening family settlement in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Dual Career Support Program
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Dual Career Support Program assists spouses and partners of recruited faculty and senior staff with customized job search services, including resume review, labour market navigation, and employer introductions through Dal’s local networks. Staff provide warm referrals to community employment agencies and credential recognition resources, helping accompanying partners secure work and supporting long-term family retention in Halifax.

solutions.text: Local Credential Navigation Hub: A community hub (physical and virtual) staffed by volunteers, retired professionals and settlement workers that helps newcomers and graduates understand credential recognition paths, bridging courses and fast-track micro-credentials.

resources.name: Employment and Bridging Services (Career Pathways for Newcomers)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides one-on-one advising to help internationally trained newcomers understand licensing and credential recognition pathways in Nova Scotia, including assessments, exams, and regulatory requirements for regulated professions. Staff connect clients to bridging programs, English for specific professions, and fast-track micro-credentials in partnership with post-secondary institutions, and leverage volunteer and retired-professional mentors to guide networking and sector-specific steps.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YMCA Centre for Immigrant Programs (Settlement & Employment Services)
resources.description: The YMCA’s immigrant services team offers a community hub where settlement workers provide personalized credential navigation, helping newcomers map foreign education and experience to Nova Scotia’s licensing and employment requirements. They host information sessions, refer to bridging courses and micro-credentials, and pair clients with volunteer mentors and local professionals to build networks and accelerate labour market entry.

resources.name: Newcomer Services at Halifax Central Library
resources.description: Halifax Central Library serves as a welcoming, walk-in hub where newcomers can meet on-site settlement staff and community partners for credential recognition guidance, referrals to bridging programs, and help accessing professional licensing information. The library’s volunteer-led conversation circles, mentorship events, and employment workshops build social networks while connecting participants to micro-credential and upskilling opportunities across the region.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) and MicroCredentials
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – IT Campus
resources.description: NSCC’s RPL advisors help newcomers and recent graduates translate prior education and work experience into academic credit, creating individualized pathways that shorten time to Canadian credentials. The college also offers stackable micro-credentials and targeted bridging/upskilling options aligned to Nova Scotia’s labour market, functioning as a practical navigation point for fast-track recognition and re-entry into the workforce.

solutions.text: Employer Partnership & Pledge Program: A campaign inviting local employers to pledge inclusive hiring practices, create apprenticeship and entry-level placements for grads/newcomers, and participate in job fairs focused on retention.

resources.name: Employer Support Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Employer Support Services helps Nova Scotia employers adopt inclusive hiring and retention practices for immigrants and international graduates through training, policy advice, and one-on-one coaching. The team partners with employers to develop entry-level placements, mentorships, and work-integrated learning, and regularly hosts sector-specific recruitment events and job fairs that connect inclusive employers with newcomer talent—directly supporting long-term retention.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: The Connector Program links recent graduates and newcomers with local employers and business leaders who commit to meet, share industry insights, and make three referrals—an employer partnership model that accelerates job matching and social integration. Halifax Partnership also convenes networking events and hiring-focused activities with participating employers, encouraging inclusive recruitment and strengthening retention by building professional networks and pathways into entry-level roles.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1101, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Management Career Services – Co-op and Employer Engagement
resources.description: Dalhousie’s Management Career Services partners with employers to create co-op, internship, and new‑graduate opportunities, and it provides tailored recruitment supports that emphasize equitable, inclusive hiring. The unit hosts large career fairs and industry days, connecting employers with diverse students and recent graduates and helping employers design early‑career pathways that improve retention in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: Rowe Management Building, 6100 University Avenue, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: Study and Stay Nova Scotia
