resources.description: Study and Stay Nova Scotia engages employers to support international students with mentorship, work‑integrated learning, and entry‑level job opportunities, fostering inclusive hiring practices for a diverse talent pipeline. The program convenes employer networking events and hiring fairs, builds employer–student connections, and provides retention supports so graduates can build careers and community ties in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1888 Brunswick Street, Suite 710, Halifax, NS B3J 3J8

solutions.text: Mentorship & Alumni Match Program: A program pairing students, new grads and newcomers with local alumni and experienced professionals for career guidance, networking, mock interviews and introductions to community networks.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Halifax Partnership’s Connector Program matches new graduates, international students, and newcomers with established local professionals (“Connectors”) for one-on-one meetings that lead to warm introductions across the Connector’s network. Participants receive networking guidance, informational interviews, and referrals that help them access the hidden job market, build social capital, and integrate into the community—directly addressing retention by strengthening belonging and professional ties.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS pairs internationally trained professionals and other newcomers with experienced mentors in their occupational field for structured mentorship focused on Canadian workplace culture, credential pathways, and local labour market navigation. Mentors provide networking introductions, informational interviews, resume and mock-interview support, and connections to community and professional associations—helping newcomers build the relationships and confidence that support long-term retention in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Dal Alumni Link
resources.organization: Dalhousie University, Office of Advancement (Alumni & Friends)
resources.description: Dal Alumni Link connects Dalhousie students and recent graduates with alumni and industry professionals for mentorship, career conversations, and targeted networking. Through guided matches and resources, participants gain advice on job search strategies, mock interviews, and introductions to sector and community networks—strengthening the social supports that keep emerging talent in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: X Connects (Alumni-Student Mentoring)
resources.organization: St. Francis Xavier University (StFX) Alumni Affairs
resources.description: StFX’s X Connects program links current students and new graduates with StFX alumni for mentoring conversations, career exploration, and professional networking. Alumni mentors offer informational interviews, resume and interview feedback, and introductions to their local and sector networks—building the community ties and social belonging that encourage graduates to launch and grow their careers in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Community Welcome Hubs and One-Stop Events: Regular in-person 'welcome' events and permanent kiosks at libraries or community centres offering information on jobs, housing, health, schools and volunteer opportunities to accelerate belonging.

resources.name: Community Navigator — Halifax Central Library
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries’ Community Navigator service provides a one-stop, in-person welcome hub at Halifax Central Library. Staff host regular drop-in hours and lobby information kiosks that connect newcomers, students, and graduates to employment supports, housing and health information, school registration, and local volunteer opportunities—helping people quickly build networks and a sense of belonging.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Community Navigator — Keshen Goodman Public Library
resources.description: At this busy suburban branch, Community Navigators run ongoing, in-person welcome drop-ins and information tables serving newcomers and young families. The permanent point-of-service inside the library functions as a local hub for guidance on jobs, housing, health care, schools and childcare, and community/volunteer connections.

resources.name: Settlement & Community Connections — Welcome Sessions and Info Hub
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS operates in-person Welcome Sessions and a walk-in settlement hub that provide newcomers and international students with coordinated information on employment, housing, health services, schooling, and volunteer/community connections. Staff regularly host one-stop welcome events and outreach kiosks at partner libraries and community centres, accelerating integration and retention through social networks and tailored referrals.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1H8

solutions.text: Interest-Based Social Circles: Community-run clubs and Meetup-style groups (sports, arts, tech, parenting) designed to build social networks quickly for students, newcomers and young families across cultural lines.

resources.name: Newcomer Services & Programs
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries runs free interest-based clubs and meetup-style activities—such as English Conversation Groups, board game nights, maker and arts workshops, storytimes, and cultural events—across its branches. These programs create low-barrier social circles where students, newcomers, and young families can quickly meet peers and build friendships across cultures, strengthening belonging alongside job and school life.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Community Connections
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections program organizes volunteer-led social and interest groups—such as conversation circles, women’s and men’s groups, youth activities, family events, and community host matches—to help newcomers form friendships and networks quickly. By convening casual, shared-interest gatherings beyond the workplace, it builds cross-cultural belonging that supports long-term retention for students, graduates, and newcomer families.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Community Events & Meetups
resources.description: Volta hosts frequent tech-community meetups, socials, talks, and student-focused events (e.g., founder meetups, Women in Tech gatherings, lunch-and-learns) that welcome students, newcomers, and professionals. These interest-based circles help people plug into Halifax’s innovation community quickly, building cross-cultural networks that make the region stickier for emerging talent.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Unit 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Dalhousie International Centre Programs
resources.description: The Dalhousie International Centre runs social and cultural programming—such as peer mentorship, conversation circles, intercultural events, and support for student clubs—that connect international and domestic students through shared interests. By offering welcoming, meetup-style spaces to form friendships and participate in campus life, it strengthens belonging and improves post-graduation retention.

solutions.text: Micro-Internship & Project Bank: A repository of short paid projects from local businesses and non-profits that give newcomers and recent graduates locally relevant experience, references and employer contacts.

resources.name: DeepSense Student Internships & Industry Projects
resources.description: DeepSense brokers short, paid, data and AI projects between ocean-sector companies and student talent from Nova Scotia universities and colleges. Employers submit defined project briefs, and DeepSense recruits and pays students to deliver them over a few weeks to a few months, giving newcomers and recent graduates local experience, references, and direct employer contacts.
resources.address: Steele Ocean Sciences Building, 1355 Oxford Street, Halifax, NS B3H 4R2

resources.name: NSCC Applied Research & Innovation — Student Industry Projects
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) — Applied Research & Innovation
resources.description: NSCC’s Applied Research & Innovation team coordinates a roster of short, industry-defined projects with Nova Scotia SMEs and community organizations and hires student research assistants to execute the work. These paid, scoped projects function as a project bank that provides newcomers and recent graduates with locally relevant experience, industry references, and relationships with potential employers across the province.

resources.name: Blue Futures Pathways Micro-Internships
resources.organization: SOI Foundation (Students on Ice) — Blue Futures Pathways
resources.description: Blue Futures Pathways offers 60–80 hour paid micro-internships with ocean-sector employers across Canada, including Nova Scotia, where many projects are hosted by local SMEs and non-profits. Through an online portal of employer-submitted project briefs, students and newcomers complete short, outcome-based work that builds Nova Scotia–relevant experience, earns references, and expands professional networks in the regional ocean economy.
resources.address: 1740 Chemin de la Montagne, Chelsea, QC J9B 2E1

resources.name: COVE Internship & Student Project Opportunities
resources.description: COVE connects ocean technology companies in Nova Scotia with students through paid internships and short, employer-scoped projects hosted at the COVE campus and with partner firms. Their opportunities serve as a pipeline of discrete, time-bound projects that provide newcomers and recent graduates with local industry experience, mentorship, references, and direct contact with hiring managers in the regional blue economy.

solutions.text: Volunteer-to-Employment Pathways: Structured volunteer placements with clear skills mapping and employer collaboration that convert high-performing volunteers into paid positions when possible.

resources.name: Community Connections Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Community Connections places newcomers and recent graduates in volunteer roles and mentorships that match their education and career goals, alongside workshops on Canadian workplace culture. Staff map participants’ skills to host-organization needs and liaise with employers, creating structured, resume-building placements; many hosts subsequently hire high-performing volunteers into entry-level or contract roles when positions open.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Youth Leadership Program (YLP)
resources.description: HRM Recreation’s YLP is a structured volunteer program where teens and young adults support municipal day camps and community programs while completing training in leadership, safety, and child programming. Skills are documented and evaluated by supervisors, and high-performing volunteers are routinely considered first for paid seasonal roles (e.g., Recreation Leaders and Camp Staff), creating a clear volunteer-to-employment pipeline.

resources.name: Volunteer Program
resources.organization: Canadian Museum of Immigration at Pier 21
resources.description: Pier 21 engages volunteers in defined roles such as visitor services, interpretation, archives, and events, with formal orientation and role-specific training. Volunteer coordinators match applicants’ skills and languages to departmental needs and flag strong performers for seasonal and casual paid positions in visitor experience and programming, turning volunteering into employment when opportunities arise.

resources.name: SPCA Volunteer Program
resources.description: The Nova Scotia SPCA offers structured volunteer placements in animal care, thrift stores, administration, and events, with training that maps directly to operational competencies. Shelter managers and HR collaborate to recruit from the volunteer pool for paid Animal Care Attendant, thrift retail, and administrative roles, enabling high-performing volunteers to transition into employment as openings occur.

resources.name: Volunteer Program
resources.description: EAC matches volunteers to skills-based roles in outreach, research, events, and communications, providing training and documented experience applicable to environmental non-profit careers. Staff regularly recruit paid project and coordination roles from active volunteers who have demonstrated competencies and mission alignment, creating a practical pathway from volunteering to employment.

solutions.text: Community Childcare & Transit Solutions: Locally organized childcare co-ops, employer-subsidized spots and ride-share networks that remove practical barriers to employment for young families and partners.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides on-site, licensed childminding so parents can attend language training, job search workshops, and settlement appointments without childcare barriers. The organization also helps eligible clients with transportation support (e.g., bus passes for program participation), enabling both partners in a family to engage in employment and integration activities, which strengthens post-arrival retention.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Dalhousie Rideshare (RideShark)
resources.description: Dalhousie’s rideshare platform matches students, staff, and their partners for carpools, reducing commuting time and cost while expanding access to job sites, classes, and childcare across HRM. By coordinating shared rides and offering commuter tools through the Office of Sustainability, the program removes transportation barriers that often deter young families from staying in the region.

resources.name: Child Development Centre (On‑Campus Early Learning)
resources.description: MSVU’s licensed Child Development Centre offers full- and part‑time care for infants and young children with schedules aligned to the academic calendar, supporting students, staff, and faculty to study and work. As an employer‑aligned, university‑based centre, it directly reduces childcare barriers for young families and dual‑career couples, helping them remain in Nova Scotia during education and early career stages.

resources.name: Affordable Access Program – Transit Pass
resources.description: HRM’s Affordable Access Program provides a 50% discounted Halifax Transit monthly pass for eligible low‑income residents, including newcomers and families. By lowering the ongoing cost of getting to work, training, and childcare across the bus and ferry network, it removes a key practical barrier to employment and supports retention of students, graduates, and new arrivals.

solutions.text: Affordable Housing & Roommate Match Service: A community-run housing portal and roommate-matching service for students, grads and newcomers, plus landlord outreach to increase short-term rental availability and fair tenancy info.

resources.name: Housing Support for Newcomers
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides one-on-one housing navigation for immigrants and international students, helping them find affordable rentals or shared accommodations and understand local rental markets. Staff deliver tenant rights education and liaise with landlords and property managers to expand listings for newcomers, aligning with the solution’s roommate/room-rental matching and landlord outreach components.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Off-Campus Housing and Roommate Finder
resources.description: MSVU connects students and recent grads to a community housing portal powered by Places4Students that includes verified rental listings and a roommate-matching feature for shared accommodations. The university also shares guidance on tenant rights, budgeting, and safe renting, while encouraging local landlords to list student-friendly rentals—supporting both the matching service and landlord outreach elements of the solution.

resources.name: SMU Off-Campus Housing
resources.description: Saint Mary’s University offers an off-campus housing portal integrated with Places4Students, where students and grads can search affordable rentals and use roommate-matching tools to form shared households. SMU provides renting tips, safety information, and links to tenant-rights resources, and it invites landlords to advertise student-ready short- and long-term options—directly supporting the solution’s portal, matching, and landlord engagement goals.

resources.name: CBU Homestay Program
resources.description: CBU’s Homestay Program matches domestic and international students with vetted local host families for furnished rooms and inclusive pricing—an immediate, community-based alternative to traditional rentals and a form of roommate-style living. The program works closely with hosts (landlords) to expand safe, short- and long-term housing supply and provides orientation on household expectations and tenant/host responsibilities, advancing both matching and landlord outreach.
resources.address: 1250 Grand Lake Road, Sydney, NS B1P 6L2

resources.name: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service – Residential Tenancies Support
resources.description: Dalhousie Legal Aid Service provides free legal information and representation to tenants, including students and newcomers, on residential tenancies issues such as leases, repairs, security deposits, and evictions. The clinic conducts community outreach and workshops that help renters and landlords understand fair-tenancy obligations, complementing housing portals and roommate matching by ensuring participants have clear, accessible rights education.

solutions.text: Newcomer Entrepreneurship Support: Peer-led incubators and micro-grant programs that support immigrant and youth entrepreneurs with mentorship, business clinics, coworking space and connections to local suppliers and markets.

resources.name: ISANS Business & Entrepreneurship Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides immigrant entrepreneurs with one-on-one business counselling, cohort-based training, and specialized business clinics covering planning, finance, and market entry. The program pairs newcomers with mentors, offers peer learning groups, and hosts networking and market pop-up events that connect clients to local suppliers and customers; staff also help participants access micro-financing and small grants through partner programs, supporting retention and community integration.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: CEED Microloan Program & The CEED Hub
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED offers an incubator-style pathway that combines cohort-based training, mentorship, and business advisory clinics with access to microloans for early-stage founders, including youth and newcomers. The CEED Hub provides coworking, peer networks, and regular workshops that help entrepreneurs refine their models and build supplier and customer connections across Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: IGNITE Startup Incubator (Yarmouth)
resources.description: IGNITE supports youth and newcomer founders through peer-led cohorts, mentorship from industry experts, and hands-on business clinics in its rural innovation hub. The incubator provides coworking and prototyping space, facilitates introductions to regional suppliers and markets (e.g., ocean, fisheries, and municipal networks), and connects startups to non-dilutive funding opportunities like pitch competitions and grants, helping them launch and grow in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Employer Cultural Competency & Inclusion Training: Local workshops for employers and HR teams, delivered by community groups and settlement agencies, on inclusive hiring, onboarding and retention practices to improve workplace belonging.

resources.name: Employer Support & Workplace Culture Training
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers onsite and virtual training for employers and HR teams on inclusive hiring, intercultural communication, bias-aware interviewing, and onboarding/retention practices for internationally trained talent. Workshops are tailored to sector needs and include practical tools, policy guidance, and coaching to help workplaces build belonging and retain students, graduates, and newcomers.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YREACH Cultural Diversity & Newcomer Inclusion Workshops
resources.description: YREACH (YMCA’s settlement program) provides employers across Nova Scotia with interactive sessions on cultural competency, inclusive recruitment, cross-cultural communication, and practical onboarding supports for newcomers and their families. Delivered locally by settlement staff, the workshops connect businesses to newcomer services and community resources that improve retention and workplace belonging.

resources.name: Cultural Awareness Training for Workplaces
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre offers employer training that builds cultural awareness, reconciliation-informed practices, and safer, more inclusive workplaces for Indigenous and diverse employees. Sessions help HR teams and managers examine policies, reduce bias, and adopt inclusive onboarding and retention approaches that foster a strong sense of belonging.

obstacles.title: Brain Drain to Larger Markets and Remote Employers
obstacles.description: Young talent is pulled by higher salaries, bigger ecosystems, and prestigious brands in larger cities or abroad. Remote-first work can weaken local attachment and reduce community engagement.

solutions.text: Local Mentorship & Alumni Networks: Create community-run mentorship programs that connect young people with local alumni, tradespeople, entrepreneurs and professionals for career advice, internships, and long-term relationships that strengthen personal ties to the region.

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS matches internationally trained and early-career newcomers (including recent graduates and young professionals) with established local professionals for one-on-one mentoring, sector-specific advice, and networking. Mentors offer guidance on credentials, workplace culture, and job search, helping mentees secure informational interviews and opportunities with Nova Scotian employers. By cultivating long-term mentor-mentee relationships, the program strengthens newcomers’ ties to the local community and encourages them to build their careers in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Venture Mentoring Service (VMS)
resources.organization: Norman Newman Centre for Entrepreneurship, Dalhousie University
resources.description: Dalhousie’s VMS connects student, recent graduate, and alumni founders with a team of seasoned local entrepreneurs and professionals for structured, ongoing mentoring. The team-based model provides practical business advice, warm introductions, and accountability, helping young founders access internships, co-op talent, and local supply chains. By embedding founders in networks of Nova Scotian alumni and business leaders, VMS builds durable relationships that keep ventures and talent rooted in the province.

resources.name: Mentoring Program
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business (Mount Saint Vincent University)
resources.description: The Centre for Women in Business pairs women entrepreneurs, students, and early-stage founders with experienced business owners and professionals across Nova Scotia for one-on-one mentoring and peer circles. Participants receive targeted guidance on launching and growing ventures, access to local supplier and customer networks, and introductions to advisors and funders. These mentor relationships and alumni networks strengthen participants’ personal and professional ties to the province and encourage long-term commitment to building careers here.

resources.name: Mentorship and Entrepreneur-in-Residence Program
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic operates rural innovation hubs that connect youth, students, and founders with local mentors, Entrepreneurs-in-Residence, and industry partners in Nova Scotia. Through office hours, workshops, and project-based collaborations, participants receive practical advice, introductions to employers, and pathways to placements with local companies. The program builds long-term relationships between emerging talent and community-based entrepreneurs, anchoring careers and startups in the region.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

resources.name: Advisory Services and Mentorship
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides entrepreneurship training coupled with ongoing mentorship from local entrepreneurs, business advisors, and an active alumni network. Participants receive individualized coaching, connections to industry professionals, and opportunities to engage with local employers and peer founders. By fostering enduring mentor relationships and community ties, CEED helps young entrepreneurs build sustainable careers and companies in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Community Co-working Hubs: Establish affordable, well-equipped co-working spaces in towns and neighbourhoods that provide reliable broadband, meeting rooms and social programming so remote workers and local startups can collaborate and feel anchored locally.

resources.name: Volta Co-Working & Innovation Hub
resources.description: Volta operates a large, affordable co-working and startup hub in downtown Halifax with high-speed broadband, meeting rooms, event space, and dedicated offices. Through community programming, meetups, and mentorship, it helps remote tech workers and local startups collaborate, stay connected to peers, and feel rooted in Nova Scotia’s innovation ecosystem.

resources.name: CEEDspace Co-working
resources.description: CEEDspace provides co-working desks, dedicated offices, reliable broadband, and bookable meeting rooms alongside entrepreneurship workshops and peer programming. Run by the Centre for Entrepreneurship Education & Development (CEED), it creates a supportive community where remote workers and founders can collaborate and build their ventures locally in Halifax.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – Yarmouth Hub
resources.description: IGNITE’s Yarmouth hub offers affordable co-working desks, private offices, high-speed internet, meeting rooms, and a steady calendar of workshops and community events. By connecting remote professionals, students, and startups with mentors and partners, it anchors talent in Southwestern Nova Scotia and fosters local collaboration and entrepreneurship.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic – New Glasgow Hub
resources.description: IGNITE’s New Glasgow hub provides co-working space with reliable broadband, meeting rooms, and programming that supports early-stage companies and remote workers across Northern Nova Scotia. Regular events, mentorship, and community-building activities help professionals collaborate locally and reduce the pull to larger markets.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

resources.name: Navigate Startup House
resources.description: Navigate Startup House in Sydney offers co-working desks, offices, high-speed internet, and bookable boardrooms, paired with programming, mentorship, and networking delivered with local partners. The space gives remote workers and founders a home base to collaborate and engage with the Cape Breton startup community, strengthening local attachment.

solutions.text: Local Employer Hiring Coalitions: Form voluntary consortia of small and medium local employers that share job postings, offer rotational hires or apprenticeship pipelines, and coordinate outreach to retain young talent within the region.

resources.name: Halifax Connector Program
resources.description: The Halifax Connector Program convenes a network of local employers and industry professionals who collectively identify talent needs, share opportunities, and open doors for recent graduates and young professionals. Through structured networking, employer-led events, and the Work in Halifax job aggregation, SMEs coordinate outreach and promote local roles to retain youth in the region.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1101, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Cape Breton Connector Program
resources.description: The Cape Breton Connector Program brings together a coalition of Cape Breton employers to share job leads, co-host recruitment events, and mentor emerging talent. By coordinating outreach and centralizing postings through the Partnership’s channels (including a regional job board and hiring fairs), it helps SMEs create pathways that keep students and young professionals in Cape Breton.

resources.name: COVE Workforce Initiative
resources.description: COVE’s Workforce Initiative unites ocean-technology SMEs to jointly source talent, share job postings, and develop co-op and internship pipelines with local post-secondary partners. The initiative coordinates multi-employer outreach (e.g., Ocean Connector events and career activities) that exposes young people to multiple firms, building rotational and early-career pathways that anchor talent in Nova Scotia’s ocean sector.

resources.name: CANS Construction Job Board
resources.description: CANS operates a centralized job board and employer network where hundreds of small and medium construction firms in Nova Scotia post openings and coordinate recruitment. Through its workforce development and industry education activities, CANS helps members build apprenticeship and early-career pathways and conducts joint outreach that encourages young tradespeople to build careers locally.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

resources.name: Employer Support Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Employer Support Services convene a multi-employer network that shares job postings, co-hosts hiring fairs, and creates work placements for internationally educated and domestic graduates starting their careers in Nova Scotia. By coordinating recruitment and providing tailored supports to SMEs, the program builds inclusive, multi-employer pipelines that help retain young talent across sectors.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

solutions.text: Apprenticeship & Trade Pathway Campaigns: Run community campaigns and school partnerships that promote skilled trades and dual career pathways, pair students with local apprenticeships, and showcase living-wage outcomes of staying in the region.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency – Youth Apprenticeship Pathways
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency partners with school boards, guidance teams, and employers to help high school students start apprenticeship careers while they complete their education. Through outreach events, in-school presentations, and employer matching, students are connected to local, paid apprenticeship opportunities and can begin logging hours toward certification. The Agency also promotes the strong earning potential and long-term career stability of staying in Nova Scotia’s skilled trades, reinforcing local attachment.
resources.address: 2021 Brunswick Street, 10th Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 2S9

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY is a province-wide partnership that places high school students in paid summer work experiences with Nova Scotia construction employers and introduces them to apprenticeship pathways. Working with schools, the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, and industry partners, BFY provides safety training, mentorship, and connections that can lead to registered apprenticeships after graduation. The program highlights real local wage outcomes and career progression in the skilled trades to encourage youth to build their futures in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 10 Ragged Lake Boulevard, Unit 1, Halifax, NS B3S 1A1

resources.name: Women Unlimited Program
resources.organization: Women Unlimited Association (in partnership with Nova Scotia Community College)
resources.description: Women Unlimited recruits and supports women and gender-diverse people to explore and pursue careers in the skilled trades and technology, working closely with NSCC campuses and local employers across Nova Scotia. The program runs community outreach and school-linked cohorts, provides a 14-week career discovery experience, and connects participants to NSCC training seats and apprenticeship sponsors in fields like welding, metal fabrication, and industrial trades. It emphasizes the living-wage, in-demand opportunities available locally, helping participants launch sustainable careers and apprenticeships in the province.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding Inc.
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a collaborative NSCC–industry initiative that recruits Nova Scotians into trades programs aligned with shipbuilding (e.g., metal fabrication, welding), provides wrap-around supports, and connects graduates to apprenticeships and employment at the Halifax Shipyard. Delivered with partners like Irving Shipbuilding and community organizations, cohorts often focus on underrepresented groups and include mentorship, work terms, and direct links to Red Seal apprenticeship pathways. The program showcases clear, local, living-wage career trajectories in Nova Scotia’s marine industrial sector to encourage participants to train, work, and stay in the province.

solutions.text: Micro-grants & Returner Incentives: Offer small community-funded grants, relocation stipends or rent subsidies for young entrepreneurs and graduates who move back to start businesses, join local employers, or launch community projects.

resources.name: Graduate to Opportunity (GTO)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration
resources.description: Graduate to Opportunity provides a two-year salary subsidy to Nova Scotia employers that hire recent post-secondary graduates, including those returning to the province. By covering a portion of wages (higher in year one, then tapering in year two), the program reduces hiring risk and helps graduates land career-track roles with local employers, directly incentivizing young people to stay or come back and build their lives in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: More Opportunity for Skilled Trades (MOST) Tax Rebate
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Department of Finance and Treasury Board
resources.description: MOST refunds provincial income tax for eligible workers under 30 in designated skilled trades and healthcare occupations, up to a lifetime maximum, making it financially attractive to live and work in Nova Scotia. This targeted rebate functions as a returner incentive by helping offset the wage gap versus larger markets and encouraging young talent who trained or worked away to relocate or remain and join local employers.

resources.name: Invest Nova Scotia Sprint
resources.description: Sprint provides non-dilutive funding (micro-grants) and advisory support to early-stage Nova Scotia startups to validate markets and build prototypes. By offering quick, flexible capital to founders—including returning graduates and young entrepreneurs—it lowers startup costs and encourages people to establish and grow companies in their home communities.
resources.address: 1801 Hollis Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3N4

resources.name: Spark Nova Scotia
resources.description: Spark Nova Scotia is a province-wide, early-stage startup competition awarding non-dilutive cash prizes to founders in regional streams (e.g., Northern, Southwestern, and Cape Breton). These micro-grants help new and returning entrepreneurs cover startup costs and test ideas locally, encouraging them to launch ventures and put down roots in Nova Scotia’s communities.
resources.address: 1801 Hollis Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3N4

resources.name: Volta Community Grants
resources.description: Volta’s Community Grants provide micro-grants to organizations and leaders hosting events, meetups, and initiatives that grow the startup and innovation ecosystem in Nova Scotia. By funding grassroots, community-led projects that connect founders, returning graduates, and employers, the program strengthens local networks and attachment, making it more compelling for young people to stay or return.
resources.address: 1800 Argyle Street, Suite 1300, Halifax, NS B3J 3N8

solutions.text: Local Venture & Seed Funds: Create community-backed seed funds or crowdfunding platforms to provide early-stage capital for locally-rooted startups and social enterprises, keeping ownership and benefits within the region.

resources.name: Volta Cohort
resources.description: Volta Cohort is an early-stage investment program that provides seed funding and wraparound support to startups founded in Atlantic Canada, with many teams building in Nova Scotia. By coupling capital (via a convertible investment) with workspace, mentorship, and local investor connections, the program helps founders launch and scale while remaining anchored in the region—keeping ownership, jobs, and economic benefits local.

resources.name: CEED Impact Loan Program
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: The CEED Impact Loan Program offers accessible microloans to new and growing Nova Scotia entrepreneurs, providing vital seed capital that is locally administered and paired with training and mentorship. By financing founders at the earliest stages, CEED helps them retain ownership, build their businesses in-province, and contribute to Nova Scotia’s community-driven economy.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Sandpiper Ventures Fund I
resources.description: Sandpiper Ventures is a Halifax-based seed venture fund investing in women-led and diverse founding teams across Atlantic Canada. By deploying local capital into regionally rooted startups and connecting them to Atlantic mentors and markets, Sandpiper helps companies secure early financing while keeping headquarters, ownership, and talent growth within Nova Scotia and the broader region.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Concrete Ventures Pre-Seed Fund
resources.description: Concrete Ventures is an Atlantic Canada–focused pre-seed fund that writes the first institutional checks into locally founded startups, including many based in Nova Scotia. The fund supplies early capital and hands-on guidance to help founders validate and scale without relocating, preserving local ownership and strengthening the province’s startup ecosystem.

solutions.text: Community Procurement & Buy-Local Pledges: Coordinate municipal and local business commitments to prioritize local hiring and procurement—giving preference to Nova Scotia-based suppliers and creating demand for local talent.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Procurement (Social and Sustainable Procurement)
resources.description: HRM’s procurement program incorporates social and sustainable procurement practices in RFPs and tenders, encouraging local economic benefits, apprenticeship opportunities, and community impact where permitted by trade agreements. The municipality also hosts supplier information sessions and "Doing Business with HRM" outreach that connect local SMEs to municipal buyers, helping anchor procurement and hiring within Nova Scotia and creating steady demand for local talent.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Procurement — Supplier Engagement and Sustainable Procurement
resources.description: The Province’s procurement office runs supplier engagement, training, and reverse trade show events that help Nova Scotia-based businesses compete for public-sector contracts across departments, health, education, and Crown agencies. Its sustainable procurement approach integrates community benefits and workforce development considerations into solicitations where allowed, aligning institutional purchasing with buy-local outcomes that grow jobs and retain talent in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Select Nova Scotia (Buy Local Program)
resources.description: Select Nova Scotia is a provincial buy-local program that promotes sourcing from Nova Scotia producers and processors, including toolkits and campaigns encouraging restaurants, retailers, and institutions to prioritize local suppliers. By elevating local purchasing commitments and visibility for Nova Scotia-made goods, the program bolsters demand for local supply chains and the jobs and skills connected to them.

resources.name: Downtown Halifax Buy-Local and Member-to-Member Program
resources.description: Downtown Halifax Business Commission runs ongoing buy-local campaigns and a member-to-member program that encourages businesses and large employers to source goods and services from local firms in the downtown district. These initiatives coordinate commitments across employers and suppliers, channeling procurement to Nova Scotia-based companies and strengthening demand that supports local hiring and retention.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 2A2

resources.name: Halifax Chamber of Commerce — Shop Local and Business Procurement Initiatives
resources.description: The Halifax Chamber promotes shop-local and member-to-member procurement, facilitating corporate and institutional buying from Nova Scotia businesses through directories, campaigns, and events. By nudging anchor organizations and SMEs to commit spend locally, the Chamber helps build predictable demand for Nova Scotia suppliers, supporting local employment and career paths that keep young talent in the province.
resources.address: 32 Akerley Boulevard, Unit 100, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1N1

solutions.text: Hybrid Work Hubs with Childcare: Combine co-working facilities with affordable childcare and family-friendly hours so young parents can pursue remote or local work without relocating for better services.

resources.name: Early Childhood Education Centre (ECEC) and Community Hub
resources.description: The North Grove combines a licensed Early Childhood Education Centre with a community hub that offers work-friendly spaces, Wi‑Fi, and program rooms used for employment, training, and entrepreneurship supports. Parents can place their children in affordable, licensed childcare on-site while they work remotely, attend virtual meetings, job search, or join skills programs in the same building—delivering a practical hybrid work hub with childcare that reduces the need to commute or relocate.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC) with Employment & Business Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides on-site Care for Newcomer Children while parents use its employment resource centre, attend business incubator sessions, or take training in computer-equipped rooms—functioning as a co‑working‑style environment with family-friendly hours. By co-locating childcare with work and learning spaces, the program enables newcomer parents to pursue remote work, career development, and entrepreneurship in Halifax without leaving their community.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: YWCA Halifax Early Learning & Childcare + Employment Centre
resources.description: YWCA Halifax operates licensed early learning and childcare on-site alongside employment, entrepreneurship, and skills programs delivered in training rooms and work-friendly spaces with Wi‑Fi. Parents can access affordable childcare in the same facility and use the centre as a local hybrid work hub—completing remote work, attending workshops, or meeting with advisors during family-friendly hours that align with childcare schedules.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

solutions.text: Place-Based Branding & Talent Campaigns: Develop community-led marketing that highlights local quality of life, career success stories and cultural strengths to reframe the region as an attractive long-term home for young people.

resources.name: Sell Halifax
resources.description: Sell Halifax is Halifax Partnership’s place-branding and ambassador program that mobilizes local leaders, employers, and alumni to promote Halifax as a city to build a life and career. Through targeted talent-attraction campaigns, sector spotlights, and success-story content that highlights quality of life and career pathways, the program reframes Halifax as an appealing long-term home for students, newcomers, and returning youth.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Cape Breton – Unama’ki: Live, Work, Study
resources.description: The Cape Breton Partnership’s talent attraction initiative showcases the island’s lifestyle, Mi’kmaq culture, and real career opportunities through storytelling, videos, and community ambassador outreach. It pairs quality-of-life marketing with practical relocation supports (job board, welcoming network) to attract and retain young people and returning expats to make Cape Breton – Unama’ki their long-term home.

resources.name: Choose Antigonish
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Antigonish (in partnership with the Town of Antigonish)
resources.description: Choose Antigonish is a community-led place-brand that promotes the Town and County of Antigonish as a place to live, learn, work, and put down roots. By featuring local success stories, cost-of-living advantages, and cultural strengths alongside employer connections and settlement information, the campaign positions Antigonish as an attractive, long-term home for students, newcomers, and returning youth.
resources.address: 285 Beech Hill Road, Antigonish, NS B2G 0B4

resources.name: More Than Medicine (Health-Care Talent Attraction)
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health’s “More Than Medicine” campaign markets the province’s lifestyle, communities, and career growth stories to recruit and retain health professionals, residents, and students. The initiative combines compelling place-based narratives with employer outreach and relocation support, framing Nova Scotia as a rewarding place to build a life and career—directly countering brain drain in a critical sector.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

solutions.text: Local Skills Bootcamps & Microcredentials: Partner with colleges, employers and volunteers to run short, affordable training programs tied to local job needs (tech, trades, health care) with employer commitments to interview graduates.

resources.name: NSCC Microcredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College offers short, stackable microcredentials co-designed with local employers in sectors such as technology, skilled trades, and health care. Many are delivered as intensive bootcamps or compressed courses with hands-on projects and industry-recognized badges; NSCC regularly convenes employer panels, showcases, and interview days with hiring partners to connect graduates directly to local opportunities, aligning training with Nova Scotia’s labour market needs.

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding Inc.
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based program delivered by NSCC in partnership with Irving Shipbuilding and community organizations to prepare Nova Scotians—especially underrepresented groups—for in-demand trades like welding and metal fabrication. Participants complete targeted technical training and work-integrated learning, and Irving Shipbuilding commits to interview and hire successful graduates into apprenticeship and entry-level roles, directly linking short, affordable training to local jobs.

resources.name: SalesCamp (Halifax Cohorts)
resources.description: Palette Skills’ SalesCamp is a three-week, tuition-free bootcamp that prepares participants for B2B tech sales roles through employer-led workshops, simulations, and mentorship. Halifax-based cohorts culminate in hiring events where partner companies interview graduates on the spot, creating a direct pipeline from intensive, job-aligned training to interviews and roles with Nova Scotia employers.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

solutions.text: Shared Apprenticeship & Job Rotation Programs: Allow small employers to co-host apprentices or rotate young staff between firms for varied experience, helping workers build broad skills without leaving the region.

resources.name: Group Sponsorship (Multi-Employer Apprenticeship)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency recognizes and supports group sponsors—industry associations, unions, and employer consortia—that collectively hire and rotate apprentices among multiple small and mid-sized employers. This model keeps apprentices working steadily while gaining varied on-the-job experience across firms, directly aligning with shared apprenticeship and job-rotation objectives to build broad skills and attachment to Nova Scotia’s labour market.

resources.name: IBEW Local 1928 Apprenticeship and Training Program
resources.organization: International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers (IBEW) Local 1928
resources.description: IBEW Local 1928 coordinates apprenticeships across multiple signatory contractors through its hiring hall, rotating electrical apprentices through diverse industrial, commercial, and utility worksites in Nova Scotia. This shared, multi-employer placement approach ensures steady employment, exposure to varied equipment and methods, and a strong local career pathway that encourages apprentices to build their futures in the province.
resources.address: 14 McQuade Lake Crescent, Halifax, NS B3S 1B6

solutions.text: Community Maker Spaces & Arts Incubators: Support low-cost maker labs, studios and incubators where creatives, artisans and technologists can prototype, collaborate and sell locally, strengthening cultural ties and local economies.

resources.name: Start-Up Yard at COVE
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: Start-Up Yard at COVE is an ocean-technology incubator and shared prototyping facility that provides low-cost workspace, shared labs, machine shop access, and mentorship to growing companies. It enables technologists to build, test, and commercialize products locally on the Dartmouth waterfront, fostering collaboration among startups, researchers, and industry. By anchoring advanced prototyping and networks in Nova Scotia, it helps retain ambitious young innovators and strengthens the local blue economy.

resources.name: Lou Duggan Creative Studio (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: The Lou Duggan Creative Studio is a free/low-cost makerspace inside Halifax Central Library that offers tools, sewing machines, 3D printers, crafting equipment, and hands-on workshops. It gives creatives and aspiring entrepreneurs an accessible place to prototype, learn new skills, and collaborate, often showcasing work through library programs and local events. By lowering barriers to making and connecting people across disciplines, it strengthens community ties and helps young talent see a future in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: The Centre operates public studios and maker facilities in textiles, ceramics, jewellery/metal, printmaking, and more, alongside business training and gallery/retail opportunities for artisans. Affordable studio access, mentorship, and market pathways function as an arts incubator, helping makers prototype, refine, and sell their work locally to residents and visitors. This ecosystem supports sustainable creative livelihoods and reduces outmigration by creating compelling reasons to build careers in Cape Breton.

resources.name: The Deanery Project
resources.description: The Deanery Project is a rural arts and maker hub with wood and metal shops, fabrication tools, studios, residencies, and community build programs. It offers low-cost access to equipment and collaborative workshops—from boatbuilding and timber framing to media arts—culminating in local events and tangible projects. By cultivating hands-on skills and entrepreneurial pathways on the Eastern Shore, it helps young people root their creative and trades-based futures in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

resources.name: Bus Stop Theatre Co-op
resources.description: Bus Stop Theatre Co-op is a member-owned performing-arts venue that provides affordable rehearsal, production, and presentation space along with technical resources and professional development. It acts as an incubator for theatre, dance, music, and interdisciplinary arts, enabling creators to prototype new work, collaborate across disciplines, and reach local audiences. Keeping accessible stages and production capacity in Halifax helps artists build sustainable careers and strengthens the local cultural economy.

solutions.text: Local Networking & Industry Nights: Host regular sector-specific meetups, hackathons and demo nights that bring employers, students and remote workers together to build professional networks and visible career opportunities.

resources.name: Ocean Connector
resources.organization: COVE - Centre for Ocean Ventures & Entrepreneurship
resources.description: Ocean Connector is COVE’s recurring networking series that convenes ocean-tech employers, startups, researchers, students, and remote professionals for talks, demos, and open networking. By spotlighting local projects and companies and facilitating in-person connections, the series creates visible career pathways and strengthens participants’ ties to Nova Scotia’s ocean economy.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program matches graduating students, young professionals, and newcomers with established business leaders (Connectors) who provide warm introductions and invite them into sector-specific networks. Through regular Connector+ mixers and industry-focused networking events, it helps participants meet employers, discover opportunities, and build professional roots in Halifax.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: ShiftKey Labs Events & Hackathons
resources.organization: ShiftKey Labs, Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science
resources.description: ShiftKey Labs, a university innovation sandbox, hosts hackathons, demo nights, and meetups that connect students and recent grads with industry mentors and employers in the tech sector. These events provide hands-on collaboration, showcase local prototypes, and create hiring and startup opportunities that anchor emerging talent in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: The PIER Community Events & Demo Days
resources.organization: The PIER at the Halifax Seaport
resources.description: The PIER at the Halifax Seaport runs industry meetups, member demo days, and knowledge-sharing sessions focused on supply chain, logistics, and ocean innovation. By gathering startups, corporates, students, and remote workers in a living-lab environment, these events foster collaborations and make local career pathways more visible.

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Community Nights & Hackathons
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic hosts regular community nights, pitch events, and hackathons that bring together students, founders, mentors, and employers across rural and urban Nova Scotia. These gatherings build cross-sector networks, highlight local companies and challenges, and create tangible opportunities that encourage young talent to stay and grow their careers in the province.

solutions.text: Housing Co-ops & Affordable Rentals for Young Workers: Develop community-driven housing solutions such as co-operatives, shared ownership models, and subsidized rental pools targeted at early-career residents to reduce relocation pressure.

resources.name: Phoenix Youth Housing
resources.description: Phoenix Youth Housing provides safe, affordable, and supported rental apartments for youth and young adults (typically ages 16–24) who are working, in school, or in training. Rents are subsidized and paired with on-site support so early‑career residents can stabilize income, build tenancy history, and remain rooted in Halifax instead of relocating to larger markets.
resources.address: 5880 Spring Garden Road, Suite 200, Halifax, NS B3H 1Y1

resources.name: Habitat for Humanity Nova Scotia Homeownership Program
resources.description: Habitat NS offers a shared-equity, affordable homeownership model for working, lower-to-moderate income households, including early-career individuals and families. By providing below-market mortgages and partnering with homeowners’ sweat equity, the program keeps monthly housing costs predictable and attainable, anchoring young workers in their communities.

resources.name: YWCA Halifax Affordable Housing
resources.description: YWCA Halifax operates affordable and supportive rental housing for women and families, many of whom are in the early stages of their careers or education. Through below-market rents and wraparound services, the program reduces housing cost burdens and helps young residents stay, work, and participate in the local community rather than moving away.
resources.address: 358 Herring Cove Road, Halifax, NS B3R 1V8

solutions.text: Civic Learning & Community Service Pathways: Create paid youth positions in municipal projects, cultural organizations and non-profits to build local leadership, deepen civic ties, and demonstrate viable careers that contribute to community life.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship Program (CLSI)
resources.description: CLSI provides paid 9–16 week summer placements for youth (ages 15–30) with municipalities, Mi’kmaw communities, non-profits, and local businesses across Nova Scotia to deliver community-focused environmental and climate projects. Interns receive mentorship and professional development while working on civic priorities like energy efficiency, coastal adaptation, and community engagement—building local leadership, deepening attachment to place, and showcasing viable, purpose-driven careers in the province.

resources.name: Student and Youth Employment
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality hires students and young adults into paid roles in municipal services—such as recreation program leaders, aquatics staff, parks and trails crews, public works assistants, and event support—embedded in neighbourhood facilities and community projects. These municipal positions cultivate civic leadership and public-service skills while connecting youth to residents and showing clear pathways into long-term careers with local government.

resources.name: ACAP Cape Breton Green Team
resources.description: ACAP Cape Breton annually hires local youth for paid seasonal roles that deliver hands-on community environmental projects—such as shoreline cleanups, urban greening, trail and stream restoration, and public outreach—often in partnership with the Cape Breton Regional Municipality and neighbourhood organizations. The program builds leadership and work experience rooted in place while demonstrating how environmental stewardship can be a meaningful, locally based career path.

resources.name: Summer Student Employment (Museum Interpreters and Program Assistants)
resources.organization: Black Cultural Centre for Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Black Cultural Centre hires local youth as paid museum interpreters, archives assistants, and event/program staff to support exhibits, tours, and cultural programming that preserve and share African Nova Scotian heritage. These roles provide professional experience in the cultural sector, strengthen community connection and pride, and illustrate sustainable careers in arts, heritage, and community service within Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 10 Cherry Brook Road, Cherry Brook, NS B2Z 1A8

resources.name: Summer Student Employment (Programs and Community Outreach)
resources.description: Cape Breton Regional Library employs students in paid positions to deliver children’s reading clubs, digital literacy workshops, community outreach, and local history projects across its branches. Working at the library embeds youth in civic life, builds leadership and service skills, and highlights public-sector and cultural careers that contribute directly to community well-being.

obstacles.title: Support for Arts, Culture, and Creative Industries
obstacles.description: Precarious funding, space affordability issues, and limited venues threaten the creative economy. Without a vibrant cultural scene, attraction and retention of young people decline.

solutions.text: Community Arts Microgrant Program: Create a locally administered microgrant fund (seeded by municipality, businesses, and donors) that awards small, quick-turnaround grants to individual artists, collectives, and pop-up projects to cover materials, short-term venue rental, or promotion. Prioritize youth-led and underrepresented creators and simplify application and reporting requirements.

resources.name: Equity & Access in the Arts Program
resources.description: Arts Nova Scotia’s Equity & Access in the Arts provides small, flexible project grants to artists and collectives from communities facing barriers (including Indigenous, African Nova Scotian/Black, racialized, Deaf, disabled, and 2SLGBTQIA+ artists). It offers streamlined applications and quick turnaround funding that can cover materials, short-term venue rental, and promotion, directly aligning with a microgrant model that prioritizes underrepresented creators.
resources.address: 1741 Brunswick Street, 3rd Floor, Halifax, NS B3J 3X8

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty: Micro Grants
resources.description: The Downtown Halifax Business Commission’s Gritty to Pretty Micro Grants fund small-scale public art, pop-ups, and placemaking projects by individual artists, collectives, and community groups in downtown Halifax. With a concise application and quick approvals, the grants help cover materials, installation costs, temporary venue/space use, and project promotion, encouraging youth-led and community-driven creative activity in affordable, temporary venues.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 2A2

resources.name: Neighbourhood Placemaking Program
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Neighbourhood Placemaking Program provides small grants and in-kind support for community-led arts and placemaking projects such as street murals, pop-up installations, and creative public gatherings. The program uses a simplified application, offers materials support and modest budgets suitable for microgrant-scale initiatives, and encourages projects from youth and underrepresented communities, enabling quick, low-barrier activation of local creative spaces.

solutions.text: Shared Creative Hub / Makerspace: Establish a community-run shared arts hub that pools resources: studio spaces, rehearsal rooms, equipment, and affordable co-working for creative entrepreneurs. Operate on a sliding-scale membership and include drop-in hours, tool training, and rehearsal scheduling to maximize access for young people.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op
resources.description: A community-owned arts hub offering an affordable, multipurpose venue with rehearsal and performance space, meeting rooms, and technical equipment. The co-op model provides member rates and subsidized rentals, with online scheduling and technical orientations that lower barriers for emerging artists and youth. By pooling shared resources and keeping access flexible, it functions as a shared creative hub that supports the local creative economy.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: A community tool-lending library and workshop that provides access to shared equipment, drop-in hours, and skill-building workshops. It operates on a sliding-scale membership and includes safety and tool training, enabling young people and creative entrepreneurs to access tools they couldn’t otherwise afford. This pooled-resource model supports makers, set builders, and artists who need occasional equipment and workspace.

resources.name: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design – Public Studios
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: Shared craft studios offering access to specialized equipment (e.g., ceramics, textiles, and jewellery) alongside classes, orientations, and mentorship. The Centre provides memberships and studio access passes at accessible rates, with scheduled open-studio times and training that help emerging artists safely use tools and develop skills. This pooled facility model supports creative entrepreneurs and youth by lowering space and equipment costs.

resources.name: The Deanery Project – Community Makerspace & Studios
resources.description: A rural, community-run hub featuring a woodshop, fibre arts and print studios, and flexible gathering/rehearsal spaces, alongside residencies and youth programs. The Deanery offers pay-what-you-can options for workshops, tool orientations, and open studio times, expanding access to equipment and training. By pooling facilities and offering flexible, affordable access, it embodies a shared creative hub supporting young makers and artists.
resources.address: 37 Deanery Road, Lower Ship Harbour, NS B0J 1Y0

resources.name: Halifax Central Library – Media Studio and Creative Labs
resources.description: Free, bookable studios and creative labs providing audio/video production spaces, editing suites, and maker equipment like 3D printers and sewing machines. Staff-led orientations, workshops, and drop-in times provide the tool training and support needed for young people to create, rehearse, and produce work without high overhead costs. As a publicly accessible, shared facility, it pools resources and expands equitable access to creative infrastructure.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Adaptive Reuse of Vacant Storefronts for Pop-Up Venues: Coordinate a program that matches vacant commercial spaces with artists and small promoters for temporary exhibitions, performances, and markets. Work with property owners on reduced short-term rents and expedited permitting to animate downtowns and give creatives low-cost, visible venues.

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty Placemaking and Storefront Animation Grants
resources.description: Downtown Halifax Business Commission’s Gritty to Pretty program funds temporary window installations, pop-up galleries, and activations in vacant or underused storefronts to draw foot traffic and showcase local creatives. The program connects artists and promoters with property owners, supports short-term occupancy agreements at reduced cost, and helps navigate approvals so temporary exhibitions and performances can open quickly and visibly downtown.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 1Z2

resources.name: Downtown Truro Holiday Pop-Up Shop Program
resources.description: Downtown Truro Partnership coordinates short-term pop-up retail and maker spaces in vacant storefronts—especially during peak seasons—so artists, artisans, and small promoters can test concepts in high-visibility locations. The program brokers access to empty units with cooperative landlords, facilitates short-term leases at affordable rates, and streamlines logistics and permits to quickly activate unused spaces as temporary markets and exhibition venues.

resources.name: Downtown Sydney Pop-Up Shop Program
resources.description: The Sydney Downtown Development Association works with property owners to place artists, makers, and small retailers in vacant Charlotte Street storefronts for seasonal and event-based pop-ups. By arranging short-term, low-cost occupancy and assisting with municipal approvals and insurance needs, the program transforms empty units into temporary galleries, performances, and markets that animate downtown and expand opportunities for creatives.

solutions.text: Community Land Trust for Cultural Spaces: Form a community land trust (CLT) or non-profit real-estate cooperative to acquire and hold buildings for long-term affordable cultural use. Use philanthropic capital, municipal contributions, and community investment shares to stabilize rents for studios, galleries, and rehearsal halls.

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op is a member-owned non-profit that purchased and now stewards its building at 2203 Gottingen Street as a permanently affordable performance hub. Using a mix of community investment shares (community bonds), municipal and provincial/federal capital grants, and philanthropy, the co-op removed the property from speculative markets. It provides subsidized rehearsal, presentation, and creation space for theatre, dance, music, and community groups at stable, below-market rates.

resources.name: Eltuek Arts Centre
resources.description: Eltuek Arts Centre, operated by New Dawn Enterprises, owns and manages the former Holy Angels convent complex as a long-term home for artists and cultural organizations. Redeveloped with philanthropic support and multiple public funders, it provides affordable studios, offices, galleries, and collaborative spaces with rents designed to be sustainable for creatives. By holding the property in a mission-driven nonprofit, Eltuek stabilizes cultural space and anchors the creative economy in downtown Sydney.

resources.name: The Old School Community Gathering Place
resources.organization: The Old School Community Gathering Place Society
resources.description: The Old School Community Gathering Place Society acquired the former Musquodoboit Harbour school and converted it into a community arts and cultural centre. Through community fundraising, charitable donations, and municipal/provincial support, the Society maintains the building for affordable artist studios, gallery exhibitions, workshops, and a performance hall. Keeping ownership in a local nonprofit ensures long-term, below-market space for creatives and cultural groups.

resources.name: Customs House Artisan Incubator
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: The Customs House Artisan Incubator, operated by the Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design, rehabilitated the historic Customs House in Port Hawkesbury into an incubator with subsidized studios, shared equipment, gallery, and retail. Supported by public investment and philanthropy, the Centre holds and manages the building as dedicated cultural infrastructure. The program provides long-term, affordable workspaces to artisans and small creative businesses, stabilizing rents and fostering local creative enterprise.
resources.address: 402 Granville Street, Port Hawkesbury, NS B9A 2M7

resources.name: Alderney Landing Cultural Centre
resources.description: Alderney Landing Association operates a municipally supported waterfront cultural complex that includes a theatre, art gallery, studios, and market facilities. As a nonprofit facility manager for HRM-owned assets, it blends municipal contributions, earned revenue, and sponsorship to keep rental rates accessible for artists and cultural groups. This stewardship model keeps cultural spaces in community hands and buffers them from market pressures.

solutions.text: Creative Enterprise Incubator: Launch a locally focused incubator offering business coaching, grant navigation, shared admin services (ticketing, booking, invoicing), and mentorship for arts entrepreneurs and creative startups to increase sustainability and job creation among young creators.

resources.name: Music Nova Scotia
resources.description: Music Nova Scotia supports artists and music entrepreneurs with professional development workshops, one-on-one mentorship, and staff guidance on navigating grants (e.g., FACTOR and provincial programs), contracts, marketing, and export readiness. By offering business coaching, showcasing and market access opportunities, and shared resources like templates and admin guidance, the organization helps young creative businesses become more sustainable and create jobs in Nova Scotia’s music sector.

resources.name: Creative Entrepreneurship Program (CEP)
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: The Creative Entrepreneurship Program at Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design provides coaching, mentorship, and cohort-based training to help craft artists develop business plans, pricing, marketing, and export strategies. It also offers shared administrative services through its retail gallery and e-commerce channels—centralized point-of-sale, consignment management, and invoicing support—reducing overhead for emerging creative enterprises and enabling sustainable growth and employment.

resources.name: FILM 5
resources.description: FILM 5 is an intensive training and mentorship program that pairs emerging filmmakers with experienced producers, directors, and crew to develop short films and careers. Administered by AFCOOP, it includes business and producing workshops, grant-writing labs for Arts Nova Scotia/Telefilm, and access to shared services such as equipment booking, post-production facilities, and production administration guidance—functioning as a creative incubator for screen-based startups.
resources.address: 5663 Cornwallis Street, Suite 101, Halifax, NS B3K 1B6

resources.name: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op
resources.description: The Bus Stop Theatre Co-op is a member-owned venue and arts hub that provides affordable space alongside practical producer support, including box office/ticketing coordination, front-of-house services, and technical staffing. Staff and community mentors offer guidance on budgeting, grant applications, scheduling, and marketing, giving theatre, dance, and live-arts entrepreneurs shared administrative infrastructure and mentorship to build sustainable creative companies.

solutions.text: Artist-Teacher and Artist-in-Residence Partnerships: Place practicing artists in schools, libraries, and community centers for residencies that offer paid teaching, public workshops, and collaborative community projects. This creates income for artists, arts exposure for youth, and stronger community ties to creative practice.

resources.name: Community Studio Residency Program
resources.description: NSCAD University places recent graduates and practicing artists as community artists-in-residence in towns across Nova Scotia, where they deliver workshops, class visits, and collaborative projects with local schools, libraries, and community centres. Residents receive studio space and paid opportunities to teach, mentor youth, and run public programs, directly generating income for artists while expanding arts access. The program strengthens local cultural ecosystems and connects young people with creative career pathways.

resources.name: Artist Residencies at Ross Creek
resources.organization: The Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: Ross Creek hosts regional, national, and international artists for residencies that include paid community engagement—school visits, teacher professional development, and public workshops in libraries and community halls throughout rural Nova Scotia. Residents receive studio support and stipends to co-create projects with youth and community groups, culminating in exhibitions or events. This model brings practicing artists directly into learning spaces and strengthens rural cultural infrastructure.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

resources.name: Artist-in-Residence Program
resources.description: The Lunenburg School of the Arts hosts seasonal artist residencies that provide studio space, housing, and stipends in exchange for community engagement such as public workshops, artist talks, and youth programming. Residents frequently partner with local schools and the broader community to deliver accessible classes and collaborative art projects. The program generates paid teaching opportunities for artists while expanding arts exposure for young people in Lunenburg.

resources.name: Artist in Residence (AIR) Program
resources.organization: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design
resources.description: Cape Breton Centre for Craft & Design’s AIR program provides studio access, mentorship, and paid opportunities for practicing artists to conduct school visits, offer public classes, and lead community craft projects across Cape Breton. Residents deliver workshops and demonstrations in the Centre’s studios and partner sites such as libraries and community centres, engaging youth and the public. The program supports artist livelihoods and strengthens the local creative economy through hands-on learning.

resources.name: ARTsPLACE Artist Residency Program
resources.description: ARTsPLACE, operated by the Annapolis Region Community Arts Council, hosts artists-in-residence who run public workshops, school outreach, and community-engaged projects that culminate in exhibitions or events. Residents are supported with space and fees while collaborating with educators, libraries, and local groups to engage youth and broader audiences. This program directly places practicing artists in community learning environments, building cultural capacity in the Annapolis Valley.
resources.address: 396 St. George Street, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0
