Riders can pre-book subsidized trips for medical, shopping, and social/recreational activities, including evening events, and drivers provide door-to-door assistance that functions as a safe escort for seniors and youth. By filling gaps in limited public transit after hours, it enables residents to attend community programming and reduces isolation in smaller communities.
resources.address: 5288 St. Margarets Bay Road, Upper Tantallon, NS B3Z 2H3

resources.name: Tiger Patrol
resources.description: Tiger Patrol is the Dalhousie Student Union’s free evening shuttle and walking-escort service that helps students travel safely to and from campus libraries, residences, and social events after dark. The service is volunteer- and staff-supported, runs during late-night hours throughout the academic year, and is subsidized through student fees. By coordinating safe rides and escorts, it increases access to evening programming and third places, directly addressing transportation barriers that can limit participation.

solutions.text: Install lighting, seating and Wi‑Fi in public spaces: Small capital projects—better lighting, weatherproof seating, bike racks, and public Wi‑Fi—make plazas and waterfronts comfortable and safe for longer use. Local groups can lead fundraising and adopt-a-space maintenance.

resources.name: NSWiFi Public Wi‑Fi Program
resources.description: Build Nova Scotia operates the NSWiFi network that provides free public Wi‑Fi in high-traffic public spaces across the province, including along the Halifax and Lunenburg waterfronts and other community hubs. In tandem with its waterfront stewardship, the organization also invests in public-realm upgrades—weather‑resistant seating, lighting, bike racks, and power—making plazas and boardwalks comfortable, safe, and usable for longer hours and seasons.
resources.address: 1875 Upper Water Street, Suite 301, Halifax, NS B3J 1S9

resources.name: Gritty to Pretty Placemaking Grant Program
resources.description: This grant program funds small-scale capital projects—such as parklets, benches, string lighting, bike racks, wayfinding, and public art—that activate downtown plazas, alleys, and waterfront-adjacent spaces. It empowers local groups and businesses to design, co-fund, and steward their installations (adopt‑a‑space style), improving safety, comfort, and year‑round vibrancy for residents and visitors.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 3X7

resources.name: Argyle & Grafton Shared Streetscape
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality redesigned Argyle and Grafton Streets into a pedestrian‑priority public space with integrated seating, widened sidewalks, programmable and safety lighting, bike racks, and power for events—supporting nightlife and all‑season use. The streetscape creates a welcoming, flexible ‘third place’ that encourages social connection and activity in the downtown core.

resources.name: Halifax Public Libraries – Free Public Wi‑Fi
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries provides free Wi‑Fi at all branches, with strong outdoor coverage that extends into adjacent public spaces. The Halifax Central Library’s outdoor plaza and steps feature built‑in seating, lighting, and bike racks, creating an accessible, all‑ages gathering place that functions as a vibrant ‘third place’ for youth and the broader community.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Intergenerational clubs and regular social nights: Create recurring clubs (game nights, maker nights, storytelling, music) that intentionally mix youth, working-age adults and seniors to strengthen social ties and create reliable third-place routines.

resources.name: All Ages Board Games & Maker Drop-ins (Halifax Central Library)
resources.description: Halifax Central Library hosts recurring all-ages board game drop-ins, open music jams, and maker/creative lab sessions that bring together teens, working-age adults, and seniors. These free or low-cost gatherings create a reliable third-place routine where multiple generations connect over play, creativity, and storytelling, directly strengthening everyday social ties. By intentionally welcoming all ages to shared activities, the library fosters intergenerational community life year-round in a central, accessible venue.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Board Game Night and Ukulele Jam (McConnell Library, Sydney)
resources.description: McConnell Library runs regular Board Game Nights and a community Ukulele Jam that are open to all ages and skill levels, encouraging youth, adults, and seniors to participate together. These recurring, low-barrier social nights offer music-making and games as shared activities that naturally mix generations and spark conversation. The consistent schedule and inclusive format build dependable third-place routines and strengthen belonging across age groups in downtown Sydney.

resources.name: Board Game Night & Makerspace Drop-ins (Kentville Public Library)
resources.description: Kentville Public Library offers recurring Board Game Nights, craft circles, and maker-style drop-ins that invite families, teens, working adults, and older adults to create, play, and learn together. These intergenerational clubs and social evenings are free or low-cost and designed to be welcoming for all ages, building a reliable third-place routine in the town core. The hands-on, collaborative format supports casual mentorship and neighborly connections across generations.

resources.name: Family Fun Night & Community Meals (Veith House)
resources.description: Veith House hosts recurring intergenerational social nights—such as Family Fun Night, community meals, and arts/game activities—that intentionally bring together children, teens, adults, and seniors from the North End. These welcoming, low-cost evenings create a dependable third place where neighbors of all ages share food, stories, and play. By mixing generations in a community-centred setting, Veith House strengthens local social ties and reduces isolation.

resources.name: Community Arts Sundays & Coffeehouse (Ross Creek Centre for the Arts)
resources.organization: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts
resources.description: Ross Creek Centre for the Arts runs recurring all-ages community arts days and coffeehouse/music nights that bring together kids, teens, families, and seniors for making, storytelling, and performance. These accessible, regular events function as intergenerational clubs where participants share skills and creativity across age groups. The consistent schedule and welcoming rural venue provide a reliable third place for social connection in the Annapolis Valley.
resources.address: 555 Ross Creek Road, Canning, NS B0P 1H0

solutions.text: Skill-share time banks and volunteer networks: Set up a local time bank where residents exchange skills (cooking, carpentry, teaching, childcare) to lower costs of activities and build reciprocal relationships that increase belonging.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: A member-run lending library that provides access to shared tools and peer-led workshops, reducing the cost of DIY, home repair, and creative projects. Members can contribute volunteer hours in exchange for membership benefits and to help run operations and Repair Cafés, creating a practical time-exchange and skill-share network that builds reciprocal relationships and a sense of community.

resources.name: Ecology Action Centre Repair Cafés
resources.description: The Ecology Action Centre organizes Repair Café events where volunteer fixers share their skills in sewing, electronics, bike repair, and more while helping neighbours repair items for free. These hands-on, peer-to-peer sessions function as a community time- and skill-exchange, lowering costs for participants and creating welcoming third-place gatherings that strengthen social ties.

resources.name: Halifax Public Libraries Repair Cafés and Skill-Share Workshops
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries hosts recurring Repair Cafés, maker meet-ups, and peer-led classes (e.g., sewing, coding, bike maintenance) where community volunteers teach and lend their expertise at no cost. By pairing free instruction with collaborative problem-solving in branch spaces, the library creates accessible third places that operate like a time-and-skill exchange network, fostering belonging and reducing the cost of recreational learning.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: The North Grove Community Kitchens & Volunteer Network
resources.description: The North Grove runs community kitchens, gardens, and meal programs where neighbours cook, teach, and learn together, with volunteers sharing time and skills to co-host activities and support families. Participants exchange effort—like cooking, childcare during programs, and gardening—for community meals and programming, lowering barriers to participation while building strong reciprocal relationships in a welcoming third-place hub.

solutions.text: Affordable space matchmaking platform: Build a simple online or printed directory that lists available community, church, school and private spaces with rates and booking contacts so organizers can find low-cost venues for events and programs.

resources.name: Meeting Rooms Directory
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries maintains an online directory of meeting, program, and event rooms across its branches with details on capacity, amenities, availability, and low- or no-cost fees. This centralized listing with branch-level booking contacts helps organizers quickly find affordable community spaces for workshops, meetups, and programs.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Facility Rentals & Bookings
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality offers a searchable directory and booking service for community centres, gymnasiums, arenas, fields, and multipurpose rooms, including posted rates, capacities, and how to book. This municipal platform functions as a space matchmaking tool so residents and groups can locate affordable venues across urban and suburban neighbourhoods.

resources.name: Community Use of Schools (Facility Rentals)
resources.description: HRCE’s Community Use of Schools program lists gyms, cafeterias, auditoriums, and classrooms available for community rental, with fee schedules and step-by-step booking contacts. By cataloguing school spaces and pricing in one place, it enables youth groups, nonprofits, and organizers to secure low-cost venues for events and programs.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Recreation Facilities & Rentals
resources.description: CBRM Recreation provides a public directory of arenas, community halls, fields, and multi-use spaces across Cape Breton, with rental details, contacts, and fee information. This resource connects residents and event organizers with affordable local venues, supporting year-round programs and community gatherings in smaller towns and communities.

obstacles.title: Workforce Shortages in Care, Construction, and Skilled Trades
obstacles.description: Bottlenecks in critical occupations delay housing builds, childcare expansion, and healthcare delivery. Aging workers and slow training pipelines intensify shortages.

solutions.text: Community Apprenticeship Hub: Create a local hub that coordinates apprenticeships and pre-apprenticeship placements with employers, unions, community colleges, and high schools to streamline pathways into construction, care, and skilled trades.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: Building Futures for Youth places high school students in paid summer work terms with construction employers, where they can earn apprenticeship hours and industry certifications while still in school. The program coordinates among employers, unions, the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, NSCC, and school boards to streamline pre-apprenticeship pathways into construction and skilled trades, effectively operating as a community hub that aligns classroom learning with on-the-job training.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based pre-apprenticeship initiative that brings together NSCC, Irving Shipbuilding, Unifor, and community partners to recruit and train Nova Scotians—especially underrepresented groups—for skilled trades careers in shipbuilding. The program integrates customized academic upgrading, technical training at NSCC, wraparound supports, and coordinated paid work placements with the employer and union, creating a seamless hub from training to apprenticeship registration and employment.

resources.name: Employment Services – Skilled Trades & Apprenticeship Pathways
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides assessment, coaching, and employer-matched placements that help internationally trained tradespeople and newcomers enter Nova Scotia’s apprenticeship system and related employment. Working with NSAA, NSCC, unions, and local employers, ISANS functions as a community coordination hub—aligning credential recognition, safety tickets, mentorship, and job matching to accelerate entry into construction, care-related support roles, and other skilled trades.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Employment & Training Services
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Employment & Training Services connect Indigenous community members with pre-apprenticeship programs, NSCC pathways (including Pathways to Shipbuilding), and unionized employers for apprenticeship placements. Acting as a localized hub, the program coordinates essential supports—such as tutoring, transportation, and industry certifications—while brokering relationships with employers, unions, and colleges to streamline transitions into construction, care, and skilled trades careers.

solutions.text: Intergenerational Mentorship Network: Match retiring and experienced workers with youth and career-changers for hands-on mentorship, job shadowing, and skills-transfer programs hosted by community centres and libraries.

resources.name: Connector Program
resources.description: The Connector Program matches job-ready recent graduates, newcomers, and career-changers with experienced industry professionals and leaders (including retirees) for one-on-one mentorship, informational interviews, and warm introductions. These guided connections often lead to workplace visits or short job-shadow experiences that transfer practical knowledge and networks in sectors facing shortages, helping participants move into roles in trades, care, construction, and other in-demand fields.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Pathways to Shipbuilding
resources.description: Pathways to Shipbuilding is a cohort-based program that prepares participants for skilled trades careers in shipbuilding through NSCC training combined with on-the-job mentorship from experienced journeypersons at Irving Shipbuilding and union partners. Learners gain hands-on skills, job shadowing, and direct skills transfer from veteran tradespeople, creating intergenerational connections that fast-track entry into high-demand construction and fabrication roles.

resources.name: MentorAbility Nova Scotia
resources.description: MentorAbility Nova Scotia provides short-term (often one-day) customized mentorship and job-shadow experiences by pairing youth and adults with disabilities with seasoned employers and workers across sectors such as healthcare, construction, and skilled trades. Through workplace-based learning, participants explore roles and build confidence while experienced mentors transfer practical know-how and recruitment pipelines widen for occupations facing shortages.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

resources.name: Professional Mentorship Program
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ Professional Mentorship Program pairs internationally trained professionals and career-changers with experienced local professionals for guided mentorship, networking, and workplace culture orientation, with opportunities for job shadowing where appropriate. The intergenerational exchange accelerates skills transfer and integration into Nova Scotia’s workforce, helping fill gaps in priority fields including healthcare, construction-related professions, and technical roles.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Modular Micro-credential Courses: Offer short, evening and weekend modular training (safety, basic trade skills, care certifications) delivered locally by community colleges, libraries, and volunteer instructors to speed entry into jobs.

resources.name: NSCC MicroCredentials
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College delivers short, stackable micro-credential courses in areas like construction safety (e.g., WHMIS, fall protection), basic trade skills, and care-related competencies (e.g., dementia care, CCA skill modules). Many offerings are scheduled in the evenings, on weekends, and in blended/online formats across local campuses to help learners quickly earn job-relevant badges recognized by employers, accelerating entry into high-demand roles.

resources.name: CANS Education & Training
resources.description: The Construction Association of Nova Scotia offers modular, industry-recognized short courses for the construction workforce, including safety tickets (First Aid/CPR, WHMIS, Fall Protection) and practical skills and project management modules. Programs are frequently delivered in short blocks, evenings, weekends, and online, enabling rapid upskilling and faster onboarding for trades and construction jobs critical to housing and infrastructure builds.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: NSCECE Professional Learning Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education (NSCECE)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education provides short, stackable professional learning courses and micro-credentials for current and aspiring early childhood educators. Offered online and during evenings/weekends, these targeted modules help participants quickly meet regulatory requirements, upgrade competencies, and transition into childcare roles to address workforce gaps in the early learning and care sector.

resources.name: Canadian Red Cross First Aid & CPR Training – Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross delivers short, credentialed First Aid/CPR, Basic Life Support, and Psychological First Aid courses required by many healthcare, childcare, and construction employers. With frequent evening and weekend classes offered at the Dartmouth training centre and partner sites across Nova Scotia, learners can rapidly obtain essential safety certifications that support immediate entry into high-demand roles.

solutions.text: School-to-Work Pathways and Trade Camps: Partner with local schools to provide co-op placements, summer trade and care camps, and in-class modules so students get real work experience and clear pathways after graduation.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY places high school students in paid summer jobs with construction employers across Nova Scotia, combining real work experience with safety training and mentoring. Students often earn co-op credits and can begin logging hours toward apprenticeship pathways, giving them a clear route from school into the skilled trades workforce.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

resources.name: HRCE Co-operative Education Program (with Skilled Trades 10–12)
resources.description: Through in-class Skilled Trades courses (Grades 10–12) and structured co-op placements, HRCE students gain hands-on experience with local employers in fields like construction, electrical, and automotive. The program connects learning to real workplaces and can dovetail with youth apprenticeship pathways, helping students transition directly into trades and related careers after graduation.
resources.address: 33 Spectacle Lake Drive, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1X7

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health – Summer Student Employment Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health hires high school and post-secondary students for paid summer roles in care and support settings (e.g., long-term care, nutrition & food services, environmental services, and clinical support). These placements provide practical experience, exposure to healthcare careers, and a pathway into further training and employment in the province’s care sector.

resources.name: NSCC Tech & Trades Summer Camps
resources.description: NSCC hosts hands-on summer camps where youth explore skilled trades and technologies—such as welding, carpentry, electrical, and health labs—guided by college instructors. The camps introduce students to real tools and work environments, connect them with industry partners, and map clear post-secondary and apprenticeship pathways in Nova Scotia.

solutions.text: Youth Retention and Returner Supports: Organize community-funded relocation incentives, starter housing support, and peer networks to attract young people and former residents back into local jobs and businesses.

resources.name: Connector Program (Halifax)
resources.description: The Connector Program links recent graduates, newcomers, and returning professionals with established leaders in Halifax’s business community for one-on-one, warm introductions. By rapidly growing peer and professional networks, it helps young talent and returnees find local jobs in sectors facing shortages (including care, construction, and skilled trades), encouraging them to stay or come back to Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: The Cape Breton Welcome Network mobilizes community hosts and local volunteer teams to welcome newcomers and returning Cape Bretoners, helping them find short-term housing, navigate communities, and connect to employers. Its peer networks and place-based events build social ties that make it easier for young people and returnees to relocate, settle, and take up jobs in high-need sectors across the island.
resources.address: 500 George Street, Suite 140, Sydney, NS B1P 1K6

resources.name: YREACH (YMCA Rural Settlement Services)
resources.description: YREACH provides pre-arrival guidance, community orientation, housing search support, and employment referrals for newcomers settling in communities across Nova Scotia, including many rural areas. By organizing local host networks and connecting young professionals and families to jobs, training, and peer supports, YREACH makes relocation feasible and helps retain talent in sectors with shortages such as healthcare and the skilled trades.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY places high school students in paid summer work terms with Nova Scotia construction and skilled trades employers, creating clear pathways to apprenticeship and long-term local careers. By investing community and employer resources in early work experience, mentorship, and safety training, the program builds peer networks and anchors young people to in-demand trades, directly addressing workforce gaps in construction.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Employment and Bridging Programs (Mentorship, Connector, and Sector Pathways)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers employment bridging, professional mentorship, and networking programs that connect young and early-career newcomers and returnees to Nova Scotia employers, including healthcare and trades. These peer and professional networks, combined with settlement and housing navigation supports, reduce relocation barriers and help fill critical workforce shortages while encouraging participants to stay and build their lives in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

solutions.text: Employer Training Consortium: Form a cooperative of local employers that pools funds and staff time to run shared training programs, rotating placements, and joint hiring fairs to reduce individual costs.

resources.name: CANS Education & Training
resources.description: Run by a consortium of construction employers through their industry association, CANS pools member dues and staff expertise to deliver shared training in supervision, project management, safety, and essential skills across firms. It also organizes sector-wide events such as the CANS Construction Job Fair, where multiple employers jointly recruit apprentices and skilled tradespeople, reducing individual hiring costs and expanding the talent pool.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Women Unlimited Program
resources.description: Women Unlimited coordinates cohorts with NSCC and a network of construction, manufacturing, and industrial employers who contribute funds, mentors, and staff time to co-design and deliver pre-apprenticeship training. Employers host rotating work placements and participate in joint hiring days for each cohort, creating a shared, lower-cost pathway into skilled trades and technical roles across multiple companies.

resources.name: Continuing Care Recruitment & Retention Services
resources.description: Health Association Nova Scotia provides shared recruitment and onboarding services for a consortium of long-term care and home care employers that pool membership resources. The program coordinates province-wide hiring fairs, centralized screening, and standardized training/orientation (e.g., for CCAs) while arranging practical placements across member facilities to accelerate hiring and reduce costs for individual organizations.

solutions.text: Community Childcare Co-operatives: Develop locally run, affordable childcare co-ops and flexible childminding networks so workers in care, construction, and trades can work nonstandard hours or attend training.

resources.name: Care for Newcomer Children (CNC)
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides on-site, licensed childminding so newcomer parents can attend language classes, employment services, and skills training. Schedules align with program times and can include daytime and varied-hour sessions, enabling parents entering care, construction, and trades training to participate without childcare barriers. This flexible childminding directly supports workforce development by freeing parents to complete certifications, bridging programs, and employer-linked training.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Chebucto Family Centre Childminding
resources.description: Chebucto Family Centre offers free on-site childminding during workshops, programs, and support sessions so parents can attend training, appointments, and job-readiness activities. As a community-run hub, it coordinates childminding at varied times and connects families with local childcare options, easing access for those working or training in sectors with nonstandard schedules. This flexible, community-based model helps remove childcare barriers that can keep parents out of skilled trades and care-sector training.

solutions.text: Phased Retirement and Knowledge-Transfer Program: Enable phased retirement arrangements where senior workers retain part-time mentoring roles while training successors, ensuring institutional knowledge stays local.

resources.name: Developing Executives (D.E.) Mentorship Program
resources.description: CANS’ D.E. Mentorship Program pairs emerging construction professionals with seasoned industry leaders, including semi-retired executives and senior managers, for structured, goal-oriented knowledge transfer. Many mentors participate while transitioning to retirement, enabling reduced work commitments alongside formal coaching of successors. This creates an intentional succession pipeline in construction firms, preserving local institutional knowledge and easing workforce bottlenecks.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 110, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

resources.name: Mentorship Matters (Journeyperson Mentor Training)
resources.description: Mentorship Matters equips experienced journeypersons—often late-career or semi-retired—with practical tools to mentor apprentices on the job. Employers use the training to formalize reduced-hours mentoring roles for senior tradespeople, supporting phased retirement while transferring critical tacit skills in construction and skilled trades. The program strengthens succession planning and shortens ramp-up time for new workers, directly addressing labour shortages.

resources.name: Mentor-Coach Program (Practice-Based Coaching)
resources.organization: Nova Scotia College of Early Childhood Education
resources.description: NSCECE’s Mentor-Coach Program places highly experienced early childhood educators in part-time, on-site coaching roles to build the skills of newer staff and emerging leaders. These senior practitioners often use the program as a phased step toward retirement, maintaining reduced workloads while transferring institutional practices and quality standards. By stabilizing and upskilling childcare teams, the program helps expand capacity and retain local knowledge in the sector.

solutions.text: Mobile Training Units and Pop-up Labs: Deploy mobile skill-training vans or pop-up maker spaces to reach rural and remote communities with hands-on trade and care training sessions.

resources.name: Mobile Construction Experience
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Construction Sector Council operates a mobile construction training trailer that travels to schools, job fairs, and community events across the province. Outfitted with tools, simulators, and hands-on stations (e.g., carpentry, electrical, welding/VR), the unit delivers pop-up, practical trade experiences in rural and remote communities to spark interest and build entry-level skills for the construction workforce.

resources.name: Discovery on the Go
resources.description: Discovery Centre’s mobile outreach team brings a traveling STEM and maker program—complete with portable equipment like 3D printers, coding kits, and engineering challenges—to schools, libraries, and community halls across Nova Scotia. These pop-up labs provide hands-on technical skill-building in communities that lack local facilities, creating pathways into technology and skilled trades for youth.
resources.address: 1215 Lower Water Street, Halifax, NS B3J 3S8

resources.name: Dalhousie Dentistry Mobile Outreach Clinic
resources.description: Dalhousie University’s Faculty of Dentistry operates a mobile dental clinic that travels to underserved communities, where students and faculty deliver care while learners gain supervised, real-world clinical experience. The mobile unit functions as a hands-on training environment for future oral health professionals, expanding access to care and strengthening the healthcare workforce in rural Nova Scotia.

resources.name: Brilliant Labs Pop-Up Makerspace Outreach
resources.description: Brilliant Labs delivers mobile and pop-up makerspaces across Nova Scotia, setting up temporary labs with 3D printers, electronics, sewing machines, and digital fabrication tools in rural schools and community centres. These sessions provide hands-on design, build, and repair experiences that cultivate practical skills relevant to skilled trades, technology, and creative industries.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

solutions.text: Wraparound Worker Supports: Organize community transportation shuttles, tool rental, childcare stipends, and flexible scheduling agreements so people can attend training and accept jobs.

resources.name: Women Unlimited Program
resources.description: Women Unlimited recruits and supports diverse women to enter trades and technology careers in partnership with NSCC and industry across Nova Scotia. The program provides wraparound supports such as transportation assistance (e.g., bus passes), childcare subsidies, and the provision of PPE and starter tools so participants can attend training and transition to work. Staff also work with training providers and employers to structure flexible schedules and work placements that accommodate family responsibilities, directly removing barriers to jobs in construction, care, and skilled trades.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Employment Services (TEAM Work Cooperative)
resources.description: TEAM Work Cooperative operates a Nova Scotia Works employment centre that provides individualized employment services with practical, barrier-reducing supports. Eligible job seekers can access transportation assistance (bus tickets or gas cards), childcare supports while in training or starting work, and help securing required tools, PPE, or equipment to accept jobs. The team also liaises with employers to arrange flexible start dates, shifts, and schedules so candidates can participate in short-term training and transition smoothly into in-demand roles.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 316, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: ISANS Employment Services and Bridging Programs
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS delivers employment preparation and sector-bridging programs for newcomers with comprehensive wraparound supports. Clients can receive transit passes and on-site childminding for eligible classes, as well as subsidies to offset childcare and transportation when attending training, interviews, or work placements; many cohorts also supply needed devices or work-related gear. ISANS coordinates with training partners and employers to offer flexible, cohort-based schedules that help newcomers enter high-demand fields such as healthcare, construction, and skilled trades.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 4P1

resources.name: Employment & Training Program
resources.description: The Mi’kmaw Native Friendship Centre’s Employment & Training Program supports urban Indigenous job seekers with culturally safe, wraparound services. The program helps arrange transportation (bus tickets and coordination with community transit), provides or subsidizes childcare during training and job starts, and assists with work gear and tools needed to enter apprenticeships or employment. Staff also advocate with training providers and employers to create flexible schedules and placements so participants can balance family and community commitments while moving into care, construction, and skilled trades roles.

solutions.text: Tool Libraries and Starter Grants: Create community tool libraries and small grants or subsidized equipment loans for apprentices, young entrepreneurs, and caregivers starting in trades or care roles.

resources.name: Halifax Tool Library
resources.description: A membership-based lending library that provides affordable access to hundreds of hand and power tools for woodworking, construction, home repair, gardening, and more. By lowering upfront equipment costs, it enables apprentices, young contractors, and DIY caregivers to borrow the tools they need to start work, gain experience, and complete jobs without having to purchase expensive gear outright.

resources.name: Health Equipment Loan Program (HELP) – Nova Scotia
resources.description: The Canadian Red Cross lends basic medical and mobility equipment—such as wheelchairs, walkers, bath seats, and crutches—at no or low cost for short-term use. This reduces financial barriers for caregivers and home-support workers starting in care roles, providing rapid access to essential equipment so clients can be supported at home and care capacity can expand in communities.

resources.name: CEED Small Business Loans
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides accessible startup and growth financing that can be used to purchase tools, vehicles, and equipment for trades, construction, home repair, and care-service businesses. Combined with training and mentorship, these loans function as starter capital that lowers entry barriers for young entrepreneurs and new sole proprietors to begin taking on work and hiring as they grow.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Small Business Loan Guarantee Program
resources.description: Delivered through Nova Scotia credit unions, this program offers guaranteed loans for startups and small businesses—funds that can be used to acquire tools, machinery, and vehicles needed to launch or scale operations in construction, skilled trades, and in-home care services. The guarantee improves access to capital for new and young entrepreneurs, effectively subsidizing equipment costs and accelerating entry into the workforce.

solutions.text: Local Career Awareness Campaigns: Run community storytelling, job showcases, and employer open-house events highlighting career paths, earnings, and pride in local trades, care work, and construction.

resources.name: CANS Construction Career Expo
resources.description: An annual, hands-on career awareness event where thousands of Nova Scotia students and jobseekers meet construction employers, unions, and training providers. The expo features try-a-trade stations, demos, and panels that showcase real career paths, earnings, and apprenticeship options in the skilled trades and construction, directly aligning with community job showcases and employer open-house style engagement.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 301, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: NSCC Open House and Trades & Technology Showcases
resources.description: Nova Scotia Community College hosts campus open houses and shop tours where instructors, apprentices, and employer partners present skilled trades, construction, and technology programs. Participants explore labs, hear alumni stories, and learn about wages, credentials, and apprenticeship pathways—functioning as local job showcases and employer-connected open-house events that elevate pride in trades careers.

resources.name: Industry Information Sessions and Employer Showcases
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS runs recurring sector spotlights—such as continuing care assistant, health care, and skilled trades—where employers and alumni share career journeys, hiring needs, and wage expectations. These events double as local storytelling and job showcases, and often include on-site or virtual employer open houses that clarify credentials and pathways into care work and the trades.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Employer Spotlights and Sector Job Fairs
resources.description: Job Junction (a Nova Scotia Works centre) hosts regular employer spotlights, sector job fairs, and workplace tour opportunities with local construction firms, trades employers, and healthcare providers. These community events highlight real roles, pay ranges, and training routes, using panels and storytelling to build pride in local careers and directly connect jobseekers with hiring employers.
resources.address: Suite 130, 6950 Mumford Road, Halifax, NS B3L 4W1

solutions.text: Small-Business and Micro-Enterprise Support: Provide mentorship, business planning, and micro-loans through local chambers, non-profits, or cooperative development organizations to help tradespeople and care providers start businesses.

resources.name: CEED Microloan Program
resources.organization: Centre for Entrepreneurship Education and Development (CEED)
resources.description: CEED provides training, one-on-one advising, and business planning to help entrepreneurs launch and grow small businesses, alongside access to microloans and small-business financing. This directly implements the solution by pairing mentorship and planning support with flexible capital that tradespeople, construction subcontractors, and care providers can use to start or expand services in their communities.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 225, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: ISANS Business Development Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS supports immigrant and newcomer entrepreneurs with business counselling, market research, and business plan development, plus workshops and mentorship. Through partnerships with local lenders and programs, ISANS helps clients access microloans and start-up financing—enabling tradespeople, home-care providers, early childhood operators, and other service businesses to get established and fill workforce gaps.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Small Business Loan Guarantee Program
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Co-operative Council (in partnership with Nova Scotia Credit Unions)
resources.description: Delivered through Nova Scotia credit unions, this program offers guaranteed loans that can function as micro- and small-business financing, alongside advisory support from credit union account managers and the Council’s business developers. It implements the solution by improving access to capital for startups and micro-enterprises—including skilled trades, construction subcontractors, home-care and childcare providers—while pairing financing with guidance on business planning.

resources.name: Centre for Women in Business Programs & Advisory
resources.organization: Centre for Women in Business, Saint Mary’s University
resources.description: The Centre offers mentorship, cohort-based training, and one-on-one advisory to help women start and grow enterprises across sectors, including skilled trades and care services. While not a direct lender, they strengthen business plans and connect clients to financing partners (e.g., microloan programs and credit unions), thereby implementing the solution’s mentorship-and-planning pathway linked to accessible capital.
resources.address: 923 Robie Street, Sobey School of Business, Suite 416, Halifax, NS B3H 3C3

solutions.text: Hire-Local Pledge and Recognition Program: Launch a community 'Hire-Local' pledge and public recognition program for employers who invest in local training, apprenticeships, and fair hiring practices.

resources.name: Immigrant Employment Awards
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS’ annual Immigrant Employment Awards publicly recognize Nova Scotia employers who demonstrate inclusive, fair hiring practices and invest in local talent development, mentorship, and on-the-job training for immigrants. By celebrating employer champions and sharing their practices, the program creates a visible ‘recognition platform’ that encourages more organizations to pledge to hire locally and build equitable pathways into work.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Apprenticeship Employer Awards of Excellence
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency (Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency’s Employer Awards of Excellence recognize companies that hire and train Nova Scotians through apprenticeship, invest in mentorship, and support certification in the skilled trades. This public recognition highlights employer leadership, reinforces a hire-local apprenticeship pledge in practice, and motivates more firms to commit to fair hiring and robust training pipelines.
resources.address: 2021 Brunswick Street, 10th Floor, Halifax, NS B3K 2Y5

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth
resources.organization: Construction Association of Nova Scotia (in partnership with the Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency, NSCC, and industry)
resources.description: Building Futures for Youth connects Nova Scotia high school students with paid, mentored summer work placements in the construction sector, with employers committing to safe worksites, training, and pathways into apprenticeship. Participating employers are profiled and recognized by industry partners, reinforcing a community-wide commitment to hire and train local youth in the skilled trades.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Unit 103, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C4

resources.name: Game Changers Youth Retention Initiative
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s Game Changers initiative invited employers to pledge concrete actions—such as offering co-ops, internships, and entry-level jobs—to hire and retain local youth and recent graduates. Employers were publicly celebrated as Game Changers, creating recognition and peer accountability that advances fair hiring and local talent development across sectors.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

solutions.text: Paid Community Internship and Youth Work Placements: Fund short-term paid internships and summer employment in construction, childcare, and healthcare settings to give youth income, experience, and local references.

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.description: BFY places Nova Scotia high school students in paid, supervised summer work terms on real construction sites across the province. By funding and coordinating short-term placements with local contractors and trades, the program gives youth income, hands-on experience, safety training, and references that lead into apprenticeships—directly addressing construction labour shortages.
resources.address: 134 Eileen Stubbs Avenue, Dartmouth, NS B3B 2C8

resources.name: Nova Scotia Health Summer Student Employment Program
resources.description: Nova Scotia Health hires students into paid summer roles in hospitals and community health settings, including clinical support, long-term care, research, and administrative positions. These short-term placements provide income, mentorship, and local references while building a pipeline of young workers to address healthcare staffing gaps.
resources.address: 1276 South Park Street, Halifax, NS B3H 2Y9

resources.name: Co-operative Education Incentive (CEI)
resources.organization: Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: CEI provides a wage subsidy to Nova Scotia employers to hire post-secondary co-op students for paid work terms, helping organizations in sectors like construction, childcare non-profits, and healthcare administration create short-term placements. Youth gain paid, career-related experience and local references while employers address immediate staffing needs and build future talent pipelines.

resources.name: Student Summer Skills Incentive (SKSI)
resources.organization: Department of Labour, Skills and Immigration (Government of Nova Scotia)
resources.description: SKSI funds wage subsidies for Nova Scotia non-profits to hire post-secondary students for paid summer jobs, commonly including roles in childcare centres, community health organizations, and social service agencies. These short-term placements provide income, on-the-job learning, and references for youth while helping community employers meet seasonal workforce needs.

obstacles.title: Public Perception and Regional Brand
obstacles.description: Negative narratives about healthcare, housing, or limited opportunity overshadow genuine strengths. Under-marketing successes weakens attraction and return migration.

solutions.text: Community Storytelling Campaign: Collect and share short videos, photos and written stories from locals — young professionals, tradespeople, entrepreneurs and returnees — that highlight day-to-day quality of life, career pathways and neighborhood strengths; distribute through social channels, local media and partner websites.

resources.name: ISANS Client Success Stories
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS collects and shares short written profiles and videos of immigrants and returnees building careers and lives in Nova Scotia. These stories showcase day-to-day quality of life, employer connections, and clear career pathways across sectors, and are distributed through ISANS’ website, newsletters, and social media. By elevating real resident experiences, the campaign counters negative narratives and highlights community strengths to attract and retain talent.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 102, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: COVE Member Stories
resources.description: COVE produces video spotlights, photo features, and written profiles of ocean-sector professionals, founders, researchers, and skilled tradespeople working on Halifax Harbour. These stories highlight career pathways in the blue economy alongside the region’s lifestyle advantages, and are shared via COVE’s website, social channels, newsletters, and partner networks. The ongoing campaign improves public perception by showcasing real local success and opportunity.

resources.name: IGNITE Stories
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic gathers and publishes short videos, photos, and written spotlights of rural entrepreneurs, students, tradespeople, and innovators from across southwestern and northern Nova Scotia. These stories are distributed through IGNITE’s website, social media, newsletters, and collaborations with schools, municipalities, and local media, highlighting neighborhood strengths and concrete career paths. The campaign showcases everyday quality of life and opportunity to inspire youth and returnees to build their futures in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

solutions.text: Returnee Ambassador Program: Recruit and train volunteers who previously left then returned to Nova Scotia to speak at schools, online panels and recruitment events; ambassadors offer realistic insights, mentor prospective returnees and counter negative narratives with firsthand accounts.

resources.name: Halifax Ambassador Program
resources.description: Halifax Partnership recruits volunteer ambassadors — including Nova Scotians who left and later returned — to share first-hand stories at school talks, online panels, and talent-recruitment events about why they chose Halifax again. Ambassadors receive messaging and speaker resources to present realistic insights on careers, housing, and quality of life, helping counter negative narratives. Many also mentor prospective returnees through introductions and the Partnership’s broader talent-attraction activities.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: The Cape Breton Welcome Network mobilizes trained volunteer ‘Community Connectors,’ many of whom are boomerang Cape Bretoners, to welcome and speak with new and returning residents at community events, schools, and virtual info sessions. These ambassadors share lived returnee experiences, provide practical guidance on housing, careers, and community life, and introduce returnees to local networks. Their storytelling and mentoring actively counter outdated perceptions and highlight genuine opportunities across Cape Breton-Unama’ki.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

resources.name: Here We Code Ambassadors
resources.organization: Dalhousie University Faculty of Computer Science (in partnership with the Province of Nova Scotia and community partners)
resources.description: Here We Code engages ambassadors — industry professionals, alumni, and returnees — to visit classrooms, appear on webinars, and participate in recruitment events showcasing technology education and careers in Nova Scotia. Ambassadors share authentic return-to-NS stories, pathways into tech, and work-life realities, directly addressing misconceptions about limited opportunity. By mentoring students and prospective returnees, they help channel talent back to Nova Scotia’s growing digital economy.

solutions.text: Local Success Spotlight Series: Regularly profile local businesses, startups, artists and community initiatives in a newsletter and on regional platforms, emphasizing measurable outcomes (jobs created, supports available) to show concrete community vibrancy and opportunity.

resources.name: Stories
resources.description: Invest Nova Scotia regularly publishes company success stories and case studies across its website and newsletters, profiling startups and scale-ups from all regions of the province. These features highlight measurable outcomes such as capital raised, jobs created in Nova Scotia, and export growth, and they link directly to supports like venture capital funds, accelerators, and grant programs. By consistently marketing local wins with clear metrics, they showcase the province’s vibrancy and opportunity to residents, youth, and potential returnees.
resources.address: 1871 Hollis Street, Suite 1101, Halifax, NS B3J 0C3

resources.name: Volta Stories
resources.description: Volta runs an ongoing series of founder features and community stories on its blog, newsletter, and social channels that spotlight Nova Scotia startups and ecosystem partners. Profiles regularly surface concrete results—such as Volta Cohort funding awarded, team growth, customers acquired, and revenue milestones—and direct readers to supports including mentorship, programming, and workspace. This steady amplification of measurable achievements builds a visible narrative of local innovation and opportunity.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: Business Voice Magazine
resources.description: Business Voice is the Halifax Chamber of Commerce’s bi-monthly magazine and digital platform that profiles local companies, entrepreneurs, and community initiatives. Articles and member spotlights frequently include metrics such as jobs added, expansions, export activity, and investments, while pointing readers to Chamber programs, training, and networking supports. The publication and accompanying newsletters consistently market regional success stories to reinforce Halifax and Nova Scotia as places of growth and opportunity.
resources.address: 32 Akerley Boulevard, Suite 100, Dartmouth, NS B3B 1N1

resources.name: Alumni Profiles
resources.description: NSCC’s Alumni Profiles and news features regularly spotlight graduates working in trades, technology, arts, and community services across Nova Scotia. These stories emphasize tangible outcomes—employment roles, businesses launched, industry certifications, and career progression—and connect readers to NSCC programs, career services, and employer partnerships. By showcasing real results and clear pathways, the series demonstrates local opportunity and supports retention and return migration.

solutions.text: Community Welcome Hubs: Set up volunteer-run welcome hubs or pop-up centers where newcomers and returning residents can get housing leads, job referrals, health resource navigation and community orientation; hubs can operate at libraries, town halls or festivals.

resources.name: Newcomer Services at Halifax Public Libraries
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries operates welcoming, volunteer-supported newcomer hubs in branches like the Halifax Central Library where people can drop in for orientation, housing information, job search support, and navigation to health and settlement resources. In partnership with ISANS and YMCA YREACH, the Library hosts pop-up info tables, settlement advising, and volunteer-led conversation clubs that help newcomers and returning residents build local networks. This library-based approach directly implements community welcome hubs in an accessible, trusted public space.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: ISANS Settlement Services
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: ISANS provides a centralized welcome hub where newcomers receive settlement orientation, employment counseling and referrals, housing leads, and connections to health and community services. Staff frequently co-locate and run pop-up settlement sessions at libraries and community venues across the province, making supports visible at public hubs and events. These integrated services help counter negative narratives by showcasing tangible pathways to jobs, housing, and community life.
resources.address: 6960 Mumford Road, Suite 2120, Halifax, NS B3L 1H8

resources.name: YMCA YREACH (Immigrant Settlement Services)
resources.description: YREACH delivers mobile, community-based settlement support across Nova Scotia with regular drop-in hours and pop-up welcome sessions in libraries, municipal offices, and other local hubs. The program connects newcomers to housing options, job referrals through employer networks, health care navigation, and community orientation, often partnering with local volunteers and service providers. By bringing services to familiar public spaces, YREACH functions as a network of community welcome hubs in urban and rural areas.

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: This island-wide initiative mobilizes trained volunteer Welcome Ambassadors to meet new and returning residents at community events, municipal offices, libraries, and pop-up welcome tables. Volunteers provide friendly orientation, share housing leads and job referrals through the Cape Breton Partnership’s employer and community networks, and guide people to health and settlement resources. The Network’s on-the-ground, volunteer-run approach embodies community welcome hubs that celebrate local strengths and help newcomers integrate quickly.

solutions.text: Housing Action Coalitions: Form neighborhood-level groups of residents, landlords, small developers and non-profits to identify quick wins on affordable rentals, co-op housing pilots and information sessions that demonstrate local commitment to realistic housing solutions.

resources.name: Our HRM Alliance
resources.description: A coalition anchored by the Ecology Action Centre that convenes residents, community nonprofits, planners, and small builders across Halifax to advance complete communities and attainable housing. Through public forums, neighbourhood workshops, and issue briefs, the alliance highlights practical, near-term actions (e.g., gentle density, secondary suites) and showcases local success stories—aligning with the solution by demonstrating neighbourhood-level commitment to realistic, affordable rental options and community-led pilots.

resources.name: NECHC Housing Support
resources.description: North End Community Health Centre’s Housing Support team brings together residents, landlords, and local service partners to rapidly match people to affordable rentals and stabilize tenancies in Halifax’s North End. The team hosts information sessions for both tenants and property owners, pilots practical tools like landlord engagement and rent-supplement navigation, and coordinates with community nonprofits—operationalizing a neighbourhood-level housing action coalition that delivers quick wins and visible results.

resources.name: Cape Breton Community Advisory Board on Homelessness (Reaching Home)
resources.description: Hosted by United Way Cape Breton, the CAB convenes residents, municipal staff, nonprofits, outreach teams, and property owners to coordinate rapid, practical housing solutions across the CBRM. It organizes information sessions and landlord-engagement initiatives, aligns funding toward quick-start affordable rentals and supportive options, and publicly shares progress—embodying a regional housing action coalition that builds confidence through visible, local solutions.

resources.name: Co-operative Development Program (Housing Co-ops)
resources.description: The Nova Scotia Co-operative Council supports communities to organize resident-led housing co-operatives by facilitating meetings with tenants, local nonprofits, municipal planners, and small developers. Through feasibility assessments, governance training, and public info sessions, the program helps launch co-op pilots and expand attainable rental options—directly implementing the solution’s coalition model for quick, realistic, community-backed housing wins.
resources.address: 60 Research Drive, Bible Hill, NS B6L 2R2

solutions.text: Micro-internships and Apprenticeship Fairs: Organize community-run short-term project placements, job shadow days and apprenticeship fairs connecting youth with local employers and tradespeople to create visible entry points into careers and reduce uncertainty about opportunities.

resources.name: Clean Leadership Summer Internship
resources.description: Clean Foundation’s Clean Leadership Summer Internship places high school and post-secondary youth in paid, short-term (typically 12-week) project roles with municipalities, non-profits, and local businesses in Nova Scotia’s environmental sector. These micro-internships give youth hands-on experience, site-based mentoring, and employer connections, creating visible entry points into green careers and showcasing local opportunities.
resources.address: 126 Portland Street, 6th Floor, Dartmouth, NS B2Y 1H8

resources.name: Career Rising
resources.description: Career Rising provides paid summer work experiences and career exploration for African Nova Scotian and Indigenous high school students, pairing them with local employers across sectors. The program includes job shadow days, employer-led projects, and mentorship, reducing uncertainty about local career paths and highlighting Nova Scotia’s opportunities.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1201, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: NSCC Get Hired Career Fairs & Industry Days
resources.organization: Nova Scotia Community College (NSCC) – Career Services
resources.description: NSCC’s Career Services team organizes campus-based employer events across Nova Scotia, including Get Hired career fairs, apprenticeship and trades showcases, and industry days that connect students with local companies and unions. Many campuses also facilitate short-term, project-based work-integrated learning and job shadow opportunities, giving youth clear entry points into trades and emerging fields.

resources.name: Nova Scotia Works Employment Services (TEAM Work Cooperative)
resources.description: TEAM Work Cooperative, part of the Nova Scotia Works network, runs youth-focused hiring events, employer info sessions, and coordinated job shadow/short-term trial placements with local businesses in HRM. These community-run connections give young people practical exposure to workplaces and tradespeople, easing transitions into jobs and apprenticeships.
resources.address: 7051 Bayers Road, Suite 501, Halifax, NS B3L 4V2

resources.name: Phoenix Employment Services (Phoenix Centre for Youth)
resources.description: Phoenix provides individualized employment support to youth, including arranging job shadowing, short-term work trials, and subsidized placements with local employers. The program hosts employer meet-and-greets and mini hiring fairs, giving young people tangible pathways into careers while building confidence and networks in the community.

solutions.text: Neighbourhood Open Homes and Employer Tours: Host regular open-house events where residents tour workplaces, co-working spaces, maker spaces and sample neighborhoods to experience local workplaces and lifestyle firsthand, dismantling misconceptions through direct exposure.

resources.name: Volta Tours and Open House Events
resources.description: Volta invites students, newcomers, and residents to tour its downtown startup hub, with regular open houses and bookable tours that take visitors through co-working floors, startup offices, and community event spaces. By meeting founders and seeing companies at work, participants get firsthand exposure to local career and entrepreneurial paths in tech, helping counter negative perceptions about opportunity in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 1505 Barrington Street, Suite 100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K5

resources.name: COVE Demo Day and Facility Tours
resources.organization: COVE (Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship)
resources.description: COVE hosts public open houses, scheduled facility tours, and its annual Demo Day, inviting the community onto its waterfront campus to meet ocean-technology companies and see their workspaces and demonstrations. These workplace visits provide direct exposure to high-value ocean careers and collaborative innovation, reframing perceptions of Nova Scotia’s economy and lifestyle anchored around the harbour.

resources.name: Atlantic Open Farm Day (Nova Scotia)
resources.description: Atlantic Open Farm Day invites the public to visit participating Nova Scotia farms for guided tours, demonstrations, and conversations with producers. These behind-the-scenes workplace visits let residents and returnees experience rural livelihoods and agri-food innovation up close, dispelling myths about the sector and showcasing quality of life in farming communities across the province.
resources.address: 7 Atlantic Central Drive, East Mountain, NS B6L 2Z2

resources.name: Port Days Community Open House and Tours
resources.description: During Port Days and related open-house programming, the Halifax Port Authority offers guided tours and public events that bring residents onto port properties to meet terminal operators, logistics firms, and marine service providers. By opening these workplaces and explaining operations firsthand, the port demystifies career paths and highlights the global opportunities and quality of life connected to Halifax’s working waterfront.

resources.name: Doors Open Halifax
resources.description: Doors Open Halifax is an annual city-wide open house that gives the public free access to dozens of buildings, including workplaces, studios, and civic facilities across multiple neighborhoods. By letting people explore work environments and communities they might not otherwise visit, the event replaces outdated narratives with direct, positive experiences of Halifax’s people, industries, and lifestyle.

solutions.text: Regional Brand Cooperative: Create a community-led cooperative of municipalities, businesses, non-profits and cultural groups to pool modest funds and coordinate consistent messaging, visuals and campaigns that celebrate local strengths and correct misinformation.

resources.name: Downtown Halifax Business Commission (DHBC)
resources.description: DHBC is a business improvement district that pools levy funds from member businesses and works in partnership with the Halifax Regional Municipality and cultural organizations to deliver unified branding, marketing campaigns, and events for Downtown Halifax. By coordinating consistent visuals, messaging, and storytelling about downtown’s strengths (entrepreneurship, culture, safety, amenities), DHBC counters negative narratives and showcases real opportunities to live, work, and thrive in the city’s core—supporting talent attraction and retention for young people.
resources.address: 1546 Barrington Street, Suite 104, Halifax, NS B3J 2A2

resources.name: Downtown Truro Partnership
resources.description: Downtown Truro Partnership is a collaborative of local businesses, the Town of Truro, and cultural groups that pools resources to operate coordinated marketing, promotions, and placemaking for the downtown district. Through shared branding (e.g., seasonal campaigns, event marketing, and business spotlights) and consistent messaging about quality of life and opportunity in Colchester County, it amplifies local success stories and corrects misconceptions, helping attract visitors, new residents, and returning youth.

resources.name: Lunenburg Region Partners for Economic Prosperity (LRPEP)
resources.organization: Lunenburg Region Partners for Economic Prosperity
resources.description: LRPEP is a multi-municipal partnership (Municipality of the District of Lunenburg, Towns of Bridgewater, Lunenburg, and Mahone Bay) working with businesses and non-profits to build and manage the unified Lunenburg Region brand. By pooling municipal and private-sector resources, LRPEP delivers consistent regional messaging, brand assets, and campaigns that highlight local strengths—entrepreneurship, trades, ocean tech, and arts—and uses data-informed stories to counter misconceptions about opportunity and lifestyle on the South Shore.

solutions.text: Community Festivals that Showcase Opportunity: Build festivals or pop-up markets focused on local innovation, trades, arts and food where young people can exhibit projects, entrepreneurs can pitch ideas and employers can recruit, making opportunity visible and celebratory.

resources.name: COVE Demo Day
resources.organization: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship (COVE)
resources.description: COVE Demo Day is an annual showcase on the Dartmouth waterfront where local ocean-technology companies, student teams, and startups demonstrate innovations to the public. The event includes pitches, hands-on demos, and networking spaces where employers recruit talent and connect with youth, making opportunities in Nova Scotia’s ocean sector visible and celebratory.

resources.name: Hants County Exhibition
resources.description: The Hants County Exhibition is a multi-day agricultural fair that features 4-H youth competitions, local food vendors, artisans, and machinery/trades demonstrations. It brings together young people, entrepreneurs, and employers in agriculture and related trades to exhibit projects, sell products, and recruit, celebrating rural innovation and opportunity in Nova Scotia.

resources.name: New Glasgow Farmers Market Night Markets & Pop-Up Events
resources.description: The New Glasgow Farmers Market hosts seasonal evening markets and pop-up events that combine local food, live music, artisans, and youth-led ventures. These community gatherings give young entrepreneurs a platform to sell products and showcase skills, while employers and community partners engage through booths and demonstrations that highlight local opportunities.
resources.address: 97 Glasgow Street, New Glasgow, NS B2H 5C8

resources.name: IGNITE Atlantic Startup Showcase & Community Pop-Ups
resources.description: IGNITE Atlantic runs recurring showcases, pitch nights, and pop-up markets in rural communities where startups, student teams, and makers present products and prototypes to the public. Employers, mentors, and investors attend to network and recruit, turning innovation into a celebratory, community-facing experience that spotlights opportunity in Nova Scotia.
resources.address: 352 East River Road, New Glasgow, NS B2H 3P7

resources.name: Devour! The Food Film Fest
resources.description: Devour! is an international food-and-film festival in Wolfville that pairs screenings with culinary events, industry sessions, and youth education programs. It showcases chefs, food entrepreneurs, and local producers through pop-ups and markets, giving young people and emerging businesses a high-profile platform while connecting them with employers and collaborators in the culinary sector.

solutions.text: Youth Retention and Return Council: Establish a youth-led advisory council that identifies barriers, pilots retention initiatives (e.g., transit passes, mentorship), and co-designs messaging for peers to ensure authenticity and greater buy-in from younger audiences.

resources.name: Halifax Regional Municipality Youth Advisory Committee
resources.description: The HRM Youth Advisory Committee is a youth-led body that advises Halifax Regional Council on issues affecting young people, including transportation, housing, recreation, and civic engagement. By identifying barriers and recommending pilot initiatives (such as youth-friendly transit options, mentorship and volunteer pathways, and inclusive public engagement), the committee helps shape programs and co-design youth-facing communications that authentically reflect local youth perspectives—supporting retention and positive regional narratives.

resources.name: NextGen Unama’ki (Cape Breton)
resources.description: NextGen Unama’ki is a youth-led initiative that amplifies the voice of young people in Cape Breton to identify barriers to staying or returning, and to inform employer, municipal, and community responses. Through peer-designed events, mentorship and networking (in collaboration with the Cape Breton Connector Program), and storytelling campaigns like the Vital Awards that showcase youth success, it co-creates authentic messaging and practical pilots that improve youth attraction and retention.

resources.name: Municipality of the County of Kings Youth Council
resources.organization: Municipality of the County of Kings
resources.description: The Kings Youth Council is a group of youth residents who advise municipal leaders on policies and services through a youth lens, surfacing barriers in areas like transportation, recreation, housing, and employment. The council helps co-design peer-facing outreach and engagement, and collaborates with municipal staff and community partners to test practical retention pilots (for example, youth transit access, mentorship and volunteer pathways), strengthening positive perceptions of opportunity in the region.
resources.address: 181 Coldbrook Village Park Drive, Coldbrook, NS B4R 1B9

resources.name: IWK Health Youth Advisory Council
resources.description: The IWK Health Youth Advisory Council engages youth patients and clients to advise on policies, services, and communications so care is more accessible, youth-friendly, and responsive to their needs. By identifying barriers in healthcare access and co-designing messaging and navigation tools that resonate with peers, the council addresses negative narratives about healthcare in Nova Scotia and builds confidence in local systems—an important factor in youth retention and return.

solutions.text: Digital Local Living Portal: Develop a community-maintained website or app aggregating jobs, housing listings, health and childcare resources, events and newcomer guides so accurate, up-to-date local information is easy to find and share.

resources.name: 211 Nova Scotia
resources.description: 211 Nova Scotia is a free, province-wide digital and phone portal that aggregates and maintains a searchable database of community and government services, including housing supports, health and mental health resources, child care, employment programs, newcomer assistance, and local events. Information is continually verified and updated with service providers, giving residents a reliable, up-to-date way to find and share local supports in one place, directly addressing information gaps and negative perceptions.

resources.name: Newcomer Services (Halifax Public Libraries)
resources.description: Halifax Public Libraries maintains an online newcomer hub that consolidates practical, local information on job search supports, housing resources, health care and child care navigation, language learning, and community events across HRM. Librarians and community navigators keep guides and calendars current and link users to partner programs, functioning as a community-maintained digital portal that helps residents and newcomers find accurate, up-to-date local information.
resources.address: 5440 Spring Garden Road, Halifax, NS B3J 1E9

resources.name: Newcomers to Halifax
resources.description: Halifax Regional Municipality’s Newcomers to Halifax portal gathers key local living information in one place, including links to jobs and employment services, renting and homebuying, health care and child care access, schools, transit, and community events. The municipality curates and updates guides and partner listings so people moving to or returning to Halifax can quickly discover opportunities and quality-of-life amenities, reinforcing a positive regional brand.

resources.name: ISANS Newcomer Resources & Events
resources.organization: Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia (ISANS)
resources.description: The Immigrant Services Association of Nova Scotia operates a province-wide online portal that brings together job postings and employment programs, housing and settlement guides, health and child care information, and a continually updated calendar of newcomer workshops and community events. Staff and sector partners contribute and maintain content, making accurate, localized information easy to find and share while showcasing Nova Scotia’s supports and opportunities.
resources.address: 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1020, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2

resources.name: Cape Breton Welcome Network
resources.description: The Cape Breton Welcome Network provides a one-stop digital guide for living and working in Cape Breton, with sections for employment, housing, health care, child care, schools, community groups, and local events. Community connectors and regional partners help keep listings and guides current, showcasing the island’s strengths and making practical, up-to-date local information easy to access and share for newcomers, returnees, and residents.
resources.address: 275 Charlotte Street, Suite 204, Sydney, NS B1P 1C6

solutions.text: Community Employer Pledge and Recognition: Invite local businesses to sign a public pledge on hiring youth, offering clear career pathways and supporting flexible arrangements; recognize participants with a community-backed seal to build trust and attract talent.

resources.name: Game Changers: Experiential Learning Pledge
resources.description: Halifax Partnership’s Game Changers invites employers to publicly pledge to create work-integrated learning (co-ops, internships, project work) and entry-level roles for students and recent graduates, building clear pathways from education to full-time careers. Signatory employers are showcased through Game Changers communications and can promote their participation as a badge of commitment to local youth, strengthening Halifax’s talent brand and helping attract and retain young people.
resources.address: 1809 Barrington Street, Suite 1100, Halifax, NS B3J 3K8

resources.name: Building Futures for Youth (BFY)
resources.organization: Construction Association of Nova Scotia (in partnership with Nova Scotia Apprenticeship Agency and the Nova Scotia Department of Education and Early Childhood Development)
resources.description: BFY enlists construction-sector employers to host paid, mentored summer placements for Grade 11 students, with employers committing to safe worksites, skill development, and pathways into registered apprenticeship.
